Here my honest review. 
Game is worth the money, yes.
Is game worth a console if you own a pc, no.
Does the 30fps make the game unplayable, no.
Do you feel the frames of 30fps… Here’s where we get into it.

Did you complain then? No. What’s your excuse “we’re in 2026, I need my 60fps”. Most of you who say this have never even realized a lot of 60fps games are visual pleasing and or have never played on a pc. Would I have loved for this game to come out on pc instead of dropping 641$ on a digital ps5. Yes and I’m really complaining? No.

Do you honestly want to spend 80+ hours at a desk playing a game because you want 60fps or somewhat better looking graphics? I know some of you are already doing this but I don’t know how.

author: MrSpeznas
quote:
After reading some of the reviews here, I just had to write one myself. Seriously, some of the complaints are absolutely ridiculous.

The driving physics are a fantastic mix of GTA IV and GTA V, leaning much more towards GTA IV. It takes some practice to get used to, but that's exactly what makes it great!

And then I see people complaining that you're supposedly FORCED to go shopping or maintain relationships. Are you kidding me? You don't HAVE to do any of that! These are optional features that make the world feel more alive. Want to maintain a relationship? Go ahead. Don't want to? Then don't. It's literally that simple.

And people complaining about sexual content in an 18+ game? That's like watching an R-rated action movie and complaining there's too much blood. Seriously, what did you expect?

Some people seem absolutely desperate to find reasons to hate this game instead of just enjoying it. Not every feature you personally dislike makes a game bad.

For me, GTA VI is already an absolute masterpiece. The attention to detail, the atmosphere, the characters, the freedom... It's everything I wanted and more.

author: Roach00001
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI – 10/10

Honestly, GTA 6 is amazing.

The driving is one of my favorite parts of the game. It feels like Rockstar found a really good middle ground between GTA 4 and GTA 5. You get some of that weight and physics from GTA 4, where cars actually feel like they have mass, mixed with the more responsive handling of GTA 5. It's a great combination of both worlds.

The beginning is definitely a slow burn. Chapter 1 takes its time, and while I personally enjoyed it, I can see some players getting impatient. If you're jumping in expecting absolute chaos right from the start, you might be disappointed. I think a lot of people went into this expecting GTA 5 Version 2, and that's not really what this game is.

Chapter 2 is where things really start opening up. You get more freedom, more opportunities to explore, and the world starts feeling like it's truly yours to experience.

Gunplay feels great, and the police system is something else entirely. It's a noticeable improvement over previous games. Police encounters feel more engaging, and you actually have to think twice before doing something stupid. You can't just expect every situation to play out like it did in GTA 5.

And honestly, I think that's a good thing. GTA 6 feels like Rockstar has taken what worked in previous games and pushed things forward rather than simply repeating the same formula.

Overall: 10/10.

An amazing experience. If you're expecting GTA 5 with a new map, you might walk away disappointed. If you're willing to let GTA 6 be its own game, there's a whole lot to love.

author: VloneBrazy
quote:
An amazing game that is really immersive. It takes some things from the older GTA games that make them feel like ”life simulators” like working out, eating, playing sports, buying houses and stealing cars but develops them further.
Some people can feel it becomes overwhelming but it is part of the charm and also a modern and more complex version of what always was in GTA games.
The story is captivating but I have to admit that these so far for me are the worst characters in GTA history. They’re less funny, less charming, less cool, less quirky, less intelligent. They’re less of everything it seems like. The focus is more on the relationship between the main characters which is obviously the strongest it has ever been. The world is also more developed than ever. It just feels like when it is all said and done we will remember older GTA games characters more than this one.
The graphics are top notch and in due time with a PC release will be an absolute marvel to look at. But currently it doesn’t get to shine through all the way thanks to the 30fps. Nothing that makes it unplayable but something that holds back the insane graphics of this game. It really is beyond its time.
The driving is insane. It really feels different from GTA 5. More like GTA 4 but heavier and a bit less of the suspension. But the card feel heavy, it is easier to drift and lose control and the crashes actually feel like you are crashing and destroying traffic. You lose health and the car gets totally wrecked and almost undrivable. So it favors skill.
All in all I recommend this game a thousand times to anybody who loves rockstar games and most importantly their modern games like RDR2. Also anybody that loves the thrill of crime games and series but also things like Sims for the feeling of a life simulator.

author: Kelien83
quote:
Bien plus qu'un jeu, une émotion
Je joue aux jeux vidéo depuis des décennies, et pourtant, je ne m'attendais pas à ressentir une telle émotion en découvrant GTA 6.Bien sûr, le jeu est incroyable. Mais ce qui me touche va bien au-delà de ses qualités techniques, de son ambition ou de son univers. Il y a cette atmosphère si particulière, cette impression de découvrir un monde qui ne se contente pas d'être spectaculaire, mais qui semble véritablement vivant. Et puis il y a la bande originale, dont l'identité musicale participe pleinement à l'univers du jeu. La musique possède ce pouvoir extraordinaire de donner une autre dimension aux images, aux personnages et aux histoires. De transformer une scène en souvenir, un instant de jeu en véritable émotion. Et je suis convaincu qu'elle contribue énormément à la force de cette expérience. Et puis il y a un autre sentiment, plus surprenant encore : je suis profondément heureux que ce jeu rencontre un tel succès. Je regarde les chiffres de vente, l'engouement, l'ampleur du phénomène, et j'en éprouve une satisfaction presque inexplicable. Comme si j'assistais à un moment historique du jeu vidéo et que, d'une certaine manière, j'avais la chance d'en faire partie. Mais ce qui rend cette expérience encore plus belle, c'est l'envie de la partager. Hier, au déjeuner, j'en ai parlé avec tellement d'enthousiasme à un collègue que, dès ce matin, il m'envoyait une photo de son écran de lancement. Et cette simple photo m'a fait un plaisir immense. Pas parce que j'avais réussi à le convaincre, mais parce que quelqu'un d'autre allait à son tour découvrir ce qui me bouleverse autant. C'est peut-être cela, finalement, qui me touche le plus. Cette capacité qu'a une œuvre à provoquer une émotion si forte qu'on ne souhaite qu'une chose : la transmettre, la faire vivre à d'autres, même si chacun la ressent à sa manière. GTA 6 est pour moi bien davantage qu'une réussite vidéoludique. C'est une expérience émotionnelle, musicale et humaine. Et après toutes ces années passées à jouer, je trouve assez extraordinaire qu'un jeu puisse encore me surprendre à ce point, me donner des frissons et presque m'émouvoir aux larmes rien qu'en en parlant. C'est aussi pour vivre des moments comme ceux-là que j'aime autant le jeu vidéo.

From alligator-infested swamps to crowded beaches where NPCs film your chaos for social media, every square inch feels genuinely **** the heart of the story are Lucia and Jason, whose electric Bonnie-and-Clyde dynamic grounds the razor-sharp satire with real emotional weight. author: MTP1
quote:
Gorgeous world, but the story doesn't feel like GTA

Let me start with the positives, because there are a lot of them. Graphically this game is close to perfect. The world is incredibly detailed and feels alive, and the interactions with NPCs and the environment are on another level. As an open world sandbox it's easily the best Rockstar has ever made.

The story is where it falls apart for me. From the very first mission it just doesn't feel like GTA. The tone and pacing are off, and it took a long time before the game felt like the series I know. The first part of the story especially is a strange start.

The characters don't fit either. Compare them to Tommy Vercetti in Vice City or Vic Vance in Vice City Stories. Those characters had personality, attitude and that classic GTA crime story energy. Jason and Lucia don't come close to that. I understand what Rockstar was going for with the relationship between them, but it just doesn't belong in a GTA game. It feels like a different franchise.

There are also some technical and design choices I don't understand. There's no first person mode, which is strange since GTA V had one and it was a great way to experience such a detailed world. Performance on PS5 isn't always stable either. In some moments the framerate drops below 10 fps, which really hurts the experience in a game that looks this good.

A smaller thing that bugged me: Jason's movement sounds are almost identical to Arthur Morgan's from Red Dead Redemption 2. Once you notice it, you can't stop hearing it, and it pulls you out of the experience.

Overall, the world, graphics and gameplay are almost flawless, and that alone makes it worth playing. But if you're coming in for the classic GTA story and characters, you might be disappointed like I was. 8/10.

author: Saritza
quote:
Rendimiento técnico: en mi experiencia apenas he tenido bugs y no he notado problemas de rendimiento graves, en algún que otro punto note pequeñas bajadas sobre todo en Vice City, pero no es algo alarmante ni nada mas de 5 fps en uno de los peores casos, es el juego mas pulido de Rockstar para que engañarnos. Muchos de los bugs que circulan x twitter son bugs provocados por los usuarios o IA en algunos casos que si no te fijas en ellos te la pueden colar, pero como mires mas de 5 segundos ves el clip modificado en IA.

En cuanto al Gameplay es entretenido, hay muchas actividades por hacer pero todas se concentran en el final del capitulo 2 e inicio del capitulo 3, de hecho yo tengo un colega que se ha pasado 20h haciéndose el capitulo 1 y perdió todo su dinero acumulado, asi que os daré un pequeño consejo en ese aspecto, GUARDAD VUESTRO DINERO EN EL BANCO por que va a pasar un evento del que hablaremos mas adelante en el que vais a perder el dinero del alijo o que tengáis en mano, incluido el vapid del 71 de Jason así que antes de completar la misión de Mattia, guardad el dinero en el banco y vender todos los alijos que tengáis a Brian aunque os pague una miseria. 

La policía es de lo mejor que hay en este juego y deberíais tener en cuenta que vuestros perfiles criminales dependerán el reto que busquéis, cuanto mas matéis o empleéis la violencia mas agresivos serán, cuanto menos violencia uséis y mas profesionales seáis la policía será mas "permisiva" con vosotros, por ende el juego te incentiva a ser "profesional" y a causar el menor daño posible dentro de su entorno criminal.

Historia:

La historia nos lleva de la mano de Jason ( el criminal de sangre fria, estoico y realista ) y Lucia quien en su contraste es todo lo opuesto de Jason,  uno de los grandes problemas que veo en esta dinamica es que todo el desarrollo se centra en Lucia mientras que con Jason en si se siente mas como un personaje de apoyo o el "miedo" a no poner sola una mujer como protagonista por ver que dirá la fanaticada. A medida que vamos avanzando vamos viendo una conspiración de corrupción en las altas esferas que llevará a nuestros protagonistas a tres finales.

Puedes jugar como un psicópata todo el juego y si o si vas a tener uno de los dos finales malos o cultivar la relación, ser un criminal "profesional" y cumplir los objetivos de la cuenta y obtener el "mejor final" dentro de lo malo, y en este aspecto se nota que Rockstar han querido hacer un RDR2 con la apariencia de GTA demostrando que la saga con la que crecimos que transmitia una fantasia de poder, sexo, y drogas en los 80's busca crear una historia mas humana y mas alejada de la fantasía "push it to the limit" que caracterizo a Tommy Vercetti ( curioso que el nombre del hijo de la pareja sea una referencia a este criminal ) .

Vamos a los tres finales y a sus perfiles. [ Aqui llegan los spoilers ]

A diferencia de GTA V donde todo se reduce a A) B) o C) aquí tus acciones en Vice City tienen peso, asi que medita que tipo de criminal quieres ser por que el truco de ser un ser desalmado y luego donar ingentes cantidades de dinero al campamento para obtener honor alto con Arthur aquí no te va a servir.

Final "bueno", si con ambos personajes logras un perfil profesional y los 2 millones en los ahorros familiares,  Jason y Lucia sobrevivirán, esta ultima será libre a costa de que Jason sacrifique su libertad, Lucia logrará su deseo de reunirse con su hijo y Jason de conocerlo, lo que implica que Jason asume las culpas por Lucia dándonos un cierre amargo, pero el mas positivo de los tres.

El segundo tiene dos ramificaciones dependiendo de la relación que tengas con ambos, y es una clara referencia a Bonnie y Clyde y la forma en la que mueren siendo acribillados, independientemente de si mueren sin llevarse a nadie por delante o se llevan a varios polis en su ultima pelea a lo "john marston" en beechers hope.

El tercero es que la corrupción de Vice City los devora y Méndez los asesina fuera de cámaras.

GTA VI es un recordatorio de que las personas que se adentran en el crimen rara vez acaban bien, y una deconstrucción perfecta de la ciudad del vicio, agarrando todo lo que hizo grande a Vice City de 2002 y llevándolo al extremo opuesto, si Vice City de 2002 era una oda del criminal que no tenia y logra su fantasía de Scarface aquí vemos todo lo contrario, criminales de bajo perfil con antecedentes que pudieron reconducir sus vidas y que su deseo de obtener ingresos rápidos les termina costando todo lo que tienen, el cuanto terminen perdiendo va a depender solo de ti.

8,5 / 10.

author: AlexStkross

author: DanieleKaldwin
quote:
After over a decade of waiting, Rockstar Games has delivered something truly extraordinary. Vice City and the state of Leonida aren’t just a massive map; they feel like a living, breathing ecosystem where every street corner, NPC routine, and random encounter has an unprecedented level of detail and reactivity.
​The narrative dynamic between Jason and Lucia is easily one of Rockstar’s finest achievements—grounded, sharp, and emotionally engaging, elevated by top-tier voice acting and cinematic direction. The mission design feels much more organic and flexible compared to previous entries, and the physics, lighting, and dense crowds push current-gen hardware to its absolute limits.
​Addressing the elephant in the room regarding the recent review bombing: yes, the game runs at a locked 30 FPS on console. Anyone who understands game development knows that simulating a world of this scale, density, and AI complexity simply wouldn't be possible at 60 FPS without stripping away everything that makes this world feel alive. It’s a rock-solid, visually jaw-dropping experience that sets the benchmark for the next ten years of gaming. A well-deserved 10/10.

author: deyonek
quote: Grand Theft Auto VI – Early Impressions (6/10)I have mixed feelings about GTA VI so **** years, GTA VI has been treated almost like a legendary game, something that would redefine open-world gaming. But now that we’re finally playing it, I sometimes feel like we’re getting a mix of Far Cry, Assassin’s Creed and Sleeping Dogs rather than the classic GTA ****’t get me wrong: the game looks absolutely incredible, especially on my Samsung S90C OLED. The map is fantastic, the characters are interesting, and the opening hours are genuinely engaging. Leonida Keys, where Jason lives, is one of my favorite locations so far.However, something feels different.I miss the simplicity and freedom of older GTA games. I miss being able to spend hours doing absolutely nothing, ignoring missions, driving around, causing chaos or simply enjoying the world at my own **** VI feels more grounded and realistic. You feel more like an ordinary person living in this world rather than an over-the-top criminal with almost unlimited freedom. And honestly, I don’t necessarily think that’s a bad thing. It’s just a different direction.Some mechanics, like weapon storage, also make me wonder whether Rockstar is prioritizing realism over the freedom and convenience that made previous GTA games so **** world is beautiful, the atmosphere is fantastic, and there is clearly a lot to appreciate. But I don’t want a game that constantly tells me what to do. I want a world where I can create my own fun without feeling like I always need to make **** now, I’d give GTA VI a solid 6/10.I’m still early in the story, so my opinion might change. I’m genuinely impressed by many aspects of the game, but I haven’t fully connected with its gameplay philosophy yet.

author: michele17194
quote: A Game That Truly Reveals Itself in Chapter 3I honestly don't understand many of the criticisms being directed at GTA 6. In my opinion, judging this game before reaching Chapter 3 means missing the bigger picture **** first two chapters should be seen for what they really are: an introduction, an extended tutorial designed to establish the characters, the world, the mechanics, and the foundations of the experience. They are not a true representation of what the game eventually becomes.Once you reach Chapter 3, everything starts coming together, and that's when you can finally appreciate GTA 6 for what it truly is: an incredibly immersive, ambitious, and massive experience. The world opens up, the depth becomes increasingly apparent, and the game begins to demonstrate the full extent of its potential.A game of this scale needs time to unfold. Not everything has to be revealed immediately, and not every mechanic needs to be thrown at the player within the first few hours.I believe many of the negative reactions come from judging the experience too early, without giving the game enough time to develop and reveal its true **** advice: reach Chapter 3 before forming a definitive opinion. That's when you can genuinely judge GTA 6 as the complete experience it was designed to be.Patience makes all the difference. This is a game that deserves to be experienced before it is judged.

author: FrickinLemons
quote: I can’t say enough great things about this game. Though it’s not perfect as critics have let on, it is no where near as bad as these guys on the user reviews have made it out to be. What you’re given here is a true open world experience within the confines of the story they want to tell. This is very much Red Dead Redemption 2’s camp-to-camp style story, where you will travel from place to place to experience a little bit of everything this world has to offer. Zoos, parks, gyms, beaches, and just so much more come to mind when thinking about the vastness of what I’ve sunk about 45 hours into so far. Elements from every Rockstar game leading up to this point like bullet markers when shooting NPCs showing both where you hit and also how critical of a hit it was felt like it came straight from Max Payne 3. Choice option prompts to dice up small elements within interactions and missions take inspiration from LA Noire. Vehicle customization and races feel so much more fleshed out and along the lines of Midnight Club in this entry as opposed to those from the previous games. It draws heavy elements of gameplay and progression from both Red Dead and GTA as a whole. This is a very different breed of game and it has been controversial to say the least, but I couldn’t be happier. I have not been this immersed in a world since 2015’s The Witcher 3, and I believe this game will continue to push Rockstar’s creative ideas forward in the future. Easy 9/10 from me and I’m looking forward to seeing what comes next.

author: AriaSKennedy
quote:
10/10 — A Generation Ahead. Once Again.

After 15 hours of experiencing GTA VI, I can confidently say that Rockstar Games has achieved something extraordinary.

One of the most astonishing things about this game is that even after 15 hours, I still find myself exploring Key Lento and its surrounding areas. The sheer number and variety of activities, interactions, discoveries, and things to experience make it genuinely difficult to leave this part of the world. There is always something new waiting around the corner.

Rockstar's incredible diversity, world-building, and attention to detail deserve the highest praise. The world doesn't simply exist around you; it feels alive. Its atmosphere, environmental storytelling, soundtrack, lighting, and carefully crafted vibes demonstrate an artistic understanding that very few studios can match.

And that atmosphere deserves special recognition. For four generations, Rockstar has consistently demonstrated an extraordinary ability to create memorable worlds and unforgettable atmospheres. Thank you for another masterpiece of environmental design.

For the third consecutive time, Rockstar has delivered a revolutionary leap into a generation beyond the current gaming industry. First with GTA V, then with Red Dead Redemption 2, and now once again with GTA VI. This is not merely technological progress; it is a fundamental evolution in the way open worlds can be designed and experienced.

I wholeheartedly agree with the critics' overwhelmingly positive assessment. When you consider the overall package — gameplay, world design, immersion, atmosphere, technical ambition, and attention to detail — GTA VI deserves to stand among the greatest video games ever created, alongside the legendary The Legend of Zelda.

And perhaps the greatest testament to Rockstar's achievement is something quite personal: I spend hours playing GTA VI on my console, and eventually, when I need a change of pace, I find myself returning to Red Dead Redemption 2. That is the level of quality Rockstar has established across its games.

Thirteen years of waiting, numerous delays, and enormous expectations — and somehow, this experience makes the wait worthwhile. Every bit of it.

Rockstar Games, thank you for reminding us what video games can achieve when ambition, creativity, and dedication come together.

To fellow players and reviewers: I encourage everyone to approach this game with fairness, rational judgment, and an appreciation for what has genuinely been accomplished here. Criticism is always welcome, but let us distinguish between genuine evaluation and reactionary scoring.

GTA VI — 10/10. A landmark achievement in gaming history.

author: JulianMcFly
quote:
GOTY 
One of the ultimate benchmarks of modern gaming, setting a new standard for every upcoming AAA blockbuster. Grand Theft Auto VI is the greatest open-world game ever created. It brings back gameplay mechanics that had been lost over time, both from within the franchise and from other developers, while introducing features never seen before.A 13-year wait that proved what years of hard work and professional dedication can achieve. Technically and literally, it is the most ambitious video game of all time. In an era of AI-generated rehashes and online multiplayer games built around microtransactions, it is refreshing to see that the greatest game of all time is a **single-player experience**.

author: maksy10
quote:
Gta 6 is gorgeous, bloated-in-the-best-way crime saga that loses its nerve
There's a particular feeling that comes from spending a long evening in a Rockstar world: the sense that someone, somewhere, cared about every square foot of it. Grand Theft Auto VI is enormous, packed with things to do, and yet I came away thinking of it as focused, lean and sharp rather than bloated. Each chapter plays like a season of television, with its own stakes, its own escalation and its own climax, even if the whole thing occasionally outstays its welcome.
Moment to moment, it is a joy. The gameplay is wonderfully assured, and the driving in particular is a highlight, with a weight and responsiveness that sit among the best Rockstar has ever made. You could happily spend an hour doing nothing but cruising. The world is stunning to look at, but it's the small things that linger: the easter eggs tucked into corners, waiting for the curious, and the obsessive attention to detail that rewards even a passing glance. Even the animals seem lovingly considered, which does more to make the world feel alive than any grand set piece. Then there's the radio, a curated pleasure I rarely wanted to switch off, the kind of soundtrack that turns a mundane drive into a scene.
What impresses most is how well Rockstar has stitched its systems and its open world into the campaign. In previous games, the sandbox and the story often felt like two separate ambitions politely sharing a disc. Here they finally feel woven together, and nowhere more so than in Chapters 3 and 4, where everything clicks and the game hits a stride I wish it had held from start to finish.
Sadly, the story is where it falters. The pacing is uneven, with stretches that turn repetitive and sluggish, and the ending arrives with a shrug rather than a bang. Jason is the heart of the problem: a dull, underwhelming lead who never quite earns his place at the centre of things. It falls to Lucia to supply the emotional weight, and the chemistry and complicity between the two is the glue that holds everything together. It's what made me want to experience every corner of the game, and it's what will keep me coming back. You can't help wishing the writing had given the pair a more compelling story to live in.
Technical blemishes dull the shine a little, too. Bugs and frame drops pull you out of an otherwise immaculate illusion, and the colossal weight of hype set expectations that no game, however accomplished, could hope to meet. Judged on its own terms, this is a remarkable piece of work. Judged against a decade of anticipation, it can't help but feel slightly diminished.
Verdict: A beautiful, brilliantly played sandbox, let down by a story that never matches its ambition. Great, but not the masterpiece we were promised.

author: Alan_holden_
quote:
Joguei a versão de PS5, 20 horas de gameplay e mal iniciei o capítulo 2. A qualidade gráfica, os detalhes minuciosos e realistas de gameplay, a variação de animações, o nível de interatividade com o mundo, os biomas tão vivos e a fauna extremamente diversificada.. tudo isso são coisas que definitivamente fazem desse jogo um diferencial. Você não encontrará nada com esse nível de interatividade e - me arrisco a dizer - de beleza como um todo, em qualquer outro jogo. É, no entanto, bem diferente dos demais GTA's: pode esquecer aquela coisa de fazer um massacre na praia e sair ileso como se nada tivesse acontecido, as ações são mais realistas e consequentemente mais punitivas. Os protagonistas não são mais descompromissados e sim indivíduos que se importam um com o outro, o bom relacionamento de Jason e Lucia parece intrínseco ao desenrolar do jogo, fugir da polícia é mais complicado (embora eu não tenha achado algo tão difícil quanto muitos estão dizendo). É necessário mais planejamento e cautela para realizar ações como assaltos... "O motor do carro está ok?", "devo levar a calibre 12 ou o fuzil de assalto?", "o que deixo no carro e o que levo comigo?"... Essas perguntas vão permear sua jogatina durante o jogo. Fica claro que essa é uma mistura de GTA com RDR2. Acho que é devido a essas características mais "pé no chão" que algumas pessoas estão dizendo que o jogo é ruim, embora eu considere que boa parte destes estão agindo como haters, ou jogaram pouquíssimo do jogo porque a percepção que tive é que ao se entregar à proposta do jogo e deixar-se levar por algumas boas horas de gameplay fica quase impossível não se maravilhar com a dimensão e o capricho deste novo título. 
 Os pontos negativos que aponto são a corrida dos personagens que, embora estejam fluidas, achei menos realista que a de RDR2 e até mesmo a de GTA 5, não há mais a inércia inicial no início ou final do pique do personagem ao correr. Como um amigo meu que já soma 15 horas de gameplay me disse "a corrida está mais leve". Outro ponto é o embaçamento de tela principalmente a elementos que estão mais longe (talvez para ocultar defeitos de draw distance?). Por último, por que diabos os personagens não tocam na tela do celular ao utiliza-lo? E a cerveja da geladeira tinha mesmo que "brotar" na mão do personagem? É o que as pessoas vêm apontando, ( o realismo exagerado não era a causa das opiniões mistas??). Para mim, as falhas são mínimas para um jogo tão grandioso. Considero essa, com certeza, a obra prima da Rockstar.

author: CapixabaOFC
quote: Grand Theft Auto VI é simplesmente uma obra-prima! É impressionante o nível de qualidade, dedicação e cuidado que a Rockstar colocou em cada detalhe desse jogo. Os gráficos são absurdos, com cenários extremamente detalhados, iluminação incrível, reflexos, sombras, animações e uma qualidade visual que torna o mundo muito mais realista e envolvente. É daqueles jogos em que você para simplesmente para admirar a paisagem e observar tudo ao seu redor.O mundo aberto é um espetáculo à parte. Leonida e Vice City são cheias de vida, com ambientes variados, cidades movimentadas, praias, estradas, estabelecimentos e inúmeros detalhes que fazem tudo parecer vivo. A sensação de estar dentro de um mundo que continua acontecendo ao seu redor é fantástica. O clima dinâmico, as mudanças de tempo e a quantidade de acontecimentos durante a exploração deixam a experiência ainda mais imersiva.A história também é um dos grandes destaques. Jason e Lucia formam uma dupla extremamente interessante, e acompanhar a trajetória dos dois, seus problemas, suas decisões e a relação entre eles torna tudo muito mais envolvente. A narrativa consegue misturar ação, emoção, tensão, momentos engraçados e situações inesperadas de uma maneira excelente.A jogabilidade merece todos os elogios possíveis. Dirigir, explorar, participar de perseguições, enfrentar inimigos, realizar missões e planejar assaltos são atividades que tornam a experiência extremamente divertida. As mecânicas de combate, direção e furtividade acrescentam variedade à gameplay, permitindo diferentes maneiras de enfrentar as situações.Outro ponto fantástico é a quantidade de atividades disponíveis. Corridas, pesca, exploração, minijogos, interações com personagens e diversas possibilidades de aproveitar o mundo fazem com que o jogo não seja apenas sobre seguir missões. Sempre existe alguma coisa interessante para fazer, descobrir ou experimentar.A inteligência e o comportamento dos personagens, as animações, as expressões faciais e a ambientação também merecem destaque. Tudo contribui para deixar o universo muito mais convincente. A trilha sonora e as rádios ajudam a construir a identidade de cada lugar, tornando até mesmo os momentos em que estamos simplesmente dirigindo pelo mapa extremamente agradáveis.Também é impossível não elogiar o trabalho técnico da Rockstar. O nível de detalhes, a construção dos ambientes, a apresentação cinematográfica e a atenção aos pequenos elementos mostram o tamanho da ambição desse projeto. É um jogo que demonstra o quanto um mundo aberto pode evoluir quando existe tanto cuidado em sua **** geral, GTA VI entrega uma experiência gigantesca, envolvente, divertida e extremamente bem construída. É o tipo de jogo que consegue prender a atenção por horas e fazer você querer continuar explorando mesmo depois de terminar uma missão. Cada aspecto contribui para uma experiência memorável.Sinceramente, merece nota 10 sem nenhuma dúvida! Um dos jogos mais impressionantes que já tive a oportunidade de conhecer. A Rockstar conseguiu elevar ainda mais o nível da franquia Grand Theft Auto. É difícil encontrar palavras para descrever o tamanho desse trabalho. Simplesmente espetacular, incrível e uma verdadeira obra-prima dos videogames. Vale cada segundo de experiência!

quote:
Dla mnie bez dwóch zdań gra roku, gra dekady, a w sumie to nawet gra wieku. Od pierwszych chwil widać, że ten tytuł to zupełnie inna liga i na długo odjeżdża konkurencji.
​Największą robotę robi tu ogromny, żyjący świat, w którym po prostu chce się być. Grafika jest kozacka, przyroda wygląda obłędnie, a pojazdy, fizyka, różnorodne animacje i zachowanie NPC-ów siedzą na takim poziomie, że co chwilę łapiesz się na małych detalach, których w innych grach po prostu nie ma. Wszystko tu do siebie gra i sprawia wrażenie dopieszczonego pod kątem klimatu i skali.
​Jasne, były błędy na premierę, a na konsolach są ograniczenia FPS, ale ciężko się dziwić – konsole mają swoje fizyczne granice i nie są w stanie wyciągnąć z tego więcej przy tak ciężkim, napakowanym detalami świecie. Ambicja tego projektu po prostu wyprzedza możliwości części sprzętu.
Mimo tych zgrzytów na starcie i limitów sprzętowych na konsolach, gra jest po prostu piękna i wciąga na maksa.
Jedyny duży minus to te wszystkie korzyści pod GTA+, bo to już czuć, że jest podciągane pod kasę.

author: jlimaklaic
quote:
Estamos diante da maior produção da história dos videogames. 

Você pode até não gostar, mas ignorar o terremoto que a Rockstar causou com esse lançamento é, no mínimo, miopia.

GTA continua sendo GTA, e isso é um elogio. Jason e Lucia são apresentados ao jogador de forma orgânica, sem pressa e sem atalhos, respeitando o tempo de cada sentimento. 
A progressão tem fôlego de filme de ação: perseguições de tirar o fôlego e cortes que apertam o peito na hora certa (a última missão do Capítulo 1 é de tirar o fôlego).

O jogo é também uma releitura de Bonnie e Clyde, e nada é mais "made in USA" do que um casal de criminosos que entra para a cultura popular justamente pela história de amor que viveu. Se essa história acontecesse em 2026, ela seria romantizada como foi nos anos 1930? Ou causaria incômodo pela ousadia? 

Esse desconforto é GTA VI!  A série sempre soube mostrar o espelho da sociedade americana.

E não, o jogo não é um simulador de "vida de casados".

author: PauloCarvalho
quote:
Nota: 10/10 – Uma obra-prima dos videogames!

Grand Theft Auto VI é simplesmente absurdo! Tudo nesse jogo parece ter sido pensado para elevar a indústria dos videogames a outro nível. O mundo aberto é impressionante, cheio de vida, detalhes e possibilidades. Cada rua, cada personagem e cada situação parecem fazer parte de um universo vivo e extremamente imersivo.

Os gráficos são de tirar o fôlego, a ambientação é espetacular e a qualidade visual demonstra o cuidado absurdo com cada detalhe. A história promete ser envolvente, os personagens são marcantes e a dinâmica entre eles traz ainda mais personalidade à experiência.

A Rockstar mais uma vez demonstra sua capacidade de criar mundos gigantescos que fazem o jogador esquecer que está diante de um videogame. A liberdade de exploração, o humor característico da franquia, as missões e a atenção aos pequenos detalhes tornam a experiência extremamente especial.

É aquele tipo de jogo que faz você perder horas simplesmente explorando o mapa, descobrindo coisas novas e criando suas próprias histórias.

Nota final: 10/10. Uma experiência que representa o potencial máximo dos jogos de mundo aberto. GTA VI não é apenas um jogo, é um verdadeiro acontecimento na história dos videogames!

author: ThePlayRG
quote:
A Rockstar conseguiu superar o hype sobre o game e entregou o extraordinário.

Ela conseguiu extrair o máximo de cada console e levou seu time de designers, desenvolvedores para outro patamar. 

GTA6 é a última grande obra feita por humanos. A partir de agora acredito que os estúdios usarão a IA para auxiliar no desenvolvimento.  E ainda assim vai demorar para chegar no nível técnico de GTA6. 

A sensação de andar na rua parece muito real, somada aos sons impecáveis trazendo uma atmosfera incrível. Cada nível de detalhe incrível. E não é que você precise procurar por esses detalhes, a soma deles te entrega tudo, te coloca nesse mundo. 

Estou com 40% da estória completa, não posso opinar muito sobre ela. Mas até agora achei tudo muito bem feito e digno de bons filmes policiais. 

Todo lançamento de GTA foi marcado por protestos e processos judiciais contra a Rockstar devido à liberdade de caos, mortes e cenas sexualizadas. 
Passaram-se 13 anos após GTA5, o mundo mudou. As pessoas estão ainda mais intolerantes umas com as outras e brigando por pouca coisa. 
Sinto que a Rockstar estava com menos apetite para enfrentar gente chata no tribunal. 

Uma forma da Rockstar amenizar as coisas, até pelo realismo do game, foi colocar a Lucia como par romântico. Isso atenuou muito as coisas. Afinal, todo o caos e mortes têm um propósito: o amor. 

Não dava para simplesmente entregar um realismo extremo e liberdade total. Isso trariam muitos problemas. Afinal é um game que dura 10 anos. Gerações crescem jogando GTA. 
Quem joga GTA6 agora percebe que tudo tem consequência, mas sem deixar de ser divertido.   

Uma obra prima que merece o GOTY 2026.

author: This_1s_N0body
quote:
As some one who has ACTUALLY PLAYED the game, I normally don't review stuff here and I've been noticing that this game is getting review bombed, I'm not the biggest GTA fan but this is by far one of the best games I've ever played, yeah the first chapter is slow, and some of the chores are boring, but it only goes higher and higher from there.
Pros
-the best open world in a GTA game and possibly in all of gaming in general.
-Best vehicle handling physics in the series, a lot similar to GTA4. Unlike 5 where a Hatchback is just as good on off-road as a rally car for some reason.
-Everything in the environment can be interacted with.
-The guns feel amazing, similar to RDR2.
-The crash physics are incredible, it's almost like BeamNG.
-the story is more serious compared to GTA5, kinda similar to GTA4.
-More player agency, this is something I was wishing for, RDR2 and GTA5 holds your hands so much with those captions on the bottom centre of the screen asking you to "open the door", "go to the barn" so much so if you failed at any of these simple tasks, it's game over. GTA6 is more open ended, even if you don't do certain things that the game tells you to, you can still finish the mission and for each thing you do or don't do, there's a cut scene for each.
-you plan your own heists this time, unlike in GTA5, where you only go on heists that are set by the story, this time you plan it yourself.
-great NPC interactions, sometimes you'd have a totally random NPC reactions, that feel scripted but they aren't.
-this is the most violent GTA game.
-the most difficult Police chases in the franchise.
-love the story, while it's not as high as RDR2,the story made much more sense than GTA5 which to me personally only made sense half way through the game. It's a close tie with GTA4.

Cons.
-the first chapter is slow and can hurt the impression through the amount of chores it encourages you to do, I say encourage because it's all optional.
-Cant steal every vehicle from the get go, you'd unlock tools as you progress to eventually be able to steal any car you want.
-30fps, yes at times it's very apparent. But personally it was mostly stable.

author: Miina
quote:
Love the game it is a technical and a masterful achievement. All the details, animations and just the feeling of a true open world game that is full of live makes this just amazing. 

There is some game design choices I would not have taken myself (the psycho and irredeemable meeters for instance just why would you take away things from the player it feels like a text book example on what not to do).  Plus they have added some hinders for shooting in some areas or in certain situations that I also feel are not true to the GTA experience. It is also a bit slow in the beginning. I think if they moved the house fixing and errands to a bit longer into the game when you had the time to build your relationship with Lucia some more people would not have any issues with it. The ting is as I also like more sim games I actually had no issues with those parts I liked to pimp up my house and car and try to impress on Lucia. 
It is me and my boyfriend who plays this and he does the driving and I do the sim parts and then   We play the shoot out mission alternating between us  we are having a blast!

For the characters I feel the duo of Jason and Lucia works but I personally would maybe made Lucia a bit more warmer towards Jason to make her more likable. I totally understand why she needs to be hard with others people but her partner should be able to have the nicer side of her. Also they could have made Jason have a bit more flavor he is the silent stoic type I get that but make him have some quirks of weird/ nerdy hobbies etc.. just something to make him feel a bit more unique. 
I just love the voice actor for Brian he is sooo so good! 
And omg how fleshed out all the NPCs and all characters are. It is the first game that has that in the game.

I would also in the setting add options for sensitivity for the steering when driving the car it is as now super sensitive so it is hard not to crash into things.

Final thoughts if you are thinking of buying the game and have seen all the mixed reviews. I would say play the game it is amazing and it is an experience like no other. But know that it has some restrictions that the other GTA games didn’t have plus be prepared for a slow start before it ramps up and gets really really good!

author: jpfagundes89
quote:
Jogar GTA 6 no PlayStation 5 Pro é daquelas experiências que fazem a gente parar no meio da rua só para olhar o cenário antes de apertar qualquer botão. Eu simplesmente adorei o jogo — e, para ser bem direto, ele superou todas as minhas expectativas.
Gráficos de cair o queixo
Os gráficos estão lindos em um nível absurdo. O salto visual no PS5 Pro fica evidente logo nos primeiros minutos: a iluminação, os reflexos em superfícies molhadas, a densidade de detalhes urbanos e naturais e a fluidez geral entregam uma sensação de imersão muito forte. Na minha TCL 65C845, com os ajustes de imagem e modo de jogo calibrados para o console, o contraste, o HDR e a definição saltam aos olhos tanto de dia quanto à noite.
Imersão e ritmo
Além da beleza visual, o jogo prende do começo ao fim. A atmosfera, a atenção aos detalhes espalhados pelo mapa e a forma como tudo parece vivo fazem a experiência fluir sem perder o fôlego. É o tipo de título que entrega exatamente o peso de um grande lançamento da Rockstar, mas sem parecer apenas "mais do mesmo" — ele eleva o padrão do que eu esperava ver nesta geração.
Veredito
Se a dúvida era se GTA 6 entregaria à altura de tanta espera, a resposta no PS5 Pro é um sim absoluto. Visualmente deslumbrante, envolvente e acima do que eu imaginava. Vale cada hora jogada.

author: 329-life
quote:
10/10. Ignore the noise, this game is incredible.I didn't expect GTA 6 to get review-bombed and turned into a hate campaign within 48 hours of launch, but here we are. A lot of the negative reviews are from people who are clearly triggered by something other than the game itself: the price, the digital code in the box, the "woke" talking points that started back at the first trailer. Some of them obviously haven't even played it. 

What's actually in the game: Leonida is the most alive open world Rockstar has ever built. The city, the swamps and the coastline all feel lived in, and the NPCs react to you in ways that still surprise me. Lucia and Jason work really well as leads, the writing is sharp, and the satire hits as hard as the series ever has. Driving, shooting and the little details are classic Rockstar, just pushed further than anyone else is doing it.

Is it perfect? No. It runs at 30fps on console and there were launch bugs, same as every massive release. That's worth a patch, not a 1/10. Comparing it to Cyberpunk at launch is pure drama.

If you're on the fence, play it yourself and don't let an outrage wave decide for you. This is one of the best games I've played in years.

author: Masterxpro
quote:
GTA 6 – BENVENUTI IN LEONIDA, DOVE OGNI STRADA RACCONTA UNA STORIA

Tredici anni. Tanto è passato dall'uscita di GTA 5, e in questo tempo l'attesa per il nuovo capitolo è diventata quasi una leggenda a sé. Il rischio era enorme: nessun gioco può davvero reggere un hype del genere. Eppure Grand Theft Auto VI ci riesce. Rockstar non si è limitata a costruire un seguito più grande e più bello. Ha ripensato da zero cosa significa vivere un mondo aperto.

UNA COPPIA, NON DUE PROTAGONISTI
Il cuore pulsante del gioco sono Jason e Lucia. GTA 5 aveva già sperimentato i protagonisti multipli, ma qui il discorso è diverso. Non si tratta di due **** tra cui saltare a piacimento, ma di una coppia vera, con un legame che regge tutto il peso della narrazione. I loro dialoghi, le tensioni, i momenti di complicità e quelli di crisi rendono la storia più umana di qualsiasi altro capitolo della serie. Sono, senza esagerare, i **** più riusciti che Rockstar abbia mai scritto.

L'avventura parte in sordina, in una piccola cittadina costiera nel sud della mappa, lontana dai grattacieli e dalle luci di Vice City. La città si intravede in lontananza, quasi un miraggio, ed è proprio questa scelta a funzionare: il gioco ti fa desiderare di arrivarci. Quando finalmente la mappa si apre, la sensazione di libertà è travolgente.

LEONIDA: UN MONDO CHE RESPIRA
Lo stato di Leonida, la versione Rockstar della Florida, è probabilmente l'open world più vivo mai realizzato. Non c'è la classica lista di icone da spuntare sulla mappa, niente torri da scalare né collezionabili messi lì per allungare il brodo. Si esplora perché il mondo stesso ti invita a farlo. Le palude, le spiagge, i quartieri popolari, le zone lussuose: ogni area ha un'identità precisa, abitata da persone che sembrano avere una vita propria.

La cura per il dettaglio è maniacale. Ogni tipo di auto e ogni marca ha una guida e una frenata diverse, e le auto elettriche hanno un comportamento tutto loro. La fisica è avanzata, le animazioni sono naturali e il comparto grafico lascia a bocca aperta, soprattutto al tramonto, quando Vice City si accende di neon.

LA RADIO, UN GIOCO NEL GIOCO
Da sempre la radio è uno dei marchi di fabbrica della serie, e qui raggiunge un livello mai visto. Le stazioni sono più di venti, a cui si aggiungono diversi podcast con più episodi da ascoltare. La novità è che la radio non resta confinata dentro l'auto: accompagna il giocatore anche a piedi e diventa parte integrante dell'esperienza. Tra musica, talk show e pubblicità surreali, è facile ritrovarsi a guidare senza meta solo per ascoltare.

SATIRA AL VETRIOLO
Per anni si è detto che sarebbe stato impossibile fare la parodia dell'America di oggi, perché la realtà aveva già superato la satira. Rockstar ha raccolto la sfida e l'ha vinta. Social network, influencer, politica, consumismo, cronaca: nessuno viene risparmiato. L'umorismo è tagliente, a volte scomodo, ma sempre intelligente.

LE SCELTE CONTANO
In GTA 6 si resta sempre criminali: non esiste una partita pacifista. Ma il modo in cui ci si comporta ha delle conseguenze. Chi si lancia in stragi indiscriminate per le strade vedrà cambiare il proprio Profilo Criminale, e il mondo reagirà di conseguenza. È un sistema che dà peso alle azioni e spinge a pensare prima di premere il grilletto, senza mai togliere il gusto del caos.

Rapine, inseguimenti e attività secondarie sono progettati con una varietà notevole. Le rapine in particolare sono tra i momenti più alti del gioco: preparazione, tensione ed esecuzione si fondono in sequenze che sembrano uscite da un film.

COSA NON CONVINCE
Nessun capolavoro è perfetto, e anche GTA 6 si porta dietro qualche difetto tipico di Rockstar. Le prime ore sono lente, a tratti troppo: il gioco ci mette un po' a ingranare prima di diventare un vero GTA. Alcune meccaniche legate alla relazione tra Jason e Lucia, come tenersi per mano o andare a prendere l'altro al lavoro, rischiano di sembrare più un compito che un piacere. Su console il frame rate è fermo a 30 fps, scelta comprensibile vista la mole tecnica, ma che si fa sentire nelle fasi più concitate. Infine, chi gioca su PC dovrà armarsi ancora di pazienza: la versione per computer non è stata ancora annunciata.

VERDETTO
GTA 6 è uno di quei giochi che si vivono, prima ancora di giocarli. È ambizioso, enorme, profondamente curato e capace di emozionare tanto nei momenti spettacolari quanto in quelli più intimi. I difetti esistono, ma spariscono di fronte alla grandezza dell'insieme. Rockstar ha alzato di nuovo l'asticella, e per molti anni sarà questo il metro di paragone per qualunque open world.

VOTO: 9,5/10

PRO
+ Jason e Lucia, coppia memorabile
+ Leonida, open world vivo e credibile
+ Grafica e fisica da riferimento
+ Radio e satira ai massimi livelli
+ Rapine spettacolari

CONTRO
- Avvio lento
- Alcune attività di coppia ripetitive
- 30 fps su console
- Nessuna versione PC per ora

author: LaurisPriede11
quote:
I waited for this game for over 10 years. i was somewhat hyped, and my expectations where that this game will be something like RDR2. and it is, so i love everything about this game. 

1. open world is beyond amazing, so many details, it feels alive and just how esthetic and pleasing visuals are. i walked and drove for hours to explore chapter one area. and that tells something about the open world of this game 
2. mechanics are amazing. so many activities even in chapter one, and i am so exited for what’s to come. i get it when people don’t like to much realism, its fair, and i respect that. but i am enjoying it so much i cant even believe its real.
3. lighting is on another level, it is nextgen no doubt. the reflections, the shadows . when the sunset hit and you just stand and enjoy it like you have never seen it before. amazing
4. story is interesting and feels fresh. since its a new consept to the series the relationship between two main characters and maintaining it in a good way, (if you don’t take friendship love between Michael and Trevor), i am enjoying it. a completely new GTA experience in terms of story, i am on chapter two, i haven’t experienced all story but i can say that it is good, very good.
5. technical masterpiece, it will only get better on pc and next gen console, but already its the best looking open world game. runs so good on 6 year old hardware. i know people complain at 30 fps. i can jump on that wagon, BUT its so amazing that i don’t care, i will experience it in more fps when pc version drops, so i will be patient.

overall, it runs smooth, no bugs, i am so glad i have the experience to play this amazing game and share it with others that like it. i hate review bombing, and those people haven’t even played the game or have barely started. so they think it is a life simulator or boring simp simulator. it’s not. it’s the best open world game surpassing RDR2 and Witcher 3 in terms of world building, game design, mechanics and so much more. i will continue to play the story, but i will just relax and enjoy the game and not rush it. it’s a generational game, and it’s definitely worth the hype. i don’t know if it’s possible to update review, but there is no way that i will drag down my score. even if the ending of the story is not perfect or how i want it, since everything else is perfect.

author: larouibar
quote: After years of sky-high anticipation, Rockstar Games has officially delivered a landmark achievement with Grand Theft Auto VI. From the very first moments in the sun-drenched, neon-soaked streets of Vice City and the wider state of Leonida, it becomes clear that this is not just another sequel—it is a monumental leap forward for open-world video games.A Living, Breathing World Beyond CompareLeonida is without question the most extraordinarily detailed virtual world ever constructed. Every street corner, sunset highway, and bustling beach feels genuinely alive, packed with realistic NPC behaviors, dynamic events, and endless opportunities for exploration. Whether you are pulling off a high-stakes heist, customizing cars down to the smallest engine detail, or simply soaking in the atmosphere, the level of polish and immersion is staggering.Unforgettable Characters and StoryAt the heart of this massive sandbox is an unexpectedly grounded and emotionally resonant story. Jason and Lucia form one of the most compelling duos in gaming history. Their dynamic—reminiscent of a modern-day Bonnie and Clyde—adds genuine heart, tension, and stakes to every mission, elevated by phenomenal voice acting and lifelike character animations.Best-in-Class GameplayRockstar has refined every core mechanic to perfection. Driving feels weighty and exhilarating, police chases are more intense and unpredictable than ever, and gunfights carry a visceral, cinematic punch. Even the smallest side activities feel meaningful, rewarding curiosity at every **** Verdict: 10/10Grand Theft Auto VI doesn’t just live up to the impossible hype; it **** it. It is an uncompromising, endlessly entertaining triumph that sets a new gold standard for the entire industry. An absolute must-play

author: Oblivizilla
quote: I’ve seen many reviews, both positive and negative, and thought to put my piece. I am around 50% through, which is far more than most of these reviews evidently. Now, for those walking in blind, I would say this. Don’t expect the traditional GTA pacing or nature, you will be dissapointed. It’s far more grounded and slow, especially in Chapter 1 and 2. Minimal robberies occur, and the focus is primarily on world building and the relationship between Jason and Lucia. Chapter 3 is where it starts to feel more like a Grand Theft Auto installment however, with more heists being planned and robberies throughout. The world in this game is truly like no other, the detail is unmatched and I’m hopelessly addicted to driving around and just seeing what happens, you’ll never be bored doing that. Pair that with the insane graphics, match made in heaven. Where this game does fall somewhat short is its ability to make you connect with characters and story. I find myself really liking Cal, and the general bond between Jason and Lucia, but compared to previous Rockstar games, it doesn’t reach the same connection I felt with Arthur Morgan from RDR2. TLDR; it’s a great game, with a world brimming with life and exploration, but it falls short with its story at times, feeling slightly messy and rushed. Nontheless, it actively picks up from Chapter 3, and if you like slow paced games this is for you. Don’t expect a GTA 5 v2.

author: kengpavel
quote:
I completed Grand Theft Auto VI in a single 60+ hour marathon session right at launch—and what says the most about this game is that I barely even felt sleepy because the immersion was that strong. Having recently replayed the previous entries back-to-back with zero rose-tinted glasses, I went into GTA 6 with a cold, objective mindset.

Let’s address the main flaw right away: mission structure. Perhaps it’s a bit of series fatigue on my part, but at their core, the quests in GTA 6 still follow Rockstar’s familiar formula. The difference is that the sheer level of direction, staging, pacing, and visual fidelity elevates those familiar mechanics so much that playing through them feels ten times more engaging and rewarding than before.

Do I agree that GTA 6 is "the highest-rated masterpiece in the solar system" without a single flaw? Not 100%. However, I completely stand behind these four facts:
1. It is undeniably the Game of the Year.
2. It is the best and most important video game released in the last six years since 2020.
3. It features the most alive, reactive open world and the best visuals in the entire industry.
4. It is the largest, most epic, most cinematic, and overall the absolute best Grand Theft Auto ever made.

Rockstar didn’t reinvent every single wheel from scratch, but they perfected their craft to an unreachable benchmark. A historic milestone for gaming.

author: Mr_Meling
quote:
10/10 – An Absolute Masterpiece

GTA VI is nothing short of a masterpiece. Rockstar has clearly taken inspiration from Red Dead Redemption 2 while bringing together the very best elements of GTA IV and GTA V. 
The result is a more grounded, mature and believable experience without losing what makes Grand Theft Auto special.
The story is exciting, the world feels incredibly realistic, and the overall quality is simply outstanding. The attention to detail, atmosphere, characters and sheer level of craftsmanship are on another level.
That being said, if you were expecting GTA V 2.0, with its sometimes over the top, almost cartoonish approach, this might not be the game for you. The same goes for people who never appreciated the more grounded tone of GTA IV or the slower, more immersive experience of RDR2. 
Personally, I think Rockstar made absolutely the right decision by moving in this direction.
What I find particularly ridiculous is the amount of review bombing from people calling the game “woke” or “feminist”. I genuinely struggle to understand that criticism, especially when so much of it comes from people who haven’t even played the game and are handing out 0/10 scores based on a YouTube video. That’s not reviewing a game. That’s pushing an agenda.
And frankly, if you’re disappointed because Rockstar didn’t simply give you GTA V 2.0, tough luck.
Is the story quite as deep or emotionally powerful as Red Dead Redemption 2? Perhaps not. But that doesn’t take anything away from what Rockstar has achieved **** VI is a technical and artistic achievement of the highest order. An incredibly immersive world, an excellent story and a level of polish that very few developers can even dream of **** absolute masterpiece, and easily one of the greatest games ever made.

The sunsets over Vice City, the neon at night, the swamps and the beaches all look incredible, and I kept stopping just to take it all **** story is next level. Lucia and Jason are the best protagonists Rockstar has ever written. Their partnership feels real and earned, the writing is sharp, funny and sometimes surprisingly emotional, and I actually cared what happened to them from start to finish. This is the first GTA where the story hit as hard as the gameplay.

The UI is amazing too. Menus are clean and fast, the map and phone are easy to use, and everything gets out of the way so you can stay immersed. It's a huge upgrade and makes the whole game feel polished.

About the user score: many of the low ratings here are clearly not about the game. Some were posted before anyone could even play it, and others are about pricing, the wait or online drama, not what's actually on the disc. A 0 for a game you haven't played doesn't help anyone decide whether to buy it. Play it, then judge it. I did, and it's a masterpiece.

author: Lion_171974
quote: GTA VI has managed to reach my unbeatable expectations. On the gameplay side, it’s slower paced than GTA V but faster than RDR2 and strikes a perfect balance between immersive and almost monotonous moments and high tension combat and action sequences. The end result is a fenomenal and contrary to belief buggless experience. The characters, world building and storyline are truly amazing. Jason and Lucia are the most believable power couple in games and one of the best in media in general. Even though they are still the heroes of the story and don’t live a normal life, their interactions are so real and relatable to real life couples that you genuinely connect with them by the time the first major story sequences happen in chapter 1. The world is the most alive and beautiful recreation of America in the history of media. The developers have managed to recreate every bit of the essence of Florida up to the lighting and the foliage. Every npc that you can interact with like your neighbour or a random gas station employee feels like a real person and it all connects to truly immerse you. I have over 20 hours on the game and the first 14 I spent in key lento and the towns around it. The world is that big that I don’t think 100 hours will unlock me the whole map. The storyline suffers the classic open world game problem of going to do side content and having the story feel stretched out but it is not noticeable at all and without any spoilers the story in GTA VI is a masterclass of storytelling and writing. Overall the game is worth every cent and deserves a 10.

author: Da_Alex
quote:
Un vero capolavoro indiscutibile.
Non ci sono parole per descrivere ciò a cui siamo di fronte, non è più un semplice modo di concepire Gta ma una vera e propria evoluzione tecnica che porta il realismo a livelli mai visti. E tutto ciò gira benissimo su una Playstation 5 base (i 30 fps non si notano per niente). 
Questo capitolo verte di più verso un life/world simulator che a molti potrà dare fastidio ma questo low pace occasionale e molto realistica da al gioco un qualcosa in più che proprio serviva e che ha reso quello che è rdr2 un capolavoro. 
La guida delle auto è meravigliosa, ogni veicolo ha la sua cura nei controlli che differiscono tutti in base al tipo e alle modifiche apportate. 
Il mondo è VIVO... ma davvero vivo, tanto che fa impressione investire qualcuno o fargli del male. 
Gli npc e l'ia è studiata ad un livello mai raggiunto e l'immersione è totale, movimenti, reazioni e azioni riproducono molto similmente la realtà. 
Il comportamento della polizia è tantissimo passi avanti, ti tengono con il fiato alla gola e fanno paura. Dopo l'inseguimento se non cambi abito e auto ancora ti possono beccare e tornare ad inseguire aggiungendo una meccanica fantastica e devo dire poco problematica al fine del gameplay. Hanno lasciato un leggero margine arcade per le basse stelle proprio per non essere invadenti mel gameplay.
La varietà e la cura delle creature è meravigliosa, tra marine, terrestri e volatili per non parlare del cosa più incredibile, la qualità dell'acqua. Osservare il mare con le sue varie sfumature ti lascia sempre a bocca aperta e anche sott'acqua è finalmente e realisticamente ciò che cercavo (l'endless ocean 3 che mai abbiamo avuto). 
Gli eventi atmosferici sono anch'essi meravigliosi e percepire con interferiscono con la guida dei veicoli è un chicca spaziale e immersiva. Le nuvole volumetriche e il volarci dentro è ciò che un amante dei velivoli come me aspettava da troppo tempo che non fosse in Flight Simulator. Le pozzanghere lasciate dopo un temporale o dopo una notte ti fa percepire quanta cura anche nello studio delle condizioni atmosferiche e le sue conseguenze. 
Gli eventi casuali che capitano sono tantissimi e tutti spettacolari.
Sulla trama dico poco perchè sono ancora all'inizio e in questo mondo ti ci perdi a esplorare e scoprire ma vi racconterò questo : ho beccato dei contrabbandieri appartati al buio vicino a un piccolo molo di scarico ed erano intenti a fare uno scambio di merceentre erano armati e così ho deciso di nascondere la mia auto e avvicinarmi di soppiatto mel buio tra l'erba alta e mentre stavano finendo lo scambio li ho sparati sulle gambe per non ucciderli. Il vedere come si trascinano se hanno preso un colpo sulla gamba ti fa capire il realismo nei dettagli che rockstar games ci ha messo, un qualcosa di fuori di testa. Ffinita la sparatoria ho rubato il bottino di dollari e armi. Fare questa azione per decisione mia e viverla a questo realismo è stato qualcosa di difficilmente descrivibile.
Ci sono troppe cose da dire per parlare di questo gioco ma per ora è ancora presto. 
Le cose negative che per ora posso dire sono:
-La mancanza di una prima persona che però tramite un glitch si vede che c'è gia ma hanno deciso malaanamente di rimuoverla per chissà quali scopi 
-Non puoi spogliare i ****, non è tanto un discorso erotico ma in un mondo dove ci sono nudisti non poterlo fare anche tu è una barzelletta, ma comprensibile dato il livello di realismo che raggiunge visivamente questo gioco magari sono stati più duri nelle regole per coprirsi da possibili problemi legali.
- C'è un costante effetto lente sulla parte superiore che scurisce leggermente e non si può disattivare, non capisco da cosa sia dovuto o perchè lo abbiano messo
-Nella prima persona applicabile con L2 e poi R3 da fermi si nota un delay nel caricamento di ciò che vedi, ci vogliono circa 3/4 secondi per caricare le texture e i contorni rimangono comunque sfocati, forse non ancora implementato bene? O forse il vero limite del hardware per via di questa grafica?

Grazie Rockstar Games per questo immenso capolavoro videoludico

quote: Rockstar Games Should Be Held to a Higher StandardWhen it comes to Rockstar Games, expectations are naturally high. They are one of the most respected developers in the industry, and a game as ambitious as GTA 6 should reflect that reputation through exceptional quality, stability, and technical polish.I believe GTA 6 should not be released with an excessive number of bugs, technical issues, or performance problems that negatively affect the overall experience. Developing such a massive open world is undoubtedly challenging, but that should not be an excuse for compromising the final **** Dead Redemption 2 is proof of what Rockstar is capable of achieving. It was an outstanding game, with an incredibly detailed world, remarkable atmosphere, excellent storytelling, and an impressive level of polish. It set a very high standard and demonstrated that ambition and technical quality can go hand in hand.That is precisely why my expectations for GTA 6 are so high. I am not expecting perfection, because no game is perfect. However, I do expect Rockstar to maintain the level of quality and attention to detail that made Red Dead Redemption 2 such an extraordinary experience.Ambition should never come at the expense of polish. GTA 6 should be remembered for its innovation, quality, and gameplay experience, not for the number of patches required to make it feel complete.

author: Allanon432
quote:
After 13 years of waiting, GTA VI has reminded me why I fell in love with video games. Playing on PS5 Slim, I’ve just reached Chapter 2, and I’m already blown away by Rockstar’s extraordinary attention to detail. Vice City doesn’t just look alive, it FEELS alive. NPCs have realistic conversations, argue on the phone and behave as if they have lives of their own. Even iguanas casually crossing the road contribute to an incredible sense of immersion. Graphically, it’s breathtaking: textures, lighting, reflections and environmental details are unlike anything I’ve experienced before. Playing at night on an OLED is simply spectacular. There are a few minor technical issues, such as slightly raised black levels in certain daytime scenes, occasional blurriness and HDR calibration that could use some refinement. But the storytelling is just as impressive as the technology. Jason, Lucia and the supporting characters feel authentic and remarkably well-written, with believable relationships, excellent dialogue and unexpected plot twists that keep me completely invested. Even simple activities like renovating Jason’s house or working out demonstrate an astonishing level of care. And I’ve barely scratched the surface! For years, I’ve struggled to find games that genuinely excite me. GTA VI has finally brought back that feeling of wanting to rush home just to play. Regarding the review bombing, legitimate criticism is always welcome, but deliberately attacking a game without giving it a fair chance is unfair to both developers and players. Rockstar has created something extraordinary, and it deserves to be judged honestly. GTA VI isn’t just the game I’ve waited thirteen years to play. It’s the game that made me fall in love with gaming all over again. 

10/10.

author: Jk82482
quote: Before diving into the gameplay, it’s worth addressing the early discourse surrounding performance. While there has been a lot of noise online regarding frame rates and technical stability, my hands-on experience—alongside feedback from over a dozen players across base PS5, PS5 Pro, and Xbox Series X|S—tells a very different story. Gameplay has been remarkably smooth and free of major bugs. Would a 60FPS mode be ideal? Without a doubt. However, the locked 30FPS is rock-solid and never detracts from the overall experience.Unlike GTA V, which threw players straight into a high-octane heist within minutes, GTA VI takes a much more deliberate, slow-burn approach to its opening. It can feel like a jarring pace change at first, but once you push past Chapter 1, the narrative momentum kicks into high gear.Visually, the realism is staggering. Down to the finest environmental details, this is easily one of the most gorgeous games ever built. That fidelity shines brightest when exploring on foot, particularly when using the closest on-foot camera angle (one of three adjustable perspective options), which makes the world feel remarkably intimate and grounded.From a mechanics standpoint, Rockstar has refined its core pillars:* Gunplay: Shotguns and rifles carry heavy, impactful weight, though handguns feel noticeably lighter by comparison.* Driving: The vehicle physics are a standout triumph. Rockstar successfully blended the responsive, arcade-friendly handling of GTA V with just a touch of the heavy, realistic body sway from GTA **** the heart of the narrative are Lucia and Jason, two compelling leads whose dynamic drives the experience. When hanging out at your safehouse, the game occasionally leans into "dating simulator" territory. Because the story is so tightly anchored to their partnership, classic sandbox features—like picking up random NPCs—have been removed.While the commitment to a cohesive narrative is admirable, it would have been great to have the agency to temporarily step away from the relationship and return later, especially during a specific, pivotal moment in the story where Jason is heavily tested.Ultimately, the world map is an architectural marvel that already surpasses GTA V in depth and atmosphere. There is still a massive amount of content left to uncover, and I plan to revisit this review once I’ve pushed toward the Platinum trophy. For now, Grand Theft Auto VI easily earns a 9.5/10—ignore the bad-faith review bombing and experience it for yourself.

author: Thomas_2000
quote: I am 21 hours into the game and I can say that this is the best game I’ve played in some time. To start with, the gameplay feels smooth for the fact it only runs 30fps. I will be honest and say that at certain moments it drops to around 25fps at most, but that’s to be expected from a game that has to run so much on a console. The story up to now is amazing, I already feel a close connection to Jason and Lucia as well as other characters like Cal and Dunk. Yeah there are moments that feel like you’re doing tasks rather than playing the game but that is the whole point of the relationship between Jason and Lucia. This is also optional and you can choose to not do things like workout, shower, buy groceries, etc. which will affect the relationship negatively. The clear character development is obvious, you have Jason who starts off as a shy and timid character but gets more vocal along the way, then you have Lucia who is messy and rowdy when it comes to certain things but starts to learn how to be patient and relaxed. The graphics are amazing, it’s one of those where you can say “If somebody told me this was real life and not a game, I’d believe them.” They do this with the realism in the game such as the weather system or the reflections in mirrors or even the minor details left behind in incidents like car crashes or shootings. The car mechanics in this game are impeccable, not only did they make the driving realistic, but they made the customisation better than most car games. From changing your engine to make the car work better and faster to adding off road wheels so your car can handle dirt trails better. They even have different garages that work better with different types of cars, which I personally like. But it isn’t the detail or realism that makes the game a ten, for me it’s the amount of endless things you can do. The game can never get boring as no matter what you’ll always have something to return to. Whether that’s side missions where you take down gangs to sell drugs or find cash to interacting to npc’s to start random events. The love I have for this game really comes from the endless possibilities that make the game entertaining and one you can’t miss.

author: Chimeraaaa
quote: After spending 20 hours with GTA VI on PS5 Pro, I can confidently say that Rockstar has delivered one of the most extraordinary open-world experiences I’ve ever played. What impresses me most isn’t just the stunning graphics or the incredible attention to detail. It’s how alive and interconnected the entire world feels. Traffic, pedestrians, public transportation, vehicle ownership, and countless everyday interactions create a remarkably convincing sense of reality. Even something as simple as driving through an intersection or taking a bus feels meaningful. The slower, more deliberate pacing might not appeal to everyone, but I genuinely appreciate it. Rather than rushing players from one spectacle to another, GTA VI encourages us to actually inhabit its world. The technical achievement is astonishing, especially considering the hardware it’s running on. Yet the greatest accomplishment is how naturally all these complex systems come together. It’s still early to judge its long-term historical influence, but GTA VI has already raised my expectations for what an open-world game can be. An unforgettable achievement. Absolutely deserving of a 10/10.

author: Loryiannu
quote: GTA 6 is an absolute masterpiece that sets an entirely new benchmark for open-world gaming. From the very first frame, the extremely detailed graphics blow you away—every neon reflection on wet asphalt, blade of grass, and weathered texture looks astonishingly lifelike. What truly makes this world feel alive, however, are the 600,000 animations seamlessly woven into every movement, interaction, and firefight. There is zero stiffness or robotic repetition; characters shift their weight naturally, react dynamically to their surroundings, and move with uncanny fluidity.Speaking of realism, the variety of NPCs is unmatched. Crowds feel genuinely unpredictable, packed with distinct personalities, routines, and reactions that make every street corner a story waiting to unfold. You never run out of things to do either, thanks to a massive roster of activities that are abundant and genuinely distinct from one another, keeping the pacing fresh whether you are pulling off high-stakes heists or messing around off the clock.Even though we are still in Mariana County, the settings feel completely reinvigorated, expansive, and bursting with fresh atmosphere and detail. GTA 6 isn't just a sequel—it is an unforgettable, thrilling triumph that raises the bar for the entire industry.

author: EazeDuziTt
quote: Let me start by saying that GTA VI looks absolutely incredible graphically. There’s no denying that Rockstar has put a tremendous amount of work into making the world look beautiful, detailed, and realistic. However, amazing graphics don’t automatically make a great game.After seeing the gameplay and the number of glitches, bugs, and visual issues throughout the game, I’m honestly not satisfied with what I’m seeing. A game of this size and with the amount of anticipation surrounding it should deliver more than just impressive visuals. Gameplay, stability, performance, and overall quality matter just as much.Rockstar has built its reputation on delivering some of the biggest gaming experiences in the industry. That’s exactly why I expect more from them. I don’t believe players should have to settle for a game filled with noticeable bugs and glitches simply because it looks **** while I understand that delaying a game is never an easy decision, I’d much rather see Rockstar take the extra time to fix the problems than release something that feels unfinished. We’ve waited years for GTA VI. Waiting a little longer for a polished, properly tested experience would be worth it.Graphics get your attention, but quality keeps players playing. GTA VI has enormous potential, but from what I’m seeing, it definitely needs more work before it’s ready.Rockstar, please don’t let the hype outweigh the quality. We want an incredible game, not just an incredible-looking trailer.

author: NicbaSRB
quote:
After so many years of waiting, it’s finally here. I can’t believe the game is finally out and that I’m already playing it. The game is meant to be played slowly and without rushing—it’s not supposed to be a marathon of one mission after another.

Guys, just enjoy the game. I read somewhere that it’s a "boyfriend simulator"—not *GTA* or anything like that—and they’ve executed it in a very authentic and realistic way. Any reasonable person might do the same things for their girlfriend as what happens in the game. I personally fell into a rut where no game could truly satisfy me. We’ve lost that feeling we had as kids—that eager anticipation of getting home just to play games. That feeling had faded over the last few years—I lost it myself—but now I’ve managed to get it back.

Experience every game for yourself—don’t just watch clips on YouTube, Instagram, or TikTok. Explore, observe, experiment, and—most importantly—enjoy it. It’s perfectly fine if someone doesn’t like GTA 6, but many people go overboard with their negative comments. When someone promises you the world, keep your expectations in check. Some people expected too much and ended up disappointed... There will be time to tweak things through various updates.

I love GTA 6—thanks, Rockstar!
