author: iHanatos
quote: GTA 6 — A Game for the Ages. 10/10. No Damn Question.I've waited 13 freaking years for this game. Thirteen. And after finally getting my hands on it, playing on a PS5 Pro connected to a 65-inch LG G5 OLED, I can confidently say one thing: this isn't just the game of the year. This is a generation-defining masterpiece.Rockstar didn't just meet my expectations. They blew them out of the damn water.First, let's address the ridiculous complaints I've been seeing online. People whining about having to throw away trash or not being able to kill certain NPCs. Seriously, get the hell outta here. Some people will find anything to complain about. If that's what you're focusing on instead of appreciating what Rockstar has accomplished, I don't know what to tell **** me, this is a straight-up 10/10 **** realism, attention to detail, world design, and graphics are absolutely insane. Everything feels alive. The amount of things you can do is unreal. Wanna swim? Go for it. Explore underwater? Absolutely. Hunt for buried treasure? You can do that too. There's so much freedom that you can spend hours exploring without even touching the main **** the graphics? Holy ****. On my LG G5 OLED, this game looks gorgeous. I can only imagine how insane it'll look on PC. I'm 100% buying it again, no **** driving mechanics are one of my favorite things about GTA 6. They remind me of GTA IV, which, in my opinion, had the best vehicle handling in the entire series. GTA V's driving felt like a step backward. Here, Rockstar combined the best elements of both games and created something damn near perfect. Cars have weight, handling feels satisfying, and driving is fun as hell.Vehicle customization is awesome, gunplay feels great, and the story is fantastic — a huge improvement over GTA V in my opinion. There are Easter eggs everywhere. It's classic Rockstar magic. You can tell how much love and effort went into this world.Sure, there are a few minor texture issues. I even had a baseball bat clip through the environment once. But seriously, who cares? What game launches without bugs? Considering the scale and insane amount of detail, that's barely worth mentioning. I'm not letting a few glitches ruin an otherwise incredible experience.Interestingly, GTA 6 reminds me more of Red Dead Redemption 2 in how it feels to play. And I absolutely LOVE RDR2. The character movement, weight behind every action, and realistic animations are all reminiscent of RDR2. Some might not like that, but I think it's fantastic. It makes the world feel more believable and immersive.Most importantly, I never get tired of playing this game. I constantly wanna jump back in and discover something new. That's truly **** someone who's also a video game developer, I have an even greater appreciation for what Rockstar has accomplished. author: Stems
quote:
What impresses me the most about GTA VI isn't just the graphics or the sheer scale of the world. It's how incredibly alive everything feels.

NPCs seem to have their own routines, random events unfold naturally, and even something as simple as following a stranger through the city can turn into an interesting experience. It reminds me of Westworld in a way. The world doesn't seem to exist solely for the player. It feels like it has a life of its own. 

I've seen people complaining that the gameplay looks too slow or that certain activities seem boring. But that's precisely what makes Rockstar's approach so interesting. Not everything needs to be fast-paced or constantly rewarding. 

Sometimes you're supposed to slow down, explore, observe, and simply enjoy being part of a believable world. I think we've reached a point where people are so conditioned by TikTok and instant dopamine that they struggle to appreciate anything that requires a little patience. And honestly, that's a shame.What's equally impressive is that Rockstar seems to have preserved the DNA of GTA despite all the concerns about the franchise losing its identity.

Of course, you can always find tiny imperfections if you look hard enough. But focusing on those while ignoring the insane amount of work, detail, and ambition behind this game feels completely absurd to me. 

From everything I've seen so far, GTA VI looks like an extraordinary achievement in open-world design. 

Not because it constantly tries to entertain you every second, but because it creates a world worth spending time in.

author: M3ssz
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI Review: An Unmatched Open-World Benchmark
After more than a decade of anticipation, Grand Theft Auto VI does not merely clear the astronomical bar set for it—it completely redefines what an open-world video game can be. Returning to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and the sprawling state of Leonida, Rockstar Games has delivered a staggering technical, narrative, and interactive triumph.
A Living, Breathing Leonida
The true star of GTA 6 is the sheer density and believability of its world. From packed nightclubs pulsing with bass to serene, wildlife-filled wetlands, every square inch of Leonida feels meticulously handcrafted. The traffic and pedestrian density are unlike anything seen before on consoles. You aren't just playing in a backdrop; you are existing inside a bustling ecosystem where emergent events happen organically around every corner. Whether you are pulling off a multi-stage bank heist, lifting weights at the beach, or simply people-watching on the boardwalk, the immersion is absolute.
Jason and Lucia: Heart in the Chaos
While previous entries relied heavily on cynical satire, GTA 6 anchors its signature chaos with a grounded, surprisingly tender dual-protagonist dynamic. Stepping into the shoes of Jason and Lucia—the series' first female lead—gives the story an emotional core that elevates the entire experience. Their Bonnie-and-Clyde partnership isn't just a narrative hook; it directly shapes gameplay, allowing you to coordinate tactical robberies, manage your shared stash in the trunk of your personal car, and watch their relationship evolve based on the choices you make in the heat of the moment.
Refined Gameplay and Mechanics
Rockstar has clearly listened to player feedback regarding how its games actually feel to play:
Driving and Vehicles: Car handling is the best in franchise history, giving every vehicle class—from heavy muscle cars to silent electric vehicles—a distinct weight and braking profile.
Overhauled Combat: The clunky shooting of past titles is gone. Gunplay is snappy and responsive, featuring a new focus system that lets you target specific weak spots, like shooting a weapon out of an enemy's hand.
Grounded Realism: Borrowing the deliberate, weighty animation style of Red Dead Redemption 2 without bogging down the pacing, GTA 6 strikes the perfect balance between tactile realism and arcade fun.
Technical Execution
On current-generation consoles, GTA 6 is a visual showstopper. The lighting, weather systems, and environmental details look phenomenal. The one notable caveat for frame-rate purists is the targeted 30fps cap on consoles. However, the frame pacing is rock-solid and virtually bug-free, making it a small price to pay for the sheer scale of the simulation running under the hood.
The Verdict
Grand Theft Auto VI is a modern masterpiece. It effortlessly blends blockbuster cinematic set-pieces with infinite sandbox freedom, backed by two of the most compelling protagonists Rockstar has ever written. It is a generational landmark that sets the standard for open-world gaming for years to come.
Score: 10/10

author: Swerve98644
quote:
Grand Theft Auto 6 surprises in many ways. On the front end the game is a technical masterpiece with graphics and physics that trump anything else on the market. In my 20+ hours of gameplay I have not encountered any technical issues which is wild in the industry today, you can tell why this took 13 years to bake. Rockstar has spent the time to perfect the world and stuff it full of engaging side content. Story-wise, the game starts as a slow burn. I understand why some people may be put off by this, however it builds out Jason and Lucia’s relationship before the game truly begins in chapter 2. Once some events take place, the game truly opens up and becomes a classic GTA title. The only gripe that I have is that it takes a LONG time to get to that point. It would be great to see this trimmed down, or skippable on subsequent play throughs. Gameplay wise this is the best GTA has been. Guns are satisfying, Vehicles have weight, and movement has never been better. Truly the largest gripe I have with the game is that it is at 30 FPS. In 2026 this is simply something that should not be overlooked. This decision has severe impacts on the game’s presentation and playability. It would have been nice to include a non-ray-traced mode to allow the consoles to push 60 frames for a more complete experience. 

Overall, this GTA is phenomenal. The story, characters, and world shine through. Do not allow your self to be turned off from the opening hours. If you can push through you will not regret it!

author: DarkMythHunter
quote: 10/10 - Honestly, I don't even know where to start. GTA 6 is one of those games that reminds you why you fell in love with gaming in the first place. After all the years of waiting and all the expectations surrounding it, I can confidently say that Rockstar delivered something truly special. It's not just another GTA game with better graphics; it feels like a massive step forward in almost every aspect. The graphics are absolutely insane. The amount of detail in this game is something else. The lighting, reflections, water, character models, animations and environments are all incredibly well done. What impressed me the most, though, is how alive everything feels. Driving through the city at night, watching the lights reflect off the streets, or simply walking around and noticing all the little details makes the world feel incredibly realistic. There are moments when I genuinely stop playing just to look around and appreciate how beautiful everything is. The gameplay is incredibly satisfying too. Driving feels great, shooting is enjoyable, and there is so much freedom in how you approach different situations. I love how many activities are available outside the main missions. You can spend hours exploring, discovering random events, interacting with characters or just doing whatever you feel like. Sometimes you start playing with a specific mission in mind and somehow end up spending two hours doing completely unrelated things. That's exactly what makes a GTA game so enjoyable. The sound design is another highlight. Cars sound fantastic, weapons have a satisfying impact, and the ambient sounds make the world feel much more believable. The radio stations are also a huge part of the experience, as always. There's something special about driving around Vice City with your favourite song playing in the background. The voice acting is excellent too, and the conversations between characters feel natural rather than forced. The story is also a major highlight. Jason and Lucia are genuinely interesting characters, and their relationship gives the whole experience a different emotional depth. I really like that the game isn't just about crime, money, explosions and ridiculous situations. There are quieter moments that allow you to understand the characters better and actually care about what happens to them. The writing, dialogue and character interactions make the story feel much more personal. It has the action, humour and chaos you'd expect from GTA, but it also knows when to slow down and tell a more meaningful story. There is also a ridiculous amount of content to enjoy. The main story offers plenty of entertainment, and that's without even considering all the side missions, activities, random encounters and things to discover. What I appreciate most is that the extra content doesn't feel like something you have to complete just to make the game longer. There's always something interesting to do, and exploring the world is enjoyable in itself. Even after finishing the main story, there is plenty of reason to keep playing. When it comes to innovation, what makes GTA 6 special is how Rockstar managed to improve so many different aspects without losing what makes the series unique. The world feels more dynamic, the characters feel more believable, and the overall experience is much more immersive. The attention to detail is honestly ridiculous. It's not necessarily about introducing one completely revolutionary mechanic; it's about improving hundreds of little things that, together, make a massive difference. And at the end of the day, this is probably the most important thing: the game is simply fun. I can't remember the last time a game made me want to keep playing for hours without even noticing how much time had passed. Whether I'm following the story, driving around, exploring, getting into random trouble or simply messing around, there's always something entertaining to do. GTA 6 is everything I wanted it to be and honestly even more. It has incredible graphics, satisfying gameplay, amazing sound design, a memorable story and an absolutely massive world filled with things to discover. Of course, no game is completely perfect, and there are always little things that could be improved, but none of that changes how incredible the overall experience is. Rockstar clearly put an unbelievable amount of work into this game, and it shows. This is the kind of game that sets a new standard for open-world experiences and will probably be talked about for years. A well-deserved 10/10. Absolutely worth the wait.

author: Tfoxnkzl
quote:
10/10 – A Masterpiece That Deserves Every Bit of Praise

GTA VI is an incredibly complete experience and deserves all the praise it receives. From its world design and graphics to its storytelling, characters, attention to detail, and gameplay, everything shows an extraordinary level of ambition and quality. Rockstar has pushed the boundaries of what an open-world game can be.

I also believe many of the 0/10 user ratings are not genuine reflections of the game's quality. Some appear to come from frustrated PC players who are disappointed that the game hasn't been released on PC yet. Not owning or being able to play a game on your preferred platform is not a valid reason to give it a zero.

A game should be judged on its actual quality, not on platform frustration or personal disagreements.

A well-deserved 10/10.

author: adrian-belmont
quote:
GTA VI is nowhere near the extraordinary experience many people claim it is.After years of waiting, endless hype, and sky-high expectations, I expected a game that would surprise me and keep me hooked from the very beginning. Instead, so far, I've found the experience rather boring.I won't deny Rockstar's impressive technical achievement. The world is incredibly detailed, and you can clearly see the enormous amount of work and money invested in this project. However, I think we're reaching a point where technical production value is being confused with actual video game quality.
After such a long development cycle and years of waiting, running into technical issues is disappointing. I'm not demanding perfection, but I do expect a product that lives up to its enormous budget and the expectations the industry itself helped create.
GTA VI should stand on its own merits, without comparisons or immunity from **** problem isn't that GTA VI is a bad game. My problem is that, after all these years of waiting, I'm simply not getting the extraordinary experience that was promised. Maybe my opinion will change as I progress further, but I'm not going to give it an outstanding score just because of its name, its budget, or because other people tell me how I should feel about playing **** the end of the day, video games are meant to be enjoyed, not worshipped.

O mais incrível é que essas atividades não parecem estar ali apenas para preencher o mapa: elas fazem parte da própria dinâmica do jogo. Guardar dinheiro no banco, pintar um carro, abastecer, comprar roupas e realizar outras tarefas tornam o cotidiano dentro desse universo muito mais natural e convincente.É surreal perceber o cuidado com os detalhes e a forma como cada elemento contribui para a imersão. GTA 6 não é simplesmente um jogo que você liga para cumprir missões; é um mundo no qual você entra, explora, vive experiências e perde completamente a noção do tempo. Uma experiência simplesmente extraordinária.

author: MisoHoniii
quote:
Honestly, only putting 10 because a 9.5 is not available and it's more deserving of rounding up, rather than down.

Here's the truth; **** or straight up leaving a 0 is so ridiculous, no matter what your preference is when it comes to your expectation or preferred genre. And whining about critics not leaving a "real" review but following that up with a 0 of your own review is hypocrisy at its finest.

GTA6 is FILLED with content and stuff to do. I'll admit the game starts off a tiny bit slower than it needs to. However, most of the tedious or chore-like missions are completely optional. 

I think the handling of every vehicle has been upgraded to a more realistic expectation. Mod options are insanely vast. The way a vehicle is damage is also incredibly realistic to how that would effect the way it drives.

Every character I've met so far (currently in chapter 3) is super memorable and has a gta feel to it, except Jason. Not that Jason is a bad character I actually really like him as a character, but his voice actor felt wayyy too emotionless (where as a gta character is typically really exaggerative). You can kinda start to hear a little bit of emotion in chapter 2 but he's just too monotone to be a successful gta character in my opinion. 

30 frames is rough, nobody in 2026 will say its acceptable, nor fun to experience, but once your eyes adjust and take in the graphical masterpiece, its not difficult at all to forget about the 30 fps issue. 

Combat is way more fun and difficult without the L2 to auto aim, then quick flick up to the most free head shot in any game ever. I always disliked combat in previous gta games. GTA6 combat doesn't revolutionize the combat, but it's definitely upgraded.

GTA6 also has succeeded in making this world feel the most alive it has ever felt. You dont see the same 10 npc's walking around, you see hundreds. The amount of decor in the world to make it feel living and breathing is truly amazing. The variety in behavior is just flat-out great. Ive never put in a large amount of hours in previous gta entries but I can definitely see myself wanting to explore every city and nook-n-cranny here. Not to mention the density of each location as well. Previous games felt like there were enormous sections of long roads with straight up nothing to explore, where as GTA6 feels like they've filled in those areas AND has something to do every 1/10 of a mile. 

There ya go, there's a real review. Not a 10/10 in actuality but definitely 9.5 because honestly, a 9 is too low.

author: Valtiel88
quote: What can I say? Absolute masterpiece!Ignore all the idiots giving this game a 0 without even having played it. GTA VI feels incredibly realistic and mature, especially when it comes to the storyline and the relationship between the two protagonists.People were expecting yet another GTA for idiots who just want to act tough, cause chaos and blow everything up, but Rockstar has delivered something much more ambitious. The world feels alive, immersive and full of personality. The attention to detail is incredible, and the atmosphere makes you feel like you're actually part of that world rather than just playing another open-world game.What I appreciate most is the balance between the crazy, over-the-top nature of GTA and a more serious, emotional narrative. The characters feel more human, their relationships have real depth, and the story gives you reasons to care about what happens to them.I'd describe it as the perfect blend of GTA and Red Dead Redemption: the freedom, satire and madness of GTA combined with the storytelling, atmosphere and emotional depth of Red Dead.Rockstar has once again shown that an open-world game can be much more than just causing destruction and having fun. author: Negueba
quote: O jogo se passa em diversas cidades, todas elas com suas próprias personalidades, características e estilo de vidas distintas entre si. Os personagens principais são incriveis e os de apoio memoráveis, nenhum foi escrito pra ser o durão, mas sim pra ser 100^ humano, fazendo com que todos sintam o peso de cada acontecimento da história, abro destaque pra Jason e Lucia, o desenvolvimento deles foi rápido e prestativo, notei isso mesmo estando no capítulo 2. O jogo não sente pressa em desenvolver a história, vai com calma, te apresenta coisas essenciais sem desespero, desenvolve o que precisa ser desenvolvido e fazendo ser impressionantemente boa e divertida, embora algumas partes sejam um pouco tediante, mas em sua maioria te abraça e te joga pra ação. Tecnicamente e artisticamente, o jogo veio bem feito, com alguns problemas, claro. Problemas esses que não enfrentei, mas outros jogadores sim e vale ressaltar, relataram bugs, frame rate desregulado e etc, mas nada que estragasse o jogo. Sobre minha experiência, foi quase perfeita, não tive nenhum bug, frame rate cai apenas em partes exigentes, mas cai aproximadamente 2, coisas que eles podem corrigir com patches. Graficamente, é o melhor jogo da história, excremento cada gota de TODOS os consoles. A jogabilidade é incrível, mesmo que as vezes pareça meio travadinha com erros de animações ou animações estranhas. A direção do mundo aberto está maravilhosa, sinto que a gente não precisa chegar a tal lugar pra que algo ocorra, a cidade não responde a você e sim a quem mora lá. Cenas bem dirigidas, missões em geral bem pensadas, tudo bem amarradinho. Bom, sobre o 30 quadros por segundo, no meu caso não atrapalhou e literalmente nada, pois sempre joguei em modo fidelidade então muda nada, fora que os 30 quadros deles parecem mais fluidos. Então vocês que estão lendo essa onda de resenhas negativas, saibam que a maioria nem jogou o jogo e querem apenas o boicotar. Se alguém lendo estiver em duvida se deve comprar ou não, apenas compre, coloque o celular no não perturbe e mergulhe em Leonida, sinta-se abraçado por cara pixel de sua tela.

author: Noxium
quote: GTA VI — 10/10 : Rockstar vient de placer la barre très haut.Après Red Dead Redemption 2, impossible pour Rockstar de revenir au gameplay ultra-arcade de GTA V. J'ai aimé ce dernier, mais son manque de réalisme m'a toujours dérangé. Sa longévité doit aussi énormément à GTA Online et au RP. GTA VI devait prolonger l'évolution amorcée par RDR2, pas revenir treize ans en **** quelle claque ! Vice City et Leonida sont d'une beauté folle. La densité du monde, les animations, la physique, les réactions des PNJ, les interactions et les détails donnent l'impression d'un écosystème vivant, pas d'un simple décor. Chaque rue raconte quelque chose. Ce niveau d'immersion est **** duo Jason et Lucia est une réussite. Leur complicité, leurs tensions et leur relation donnent de l'épaisseur au récit. On n'incarne pas seulement deux criminels : on suit deux personnages qui ont quelque chose à perdre. C'est précisément ce que j'attends de **** à ceux qui crient au « woke » parce qu'une femme tient un rôle majeur ou qu'un couple se comporte comme un vrai couple : vous avez découvert les relations humaines ? Bouhou, vous ne pouvez pas aller aux putes comme vous voulez ? Bah branlez-vous et passez à autre **** n'a jamais été qu'un simulateur où la liberté consiste à tuer des passants ou à payer des prostituées. C'est une satire de l'Amérique, des personnages, un scénario, une ambiance et un monde qui réagit à nos actions. Si votre vision de GTA s'arrête à ces deux activités, vous êtes passés à côté de **** les 30 FPS ? Évidemment que 60 seraient préférables. Mais personnellement, une fois plongé dans le jeu, je les oublie. Il faut comparer ce qui est comparable : faire tourner un monde ouvert aussi dense, détaillé et vivant n'a pas les mêmes contraintes qu'un FPS plus linéaire ou un petit jeu en pixel art. Si c'est si facile, créez donc un univers de cette ampleur à 60 FPS constants sur console. On regardera le résultat !Quant au review bombing, c'est affligeant. Mettre 0/10 à un jeu de cette ambition parce qu'on a entendu un influenceur hurler au « wokisme », c'est de la mauvaise foi, pas une critique. On peut ne pas aimer GTA VI, préférer l'arcade de GTA V ou discuter de ses limites techniques : aucun problème. Mais une note doit refléter une expérience de jeu, pas un caprice idéologique. Et je me demande combien de ces 0/10 viennent de gens qui y ont réellement **** VI n'a pas à plaire à tout le monde. Pour moi, il est l'aboutissement de l'évolution entamée avec RDR2 : un monde ouvert vertigineux, une réalisation époustouflante et une aventure portée par un duo **** monde de GTA VI est immense et ouvert. Dommage que l'esprit de certains de ses détracteurs le soit si peu.10/10. Merci Rockstar.

author: ismation2027
quote:
10/10. El juego del año.

Lo que más destaco es el mundo abierto. Como en Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar le dio vida a cada rincón de Leonida: te alejas de las misiones y hasta un bosque o una casa abandonada tiene una historia que contar. Y puedes hacer de todo: bucear, navegar, pescar, comer sano, hacer ejercicio, cortarte el pelo, comprar o reaccionar ante eventos con NPCs.

Las misiones transmiten muchísimo. Te contagias de la tensión, la amargura y las emociones de los protagonistas.

La economía es otro acierto: ganar dinero cuesta, y casi siempre es delinquiendo. A diferencia de GTA V, donde esperabas a la policía para hacer explotar todo, aquí te preocupa que alguien llame, que te reconozcan o que llegue la policía. Esa tensión se siente real. Y gastar también se disfruta, con una personalización profunda de vehículos y armas.

Gráficamente no hay nada mejor en PS5, y lo más impresionante es el rendimiento con ese nivel visual. Tuve un par de bugs menores, nada que interrumpiera una misión.

Lo único negativo es la relación entre Jason y Lucia. Cuando quieres hacer una misión, Lucia te llama para que vuelvas a dormir a casa o para que la busques en el trabajo. La gracia de un GTA es la libertad, y esas obligaciones restan horas de disfrute.

Aún así, es una obra maestra.

quote:
Игра не разрушила мои ожидания, она осталась именно на том уровне, на котором и должна была быть GTA VI. 
Те кто утверждают, что GTA VI должна была быть совсем другой, это те, чьи ожидания были не оправданы. Для меня, эта игра оправдала абсолютно все ожидания:
Отличная графика: Да, эта игра сделана на высшем уровне, сравниваяя ее с GTA V, здесь в разы больше лесов, а качество воды, отдельный уровень. Да, Rockstar делают изумительную систему графических механик и с каждой новой игрок, видно как она эволюционирует, поэтому она просто не может стать хуже. Видно, что это графика RDR2, но с улучшенными на ступень, всеми аспектами. И я не понимаю игроков, что считают, что эта игра независимо создавалась 13 лет, ведь активная разработка была на протяжении 8 лет.
Сюжет: Один из лучших сюжетов, харизма персонажей и их взаимодействие друг с другом просто на высоте. Последние разы я так сопереживал героям только в RDR2 и KCD2.
Мир: В этой части самый живой мир, опять же, не без заслуги систем которые перекочевали сюда из RDR2. Встречи незнакомцев, плотный трафик, куча активностей, этот мир буквально живет своей жизнью. Ну и конечно, просто огроменная карта.
Для меня GTA VI, однозначно игра года, несмотря на 30fps (которых вообще не заметно) и мелких багов (какая игра выходит без багов?).

author: hbk321
quote: Grand Theft Auto 6 is overall a good gaming experience for modern industry standards but doesn't live up to the extreme hype that surrounded the game. My biggest Pros are surely the graphics. Truly remarkable for an open world experience which is harder to build than a level based game. The world building and the atmosphere it's great, the game has a lot of activities, accessible buildings and the map feels truly big. The main story is no short of 50hours and for modern gaming it's very positive. To 100% the game you'd need at minimum 100h. My biggest Cons. At the cost of having such detail map not every bit is interactable, for example some angle and some bushes have some kind of invisible wall, this can cause teleportation if you fall from above, also sometimes you get stuck in places, with not even high obstacles as the character not being able to jump far enough, obstacles that every other GTA character would get through. The game hold your hand too much, too many times. Some mission are too linear with the game being too strict and in some you can't even fail. That's very bad for me. Many times trying to achieve realism the game turns up to be less realistic and very limiting on fun. a stupid but famous example Many players might have seen that the train stops and you can't have fun with it. A train that have should not even be able to stop in time that fast, that limits fun and expression for the player in return for something that is not even realistic. I think a gta game should always find the balance between realism and fun/chaos, Gta 6 does not have that balance up to the standards of what Grand Theft Auto means to me as a Franchise. The game limits the player freedom too many times and it even prohibites you from killing certain groups of NPC outside missions. Something never seen in a GTA. sometimes the games feels to soft to be a GTA. Overall the game can be very fun, maintains the right spirit on other aspects and can be enjoyable in it's story. But shift too much from the nature of GTA and can't be more than an 8. Surely not a 9 or a 10

author: TewhiBear
quote:
I am playing on launch ps5 and currently at the beggining of chapter two in the story. Heres my opinions on the game so far.

Performance
The performance is very solid for 30fps. Personally i havent has any noticable drops in framerate and its been very smooth so far. No complaints there.

Graphics
They are absolutely phenomenal. Its crazy how the game looks this good and realistic. Im very impressed with the work.

Characters
I find the characters in this game very lovable and entertaining. Theyre all so different and very easy to get invested in. 

Story
Story so for has been very good. Im very happy to see rockstar take the relationship approach in the series, it feels like something different and fresh. I am very invested to finish the story and see how Jasons and Lucias relationship blossom even more. 

Side content
The game is very immersive and il having so much fun roleplaying even outside the missions. Theres so much to do and discover it feels very rich in content. The random events are very funny too.

The map
Its huge, all the different place have their own little personalities and ready to explore im honestly a bit overwhelmed with how big it is but ill eventually get to explore all the corners of this map and im excited to see what i find.

author: JanRat09
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI is an absolute masterpiece that sets a completely new standard for open-world gaming. From the very first minute, the scale and attention to detail in Vice City and the wider state of Leonida are breathtaking. The world feels genuinely alive, packed with dynamic events, vibrant nightlife, and realistic NPC interactions that make exploring every corner a pure joy.
The story is gripping, emotional, and brilliantly paced. The dynamic between Lucia and Jason brings fresh energy to the franchise, blending high-stakes crime with genuine human emotion and sharp satire. Every mission feels cinematic yet gives you the freedom to approach situations your own way.
Visually, the game is a technical triumph. The lighting, weather effects, and character animations are unmatched, running smoothly while delivering next-level immersion. Combined with an incredible soundtrack and tight, responsive gameplay, GTA VI isn't just a great game—it is a landmark achievement in entertainment. 10/10.

author: rank1dedasl
quote:
The pacing of the story is excellent, maintaining a natural balance between the narrative and gameplay. The ups and downs of the storyline feel well-placed, keeping the experience engaging throughout the journey.

Jason and Lucia's relationship is one of the highlights of the story. Their love and affection for each other remain evident throughout most of the game. They consistently support and defend one another, always having each other's backs. Although they occasionally disagree and have conflicts, their strong feelings for each other make their relationship feel genuine and believable without becoming overly cheesy or cringe.

The soundtrack is another major highlight, with beautiful and atmospheric music playing in the background at just the right moments, perfectly complementing both the gameplay and emotional scenes.

The gunplay and gameplay are incredibly enjoyable, featuring exciting combat encounters and intense firefights that genuinely get your adrenaline pumping. However, frame-rate drops occur frequently in crowded areas and during most combat encounters, sometimes bringing performance down to around 20–22 FPS during firefights and 22–25 FPS in crowded areas. Unfortunately, these drops noticeably affect the smoothness and excitement of the experience, preventing some of the game's best action moments from reaching their full potential.

Despite these technical shortcomings, the overall experience is outstanding. The storytelling, character relationships, gameplay, soundtrack, and attention to detail make this an incredibly memorable experience.

**10/10 from me.**

The best GTA ever made, and honestly, it's not even close.

I love the pacing too. Not as frantic as GTA V, not as slow as RDR2. Just the perfect balance. Both main missions and side activities are genuinely enjoyable, and those little things some people find boring? They're optional, and they make the world even more immersive.

Rockstar hasn't just made another open-world game. They've created a world you actually want to live in.

author: Redullergy
quote:
After spending a lot of time with the game, I honestly think it's one of the best open-world experiences available.
There is an incredible amount of content and things to do. I feel like some of the negative user reviews come from players who haven't invested enough time into the game to see what it really offers. In my opinion, the game gets significantly better after the early chapters, and from Chapter 3 onwards it becomes absolutely amazing.
The world is packed with activities, the graphics are stunning, and the attention to detail is on another level. The story, exploration and overall gameplay kept me hooked for hours.
My only real criticism is that I would have liked more freedom when it comes to purchasing and customising properties and vehicles. Being able to properly buy houses and cars would have added even more depth to the experience.
Apart from that, I genuinely have very little to complain about. If you're willing to invest some time into it and get beyond the opening chapters, you'll find an incredible game with a huge amount to offer.
Rating: 9/10

author: kkigamers
quote:
There are video games that entertain you, games that immerse you, and then there is Grand Theft Auto VI — a phenomenal achievement that pushes the boundaries of gaming technology, storytelling, realism and interactive world-building to an entirely new level. Rockstar Games hasn't simply created another GTA. It has created an entire living, breathing world. Graphics, Technology & Open-World Realism: The graphical fidelity is absolutely breathtaking. From incredibly realistic facial expressions, detailed character models and natural animations to spectacular lighting, reflections, weather effects and stunning landscapes, almost everything feels unbelievably lifelike. Vice City and the wider state of Leonida are extraordinary. The world doesn't feel like a collection of buildings and scripted missions; it feels like an actual functioning society. NPCs are a massive achievement. Their behaviour, conversations, reactions and unpredictable activities make the environment feel genuinely alive. They aren't merely decorative objects wandering around the map; they contribute to a dynamic and immersive world. The police system is another phenomenal achievement. Its investigative behaviour, vehicle tracking, responses to criminal activity and pursuit mechanics make escaping law enforcement a genuine strategic challenge. Your actions have consequences, and simply turning a corner is no longer a magical solution to every police pursuit. The sheer attention to detail demonstrates Rockstar's extraordinary technical ambition. It raises the standard for what an open-world environment can achieve. Storytelling — Emotion, Action & Consequences: Jason and Lucia's relationship provides the emotional foundation, while the criminal underworld, betrayals, dangerous encounters and intense action sequences deliver the adrenaline. The narrative explores loyalty, trust, love, ambition, survival and the consequences of personal decisions. It isn't simply about committing crimes and making money; it is about the human relationships and difficult choices behind them. Perhaps most impressive is the reported multiple-ending system, featuring more than 10 possible ending variations. Outcomes reportedly depend on interconnected factors, including financial circumstances, Jason and Lucia's relationship, criminal reputation and decisions made throughout the story. This makes the campaign feel meaningful. Your choices can influence not just individual missions but potentially the ultimate fate of the characters. A Brilliant Satirical Reflection of Real Society: This is where GTA VI becomes particularly fascinating. Beyond the graphics and entertainment, Rockstar delivers a remarkably cynical social commentary. The game explores an uncomfortable reality: sometimes, it isn't simply about whether you committed a crime; it's about whether you possess enough money, influence and resources to escape its consequences. A player who conducts crimes carefully, maintains a low criminal profile, avoids unnecessary attention and accumulates sufficient financial resources may secure a much more favourable outcome. Meanwhile, someone who attracts police attention, builds a damaging criminal reputation or lacks financial security may face tragedy or imprisonment. The satire becomes even more interesting when corruption enters the picture. Imagine exposing a corrupt senator, only to discover that doing something morally defensible doesn't necessarily guarantee justice or personal protection. Without sufficient resources or the ability to avoid the authorities, you could still end up behind bars. Money can buy protection. Influence can change consequences. Concealed crimes can remain hidden, while someone without power can suffer even when pursuing a morally defensible cause. The game challenges conventional ideas of morality by confronting players with the difference between doing what is right and possessing enough power to survive the consequences. This is brilliant social satire. It makes players experience the very inequalities that the narrative criticises. Final Verdict: Grand Theft Auto VI is an extraordinary combination of technological innovation, cinematic storytelling, emotional depth, intelligent gameplay mechanics and social commentary. Its breathtaking graphics, sophisticated NPC behaviour, improved police intelligence, enormous open world, dynamic criminal systems and interconnected narrative decisions establish an exceptional standard for the gaming industry. But its greatest achievement might not be its graphics or technology. It is the way Rockstar transforms a fictional criminal sandbox into a disturbing reflection of real society, where wealth, influence, reputation and access to protection can sometimes matter more than morality itself. GTA VI is not merely a game you play. It is a world you experience, a story you influence and a society whose uncomfortable realities you are forced to confront.
10/10 — An absolute masterpiece.

author: ahmeddz22
quote:
A generational open world held back only by its 30fps ceiling
After more than a decade of waiting, Rockstar actually pulled it off. Leonida—from the neon streets of Vice City out to the Leonida Keys—is easily the most dense, reactive open world ever built. Walking down a block feels genuinely unpredictable, and side activities like fishing, pool, and street-level car tuning naturally pull you off the main path.
Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos are the best protagonists the series has had. Their dynamic grounds the story in a way GTA V never quite managed, and the heavier, Red Dead Redemption 2-style character movement makes gunfights and exploration feel much more deliberate. Pulling off dynamic bank heists outside of story missions—and dealing with smarter cops who don't just forget you exist the second you leave a search circle—adds real tension to free roam. Driving is also a massive leap forward, with detailed engine customization and realistic crash physics where panels buckle and wheels can actually tear off.
The only real drawback at launch is the locked 30fps target on consoles, along with some heavy post-processing and motion blur that you can't fully dial back. Even with minor frame dips during massive explosions, the sheer scale and craft on display make this an easy 9/10.

author: Sebooste
quote:
Un chef-d’œuvre!

Et certains semblent avoir oublié ce que sont les jeux vidéo.Honnêtement, la vague de critiques négatives autour de GTA VI devient ridicule. Entre les débats interminables sur le wokisme, l’antiwokisme et l’obsession du 60 FPS, on finirait presque par croire que certains ont oublié pourquoi on joue aux jeux **** VI est un véritable chef-d’œuvre. 
Le niveau de détail, la qualité visuelle, l’atmosphère, l’ambition, l’immensité de ce que Rockstar a créé… C’est tout simplement hallucinant. On regarde ce jeu et on se demande sincèrement comment ils ont réussi à produire quelque chose d’aussi impressionnant.
Mais au-delà des graphismes et de la prouesse technique, il y a surtout l’essentiel : le plaisir de jouer. Le gameplay est un régal, le monde semble vivant et l’expérience dans son ensemble est un bonheur. C’est précisément cela qui devrait compter. Non, un jeu n’a pas besoin de tourner en 60 FPS pour être exceptionnel. 
Non, chaque choix artistique ne doit pas être passé au filtre d’une bataille idéologique. Et non, un jeu vidéo n’a pas à satisfaire toutes les indignations d’Internet pour mériter d’être reconnu à sa juste valeur. Un chef-d’œuvre ne devient pas moins exceptionnel simplement parce qu’il ne correspond ni à votre idéologie ni à votre fréquence d’images préférée. La critique est légitime, bien sûr. Mais quand certains passent plus de temps à chercher des raisons de détester un jeu qu’à apprécier ce qui a été accompli, le problème n’est peut-être pas le jeu. Peut-être avons-nous simplement oublié comment apprécier les choses.

Rockstar place une nouvelle fois la barre très haut. Et c’est bien cela qui mérite qu’on en parle.

The intro is a bit slow to develop characters so you actually invest in them emotionally and care what happens to them. If that didn’t occur the whole thing wouldn’t work. I’m the first person that would call BS on anything woke and I see nothing so far that I would find offensive outside of Lucia being able to beat up 250 lb men without breaking a sweat. You can also break off from her and go do what you want solo at any time after the first chapter so I’m not sure what the issue is? What I see is the game focusing on an adult relationship and the game is incredible for it. Rather than mindlessly running around killing everyone you begin to actually think about your actions which is a very mature and much needed introduction to this series. Rockstar needed to do something different and I feel like they succeeded brilliantly. This game is made for mature adults that have lived beyond mommies basement and actually been in intimate relationships Irl -not 15 yr olds with tic tok brain. I think this is the main reason for the division in audience reaction. The story elements go right over some players heads because they have no way to relate. Also the 30 fps nonsense can ****! They had to run this thing on 7 yr old hardware and MS junkbox series s- it’s a miracle they got it to run in first place! I’ve seen things happen in this game that other games wish they could accomplish on a regular basis and some of the best moments I’ve ever experienced in a game and probably ever will. Everyone is entitled to an opinion but review bombing this product is childish and unwarranted. Thank you Rockstar- for the game of a lifetime!

author: NoahThatsWack
quote: I think a lot of people are missing what Rockstar has accomplished with GTA VI. This isn't just GTA V with better graphics and a bigger map. It's a fundamental evolution of the open-world crime game. Instead of relying on scripted missions for its best moments, it gives you systems that reward planning, creativity, and adapting when things go wrong. Ironically, the slower, more grounded gameplay people are criticizing is what makes that freedom ****, 30 FPS ****. But getting a world this detailed and complex running on a PS5 or Xbox is impressive in itself. Like GTA V and RDR2, it feels like a game pushing current hardware to its limits. I can't wait to see it on PC and next-gen consoles.People keep calling it slow, and I wonder how many actually made it past the first chapter. Once the world opens up, the possibilities are ridiculous.I wanted to rob three jewelry stores in Downtown Vice, but after casing the area, I knew escaping on the ground would be a nightmare. So I left, stole a helicopter, and landed it on a rooftop with ladder access about 150 feet from the stores. The heist went well until things erupted into a shootout. It was chaotic, nerve-racking, and insanely fun. And here's the point: none of that was scripted. I thought up the plan, and the game let me execute it.That's the freedom I've wanted from GTA for years.I get why people coming from GTA V, especially if they never played RDR2, might dislike the slower approach. But think about GTA V: for a game about crime, how much worthwhile crime could you actually commit outside missions? Robbing stores paid next to nothing. Making real money mostly meant following scripted **** VI changes that. It makes you learn through trial and error. You might fail once, or five times, but you start understanding how to plan better, cover your tracks, and respond to unexpected problems. That's far more rewarding than having everything laid out for **** first time I robbed a loan store, the bills exploded with dye and covered me in pink. I escaped, or thought I had, until cops spotted me walking around like a giant highlighter and picked up my trail again. I literally had to shower the dye off when I got home. It's hilarious, but it also shows how consequences follow you beyond the robbery **** the police AI? Rockstar absolutely cooked.Escaping isn't just driving fast until your wanted level disappears. Changing clothes, hiding or ditching weapons, and choosing where to go actually matter. Cops search nearby hiding spots and can even follow footprints. I found that out when officers yelled "I FOUND THEIR TRACKS" and started walking STRAIGHT TOWARDS ME while I was stealing a car. Thank god I'd already changed clothes LMAO.There's nothing quite like pulling off a heist, covering your tracks, and watching a cop drive right past you without realizing you're the person they're **** NPCs are another huge leap. They don't just fill sidewalks; they create opportunities. Some are normal, some are absolute freaks, and others are committing crimes of their own. You can stumble across a robbery, let the criminals do the work, then steal their loot. Cars and planes can crash and scatter drugs, jewelry, and cash, and other NPCs might scramble to grab it before you do. A random encounter can turn into complete chaos in seconds.That's the difference between a world that looks alive and one that feels alive. These events aren't just spectacle. They give you situations to react to and choices to **** slower pace is part of why it works. A robbery wouldn't be satisfying if escaping were effortless. The police wouldn't be interesting if disguises, evidence, and surroundings meant nothing. The game's complexity gives your decisions actual **** don't have to enjoy every design choice. If you prefer GTA V's arcadey approach, fair enough. But dismissing GTA VI because it isn't more of the same ignores the huge creative leap Rockstar made. I've had unforgettable experiences that weren't laid out by a mission designer. The systems let me create them **** me, that's the future of open-world games. Game of the decade. A perfect 10/10.Which is why seeing a 5.5/10 user rating is so disappointing. Gamers complain endlessly about recycled formulas and studios refusing to take risks. Then we get something this ambitious and people punish it for not playing exactly like the last ****'s like being served steak and lobster on a gold-and-diamond-encrusted platter and complaining the steak is too juicy and the lobster too buttery.Criticism is fair. But if we dismiss genuine innovation whenever it challenges our expectations, why would developers keep taking risks?Seriously, get a grip. What the **** are we doing?

author: HamishEmmett
quote:
I can appreciate many of the criticisms this game has received, but disagree with all of them. This is a masterpiece, and technically the best game ever made.

The cons

Yes, the 30 fps can be frustrating if used to higher frame rates, and it does mar the experience slightly. however, this is not a reflection of the game itself; indeed, with the graphical quality, density of cars, and realism that Rockstar has imbued unto GTA6, it is a testament to their effort that 30 fps is achieved. The frame rate issue is simply a reflection of the bureaucratic decisions that Rockstar has taken to make their game initially console exclusive, and thus the CPU's unable to handle the game, While I can appreciate the frustration with this, it should not be taken into account as a criticism of the game.

Likewise, the price of the game, (160 for ultimate in AUD) is highly steep. But this game sets a benchmark for quality, costing more to make than any other game, twice the size of its predecessor, and 3 times the size of RDR2, with even greater quality put into the design. While it can be annoying, ultimately this is a premium price put onto a premium game.

Third, the pacing; yes, the game is slow, but it is part of a story that takes a different direction from the others in the series, developing the relationship between the protagonists in a highly impressive manner that builds into the classic GTA feel in later chapters, and the pacing is part of what makes the game so incredible.

Now the pros.

This game acts as an accumulation of everything the gaming industry has been developing; the story is a masterpiece, and a mix of the last two Rockstar games, with the quality of red dead, and the modern setting of GTA which leads to highly satisfying pay offs especially with a slower start and an ending I'm eager to reach.

The world is by far the biggest I have seen, and 30+ hours in, I have yet to scratch the surface, in spite of all the exploration, and feels incredibly alive, with the dual protagonist system done very well, and an immeasurable number of random events that feel real. I'm sure there are dozens of easter eggs and secrets hidden lovingly throughout the game which will take months to find.

Similarly for Rockstar, the combat is massively improved, and actually handles like a proper shooter game, unlike their previous ones, which was rather limited, with guns handling differently and having the levels of customization that was also previously lacking.

The realism; this game is incredibly immersive, but is done to an extent that is arguably more subtle than RDR2, with intricate details throughout keeping the Florida setting alive such as comics, radio stations, house interiors. This comes alongside immersive realism  tiny details such as refueling, eating and working out all of which have impacts on the characters. However, the game does it to a right extent; enough to be appreciated as a feature for role play, but something that does not detract from a persons experience if they simply want to drive fast cars and shoot at cops.

Ultimately this game is a development from GTA5, and something fans may be angry about regarding the pacing, but beyond changes players may struggle with is an incredibly perfected and polished world in an echelon unmatched in the gaming industry

author: itsvellox
quote: This game is getting a ridiculous amount of review bombing right now, and a lot of it feels completely undeserved. I’ve been playing games for about 20 years, and after putting a solid amount of time into GTA 6 since launch, it’s easily one of the strongest experiences i’ve had in the series and one of the best open world games i’ve played in general.Visually it’s a clear step up from Red Dead Redemption 2. The lighting, reflections, water, and physics all feel more refined and natural. The map of Leonida is massive and densely detailed, with distinct regions that each have their own atmosphere. There’s a lot to explore both on land and underwater.There’s no shortage of things to do different types of races, shooting ranges, skydiving, bars with mini games, clubs, and plenty of smaller activities scattered around. NPCs feel more reactive and context aware than in previous GTA games their behavior actually changes based on location and situation instead of just standing around as background. Vehicles handle really well and feel like the best the series has offered so **** the story side (no spoilers), the dual-protagonist setup with Jason and Lucia works better than i expected. Their relationship feels natural and well written, and the overall narrative is more grounded and character driven than some earlier entries while still delivering the scale and chaos you want from a GTA game. It doesn’t feel like it’s trying too hard to be cinematic it just lets the characters and the world carry it. It’s not perfect the usual launch day quirks and the locked 30 fps on console are real, but the strengths far outweigh the issues for me. The review bombing is doing the game a disservice.

author: Jordan98
quote:
The negative reviews for this game are completely laughable. They are either targeting the locked 30 FPS or the fact there's a playable woman character.

I've played every Rockstar game ever, from PS2 Warriors, Bully, Man Hunt, all the way up to PS4 Red Dead 2, and what I can tell you is that this is the most dynamic, innovative, cinematic world I have ever explored in a video game.

The story is engaging even at the start in Chapter 1, when Rockstar takes their usual approach and doesn't show high-octane action. All characters you meet feel like main protagonists, all unique with their own personalities, and the two main protagonists bounce off each other so well.

Gunplay is similar to Red Dead 2 but takes another leap forward. Ragdoll physics are amazing, NPCs react to where they are shot, and the game feels immersive.

The car driving is a mix between GTA 4 and GTA 5. Not too weighty like 4 and not too arcade-like like 5. The combination between the two makes for the best feeling in a driving game. It genuinely makes you wonder why you'd ever play Forza Horizon or Gran Turismo; it's that fun. The car destruction physics are truly on another level. Windows break in certain places from gunshots, realistic dents in the metal of the car doors, car tyres blow out and topple over. The animations to get out of a car when it's toppled over, where you have to climb out or, if there's not much space, squeeze out. You can tell there was so much love and time spent on every animation.

There have been so many random events, all to make the world feel alive. The most I enjoy about the world is walking around, getting into verbal fights with the NPCs similar to Red Dead 2 and watching how it unfolds, which could end in a de-escalation, a fist fight, other NPCs getting involved, or a shootout with a gang and them hunting you down in a car chase.

The police system is a massive step up. You genuinely need to think about what you're going to do for robberies now. Bring a silencer on your pistol, try to go in stealthy, take out the guards, just for a random abiding citizen trying to be the hero to tackle you down, in which your partner helps grab them off. The chase can go from being shot at from a police helicopter, changing cars and outfits undetected, to cruising out unnoticed past the police. All the way to your car tyres blowing out from spike traps and running on foot to be taken down by the K9 unit. The possibilities in the world are endless.

There's so much more I could say about the game. It's something words genuinely cannot describe; you simply have to play it to understand. The game is an absolute masterpiece.

author: bryant25
quote:
GTA VI es exactamente el tipo de juego que esperaba de Rockstar. Una experiencia que no tiene miedo de probar cosas nuevas, de arriesgarse y de ofrecernos la calidad que merecemos como jugadores.

Jason y Lucia me han encantado como protagonistas. Su relación, sus personalidades y la forma en que sus decisiones influyen en la historia hacen que GTA VI se sienta como algo más que otro juego de mundo abierto. Son personajes con los que realmente quieres involucrarte, y eso es algo que valoro muchísimo.

Me gusta que Rockstar haya apostado por una historia diferente, por una relación que tiene sus propias dificultades y por un mundo que se siente vivo. No se trata simplemente de seguir una misión tras otra, sino de vivir una experiencia en la que nuestras decisiones tienen peso.

El tema de los finales es algo que me ha parecido especialmente interesante. Aunque no todos me resultan igual de satisfactorios, creo que eso no define la calidad de toda la historia. Cada final puede interpretarse de manera diferente, y considero que el desenlace también refleja cómo hemos llevado nuestra relación con el otro protagonista y qué clase de personas hemos sido durante el juego. A veces, el final que más nos gusta no es necesariamente el que mejor encaja con nuestras acciones.

GTA VI no es perfecto, pero eso no le quita mérito. Es un juego que se atreve a hacer cosas nuevas, que tiene personalidad y que demuestra el enorme trabajo que hay detrás de su creación. Para mí, eso vale mucho más que cumplir con las expectativas de quienes solo quieren que todo siga siendo exactamente igual.

Y ahora, sobre quienes están intentando hundir su valoración:
Es lamentable que haya personas que no puedan reconocer la calidad de un juego simplemente porque ha superado a otro que consideran superior. Darle un 0 a GTA VI sin jugarlo, utilizar cuentas externas y organizarse para manipular su puntuación no es una crítica. Es una rabia.

Y si el motivo es que GTA VI ha superado a Zelda, entonces el problema no es GTA VI. El problema es la incapacidad de aceptar que otro juego pueda alcanzar o superar algo que consideraban intocable.

Zelda puede tener sus grandes juegos, sus méritos y su historia. Nadie necesita destruirlos para reconocer lo que GTA VI ha conseguido. Pero tampoco voy a fingir que una saga es intocable solo porque tiene una comunidad que no soporta que otra destaque.

Si GTA VI merece un 0, que expliquen por qué. Que hablen de sus errores, de sus problemas, de sus decisiones de diseño. Pero que no vengan a disfrazar de crítica una campaña de **** VI merece ser valorado por su calidad, no castigado por el éxito que ha conseguido.

Mi valoración es por el juego que he disfrutado, por sus protagonistas, por su historia y por la ambición de Rockstar. No por una guerra de comunidades, ni por la necesidad de demostrar que una saga es mejor que otra.

GTA VI es una experiencia que me ha gustado muchísimo y que merece todo el reconocimiento que ha recibido. Y quienes intentan hundirla sin siquiera jugarla no van a cambiar eso.

author: rikympj211
quote:
​Take the user score here with a massive grain of salt. Half the negative reviews are from people review-bombing the game because they haven't even played it yet, or from folks who played for ten minutes at a friend's house and think they have the whole experience figured out. You are entitled to your opinion, sure, but bombing a game without actually putting the hours in doesn't make your take valid.
​People are also crying about the 30 FPS. Honestly, frame rate usually bothers me too, or at least I thought it would, until I actually started playing. The game pulls you in so hard that you straight-up forget it's 30 FPS. The world feels unbelievably alive, and I have yet to walk around without being genuinely surprised by some random civilian interaction or event happening right in front of me.
​The complaints about bugs are also completely overblown. Anyone comparing this to a broken launch clearly forgot what Cyberpunk 2077 was like on day one, where you couldn't even walk into Night City without running into constant glitches. Of course a game this massive has a few bugs at launch, that's just the reality of a world this dense, and what is actually impressive is how rare they are and how little they affect the experience. Most of them are minor things that will get patched quietly without most players ever noticing.
​What really gets me, though, are the Ocarina of Time fans bombing this page. I say this as someone who loves Ocarina with all my heart, since I first played it on my Nintendo 2DS as a kid and it still holds some of my best gaming memories. That game is an untouchable classic, and it doesn't need anyone's protection. Seeing fellow fans drop 0s on GTA VI out of some desperate need to prove old is still gold is just sad, because celebrating a masterpiece from the past shouldn't mean tearing down a modern one out of insecurity. Ignore the noise from the sidelines, and experience this game for yourself.

author: Max0n04
quote:
Masterpiece.

After waiting for so long, people got hyped up beyond any logical point and Rockstar still deliveree.

Good:
- Great open world, loaded with content, side missions and stuff to do. Around 33 hours in, still half the story is left to do and just exploring stuff.
- Jasons and Lucias relationship are main part of the game which is clearly visible and is done pretty good.
- Car physics are something else, they handle and crash just like in real life. Sportcar have stiffer suspensions while old musclecars have a more soft suspension which forces you to adapt.

Bad:
- optimization is ok, but clearly this game is for next gen. Not as bad as with cyberpunk still.
- occasional bugs, though it is expected at this point of release.

Overall this is a generational game. Game is for people who can appreciate story driven and more slow pace, rather than constant action dopamine push.

author: calebebonfa
quote:
Para quem não conseguiu compreender a proposta do jogo, talvez esta geração não esteja preparada para entender o que a Rockstar criou. Uma geração cada vez mais imediatista, que reclama de tudo e parece ter esquecido o que significa viver uma experiência de verdade.

Mas vamos lá...

GTA VI é simplesmente incrível. O mundo é vivo, dinâmico e reage às suas atitudes. Suas escolhas têm consequências. Não dá para sair por aí roubando carros, cometendo crimes e causando o caos sem esperar algum tipo de reação. O jogo não quer apenas que você jogue, quer que você viva aquele mundo.

A Rockstar não criou apenas mais um GTA. Criou uma experiência pensada para marcar os próximos 10, 15 ou até 20 anos da indústria dos games.

É um trabalho extraordinário, cheio de personalidade, detalhes e ambição.

GTA VI não é apenas um jogo. É um novo patamar.

____________________________________

For those who failed to understand what this game is trying to achieve, maybe this generation simply isn't ready to appreciate what Rockstar has created. A generation that wants everything instantly, complains about everything, and seems to have forgotten what it means to truly experience a game.

But let's get to it...

GTA VI is simply incredible. The world feels alive, dynamic, and reacts to your actions. Your decisions have consequences. You can't just go around stealing cars, committing crimes, and causing chaos without expecting some kind of reaction. The game doesn't just want you to play. It wants you to live in its world.

Rockstar didn't just create another GTA. They created an experience designed to define the next 10, 15, or even 20 years of the gaming industry.

An extraordinary achievement, full of personality, detail, and ambition.

GTA VI isn't just a game. It's a whole new level.

author: BurnedTomato
quote:
Here is a full no spoiler review after playing all GTAs since GTA Vice City:

You get put into this massive open world version of Miami that is in alot of places 1:1 recreations that looks absolutely stunning. You start in a prologue that gives you the basic mechanics which you needs to learn since it differs from previous gta mechanics where X is no longer running (tho this can be changed in settings if you still want the classic way). Now I won’t get into the story too much so short said:
The story takes its time, you get to learn the different characters, who they are, what they do, how they think. Everything does take time as it would be when starting fresh. The game takes more of a Red Dead Redemption approach with the story which I personally like. I like to see the world and actually see character development and learn about them more than just a shootout. A lot of people have been complaining with a lot of different stuff which is:

- “it’s just Sims or boyfriend simulator you just fix things in the house to make your girlfriend happy”. 

No. How you approach your relationship with Lucia is optional and none of the shopping and fixing is required except for a mission where you move some furniture and build a table. Granted those are a bit slow but frankly short and people seem to forget the Yoga mission or container mission in gta5. 

- “You can’t steal cars”

You can absolutely steal cars, however as real life, some cars have more advanced anti theft technology requiring different tools we don’t have from the start. There is actual progression, but this only applies to parked cars. You can absolutely steal a high end car if someone is in it and it’s unlocked. It has a tracker so you can’t keep it but that will be unlocked later on. There’s actual progression which gives the game a purpose.

- “Video of the plane not exploding after hitting a tower”

You can turn vehicle damage to a minimal in settings practically making them unbreakable so that is a setting that has been changed for clip farming

- “You can’t shoot inside a club”

Yes granted that is a weird place to add that restriction but gun restriction in gta5 has also been a thing as not being able to shoot specific people as they are essential to the story or side mission. Here the game is more realistic where you can’t just kill certain important characters for fun and they magically come back with the mission again and just sends you a text and a medical bill. The restrictions are minimal and not a big deal whatsoever.

Mechanics:
- Driving feels absolutely amazing, the cars have different weights and feeling and how they grip on the ground depending on your tires and different mechanics specializes in different types of tuning so there’s is such a big variety of customization and builds its amazing

- shooting feels so satisfying. The guns have weight, they’re hitting hard and they hit like they hurt as they should. Where you shoot npc also have an effect. Shooting their knee or other places to handicap them will not kill them but make them lay on the ground hurt and screaming unable to move properly. Some other places like the heart and head is of course lethal. People don’t feel like all the same where shooting them in the foot makes them lay down and die in 4 seconds like gta5. It feels alive 

- flying feels amazing too. It has weight, and it feels different depending on the plane or helicopter of the weight and such. Gta5 had this too but gta6 has made it so much better.

Overall the game is absolutely amazing it is the most alive game I’ve ever seen. So many small random moments and events that makes everything so unique and all characters so highly detailed and unique til including npcs and their reactions to everything. It has a lot of red dead redemption mechanics and that too is an amazing game. Of course it’s different from gta5. There’s always changed. Same goes with gta4 to gta5 where other restrictions have been put on or features removed and so on. We are blinded by nostalgia and the fact we’ve been used to those mechanics and ways for 13 whole years. This game has been out for 2 days. It’s gonna take time to give the game the same love as gta5 as it’s been such a big part of our lives, but it is truly amazing and I’m looking forward to keep playing and exploring new things

author: DONGULI
quote: This game has received a ridiculous amount of undeserved review bombing. As someone with 20 years of gaming experience and around 4,000–6,000 games played, I can honestly say GTA 6 is the best experience I’ve ever had in a video game.Visually, it’s a straight-up upgrade over RDR2. Lighting, reflections, water, physics — everything looks and feels incredible. The map is huge and insanely detailed, with tons of places to explore, both on land and underwater. Every area has its own atmosphere, stories and characters.There’s plenty to do: drone, car, plane, bike and dirt races, shooting ranges, skydiving, bars with minigames, clubs and much more. Almost every venue offers something interesting. NPCs are also a huge improvement. Their behavior depends on where they live, their social status and other characteristics. They feel like actual people rather than random decorations.Vehicles are probably the best in the series. I’m a huge Forza Horizon fan, but GTA 6 delivers an incredible driving experience. Every car feels different. Handling sits somewhere between GTA 4 and GTA 5. You can feel vehicle weight, differences between FWD and RWD, and how engine placement affects handling. Muscle and sports cars struggle in mud, while sport bikes are barely manageable on dirt.Customization is basically Midnight Club: LA all over again. You can turn ordinary SUVs into ATVs, build lowriders, DONKs and crazy street racing cars. The possibilities are insane.Planes and helicopters are mostly based on GTA 5, with some realism improvements. Jets are more interesting, though: dogfights feel better, and military jets can actually hunt you down. You can also operate trains, excavators, bulldozers, yachts, kayaks and scooters. Excavators are fully functional — you can literally pick up cars with them, lol. You can even derail trains using heavy **** can rob pretty much everything, from barber shops to jewelry stores. Robbing places with a partner is especially fun. They can control hostages, wait in a getaway vehicle or come to your rescue if you can’t escape the police. Robberies are profitable and genuinely satisfying. There’s a real dopamine rush when everything goes smoothly and you successfully get away.Police AI is surprisingly good. They keep track of how many people are involved, what you’re wearing, your vehicle and even your weapons. Escaping two stars is generally manageable, but anything above that becomes a nightmare. Four or five stars require serious effort, while at six stars you’re pretty much screwed. You actually have to plan your escape.There are around 60 firearms available. Differences between weapon classes are noticeable, although individual weapons within the same class don’t always feel distinct. SMGs have less impact than assault rifles, for example, but there’s barely any difference between an M4 and an FAL.Gunplay is really good. Recoil feels satisfying, hits have noticeable impact, and enemies react depending on where you shoot them. Shots to the throat result in slow, brutal deaths, while shooting someone’s knees leaves them crawling on the ground. Enemies can also become incapacitated from shock. You can blow off heads and limbs, and even running over NPCs can completely smash their bodies. The dismemberment system is brutal.Shooting and reloading animations are great for a third-person game, roughly on the level of RDR2.Enemy AI outside scripted encounters is surprisingly competent. They use cover, flank you, suppress your position and try to disarm you at close range. They don’t just stand around waiting to be shot, making firefights much more engaging.Overall, what makes GTA 6 special isn’t just its graphics or the amount of content. It’s how everything comes together. You can spend hours without touching the main story and still have a great time. There’s always something to explore, discover or try. I genuinely haven’t experienced anything quite like it in another game.

author: JustGoToSleep
quote:
To the reviewers who complain about everything

A lot of you are giving this game low scores without buying it or doing any research. Fine. I haven't bought or played it either, so I can hand out a perfect score out of pure ignorance too. Same logic, right?

Get real. The game came out less than a week ago, and plenty of other games shipped locked at 30 FPS on their launch consoles. News reports and reviews have made it clear that the cap isn't about lazy graphics optimization. It comes from CPU bottlenecks caused by the advanced NPC interactions players have waited 13 years for. That will be resolved with a PC version or a next-gen console release. That's how it works.

And to those of you who bought it, played it, and then review-bombed it over minor issues: Rockstar announced the 30 FPS lock on all consoles before launch. You knew what you were getting. If you couldn't wait for the PC version and bought it anyway, then accept the trade-off instead of punishing the game for it.

This is yet another reminder of how unreliable user reviews are when people score purely on their own preferences. Stop the nonsense and go live your real lives, friends.

author: snypchase
quote:
I would give it a 10, as the game is spectacular—a true milestone in gaming history.

However, I want to address the low scores people have been giving it—a phenomenon known as "review bombing."

- Most of the criticism centers on the game’s alleged "woke".

- Another point of contention is that the game was nominated for Game of the Year (GOTY) before it was even released.

- Furthermore, fans of other games—either those that didn't make the GOTY list or direct competitors—are trying to drag down this game's score.

Here is my take…These are three baseless criticisms. 

The first doesn't even warrant a response, and regarding the GOTY nomination, that’s not the game’s fault—it’s an issue with The Game Awards needing to properly adjust their criteria.

The Game Awards allows games released commercially by November 20th of each year to be eligible, yet they announce the nominees a few days prior to that date.

Ultimately, a large portion of this crowd is just a bunch of frustrated kids who love to lash out on "Twitter."

author: PiotrDaniello
quote: GTA 6 is genuinely one of the most impressive open-world games I’ve played. From the moment you start playing, you can see just how much effort Rockstar has put into creating a world that feels alive. The graphics are absolutely stunning, the attention to detail is incredible, and the overall atmosphere makes the game feel like something completely different from previous GTA **** thing I particularly appreciate is the direction Rockstar has taken with this game. Rather than simply making another GTA 5, they’ve created something that feels fresh, modern, and much more immersive. The world feels incredibly realistic, from the physics and character animations to the NPC interactions and the sheer number of activities available. Sometimes I find myself just enjoying everyday activities instead of rushing through the main **** course, the game isn’t perfect. Certain activities and gameplay elements can become slightly repetitive after a while, although this isn’t a massive issue considering how much content there is to explore. Another criticism I have is that certain things feel unnecessarily censored or restricted, almost as if Rockstar has become a little too cautious about political and social sensitivities. For a franchise historically known for pushing boundaries and controversial humour, this can occasionally feel disappointing.However, these criticisms don’t take away from what is otherwise an incredible experience. The gameplay is enjoyable, the world is beautiful, and there’s always something interesting to discover. I genuinely appreciate Rockstar taking risks and moving the franchise in a new direction rather than relying entirely on nostalgia.Overall, GTA 6 is a fantastic game that feels like a major evolution of the series. It isn’t flawless, but it’s incredibly entertaining, immersive, and absolutely worth experiencing. I would highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys open-world games.

For example, GTA 4 had great humour, but the game itself felt way too depressing for me and I did not have that much fun playing it. GTA san andreas’ story felt more bittersweet & emotional for me in comparasion. 

Other lame comments include the “wokeness” of the game - please just play it before you comment. Definitely aint that.

Overall, a really great experience for me personally, the grounded  story  makes for very thrilling action missions when they happen, definitely went above and beyond my expectations. And before some of y’all think “you defendinh multi billionh dollah corporationuh” - naw, man. I enjoy the game, I waited for it for 13 years, and my expectations were blown away. I am presenting my genuine experience, not defending the company that made this game. Could care less for rockstar.
