author: Doc1975
quote:
When I saw the reviews and top ratings of progressive toilet papers as Ign, Multiplayer, Everyeye, I started out very prejudiced: they are the same ones who had given stellar ratings to Veilguard and then lowered after a few weeks when users had rightly massacred it. Let's start by analyzing GTA6, to understand if it is truly the masterpiece they say (spoiler: no). 
- Graphically it is excellent, at times also photorealistic. 
- Very good also in terms of the soundtrack in which famous artists like Dua Lipa were involved, but it lacks a truly identifying key piece. 
- The performances are mediocre, it lacks fluidity, let's hope for a PC recoding in which mods can be installed, because it really needs them to have an optimal experience. 
- The story: mediocre, It lacks that nastiness and outrage typical of the series. 
- The map: very large, detailed, full of Easter eggs and things to do. 
- Gameplay: the movements are slower and more controlled, RDR2-style, away from the arcades, for me it's a very positive aspect. For the rest we are in front of the usual third-person action, typical of the series, nothing innovative. It's fun to wander around the map and do side missions, Even if at times it feels more like being inside a chapter of The Sims than GTA. There is a total lack of romance or sexual situations, the best you can get are stripteases on 3 levels of spiciness but definitely not memorable. Hookers collectible cards seems like a joke. Very bad. 
- Politicization: while not being unabashedly a woke game (like Veilguard or Spiderman2) there are certainly forced situations that make it clear that a certain type of progressive indoctrination has been inserted in a profound, less visibile way, but those with some gaming experience will notice it immediately (unrentable hookers, unkillable activists, servant unmacho males, unsexy women without curves and much more). 
- Overall then: a good game, very extensive and at times fun. Absolutely not innovative. I put it behind GTA San Andreas and GTA5 in the series rankings. It will certainly win the Goty for marketing reasons but remains light years away from last year's artistic masterpiece Expedition 33.

author: Buju3000
quote:
The Best Game Ever Made. Period. 

Rockstar has absolutely outdone themselves with this release. I genuinely believe this is one of those rare games that will be remembered for generations, and potentially the greatest game ever made

What makes this experience so special is how much it feels like a natural evolution of what Rockstar accomplished with Red Dead Redemption 2, rather than simply another iteration of Grand Theft Auto V. It takes so much of what made RDR2 special, including the immersion, attention to detail, world building, character interactions, atmosphere, and incredible sense of realism, and brings those elements into the GTA universe.

And that's where this game truly shines.

The world feels alive in a way that very few games have ever managed to accomplish. It's not simply a massive map filled with activities and icons to check off. It's a living, breathing environment that feels like it exists independently of the player. The little details, the interactions, the environmental storytelling, and the sheer amount of effort put into making the world feel believable are what separate Rockstar from practically everyone else in the industry.

I also love the direction Rockstar has taken with the overall gameplay and presentation. It feels like they've leaned further into the grounded, immersive approach that made Red Dead Redemption 2 such a remarkable experience. Rather than constantly trying to overwhelm you with action, the game gives you room to exist in its world. That might not appeal to everyone, particularly those who prefer the faster paced arcade experience of GTA V, but for me, it's exactly what I wanted.

There is something incredibly special about the way Rockstar approaches game development. Their worlds have a level of personality, character, and authenticity that is incredibly difficult to replicate. You can practically feel the time, resources, and passion that went into creating this experience.

And that's ultimately what makes this release so impressive. This isn't just another big budget video game. It's a reminder of what happens when a developer has the resources, ambition, and creative freedom to push the medium forward.

I understand that personal preference will always play a role in determining someone's favorite game, and there's nothing wrong with that. But regardless of whether this is your particular cup of tea, it's incredibly difficult to overlook the sheer scale of what Rockstar has accomplished.

They didn't just deliver another Grand Theft Auto experience. They raised the bar.

Rockstar absolutely cooked. An absolute masterpiece.

author: Mohammedbisha
quote:
GTA VI is not just a game; it represents the pinnacle of creativity and technological advancement in the gaming industry. From its graphics and visual details to its lighting, shadows, and weather systems, from its world design and scale to character interactions, NPC behavior, traffic systems, physics, animations, sound design, and storytelling.

Every detail feels meticulously crafted, and every element of the world has a purpose, making you feel as though you are not simply playing in a virtual world, but living in a complete, breathing world.

The greatness of GTA VI isn't just about graphics. It's about bringing all these elements together into one seamless experience that is incredibly difficult for any other game to match.

Other studios may create games with better graphics, better stories, or impressive gameplay mechanics. But bringing all these aspects together at this level of ambition and cohesion? That's where the real magic lies.

GTA VI isn't a game that can be replicated simply by having a massive budget. It requires vision, experience, ambition, and an extraordinary amount of time. In short: You can create a great game, but creating a game like GTA VI? That's something else entirely.

author: Gl1tchNs
quote:
This is a huge step up from GTA V. You get to rob way more stuff than even RDR2 and the payment from casualy selling drugs, market bills, jewelry and cars is a big change for the better. Stealing cars feels way better for the long run in this game than GTA V, where it felt very stale and not so special. In a car theft game it's very important you make it compelling to also steal cars which GTA VI has done very well. 

Things I thought GTA V lacked was some roleplay features, as I have several thousand hours on it it gets a bit too easy just going around with no consequence but GTA VI has added many thinks I actually felt I wanted in GTA V like fuel, more interiors, and more complex and less all knowing cops. And the NPC interactions are very unique and engaging. Very many funny voice lines and out of pocket things that can happen. 

Graphics is just phenomenal and the density is turned way up than from GTA V and RDR2. The physics are incredible for the hair, clothes, water, mud and so much more. When 30 FPS is not ideal I don't mind it at all, you get used to it pretty fast.

The car customization feels very good and has way more details than many car racing focused games. This was a big thing I was hoping they would make good and I'm very pleased to see they went really hard making it. 

Jason: To me he feels very secretive and shut off. I would like to know more of his backstory which I will know in due time I hope. 
Lucia: Very outgoing and a bit of a boss. Sometimes she can be annoying it doesn't ruin the moment. I like how she completely changes her voice when speaking to Jason and their dynamic is very good. 

Won't say much about the story. It's a slow pace start to lean you into the different mechanics but later ramps up at the end of Chapter 1 to begin the arc.

I can already imagine the potential the freeroam online will give. But that's at the moment uncertain until Rockstar says anything about online.

There's so much effort put into this game it can become overwhelming seeing it all. They have made tv shows, ads, podcasts (with easter eggs and more lore) and more activities than GTA V already had.

To sum it up it really is a GTA V and RDR2 merged with even better customization, dialoges, graphics, physics, mechanics, activities and exploration. 
I have only seen a few bugs myself and none of them were game breaking at all. This is in my eyes the closest game that has ever been released to be the perfect game.

author: jpsDarko
quote: GTA VI – My Honest Review So Far  10/10 (NO SPOILERS)I’ve seen GTA VI getting absolutely review bombed online, and as someone who’s been passionate about Grand Theft Auto for as long as I can remember, I feel like I need to defend it a little.Especially considering the franchise was born in my hometown of Dundee, Scotland. There’s always been a sense of pride knowing that one of the biggest gaming franchises in history started right here.First off, I was genuinely disappointed when Rockstar announced there wouldn’t be a physical release at launch. As someone who loves collecting physical games, that was a massive letdown. I actually left it until the very last minute to decide whether I was even going to buy it digitally.Well, I’m bloody glad I did! I’m still holding out hope that Rockstar eventually gives us a physical edition, preferably a nice collector’s edition that deserves a place on the shelf.Anyway, onto the actual game…I’ll admit, the first chapter is a slow burner. It feels more like an extended tutorial than anything else, and I can understand why some people might find the opening a little **** chapter 2 onwards? Absolutely **** world Rockstar has created is genuinely breathtaking. The attention to detail, the environments, the atmosphere, the characters… it’s honestly incredible. There have been moments where I’ve just stopped playing to take everything **** then there’s the whole “woke” argument floating around online…I’m genuinely struggling to understand what exactly makes this game woke? Is having a female protagonist who can fight, shoot a gun and hold her own considered woke nowadays?If that’s the case, then call me woke! Remember Lara Croft? Tomb Raider? Yeah, woke AF, apparently. Seriously though, I feel like some people decided they were going to hate this game long before they even played it. There’s absolutely nothing wrong with constructive criticism, and no game should be immune to it, but some of the outrage surrounding GTA VI is just **** me personally, it’s a solid 10/10. And here’s the thing… I’m not even 50% through the game yet!Could my opinion change by the time the credits roll? Absolutely. But based on everything I’ve experienced so far, Rockstar has delivered something truly **** don’t have to love every game, and everyone’s entitled to their own opinion. But at least give it a fair chance before jumping on the hate bandwagon.Dundee gave the world Grand Theft Auto, and I’m still bloody proud of that.

author: Unknownbr
quote: Se eu pudesse voltar ao passado, quando tinha 23 anos no lançamento do GTA 5 que acabava de ser lançado, e tivesse a oportunidade de jogar aquele jogo sabendo que seu sucessor, GTA 6, poderia ser ainda mais formidável, minha resposta seria: NÃO! Naquele momento, eu estava completamente atônito com o que estava vendo e vivendo. Para mim, aquele era o auge dos videogames, e nenhum outro jogo poderia entregar algo superior. Mas esperar 13 anos depois do lançamento daquela obra-prima é algo difícil até de explicar. Eu não sei descrever o que esse jogo provoca emocionalmente na gente. Dar o play, perceber que aquele grande dia finalmente chegou e saber que pude compartilhar e participar de todo o hype criado em torno desse lançamento é surreal. Valeu cada ano de espera e cada centavo gasto para poder viver esse momento. O que a Rockstar conseguiu fazer foi criar um dos mundos abertos mais incríveis, fascinantes e empolgantes que já tive o prazer de explorar em um jogo. Cada região de Leonida foi cuidadosamente construída à mão e está repleta de lugares memoráveis, segredos e Easter Eggs para serem descobertos. E olha... um mais louco que o outro. Seja na região dos Keys, onde pude mergulhar em busca de tesouros, passar um tempo bebendo no Rusty Anchor com meus amigos e simplesmente aproveitar o ambiente; nos Grassrivers, onde saía à caça de negócios clandestinos envolvendo drogas em regiões isoladas e pantanosas; ou no centro de Vice City, onde podia ir a uma boate e, de repente, mudar completamente de ideia para sair e assaltar uma boutique. Existe uma quantidade impressionante de acontecimentos e atividades ocorrendo naturalmente a cada dia ou noite. É impressionante como tudo parece orgânico e natural. A população, o ambiente, a densidade dos cenários e o nível de capricho nos detalhes fazem toda a diferença. E, principalmente à noite, quando tudo está iluminado, com letreiros em LED, luzes e reflexos por toda parte, a sensação é de estar dentro de um verdadeiro seriado de televisão. A história do casal rapidamente deixa para trás a rotina comum e se transforma em uma narrativa de sobrevivência no melhor estilo Bonnie e Clyde. Os personagens também acabam se tornando dois dos protagonistas mais memoráveis da franquia. Na minha visão, Lucia é a grande estrela do jogo, mas isso não diminui em nada a importância de Jason. A dinâmica entre os dois é um dos pontos que tornam essa experiência tão especial. Agora fica claro por que a Rockstar Games não quis entregar apenas MAIS UM JOGO qualquer. Enquanto tantas outras empresas parecem se preocupar em lançar jogos cada vez mais caros, mas que muitas vezes não entregam nem um 1/3 que GTA 6 proporciona, a Rockstar demonstra o que acontece quando existe um nível absurdo de dedicação, ambição e atenção aos detalhes. E tenho certeza de que este será mais um daqueles jogos que continuarão sendo assunto daqui a 10 anos, assim como acontece com Red Dead Redemption 2. Ainda estaremos descobrindo segredos, encontrando novas possibilidades, explorando detalhes que passaram despercebidos e falando sobre coisas que nem imaginávamos ser possíveis.

author: Cheesecake278
quote:
The amount of lies and misinformation around this game is baffling. Discourse around anything is now all rage bait and pettiness so people have the right to a “moral” high ground. As they go back to their miserable lives. 

You can indeed steal cars and commit crimes in Grand Theft Auto 6, and no it’s not anymore “woke” than any other Rockstar game. I also find it incredibly weird how people are calling Jason a “cuck”? Not only is that not true it also makes no sense, i know 90% of gamers don’t have a significant other and dont understand how relationships works but what Jason does for Lucia doesn’t even qualify as “cuck” or “simp” behavior. (have people just forgotten what those words mean?) The criticism of it being a “chore” game also falls apart if you play the game for more than a hour, most of the “chores” are optional and do play a major factor in the story or gameplay. It shows that people are struggling to get past chapter one, because attention spans are at an all time low. As soon as you enter chapter 2&3 the game picks up and becomes more akin to the other GTAs you know. The amount of content (major and side) is just outstanding. The world also feels alive and immersive, I actually stopped what I was doing to hear the dumb and funny conversations NPCs have. While graphics aren’t everything for me, I would be lying if Rockstar didn’t surprise me with just how detailed everything looks. Driving is also a huge upgrade from V, each car type now has a different unique feel, alongside being more interactive. I could go on and on about how this game has been able to reel in for hours without getting bored, and I might edit this review once I completely finish the game and get 100% completion. (Around 47% at the moment) 

I am however not naïve enough to understand that this game is not perfect and can be a lot better. It’s not the second coming of Christ as some people think it is, but it’s no where near as close as bad as the launch of cyberpunk (seriously people, stop trying to rewrite history).
Overall I would recommend this game.

author: TheTurkTM
quote: After years of anticipation, GTA VI is finally here. And there is no denying that Rockstar has delivered something extraordinary in several aspects. However, after spending time with the game, I find myself having two very different opinions about **** one hand, this is arguably the most impressive open-world gaming experience ever created. On the other, I genuinely believe Rockstar has lost some of the identity that made Grand Theft Auto what it **** me break it down into three main areas.1. Gameplay Mechanics & Graphics – 10/10I genuinely don’t think I’ve ever experienced a game that feels this **** graphics are phenomenal, but what makes GTA VI particularly impressive is how the visual quality translates into the actual gameplay experience. Driving, movement, character animations, environmental details, lighting and physics all contribute to an unprecedented level of **** isn’t simply about looking at a beautiful environment. It’s about feeling like you’re actually existing within **** attention to detail is ridiculous. From the smallest environmental interactions to the way vehicles behave, Rockstar has raised the bar considerably.There are moments when you genuinely forget you’re playing a video game.This isn’t just a graphical upgrade over GTA V. It’s a substantial evolution of the entire gameplay experience.2. Open World, NPCs & Interactions – 10/10This is where GTA VI truly separates itself from practically every other open-world **** world feels alive in a way I’ve never experienced before. NPCs aren’t simply background characters walking around waiting for you to interact with them. They have their own behaviours, routines and **** level of detail in how the world responds to your actions is **** of my favourite examples is the wanted system. Getting away from the police is no longer just about driving around a corner, hiding in an alley and waiting for your wanted level to disappear.Your exposure matters.Depending on what you’ve done and how much attention you’ve attracted, you may need to change your vehicle, outfit or even hairstyle to avoid being recognised. The world remembers what you’ve done, and you have to adapt **** interactions are another massive achievement. Characters can recognise you, react to previous encounters and make the world feel considerably more personal. Even the animals and their interactions with the environment deserve recognition.These might sound like relatively small details, but collectively they completely change how you experience an open-world game.Rockstar has managed to create an environment where simply walking around, observing people and interacting with the world can be as entertaining as completing missions.This is what an open-world game should aspire to be.3. The Storyline & GTA’s Identity – 5/10Unfortunately, this is where GTA VI loses **** me, the storyline is genuinely disappointing. And it’s not because I expected another GTA V or Red Dead Redemption 2. It’s because I expected Grand Theft Auto to retain the identity that made the franchise so **** has always been provocative. It has been crude, politically incorrect, offensive, racist, homophobic, vulgar and unapologetically raw.That was part of its **** was a franchise that pushed boundaries, made fun of practically everyone and everything, challenged social conventions and allowed players to experience a fictional world without constantly feeling like someone was trying to teach them a **** wasn’t supposed to be politically correct. It was supposed to be Grand Theft **** biggest disappointment is the feeling that modern political and cultural sensitivities have found their way into the creative direction of the **** problem isn’t diversity or the inclusion of different characters. GTA has always had a colourful and diverse collection of characters. The problem, in my opinion, is when social messaging starts taking priority over entertaining storytelling.I want satire. I want uncomfortable humour. I want ridiculous characters, controversial dialogue, outrageous situations and the kind of humour that makes you question whether Rockstar actually had the courage to put something in the game.Instead, I find the narrative considerably less enjoyable than I expected. The story feels like it has lost some of that rebellious spirit that made previous instalments so **** that’s a shame, because Rockstar has clearly demonstrated that it has the technical ability to create something extraordinary. I just wish the same ambition had been applied to the writing.Final VerdictGTA VI is an incredible technical achievement. The gameplay mechanics, graphics, world-building and NPC interactions are arguably setting a new industry standard.However, a technically impressive game doesn’t automatically make it a perfect Grand Theft Auto experience.

author: Jinx9262
quote: After waiting 13 years, it felt almost impossible for GTA 6 to live up to the hype. Somehow, Rockstar pulled it off. Two hours into exploring Leonida, you realize this isn't just another good sequel. It is easily the best video game ever made.Returning to Vice City and the surrounding swamps is unreal. Most open worlds feel like a pretty backdrop, but Leonida feels genuinely alive. NPCs have real routines, react to sudden rainstorms, and pull out their phones to livestream whatever chaos you cause. Half the time, I completely forgot about my main mission because stumbling into weird roadside events or late-night street races was just too **** story is also Rockstar's best yet. Instead of the loud, over-the-top Hollywood vibe of GTA 5, Jason and Lucia feel grounded and real. Their Bonnie and Clyde relationship actually shifts based on how you play and handle jobs together, which makes you genuinely care when things go wrong during a heist.Gameplay finally matches the world, too. Cops actually track your license plate and clothes now instead of magically knowing where you are, so ditching a car in an alley and changing outfits actually works. The gunplay feels heavy, robberies give you real freedom to improvise, and classic features like gyms and deep car customization are back.Visually, the lighting, weather, and facial animations make everything else in my gaming library look a generation behind. Even at 30fps on console, it runs super smooth considering how much is happening on screen at once.Rockstar took everything they learned over the last decade and made a masterpiece. Nothing else even comes close.

author: Aki_17
quote: # GTA VI — The Greatest Game I've Ever Played. Period.**10/10. An absolute masterpiece.**I'm only in Chapter 2, and I can already say without a shadow of a doubt that this is the greatest video game I've ever played. Chapter 1 alone convinced **** world, NPCs, mechanics, vehicles, interactions and sheer attention to detail are unlike anything I've experienced. Just when I wondered whether the missions could match GTA V, the end of Chapter 1 delivered one of the greatest missions in GTA history.What genuinely baffles me is the criticism surrounding realism and supposedly unnecessary **** over 20 years, we've been stealing cars, shooting hundreds of enemies, escaping police, fighting armies and causing mayhem. We've loved it. But haven't we also spent those years asking for more? More accessible buildings, meaningful NPC interactions, activities and ways to experience the world?**Rockstar has finally delivered exactly that.**RDR2 showed us how alive a virtual world could feel. GTA VI takes that philosophy to another level. I've played for over 10 hours and barely explored a tiny corner of the map!And yes, there are restrictions. You can't carry a hundred weapons anymore. Stealing vehicles requires more effort. The wanted system encourages caution, stealth and planning.**I LOVE THAT.**It makes your decisions meaningful. You're no longer just walking into places, shooting everything and escaping without a thought. That's evolution, not necessarily a **** my single favourite improvement?**MONEY FINALLY MATTERS.**Previous GTA games often left you swimming in cash with little reason to earn or spend it. Here, robbing stores, boosting vehicles and exploring different opportunities make earning money feel genuinely rewarding. There's so much more purpose to everyday activities.Even the smallest details amaze me. Vehicle indicators, hazard lights, NPC behaviour, environmental interactions — everything contributes to a world that feels astonishingly **** it perfect? Technically, no. I've experienced bugs myself, including a six-pack of beer getting stuck to Lucia's hand across three missions and a persistent button prompt that required restarting the game. I'm also not thrilled about 30 **** these are issues that can be improved through patches. **When I'm actually playing, the experience is so extraordinary that I barely care.**And regarding some of the backlash, there's a difference between legitimate gameplay criticism and the racist, misogynistic insults directed at Lucia. The latter says far more about the people making those comments than the game itself.Everyone is entitled to their preferences. But sometimes it feels like negativity gets more attention than appreciation.I cannot imagine the countless hours of dedication, creativity and engineering required to build something like this. Every developer who contributed deserves enormous **** those of us who play games to escape reality and immerse ourselves in another world, GTA VI is something truly special.**It feels like RDR2 reimagined in the modern world with years of technological progress behind it.**Whether its story can surpass RDR2 remains to be seen. That's an incredibly high bar. But in terms of world-building, immersion and interactivity, I genuinely believe GTA VI has established a new benchmark.I'm not writing this as a professional reviewer. I'm simply a lifelong gamer expressing my appreciation for an extraordinary achievement.**Rockstar, thank you. This was worth every single day of the wait.****GTA VI isn't just another game. It's the kind of virtual world I've spent my entire gaming life dreaming about.****10/10. The greatest game I've ever played. What makes this especially remarkable is that Rockstar hasn't simply created a bigger playground for destruction. They've created a world where ordinary activities can be as fascinating as the spectacular ones. I can spend hours exploring, interacting with people, discovering buildings, earning money and experimenting with mechanics without even touching the main **** that's exactly what many of us have wanted from GTA for decades.I don't want every interaction to revolve around shooting someone or escaping a five-star wanted level. I want to feel like I'm actually living in this world, with its own opportunities, consequences and surprises.That's also why I appreciate the more grounded approach to crime. Having to think about my actions makes the experience more engaging, not less.I understand that some players prefer the old formula, but personally, this is the evolution I've been waiting for.

author: Nosferya
quote:
After around 25 hours, GTA VI has been an outstanding experience for me, and above all, a remarkable achievement by Rockstar.

What impresses me most is the staggering attention to detail, the consistency of the world, and how organic and believable everything feels. Exploration and curiosity are constantly rewarded. Simply rushing from one main objective to another would mean missing out on much of what makes this game so special.

I understand why its slower pace might disappoint players who prefer the more arcade-like nature of previous GTA games, where stealing cars, starting shootouts and causing chaos was much more immediate. Here, almost everything requires a little more thought and patience. Stealing vehicles takes longer, driving is more demanding, and the mechanics encourage you to slow down and pay attention to your surroundings.

But that's exactly what I love about it. To me, GTA VI strikes an excellent balance between the identity of Grand Theft Auto and the immersive philosophy of Red Dead Redemption 2. Rather than simply delivering GTA V with modern graphics, Rockstar has chosen to evolve its formula.

That doesn't mean everything is perfect. I'm not particularly convinced by the criminal morality system, which can feel frustrating when you're penalized for actions that are difficult to avoid. I'm also not entirely sold on Jason and Lucia as characters just yet. This is where the comparison with Red Dead Redemption 2 falls short for me: after 25 hours, neither protagonist has come close to the emotional depth or impact of Arthur Morgan. Of course, I'm still relatively early in the story, so my opinion on that may change.

On a technical level, my experience on the base PS5 has been excellent. I've encountered very few issues, the 30 FPS target doesn't particularly bother me, and I never feel like I'm playing a significantly compromised version of the game. The fact that a world this detailed and ambitious runs so well on the original PS5 is an achievement in itself.

GTA VI might not be the game everyone expected, and I can understand why some players are disappointed by its different approach. But for me, its ambition, variety, atmosphere, and extraordinary attention to detail make it something truly ****'s not just a game that entertains you. It's a world you genuinely want to spend time living in.

author: Spectre92ITA
quote:
Let me preface this with: if you're expecting GTA V-2, you'll be disappointed. If, on the flip side, you're expecting the natural evolution of all the work done in RDR2, coupled with a surprisingly (for the series) mature story, you will be in for a genuine once in a lifetime experience.

Graphics:
Even on a base PS5, there is wizardry at work. Beautiful ray traced reflections and light create absolutely stunning vistas just about anywhere you decide to look at, from whatever point of view. Flying a plane around, driving your boat along the coast, speeding through the (exceptionally narrow) streets of Vice City (BABYYYYYYYYYY)... It looks incredibly real, except for the people who have a slightly stylized look to them and their proportions at times which helps soothe the uncanny valley effect, and incredibly detailed. This clearly comes at a cost: the framerate DOES drop. Out of more hours than I feel comfortable admitting at my age, played basically nonstop, with the PS5 not complaining or making noise once mind you, I've had quite a few cases where I "jumped" a frame, a real split second thing, and only one where the FPS clearly dropped to around 24 for a solid 5 seconds, during some ridiculous mayhem I had caused with the police.

Sound:
The music speaks for itself. No seriously, between all the songs and radio stations, and the way songs are used during certain moments and set pieces... Holy ****.
And in general, the sound department is solid as it gets: engines purring beautifully, every step you take on any kind of material, a door opening just a wee bit too quickly or creaking just right telling you (or your enemy) that someone is nearby... No notes and no complaints here.

Story:
This 100% will be the one of two main points of complaints from all the people who have played the intro and nothing else so yes, full disclosure, the intro (which is basically the very first chapter of the game and lasts a good few hours even if you only focus on main missions and main missions only) is VERY slow compared to previous GTAs. It's not RDR2 chapter 1 levels of slow, and not even remotely as restrictive either, but it IS slower than most had expected.
Taken that away, from the end of chapter 1 itself, more and more and crazier and crazier missions and characters will show up and I will not spoil anything here but some of these sequences I've witnessed have instantly placed themselves in my personal pantheon of best gaming and narrative moments for me.
It is also not exactly unpredictable, some things are very much phoned in, but are made to work and be enjoyable anyway. 
It is a completely different story from what we're used in GTA, and closer in tune and tone to something I would've expected in a RDR3. This game really is Grand Theft Redemption VI in many ways.

Gameplay:
The other "problem" many people have. There are a lot of gameplay elements, that are COMPLETELY OPTIONAL TO ENGAGE WITH, that involve nurturing your relationship between the two. If that is something you want to see blossom, you will have to put some effort in (really not much at all mind you, just hang out and drive around together, do robberies, races, anything you do together can count, along with just interacting with each other at home and in other places)

Other that that, it plays like a slightly snappier RDR2, with similar limitations in loadout and how to handle it.

Cops are **** scary and the wanted level is handled differently from previous entries and is much more in depth, and the cops are no longer a joke: far from it. You generally really DO want to get the **** out and leave as little traces as possible and disappear before a cop sees you.
The game also offers a plethora of side activities and way more random encounters than you would ever imagine, and from what I can tell they also all lead to something cool or reward you directly.
I saw a swat team break into a motel room and come out with two bags they split between two cars, I managed to wait and grab both of the bags before they drove off and escaped the inevitable shootout and chase after to find a cool 20K worth of loot in the bags, I saved a drunk girl who was being arrested for a DUI and there was a whole ass specific dialogue because I did it by waiting for her to be sat in the car by the cops and then stealing the cop car and driving away... CRAZY level of interaction and detail. And I've helped someone lift a sofa and got tazed in the neck once done... And boy do I wish that were the end of this specific encounter... Insanity.

I wish I could write more but I'm out of characters for a game that would require an essay instead of a review.

It's bonkers, it's really unlike anything in the market currently, or I feel that will ever be in the market again. It really has earned that 99 score honestly. My expectations for VI were pretty low, and I have been completely blown away to the point of genuine shock at what I was witnessing over, and over, and over. Absurd.

author: Adrigl12

I was expecting a great game, perhaps even one of the BEST games of all time. And somehow, despite those incredibly high expectations, Grand Theft Auto VI has managed to surpass them. I have absolutely no doubt that I'm playing the greatest game ever made.

There's always something going on, unexpected encounters, little details and countless moments that make the world feel like a real place rather than just a playground for the player.

The soundtrack is another masterpiece. The variety of music, the different genres and the way it complements the atmosphere make simply driving around or exploring the world an experience in itself. Rockstar has always understood how important music is to its worlds, and they've absolutely nailed it once again.

I haven't finished the story yet, but so far, it genuinely feels like it could reach the same heights as Red Dead Redemption 2. And that's saying something.

Grand Theft Auto VI is more than just a video game. It's a masterpiece, a genuine work of art. Every little detail, every interaction and every aspect of this world shows what happens when Rockstar puts its heart, talent and almost absurd attention to detail into something.

Rockstar doesn't just make games. They create magic.

author: Banane60
quote: Ca y est on a notre jeu ultime !Le sixième épisode de la saga Grand Theft Auto a mis la barre très très très haute ! Bon courage aux autres boites de JV !Un monde ouvert vivant, le plus crédible jamais conçuLeonida, version fictive de la Floride, est un terrain de jeu fascinant. Rues de Vice City baignées de néons, marais, plages, petites villes et campagne : chaque zone a son identité, son ambiance et ses habitants. Le monde ne se contente pas d’exister autour du joueur, il continue de vivre sans lui. Les passants réagissent, les quartiers changent selon l’heure, la météo et le contexte. On se perd volontairement, juste pour regarder.Graphiquement, GTA 6 est une claque. Les éclairages, les reflets sur l’asphalte mouillé, les foules denses, les animations faciales et les effets de chaleur donnent un réalisme saisissant. Le moteur gère des scènes d’une densité folle sans jamais casser l’immersion. Chaque coucher de soleil sur Vice City mérite une capture d’écran.Lucia et Jason forment un tandem criminel d’une rare force d’écriture. Leur relation, tendue et sincère, donne à l’histoire une vraie charge émotionnelle. Rockstar excelle dans l’art de rendre attachants des personnages pourtant moralement discutables. On s’investit, on doute, on rit, et on se laisse surprendre jusqu’au **** sens de l’humour de la série est intact. Radios, publicités, émissions de télé, réseaux sociaux : la satire de la société américaine est féroce, drôle et pertinente. Chaque conversation entendue au hasard d’une rue peut devenir un moment culte. La direction artistique, nourrie de cinéma et de culture pop, est d’une finesse remarquable.Braquages minutieux, courses poursuites, activités secondaires, missions inattendues : GTA 6 laisse le joueur composer son propre rythme. Les possibilités se croisent et les systèmes se répondent, si bien qu’aucune partie ne ressemble à une autre. Même les moments de pause, comme une balade en voiture avec la radio à fond, sont un plaisir en soi.Fidèle à la tradition de la série, la sélection musicale est exceptionnelle. Elle couvre les genres et les époques, et accompagne parfaitement chaque situation. Certains morceaux resteront associés à vos meilleurs souvenirs de jeu pour longtemps.C'est 20/20 ! Ceux qui mettent moins de 19 sont juste des rageux PC et Nintendo, cherchez pas !

author: enderson
quote:
This isn’t a game; it’s real life. The level of detail is unbelievable. You can play basketball in your backyard, renovate your house, and have pets. Even the simplest actions, like drinking water, drinking beer, or eating an apple, have incredible animations and attention to detail.
Different TV channels have their own content, and the radio has always been amazing, but this time there’s even more variety. The day-and-night atmosphere, vehicle lighting, and all the little details in the environment are genuinely impressive.
Some people might say these things don’t matter to them, but what I’m trying to convey is just how meticulously crafted and detailed this game is. The missions are smooth, and so far, I haven’t had a single boring moment.
Of course, like any game, bugs will probably start showing up over the coming days. But based on my first 3–4 hours, I can honestly say this is a game you can spend hours playing without ever getting bored.

author: AJW83
quote:
The depth and detail of this world is mind blowing. I feel the series has evolved past previous iterations and is now more akin to Red Dead style of gameplay but in a GTA skin and I'm all for it. 

Offering a slower pace to previous GTAs really works and allows you to be absorbed into the world they have created without mindlessly going on constant rampages. This of course is still an option, but this time around I find myself being more careful with driving and generally existing in the world. 

The graphics are also mind blowing, probably the only time on the PS5 where I've genuinely been taken aback with the leap in how a game looks. The world feels so alive and natural and you can get lost for hours just exploring. The random events you see whilst existing in the world are also so perfectly written and executed that it only adds to the feeling you are in a living, breathing city.

I've seen some negatives around slower parts, such as fixing up Jason's house and I understand why this sort of thing isn't for everyone but again, for me at least it only adds to embedding you within the world they have created. You can of course choose not to do any of this if you wish.

Overall, it would seem some of the negative reviews are down to the dopemine additicted world we exist in, and if there isn't constant action people take that as a bad thing, but that's not what this game is about. Take your time, explore, exist, take it all in as I don't think we will see a game quite as intricate, organic, well paced and visually impressive as this again for a very long time.

Hats off to R*, they have taken what GTA was and matured it, improved it and made one of the greatest experiences you can have playing a video game of all time.

I can't put the controller down because I'm too busy exploring this **** you want flying motorcycles and spaceships, play Saints Row. author: currylook
quote: I never normally speak out about games. I don't write reviews—I simply don't have the time for it. However, seeing what is happening with GTA 6 on Metacritic right now, with the user score sitting around 5.5 out of 10, made it impossible for me to stay quiet. I had to write this to set the record straight, because it is honestly absurd how people are talking about this masterpiece—a game that single-handedly brought back my joy for gaming after years of market stagnation and recycled **** 6 is easily the best game you are going to play for the next 10 years. The sheer scale of the world is unbelievable. The NPC behavior, the way they dynamically react to you, and the sheer volume of random events happening across the map are on another level.There is a lot of talk claiming that the opening hours are boring. That is completely untrue. Yes, the pacing at the very beginning is a bit slower, but that gives you the breathing room to actually explore the world, get familiar with it, live in it, and get immersed. I completely disagree with the "boring" narrative. Furthermore, all those slice-of-life activities involving Lucia aren't mandatory to progress. If you don't feel like doing them—if you don't want to do the infamous "house-fixing" chore that everyone keeps bringing up—then just don't do it. Nobody is forcing you. Just skip past that part of the story and move on.I am currently 20 hours into the game and I literally cannot put the controller down. The number of mechanics and the complexity of the world are overwhelming in the best way possible—it's incredible. I can't stop exploring. The world is gorgeous, richly detailed, filled with genuinely interesting side characters, and, of course, features an amazing soundtrack.

quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI: A Visual Masterpiece That Prioritizes Storytelling​

On PlayStation 5, the game is a technical marvel. While it runs at 30 frames per second, it showcases brilliant optimization: in motion, there are no noticeable frame drops or stuttering, delivering a completely smooth experience and impeccable image quality even during the most graphically demanding moments.​

The story hooks you from the very first minute. Although the opening slows the pace down a bit, it serves as the perfect adjustment period to get familiar with the mechanics before the plot unleashes its full force and begins to shine with a powerful narrative—packed with those hilarious moments that are a signature hallmark of the franchise.​

Beyond the main campaign, the world feels alive and brimming with possibilities. You’ll stumble across a massive amount of side activities, organic mini-stories, and sudden encounters that pull you off the beaten path, guaranteeing dozens upon dozens of hours of gameplay.

​It is a well-rounded installment that balances an impeccable technical showcase with a memorable story and an endless open world.

author: Ramah17
quote:
After years of anticipation, Rockstar has finally dropped us into the streets of Leonida and Vice City. Rather than just offering a massive map, the game raises the bar for detail and realism in open-world gaming to a whole new level. Here are the standout pros and cons—spoiler-free:
 Pros (Strengths):
A Living World Packed with Detail: Leonida feels genuinely alive. NPC reactions, spontaneous street encounters, and attention to the smallest touches—from vehicle paint and weather effects to environmental storytelling—make the setting feel remarkably real.
The Jason & Lucia Dynamic: Mature dramatic writing and a shifting relationship shaped by your playstyle and choices, backed by top-tier voice acting and performances that make the leads easy to invest in.
Smarter Gameplay & Police AI: The wanted system feels more tactical, with law enforcement reading context like outfits and vehicles rather than just a simple radius chase. Driving physics, heist prep, and in-game phone/social features add plenty of variety.
Nostalgia Meets Next-Gen Polish: A fresh modern take on classic Vice City energy, paired with strong DualSense features, crisp sound design, and a standout soundtrack.
 Cons (Weaknesses):
30 FPS Cap at Launch: Being locked to 30 FPS without a 60 FPS performance mode at release is a letdown for players chasing ultra-smooth motion.
Occasional Pacing & Clunky Interactions: Certain stretches of the story drag a bit, and lining up with specific angles to interact with doors or nearby objects can feel slightly rigid.
Limited Enterable Interiors: While there are plenty of shops and spots to visit, the number of open buildings still feels modest compared to the sheer scale of the map.
Edition Perks & No Online Yet: Locking extra outfits or side content behind higher editions, along with GTA Online not being live right at launch, takes a little shine off the rollout.

author: Ali_Nas
quote:
All these weirdos complaining about woke agenda and DEI and review bombing this game just need a reality check. They haven’t even played the game and just sat on discord all day talking about how life used to be better. Get out of your room hit the showers and shave that neckbeard you ****. 

Non spoiler review-
Onto the actual game as a life long fan of rockstar games there’s not particularly anything super new about this game but it just pushes everything to the max. So far there hasn’t been a novel new idea that makes this game gameplay far superior to the old ones it’s just that it takes all the previous concepts and pushes them to the absolute peak possible on modern consoles. Graphics are by far the most outstanding part and this is nothing new they have always pushed this so i don’t understand the 30fps criticism and anyone making it is quite silly. You’ll need a high end rig when the pc version drops if you want to have 60fps and thankfully there’s no pc right now with higher specs than mine and I will be replaying it on there. The only real complaints for me are technical complaints that highlight the Ps5 Pros weakness i.e. pssr tree shimmering. Light is noisy when there is fog or smoke effect and the denoising is not good. Ghosting when driving at high speeds. But again these aren’t exactly areas the game can help in this is a pssr issue and when this comes to PC dlss will not have these issues.

I need to speak about the lighting. Rockstar really outdid themselves here because I did not think this was possible on modern consoles. I thought we’d start seeing RT of this level start to creep in with the PS6 but this is outrageous on ps5 pro. It’s better than some path traced solutions on PC. It’s obviously not perfect at the moment but that’s mostly as I said above really more to do with these consoles not being able to handle RT that well. These seem to be fixable traits that originate from PSSR being a mediocre upscaling model. Average gamer may not pick up on these but if you have a technical eye it may bug you slightly. It did for me when i saw the noise on fog lighting. Rockstar technologically pushed major boundaries here and I honestly think it’s the greatest looking game ever without the PC Port and I don’t say that lightly as someone that put in major hours into cyberpunk path traced. 

Gameplay wise it’s interesting the driving is more reminiscent of GTA IV than V. Cars are destroyed really easily. Traffic density is brilliant. Roads are much tighter than V and more realistic and make you pay more attention as you drive. Enemies feel a little spongy, headshot obviously instakills but body shots sometimes i be putting in like 8 shots before a mf dies.

Non spoiler story review- Absolutely peak. Won’t say more than that. I’d prefer not to spoil anything.

author: jimmymc
quote:
The most impressive open world ever created, now given a story and characters worth caring about, and mission variety that is unmatched.

What is keeping me back from full marks is that the controls are slow to respond so you have to pre-empt the actions you want to take, and the control layout is occasionally unclear. Neither of these issues are new to the 6th entry, but I was hoping to see those things improved. There's also a fair bit of assumed knowledge - like, I don't go to the gym and don't know what counts as a rep with a bar bell. The controller feedback makes me feel like I am doing something wrong if I lower it all the way to my chest, but if I lift it back up an inch or two earlier then it doesn't count as a rep - it would just be handy to have more tutorials available to see what the game wants from me. I totally get that this will be a silly example to people who knows that habit in real life, but it's just an example of where my character would understand something that I don't - it happens with most mini-games available in the game (e.g. I didn't know if the target moved in hot-wiring or if I just had to find a single position and that took trial and error. Shooting a panel to open a security gate didn't tell me which part of the panel to shoot and seemed to take several shots - I still don't know if that was intended or if I was doing something wrong, etc).

The game is more impressive for what it lets you do than how it feels to do it. But it does have so much to do, and it all looks and sounds incredible and while the controls are occasionally unclear or sub-par, they do all work. author: LatinCritic13
quote:
After 13 long years of waiting, Rockstar Games has delivered an absolutely phenomenal experience with Grand Theft Auto VI! This is what happens when ambition, creativity, attention to detail, and an incredible amount of passion come hot together.

From the breathtaking visuals and incredibly immersive world to the characters, romance, storytelling, atmosphere, and sheer amount of detail packed into the environment, everything feels like a massive leap forward for the franchise. Rockstar has once again demonstrated why they are among the most talented developers in the gaming industry.

My only minor nitpick: The driving mechanics felt a little slippery at times, almost as if the vehicles had less traction than expected. However, that's certainly not a dealbreaker! It's something that could take a little getting used to, and it doesn't take away from the overall enjoyment.

At the end of the day, Grand Theft Auto VI represents 13 years of anticipation, evolution, and Rockstar's dedication to pushing gaming forward. This isn't just another GTA installment; it's a monumental moment for the franchise and gaming history.

Jason and Lucia are those characters that felt hot together and I believe it. Lucia is one of the best written female protagonists we've seen in a long time and Rockstar simply had a role that's ready for Manni L. Perez to crush it and she did. Dylan Rourke's Jason reminds me of Arthur Morgan and his voice is iconic. Wasn't expecting that Rupert Humphries to pull off the writing quite well without Dan Houser's involvement and I can confirm that it's amazing. 

Rockstar, you all absolutely nailed it. 13 years in the making, and I couldn't be happier. As a 30 year old man. I'm so glad to be back in Vice City after 20+ years!

author: alexGof

Grand Theft Auto VI es una auténtica demostración de hasta dónde puede llegar la industria de los videojuegos. Rockstar Games ha conseguido crear un mundo extraordinariamente detallado, inmersivo y lleno de vida, donde cada rincón de Leonida transmite personalidad.

Su apartado gráfico es impresionante, pero lo que realmente destaca es la atención al detalle, la naturalidad de sus personajes y la profundidad de su mundo abierto. Jason y Lucia aportan una historia mucho más personal y emocional, acompañada de una narrativa que consigue mantener el interés.

La ambientación de Vice City es simplemente espectacular. La música, los escenarios, el humor característico de la franquicia y la libertad de exploración se combinan para crear una experiencia difícil de igualar.

GTA VI no solamente cumple con las expectativas de años de espera, sino que demuestra que todavía existen formas de sorprender e innovar dentro de los videojuegos.

author: ankur123
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI is an extraordinary achievement in gaming. Rockstar Games has not simply created another open-world game; it has created an astonishingly detailed living world that pushes the boundaries of what modern video games can accomplish.
The graphics are absolutely breathtaking. From the lighting, reflections, weather effects, character animations, vehicle interiors, and environmental details to the sheer density of the world, practically everything feels meticulously crafted. The technological achievement behind this game is phenomenal. The NPCs don't feel like lifeless background characters following repetitive scripts. They make the world feel genuinely inhabited. Their reactions, daily activities, interactions, and unpredictable behaviour make Leonida feel like an actual functioning society.
The police system deserves particular praise. Law enforcement feels considerably more intelligent and responsive. Your actions, approach, criminal behaviour, and efforts to conceal evidence can make a meaningful difference. Planning a crime, avoiding witnesses, changing your appearance, and escaping without attracting attention create an entirely different experience from simply committing crimes and running away from endless police cars.
But the greatest achievement of GTA VI, in my opinion, is its storytelling and social commentary.
The story combines spectacular action with genuine emotional depth. Jason and Lucia's relationship gives the narrative a human dimension that balances the criminal activities, betrayals, violence, ambitions, and relentless pursuit of money. Their relationship, personal decisions, and circumstances make the story feel much more consequential.
What makes the experience particularly fascinating is its multiple ending sequences. There are more than ten possible ending variations, influenced by factors such as your financial situation, relationship, criminal profile, and decisions throughout the gameplay. Your actions genuinely matter.
And this is where Rockstar delivers something remarkably satirical.
The game presents an uncomfortable reflection of real-world society: justice does not necessarily operate equally for everyone.
Having enormous financial resources can make it easier to escape consequences. Knowing how to conceal criminal activities, maintaining a low criminal profile, and having the resources to cover your tracks can allow you to get away with things that would destroy someone else's life.
Meanwhile, someone without sufficient money, influence, or the ability to conceal their crimes can face a completely different fate. You might even attempt to expose a corrupt senator, uncover wrongdoing, or pursue something resembling justice, only to end up imprisoned or suffering a tragic ending because you lack the financial resources and protection necessary to survive the system.
Think about that.
The game essentially asks whether justice is really about right and wrong, or whether it is also about how much money, influence, and protection you possess.
This is an incredibly clever way of exposing the hypocrisy and inequalities embedded in society. The very same criminal behaviour can have radically different consequences depending on the resources available to the person committing it. Rockstar manages to turn the player's financial decisions, criminal choices, and relationships into a larger commentary on class, privilege, corruption, and institutional power.
It is not simply about being a good person or a bad person. It is about navigating a world in which morality, money, power, and survival constantly collide.
The extraordinary graphics and technological advancements might initially attract players, but the living open world, intelligent NPCs, sophisticated police system, emotional storytelling, consequential decisions, and surprisingly sharp social satire are what make this experience so memorable.
GTA VI is not just a game about crime. It is a game about the society that determines who gets punished for it and who gets away with it.
Rockstar Games has delivered something truly exceptional. A breathtaking technical achievement, an emotionally engaging crime drama, and an outstanding satire of wealth, privilege, and justice.
10/10. Absolutely phenomenal.

author: gdub33
quote:
9/10 after chapter 1.  I feel like they paid homage to every genre (paint walls=real estate sim, wash the side of the boat = power washer simulator etc.) in small ways and early in the game that is hurting it for the general fan base.  Non gamers won't get it and they tried to please too many people when most GTA fans want certain things. You need to start off with a bang to keep attention spans these days.

Rockstar also seemed to take a lot of other aspects from popular games (watch dogs, heavy rain, sleeping dogs, the last of us etc) and the mechanics resulted from this are mixed.  I like them, but then again I'm more of an RPG fan.  A lot of the fans of GTA 5 don't want to deal with this stuff.

However there are so many positives and randomness that treats the player to such a unique experience unlike any other; 

There was one side mission that was spectacular..I was to go find some drugs that got lost in the Everglades.  I pulled up on the dirt road heading to the location and heard a weird roar. I thought it was a dinosaur or something so I got out of my car to investigate. I walked up on some crazy hairy thing eating a dear. It ran off and I tried to shoot it. Couldn't get it. So I re-pivoted to the mission and went to try to recover my friends stash but then a plane crashed nearby.  I ran up to the crashed plane, saw the pilot die, and then quickly tried to pick up the drugs scattered around. I heard cars coming so I hid in the brush and took the incoming enemies out one by one. I got in their lifted truck and then the plane exploded and blew the truck sideways into the mud of the landscape.  It was done for. But I was on the side mission to recover the drugs and I was very close as I heard police sirens from cop cars coming from the opposite direction. So I ran over to my objective eluding the police and scouted my enemies.  They were trying to blow up alligators and had a little shack and platform they were on. I used my shotgun to shoot the legs of one of them and he dropped in the water only to get eaten by the alligator he was hunting.  I took them out and then a couple on a fanboat came in as defence and started attacking me. I shot them to hell but also shot the fanboat engine in the meantime.  So I finally had a mode of transport but it wasn't going to last long.

I was able to take the smoking fan boat to another dock, it was some abandoned trailer park and I literally got eaten by a tiger there.  One of the scariest environments I've been in a video game. 

Thankfully It reloaded me next to the broken fan boat pre cat meal and I decided it would be best to go up the river some more to a dock where I could steal a decent fishing boat. I found the perfect unoccupied boat and was finally able to gun it to my dock to finish the mission. It was one of the best gaming experiences I've ever had, the randomness working together to create something fantastic like that made my night. I felt like I was crawling my way out of the Everglades barely surviving, just like it should be in real life.

I think the people giving poor reviews never gave the game a chance or were feeding off propoganda takes.  It's a great game, and it's only getting better at the start of chapter 2.

author: Scorpian_Brazil
quote:
GTA VI is an extraordinary achievement and a remarkable demonstration of how far the video game industry has evolved. Rockstar has raised the bar in almost every aspect of the experience. The level of detail throughout the open world is astonishing, from the density of the cities and the variety of NPCs to the animations, lighting, reflections, physics, and dynamic weather systems. What makes it truly impressive is that the world doesn't feel like a simple backdrop; it feels alive, constantly evolving through spontaneous events, believable characters, and incredibly detailed environments.

Vice City and the entire state of Leonida are outstanding examples of world-building, combining artistic direction with remarkable technical sophistication. The sound design, environmental details, and overall atmosphere demonstrate an exceptional level of craftsmanship. Jason and Lucia also bring a new dimension to the franchise, with a compelling relationship and genuinely engaging character development.

The technological evolution compared to GTA V and even Red Dead Redemption 2 is remarkable. Rockstar has managed to combine an enormous world with an extraordinary level of detail, interactivity, and immersion. While the experience isn't without flaws, with certain mechanics that could be refined and occasional pacing issues, these shortcomings don't diminish the scale of what has been accomplished.

GTA VI is much more than a graphical showcase. It is an impressive integration of technology, animation, artificial intelligence, physics, narrative design, and world simulation. This is the kind of game that establishes new expectations for the open-world genre. Rockstar has delivered an experience that demonstrates an exceptional level of ambition and craftsmanship, setting a remarkable benchmark for the future of video games.

author: Sergiu26
quote: I’ve played video games since I was 8 or 9 years old, and I’ve experienced many generations of gaming. I’ve spent countless hours playing open-world games, including GTA V, so I know what makes this series **** honestly? GTA VI is something else.What makes this game incredible isn’t just its graphics, its animations or its attention to detail. It’s the world itself. It feels alive. You can walk down the street and something completely unexpected happens. NPCs interact with each other, people argue, random situations unfold, and sometimes I find myself simply standing there, watching what’s happening around me.I spent 9 hours in the opening area without even focusing on the main missions. I was driving around, stealing cars, exploring, making money and discovering little details. And I never felt bored.I actually love the ordinary activities too. Fixing a house, buying flowers, taking care of everyday things. Some people might find these details pointless, but to me, they make the world feel more believable. And when I want some action, there’s always something to discover. A random encounter, a fight, a car to steal or a situation that turns into complete **** for the 30 FPS debate, honestly, it doesn’t bother me. Of course, 60 FPS would be welcome, but I’d rather have a rich, detailed and immersive world than a technically smoother game that feels empty. Performance matters, but it’s not the only thing that makes a game enjoyable.I’ve also seen people complain about almost everything: the gameplay, the social elements, the realism, the direction Rockstar is taking and even the game’s representation of modern society. Not everything has to appeal to everyone, and criticism is perfectly fine. But sometimes I feel people are so busy looking for flaws that they forget to actually enjoy playing.Even my wife, who isn’t someone who normally spends hours playing video games, ended up playing GTA VI for almost an hour. That says something about how engaging this world can **** me, GTA VI isn’t just about completing missions, shooting people or stealing cars. It’s about being part of a living world where you can create your own experience, even when you’re doing absolutely nothing important.Rockstar didn’t just make another GTA. They created a world I genuinely want to spend time **** that’s what makes this game special to me.

author: Simiwee
quote:
TLDR: do yourself a favour and play this game… it’s an achievement in media not just gaming.

I could bang on about the graphical fidelity, mechanical and open world depth, the admittedly slow start to a story that picks up and becomes a crime drama thriller or just how alive the world feels.

But I’ll address common criticisms I see…

•The romance is optional…. No one forces you to play a dating simulator
• The patented GTA humour is still there… along with the same “now woke” criticisms of American and modern culture present since GTA San Andreas (that’s as early as I played)
• idk what kinda build some of the harsher critics are playing on I’ve had 35 hours and the only bug I’ve had was a store employee vanishing when I gave him a vape (ps5 slim btw) 
• various nitpicks like not being able to shoot or steal cars in your neighbourhood or commit hate crimes objectively don’t warrant 6/10 or lower reviews… grow up

As for my own criticisms? They fall into the nitpick category, I would appreciate the OPTION to date other people especially if the Jason/Lucia romance is optional, the cars are a little weak (can be changed in settings to reduce damage), the first hour or two (although not bad) is a little slow.

What I do like though? 
•Npc’s are overhauled and genuinely have their own personalities and can engage with or fight with just EACH OTHER or YOUR CHARACTER.
• there’s more skill and finnesse, police are lowkey scary even at 2-3 stars and the ai is so smart, roads are slimmer and population is so dense so wanted evasion actually takes a braincell or two comp to Gta5 
• this game looks incredible even on my 1080p TV and the environments are basically photorealistic both on the 1080p and 4k family TV 
•for a 232gb game of this scope or even not considering the size and detail… it runs so well
•there is so much crime to do, gang territories to run up on and activities to do 
• you can lose hours customising your characters, weapons and cars 
• the more grounded gameplay mean your methodical and have to actually think and plan if you want to be successful

10/10 genuine Technical marvel and a marvel in gaming and media as a whole.

author: NixPark
quote:
This review has 0 story spoilers. Played on PS5 PRO, 30 hours so far.

This game is very different to older GTA games, feels more like RDR2 in a GTA setting, which at least for me is absolutely perfect. People cry about how it's real and boring, yeah you gotta use your brain while playing a game, who would've said right.

Both protagonists are exceptionally well written, almost feels like real people to me, the level of detail of conversations, activities you can do is absolutely insane. The relationship system works also very well here and makes sense to the games story, it's optional though. The new career profile is also a great touch, as it remembers your actions very well. If you wanna go in town with a bazooka and cause an absolute mayhem, go play GTA V. Not like you can't do that here, you absolutely can, but the game will remember it and then judge you based on your actions, kinda real life feeling, actions have consequences, which is truly awesome. Side activities are more than plentiful here, you can dive and hunt for treasure, do various kinds of races, shooting range competitions, you can play golf, pool, backyard wrestling and many more. You can just chill and go on a date, or just watch TV if you don't feel like doing anything. There's also upgraded version of character stats and their tuning from GTA San Andreas, you can buff health, stamina and focus and also raise their levels by working out, or not if you feel like it.
Regarding missions, there's a insane number of various story or side missions to complete, all missions I've played so far felt really good and interesting. The story itself is so far a total blast, feels like a gritty struggle for survival of 2 people close to each other, I'll leave it at that.
People complain as well how woke the game is. I've played 30 hours so far and haven't seen 1 woke thing. None. Satire is kept here as well, but it's tweaked to the modern setting.

Gameplay feels buttery smooth, I'd say it's the most smooth game on launch Rockstar has put out. You can customise literally everything in the game settings, cars behaviour feels like a mix of GTA IV's real physics and GTA V's arcadeness, great overall feeling while driving.

The sense for realism is on another level here. You gotta eat, sleep, refuel your cars. Also the cops and wanted system got a huge improvement. Cops now act smart based on your actions. I'll share an example.

You go rob a pawnshop. While you absolutely can go in front door, guns and blazing, the shop owner might bring his own gun to the formula, while the shopping npcs can try to disarm you. I always go from the back of the store, check security, destroy camera evidence and disable alarms if I can. Then you can easily rob the whole store and make your escape. The cops remember your gun, attire, face and if you were with your partner or not. You can use a different vehicle to make your getaway, then approach your owned car, change outfits, drop the weapon you were seen with and split up with your partner and cops have nothing. Just requires a bit of planning and thinking. Awesome system.
You can mod cars, weapons as you like with various options here, improving stats as necessary. 
The graphics and art are truly mesmerising. You can see detailed water reflections, the draw distance is jaw dropping, I'm honestly stunned how could they pulls this **** off on this generation of consoles. 

There's definitely over a thousand things I forgot to mention here, but I need to go back into the game. This is the best GTA game at least for me.

If you like RDR2, Crimson desert or KCD2, you will most likely love this game. On the other hand, if you want to go and just mindlessly blow **** up, don't like realism or a life simulation, I suggest go play something else.

author: Antika
quote: Well, I have to say, the game turned out pretty good. I’m really glad they got rid of that awful, *GTA V*-style humor and moved things closer to the *RDR2* vibe. A lot of people call it boring, but I disagree—I enjoyed the slow pace of *RDR2*, and I’m enjoying it here too, just spending my days in Leonida. It does feel a bit like *The Sims* at times, but I don’t really mind that. I can’t say anything about the story yet since I’m taking it slow, but the characters seem decent—they’re memorable. author: dx_DANI89
quote:
A Living, Breathing World

Rating: 10/10

GTA VI is an incredible achievement in open-world game design.

What makes this game so special isn't just its graphics, animations, or enormous world. It's the unbelievable amount of detail and interaction Rockstar has put into almost everything.

The world feels alive. NPCs react to your actions, people remember your behavior, and even the smallest decisions can make the experience feel more personal. The police and civilians don't simply feel like background elements; they make the world feel dynamic and believable.

One of my favorite details is the morality system. Even something as simple as drinking a bottle and throwing it into a trash can can receive positive feedback. These little interactions might seem insignificant, but they make a huge difference in immersion.

I constantly find myself doing things that have nothing to do with the main story, simply because exploring the world is so enjoyable. Sometimes I genuinely forget that I'm playing a video game.

And that's probably the biggest compliment I can give GTA VI: it doesn't just make you play in its world; it makes you feel like you're part of it.

I'm still progressing through the story, and I honestly don't want it to end. I want to explore every corner, discover every little detail, and spend as much time as possible in this world.

Rockstar has created something truly special.

This isn't just another open-world game. It's an experience.

author: TheHardcoreMARK
quote:
This is, without a doubt, the best GTA I've ever played. And what's incredible is how little it feels like the previous games.
For the first time in years, an open world doesn't feel like a plastic showroom where your interactions are limited to vending machines, scripted NPCs, and prostitutes.
You can try opening almost any door, and the world actually responds. Stealing cars is more challenging. Escaping the police takes real effort. You can interact with practically anyone, provoke strangers, be friendly, or simply observe how they react. Random encounters are more varied, unpredictable, and genuinely exciting.

And then there's STEALTH. Actual stealth in GTA! You can finally move bodies. You can no longer carry an entire Ammu-Nation store in your back pocket. And honestly? That's **** the biggest achievement is something else **** the first time, I don't feel like I'm just playing in a GTA world. I feel like I'm living in **** can take a shower, work out, buy food and drinks, walk into a bar ON YOUR OWN instead of watching a cutscene with your buddies, and actually order whatever you want. These might sound like small details, but together they completely transform the **** the story? The mission at the end of Act One alone puts half of today's blockbuster movies to shame in terms of writing, direction, tension, and sheer **** once, the protagonists feel like real people rather than empty shells designed to carry the plot forward. Their relationship and chemistry exist beyond scripted missions. 
They interact naturally, and you actually believe in **** amount of side content is ridiculous. Fishing, treasure hunting, racing, collecting items, random encounters, and countless little discoveries.I was literally just driving around when I saw a plane falling out of the sky. I followed it into the swamps, found the wreckage, a barely surviving guy, and the mysterious "cargo" he never managed to deliver.That's the kind of experience I'm talking about. Nobody told me to go there. I wasn't following a mission marker. I was just exploring, and the world gave me a story.
Every time I drive through these locations, I see a detailed, believable, living world. A world that doesn't just look real, but makes you want to believe in it.Vehicle damage is also vastly improved compared to GTA V, and the driving physics feel noticeably better. Cars have more personality, weight, and are simply more fun to **** finally, to everyone giving this game a 0/10 while claiming it's "just the same GTA again"...I get it. Not getting a PC release at launch must be **** judging a game you've never actually played says more about your frustration than the game itself.

Watching GTA VI on YouTube isn't playing GTA VI. Your entire gameplay experience consists of two buttons: pause and volume.This isn't GTA V 5.1. 
This is the GTA I've been waiting for all these years.

10/10.

author: pesomvp
quote: Thirteen years of waiting, and Rockstar didn't just deliver a good game. They set a new standard. Leonida doesn't feel like a game world; it feels like a place that would keep living even if you put the controller down. Every street, every passerby, every little moment happening on the sidelines feels deliberate. The level of detail is almost absurd, and the more time you spend there, the more you notice how much care went into every corner of it.Jason and Lucia carry the story with real chemistry. They're not just another interchangeable crime duo; they're two characters you actually care about, and their dynamic gives the whole game an emotional core the series has never had quite like this. Add to that an endless list of side activities, from fishing to scuba diving, that you don't just tick off a checklist but genuinely enjoy. Missions are varied, the pacing gives big moments room to land, and the world constantly surprises you with things you didn't **** then there's the hate. "Overrated." "Boring." "Too slow." Honestly, I don't get it. Or maybe I do: GTA 6 takes its time. It builds tension, lets missions breathe, and trusts you to immerse yourself in its world. If you put the controller down after ten minutes without an explosion because your brain is screaming for the next 15-second clip, you're never going to appreciate what this game is doing. That's not a flaw in the game. That's an attention span problem.Some so-called "fans" have apparently spent so many years staring at TikTok leaks, trailer breakdowns and reaction videos that they've forgotten how to just sit down and play a game. They built up an imaginary version of GTA 6 in their heads, one that's nonstop chaos every second, and now they're mad that the real thing has depth, patience and actual storytelling. A masterpiece doesn't owe you a dopamine hit every 30 seconds. A masterpiece that rewards you for giving it your time, and that's exactly what makes it great. If you bring patience, you get the best open-world experience in years. If you don't, well, you can always keep scrolling.
