author: jjoacocarrera47
quote: I’ve played GTA VI, and I think it’s a great video game, though its score doesn't really do it justice—and it feels unfair to other titles that truly deserve that kind of rating, like 1998's Ocarina of Time with its 99. I played it on PlayStation 5, where it launched at 30 fps. While it feels very strong narratively with a really good story between Jason and Lucia, it’s nothing we haven't seen in previous GTA games. It’s the classic story of criminals pulling off their jobs and reaching the end, without innovating, showing anything truly different, or bringing anything new to the table aside from incredible graphics—which, in my opinion, are the best graphics released to date.However, launching at 30 fps—with frame drops down to 20 during heavy explosions—and releasing with a lot of bugs means it doesn't deserve a 99. To me, a 99 means a game is near-flawless in every single aspect, and this one isn't. In my view, a 99 is reserved for a revolutionary game that sets trends in how games are designed and programmed, just like Ocarina of Time did as the one true 99 game in the world. Giving GTA VI a 99 right now feels wrong to me.I'm not saying it's a 70-point game, and I don't understand Nintendo fans who review-bomb Rockstar games, nor Rockstar fans who review-bomb Nintendo games. I think it's a solid 94 or 95, held back by some bugs and repetitive, unintuitive missions. It feels like the game holds your hand step by step through everything you have to do, instead of letting you as a player figure things out, reason, and decide where to go. It constantly tells you: "come here, take this over there, kill this guy, do this," and in my opinion, that takes some of the fun out of gaming. Even if the story is linear inside an open world, it shouldn't stop you from having to think for yourself.Contrast that with something like the Ocarina of Time remake, which in my opinion deserves over 95 points—even though its score was dragged down by people giving it 85s or 70s, which I think is unfair. Even as a modern remake made slightly more accessible for newcomers to Nintendo, it still forces you to stop and think about how to solve things. Speaking from my own experience playing the Ocarina of Time remake as a newcomer, that’s the core of my criticism. Overall, though, I think GTA VI is a solid 94.

You can approach robberies, even of small shops, in various ways: you can disable the alarm, enter through the back room, or seize the security camera footage. The story is good so far. As for those claiming you can’t crash a plane into a building—that’s a lie; the people who made those videos simply adjusted the vehicle damage settings. Some also complain that you can’t kill protesters, but if you complete a certain quest, you actually can. And to those who say it’s no different from GTA V—are you idiots? GTA V feels like cardboard, like it’s not real; but here, I truly believe in this world—it’s alive. On the downside, there’s no first-person mode, and some missions can be a bit dull—though there aren’t many of them, and it’s perfectly normal for a game to have a few. There are bugs, sure, but I’ve personally encountered very few; it’s impossible to create a game with a world this detailed without having any bugs at all.

quote: I’m 33. I’ve got a wife, a kid, a dog and **** to do in the morning. If I put on a movie or a show late in the evening, I usually fall asleep halfway through. Same with games. By midnight my body’s like “yeah, we’re done.” But I **** came prepared for GTA VI. I live in Kyiv, and between the blackouts and the ballistic missile alerts at night, I wanted to at least be able to play when the power went out. So yeah, I’ve got a whole backup power station just for my PS5.I started playing the second it went live and I felt like a teenager again. Got back on the next day and it was just as hard to put down. It feels like a mix of GTA IV, GTA V and RDR2 with a little Max Payne 3 in there.I’ve spent maybe 80% of my time just exploring, doing random side missions and seeing what happens. I’m slowly getting through the story, but honestly, at this point I feel like I live in a little town outside Miami. Lucia and Jason already feel like a real couple. Some of the everyday stuff you do with them feels a lot like the stuff my wife and I have to get done. And the amount of detail is ridiculous. I can barely stay awake watching my own TV, yet here I am watching TV in GTA and actually sticking around for the ads. Some of the **** they put in the shows and magazines had me crying laughing.Yeah, I know the hype is insane. We’ve all been waiting forever. But playing this at launch, before I’ve seen every funny encounter in a clip and while the tech still has me wondering how the hell they pulled it off, is something special. This is what next-gen feels like to me.I’m gonna take my time with this one. If you’re going to play it, do yourself a favor and go in before you’ve watched a dozen reviews. author: Patrick26
quote:
This game doesn't even feel real.

The open world is incredible: alive and constantly evolving, filled with events unfolding all around you, intricately interconnected and supported by an extraordinary depth of lore. Every billboard, every TV scene, every radio conversation, every venue and every character is remarkably well crafted and full of personality. The result is a level of depth and world-building in Leonida that I have never experienced before in a video game.

I also absolutely love the new movement systems, vehicle handling and overall physics. Everything has a genuine sense of weight, making the experience feel incredibly realistic. You actually feel like you're controlling a real person or driving a real vehicle. Running over a person or crashing into an object feels genuinely impactful, rather than simply interacting with lifeless props placed in the world for the sake of filling it up.

I could spend hours writing about how extraordinary this game is, but I want to highlight what is probably the most impressive achievement of all: the technical side of things. I'm playing on an Xbox Series S, and I honestly wouldn't have believed anyone who told me the game would run this well. There are certainly some frame rate drops in the busiest areas of Vice City, but the mere fact that something of this scale runs on an Xbox Series S speaks volumes about the incredible amount of work and attention to detail put in by the developers.

A few words about the story: I agree with many people who say that it isn't the most compelling or memorable story in the GTA franchise. However, I genuinely appreciate Rockstar's attempt to deliver something more realistic, nuanced and thoughtfully written. It's a story that confronts us with a world that feels real, rather than the more straightforward and often over-the-top worlds that have traditionally characterized previous entries in the series.

This game is a masterpiece. The review bombing we've witnessed over the past few hours clearly demonstrates how some gamers have lost the ability to appreciate what it actually takes to develop something on this scale. More importantly, they seem unable to recognize Rockstar's attempt to take the franchise in a new direction, rather than simply delivering another more-of-the-same experience that would inevitably have led to GTA becoming just another predictable sequel.

As far as I'm concerned, this is the greatest video game ever made. I can only thank the developers for giving me the opportunity to experience a world as alive, immersive and incredibly deep as Leonida.

If only we had more masterpieces like this.

Thank you, Rockstar.

author: Joseph2446
quote: Ten hours in on Xbox Series X and at roughly 18% completion, it is already clear why Grand Theft Auto VI sets a new benchmark for modern open-world design and marks a true structural evolution for Rockstar Games. Deep into Chapter 1 (Just Like Paradise), the most striking quality is its deliberate, unhurried pacing—even slower in its opening stretch than Red Dead Redemption 2. Rather than rushing into over-the-top chaos, Rockstar clearly aims to push its cinematic ambition to the absolute limit, adopting a grounded, prestige-film rhythm that lets you absorb the sun-drenched, humid atmosphere of Leonida while naturally establishing Jason and Lucia’s dynamic. This sharp attention to narrative craft extends even to minor side activities: neighbor item requests are written with far greater personality and natural context than Red Dead Redemption 2’s camp errands—where, for instance, little Jack would ask for a storybook without giving you any real clue where to look—whereas here the game naturally points you toward the exact location rather than sending you on a blind map-wide scavenger hunt.From a gameplay standpoint, blending the tactile physicality and systemic depth of Red Dead Redemption 2 into a dense, contemporary urban sandbox works effortlessly. Tactical constraints—such as storing heavy weaponry in your vehicle’s trunk—combined with revamped vehicle theft mechanics, witness behavior, and far smarter police AI turn even minor heists and getaways into tense, emergent scenarios. Driving physics finally deliver a satisfying sense of weight and traction across different vehicle classes, while gunplay feels noticeably crisper and more responsive than in previous entries. That said, the new Incapacitate Enemies mechanic—which lets you neutralize targets non-lethally by hitting limbs to preserve a cleaner Criminal Profile—could use slightly tighter tuning: downed opponents often linger in an incapacitated state for a bit too long, frequently surviving up to five bullets before actually expiring. Ultimately, it is the world-building that earns a 10 within the first ten hours. Vice City and its surrounding regions never feel like static set dressing: crowd density, believable NPC routines, richly detailed interiors, and constant spontaneous encounters create an ecosystem that feels genuinely alive. In that context, much of the online discourse surrounding the frame rate feels largely sterile: on Xbox Series X, performance remains remarkably consistent, dipping below 25 fps only once across ten hours of play, more than justifying the trade-off with staggering global illumination, image stability, and atmospheric depth. If these opening ten hours are merely the foundation, GTA VI is a generational landmark.

author: HippoPippo
quote:
Thirteen years of waiting, and it was worth every one of them.

Some games raise the bar, and some move it somewhere you didn't know it could go. Grand Theft Auto VI is the second kind. Rockstar has made a game so dense, so alive and so sure of itself that after the first few hours it stops feeling like an open world and starts feeling like a real place you happen to be visiting.

That place is Leonida, Rockstar's sunburnt, neon-soaked parody of Florida, and it's the real star. Vice City's skyline shines at dusk, the Keys sprawl out in turquoise and mangrove green, and the swamps and small towns in between are packed with life. Nothing here feels like set dressing. People argue, film each other, make deals and fall apart in ways that blur the line between scripted moments and pure chance. You can lose an entire evening without starting a single mission, just watching the world go about its business.

When you do follow the story, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos carry it brilliantly. Pairing them up Bonnie-and-Clyde style was a risk, and it pays off in the series' most mature and emotionally grounded story yet. These two feel like partners rather than archetypes, and their relationship gives the crime and chaos real stakes. The writing still has the series' trademark bite and satire, but this time there's heart under the cynicism, and the finale lands harder than you'd expect.

The missions are more flexible than ever, so you can approach jobs your own way instead of following a single scripted path. Driving, shooting and movement feel weighty and precise, and the side activities are endless, from fishing and diving to completely pointless distractions that somehow turn into your favourite memories.

Technically, it's astonishing. The lighting, the crowds, the sheer amount of detail on screen at once: this is what current-generation hardware was waiting for.

Is it perfect? Nothing is. The world is so big it can be overwhelming at first, and PC players are still waiting. But measured against what it sets out to do, GTA VI doesn't put a foot wrong. It's a generational landmark, and the new benchmark every open-world game will be measured against.

Verdict: 10/10. A masterpiece, and essential playing.

author: 3xplosve
quote:
Rockstar has created a game world so vast and detailed that you practically want to fall in love with almost every corner of it. Visually, GTA 6 is a real powerhouse. You can certainly notice the 30 FPS in a few spots—especially when speeding through dense forest areas while 10 to 15 cars pass by at the same time, but it barely detracts from the overall impression.

What blows me away the most so far is the incredible immersion and dynamic nature of the world. Things are constantly happening completely outside of the main missions that make the setting feel truly alive: right in the middle of downtown, a tow truck runs a red light and T-bones another car. On the highway, I lightly clip a vehicle, which then realistically slams into the guardrail and flips over. Or I speed into the city a bit too fast, a patrol car briefly blips its siren to pull me over and then drives off with an annoyed remark once I immediately slow down. Moments like these create an atmosphere unlike anything we've seen before.

Gameplay-wise, you immediately feel the DNA of Red Dead Redemption 2 , just way more opulent and with even greater depth, almost like a "Red Dead 3" in a modern GTA disguise. The controls feel pleasantly grounded and responsive without ever feeling like you're driving on rails. On top of that, you aren't constantly forced into loud shootouts. Instead, you can often choose for yourself whether to go full action or take a quieter, more subtle approach. Anyone who didn't enjoy the pacing and feel of Red Dead 2 should definitely keep that in mind. For me personally, though, this exact blend is a massive plus—a truly exceptional game.

author: Vigas87
quote:
GTA VI - A Game Worth Waiting For ️

I've never written a game review before, but GTA VI deserves to be my first.

I've been waiting for this game for so many years. I followed every bit of news, watched the trailers countless times, counted down the days, and eventually even the hours until release. And honestly, the feeling of finally launching GTA VI was something special.

Rockstar has always had this incredible ability to create more than just video games. They create entire worlds that feel alive. Worlds where you don't just want to complete missions, but simply explore, drive around, discover little details, and enjoy every moment.

What makes this experience even more special is realizing that the game I've dreamed about playing for so long is finally here.

For some people, it's just another video game. For me, it's something much bigger. It's an experience I've been looking forward to for years, and one I'll remember for a very long time.

Thank you, Rockstar Games, for making this dream a reality. ️

Some games are worth the wait. GTA VI is one of them.

However, I strongly believe that GTA 6 is not a game for children. It contains mature themes, violence, strong language, and adult content, making it much more suitable for older and mature players who can fully appreciate its story and atmosphere.
In my opinion, GTA 6 has set a completely new standard for open-world gaming. It is more than just a video game — it is an unforgettable experience.

author: elidgaf
quote:
Overall amazing game, it is generational. I will update when I fully beat the game, but I can already tell that it's a 10/10 and I probably will have thousands of hours on it.

The positives off the top of my head:

• Graphics are INSANE, especially for it to be on console. PS5/XBox series X games have reached a point where they're always going to look good, but GTA 6 takes it to the next level. Very impressed with it every time I play. Especially with the sunsets, the water/underwater, the swamps, the rain, and everything in between.

• Guns - their models/appearances - received a major overhaul. They sound and look better than the guns from previous games (RDR2, GTA 5).

• Leonida offers SO MUCH to do. RDR2 offered a lot additional to the main story, but GTA 6 has so much more to offer besides the main story. There are so many robbery opportunities, racing opportunities, gang hideouts, carjackings & sellings, collectibles, hunting, and so on and so forth.

The only very minor flaws are:

• The free aim feels clunky, even with max sensitivity and look acceleration. Rockstar could have capped the sensitivity higher instead of 14 (like 20, for example).

• The frames drop when the area is densely crowded - either by people/npcs or foliage. Not nearly as bad as some make it out to be though.

• They could have done better with the melee - it feels like just spamming square/X. I'm not asking for a boxing game, but the ability to throw a punch with your left/right depending on the button - like pressing square/X to throw a left punch and circle/B to throw a right punch - would have been a nice detail.

author: RealGamer88
quote:
I honestly don't even know where to begin,  after putting about 30 hours into the game i think i have played long enough to see that this is the best open world game ever created, regardless of how you feel about the narrative of the game, what Rockstar has built here is something truly special, Leonida feels like a living breathing place where even the fish in the ocean are highly detailed, and seeing the same NPC twice is pretty much impossible because they are no longer just premade characters that the game places into the world, instead they are randomly generated based on body type, gender and even the clothing is randomly generated. 

If you just drive around without rushing from mission to mission you will see all kinds of crazy stuff happening, police arresting people, people getting into fights, car chases etc. 

The game has this side mission system called "random encounters" similar to RDR2 where you will just stumble upon characters that need your help, it really gives you a reason to want to explore.

In older GTA games you pretty much only had main missions and going on killing sprees, but this is the first GTA game that is packed with so many things to do and where it just feels so real that i don't even want to commit crimes, it's satisfying just doing normal activities, even shooting hoops at your safehouse is fun.

I also have to add that alot of what you are hearing about this game is just flat out wrong, and if you go into the game without preconceived notions you will see that it's a masterpiece and that the core GTA DNA is all still here.

People praise GTA 5 way too much when as far as i'm concerned it is by far the worst game in the series narratively speaking, it's disjointed and rushed and the 3 protagonists dont get their own personal stories fleshed out properly, it is the primary reason why the game narratively fails, same thing happened to the movie Spiderman 3 with Tobey Maguire, they tried to do too much by adding in all of those villains and they turned it into a mess, and GTA 5 suffers from the same issues unfortunately, but anyway, GTA 6 fixes all of those issues, i just hope that you are all smart enough to see through this fake outrage.

You can tell who played a gta story before and who came from gta online. Most of the negative reviews here show that clearly. The game is amazing. And for 30 fps, it runs butterly smooth. Idk if its because my smart tv has a secret ai frem generation in the gaming mode. But it feels very smooth without stutters. For anyone who is unsure due to the reviews, i wanna adress the biggest complaints and explain why i think they are garbage made by people who never played a gta story or read dead. Since gta 6 is the mix from the best of those: 

Framrate: idk what y'all did with your ps5. But like i said previously, it runs buttery smooth on my 5 year old base ps5. 

Jason the "cuck": just because he has a stable relationship, y'all call him a cuck? I am 11 hours down and as far as I know, Lucia did not bang with a different dude in front of him. Either you guys are misogynistic af, thinking that doing acts of love for your partner is pathetic, or y'all are just misogynistic. Nobody called Michael a cuck, even tho he was the real one. Bugs: this is just dishonest. People do nothing but search for them for the whole time. In my 11 hours of playtime, I did not have a single one, neither did any of my friends who are as far as they got. 

Chores: they are fun, take 2 minutes in total. Red dead had a lot more chores. And people glazed it for it.

13 years of development for this ****: no. Gta 6 was actively in development for 8 years. After red dead was finished. The time between gta 5 and red dead had no actual development for this game. We waited 13 years. But this game did not take 13 years. 

The only real critique i have is the fact that Rockstar took core stuff out to sell it back with the deluxe edition. Barbershops, cars, etc. And that you can use gta + for a single player story game. The work put into it is fascinatingly realistic and pushes GTA to a whole new level.Following in the footsteps of its predecessors, but especially its distant cousins GTA IV and San Andreas, Rockstar delivers a magnified version of its vision of realism.

For instance, having to change clothes if you are in nightwear when moving away from Jason's house, or the fact that weapons disappear as soon as you step inside. 

These are details, sure, but ones we would have appreciated seeing polished, given how incredibly well-executed the rest of the details are (and these are just two examples among others).

Regarding the story:

The direction feels bold but takes inspiration from RDR2, where you actually take your time: the brief morning chats, the texts, the phone calls, how characters behave around others... 

You observe, you grow attached, you **** takes time, and this pacing slowly allows us to understand these characters and appreciate them for who they truly are.There are no caricaturale characters like in GTA V, which, in my opinion, has the worst storyline of the GTA saga, where everything is predictable and easy.

In GTA 6, we are not in a Michael Bay movie. We are facing a story, a drama that asks us to take our time, to listen, and to **** course, the theme won't appeal to everyone—especially players who only view GTA through the lens of GTA V's Online mode or its campaign. Granted, it is not as dark as 4 or San Andreas, but it is touching.Much like RDR2, it isn't simple. It takes us into another era that echoes our own, with all its flaws and qualities. And it does this remarkably well, both in the main missions and the side quests.

To conclude:

There shouldn't be a need to give GTA 6 a 10, but it is necessary. When I see the amount of 0s or ratings below 5, it's an absolute joke.This game, even in the worst-case scenario, should never get a score below 5. Nobody makes games like this. 

You might not appreciate the creative choices or care for the story, but it remains something rare.When I look at our society and the way we treat people, the way we treat works of art—especially since the rise of social media... Honestly, the satire isn't even pushed far enough. The behavior and motivations of some people leave real doubts about their true intentions, particularly their ability to be fair to themselves and to others.

author: Kritorum
quote:
​I love GTA VI. I can't stop playing, and I'm spending a lot of my time doing everything alongside the main questline. Every time I set out to progress the story, something on the side catches my attention, and honestly, that’s where the game shines the most.

​Just cruising around Leonida feels rewarding on its own. Whether I’m stumbling into random street encounters in Vice City, exploring the swamps, or just soaking in the atmosphere and watching how alive the NPCs feel, the world constantly gives you great things to discover. The side quests and activities don't feel like cheap filler either. They blend so naturally into the environment that you end up doing tons of side content without it ever feeling forced.

​When I read the negative user reviews, it honestly frustrates me how many people keep comparing the new GTA to the older games. This GTA is a completely new generation, a fresh chapter with its own identity, technology, and vision. Judging it solely through nostalgia instead of appreciating what it actually achieves on its own misses the whole point. On top of that, I feel like a lot of the bad reviews are just coming from people who are mad that it isn't out on PC yet. I'm a PC gamer myself, and right now I'm just enjoying sitting in a party with my friends, talking, and casually exploring the world together. Honestly, it has been a long time since a game has made me want to play this much.

author: darkassassin97
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI – A Fantastic Experience, Despite Its Flaws

After around 40 hours of playing GTA VI, I can confidently say that this is an incredible experience. Is it a perfect 10/10? No. But is it anywhere near a 0/10? Absolutely not.

I honestly don't understand the amount of negativity and pressure coming from certain users. Some reviews criticize things that don't even reflect what the game actually offers. Constructive criticism is perfectly fair, but some of the scores and comments seem completely disconnected from the actual experience.

Visually, the game is absolutely fantastic. I'm playing on PS5 Pro, and performance is generally stable. There are a couple of specific areas where FPS drops occur, mainly in locations with dense vegetation and lots of objects being rendered simultaneously. However, these issues are relatively limited and don't ruin the overall experience.(And yes, the game runs at 30 FPS. As a PC player, I found it difficult to get used to at first, but eventually I adjusted. However, try playing Red Dead Redemption 2 at its locked 30 FPS on consoles and then jump into GTA VI. It's simply not the same experience. GTA VI feels noticeably smoother, and you don't feel the 30 FPS nearly as much as you do in RDR2. In Red Dead Redemption 2, the 30 FPS limitation is much more noticeable.)

The gameplay mechanics remind me a lot of Red Dead Redemption 2, but Rockstar has taken things a step further. The attention to detail, interactions, animations and overall gameplay systems are outstanding.

I particularly love the heists. The way Lucia and Jason handle their weapons and hide their pistols is such a small detail, but it makes the experience feel incredibly authentic. These are the kinds of details that make Rockstar games special.

Regarding the story, I actually agree with some of the criticism. So far, I wouldn't consider it Rockstar's strongest narrative. GTA IV had an exceptional story, and that's a very high standard to live up to.

However, when it comes to gameplay and vehicle physics, GTA VI is a massive improvement over GTA V. I genuinely don't understand how anyone can say that GTA V had better driving and damage mechanics. In GTA V, you could crash a car and barely leave a scratch. GTA VI brings back the impressive vehicle deformation and physics that made GTA IV so memorable, while taking them even further. Cars feel much more realistic, and the damage system is on another level.

You can drive almost anything, interact with the world in countless ways, and constantly discover new details. The world feels alive.

And regarding the PC version: seriously, why are people acting surprised? Rockstar has released its major titles on consoles first and PC later for years. Red Dead Redemption 2 followed the same approach. I'm a PC player myself, and I absolutely intend to buy GTA VI again when it arrives on PC. That's simply how Rockstar releases its games.

I also agree with some of the criticism regarding the bugs. Yes, there are a few minor bugs here and there. They don't significantly affect the gameplay experience, but they are definitely present. After 13 years of waiting, I honestly expected a more polished release. That said, I'm confident Rockstar will address most of these issues through future updates.

Overall, GTA VI isn't flawless, and it certainly deserves criticism where criticism is justified. But the amount of hate and extremely low scores is difficult to understand.

I'm having a fantastic time with this game after 40 hours, and I can't wait to see what else Rockstar has prepared.

My final score: 8/10.
If Rockstar fixes the remaining bugs and improves the overall polish, I could easily see this becoming a 9/10 experience for me.

author: ryukenishida

GTA 6 is an incredible game—easily the best-looking title ever made, packed with insane interactivity, great music, and pure fun. It completely deserves a 95 to 97.
​Tying Ocarina of Time at 99, though, is wrong. Ocarina earned its 99 by literally inventing the blueprint for modern 3D gaming—figuring out how 3D movement, object interaction, dynamic cameras, and lock-on combat actually work, alongside one of the best stories and the greatest soundtrack in gaming history.
​Even compared to Red Dead Redemption 2 (97), RDR2 still holds up as one of the best-looking games ever, matches that deep interactivity, and easily beats GTA 6 in story.
​GTA 6 is a phenomenal 95–97 game—just don’t confuse peak modern polish with the game that invented 3D gaming itself.

author: SirBloo
quote:
I really love this game. The gameplay, the story, and honestly, I even love the slower pace they've gone for. I don't think any game has ever gone to this level of detail either, except maybe Red Dead 2. It's genuinely incredible what they've managed to create.

That said, I do think this new identity for GTA has perhaps overlooked some of what made GTA 4 and 5 so much fun. It's a lot more difficult to just go out and cause absolute chaos, and I do miss some of that arcade-style madness from the previous games.

Don't get me wrong, this isn't a bad GTA. It's just different. In many ways, it feels more like Red Dead Redemption 2, which isn't necessarily a bad thing. I just think there's room for both styles, and I'd be lying if I said I didn't miss some of the craziness of the older games.

I'm genuinely so happy to have played this game and experienced everything it has to offer. My advice would be to stick with it, because it's absolutely worth playing.

However, I do think the critics have perhaps overrated it slightly. Technically, it's a masterpiece, and the level of detail is something else. But where I think it falls slightly short is in actually making the game as fun to play as some of the previous entries.

A fantastic game, but it's not the most fun I've ever had with a GTA.

author: muteburrito
quote: 13 years. That’s how long we’ve waited for this game, and somehow Rockstar has managed to remind me exactly why I fell in love with gaming in the first place.There’s just something different about Rockstar games. It’s not only about the graphics, the missions, or how massive the world is. It’s the little things, the attention to detail, and the feeling that you’re actually part of a living, breathing world. You can spend hours doing absolutely nothing related to the story and still have a great time. That’s something very few developers manage to pull **** honestly, seeing some of the negativity surrounding this game is just ridiculous. Everyone is entitled to their opinion, and genuine criticism is absolutely fair. But there’s a difference between actually criticizing a game and blindly hating on something because it’s popular. Some of these reviews make you wonder whether people even gave the game a fair chance. I’m not saying GTA VI is beyond criticism, but review bombing and jumping on hate bandwagons don’t help **** me, games like GTA VI are exactly why gaming is so special. You can see the ambition and the years of work that go into creating something of this scale. In an industry where so many games feel rushed or designed around monetization, it’s refreshing to see this level of attention given to a single-player experience.Rockstar, thank you for reminding us why video games are more than just entertainment.Absolutely worth the wait. 10/10.

author: Arifadac
quote:
I think the story has been quite successful so far. I believe the game does a great job of conveying the bond between Lucia and Jason, as well as the romantic relationship between them. At least, it worked for me. The gameplay mechanics also feel like a mix of previous GTA titles and Red Dead Redemption 2.

I haven't finished the story yet, so I don't want to make any definitive judgments about its later chapters. One thing I'm particularly curious about is how far the narrative is willing to take risks and how much it will challenge its characters. Will we see situations with genuinely high stakes, where life and death become central to the story, similar to what we experienced in Red Dead Redemption 2? I honestly don't know yet, but we'll see.

I'm generally a story-focused player. However, even when I actively try to focus on the main story in GTA 6, I find it almost impossible to do so. There's always something catching my attention, something worth exploring or somewhere else I want to go. I constantly find myself getting distracted by the world around me. I've played approximately 16 hours so far and have completed around 35% of the story. And that's despite trying to progress through it a little faster than I normally would.

I bought the Ultimate Edition, but I don't think the differences between the Standard and Ultimate Editions are particularly significant. To be fair, I wasn't expecting them to be groundbreaking in the first place.

Overall, my experience has been extremely positive so far. I still have a long way to go before finishing the story, but one thing is already clear: Rockstar has done it again. Hats off to Rockstar. They've outdone themselves once again.

author: GAME7hao
quote: I’m giving GTA VI a 10/10 for one very specific reason: it is the first huge game that actually describes the era we’re living through right now. We are drowning in mobile social media, endless feeds, notifications, hot takes, group chats, and trivial information—and most of us have no real idea where any of it is supposed to lead. GTA VI doesn’t just acknowledge that; it builds its world out of it. The information is petty and fragmented, the days are long, and daily life is often boring in a way that feels painfully **** decades, we were used to a different texture. The 90s, the 2000s, even the 2010s gave us a sense of forward motion—economic growth, crime waves, social unrest, and the feeling that we were moving through a world that at least had momentum. Entertainment was everywhere, and it felt like it was keeping pace with a society that was changing fast.Then came 2020–2026. Not apocalyptic, not even especially dramatic—just flat. Life feels like lukewarm tap water. There’s more content than ever and less that lands. That is the exact atmosphere GTA VI **** series has always been a crime saga, but the eras matter. GTA IV was the middle of the crime boom. GTA V was the handoff between the peak and the end. GTA VI is about a world where crime can no longer make you rich—where the old ladder is gone, and the underclass has to figure out what to do next. That’s a far more interesting question than “how do I get to the top,” and the game knows it.That’s why it’s a 10 for me. It doesn’t pretend we’re still living in the old story. It looks at the feed-scrolling, trivial, lukewarm present and says: this is where we are. And somehow, that makes it feel more alive than most games I’ve played in years.

author: iop90cwl
quote:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is simultaneously one of the most incredible games I’ve ever played and also a frustrating and lackluster experience. The graphics, overall level of detail, and vibe are second to none. At the same time, gameplay elements intended to reinforce realism render it downright annoying at times, the story is middling at best, and what I think is most unforgivable: It lacks the edge that GTA games are known for. There is no bite to the dialogue; it is the epitome of “safe edgy”. Considering the proportion of millennial college graduate women at Rockstar Games, this is hardly surprising. What has passed for content on GTA 5 online over the last ten years should have made it obvious that this would be the case.

While not as outlandishly progressive as some online detractors are making it out to be, the tone that every GTA game since 3 has had is simply missing. On paper, it has everything. It checks all the boxes. But while playing you realize that all of the characters are just boring as hell, with a few fun exceptions. Every PS2 GTA game made me care more about their characters than this one has.

The wanted system is mostly fun and implemented well, and the realistic game mechanics can be fun to plan around once you get used to them. But having a car engine get destroyed because an NPC car decided to pull out in front of you and having to pay $600 to get it repaired in the very first chapter when you’re broke is not a good way to introduce legacy players to the new mechanics.

Because of its massive scope and mind bending duality, it’s basically impossible to give this game an actual out-of-ten score. I will give it a quantum score. It is both 10/10 and 6/10, at the same time.

author: Grinderbar
quote:
10/10 – More Than Just Another Grand Theft Auto

What makes GTA VI special to me isn't simply its open world, its mechanics, or the usual Rockstar madness. It's Jason.

For once, we get a protagonist who feels like an actual grown man. Someone who has probably seen enough violence, made enough mistakes, and reached a point in life where he doesn't need to prove himself to everyone. He is capable of violence, but he doesn't seem eager to use it. And that distinction makes him incredibly interesting and relatable.

This is what really caught my attention. GTA has always been about chaos, excess, crime, and spectacular action. But Jason brings something different to the experience. There's a sense of maturity to him, almost like a man who has already been through the kind of life that other GTA protagonists are just getting started with.

The driving and vehicle mechanics are another massive highlight. Cars and bikes feel like more than just transportation. They make exploring the world enjoyable in its own right. I also love the idea of having a world where you can slow down, ride around, discover places, and simply exist without constantly chasing the next explosion.

That's what I want from an open-world game: freedom that doesn't always have to mean destruction.

Rockstar seems to understand that an interesting world isn't just a map filled with activities. It's a place where you actually want to spend time.

For me, GTA VI has something that goes beyond the traditional appeal of the franchise. It's not just about being the biggest criminal, causing the most chaos, or completing the next mission. It's about the characters, their lives, and the world around them.

And honestly, that's what makes me excited.

10/10. Not because it's perfect, but because it gives me exactly what I want from a video game: a world I want to live in, not just a game I want to finish.

author: akaguru
quote: Honestly, GTA 6 feels different from SA, VC and III. Those games had a clear identity and theme, whether it was the gangster lifestyle, Scarface or Mafia influence. GTA IV felt like a movie, while V improved on that formula but lost some of what made SA special. GTA 6 takes a different approach. It’s visually stunning, mechanically great, and the driving feels like a mix of IV and V. Having grown up in Florida, I love how much of the world reflects things I’ve actually seen and experienced. The characters are okay, basically Bonnie and Clyde in GTA, set in Miami. The story isn’t bad, but I don’t feel as connected to them as I did with previous characters, and sometimes the relationship feels forced. I played on release, so there were some glitches, but on my PS5 fat it still looks and runs great. To me, it’s like RDR2 mixed with GTA RP. I love the realism and consequences of your actions, and while I understand why longtime fans might feel let down, personally I enjoy it for what it is.

author: Yanntastisch
quote:
Sadly launched in a near-cyberpunk-like state, despite countless delays and being console-exclusive on release. Frame drops below 30 FPS, glitches, softlocks and even clipping through the ground. Simply not acceptable for a 80-100$ game with 2 billion budget.

What's lacking technically can't be said about the graphics and art. As expected, this is one of the most visually stunning games of all time. Super realistic lighting and human models that look real but almost never reach the uncanny valley. The world feels incredibly lived-in in a way that cannot be said for pretty much any other open-world game. Every NPC is unique, there is eye for detail in the smallest corners of the city. Rockstar produced entire animated series, music albums and games within the game just to make it feel even more real. A great story, well-written characters, and some of the best political satire in the series.

While the game finds a surprisingly good balance between realism and QOL, gameplay greatly relies on QTE chores and honor systems that feel more like Red Dead Redemption than Grand Theft Auto. GTA 6 should've given you more freedom than GTA 5 but does the opposite, actually adding restrictions like not being able to steal certain cars or shoot certain NPCs. Players should have the choice of whether they want to be good or evil, not be subtly forced to be good for the sake of the story.

Another big issue for content creators specifically is that copyrighted music can only be muted, not replaced, making the game an uncomfortable mess since nearly all important scenes use copyrighted tracks. Target audiences were clearly missed out on in some cases.

Overall, an artistic masterpiece but with a bad first impression. Hopefully, Rockstar makes sure to get more stable PC and Online releases.

author: Adokill
quote:
After years of waiting and massive hype, GTA VI feels surprisingly unpolished. The graphics and open world are impressive, but they cannot excuse the frustrating technical problems. Players have reported constant crashes, unstable frame rates, blurry visuals, audio glitches, broken missions, and even lost progress due to saving issues.

The shooting mechanics feel clunky, the controls can be frustrating, and the slow progression makes the experience unnecessarily tedious. For a game with such a long development cycle and an $80 price tag, expectations were understandably much higher.

GTA VI has enormous potential, but its launch problems make it difficult to recommend without reservations. Rockstar should have delivered a more polished experience instead of relying on future patches to address major issues. Beautiful world, disappointing execution

author: Tommy3009
quote: After 13 years of waiting, GTA VI has exceeded my expectations.I’ve been playing GTA since the very first game, and what Rockstar has achieved here is genuinely extraordinary. It’s not just about the stunning graphics or the massive map. It’s about how alive, reactive, and unpredictable the world feels.Here are some of my personal gameplay experiences:I was simply heading to a gun store when three gang members suddenly confronted me, apparently seeking revenge for an earlier mission. After a shootout, I crashed my car while escaping and had to continue on foot. Later, I discovered that the police were still investigating the original crime scene.Another time, I heard police sirens in the distance and decided to investigate. Officers were arresting someone and confiscating a bag. I casually approached them, made some friendly small talk, waited for the evidence to be placed inside their patrol car, and then stole the entire police vehicle!The new wanted system is incredible. After a minor collision with a police car, I got out, apologized to the officer, and the situation was resolved without a chase. In another incident, I managed to walk past officers searching for me after changing my appearance. They told me to leave the area, and I simply walked away.I’ve also been randomly mugged outside a gun store in broad daylight. Unfortunately for the robber, I had no cash on me. His frustrated reaction? “****, nobody has any money around here!” And one of my favorite discoveries happened when I followed a group of stray dogs through Port Gellhorn. They disappeared through a hole in a wall, leading me to a creepy abandoned building containing missing-person posters, disturbing mannequins, and mysterious photographs. Investigating the photos actually unlocked a new mystery involving the locations where they were taken.None of these experiences were things I had planned.That’s what makes GTA VI so special. You start with a simple objective, get distracted by something happening in the world, and suddenly find yourself in an entirely different adventure.I’ve spent countless hours exploring and still feel like I’ve barely scratched the surface of **** atmosphere is phenomenal, the attention to detail is staggering, the satire is hilarious, and the interconnected gameplay systems create a level of immersion I’ve rarely **** it technically flawless? No. I’ve encountered a minor animation bug, and the 30 FPS limit is a legitimate criticism. But neither comes close to overshadowing what Rockstar has **** VI doesn’t just give you missions to complete. It gives you a world in which your own stories unfold **** me, that’s the greatest achievement an open-world game can accomplish.

author: rokan_91
quote:
TLDR: This game is not GTA. Whoever worked on the previous *actual* GTA games are clearly no longer at Rockstar and the people who replaced them do not understand the core DNA of GTA and what made it fun for the world to halt for its release. Also, Gaming Journos and Critic reviews are highly misleading. Do not buy the game unless its on a steep discount.


Pros: The environment and lighting looks phenomenal and is setting a high bar for AAAA game.


Cons: The environment and lighting looks phenomenal as long as you do not move too much through the environment as the Frame rate drops well below 30 FPS during driving and moving through places with a lot of things going on. These frame drops are highly distinguishable on a PS5 Pro, I would not be surprised if the experience is even worse for the base PS5 users displaying a lack of any meaningful game optimization.

If you have played any GTA game previously, it is abundantly clear that this game is not Grand Theft Auto or even remotely close to it as the story is an absolute mess and quite far from the usual dark comedy like elements that GTA traditionally follows. The "partner" mechanic is an odd choice with non-optional game mechanics and *chores* that are mind numbing but sortof mandatory as it impacts the actual story ending - whoever thought this was a good idea at Rockstar needs to be removed from their position.

You cannot cause chaos and kill NPCs etc in the world freely as you stack up bad "Karma" which again impacts the story ending - this is a far departure from the core GTA mechanics in previous games where players could treat the world as a sandbox and cause chaos and this would not impact the main story. These types of story impacting mechanics are horrible and quite anti-GTA like as if the people finalising these mechanics as features at Rockstar never actually played any of the GTA games. If you do want to cause chaos - create backup save files otherwise it will impact the story ending.

For a game called Grand Theft Auto, you actually cannot commit *Grand Theft Auto* freely. The new mechanics cripple the core features that made GTA fun, such as being able to take over different cars and try them out across the open world as now you cannot steal any and all cars you see and require kits/things to be able to *try and steal* them.

There are rendering bugs where objects appear out of nowhere when you get close to certain environments, such as a ship appearing in the middle of a highway, patches of grass suddenly appearing on the side of the road when you drive by, Lucia's torso and legs missing etc.

Weird and unnecessary limitations on killing certain NPCs till a particular story event (relating to a bear) which again take out the fun from GTA.

Gatekeeping certain stores behind a Premium and more expensive edition of a digital game is a plain cash grab.


All in all, the gaming journalists and critic reviews come across as misleading as there are clear and significant gaps in the game overall. Just because a game looks graphically beautiful (mostly when stationary) does not qualify for a high score and even from a somewhat open world sandbox environment, there are far better games out there that have done a better job at being gamer centric, such as Crimson Desert. Anyone looking to try out "GTA 6" please know that this is a RDR2 like game pretending to be GTA and is not worth its price. Wait for massive discounts if you are really curious about it. Also, for anyone stating that the game is being review bombed - the name Grand Theft Auto has a lot of nostalgia for players such as I who have played every single GTA starting the 90's. Seeing the game being crippled and destroyed in the way GTA 6 has done is heartbreaking.

author: Leira_Martin
quote:
The greatest game of all time. In an era where dopamine is abundant, the game starts off slow—just as things normally would in real life—and that’s going to turn off a lot of people, just like what happened with RDR2.
It gradually pulls you into a love story where every detail—both in missions and in downtime—gives you a feeling that easily mirrors real life. A lot of people get stuck on that first impression of potential frustration because of the hype they built up themselves. Playing RDR2 makes you appreciate this GTA more and have more patience for it. It’s not what many would expect from a GTA, but it’s what the franchise needed; you have the other GTAs if you want to play the same old formula that used to define GTA, where you didn’t have an honor system or communication with NPCs, just to name two legacies from RDR2. In a few months, the game is going to be much more appreciated, just like what happened with RDR2.

author: Michaelhrustic
quote:
8.5/10 for me!
GTA 6 is phenomenal visually, and the open world feels incredibly alive. There’s so much to explore that I can play for hours without getting bored. I really like Jason and Lucia, and the story has been interesting so far at around 33% completion. 

My biggest issues are the clunky controls, particularly shooting, and the painfully slow progression. Even after 30+ hours, a lot of core content is still locked, while stores and other activities often feel lacking. The world looks incredibly detailed, but it doesn’t always have the depth to match it. NPC interactions are often limited to basic dialogue, with very few meaningful relationships outside of Lucia. It’s also strange that the phone no longer has a number pad, removing the ability to call random numbers like in previous games.

Despite these issues, I’m really enjoying it. It feels fresh, and I can easily see myself putting many more hours into it.

author: Anchorsify
quote:
A modern-day love story told in the satirical and larger-than-life stylings of GTA, in a way that no one else can do it.  If you aren't *looking* for a love story (and as the user scores will show you, many people did NOT want a love story), then it may not be your cup of tea--but they were never hiding the fact that it's about two people in a relationship, and the marketing was honest about it from the start they were involved and could not be fully separated. 

But just as you couldn't just decide as Michael (or Trevor, or Franklin) to simply up and abandon the other two main characters, you can't do so now, only 'this' time it is a problem because there's a romantic relationship involved as well.  

In a lot of ways this game is more of a modern RDR2 than it is a visually upgraded and improved GTA5--the game is slower at times, it knows how to let itself (and you) breathe, and it isn't as much of a parody of itself in the way that GTA 5 was.  It takes itself more seriously, and expects you to take it more seriously (partially through a reputation system that can see you become 'irredeemable', locking you into a 'bad' ending), likewise.  But if you were okay with *the world* around you being satirical while you yourself played the straight man to the nonsense going on around you, then you'll enjoy it plenty.

The wanted system has been greatly improved with a "heat" system that, like with RDR 2, takes into account more than just your wanted level, but also takes into account your clothing, your car, and even whether you are riding solo or with your partner, and changing your clothing/car/splitting up can result in you losing the cops easier than if you just tried to make a run for it.  The police are smarter about chasing and the higher wanted levels are more dangerous than before, adding to the stakes the game is setting up for you as a pair of criminals trying to make it as they start from rock bottom and work their way up.

They took risks, and some people aren't happy about it, but you can't deny that they had a clear idea of what they wanted to do and they did it well, and with style that goes on for miles and miles.  GTA 6 is a game where you can literally get lost in it for hours, days, weeks at a time, and you could spend months traveling around Vice City and not see everything there is that's been hand-crafted for you to find.  The sheer breadth of the game's complexity is mind blowing, and it is a clear work of passion, and art, that is unlikely to ever be replicated (owing, in part, to the sheer insanity of its budget, that was made back within the first day of its release, possibly two times over).

It's a must-play, in much the same vein as the likes of Ocarina of Time, Metal Gear Solid 3, Chrono Trigger, Elden Ring, and Terraria.  It is a game that is unlikely to ever be matched, much less surpassed, in its genre, and it knows it by the way it presents itself, from start to finish.

author: oldhermittt
quote:
Technically Impressive, Artistically Underwhelming:

The environmental fidelity, asset density, material rendering and world simulation are exceptional. However, the visual presentation feels surprisingly generic and sterile. The extensive reliance on photorealistic assets, physically based materials and high-frequency environmental detail creates a convincing world without necessarily establishing a cohesive artistic identity. Some scenes remind me of Watch Dogs Legion, Just Cause or any other contemporary Ubisoft titles.

I'm also questioning R.A.G.E's rendering and camera presentation. The in-game camera, field of view, focal perspective, exposure and post-processing seem to produce a somewhat flat, neutral image. It lacks the distinctive cinematic composition, atmospheric depth and visual hierarchy that made RDR2 so compelling. I wonder whether Rockstar has changed its camera configuration and rendering pipeline in ways that favour realism over its previously recognizable visual signature. Vice City had a deliberately constructed visual language; RDR2 had exceptional atmospheric composition, colour grading and environmental storytelling. GTA VI currently feels more focused on geographical realism than artistic interpretation.

Mission design is another concern. Repetitive acquisition objectives, criminal errands and relatively linear sequences make progression feel procedural rather than rewarding. The issue isn't the activities themselves, but the limited mechanical variety and escalation between missions. Narratively, Jason and Lucia are an interesting dual-protagonist concept, but their shared motivations provide less character contrast than GTA V's three protagonists. So far, the campaign hasn't established the emotional complexity and character development that made Arthur Morgan's journey so compelling.

GTA VI demonstrates extraordinary technical execution, but graphical fidelity, simulation complexity and environmental density are not substitutes for art direction, gameplay variety or narrative cohesion.Rockstar has seemingly perfected the technology of building a believable world. I'm still waiting for that world to feel unmistakably like a Rockstar creation.

author: Al_noire_
quote: 10 hours into the game, and I haven’t even finished Chapter 1. The world feels so alive that I just want to live in it for as long as I can.This is the first Rockstar game where I’ve found myself putting my character to bed, making sure he eats well almost every day, and genuinely enjoying all these little routines. They already touched on this territory in RDR2, which is now my second favourite game, but here they’ve gone all in on realism.Late-night drives through Leonida Keys remind me of being on vacation somewhere warm. There’s something genuinely joyful about just stopping by an in-game version of 7-Eleven to grab a late-night **** story and characters are already the most compelling of any GTA game for me. From the moment I saw the prologue, I was hooked and on the edge of my seat, wanting to make the best possible life for these two. Of course, there’s still a lot more to **** terms of gameplay, even almost causing an accident makes me physically lean forward in my seat because of how much weight and responsibility I feel behind the wheel.I was also pleasantly surprised by the stealth mechanics. It’s a huge step up from previous Rockstar games. In something like Cayo Perico, you basically had one optimal approach if you wanted to stay undetected. Here, Rockstar gives you a proper sandbox with different ways to approach situations, and I love that.

There is no 'grand theft auto' once you get to open world. (Took me about 30mins to speed run it til the world opens up). Once the game starts,  you are automatically on a series of chore quest lines. Fixing up your house,  getting groceries for your ex con gf, getting her flowers, if you're looking to play gta: the Sims edition,  this is for you.  But if you're looking for an escape from reality, this is NOT for you. Best part is,  if you're like me and got sold on it based on gta3-gta5 or RDRD2, and you preloaded it, that voids any option for a refund.  If you told me 13 years ago that I would end up hating gta  6, I'd say better chance that AI will take over the world  the promise and hype plus the pedigree of Rockstar sold me to blindly preorder. I can wait for the PC version to fix the performance issues, but nothing can change what's fundamentally wrong with the game.  It's not true to past gtas and has political agenda all over it.  This is a woke edutainment game that is a PG version of what made it famous/infamous. I just can't understand the $2.5 billion budget that ignores the fan base that blindly gave them billions of dollars in preorders. If Rockstar is still around for gta 7, I certainly won't be.  You live and you learn.  Luckily they only got me for only $80, but I have many dedicated friends who lost $100, just so they can access haircut shops, tattoo and couple side missions (that they will never see because they have no plans to get that far into the game). This game is the epitome of financial and fan base  hype into disappointment. Creating something so great and then choosing to go the opposite way because of political agenda is crazy when this was created under capitalism.  I never thought I'd say this but I hope saints row learns from this and comes out with their own counter/antiwoke version.  Sorry if I yucked your yum. This was not made for me.  I can keep gong on for hours about what's wrong about this game. But there's actually good games i have to get to.   I may update to take up the remainder 2000 characters o have left.

author: edwinvs
quote:
Una auténtica obra maestra para disfrutar. Rockstar vuelve a demostrar por qué está en otro nivel cuando se trata de crear mundos abiertos. Y es que lo que más me sorprende de GTA VI no son solamente sus gráficos o su apartado técnico, sino la vida que tiene cada rincón del juego.

La evolución que vimos en Red Dead Redemption 2 se siente muchísimo aquí. Los NPC, sus comportamientos, las conversaciones, los acontecimientos aleatorios y la cantidad de detalles hacen que el mundo se sienta vivo de una manera increíble. No tienes la sensación de estar recorriendo un mapa esperando la siguiente misión, sino de estar dentro de un mundo que sigue funcionando incluso cuando tú no haces nada.

La ambientación, los personajes, la libertad y la atención al detalle son sencillamente espectaculares. Me encanta que Rockstar no se haya limitado a repetir la fórmula de sus entregas anteriores, sino que haya tomado todo lo aprendido durante estos años para llevar la experiencia a otro nivel.

Entiendo que muchos sientan nostalgia por los GTA clásicos, porque yo también crecí con ellos, pero creo que hay que saber apreciar la evolución de una saga. No todos los juegos tienen que hacernos sentir lo mismo que hace 15 o 20 años para ser buenos.

Para mí, GTA VI es de esos juegos que te recuerdan por qué te enamoraste de los videojuegos. Es una experiencia que va mucho más allá de completar misiones. Poder perderte en su mundo y disfrutar hasta de los pequeños detalles es algo que muy pocos estudios consiguen. Un 10/10 más que merecido.

author: marcprat23
quote:
A masterpiece. We won't experience anything like this in the industry for many years to come.

It has the most alive, polished, and organic open world I've ever seen.

One day, you wake up in the morning and find yourself in the Grassrivers, stealing cocaine from drug dealers. Another day, you're in Hamlet racing motocross bikes. The next, you're robbing a liquor store or taking your partner out dancing at the most exclusive nightclub in Vice City. Who knows, maybe one day you'll even be stealing your neighbour's bike.

GTA VI is fun, varied, and deeply immersive. It's a game with a slow-paced but profound narrative that makes you empathise with each protagonist. You'll have to make a conscious effort to remember that you're playing a video game, because most of the time, you'll feel like you're a criminal living in the craziest, most ambitious, and most incredible city ever created.

author: RyuuTearzz
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI — 10/10
A Masterpiece Being Judged by People Who Would Rather Complain Than Play
Score: 10/10
Grand Theft Auto VI is nothing short of extraordinary. Rockstar has once again demonstrated why they remain in a league of their own when it comes to open-world gaming. The level of immersion, attention to detail, storytelling, world-building, and sheer ambition on display here is something that deserves to be celebrated, not buried underneath an avalanche of review bombing from people who seemingly had their minds made up before even picking up a ****'s talk about the actual **** immersion is absolutely insane. The world feels alive in a way that very few games have ever managed to accomplish. The graphics are phenomenal, the environments are incredibly detailed, and the attention Rockstar has put into making the world feel believable is staggering. This isn't just a pretty map filled with activities. It's a living, breathing world that constantly gives you reasons to explore, experiment, and get lost in **** storytelling and character development are another massive achievement. Lucia and Jason bring something special to the experience, and the relationship between them adds another layer to the narrative. Rockstar deserves credit for taking the time to develop these characters rather than simply throwing players into another generic crime story.
And speaking of Lucia, can we address some of the ridiculous complaints surrounding the relationship mechanics? Apparently, some people cannot comprehend the concept of OPTIONAL content. You aren't being forced to participate in every relationship interaction or engage with every mechanic. It's there for players who want to experience that side of the game. Don't like it? Don't participate. It's genuinely that simple. Not every optional feature needs to cater to every individual player's preferences.
The new wanted system is another fantastic evolution. Police encounters feel more dynamic, the consequences of your actions are more interesting, and escaping the law feels like an actual experience rather than simply driving around until your wanted level disappears. It's a meaningful improvement to one of the most recognizable mechanics in the entire franchise. There's also the freedom to make money and approach the criminal lifestyle in different ways. Having more opportunities to earn money, explore different activities, and build your own experience makes the world feel considerably more engaging. It's the kind of freedom that makes Grand Theft Auto what it **** perhaps the most disappointing part of this entire release is watching people attempt to discredit the game for reasons that have absolutely nothing to do with its actual quality.
Review bombing because you disagree with a character, a storyline, a relationship mechanic, Rockstar's creative decisions, or some perceived agenda isn't legitimate criticism. You're entitled to dislike whatever you want. You're entitled to have your own opinions. But there's a pretty significant difference between criticizing a game you've actually experienced and deciding you hate something before giving it a fair chance. A review score should reflect the game itself. The gameplay, presentation, storytelling, technical achievements, immersion, and overall experience. Not personal agendas, internet outrage, or an attempt to punish developers for making creative decisions you don't personally agree **** don't have to love every single feature. You don't have to agree with every narrative decision. But pretending those disagreements somehow erase the enormous amount of craftsmanship that went into this game is ridiculous.Rockstar didn't just make another Grand Theft Auto. They pushed the boundaries of what an open-world experience can **** immersion is incredible. The storytelling is compelling. The world is breathtaking. The gameplay systems have evolved. The freedom to play your way is still at the heart of the experience.**10/10.**And to anyone review bombing this game without giving it a legitimate chance: you're welcome to your opinion, but at least have the integrity to judge the game you're reviewing rather than the imaginary version you've convinced yourself to hate. This is Grand Theft Auto. And Rockstar has delivered.

author: bielll007l__
quote:
Sinceramente, eu não consigo entender algumas das críticas negativas que estão sendo direcionadas a GTA 6, principalmente quando vejo a nota de usuário como 5,5 no Metacritic. E a pergunta que fica é: o que exatamente essas pessoas estão esperando de um jogo? Porque, pelo que foi apresentado até agora, estamos diante de algo que tem potencial para redefinir mais uma vez os padrões da indústria dos videogames.

Vamos começar pelos gráficos. O nível de detalhe apresentado é simplesmente absurdo. Não estamos falando apenas de personagens bonitos ou cenários com texturas em alta resolução. Estamos falando de um mundo que transmite vida, com iluminação impressionante, reflexos, vegetação, ambientes extremamente detalhados e uma qualidade visual que, em diversos momentos, chega a parecer cinematográfica. Cada trailer divulgado demonstra um cuidado técnico gigantesco.

Mas o que mais me impressiona não é apenas a parte visual. É a sensação de que estamos diante de um mundo verdadeiramente vivo.

Os NPCs, por exemplo, merecem uma atenção especial. A Rockstar parece estar elevando o nível de interação e comportamento dos personagens secundários. A movimentação das pessoas, as situações acontecendo nas ruas, as reações, a variedade de atividades e a sensação de que existe uma sociedade funcionando ao redor do jogador são aspectos que podem transformar completamente a experiência. Não é simplesmente colocar milhares de personagens andando pelo mapa. É fazer com que o mundo pareça existir mesmo quando não estamos olhando para ele.

E isso é algo que não pode ser ignorado.

A ambientação de Vice City também parece extraordinária. A riqueza dos cenários, a identidade visual, a diversidade dos ambientes e a quantidade de detalhes demonstram uma produção extremamente ambiciosa. Parece que cada região foi pensada para transmitir uma personalidade própria.

Outro ponto importante é a evolução da tecnologia utilizada para construir esse universo. A Rockstar não está simplesmente tentando entregar mais do mesmo. A impressão é que existe uma preocupação enorme em aprimorar praticamente todos os elementos que fizeram GTA V ser um fenômeno mundial: mundo aberto, narrativa, personagens, física, animações, imersão e liberdade.

E é justamente por isso que eu questiono essa nota 5,5.

Será que algumas pessoas estão realmente avaliando o jogo pelo que foi apresentado ou estão descontando expectativas pessoais, frustrações e até mesmo implicâncias com a Rockstar? Será que estamos perdendo a capacidade de reconhecer quando um estúdio demonstra um nível de ambição técnica e artística fora do comum?

É claro que nenhum jogo está acima de críticas. GTA 6 também precisará ser avaliado por sua história, missões, jogabilidade, desempenho, otimização e conteúdo quando estiver disponível. Não estou dizendo que o jogo precisa receber nota 10 automaticamente ou que não possa decepcionar em algum aspecto.

Mas existe uma diferença enorme entre ter expectativas e simplesmente desvalorizar um projeto antes de conhecer sua experiência completa.

O que vimos até agora demonstra um trabalho impressionante. A atenção aos detalhes, a construção do mundo, a qualidade visual e a ambição de criar uma experiência ainda mais imersiva são motivos suficientes para reconhecer que estamos diante de um dos projetos mais importantes da história dos videogames.

A Rockstar já demonstrou diversas vezes que sabe construir mundos memoráveis. Red Dead Redemption 2 é um exemplo gigantesco disso. E GTA 6 parece querer levar essa filosofia para uma escala ainda maior.

No final das contas, minha dúvida continua: o que exatamente essas pessoas não estão gostando? Os gráficos? A ambientação? Os NPCs? O nível de detalhes? A evolução técnica?

Quero entender quais são os argumentos por trás de uma avaliação tão baixa.

Porque uma coisa é não gostar de GTA, outra é não reconhecer a dimensão do que está sendo apresentado.

GTA 6 tem potencial para ser um divisor de águas. E, sinceramente, depois de tudo que foi mostrado, acho muito cedo para tratar um projeto dessa magnitude como se fosse apenas mais um lançamento qualquer.

A Rockstar não está apenas fazendo mais um GTA. Está tentando estabelecer um novo patamar para os jogos de mundo aberto. E isso, por si só, já merece ser reconhecido.

author: DarkSaibot3
quote:
Is this the greatest game of all time like many claim? No, not even close. Both sides  of the spectrum are objectively wrong however & don't actually believe what they say about the game. 
Those claiming it is perfect like to ignore all of the game's faults & attempt to make a negative into a positive whereas many detractors find faults where there are none.
So here is a proper review not fueled by bias, the mission design is as bad as it has always been & Rockstar still fails to innovate their mission design since 2001. The story? Pretty good but nothing ground breaking & certainly weaker in comparison to GTA V or GTA IV & repeats previous story beats such as the police corruption story-line. The characters? Immaculate & Rockstar always has been very good in creating compelling characters & they still are here & I love the realistic way in which people are portrayed, it feels natural. 
Now on a different note about realism, the realistic mechanics just aren't implemented that well, fuel exists even though it really doesn't matter I have only ever needed to refuel my car about 3 times in the entire playthrough.
I love how the game handles money, it really feels like a slow grind at the start but as Jason & Lucia begin to expand their talents across south beach, money comes easier & it's a really well done natural progression unlike in GTA V which faulted in that area. 
The dynamic between Jason & Lucia is handled really well & the acting is also superb however, Jason feels like a blank slate, he feels like a Claude Speed who can talk whereas Lucia has a really strong personality. It works well together but makes playing as Jason alone a little underwhelming.
The map, it's massive & it's beautiful, but it's also a waste of space. I know the map was likely designed with multiplayer mostly in mind because in multiplayer big empty maps are good to divide players but it doesn't work well in single player. As gorgeous & well designed the world is, it's relatively barren, the claim that most of the interiors in the game are accessible is technically correct, they just padded that number by just putting in hundreds of little shops all across Vice City that you will almost never need to access & are direct clones of one another & you cannot enter most other interiors such as houses along the Keys unlike San Andreas.
The frame rate is in fact a bit of an issue, during normal gameplay on foot or combat sections the frame rate is generally hitting that 30 FPS limit & it works fine, however, when you go out into the forest... I was hitting 10 FPS at one point & driving fast will naturally break the frame rate which does hurt the game as you do need to drive fast in many an instance.
All those complaining about all the nudity clearly haven't been outside in a very long time, it's not like the Sopranos is considered one of the greatest shows of all time & takes place in a Strip Club half the time... it's not like Game Of Thrones has sex in it that is more explicit than implicit... it's just a nonsensical argument made by nonsensical people. To be jealous about a bunch of pixels? That's crazy.
The combat is fine but nothing new or groundbreaking yet again, the stealth mechanics are very bare bones & enemy AI is as dumb as ever in this game. They do not have a semblance of peripheral vision that is for sure. 
Also the story is a little over 30 hours long so I have no idea what those reviewers were talking about it being 80 hours.
The new phone mechanics were cool but clearly are there to be built upon & this wasn't a finished version of them because it still feels pretty useless, going on Snapmatic can be a little fun but really doesn't offer much. The purchasable properties are pretty lackluster & I kinda woulda hoped they added GTA Online mechanics to the single player such as running businesses in single player but alas it is not to be. 
The main thing that brings this game down was the hype around it. While I was never delusional enough to ever think this would be the greatest game ever made, I thought that maybe Rockstar could actually innovate their game design for this game & iron out the flaws from previous titles but it didn't. Rockstar games have always been overrated, they're good not great games & I feel like too many people use nostalgia to convince themselves they're playing greatness. 
It's not like things never live up to the hype, LeBron lived up to his hype, Wembanyama has been living up to his hype & if you know anything about sports you know the hype was just as big as GTA VI as it was for these dudes, it's just a good game, not great, not some second coming of Jesus, & it certainly does not live up to the hype. (Also the graphics are superb but hardly what matters in a game otherwise Undertale would be a bad game right?)

author: banhmisaurus
quote:
Here's the review from someone who actually play the game and didn't give a damn about political scandals around this game then complains about something because they experienced it via Youtube or X/Twitter:

I've spent 35 hours into the game, might be progressed half of the story. This game is now my number 1 open-world sandbox experience.

Just like RDR2, the game have very slow start but everything eventually came into the right direction. I am a big GTA series and RDR2 fan, I believe this game would please RDR2 fans more than GTA V fans.

The game had big expectations from everyone but I personally see it passed for most of what I expected it needs to be. The story is what expect very little because Dan Houser left, the one who took the most responsible for all the games of Rockstar before GTA VI. He laid the foundations of what Rockstar Games is today.

Obviously, the graphics is great. I can't say enough about it. The world details and environments. The density of the cars and NPCs is so insane that I thought my PS5 Pro would explode. I thought the NPCs would make me want to kill them less like how RDR2 did to me, but they most of them ended making me want to slaughter them like how GTA V did.
Obviously, it will be much better if it comes to PC, I am happy to buy this game again there (hopefully Steam pls)

What I disappointed the most would be the aircraft mechanics, I hoped it could get a bit more complicated. It ended up being pretty much the same as GTA V.

The story is weak. Might be the weakest and most anticlimactic story in the franchise, that was the first impression of mine until the end of Chapter 1. However, the game focused too much on the relationship between Jason and Lucia too much is also make it the most boring parts of the story.

The game had a slow start and i can see that many people will quit before they can get to Chapter 2, which I believe they would stuck like 6-10 hours in chapter 1. Same as RDR2, I know many people quit the game because Chapter 1 bored them because how slow it was. Unlike GTA V where the game started with a bank robbery, GTA VI started with a slow love story. They should've understand that adults is the one that playing this game the most and love stories isn't consumed as well as teenagers anymore to decide the game pacing.

Overall, this is not a game you can judge without playing it. I had friends on Discord who didn't interest on the game until I stream it for them and let them decide what I do in that game and now they asking me to go find all those stuffs they saw on Tiktok about this game.
