author: Aridian
quote:
If you read nothing else, read this…

GTA6 is a breath of fresh air. The gaming industry is plagued by games giving you the straight line and making everything linear garbage. Rockstar & T2 have found a way to give you an immersive world that feels like you’re actually living inside of it. People keep throwing around buzzwords like “simp” “slop” “woke” and other controversial slang to feel like they’re a part of something that’s standing for the greater good. For the most part the reviews that are low are “ZELDA GOOD, THIS BAD!” Which is like comparing apples to oranges. 

Yes, OoT is fantastic, but GTA has reinvented the open world experience in a once-in-a-lifetime package. Comparing this game to anything that came before it is unreasonable and just distasteful. 

Lucia is a feisty Latina and her actions and mannerisms are exactly as you’d expect them to be when she’s challenged, tried, and forced to act out of self defense. We are introduced to her and Jason as convicts and people trying to do right in life. Of course, given the nature of the game it’ll be a complex issue and they’re going to delve into a life of crime. 

As for the NPCs surrounding the game, it feels alive. I watched a TV show for around thirty minutes before I could pull myself away to continue the story. I shot pool at a dive bar, I went diving for treasure, I went fishing, I partied in a club, I adventured and ran cocaine. This game has a little bit of enjoyment for anyone seeking it as long as you’re not focusing on steamrolling the story. It deserves your time and attention, that’s what I liked about the chores, housekeeping, working out, and fixing the house for your baby mama to have a nice place to relax. 

There’s 100 naysayers for every 1 positive review, I get it. But if your basis on choosing **** is good or not revolves around some loser online who otherwise can’t get a grasp on reality themselves, you need help as is. This game is as perfect as it gets, don’t listen to the online Chads, review bombing crybabies, and the “ITS 30FPS” crowd. In my 15 hours of gameplay I just completed Chapter 1 and I’ve not experienced any issues that make the game even feel like it stutters. 

Get out there in Vice City and have the time of your life. This game is a 10/10 for a reason, most people just can’t see it because their heads are infested with political buzzwords and a common lack of understanding what makes a game feel original and fleshed out.

author: armalock
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI — 9/10

GTA 6 is an incredible experience and easily one of the most memorable games I've played. The world is ridiculously detailed, the atmosphere is phenomenal, and the amount of effort put into making Vice City and Leonida feel alive is genuinely impressive. The characters, storytelling, world-building, random encounters, and countless little details make exploring the world an experience of its own.

What makes this game special is how immersive everything feels. You can tell Rockstar put an insane amount of work into creating a living, breathing world. There's always something interesting happening, and the attention to detail is on another level.

However, I do have two criticisms.

First, the 30 FPS cap. For a game this ambitious, I really wish we had a 60 FPS option. The experience would feel considerably smoother, especially during driving and combat.

Second, Jason's character portrayal. I wasn't entirely satisfied with how his character was written and presented. I think there's room for improvement in his personality and overall characterization.

Despite those criticisms, GTA 6 is still an outstanding game. Neither issue takes away from the incredible world Rockstar has created.

Final Rating: 9/10

author: MMartinsArt
quote:
GTA 6 is about much more than celebrating crime. It's a biting satire of contemporary society, its contradictions, and its hypocrisies.

The game uses exaggeration, sarcasm, and provocation to satirize just about everything: lifestyles, behavior, values, and ideological movements. No one seems to be above criticism. The culture of conspicuous consumption, the superficiality of human relationships, the obsession with money, moral hypocrisy, the erosion of values, and the desperate need for validation are all portrayed in deliberately grotesque ways.

And here's a point that seems to fly over the heads of many critics, especially those who insist on seeing some supposed glorification of criminal activity: as the story unfolds, that accusation becomes increasingly difficult to defend. GTA 6 doesn't portray crime as some glamorous path to freedom, success, or upward mobility. Quite the opposite. It depicts a world defined by violence, paranoia, betrayal, instability, and consequences. The money may come, but peace of mind disappears. Power may be gained, but it comes at a price. And the freedom everyone longs for often ends up becoming a prison of their own making.

That's precisely where the storytelling becomes so compelling. At certain points, the character development bears a striking resemblance to Breaking Bad: we watch morally compromised individuals gradually deteriorate, rationalize their own decisions, cross one line after another, and ultimately become prisoners of their own ambitions.

The problem is that some critics seem to struggle with a fairly basic distinction: depicting something doesn't mean endorsing it, just as satirizing something doesn't mean defending it. Portraying criminals doesn't mean glorifying crime. Exposing a decadent society doesn't mean celebrating its decadence. A work of fiction doesn't need to turn its characters into moral role models to offer a meaningful moral reflection.

And this discussion becomes even more interesting when we look at the tendency among certain corners of cultural criticism to interpret works of art through ideological filters, as though every portrayal must undergo some kind of moral approval process or conform to a particular political alignment. When a work challenges, mocks, or satirizes certain behaviors and ideas, the first instinct of some critics seems to be hunting for a supposedly problematic message rather than understanding the context and narrative **** 6 seems to do precisely the opposite of what its more superficial critics claim: rather than turning crime into an ideal way of life, it exposes the illusion behind it. Behind the flashy lifestyle lies emptiness. Behind the promise of easy money lies instability. And behind the appearance of freedom lies an ever-growing dependence on violence and increasingly destructive choices.

Ultimately, perhaps GTA 6's most powerful criticism isn't directed solely at the criminal underworld, but at contemporary society itself, which seems to have lost the ability to distinguish success from showing off, freedom from a complete lack of boundaries, and personal fulfillment from instant gratification.

The game doesn't need to deliver a preachy moral lecture to show that crime doesn't pay. It simply needs to show what happens to those who make it their way of life. And perhaps that's exactly what makes it so uncomfortable for some people: GTA 6 doesn't offer a sanitized narrative designed to satisfy ideological expectations. It challenges, satirizes, and exposes contradictions. It's up to the audience to have the maturity to understand the difference between a work that portrays reality and one that seeks to dictate how we should see it.

The game is packed with satire and humour across its story, characters, radio stations, adverts and world, the game world  is still just as hilarious as any other entry into the GTA franchise, the only difference being that its main story is much more like the serious and grounded story of RDR2 or even GTA 4 than the more goofy and unrealistic (but definitely very fun) story of GTA 5 

Sidenote - to the People saying this game is cuck simulator or that Jason is a simp, it is clear you have A) never had a functioning and healthy relationship , or B) Your chronically single and unloved. 
Doing (completely optional by the way) quests like buying flowers or buying groceries for your partner is genuinely what a good partner should do, if you think that buying gifts for your partner is being a simp, then maybe reflect on why all of your relationships have been so dysfunctional and realise that loving someone enough to do selfless favours for them is not some sort of emasculating thing, it’s genuinely the opposite, coming from a man in long term relationship. Anyways rant over 

Overall, if your into more intimate games that focus on truly immersing yourself into the game world and all of its endless side content (with the occasional rampage and murder fest), you will Honeslty love this game 

If your more into arcade style games, where the story takes the back seat and is moreso there to facilitate intense and slapstick action and humour, then you will probably struggle to enjoy this game 

I give this game a 9/10 out of my own personal experiences and preferences , but I can understand why people would put it lower (anything lower then a 6 I would say are objectively wrong, even if you don’t enjoy the story, you have to atleast appreciate the games immense scale and endless amount of side content)

author: MorfenA
quote: Grand Theft Auto VI: A Disappointing ExpectationMaybe my expectations were simply too high, but after 20 hours, I find myself struggling to understand what makes this game so extraordinary. In fact, the biggest indicator of my disappointment is that I can comfortably put the controller down, go to sleep, and continue my normal schedule. I don’t feel that irresistible urge to keep playing. I actually had to force myself through those 20 **** first 15 hours feel more like a romantic drama about a boyfriend and girlfriend than a Grand Theft Auto game. I’m not saying Jason and Lucia are inherently uninteresting characters, but their relationship takes up so much of the experience that the criminal world I came here for feels secondary. Jason, in particular, comes across as strangely robotic rather than a believable human being. I struggled to connect with him.Coming from Red Dead Redemption 2, where Rockstar managed to create such a compelling and powerful protagonist, the contrast is difficult to ignore. I simply don’t feel that same presence, personality, or sense of masculinity in Jason. The overall tone also feels surprisingly soft and relationship-driven for a franchise that built its identity around crime, chaos, and criminal **** be fair, the mechanical side of the game and its world-building have their strengths. There is clearly an impressive amount of work behind this world. However, technical performance is another major disappointment. The 30 FPS target is not even consistently maintained, with noticeable drops that make the experience considerably worse. As someone accustomed to playing on PC at 80 to 100 FPS, adjusting to 30 FPS, sometimes dropping even lower, is genuinely frustrating.Ultimately, I’m not saying GTA VI is a bad game. But after all these years of anticipation, I expected something that would completely consume my attention. Instead, I find myself having to convince myself to play it. And for a Grand Theft Auto game, that might be the biggest disappointment of all.

author: 2CROW7
quote: Grand Theft Auto VI: Una obra maestra que redefine los videojuegos (10/10)Grand Theft Auto VI es una auténtica maravilla del entretenimiento interactivo. Rockstar Games ha conseguido superar las expectativas de millones de jugadores y ofrecer una experiencia que demuestra hasta dónde puede llegar la industria cuando se combina ambición, creatividad y atención al **** historia de Jason Duval y Lucia Caminos es uno de los mayores aciertos de esta entrega. Su relación constituye el corazón de la aventura. No estamos ante dos criminales que buscan dinero y reconocimiento, sino ante dos personas que intentan encontrar una oportunidad para cambiar sus vidas mientras el mundo parece empeñado en destruir sus **** química entre ambos protagonistas es excepcional. Sus conversaciones, discusiones, momentos románticos y situaciones cotidianas aportan una humanidad impresionante. Rockstar consigue que nos preocupemos por su futuro, haciendo que cada acontecimiento tenga un peso **** comienzo de la aventura, con Lucia saliendo de prisión y reencontrándose con Jason, establece perfectamente el tono de la historia. Lo que parece una oportunidad para conseguir dinero termina convirtiéndose en una peligrosa cadena de acontecimientos que involucra conspiraciones, traiciones y enfrentamientos con personajes **** llegada a Vice City y el contacto con figuras como Boobie Ike, Dre'Quan Priest y Raul Bautista amplían enormemente las posibilidades narrativas. Cada personaje aporta personalidad y profundidad a un universo criminal que se siente más vivo que **** de los aspectos más interesantes es cómo evoluciona la historia. El incidente del aeropuerto VCIA, la muerte de Karim y las consecuencias de los negocios criminales demuestran que los acontecimientos pueden tener consecuencias devastadoras. Especialmente impactante resulta el destino de Raul Bautista, cuyo desenlace aporta uno de los momentos más oscuros de la **** traición de Giorgio Gallo también merece una mención especial. Descubrir que alguien en quien los protagonistas depositaron su confianza termina convirtiéndose en una amenaza demuestra la capacidad de Rockstar para construir giros argumentales que mantienen al jugador **** recta final consigue mantener la tensión hasta el último momento. El enfrentamiento contra quienes han manipulado y utilizado a Jason y Lucia representa una conclusión cargada de emociones. Además, la posibilidad de diferentes desenlaces aporta un valor adicional, haciendo que el destino de los protagonistas sea todavía más **** el apartado técnico, GTA VI es sencillamente impresionante. Leonida es uno de los mundos abiertos más fascinantes que se pueden experimentar. Vice City está llena de personalidad, con una ambientación espectacular, escenarios detallados, personajes expresivos y situaciones que hacen que explorar sea una experiencia constante de **** gráficos, las animaciones, la iluminación y los efectos ambientales demuestran un nivel de trabajo excepcional. No se trata únicamente de ofrecer una imagen bonita, sino de construir un mundo que transmita autenticidad y mantenga al jugador completamente inmerso.También es admirable la cantidad de actividades y posibilidades que ofrece fuera de la historia principal. GTA VI entiende que un mundo abierto debe ser mucho más que un escenario para completar misiones. Su mayor virtud es conseguir que incluso los momentos alejados de la campaña resulten **** banda sonora, las emisoras de radio, el humor característico de la franquicia y la sátira social demuestran que Rockstar conoce perfectamente la identidad de Grand Theft **** más impresionante es que GTA VI consigue mantener su propia personalidad sin depender exclusivamente del legado de GTA V. Es una evolución natural, ambiciosa y respetuosa con aquello que convirtió a la saga en un fenómeno **** difícil encontrar una producción que reúna tantos elementos de calidad. Su narrativa, personajes, mundo abierto y presentación audiovisual forman un conjunto extraordinariamente sólido.VEREDICTO: 10/10.Grand Theft Auto VI es una obra maestra y una de las mayores demostraciones del potencial de los videojuegos. Jason y Lucia protagonizan una aventura memorable que combina acción, humor, drama y emoción de manera excepcional.Rockstar Games no solamente ha entregado una nueva entrega de Grand Theft Auto: ha construido una experiencia que merece ser recordada durante generaciones. Una auténtica celebración de los videojuegos y una aventura imprescindible.

author: Socrat72
quote:
Minor non-story spoilers and mild profanity.

Pure fun. Main criticism I had for GTA V was that I couldn’t properly feel like a criminal in the open world. This game fixes that by making literally EVERYTHING robbable (heistable?) Aside from that, Ive been having fun just throwing iguana corpses at pedestrians and witnessing the **** crazy random events in the world. The only reason its not a 10/10 is because I feel weirded out by the morality system, doesn’t really feel like GTA to me. Nonetheless, it isn’t that restrictive, you can maintain a good reputation by occasionally popping some poor schmuck’s knees during combat if it’s important to you. Reading other reviews, some people think it’s filled to the brim with chores, but that hasn’t been my experience. The few chores you do for Lucia only show up in chapter 1 and take a few minutes to do. If that’s still too much for you, they are completely optional. 

In terms of the main characters, they're a step below the writing of GTA V. Lucia is fine, Jason is boring. I don’t think it’s that big of a deal to warrant taking off a point, but it’s still important to mention. Side and background characters are funny as hell though, and it’s just fun doing whatever the **** outside and coming back to find a drunk guy asking for food in your car and refusing to get out. (I resorted to blowing his head off, but you can choose what to do with him yourself).

Overall, the game is just fun. It’s not this groundbreaking once-in-a-lifetime game like a lot of people wanted it to be, but it’s still very much worth experiencing. Only got through half of the story before writing this, but that’s been pretty good too, it isn’t anything crazy deep or extraordinary, but it’s engaging enough to make you want to continue. I’ve always been more about the fun factor of the game, but if you’re the type of person who cares more about the story, I think it’d be a 7.5/10 for you.

author: Shahinhp
quote:
My take after 30 hours of playing:
1. It's not "GTA" in the way people **** gameplay and graphics are incredible, but it isn't the GTA where you can go wild, kill anyone, and blow up the whole city without consequences. Rockstar designed the game so that the smallest mistake gets you wrecked, and escaping the cops, especially once you hit three stars, is extremely hard. It doesn't have the classic GTA thrill of mass chaos. But! But! This is exactly what everyone asked for. The chase system was talked about many times before release, so the complaining from some people is completely baseless when you knew it would be like this.
2. It has nothing to do with "woke."The "woke" stuff you see in other games just isn't here. The complaint is that you can't kill everyone, but the game revolves around the relationship between two people, so again, no complaining! You should have known that when a duo is at the center, the relationship has to be preserved. Fixing pipes, stairs, and roofs doesn't count as woke either, because exactly where Lucia can't do something properly, Jason does it right, which itself shows it isn't woke. If the game were woke, Lucia would do everything on her own without needing Jason.
Those are two of the main reasons players gave low scores. Otherwise, the game is great in every way, though not 100 out of 100, more like 92 to 95:
1. The game is extremely dynamic and everything feels alive, easily ten steps above Red Dead.
2. This graphics quality is perfectly fine at 30 FPS.
3. There are tons of buildings in the game that it never points you to, but you can walk in, explore, or rob them.There are so many things to do that you won't even know about them all.
Overall, it's a huge world that will keep you entertained for hundreds of hours, so don't doubt it for a second, and don't listen to the illogical **** for scoring, critics always hand out inflated scores to three companies, Rockstar, Nintendo, and FromSoftware, whether the game is good or bad. It's practically a tradition. Many games from these companies weren't at the level of a 95+ score, but they get one anyway.
This game isn't a 99 either; at best, it's a 93.

quote:
GTA 6 REVIEW – A MASTERPIECE WORTHY OF A PERFECT 10/10! 

Final Score: 10/10

If there is one game capable of redefining the entire gaming industry, Grand Theft Auto VI is undoubtedly one of the strongest contenders.

From its stunning trailers to its incredible attention to detail, GTA 6 has generated unprecedented excitement among gamers worldwide. Rockstar Games appears ready to deliver an unforgettable open-world experience that pushes the boundaries of modern gaming.

1. Graphics – 10/10

GTA 6 features breathtaking visuals, realistic lighting, detailed environments, impressive character animations, and incredibly immersive weather effects. Vice City looks more alive than ever, creating an open world that feels almost indistinguishable from reality.

2. Open World – 10/10

The world of GTA 6 looks incredibly rich and dynamic. Every location offers opportunities for exploration, interaction, and unexpected experiences. The level of freedom promises to make every player's journey unique.

3. Story and Characters – 10/10

Lucia and Jason bring a fresh perspective to the GTA universe. Their relationship, criminal ambitions, and dangerous adventures promise an emotional and action-packed storyline filled with unforgettable moments.

4. Gameplay – 10/10

From intense shootouts and thrilling car chases to exciting missions and countless activities, GTA 6 is expected to deliver an incredibly engaging gameplay experience.

5. Sound and Immersion – 10/10

The soundtrack, environmental sounds, voice acting, and atmosphere help create an authentic Vice City experience. Every detail contributes to making the game world feel alive.

FINAL VERDICT

GTA 6 is more than just another video game. It is one of the most anticipated entertainment releases in gaming history.

Rockstar Games has the opportunity to redefine open-world gaming once again, delivering an experience that could set a new standard for the entire industry.

FINAL SCORE: 10/10 – AN ABSOLUTE MASTERPIECE! 

If Rockstar delivers on everything it has promised, GTA 6 could become one of the greatest video games of all time.

GTA 6 – More than a game. A whole new era of gaming!

author: Kubalito
quote:
GTA 6 is a masterpiece, and I don't say that lightly. It is a breathtakingly beautiful game: every sunset, every neon glow on rain-slicked asphalt, every corner of its world feels painted with devotion. Wandering through it, I kept thinking of what Tarantino did with Once Upon a Time in Hollywood: the same razor-edged nostalgia, the same love for an era, and the same awareness that its splendor is already fading.

That is where it goes deepest. It is the finest embodiment of the Venus archetype the medium has produced: seduction, pleasure, beauty and desire, with their shadow always lurking. In that sense, the game portrays both the apogee and the fall of Western culture. It dazzles, it mesmerizes, and it consumes itself, all at once.

A perfect game for the end of an era.

author: ChrisLopresti
quote:
Simply fantastic. It’s one of those games where you can sync 6–8 hours and not even realize it.

The world is self is extremely immersive. You can live the life of a criminal even the boring parts. But what makes this game amazing is the random encounters and funny Easter eggs. The shooting is a mixed bag. Sometimes it’s great other times it doesn’t feel punchy enough, but it’s still good. The story itself is pretty simplistic, but what really shines through is the performance from the characters and the emotional investment you have in them. You actually care if they live or die. 

Graphically it is a shame it is at 30 FPS, but the world still looks great. In terms of performance there isn’t many issues. Some small pop in here and there. A stutter here or there. A crash here or there. But nothing crazy or game breaking. Overall its well polished, looks nice and well optimized even at 30 FPS.

Something I don’t like about the game is the driving. You fishtail way too easily. 

Sometimes the button system isn’t very intuitive but you could change it to the original GTA button layout, but in general not intuitive.

One thing I didn’t like is more of a personal preference, but in the game Jason cannot even flirt with other women, which is fine if they pigeon holed you into being the boyfriend, but you could totally ignore Lucia, and you will just be a platonic partnership. They should’ve built in alternative romances for Jason and Lucia. Nothing crazy but something, something like the boyfriend/girlfriend system in GTA 4.

author: Arcess
quote: Grand Theft Auto VI: Una obra maestra que redefine los videojuegos (10/10)Grand Theft Auto VI es una auténtica maravilla del entretenimiento interactivo. Rockstar Games ha conseguido superar las expectativas de millones de jugadores y ofrecer una experiencia que demuestra hasta dónde puede llegar la industria cuando se combina ambición, creatividad y atención al **** historia de Jason Duval y Lucia Caminos es uno de los mayores aciertos de esta entrega. Su relación constituye el corazón de la aventura. No estamos ante dos criminales que buscan dinero y reconocimiento, sino ante dos personas que intentan encontrar una oportunidad para cambiar sus vidas mientras el mundo parece empeñado en destruir sus **** química entre ambos protagonistas es excepcional. Sus conversaciones, discusiones, momentos románticos y situaciones cotidianas aportan una humanidad impresionante. Rockstar consigue que nos preocupemos por su futuro, haciendo que cada acontecimiento tenga un peso **** comienzo de la aventura, con Lucia saliendo de prisión y reencontrándose con Jason, establece perfectamente el tono de la historia. Lo que parece una oportunidad para conseguir dinero termina convirtiéndose en una peligrosa cadena de acontecimientos que involucra conspiraciones, traiciones y enfrentamientos con personajes **** llegada a Vice City y el contacto con figuras como Boobie Ike, Dre'Quan Priest y Raul Bautista amplían enormemente las posibilidades narrativas. Cada personaje aporta personalidad y profundidad a un universo criminal que se siente más vivo que **** de los aspectos más interesantes es cómo evoluciona la historia. El incidente del aeropuerto VCIA, la muerte de Karim y las consecuencias de los negocios criminales demuestran que los acontecimientos pueden tener consecuencias devastadoras. Especialmente impactante resulta el destino de Raul Bautista, cuyo desenlace aporta uno de los momentos más oscuros de la **** traición de Giorgio Gallo también merece una mención especial. Descubrir que alguien en quien los protagonistas depositaron su confianza termina convirtiéndose en una amenaza demuestra la capacidad de Rockstar para construir giros argumentales que mantienen al jugador **** recta final consigue mantener la tensión hasta el último momento. El enfrentamiento contra quienes han manipulado y utilizado a Jason y Lucia representa una conclusión cargada de emociones. Además, la posibilidad de diferentes desenlaces aporta un valor adicional, haciendo que el destino de los protagonistas sea todavía más **** el apartado técnico, GTA VI es sencillamente impresionante. Leonida es uno de los mundos abiertos más fascinantes que se pueden experimentar. Vice City está llena de personalidad, con una ambientación espectacular, escenarios detallados, personajes expresivos y situaciones que hacen que explorar sea una experiencia constante de **** gráficos, las animaciones, la iluminación y los efectos ambientales demuestran un nivel de trabajo excepcional. No se trata únicamente de ofrecer una imagen bonita, sino de construir un mundo que transmita autenticidad y mantenga al jugador completamente inmerso.También es admirable la cantidad de actividades y posibilidades que ofrece fuera de la historia principal. GTA VI entiende que un mundo abierto debe ser mucho más que un escenario para completar misiones. Su mayor virtud es conseguir que incluso los momentos alejados de la campaña resulten **** banda sonora, las emisoras de radio, el humor característico de la franquicia y la sátira social demuestran que Rockstar conoce perfectamente la identidad de Grand Theft **** más impresionante es que GTA VI consigue mantener su propia personalidad sin depender exclusivamente del legado de GTA V. Es una evolución natural, ambiciosa y respetuosa con aquello que convirtió a la saga en un fenómeno **** difícil encontrar una producción que reúna tantos elementos de calidad. Su narrativa, personajes, mundo abierto y presentación audiovisual forman un conjunto extraordinariamente sólido.VEREDICTO: 10/10.Grand Theft Auto VI es una obra maestra y una de las mayores demostraciones del potencial de los videojuegos. Jason y Lucia protagonizan una aventura memorable que combina acción, humor, drama y emoción de manera excepcional.Rockstar Games no solamente ha entregado una nueva entrega de Grand Theft Auto: ha construido una experiencia que merece ser recordada durante generaciones. Una auténtica celebración de los videojuegos y una aventura imprescindible.

quote: 10/10 — An Unmatched Masterpiece of Detail and Immersion​Grand Theft Auto VI sets an entirely new benchmark for open-world gaming. author: Billa_XD
quote:
10/10 — Easily the best game on PS5 right now.

Honestly, GTA 6 is insane. First off, the graphics are completely next-level. I genuinely didn't think the PS5 was even capable of pulling off visuals like this—everything from the lighting to the tiny details in the city looks straight-up real.

What really caught me off guard, though, is the story and vibe. Every other GTA game has always been just non-stop chaos, crime, and madness. Don't get me wrong, all that classic GTA mayhem is still here, and it's just as fun as ever. But having a proper relationship system and a female lead completely changes how the game feels. Playing through Jason and Lucia's bond gives it this grounded, almost family-like connection that I've never experienced in a GTA game before. It's refreshing to finally see something different, and I honestly love how it balances the crazy action with actual heart. On top of that, the map is ridiculously huge. There are so many side activities and random things to do everywhere. Between just cruising around, messing with the side stuff, and soaking in the world, I can easily see myself playing this for years.

Rockstar really nailed it. Easy 10/10 for me.

author: ILikeSmoothies
quote:
Before GTA VI, I didn't really care much for the series; while they've always been technically impressive games, the stories were comically hard to engage with. They're usually based in parody and satire, so you aren't ever really welcomed to feel like you're playing out a story more than you're simply part of a skit based on gangster caricature. Finally, we have a GTA game with a compelling story.

A little extra on the "technical achievements": The world feels much more alive, there's so much detail incorporated into the world, you'll honestly find yourself noticing the small pieces just as much as the big ones. The way Rockstar has managed to make all the details feed into each other makes it SO much easier to get immersed in the story. Granted, 30FPS isn't optimal, but it is a STABLE 30FPS, allowing you to remain in the world, rather than getting pulled out of it by constant frame stuttering/drops. 

The most enjoyable part of the story so far is simply how grounded it feels. Only naturally, as a GTA game, it features the typical violence & chaos, but it no longer feels like the driving force of the story. There's a much bigger focus on the characters themselves, the relationships between those characters, and how their decisions affect both them as individuals and their dynamics with other characters. In the previous games, Jason & Lucia would've been simple caricatures of gangsters, whereas they're now both their own fleshed out piece of a much deeper story.

Overall, it's the first GTA game where I've found myself caring about the story and its characters. The usual chaos & satire has shifted from being the defining feature of the story to just an enjoyable piece of a much larger puzzle.

If you've never really clicked with GTA in the past, I'd recommend giving VI a chance; it's the first time I've ever cared about what happens in GTA.

author: SadSolution
quote:
Many streamers and gamers seem to misunderstand the development timeline.
Some claim it was 13 years in development and compare it directly to Cyberpunk, ignoring that active development likely only started around 2018–2019. Considering its visual beauty and depth, it runs remarkably well on PS and even on the budget Xbox models. The complaints about bugs feel exaggerated, as minor issues are entirely normal for a launch of this scale and nowhere near as severe as past industry examples. 

Furthermore, the developers clearly recognized the popularity of roleplay servers, making the experience more grounded and deliberate. There are countless features that create deep immersion, alongside numerous random world events that players completely miss if they rush through the experience. 

This represents a evolution from previous titles—incorporating elements from Red Dead Redemption into a modern urban setting with cars and helicopters, while keeping the pacing a bit quicker. It can be compared to the relationship between Dark Souls and Sekiro: both share a core philosophy, but require a different approach to truly appreciate. The game establishes its internal rules right from the start, but some players seem unwilling to adapt or analyze the mechanics. 

There is constant criticism of games journalists, yet many player reactions show a similar lack of critical analysis. 

Watching streams and observing others play suggests that some audiences struggle to process the guidance provided by the game. Features like the focus mode offer clear indicators, and the minimap explicitly highlights objectives for all missions and activities. Despite years of gaming experience, some players seem oblivious to these communication tools, overlooking obvious on-screen directions and then complaining about being stuck. It is difficult to discuss deeper mechanics when basic interface elements are ignored. 

Regarding the technical state, launch bugs are common and will likely be patched quickly, much like what occurred during the launch of GTA 5. These are minor visual anomalies, such as occasional object clipping, rather than game-breaking issues. Criticisms regarding item spawning, like protein drinks or beverages appearing in the fridge, overlook the fact that this is a video game balancing realism with convenience. Implementing a fully realistic mechanic for stocking items would only frustrate players. 

Ironically, the same critics who complain about minor unrealistic details also complain when the game introduces grounded tasks, such as minor property maintenance. The balance achieved between realistic immersion and traditional gameplay mechanics works well for the format. 

P.S. I translated this text using a translator, so sorry if anything came out sounding weird or inaccurate.

quote:
I’ve put over 20 hours into this game, and I’ve been having an absolute blast. The amount of content, activities, and things to discover is unbelievable. There’s always something to do, and the world constantly finds ways to surprise you. And don’t even get me started on the graphics. They’re arguably the best in the entire gaming industry. From getting abducted by aliens to boosting cars, this game has something for everyone
. Honestly, most of the criticism I’ve seen feels unjustified. It seems like some people either had unrealistic expectations or simply hate to hate. GTA VI: El mejor videojuego de la historia

Grand Theft Auto VI no es simplemente un videojuego, es una auténtica revolución en la industria del entretenimiento. GTA VI tiene todo para convertirse en una obra maestra y en uno de los videojuegos más importantes de todos los tiempos. No se trata solamente de jugar, sino de vivir una experiencia que puede cambiar para siempre la forma en que vemos los videojuegos.

author: gabrieljoestar8
quote:
Ignore the 0/10 review-bombing spam flooding this page—Grand Theft Auto VI is genuinely peak gaming. There is a reason it tied the all-time critic record with a 99 Metascore and sits at 5/5 stars on platforms that actually verify ownership.  
Rockstar took the pure sandbox freedom of GTA V and blended it with the insane world immersion of Red Dead Redemption 2. Leonida and Vice City feel completely alive—every street corner, NPC interaction, and random encounter has an absurd level of detail. Jason and Lucia's story hits hard, the driving physics have way more weight and satisfaction, and the mission variety keeps you hooked from start to finish.
Half the people dropping zeroes here haven't even bought the game or played past the intro; they're just mad about console frame rates, no day-one PC release, or trying to tank a 99-rated game for attention. If you actually play it, it lives up to over a decade of hype and easily sets the new bar for open-world games.

author: Sleepyyyyyy-_-
quote: In 2026, all it takes for a game to be called “woke trash” or a “0/10” is having a female protagonist who does something other than make you a **** sandwich. 🫩It’s embarrassing how many men lost their minds over this **** the story a masterpiece? No. Is it good? Absolutely. Some missions are fantastic, others mediocre. But the world is a technical marvel. If you genuinely can’t find ANYTHING entertaining here, I question whether you even enjoy video games.Half these reviews sound written before anyone installed the game. Before some idiot calls me a Rockstar ****, here are my **** NEGATIVES:1. The story isn’t perfect.Some missions are incredible, others forgettable. The writing loses steam. But if the story shocked you, what the **** were you watching during the trailers? Rockstar spelled it out.2. The lack of sexual freedom and relationship options.Unlike previous GTA games, there’s no prostitution, alternative NPCs to date, or meaningful relationships outside Jason and Lucia. And yes, Rockstar missed the ****’s GTA. People want to do stupid, immoral ****. That’s part of the franchise’s identity. Forcing players into a relationship and expecting them to maintain it was questionable. Rockstar could’ve told the same story while allowing more freedom. But criticizing restrictive game design is different from crying because a woman has an actual personality.3. The 30 FPS limitation is ****’s 2026, and we’re playing one of gaming’s biggest releases at 30 **** FPS. Yes, I understand why. GTA VI is demanding, with complex NPCs, physics, and a massive open world running on aging PS5 hardware. But understanding WHY doesn’t mean I have to **** like it.Thirty FPS feels less responsive than 60, especially during driving and shootouts. Could Rockstar have sacrificed graphical fidelity for a performance mode? Maybe, but reducing graphics doesn’t magically solve CPU limitations. There’s a difference between poor optimization and hardware **** you lock a $70–$100 game to 30 FPS, it better stay there. I wanted a simultaneous PC release for higher frame rates. But RDR2 launched at 30 FPS on consoles and was still incredible. This is a legitimate negative, not an automatic **** POSITIVES:1. The open world absolutely **** on GTA V.Sorry, but nostalgia has rotted your brains. GTA V has a massive map, but outside the main story, much of it feels empty. Here’s a challenge: Play GTA V’s STORY MODE and name 30 genuinely different activities outside main missions. And no, visiting Ammu-Nation, convenience stores, the strip club, or your house doesn’t magically make the world content-rich.A massive map doesn’t equal a living world. GTA VI actually gives you reasons to explore and interact with its environment.2. The amount of content is **** ridiculous.This game takes RDR2’s open-world philosophy and expands on it. The optional activities and attention to detail are absurd.I bet plenty of people calling it empty played four to eight hours, rushed the story, ignored everything else, then ran online to declare Rockstar dead. Congratulations, you treated a sandbox like a linear campaign and complained there was nothing to do.3. The NPCs, graphics, and world simulation are phenomenal.Comparing this directly to GTA V is laughable. The world feels alive. NPCs seem like they belong in their environments rather than existing solely to walk down sidewalks. The graphics, environmental detail, and simulation are **** V was revolutionary, but its NPCs feel like robots now. Give it a year and people will post “GTA VI Was Actually a Masterpiece.” Some of you need 13 years of nostalgia to appreciate **** FINAL THOUGHTS:For the love of God, develop your own **** opinion. Play the game. Explore. Experience the content. Criticize what actually deserves criticism.Stop letting miserable, self-proclaimed alpha males convince you a game **** because a woman isn’t relegated to being eye candy. And stop pretending every positive review comes from a corporate shill.Rockstar wouldn’t piss on me if I were on fire. I paid $100 the moment preorders went live, and if this game were an unplayable, overpriced pile of ****, I’d have ZERO problem saying so. I’d uninstall it and play something **** can dislike GTA VI. Hate the story, relationship system, or 30 FPS. Prefer GTA IV, GTA V, or San Andreas. That’s completely **** if your criticism boils down to “female protagonist = woke garbage,” or you’re deliberately ignoring everything impressive to farm engagement, your review isn’t worth the electricity it took to post.Criticism is fine. Being a contrarian for attention is **** VI isn’t perfect. Rockstar isn’t perfect. But pretending this game has NOTHING going for it is one of the dumbest **** takes I’ve seen in gaming.Some of you don’t want better video games. You just want something new to **** about.

author: tp6u4xup6
quote: 10/10 – The best game I've ever playedGTA VI is the best game I've ever played, and I don't say that lightly. Rockstar spent over a decade on it, and you can feel it in every corner of Vice City. The world feels alive, reacts to you, and is full of detail that rewards you for slowing down and exploring.What surprised me most is the story. Jason and Lucia's relationship is the emotional core of the game, and it works. I can genuinely feel that these two love each other, so the relationship missions and the small moments between them never felt like chores. I kept doing things to build their bond because I wanted to, not because the game forced me to.I've seen a lot of complaints that the romance takes away the player's freedom or turns Jason into a "simp." I don't agree. GTA has always given you freedom in how you play, not the power to rewrite the story. Niko, Michael and the rest all had fixed relationships and backstories too. This time Rockstar just chose to tell a more mature, more emotional story, much like GTA IV did. It's still GTA: the satire, the crime and the chaos are all there.Many of the negative reviews here seem to come from people who've only watched streams or played the first chapter. Give it time. If you let yourself care about these characters, GTA VI is an unforgettable experience. A masterpiece.

author: jman999
quote: I’m a longtime pc and console gamer. I’m 25 years old and have played games every day since I was old enough to hold a controller. I’ve played over a thousand games with 10x that in hours spent in them. This is the single most impressive video game i’ve ever seen or played. Nothing even comes close to what rockstar is doing in its open world here. It’s a disservice to the entire gaming industry for anyone to deny this game is a 10/10. It’s by far and above the single most immersive and detailed ecosystem and open world to date in a video game. It has an impressive scale to it without feeling empty. It feels intuitive and easy to play from the jump. The UI Displays exactly the information you need without being taking up too much of the screen. The open world feels the most lived in with the most interactive npcs ever displayed in a game. The story isn’t some original masterpiece or a complete reinvention ****. But it’s good on top of everything else this game is doing to perfection. The driving is amazing better than any game i’ve played and anyone who says otherwise probably hasn’t comprehended the nuance of how deep the mechanics are. The characters and cast is memorable and likable. The story goes hard and doesn’t pull its punches. The stakes are real and choices have consequences even ones you may not have realized was a choice at all. There’s not a single thing about this game that isn’t industry leading and it is extraordinarily polished on top of that. The janky animations of amazing games like The witcher 3 do not exist here. Rockstar is creating the most seamless experience from reality anyone has ever made. Not to say it’s indistinguishable, it’s still a video game. If you walk into a weird position you can get some goody ragdolls. But anyone trying to say this game isn’t the most impressive technological achievement in gaming so far is lying to themselves and to you.

author: gembuss
quote:
Rockstar finally did it. GTA VI doesn’t just throw you into the deep end **** metropolis and call it a day. Instead, you start almost out in the suburbs, and that decision changes everything.

Jumping into these quieter, more lived-in neighborhoods first is a breath of fresh air. You actually get to play around in these places, learn the streets, meet the people, and feel the rhythm of the world before the neon of Vice City starts pulling you in. The slow, deliberate build-up toward the big city is one of the smartest things the game does. It makes the eventual arrival hit harder. You earn Vice City instead of being dumped into it.

What really sells the experience is how much life exists between the missions. Doing chores, looking after your partner, hanging out with friends… these aren’t throwaway side activities. They fill the gaps and give the game real character. The world doesn’t just wait for you to start the next big job; it keeps moving and demanding your attention in small, human ways. That texture makes the whole thing feel denser and more personal than previous entries.

On the technical side, the PS5 version running at a locked 30fps is perfectly fine. Get a good TV and the image holds up beautifully for long sessions. The water physics are a standout, exploration is constantly rewarding, and the overall package just feels rich and alive.

GTA VI understands that the best open-world games aren’t only about the big set pieces. They’re about the hours you spend just existing in the world. This one gets that balance right. Highly recommended.

author: JoeJoeMcTwist
quote:
Awesome game so far, they took all the detail from red dead redemption 2, beefed up the driving mechanics and made them better than GTA 4 and 5 combined.

You have to be smarter when committing crimes. Cop chases better and more adrenaline fueled than ever before. No longer do you see cops on the radar. You have to use your wits to evade and use the environment to your advantage in a more sophisticated wanted system that allows you to do more than just escape the circle.

The story is engaging so far, with great acting and believable characters. NPCs feel more alive as they go about their daily routines with spontaneous interactions happening all everywhere. Not just interacting with you but also with each other creating a immersive experience. 

Visually the game looks stunning even at 30 FPS. The city is alive and bustling with life, draw distances are insane and weather effects are more detailed and nuanced. 

Vehicle physics feel great, cars feel controllable to drive but also can easily go out of control if you hit the gas too hard around corners. They finally fixed drifting allowing you to maintain speeds coming out of a drift, best driving in any GTA ever. Crashes feel intense whether you're hitting a hydrant at low speeds causing your car to stop a dead halt or having a head on collision at 100 mph viceraly totaling your car and making it undrivable.

Combat is intense, whether it's a fist fight or weapons are involved. Shootouts feel intense and frantic , It really feels like a true leap in evolution for a GTA game.

Every system has been built upon and evolved to another level. Whether you want to explore the world and be a tourist or cause havoc. The choice is yours, you're free to role play as you please.

author: taketeo
quote:
I've played every game in the series since GTA III, including spin-offs like Chinatown Wars and Liberty City Stories, with 1,500 hours in GTA Online and 400 hours in Red Dead Redemption 2. Here are my impressions of GTA VI so far.
First, the graphics are overwhelming. The character models are the best I've seen in any game, period, and the overall visual quality is on another level.
The vehicle physics sit somewhere between GTA IV and GTA V. Unlike GTA V's cars, which felt like RC toys and were honestly no fun to drive, these have real weight while still being thrilling and satisfying to handle. It feels like Rockstar finally found the perfect balance.
Combat feels like the ultimate evolution of RDR2's system. The physics engine is stronger than ever. Shoot someone in the leg with a high-caliber rifle and they'll collapse and drag themselves away. Hit zones are far more numerous and precise, so enemies can be incapacitated in many different ways long before they die, which is extremely satisfying. One-handed pistol point-shooting, something GTA V never had no matter what, is finally here like in RDR2, and you switch to a two-handed grip when you aim down sights. It turned out exactly the way I always wished it would.
You can carry two long guns and two pistols, but what really impressed me is the "carry hand" system. You can hold all kinds of things: guns, duffel bags, drinks, basketballs, knives, a second duffel bag, and so on. Hop on a motorcycle while holding a mission item and you'll ride one-handed. Carry a second bag while wearing one on your back, and you hold it in one hand while shooting with the other. Pick up a pack of beer and you'll hold it in one hand while pulling out a can to drink with the other.
The most impressive improvement is melee combat. The animations are incredibly varied yet hard-hitting, and the huge range of strikes, disarms and other moves looks remarkably natural.
NPCs are vastly more diverse, too. I haven't seen a single repeat. Body types, clothing, everything is completely different. Walk down the street and you'll see cops running DUI checkpoints, or a cyclist so distracted by something happening nearby that he rear-ends the car in front and goes flying. Carjacking at gunpoint, which was cut from GTA V, is back, and cops will throw themselves at you to tackle you. Nothing feels copy-pasted.

author: Hyokkuda
quote:
I will go straight to the point here. The "woke" complaints are the most hilarious part because they are factually illiterate. You are mad that Jason has to buy groceries? Cool. You can walk away. You are mad he has to fix a sink? You can leave the apartment. The "chore" mechanics are optional relationship upgrades, not mandatory quest objectives. If you are playing an 80-hour criminal epic and you are crying because you didn’t want to stock the fridge, you aren’t a gamer. You’re a toddler who threw a tantrum because the ice cream was vanilla. And the "cuck simulator" crowd? They played thirty minutes of a story about a couple, saw a woman, and immediately reached for the keyboard. It’s like complaining that Titanic is "too feminist" because the woman survives. The game is a Bonnie and Clyde story. They are partners. If you want a woman to be a prop, go play a dating sim where the NPC is literally a vending machine. Here, she’s a co-conspirator. Deal with it.

Then there’s the 30 FPS rage. "Why isn’t it 60 FPS?" Dude, look at the hardware. You are asking a console that is about to hit its seven-year mark to render a dense, open-world city with dynamic weather, complex NPC, and ray-traced reflections at a buttery-smooth 60. That's a stupid take. If Rockstar dropped the graphics to hit 60, you’d be mad the city looked like a PS3 texture pack. They made the right call: prioritize the visual fidelity of the world over the frame rate of the chase. If you need 60 FPS to feel like you’re driving, buy a PC. Stop blaming the artist for the canvas size.

The real masterpiece here is the review bombing. The game made more money in 24 hours than Avengers: Endgame made in theaters. And what are the "haters" doing? Posting "woke woke woke" in the user reviews. You are not reviewing the game. You are posting a suicide note for your own credibility. Congratulation! 

So, here is the verdict: GTA 6 is a technical marvel wrapped in a narrative that actually respects its characters. The "woke" complaints are the noise of people who can’t handle a protagonist who isn’t a caricature. The performance complaints are the noise of people who don’t understand GPU architecture. And the review bombing? That’s just the sound of the crybabies who got a pair of socks for Xmas while there's money hidden inside of it. Typical.

author: Turbolone
quote:
10/10 – Ein herausragendes Spiel, dem man eine echte Chance geben muss!

Es ist erschreckend, wie viele Menschen GTA 6 offenbar absichtlich schlecht bewerten, ohne das Spiel selbst richtig gespielt zu haben. Statt sich eine eigene Meinung zu bilden, wird einfach die negative Stimmung anderer übernommen.

Natürlich sind Geschmäcker verschieden, und niemand muss jedes Spiel mögen. Man sollte aber verstehen, dass GTA 6 gegenüber GTA 5 deutlich erwachsener geworden ist. Die Geschichte, die Charaktere und die gesamte Atmosphäre sind tiefgründiger. Wer lediglich oberflächliche Unterhaltung erwartet oder wenig Verständnis für emotionale und komplexere Geschichten mitbringt, wird möglicherweise nicht verstehen, was dieses Spiel eigentlich vermitteln möchte.

Ja, der Einstieg ist langsam. Man sollte dem Spiel durchaus 10 bis 15 Stunden Zeit geben, um sich darauf einzulassen. Doch sobald man richtig in diese Welt eingetaucht ist, merkt man, was für ein herausragendes Spiel Rockstar erschaffen hat.

Meine Lebensgefährtin spielt auf einer normalen PS5, während ich auf der PS5 Pro spiele. Auf beiden Konsolen hatten wir bisher praktisch keine nennenswerten Bugs und nur äußerst vereinzelte, minimale Framerate-Einbrüche. Die Grafik ist wunderschön, das Gameplay hervorragend und die gesamte Spielwelt wirkt unglaublich detailliert, stimmig und durchdacht.

Man merkt an vielen Stellen, wie viel Arbeit und Liebe zum Detail in dieses Spiel geflossen sind.

Nicht jeder muss GTA 6 eine 10 geben. Aber wer dem Spiel wirklich eine faire Chance gegeben hat, müsste zumindest seine Qualität und den enormen Aufwand dahinter anerkennen können. Eine Bewertung von 0 Punkten ist für mich angesichts der gebotenen Qualität kaum nachvollziehbar und erweckt vielmehr den Eindruck von gezieltem Review-Bombing.

Die Menschen sollten endlich wieder anfangen, sich eine eigene Meinung zu bilden, anstatt blind auf einen negativen Meinungstrend aufzuspringen.

Wer sich mit etwas Offenheit, Empathie und Geduld auf dieses Spiel einlässt, kann hier ein außergewöhnliches Spielerlebnis entdecken.

Für mich persönlich verdient GTA 6 ganz klar eine 10 von 10 Punkten.

author: Raiden_Master7
quote: ​At the time of my early review, I’ve reached Chapter 2, with my personal experience at 20 hours in-game. Compared to the "next-gen" games over the last 6 years (since PS5 and Xbox Series X and S launched), this is the only title that can finally be considered NEXT GEN! Incredible, very heavy physics, similar or equal to GTA 4 but softer compared to the Euphoria Engine, way better than GTA 5, which feels more arcade-like in things like driving or the weapon wheel. Speaking of the weapon wheel, its absence didn't bother me; using a pistol, your own gun, or picking up weapons off the ground has probably been seen somewhere else for sure, but seeing it in the GTA 6 series is already a revolution because it still gives you that extra touch of realism and therefore lets you use your car trunk as a supply stash for white powder, bodies, weapons, and clothes. It’s improved in many ways, including being packed with micro-details everywhere that you don't notice right away (even though it’s not without small flaws like a beer spawning inside the fridge or a clipped throw of some trash), but I mean... this game has revolutionized the gaming world once again, for the better! A system very similar to and improved over the old "honor" system from RDR2, called the "criminal profile," changes based on your professionalism as a criminal: things like taking out enemies non-lethally or getting in and out clean on a heist, without leaving casualties in a professional way. A gigantic map that feels very spread out, though you get used to it after a while. Is messing around limited? Many people say messing around is limited and the game holds your hand a lot in Chapter 1, from how I found it, I wouldn't say so, it wasn't guided, after a bit it still had you doing plenty of activities and you can explore and do tons of activities compared to GTA 5. Right from the first minutes of gameplay I told myself how much photorealism there was, even on a base PS5; another crazy thing is the reflections and lighting which are all Ray Traced except for the shadows which are done traditionally, something you see pretty rarely in a console game—great Ray Tracing, not done in bits and pieces and used just for flashy reflections, no, here there’s lighting and reflections and even though the shadows aren't Ray Traced, I didn't notice jagged edges or major flaws. During my nearly 20 hours of gameplay between messing around, side stuff, and gunplay, I found some tiny framerate dips and especially an exaggerated ghosting effect, tested both on my monitor and on my LG TV; turning up motion blur (in my case set to 6) or disabling motion blur and enabling TruMotion on my LG TV makes the issue fade or almost completely disappear. It doesn’t always guarantee total smoothness in the game or the complete absence of ghosting, but it’s a good compromise for me—30fps, since being a fan of both platforms, 30fps doesn't bother me, which I think is still relevant on a game like this, jaw-dropping graphics with a fair compromise that you can get used to after a bit. Talking about the novelty that barely existed in previous entries is the life-sim or roleplay: managing your own events whether you’re playing as Lucia Caminos or Jason Duval, it’s something I like—waking up, sleeping at night, scrolling social media and liking posts, watching TV, feeding animals, talking to NPCs and getting positive or negative interactions, taking care of your girlfriend, texting people or ignoring them, going to the gym or eating healthy or junk food. Those are activities borrowed, yes, from many games, but they’re expanded in a Rockstar Games title, where in GTA 5 you couldn't do these things, in GTA San Andreas and 4 they were there, but very limited for the time; finally in this GTA 6, we can see in its definitive form everything a life-sim can offer.

author: SaluteLegend263
quote:
9/10 (base PS5): A landmark open world held back by technical rough edges GTA 6 is an outstanding achievement. Rockstar has built a remarkably detailed, living world, and the new mechanics make it compelling to explore and play. It easily earns its place among the best games of the generation.

That said, a few issues keep it from a perfect score.

Performance: Playing on a base PS5, I ran into bugs and noticeable stuttering during my playthrough. These don't ruin the experience, but they break immersion in a game that otherwise feels so polished. Hopefully post-launch patches will address them.

Weapon handling: The loadout of two long arms and two sidearms feels clunky in practice. Cycling between four weapons mid-combat is more cumbersome than it needs to be. A simpler loadout of one long arm and one sidearm would make switching quicker and more intuitive, and would better match the game's grounded, realistic direction.

Overall, these are refinements rather than fundamental flaws. GTA 6 is an exceptional game that will only get better with updates. Highly recommended.

author: elpatronsw
quote:
10/10 ... An Absolute Masterpiece! Rockstar Did It Again! 

I honestly cannot understand all the hate and frustration from some players. Are we even playing the same game?! 

GTA 6 is an absolutely incredible achievement in gaming. The story, characters, atmosphere, breathtaking graphics, insane attention to detail, and endless possibilities are simply on another level. Rockstar has created something truly special here.

The open world is absolutely mind-blowing. The city doesn't just look beautiful, it feels ALIVE! The traffic, pedestrians, NPC interactions, animations, weather, lighting, and countless tiny details make everything feel incredibly realistic. Everywhere you look, something is happening. Sometimes just driving around and exploring the world is an experience in itself. The level of immersion is ridiculous!

And the story? Absolutely fantastic! The characters, dialogue, cinematic presentation, and storytelling are exactly what makes Rockstar games so special. Combined with the freedom and possibilities of this massive world, it's an experience very few developers can deliver.

Now, let's talk about those 30 FPS complaints... Seriously?! 

Some people really need to understand how hardware works. You're playing on a PlayStation, NOT a high-end gaming PC with a $2,000 graphics card!

Consoles have limitations. When you're rendering a gigantic, highly detailed open world with realistic lighting, complex physics, countless NPCs, traffic, and so many systems running simultaneously, compromises are inevitable.

It's not like Rockstar has some magical 60 FPS button they're refusing to press. Obviously, 60 FPS would be nice, but achieving that without sacrificing visual quality on console hardware isn't always realistic.

Personally, I'd take breathtaking, realistic graphics and a stable 30 FPS over significantly downgraded visuals just to reach 60 FPS. EVERY SINGLE TIME!

And let's remember something: THIS IS GTA, NOT CALL OF DUTY! This is a massive, incredibly ambitious open-world adventure, not a competitive shooter where every millisecond matters. Immersion, world-building, realism, and storytelling are far more important to me than obsessing over an FPS counter.

And then there's the ridiculous "GTA 6 is too woke" argument... WHAT?! 

Have some people completely forgotten what GTA is?!

Rockstar has ALWAYS made fun of society, politics, celebrities, stereotypes, consumerism, and basically everything happening in the real world. That's literally the identity of Grand Theft Auto!

GTA 6 reflects modern society and exaggerates its absurdities in classic Rockstar fashion. It's satire! It's parody! It's supposed to be provocative, offensive, hilarious, and uncomfortable sometimes. Nobody is safe from Rockstar's humor, and that's exactly why it's brilliant.

Just because the game reflects aspects of today's society that you personally dislike doesn't automatically make it some political agenda. Rockstar is doing what Rockstar has always done: holding up a ridiculous mirror to an already ridiculous world. 

Of course, constructive criticism is perfectly reasonable. No game is flawless. But some people seem so obsessed with frame rates and political arguments that they've forgotten how to actually enjoy video games.

Gaming should be about the EXPERIENCE, not just numbers and outrage!

For me, GTA 6 delivers everything I wanted and more. An incredible story, fantastic characters, stunning graphics, an unbelievably detailed living world, endless freedom, and that unique Rockstar atmosphere.

The ambition behind this game is absolutely insane. Very few developers are capable of creating worlds with this much personality, detail, and immersion.

Rockstar didn't just create another open-world game. They created an experience that reminds me why I love gaming in the first place.

10/10. An absolute masterpiece. Worth the hype. Thank you, Rockstar!

author: Hashasinh
quote:
Hay videojuegos que entretienen y después están los que consiguen hacerte sentir que estás habitando otro mundo. 

GTA VI pertenece a la segunda categoría.

Lo primero que impresiona es la escala de su mundo. Vice City y sus alrededores no se sienten como un simple escenario construido para colocar misiones, sino como un ecosistema que parece existir independientemente de lo que estés haciendo. 

La cantidad de detalles, las animaciones, el comportamiento de los personajes y la atención puesta en los pequeños acontecimientos cotidianos consiguen que incluso pasear sin rumbo tenga cierto atractivo.. visualmente es una auténtica barbaridad. No se trata solamente de tener buenos gráficos, sino de cómo se combinan la iluminación, la ambientación, los escenarios y las animaciones para crear una experiencia coherente. 

Hay momentos en los que uno simplemente deja de jugar para observar lo que sucede alrededor.

También destaca la relación entre sus protagonistas. 

La historia consigue que los personajes tengan una identidad propia y que sus interacciones aporten algo más que una excusa para pasar de una misión de acción a otra. 

Es una de las cosas que más ayudan a que el mundo tenga personalidad.

Por supuesto, no es perfecto., aalgunas decisiones de diseño pueden resultar discutibles, y hay aspectos que podrían ofrecer más libertad al jugador. taampoco todas las actividades tienen la misma profundidad.. pero son defectos relativamente pequeños frente a la ambición y la calidad general del juego más impresionante es que Rockstar sigue demostrando que entiende algo fundamental: un mundo abierto no debería limitarse a ofrecer cientos de iconos en un mapa. 

Debería despertar curiosidad, debería conseguir que quieras desviarte del camino, explorar una calle que no conoces o simplemente conducir sin tener ningún objetivo y ya.. el gta VI no necesita reinventar absolutamente todo para justificar su existencia. 

Le basta con ejecutar su visión a un nivel extraordinario y aprovechar la experiencia acumulada durante décadas, es una demostración de lo que puede conseguir una producción de videojuegos cuando se combinan recursos, talento, paciencia y una enorme atención al detalle!!

author: KirbyVonPoyo
quote:
GTA 6 – Review

GTA 6 ist ein gutes Spiel, das vor allem durch seine offene Welt, die Grafik und die vielen Möglichkeiten überzeugt. Vice City ist sehr detailliert gestaltet und bietet einiges zu entdecken.

Auch die Story rund um Lucia und Jason ist interessant und sorgt für einige spannende Momente. Besonders die Atmosphäre und die kleinen Details machen das Spiel zu einem gelungenen GTA-Erlebnis.

Natürlich ist nicht alles perfekt. An manchen Stellen hätte man sich etwas mehr Abwechslung gewünscht, und nicht jede Erwartung wird vollständig erfüllt.

Insgesamt ist GTA 6 ein starkes Spiel, das viel Spaß macht und einiges zu bieten hat. Es ist nicht perfekt, aber definitiv einen Blick wert.

Meine Bewertung: 8/10

Anmerkung: Unter dieser Review finden sich leider viele Fake-Bewertungen von Zelda-Fanboys, die das Spiel offenbar nicht einmal eine Minute selbst gespielt haben. Statt einer ehrlichen Meinung wird einfach grundlos schlecht bewertet. Man sollte Reviews schreiben, nachdem man das Spiel tatsächlich gespielt hat, und nicht nur, um es schlechtzureden.

author: DarkWraithJedi
quote: Watching the wave of online outrage and review-bombing aimed at Grand Theft Auto VI over the tiniest, most trivial nitpicks is genuinely baffling, because once you actually sit down and play it, the game is an absolute blast. Beneath all the internet noise sits arguably one of the best, most thoroughly realised open worlds ever put together, paired with a narrative focus that feels like Red Dead Redemption 2 and Uncharted 4 had a baby. You get that same dense, lived-in atmosphere where the world carries on breathing around the corner, combined with tighter, more cinematic storytelling that actually pulls you forward.Taking a bit of time to adjust to the revamped controls is well worth the initial muscle-memory hurdle, particularly once you get behind the wheel. The driving physics are noticeably more demanding than GTA V's, and frankly, that is one of the best decisions Rockstar could have made. Having always loved the weighty, physical handling of GTA IV and hated the floaty, arcadey feel of V, finding a middle ground here that leans much closer to realistic handling and proper vehicle damage is a huge relief. Cars actually have mass again, you have to judge your braking distances into corners, and **** through a tight getaway feels **** whole experience is clearly built to encourage proper roleplay and immersion rather than mindless chaos, though people seem to forget that it is still a video game at the end of the day and nobody has locked the sandbox doors. Most of the grounded mechanics serve the specific story the writers want to tell, and plenty of them remain optional anyway. Unlike past protagonists who often defaulted to feeling like mass-murdering psychopaths the second a cutscene ended, Jason and Lucia are written with actual restraint and humanity. Nothing physically stops you from going on a classic spree if the mood takes you, yet bringing over the Honor system makes a world of difference—rewarding discretion and clean execution over indiscriminate shooting, whilst nudging you to consider the moral weight of how your characters operate.I am roughly twenty-six hours in and still only on Chapter 2, which probably says enough on its own about how easy it is to lose track of time just soaking up the world and taking things at a steady pace. Technically, it has a few rough edges; I have run into a couple of glitches so far, including a fairly glaring culling issue during a seaplane cutscene. Even so, in a sixty-plus-hour open-world game juggling dozens of missions and interlocking systems, a few stray visual hiccups are hardly a surprise, and they do very little to take the shine off what is shaping up to be something special.

author: Pedroemper
quote:
I am 15 hours into GTA 6 on PS5

I can say that
- The 30 FPS are not bad at all, I can’t perceive any frame drops and the game feels smooth despite it being 30 FPS. Would 60 FPS have been nice? Yes, do I care enough to make it affect my view of the game? No
- I have not encountered any game breaking bugs or glitches, it’s been flawless for me so far besides some NPCs tweaking out, or one car disappearing out of nowhere when exploring. But that’s minor stuff that doesn’t matter to me.
- The “annoying chores” everyone mentions are entirely optional, you can do them to improve your relationship with Lucia. You don’t have to do them. 
- It feels like no matter what Rockstar did, they’d still get bad reviews and hate. It also feels like 90% of the people complaining are mad about the RDR2-like mechanics and just wanted a prettier GTA 5, but then if the game was like that these same people would’ve complained saying “13 years and for what?” “2 billion dollars and for what?” “Rockstar can’t improve! Trash game!”

The best advice I could give is buy the game and form your own opinions. If you can’t afford it or don’t want to buy it (or don’t have the platform required to play it) then watch a walkthrough or gameplay. The game is not as bad as its being made out to be.

author: tythg13
quote: GTA 6 review — 10/10. I have to praise the incredibly cool graphics, the car destruction, the facial detail, and the atmosphere. But I also have to add that GTA 6 has moved away from the GTA series and turned into RDR2, with its restrictions on freedom — for example, you can’t steal your neighbors’ cars, and there are these slow-mo moments. As for the downsides: the animations are jerky, as if they’re running at 15 fps. Ammu-Nation disappointed me: instead of proper weapon inspection in the open world, everything was shoved into a black box, like in a Ubisoft product. In GTA 5, and in the GTA series in general, this was implemented better, especially in GTA 5. The UI for everything is terrible; the design looks as if an AI was told to make it in a minute. In GTA 5 and RDR2 it looked much better. Besides the bad UI, the inventory was taken from RDR2, with its unnecessary clutter and dozens of different products that do the same thing. I can’t say much about the story yet, but I personally don’t like the chapter-based story structure like in RDR2, because the story feels like it isn’t whole but is scattered across chapters. As for the prologue and the first missions — maybe it’s because of the novelty — it seems worse than in GTA 5. There, the opening was dynamic, with shootouts with cops, then dynamic driving in a sports car through the city; it set the pace of the game and showed its dynamism and craziness. In GTA 6, the introduction has time skips and events between which you’re only allowed to participate a little, then a boat ride through “checkpoints,” where there’s an ordinary shootout at the end. In my opinion, Dan Houser’s departure had a very bad influence on GTA 6’s story. Overall, despite all the flaws and shortcomings that I personally didn’t like, this game is revolutionary in many aspects.

author: Milo_29_
quote:
There are games that entertain you, and then there are games that completely absorb you into their world. GTA VI belongs to the latter category. Having reached the third chapter, I can already say that Rockstar has delivered something truly exceptional.

What stands out most is the incredible attention to detail. The world feels alive, authentic, and constantly evolving, making every moment of exploration feel meaningful. The atmosphere is phenomenal, the presentation is outstanding, and the overall level of immersion is something very few games can achieve.

The characters and storytelling are equally impressive, creating an experience that feels engaging rather than simply being a sequence of missions. There is a remarkable sense of personality throughout the game, and it is clear that an extraordinary amount of passion and craftsmanship went into its creation.

What makes GTA VI special is not just its technical ambition, but the way all its individual elements come together to create such a captivating experience. It feels like a genuine evolution of the open-world genre.

I still have a long journey ahead, but if the quality so far is any indication of what awaits, Rockstar may have created something truly unforgettable.

An outstanding experience and, already, one of the most impressive gaming experiences I have ever had.

author: cazytheo80
quote: Une nouvelle référence du monde ouvert. Rockstar joue dans une autre **** y a des jeux auxquels on joue pendant quelques dizaines d’heures, et il y a ceux dans lesquels on a véritablement l’impression de vivre. GTA VI appartient à cette deuxième **** que j’attends d’un monde ouvert, c’est avant tout un univers vivant, crédible, cohérent, immersif et rempli de possibilités. Je veux avoir le sentiment que le monde continue d’exister indépendamment de mes actions, que chaque rue, chaque quartier, chaque personnage et chaque situation peuvent potentiellement me réserver une surprise. Je veux de la profondeur, de l’interactivité, une véritable sensation de liberté et surtout cette impression permanente de ne pas avoir encore tout **** c’est précisément là que Rockstar excelle.Après des heures de jeu, on a encore cette sensation incroyable de n’avoir exploré qu’une partie de ce que le jeu a réellement à offrir. On découvre constamment de nouveaux détails, des interactions, des comportements, des situations inattendues. Le niveau de finition et l’attention portée aux détails donnent presque l’impression que chaque élément du monde a été pensé pour exister naturellement.Rockstar ne se contente pas de créer une immense carte remplie d’activités. Le studio construit un véritable écosystème. La densité du monde, la vie qui l’anime, les animations, les comportements des PNJ, la circulation, la physique, les environnements, la météo, les éclairages et toutes ces petites choses auxquelles on ne prête pas forcément attention au premier abord participent à une immersion **** qui me fascine particulièrement, c’est cette capacité à pousser pratiquement chaque composante d’un monde ouvert à un niveau supérieur. On a parfois le sentiment que Rockstar développe avec plusieurs années d’avance sur le reste de l’industrie. Là où beaucoup de studios cherchent à créer des mondes toujours plus grands, Rockstar semble chercher à les rendre toujours plus **** parlons de la technique. Réussir à faire fonctionner une expérience d’une telle ambition sur une console de cette génération est une véritable prouesse. Il faut prendre en considération la quantité de systèmes qui doivent fonctionner simultanément, la complexité de la simulation et la richesse des environnements. On peut évidemment discuter des compromis techniques, notamment de la fréquence d’images, mais il faut aussi regarder l’ensemble de ce qui est accompli.Tout n’est pas nécessairement parfait, et Rockstar ne doit bénéficier d’aucune immunité face à la critique. Mais il faut savoir reconnaître quand un studio repousse réellement les limites de son médium.Pour moi, Rockstar reste la référence absolue lorsqu’il s’agit de concevoir des mondes ouverts. Ce qui distingue leurs productions, ce n’est pas simplement leur taille ou leur beauté graphique : c’est leur capacité à donner l’impression que l’on pourrait continuer à y jouer des centaines d’heures sans avoir épuisé toutes leurs **** VI ne donne pas seulement envie de terminer une aventure. Il donne envie de rester dans son univers, de se promener, d’observer, d’expérimenter et de découvrir ce que l’on n’a pas encore vu.C’est exactement ce que j’attends d’un jeu vidéo de cette envergure.Rockstar ne joue pas simplement dans la même catégorie que les autres. Le studio contribue à définir ce que doit être le monde ouvert de demain.
