author: greysymmetric
quote:
My Thoughts on GTA 6 After Playing It for a Few Hours

Positives:

- Amazing Graphics: I usually don't **** graphics, but here, they genuinely make the game look beautiful. Especially the lighting, with lights really popping out at you.
- Great Soundtrack: Not just the radio stations, but the Original Game Soundtrack as well.
- Improved Wanted System: Uses an improved version of GTA 4's Wanted System, with a new mechanic called "Heat." Basically, certain areas become dangerous because cops will recognize you unless you change your appearance, including your clothes and accessories. You also have to change your vehicle to fully clear your Heat.
- Vehicle Mechanics: Vehicles now have an engine condition and gas bar, so you know when your car is about to break down or run out of fuel.
- HUGE MAP: The map is absolutely massive, with plenty of places to explore.
- Improved Boat Controls: Boats handle far better than they did in previous GTA games.
- Photo Mode: A very welcome addition, especially considering how beautiful this game looks.
- Crouching Returns: Instead of GTA 5's weird sneak walk, we finally have proper crouching again.
- Looting System: You can loot ammunition, guns, and even some clothing from enemies you take out.
- Inventory System: You can carry items that restore your health when needed instead of relying on GTA 5's automatic health regeneration.
- Improved Stealth and Combat: Combat and stealth have been improved, with takedowns and the ability to use people as human shields.
- Characters and Dialogue: I'm actually really liking the characters so far. They're very enjoyable, and their dialogue and relationships feel realistic.
- Social Media: The in-game social media is surprisingly fun to browse. It's great for world-building and provides plenty of laughs.
- GORE IS BACK AND IT'S BETTER THAN EVER.
- YOU CAN PET DOGS AND CATS.

Negatives:

– Lengthy Prologue: The prologue is a bit longer than GTA 5's. It's noticeable, but it's not the worst thing in the world, and it doesn't take too long to get into the gameplay.

– No Mission Replay: Not having Mission Replay ****. It's disappointing that you can't simply go back and replay completed missions without starting over.

Glitches/Bugs Encountered:

Only one so far.

Addressing Disingenuous Criticism

I also wanted to take some time out of my day to debunk some of the disingenuous reviews surrounding this game, most of which provide absolutely nothing of substance and instead resort to screaming buzzwords like "woke" or "cuck."

Since the very first day of release, several misleading claims about the game have already been challenged. A lot of these criticisms involve deliberately exploiting game mechanics to make the game look worse than it actually is, taking gameplay completely out of context, or outright editing clips to manufacture problems.

For example:

- Editing lag into gameplay footage to make the game's performance appear worse than it actually is.
- Claiming you can't kill protesters, when you actually can. The footage being circulated takes a specific mission completely out of context.
- Claiming plane destruction is bugged, when they're simply taking advantage of an accessibility setting.
- Claiming you can't steal cars, while ignoring the contextual reasons behind certain restrictions and the new mechanics involved.
- Claiming you can't shoot up "gay" clubs, when the restriction actually applies to every bar in the game, regardless of what kind of establishment it is.

There's a difference between legitimate criticism and deliberately misrepresenting a game to push a narrative. GTA 6 isn't above criticism, and there are absolutely things worth criticizing, but spreading misinformation or exploiting mechanics for engagement doesn't constitute a legitimate review.

I'd encourage people to watch actual, uninterrupted gameplay instead of relying entirely on cherry-picked clips designed to make the game look bad.

author: Duzziverse
quote: I understand the frustration. A 4.9 is probably unrealistic, but this certainly isn't a 10/10 either. I'm still in Chapter 1, so these are just my early impressions. Rockstar really took things slow, starting us off in a town outside VC. My biggest concerns so far are performance and image quality. I'm playing on a base PS5, and the first shootout with the Kingfishers dropped below 30 FPS. It was horrendous. Things improved around Key Lento, but I'm worried about how the game will perform once we're in the densely populated Vice City.I'm also not entirely sold on the simulation elements. Cleaning the house and washing a boat for Brian and Cal are immersive, sure, but sometimes they feel out of place in a GTA game. Outside of these issues, though, the game is a marvel. The underwater treasure hunting sequence genuinely blew me away. I'm hoping things only get better from here. The small details are honestly amazing. There was one moment when I was about to go to bed in the game, and I heard the refrigerator compressor kick in. I was genuinely shocked by how much attention Rockstar paid to something so insignificant. It's these little details that make the world feel alive. Also the random things that are happening are funny and surprising. The graphics, while not perfect, are outstanding. It's the combination of these details, world-building, and visual fidelity that makes GTA 6 such a marvel. I cannot wait for the next chapters. If R updates this game soon to at least make a DOF, RT, Film Grain slider I would rate this 9/10. I would gladly trade these visual effects for resolution and stability. TAA upscaler is just blurry for me, I feel sometimes uncomfortable. So far it is an 8/10 for me.

author: zaphod6502
quote:
13 hours in and currently playing Chapter 2. It is the greatest open world game I have played in the long history of my gaming hobby. I love the characters, the laugh out loud moments, and the superlative graphics and sound. The sheer attention to detail within the game is incredible. 

My only criticisms are the 30fps framerate which I have become used to. I turned up blur setting to max which helps a lot with the framerate perception. For someone who has a top tier PC that can run games at 140fps plus it was a big adjustment and took about 3 hours of gameplay to get used to but now it is no problem for me.

I encountered one glitch where I was sitting in the back of a boat and during a cutscene and the waves clipped over my eye level and I could see the ocean floor graphics.

I love the RDR2 style of gameplay where you live in the world and can do chores and other types of jobs. I love the random little events that popup when you are driving around the world that can lead to interesting side events and emergent gameplay.

I like that I have to consider being a bad guy with resulting ramifications and it encourages me to not just go in guns blazing. I am even careful how I drive depending on what task I am doing at the time. The game has addressed every concern I had with GTA V which was a highly simplistic game compared to GTA VI. Considering the limitations of the PS5 console platform Rockstar has done an amazing job with GTA VI.

author: VewonX
quote:
GTA VI is genuinely the greatest game ever made, and I don't say that lightly.

From the gameplay mechanics to the storytelling and the insane attention to detail, Rockstar has completely reinvented what an open-world game can be. I'm currently in Chapter 2, and I genuinely can't stop playing. The craziest part is that the game just keeps getting better the further you progress.

Seeing all this review bombing is honestly embarrassing. As someone who's been gaming for years, I felt like I had to leave a review because some of these people clearly don't understand what Rockstar has accomplished here.

I guarantee many of these are the same people who called Red Dead Redemption 2 boring because they couldn't even make it past the snowy opening. Now RDR2 is considered one of the greatest games ever made.

And all this nonsense about GTA VI being "woke"? Have you actually played the game? Rockstar is literally making fun of woke culture and modern society through its signature satire. That's what GTA has always done.

To everyone complaining, name one game available today that does what GTA VI does better. I'll wait.

The funniest part is that many of the people complaining about realism are the same ones who used to install dozens of realism mods in previous GTA games or spend hundreds of hours playing GTA RP servers. Rockstar finally delivers an incredibly immersive, detailed world, and suddenly it's a problem? What exactly do you people want?

And the 30 FPS complaints? Rockstar told everyone about that beforehand. I'm primarily a PC gamer who's used to playing at 120 FPS, and I'm telling you, this game is absolutely incredible even at 30. Would 60 FPS be better? Obviously. But pretending that 30 FPS somehow ruins this masterpiece is ridiculous.

Let's also remember that when GTA IV launched, people complained about its driving mechanics, physics, and slower gameplay. Some even called it Rockstar's worst GTA. Fast forward to today, and those same features are constantly praised as revolutionary.

The same thing will happen with GTA VI.

What's even more ridiculous is that a huge portion of the negativity seems to come from people who haven't even played the game. They've watched a few clueless streamers, repeated their opinions, and decided they know everything.

If you genuinely dislike the game after playing it, that's completely fair. But review bombing something because it doesn't match your imaginary expectations is pathetic.

Rockstar didn't just raise the bar. They completely redefined it.

This isn't just Game of the Year. This is Game of the Decade, and potentially the greatest video game ever created.

10/10. An absolute masterpiece.

Now go back to Fortnite, kids.

author: RandyRand567
quote: If you ask the head of Take-Two Interactive what the mission of their company is, he will likely reply with the following: "Our mission is to create the best entertainment product on earth.". I think most regular people would shrug it off. Isn't that the mission of any entertainment company? Some gamers would add, "Look at your major sequel releases for the past few years—you're clearly failing at your mission." And I think that's actually fair, except for one studio they have in their portfolio: Rockstar Games. I don't know why, but somehow Rockstar keeps pushing boundaries with every major release. It genuinely surprises me, given the current state of the gaming industry—many studios having huge layoffs, many major sequels over the past few years clearly not delivering. So why wouldn't Rockstar be the same? How can a studio of this size still keep innovating? Imagine how many bureaucracy barriers you need to break to introduce a new feature — especially features that seem to bring very small value, like blinkers on cars or opening windows on cars. This is where Rockstar shines; they are kings at sandbox games. They keep adding more and more small, neat features, and all of them combined create an experience you cannot even call a video game anymore. What is it, a life sim?When a car drives through Leonida, the game's version of Florida, through the rain, and you see windshield wipers working on an old car at night, it creates a magical feeling of immersion. Soon you start following traffic rules in the game, and then you don't want to rush things—you want to keep the pace it sets for you. Jason's (the main protagonist) routine starts resembling your routine: morning coffee, home gym, doing some chores, maybe driving around to a local barber shop and clothing store, or maybe skipping driving altogether and just going on foot. I've played over 7 hours over the past 2 days, and to be honest, I have never seen anything like it. It's very hard to explain until you experience it yourself. A Digital Foundry review shows it best, but it's not quite like experiencing it yourself. If I wanted to explain GTA 6 to a non-gamer, I would say something like this. Imagine you're a fan of any famous person — athlete, artist, etc. Imagine that famous person is the best at their thing, there is literally no one who can compete, and you probably expect them to relax because their peak has already passed. Now, imagine this person, whom you haven't heard from in 13 years, comes back and beats their own record two times over—this is what happened with GTA 6 today. Somehow they again did the impossible. Every chance was stacked against them, yet they delivered. As for the 30 fps complaints: ever since I was a young person and got GTA 3, I didn't have the hardware to run it without issues on PC, and that happened for every GTA game, including GTA Vice City, GTA San Andreas, GTA IV, and GTA V. GTA games always release ahead of their generation. It will take a few years (or maybe months on PC) for gaming hardware to catch up, but even in its current state, it's incredible. So did the Take-Two CEO lie when he said that their mission is to create the best entertainment product on earth? No, he said it exactly like it is. With the current state of the gaming industry today, and as a gamer with almost 30 years of experience, I can tell you that GTA 6 is indeed the best entertainment product on earth today.

author: lolip008
quote:
A Great Game, but Some Decisions Hold It Back
The world is huge, filled with a wide variety of side missions and an immersive atmosphere that makes it easy to lose yourself in it. The NPCs are diverse, and the world feels genuinely alive. The story is enjoyable, the missions are well designed, and the protagonists are great. Overall, it's an excellent game that has a lot to offer, although it takes some time and patience to fully get used to it and appreciate everything it has to offer.

The story suffers from inconsistent pacing. It starts off too slowly, only to become rushed later on, making it difficult to remain immersed. The Criminal Profile system influencing the ending is another disappointing design choice. I honestly don't understand who thought this was a good idea. GTA has always been about creating chaos, allowing players to commit crimes, and rewarding them for it. As a longtime fan of the series, this decision was particularly frustrating and negatively affected my overall experience.

The restrictions on shooting in certain locations or targeting certain characters because of their gender identity or similar reasons are equally disappointing. I'm playing a crime game, not a game that imposes its own moral boundaries on me.

The gameplay also suffers from some poor design decisions. Having to press a button just to pick up a weapon feels unnecessary, especially when older GTA games handled weapon pickups in a much more convenient way.

I also don't understand why Rockstar removed the heist planning system from GTA V. Being able to plan heists and approach them in different ways, particularly during main-story missions, added a lot to the experience. The removal of mission replayability is another baffling decision, and I see no good reason for taking away such a useful feature.

Finally, locking cheats behind challenges is pointless. Cheats are supposed to be there for fun and experimentation, so forcing players to complete challenges just to unlock them feels unnecessary.
Despite these shortcomings, GTA is still a great game with an incredible world and plenty to enjoy. However, these design decisions hold it back from being the experience it could have been.

author: Leene
quote:
10/10 – 13 years in the making, and worth every minute

I've been playing GTA since the days of GTA III. I've been there through the evolution of this franchise, from GTA III and Vice City to San Andreas and GTA V. I've grown up with these games, experienced what each generation brought to the table, and spent well over 100 hours in GTA V alone. So when GTA VI finally arrived after 13 years, I came in with enormous expectations.

And Rockstar has delivered something truly special.

For me, GTA VI isn't simply about completing missions, causing chaos or chasing the next objective. It's about being part of a living, breathing world. I can spend hours doing absolutely ordinary things and still have an incredible time. Driving around, exploring, fishing, visiting beaches, shopping, customising cars, going on dates and discovering unexpected encounters. The world constantly gives me reasons to stay.

Jason and Lucia are a huge part of what makes this game so special. Their chemistry, relationship and everyday interactions make them feel like real people. I genuinely enjoy spending time with them, whether I'm progressing through the story or simply taking them out for a drive. They're a fantastic pairing, and I find myself more invested in their relationship than I ever expected.

The world itself is phenomenal. Vice City feels alive, crowded, vibrant and full of personality. The contrast between the city, the Keys and the quieter parts of Leonida makes exploration rewarding. Random encounters can turn into entire adventures without the game even telling you where to go. Some of my most memorable experiences have happened completely outside the missions.
And the music! Rockstar understands how important radio is to GTA. Driving around listening to the stations, hearing songs from different eras and occasionally stumbling upon something that brings back personal memories is an experience in itself. One particular song even brought back an emotional memory of my late father. That's something I never expected a video game to do.

Technically, I play at 30 FPS and genuinely enjoy the cinematic presentation. I prefer atmosphere, visual detail and immersion over chasing higher frame rates. For my style of gaming, the experience works beautifully.

Having played GTA III, Vice City, San Andreas and GTA V, I don't buy the argument that GTA VI has lost its identity or that it isn't GTA anymore. Franchises evolve. They shouldn't be expected to remain frozen in time. This is a new generation of GTA, and I love the direction Rockstar has taken.

No game is beyond criticism, and there are things that can be improved. But the overall experience, the characters, the world, the freedom, the music and the sheer amount of detail make this something special.

After 13 years, I didn't just want another GTA. I wanted a world I could lose myself in.

Rockstar, you've given me exactly that. 10/10. Worth the wait.

author: Bootiyboyboopbi
quote:
Pros:graphics, humor, immersion, expanded robbery system, characters, story, combat, expanded stealth system, random events, things to do, vice city as a whole, how big the map is, heat, cutscenes, very interactive vehicles, incapacitation, social media system.

Cons: npcs (context), Jason’s voice acting, fps drops down concerningly often.

When you look at these reviews you see the same stupid criticism, such as it being “woke”, which is a recurring criticism which has been debunked loads of times, fueled by conservatives that see every little thing as woke. Much of the other criticisms are just unrealistic demands like you not being able to destroy a building with a plane (obviously you cant do this dumbasses) which fuels the narrative that the graphics are underwhelming, which is also fueled by online clips that purposely wash out the graphics. You also see loads of people complaining about the ultimate edition, which is fair, in a way atleast, because i get that you’re mad about the “paywall” but the truth is that you aren’t missing out on anything at all and its not bothering me, atleast, in the slightest. We see people complaining about certain missions in chapter 1 such as where you have to fix jason’s house, which is pretty stupid criticism because first of all, its optional, second of all, it takes around 2 minutes and isn’t even that boring. 

There are some valid criticisms, tho. this is my personal criticism and i dont know if anyone thinks the same but the npcs feel underwhelming, which is disappointing considering they apparently had a whole team dedicated to them. For example, i kicked someones dog (accidentally) and they just  looked at me giving one insult and walking away, same goes for shooting up places, i shot up the mall and some npcs just stood still with a looped frightened animation which for me feels outdated.

The fps is concerning too. When i first heard that it going to be 30fps i didn’t care at all, the game is huge and too much for the ps5 to run at a stable 60fps. I had rdr2 in mind which despite having 30 fps, looked surprisingly smooth. In gta6 tho, the frame rate unfortunately doesn’t look as smooth. Well, im used to low fps so it isnt a problem for me but for other people who play games at 60 or 120fps it is a big problem. Another big problem with the 30 fps is that it often drops down to around 20-25. Rockstar said they will fix this on november 25 along with all the bugs (which i havent gotten yet) so its nothing to be concerned about i hope.

Gta6 has surprisingly met or even exceeded expectations for me, the pros noticeably outweigh the cons. This game is a masterpiece and open world wise is better than another rockstar masterpiece, rdr2. Can’t say much about the story yet but it is good so far.

Solid 9.

author: Yippiekayo
quote: 10/10: A Masterpiece That Sets a New Standard I am about 25 hours into Grand Theft Auto VI now, and I can honestly say I have never played anything better. Even though we still have to wait and see what the rest of the game and everything after brings, it is already an instant 10 out of 10 in my book. The characters are unforgettable from the very first minute. Their chemistry, sharp dialogue, and emotional depth make every cutscene and chaotic road trip feel alive. The massive world is genuinely overwhelming in the best way. Every neighborhood, swamp, highway, and coastline feels dense with life, secrets, and stories waiting to be discovered. Even better, it is a gorgeous world. Lighting, water reflections, weather changes, and tiny environmental details look breathtaking at every turn. The missions never get stale. Whether you are pulling off tense heists, tearing through high speed chases, or diving into creative side activities, the variety and pacing keep you hooked hours on end. And to anyone worried about the grounded, everyday moments where you do something with Lucia: those parts feel completely natural, just the kind of normal, relatable things anyone in a relationship does, and they only make up a tiny fraction of the overall game anyway. Regarding the 30 FPS: yes, you can visually notice it in certain moments, but it is implemented in the best way possible. The frame pacing is so smooth that you genuinely do not feel it while playing. On top of all that, the little details really push the game over the top. Crowds panic realistically, traffic adapts to chaos, and the police feel smart and unpredictable rather than scripted. The radio stations, commercials, and soundtrack are packed with personality and set the mood effortlessly while you drive, and the freedom is completely seamless. You can go from a quiet, scenic moment on the water to full blown mayhem in seconds without ever breaking immersion. My only real disappointment has nothing to do with the game itself: it is a real shame there is no physical disc release, as a game this good definitely deserves to be in a physical collection. Also, all this pointless review bombing is completely ridiculous. People really need to start thinking on their own and form their own opinion instead of blindly parroting their favorite streamers. So far, Grand Theft Auto VI delivers everything fans wanted and more, and if it keeps this up, it will easily stand as one of the greatest experiences in gaming history.

quote: Una experiencia que redefine lo que significa jugar un videojuegoPocas veces un videojuego consigue sorprenderme hasta este punto. GTA es, sencillamente, una producción extraordinaria y probablemente la mejor experiencia que he tenido en muchos años. Desde los primeros momentos queda claro que estamos ante algo especial, una obra desarrollada con una ambición y un nivel de calidad difíciles de **** apartado gráfico es espectacular, pero lo realmente impresionante va mucho más allá de la fidelidad visual. La iluminación, los escenarios, las animaciones y la naturalidad con la que se comporta el mundo construyen una inmersión pocas veces vista. Es de esos juegos en los que uno deja de sentir que está recorriendo un escenario virtual y empieza a percibir que forma parte de un mundo **** historia merece un reconocimiento especial. Su desarrollo narrativo, los personajes y la manera en que se construye cada situación demuestran un trabajo creativo de primer nivel. A esto se suma una atención al detalle extraordinaria: hay una intención y un cuidado detrás de prácticamente cada elemento del juego.Respeto las opiniones de quienes no han quedado satisfechos, porque la percepción de cada jugador es subjetiva. Sin embargo, me resulta difícil comprender el fundamento de algunas críticas cuando el resultado evidencia semejante despliegue de calidad, creatividad y excelencia **** estamos simplemente ante un buen videojuego. Estamos ante una producción que eleva el estándar de la industria y demuestra lo que se puede conseguir cuando no se escatima en ambición ni en detalles.Para mí, es una obra maestra. De esas experiencias que justifican por qué amo los videojuegos y que permanecerán en la memoria durante muchos años.

author: Joel0520
quote:
The game features a wonderful story that encourages you to grow attached to its locations and **** graphical quality and level of realism are far superior to any other game released during the same period; the realism, in particular, is absolutely beyond reproach.
Some missions may seem pointless at first, but they actually serve to help you bond with the character and become familiar with their daily routines.Honestly, this game is very different from GTA 5 and really shouldn't be compared to it, for two reasons:
- There is a 13-year gap between the two games.
- They tell different stories.

Naturally, it has its flaws—which is to be expected, given that it was released only recently.
There are occasional bugs, and—based on what I’ve seen online (though I have yet to verify this myself)—it seems you cannot run over every type of NPC.
Is this a limiting factor? Not necessarily. You just have to know how to enjoy the story—though I do understand that in a game where you’re supposedly able to do anything, you’d expect to be able to do exactly that.

author: N1NJAPIG
quote:
Don't listen to the haters! Social media has genuinely ruined parts of gaming by turning everything into a competition over who can hate something the loudest. People purposely nitpick, spread negativity, and jump on whatever hate trend is popular that week. Honestly, it's getting old. One of the most annoying things about modern gaming is seeing people label practically every game with female characters as "WOKE."  Can we just enjoy video games again?

GTA 6 takes immersion to an entirely different level. Sure, the story takes a little time to get going in Chapter 1, but give it time. Things pick up, the story gets juicy (just like Lucia's ), and before you know it, you're completely invested.

And here's the thing: GTA 6 isn't just about rushing through missions. It's about living in the world. If you're getting burned out on the story, there's an entire world waiting for you to explore. This isn't a Call of Duty campaign that you finish in a weekend. Think Red Dead Redemption 2, but with the insanity, freedom, and personality that only GTA can deliver.

Buy guns, go fishing, get into random fights, steal wheelchairs, steal cars, shoot stuff, explore the incredible underwater environments, check out the aquatic life, hit the gym, lift weights, drink protein, interact with strangers, discover random encounters, explore businesses, cruise around Vice City, and get lost in all the ridiculous things happening around you.

It's the little details that make this game special. The environmental interactions, NPC behavior, incredible animations, weather, wildlife, vehicle details, character interactions, and the sheer amount of activity happening around you make the world feel alive. You can start out intending to complete one mission and somehow spend the next two hours doing absolutely everything except that mission. 

And PLEASE, stop letting fake gaming news and rage-bait content dictate your opinion before you've even experienced a game yourself. A few things to remember:

• Check your sources. Look for information from Rockstar's official website and verified social media accounts.

• Don't trust random thumbnails. Just because someone puts "LEAKED," "CONFIRMED," or "BREAKING NEWS" in giant red letters doesn't make it true.

• Be careful with out-of-context clips. Edited gameplay, old footage, fan-made trailers, and AI-generated content can easily fool people.

• Look for multiple sources. If something sounds unbelievable, wait for credible gaming outlets to verify it before sharing it.

• Stop confusing opinions with facts. Someone disliking a game doesn't mean it's objectively bad, and someone enjoying it doesn't mean they're wrong either.

At the end of the day, gaming is supposed to be FUN. You don't have to love everything Rockstar does, and constructive criticism is perfectly fine. But there's a difference between having an opinion and making it your mission to ruin everyone else's experience.

I'm having an absolute blast with GTA 6 right now. The world is ridiculously immersive, there's always something happening, and I genuinely find myself not wanting to leave it.

Stop watching people tell you why you shouldn't enjoy a game and go experience it for yourself.

This game is like crack.

author: chudLuc
quote: I feel like a lot of people are so focused on finding reasons to hate GTA 6 that they're overlooking just how much work and attention to detail has gone into it.After playing it, what impressed me the most wasn't even the graphics themselves, but the sheer level of craftsmanship behind the entire experience. The subtle character animations, the environmental details, the way everything is designed and put together, even the smallest interactions that most players probably wouldn't think twice about. There's an incredible amount of thought behind things that seem so effortless on the **** that's what I think people underestimate. Creating a world that feels believable isn't just about making it look realistic. It's about making thousands of tiny elements work together naturally, to the point where you barely notice how complex they actually are. That kind of polish doesn't happen by accident. It takes years of development, countless iterations, and an insane amount of coordination between artists, animators, programmers, and **** course, the game isn't above criticism. No game is, especially one carrying expectations this massive. But there's a difference between genuinely criticising something and completely dismissing the work behind **** don't have to think GTA 6 is a masterpiece to appreciate what Rockstar has accomplished on a technical and creative level. Personally, I think the attention to detail alone deserves far more recognition than it's getting. Sometimes I feel like we've become so accustomed to technological progress that we forget just how difficult it is to create something at this scale.

author: Scupio
quote: I'm 40 years old, I've played every single GTA game, and I've been looking forward to this one for what feels like **** something happened over the past few years. Video games just stopped holding my attention the way they used to. I'd start a game, enjoy it for a while, and then eventually lose interest. I honestly started wondering if I'd simply outgrown that feeling of being completely absorbed in a game.Well, GTA VI brought it back.I actually took two days off work for the release, with the whole weekend still ahead of me. I played pretty much all day yesterday. And when I woke up this morning, the first thing I felt was genuine excitement about getting back into the game.I haven't felt that in such a long time. And man, it feels good.Yesterday, my brothers and I were all playing separately while hanging out on Discord, constantly telling each other about the little things we'd discovered. Everyone I know who's playing seems just as blown **** the funny thing is, I've barely explored anything yet.I'm still hanging around the area near The Cheeky Mutineer and that nudist bar. I haven't even properly left the neighborhood. The furthest I've progressed in the story is the mission where you get your car repaired.That's it.Instead, I've been walking everywhere. Grabbing coffee, sitting by the ocean, fishing, diving, watching NPCs and their reactions, looking for random events, exploring nature, scanning wildlife, taking selfies with **** somehow, just doing all of that is already giving me more joy than most games have in **** can we talk about the graphics for a second? I'm playing on a PS5 Pro with an OLED TV, and I honestly don't think I've ever been this blown away by a game's visuals. The lighting, the atmosphere, the level of detail... it's absolutely breathtaking. And despite all the discussions about 30 FPS, I genuinely don't notice it while playing. I'm just completely immersed in this world.I haven't even made it to downtown Vice City yet. I can't wait to eventually cruise down Ocean Drive, explore the clubs, discover new neighborhoods, and see what else Rockstar has waiting for me.I've seen such a tiny fraction of this world, and knowing how much is still out there makes me ridiculously happy.After all these years, I finally have that feeling again. That feeling of wanting to get lost in a video game, of thinking about it when I'm not playing, of waking up excited to jump back in.I didn't realize how much I'd missed it until GTA VI gave it back to **** honestly, that's probably the best thing I could say about this game.

author: jbalves2003
quote: Honestly, review-bombing GTA VI with a zero because it runs at 30 FPS is just wild. Maybe it’s people who can’t get into the game and fall back on the same tired excuse. When I’m actually playing, I never even think about the frame rate. This game is so immersive that the number in the corner stops mattering. And let’s be real: in a while we’ll be able to play it on PC at whatever frame rate we want, so it’s a temporary issue at **** for the game itself: I didn’t expect anything less from Rockstar, but they still managed to surprise me. GTA VI feels like the true heir to Red Dead Redemption 2. It has the same obsessive attention to detail, the same patience, and the same love for world-building, but with the chaos and humor that only GTA can **** most impressive thing for me is how alive the world feels. I’ll set a waypoint for a mission and start driving, and then something happens on the way. A random encounter, a chase, something absurd on the street. Next thing I know, I’ve completely forgotten about the mission. That’s the sign of a truly great open world: the journey is just as good as the **** characters are incredible, the atmosphere is unreal, and the events that unfold around you make the world feel like it keeps moving whether you’re there or not. Does it have bugs? Sure, and that’s normal for a game this massive and ambitious. Haha, they’re mostly part of the charm, and nothing that breaks the experience.Rockstar did what they’ve always done: they raised the bar again. I just want to say thank you for giving us GTA V, Red Dead Redemption 2, and now GTA VI. And I won’t even list the older games, because they’re part of our childhood too, and they’re the reason so many of us were here on day one.Verdict: a generational masterpiece.

author: joshbegood07
quote:
Genuinely one of the best games I have ever played. It's a 10 from me but I'll list a couple things I've noticed. 

Pros:
Graphics are really good
Story is good so far (on chapter 3 as I'm writing this) the dynamic between Jason and Lucia is amazing, you can tell that there relationship has its rockyness to it but it seems they are doing their best to try and not repeat/relive that.
The side quest experience/exploration is top notch, I really like that the ways to make money are highlighted on the map so I'm not left guessing if what I'm doing makes me good money or not.
The driving is so much better than GTAV (besides NPC's want to cut me off when speeding on the highway)
The police system is really neat, I like that I can lower the heat by changing clothes, which forces me to take a look and go to all the shops and explore the locations.
Moses' car repo missions were really fun and rewarding!
As of right now I dont have many cons
Cons:
NPC driving that I mentioned earlier.
It seems really easy to fall off of dirt bikes, especially when offroading (I'm talking about a branch on the ground knocked me off.
The shooting system isn't as good as GTAV IMO, sometimes I'm left guessing where my shots are going.
In the police chase before you go to vice city, the cops seemed to spawn in the foliage (?) 
Other than that, I have loved my experience so far and will be playing a lot more.
Hats off to Rockstar!

quote: Grand Theft Auto VI is a game that, despite the decade-plus gap since its last installment, still manages to exceed expectations. It features unprecedented interactivity and reactivity, something that makes past titles, as amazing as they were, look rudimentary in comparison. This is a game with a razor-sharp focus and vision. It prioritizes player involvement to make you feel grounded in its world in a way no other title has, especially not this generation. Rockstar fixed practically all of its past gameplay design pitfalls, from narrow mission parameters to painfully easy aiming and weightless driving. Everything here is beautifully executed. author: Fosquiitoo
quote: I’ve put 12 hours into the game and I’m absolutely loving it. The world feels alive, and I really appreciate how the gameplay draws inspiration from *Red Dead Redemption 2*—the way it adopts that deliberate, measured pace where actions have real consequences is just incredible. Speaking of *RDR2*, I think it was a brilliant decision to lean into that style; in a map as vast and feature-rich as Vice City, it’s essential that the world feels alive. Furthermore, the possibilities within the game—many of which I’ve yet to even discover—seem endless; something different is happening at every turn. Naturally, not every element from *RDR2* has been carried over—it’s clear they aimed for a blend of realism and high-octane action, combining the DNA of *GTA V* and *RDR2*. In my view, they’ve pulled it off perfectly; I have no complaints. As for the story, it’s been spot on so far—it hooked me from the very first moment and continues to meet all my expectations. Regarding the bugs, I can certainly understand why some people are disappointed. After years of wait, it’s only natural to feel let down by such issues—some of them really make you wonder: "How could a company like Rockstar let this happen?" That said, I haven’t encountered any myself, and I hope my luck holds. To be honest, most of these bugs aren’t even that bad. As for the gameplay: if you’re expecting an open-world game where your actions have no consequences—where you can simply go around destroying cars—then I’m sorry to say this game isn’t for you. While you certainly have the freedom to do such things within the open world, there will be consequences. If your only goal is to destroy things and flee from the police, you might as well stick to *GTA V*. It feels to me that, although the developers may have aimed to blend *GTA V* and *RDR2*, the result is much closer to *RDR2*; it’s a game meant to be played at a measured pace, allowing you to appreciate the atmosphere and the remarkably well-realized interactions with NPCs. Graphically, it’s mind-blowing—without exaggeration, it’s the best I’ve ever seen in a video game; I can’t find a single flaw in this regard. In conclusion, based on my time with it so far, it feels like a perfect game. While I haven’t finished the story yet, even if the narrative doesn’t quite meet my expectations, everything else certainly does—which is why I give it a 10/10.

author: DenMikers
quote:
I'm somewhere between 10 and 30 hours in, and I can already say Rockstar has done it again. Vice City doesn't feel like a map to clear. It feels like a place that carries on whether or not you're there. Buildings you can actually walk into and random encounters that catch you off guard make the world feel lived-in, and the NPCs behave like people with their own business, not set dressing waiting for you to cause chaos.

The heart of it is the partnership between Jason and Lucia. Rockstar has built plenty of memorable leads, but here the bond between the two is the engine of the story, and I bought into it completely. 

The end of Chapter 1 is the best example: a perfectly judged moment that I won't spoil, but it hooked me for everything that followed.

Story, world, gameplay, and tech all land, and each one lifts the others instead of competing for attention. I haven't finished yet, so this is a verdict in progress, but nothing so far suggests it will slip.

author: matuebr
quote: Clearly, some of the criticism stems from pure ill will, or simply from ignorance and a lack of understanding—but let’s examine this more calmly. GTA VI is, without a doubt, the most ambitious game of this generation. From its graphics to the intricate details of its gameplay, the title draws strong inspiration from its predecessor, RDR2—in some respects, even surpassing it. The visuals are the best seen this generation, pushing the PS5 to its absolute limit. The gameplay is arguably the most realistic in the franchise; cars, motorcycles, and other vehicles feel more authentic and are far more enjoyable to drive. The shooting mechanics have also been refined, striking a perfect balance between challenge and accessibility—avoiding the overly simplistic feel of the previous title. The variety of vehicles in the world is equally impressive; it is rare to see the same car twice, which gives the environment a natural, lived-in quality. As for the characters, they represent two extremes. Lucia is entirely impulsive—she is always drawn to activities that promise quick, high-risk rewards. She is a skilled shooter and an expert behind the wheel, all paired with a natural, magnetic charisma. Jason, on the other hand, is the complete opposite. A former military man carrying significant trauma, he is cold, reserved, and a man of few words. He constantly strives to maintain control over any situation, remains unimpressed by luxury, and is focused solely on survival. Taking all this into account—and keeping this review spoiler-free—GTA VI offers a true gaming experience; it challenges players to test their own limits and choices. The freedom afforded when undertaking activities even allows you to put your own character to the test—all wrapped in stunning graphics and a cinematic soundtrack.

author: SolaireFlair
quote:
I'm having a good time so far. No, I don't think the game is the next coming of Jesus like all these outlets would have you believe, but it's a really solid entry in the GTA series.

I know some people are complaining about some of the chore-like side activities, which is a fair criticism if you're more accustomed to GTA games that get to the point with the high-octane action, but this game inherits more DNA from Red Dead Redemption 2 than it does GTA, which is why it has so many life simulation activities that you can partake in.

The game handles like any other GTA game, with a few modern updates like left stick click to sprint instead of mashing the A (or X on PlayStation) button to sprint, gunplay feels crisp, and even at 30 FPS, I don't find myself fighting against the controls or experiencing any sluggishness.

The standout for me has been Jason and Lucia's relationship. Gone are the broken household dynamics of Michael De Santa in favor of a more loving, realistic portrayal of relationship dynamics. Early on in the story, the game tasks Jason with buying flowers, repairing the house, and doing a few other odd-job chores in preparation for Lucia's arrival (which contrary to some online personalities do not make you a cuck. Imagine thinking that doing nice things for the person you love makes you lesser for it), and it's all really refreshing in a series that typically indulges in stereotypes of toxic relationship dynamics. I find myself caring for them, their relationship, and it pushes me to go out of my way to engage with the relationship mechanics because I'm invested in seeing them do well together. The two of them feel like deep, realistically written characters that I find myself truly enjoying.

GTA6 has a whole lot of positives going for it, but I don't think it really evolves beyond what Rockstar has done in the past. It's an amalgamation of some of the best features of Rockstar's catalogue of excellent titles, but it doesn't really feel like such a huge evolution that it deserves this grand, vaunted status that many people are giving it. It's a great game, but I don't really feel like it's revolutionary. Maybe my opinion will change the deeper into the game I get and I'll come back to edit my review, but for now I don't think it's the best thing since sliced bread, it's just a really tight, well written open world action adventure that slots neatly into Rockstar's game lineup.

author: DhiAllTheWay
quote: Imagine taking everything that made Grand Theft Auto San Andreas,Grand Theft Auto IV  and Red Dead Redemption 2  unforgettable and dialing it up to 11, all without sacrificing the classic open world chaos the series is famous for. That is GTA VI.From the moment you step into Leonida, the world feels truly alive. You don’t just pass through the environment; you physically interact with objects, feel genuinely noticed by surrounding NPCs, and stumble into side content that unfolds emergently just from engaging with your surroundings. Exploration, whether on foot or diving underwater, is endlessly rewarding, especially across a massive map packed with hundreds of lootable interiors. Best of all, Rockstar has finally reinvented its mission design: getting slapped with a "Mission Failed" screen just because you stepped 50 meters off the beaten path is officially a thing of the past.Core gameplay has received a massive overhaul. Between an innovated wanted system, a revamped weapon inventory, and emergent open world heists, even everyday crimes feel tense and immersive. For the first time, stealing a car or robbing a store isn't just a mindless reflex. You actually have to make a plan before executing it, because the upgraded police AI makes every pursuit genuinely challenging and thrilling. Behind the wheel, every vehicle has a satisfying, weighty feel with fun handling across the board, brutal car crashes, and the Euphoria physics engine operating at its absolute **** narrative matches the gameplay step for step. The writing is impressive, and the pacing is masterful, taking its time as a slow burn so you build genuine attachment to the characters before the story explodes into massive heat and packed action.Visually and technically, this is the best real time rendering we have ever witnessed. Every detail shines, from individual hair strands and physics to realistic muscle and fabric physics, insane global illumination, a massive draw distance, and ultra detailed water and sand textures. Leonida looks breathtaking whether you're a mile up in the sky or an inch away from a surface. Even the animation system is on another level, dynamically changing how you perform the exact same interaction depending on your walking state, approach angle, or whatever you are currently **** VI is a true masterpiece. With this sheer density of mechanics and content, it’s clear this world is built to be an unmatched platform for future Online updates and RolePlay servers. It was worth every single day of the 13 year wait.

author: Goat_Man

Like Red Dead Redemption 2, it opens slowly and favors a deliberate pace, rewarding players who take their time and soak in the world. The 30fps cap is noticeable at moments, but it's a fair trade for a game that feels like it was beamed back from the past. It is disappointing to see some corners of the internet stoking outrage over a game that was never made for them. Does it have flaws? Of course. But don't let the loudest voices, those who profit from negativity and recycle bad-faith takes, shape your opinion. Play it and decide for yourself.

author: OverG101
quote: GTA VI — The Instant Gratification Generation Has Forgotten How to Appreciate Video Games.**It's honestly ridiculous to watch the review bombing of GTA VI and realize how part of the gaming community has completely lost the ability to appreciate a game that requires patience, attention, and ****'re living in the TikTok generation. A generation addicted to 15-second videos, constant stimulation, instant dopamine hits, and the desperate need to be rewarded every five minutes. People have become so conditioned to instant gratification that anything requiring them to slow down is immediately labeled boring.A good portion of these complaints seem to come from people who expected GTA VI to be nothing more than a glorified GTA RP server. Drive around, cause chaos, chase cheap thrills, and repeat. The moment they're presented with an experience that prioritizes atmosphere, storytelling, realism, world-building, and attention to detail, suddenly the game is "too slow."Rockstar didn't spend all these years building a world of this magnitude just to deliver another mindless dopamine simulator. There's value in taking your time, observing the environment, exploring without rushing, listening to conversations, and allowing a story to unfold naturally.That doesn't mean GTA VI is perfect or immune to criticism. Technical issues and questionable design decisions deserve legitimate discussion. But there's an enormous difference between thoughtfully criticizing a game and throwing out zero scores because of unrealistic expectations, frustration, or an inability to appreciate something that doesn't constantly stimulate your brain.**Maybe the problem isn't that GTA VI doesn't provide enough stimulation. Maybe the problem is that part of this generation has become so addicted to instant dopamine that they can no longer appreciate anything that demands patience.**Not every game needs to function like an endless TikTok feed. And not every masterpiece needs to compromise its identity to satisfy an audience that has forgotten how to slow down and enjoy an experience.

author: Havoken
quote:
I did not expect to enjoy this game as much as I have.
The story is rather sweet, and you’re not forced to do things for Lucia in the beginning as some may claim. You can choose to not help her and their relationship dynamic changes based on your actions. There’s a great story, that is refreshingly slow to kick into action. You have a choice to speedrun or slow down and take in the breathtaking sights. There’s great characters with their own sense of humour that makes the world feel alive. 
Chapter 2 is where this really shines. I appreciate the “ride or die” dynamic between Jason and Lucia and you can really see how much love went into this game and its characters. 
The hospital shootout into driving away in an ambulance was an epic sequence where you can really feel how one’s world can be turned upside down in mere minutes - with everything on the line (such as savings for Tomás and the crib you had built.) Finding your feet afterwards is where the world unlocks even more, where you can now freely swap between Lucia and Jason - and it feels seamless (like driving as Lucia and swapping to Jason in the same car, and she stays on the route you’ve set.)
Not to mention the amount of hidden collectibles across this world. There is so much to discover and explore that i’m so excited to see this from start to finish. It’s baffling how people can make negative reviews when there’s still so much story and exploring to go. The interactions. subtle body language and facial expressions that the team did such an amazing job it looks almost real. Not to mention the wanted mechanics of changing clothes, cars and appearances - or even your loadout being visually represented on your back. I half expected to see a gun clipping with a duffel bag on my back but no, small details adds up. Like if you’re dancing, with a coffee in your hand - you can see the liquid slosh around in the cup. 
This game is dangerous, because it’s so easy to get lost in. 
While minor bugs happen, but none too big to note - the gameplay itself makes up for it. 

The only real gripe is 30FPS and it being console-only for now. None of this nonsense about “having” to be a good boyfriend to Lucia or “too slow” You can make that choice yourself. Make your own playthrough. How the rest of the story goes is dependent on *your* choices. 
It’s a fantastic game and well deserved the anticipation.

author: Plumblmp
quote: I waited 13 years for this, like everyone. After the first few days, here's my honest take: it's an incredible game, but it is not the flawless 99 the press is **** good: the world is aliveOne session went like this. I rob a store and lose the cops. A car crashes right in front of me, two guys run off and leave their loot, I grab it, and a police car chasing them spots me. Back to running. Then my neighbor stops me and asks me to buy her some booze. At the liquor store something looks off in the back, so I check it out: there's a drug deal going on, I take everyone out and walk away with the cash and the coke. Then I look at the clock and realize I have to go to work. None of that was a mission. No other open world does **** best thing in the game: MattiaI'm Italian, and for once an Italian character in GTA isn't "mamma mia, pizza, mafia." Mattia is a real Italian guy from 2026: he says "bro" every three words, mixes Italian and English ("ma bro come on", "let's go there dai bro") and acts like he owns the place. In the pool scene a guy calls him "Mario" to mess with him, and he doesn't take the bait. He just says "amore, let's go somewhere else" and leaves. That's exactly what my friends and I would do abroad. We're loud and cocky, but when things get serious, you walk away. Jason says "let's go outside," throws punches and gets the cops called on him. In one scene you learn who both of them are. Mattia could honestly be in my group of friends, and that's the best compliment I can give the **** bad: bugs, and a lot of themOn Series S I've had my car clip through lamp posts and got stuck behind a hedge with no way out, not even a grenade to kill myself and respawn. Then I fell into a giant water tank with no ladder. The cops jumped in after me and we all just swam there together, trapped, until a police helicopter shot me from above. Funny, sure, but it shouldn't happen in an $80 game. The Series S version also runs at 720p with frame drops, and there's still no post-launch patch and no word from **** other problem: it's too muchThe map is huge, and at some point exploration turns into dispersion. Some story missions won't unlock until you've made enough money, so the game pushes you into side activities and then floods you with distractions. I played 6 hours before seeing Lucia, the co-protagonist from every trailer. On top of that you get a mandatory mission where you play Tenebrae Lux, a black-and-white "artsy" game inside the game. I get the joke, but it's deadly boring and it sits in the slowest part of the story. The bank turning you down because of your credit score felt forced too, even though I see the satire.VerdictGTA 6 is a masterpiece buried under too much content and too many bugs. When it works, nothing comes close. But a game this good doesn't need to be this big. Play it on PS5 or Series X if you can, and wait for patches if you're on Series S

+ The driving physics are a big improvement for me. GTA 5 driving always felt too arcady for me. I just find myself abiding to the traffic laws because it feels so realistic.

- Feeling a bit handcuffed. Sometimes I don't want to care about what criminal actions I take, but the 'psycho' criminal status is always there. 

- Some of the missions are time sensitive and need to be completed immediately. Wish they could be completed anytime, so I wouldn't feel rushed to go do them immediately.

Cada misión está meticulosamente diseñada para ofrecer momentos de alta tensión, cinemáticas memorables y una libertad de acción que permite resolver los desafíos de múltiples maneras, premiando tanto la creatividad como la **** definitiva, vivir esta aventura ha sido un recordatorio de por qué este medio es capaz de trascender el simple entretenimiento. author: zantiagod7
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI es exactamente lo que esperaba: llevar las mecánicas, el nivel de detalle y la inmersión de Red Dead Redemption 2 a un mundo abierto moderno. Es como ver todo lo que Rockstar aprendió con sus anteriores entregas llevado a una nueva dimensión.

Lo que más me ha impresionado es la interacción con los NPC. El mundo se siente increíblemente vivo, tanto que terminas perdiéndote en él sin darte cuenta. Nunca he sido alguien que disfrute especialmente haciendo misiones secundarias, pero este juego consigue que quieras salir a explorar, interactuar con los personajes y descubrir qué puede ofrecer cada rincón del mapa.

Otro apartado que me ha encantado es su banda sonora, que acompaña perfectamente la ambientación y consigue darle todavía más personalidad al mundo. Y qué decir de su introducción: esa secuencia icónica del principio, con la presentación del logo de Rockstar, es de lo mejor que he visto en un videojuego. Es de esas intros que, por lo bien logradas que están, te dan ganas de volver a ver una y otra vez incluso después de haberlas visto varias veces.

Llevo apenas 13 horas jugadas y, sinceramente, es de lo mejor que he experimentado en un videojuego. Lo más impresionante es que ni siquiera he conseguido salir de los Cayos de Leonida. Hay tantas cosas por descubrir, tantas posibilidades de interacción y tanto por experimentar que siento que apenas he arañado la superficie. Es un mundo verdaderamente explotable, que constantemente te invita a perderte en él y a descubrir algo nuevo.

En definitiva, Grand Theft Auto VI está cumpliendo con creces mis expectativas. No se trata solamente de tener un mapa enorme o gráficos impresionantes, sino de conseguir que el mundo se sienta vivo y que quieras formar parte de él. Y si con apenas 13 horas siento que todavía tengo tanto por descubrir, no me imagino todo lo que me espera.

author: Mottakk7
quote: **8/10**The game is absolutely fantastic. The hand-to-hand combat is incredible, and the shooting mechanics retain the best aspects of RDR2 while introducing adjustments that make gunfights feel more dynamic and less sluggish.Vehicle physics are outstanding. You can genuinely feel that every vehicle has its own characteristics, from older cars and sports cars to motorcycles, which are particularly impressive. Aircraft are also very well implemented. Vehicles now feature deformation, and collisions are fantastic, with impressive damage physics that surpass GTA IV in several aspects. There are also plenty of small details that we love in GTA, such as being able to roll down windows and use turn **** open world is beautiful, from its graphics and atmosphere to its density and overall sense of life. Random events happen constantly, making the world feel unpredictable. You might steal a vehicle and suddenly find yourself in an unexpected situation, or attempt to rob a store only to discover that someone is already robbing it. Everything feels incredibly immersive, realistic, and **** new police system is also very well designed and balanced. However, I found escaping from up to three wanted levels a little too easy. Nevertheless, the system itself is excellent, and it is now possible to commit crimes without even triggering a police response if you manage to do them cleanly.Regarding the story and missions, the narrative is good, offers multiple endings, and provides a satisfying experience overall. Most main missions follow the same design philosophy as RDR2, which might frustrate some players. Personally, I don't mind this during the first playthrough, but it hurts replayability. The inability to replay individual missions is also disappointing.Furthermore, missions still follow the traditional GTA formula: go from point A to point B, eliminate enemies, and if you attempt to do something outside the intended approach, the mission fails. This lack of freedom in mission design is one of the game's biggest shortcomings.**My final score is 8/10.**- Gameplay: 10/10- Graphics: 10/10- Open World: 10/10- Story: 8/10- Missions: 8/10

author: mclandry99
quote:
The game feels phenomenal in all areas. The graphics are amazing and the world is immersive in the best way, with the player getting lost in all Vice City has to offer, even before most of the content has been unlocked through progressing in the main story. The NPC’s have unique qualities and attributes and even appearance contributing to this immersive world. These characters do not feel like “filler” but rather part of the world that has been built. The story waste no time making quick turns or “wow” moments keeping the player invested. The driving feels smoother and less uncertain as seen in previous titles, while vehicle health is more impactful making reckless driving a decision to be made rather than a default behavior. Money feels impactful and important making saving, spending, customizations, and deaths consequential. The combat feels smooth and well-designed both with and without a weapon. The protagonist customizability is expanded upon while also limited to protect the character’s backstory and place in Vice City.

Side note on editions:
The base game is amazing as aforementioned while in no way is limited substantively by a players choice to not buy the ultimate edition. The ultimate edition is an addition to an already immersive and expansive game giving the player more customizability options and extra content that is not pivotal to the overall experience of the game. It does not go the same route that some designers and studios go where it makes the player spend extra money or they are being left out and certainly is not pay-to-win in any capacity.

author: PrimordialGamer
quote:
As is often the case, the truth is somewhere in the middle:

GTA6 is not a 0/10 game.
However,  it is not a 10/10 game either. 

Graphics: 10
Performance: 5 (7 on ps5 pro)
Story: 6 (Subjective)
Controls: 7
Gameplay: 8
Sound effects: 8
BGM: 10

A solid game that attempts to take the series in a new direction. That is not necessarily a better direction but this will be different for everyone.

Visually, we have a flawed masterpiece. While the game is hyper-realistic, and altogether gorgeous, the performance WILL be noticed and will hurt the experience.  Less so on PS5 Pro. 

The writting is hit and miss. There is some of that old GTA charm mixed with a more serious and sometimes personal tone. Sometimes it lands, oftentimes it doesn't. 

The games sound may actually be the best part. The effects are solid and the dynamic music mixed with an amazing soundtrack is pure perfection.  Someone deserves a serious pat on the back for this.

The controls are good but at times there is some wonkyness to the vehicles. The Bullet time effect that you eventually get is fun, obviously this is not new territory. 

Overall gameplay is solid, you will find the classic random acts of violence style of GTA mixed with some more realistic aspects such as limited inventory space.

Prefiero mil veces un mundo que me haga sentir parte de él, donde tenga que pensar, adaptarme y disfrutar incluso de las actividades más cotidianas.Después de tantos años, puedo decir que valió la pena la espera. author: Sjogrenelis
quote:
An exceptional experience!
First of all, the graphics and physics are absolutely incredible. The improvements in environmental details, especially the water physics, waves, storms, and wind, are genuinely impressive. The world feels more realistic and dynamic than ever before, and the attention to detail is on another level.
The open world is absolutely massive, incredibly detailed, and, most importantly, alive. There’s something to do almost everywhere you look, and even when you’re not actively searching for activities, you’ll regularly stumble upon interesting characters, random encounters, and situations that lead you into even more things to explore. The world feels like it exists independently of the player, which is something Rockstar has become exceptionally good at.
Driving has also seen some welcome improvements. Vehicles feel noticeably heavier and more grounded than in GTA V, which I personally consider a positive change. The handling feels more deliberate and satisfying, striking a good balance between realism and enjoyment. The police system is another significant improvement, making encounters feel more dynamic and believable. I particularly appreciate smaller details, such as being able to target weak spots on vehicles to cause them to lose control or crash.
As for the story, both Jason and Lucia really grow on you as the narrative progresses. Their personalities and relationship develop naturally, and I found myself becoming increasingly invested in their journey. The supporting cast deserves recognition as well. Characters like Brian, Trenton, Cal, and Raul are genuinely well-written and contribute a lot to the overall experience.
One thing I genuinely struggle to understand is the amount of criticism the game has received during its first few days. Of course, everyone is entitled to their own opinion, and the game certainly won’t appeal to everyone. However, I believe a lot of the initial negativity comes from expectations that don’t necessarily align with what Rockstar was trying to achieve. I suspect that once more people have given the game a proper chance and experienced the story in its entirety, the general reception will become much more positive. The extraordinary critical reception, including its 99 rating, certainly reflects the quality I experienced.
For some additional context, Red Dead Redemption 2 has been my favourite game for years. Because of that, transitioning into GTA VI felt incredibly natural to me. I appreciate the slower, more deliberate pacing, the emphasis on immersion, and the way the game encourages you to experience its world rather than simply rush through the main storyline.
That said, I can understand why someone coming directly from GTA V might initially find the change in pacing and progression a little jarring. GTA VI takes a different approach in several areas, and I think adjusting to that philosophy is important to fully appreciating what the game offers.
Ultimately, GTA VI is an extraordinary achievement in open-world game design and storytelling. A truly exceptional experience, and another outstanding achievement from Rockstar Games. 10/10

author: BiGNekoOnKick
quote: Gta6 is a good step in a more immersive future for all rockstar games but that doesn’t mean it don’t come without problems. While 6 has introduced us to a whole slew of new elements to make not just the world of Leonida the most immersive but the next generation of games, it also reuses a ton of assets and systems from Red Dead Redemption 2. Putting it into my own words we basically done knew how this game would end before the first trailer even dropped. The ending well endings relatively end in a Bonnie and Clyde type style which in my opinion is the most basic way they could have ever taken the story direction of this game. The bad endings I personally have gotten have all included Jason and Lucia dying to the police during their final “getaway” and the only good ending I have got ended with Jason surrendering himself to save Lucia which I also think is a basic ending for such a acclaimed series. Overall however, GTA6 is a strong entry in the series that will age better with time. The story may lack and disappoint more than people could have ever thought but the fundamentals and world building of the game are the best in the entire franchise. The entire world of Leonida feels completely alive with something happening at all times, there is never a dull moment. To end this off, I have given it a 8/10 review mainly due to my gripe of so many reused systems and animations from Red Dead 2 and my huge disappointment in the story

author: Mohcent
quote: It’s the most beautiful GTA game ever made and arguably the best looking video game of all time. If anyone wants to see the absolute peak of what this generation of consoles is capable of, this game showcases it wonderfully. The unfortunate reality is that not every developer has a billion dollars to throw at making something like this happen. That said, the game does have performance issues and bugs that need ironing out. But let’s be realistic, there isn’t a single game of this scale and ambition that launches without its fair share of technical problems. I’m confident Rockstar will iron most of them out. But GTA 6 isn’t remarkable simply because of how incredible it looks. It’s remarkable because of the attention to detail in just about everything. From the liquid physics inside a bottle to Jason crossing his hair when his hair gets too long, to random NPCs having entire questlines unfold simply by going about their daily lives, whether you choose to interact with them or not. I watched a drug deal go down, followed the car transporting the drugs, tracked it all the way to its destination, and ended up blowing up the entire operation for my own profit. These are the kinds of experiences you rarely see in other video games, and GTA 6 is absolutely filled with ****’s all these seemingly insignificant details and interactions that come together to create something so much bigger than the sum of its parts. If a perfect video game ever exists, this might be it. No game is truly perfect, but GTA 6 deserves credit for coming closer than just about anything I’ve ever played.

author: Am1203
quote: Comprehensive Review and Initial Impressions of Grand Theft Auto VITo Whom It May Concern,I am writing to share my formal critique and initial impressions of Grand Theft Auto VI, having progressed nearly to the conclusion of the second chapter. Thus far, the title represents an extraordinary achievement in interactive entertainment, distinguishing itself markedly from its predecessors through its narrative depth, technical execution, and world-building.First and foremost, the opening sequence sets a distinct precedent for the franchise. Rather than relying on conventional series tropes, the game commences with a cutscene characterized by breathtaking visual fidelity and cinematic direction. This immediate immersion is sustained by the compelling dynamic between the dual protagonists, Jason and Lucia. Their partnership evokes the historical archetype of Bonnie and Clyde—the infamous criminal duo of the Great Depression. Much like Bonnie, Lucia is driven by a desire to escape poverty and achieve rapid financial security, whereas Jason mirrors Clyde through his background in the criminal underworld.Furthermore, the psychological complexity underlying Jason’s attachment to Lucia is particularly noteworthy. Raised in a harsh, crime-ridden environment, Jason attempted to alter his trajectory by enlisting in the military, only to return with psychological trauma and a profound lack of institutional or governmental support. Consequently, he appears to view Lucia not merely as a partner, but as a source of redemption and an opportunity to establish the family unit he was denied. His deep devotion to her—and his palpable fear of losing her—stems from an underlying fear of isolation.Their contrasting temperaments create a remarkably balanced interpersonal and tactical dynamic. Shaped by his military discipline, Jason maintains a calm, calculated demeanor that tempers Lucia’s impulsiveness, which is rooted in her upbringing on the streets. Conversely, Lucia’s boldness injects a necessary sense of momentum into Jason’s cautious nature. This synergy extends seamlessly into combat encounters, where Jason serves as the primary offensive force while Lucia provides vital tactical support. Additionally, the supporting cast, including characters such as Cal and Brian, are endowed with distinct backstories and personal ambitions that enrich the broader narrative tapestry.From a technical and mechanical standpoint, the vehicular handling model is a triumph. The developers have successfully synthesized the realistic weight and physics of Grand Theft Auto IV with the responsive accessibility of Grand Theft Auto V, resulting in a finely tuned driving experience. This is complemented by extraordinary vehicular detail and a remarkably authentic collision physics engine.Finally, the environmental design of the game world is nothing short of breathtaking. The map offers remarkable ecological diversity, transitioning seamlessly from sun-drenched beaches to dense woodlands. Vice City itself is rendered with astonishing intricacy, particularly at night, when its vibrant atmosphere and lighting truly come to **** conclusion, Grand Theft Auto VI has delivered a truly exceptional experience thus far, seamlessly blending nuanced character drama with industry-leading technical craftsmanship. I look forward to experiencing the remainder of the narrative.

author: ImaSpecialBoi
quote: 10/10 — Rockstar Has Redefined Open-World Gaming. An Absolute Masterpiece.After 30 hours with Grand Theft Auto VI, I can confidently say this is one of the most extraordinary games I’ve ever played. I’ve experienced hundreds of titles across PC and consoles, and very few have impressed me on this level. Rockstar hasn’t simply improved its formula; it has raised the standard for what an open-world game can be.What amazes me most is the realism and attention to detail. The world feels genuinely alive rather than like an enormous map built solely around the player. Every neighborhood, street, and environment feels meticulously crafted. NPC behaviors, environmental storytelling, animations, and countless small interactions combine to create a believable world that seems to carry on whether I’m watching or not. Even mundane moments can be fascinating because the setting is so convincing.Thirty hours in, I still regularly discover details that make me stop and appreciate the sheer amount of work behind this game. I can lose myself simply exploring, observing the people around me, or seeing what happens when I interact with the environment. That sense of immersion is rare, and GTA VI delivers it **** amount of side content is equally staggering. There’s so much to experience outside the main storyline that I never feel pressured to rush from mission to mission. Whether I’m exploring, trying another activity, or stumbling into an unexpected encounter, there’s always something new to do. The world rewards curiosity, and after 30 hours, I still feel like I’ve barely scratched the surface. Importantly, it doesn’t feel like a giant checklist of repetitive tasks. It feels like a place full of possibilities.World design is where Rockstar truly separates itself from the competition. Plenty of games offer enormous maps, but size means little without substance. GTA VI delivers incredible density, variety, atmosphere, and authenticity. Every area feels distinct yet part of one cohesive world. The care poured into its environments makes exploring just as rewarding as progressing through the **** the realism goes well beyond graphics. It’s the combination of physics, character animations, environmental reactions, believable behavior, and interconnected systems that makes everything click. Any one detail might seem minor in isolation; together, they create an experience that feels remarkably natural. This is the difference between a technically impressive open world and one that genuinely feels alive.I also think Rockstar deserves credit for the engineering ambition here. As someone accustomed to high-performance PC gaming, I appreciate smooth frame rates, but I also recognize that technical excellence isn’t measured by FPS alone. The environmental complexity, visual fidelity, simulation, and sheer scope of this world are astonishing, especially considering the hardware the developers are working with. It’s an impressive achievement that deserves to be judged as a complete **** years, Red Dead Redemption 2 was my personal gold standard for immersive open-world design. Its atmosphere, environmental storytelling, and obsessive attention to detail felt almost impossible to surpass. Yet Rockstar has somehow done exactly that. GTA VI takes the same commitment to authenticity and pushes it even further, creating a world that feels more dynamic, densely realized, and endlessly engaging.What makes GTA VI special isn’t a single revolutionary feature. It’s how everything supports everything else. The realism makes the world believable. The world design makes exploration irresistible. The side content makes every session feel full of opportunities. All those systems work together to create something greater than the sum of its **** course, 30 hours isn’t enough to experience everything a game of this scale has to offer. But it’s more than enough for me to know how exceptional the experience has been so far. I still find myself eager to explore the next neighborhood, discover another detail, and see what else Rockstar has **** VI has set a new gold standard for open-world gaming, surpassing even Rockstar’s previous masterpiece, Red Dead Redemption 2. It’s a monumental achievement in realism, immersion, and world design, and I believe other developers will be measuring their games against it for years.10/10. Thirty hours in, and I’m still completely blown away. Rockstar has outdone itself again.
