author: Manu1026
quote:
Exactement ce que j’attendais de ce GTA VI. Je ne suis absolument pas surpris de la direction prise par Rockstar. Les seuls qui râlent sont les joueurs habitués aux jeux sandbox et à GTA V Online, qui n’ont probablement jamais pris la peine de jouer à RDR2.

Et c’est assez marrant de voir les joueurs console se plaindre du 30 FPS alors qu’ils n’ont quasiment connu que ça jusqu’à l’arrivée de la PS5 et de la Xbox Series X !

Il faut aussi rappeler que ces consoles ont déjà 6 ans et qu’elles utilisent des processeurs basés sur l’architecture Zen 2, alors qu’on arrive bientôt au Zen 6 sur PC ! On ne peut pas demander à du matériel vieux de six ans, basé sur une architecture qui a déjà plusieurs générations de ****, de rivaliser avec les technologies actuelles. À un moment, il faut aussi comprendre les limites du matériel sur lequel on joue.

Personnellement, je trouve que Rockstar a pris la bonne décision en privilégiant des environnements extrêmement détaillés, vivants et une simulation du monde poussée plutôt que de sacrifier une partie de ses ambitions pour nous proposer du 60 FPS avec moins de détails, moins de vie et potentiellement moins d’interactions. Dans un jeu comme GTA VI, la densité de population, les comportements des PNJ, la circulation et toutes les interactions avec l’environnement demandent énormément de ressources processeur. Ce n’est pas simplement une question de carte graphique !

Pour moi, il est donc difficile de reprocher quoi que ce soit à Rockstar concernant les 30 FPS. Si certains ont des reproches à faire, c’est les propriétaire de PS5 Pro. Mais ils devraient plutôt en vouloir à Sony plutôt qu’à Rockstar.
 Une console vendue 900 € qui conserve une architecture CPU très proche de la PS5 classique, avec seulement un léger gain de fréquence côté processeur. Le véritable gain se situe surtout au niveau du GPU et des capacités graphiques. Sony aurait dû fournir un processeur avec une nouvelle génération d’architecture Zen 3 où Zen 4 et là je suis quasiment sûr qu’une version 60fps aurait vu le jour sur la PS5 Pro!

author: RateMN29
quote:
This game looks fantastic, feels alive and is extremely funny sometimes. When playing it for hours straight you get **** in the world of Leonida. However this game does have some slight flaws unlike other people might suggest.

The story starts of slow, which I am kind of disappointed about, since GTA 5 started off with a big heist. However the action is reserved for later in the game which is fine. With every mission you don't know how it will end and that's what keeps you playing. There is so much to do in this game it is quite overwhelming, in a good way. I do not like the voice of Jason, it just kind of feels forced. But that's not a big deal breaker for me. Rockstar games really tried to change their mission style, and I appreciate that. But it still has very linear missions for an open world game. 

I am not a big fan of RPG aspects myself. Like maintaining weight, leveling up health, stamina, etc. For me it just feels like chores especially when I want to get in to the action, but I can see why other people would like it. The 30 FPS is expected for such a big game, and feels fine after getting used to it.  

I am a big fan of graphical realism but a game shouldn't realistic in every way. Like having animations for everything, needing to refill and repair your car. This game almost crosses the line of being too realistic in that way. I do think this is the best "fictional world" Rockstar games has ever made, but it's not my favorite story. Red Dead Redemption II still takes that win. 

The music in this game is awesome, just like in every other GTA. The "new" podcasts are hilarious.

I also do not recommend buying the ultimate edition, because it is just not worth it. The game is worth $80 though, for how much content you get.

All and all this game deserves all the hype it has been getting. This game is so big that even if you don't like some aspects of it there still will be a lot of things you will like. In most ways this game is a step up from it's predecessors, and that feels good after 13 years. I see the potential in online and I think this game's future is very bright. 

I think an 8 is very reasonable since I will never give out a 10 because perfection doesn't exist.

author: Idkwn
quote:
Idk what hooked me up so bad on this game, if its the world, the story, i dont really know, but i didn’t have this much fun in a while now. This game can’t even be compared with other from the series, and also just set up a new standard for the open-world games. The haters gonna hate it how much they like, but it is really one of the greatest, if not the greatest game of all time. The world is so immersive that you get lost in it, waking up 2-3 hours later that you still didn’t got to the mission you wanted to do. The story feels great, i think that the last mission from the chapter 1 was one of the greatest finale **** chapter ever. I am currently in chapter 3, and this game grows bigger and bigger on me. The only minus is that it is locked to 30 frames, but if you have a good enough monitor/tv and activate some things in the display settings, it is just incredible. The amount of diversity in random events, in npcs, in interactions, it is just CRAZY. The only game that will surpass this will probably be one from the same developers lol. These guys never miss.

Also, i can compare this game with a lot of newer games that i played, like RE Requiem/Crimson Desert/PB0, even Cyberpunk can be in this list if you would like. I think every one of the above have something special in their category of games, but GTA 6 is the only one here who deserves to be claimed as the best. It is the only one who brings something new on the table. For the Cyberpunk fans that still claim that cyberpunk has the most exciting open-world, wake up.


Bringing it back to the 30 frames per second, i think console players never experienced this kind of graphics and this kind of level of details ever. I think Rockstar just genuine uses some kind of magic to make it work in 30 fps on these 2020 consoles. 

In almost 19 hours of gameplay i only experienced 2 or 3 bugs, which i find in normal in a new released game, idk what other people say about one million bugs or whatever. 

I am 100% sure that no other games in 10 years from now will surpass or even be on the same level with this one.

I am not talking so much about the story because i didn’t finished it yet, but so far its really nicely done.

author: davidpuesgg
quote:
Without a doubt, this is one of the best games I've played in a very long time.

My journey with this franchise began back in 2008. Since then, I've made it a point to explore its other games, discover their stories, dive deeper into the lore, and follow the legacy that has been built over the years.

GTA VI is everything I've been waiting for. It delivers across the board: visually, narratively, and in terms of gameplay. I know developing a game on this scale is no easy task, and I expected there to be a few bugs along the way. That's understandable, especially with a project of this magnitude, and nothing that can't be fixed.

People tend to focus exclusively on the flaws, overlooking everything the game does remarkably well. They get caught up in pointing out what's wrong instead of appreciating everything it has to offer. Yet all that noise only makes me appreciate this installment even more, because it shows just how much there is to admire beyond what this vocal minority is willing to acknowledge.

This game is a testament to how beautiful something can become when years of dedication, passion, and hard work come together. It also shows how absurd it is to search for the smallest flaws just to diminish something's worth, simply because some people refuse to let it shine.

author: TommyHudd
quote:
Ignore people hating on this game. I wanted to be one of them because GTA 6 represents some of the worst aspects of the industry (it being nominated for GOTY despite not being in players' hands yet being the biggest offender.) However, the game is undeniably brilliant. Is it flawless? No. The biggest gripes are:

- 30FPS. But surprisingly I actually don't consider it to be THAT bad because a game like GTA can get away with it, it's not a fast twitch shooter like Call of Duty where how smooth the game is can be the difference in life and death. For the most part the game actually runs well enough and I didn't find myself struggling to get used to it again like I feared.

- Gunplay is still mid and your character controls like a tank, it is clunky as per all R* games.

- Some of the characters so far are hit and miss. I feel Jason is a bit flat in comparison to Lucia and his voice acting isn't great. He's kind of just a cookie cutter protagonist especially in comparison to those who came before him.

- The first act is a bit of a slow burn, but I actually enjoyed that because it gives you a chance to get absorbed into the world and build the relationship earlier.

Now, onto the positives:

The game is utterly stunning in terms of Graphical fidelity. I am not joking, this is the best looking game I have ever seen and it will have you in awe sometimes at what they have managed to achieve.

There is tons of content and side activities to do. Racing, robbing, shopping for clothes / ammo, stealing and sealing cars, flying planes, diving for treasure, stealing drugs etc. Yes even the **** you've heard about like fixing the house and whatnot (even though that **** is optional if you don't give a ****.) Events pop up often enough which can whisk you away at a moments notice from the main path.

Jason and Lucia's relationship is interesting to see and develop. I like trying to get them to do anything together but they can also just cut about doing their own stuff. 

The story itself is interesting and I like the way it gives you a bit of freedom in later acts on how you go about handling stuff like in chapter 2 and onwards.

Overall the game is very fun and they've managed to create a world that feels alive. It is not without flaws, but this really is a ridiculous achievement that they've pulled off and I think if you're a fan of GTA games already, you'll find the majority of what you're looking for and then some here.

author: stefun9
quote:
Before any details, I bought the game, played now for about 21 hours, got to chapter 3, done a few main missions in it and I'm about 40% main story completion. 

Small note: came to leave a review also because of all dumb people just making opinion on someone elses opinion then review bomb the game. 

That said, the game is great and, yes, it has some flaws like any other great game (and not only) have. Like it's most recent counterparts - GTAV and RDR2 - 90% of the things are great. 

The good 

Story
There are some moments in the story that got me excited, some in which I laughed because the satire is still there, some were tense.  It builds up slowly and right when feel you are on your feet, you are back down again. 

Gameplay
There are some new mechanics added that add to the much hated realism of the game. It's nice to have a slower pace sometime and to be a headless chicken just going from rampage to rampage with some time in-between to do almost nothing. You have lots of different activities, people to meet, encounters to find (a lot more than we had even in RDR2) and so many other stuff. 

Graphics/Performance
The game looks great and can't wait for a ps6 version of it. There are some scenes in there that are simple magnificent. And you can easily take your time looking. I also like that is one of the few games that hide ALL UI. When you walk for example, the UI goes away, helping on that immersion. Sure, it's not the first one to do it, but I'm glad is here. I find myself taking walks around because I also have what to do.

The bad stuff (all in one, no categories)
Although I prefer to have this density of people, the fps really drop at some points, even without crowds (Chapter 1, docking at my house got me constant fps drops) and there is a yellow-ish tint from time to time that I'm not sure if it's intended or not. I had encountered a few bugs too, some invisible walls once, some glitches/clipping, weird npc behaviours,  weird animations when pulling out the guns, but nothing game breaking and somewhat expected at this scale, especially when the world opens more. The characters and their dynamic (especially Jason and Lucia) is not that great, even though I like Jason, was hoping for another Arthur Morgan and maybe he will become later in the game (it had a funny story moment that was a big surprise). Their dynamic is pretty normal, nothing I did not see - quiet, calculated ex-military guy meets blood-boiling latina with a big mouth. 

Overall, after spending my 20ish ours I know I'll be spending much, much more after finishing the story. For me it's not perfect and not even RDR2 was perfect, a game that I've played 3 times and enjoyed it every time. Technical issues will be cut out little by little as almost all games do, especially something this from a company like Rockstar.  People will complain about being woke - which it isn't, there literally **** and **** cartoons on tv, about the game not being GTA (which partially is fair, it feels more like RDR2), about having a girlfriend and so many more. People are reluctant to change and to come from a chaotic adrenaline fueled GTA5 to a more calculated/down to Earth system in 6 is quite a lot, but don't forget, Arthur Morgan was **** until we all cried at the end and now we all want it. Not saying Jason will be Arthur, but time will make this game be in the right place, as one of the greatest of recent history.

author: Oscur0
quote: GTA 6 graphically is beautiful and the sound department is top notch. Where the game lacks  is the fact that there isn’t a mission replay like the previous installment and a lot of other features that made GTA 5 etc amazing. It’s is a very buggy and clunky game and the story is kinda lackluster and has lost it’s GTA story edge that all the other GTA’s had in the past. The whole plot on revenge was poorly executed and a lot of side characters are not memorable. The physics, oh now this is where I unfortunately have to drop the score even more. We can’t roll while shooting, taking cover is horrendous and aiming is so clunky. Driving even though I like the weight of vehicles it feels so clunky and not as responsive as if there is latency or a delay in the front tires of every car, it’s just awful! Now the story, I don’t want to spoil much but it is definitely a huge step backwards, not sure what’s with the writers at Rockstar since they made so many memorable characters but you play a few chapters and it feels like all those characters just didn’t leave a real impact within those chapters. I can still remember Little Jacob, Catalina etc but these characters just don’t have exciting lore, it’s as if AI wrote a slop story of Bonnie and Clyde but way worse. I will give them grace for the tremendous map, customization and bring back the eating and working out features from GTA SA, also the time it takes from A to B is genuinely amazing and it’s a beautiful scenery. I love the random npcs and I think those are the best random npcs they have ever made! I hope the next GTA installment comes within 5-6 yrs and takes some of the good parts of GTA 6 and keeps those edgy stories of the past and all those other amazing features and especially PHYSICS! Overall I wouldn’t recommend buying the game right now and if anyone who has a powerful enough PC reading this to just wait for better fps and less of these technical issues, it’s not a terrible game and maybe you will enjoy the physics and story more than me as this is my opinion of the game.

author: ersulba
quote:
It’s undeniably a good game, though hardly the second coming of Christ. The main story starts off way too slow and feels pretty flat—no spoilers, but the pacing is rough and the overall payoff is underwhelming.

Where the game truly shines is its open-world sandbox and random events. Rockstar leaned heavily into RPG elements and relationship-maintenance mechanics that feel much closer to cozy gaming than traditional GTA. Hardcore longtime fans might hate this direction, but as someone who loves cozy games, I actually enjoyed it a lot.

Gameplay-wise, it stumbles: the UI is clunky, the controls feel somewhat heavy, and the weapon wheel is awful, often getting in the way of smooth combat. Replacing the series' classic controller auto-aim with a mild soft aim assist also changes the feel entirely. 

Overall, I’d recommend it for the sandbox and social mechanics, even if the steep launch price feels like a bad business practice.

quote: Coming from Rockstar Games, given the team's ambition and the many years invested, I already expected the game to be a majestic masterpiece. But honestly, GTA 6 far exceeded my expectations. The game feels extremely alive—something is happening in every single part of the map, from everyday routines to unexpected car accidents. Rockstar Games raised the technical bar tremendously here. There is a noticeable leap in graphics and textures, vehicle physics and handling, NPC AI, the dynamic weather system, atmosphere, world scale, and even the story's plot. author: CreativePlay01
quote:
While I cannot deny the game world is beautiful, that is all it has going for it.

 Firstly, the performance of the game is atrocious on base consoles; In most, if not all, action sequences the game significantly drops below the targeted 30 frames per second into the low 20s and high 10s. Even when you're not in these sequences there are frame drops all over the game. You shouldn't be expected to purchase a 1k plus console to play your 80-100 dollar video game. Akin to the game performance, the game is riddled with glitches; sure open world games as big as this are bound to have glitches, it's hard to catch them all. But, having game breaking glitches during the first missions of the game? Ie falling through the floor and getting caught in soft lock areas. If the first part of the game cannot properly be debugged what does that say for the rest of the game? It shows how unpolished the game is and should have delayed to fix these issues.

Moving on to the games story, the first several hours of the game after the first initial sequences, are bland, monotonous, and boring. People do not want to come home from work, take off work, or play games on their days off just to go to work on a game. In games such as GTA people expect action, unruly, and the crime simulator that they have known to love. You want the first part of your game to entice people to pick it up and continue playing, not complaining about how boring it is. Sure the game picks up after the first few acts but you're still expected to drop everything you're doing to go cater to your girlfriend's needs, which wouldn't be a problem if you could ignore it but, it's required if you want to get the best ending to the game. In a game such as GTA there should be the freedom to do whatever you want when you want and not feel bogged down or anticipating that you have to leave what your doing at the drop of a pin to ensure you get the "true" ending to a game. Speaking about the ending, you're also required to keep up with your empathy meter throughout the game. In a game about crime and doing what you want, being forced to apologize or make sure you don't do too much crime so that you can get the true ending leaves a bad taste in the mouth of the gamers who just want to play a game about theft.

This game, had some strange choices to what you can and can't do. In a game about stealing cars, shootings, hookers, among other illegal things, you sure are restricted in ways other GTA have not been in the past. You can not cheat on your partner, cannot shoot or kill protected groups of individuals, it makes it much more difficult to steal vehicles, especially if they are parked or basically impossible if they are in your neighborhood. This is a game, I understand and as do most of the playerbase, the things you're doing in this game are not real and is just a video game, a sandbox video at that. There should not be forced restrictions of what can and can not be done, as with previous GTA games.

In conclusion, the game looks beautiful most of the time; it has atrocious frame rate and performance issues, lack of quality control, and falls short in almost every other aspect of its game design. One right can not make up for it's shortcomings. The game gets a 4/10 just for how beautiful it's game world is.

Wait until it's on PC and the performance issues are fixed, and the modding scene chances these unnecessary restrictions.

author: RzetelnyGracz
quote:
GTA VI is honestly incredible in a lot of ways. The world simulation is just on another level, I don't think any other developer comes even close. The roleplay elements are fantastic and really help you get immersed in the world. I also love the random encounters. They happen naturally as you explore, they're often funny or genuinely interesting, and most importantly, they never feel forced.

The game looks absolutely insane, especially the lighting. The soundtrack is amazing as well, easily one of the best parts of the game. Gunplay feels much better than in GTA V. Weapons actually have some weight to them, shots feel impactful, and enemies don't just drop after one or two hits anymore unless you hit a vital spot. It's basically an improved version of what we had in RDR2. Vehicle damage is also a massive step up from GTA V.

Underwater exploration is surprisingly good too. There's so much more marine life and vegetation, and actually exploring the ocean feels worthwhile now. The writing is great for the most part, with plenty of funny dialogue, excellent voice acting and some really interesting side characters. 

As for the 30 FPS, you do get used to it after a few hours. It's obviously not ideal, but I wouldn't say it takes much away from the experience either.

Now, there are a few things that bother me.

For one, I thought we'd have more freedom when it comes to Jason and Lucia's relationship, but apparently you can't romance anyone else. You can't even hook up with strippers or have casual encounters with other women like you could in some previous GTA games.

There are also some weird omissions in the world simulation. You can't call emergency services anymore, ambulances barely show up after shootouts, bodies are just left lying in the streets, and cops don't even react to bags of drugs lying on the ground. Considering how much attention to detail there is everywhere else, this stuff feels pretty strange.

And finally, Lucia. I find her annoyingly naive at times, and I actually think some of the complaints about Jason being too submissive around her are fair. I don't really understand why he acts the way he does around her, and the game doesn't do a particularly good job of explaining it. Personally, I'm just not a big fan of their dynamic

Overall, it's an amazing game and probably the most impressive open world I've ever experienced. I just wish Rockstar had paid a little more attention to some of these smaller details, especially considering how much they got right.

author: HadrianDark
quote:
I will start with the bad because its not much. Of course there are things to be said about 30fps without a performance mode offering 60fps. The game also has a very slow start, with some chore quests feeling unnecessary but mandatory (they arent but it for a completionist it feels mandatory), but picks up quickly at the end of chapter 1. There are a few bugs with objects clipping into each other, I have not experienced these issues myself. It takes a while to fully unlock the 2nd playable character.

Now the good. 
The game is extremely detailed and immersive . I truly feel like I am a part of Vice City. The map is huge and crawling with things to do. The NPCs all feel unique and have something to offer with every interaction. The cars are designed well and we have the best driving of any GTA yet. There seems to be a huge gun variety with customizations. The new controls are easy to get used to, and they make it easy to return to the classic control style. Free aim is the default but lock-on can be enabled. There are also options to turn turn off the gore if you want that. The story brings a lot to the table, the characters are written well and I truly grew to love, or hate, some characters. Jason and Lucias relationship feels authentic and to some, very refreshing, bringing an "Us against All" vibe to the world. 

This game would be a 10/10 for me if we could up the framerate, fix the bugs, and had an online mode.

My actual review of this is around ≈ 9. But for the sake of review bombing I made it a 10, because ain't no way this game is under a 5. I guarantee half of these "reviews" haven't even  played it. Nobody was forced to do the missions that involved building, the relationship building missions or anything of that sort it is OPTIONAL. 


I'm 17+ hours in and I've early in chapter 2. The big negative of the game is the targeted 30fps, I do believe they could have has a 60 fps mode if they reduced the details, fidelity and npcs. But its a two sided deal, with the decision to lock it at 30fps you get some truely  impressive fidelity that sets the new benchmark of what games can look like. The story starts a bit slow, but I think its needed for proper development of characters. I could have finished chapter 1 within 3-4 hours but I often get distracted buy some of the most interesting events, 1 for example was a plane that crashed in the marsh area, I went to investigate and found some cocain, $ and some unwanted guest to dispose of. There are so many interesting random events that it truely give the world a sense of life. Speaking of the world, its massive, dense and I find myself in awe of how beautiful it is. I can easily see myself spending countless hours just exploring its ultimately a testament to how Rockstar handles their games. The game has set a new standard in open world design, the closest one to it is another Rockstar game RDR2. And for a recent release Crimson Desert. I'm eager to get back into the world of GTA 6 and you should be too!

author: atruereview
quote:
A really good installment. Was it worth the 13 year wait? Put simply, Absolutely.
Now the reason it comes out to an 8 for me is because of the final act of the game. 
The free roam? Amazing. The story? Phenomenal. The endings? Yikes.  

The final mission is where the developers just thought: "you know what, just throw in everything that a fast and furious teen would think is cool". In other words its really disappointing. 
I would even go as far to say that it is awful.
Its a shame that they really failed at the finish line, I could look past the hiccups of the midway points of the game but failing the endings is why I didn't give it a 9/10.
But of course, opinions are subjective so someone could and probably does feel different.

Now, should a GTA fan get this game? Of course. Its not exactly a masterpiece but there is TONS and TONS of stuff in this game to keep a fan occupied with.
Think if GTA 5 had the same amount of content as Red Dead Redemption 2 and then some more. 

So overall, rockstar killed it once again. 
Obviously.

quote: I'm 25 years old, and honestly, I didn't expect to get this addicted to GTA VI! I deliberately avoided reviews and YouTube opinions because I wanted to experience everything myself. And I'm absolutely loving it!I genuinely don't understand all the negativity. The world is fascinating, the characters are interesting, and the amount of detail, innovative technology, interactions, random encounters, and activities is unbelievable. There's always something new to discover!I keep seeing complaints about 30 FPS, but I'm playing on a TV with VRR, and the experience feels incredibly smooth to me. I honestly don't see it as a **** I think the TikTok generation is slowly damaging the gaming industry. People seem to have lost the patience and attention span to truly immerse themselves in a game. Watch Dogs 2 is another example of a fantastic game that deserved much more **** you even know how to roleplay anymore? How to explore, experiment, pay attention to details, and create your own experience?THIS IS NOT A MARATHON TO REACH THE ENDING FIRST! Just relax and enjoy the journey. GTA VI gives you so many possibilities that you don't even know where to start. You can approach the world in so many different ways. My boyfriend always dreamed **** where you could truly roleplay like this, and now that it exists, people are rushing through it instead of appreciating it.RDR2 was an absolutely magnificent, realistic game. author: Rayanggu
quote: I have been playing Grand Theft Auto VI for about 35 hours now, and honestly I am still in Chapter 1 because I just cannot rush through it. The world is straight up amazing, and the NPC interactions feel historic, like you are genuinely dealing with real human beings rather than stiff video game puppets. You can just stand around, watch how people react to what happens around them, and feel like the city breathes on its own. The physics are super realistic and awesome too, to the point where just watching things react and collide on its own is seriously fun. As for Jason, he is nowhere near as bad as people online make him out to be—right now I think he is solid and I am really hyped to see how his character develops as the story moves forward. Close-quarters combat is crazy good with lots of varied moves that feel great to pull off, and gunplay is rock solid just like you would expect from Rockstar. Driving feels heavy and grounded, giving you that real sense that you are actually steering a real car instead of gliding on rails. Still, I am completely hooked on this world and having a blast exploring every corner of it. On the downside, the most annoying thing at first is being locked to 30 fps, though after a while you get used to it and it feels fine. The catch is that whenever there is any frame drop below that, you notice it immediately and it pulls you out of the moment for a second. Even with that frame rate quirk, I am super immersed and having an unforgettable time so far.

author: anton3255
quote:
10/10 – Absolute masterpiece
Grand Theft Auto 6 is a generational leap. The world of Leonida feels incredibly alive, the RAGE engine delivers stunning realism in lighting, vehicles, and the day/night cycle, and the attention to detail is on another level. Military vehicles like the Apache, Hummers, and tanks look and feel shockingly authentic.
One of the best surprises is the freedom to steal large aircraft — from full-size passenger jets at the airport to fighter jets at the military base. What makes it even better is the realistic response: steal a big passenger plane and fighter jets get scrambled to intercept you, just like in real life during a hijacking or major threat. It adds that classic GTA sense of chaos and scale in the best way possible.
The storytelling, characters, and open-world systems (including the new car theft and tracker mechanics) make this feel fresh while staying true to what makes GTA special. Rockstar has delivered something special.
10/10

author: shinjunmin94
quote:
GTA 6 delivers an incredible experience with its breathtaking graphics and massive amount of content.

Despite the unfortunate limitation of 30 FPS, the game completely immerses me in its world. I'm constantly excited to discover what kind of encounters await me and what missions I'll come across next.

This is the best game I've played since Red Dead Redemption 2. Is there really any developer better than Rockstar when it comes to open-world games? A development budget of 3 trillion won certainly doesn't feel wasted.

I'm also very satisfied with the more realistic police system. In previous games, I could openly carry a gun without attracting any attention from the police. Even worse, simply having a police car crash into mine could give me a wanted level. Now, if I accidentally bump into a police car, the officers may simply give me a warning and let me go.

However, there are a few things I wish were handled differently. I wish I could call 911 myself. Sometimes, I'm the one who gets attacked first, and even when I only fire back in self-defense, I still end up getting a wanted level. That's disappointing.

Another minor disappointment is the automatic grocery restocking system. During the mission where I wait for Lucia, I initially thought I was being taught how to restock groceries myself. Instead, I discovered that the groceries simply replenish automatically at home. I would have preferred being able to do it myself.

Just like in Red Dead Redemption 2, I have to retrieve my weapons from my car or home rather than having immediate access to everything. This can be a little inconvenient, but I can appreciate the realism behind it. I especially like that I can only retrieve my weapons from my own personal vehicle. It gives me a reason to actually use and bring my own car to missions instead of casually stealing someone else's. In previous games, I often couldn't be bothered to drive my own car, so I appreciate this change.

With its incredible variety of activities and sheer entertainment value, GTA 6 feels like an entire lifetime brought to life in an open world.

10/10

I wish I could give it 100 out of 10.

author: Ianchus
quote:
He jugado juegos realmente inmersivos que cuando hablamos de crear mundos sistémicamente buenos, grandes, enormes e interactivos muchos de ellos dan la talla y cumplen expectativas. Sin duda alguna, Grand Theft Auto VI no es simplemente un mundo enorme, sistémicamente MASIVO e interactivo con un techo gráfico jamás alcanzado en la industria. Es la representación de inmersión en cualquiera de sus ramas llevado al más altísimo nivel jamás antes visto, en donde no existen precedentes. Es la redefinición de lo que llamamos un mundo abierto. Es complicado poner simplemente en palabras lo abrumadoramente detallado que este juego, porque no solo incentiva la curiosidad del jugador, sino que literalmente pasas a ser parte de Leonida y disfrutas al máximo de las interacciones, de lo tan exageradamente vivo y natural que este mundo. Es, de nuevo, de una viveza y naturalidad llevada al más extremo nivel. Son las enseñanzas de 50 años de lo que lleva la industria creando videojuegos, llenos de aprendizaje, plasmados en un solo videojuego de mundo abierto. Una narrativa pausada, interesante, una sátira exagerada y cinematográfica en donde logra a la perfección conectar lo humano a través de la debilidad de sus personajes. Un Grand Theft Auto con todas las letras. Mantiene su esencia y una identidad y dirección artística en la que Rockstar Games tanto se esmeró en crear.
Puedo hablar de muchas cosas como lo puede ser el clima, la naturaleza, las playas, las aguas, los NPCs, las calles, los coches. No podría terminar de enumerar cada uno de ellos, pero todas esas cosas que menciono y que podría seguir mencionando, reitero, está llevado a un siguiente nivel que ningún titulo actualmente tiene. Arte puro y una obra maestra de la más alta calidad.

author: jose_micael98

No centro de tudo estão Jason e Lucia, uma história de crime que, contra a expectativa, tem coração. Entre tiros e fugas, existe cumplicidade, e é isso que faz o jogador se importar.
Depois de mais de uma década de espera, o jogo entrega o que prometeu: liberdade, detalhe e personalidade. Não é só um jogo, é uma experiência.

author: Baka958
quote: Uma obra-prima da imersão e da cultura modernaSimplesmente o jogo mais imersivo que já **** detalhes, o cuidado com cada elemento e a atenção às pequenas coisas dão um brilho absurdo à jogabilidade. Ao contrário do que muitos dizem, considero a cadência do jogo muito bem construída. O cotidiano dos personagens não é um defeito ou uma lentidão desnecessária: é justamente uma das coisas que tornam esse universo tão **** carregamentos são surpreendentemente rápidos, algo que eu sinceramente não esperava, principalmente lembrando o quanto GTA V demorava uma eternidade para carregar no PS4. E sobre a limitação de 30 FPS: sacrificar uma taxa de quadros maior para entregar esse nível de experiência visual e imersiva não deveria ser tratado automaticamente como uma imperfeição. É uma escolha técnica que, na minha opinião, faz sentido dentro da proposta.Estamos diante de um primor dos videogames e de uma obra que dialoga diretamente com a história e a cultura **** 6 não é apenas contemporâneo: é um reflexo da própria realidade. Seus diálogos, ironias, conversas atravessadas e situações cotidianas constroem uma sátira extremamente afiada, especialmente sobre a decadência dos Estados Unidos. É impressionante como o jogo consegue transformar aspectos tão reconhecíveis da sociedade em entretenimento, crítica e arte.O que mais me surpreendeu foi perceber que comecei a criar uma rotina para os personagens. Esperar o outro chegar em casa, buscá-lo, respeitar as leis, prestar atenção aos horários e aproveitar momentos que não necessariamente envolvem missões. O jogo não me obrigou a fazer nada disso. Eu simplesmente quis. A imersão foi tão natural que passei a querer aproveitar aquele universo daquela maneira.E, para quem diz que isso é apenas um jogo e que deveríamos ir viver a vida real, eu diria o seguinte: talvez você esteja deixando passar muita coisa.Acredito que, se alguém jogar GTA 6 com atenção e disposição para observar o que está acontecendo ao seu redor, poderá sair dessa experiência com uma percepção diferente até mesmo sobre determinados aspectos da própria vida.Porque, no fim, nem toda arte precisa estar pendurada em uma parede.Isso também é arte.

So don’t pay much mind to the review bombers handing out low scores just to tear it down.
As for bugs, I’ve only run into 2 or 3 minor ones in 23 hours, and none of them were game-breaking or ruined the experience. All in all, the game is rock-solid, fun, and well worth playing.

author: glauciobg
quote:
GTA VI — A New Benchmark for Open-World Gaming (10/10)
I’m genuinely astonished by what Rockstar has accomplished. GTA VI isn’t merely a bigger, prettier GTA. It’s a remarkable evolution of what an open-world game can **** level of detail, environmental storytelling, NPC behavior, and systemic immersion is extraordinary. From grocery shopping, cooking, personal hygiene, and home maintenance to realistic driving, persistent criminal consequences, and spontaneous encounters in the wilderness, everything contributes to a world that feels astonishingly **** its greatest achievement might be its humanity. Jason and Lucia aren’t simply criminals chasing money and chaos. They’re people trying to build a life together, with genuine affection, responsibilities, and something meaningful to lose.Rockstar hasn’t abandoned its biting social satire. Instead, it has found a more mature balance between absurdity, intimacy, freedom, and **** perhaps most impressively, the game allows me to inhabit this world at my own pace, without constantly pushing me toward the next ****’s the immersive freedom of GTA, the everyday-life simulation of The Sims, and the grounded physicality of Kingdom Come: Deliverance II, brought together with Rockstar’s extraordinary production values.Sixteen hours in, I’ve yet to encounter a single noticeable bug or performance issue on my base ****’s far too early to judge the complete experience, but GTA VI already feels like a generational achievement — and a serious contender for the greatest open-world game ever made.

author: ImSisyphus
quote:
GTA VI is the best open world ever made. 

Rockstar didn't let us down. The map is huge, and more importantly, it feels alive. Every street, beach and random corner makes you want to stop and explore, and the graphics are the most realistic we've seen in a game so far. Just driving around in cinematic mode is an experience on its own.

That said, this isn't a perfect game, and the story is where it falls short. It's not what most of us were expecting. The opening hours are slow, and the plot never really hooks you. At some point I was pushing through missions out of obligation, hoping it would get better.

The characters are a mixed bag. Lucia is fantastic: well written, detailed and easy to care about. Jason is the opposite. He has almost no personality and it's hard to connect with him.

The gameplay is fun, but Rockstar added so many mechanics that it can get overwhelming. Twenty hours in, I still didn't feel fully comfortable with all the systems.

Outside the game, two decisions are hard to defend. Not releasing a physical edition is a tough pill to swallow for a lot of players. There's also still no Spanish dub, which is disappointing for a huge part of the fanbase.

Even with all that, GTA VI is a must-play. The open world makes it worth it. But this is the most expensive game ever made, and it has to be judged like the biggest investment in gaming history. At that level, a slow story, a forgettable protagonist and a 30fps launch with frame drops in certain areas are hard to overlook. There are also a few bugs, though none of them affect the core of the game. That's why it's an 8/10 for me.

author: MarioCre
quote:
At times, it is GTA, at others, it can be FH6, Flight Sim, House Flipper, Sims and all that. Point is, it’s got it all and it’s missing nothing. Graphics, atmosphere, liveliness of the city makes you stop caring about the locked 30fps limit, which doesn’t even feel that bad considering most of us are playing on 6yr old consoles that had an RRP of ~500 (£€$).

The fact that people are complaining and giving 0’s just because of the relationship mechanic and empathy.. crazy. Especially since it’s OPTIONAL! 

10hours in, Chapter 1 still long to go and Keys area is still giving me all the enjoyment I need. No rush, no running around trying to speed run this game. Perfectly blends in mission (gta time) with random events, npc interactions, lucia time and perhaps fishing and enjoying the graphics. 

Clearly not a game for those whose attention span can’t take a slow-down or those that lack basic comprehension to understand the difference between main, side missions & optional (random) side QUESTS.

If anything that should be better, is just chapter replay.

quote: 说实话我不是这个系列的粉丝，我不太喜欢做个法外狂徒，我想这游戏刚开始的杰森其实也不太想，虽然他还得做些烂活儿，毕竟他在美国而且他缺钱。gta6是史上规模最大的游戏吗？可能是吧，我猜。但是归根到底，我没法体验到这个游戏是好玩的。它不能带给我足够乐趣，而且这代的剧情极度糟糕。五代的时候不管怎么讲，那个剧情我尚且能够接受，讲故事讲的比这代要好多了。讲真的，我看bug集锦都要比打这个游戏觉得开心，但是我们都能理解遇到bug时的我们是多么糟心，有人丢了存档，有人被困在bug中不得不从来，那并不好笑，甚至有些痛苦，有些人可能会想放弃继续游玩。我给分是按照游戏体量，制作精细度以及可玩度来的。我剥离了我对这个游戏的一切场外内容的影响来看，这算是今年一款很不错的游戏，对于它的受众这款游戏有着很高的可玩性，包括后续还有线上模式不是吗？这个规模应该会让他们感到开心。但是从我个人来讲，我在当作rpg来玩时很难带入到这两个角色里是事实，所以我大多时候过于像局外人，而且露西亚很令人讨厌，所以我玩起来会相当难受。有些彩蛋还是挺令人开心的，不过那都是添头，不能作为主菜。我知道很多人会带着情绪评分，因为这毕竟是13年等待，花了很多钱和时间，然后你得到了什么呢？一个让你觉得失望的游戏。这是可以理解的，不过我觉得即使我给这个评分也可能会被冲……所以就这样吧…至少没像2077和星空那样极度令人失望不是吗…还好啦，游戏而已啦。

Jogo Grand Theft Auto desde 2016 e posso dizer que sou um grande fã dessa franquia. Acompanhei o GTA 5 inteiro e esperei por esse grande momento.

Minha única reclamação até agora é a interface de seleção das rádios dentro dos veículos. Eu não gostei muito do novo visual e acredito que poderia ser igual do GTA 5

Fora isso, estou adorando cada momento. Como fã de longa data, posso dizer que minhas expectativas foram atendidas. É uma experiência que demonstra o potencial do GTA

E eu sei que a maioria estão criticando, não posso julgar, porém como eu sou apaixonado pelo GTA, eu falo: Esse jogo merece o GOTY, mesmo que o Zelda fez marco histórico.

100/10

author: JustIsma
quote: Rockstar Games has somehow outdone itself once again. Grand Theft Auto VI isn’t just another entry in the franchise, it is an absolute triumph of open-world design that sets a brand-new benchmark for the entire gaming industry. From the very first hour, the sheer scale and density of Vice City and the surrounding state of Leonida feel completely unmatched. The world isn't just massive; it’s genuinely alive. Every street corner, neon-lit club, and sun-drenched stretch of coastline is packed with unique, memorable characters. Rather than feeling like mindless background NPCs, the people you meet react dynamically to your presence, leading to spontaneous, unscripted moments that make every session feel personal. Visually, the game is nothing short of breathtaking. The lighting system transforms the atmosphere from blinding, humid afternoons into vibrant, rain-slicked nights where every neon sign reflects off the asphalt. Paired with hyper-fluid character animations and an obsessive level of environmental detail, from subtle facial micro-expressions to the way vehicles handle and deform, the immersion is total. Beyond the technical showcase, the core gameplay and storytelling hit just as hard. The writing is sharp, witty, and grounded, brought to life by incredible voice acting and natural dialogue. The missions seamlessly blend high-octane spectacle with intimate character moments, while the upgraded AI ensures that gunfights, police chases, and casual interactions feel unpredictable and **** is genuinely staggering to think about how Rockstar managed to pack this level of polish, depth, and ambition into a single experience. GTA VI doesn’t just live up to over a decade of anticipation, it easily earns its place as one of the greatest video games ever made.

author: DRazwx
quote: When looking at the expectations surrounding GTA 6, it’s difficult to imagine how Rockstar could have possibly made a game that lived up to the amount of anticipation it received. Considering the success of GTA 5 and the amount of time that has passed since its release, I had extremely high expectations for nearly every aspect of the game. Despite this, I genuinely think Rockstar managed to create something that not only meets these expectations, but exceeds them to an extent that I really didn’t think was **** first thing that stood out to me was the amount of detail throughout the world. When exploring Vice City, there is an almost overwhelming amount of things happening around you, whether it’s the people walking around, the traffic, or just the general environment itself. This makes the world feel significantly more realistic than what we’ve seen in previous GTA games. I think this is especially important because a major part of GTA has always been the freedom to explore and do things outside of the main storyline. Because of this, the amount of attention Rockstar put into the world itself makes even the most basic activities entertaining. There were times where I would spend hours simply exploring the map without progressing through the story at all, which I think shows just how much there is to experience.Another thing I found particularly impressive was the overall quality of the missions and characters. Something that I think many open world games struggle with is maintaining the player’s interest throughout the entire storyline. However, GTA 6 manages to avoid this almost entirely. The missions are consistently entertaining, and the characters actually make you interested in what happens next. This is especially impressive when considering just how much content there is throughout the game. I also think the improvements to the gameplay make a massive difference, as nearly everything feels more enjoyable compared to previous Rockstar titles.When considering the broader impact of GTA 6, I think it’s reasonable to say that it has established an entirely new standard for open world games. While there are obviously other games that have managed to create extremely detailed worlds, I really don’t think anything comes close to what Rockstar has accomplished here. It’s not necessarily one specific feature that makes the game so impressive, but rather the combination of so many different aspects that are all done extremely well.Overall, I genuinely struggle to think of anything significant that I dislike about GTA 6. I went into the game expecting it to be one of the best games I’ve ever played, and somehow it still managed to surprise me. I think it is easily the best game Rockstar has ever created and I honestly wouldn’t disagree with anyone who considers it the greatest video game of all time. I would give it a 10/10 without any hesitation, and I think it’s going to be extremely difficult for any other developer to create something that can compete with it.

author: Josicx
quote:
What stands out most about GTA VI is that Rockstar actually took a real creative risk. With a budget this massive, the safe, easy move would have been a mindless, consequence-free chaos sandbox—basically GTA V with better graphics. Instead, they slowed the pacing down, prioritized grounded storytelling, and built a world where choices and actions actually carry weight.

Calling a crime drama about a couple "woke" simply because their relationship matters to the story is beyond ridiculous. It’s totally fair if a slower, more realistic approach isn't everyone's cup of tea, but a studio refusing to play it safe deserves respect, not a flood of bad-faith zeros.

author: Mayorris
quote:
Rockstar did it again, and then some.
The expectations were insanely high, and somehow Rockstar managed to surpass them anyway. The level of detail is monumental. Every street, every shop window, every background conversation feels deliberately crafted. You can tell how much time and care went into the smallest things, and it pays off in immersion. The story, so far, is on par with Red Dead Redemption 2, if not better. The characters are memorable, the writing is sharp, and I’m completely invested in where it’s going. And the open world? It’s simply alive. It doesn’t feel like a backdrop waiting for you to show up, but like a place that keeps going whether you’re there or not. You can’t really put this into words. You have to witness it for yourself.
A masterpiece. 10/10.

author: im_benthebigman
quote:
I’m gonna update this as I progress through GTA 6 but as of right now it’s exactly what I expected it to be a very good adaptation of the improvements RDR2 made to rockstars game formula but in a GTA game. And as I’m still early on I’ll just be listing pros and cons.

Pros:
Absolutely stunning graphically
The gameplay is surprisingly fun and experimental for a rockstar game allowing you a certain level of freedom during missions has worked wonders so far.
The relationship between Jason and Lucia is great.
The way everything logically works in the environment makes you feel very immersed in this world.
Gunplay and combat overall take cues from RDR2 and are just as good as they are there.
Driving feels a bit heavier compared to GTA V but it makes it feel more rewarding to go through long stretches of roads without crashing.
The in depth systems of fitness and other little systems helps add to immersion and acts as basically a difficulty slider in a way. 
Cons:
Frame-rate dips a bit too frequently.
I’ve had the cover system drag me over to a wall I was not aiming for.
The side characters are surprisingly not very interesting compared to previous rockstar games.
The writing overall has taken a bit of a dip in quality (likely due to the lack of Dan Houser) it’s not bad tho it’s still quite good.
Jason’s voice actor is good overall but has frequent enough bad delivery’s where it’s either to hard to even understand what he’s saying or his delivery completely takes you out of it.

The pros definitely outweigh the good so far. This definitely isn’t the perfect game people will try and tell you it is (although no game is perfect) and it’s definitely not the broken mess others will tell you it is. So far I can conclude that if you’re a fan of rockstar or triple a cinematic games then you’ll definitely find enjoyment in GTA 6.

quote: I think it's safe to say that GTA VI has lived up to its hype and I can almost find nothing negative to write about the game, it's just perfect. It is Rockstar Games' magnum opus. I did not only like the astounding graphics of the game, but loved the general vibe and aesthetic of Leonida and the warm, vibrant color palette helps a lot with that. It gives summer vibes. The music is good too, and I especially liked the diversity of quests in the game. There's just so many different kinds of situation you may find yourself in. I saw some other players complaining about "trivial" minor quests, like buying flowers for Lucia and stuff, but I personally find them to be enjoyable. It adds to the simple yet diverse and unique quest design and makes the games' world more lively. I think it's what made GTA, GTA. Even in the older titles in the series, the games had all kinds of simple yet unique quests. I could compare it to Postal 2, where you go to buy some milk one day and the other day you ask random people to sign a petition, so the angry congressmen will play violent video games. Simple objectives like this can be hilarious and refreshing sometimes. GTA was never about shooting people all the time and running over them with a car mindlessly while stacking wanted stars anyway. In the end, they all served a greater purpose; a ****'s a game where you can lose yourself in its world for hours on end without even noticing it. It's a great game with so few flaws in it. You have to give credit where it's due. GTA VI is not just a video game, it's an experience.

author: Galars
quote:
PS5 Pro - The performance has been great and the game is beautiful. I enjoyed the open world mechanics far more than the story though. This GTA feels punishing in a way no previous title in the franchise achieved. I find myself considering the consequences of my actions before committing crimes and it feels much more satisfying to me than the previous titles. 

I like the driving a lot in this one, putting the pedal to the metal down a busy road is likely to cause a major crash and waste a good chunk of money so I find myself passing in the turn lanes and quickly checking both ways before gunning it through red lights which I think is awesome. 

The NPCs feel more alive in this game than any previous title, they actually have personalities and will get pissed off at you for driving poorly. I accidently clipped a guys truck and he started yelling before turning around and ramming me off the road while flipping me off, this made me laugh so hard at the absurdity of the situation

One small thing that I would change is the frowny face you get when you do aggressive actions. I get that shooting at some gang members who pulled guns out was aggressive, but when I see the frowny face my initial thought is that I did something wrong but its not the wrong option to be aggressive in GTA. I think it would be better if all of the morality reactions were smiling with the smile getting more sinister for the worse morality options (similar to how the psycho one already is)

For the story, I do not like that Jason and Lucia have to be in a decent relationship. I personally wouldn't have cheated on either character but I think it would have been cool to allow us to have that option. Could have made a similar system to the psycho meter with a relationship meter that can be permanently ruined by being unfaithful or being rude to each other. To make it fit into the story they could have made it so that they continue working together on jobs because theyre focused on getting money for their son and maintain the appearance of being a couple in public to get their child back from CPS but actually be dysfunctional and fighting at home. 

Overall, the story was pretty good, Id give that a 7/10 but the gameplay and world are what take it up to a 9/10 for me. If the story had been better and allowed me to have more freedom about how I act then this game could have been a 10

author: broyo
quote:
GRAND THEFT AUTO VI — A GENERATIONAL MASTERPIECE
Rating: 10/10
Some games entertain you. Some games leave you speechless. And then there's Grand Theft Auto VI.
Rockstar Games hasn't just created another open-world game; they've created a world that feels genuinely alive. From the streets of Vice City to the smallest interactions with the environment, everything feels meticulously crafted. The level of detail, realism and immersion is something that makes you forget you're playing a video game.
THE WORLD — 10/10
Leonida is an absolute achievement in open-world design. Random encounters, dynamic NPC behaviour, environmental details and seemingly insignificant interactions make exploration an experience of its own. There's always something happening, something to discover and something that makes the world feel authentic.
It's not just a map filled with activities. It's a living, breathing world.
IMMERSION — 10/10
This is where Rockstar truly shines. The little details make the biggest difference. The interactions, animations, atmosphere, sound design and unpredictable moments create an experience that feels incredibly natural.
You don't simply play GTA VI. You exist in its world.
GAMEPLAY & PRESENTATION — 10/10
Rockstar's attention to detail is once again on another level. The animations, physics, environmental interactions and overall presentation demonstrate an extraordinary amount of craftsmanship.
It's the kind of game where even doing absolutely nothing can be entertaining.
THE EXPERIENCE — 10/10
What makes GTA VI special isn't just its graphics, gameplay or scale. It's how seamlessly everything comes together. It constantly gives you reasons to explore, experiment and lose track of time.
There are imperfections, and no game is completely flawless. But they don't take away from what makes this experience so extraordinary.
FINAL VERDICT
GTA VI is more than a sequel. It's a statement about what open-world gaming can achieve when a studio spends years obsessing over the smallest details.
Rockstar has once again reminded the industry why its games create cultural moments rather than simply launch as entertainment products.
A world worth getting lost in. An experience worth remembering.
10/10 — A GENERATIONAL MASTERPIECE.

author: GLGTAplayers917
quote:
I've put about 20 hours into this game so far, and the sheer scale and ambition behind it are nothing short of a miracle.

I've seen a lot of people complain that the male protagonist is a bit too submissive to the female protagonist. And yeah, judging from Chapter 1, I do think some missions have issues with their storytelling, and certain details could've been fleshed out better. But overall, these flaws don't take away from what the game achieves. I still think the story is largely solid.

I honestly don't see anything wrong with the critics giving this game a 99 on Metacritic. Critics are supposed to evaluate games from a broader, more comprehensive perspective, while players tend to focus on specific aspects they personally like or dislike when giving their scores. And that's completely fair too. I have no problem with players criticizing certain parts of the game. I just think both perspectives are valid, and neither side is necessarily wrong.

That being said, I'm still absolutely blown away by how incredibly detailed and immersive this world is. In terms of production quality, technical achievement, and sheer scale, I genuinely believe this is the biggest and most ambitious game of the 2020s, if not one of the greatest achievements in gaming history. It's really hard for me to give it anything less than a 10/10.

And frankly, I feel like a lot of the people jumping on the hate train haven't even played the game themselves. They're just getting swept up in online outrage and following whatever the internet tells them to think.

I really hope people give this game a little more time and patience. I'm confident its user score will eventually go up.

The everyday activities, character interactions, random encounters, going about your characters’ daily lives, and all those little details that make the world feel like an actual living place. The life-sim elements are surprisingly enjoyable, and I love how Rockstar makes even the most ordinary activities feel worthwhile.Combat is also a noticeable improvement. Gunfights feel more engaging, weapons have a satisfying feel, and there’s more emphasis on positioning, cover, and how you approach encounters. Driving is fantastic, too!And visually? Absolutely insane. The amount of detail Rockstar has packed into this world is something else. Performance has been pretty good on my PS5 so far. I did notice a few frame-rate dips during one particularly demanding mission, but nothing game-breaking or that seriously affected my experience. Sure, the 30 FPS cap isn’t ideal, and I would’ve loved a 60 FPS option, but overall, the game still looks gorgeous and plays well.Honestly, I haven’t felt this immersed in an open-world game in a long time. There’s just so much to see, do, and experience that I don’t even feel the need to rush through the story.Hands down, the most immersive game I’ve ever played and the best open-world game I’ve ever experienced. Rockstar really outdid themselves with this one! Masterpiece

author: remzula
quote:
Rating: 9.1/10

GTA 6 is genuinely one of the most enjoyable gaming experiences I've had.

Rockstar has once again created an incredible open world that feels alive. There's always something happening, whether you're following the main story, exploring Leonida, doing side activities, or stumbling into some of the most ridiculous encounters imaginable.

The story is a noticeable step up from GTA V, although I wouldn't put it above Red Dead Redemption 2. Nevertheless, the characters, interactions, and overall experience have kept me invested.

Jason Duval is probably my favourite character so far. Initially, I wasn't particularly fond of his stoic personality, but the more time I spent playing as him, the more I appreciated him. There's something incredibly entertaining about watching this seemingly calm and collected guy navigate the most absurd situations imaginable. He's grown on me considerably.

Lucia is also a great protagonist, and playing between the two characters makes the experience even more enjoyable.

One thing I particularly appreciate is how Rockstar balances realism with absolute insanity. One moment you're immersed in a grounded criminal storyline, and the next you're encountering something completely surreal. That's part of what makes GTA GTA.

I also appreciate the freedom to approach the game at my own pace. I've spent considerably more time exploring and enjoying side activities than rushing through the main story.

If there's one thing I can say, it's that GTA 6 reminds me why I love video games in the first place. It's entertaining, immersive, unpredictable, and genuinely fun.

Rockstar has delivered something special. I can't wait to see what else this game has to offer.

author: Chrislemale
quote:
GREAT TECHNOLOGY, DISAPPOINTING DECISIONS
NEGATIVES
• Anti-consumer practices: No genuine physical edition, undermining consumer ownership and freedom of choice.
• Excessive romance: At times, GTA VI feels more like a relationship simulator than a traditional Grand Theft Auto game.
• Character inconsistency: Lucia's lapdances with female strippers feel unnecessary and out of character, despite her noticeably less sexual interactions compared to Jason.
• Lucia's personality: Often unnecessarily abrasive, unfriendly and lacking femininity, making her difficult to sympathize with.
• Introducing paid subscription benefits into a full-priced single-player game is another example of corporate greed. This is why I believe independent studios are the future of gaming, prioritizing creativity, consumer rights and genuine ownership over excessive monetization.
• Artificial restrictions: Forced character switching and selective combat restrictions undermine player freedom and immersion.
POSITIVES
• Jason is an excellent, immersive player avatar.
• Outstanding open world and attention to detail.
• Excellent fitness mechanics, everyday activities and gameplay possibilities.
Introducing paid subscription benefits into a full-priced single-player game is another example of corporate greed. This is why I believe independent studios are the future of gaming, prioritizing creativity, consumer rights and genuine ownership over excessive monetization.
FINAL VERDICT 
GTA VI is technically impressive and certainly not a bad game. However, its anti-consumer business practices and questionable design decisions prevent me from recommending it.
Respect your customers, Rockstar.

author: JamesWishhh
quote: After a 13-year wait, Rockstar has delivered a technical and artistic landmark. Leonida is the most alive, dense, and reactive open world the series has ever produced. Everyday moments (grilling burgers, mini-golf, random dog fetch) sit right next to explosive heists, and the contrast works. Jason and Lucia’s relationship gives the crime story genuine heart, and the level of environmental detail, lighting, and systemic reactivity sets a new bar for the medium. Critics have scored it near-perfect for a reason. That said, it is not flawless. The game is locked at 30 fps even on PS5 Pro, and while the trade-off buys stunning fidelity, the frame rate still feels dated—especially in dense traffic or chaotic firefights, where some players report noticeable dips. Gunplay is improved and more tactile than GTA V, but it remains a bit clunky on controller; free-aim and heavier recoil demand more precision than the series traditionally required. Early missions can drift into “criminal errands,” and some of the satire and humor lean on familiar Rockstar tropes rather than feeling freshly sharp for 2026. Jason, in particular, can come across as flatter than Lucia. GTA VI is still the game of the generation—an imperfect masterpiece that mostly earns the hype. Worth playing, worth losing yourself in, and worth criticizing precisely because its ambitions are so high.

author: DihedralCrux
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI lands at a 7 / 10 for me—an ambitious, richly detailed sandbox and a compelling Jason-and-Lucia partnership that gets real credit for its craft, yet leaves me genuinely uneasy about what the way this launch was handled means for the rest of the gaming industry. Leonida is packed with dense crowds, road heat haze, layered audio, and smarter crime prep like trunk disguises and target scouting that give the open world real texture. Those strengths make it easy to see why people get pulled into the setting, even when the underlying experience feels less like a clean leap forward and more like a mixed bag.

Where the game earns genuine praise is in how Jason and Lucia anchor the story and how your habits shape their dynamic. Rather than locking you into a single predetermined vibe, you can steer their relationship toward real partnership or keep things cooler and more transactional, while your criminal profile, mission choices, and savings habits feed into how the story wraps up. Still, plenty of smaller mission beats follow familiar Rockstar rails, and the slower pacing, travel time, and heavy side and collectible sprawl ask for a lot of hours if you want to see it all.

Technically, the ambition of the world pushes current consoles right up against their limits and shows real trade-offs. A 30 FPS cap that dips into the 20s when action or driving heats up, paired with temporal anti-aliasing blur and ghosting in motion, holds back the visual clarity—even if hard crashes are much less common than frame-rate complaints. Temporal anti-aliasing helps keep dense foliage, crowds, and geometry from shimmering apart on tight hardware budgets, yet the trade-off in motion blur and ghosting is hard to miss when things move fast.

What worries me most, though, is what this release normalizes for the wider industry. Pushing a $79.99 base price, an even steeper $99.99 Ultimate Edition with gated extras and a separate add-on split, and online or subscription nudges sets a precedent that other publishers will gladly copy without having Rockstar's scale or polish to back it up. Even if GTA VI has enough content to justify the outlay for plenty of players, cheering on higher price tiers and edition gating risks turning $80-to-$100 games and nickel-and-diming into the new default across every mid-tier release.

All told, GTA VI has a memorable duo, a dense world to explore, and enough scale to keep you busy for a long time, which is why it still clears a 7 / 10 for me rather than falling flat. If you do not mind 30 FPS console limits, motion softness, and a heavy price tag, there is plenty here to dig into—just do not be surprised if the industry uses this launch as cover to charge more for a lot less.

author: TheWhatDog
quote:
The world design, character depth, and true(r)-to-life pacing are exactly what I look for in a video game.

Rockstar are just simply more capable than any other developer when it comes to crafting authentic physical environments - the passing chatter of pedestrians, the crunch of gravel beneath car tires, or the white-capped wake left behind a boat.
Driving Jason's boat at sunset is simply the most visually impressive gaming experience I have ever had. 
This game has struck the perfect balance of realism and art direction and is the most beautiful rendered world since RDR2.
Vice City feels like it existed before I stepped into it, and that it will go on each time I hop off.

Rockstar rarely forces you to spend your time in their world's with characters you don't like - every character with a voice has brought with it a level of depth and reality (Claude may be my OG, but let's be real, was an avatar at best). Even their most deranged and psychotic characters are imbued with a level of humanity that makes us care for them and, ultimately, strive for them to make it out of their stories alive - think about how upsetting it was to have Johnny literally stamped out by, at the time a stranger to the player, Trevor, only for us to all choose Ending C (seriously, who picks A or B?) - not wanting to see our misunderstood hero taken out.
Here, they've done it again. Jason and Lucia are conventional heroes and are safely within those archetypes - the strong, silent ex-military specialist and the outspoken, but with a heart-of-gold, fighter with a chip on her shoulder.
They exist safely within their conventional boundaries, but are written with care and are thoughtfully portrayed - I want them to succeed and luckily I'm the one in control of that.

The narrative takes it's time - I'm 24 hours in and roughly halfway through Chapter 2 - and this, to me, is ideal. I'm one who'll happily sit with a 3+ hour film or some slow-burn series that starts with a quiet pop rather than a loud bang.
The slew of side characters bring differing levels of depth but are all, at the very least, entertaining and keep the humour and story going in the early sections.
There are moments of languishing in long boat rides out to another treasure dive - but then you dive under water and experience the beams of light that penetrate the surface, and the boat ride acts as the 6 minute 57 second build up to the solo in Lynard Skynyrd's Free Bird (extended version). 
Worth it.
These slower moments only act as further delayed gratification before the action-packed set pieces that dot the storyline. The end of Chapter 1 being one of the best in the series and I only expect them to grow more epic in scale and repercussion.

Is it flawless? No. 
There are technical itches - weird sharpness issues, shadow pixelation, and the odd choppiness when things get hectic - but they are scratched by the overwhelming impressiveness of everything else.
Do I enjoy being forced into singular character exploration at some early points? Not always, but I see that it serves a narrative purpose.
Do I have my preference for who I play as? Yes, and playing solo as that character is what I would prefer - but that too serves it's purpose and, screw it, I like them both.
To me, however, perfection requires some level of flaw. It gives a thing it's identity.

This is my perfect game. I could not be happier to be finally playing it.

author: Zelarom
quote:
GTA VI Is Simply Incredible – 10/10

Grand Theft Auto VI has honestly blown me away. I expected something amazing from Rockstar Games, but experiencing this game for myself has been something else entirely.

First of all, the graphics are absolutely stunning. I can't remember the last time a game made me stop so often just to admire the world around me. The level of detail is almost unbelievable. Everywhere I look, there's something that catches my attention. It could be a building, a street, the environment, or even something completely ordinary that I would normally ignore in another game. Somehow, Rockstar has managed to make even the smallest things interesting to look at.

There have been so many moments when I'm supposed to be doing something in the game, but instead, I find myself just standing there, looking around and appreciating how beautiful everything is. Sometimes I completely forget what I was doing because something as simple as a random detail in the environment catches my eye. That's how impressive the visuals are. It's not just about having good graphics; it's about how much care and attention went into creating this world.

And the gameplay? It's on another level. Everything I've experienced so far has been incredibly fun and engaging. The way NPCs interact with you and the world around them is genuinely impressive. It makes the environment feel alive instead of just being a beautiful background. Even the hand-to-hand combat is surprisingly entertaining. I've had so much fun with something as simple as getting into a fight, which says a lot about how enjoyable the gameplay really is.

Another thing I really appreciate is the characters and their stories. Their backgrounds are interesting, and there's an emotional side to their struggles that makes them feel more believable. They aren't just characters moving the story forward. They have problems, personal challenges, and situations that I think a lot of people can relate to. I really like that Rockstar managed to bring that human side into a game with so much going on.

What I love most about GTA VI is that I don't feel like I need to constantly complete missions to enjoy myself. Sometimes just exploring, watching the NPCs, or admiring the scenery is enough to keep me entertained. Very few games have made me appreciate the world itself this much.

The crazy part is that I'm only halfway through the game. I still have so much left to experience, but I've already seen enough to confidently give it a 10/10. Could something happen later that changes my opinion? I seriously doubt it. That's how much I've enjoyed everything so far.

For me, GTA VI isn't just a great game with beautiful graphics. It's one of those rare experiences where the visuals, gameplay, characters, and world all come together to create something special. You can really feel the amount of work that went into it, even in the smallest details.

I genuinely believe Rockstar has delivered something incredible, and I can't wait to experience the rest of it.

10/10. An amazing game that deserves every bit of praise it gets.

author: WinniesRims
quote: Grand theft auto six is one of the most visually impressive and densely packed games and game worlds that any developer has created, and while the game, in my opinion, is an absolute must play, it is not perfect and is not for everyone overall, you’ll be blown away by the visuals and performances that the game has to offer, as well as the plethora of activities that are available. However, there are some issues which I do think, hold the game back and lower the rating, firstly. The performance on console is frankly very distracting. since the summer of 2025, almost every game that has come out on current gen consoles, whether that be the Switch, the Xbox, or the PlayStation have almost all ran at least at 60 FPS, and while there are some examples of that not being true, the majority of big budget or blockbuster games tends to hold to that pattern. However, GTA6 runs at 30, even on the more powerful PS5 Pro, which I played on and while up until this generation, a lot of those bigger blockbuster games were running at 30, it is very jarring to go back to playing at 30, especially in a game that looks as visually stunning as GTA6. I almost wish they would have offered a decreased resolution mode with a higher frame rate, as I found in many cases in high-intensity scenes such as car chases or shootouts, the lower FPS did detract from my overall enjoyment. Secondly, the control scheme itself is a control scheme that many rockstar fans are familiar with, and while I do think it does get the job done in most cases, it feels very dated compared to other games and more recent titles from other franchises. In my opinion it should be overhauled for the next title. My final issue with this game that really keeps it from being rated higher, as I can forgive the other two in most cases, is that in my own opinion the game itself, in some gameplay instances and story instances, just isn’t very engaging, at least compared to other rockstar titles such as Red Dead Redemption 2 or GTA V. after reaching about my six hour mark of playtime, I found myself asking, is this it, much of the gameplay, at least at the start, is very toned down from previous titles and really takes a good couple of hours or more depending on how fast you play to really start to pick up, and while a slow burn can be engaging if done properly, such as Red Dead Redemption 2, for example, I have found this to be excessive to give an example, I’m sure we’ve all seen the jokes and memes about chore simulator six, and while I do feel those are grossly over exaggerated, I do have to, in some cases, agree with those jokes never once have I thought to myself, it sure would be fun to paint a bedroom or assemble furniture or fix a roof in a game, and while I get this dos add to the overall story, if I wanted to do chores, I’d simply go out in my own backyard and rake the leaves. GTA VI is a complicated title to me. It had almost unprecedented hype, and as of now is the best-selling media event in the history of the world, and while I do believe the budget and the time and the people that went into this game deserve their praise, I find the game itself lacking in a couple of cases or areas that truly make it worth a 10 out of 10 if you are a fan of some of their previous titles like Red Dead Redemption II, this will surely be right up your alley, but if you are looking for a more traditional GTA experience, I may suggest waiting for the online to come out at a later date or going back and playing previous titles such as Grand Theft Auto V.
