author: v1nc3st4r
quote:
Grand Theft Auto 6 is not a perfect game. No game is. Not even Ocarina of Time. That game is a masterpiece. I have a lot of good to say about this game, and there's bad too. 

The games' immersion is great, I love the weight on the vehicles, the fact that it's not too easy to get money, graphically, the game is stunning. The characters look their greatest in the series. I have no issues with the game being in 30 FPS, I'm used to it, 60 FPS would be nice, but it's not a turn off for me. There's so much to do in this game, seriously. I get distracted by side activities that randomly occur while I'm driving, and it's great to just cruise around and explore the map.

As a person with thalassaphobia, going underwater is a genuine fear which translates to video games. I do not want to explore the deep seas of Leonida, especially with the fact that there are SHARKS, ALLIGATORS. That'll be the death of me. It was a problem for me in Red Dead Redemption 2 with the gators, and literally most of the sea creatures (whales, sharks, fish..) in GTA 5. But it just looks so beautiful, I want to explore it all. Perhaps I can cross out a fear.

The game has its occasional stutters, especially in action packed scenes or when I do some sharp turns, but other than that, nothing really is noticeable. I haven't experienced any crazy glitches that I've seen online which is good news. I wish I was able to break into more houses, it would be cool to rob my neighbors.

Story wise, not too bad. I'll admit I'm only on Chapter 3, but so far, I'm enjoying it. Chapter 1 was really chore and driving heavy, but it was a nice way to explore the game at the start at least. Chapter 2 was where I was starting to feel immersed as I could finally take on stick ups, jack cars more easily, and just get into the action. 

Police are smarter than ever. A lot of mixed feelings on that, personally I think it's fine. Better than the rage monsters in GTA 5. 

Physics, I love the physics. Throwing people off balconies, the new combat is great, incapacitating, the gore, I love it. It's what I wanted in other GTA games and now we finally get it.

I'd give GTA 6 a solid 9.4/10 for now, I'll likely come back to this review when I finish the game.

author: Kaifox337
quote:
Beautiful graphics and the game runs smoothly on my base PS5, I have not noticed any stutters or frame dips, even in the heart of Vice City at night. 

The biomes are varied and insanely detailed, the fact I can drive around my small town in the keys, then go swimming through a reef and then hop on my boat, go see the gators and rednecks of the grassrivers, before loading my boat onto my truck and cruising through Vice City is amazing and the map design, both visually and it's seamless cohesion is GTA 6s biggest strength imo.

To my surprise, I also actually enjoy Jason and Lucia's story, I thought it was going to be a Bonnie and Clyde F the world duo that cared nothing about anything, but the actual ability to choose whether to pursue their relationship or ignore it all together was a sigh of relief, it no longer became a forced and scripted relationship and actually became something you had direct control over, I also loved that they had a child and Jason, who didn't ever see himself being a dad, was overfilled with joy when he learned, and his personality immediately went to thinking of the boy and wanting to do everything he could for him. In reality however, they should have went completely straight and figured things out, but this is a GTA game after all so of course they pursue less legal means of income procurement. All in all, for the duo, I didn't find Lucia nearly as annoying as I thought I would have and Jason turned out to be far more in depth than the idgaf, washed up, blame it on everyone else, person I originally thought he would be.

The driving mechanics are great, the cars feel much more realistic than arcadey, which personally I prefer, but I know many people will not like the realism over arcade style driving. The level of customization is the best in the series, in some cases, it even gave me vibes of the midnight club games, which rockstar should definitely revive btw. I do and don't like the car thefts, while I believe it's incredibly realistic that you need only a slim jim for older cars and key cloners for new cars and this mechanic also really helps set the pace of the game and drive home the idea that your working your way from the bottom, sometimes I just want to steal a sports car and go crazy speeding across the map and that is literally the name of the game, and this iteration makes that incredibly difficult, especially in the early game. 

The police AI is what I've been asking for for as long as I can remember, no longer are police a dumb but vast force trying to ram you and shoot you off the road, but they are actually a intelligent enemy that has to work within certain confines, they do not just magically know you committed a crime if there are no witnesses, they have to have a description of you, or your vehicle in order to stop you, I love this level of realism.

Now, for a couple bad things during my playthrough, let's address the elephant in the room, this game was made by and large by woke leftists, it just is the truth of the culture at large corporations, especially creative corporations such as game developers, they do not have diversity of thought and operate on a hivemind, now to be fair, GTA 6 is nowhere near as woke as I thought it'd **** it is woke, the radio stations and talk shows, and dialogue in the game almost exclusively punch one direction, making fun of white conservative type people, which in and of itself is fine, if it's applied equally, make fun of everyone equally but GTA 6 is scared of the woke cancel culture mob (which happens to be 90% of its employees) and as such do not make significant jabs at LGBT, socialism, trans, BLM, Welfare state, illegal immigration, or really any leftist ideology. There's a viral video even showing a leftist protester and he cannot be harmed by the player, so now it has moved to rockstar actively protecting leftist ideologies and figures within the game. Politically the game ****, it doesn't make fun of everyone and anyone like previous titles and only makes fun of "safe" targets, I.e conservatives or whites, it's appalling and cowardly, but if you go into this game not giving a damn about politics, it is still an enjoyable experience.

Another issue I had, and this is more **** issue, it's just not fun in some places, realistic sure, fun, no. For example, I'm boating along the grassrivers, I hear a monstrous growl and see something akin to Bigfoot, so I turn my boat in that direction, only to bottom out my boat because I didn't see a small bit of land that was to shallow for my boat to traverse, I now had to spend 30 minutes pushing on the boat and mashing square to try to get it unstuck...that's not fun, it **** me right out of the immersion of trying to find the Bigfoot and turned the game into a chore, there are many other examples like this where the game feels more like a chore than a game, and while yes it is realistic, it takes away from the fun of the game.

Overall, I rate it a 80/100.

You genuinely feel the weight of a car biting into a corner, and the damage modeling plus cover flow feel way smoother and punchier than older entries. Even the mission design breaks out of the old "go here, shoot everyone" loop with setups that reward actual planning and quick improvisation.Honestly, I’m slowing down on the main story right now just to poke into corners, side activities, and random street encounters—that’s where the game's real magic pops up. author: Libergy77
quote: A Once-in-a-Generation Masterpiece. An Absolute Triumph of Video Game Art.There are video games, there are masterpieces, and then there is Grand Theft Auto VI. Rockstar Games hasn’t simply delivered another installment in one of the most successful franchises in entertainment history. It has seemingly redefined what an open-world video game can aspire to be.From the very first moments, GTA VI establishes an extraordinary level of ambition, craftsmanship, and attention to detail. Everything about this experience feels meticulously considered, from its breathtaking environments and incredibly sophisticated world design to its characters, atmosphere, animations, and environmental storytelling. This isn’t merely a map filled with activities. It’s a living, breathing world that feels as though it exists independently of the player.What makes GTA VI particularly remarkable is its commitment to immersion. The sheer density of its environments, the authenticity of its characters, the subtle interactions, and the incredible attention paid to seemingly insignificant details create an experience that goes far beyond traditional open-world design. Every street, every neighborhood, every encounter contributes to an overwhelming sense of realism and believability.Visually, Rockstar continues to demonstrate an almost unreasonable level of technical mastery. The lighting, reflections, weather systems, character models, facial animations, environmental details, and overall presentation establish an extraordinary standard. The visual fidelity isn’t impressive simply because it looks beautiful; it’s impressive because every technical achievement serves the atmosphere and **** technical excellence alone doesn’t make a **** heart of GTA VI lies in its world, its characters, and its storytelling. Rockstar has always understood how to create memorable personalities and compelling narratives, combining satire, social commentary, dark humor, emotional moments, and spectacular cinematic sequences. The relationship between its protagonists brings an additional emotional dimension to the experience, making the narrative feel considerably more personal and **** then there’s the world itself. Vice City and the surrounding state of Leonida represent everything that makes Grand Theft Auto so special. A beautifully constructed playground filled with absurdity, social contradictions, unforgettable locations, and endless opportunities for emergent storytelling. It’s an environment that encourages exploration not because the game constantly demands it, but because simply existing within this world is **** level of polish and ambition is particularly impressive considering the expectations surrounding this release. Following the extraordinary legacy of GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar was facing an almost impossible challenge: delivering something that could justify more than a decade of anticipation. GTA VI represents the kind of artistic and technological ambition that very few studios are capable of pursuing.Most importantly, it feels like a genuine evolution rather than a superficial sequel. It doesn’t simply rely on the success of its predecessors. It pushes the franchise forward and demonstrates what happens when a studio is given the resources, time, and creative freedom to pursue an uncompromising vision.I also believe GTA VI deserves recognition for something that is becoming increasingly rare in the industry: ambition without compromise. In an era dominated by repetitive formulas, aggressive monetization, and increasingly interchangeable open-world experiences, Rockstar continues to pursue a distinct creative identity. Its attention to detail and commitment to world-building are exactly what make its games so special.Could anything be improved? Perhaps. No video game is objectively flawless. But perfection isn’t necessarily the absence of imperfections; sometimes, it’s the ability to deliver an experience so extraordinary that its shortcomings become almost irrelevant in the grand scheme of **** VI isn’t simply competing with other video games. It’s setting expectations for an entire generation of developers.Final verdict: 10/10.A monumental achievement, an extraordinary celebration of interactive entertainment, and potentially one of the most important video games ever created. Rockstar has once again demonstrated why it occupies a category of its own.Some games entertain you for a few hours. Some stay with you for years. And then there are games that redefine your expectations of the medium entirely.Grand Theft Auto VI belongs in the latter category. A generational masterpiece.

author: COPPET
quote:
It's a slow paced and long game, you should know this before going into it. 

Pacing: If you want action, fighter jets and rocket launchers after the prologue... this is not the game for you. The slower and grounded pace makes the fast pace action missions far more satisfying. 

Map / Detail: It's THE best aspect of the game, I genuinely don't know how they pulled this off and got it to run on a console. It's hard to describe but it feels real, the map alone is enough to make you immersed.

Story: Hot take but, I think the couple stuff is cute and accurate to my experiences... primarily the waiting around. The characters around the protagonists are good but not the games strongest point. I haven't finished the main story yet but so far I remain very satisfied with the game. 

30fps: Yeah... this is easily the biggest flaw. I come from 360Hz PC gaming and this was painful at the start. That being said, I got used to it after turning off motion blur. I'm not saying I like it or you should but, if I got used to it then anyone can. It's a miracle they managed to pull this off on console and I would take what we have now over a lower detailed game at 60fps any day of the week. 

Summary: This is easily one of the best games I have ever played, we shall see how the remainder of the game goes but it might go down as the best. I had high expectations and was prepared to be disappointed, I wasn't. I get people might not like the slower pace and 30FPS might be annoying but the hate? If you put 10h into this game and hate it... then you probably would have hated on it no matter what R* did.

author: Quandie
quote:
Absolute masterpiece, built on everything they got right in Red Dead Redemption 2 and pushed it to 11. 

A lot of the early online discourse has focused on the early mundane missions but like most of Rockstars recent games don't be fooled by this slow start there are plenty of opportunities for chaos as things progress but a little more thought needs to be put into what your way out will be once the police are on your tail and I think that's a great evolution in the series and only adds to the immersion. 

If you liked RDR2 and have been a long time fan of the craziness and satire GTA has been known for then I'm sure you will find plenty in this game to throw yourself at. I can't wait to spend hundreds more hours exploring what this world has to offer and I'm already excited to see how different approaches change my game in my next play through.

author: HankJames
quote:
God I would hate to be on the fence for this one. On one hand, you have devout fans who would never besmirch a Rockstar Game’s release. On the other, you have an overwhelming majority of loser’s with nothing better to do than to nitpick and review bomb a great game. The majority of that majority will never have owned or played the game in any capacity, mind you. 

GTA6 is massive. The map is massive. The depth of the characters is massive. The story is, you got it, massive. Be it treating the game as a demented sandbox, or playing through the nearly 80 storyline, the sheer amount of fun you can have playing this game is just so goddamn impressive. 

If you don’t know what to think, I don’t blame you. I encourage potential players to just watch through a couple of hours of gameplay on YouTube rather than listening to someone like me go on about how great it is, or worse, listen to them go on about how bad it is. 

Nothing is perfect, I won’t sugar coat it. But this, for me, is the closest to a ten out of ten game I’ve played through in a very long time. It deserves your attention.

quote:
GTA 6 exceeds my expectations and is one of the most impressive games I’ve seen technologically. I really appreciate the more mature or adult tone they’ve gone for over gta v. 

I think the relationship dynamic works well for the main protagonist without being too overbearing. 

It was slightly frustrating at the start getting used to all the new systems I was not familiar with but came to love them the further I got into the game. I would’ve loved to see this game at 60fps but there has to be compromises somewhere for a game like this.

Overall I love the direction the game has taken with elements of gta 5, gta 4 and red dead redemption 2 that all work so well together. This has been the most adult, mature and sometimes heart breaking story grand theft auto has ever seen.

author: Luminark
quote:
Despite its performance issues even on Playstation 5, GTA VI proves that AAA games could have done much better when it comes to producing games for the current generation of gaming consoles. Graphics are breathtaking, just as its immersion level makes you forget that its just a game sometimes - that's realism taken to the next level, ladies and gentlemen. The story is not to be overlooked. Any mature person who's at least in their 30s may relate to the everyday life struggle that's portrayed within the game's story. Love is indeed a double-edged sword, sometimes it works as fuel to one's ambitions, but sometimes it hits you so hard you feel like you're losing it for good.  The sound design is so realistic that when my wife and I were playing it without wearing any headphones, we would often think that some noise was coming from somewhere near our living room when it was actually in the game. Painting, shooting, walking, people talking, those are noises you hear EXACTLY like they sound in real life. 
This is a compelling story about doing your best as a criminal who wants to overcome obstacles and provide whats best for your son - all that in a fictional Miami, and God, do we know Miami is home to some of the worst crooks in the world.
Now, as to why I'm not rating it 10. First of all, any review that starts with 'despite something' is not a 10. 30 FPS with no option for a performance mode is disappointing to say the least in 2026. Secondly, it must be taken into account that many bugs in this game are not so easily overlooked. From trucks and cars that simply disappear in front of you to motorcycles being driven by...well. apparently nobody, there is no shortage of examples here. Did that affect my gameplay? Not really, but still, you don't "purchase" (digital only, so may we really call that purchasing if we do not really own it, according to Sony itself?) a game for about 100 bucks (80 euros, 550 BRL) and pretend it's just fine to stumble upon bugs and, well, getting stuck between invisible pixels and stuff.
Does it deserve that much hype? Yes, of course. Is it a 99? Not at all.
Between this and a remake of the most critically acclaimed (by both users and, well, professional critics) 2026's game of the year ought to be a closer call than we imagine.
Ps: this is a fun game, just not like GTA V or San Andreas. Pay no heed to incels who are apparently hurt by the fact you can't, idk,  hire hookers or mass murder minorities or whatever it is they play GTA for.

author: Alex_902
quote:
An Absolute Masterpiece – 10/10 
Honestly, I genuinely cannot understand the amount of hate Grand Theft Auto VI is receiving. And I don't mean reasonable criticism or legitimate concerns. I'm talking about the ridiculous amount of negativity, outrage and unnecessary complaining surrounding this game. At this point, some of the reactions are genuinely unbelievable. Rockstar has spent years developing what is arguably one of the most ambitious video games ever created, and instead of appreciating the incredible amount of work, passion and dedication that has gone into it, people seem determined to find absolutely anything to complain about. Whether it's the female protagonist, accusations of the game being too woke, the characters, the setting or practically anything else, there always seems to be another completely exaggerated **** honestly, what is happening to the gaming community? GTA has ALWAYS been a franchise built around satire, controversy, social commentary and making fun of practically everything. That's literally part of what makes Grand Theft Auto Grand Theft Auto. Yet somehow, having a female protagonist or approaching certain subjects differently suddenly seems to be enough for some people to declare that Rockstar has ruined the franchise. It's honestly ridiculous. What's even more frustrating is how much of this negativity seems to come from people who have already decided that they hate the game before even giving it a fair chance. Everything gets turned into a controversy, every decision gets criticized, and every new piece of information becomes another opportunity to complain. At some point, it genuinely feels like certain people don't even want the game to **** that's what I find so unbelievably absurd. We are talking about Rockstar Games, a studio responsible for some of the greatest and most influential games ever made. The level of detail, technical ambition, world-building and storytelling Rockstar brings to its projects is something very few developers can even come close to matching. The graphics are absolutely breathtaking. The world of Leonida feels incredibly alive, the environments are stunning, the character models and animations are incredibly detailed, and the attention to detail is simply insane. The gameplay offers the freedom and variety that have always made GTA special, while the story, Jason and Lucia, and their relationship provide a fresh and exciting direction for the franchise.Everything about this game demonstrates an incredible amount of ambition. The atmosphere, soundtrack, radio stations, humour, world design and storytelling all come together to create something truly **** no, that doesn't mean GTA VI is above criticism. No game is. If there are genuine problems with performance, gameplay or technical quality, absolutely discuss them. But there is a massive difference between legitimate criticism and actively looking for reasons to hate something.I genuinely find it astonishing that a game can generate this much excitement and anticipation while simultaneously attracting so much completely unnecessary hostility. Instead of celebrating what could be one of the biggest achievements in gaming history, parts of the internet seem more interested in inventing controversies and finding something to be offended by. Personally, I think the amount of hate surrounding GTA VI is absolutely ridiculous. Not every creative decision needs to be turned into a political debate, and not every new direction needs to be treated as an attack on the franchise. Sometimes, people should simply let developers create something, experience the result and judge it fairly.Grand Theft Auto VI deserves recognition for its ambition, creativity and the incredible work behind it. Rockstar has once again demonstrated why it is one of the most respected studios in the entire industry. 10/10. An absolute masterpiece. And honestly, the amount of unnecessary hate this game receives is almost as unbelievable as the game itself.

author: Matters05
quote:
GTA VI is a gamers game. On the surface the hyper realistic graphics can hook anyone in, but what keeps you is everything else. The open world opens up pretty early on, so you can steal a jet or tank from the military base before long, but what makes this game so special is how unlike in past GTA games, the story missions enhance the open world like never before. In GTA 4, completing story missions would unlock new guns, which was cool, but in GTA 6 this is taken to the next level, you are given more tools to elevate your criminal acts such as a Slim Jim to help you steal cars or devices to jam ink bags stolen during heists.

Even without completing story missions, the open world hooks you instantly, I can't count how many times I've slowed down to investigate screams, or a traffic stop - in one instance the lady was being given a ticket and fled, giving me the perfect opportunity to steal her fast car easily. This brings me back to why it is a 'gamers game', you can choose to not take part in any encounter and speed through all the main missions, which I can admit is tempting as they are essentially action movies, but if you did so you wouldn't have nearly as much fun as if you would engage with the open world aspect. 

I feel as though rockstar games have taken everything they learnt people found fun, such as heists in GTA online, and integrated it seamlessly into this world, and in cases where players have had qualms, such as the linearity of missions in earlier games - Rockstar have innovated. Thus this game warrants a perfect 10/10 rating from me as I believe it is Rockstar's magnum opus, every design choice is intentional, guided by their past successes & mistakes, and my biggest problem with it is pacing myself to not finish it too quickly.

author: CabesaYt
quote: Grand Theft Auto VI supone un nuevo paso adelante en la saga. Rockstar Games nos ofrece una experiencia de mundo abierto que destaca tanto por su apartado técnico como por su ambición narrativa. Ambientado en Leonida, un territorio inspirado en Florida, el juego presenta un entorno lleno de detalles, actividades y situaciones que hacen que el mundo se sienta dinámico y **** de sus mayores aciertos es la construcción de sus protagonistas, Jason y Lucía, cuya relación aporta un enfoque más personal a la historia. A esto se suma una ambientación sobresaliente, con gráficos, animaciones y una variedad de escenarios que elevan considerablemente la inmersión.También resulta interesante observar cómo GTA VI recoge y adapta muchas de las ideas que Rockstar perfeccionó en Red Dead Redemption 2. La atención al detalle, la naturalidad de las animaciones, la interacción con el entorno y esa sensación de que el mundo está vivo recuerdan mucho a la obra del oeste. Esto es especialmente destacable, ya que Red Dead Redemption 2 es uno de mis videojuegos favoritos, y ver parte de esa esencia trasladada a un universo moderno me parece un gran **** el apartado jugable, GTA VI mantiene la libertad característica de la franquicia, permitiendo al jugador explorar, realizar misiones y experimentar con las posibilidades que ofrece su mundo. Aunque algunas mecánicas pueden resultar familiares, la evolución de los sistemas y la influencia de anteriores títulos de Rockstar consiguen que la experiencia se sienta más **** definitiva, GTA VI destaca por su enorme calidad, su atención al detalle y su capacidad para ofrecer una experiencia memorable. No reinventa por completo el género, pero perfecciona muchos de sus elementos y aprovecha lo aprendido en anteriores proyectos para convertirse en un título sobresaliente.

author: 8irrelevant8
quote: # Technically Impressive, But Where Is the Innovation?Grand Theft Auto VI is undoubtedly an impressive production. Its graphics, visual presentation, attention to detail and world design deserve recognition. Rockstar clearly knows how to create a living, atmospheric and visually stunning world. The enormous production effort is unmistakable.However, technical brilliance and a gigantic production budget should not automatically be confused with genuine **** its core, GTA VI feels like another evolution of an already established formula. Many of its gameplay mechanics and concepts are familiar from previous entries and other games. The presentation is more sophisticated, the world is more detailed and the overall experience is more extensive. But where are the truly groundbreaking ideas? What does this game introduce that fundamentally changes our understanding of video games?For a production of this scale, I expected considerably more than another refinement of already familiar concepts.There are also technical shortcomings worth criticizing. Being limited to 30 FPS on consoles feels simply outdated in 2026, especially for a blockbuster of this magnitude. A production that places so much emphasis on technical excellence and visual presentation should deliver a smoother frame rate. To me, this technical limitation is a significant disappointment.Another criticism is the lack of a simultaneous PC release. At a time when PC gaming has long been an integral part of the gaming industry, excluding an entire player base at launch feels increasingly outdated and unnecessarily **** VI may be an excellent blockbuster, but technical perfection does not automatically mean redefining the boundaries of the medium.A game does not become legendary simply because it costs hundreds of millions to produce, looks spectacular or offers an enormous open world. True greatness comes from creating something new, setting new standards and having a lasting influence on the future of the gaming **** VI gets many things right and deserves recognition for its craftsmanship. However, when it comes to genuine innovation, it falls considerably short of my expectations.A good game, perhaps even a great one — but certainly not the revolutionary masterpiece some have already made it out to be.

author: AeacusXCIX
quote:
Después de tantos años de espera y unas expectativas prácticamente imposibles de cumplir, Rockstar Games volvió a demostrar por qué ocupa un lugar tan importante en la industria. GTA VI no es simplemente un GTA V con mejores gráficos. Es una evolución enorme de la fórmula que conocemos, y un videojuego que establece nuevos estándares en muchos aspectos.

Lo primero que impresiona es su mundo abierto. Leonida no solo es gigantesco, sino que está lleno de vida. La cantidad de detalles, la densidad de NPC, sus comportamientos, las interacciones y los acontecimientos que suceden a nuestro alrededor hacen que explorar sea una experiencia por sí misma. A diferencia de entregas anteriores, el mundo se siente mucho más orgánico, como si tuviera vida propia independientemente de nuestras acciones.

Gráficamente es una auténtica locura. Las animaciones, la iluminación, los reflejos, el clima, las expresiones faciales y el nivel de detalle de los escenarios son impresionantes. Pero lo verdaderamente destacable es que no se trata únicamente de gráficos bonitos: todo ese apartado técnico contribuye a una inmersión pocas veces vista.

La jugabilidad también presenta mejoras importantes. La conducción, los tiroteos, el sistema de coberturas y la respuesta de los controles se sienten más refinados. El sistema policial es mucho más elaborado, y ahora aspectos como nuestra vestimenta, el vehículo utilizado y la planificación de los delitos pueden influir en cómo nos persiguen las autoridades. Son cambios que aportan profundidad y hacen que nuestras acciones tengan mayor peso.

Otro de sus mayores aciertos es la cantidad de actividades disponibles. Desde explorar, pescar, bucear y practicar deportes hasta disfrutar de pequeños momentos cotidianos, el juego consigue que incluso las cosas más sencillas resulten entretenidas. Esa mezcla de libertad, realismo y diversión es precisamente lo que siempre ha caracterizado a GTA, pero aquí alcanza otro nivel.

En cuanto a la historia, Jason y Lucia aportan una dinámica diferente a la de protagonistas anteriores. Su relación permite desarrollar una narrativa más personal y madura, sin abandonar el humor, la sátira y las situaciones absurdas que forman parte de la identidad de la franquicia. Además, las interacciones entre ambos y las consecuencias de determinadas decisiones añaden una dimensión interesante a la experiencia.

También merece reconocimiento el apartado sonoro. La selección musical, los efectos ambientales, el sonido de los vehículos y la ambientación general son extraordinarios. Todo está trabajado para que el mundo resulte convincente.

¿Es perfecto? No necesariamente. El límite de 30 FPS, especialmente en PS5 Pro, resulta decepcionante considerando el hardware disponible. Algunas misiones todavía conservan estructuras demasiado guiadas, ciertos controles podrían ser más cómodos y el ritmo narrativo puede sentirse algo lento en determinados momentos. Sin embargo, son aspectos que, personalmente, no consiguen opacar todo lo que ofrece el juego.Para mí, un 10/10 no significa que un videojuego esté completamente libre de defectos. Significa que sus virtudes, su ambición y la experiencia que ofrece están a un nivel excepcional. Y GTA VI cumple con eso.

Por último, quiero dejar una reflexión sobre la comunidad.

Sé que no tengo muchas reseñas publicadas aquí, prácticamente ninguna. No acostumbro a escribir este tipo de cosas, pero me parece realmente decepcionante ver cómo algunas personas recurren al review bombing simplemente por envidia, rivalidades entre comunidades o fanatismo hacia otros videojuegos y compañías.

No hay absolutamente nada de malo en que GTA VI no te guste. Todos tenemos gustos diferentes, y las críticas negativas bien fundamentadas son completamente válidas. Lo triste es ver a alguien ponerle un cero a un juego que ni siquiera ha probado, únicamente porque pertenece a una compañía que no te gusta o porque quieres favorecer a otro título.

Los videojuegos deberían ser algo que nos una y nos permita disfrutar, no una competencia absurda para demostrar qué compañía o comunidad es superior.Disfruten de los videojuegos que les gustan, permitan que los demás disfruten de los suyos y aprendamos a reconocer el buen trabajo, independientemente de quién lo haya desarrollado.

La vida es demasiado corta para vivir amargados por el éxito de un videojuego.

author: ItsDanX97
quote:
Plus de dix ans d'attente, et Rockstar réussit pourtant à tenir toutes ses **** cœur du jeu, c'est le duo Jason et Lucia. Leur histoire fait immédiatement penser à Bonnie & Clyde : deux amoureux soudés contre le monde, prêts à tout l'un pour l'autre, avec cette tension constante entre complicité et danger. Leur relation donne un vrai poids émotionnel à l'aventure et rend chaque situation plus marquante.

Vice City est un monde ouvert d'une densité impressionnante. Même en roulant sans but précis, on tombe sur des détails et des situations qui donnent l'impression d'une ville vivante. L'ambiance, les graphismes et la bande-son renforcent encore l'immersion.

Comme souvent avec un jeu aussi ambitieux, tout n'est pas parfait : le côté réalisme peut déranger mais on s’y fait. Le côté réaliste n’entrave pas le plaisir de jeu.

Verdict : une aventure criminelle ambitieuse avec du réalisme, portée par un couple de héros attachant et un monde à la richesse rare.

author: splashyy77
quote:
I’ve played 20 hours on PS5 so far, and what impressed me most is how alive and interactive the world feels. The new car physics are incredibly satisfying, and so are the NPC ragdolls. The wanted system also feels like a big step up. That said, it might frustrate players who just want to cause chaos, so I’d love to see a Director Mode that lets you turn those mechanics off. And that’s just a small part of what I’ve enjoyed so far.

Is 30 fps a letdown? Sure, that’s a fair criticism. But this is easily Rockstar’s most polished launch ever, and it should only get better on next-gen hardware.

As for the review bombing: I honestly don’t get it. Calling it “woke” makes me wonder if we even played the same game. And if another game you love loses an award to this one, that’s no reason to tank its score. Rate what you actually played so others can have a good experience too.

You have to live in **** mission structure is excellent. There are tons of quality of life improvements that make everything feel modern and smooth. Combat is snappy. Honestly, everything is snappy. The whole game moves with a responsiveness that a lot of open worlds never get right. The driving feels closer to Forza than to old GTA, in the best way. It has real weight and **** customization is staggering. Even though Jason and Lucia are pre-made, they are two of the most unique and well-written protagonists in the series. They feel like real, specific human beings, not blank slates. Their story pulls you **** standout for me is the new morality system. Your choices carry weight in a way that mirrors real life, and that single addition deepens the immersion more than I expected. It makes the world feel like it is reacting to who you actually are.I highly recommend GTA 6. If I had to recommend a single game to anyone, this would be it.

quote: 10/10 — Une claque monumentale. Rockstar Games vient encore de rappeler pourquoi ce studio joue dans une catégorie à **** niveau de détail, l’immensité du monde ouvert, la liberté offerte aux joueurs, les animations, l’ambiance, la narration et le travail colossal derrière chaque élément du jeu méritent un immense respect. Des milliers de personnes ont consacré des années de leur vie à construire cette expérience. Et franchement, chapeau aux développeurs. GTA VI est une véritable prouesse.Maintenant, parlons des champions du review bombing. Il faut avoir atteint un niveau assez spectaculaire de mauvaise foi et de stupidité pour attribuer un 0/10 à un jeu simplement parce qu’on peut incarner une femme ou parce que certains personnages ne correspondent pas à sa petite vision étriquée du monde.Imaginez être tellement obsédé par le mot « woke » que la simple existence d’une protagoniste féminine suffit à vous faire oublier tout le travail technique, artistique et créatif derrière un jeu de cette envergure. À ce stade, ce n’est même plus de la critique vidéoludique, c’est un concours de fragilité intellectuelle.Vous avez parfaitement le droit de ne pas aimer GTA VI. Mais confondre une véritable critique avec une crise de nerfs idéologique, c’est surtout démontrer qu’on n’a absolument rien de pertinent à **** le plus ironique dans tout ça ? Ces grands défenseurs autoproclamés de la virilité sont apparemment terrifiés à l’idée de contrôler une femme virtuelle avec une manette. Rockstar a créé un monde entier à explorer, et certains n’ont toujours pas réussi à sortir de leur propre petite tête.10/10. Bravo Rockstar. Et courage aux guerriers anti-woke : survivre à la présence d’une femme dans un jeu vidéo doit être une épreuve absolument insurmontable.

author: Nugget23
quote: I read the reviews, and most of the complaints boil down to “This game is more like RDR2 than the previous GTA games.” Most people aren’t evaluating the game itself, but rather its соответствие to the outdated parts of the series. I don’t understand the criticism about it being boring at all. I’ve played for about 20 hours and I’ve encountered so many things. The story is actually quite good for such a large‑scale game. For me, GTA 6 is much better than RDR2 in terms of story and characters. It’s more memorable. I found RDR2 to be very tedious, and I dropped it twice in the third chapter. Some people might like it, while others don’t like GTA 6 — that’s fine, but the criticisms of GTA 6 are too unfounded, consisting of just a couple of sentences, rather than detailed, explanatory reviews. Besides, it’s only the game’s second day. I doubt that many people, like me, have managed to play for 20+ hours in that time. Even in that time, it’s impossible to draw serious conclusions — and if you do, then I like everything about it. Look at the game honestly, not through the lens of imagined expectations and previous parts that were much more primitive than the six. The game is simply wonderful and doesn’t get boring! It’s silly to find fault with the fact that the game is moderately realistic and focused on its narrative and interaction with a vast, well-developed world, rather than being a fun sandbox where you can cause chaos. Play it to the end, explore everything, and then draw your conclusions. In short, play it yourself, enjoy it, and don’t listen to anyone️

author: driley97
quote:
At a little under 10 hours into the story, i am enjoying this game and getting immersed in the open world. This feels like RDR2 in the best ways, although some things are a slog early on (namely the story being very tame in the first chapter). Performance also leaves a lot to be desired as the game isn’t a locked 30 FPS. 

Graphically this game is impressive if you look beyond the performance numbers. The world looks real, the cars look like they could exist in real life, and the NPC designs are quite varied. However the character models display uncanny valley qualities that feel noticeable enough to me know this isn’t real life, it’s a game. That might be my only criticism of the visuals, as everything else is amazing.

When it comes to the open world itself, the dynamically generated events that happen have been surprising. I was driving accross a bridge and saw a plan in the sky lose its engines and crash into a swamp. I’ve seen NPCs road rage. I walked onto the ground of a run down motel in the grass rivers and stumbled into a tiger attacking someone in their room (and unfortunately I couldn’t save him). After investigating the room I found a bunch of cash and then a group of guys sowed up outside in the truck and saw what I was taking and started a gunfight with me. The cops got radioed for a disturbance but nobody saw me so I had no heat level. When I came back through later, the cops were still investigating but had no suspicion it was me. I loved these interactions and they made the world feel alive on top of looking beautiful.

As far as nitpicks goes, the slow story in Chapter 1 makes this feel less like a crime conspiracy and more like a dating simulator in an open world that occasionally has you running drugs and shoot your gun. And of course on the PS5 slim the performance isn’t a locked 30 as I stated before. I am really looking forward to a PC release to hopefully have better performance. 

I can’t speak to the whole game yet, but so far I’d say  my expectations have mostly met, but this isn’t the 10 out of 10 game reviewers want to say it is and I believe that Ocarina of Time firmly remains the best game of all time and San Andreas and V remain the best GTA games ever personally. I look forward to seeing the rest of the story and what the eventual online mode will look like.

100%, 10/10, best game of ever? Sorry for me! I would say 85-90!

First of all it is a very good game! It looks stunning, it has a nice game flow and it works! Rockstar do a good job, but its only a 30fps game! But it to not stay on 30fps, there are enough scenes where it drops to 20-25 or even less, but mostly it says between 25-30. And that can't be a perfect score, if you have such frame drops! Also it has glitches, textures that stick in others, sometimes crazy bugs, but it is not a Cyberpunk 2077. But why journalist say its 10/10 when it is not a perfect game on the technical side?!

The gameplay, yeah.. its not really a GTA successor, its the grown up Telenovela version of GTA. Yes you steal cars, yes you do crimes, yes to have a decent story, but with the same downsides Rockstar Games has always. Is it woke? Yes at some points where you can't harm people who are mysteriously not harm-able. And that is not really a GTA game! GTA was total chaos in 1,2,3 and 4. 5 was more and more a washed out version of it and 6 is way more washed down, but it counter it with realism! That is a nice touch, but the realism goes to far!

To have a mostly one sided relationship with a Latina, who do mostly nothing for you, but you do all the chores for her, looks like a one sided relationship. The things you do for her do not really have a big impact, it feels more like a "i need to bring her flowers to get 1 Latina point, i am a good boy!" not like a realistic relationship. Cyberpunk 2077 do a better job with it. Because the stories and the help you give has benefits for both sides. You earn the trust, by doing important task, not bring her flowers and paint the wall for her. Also the story is decent, but has its downside, it gets boring at some times and sometimes it is clearly written by someone who think the relationships in "breaking bad" are realistic. Its to much cliche for my taste.

But here it do not end, the game overall is not my type and to only play as a male protagonist who get the girl involved, is not my style. Why Rockstar Games do not make a overall immersive experience with a "my destiny in game" would be far nicer. You choose thing, a guy or gal out of germany who is a military contractor or a russian nobody who try his luck in the usa or a japanese model or something else that give you some kind of backstory. Than you get 60% a red line story and 20% your chosen protagonist background and the rest 20% to date different people not only on Latina!. 

For me this is the most disappointing thing! In a game that has a world wide release, why i can't play heterosexual, homosexual or bisexual, why i must choose to play a men if i do not want. Also why i have not different partners who make the game replay-able. Like the Latina, a Italien Mafia guy who is transsexual and what to be a women and you help him to become a her! A chinese pro criminal, way beyond your level of crimes, but she helps you because you earn her respect. Or a movie star who is bisexual and you can help him, date him, be together with him. Rockstar Games is to narrowed down to the pair and that make the whole story boring! I do not want to be the simp for a needy Latina! I would even date a broken down woman with 3 kids in the game, who game my avatar in the game the feeling of "i have a family now, i am not alone anymore". And for such a game, that is way to less to get a 100/100 perfect score.

I can say more things, but that would lead only to spoilers... and for me its a good game, perfect in no way and that it do not release on PC on the same day is for me also a downside. I think Rockstar Games want to double dip again! Like in the old games, first on the worst possible console generation! Than on the next generation and finally on the PC, where you get most of the power! I do not take points out of my score for it, but it is a bad practice from a company who say they need mostly 10 years of development for that.

A must play, only if you like Rockstar Games, but have more emotional connection t Mass Effect 2 and Cyberpunk 2077 as to this game. Maybe when i am fully done, but i doubt it.

author: ThatOneReaper
quote:
I genuinely don't understand why this game has such a low player rating. It's currently sitting around a 5.1, and I'm confident that rating will eventually go up. I believe a lot of the negativity comes from players who follow popular streamers and jump on the bandwagon of criticizing the game simply because it's running at 30 FPS. Because of that, they're overlooking everything this game actually does right.

Putting the 30 FPS debate aside, this game is absolutely amazing. The random encounters, optional activities, robberies, side missions, and countless other things to discover make the world feel incredibly alive. There are so many side stories that they almost feel like entirely separate main storylines.

For context, it took me approximately 19–20 hours to get through Chapter One, and I'm still not even finished with everything available. That's because I'm actually taking my time. I'm completing side missions, participating in optional activities, exploring, doing robberies, and approaching the game like an actual criminal would. I'm not rushing from one main mission to another just to finish the story.

If you approach this game with that mindset, the experience is incredible. The graphics have genuinely blown my mind, the world feels alive, and the sheer amount of content available is impressive. This is, without a doubt, the best Rockstar game I've ever played so far, which is saying something considering how highly I regard Red Dead Redemption 2.

I genuinely believe this game deserves far more recognition than it's receiving from players. The critical reception speaks for itself, and I think there's a reason professional reviewers have recognized just how much this game accomplishes.

As for the story, Lucia is an incredible character. She's easily one of my favorite female protagonists in gaming. The overall storyline is fascinating, and I'm excited to see where it goes.

If you're reading this review and haven't purchased the game yet, I wholeheartedly recommend giving it a chance. I would recommend it 200%, especially if you're someone who enjoys slower-paced gameplay, immersive storytelling, criminal roleplay, and taking your time exploring an incredibly detailed open world.

Don't let the 30 FPS arguments or online negativity discourage you. There's so much more to this game than its frame rate. Take your time, experience the world, and you'll understand why I think this is one of Rockstar's greatest games.

author: Crstv
quote:
20 hours in and the game is pretty fun. To me the game lives up to the hype. It’s everything you expect **** game but more content and with new mechanics.

The story so far is really fun, the characters are more realistic compared to older gta series. They also clearly tried to make it more of a serious story, which so far I’m not complaining about. The last mission of chapter 1 was a goddamn banger lol. 

The new mechanics are really fun and challenging. Stealing cars is more challenging which is pretty cool to see. If you want a fast car you can steal it but you need to have a strategy beforehand. Alarms, trackers and key cloners are such a cool idea. The vehicles this time around also take damage and need gas, which at first I was a bit sceptical of. I was scared it might hinder the movement/freedom of what makes a gta game, but I’m happy to say it doesn’t. They’re pretty cool mechanics that are just there to make it a bit more immersive. So far I didn’t have any issues with the gas mechanics. Fitness comes back from gta San Andreas with a more in depth system. So far so good, I made my Jason a fat chud. Again doesn’t really feel like it hinders the game, it’s just there if you want to use it. The new buddy mechanic between Jason and Lucia is really fun, robbing stores has more weight to it now. The new cop system as well, they’re no joke. You need to plan ahead before committing any crimes, which adds a new sense of accomplishment every time you do a robbery. The holding hands mechanic is a bit wonky at times, other than that also fine. 

Open world and side content, this is where the game excels. There is so much to do and never does it feel like you’re doing the same type of activity. This time around it feels like you have more freedom when approaching the missions. The open world itself has so many random encounters, a talking cow lol, never does it seem the same. It feels rewarding to explore. This for me is my favourite part of the game and the selling point. 

Performance was fine. It runs at a perfect 30fps and sometimes but rarely drops below that. Personally I didn’t encounter any bugs during my time playing, although some people say the game is riddled with bugs. Idk where cus I haven’t encountered any. It is a bummer that it only runs at 30 fps, but the game is still playable. Goddamn does the game look good. This is genuinely a marvel of technology. Again in my time of playing I haven’t found any bugs. It doesn’t mean there aren’t any so maybe I’m just lucky. 

Don’t really have any problems with the game itself. The 30fps, no disc, 80 euro price tag and no pc release at launch are my only reasons why it doesn’t get a 10. It also isn’t the holy grail and perfect game as some people say it is, this game isn’t for everyone. It still has some little flaws here and there. But they are hidden with the sheer amount of content. 

If you like gta, Red Dead Redemption and max Payne then give this a try. If you’re expecting this game to be the cure for cancer or the second coming of Christ then maybe lower your expectations. Some people have an idea that this game should have been THE GAME OF ALL GAMES, but that’s just not realistic. 

All in all the game is really good, if you have some money give this a try. 

If you’re a chud lifeless loser who doesn’t like buying flowers for your girlfriend then maybe this isn’t for you either.

author: DefaultMan
quote: First of all, I should mention that I'm not the kind of person who usually creates an account just to leave a review. However, seeing how unfairly this game has been criticized made me feel almost obligated to write one. And let's be clear: a significant number of the negative reviews here seem to be either fake or written by Zelda fans who are more interested in tearing the game down than judging it ****, onto the game itself.From a technical standpoint, this is a nearly flawless Rockstar experience. I genuinely don't understand why people are blaming the game for running at 30 FPS. If anything, that's more of an issue with Sony and the console's hardware than with the game itself. I've been playing on my PS5, and I haven't encountered any performance issues serious enough to interfere with my enjoyment.I won't go into detail about the story since I haven't finished it yet, but I can already say that I've grown attached to the characters. So far, the narrative has been engaging, and I'm genuinely interested in seeing where it **** where this game truly shines is its open ****'s absolutely enormous, incredibly alive, breathtakingly beautiful, and packed with things to discover. I've rarely experienced a world this massive that also feels so detailed and carefully crafted. Simply existing in it is enjoyable. Whether I'm exploring the city, driving around, or just wandering without a particular destination, I'm constantly having a great **** soundtrack is fantastic, and the driving mechanics are a massive improvement over GTA V. That weightless, almost disconnected feeling from the previous game is completely gone. Cars actually feel satisfying to drive, and the narrower roads contribute significantly to a more immersive and realistic driving experience.What impresses me most is how unpredictable the world feels. You can be driving somewhere with a specific destination in mind and suddenly stumble upon something completely unexpected. There's always something happening, something to explore, or something that catches your attention.I've already spent around 20 hours playing, and I still haven't uncovered the entire map, despite deliberately spending time trying to explore as much of it as possible. That alone should give you an idea of just how massive and content-rich this world really **** sum it up: the graphics are phenomenal, the physics engine is outstanding, the story is promising, and the sheer amount of activities and attention to detail is incredible.This isn't just a game where you rush from one mission to the next. It's a world you actually want to spend time **** perhaps that's the biggest compliment I can give it: I haven't even finished the game yet, and I already know I'm going to miss this world when it's over.

Listen, guys, I love GTA 6 and everything it has brought to the table, and this is only the beginning. However, as a community, we need to stop review-bombing other games simply because we’re unhappy with our own user score.
Regardless of what our score is, GTA 6 currently has a 99, which is already an incredible achievement. Review-bombing other games isn’t going to improve our situation. If anything, it makes us look worse as a community. Instead, we should focus on leaving positive reviews for our game and reporting obvious review bombs when we come across them.
I also know there’s been some concern about OOT players being responsible for most of this behavior. However, I can confidently say that isn’t the case. Based on the review bombs I’ve personally reported, OOT players make up only a tiny fraction of them. The main culprits appear to be people deliberately review-bombing the game or individuals who simply didn’t enjoy it as much as the rest of us.
With that said, we should set a better example and avoid retaliating by review-bombing games like OOT just because others are doing it to us. We don’t need to stoop to that level. We’re better than that, and I think you guys know it.

author: scotot
quote: I have yet to complete the game but that doesn't really feel relevant to the scoring. Maybe 1 point would come off if the story doesn't stick the landing. This is the most visually and technically impressive piece of software I have ever seen. It is detailed to a degree that can only be accomplished by throwing thousands of people and millions of dollars at it for a decade. This is a feat we will likely never see matched. This has been the funniest GTA in my opinion, both in writing and in the wacky situations you can get yourself in. Ive never seen a game handle cutscenes this cinematically, it not only looks like a movie, but a notably well directed one. It takes every aspect I loved about previous GTA games and removes the ones I didn't like. It borrows more from red dead 2 than anything and I couldn't be happier. The gameplay loop of robbing and running from the cops is the ethos of this series and has seen very little innovation until now. It reminds me of the jump breath of the wild made within the Zelda series. Its missing some of the more "video game" parts from previous entries in pursuit of getting back to the series roots and reinventing what it means to see that original vision come to life in the modern era of gaming. And like with breath of the wild, this might upset a lot of people, but I think its worth it to alienate those people. In fact, with something this big, you will have to alienate a large amount of the player base if you want to say or do anything interesting as a creator.

I don’t believe this is entirely the game’s fault, but rather a limitation of the PlayStation hardware and its capabilities. In my opinion, this could potentially have been addressed through the implementation of AI-powered frame generation at the system level on **** second disappointment is the lack of a first-person perspective. What’s frustrating is that most of the foundations for this feature already seem to be present in the game. This makes me hopeful that it could be introduced in the future, and I sincerely hope to see it added through upcoming updates.Despite these shortcomings, GTA VI is a revolutionary and groundbreaking experience. It represents a massive leap forward in almost every aspect and sets a new standard for the GTA series.

author: Yannis91270
quote: GTA VI n’est pas simplement un jeu vidéo, c’est une véritable démonstration de ce que l’industrie vidéoludique peut accomplir lorsqu’elle repousse toutes ses limites. Rockstar Games livre une expérience monumentale, d’une ambition rarement égalée, qui redéfinit les standards du monde ouvert.Chaque détail semble avoir été pensé avec une précision exceptionnelle. La richesse de l’univers, le réalisme des environnements, la densité de la vie urbaine et la personnalité des personnages donnent naissance à un monde qui paraît vivant à chaque instant. On ne se contente pas de parcourir la carte : on a réellement l’impression d’habiter cet **** narration constitue également l’un des grands points forts de l’expérience. Les personnages sont profonds, attachants et complexes, tandis que l’écriture mêle habilement émotion, satire sociale, humour noir et moments spectaculaires. L’alchimie entre les protagonistes apporte une dimension humaine qui dépasse largement le simple divertissement.Mais ce qui impressionne le plus, c’est cette attention presque obsessionnelle aux détails. Les animations, les interactions, les activités secondaires, la mise en scène et l’immersion générale témoignent d’un travail colossal. Chaque session peut devenir une aventure différente, chaque détour peut réserver une **** direction artistique et la réalisation technique viennent sublimer l’ensemble. Vice City et ses environs possèdent une identité visuelle incroyable, avec une atmosphère qui donne envie d’explorer chaque recoin du monde.Certains jeux marquent une génération. D’autres définissent une époque. GTA VI appartient à cette seconde **** jeu ambitieux, immersif, spectaculaire et profondément mémorable. Une expérience qui rappelle pourquoi le jeu vidéo est un art à part entière.

author: Pablohenaog
quote:
He jugado GTA VI y, sinceramente, siento que estamos ante un hito técnico en la industria de los videojuegos. Me parece absurdo que se esté castigando de la manera en que se está haciendo en algunas reseñas de Metacritic, especialmente cuando creo que estamos frente a un título que acaba de elevar el estándar de lo que esperamos de un videojuego **** VI no viene necesariamente a cambiar el mundo, porque a estas alturas de la industria sería ingenuo esperar que un solo videojuego revolucione absolutamente todo. Pero sí está sentando nuevas bases sobre cómo se construyen, se desarrollan y se gestionan los mundos abiertos. Algo muy parecido a lo que consiguió GTA V y, especialmente, Red Dead Redemption 2 en su momento: cambiar nuestra percepción de lo que puede ser un mundo virtual y de hasta dónde puede llegar la interacción con él.
¿Es perfecto? No. Tiene aspectos por mejorar y seguramente habrá jugadores que experimenten bugs, problemas de rendimiento u otros inconvenientes. En mi caso, más allá de algunas caídas de frames, no he tenido problemas que hayan comprometido mi experiencia. Y sí, el rendimiento importa, la optimización importa y Rockstar también debe responder por ello. Pero una cosa es reconocer sus defectos y otra muy distinta es desconocer lo que este juego está consiguiendo. Personalmente, le doy un 10. Y no lo hago porque crea que no tenga nada que mejorar, sino porque pocas veces un videojuego consigue involucrarme emocionalmente de esta manera. La historia me parece increíble. Ya he llorado y ni siquiera he terminado el primer capítulo. ¿Cuántos juegos consiguen mantenerte más de 10 horas en una primera parte de la historia sin que sientas que estás alargando artificialmente la experiencia? ¿Cuántos consiguen que quieras detenerte, explorar, observar y simplemente vivir dentro de su mundo? Eso es lo que más me impresiona: GTA VI no se siente como un videojuego que simplemente tienes que completar, sino como un mundo en el que quieres permanecer. Creo que estamos tan acostumbrados a exigirle a la industria que nos sorprenda que, cuando aparece algo que realmente intenta llevar el medio un paso más allá, terminamos evaluándolo con una vara que a veces pierde de vista el contexto. La crítica es necesaria, por supuesto, pero también lo es reconocer los logros y entender el impacto que una producción de esta magnitud puede tener en el futuro del medio. Quizás dentro de unos años miremos atrás y entendamos mejor lo que Rockstar acaba de hacer. Como ocurrió con sus antecesores, el verdadero alcance de GTA VI posiblemente no se mida únicamente por sus ventas, sus puntuaciones o sus primeros días de recepción, sino por todo aquello que otros estudios intentarán replicar a partir de él.Para mí, GTA VI no es solamente un gran videojuego. Es una demostración de hasta dónde puede llegar este medio cuando se apuesta por una visión ambiciosa, una narrativa potente y un mundo construido con una atención al detalle extraordinaria. Y si todo esto apenas comienza en el primer capítulo, no quiero imaginar lo que todavía me espera.

author: Enasni89
quote: Grand Theft Auto VI Review: A Technical Masterpiece Held Back by 30 FPSRating: 8/10Grand Theft Auto VI is probably the best GTA we could realistically hope for in today’s climate without the game outright getting banned. Rockstar had a massive tightrope to walk here, and for the most part, they’ve pulled it off.Attention to DetailLet’s start with the obvious: the attention to detail is by far the best I have ever seen in a video game. The sheer density of the world, the lighting, the animations, and the little environmental touches make Leonida feel genuinely alive. From a pure craft perspective, Rockstar is still operating in a league of its **** Story & ToneSo far, the story is just okay. It’s fun—going to parties, soaking in the atmosphere, and messing around in the world is a great time—but it hasn't hooked me the way GTA: Vice City or GTA IV did. To be fair, GTA V had a similar issue. The three-protagonist dynamic and the heists were awesome, but the actual narrative wasn't the kind you couldn't put down; plenty of people played it for years and never actually bothered finishing the campaign. GTA VI feels like it's landing in that same **** for the edge the series used to have, it’s pretty clear there are things Rockstar had to rein in. That’s just the reality of today’s softer society and a younger generation of gamers who expect more "woke" sensibilities. Like it or not, Rockstar is a business first, and they had to find a balance that kept the GTA DNA intact without triggering a massive backlash or getting pulled from shelves. Given the environment they're releasing into, they threaded that needle about as well as anyone **** Biggest Disappointment: 30 FPS & No PC LaunchMy biggest gripe—and the main reason this isn't a 9 or 10—is the 30 FPS cap. A lot of console-only gamers who have never touched a high-end PC might not notice or care (much like Xbox Series S owners happily cruising along at 17 FPS), and good on **** if you’re used to playing games on Ultra settings at 80 FPS, the difference in smoothness is night and day. 30 FPS just isn't comparable. I notice it constantly, and it actively pulls me out of an otherwise incredible visual experience. It’s genuinely frustrating that Rockstar chose to hold back the PC release yet again. As gamers, we should have options—whether that’s a proper performance mode or the freedom to run it on hardware that can actually do it justice.VerdictGTA VI is an unbelievable technical achievement and a seriously fun sandbox, even if the story hasn't reached the heights of the classics and the humour has had to adapt to the times. Once it finally hits PC and we can play it at a proper frame rate, it’ll be something else entirely. Right now, though, the 30 FPS lock keeps it grounded at a solid 8/10.

There are a few things that make me feel this isn't a 99-rated or perfect game like Metacritic suggests, but it's definitely a 9/10 or higher.

- 30 FPS with occasional drops (still plays very well overall).
- An increased woke influence in a game that's supposed to offer freedom.

author: Simplyich
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI is not a bad game, and it easily earned its hype as the most anticipated release of the decade. Still, the 10/10 masterpiece narrative that everyone is clamoring about easily falls apart once you look past its visuals and examine how it actually runs, plays, and tells its story. At its core, this is a solid 8/10 game held back by technical issues, restrictive design, and uneven writing.

THE GOOD:
Visually, GTA 6 is stunning. Vice City is packed with environmental detail that actively evolves over the course of your playthrough. Inside the main city, the atmosphere and presentation set a high bar for open-world immersion, backed up heavily by the NPCs. Citizens feel far more alive than in past entries, offering a large range of interactions and dynamic behaviors that make the streets feel genuinely reactive instead of just filled with background props. Gameplay also brings smart upgrades borrowed from Red Dead Redemption 2. The revamped Wanted system clearly shows what police can identify about you, adding real planning and depth to your crimes. Unlike past entries, you do not automatically go back to being anonymous the moment you escape the law, meaning your actions keep you on their radar and force you to actually think ahead. Between the 80-hour campaign and Vice City's side activities, there is no shortage of content here.

THE BAD:
Technical & Performance: For a console-exclusive launch, the technical state is rough. The game is locked at 30 FPS across every console, including the PS5 Pro, with no 60 FPS or 40 FPS performance mode like most modern games offer. Even at 30 FPS, base PS5 and Xbox Series X dip during fast driving and drop into the mid-20s in heavy combat and explosions. On PS5, crashes have been a common occurrence during cutscenes, loading screens, and gameplay. Because there is no autosave, a crash wipes your unsaved progress and sends you straight back to your last manual save point, which is a massive oversight for a modern release. Noticeable visual, physics, and scripting bugs only add to the unpolished state the game launched in.

Gameplay & Mechanics: Older GTA games let you carry a full arsenal at all times, so stripping the loadout down to 4 to 5 weapons with strict ammo storage kills variety and severely limits the chaos you can cause. Realism gets in the way elsewhere too, with punishing vehicle damage and overly dense traffic slowing down driving. Add in no mission replay, losing money on death, excessive hand-holding, core mechanics being locked behind progression, and zero unique protagonist abilities for Jason or Lucia, making the loop feel mechanically flat compared to GTA 5.

Sandbox Restrictions: GTA 6 actively pushes back against classic GTA freedom. Outside of Vice City, the wider map of Leonida feels sparse with far less to do. Car theft is progression-locked so you cannot freely steal every vehicle you see, weapons cannot be drawn inside interiors, and certain NPCs cannot be killed. Series staples like prostitutes and side dating are gone, replaced by a one-sided, toxic relationship. Worst of all, the morality system directly penalizes you for causing the kind of mayhem expected from the series, since unlocking the good ending requires avoiding the exact chaos people play GTA for.

Story, Pacing & Characters: The story is a major letdown. Jason feels like a blank character stuck doing domestic upkeep, while Lucia comes across as impulsive, selfish, and hard to root for. Unlike past entries anchored by iconic antagonists like Tenpenny, Dimitri, or Sonny, there is no standout main villain, just rotating local bosses, corrupt cops, and shallow money trouble. Pacing drags with mundane errands, chores, and relationship drama instead of action. The side cast lacks breakout personalities, and classic GTA satire is largely replaced by dry crime drama and pop-culture celebrity cameos. On top of that, without spoiling anything, there is a returning cameo from a past entry that feels completely wasted, mishandling a legacy character by reducing them to a brief, throwaway nostalgia bait that adds nothing to the story.

VERDICT: 8/10

GTA 6 is a gorgeous, ambitious open world with great atmosphere and presentation, which keeps it firmly in good territory. Still, between the crashes, choppy 30 FPS performance, gutted sandbox freedom, and underwhelming story, it is nowhere near a flawless 10/10 masterpiece. An 8/10 is the fair, honest score.

author: RXstarGaming
quote:
A Masterpiece of Character, Creativity, and Ambition — 10/10

Rockstar Games has done it again. And honestly, this is exactly what I expected from a studio that understands storytelling and character development on a level very few developers can match.

I always believed in the direction Rockstar was taking with Jason and Lucia. While people were questioning Jason, calling him boring or trying to label his character before even understanding him, I saw something different: the potential for another Arthur Morgan, but with an entirely different identity and an evolution of Rockstar's character-writing philosophy.

And Lucia? She's an incredible protagonist. Her personality, presence, ambition, and chemistry with Jason make her much more than just another playable character. She's a character you genuinely become invested in.

What makes Rockstar's creativity so special is the contrast between its characters. Plus and minus. Strength and weakness. Two different personalities, two different perspectives, yet neither needs to overshadow the other. They complement each other. One's strengths can balance the other's weaknesses, and that contrast is what makes their dynamic so compelling.

This is what Rockstar understands: a great protagonist doesn't need to be perfect. They need depth, flaws, personality, and a reason for players to care.

GTA VI represents the kind of ambition, attention to detail, world-building, and creative storytelling that makes Rockstar stand apart. It's not simply about making a bigger open world or improving graphics. It's about creating an experience that feels alive, memorable, and worth getting lost in.

I've believed in this project, its characters, and Rockstar's vision from the beginning. Seeing that vision come together is exactly why I had such high expectations.

10/10. Not because it's GTA, but because Rockstar understands what makes a masterpiece.
