author: DoomKeeper
quote:
​Not a 99, Not a 4.9: Honest Thoughts After 10 Hours​
Looking at the 99 critic score alongside a 4.9 user score on Metacritic, it feels like everyone is shouting past each other. Part of that user backlash clearly comes from frustration over pre-launch Game Awards nominations before players could even experience the game. After 10 hours of playing it myself, I don't think GTA 6 is a 99/100 masterpiece nor does it deserve a 4.9 review-bombing score. It is a strong game that easily sits around 92/100, even with a few rough edges and frustrating mechanics.  ​
Driving, Fuel, and Mechanics​:
Car handling has always been a mixed bag in GTA, and here it still takes a delicate touch. Steering feels a bit loose or wobbly if you push too hard into turns, especially at high speeds during races where precision matters most. On the flip side, adding fuel and engine damage is a great direction having to pull into a gas station for fuel or deal with engine damage after heavy impacts adds real weight. What bothers me is instant one-button repairs at a gas station when you have the cash; having to head to a proper garage would feel much more grounded.​
Customization and World Details:
​The customization menu itself is a bit clunky and confusing, though it does offer varied color palettes and shades. The bigger disappointment is hair and facial hair: instead of distinct styles or cuts like a full stubble, goatee, or Stark beard, or varied hairstyles such as braids, dreadlocks, or different cuts you mostly get different lengths of the same base style. Locking places like the tattoo parlor behind the Ultimate Edition also feels exploitative, like milking players just for cosmetic options.​Where the game shows real vision is underwater exploration. Even if the treasure hunting is relatively simple, having Rockstar build out layered underwater activity gives the map more personality. By contrast, weapon and clothing swaps when entering restricted spaces feel abrupt if you can't carry a shotgun indoors, tying that smoothly to stashing gear in your trunk would make way more sense than sudden despawns/respawns.​
Story, Lucia, and Pacing:
​Lucia and Jason's dynamic can sometimes feel like Grand Theft Errands running around to keep things smooth, doing favors, or getting pulled into trouble even when Jason tells her to stay out of it. From Lucia splitting off earlier, having a child, getting caught in a currency exchange heist, calling from jail about a nine-month parole window, and then jumping straight back into high-risk circles and yacht parties once out, her choices often feel like trouble snowballing out of nowhere and she rarely lets Jason handle Brian's jobs alone even with an ankle monitor.  ​
Some routine loops also clash with urgency: opening a bank account for community service pay has realistic operating hours (with time-skipping via X), yet Brian says to come right away or risk rent, only to tell you to come back in the morning if you arrive late after rushing a side activity.​
Verdict:
​GTA 6 isn't flawless, and it doesn't match the 99 hype, but writing it off at 4.9 misses what actually works well here especially the underwater treasure hunts, fuel/damage stakes, and solid core gameplay once you adjust to its quirks.  ​Score: 92/100

author: Kyrimia
quote:
Faut savoir déjà que je ne suis pas fan de GTA, et je risque d’en choquer plus d’un, mais l’idée même du jeu ne m’intéressait pas, c’était un peu le cliché des gangstas moches et inutiles à la société, qui font des conneries dans un monde semi-réaliste où voler des voitures semblent monnaie courante. J’ai joué 30h au V en mode online, la communauté était vraisemblablement à l’image du jeu : des crevards.
Alors pourquoi j’ai acheté le VI? une bonne raison : Lucia. En tant que femme, retrouver un personnage principal féminin me fait toujours plaisir. J’ai adoré Cyberpunk, jamais touché à Kingdom Come parce que je ne pouvais pas jouer une nana, parfois ça me dérange pas comme dans les J-RPGs ou d’autres RPGs où l’immersion est importante (The Witcher étant, à mes yeux, une exception, étant fan des livres).
Ainsi, j’ai retrouvé en Lucia quelque chose qui m’a attirée, alors j’ai sauté le pas. Je ne suis pas déçue. Loin d’être le jeu parfait, le gameplay est beaucoup moins lourd que celui de GTA V. Quand je bougeais, j’avais l’impression de me trimballer toute la misère du monde sur les épaules. Là, le choix des armes est beaucoup plus fluide, la visée ne me donne pas la nausée, et les personnages sont moins « tanky » malgré eux. C’est un point important parce que la lourdeur de GTA V, puis de Red Dead 2, m’avait un peu rebutée à l’époque.
Le principe reste le même, des braquages, vols, de la drogue, des pu… ah non, il n’y en pas, apparemment. Ce qui semble décevoir les joueurs puritains car comment ça GTA n’en a pas? c’est terrible. 
Parlons-en d’ailleurs des choses qui choquent les joueurs, tiens! La relation Jason-Lucia. Pour certains, il s’agit d’une plaie, pour d’autres, à l’instar de San Andreas, est très aboutie. 
Pas question de laisser madame en vu pendant plus de six heures, sinon la relation se détériore, et ça donne de méchantes envies aux hommes forts et indépendants de se taper les burnes histoire de faire passer la pilule. Le jeu ne se contente pas de leur donner un manuel méticuleux sur comment bien traiter sa copine, il leur apprend également à être gentleman, réparer la maison quand c’est important, et surtout, se laver, avec des réactions différentes de leur chère et tendre Lucia. 
Ainsi, plutôt que d’encourager les joueurs à s’encrasser, se complaire dans leur misère, le jeu leur apprend que l’hygiène, et bien c’est important pour choper les dames, Mandy ne dira pas le contraire. Et si certains sont envieux de Jason, il faut dire que le gars, c’est un bon type. Et il est beau.
On va parler de l’écriture des personnages, mais Jason et Lucia sont incroyables. Les deux se complètent dans un Bonnie & Clyde cliché à souhait, à base de bracages, et de soirées mondaines dans des yachts, mais ça fonctionne, car ils sont vivants. Leurs interactions sont adorables. Outre des personnages principaux intéressants, drôles, avec de la répartie (sacrée Lucia, elle qui ne veut pas qu’on mette les pieds sur la table, damn), on retrouve des personnages secondaires tout aussi colorés, comme Cal, ce pote geek dans son fauteuil, ou Mattia et son accent italien agaçant à souhait.
On découvre donc des personnes hauts en couleur, et ils fonctionnent dans leur cliché. Clichés qui sont le moteur de fonctionnement de GTA.
Quid de l’histoire? rien d’exceptionnel, mais le slice of life semble prendre une bonne partie, c’est définitivement plus chill et cosy que les anciens, moins rythmé, et surtout, on a l’impression de jouer aux Sims. Se réveiller le matin, prendre une barre aux céréales, un café, muscu, ****, travail, métro, dodo. Routine qui comblera les plus rigides d’entre nous, même si voir une bouteille apparaître de nulle part aura toujours ce petit effet d’inachèvement amer.
Derniers points, mais le jeu est beau. C’est du 30fps faut pas espérer que la PS5 atteint des bêtes de frame, apparemment ça chute des fois, je fais pas attention. Compte tenu de l’année de sortie de la bestiole, le jeu reste un exploit, et plutôt stable, ce qui est impressionnant. Le réalisme est poussé à son paroxysme, encore une fois, avec des PNJs vivants, qui arrivent même à se souvenir de vous, à tel point qu’il faut carrément vous changer pour être oublié.
Les voitures, quel plaisir. Finir dans un ravin parce que je ne sais pas conduire, femme oblige, est un rituel de passage obligatoire dans ce genre de jeux.
Les musiques des radios sont sympas, agréablement surprise de trouver Katseye parmi la sélection, aux côtés de Tame Impala, Travis Scott, Billie Eillish, The Weeknd… bref, des mastodontes de la musique.
Les bugs, je n’en ai pas eu de très importants, des PNJs qui se TP, du clipping, rien d’alarmant
Ainsi, ce jeu, non content de se moquer de ses joueurs et de leur comportement, est à mes yeux un véritable step up par rapport aux anciens. Tout est plus beau, plus grand, plus attachant.
Et bizarrement, pour une fois, je comprends la hype.
Alors merci Rockstar de faire des jeux excellents, et continuez comme ça.

author: cgandrade
quote: Grand Theft Auto VI: Un mundo extraordinario que no siempre consigue estar a la altura de su propia historia. Trece años de espera son demasiados para cualquier videojuego. GTA VI tenía que hacer algo más que verse espectacular: tenía que justificar toda una generación de expectativas. Y Rockstar consigue algo extraordinario, aunque no necesariamente **** primero que sorprende es su mundo abierto. Leonida y Vice City transmiten una sensación de vida difícil de encontrar en otros videojuegos. No se trata solamente de recorrer un mapa enorme con mejores gráficos. Se trata de observar lo que sucede a nuestro alrededor, descubrir situaciones inesperadas y comprobar que el entorno tiene una personalidad propia. Los NPC, las actividades, los animales, el tráfico y la cantidad de detalles convierten la exploración en uno de los mayores atractivos del juego.Pero el verdadero corazón de esta entrega está en Jason y Lucía.Rockstar apuesta por una historia de crimen, ambición, supervivencia y, sobre todo, una relación sentimental. La dinámica entre ambos protagonistas es una de las decisiones más interesantes de esta entrega. No son simplemente dos personajes intercambiables que participan en misiones; existe una relación que evoluciona, con complicidad, discusiones, momentos cotidianos y una dependencia emocional que aporta profundidad a la **** embargo, la historia también tiene sus problemas. El comienzo puede resultar excesivamente lento y la progresión **** en alcanzar el nivel de intensidad que uno espera de Grand Theft Auto. Hay momentos en los que el desarrollo narrativo parece detenerse demasiado tiempo en situaciones que no necesariamente aportan algo significativo a la trama principal.Jason y Lucía funcionan como pareja protagonista, aunque no todos los personajes tienen la misma fuerza. Especialmente Jason puede sentirse menos carismático de lo esperado. También se echa de menos una mayor cantidad de diálogos memorables y personajes secundarios con esa personalidad exagerada, impredecible y hasta absurda que caracterizó a entregas anteriores.Y aquí aparece una de las principales contradicciones de GTA VI: su madurez narrativa puede ser una virtud, pero también puede restarle parte de la irreverencia que convirtió a esta franquicia en algo **** humor, la sátira social y la provocación siguen presentes, pero algunos jugadores echarán de menos aquella capacidad de Rockstar para hacerte reír en medio del caos más absurdo. No todo tiene que ser realista, profundo o emocional para ser divertido. A veces simplemente queremos que Grand Theft Auto sea Grand Theft **** cuanto a la jugabilidad, encontramos una evolución importante en la inmersión, las interacciones, la conducción y el comportamiento del mundo. No obstante, algunos controles se sienten menos intuitivos de lo deseable, los tiroteos todavía tienen aspectos mejorables y determinadas mecánicas parecen priorizar el realismo por encima de la diversión **** rendimiento también merece una crítica. Los 30 FPS representan un compromiso considerable para un título de esta magnitud. Los gráficos pueden ser impresionantes, pero la espectacularidad visual no debería utilizarse como excusa para dejar de exigir **** que resulta innegable es que Rockstar ha construido un universo en el que perderse durante horas es una experiencia en sí misma. Puedes pasar una **** entera sin avanzar en la historia y aun así encontrar motivos para seguir jugando. Ese es un mérito enorme.¿Es el mejor Grand Theft Auto? Tiene argumentos para serlo, especialmente por su mundo, su ambientación y la profundidad de sus protagonistas. ¿Es una experiencia perfecta? Definitivamente **** VI demuestra que Rockstar sigue estando en una posición privilegiada para transformar la industria, pero también demuestra que una producción gigantesca no garantiza que todas sus decisiones narrativas y jugables sean acertadas.Después de trece años, esperaba una revolución en todos los aspectos. Encontré una revolución en la construcción del mundo, una evolución interesante en la narrativa y algunos pasos atrás en aspectos de jugabilidad que deberían sentirse más **** VI es un videojuego extraordinario, pero no intocable. Merece reconocimiento por sus enormes virtudes y también merece críticas por sus oportunidades desaprovechadas. La nostalgia, la expectativa y el nombre de Rockstar no deben sustituir nuestro criterio como jugadores. Calificación final: 8.5/10.

author: digitalral
quote:
It feels like many people are rating this off strong feelings and expectations rather than how the actual gameplay plays out. Give it a fair look for what's happening on screen—there's plenty to like and plenty to debate once you're actually playing.   GTA VI offers grounded, detailed gameplay with weightier movement, more tactical takedowns and escapes, and a super reactive world—though slower pacing stretches and uneven frame rates on PS5 hold it back from feeling completely effortless.   Playing Grand Theft Auto VI on PlayStation 5 is a study in high-ambition contrasts. Where the game shines brightest is its open world and granular detail: crowded streets, lived-in neighborhoods, reactive NPC behavior, and localized vehicle wear make the setting feel genuinely alive rather than like a static playground. Grounded movement, more deliberate gunplay, and tactical takedowns or escapes also give moment-to-moment action more weight. At the same time, those ambitions bring clear trade-offs. Certain stretches slow down for quieter routines and lower-stakes beats, which adds texture if you enjoy a slower burn but can test your patience if you want nonstop momentum. On PS5, the dense visuals and lighting also come with occasional frame-rate dips during heavy action and minor physics or collision hiccups. Overall, it's an impressive, richly detailed open-world experience—best judged by how it plays in practice rather than the loudest hype or backlash. 

Highs: Dense, reactive open world; rich environmental storytelling; weightier movement, takedowns, and escape systems.

Trade-offs: Slower-paced stretches between peak action; PS5 frame-rate fluctuations under heavy load and occasional physics quirks.

Overall: Rich open-world detail and weightier gameplay/escape mechanics carry a lot of appeal, even with slower pacing stretches, PS5 frame-rate dips, and occasional physics quirks getting in the way.

author: hunn3r
quote:
It's genuenly a good videogame. 
Lets's start with the elephant in the room: It doesn't deserve the glazing it got from the games media. 
It's runs like ass. (TAA upscaling on base PS5 makes everything a blurry mess too!)
It has multiple bugs (some hilarious some annoying, some even progression breaking). 
It has a mid story with predictable story beats. The protagonist couple dynamic takes away from the formula instead adding to it. 
The new wanted system first seems fun and a good addition, but really just adds a layer of tedium to the game, for no good reason with the constant menu fumbling and toggling on or off your clothes and etc.
The carjacking dynamic is a necessary evil of making the game more realistic, a point which comes across multiple ways in this videogame.

They made this game realistic, and sacrificed the fun for the sake of it. On RDR2 it worked, because nobody -or very little- are actually a cowboy, so living the cowboy life is new and exciting, but running errands and doing gym sessions eating food and grinding for life is what we are more or less doing with our life on a daily basis. It doesn't make this game exciting. It simply falls short where Red Dead excelled.

I could mention many more gripes i had while playing this videogame, the missing features, the changed systems, the lack of inventions to the formula but i think i already said my piece, to make this a valid review.

The GTA+ subscription on itself takes a point off from the final score, it would be a 9/10 so it goes down to an 8.

author: espiritoheroico
quote:
GTA 6 é sólido. É a prova de que a Rockstar sobe degrau por degrau a cada jogo e sempre demonstra uma força e influência absurdas no mundo dos games. Tecnicamente, o jogo é uma evolução de tudo o que já vimos, com melhorias obrigatórias da nova geração, como RTGI, HairWorks, mudanças climáticas, IAs responsivas e acabamento técnico na forma como a polícia e os inimigos trabalham.
Em relação à estética e à UI desse novo game, ela é 99% perfeita, com o único erro de ter a pior HUD de armas da franquia. A escolha das cores, o branding e a identidade visual são simplesmente o ápice da série. Uma verdadeira obra de arte, que vai servir para inspirar muitas outras obras.
Sobre a narrativa, é sempre a parte mais difícil de avaliar. GTA nunca teve uma história digna do seu próprio universo. Sendo talvez a história de Nico a melhor da franquia. Como é possível Red Dead ter uma história tão artística, filosófica e provocante em comparação ao GTA? Eu não consigo responder essa.
O prólogo é razoável. GTA V teve um dos melhores prólogos da história dos videogames. A cena do falso enterro do Michael, e logo depois os personagens se conectando, aquilo é uma obra-prima. No novo game, Lucia, por birra, quer ir roubar, e isso desencadeia nove meses de cadeia para nossa protagonista.
Jason é um personagem muito fraco na narrativa. Percebemos que ele não é mau, mas isso também não desencadeia eventos importantes na trama. Ele perde rapidamente o foco quando outros personagens entram em cena e falam mais que ele. 
As missões são sólidas, criativas e com repetições razoáveis de método. Mas com muita bala e muita porrada. As sidequests e os easter eggs são o auge de GTA 6. Gosto de mencionar como a Rockstar sabe fazer bons segredos.
Em relação à cidade... poderia ser melhor, honestamente. A cidade não é um "personagem" aqui, como é em outros jogos. Compare o seguinte: todo universo contém coisas únicas. Gosto de como GTA San Andreas é o exemplo perfeito para descrever como uma cidade se torna um dos pilares do game. Gangues dominando locais, grafites e pichações, as pessoas se vestindo de forma diferente em cada parte do mapa, o vocabulário mudando, a estica única dos bairros, lugares mais limpos ou mais sujos... Podemos citar o caso de Night City, em Cyberpunk2077, e o quanto a cidade por si só fala uma língua diferente. Eventos importantes na cidade provocam mudanças significativas e temporárias. E o fato de as pessoas amarem e odiarem a cidade transforma ela em paraíso ou pesadelo, e isso também implica em decisões ao longo do jogo.
Eu esperava ver uma Leonida com mais coisas acontecendo e com nossos protagonistas provocando mudanças. As rádios e as músicas são simplesmente perfeitas. Não tem música ruim, podem ter certeza.
GTA 6 bebeu da fonte de muitas inspirações e concorrentes. Temos um sistema de luta mais encorpado, similar aos games da Sony. Temos uma dirigibilidade e carros que nos lembram muito Forza e NFS. Temos um gráfico impecável, temos interações novas com o celular e customizações variadas. Notamos que agora o stealth é importante e foi adicionado, finalmente. E temos um fim de ciclo. Podemos dizer que a Rockstar fez bem o dever de casa.
Não vou avaliar a questão dos 30 FPS, porque isso é decepcionante demais. Vou focar naquilo que eu mais amo nos jogos: a quantidade de amor envolvida para criar algo único. E isso ficou evidente neste projeto.

Parabéns, Rockstar.

author: WingmanVI
quote:
Top-tier game, easily the best entry in the series! 10/10.

Yes, it’s not like the previous games in the franchise—it’s so much more. It plays completely differently, like a mix of GTA V and RDR2, which is the best possible combination.

The game is also built for all types of players. You can heavily casualize it and make it easy through the settings, but only by turning off all the assists do you get the real thrill out of it—everything feels intuitive, and you immediately understand what to do and how.

The driving is a blast, and the destruction is amazing too.

There’s a great variety of missions: some are so action-packed they take your breath away from start to finish, while others focus on everyday routine, which is portrayed really well.

There’s only one downside: FPS drops on a 6-year-old console that’s honestly showing its age today (PS5 Fat), yet even so, it plays great. Trust me, once you get used to 30 FPS, going back to 60 feels like watching on 2x speed—like you stopped watching a movie and clicked on some random YouTube clip.

All my friends who own a PS5 or Xbox Series, plus my brother and a coworker, are playing it and can't put it down—just like me.

P.S. if PC players couldn't post reviews based on viral FAKE videos, the user score would be around 8–9. Since anyone can leave a review, half of the negative ones are just pure jealousy over the game not being on PC.

author: Ayeezeeeee
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI – 10/10

GTA 6 is everything I hoped it would be and more. What makes this game special isn’t just the incredible visuals or technical achievement. It’s how all the different pieces come together to create an experience that feels genuinely **** story and characters are a huge part of that. Lucia and Jason bring a different dynamic to the series, and having a story built around their relationship gives the narrative a personal element that makes you invested in what happens to them. The writing, character interactions, dialogue, and presentation make the experience feel like you’re participating in a living story rather than simply completing a checklist of missions.Then there’s the world itself. The level of detail Rockstar has put into Leonida is ridiculous. From NPC interactions to environmental details, random encounters, activities, and all the little things happening around you, there’s always something that makes the world feel alive. You can spend hours doing absolutely nothing related to the main story and still feel like you’re getting something out of the **** gameplay deserves just as much credit. The freedom, exploration, activities, and attention given to smaller mechanics make simply playing the game enjoyable. I especially appreciate that there’s so much to discover when you slow down and actually take everything in. Not every gaming experience needs to be ****, is it perfect? **** 30 FPS cap is disappointing, especially considering the hardware we’re playing on. There are also moments where I wish certain gameplay mechanics offered more freedom, and some aspects could definitely use additional refinement. These are legitimate criticisms, and pretending otherwise wouldn’t be **** here’s the thing: none of those shortcomings take away from what Rockstar has accomplished overall. I can acknowledge things I would change while still recognizing the extraordinary quality of the **** me, a 10/10 doesn’t mean a game is mathematically flawless. It means the experience as a whole is exceptional, memorable, and something that sets a standard for the **** 6 delivers on that for me. The storytelling, characters, immersion, world-building, presentation, and sheer ambition all come together in a way that very few developers can replicate.I don’t need every aspect to be perfect to recognize something special when I experience it.10/10.

- Side quests (like Skunk Ape) are its strongest narrative.
- The more grounded realistic interactions and details are great.
- Animations are as good as expected for GTA
- Acting quality is good (with some exceptions) meaning the actors deliver their lines well.

Cons:
- The Bonnie and Clyde main story falls short of expectations. It's slow in a bad way (not in the good 'Better Call Saul' way), has poor pacing, and feels distinctly not-GTA.
- Mission design often limits freedom and requires you to do things in a very particular way.
- Both protagonists are weak, and in some cases unlikeable, which leads me to not care.
- Sandbox gameplay sometimes lacks options despite a lot of simulation depth 
- No graphic preset options, no customization of the graphic experience to tradeoff quality for performance. Performance on base ps5 is on the edge of acceptable and sometimes fall below it.

Overall it tries to be red dead 2 in many ways and succeeds, but falls short on red deads core of a compelling story and protagonists.

author: Noir_Ri
quote:
My actual rating: 8.7/10

Grand Theft Auto VI is an extraordinarily ambitious achievement and one of the most visually impressive open-world games ever created. However, its remarkable presentation should not exempt it from rigorous criticism. Rockstar has delivered an exceptional world filled with environmental detail, impressive animations, atmospheric effects, and a convincing sense of activity. Nevertheless, visual excellence does not automatically translate into excellence across every aspect of game design. Jason and Lucia provide a compelling narrative foundation, and their relationship adds an interesting emotional dimension to the story. Unfortunately, the campaign suffers from inconsistent pacing, repetitive assignments, and supporting characters who occasionally lack meaningful development. The open world is undoubtedly one of its greatest strengths, but there is a significant difference between visual density and genuine systemic depth. A populated city is not necessarily a sophisticated simulation. Red Dead Redemption 2 remains a remarkable benchmark for environmental storytelling, character interactions, and world consistency, and GTA VI does not automatically surpass it in these areas. Gameplay is an improvement over previous installments, particularly in movement, contextual interactions, and driving, but the combat system is considerably less impressive. Enemy AI can feel conventional, encounters rely heavily on familiar cover-based shooting, and tactical depth often fails to match the sophistication of the surrounding environment. For a production of this magnitude, more intelligent enemies and greater combat variety should have been fundamental priorities. Technically, the game is spectacular, featuring outstanding lighting, reflections, weather effects, water rendering, and facial animations. However, this is also where my greatest disappointment lies. After thirteen years between numbered installments, I expected an exceptionally polished experience. Instead, the bugs I encountered repeatedly damaged my immersion and, at times, genuinely ruined the gameplay experience. These were not simply insignificant visual imperfections. Issues involving broken animations, inconsistent collisions, objects and characters clipping through the environment, disappearing textures, erratic physics, audio problems, and progression-blocking situations are particularly frustrating. Reports of crashes, freezes, and potential lost progress make matters worse. No open-world game is entirely free of bugs, but development complexity is not a permanent excuse for inadequate quality control. Technical reliability is part of the product, not an optional bonus. The 30 FPS performance target on consoles is another considerable compromise, especially in a game built around high-speed driving, rapid camera movement, and action sequences. A stable 30 FPS can be understandable, but it should not be celebrated as an achievement. Sound design, environmental audio, and radio programming are excellent, contributing significantly to the atmosphere. Comparisons with GTA V reveal substantial improvements in presentation and world-building, but GTA VI must also be judged by its actual gameplay evolution, mission quality, and mechanical depth. Cyberpunk 2077 offers an interesting reference for urban immersion, while The Last of Us Part II demonstrates exceptional audiovisual refinement and encounter presentation. These games have different design philosophies, but they prove that technical ambition alone does not guarantee superiority. Ultimately, GTA VI is an impressive achievement, but it is far from flawless. Its extraordinary world, presentation, and production values deserve recognition, yet inconsistent pacing, conventional combat, limited enemy intelligence, performance compromises, and frustrating technical issues prevent it from reaching genuine perfection. Personally, the bugs were particularly disappointing because they repeatedly interrupted an experience I had waited thirteen years to enjoy. Rockstar deserves credit for its ambition, but it should be held to the same demanding standards as every other developer. A masterpiece must deliver more than extraordinary graphics; it requires consistent gameplay, meaningful innovation, narrative quality, mechanical depth, and technical reliability. GTA VI succeeds brilliantly in several areas, but it does not achieve that standard consistently

author: Pseudolike
quote:
Fact check:
Can you have a train run over people? Yes, and it's gory as ****, they lose limbs and their head.

Can you fly a plane into buildings and it blows up? Yes, people were intentionally falsifying footage by disabling vehicle damage to push an an agenda that it wasn't allowed.

Are you forced to buy groceries and renovate your house? No. Optional.

A technological masterpiece. It's very sad the misinformation campaign that's happening with this game. 

Equally, a 10 does not mean perfect. Somehow people believe this has launched like Cyberpunk 2077, which isn't true and there's tons of people who haven't played this falling for this campaign. Cyberpunk 2077 is also the worst game ever created from a modern company, and it's wild people can say that's a good game. It's extremely limited, just compare it to this. You'll unfortunately find it difficult to find valid criticism of the game anywhere due to this. It was not developed for 13 years. And even if it were, you will never find any video game without bugs. It is not possible. On top of this, the budget is not conclusive evidence it being spent on tech. Employees need to be paid (probably poorly), marketing, music rights and licenses as well as original music created, and then costs of development. 

This has pushed the boundaries of what an open world game is with detail, story, design, and gameplay mechanics. Every other open world game from now on will be complete **** in comparison. 

That said, there's some aspects it falls short in. For example, you can slink between cars that are parked too close which is incredible detail. However, parking two cars blocking another teleports you out. Sleeping Dogs solved this issue years ago. There's a few characters that I personally find absolutely horrible, but this is a GTA problem. There's many many characters over the course of years written poorly. Mainly the drug addict characters. Perhaps I don't find them relatable, sure. It's valid. Some people don't like Jason's voice, fair criticism. I think it fits. 

There is a store with very limited cosmetics, mainly discounts that are locked behind GTA+. It's stupid, and not worth it. But this is Take-Two. Look at NBA 2K, look at WWE2K. That's what needs to change significantly before this gets more egregious.

I urge you to stop being so miserable, chronically online and easily influenced, and play it and make up your own decision. The culture war is actually abysmal and needs to end. People are incredibly incredibly stupid nowadays.

author: oildboy29
quote: A True Evolution That Captures the Soul of South Florida. After more than a decade of anticipation, Grand Theft Auto VI doesn't just meet the astronomical hype—it surpasses it. This is a true evolution for the franchise and open-world gaming as a whole, raising the bar in every meaningful way, from world density and environmental storytelling to mission design and interactivity. As a South Florida native of over 20 years, what blows me away most is how authentically Rockstar captured the spirit of the region. Leonida and Vice City aren't just a neon-soaked parody; they nailed the unmistakable atmosphere, architecture, cultural energy, lighting, and chaotic charm that make South Florida feel like nowhere else. Driving down the causeways and exploring the neighborhoods feels remarkably true to **** only real critique on the PS5 is the lack of granular control over the graphics options. While the game is a massive technical showcase—especially given the hardware's 30fps target—having more freedom to tweak visual settings or trade fidelity for performance headroom would have been a welcome addition for console players.Even with that minor wish, GTA VI is a generational achievement. It sets a new standard for the industry and proves why Rockstar remains in a league of its own!

author: pepet4444
quote:
It’s a good game, sure—but they’ve completely gutted the soul of what GTA is supposed to be.

At its core, Grand Theft Auto has always been about being edgy, pushing boundaries, dark humor, crime, debauchery, and taking everything to the extreme. It was meant to be a caricature and a sharp critique of society as a whole. Whatever this is, it’s something else—it’s not GTA.

I honestly expected them to lean into crazier, more unhinged territory—things like snorting cocaine off a stripper’s ****, partying with dwarfs like Lamine Yamal, or adding full-on kidnapping and torture mechanics—staying true to the raw, unfiltered DNA of Grand Theft Auto. Instead, they pivoted toward a sanitized, overly wholesome young romance that feels completely out of place.

To me, that dynamic comes across as way too idealized and detached from how human beings actually think and act in the real world. By trading its signature cynicism and excess for a sweet, romanticized narrative, the game fundamentally alters its own soul and tone—even if I’ll gladly admit it still delivers plenty of genuinely hilarious and unforgettable moments along the way.

The mere fact that they’ve restricted killing inside a gay club or harming protesters is philosophically disgusting. What’s the logic here? Stealing, running over regular people, or killing cats is totally fine, but certain groups are off-limits? It’s pure ideological posturing designed purely to generate headlines and make people talk. GTA used to be above that kind of selective moralizing.

The characters feel like they belong in a completely different game, and the same goes for the story. You can tackle a thousand social issues and whatever real-world mess you want, but that’s what abstraction, metaphor, and actual artistic craft are for—not heavy-handed censorship and double standards.

author: Rickslin
quote:
Nota: 10/10

GTA VI é simplesmente um absurdo de jogo. A Rockstar conseguiu elevar praticamente todos os aspectos que fazem a franquia ser tão especial, e Leonida é, sem sombra de dúvidas, um dos mundos mais impressionantes que já vi em um jogo. A quantidade de detalhes, a ambientação, a vida acontecendo ao redor do jogador e a sensação de estar dentro de um mundo que não gira exclusivamente em torno de você são coisas que tornam a experiência simplesmente fantástica.

O que mais me impressiona é a gameplay. Não se trata apenas de andar por um mapa bonito, mas de fazer com que cada interação, cada perseguição, cada confronto e cada momento de exploração tenha personalidade. O mundo é extremamente vivo, e a maneira como a Rockstar trabalha a imersão faz com que você perca facilmente a noção do tempo enquanto joga. É aquele tipo de jogo em que você sai para fazer uma missão e, meia hora depois, percebe que passou esse tempo fazendo absolutamente tudo, menos aquilo que deveria.

Leonida também é um espetáculo à parte. A variedade de ambientes, a identidade de cada região, a atmosfera de Vice City e a quantidade de situações que podem acontecer durante a exploração fazem com que o mapa não seja apenas gigantesco, mas interessante de percorrer. E isso, para mim, é muito mais importante do que simplesmente entregar quilômetros de terreno vazio.

Jason e Lucia também dão uma identidade muito forte à experiência, principalmente pela dinâmica entre os dois. A proposta de acompanhar personagens com suas próprias personalidades, conflitos e relações torna tudo mais interessante, e é justamente esse tipo de construção que diferencia GTA de tantos outros jogos de mundo aberto.

Se existe algo que ainda poderia melhorar, são alguns problemas pontuais de desempenho e bugs, além de certas situações em que a experiência poderia ser um pouco mais refinada. Nada disso, porém, foi suficiente para comprometer o que considero uma das experiências mais impressionantes que já tive com um videogame.

GTA VI não é apenas mais um lançamento da Rockstar. É a demonstração de até onde um estúdio pode levar um mundo aberto quando existe atenção aos detalhes, ambição e uma preocupação genuína em fazer o jogador se sentir parte daquele universo.

Leonida é extraordinária, a gameplay é viciante, a imersão é absurda e, sinceramente, não consigo pensar em outro GTA que tenha me proporcionado uma experiência tão completa. Para mim, GTA VI não é apenas o melhor GTA já feito, mas um dos melhores jogos de todos os tempos.

author: Supernaught
quote:
Most of the negative reviews seem to be regarding the slow pace of the first couple hours. But once you get Lucia playable, the game unveils the truly remarkable, granular attention to detail Rockstar spent 13 years focusing on to bring us the most immersive open-world sandbox crime drama ever created in video game format.

Adding elements from RDR2 and improving on them adds a whole new dynamic to a game system that was getting stale in GTA V. The honor system is expertly implemented to make things difficult for you when engaging law enforcement, punishing you accordingly for getting apprehended, yet making you more empowered to unleash hell on the populace if you choose brutality over stealthy or measured resistance. 
Melee fighting is best in class for GTA games, and the multitude of mischief I've discovered in only a few hours of playing promises truly diabolical hijinx to come. 

The main characters and their backstory add a touching motivation for this Bonnie and Clyde crime drama, leaving you to decide outcomes.

The technology behind the variety of mechanics, the ridiculous number of NPC's, side missions, fully explorable indoor areas (a first for the series) and revamped stealth gameplay to offer even more choice in how you tackle missions is nothing short awe inspiring.

The visuals are beyond what I would have expected in a game world of this magnitude, in spite of the 30fps limitation. It has to be seen to be believed.

Despite ditching the hooker-health minigame, and limiting violence options in SOME indoor areas, this game reigns supreme in too many categories to write about here.

If your biggest concern is the 30fps frame target (practically locked on PS5 Pro), don't bomb tbe game for it. Wait until hardware becomes available to realize a 60-120fps GTA VI.

author: MrFair

I Understand both the hate and praise this game gets, on one hand GTA VI is an in depth, high quality, graphically astonishing masterpiece, on the other hand, its long story, release bugs and glitches as well as new, restrictive features and more complex actions that are not present in games prior, may put a bad taste in gamers mouths. In my opinion GTA VI doesn't deserve the hate that it gets, but it must also be said that we shouldn't overlook some aspects of the game that we dislike just because of the hype and long wait for this game. 

As for GTA VI receiving GOTY, even though I'm a Zelda fan at heart, I fully believe GTA VI deserves that title, I feel this way simply due to how I view the Game Awards. GOTY only has one requirement, be the most popular and  most liked, and GTA VI achieves this by a long-shot, unlike many of the other GOTY contenders. But in terms of a 99/100 on metacritic? I heavily disagree with this scoring. 

GTA VI 100% deserves to be in the late 90% region but, for the game to essentially be perfect, issues such as feeling slow, or having bugs on release and being too constrictive, should be virtually non-existent especially for such a long wait time. I believe GTA VI deserves a 97/100 at least for the console release.

author: Illogikal
quote: People are review bombing because their individual expectations were built far too high (which may be rockstars fault for holding out far too long), everyone was expecting the game to be within their own vision, which is impossible. Does the game start slow? Yes. Does it build character development? Yes. Is this your average gta introduction experience? Not exactly. Some are angry about the boyfriend girlfriend dynamic, yet if it were another group of guys just robbing banks, I’m sure the complaint of “this games just a copy and paste of the last one” would make an appearance as it does with every call of duty. The game really starts to become what it’s meant to be after chapter 1, however the content within chapter 1 remains relevant. I think many refused to even get through this area of the game, simply because they didn’t find exactly what they wanted when they wanted it. To each their **** game is high quality, gun mechanics along with driving I find to be smooth and satisfying. The cinematics are next level and the many random encounter can be quite entertaining. The characters are very easy to get attached to and written well. People saying that it’s a boyfriend simulator, sure the way you interact with Lucia can change outcomes, but the interactions are almost all optional. To say the game is too woke is a bit of an overstatement, I’d compare it to a South Park episode where both sides take some heat (I’ve heard some questionable things on the in game radio plus the hilariously negative interactions with furries). In my almost 20 hours of game time I’ve run into a single tracing error during a cutscene, I’m sure others have run into more glitches but this is my personal experience. I was really going into this game ready to hate on it when I heard of the 30 fps, however once I started getting into it i realized it’s not that big of a deal. The consoles cpus themselves are the issues, rockstar simply did what they could with modern consoles. Would everyone have preferred they waited to play until next gen consoles released? I think that once the game releases on pc (I agree they should have just released pc with console) people will be much more pleased without the fps lock. And once again the slow start may bother many people but any other way people would have claimed “copy and paste” as some already are. I like the Bonnie and Clyde dynamic, I think it fits well. The house takes all of ten minutes to fix up, it’s a ridiculous complaint (however I understand that’s far from the only thing you have the option to do for Lucia). Anyone that’s giving this game a rating of 0 is simply hopping on the hate bandwagon and has trouble thinking for themselves (99% of the negative comments don’t even have more than a paragraph, quite literally zero thought or effort). Although I gave the game a 10, I would personally give it closer to a 8.5, however the score needs to be averaged. I was ready to hate on the game coming into it and here I am leaving a honest and positive review. People need to relax imo lmao

author: imol
quote:
Es un juegazo en toda regla, se nota la ambición de rockstar por llevar su mundo al siguiente nivel en todo aspecto de inmersión. Aunque cabe aclarar que para el presupuesto gastado en el juego, no esperaba menos y lograrón cumplir con lo esperado en cuanto a su mundo. Tambien en el aspecto de personajes e historia esta bien trabajado. 

Es un juego que toma más del estilo narrativo de la saga read dead redemption, dejando de lado ese sandbox más arcade que suele caraterizar a la mayoria de juegos de la saga GTA. Lo cual no es un punto bueno ni malo, simplemente es diferente, en mi caso que me encanta RDR2, me gusta que este juego tenga un estilo similar, pero desde un rol de la vida criminal. Sin embargo, entendería totalmente si alguien que viene de gta 5 sin jugar RDR2, le parezca un juego con un ritmo lento y capaz no le puede llegar a gustar. 

Como puntos negativos destaco:

- el tema de la jugabilidad, rockstar a nivel jugable nunca ha sido de dar la mejor sensación a los mandos. En este juego se siente un poco más agil que en entregas anteriores, pero sigue siendo muy rockstar en este aspecto. 

-tampoco me agrada del todo que el formato de misiones sigua siendo el tipico de rockstar con mejoras leves, lo cual era algo que esperaba mejorias. 

- se que las consolas no dan para más, pero 30 fps con bajadas a 20 en pleno 2026 es complicado de asumir en muchos casos. Espero con ansias la versión de pc para poder jugarlo a la calidad que el titulo se merece. 

Por lo demas no tengo quejas más que uno que otro bug, pero no afecta a la experiencia jugable y dan hasta gracia. 

Lo que si me parece fatal son los analisis de los medios "especializados" los cuales son muy poco honestos con sus notas, he leido uno que otro caso donde en el analisis dicen varios puntos negativos por los cuales le bajarían nota a cualquier otro juego, pero en este caso dicen los puntos malos e igual les dan un 100.  Al igual que los usuarios que son haters forzados, que seguro buscaran bajarle la nota de usurio poniendole un 1 o 0, esa gente esta aún peor que la prensa. 

Dicho esto, es un muy buen juego se nota la ambición detras del juego y si les gusta la saga y se lo pueden permitir adelante muy recomendado. Mi nota es un 8/10.

author: MaleOreo
quote:
Game is being review bombed since you don't need proof of ownership, PS Store has ratings at 4.8/5 from 166,000+ People. The game is next generation and lives up to the hype. By every means this is Grand Theft Auto and after chapter one it goes balls to the wall. I will say Chapter 1 is slow burn but it's important as it sets up the world and gets you interested in the characters and their backgrounds. 

The progression of 'Grand Theft Auto' and the Wanted System is really good, it adds depth to systems that previously felt barebones, now you need to play smart and prepare. Ranging from the WAiNK IT phone app to scan cars worth and security details you really feel the sense of progression as you unlock more tools and align trust with the car mod shops to cash in on car jacks. Same for the wanted system, its not longer easy to game and boring, every police encounter feels unique and requires coming up with a new solution. You now have wanted areas that you have to clear by any means(Car wrap, outfit, styling) and it just works really damn well. 

The story is pretty good but as said slow burn from the go and builds into the all out action you are familiar with. The Jason & Lucia dynamic is different than previous entries and I think this is where a lot of people have voiced their opinions online. I personally enjoy it, it's also very optional and minimal effort despite what some people say online. If you ignore Lucia/Jason side missions completely it becomes a very lowkey relationship where you can just do crime if you like. It's also extremely easy to fix your relationship should you choose, and much harder to break.

I would give it a 10 but I think console hardware griefs its potential, 30 fps dips to 15 in action scenes on a base console. PC release will let this game shine to it's true potential, but even with that said I'm still having a blast. Ignore the ragebait social media clips, they are farming you for a cheap buck.

author: jbrock11
quote:
First, I want to say I was somewhat skeptical going into GTA 6. With a lot of the founders of Rockstar leaving and the company just feeling more corporate in general, I thought we may get a watered down GTA despite the 1 billion+ spent to make it. I'm happy to say, I couldn't have been more wrong. Not only is this game not watered down, I'd argue it's the best GTA ever by a WIDE margin.

Just for some background, the only GTA's that I thought were GREAT were GTA 3 and GTA: Vice City. All the others, before and after were good but I felt were lacking in some way or another and never really stayed with me after I played them. I think this was a combination of the story, characters and direction not being that great despite a very fun gameplay formula that has been consistent since the beginning. GTA 6 on the other hand, absolutely shines in those departments.

It's very rare you get a game with a great story, characters, acting, directing AND it also has mass appeal. A good example is Death Stranding. It's an all time great game AND one of the most unique experiences ever made but really doesn't appeal to everyone. GTA 6 on the other hand is that level of quality but a game I think everyone can enjoy. It's so good, I fully expect a movie or TV series to be made because of how good it is. 

Overall, I think it definitely deserves to be thought of in the same light as OoT as being one of the best rated games of all time because it is imo. Congrats Rockstar on making a modern masterpiece. 10/10

The direction Rockstar has taken with realism is one of the best decisions they could have made. It brings something incredibly fresh to the series, making the entire experience feel more immersive, believable, and alive than ever before. 

It’s a significant change from previous GTA games, and honestly, it’s a breath of fresh air. The relationship between Jason and Lucia is another huge highlight. 

Their story isn’t just something happening in the background. It’s an essential part of the experience, and the dynamic between these two characters makes everything so much more interesting, emotional, and engaging. 

A massive congratulations to Rockstar Games and everyone who worked on this incredible project. You’ve created something truly exceptional, and it absolutely deserves recognition.

And to all the people spreading unnecessary hate or trying to review bomb this game: you can honestly get lost. You’re not going to change the fact that GTA VI is an extraordinary achievement. Trying to drag down its score won’t erase its quality, its ambition, or the incredible work behind it.

GTA VI isn’t just another Grand Theft Auto. It’s the evolution of the franchise, and for me, it’s the greatest GTA of all time.Thank you, Rockstar. You absolutely nailed it. 10/10.

author: NutellaGuyAU
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI is a near masterpiece,

Every aspect of GTA6 when compared to GTA5 and RDR2 has been added upon and improved, from gun play, sound design, the way vehicles handle and interact with the world. 

There are a lot of people hating on the game currently because it's the popular thing to do, they're looking for engagement or maybe they've never really played a GTA game before or too young. The only real issue for me hence the 9/10 is the performance, visually the game is beautiful, R* has pushed these obsolete consoles to their limits once again and for this the 30 to sub 30fps frame rates often experienced can be less than ideal. Anyone with half a brain knows the PC version will be the definitive version, and the next Gen consoles will get a performance boost when they launch and the game is inevitable re-released. 

Overall 9/10 the absolute most fun iv had with a video game in over a decade, the attention to detail within this game is next level and won't be seen again until the next R* release.

author: Olexander
quote:
Quick first review of GTA 6 after completing Chapter 1 and spending 15 hours in the game.

I only give a 10/10 to games where every aspect is exceptional.

So far, I have given only three games a 10/10. GTA 5 wasn't one of them. I gave it an 8 or 9, I can't remember exactly. However, RDR2 definitely earned a 10/10 from me.

For now, GTA 6 has already earned a solid 8/10.

I am pretty sure that the PC version, which I will review later, has the potential to earn a 9/10.

That being said, I don't like some of the changes Rockstar has made this time. And no, it has nothing to do with having a girlfriend in the game being "woke".

The game simply feels less fun to play because of some of the new mechanics, particularly the police and morality systems. It feels like the game punishes you for playing it like GTA.

Performance also needs a significant boost. Hopefully, the PC version will address that.

Overall, I'm enjoying the game and will definitely finish it.

Good luck, everybody!

author: ShiroKiro
quote: There are a lot of review bombs up here, so I'm going to give my honest feedback.This is one of the best games I've played from Rockstar in a long time. The story is significantly better than GTA 5, and I think that's largely because there's an actual sense of progression this time around. You don't become rich within the span of a few missions or jump straight into pulling off heists shortly after starting the game. Instead, the story takes its time developing the characters and setting.What does the story lack? Compared to the previous game, it doesn't offer quite the same level of interaction. However, it makes up for that with a slower-paced experience. It's very similar to Red Dead Redemption 2, focusing on realism and slower-paced storytelling through chapters. I know there are a lot of people review-bombing the game and calling it woke, but ironically, there are plenty of moments where the game itself makes fun of woke aspects of the real **** for performance, I haven't encountered a single bug throughout my entire time playing. A lot of the things people complain about can also be adjusted through the settings. Even the relationship aspect with Lucia is completely optional. You can choose to ignore things like repairing the house, buying flowers for Lucia, and getting her a necklace. These choices can also affect how the characters interact with each other throughout the story.Gameplay-wise, the combat feels great, the driving feels fantastic, and the world is incredibly detailed. There's a **** ton of interaction between NPCs, animals, and the environment itself. One thing I particularly appreciate is the number of lore references to characters from GTA 5 and previous entries. It really shows the love and attention to detail Rockstar put into this world. I won't spoil any of it, but some of these references get really interesting.I'm currently around 11–15 hours into the game, and I've only just reached Chapter 3. That's with me primarily focusing on the main story. If I spent more time exploring the world and participating in its various activities, I could easily see myself spending many more hours playing.Negatives: The only real negative I've experienced so far is the 30 FPS. However, it hasn't taken away from my enjoyment of the game. You eventually get used to playing at 30 FPS, and Red Dead Redemption 2 ran at the same frame rate without it being a dealbreaker for most **** an 8/10? Simply put, I haven't experienced enough of the game yet to justify giving it a 10/10. I've only just reached the beginning of Chapter 3, and I want to experience everything the game has to offer before making that judgment. That being said, based on everything I've played so far, I genuinely believe this game has the potential to be a 10/10.

author: TheInsinuator
quote: There is a simple reason why I give this game a 10 and not a 9. There are many review bombs which will negate my rating, should I give it a 9. This is an unfathomably large video game with an insane detail. The developers have taken the route of more immersion, thereby compromising the gameplay for the first few hours. However, this only makes the hit of grand robberies better. The game is not "woke" or rightist either. It maintains a balance and true to the essence of GTA, it parodies every thing and every person. The game is grand, and the open world has a map so large which is so alive that I cannot believe it. However, before launch, it was claimed that Jason and Lucia could be simply partners, letting each have their own flings and romantical partners. But something happens early on which confirms that not only is this not to be, but something ties them to their relationship. I understand the reasons for the game not letting you complete freedom in such aspects, but I can't say I loved it. There are many people who don't care about this, and this will not affect you whatsoever. The performance of the game is decent, depending on the console, it can lock at thirty frames per second for majority of the times. The game finally brings some actual difficulty to the franchise, which is a real delight. Players have to keep a check on their ammo and actually aim. In terms of combat, the removal of aim assist is a welcome feature. For the world itself, it is jaw dropping how many people have their own stories, how many details the game holds. The regions of the game are like real life in terms of their scale and density. The most important thing to remember is that a player must keep some time in their schedule to play it. The game takes its time with immersive activities helpful for roleplayers before opening up with action missions. Someone not interested in roleplay should definitely spend some time in the game before commenting on it. My final words are that this game is a must buy. An absolute must buy. I would like to, but have not, deduct a point for poor weapon and item UI, and frame drops.

author: Kolip
quote: GTA VI is the new benchmark for open-world games. Everything else now feels outdated. Leonida is enormous and incredibly dense — Vice City's neon streets, rural swamps, and small towns all feel handcrafted. NPCs live their own lives, the weather affects how the city behaves, and every corner rewards exploration. It's the most believable open world Rockstar has ever built. Missions give you freedom instead of forcing a script — rob a store quietly or go loud, the game adapts. Driving feels weighty, shooting has real punch, and the smarter wanted system makes escapes genuinely tense. Side activities are woven into the world so naturally that nothing feels like filler. Technically, GTA VI makes other open-world games look primitive — character models, lighting, and animation operate on a level that shouldn't be possible on current hardware, and it runs smoothly without a single crash. Ambitious, mature, and technically astonishing, GTA VI doesn't just meet expectations — it sets a new standard for the entire genre. 10/10.

author: martimgomes7
quote: Grand Theft Auto VI is a perfect game; everything I saw while playing was great, every corner of the map, every detail. Honestly, I loved the story, the relationship between Lucia and Jason, their progress in their achievements—it's perfect. The level of realism in the gameplay is very good, the graphics, the size of the map—I spent 5 hours of my day just buying clothes around the city and visiting places. All those reviews with a 0 rating are ragebait; it's just not accepting that the game deserves a 99. I honestly think the game deserves GOTY and deserves many hours of playtime from every player. As the game progresses and the story unfolds, we see that Jason and Lucia truly want the best for their family, and this is done and told in a very beautiful way, showing the problems they both went through until they reached their final goal. Honestly, this game revolutionized what we know about open-world games and will continue to revolutionize it as the years go by and more details and mysteries of every corner of Leonida are discovered. Speaking more about the graphics, they are absolutely stunning. The 30 fps doesn't bother you at all; only Rockstar Games can achieve this. The game is quite colorful where it needs to be, and has a color palette that makes it very realistic. The physics are quite impressive: the hair, car crashes, destruction, shooting at the wheels of moving cars—I could talk about countless things. Every NPC is interactive; so far I haven't found a single repeated NPC, and the sheer number of NPCs and cars in the environment is jaw-dropping. Rockstar Games really developed this game with love. The game does have some bugs, but nothing that ruins the experience. They need to be fixed because they are annoying and visually unpleasant, but nothing major. The game has a lot to offer, whether in side activities, etc. Some places aren't even marked on the map, which makes everything interesting. In terms of gameplay, it's simply phenomenal, whether it's driving, shooting, or just walking hand-in-hand—it's all very impressive and shows attention to detail.

author: JYIXpro
quote:
Incredible game world, but 30 FPS, pricing, and bugs hold it back from a top score

​Review:

At its launch state (November 19, 2026) on PS5 and Xbox, Grand Theft Auto VI delivers an extraordinarily detailed, vibrant open world alongside a well-crafted atmosphere, great sound design, and a strong soundtrack. The massive scope, freedom of gameplay, and overhauled AI also stand out as clear strengths. 

​However, it falls short of a 9 or 10 for me: locking the game to 30 FPS—even on the PS5 Pro—is a noticeable drawback. On top of that, there is the steep €80 price tag, a "physical" edition that only includes a download code without a disc, and reports of GTA Online missing at launch. Visible physics, clipping, and graphical bugs in circulating clips (even if not necessarily representative) also hurt the polish, and the mission design can feel somewhat formulaic at times. 

​Overall, it is a very strong open-world game with standout world-building and atmosphere, but technical compromises, pricing decisions, and a lack of polish warrant clear deductions. A solid 8/10.

If you play GTA just to blow up oil tanks, rob hookers, and mow down pedestrians, you'll likely be disappointed by the unmistakable tonal shift in this latest installment. It relies far less on arcade-style chaos, but it more than makes up for it by incentivizing and rewarding grounded, realistic decisions. If you approach GTA as a true roleplaying game and actually play the part of a criminal, you will be blown away.

After 22 hours of gameplay, I can safely say GTA VI is the quintessential "criminal simulator."

author: cbrown3380
quote:
Rockstar has done it again. Absolutely one of the greatest video games ever made. You can't walk 100 feet without finding some mind-blowing technical detail. The animations, the NPC intelligence, and the atmospheric effects are by far the most impressive in gaming history to date. You can spend tens if not hundreds of hours just exploring the *massive* open world and encountering your own adventures, before even touching the story, which is impeccably acted and arguably Rockstar's most mature and moving story to date. Both protagonists are extremely likable and you'll be rooting for them from the moment they step on screen. The game also runs incredibly well given what a powerhouse it is (though I do recommend disabling screen shake and motion blur to assist with the frame rate, which can struggle in high intensity segments). Several dozen hours in and I haven't experienced a single glitch or crash of note, and I'm just perpetually amazed at how smoothly it runs and operates. 

Unfortunately BECAUSE this is a GTA that is seeking to tell a mature story for adults, it has triggered the most immature people on the internet. Incels who can't handle a love story or the presence of a woman in GTA whom they can't bludgeon or solicit. This is where the review bombing is coming from. I strongly suggest ignoring these people. Anyone giving this titan **** a 1 is not serious and is trying to push a political agenda, not assess the game. If you listen to them, you will be robbing yourself of the gaming experience of the decade, if not the millennium. Go in with the mindset of letting Rockstar take you on this journey, immerse yourself in the world, and I promise you will be in for an experience unlike anything you have felt before in gaming.

This is the pinnacle of the franchise and a landmark accomplishment in the industry, up there with other game-changing moments in gaming development history like Super Mario 64 and Halo. Rockstar has not only lived up to the impossible hype, they have exceeded it. It has raised the bar for what is possible in gaming, and will be remembered, discussed, and played for years to come. Everyone involved in its making should be very, very proud.

author: xamrah
quote:
The story is fairly good, the gameplay is an evolution of RDR2, so of you didn't like that game style with more immersion and less chaos, this probably isn't made for you. The simulation elements are revolutionary here, from the way the NPCs interact with you to the way the wanted system works. People who play a lot of RP will absolutely LOVE this game. 

The world design is insanely dense, and the attention to detail is unlike any game I have seen. Everything feels authentic to the region and the way lighting reflects around the world from city lights or sunsets is fantastic. 

Performance is rock solid, at 30 fps. That's literally the ONLY issue with this game. It is a very smooth 30 and is well optimized, but you still notice a tiny bit of jitter. I would say as a 60 fps purest I don't hate it, and I find I adjust to it fairly well after a minute or two. Bugs have been completely non-existent on PS5 pro, except for one rendering bug in heavy traffic where a truck had plato graphics for a few seconds. Otherwise, it is absolutely flawless. I see other reviewers complaining about it being broken and full of bugs (with no examples) and I can't speak for their experiences, but I have been playing since launch minute and have not experienced any notable ones. 

The gameplay is fun, well tuned, definitely balanced around role play systems more than previous titles but it's trying something new and it works extremely well. There is so much to explore and the physics allow for some wild fun if you need a break from the story missions or side missions.

They have another banger on their hands here! Obviously there are an insane number of 0's on here but user your brain, read actual fair reviews that talk about the game, not some clip they saw on social media. 9/10 recommended!

Quite a few restrictions in gameplay freedom, overall dialogue and missions aren't as funny as the previous GTA games. The mockery of current trends is fine, but GTA6 plays these safe.

I believe if this game launches online and especially PC multiplayer and custom servers, I believe this will quickly turn into a 10/10 experience.

author: Eagledivine
quote:
Depois de tantos anos aguardando GTA VI, acompanhando trailers e vazamentos, criei uma expectativa enorme. Felizmente, fui surpreendido positivamente.

Vejo muita gente dizendo que GTA VI é apenas um GTA V aprimorado, mas discordo. Para mim, é praticamente um Red Dead Redemption 2 dentro do universo de GTA, com uma experiência mais fluida. A Rockstar conseguiu aproveitar o melhor de GTA IV, Red Dead 2 e adicionar uma pitada de GTA V.

A liberdade oferecida ao jogador é excelente, assim como as mecânicas, principalmente a maneira como o personagem utiliza e administra suas armas, sem precisar carregar um arsenal inteiro no bolso.

Os NPCs são um dos maiores destaques. O mundo está constantemente acontecendo ao seu redor. Às vezes, você marca uma missão e passa duas horas explorando, simplesmente porque sempre surge alguma situação interessante pelo caminho. As atividades secundárias e os colecionáveis também são muito superiores ao que encontramos em diversos jogos.

Sobre os personagens, particularmente gostei muito mais do Jason do que da Lucy. Encontrei características nele com as quais consigo me identificar. Algumas atitudes da Lucy me incomodam, principalmente quando toma decisões sem considerar as consequências. Mas acredito que essa diferença de personalidade torna a relação entre os dois interessante.

Também vejo muitas reclamações sobre quedas de FPS, bugs e problemas com salvamentos. Felizmente, não presenciei nada disso. Jogo no PS5 e tenho amigos em diferentes consoles que também não tiveram problemas significativos. Isso não significa que os relatos sejam falsos, apenas que cada experiência é individual. Problemas técnicos devem ser cobrados, mas também precisamos considerar a dimensão e a complexidade desse mundo aberto.

Graficamente, o jogo é extraordinário, com paisagens variadas e um nível de detalhes impressionante.

Atualmente, tenho aproximadamente 30 horas de jogo e ainda não terminei a campanha. Mesmo assim, continuo descobrindo coisas novas.

Minha nota é 10/10. GTA VI representa uma evolução gigantesca para a franquia e entrega exatamente a experiência que eu esperava depois de tantos anos de espera. Ainda existem pontos que podem melhorar, mas, considerando tudo o que o jogo oferece, estou extremamente satisfeito. E o melhor é saber que ainda tenho muito para descobrir.

quote: One of my favorite things about GTA VI is its slower, more natural storytelling. Rockstar really understands that great immersion isn't just about action and spectacular missions. Sometimes it's about the little moments and the feeling that the world doesn't revolve entirely around **** particular moment really impressed me: preparing for Lucia's release from prison. At first, I thought I could simply postpone this moment, take my time, explore the world, and come back to it whenever I felt ready. But no! Lucia isn't going to wait forever, and apparently, you can actually damage your relationship with her by putting things off.That is such a fantastic detail! It makes the characters feel independent, gives your decisions more weight, and makes the world feel much more believable.I absolutely love this approach. It's realistic, unexpected, and adds a completely different dimension to the experience.Rockstar, this is brilliant. Just WOW!

author: Edisonteran10
quote: GTA 6: el mejor juego de la historia de Rockstar (y posiblemente de esta generación)Después de 13 años de espera, Grand Theft Auto VI no solo cumple las expectativas… las destroza. Rockstar ha entregado un mundo tan vivo, tan detallado y tan adictivo que es difícil recordar cómo era jugar a cualquier otro open world antes de **** mapa de Leonida (con Vice City como corazón) se siente enorme sin ser vacío. Cada barrio tiene personalidad, los NPC reaccionan de forma increíblemente realista y el nivel de detalle es absurdo: desde la forma en que la gente camina y habla hasta cómo el clima, la hora del día y hasta el tráfico cambian el ambiente. Visualmente es una locura; en PS5 se ve espectacular y se mueve con una fluidez que pocos juegos de este tamaño logran.Jason y Lucia son la mejor pareja de protagonistas que ha tenido la saga. Su química funciona, la historia tiene peso y humor negro al mismo tiempo, y las misiones se sienten más cinematográficas y variadas que nunca. Rockstar ya no se conforma con “hacer un buen GTA”: aquí hay una ambición narrativa y de diseño de mundo que se nota en cada hora de **** gameplay está más pulido que nunca. La conducción, los tiroteos, las persecuciones y las interacciones con el entorno se sienten más responsivas y satisfactorias. Y lo mejor es que el juego te deja ser quien quieras ser: puedes seguir la historia principal o simplemente perderte haciendo locuras durante horas sin que se sienta repetitivo.Después de tanto hype, lo normal es que algo se sienta un poco decepcionante. Con GTA 6 pasa lo contrario: salís de cada sesión con ganas de volver a entrar. Es el tipo de juego que justifica la espera y que marca un antes y un después.Veredicto: 10/10.

author: Ghosty8K
quote:
Thirteen years later. 

We're finally here. My journey with Grand Theft Auto started with Vice City. From there, I moved on to San Andreas, GTA IV, GTA V and everything in between. This franchise has been a part of my life for as long as I can remember. I've grown up with these games, experienced their launches and watched Rockstar take the series from one generation to the next. But nothing quite compares to the wait for GTA VI. Thirteen years. 
It's honestly hard to wrap my head around that number. Over the years, we've had rumours, leaks, speculation, countless discussions, trailers, delays and more memes than I can count. At some point, GTA VI almost became a running joke. We all knew it was coming, but it felt like one of those things we'd be waiting for forever. And now we're here. It's actually out. I was here for the midnight release, and after all these years, I finally got to sit down, turn on my Ps5 and play the game we've been talking about for so long. I don't even know how to describe that feeling. 
Even after spending hours with it, there's still something surreal about the whole thing. Part of me still hasn't quite processed that I'm actually playing GTA VI. Seeing the entire gaming community come together for this release has been something else too. Millions of people watching and playing at the same time. Everywhere you looked, people were talking about GTA VI. Something that spent years being a meme has finally become reality.

One thing I also want to mention is the DualSense integration. Rockstar has done a fantastic job with it. You feel practically every bump in the road while driving, the impacts of collisions and so many little details through the controller. The adaptive triggers are particularly impressive. Accelerating and braking actually feel different, with resistance that makes it feel like you're pressing real pedals in a car. Even the built-in controller speaker is used in such a nice way. It's these little details that make the experience feel that much more immersive.

And then there's the Metacritic achievement. For almost 28 years, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time held the top spot with a score of 99. As someone who genuinely loves that game and appreciates what it means to gaming history, seeing GTA VI reach that same score and take the number one position is pretty incredible. It's almost difficult to believe that we're witnessing this after all these years. But perhaps what makes this whole experience even more special to me is how everything has come full circle. 
My very first GTA game was Vice City. That's where it all started for me. I went from there to San Andreas, GTA IV and GTA V, and now, thirteen years later, I'm back in Vice City again. There's something incredibly fitting about that. I never would have imagined all those years ago that I'd eventually find myself here, waiting for another game set in the same place where my journey with this franchise began. And who knows, this might even be the last GTA game I get to experience at launch. I have no idea what the future holds or whether I'll be around for the next one. But if this does end up being my final chapter with the franchise, I honestly couldn't ask for a more fitting one. And of course, there's also the question of what's next. I'm genuinely excited to see what Rockstar has planned for the online component. GTA Online was such a huge part of GTA V's lifespan, and I'm really curious to see how they'll approach it this time around.

One thing I'd particularly love to see is more roleplay-oriented features. Little details like being able to send money between bank accounts, transfer money to your significant other or simply manage your finances through the in-game banking system, as we see in GTA VI, would be fantastic additions to the online experience. I'd love to see Rockstar expand on these kinds of everyday interactions and give players more freedom to build their own lives in the game. More features that encourage roleplay, interaction and making the world feel like somewhere you actually live, rather than somewhere you simply play. As for the game itself, I don't think I have the words for it yet. There's something strange about spending so many years looking forward to something, only to finally have it in front of you. You spend so long waiting, counting down and wondering what it'll be like. Then one day, you turn on your console and it's just there.I think it'll take me some time to fully process all of this. Rockstar, thank you. For the memories, the journey and finally giving us this moment.Thirteen years later, we're finally here. And somehow, it all started and ended in Vice City.

author: Maurops5
quote: Grand Theft Auto VI is a remarkable achievement in open-world game design, delivering an experience that stands out not just because of its scale, but because of the incredible sense of freedom, immersion, and attention to detail it offers.**One of the game's greatest strengths is its freedom.** GTA VI truly shines when it allows players to explore the world at their own pace, without constantly pushing them toward the next objective. Whether you're driving through the streets of Vice City, exploring remote locations, interacting with NPCs, or simply enjoying the atmosphere, the world feels like a place worth experiencing rather than just a backdrop for missions.**The missions are another major highlight.** The storytelling, character development, and variety of scenarios create an engaging experience that balances intense action with quieter, more personal moments. However, while the open world offers tremendous freedom, certain missions can still feel somewhat restrictive and scripted. Giving players more flexibility in how they approach objectives would make the experience even stronger.**The diversity of the map's biomes is particularly impressive.** From the vibrant streets of Vice City and its beautiful beaches to the dense swamps, rural communities, forests, and surrounding wilderness, each environment has its own atmosphere and identity. This variety makes exploration genuinely rewarding. The map isn't impressive simply because of its size, but because of how distinct and carefully crafted its different regions feel.What truly sets GTA VI apart is its ability to make even the simplest activities enjoyable. You don't always need a mission, a shootout, or a major event to have fun. Sometimes, driving along the coast, watching the city come alive at night, or discovering an unexpected detail in the environment is enough to appreciate the extraordinary work behind this **** course, no game is perfect. Some aspects of mission design could benefit from greater player freedom, and the sheer ambition of such a massive open world doesn't automatically guarantee that every activity will be equally engaging.Nevertheless, GTA VI represents an extraordinary step forward for the genre. Its greatest achievement isn't simply creating a massive world filled with things to do, but making that world feel believable, diverse, and worth getting lost in.**Ultimately, GTA VI is at its best when it trusts players to create their own experiences. That sense of freedom, combined with its environmental diversity, immersive atmosphere, and cinematic storytelling, is what makes it such a memorable game.**
