author: MrExtra
quote: A game can be evaluated from many different perspectives. The first thing that catches any gamer’s attention in any game is its **** graphics in this game are, at the very least, two generations ahead of what we currently have. I honestly don’t think even a linear game will be able to come close to this level of visual fidelity for several years, perhaps even an entire decade, or even achieve this level of visual quality on any ****, the game runs at 30 FPS. However, 30 FPS is absolutely incredible considering the graphical quality on display here. As someone who places great importance on smooth visuals and usually struggles to get comfortable with 30 FPS, the graphics in this game are so extraordinary that I never once found myself questioning its 30 FPS **** launch day, I was playing the game alongside a friend of mine who is a PC gamer. During our playthrough, he made an interesting observation. He said that this game looks like GTA V with DLSS 5. Let me take that comparison a little further: this is GTA V with a map three times larger, dozens of times more detail and environmental complexity, higher graphical fidelity and resolution, ray tracing, and DLSS 5 on top of all that.Furthermore, enabling motion blur in the graphics settings can help make the 30 FPS experience feel a little smoother and less noticeable.Moving beyond the graphics, the environmental details and the level of detail throughout the game’s map are simply phenomenal. This is the most detailed and richly realized game world I have ever experienced. The map is also incredibly large. It is so massive that it can keep you entertained for hours, weeks, and even months if you are someone who genuinely enjoys exploring. You can discover places that perhaps even Rockstar never intended players to find.Character development and the cast of characters:I haven’t finished the game yet, but up to this point, I don’t feel that I know enough about the backgrounds and past experiences of the characters I’m playing as. I also haven’t been able to develop as deep an emotional connection with the protagonists as I would have liked.However, I don’t consider this a weakness of the game just yet. Red Dead Redemption 2 showed me exactly how Rockstar can gradually build a deep emotional connection between players and a character like Arthur Morgan, simply through dialogue, conversations, and the gradual revelation of his past. Arthur eventually became such a remarkable character that he is now considered one of the most influential and beloved characters in video game **** that reason, I’m still giving this game time. Perhaps as I progress further, there will be certain missions or moments that allow me to develop that deeper connection with the characters and understand their pasts more thoroughly. I will update my review if that happens. And even if it doesn’t, I will come back and update this review to acknowledge that character development was a **** story:Aside from the beginning, which I personally found somewhat underwhelming, the story gets better and better as you progress. The initial impression was partly due to the enormous amount of hype surrounding the game before its release, which naturally raised my expectations considerably. Nevertheless, as the story unfolds, it becomes increasingly **** story in this game is phenomenal.Side activities, side quests, and live events:There is only one thing I can say about the amount of additional content this game offers: if you’ve played Red Dead Redemption 2, this game gives you even more content to explore and enjoy.I’m not comparing this game to previous GTA titles because, generally speaking, older GTA games haven’t offered the same level of variety and depth when it comes to side activities. Instead, this game feels like a fusion with the world of Red Dead Redemption, and in many ways, it goes even beyond that. Between the side quests, optional activities, exploration, and live events taking place throughout the map, there is an incredible amount of content waiting to be discovered.Overall:In my opinion, even more than thirteen years of waiting was worth it for this game.This game is a work of art, and Rockstar is the artist behind it.

author: BigShotty
quote: 10/10 — The Most Alive I’ve Ever Felt a Video Game World BeI’ve been gaming for most of my life, and I can confidently say Grand Theft Auto VI is the greatest video game I’ve personally experienced. And it’s not particularly **** Dead Redemption 2 and Cyberpunk 2077 were among my favorite games ever, but GTA VI has taken immersion to a level I genuinely didn’t think was possible.What makes this game extraordinary isn’t simply the graphics, the enormous world, or the production quality. It’s the attention to things most developers wouldn’t even consider.NPCs feel like individuals rather than background decorations. They notice your behavior, confront you, react emotionally, defend themselves, and sometimes surprise you in ways you never anticipated. I’ve witnessed interactions that felt completely natural and unscripted, leaving me genuinely **** world doesn’t feel like it exists solely for the player. It feels like you’re stepping into a place where people already have lives of their own.Jason and Lucia are phenomenal protagonists. They have distinct personalities, physical movements, and fighting styles. Their chemistry is excellent, and I genuinely enjoy spending time with both of them. The performances and characterization make even ordinary moments **** that’s perhaps my favorite achievement: Rockstar has made the ordinary extraordinary.Working out, shopping, driving, boating, exploring neighborhoods, watching people interact, listening to conversations, and simply existing in Leonida are genuinely entertaining activities. I can spend hours without progressing the story and never feel **** animations, environmental detail, atmosphere, character interactions, and sheer density of the world come together to create something special.Even the combat and police encounters feel more engaging. Fighting requires more attention, opponents can surprise you, and escaping the police feels exciting rather than **** the game literally flawless? Of course not. No game is. But perfection isn’t the absence of every technical imperfection. What matters is the overall experience, and GTA VI has delivered something extraordinary.I waited years for this game with incredibly high expectations. Somehow, Rockstar exceeded them.I’m still early in the story, so this is a review of my experience so far rather than a verdict on the entire narrative. But after spending so many hours exploring this world, I can confidently say I’ve never experienced another game quite like it.This isn’t just a beautiful open world. It’s a world I genuinely want to spend time **** me, Rockstar has created a masterpiece.

author: ArnauSayan2004
quote: Esta review podría centrarse en las apoteósicas hazañas técnicas que se han logrado en este juego, sobre lo vivo y orgánico que se siente todo el mundo y sus NPCs, por su inmersión en el juego gracias al feedback sonoro y táctil que te da el mando o por demás opiniones que al fin y al cabo, son conceptos subjetivos que van arraigados a los gustos y pareceres de cada individuo que somos como **** vez de eso, prefiero centrarme en los datos objetivos y demostrados que este juego ha conseguido, y que por más que los haters traten de desprestigiar con diferentes mensajes como “Los críticos de antes sí tenían criterio” o “La prensa está claramente comprada”, entre otros múltiples mensajes manipulados o sacados de contexto solo para desprestigiar un trabajo que parece **** primero y más importante es que, después de 28 años, lo que parecía imposible ha ocurrido: algo ha podido quitarle el trono a The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998) como el juego más valorado por la crítica de la historia. No es que la comparación haya sido bastante ajustada, sino que la diferencia es de casi 7 veces más críticas pensando lo mismo; ya que mientras The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (1998) consta con 22 críticas que le ponen la máxima nota, GTA 6 tiene 151 críticas que le otorgan también ese máximo prestigio.Como segundo dato, este juego ha conseguido algo que rara vez se ha presenciado en la industria: antes de su lanzamiento, la empresa ya estaba en ganancias económicas.Como tercer dato, este juego es considerado por múltiples medios —incluso los que no están centrados en los videojuegos— como el producto de entretenimiento, ya no solo de videojuegos, más importante de la historia.Como cuarto dato, hay que recordar que la salida de este videojuego ha provocado pérdidas de miles de millones de dólares en la economía mundial, porque muchos trabajadores se han ausentado de su puesto bajo “extrañas circunstancias” para poder estrenar este título.Aquellos que dicen que este juego tiene tantos bugs como Cyberpunk 2077 en su lanzamiento demuestran que, o la gente se olvida muy rápidamente de las cosas, o claramente no saben de lo que están hablando, o peor: que son plenamente conscientes de sus palabras y aun así siguen compartiendo estas mentiras ante el mundo. Conviene recordar lo que ocurrió con la salida de Cyberpunk 2077, pues salió en dos generaciones a la vez, tanto en PS5 y Xbox Series como en PS4 y Xbox One. No solo estaba plagado de errores visuales o de fallos en el movimiento o el combate que destrozaban la experiencia, sino que en la old gen era literalmente injugable. Las consolas se crasheaban constantemente y no se podía jugar, a tal punto que el juego tuvo que retirarse de las tiendas digitales, tuvieron que hacerse reembolsos masivos y CD Projekt Red tuvo que pedir disculpas oficialmente por el desastroso lanzamiento.Quienes siguen diciendo de forma no irónica que GTA 6 tiene tantos bugs como Cyberpunk 2077 claramente están esparciendo bulos y mintiendo sin ningún tipo de remordimiento. Esto no quiere decir que GTA 6 esté ausente de bugs, pues eso es imposible, ya que las totalidades absolutas no existen. Pero una cosa es decir que tiene algunos bugs aislados que han mancillado la experiencia de ciertos jugadores, y otra muy distinta es decir que su lanzamiento ha sido desastroso y que una gran cantidad de jugadores no han podido **** otro lado, tenemos otros supuestos fallos que circulan por las redes, como el famoso vídeo del avión que no explota, otros vídeos sobre la densidad de población en diferentes áreas mostrando la playa sin gente y acusándolo de engaño por decir que el tráiler estaba manipulado con multitud de bañistas, e incluso vídeos donde acusan a GTA 6 de llevarte de la mano mientras juegas o de que no puedes perder. Estos casos están manipulados por el siguiente motivo: son parámetros que se pueden ajustar en la configuración del juego o no tienen en cuenta el reloj interno, que influye en la afluencia de personas.A lo que quiero llegar con todo esto es que se podría ignorar lo que es este juego en sí —ya que podría ser perfectamente un juego de hacer hamburguesas o de recoger piedras por la montaña—, porque lo que ha significado su salida es un acontecimiento que muy difícilmente podrá ser superado por otro producto de entretenimiento, sea de la categoría que sea. No me parece descabellado decir que a lo mejor no volveré a ver en vida un acontecimiento de tal importancia como el lanzamiento de GTA 6 y todo lo que ha implicado.

author: AT_Galaxy94
quote:
Score: 10 / 10 – Hands down, the absolute Game of the Year and a historic masterpiece!

Hands down, the absolute Game of the Year! The world has waited thirteen years for this moment—and Rockstar Games hasn't just delivered, they have completely **** every expectation. Grand Theft Auto VI is far more than just the next installment in a legendary franchise; it is a landmark achievement in video game history.

A World That Truly Breathes
From the very first minutes, returning to Vice City and exploring the state of Leonida is nothing short of breathtaking. The attention to detail is unprecedented: from the shimmering neon lights of Ocean Drive to the dense, dangerous swamps of the Grassrivers, every square inch feels alive. NPCs react to their surroundings so convincingly and dynamically that you often find yourself just standing still, watching the streets come to life. The visuals, lighting, and physics engine set an entirely new standard on current-gen consoles.

An Unforgettable Duo
With Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, Rockstar has pulled off the most emotional and compelling narrative stroke in the series' history. The chemistry between the two protagonists effortlessly carries this gripping crime story. Their dynamic brings a level of depth to the heists, high-speed chases, and quieter character moments that is rarely seen in this genre.

Gameplay Perfected
Whether you are pulling off daring heists, tearing through high-stakes races, or simply exploring off the beaten path, every element blends together seamlessly. Gunplay feels punchy and precise, driving mechanics are perfectly balanced, and the sheer variety of activities ensures there is never a dull moment. Topped off with an outstanding soundtrack that captures the exact vibe of Vice City, the immersion is absolute.

Verdict
GTA VI is a triumph in every conceivable way. It combines a gripping narrative with an unmatched open world and near-flawless gameplay. An absolute must-play for anyone who loves video games—it simply doesn't get any better than this!

author: jvgamer
quote: There is no denying the sheer scale of GTA VI. From its sprawling open world to its obsessive attention to micro-details, it looks and feels like a technological juggernaut. Yet beneath all that grandeur lies a surprisingly shallow experience—one that lacks the unmistakable charisma that once made the franchise feel alive and rebellious. Rather than ushering in a new golden age, GTA VI feels like a symptom **** industry pushing itself toward collapse.​Today’s AAA studios have trapped themselves in an unsustainable arms race over photorealism and trivial minutiae. Spending hundreds of millions of dollars and nearly a decade perfecting hyper-realistic physics, dynamic lighting, or overly elaborate background details does nothing to make a game inherently more fun or meaningful. It only inflates budgets, stretches development cycles to absurd lengths, and makes taking creative risks nearly impossible. When every studio chases this bloated standard, fewer actual games get made, and the ones that do arrive carry the weight of impossible expectations.​For all the time and money poured into GTA VI, it still ships with noticeable bugs that break immersion and remind you of the cracks beneath the polish. Worse still, locking the experience at 30 fps on modern hardware is nothing short of shameful. When a flagship release struggles to deliver smooth performance in favor of visual excess, it exposes just how skewed the industry's priorities have become.​GTA VI may be a massive spectacle, but it is a hollow triumph—proof that obsessing over surface-level perfection while sacrificing soul, smoothness, and sustainable development is a fast track to sinking the entire medium.

The free-roam robberies and new wanted/heat system are genuinely addictive and work extremely well. The graphics look almost real-life. There isn’t a single area of the game that isn’t packed with detail. There are so many NPCs and cars, and the traffic finally flows like real life, with a wide variety of driver types and behaviors.
There’s tons more I could go over, but the bottom line is this: it’s the most immersive game you’ll ever play. You genuinely forget you’re playing a game. It’s kind of nuts.

author: AugustoJaraa
quote:
En síntesis, Rockstar consigue resultados impresionantes en prácticamente todo el apartado técnico: gráficos, animaciones, iluminación, físicas y simulación del mundo. Sin embargo, considero que fracasa en lo más esencial de un videojuego: su gameplay.

GTA 6 podrá tener ciudades visualmente impresionantes, cientos de NPCs con diferentes formas y tamaños, una iluminación tan realista que incluso permite que te veas reflejado en la pintura de los vehículos y una cantidad absurda de detalles que demuestran el enorme trabajo técnico detrás del juego. Pero ¿de qué sirve todo eso si, a la hora de jugar, la experiencia se reduce a manejar un automóvil y dispararles a NPCs con una inteligencia artificial pésima? Una IA tan mediocre que podés enfrentarte a tres tipos armados utilizando únicamente tus puños y salir victorioso.

Las misiones tampoco parecen ofrecer demasiado. Básicamente, consisten en ir al punto A, presenciar una cinemática, trasladarte al punto B, participar en un tiroteo que podría resolver mi hermanito de tres años y repetir el proceso. No hay demasiada profundidad en las mecánicas, los enfrentamientos carecen de desafío y las actividades terminan volviéndose extremadamente repetitivas. El gameplay es tan insulso que, después de unas pocas horas, siento que ya experimenté prácticamente todo lo que el juego tiene para ofrecer a nivel jugable.

Lo único que podría llegar a salvar la experiencia es la historia. Sin embargo, tampoco considero que destaque demasiado. Los diálogos, en varias ocasiones, resultan bastante cringe; Jason me parece un protagonista extremadamente aburrido, con muy poca personalidad y carisma. De hecho, mi propio ChatGPT me resulta más carismático. Lucía, por otro lado, se roba completamente el protagonismo: es mucho más interesante, tiene más personalidad y resulta considerablemente más entretenida. La diferencia entre ambos protagonistas genera un desequilibrio bastante negativo para la narrativa, especialmente cuando uno de los dos resulta tan poco interesante en comparación con el otro.

Mi opinión sobre GTA 6 es prácticamente la misma que tengo sobre Red Dead Redemption 2. Ambos son videojuegos extraordinarios desde el punto de vista técnico, pero considero que tienen deficiencias importantes en su gameplay. La diferencia es que Red Dead, al menos, tenía una historia que justificaba buena parte de la experiencia. El final de Arthur Morgan me hizo llorar y fue un momento que realmente quedó marcado en mi vida. GTA 6, en cambio, hasta donde jugué, no me está ofreciendo nada que me haga pensar que existe un apartado capaz de compensar sus deficiencias jugables.

Por último, quiero dejar una frase que resume bastante bien mi postura:

Que algo sea visualmente impresionante o requiera un esfuerzo técnico extraordinario no significa que mejore proporcionalmente la experiencia de juego.

Al final del día, estamos hablando de videojuegos, no de demostraciones tecnológicas. Los gráficos, las animaciones y los detalles visuales pueden enriquecer una experiencia, pero no reemplazan aquello que hace que un videojuego sea divertido: sus mecánicas, su jugabilidad, su desafío y la libertad que le ofrece al jugador.

quote: Era el juego más esperado de la historia de los videojuegos, un juego esperado desde hace no menos de 13 años aunque su producción se desarrollara en años posteriores; un juego que ha costado alrededor de 3 billones de dólares y que lamentablemente no ha cumplido con las expectativas de una saga de este calibre. En el día de salida se puede entender (a duras penas) que haya algún pequeño problema técnico debido a las dimensiones del juego sin embargo es inexplicable que tras numerosos retrasos por parte de la compañía para lanzar el juego haya tantos fallos y errores que honestamente arruinan la experiencia, desde "bugs" que lanzan al personaje por los aires, vehículos colisionando y traspasando el suelo, el personaje cayendo por debajo del mapa, Npc's con objetos que no corresponden a la acción que están desempleando, fallos en las animaciones o la total falta de reacción cuando una aeronave colisionando con un edificio puede traspasarlo o simplemente chocar, caiga y no le pase absolutamente nada. Es imposible nombrar realmente la total cantidad de fallos existentes, por otra parte el juego se debería ver a unos limitados 30 fps y deberían de ser "estables" lamentablemente en Play 5 esto no sucede, el juego sufre de caídas de fps en varias ocasiones, ya sea al entrar en animación, objetos explotando etc. Dejando a un lado el apartado técnico, nos encontramos con un mapa realmente sobrecogedor con multitud de escenarios distintos, diversos biomas y lugares que explorar; unos gráficos sobresalientes que son limitados por los fps y dientes de sierra. Ahora, la historia sin spoilers, es para ser sinceros mediocre, el juego tiene un inicio lento, que puede llegar incluso a ser pesado si lo que buscabas era tener un inicio lleno de acción y una trama por desarrollar que te envuelva, en esta edición se trata de una narrativa lenta que se desarrolla poco a poco, mejorando algo cada vez ya que va por capítulos pero no logra alcanzar ningún punto álgido, los personajes son bastante planos sin a penas evolución aparente y las interacciones se encuentran muy limitadas por la historia; el juego cuenta con 4 finales, buenos, malos y "neutros" según como se haya desarrollado la historia pero carecen de emoción o sorpresa al ser perfectamente predecibles y simples. En resumen y en mi más sincera opinión tal y como está ahora mismo el juego solo puedo darle una nota de entre 6 o 7, tuvieron mucho tiempo para desarrollar una mejor narrativa, unos personajes mucho más carismáticos como lo podían ser cualquiera de los personajes principales de anteriores entregas de la saga, que en esta edición dejan bastante que desear, tuvieron el mayor presupuesto de la historia para garantizar que no hubiera fallos importantes o multitud de "bugs" y aún así los hay, no hay ninguna innovación más allá de unos mejores gráficos y como dije anteriormente, este era el juego más esperado de la historia que no ha sabido cumplir con las expectativas de sus jugadores

author: LiPau9
quote:
Looks incredible, other than the constant dropped frames, stuttering, and lag. Story takes some time to get into, but improves eventually and ends up being pretty okay. Not amazing, but not bad. Just okay. Writing is hit-or-miss. Characters are often bland, uninteresting, or just poorly written, with some notable exceptions. Stephen Root is great, as always. Lucia's voice actress does a great job. Overall, it's a good game. Not the "greatest video game ever made", as early "critic" reviews hysterically claimed, but it's a solid 7. If the technical issues are solved in the future, then it's probably a 7.5 or so. 

As an aside: Nobody should be rating GTA6 a zero (I assume these are trolls). That's ridiculous, and devalues well-meaning criticism by making it seem that it's only trolls who are not buying into the hype. GTA6 is not a zero, no matter how you try to spin it. It's entertaining, moderately fun, and moderately interesting. The definition of a 7.

author: TobiasWatson96
quote: A caveat: Lets all try and aim at being level headed and objective (as possible) whilst reviewing things, it then helps others discover things thry wouldn't otherwise have known about. Reviews are ultimately for others after all. My review of GTA VI is an honest one, based on the various different factors of the game; some of which I thought worked well, and some that had issues which affected playability. The story does start off slow, but it picks up pace later on. Some new mechanics aren't as fun as previous titles. (Restrictions on what to do, where to go). The performance also leaves a lot to be desired, with frame drops littered throughout the map. Graphically, it is phenomenal, with immersive lighting effects. The visuals cannot be beaten. That being said, the gameplay does not hold a candle to some of the previous GTA releases. Pros: Beautiful Graphics, Exciting and dense World Design, Great voice acting. Cons: lacking story mode (some is excellent as expected, some of it is terribly paced), performance issues, lack of freedoms of previous titles.

author: ShaGan
quote:
To be completely honest, I would rate the game somewhere between 7 and 8 out of 10. A Metacritic user score of 5.5/10 reflects the dishonesty of the gaming press and a lack of critical thinking.

This is not just about unstable frame rates, but also about the numerous lies told by the studio.

1. No prostitutes and no romances with other women.

The studio justifies this decision by referring to the narrative concept of GTA 6. Jason and Lucia are a couple, and their relationship is one of the main elements of the story. Rockstar wanted the game's mechanics to support that narrative.

The romance between Jason and Lucia is optional, meaning you don't have to develop their relationship or engage in dates and romantic interactions. Regardless of how their relationship develops, they will continue to work together, carry out heists and remain partners in crime, as confirmed by Rob Nelson from Rockstar North.

In my opinion, this is evidence of numerous narrative changes made during development, which nobody bothered to properly verify before release. I would even go as far as to suggest that the production team was trying to adapt to the prevailing political trends of the time, which kept changing throughout such a long development cycle.

2. Jason's role in the story feels like something that was forced into the narrative at a later stage, rather than being part of the original concept.

This is evident in the story itself. In many sequences, his involvement is barely noticeable. This leads me to believe that GTA 6 was originally intended to be the first instalment featuring a female protagonist, but that concept evolved during development.

3. Restrictions on stealing cars in certain areas, or introducing characters from specific social groups only to grant them special privileges bordering on invincibility, feel like a deliberate provocation aimed at the audience.

This is an audience that fell in love with the series because of its freedom and its ability to make fun of reality. Now, however, it seems that the game is increasingly trying to dictate what players should do and how they should behave.

4. There are simply too many mechanics introduced during the opening hours, making the game feel more like a life simulator such as The Sims than the GTA we all know.

Seriously? Painting, repairing roofs, building IKEA-style furniture? And all of this unnecessarily extends the introduction instead of being introduced as optional activities later in the game. Jason isn't the one wearing an ankle monitor and being confined to his house...

5. Car customisation, clothing choices and hairstyles are so basic that they offer more than GTA Vice City, but less than GTA San Andreas.

6. The numerous bugs, combined with poor optimisation, are somehow being forgiven by players when it comes to a studio with practically unlimited financial resources, a workforce of over 2,000 employees and a total development period of around eight years.

This is simply unacceptable for a studio with so much experience when developing another instalment in an established franchise.

Meanwhile, Cyberpunk took a massive hit for releasing on both consoles and PC in such a poor state, despite having a development period of around four years. It was also their first game featuring firearms and only their third title built on their own proprietary engine.

There is a reason why so many people considered Cyberpunk the better game. CD Projekt RED improved and expanded it over the years, but they didn't have to fix its story.

Does anyone genuinely believe Rockstar will rewrite and fix the narrative **** that has already been released and is on sale?

We forgive Rockstar for all of this despite its years of experience, enormous budget and considerably less time pressure than CD Projekt RED...

author: Roxas9611
quote:
Parto con due principali premesse: NON ho giocato il gioco ma lo ho visto giocare da amici e ho guardato parecchie review/gameplay no commentary e documentato sulle missioni più di spicco del gioco. Il mio voto é tarato sul fatto che non darò MAI un 10 ad un videogioco perché nemmeno capolavori come Metal Gear Solid sono perfetti, così come non darò MAI uno 0 ad un videogioco perché anche le pattumiere peggiori hanno un minimo da offrire. La mia votazione quindi parte da un 2 fino ad un massimo di 9.5.

Detto questo c'è da partire sulle origini e la base del brand. GTA è stato da sempre la massima espressione di libertà (soprattutto caotica)concessa al videogiocatore ed è stato sempre un videogioco in grado di raggiungere standard sempre più alti per l'industria. Ogni GTA ha sempre introdotto qualcosa di nuovo non solo graficamente o a livello sceneggiati o ma anche di gameplay. Ed é importante specificare questa cosa.
Inizialmente ero spaventato da GTA VI perché avevo timore sarebbe stato un "GTA V Remake"(e così per fortuna non è stato) quindi ero partito già con un hype veramente moderato. A far crollare completamente le mie speranze é stato l'aberrante marketing che ha ricevuto: copia fisica del gioco non presente ma il CD fisico della colonna sonora a 120 euro si, collector scialba e di dubbio gusto a 400 euro+spedizione senza gioco compreso, gameplay molto spesso tenuto molto da parte come se si volesse nascondere che non fosse niente di eccezionalmente nuovo(toccheremo questo punto più avanti) ed infine grafica e densità di NPC boostata rispetto al prodotto finale. Tutto questo aveva spento il mio interesse per il gioco.
Quando il gioco finalmente è uscito mi sono subito fiondato a guardarlo e ad ascoltare le analisi di molti e queste sono le mie conclusioni.
Graficamente é eccezionale nulla da dire ma era abbastanza scontato lo sarebbe stato così come l'ambiente design con la sua densità e meticolosità incredibile é eccelso. Parliamo delle animaizoni:Rockstar nel suo marketing ha millantato il suo aver fatto una roba come 500000 animazioni diverse per rendere il gioco credibile ed immersivo ma poi nel prodotto finale ne mancano di importanti. Jason fa scomparire la tazzina del caffè se compi un'altra azione con essa in mano. Oppure se blocchi entrambe le portiere di un'auto il **** magicamente si teletrasporta via quando invece in giochi come sleeping dogs si ha un'animazione unica in cui viene rotto(irrealisticamente) il vetro anteriore per uscire. E ancora, i vestiti che spawnano addosso quando esci di casa. Non é un appunto per fare fronte alla realisticitá quanto per sminuire il millantare queste enormi animazioni per poi non aver cura di dettagli non proprio di poco. C'è comunque da dire peró, che quelle che sono presenti sono assurde.
Sceneggiativamente il gioco ha alti e bassi e la relazione tra i due **** non é così libera come uno possa credere tanto che in alcuni momenti il gioco chiede di avere un certo rapporto per poter intraprendere una determinata missione. La libertà caotica del gioco viene meno per poter essere coerente con la sceneggiatura e questo per me evidenzia un grosso problema di fondo. Non tutti magari si ricordano ma in GTA San Andreas avevi la possibilità in maniera completamente terziaria di avere una relazione da accudire ma senza limitare minimamente la libertà del giocatore(come per esempio andare a prostitute) e questo é un grossissimo punto a favore di un vecchio GTA rispetto ad un nuovo. Avrei preferito avere la libertà totale in tutto ed avere qualche dialogo opzionale in più sulle cattive azioni che avrei potuto compiere. L'ho trovata una scelta molto pavida e pigra.
La libertà in generale viene meno anche nella componente di maggior spicco del gioco:il rubare auto. Rubare le auto in GTA é sempre stato immediato, qui invece devi girare intorno a molti sistemi che lo rendono poco accessibile o addirittura inaccessibile talvolta. E allora mi chiedo: a cosa mi serve un ambiente così ampio e ben costruito come Leonida se poi veniamo meno alla libertà di azioni che posso compiere?
Lato gameplay effettivo invece trovo il mission design ormai obsoleto senza aver introdotto niente di nuovo e il gameplay shooting terza persona completamente invariato da sempre senza un minimo di introduzione di qualche piccola stupida meccanica nuova. E quindi tutti questi anni di sviluppo per cosa? Sviluppo cinematografico e di ambient design? Non dovresti da casa di sviluppo di VIDEOGIOCHI innovare prima di tutto il gameplay? 
Lascio per ultima(perché tale la trovo) la questione FPS(con i suoi cali) e bug vari che sicuramente spariranno nelle **** a loro) re-release su successive console e PC.

A fronte di tutto questo non mi sento di dare da spettatore, PER ADESSO, non più di 7 con la consapevolezza che su PC sicuramente sarà un voto più alto ma anche consapevole del fatto che non è come in tanti lo definiscono "il gioco del secolo".

author: Prossias
quote:
Beautiful and dull. It's like watching a master musician flawlessly perform Imagine Dragons' "Thunder" for 80 hours straight.

There's a real problem with pacing and freedom. It's even slower than Red Dead Redemption 2. While the first few hours of that game have you robbing a moving train and fighting dozens of enemies in the snow, GTA VI has you spending hours on pointless activities, like listening to a 15-minute conversation about opening a bank account, dragging furniture around, or spending an hour at a party having endless, mind-numbingly conversations with random characters.

The controls on PS5 are terrible, especially when driving and shooting. It's insane that no media reviews seem to mention this, especially in a year with games featuring excellent controls, like Onimusha. The game is ridiculously easy. I challenge you to actually die in a shootout. You can go full Rambo, standing out in the open and shooting everyone with auto-aim locking onto enemies' heads. It's even easier than Ocarina of Time Remake, whose lack of difficulty has been widely criticized. Nighttime lighting is awful, and you're more likely to die by crashing into an obstacle you couldn't see in the dark than during a shootout in a main story mission.

Story-wise, the media will tell you it's on par with The Wire or Disco Elysium, but everything here is painfully linear and predictable. Even the supposedly hidden side stories will literally blow up in your face while you're just driving down the road. The game constantly wastes your time with long, painfully unfunny jokes. The only other game I can remember disrespecting my time this much with such terrible humor was Paper Mario: The Thousand-Year Door.

The game isn't even woke. Lucia is essentially written as a man, displaying stereotypically masculine behavior, with the writers apparently believing that making her obnoxious and constantly treating her husband like **** is enough to portray a woman (no evolution from the stereotype of Michael's wife in GTA V). Rather than creating a convincing female character, they end up reproducing a deeply misogynistic stereotype. The irony is that criticizing this game will get you called a misogynist by a horde of middle-aged, right-wing white men desperate to defend their beloved video game, despite having neither the lived experience nor the personal conduct to make such judgments.

But the biggest problem is that the game simply isn't fun. Over the past 15 years, I've watched countless franchises reinvent themselves and modernize their gameplay (Resident Evil, Zelda, Final Fantasy), yet GTA VI still plays essentially like GTA: San Andreas. That wouldn't necessarily be a bad thing, since San Andreas is an excellent game, but somehow Rockstar has managed to make everything that made its gameplay fun unnecessarily bureaucratic.

author: vanburenjulius
quote: A great game, but it feels like Rockstar sacrificed some of GTA’s freedom. I’m genuinely enjoying GTA 6, and I think there’s a lot Rockstar has done incredibly well. However, one of my biggest disappointments is how much the relationship between Jason and Lucia seems to influence the overall experience. I don’t mind having a romance or a strong relationship between two protagonists, but I feel like it shouldn’t be the central focus of the game to the point where it limits player **** has always been about more than just following a story. It’s about freedom, making your own choices, getting involved in random situations, meeting people, causing chaos, and living your own life in an open world. I wish Jason and Lucia had been treated more as two independent protagonists who could work together as a criminal duo without their relationship defining so much of the experience.I would have liked more freedom in their personal lives as well. For example, being able to pursue other relationships, flirt, accept or reject advances, or simply make your own decisions without feeling restricted by the game’s predetermined relationship dynamic. These options wouldn’t have to affect the main storyline at all. Players who wanted Jason and Lucia to remain loyal and develop their relationship could do so, while others could focus entirely on the criminal side of the game.I understand why Rockstar made certain choices, and I don’t think every game needs to offer the same freedom. Red Dead Redemption 2, for example, works perfectly well with Arthur Morgan having a more defined personality and fewer personal options. But GTA is a different franchise. Its modern setting, sandbox nature, and emphasis on player freedom make these restrictions feel more noticeable to me.Ultimately, I still enjoy GTA 6, but I think it could have been even better if Rockstar had given players more freedom to shape Jason and Lucia’s personal lives instead of making their relationship feel so central. I want to experience the story Rockstar created, but I also want the freedom to create my own experiences within the world. That’s what has always made GTA special to me.

author: Zeukrob
quote:
Are good graphics enough for an overall assessment? Is the brand name enough for an overall assessment? Is a famous, omnipresent acronym (GTA) enough for an overall assessment? 

To anyone with a bit of common sense, the answer is no—it is not enough. As with any activity, medium, or life itself, a "good experience" is the sum of many factors that, taken together, create the complete experience.

In terms of graphics, *GTA VI* is excellent—but that is where the "good experience" ends. A multitude of other factors fall so short that the game becomes a form of torture.

The story: Heavy-handed, uninteresting, and boring—to the point where you just want to scream, "Enough! Set me free from this torture!"

The characters: Just as bad—boring, charmless, stereotypical, and impossible to empathize with. Furthermore, there is a recurring, stereotypical anatomical trait applied to the women throughout the entire game world.

Gameplay: The interface is dull and ugly—especially the radial menu; other games, such as *RDR2* or *Days Gone*, handle this much better.

Performance: It is what it is on consoles—limited. Only on PC will the game’s true performance be revealed.

And then there is a broader, perhaps less critical aspect that has always been part of the *GTA* identity: the color palette. Each *GTA* title has had a very distinct look. *GTA: San Andreas* featured warm, amber, and orange tones; *GTA IV* leaned into grays, desaturated browns, and muted colors; *GTA VI*, meanwhile, is drenched in pinks and purples—looking for all the world like a teenage girl’s streaming bedroom.

author: manohibou
quote: Un jeu impressionnant et généreux, mais très loin de la perfection à 99 % annoncée par la presse.Soyons tout à fait honnêtes dès le départ : Grand Theft Auto VI est un très bon jeu, et même une œuvre marquante à bien des égards. Visuellement, c'est une claque monumentale qui redéfinit les standards techniques de l'industrie. L'État de Leonida, avec Vice City en tête, est d'une richesse, d'une densité et d'un réalisme absolument bluffants. La gestion de la lumière, la météo dynamique, la foule qui réagit de manière crédible à ce qui l'entoure et le niveau de détail dans chaque recoin de la carte forcent le respect. On sent immédiatement les années de développement acharné et le budget colossal investis par Rockstar Games derrière chaque rue, chaque intérieur et chaque ligne de dialogue. La mise en scène est digne des plus grandes productions cinématographiques, la bande-son est toujours aussi soignée et l'écriture satirique de l'Amérique moderne fonctionne à merveille.Cependant, il faut garder la tête froide face à l'enthousiasme délirant de la presse spécialisée. Le score quasi parfait de 99/100 attribué par de nombreux journalistes est, à mes yeux, largement exagéré et déconnecté de l'expérience réelle manette en main. Un tel score laisserait entendre que le jeu a tout révolutionné et qu'il est exempt du moindre défaut. Or, malgré ses immenses qualités artistiques et techniques, le titre traîne des lourdeurs et des défauts bien réels qu'il est tout simplement impossible d'ignorer lorsque l'on joue plusieurs dizaines **** point le plus marquant, et celui qui divisera le plus les joueurs, reste sans conteste son gameplay très lourd. Dans la droite lignée de Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar a fait le choix du réalisme absolu au détriment de la réactivité immédiate. Les déplacements des personnages ont une inertie extrêmement pesante : chaque demi-tour, chaque mise à couvert, chaque interaction avec un objet ou ouverture de porte demande un temps d'animation incompressible. Il faut clairement accepter cette philosophie de jeu dès le lancement sous peine de s'agacer très vite. Si cette lourdeur sert effectivement l'immersion et donne du poids aux protagonistes, elle rend aussi les phases d'action, les fusillades en intérieur et les situations d'urgence particulièrement rigides, parfois même frustrantes. On a souvent l'impression de lutter contre les contrôles plutôt que de maîtriser pleinement son personnage, ce qui nuit au plaisir pur et à la nervosité que l'on est en droit d'attendre d'un jeu d'action moderne.À cette prise en main exigeante s'ajoutent des choix de game design qui commencent sérieusement à dater. La structure des missions principales reste encore beaucoup trop dirigiste. Dès que l'on s'éloigne un tant soit peu du chemin prévu par les développeurs ou que l'on tente une approche un peu trop créative lors d'un braquage ou d'une filature, le jeu sanctionne immédiatement le joueur par un écran d'échec. Ce contraste entre la liberté totale offerte en exploration libre et le carcan très rigide des missions scénarisées crée une vraie rupture de rythme. On aurait aimé que Rockstar fasse davantage confiance à l'intelligence du joueur et propose des objectifs plus ouverts, à la hauteur de l'immensité de son monde **** le plan technique également, tout n'est pas irréprochable. Si la direction artistique et la richesse visuelle sont indiscutables, cela se paie au prix fort sur consoles avec un framerate bloqué à 30 images par seconde. Couplé à la lourdeur naturelle des animations, ce manque de fluidité accentue encore la sensation de latence dans les commandes, notamment lors des poursuites à haute vitesse ou des échanges de tirs intenses. L'interface et les menus mériteraient aussi d'être beaucoup plus ergonomiques et modernes, certaines actions simples demandant encore trop de manipulations **** résumé, GTA 6 est incontestablement un grand jeu vidéo, une prouesse technique et une aventure solo généreuse qui occupera les joueurs pendant des années. Il mérite largement d'être salué pour son ambition démesurée et la vie incroyable qui anime son univers. Mais entre son gameplay extrêmement lourd qu'il faut apprendre à digérer, sa rigidité dans la construction de ses missions et ses compromis techniques, il est très loin d'être le chef-d'œuvre absolu et sans faille que les notes de la presse veulent nous vendre. C'est un excellent divertissement, mais certainement pas un jeu à 99 %

author: tidusz10685
quote:
GTA 6 – A Masterpiece or a Double Standard in Gaming Reviews?
Apparently, in today's gaming industry, poor optimization only matters when the Rockstar logo isn't on the screen.
Days Gone? Frame rate drops — heavily criticized.
Cyberpunk 2077? Terrible performance on last-gen consoles — absolutely slammed by reviewers.
Pokémon Scarlet and Violet? Technical problems — lower review scores.
GTA 6? Reported frame rate drops on the standard PS5, inconsistent performance, and noticeable responsiveness issues. Yet somehow, we're seeing perfect 10/10 scores and endless praise for a supposed technical masterpiece.Interesting how the standards suddenly change, isn't it?
I'm not saying GTA 6 is a bad game. Far from it. But when reviewers acknowledge technical problems and still award a perfect score, they should at least explain why those problems apparently don't matter.20 FPS doesn't magically become 60 FPS just because Rockstar made the game.
People playing on a standard PS5 deserve an honest assessment of how the game actually performs on their hardware — not a love letter to the developer.A 10/10 should represent an exceptional gaming experience, not a reward for brand recognition, a massive marketing budget, or years of hype.
If poor optimization costs other games points, GTA 6 shouldn't get a free pass.Either hold every game to the same standards, or stop pretending these review scores are objective.

author: Adsherd
quote:
GTA VI : 13 Years of Waiting, So Was It Worth It?

Graphics
The game is gorgeous, with several breathtaking vistas. But it's capped at 30 fps on every console, and it's most noticeable on the base PS5, where the frame rate stumbles while the PS5 Pro holds up better. The lack of a 60 fps mode is hard to ignore.

Technical Performance
The game seemed to have quite a few bugs. A fix patch looks likely.

GameplayIt
It felt more like a life simulator than a GTA game. Some NPCs seemed untouchable, certain vehicles can't be stolen, and the wanted-level system, interesting on paper, quickly becomes punishing and repetitive. To me, this is the least GTA-like GTA yet.

Story and Characters
Playing as a couple changes the dynamic, and it's divisive. Not being able to cheat on Lucia frustrated some players. Some of the "couple life" missions felt like too much to me. Jason, despite his openly embraced bisexuality, came across as bland.

Verdict
An ambitious and beautiful game, but a series that's changing its tone and won't suit every fan.

author: akashipov
quote:
First of all, I want to say that the overall quality of the game is absolutely incredible. The optimization, graphics, attention to detail, and countless little interactions are genuinely impressive. It's obvious that an enormous amount of time and effort went into making the world feel alive, with all kinds of unique situations and small details.

But here's the problem: the gameplay itself — arguably the most important part of any game — is just boring.

I expected much more variety in missions, more interesting weapons (like swords or bows), and a deeper weapon customization system. Imagine being able to upgrade different types of ammunition, modify weapon stats, or unlock entirely new ways to approach combat.

The 80-hour main story feels artificially stretched out. And considering how advanced the game's physics engine is, I honestly think Rockstar could have done so much more with it. There's an incredible amount of untapped potential here.

Why aren't there more creative missions? Imagine fighting your way through a luxury yacht, sneaking aboard a heavily guarded ship, or completing missions that actually encourage different playstyles.

Another issue is that the game sometimes takes realism way too far. GTA is supposed to be about freedom, chaos, and having fun — not simulating every aspect of real life. That level of realism works perfectly in Red Dead Redemption 2, but GTA has always been a different kind of experience.

I would have loved to see a proper skill progression system. Imagine learning new fighting techniques, improving your stealth abilities, or unlocking unique combat moves that you could actually use throughout the game.

Or having access to more unconventional weapons. A bow could be incredibly fun with this physics engine. Swords, melee combat with proper damage physics, creative stealth mechanics — there's so much they could have explored.

Instead, we get endless conversations with your girlfriend, followed by more conversations between your girlfriend and her friends.

GTA shouldn't primarily be about relationships. It should be about freedom — the freedom to experiment, explore, and interact with the world in as many ways as possible. Freedom in relationships also... I think a lot of people wanted to see relationships with other girls in the game.

And that's what disappoints me the most. Despite all the technical achievements, I struggle to see any meaningful evolution in gameplay compared to GTA V.

The world is bigger, prettier, and more detailed than ever. But is it actually more fun?

For me, that's the biggest missed opportunity.

author: faultlessdark
quote:
I like the simulation side of this, the world feels lived-in and the dynamic interactions and events that can just happen with NPC's walking down the street is fun to witness and interact with.

But the story is slow, the gameplay is slow, and dear god does it run terribly on the base PS5. If it was running at 4K I'd probably give it some slack for targeting 30fps (targeting, only maintaining it on a PS5 pro), but it's 1440p rendered and upscaled to 4K which can make some scenes ghost quite badly (like when Jason paints the walls). I don't know, maybe this really will get a higher score from me when it releases on PC where it can stretch it's legs, but I'd still never give it a 10 because that story pacing can't be fixed by a hardware upgrade.

It's a fun game, and I'd class it as "good", but it's nowhere near "a masterpiece" as the critic reviews suggest - go read some of those reviews. Some of them criticise the game in similar areas but still award a 10/10.

author: lostit
quote:
I'm not going to fall into either crowd. Half of the people are saying woke slop, and the other are saying greatest game of all time. Personally, I think  I would've really enjoyed this game if it didn't run horrendously. 

When it comes to GTA, I enjoy grabbing 5+ stars every now and then for fun. When I had 6 stars yesterday, the frames dropped to at least 25 fps. 

I've spent the last week playing RDR2 to get used to this game, but when you have frame drops during driving, it seems your playing two things at one time. 

The story can be better yes, but the insane amount of side content helps. But, when my Series X is dropping frames simply traveling the world to pursue said side-content, it takes away the immersion. This is the first game I've ever played to give me motion blur headaches, and I've been gaming for a very long time. I appreciate the heights Rockstar has tried to take this game. I was really pumped to dive into this world, but I have a problem with it sadly.

A performance update (at least maintaining said 30fps) would boost my score from a 6 to an 8. 

If I sound spoiled, I'm sorry. I don't have a PC, but have enjoyed performance mode on my Series X for years now. If this game was a solid 30fps at all times, I don't think I would've made this review.

Dissapointing. Really dissapointing. 

I could see myself really enjoying this game, but not in its current state.

A billion dollars.

author: justinb113
quote:
GTA6 is finally here and sadly it doesn’t quite live up to the hype.  But it’s not as terrible as some will have you believe.  Here’s my honest assessment starting with the negatives.

The game is just very slow and you feel it from the moment you first get to move.  I guess it’s the low fps but the characters move slowly and also the responsiveness from the controller isn’t quite right, everything feels sluggish and delayed and this is especially noticeable in combat.  You are also asked to press triangle or press and hold triangle for two different actions and while I might get used to this I’m always doing the wrong thing.  The weapon wheel seems quite cumbersome and slow too and I keep pulling out my flashlight.

I’m about mid way into the game and honestly I actually like the story but I don’t think it will be everyone’s cup of tea.  I won’t give any spoilers but it’s about a couple of criminals.  Now Lucia, I think is great and I’ll come onto her, but Jason is rather bland.  It’s like they wanted a female MC but didn’t dare go the full way so they brought her boyfriend along.  He’s terribly voice acted and his lines are very bland, to the point my initial guess was he was going to get killed off early in the game, but no he does appear to be a main character and must be the least interesting protagonist in GTA.  Most of the NPCs are rather dull too.

Finally it is quite clear the game has been “sanitized” somewhat.  The left will tell you it’s pro right because of the violence, the right will tell you it’s woke because there’s no hookers.  But generally I don’t think it’s either, it’s just safe to not offend anyone.  They poke fun of both the left and the right but there’s no sleeping with sex workers and putting them in the boot of the car, and there’s some controversial characters that have been made invincible likely because Rockstar doesn’t want the publicity of players murdering them which makes sense but it feels censored.

Now the positives, the obvious one is the graphics, even on base PS5 it’s the best looking video game ever made and it’s not even close.  The whole area looks amazing, and the water and sky particularly are incredible, it feels like a different console generation than everything else.   The menus are very clean, and from the start up of the game setting brightness and things to viewing your collectibles it’s all very crisp, this game just looks very very good on all levels.

As mentioned before I honestly love Lucia, I think they did fantastic with her!  Some will complain about girlfriend simulator etc but I honestly think she’s great and a really complex and fun protagonist that does rival some of the older games.  She looks fantastic too, and I’d play the whole game as her if I could.

As for gameplay, I quite like a lot of the “mundane” stuff people complain about.  I enjoyed painting the house and things.  It is just pressing buttons but many overexaggerate this as bad, it’s a small part and I find it very immersive.  I love the car customisation as well, and the clothes and everything.

I will say, it doesn’t feel like GTA to me.  I can’t just get out my car, get another one off the street easily and fast, go on a police chase and then take over that car and get it painted etc.  they’ve changed the police and removed car ownership to the point it doesn’t feel like GTA.  But I do like it in its own right.  This could have been a new IP and I’d be thrilled with the driving and things.  But as GTA6 I was expecting a bit faster pace and more action.  But overall the gameplay is okay.

I find the game and world very immersive and it’s been fun to find the collectibles, there are funny trading cards and I love the TV.  As usual the radio is fantastic and I like far more stations than usual.

So my final score?  Probably 7.5.  I think it’s a good game.  Best Game of all time?  No that’s nonsense.  Game of the Year?  No I liked Zelda more.  Best GTA?  Not right now, but I’m only halfway, if it gets a good ending it might get close we’ll see.   But I would recommend it just for the graphics and to see the cultural phenomenon that it is.

author: AufsAuge
quote:
I only got an account to actually rate it so yeah don't expect me to review more than this one here.

For me it’s a 5/10 at most. I find the story boring and seriously lacking. Missions are over before anything really happens, and the cutscenes, while well made, bored me to death. I’m in Chapter 3 and just finished Raul’s mission, and I’m sorry, but it’s not good. The planning is up until now non existent. If you thought you would maybe plan a big heist until now? Yeah tough luck buddy, there is no planning. 
Both Jason and Lucia are exhausting to play. Lucia in chapter one is constantly doing **** and catching one stray bullet after another for her probation. Like why are you INSISTING to do a job with Jason AND your ankle monitor, stay at home for ONCE. She doesn't get better for me, and I was excited to hjave her as playable character. I catch myself just playing dress-up with Lucia and hoping I don’t have to play them together. Jason can barely hit an enemy even when he’s standing right in front of him. Also Jason is just there it seems, he doesn't really do anything else. He had a nice quiet and low criminal life which was perfect for him. I really don't think their relationship is anything more than a fling for me. 
Lucia, on the other hand, makes me angry with her constant drive to do some **** to get money. I actually found the start not too bad. I didn’t mind doing all those chores before Lucia got out of prison, but as soon as she did, she got on my nerves fast, trying to force us into working for her con bestie and her **** DJ/mafia boyfriend. Donnie felt like an afterthought, as someone once said on the web. For me he had some Lamar vibes, just not in the funny way, more in the infuriating way. Cal is just there, and so are Lucias friends. They all feel so unpolished and bland that I could barely remember them by the time I reached Rauls mission. (You can see I rant over those 2 protagonists, you get my point they are maybe the worst from all the other games in comparison)
The world, on the other hand, is wonderful, beautiful and detailed, with some great NPC moments, like the guy ranting about being spied on by an elite agency right before his head gets blown off in front of you, or the cop annoyed at how “indecent” Lucia is dressed ( I dressed her in a sequin dress with a very low cut and some high heels). It’s funny and strange, but it doesn’t get the game to a 10/10 for me. I really miss the obscure, over-the-top action and craziness of the older games. The hair is something that I found the most amazing. Lucias actress even made her movements seem more natural than Jasons "I have to scratch my beard every 10 or so seconds" actor.

I didn’t have any game-breaking bugs, but more than once the minimap disappeared and I had to open the map just to bring it back. I don’t know if that’s a bug or if it’s supposed to vanish that quickly. The most I had were more frame drops.

It is not perfect as most critics are telling you. It is not the over the top crazy that made the franchise what it is, like it feels more as if Red dead redemption got a modern part in their franchise. Which if you loved those, you will love this game, but it just isn't for me unfortunately. I will still play it through once but I will likely never play through it again considering how boring it is for me. Also my biggest wish for Rockstar. PLEASE fix the auto aim, I am **** at aiming and as of right now it hits the enemy not even once.

author: Rosenrot88
quote: 60 ore di gioco, fin dal primo minuto del lancio, ho finalmente finito GTA 6. E il finale l’ha resa ancora peggiore. Sarò onesto: la grafica è straordinaria e Vice City è la città più dettagliata mai costruita. Ma è lì che finisce tutto. L’atmosfera da gangster è svanita. Questo sembra più una storia di relazioni femminista che un gioco GTA. Rockstar ha trasformato Jason in un patetico zerbino. Compri fiori a Lucia, ripari il lavandino di Mandy, fai le sue commissioni e la tieni felice, altrimenti il tuo indicatore di relazione cala. Mandy flirta con Jason, il gioco ti dà scelte di dialogo, e poi non succede niente, perché Rockstar dice che tradire non è “complementare al sentimento e alle motivazioni” della storia. Le prostitute sono sparite per la prima volta da GTA 3, e non puoi rubare le migliori auto fino al Capitolo 3. 5 capitoli, 91 missioni, e la maggior parte sono faccende noiose. Il Capitolo 2 è puro riempitivo. L’atto finale ruota attorno a un hard disk con pettegolezzi su un senatore. Poi i poliziotti intrappolano Jason e Lucia su un ponte, e hai una sola scelta: non arrenderti e muoiono in macchina tenendosi per mano, o arrenditi e Jason finisce in prigione mentre Lucia se ne va libera con suo figlio. Il miglior finale è bloccato dietro un indicatore di relazione pieno e 2 milioni di dollari risparmiati. Dopo i crediti, il gioco si riavvolge semplicemente e ti chiede se sei “pronto” di nuovo. I codici cheat si sbloccano solo dopo l’ultima missione, quando non c’è più niente da fare. Niente replay delle missioni, solo 15 slot di salvataggio, 100 dollari per il viaggio veloce, e è bloccato a 30 FPS, persino su PS5 Pro. Rockstar lo chiama una storia d’amore. Io lo chiamo un lavoro da babysitter con un livello di ricercato. Tommy Vercetti ha preso il controllo di Vice City. Jason chiede il permesso. 13 anni e 80 dollari, e la ricompensa è una scelta tra morire e prigione. Il mio punteggio: 3/10. Il GTA meno gangster mai realizzato. Seguitemi, continuerò a postare recensioni di GTA 6, gameplay e segreti

author: Devilson47
quote:
The main problem with GTA 6 is that it was designed for a different target audience than the previous installments in the franchise. It's "Bonnie and Clyde" story would of been great as an RDR game, but going that route in a GTA game made it inevitable that it wouldn't meet the expectations of people who waited 13 years that didn't want a story heavily affected by the romantic relationship between the two protagonists.

 That being said, the physics and the level of detail in the game are second to none. It would of been nice to enjoy those improvements in 60 fps, but the current gen hardware seems incapable of doing that. A next gen version of this game with an online mode that has the freedom of GTA 5 would be the perfect game imo.

author: PaulaAmato
quote:
This is The second game My Fiance suggested I play. 

I honestly came into this not knowing what to expect He made me Play Baldur's gate 3 first with him and maybe the aspects of that game when it came to character interactions and the world furthermore story Kept me from fully enjoying This game. 

First it's weird How this game portrays itself opposed to have being told it's satirical of American culture, its Commentary on Capitalism and other Socio-economic issues. It lacks in that department especially in it's Story as it's a Copy of the obvious legend of Bonny and Clyde. 

Speaking of Bonny Clyde I found myself drawn to Lucia not because I am a woman but mostly the fact she's strong willed and Knows how to survive a tough situation, yet I'm also disappointed in the fact that is her only best quality in terms as a character and to her Counter part, Jason he clearly reminds me of my silent but ever so resourceful partner though without the ability to be engaging outside of his random Shenanigans. Like Jason though my partner does find himself in rather awkward funny positions too though. Also what was that Voice acting for Jason it's rather uncanny. 

When my Partner laid his head on my lap I was busy Making the two main characters go out on dates and show eachother love that's one aspect I believe the game captured well. The love was unconditional as unrealistic it was when you maxed out as it lacked friction. Because even though my Partner showers me with love as I do the same, we sometimes do Bud heads over the smallest things. It would've been nice if Overspending your money and savings in the game meant Lucia or Jason text the other rather irritated or they Jab each other at who annoys who the most outside of scripted interaction. 

The Story it's a 6 for me... As I have said it's just an unoriginal Bonny and Clyde story. It lacked depth and a little bit of Finesse... Their kid personally for me should've gotten a lot more screen time and what I mean by that is We should've seen some yearning parental urge from Lucia and Jason either stalking the kid, checking in secretly be allowed to leave some money Via a backdoor and stuff to further make it feel like they're parents. 

The Gameplay for my first Open world Sandbox whatever my fiance calls it... was probably the most brained turned off fun I've had. From the clothes, styling, cars and Interactions with random strangers I was having fun I was giggling at every Interaction. Though my partner was disappointed I did spend my time Being a bad person I enjoyed the gameplay. 

A nice 7/10 Might play once more but that's it.

But once you strip away the hype and actually play it, I find that GTA 6 truly excels in very few areas. The open world and the sheer number of interactions are impressive, but that alone doesn’t make an exceptional game.

The story moves slowly, and the characters have surprisingly little personality. Jason, in particular, feels flat. He lacks the charisma and distinctive personality that would make me invested in him as a protagonist. As impressive as the world is, I also want a story and characters that give me a reason to keep playing.

I also wonder whether Rockstar would have been better off waiting for a next-generation console release. Perhaps that would have been a better opportunity to deliver on the enormous expectations.

The perfect scores from critics are difficult for me to understand, especially alongside the criticism from players. It makes me question how much Rockstar’s reputation and the immense hype influence those assessments. Of course, opinions differ, but I see clear shortcomings that are difficult to reconcile with a score of 100. For me, GTA 6 doesn’t deserve that score, let alone the title of “the greatest game of all time.”

author: Akhelian
quote: The graphics and world design are great. However, some of the mechanics aren't, such as flying, crash sites, gunfights, collisions, etc. (Maybe it's because the game runs at 30 FPS, I don't know.)You can tell that the game makes your character tougher than in previous GTA games because they want less-skilled players to be able to enjoy it as well. That's something I don't like.This is an $80–$100 game rated 18+, and I believe the core target audience should be the people who have grown up alongside the franchise since its launch. (I'm a gamer, and I've been playing GTA since GTA 1.)I expected more freedom when it comes to the characters I play. For example, I don't want to spend my time pleasing a woman by being her lapdog, buying her everything she wants, and listening to her complaints in a game called Grand Theft Auto. If that's what you enjoy, go play The **** can't do as much as you could in the previous game to live out that gangster fantasy. It feels like they've taken away some of the freedom that made GTA what it is.When you use social issues as an excuse to take away players' freedom within a game, you end up undermining the very realism you're supposedly trying to defend. You want everyone to be able to succeed in the game, but let's not forget that this is an R-rated, 18+ franchise. You know exactly who your core audience is. Yet instead of standing by that audience, you try to appeal to such a broad demographic that you end up exposing the game to criticism like this. We've waited 13 years for this game, only to see it lose some of the things that made us love the franchise in the first place.I respect different opinions and perspectives, so don't get me wrong. But these themes have always been part of GTA. They were never pushed in quite the same way they seem to be today, nor were they used as a vehicle for promoting minority agendas. Instead, GTA has always tackled controversial social issues through its storytelling, satire, and skits. Call it dark humor, social commentary, or criticism; that's what made the franchise special. It presented these subjects in its own way without sacrificing the freedom of the player.I don't know. I just can't enjoy the game with the same enthusiasm I used to have. We play games to escape what's happening in the real world, clear our heads, and have a good time. When you bring the same issues we're trying to get away from into the games we turn to for entertainment, what happens when people eventually have nowhere left to escape? I'm genuinely **** recognition of the 13 years we've waited for this game, I'll give it a 5/10.

quote: GTA VI — 7/10GTA VI è un gioco incredibile sotto certi aspetti, ma anche una bella delusione sotto altri. E sinceramente, dopo tutta questa attesa, mi aspettavo di meglio su diverse cose.Partiamo da quello che funziona: la mappa è spettacolare. Enorme, piena di dettagli, di eventi e di situazioni diverse. È probabilmente la cosa che mi ha impressionato di più. Anche le innovazioni tecniche sono notevoli, e su questo c'è poco da discutere. Il lavoro fatto sul mondo di gioco è **** problema è tutto il **** storia è noiosa, e i protagonisti pure. Jason e Lucia non mi hanno preso per niente. Per quanto sia curato tutto quello che gli gira intorno, ho trovato la loro storia davvero poco **** c'è l'intelligenza artificiale, che doveva essere chissà cosa e invece rimane parecchio stupida. Gli NPC continuano ad avere comportamenti assurdi e la polizia, soprattutto quando hai poche stelle, è spesso ridicola. Da un gioco di questa portata mi aspettavo decisamente di **** sistema d'onore, o Profilo criminale, per come è stato concepito mi fa proprio schifo. E non parlo soltanto delle conseguenze delle proprie azioni, ma anche di come sembra influenzare le sparatorie. Mi è capitato di sparare anche sette o otto colpi a una persona e vederla ancora viva, semplicemente ferita a terra. Sembra quasi che il gioco voglia a tutti i costi considerarla soltanto ferita, anche quando quello che hai appena visto non è minimamente credibile. Se questo è il risultato del nuovo sistema, per me è una regressione tecnica bella e buona. Non basta aggiungere una meccanica per chiamarla innovazione.E vogliamo parlare della fisica e delle esplosioni? Brutte, ma brutte davvero. Sono tra le cose che mi hanno deluso maggiormente. Considerando quanto è avanzato tecnicamente il resto del gioco, fanno ancora più impressione in negativo. Secondo me serviranno almeno quattro o cinque patch per sistemare decentemente certe cose. Ci sono anche bug e glitch minori, niente di devastante, ma ci sono.E sì, non puoi neanche andare a puttane. Una cosa che potevi fare nei vecchi GTA, qui è stata tolta. Anche questa è una scelta che non mi **** soprattutto, GTA VI secondo me ha perso un po' del vecchio spirito di GTA. In diversi momenti sembra quasi di giocare a Life Sim 6, più che a Grand Theft Auto. Tutto questo realismo, tutte queste meccaniche da simulatore di vita... boh. A me sembra che qualcosa si sia perso per **** è questo che mi dà più fastidio: hanno realizzato una mappa assurda, piena di dettagli e di cose da fare, ma poi ci sono aspetti fondamentali del gioco che non mi convincono per niente.7/10. Un gioco sicuramente impressionante, con un mondo aperto incredibile e innovazioni tecniche importanti, ma anche con difetti che per me pesano parecchio. La mappa da sola non basta a farmi chiudere un occhio su storia, ****, IA, fisica e certe scelte di **** aspettavo decisamente di più, soprattutto da Rockstar.

author: Marie-Eleonore
quote:
Plutôt mitigé.
Beaucoup de bien et de moins bien dans cette suite à GTA.
- La plupart des personnes rencontrées dans l'aventure sont extrêmement bien écrites et réalistes. Malheureusement, les personnages les moins bien écrits me semblent être Jason et Lucia. Jason est trop neutre et peu loquace, il paraît un peu trop vide. Pour Lucia, je n'arrive définitivement pas à éprouver la moindre sympathie pour une personne qui cache sa grossesse à son géniteur et qui abandonne son enfant dans un restaurant ; même après plusieurs heures à l'incarner, elle me laisse de marbre. Je trouve ce couple peu attachant. Commettre délits et crimes pour espérer récupérer la garde de leur enfant, tout en sachant qu'on leur a retiré cette même garde à cause de leurs crimes et délits, me paraît très peu réfléchi. J'ai beaucoup de mal à m'investir dans une histoire où le postulat de départ est si stupide.
-Côté gameplay c'est très réaliste et immersif, mais malheureusement extrêmement lent et très laborieux par moment. Les gunfights sont parfois brouillons et illisible, surtout en intérieur.
- Les déplacements sont pénibles et l'on passe la plupart de son temps à conduire. Les va-et-vient en voiture finissent par être pénibles au bout de quelques heures de jeu. 
- Il y énormément d'activités diverses, mais malheureusement très répétitives. 
- Beaucoup trop de QTE à mon goût. Mais également beaucoup de faux choix sous forme de faux QTE (pour exemple, le collier de Lucia que l'on donne a la mégère du motel comme gage, que l'on fasse le QTE ou non).
- Le jeu est extrêmement beau, le plus beau à ce jour sans doute. Mais il y a un grain flou constant sur ps5 et Tv en 4k.
- J'ai eu quelques bugs comme des voitures qui pop au dernier moment où des pnj qui disparaissent par magie, mon arme en main qui n'apparaît pas et des bugs de collisions. 

C'est donc un GTA a la sauce RDR2. Beaucoup vont adorer le côté très immersif et propice au RP. Et d'autre vont détester, troquant le fun pour avoir un côté beaucoup plus réaliste. Ne reste plus qu'à souhaiter que le Online ne s'inspire pas de celui de RDR2, qui est de loin le plus barbant et fade des modes Online que RockstarGame ait jamais proposé.

author: Elusi
quote:
Une grosse déception après plusieurs heures de jeu.

Après avoir largement avancé dans GTA VI, mon avis a considérablement changé. Si les premières heures m'avaient énormément convaincu, l'expérience devient malheureusement de plus en plus redondante au fil de la progression.

Le jeu possède pourtant de véritables qualités : une réalisation impressionnante, un univers travaillé, des personnages intéressants et des choix qui apportent une certaine variété aux cinématiques et à l'histoire.

Cependant, ces qualités ne suffisent plus à compenser les problèmes rencontrés. Les missions finissent par donner une impression de répétition, les bugs sont beaucoup trop fréquents et l'optimisation laisse clairement à désirer.

Le plus regrettable reste le 30 FPS. Dans un jeu aussi ambitieux, cette limitation nuit considérablement à la fluidité et finit par casser une partie de l'immersion. Certains ralentissements viennent encore aggraver le problème.

Je reconnais le travail réalisé par Rockstar, mais un jeu de cette envergure doit aussi proposer une expérience techniquement solide et un contenu suffisamment varié pour maintenir l'intérêt sur la durée.

Ma note passe donc à 5/10. GTA VI a un énorme potentiel et de grandes qualités, mais après avoir dépassé l'effet de découverte, ses défauts prennent malheureusement beaucoup trop de place dans l'expérience.

author: Izanagiin
quote: I'll be honest as possible because I wasn't unfortunately paid by Rockstar (though you can always hit me up if you want me to change the review), the game is just okay. You can tell it took a lot of the fundamentals of Red Dead Redemption 2 but I don't know, this game is... interesting. It's definitely a GTA game but at the same time it just really isn't and feels more Saints Row than anything. There's a lot of questionable things and design put into the game and while I personally do think it can be fun at times, it's also just a little off putting sometimes. Like all throughout me playing I would think to myself, "well, I guess it's a good game, but I wouldn't say it's THAT good." Yeah, I genuinely think Red Dead Redemption 2 simply is Rockstar's magnum opus. They really wanted to imitate that formula and stick it into a GTA game, but they're just too fundamentally different. Also, it's true the game does have a bug every here and there which is bizarre considering how long this was in development for. Others can try to justify the 30 fps with older games, but nice try, guys, those are games made for older gen hardware years ago. It's not 2018 anymore crazy I know, right? Time flies. Yeah, it's decent. Ball and gun gamers will think it's the holy grail of gaming, but it's far from that and this is also far from being an innovation or revolution in the gaming landscape. After all, no other game developers will have the budget of a billion dollars or the time they had to make this thing. On the subject of development and anticipation, I'm looking forward to Persona 6 though. Don't be surprised if that game mogs GTA 6, but the critics won't have much to say about it because they won't be receiving paychecks there. Have fun, ball and gun gamers, you could use it before you expect GTA 7 in 20 years. I just hope Rockstar themselves take this as a lesson, gets humbled, and takes the next Red Dead Redemption again or something with genuine consideration instead of relying on namesake alone or greedy shareholders. Don't listen to any of them, they just want to ruin gaming like they ruined movies and riddled pop music with industry plants

author: intisuyay7
quote: GTA 6 has a brutally detailed world and moments that work, I won’t deny that. Leonida feels big, alive, and has a scale few games ever reach. The chemistry between Jason and Lucia — even if it’s forced by the narrative — has a certain appeal, but that’s about as far as the good stuff goes. The bad part is that Rockstar has forgotten what made GTA special. I’m not looking for a life simulator like The Sims when I boot up a GTA. I want irreverent, limitless, absurd, and liberating fun. Here they prioritize ultra-realism so much that they end up cutting exactly that, because I constantly feel the game holding me back and the overall tone feels more controlled and less wild. The narrative is also way too imposing; you shouldn’t give me such a huge world to explore and then stop me from playing however I want with a story that’s so extremely rigid. And yes, sacrificing fluidity (those noticeable and annoying 30 fps) just for iguanas with more polygons in a single eye is still questionable. I’d rather have a game that feels good to play than one that looks too perfect but moves like it’s stuck in the past. This launch has been full of bugs, clipping, crashes, and lost progress. After 13 years and such an obscene budget, that’s nowhere near “normal.” The game coming out like this is definitely a failure. Rockstar delivered something ambitious and technically impressive, but they also lost part of the cheeky, irreverent spirit a lot of us were looking for. And that needs to be said clearly.
