author: Shadowexd
quote: After finishing this game (yes, I sat through it, played for two straight days, and reached the ending), I can confidently say that GTA 6 left me disappointed. One of my biggest issues is Lucia and Jason’s relationship, which ultimately turns large portions of this game into what feels more like a relationship simulator than a Grand Theft Auto experience.Their relationship is incredibly one-sided. Jason spends much of the story feeling less like an equal protagonist and more like Lucia’s errand boy. He constantly follows her lead, does what she’s told, and seems to exist primarily to support her character. At times, his behavior comes across as submissive to the point where he loses any sense of individuality. Meanwhile, Lucia is positioned as the dominant personality in the relationship, making Jason feel more like a side character in his own story. This isn’t about wanting Lucia to be less capable or independent. It’s about wanting both protagonists to have equal agency, personality, and development. Jason desperately needed more of his own identity, motivations, and moments where he could stand on his own. Instead, he often feels like a simp with very little personality outside of his relationship with Lucia.This is not what I personally want from a GTA **** second major issue is the game’s performance. Having a game of this scale run at 30 FPS in the era we’re living in today is extremely disappointing. Regardless of how visually impressive the game is, 30 FPS makes the experience feel unnecessarily restricted, especially when modern gaming has made higher frame rates an increasingly reasonable expectation.Thirdly, the game is far too restrictive in what it allows players to do. Why, in a crime game, am I not allowed to run over a crowd of protesters? It sounds ridiculous without context, but hear me out. You’re allowed to kill innocent civilians and even dogs, yet certain situations suddenly impose restrictions on what you’re allowed to do. Why can’t I steal cars in my own neighborhood and cause absolute chaos around me? Why does the game seem so selective about when it wants to give players freedom?This is Grand Theft Auto. Freedom, unpredictability, and player-created chaos are fundamental parts of the franchise. When those elements feel restricted, it takes away from what makes GTA **** be fair, the game has some genuinely beautiful mechanics, impressive graphics, and an incredible amount of production value. You can clearly see the time, money, and effort Rockstar invested into creating this world. Unfortunately, technical and visual achievements alone don’t make a great **** story simply doesn’t hold up to what I expected from a Grand Theft Auto title. The characters, particularly Jason, needed more depth, and the relationship between the two protagonists ultimately took away from my enjoyment of the narrative. I wanted to experience an incredible crime story, not spend so much of my time feeling like I was watching a relationship **** the end of the day, I honestly think GTA V is a better overall GTA experience. That is a difficult thing to say because I wanted so badly to love GTA VI. I went into this game expecting something that would redefine the franchise, but I didn’t walk away having the incredible experience I was hoping for.Rockstar has demonstrated that it can create an exceptional narrative with Red Dead Redemption 2. I hope the company takes some lessons from that experience when developing future GTA stories. Give us characters with real depth, meaningful relationships, compelling individual storylines, and the freedom to create our own **** VI is an incredibly impressive technical achievement, but for me, being visually impressive isn’t enough. I wanted a great Grand Theft Auto game. Unfortunately, I didn’t get that experience.

author: amoomeara
quote:
From someone who grew up playing 3 then Vice City, etc. - This feels like the least impactful.  I'll start by saying that.

The reason the boring, mundane tasks and slower parts of RDR2 were welcome was because the story and it's characters were written extremely well.  I have to say, Jason and Lucia are just kind of mediocre (Lucia has far more a personality than Jason).  

Negatives - There are really no new mechanics, just old things from GTA games but with some button changes.  The RDR2 interaction options have just been carried over with literally no change to it.  We have games like Crimson Desert where you can have multiple branching dialogue options with NPCs that can lead to discoveries, etc.  You'd think Rockstar could have built on it.  I haven't completed the entire story so all I can say is so far, it's just okay.  Nothing crazy, nothing terrible, but nothing incredibly moving.  I did also experience weird lag in moments, pop-in, and moments during missions, especially when things got chaotic, where the game would just freeze up and I would have to restart the whole game.  Oh, and we waited like 8+ years or whatever for this.

Positives - Obviously the graphics are great, the world is massive and it really does feel alive.  The NPCs are very reactive to what you do (which is why I was surprised you couldn't really interact with them other than the basic Greet/Taunt).  I like the more random encounters - like finding illegal operations, glad they FINALLY added loot and fences - but once again, RDR2 already had that so nothing really new.

quote: Solid but overhyped game. The over realism is not for me. I am very annoyed by some of the new features like shops closing when you commited a crime nearby, kind of kills the momentum for me. Generally, I find it less fun to play than GTA V or GTA IV at the moment. I'm also having performances issues on PS5, game running at about 15 to 25 fps most of the time. The story so far is good but really not balanced between Lucia, who is really fleshed out and interesting, and the guy, whom I can't even remember the name of, given how hollow his personnality is. His only character trait is being chill/not caring, and that really not interesting in my opinion. I loved GTA V's multiple characters because they all had such fleshed out personnalities. Here, I think Lucia should have been the only playable character. Maybe not for gameplay reasons, but story-wise. As for the "revolutionary" aspect, it's not here. I have not felt it at all. All this GTA VI does, Cyberpunk 2077 and Read Dead Redemption 2 did before him. Yes, the city is very lively and a lot happens, yes characters shot at reacts realistically, yes the AI is really good. But all of that is flavour, not core gameplay. Speaking of the core gameplay... The driving does not feel as good as GTA V. I don't know why that is, but it doesn't. I already said I wasn't a fan of the realism features. Generally speaking, this game is less arcade than the previous iterations of the franchise. You still have funny goofy things, and I'm all for it, but gameplay wise that is the case. The freedom you have in engering buildings and doing your own robberies is great, but not revolutionary either. author: Mochaep
quote: After more than 20 hours in Leonida, I’m left mostly disappointed. The technical side of Grand Theft Auto VI is genuinely impressive, but the story and characters drag the whole experience down **** world is the strongest part of the game. It feels full and alive. There’s a ton of stuff to discover, Easter eggs everywhere, and the level of detail and interaction is excellent. Graphics are top-tier — lighting, environments, and overall visual quality look fantastic on PS5 with zero performance issues or major bugs in my time with it. Driving and shooting feel good, and the map itself is one of the best Rockstar has ever built.Unfortunately, almost everything else **** story is predictable and linear. It only ever shows the world through the couple’s perspective, which feels limited compared to GTA 5’s three distinct protagonists with their own backgrounds and storylines. Lucia is just boring. She makes Jason feel weak and constantly slows him down. There’s this constant pressure for Jason to please her, but it never goes the other way. The whole narrative focuses on them trying to earn a better future for their kid, yet it refuses to lean into the actual risks and chaos that come with the robberies. Jason ends up locked out of a lot of activities because of her, which kills the fantasy. This is a GTA game — it should be about doing the crazy, over-the-top stuff you can’t do in real life, not being restricted by relationship dynamics.Other characters don’t leave much of an impression either. They’re barely involved and lack any real personality or strong behavior. Jason is the only one who feels somewhat decent by default, but even he gets held back by the writing.Some of the new systems feel completely out of place for a GTA game. The game actively pushes you toward less damage and fewer casualties — you’ll get a sad little icon when you kill people and a smile when you don’t. That’s not GTA. There’s also a lock-on system for stealing certain cars that just feels restrictive. Police chases are basically useless; drive reasonably fast and the cops lose you almost immediately. Missions lean too heavily on Lucia as well, which only makes the pacing problems worse.Biggest strengths: the graphics and the living, interactive world.Biggest weaknesses: the story, Lucia, the lack of that classic GTA freedom (including no prostitution), and the locked **** the end, GTA 6 looks and feels like a next-gen open world, but it doesn’t play or write like a classic Rockstar game. Bring back Dan Houser and the team that made GTA 5. This one feels like it lost the plot.

author: edobellic
quote:
To be honest, this story really struggles to keep you hooked. The plot starts off cliché and drags along at a slow pace, never quite building the momentum that makes you want to push forward from mission to mission.
What hurts the most is the lack of that sharp, over-the-top irony that has always made the series iconic. It misses characters capable of stealing the scene with punchy lines and absurd situations, like Lamar in GTA V, Roman in GTA IV, or Big Smoke in San Andreas. Jason especially lacks any real personality, feeling more like someone who blindly follows whatever Lucia says, even when she's clearly wrong. Without biting writing and larger than life personalities, the dialogue ends up feeling flat and predictable.
The sense of scale and freedom is also a big step down. In past GTA games, protagonists did it all storming the FIB and IAA without hesitation, stealing nuclear warheads, and pulling off heists worth millions upon millions. Here, you simply don't get the chance to experience that kind of wild, high-stakes chaos. On the gameplay side, things don't feel much better. The overall control feels clunky and sluggish, lacking responsiveness when you need pace and immediacy. I don't mind the realism but stealing cars is made way too difficult compared to how smooth and immediate it should be.
All in all, it leaves the impression of an experience that struggles to take off in both writing and mechanics, falling short of the wit, boldness, and smoothness you'd expect from the series.

quote:
This game confused me.
One time, it tries to be this cinematic RDR2 style of game and on other hand it's trying to capture that GTAV feels that resulted in mixed experience. 

Pro:
1. Graphics technology: There's no contests about this one aspect, everyone and their grandmother agree that this is one aspect that they delivered the most.

Con:
1. Story and plot: As I said in my opening review, it's a mixed bag of presentation where the final results are just mediocre especially with the 2 new characters Jason and Lucia. Jason is basically nonexistent in the game and it's just a yes man throughout the game following Lucia like some kind of sheep. Meanwhile Lucia here acts like this girl boss and almost to the point of annoying and cumbersome. I don't want to spoil the ending or anything, but let's just say the story insists upon itself too much and trying too hard to convey a moral message that doesn't make sense at all in a GTA game.
2. Gameplay: the first 6 - 10 hours of this game is just chore after chore, I guess there's a reason why people dubbed this game as Chore Simulator. The shooting, animation is the stuffs you expect from Rockstar. Having played RDR2, it's almost a carbon copy minus the deadeye mechanic. Talking about quest design, it's just the usual Rockstar formula (Accept a mission, drive here, get a call, conflict and bang bang, drive your car, get out the hotzone, cleared the mission). I get it, if it doesn't broke don't fix it, but it's really getting stale and formulaic.
3. Game's performance: There's nothing to say here if you have already watched few videos out there explaining the performance issues this game had. The fact that having UP to 30FPS in 2026 is quite confusing and updated to be quite honest. I guess it's more about pumping the realism aspect of the game to the fullest disregarding the performance and frame pacing. If you want the best experience, play it on PS5 Pro albeit also with 30FPS cap.
4. Paywalls and "Hidden" subscriptions inside a SINGLE PLAYER game, that's just something else. I get it if it's for online purposes, but the game's focus right now is still about single player experience. 

TLDR: Saw the 99/100 review score of this game and I tried it. Once again, it's not 99/100 for sure and it's just obvious that the corruption within the game journalist these days is just so deep and blatant. I rated it 50/100 for now because it's a lackluster experience so far aside from the eye candy.

author: Coffeepotamago
quote:
It's a good Rockstar game. Innovative and intuitive compared to its predecessors, and there's no denying the technical and creative work that went into it.
But is it a good GTA game? Not necessarily.

There's a distinction between making a technically impressive and well-designed game and delivering an experience that lives up to the identity and expectations of an established franchise.

Innovation alone isn't enough to justify every design decision, and being a Rockstar production shouldn't automatically shield it from criticism.

Ultimately, I can acknowledge what the game does well while still feeling that the overall experience falls short when compared to it's predecessor. A game shouldn't be judged solely by its technical achievements or the reputation of the studio behind it.

I'm not expecting a game to be flawless to deserve a high score. But there's a difference between recognizing excellence and treating a highly anticipated release as though it can do no wrong.
Ultimately, and again, I think it's a good Rockstar game, but not the best GTA title in the franchise. for me, that distinction matters.

author: Abdinuyasha
quote: Unfortunately, this is just another GTA installment that, aside from better graphics and more mini-games, doesn't really offer anything beyond what GTA 5 already provided. The story suffers from many dull stretches that make the game genuinely annoying at times. It’s a matter of personal preference, but I’m just not a fan of this slow, forced, "realistic" approach in GTA 6—something that already bothered me immensely in RDR2. If I wanted to simulate everyday life, I’d buy a simulator game, not a GTA title. Consequently, the straightforward, uncomplicated fun found in older entries is missing here; the game gets bogged down in overly granular animations, which completely destroys the flow of gameplay. Furthermore, many animations are inconsistent—for instance, when the character equips diving gear, there’s no actual animation; it simply pops onto their back. It’s not a bad game, per se, but it just doesn’t resonate with me, and many of its questionable design choices actively undermine the enjoyment. The 99% critic approval rating is absolute nonsense; most outlets likely gave it an inflated score just to ensure Rockstar keeps sending them early access builds—there are plenty of documentaries covering this very practice. Other games, like *Dragon’s Dogma 2*, were penalized for lacking a 60 FPS mode, yet for GTA 6, this doesn't even seem to warrant a negative mention. On top of that, there are numerous game-breaking bugs, glitches, and other technical issues. While it’s not as completely unplayable as *Cyberpunk 2077* was at launch, these problems are significant enough that they should have been highlighted and reflected in a lower score; the game is far from technically polished, and these issues have a noticeably negative impact on the overall experience.  Because the game struggles with technical issues, I would give it a 6. If it ends up running better technically thanks to future patches, I might bump it up to a 7 at most—but no higher.

author: Krankey
quote:
GTA 6 represents the very pinnacle of what a game can achieve technically.
It's huge and it's beautiful but that's where the praise stops.

Unfortunately GTA 6 also represents everything wrong with the gaming industry and AAA gaming in the last decade.
From reviewers who are praising it for every aspect except it being fun, to a developer who is so preoccupied with depth of systems they forgot that gaming is supposed to be escapism.

For a game which has been around nearly 30 years to have so badly lost it's identity is mind blowing and nothing shows this more than the updates to the wanted system.
The level of detail in this system is staggering with changes to appearance, weapons being carried, your car etc all helping to you evade cops.
But on top of that is the new criminal profile system where how you perform a crime or play generally the game affects a profile about who you are.

I'm going to go out on a limb here and assume that no one bought GTA 6 to spend time carefully managing their in game persona but I can guarantee that a lot of people bought it to blow stuff up and cause general mischief with little to no lasting impact.

And that's the root issue here, Rockstar have completely forgotten that this franchise was supposed to be about a lack of consequence, freedom, stupidity and being able to let off steam.

Now we're worried that quickly dipping on the sidewalk and mowing some people down is going to affect our criminal profile too much - whatever happened to GOURANGA!?!?!
In a world where posting the wrong thing on social media can loose you your job all we wanted was to be able to do stupid things consequence free.
Another great example of this over indulgence in detail is all the useless and annoying quick time events.
Want to hot wire a car? Better start spamming some buttons!
Want to tidy up your house (why is this even a thing! This isn't power wash simulator!) Better start spamming some buttons!
Want to use your phone? Better start spamming some buttons to take you into about 8 different menus.
Why do these exist? They add nothing positive to the gameplay experience and entirely detract from what the core of the game is about.

In trying to make the game 'more realistic' Rockstar have created so many barriers to fun - much like real life.
Finally, the complete lack of improvement from any of it's predecessors goes to show that just revisiting Vice City was all Rockstar had in mind for this game.

The UI feels like I've been huffing gas and staring at Excel, the cars still handle like a cow in a shopping cart and the control system/camera is convoluted and aiming still feels like I'm a stroke victim trying to learn to use a knife and fork again.

We'll not even get into the price tag and the fact it feels like a slideshow due to FPS drops at times.

In summary - GTA 6 is a game stood in it's own way. Everything which should make this game fun is still in the game but getting to it or the consequences for doing it just aren't worth it.

author: rmarissen26
quote: GTA 6 Review: Een visueel beest met geweldige zijzaken, maar verouderde hardware en trage systemen drukken de score​Na flink wat uren in GTA 6 te hebben gestoken blijft er vooral één gevoel hangen: dit is een gigantisch indrukwekkend project dat aan alle kanten schuurt. Als je een beetje een scherp oog hebt voor games en echt kijkt naar wat er op je scherm gebeurt, zie je meteen waar het misgaat. Framerates, traagheid, lichaamsdelen die door objecten heen gaan en een wereld die qua levensloop op den duur gaat vervelen. Toch kom ik uit op een 8.8, want er zit ook heel veel in dat gewoon heel erg goed en leuk is.​In de basis voelt GTA 6 toch als een verbeterde GTA 5, maar dan met meer kracht en zwaarte vanuit GTA 4 en Red Dead Redemption 2. Veel mensen hielden van 5, ikzelf meer van 4, en het rijden en de langzaamheid lijken gelukkig meer op 4. Alleen zit ook die dodelijke Red Dead Redemption 2 **** erin, met die langzame loopanimaties in bepaalde ruimtes. Red Dead Redemption 2 is zelf natuurlijk prachtig, maar dat trage wandelen en lopen op bepaalde plekken wordt op een gegeven moment gewoon echt vervelend. Je wilt soms gewoon normaal en vlot doorlopen, en het voelt alsof Rockstar weer teveel wilde doen op een oude generatie, waardoor er veel matigheid in sluipt. De verouderde kracht van de PS5 en PS5 Pro haalt de power van dit beestje gewoon naar beneden.​Prachtige wereld, sporten, voertuigen en side missions​Eerlijk is eerlijk: de wereld is prachtig en het is wel degelijk een mooie open wereld met veel te ontdekken en veel leuke interacties. Er zitten hier en daar echt prachtige encounters in en je kunt redelijk veel gebouwen in, al is het nog steeds te weinig. Daarnaast zijn de vele voertuigen, bestuurbare apparaten, sporten en side missions gewoon geweldig. Toch voelt het nog niet echt als de toekomst, waar ik persoonlijk al op hoopte bij GTA 5. Dat is ook mogelijk: je kunt een kleinere wereld maken met meer te doen en meer fun, in plaats van alles zo groot en massaal neer te zetten met grote, lege maar prachtige stukken ertussen.​Zodra je beter oplet, vallen ook de technische haken en ogen op. Je merkt dat die mooie buitenkant en de techniek eronder niet altijd synchroon lopen. De performance is niet strak genoeg en je ziet dat de hardware van de PS5 en Pro het zwaar heeft om dit allemaal soepel te draaien.​Schieten, slomo en oude missiestructuur​Het schieten zelf vind ik eerlijk gezegd een beetje tegenvallen. Wel super tof dat lichaamsdelen eraf kunnen vliegen nu, en die slomo hadden we natuurlijk al met Max Payne, maar het werkt wel. Het is vermakelijk in het moment, al is het ook weer niet zo dat het wiel opnieuw is uitgevonden. De missies zelf blijven toch grotendeels oude GTA-stijl: van A naar B, schiet wat mensen neer en vlucht in een auto.​Wapens uit het niets en items die in je hand ploppen​Je bestelt iets aan een bar of pakt iets uit de koelkast en het popt ineens in je hand op. Hetzelfde geldt voor het automatisch ineens aan hebben van kleding of een kogelvrij vest, of een shotgun die je van je rug naar je handen tovert zo strap. En dat je in je eigen neighborhood geen auto kunt jatten maakt het ook weer raar en beperkt.​Zwakke AI en clipping​Het ergste vond ik soms het vechten en hoe de AI reageert. Dat was echt gewoon dom oud GTA, soms slechter dan 4 nog. Vier mensen komen ineens heel onrealistisch mee vechten, terwijl een auto aanrijdt waar mensen in roepen dat je moet oprotten en opzij moet gaan terwijl je net vier man neer stompt. Die vier helpers stompte ik neer en die auto wilde er doorheen alsof er niks aan de hand was. Ze gedragen zich als een kip zonder kop en de AI is zwak. Hoofden en lichaamsdelen gaan door materiaal heen, zoals door het dak van een auto bij het eruit trekken. In gevechten schiet iemand van de zijkant, maar je hebt dat vier seconden niet door, vijf kogels in je lichaam en niks aan de hand. Wurgt iemand in de bank terwijl je gebukt zit, dan kijkt niemand op omdat je laag zit.​Het nieuwe politie-systeem gaat snel vervelen​Dat systeem wat ik zelf ooit had verzonnen met opvallen, dekking zoeken, van auto veranderen en kleding wisselen zit er nu in. Het kijkt nu goed, maar wordt waarschijnlijk heel sneu als je het kent. Ik kon zelfs door rood rijden terwijl de politie naast me stond. Mensen spelen het nu al zo: auto in een garage, bank beroven met een andere auto, met vijf sterren de garage in, omkleden, andere auto pakken en zo langs de popo rijden alsof ze geen check doen bij wie daar uit komt.​Bankroven en eindoordeel​Bankroven gaan na een tijdje vervelen met altijd dezelfde clerk-animatie die het geld geeft. Toch is GTA 6 prachtig, met geweldige voertuigen, apparaten, sporten, side missions en mooie encounters, maar de verouderde kracht van de PS5 en PS5 Pro drukt het omlaag. Ik wacht op de pc-versie met 60 fps en eventueel mods.

author: Lonstrong
quote:
Honestly, it’s a huge disappointment for me. As someone who, like many others, was expecting the absolute pinnacle of video games, I was purely let down, because from my personal experience, I’d say I enjoyed it less than GTA SA, IV and V. Even though I had heard it was supposed to be different from the other GTA installments, I hoped it wouldn’t be. I probably shouldn't have hoped for that, as it likely worsened my overall experience with the game. This is a preliminary review, and I don't think I'll finish the game until at least 2027, though I might give it another shot once it comes out on PC. 
The positives are definitely the graphics, the overall vibe of the environment, the creative attempts, and the game's length (though I'm not sure yet if that's strictly a positive or a negative). Meanwhile, the negatives for me are the characters (I just don't care about most of them in this game, unlike in previous entries where I at least cared about those close to the protagonist), the gameplay overall falls short of expectations, the realism (if I want a fairly realistic crime game, I’ll boot up Mafia 1 or 2, not GTA), and the freedom (since I absolutely love "complete" freedom in games, here I felt forced into making decisions I would normally ignore). Overall, it's a 6/10 for me, considering GTA IV is about a 7/10 in my eyes.

author: fmiryan56
quote:
I initially played this game on Xbox Series S during launch, and honestly, the experience was barely playable. Shooting felt difficult, there was noticeable input delay when steering, accelerating, and braking, and frame drops were everywhere. Because of that, I switched to PS5, where the game is honestly much more playable.

Now, for my actual review on PS5.

Gameplay: The game is impressive in many ways. Honestly, I really enjoyed my first day playing it. From simply driving around Vice City to admiring the insane level of detail, especially how almost every building seems to have an accessible interior, I was genuinely impressed.

However, by day two, after continuing the main story, I started getting bored.

Story: It's garbage. I honestly can't believe this is supposed to be a GTA game.

Unlike GTA V or RDR2, where almost every mission made me feel motivated to keep playing and find out what happens next, GTA 6 barely gives me any reason to stay invested in its story.

The writing is well below mediocre. It almost feels like nobody even tried to put together a compelling story, as if this were some rushed one-night project.

Gameplay mechanics: There are plenty of improvements, but unfortunately, there are also a lot of downgrades. I don't want to spoil too much, but what I can say is that the developers seem to have barely made an effort to make the gameplay as enjoyable as it was in GTA V.

Graphics: Honestly, they look amazing. No complaints here

Bugs and performance: There are way too many bugs, ranging from seriously annoying ones to relatively minor issues. Sure, patches might fix some of them eventually, but honestly, the game's launch-day experience is terrible compared to GTA V and RDR2. It's almost on the same level as Cyberpunk 2077 at launch — almost, not quite.

Overall, despite its impressive graphics and world design, GTA 6 has been a disappointing experience for me so far.

author: topicchaotic
quote:
So this game is not a masterpiece by any means nor it pushes any boundaries of the medium.  After playing through the game, it is really nothing special. 

Bland story that should be some sort of Bonny and Clyde inspired s**t. Nope its not, its just a nothing burger of the story. These people didnt even read the Wikipedia entry about Bonny and Clyde. 

Unimaginative characters - Jason and Lucia really feel like side characters in this story. They are not smart nor cunning. Stuff happens and quests just come to them. They are not the ones moving this plot forward. Both feel stiff, but Lucia is just a peace of s**t of a human being to her new-born kid and then to Jason for the rest of the game(This wasn't necessary!).

Gameplay - You cant steal from neighbours for some reason, you cant cheat on Lucia, there are no hookers anymore, you legit cant even buy your own property anymore(Why???), gunfights are nothing special and these devs that are working at Rockstar right now, don't even understand why RDR2 had "dead eye" mechanic so of course they copied it here it GTA(ffs!) it just doesn't make any sense! Both characters control the same and have same capabilities, but its good that Jason is ex military just for Marketing Material purposes. You wont see him having better arsenal than Lucia, also Lucia wont be better at fighting than Jason - so I guess good luck playing the same way with both of them. 

Sound: Its fine I guess. But after 13 years of waiting for this game and hearing that there is barely any difference in sound when firing with different **** just disappointing. 

Performance/Graphics: 30FPS in 2026 is rough man. This game has been in the making for 13 years, with active development starting around 2020(Almost 7 years at the time of release!) and all we got is 30 frame on every console, PS5-Pro included. Panning the camera hurts my eyes and it is really noticeable all the time, walking straight can feel smooth at times but come on. This should not be the standard in 2026! Include constant frame drops that I experienced.., yea they should have toned it down on CPU intensive tasks. Graphics are at times amazing and it looks good on screenshots. When you actively play and there is motion, it doesn't look as good for some reason. I even noticed that from a cut scene to cut scene character models can look less detailed and then it comes back. 

Fun: Well I guess there is some fun to be had for sure(and some people may even enjoy just shooting trough the city), but the restrictions of where and who you can shoot, not being able to steal from neighbours, non imaginative mele and gunplay mechanics are a deal breaker for me. Yes the world feels at least alive and it looks really good but I am not here to wonder modern day Miami its just a modern city nothing special. To that point in nightclubs the NPCs stand firm on the ground like a stone wall and you cant push them?, just antagonize sometimes(its just weird to me). And the stripper animations are nothing special, they mostly twerk and that's about it. 
All in all, this is not a perfect game but it is also not the worst game ever made. Its just mid and average. Its not 10x better in every aspect from GTA5. But since we were waiting for it for 13 years, Rockstar wanting 100€ (for a full version of the game) and the hype and early access reviews calling it "the best game ever made" intertwined with performance issues and just 30FPS, the "meh" feeling I got from this game is in my eyes jus an average 5/10 and I think is a fair score. Feeling disappointed in the game. I hope this review saves money for some people.

author: kanh2289
quote: After waiting 13 years and spending nearly $100, I can confidently say GTA VI is one of my biggest gaming disappointments. Rockstar has created an extraordinarily detailed and immersive world, but somewhere along the way, it seems to have forgotten what made Grand Theft Auto enjoyable in the first ****'s start with the story. Chapters 1 and 2 are painfully boring, filled with mundane activities, errands, and conversations that do little to advance the plot. Chapter 3 finally introduces some excitement, but the momentum disappears again in Chapter 4. Chapter 5 delivers an increasingly unrealistic series of robberies and a deeply unsatisfying finale. The campaign feels unnecessarily padded. GTA IV also had a slow, restrictive beginning, but its exceptional writing, memorable characters, and compelling narrative made that journey worthwhile. GTA VI fails to achieve the same.Jason and Lucia's relationship dominates far too much of the experience. Lucia repeatedly makes questionable decisions, yet the writing rarely gives those decisions the consequences or character development they deserve. The supporting cast is also disappointing. Cal Hampton, supposedly the comic relief, is more irritating than entertaining. The memorable personalities, sharp dialogue, dark humor, and fearless satire that defined earlier GTA games feel severely **** my biggest disappointment is the gameplay.This is a game called **Grand Theft Auto**, yet stealing and permanently keeping expensive vehicles has become an unnecessarily restrictive process. I spent more than 20 hours progressing through the story before unlocking the equipment needed to steal many desirable luxury cars. Even afterward, trackers, registration fees, and limited storage made vehicle ownership **** weapon system is similarly restrictive. Limited loadouts and cumbersome weapon switching make combat less spontaneous. You cannot freely purchase residential safehouses, the stock market is missing, and even the ability to replay completed individual missions has been removed.Rockstar seems obsessed with realism, but realism does not automatically translate into enjoyable gameplay. Worse, some restrictions feel arbitrary rather than **** greatest irony is that GTA VI offers a far more detailed world than GTA V while making several familiar activities less convenient and less enjoyable. I wanted better robberies, better heists, better vehicle theft, and greater freedom. I wasn't asking Rockstar to reinvent the franchise.I acknowledge the tremendous technical achievement. Vice City looks incredible, the environmental detail is remarkable, and certain aspects of the economy are improved. But beautiful graphics and impressive world simulation cannot compensate for a campaign I found tedious and mechanics I found frustrating.I finished the game not because I was enjoying it, but because I had already paid for it and kept hoping it would improve. If I had purchased it on Steam and encountered these problems within the refund window, I would have requested a refund. Instead, I completed the campaign on PS5 Pro and regretted the purchase.Rockstar may earn billions from GTA VI, but commercial success does not automatically equal customer satisfaction.**For me, GTA VI is an expensive, technologically impressive life simulator that has lost much of the freedom, humor, and entertainment that made GTA special.

author: NicoGaming
quote: **GTA 6 HAS LOST ITS SOUL — 13 YEARS FOR THIS?**I never thought I'd be this disappointed with a Grand Theft Auto game. After 13 years of waiting and a reportedly billion-dollar development budget, I expected Rockstar to redefine open-world gaming. Instead, GTA 6 feels like an incredibly expensive life simulator that has forgotten what made this franchise **** biggest problem isn't the graphics. Visually, the game is phenomenal. The problem is the gameplay, pacing, and creative **** am I supposed to get excited about running errands, shopping for neighbors, managing domestic responsibilities, and assembling furniture? There's even an activity involving repeatedly adjusting and rebuilding a coffee table. Is this really what Rockstar thinks GTA players have been waiting for? Grand Theft Auto has become Grand Theft Dishwasher.These activities might be optional, but optional content should still be entertaining. Instead, too much of the experience feels like pointless busywork designed to showcase technical details rather than deliver actual **** combat system is equally disappointing. After all these years, we're still dealing with familiar cover-based shooting, repetitive encounters, awkward movement, and heavily scripted missions. Where is the innovation? Rockstar has spent an enormous amount of money creating an incredibly realistic world, yet the fundamental gameplay formula feels painfully **** the mission design? The same old Rockstar restrictions. Follow the designated path, obey the script, and don't experiment too much. How can a game offer such an enormous open world while still making missions feel so restrictive?Then there's the performance. A 30 FPS cap even on PS5 Pro is disappointing in 2026. Digital Foundry's testing also revealed frame drops on standard PS5 during demanding action sequences. Xbox Series S suffers even more noticeable compromises. For a production of this scale, expecting a performance mode isn't **** let's address the controversial part: the increasingly politically correct **** used to be fearless. Its satire was offensive, outrageous, uncomfortable, and directed at practically everyone. That rebellious attitude was part of its **** the emphasis on relationship drama, domestic life, and certain modern cultural themes makes the franchise feel increasingly sanitized. I understand why some players describe this direction as **** no, Lucia being a female protagonist isn't the issue. The issue is whether Rockstar has traded its trademark irreverence for a safer, more socially acceptable identity.Jason and Lucia's relationship is central to the story, but the emphasis on their personal dynamics doesn't always deliver the criminal energy and outrageous storytelling I associate with GTA. The slower pacing and everyday responsibilities only reinforce that feeling.I also find the reported development costs difficult to justify when so many fundamental gameplay elements feel familiar. Whether the widely circulated $2 billion figure is accurate or not, the scale of this production makes the lack of meaningful innovation even more frustrating.What bothers me most is that GTA 6 doesn't necessarily look like a bad game. It looks like an extraordinary technical achievement built around questionable creative priorities.Rockstar has created an astonishingly detailed world, but detail isn't the same as entertainment. Realism isn't automatically immersion. Bigger doesn't automatically mean **** let's stop pretending Rockstar is immune to criticism. If Ubisoft or EA released a game with this combination of outdated mechanics, repetitive errands, restrictive mission design, and a 30 FPS cap, the backlash would be enormous.I grew to love GTA because of its freedom, chaos, memorable characters, dark humor, and complete disregard for convention. I don't want that identity replaced by a beautiful simulation of everyday **** 6 feels more interested in showing me how realistic its world is than reminding me why I wanted to play in that world.After 13 years, I expected a revolution in gameplay, not just graphics.**Rockstar perfected the simulation but seems to have forgotten the soul.****I wanted Grand Theft Auto, not The Sims with guns.**

author: DandB
quote:
A Beautiful Game That Lacks Soul
Graphically, GTA VI is in a league of its own. The visual presentation is genuinely breathtaking, and it's clear an extraordinary amount of effort has gone into creating its world. Unfortunately, impressive visuals alone don't make a great **** story is disappointingly weak, the pacing is frequently dreadful, and I found the main characters difficult to connect with or even particularly likeable. More importantly, many of the elements that made the GTA series so enjoyable and distinctive feel absent or diminished.Technical issues don't help matters either. Bugs and a 30FPS experience are difficult to overlook, particularly when the game is being held to such exceptionally high standards.
My biggest criticism is that GTA VI feels like another example of modern AAA development prioritising graphical fidelity over gameplay, storytelling and overall enjoyment. Everything looks incredible, but looking incredible isn't the same as being entertaining.Ultimately, GTA VI reminds me of a painting created with absolutely perfect technique. Every brushstroke is in the right place, the detail is immaculate, but somehow it lacks the soul that makes a piece of art truly memorable.
There are moments of fun to be had, certainly, but not nearly enough to make this the masterpiece many claim it to be. A technically impressive achievement, but a considerably less impressive video game.

author: Newday67
quote: GTA VI looks goddamn gorgeous, no argument there. But damn, at what cost? A framerate that treats 30fps like some mythical goal it can’t quite reach, and most of the actual fun from the older games just got quietly euthanized. GTA isn’t subversive anymore — it’s become the exact corporate, sanitized product it spent decades roasting. The missions are mostly a slog, the sidekicks have the charisma of wet cardboard, and the writing… yeah, let’s not talk about the writing. Rockstar decided to force-feed us the RDR2 slow-burn formula without noticing that in GTA’s chaotic urban crime playground, it lands about as well as a wet fart. Getting punished for committing crimes in a franchise that built its entire identity on celebrating crime is peak irony, and not the fun kind. Sure, the PC version will at least let you enjoy those pretty pixels at a decent framerate, but it won’t magically fix the rest of the blandness. What’s left is the jaw-dropping photorealism and the undeniable technical flex… and beyond that? Pretty much nothing.

author: Fiercedegamer
quote:
GTA 6 é espetacular. Visualmente, o jogo é impressionante, e estou genuinamente surpreso com o nível de qualidade gráfica que a Rockstar conseguiu alcançar no PS5. É uma demonstração do que a indústria pode fazer tecnicamente e, sem dúvida, um marco impressionante.

Entretanto, apesar de alguns bugs e quedas de FPS em determinados momentos, sinto que falta algo mais profundo em GTA 6. Sei que milhares de desenvolvedores trabalharam durante anos para tornar esse jogo realidade, mas, apesar de toda a sua grandiosidade, sinto que ele carece de alma e identidade.

A franquia GTA sempre foi conhecida por sua gameplay caótica, exagerada, imprevisível e cheia de personalidade. Porém, o realismo de GTA 6 é tão impressionante que, em alguns momentos, parece que o jogo perdeu parte daquilo que fazia GTA ser GTA. A obsessão da indústria por gráficos cada vez mais realistas e por simular cada detalhe da vida real nem sempre significa uma experiência melhor. Realismo, por si só, não substitui identidade artística.

Sou jogador de Destiny 2 e frequentemente vejo pessoas dizendo que o jogo está datado, que precisa de gráficos mais realistas ou de uma evolução visual mais próxima dos padrões atuais. Discordo completamente. Gosto muito da identidade artística que Destiny 2 possui hoje, e acredito que essa seja justamente uma das coisas que faltam em GTA 6: uma identidade visual e artística mais marcante, capaz de ir além do realismo.

GTA 6 é tecnicamente impressionante, mas gráficos incríveis não são suficientes para fazer um jogo ter personalidade. A Rockstar é conhecida por sua identidade, seu estilo e sua maneira única de criar mundos. Gostaria que GTA 6 tivesse mais disso, porque, no fim, um jogo não precisa ser o mais realista possível para ser memorável. 
Ele precisa ter alma.

author: D0nLucif3r
quote:
There are many new features, improvements, and an incredible leap in graphics. RPG elements have been included to enhance immersion, resulting in a more vivid and realistic world, along with a fresh approach to gameplay. 

On the flip side, many legacy features have been removed or censored, and the satire—once a hallmark of the series—has been toned down to be more "politically correct." 

It feels like a modern version of Red Dead Redemption rather than a Grand Theft Auto game. The potential has been squandered in an attempt to please everyone; the absence of the writing style of Dan Houser and his team is palpable. 

Furthermore, the game is riddled with bugs and still requires numerous patches, even on the PS5 Pro. The narrative feels forced to highlight the central duo, offering little freedom of choice and imposing a specific relationship on the player from the very start—a departure from the elements that made previous entries so successful. 

After two delays and an "old-school," diva-like approach to communication, Rockstar has failed to deliver the "ultra best" game possible. Instead, they’ve provided a mere show of force—a technical and visual marvel that comes at the expense of actual gameplay and entertainment value. This installment only managed to gain traction thanks to the hype and the series' past legacy; let’s hope that future DLCs can make up for these shortcomings and help it truly earn the "GTA" title.

author: vgarcia05
quote:
Until now, I had never played a GTA game before in my life. I did not own a PS2 back in the day so the hype never grew on me after I jumped on the PlayStation bandwagon. My opinion comes from total ignorance of what has made GTA games good in the past. 

I’d like to start by setting the ground on what a video game is to me: video, audio, gameplay, and the coding that puts those three elements  together to make it work. Each one of those elements alone exist as independent pieces of media: a movie/show, a song/podcast, or a game, to name a few.

GTA VI definitely has all of those elements: the graphics are amazing and there is so much attention to detail that I swear those locations can show up in my dreams and I’ll believe I’d been there in the past. The audio is superb—an endless array of songs played in the car, the music playing at the bar, the dialogues from the characters—it all just makes me think that im immersed in that world and not playing a game. 

As for the gameplay, well, GTA VI has it. You can press R1 to take a sip of your beer. You can press L2 and R2 simultaneously to lift weights. You can slowly drag furniture around your house. You can slowly follow someone around while they speak to you. You can drive from point A to point B, get of your car, watch a cutscene, and then drive back to point A again to watch another cutscene and consider the mission completed. And that’s where the game lost me. 

In essence, in all video games players press a button or buttons for their character to execute actions that could or could not be executed by a person in real life. This, of course, should be more fun than executing said action it in real life. Why would you mimic drinking a beer in a video game if you can drink it in real life? Well, because it gives you something to do while you watch the cutscenes: you press buttons to execute commands that have no implications or consequences in the game, just so you don’t sit there watching cutscenes. 

And don’t get me wrong, after two days of playing the game for many hours I have had some missions that require that I do something apart from watching a cutscene; my problem is that those moments are scarcely delivered among a plethora of cutscenes and playable chores that I’d rather just complete at home. 

Nevertheless, the production value of the game is unquestionable. The video and audio parts are the best I have ever seen. If they strive to make GTA VII fun then I’m sure they’ll end up with a product that not only appeals to the media but also to the players.

author: fozydra
quote:
Here is my personal review: From a technical standpoint, Grand Theft Auto VI is an undeniable achievement. The open world of Leonida is AMAZING, the attention to detail is unmatched, and the core gameplay mechanics feel smooth. The world really is alive. However, despite its stunning presentation, the game suffers from a major identity crisis. It simply does not feel like a Grand Theft Auto game (I am telling this as someone who completed all main Gta's). Because of several design choices that restrict player freedom and drag down the pacing, my final score is a 6/10. Here is the breakdown and all the reasons the game has lost a point for me;


1. Sacrificing Freedom for "Ethical Correctness" (-1 Point): 
This is my biggest "Concern", and it goes against the very DNA of the franchise. GTA has always been about total freedom—a sandbox where you can do whatever you want without the game holding your gun back because an action is "unethical". But in GTA 6, too many classic liberties have been stripped away in the name of political or ethical correctness. You can no longer freely shoot inside clubs, steal certain cars you want, kill protesters in some situations (not all of them are unkillable. But other gta's would allow every single one of them to be killable) or interact with prostitutes. There are even moments where you are artificially prevented from hitting protesters, and you aren't allowed to have Jason or Lucia cheat on each other with side characters (like Mandy), something older GTA titles would have embraced without hesitation.
*****To be clear about the reasoning of my defence: I have never even used features like prostitutes in any previous GTA game. And most of the features I said doesn't even disturb me as I play. Yet, I will also defend their inclusion—along with every other removed feature—because they represent the freedom we always had since gta 3. If we stay silent now, this censorship will only spread to future titles. Imagine a GTA 7 where even more actions are blocked just because they are deemed "unethical." Every fan should speak up against these restrictions to protect the future of the series.


2. Performance (-1 Point):
Playing at 30 FPS is not a dealbreaker for a game of this visual scale, and the frame pacing is mostly stable. Still, in an era where 60 FPS is the standard, being locked to 30 FPS costs the game a point. 


3. A Boring Story and a Forgettable Protagonist (-1 Point):
The narrative is deeply disappointing. The story is dull, and fails to leave any lasting impact. Especially Jason. Before release, many compared Jason to Arthur Morgan, expecting a deep, complex character. Instead, Jason feels completely devoid of personality, making it nearly impossible to connect with him. Lucia is fine. I liked her more. At least she got some personality. 


4. Time (-1 point) : 
To be honest, even though the game is amazing in technical and graphical sense: It was a bit of a dissapointment considering 13 YEARS. Nothing more amazing than rdr2. 

Final Score: 6/10

author: LeHai5
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI has finally hit the shelves, and while it’s undoubtedly a thrilling addition to the franchise, it comes with a few caveats. The game delivers an engaging experience that fans have come to expect, but it’s not without its minor bugs that linger in the first few days post-launch.

Despite these small hiccups, the core gameplay remains solid and enjoyable. The familiar mechanics that have defined the series are still present, which can be both a blessing and a curse. On one hand, the classic GTA gameplay style is comforting and nostalgic; on the other, it raises the question of whether enough innovation has been introduced to justify the long wait.

Graphically, the improvements are striking. The visuals are stunning, showcasing the advancements in technology since the last installment. The world feels alive and vibrant, with intricate details that enhance immersion. However, it’s hard to shake the feeling that, while the graphics have received a significant upgrade, the gameplay itself hasn’t evolved as much as one might hope.

In conclusion, GTA VI is a solid entry that will satisfy long-time fans, but it does leave some room for improvement. The bugs are expected to be ironed out in future updates, and hopefully, future expansions will bring fresh gameplay elements to the table. For now, it’s a fun ride that feels familiar, yet it could benefit from a bit more innovation to truly stand out in the ever-evolving gaming landscape.

author: DizzyingSloth
quote: I believe people are giving this game too much credit because of the series notoriety from previous entries. I would say the narrative of the story is weak in comparison to the other games in the series let alone that of basically any other story based game. The game's story so far from what I have played and have seen is only complimented by the random *mild* pokes at groups that have been done better in previous iterations. Protecting certain areas, groups and NPC's because of their affiliation to disenfranchised/minority groups that makes it seem like they are too important and not on equal standing as others is a bad choice. If you can do it to one group you should be able to do it to all of them. The player has the power, there could be consequences but the game removes the choice from the player to protect feelings which doesn't belong in these games. This game also seems to have an identity crisis as rockstar tries to take parts of the identity from red dead redemption series and places it on GTA. The game limits heavily what can be done and is extremely slow paced with minor humor and excitement. Enforces a relationship that players do not want with characters who are not memorable in the slightest. Worst of all there is no polish to these games.  This game is littered with bugs, glitches, stuttering, frame drops and crashes. On top of this the janky weapon wheel that doesnt always work and some of the hud that could be improved.  For having 13 years of development time we the consumers deserve more. When cyberpunk released in an appalling state we didnt take it, and this game should be treated the same. The last major negative is the world with alot of realism feels empty. Beaches and parts of the city were  advertised and showed as being filled and populated are barren in comparison. The beautiful atmosphere almost looks like a screensaver without the abundance that should be there. This may be the limitation of the hardware, but it is also up to the devs to optimize and sacrifice where needed to fit the game to the hardware that they are creating for. Though it may seem like there are only negatives to this game there are many positives. The graphics and attention to detail are great. The realism and heavy attention to detail can be felt especially when fighting (when not experiencing any hiccups) as you can see the reactions and detail of the body being destroyed (however being graphically impressive does not mean the game is a good game and does not justify a high rating, its a factor but many people tend to over prioritize graphics over functionality, playability and story telling). The radio shows also have some fun tidbits just like the last entry. There is alot of promise for this game, on better hardware and when multiplayer releases as there are not many redeeming qualities about the single player. Hopefully we will see many things added back with the level of detail that rockstar has given to us in the game with less restrictions. This game is not a complete failure but currently blemishes the series reputation that has been built up over the generations. I hope over the upcoming months that the game has time to improve, and over the years more enjoyability will be brought back to the beloved series. This is to not discourage or say that others are wrong for enjoying this game, but the people who are frustrated are valid because of the heavy departure of this game from previous entries.

author: Red900
quote:
So, I figured I would throw my hat in on this. Is this game a 10/10? No, it really isn't, nor is it a 1/10 like others are saying. I’d say it sits nicely at a 7/10.
It's a beautiful, open, immersive world where you can do a lot, though not everything. I love the fact that you can talk to any NPC, and the fact that you have to refuel the car, eat, and sleep to get stronger. The world really does feel utterly alive, and I commend Rockstar for this. However, they have made some really bizarre choices, like not letting you take out protesters. Like, why? Why can't I? What's the purpose behind the team saying, "Right, you can gun down Doris on her mobility scooter, but shooting Tina who is protesting? No, that's too far, we can't have that."
Jason and Lucia are really very poor characters. All Jason does is mumble and say a few words; it sounds like he needs medical attention. Meanwhile, Lucia is just plain unlikeable with a huge attitude problem. (What's that I hear? "Yet again, she's Latina, it's how they are." Ah, yeah, stereotypes. Fantastic, except where are the other stereotypes in the game?) Does Jason wanting to do nice things for her make him a simp? No, I don't think it does, but you don't have to do them. Equally, why aren't there missions where Lucia gets to go out and do nice things for Jason, like getting him some beer or cleaning his car? A healthy relationship is about doing nice things for each other and respecting each other. Instead, we have Jason doing nice things while Lucia gets in a mood and storms off, leaving a baby in a café. You know, the usual stuff people do. 
The missions tend to be good, though they also feel rushed. Again, it's like the team had a good idea, but had no idea how to wrap it up. So far, it's the main characters that are bringing this game down, and the rest of the game is doing all the heavy lifting. I'm glad I've got it, but I should have waited for more reviews to come out.

author: Mage4spell
quote:
Subject: GTA 6: A Serious Concern About Male Character Representation and Player Freedom

I want to raise a serious concern about the direction GTA 6 seems to be taking compared to GTA 5.

In GTA 5, things felt more natural and unrestricted. If a male character wanted sexual encounters, he could pursue them within the game without unnecessary limitations. He was not portrayed as someone's servant or a submissive character. He was confident, independent, tough, and had the freedom and attitude expected from a GTA protagonist.

In GTA 6, however, the male character seems to be portrayed as a pushover, constantly controlled or humiliated by women. It gives the impression that the game is deliberately promoting a one-sided feminist narrative at the expense of male characters.

The male protagonist appears to tolerate infidelity, disrespect, and humiliation, while having almost no freedom to express his own sexuality or personality. Even basic interactions, such as flirting, sexual encounters, or playful physical interactions, seem unnecessarily restricted.

Why should a male character in a GTA game be reduced to a submissive partner who serves a woman, while she can seemingly do whatever she wants? Where is the freedom, confidence, aggression, rebellious attitude, and unapologetic personality that made GTA protagonists memorable?

This feels like an imbalance in how male and female characters are represented and what they are allowed to do. Male players should not feel that their character has been deliberately stripped of his independence, masculinity, and freedom of expression.

I would like Rockstar to reconsider these restrictions and give players more freedom in how they interact with other characters, including consensual adult relationships, flirting, sexual encounters, and the ability to express a more dominant, confident, and rebellious male personality.

After all, this is Grand Theft Auto. Players expect freedom, adult themes, outrageous behaviour, and the ability to live out a criminal fantasy without unnecessary restrictions.

And one final question: what is the point of having a gym on the balcony if the male protagonist has the personality and attitude of a man completely stripped of testosterone?

I hope Rockstar takes this feedback seriously and considers giving players more freedom and balance in the final experience.

GTA is about freedom. Please don't take that away from the player.

author: gamereviewer42
quote:
This game is slow. 
The gunplay is slow, the melee is slow, the progression is slow, every time you try to do something an input prompt slows you down for the sake of realism. If you try to steal a car, you'll realize you can't steal most of the parked cars without making 10 evaluations and following a 10-step program first. If you try to steal an occupied car, you'll get through 10 cars and start 5 gunfights before you manage to get in one and drive off. Whatever car you do manage to nab, get ready to spend hours in it, because drives in this game are *long* and fast travel is economically unviable for the for a while in to the playthrough. If you were planning to pull yourself up by your bootstraps and make some good money, good luck with the reconnaissance for your next heist, because mission or quest rewards are not going to cut it and there's no stock market for you to fall back on.
Still, it is incredible what they have managed to fit in to this 80 dollar package. Every NPC feels like they have their own unique model and dialogue, every car from its exterior to its interior feels meticulously detailed, a magazine rack has dozens of fully-illustrated fake magazines ready to read, the fake social media app has enough content (and comments!) on it to facilitate an entire doom scrolling session, this game has detail, thought, and substance in the corners where you'd least expected. But even that begs the question, how does any of that count towards a franchise that got its start as an arcade-y crime simulator sandbox? 
Of course, you could point to the Criminal Profile that takes in to account your behaviour and willingness to commit violence or Wanted system that takes in to account how identifiable you are, but is that enough to offset all the slow downs the game throws at you? And, are realistic NPCs with unique personalities and appearances the kind of NPC you want in a franchise where players are used to stealing cars, running over pedestrians, and causing shootouts precisely because of the disconnect between how the NPCs acted and how real people act, precisely because it was obvious that these weren't people?
The answer is no. 
When Saints Row 2 came out, I remember people calling it the platonic ideal for a Grand Theft Auto game, however, GTA 6 couldn't be further from that ideal. So, despite the better story (which could've really done with a protagonist less bland than Jason), I can't rate this game better than its predecessors. For people expecting a GTA, this game delivers something else, and for that it can only walk away with a fraction of the score a game of its calibre deserves.

author: Hasan35x
quote: A Beautiful World That Doesn't Feel AliveAfter 13 years of waiting, I expected Rockstar to push the boundaries of open-world gaming. Instead, GTA 6 feels like a better-looking GTA 5: technically impressive, visually stunning, but disappointingly static beneath the **** biggest problem is the world itself. It looks alive, but it rarely feels alive. NPCs walk around, perform animations and participate in scripted random events, yet there is very little convincing social interaction between them. When something unusual happens on the street, the surrounding people often carry on as if nothing happened. Where are the spontaneous reactions, curiosity, laughter, fear, conversations and unpredictable chains of behavior? I don't want more scripted scenes. I want a world that doesn't need to perform for **** nightclub is a perfect example. Hundreds of people, beautiful lighting and impressive animations, but where is the actual chaos and social dynamism of a nightclub? People should move around, bump into each other, argue, react to the music, behave differently and interact spontaneously. Instead, it often feels like a collection of NPCs playing pre-arranged **** same disappointment extends to character behavior. Reactions to violence, accidents and unusual situations still seem limited and repetitive. A convincing living world needs more than crowds and animation variety; it needs believable interactions and consequences between the people inhabiting it.Then there are the missions. Why does an open-world game this ambitious still rely so heavily on linear, predetermined storytelling? I want creative heists, meaningful criminal progression and systems that allow players to create their own stories. I don't want the world to become interesting only when a mission tells it to.Arthur Morgan felt like a person with a life, relationships, regrets and an evolving personality. I expected that level of character depth and more from Jason and Lucia.Rockstar clearly has the talent and resources to build something extraordinary. That's precisely why this disappointment hurts. I didn't expect merely a bigger map, prettier graphics or more scripted encounters. I expected a genuine evolution of the open-world **** 6 is a beautiful collection of static scenes. I wanted a living, breathing world.

author: LesMiserables
quote: Full disclosure I'm 30% into the game and perhaps it will get better but so far the gist of it is this. GTA VI somehow to an even greater extend than even RDR2 sacrifices gameplay and fun for the sake of story and realism at every turn. To further illustrate my point let's compare VI and IV. In GTA IV the mission design boiled down to "Watch 3 minute cutscene, Drive and have an action sequence". Beyond the first hour of the game this is exactly how it plays from beginning to end. In GTA VI you watch a cutscene then you walk and then you listen to people talk and then you walk and then you watch a cutscene and then you drive and then you do some busywork and then you walk and then you listen to people talk and then you drive. Occasionally the game actually ramps up and provides a fun action sequence before resorting back to the original loop. The main romantic interest in GTA IV was Kate. She was never forced upon the player as Niko can sleep around and pay her no mind. Does that harm the story and her ultimate fate? Sure but Rockstar rightfully understood that forcing the friendship sim stuff would harm the gameplay so they made interacting with her or any person for that matter entirely optional. In GTA VI you are FORCED to care for Lucia or Jason (So much for it being optional). Fix the IKEA table, Paint the wall, Buy the flowers etc. or get a bad ending. All these are not cutscenes but "interactive" cutscenes and for what? To build rapport? You mean to tell me that you cared more for Jason than Niko because Lucia went and picked groceries for him ONE BY ONE?. In GTA IV it never really made sense for Niko to be a cop butchering maniac so they introduced an injury mechanic so that you could if you wanted spare enemies by shooting them in the legs. At the same time they realized that this is a GTA game and causing mayhem is an integral part if not the biggest reason why people play GTA games. In GTA VI the injury system makes a come back and now is tied to a karma system that the more you lower the worse ending you'll get. On top of that you have SAFE ZONES in a GTA game where you cannot hurt people...Alrighty then. A big problem with GTA IV was it's driving. It was a big part of the gameplay loop and if you didn't really like it then you would have a problem. Rockstar knew that so they introduced taxi's in order to make traversal faster which let's players focus on the missions and the story. In GTA VI they made taxi's super expensive in order to force you to interact with the driving and by extension all the little life sim gimmicks they attached to it. Thankfully I realized that you can break the system for a bit of negative karma to just rob the taxi drivers upon reaching your destination. And that is the crux of it so far, There have been fun moments absolutely especially in Chapter 2 where you play as Lucia and you start to get a bit more freedom to move around and rake in cash. The chases with the police, The gang hideouts where you steal their cash and stealing in general have been a blast. THAT's the sad part the game could have been great if it didn't focus so much on being an interactive movie or it's ability to cause mayhem wasn't so sanitized. I will update this review once I'm done with it completely

author: Freeger2789
quote:
I played for about 10 hours before my brother accidentally wiped my save today—and honestly, I’m relieved I have an excuse not to go back. I have better things to do in life than stare at flashy colors and scripted characters longer than the void stares back at me. 

From a purely technical standpoint, I respect the immense work the programmers put in. The physics are incredible, the cloud simulations are legitimately impressive, and it’s clearly an engineering feat. Unfortunately, engineering doesn't automatically make a compelling game, and the relentless hype surrounding this release completely overshadows what is ultimately just a safe, overpriced product. Paying $100 (400 RON) for this left me wondering what I actually bought. I will let others play and pay for it, but it is not for me.

If Gen Alpha and Gen Z (which I am part of) see this as the ultimate cultural phenomenon, all I saw was the raw code: C++ and animations. Interwar Romanian pessimism was more intellectually stimulating than watching Mandy in a suburban kitchen for 30 minutes of Chapter 1, only for the internet to turn a minor character you barely see again into an overnight **** issues started before I even reached the main menu: the pre-load corrupted the second the launch lock lifted, forcing me to redownload all 210+ GB from scratch. Once in-game, the 30 FPS cap is rough on base PS5 and does not hold steady. The opening shootout dipped hard with sluggish, frustrating aiming, and getting behind a boat with spinning propellers tanked my framerate to what felt like 5 FPS. That left a terrible first impression.

Tonally, it just isn't for me. The hyper-saturated color palette feels straight out of Far Cry New Dawn, mixed with a heavy-handed romance subplot that reads like a boring love novel. Even when it tries to distract from the narrative void with weird detours—like a swamp sequence where Jason inhales near a wooden effigy, faints, and wakes up in a wrecked car—the logic just goes full sci-fi. I missed the grounded, nihilistic tone of Days Gone (which ran far better in overcrowded environments on the PS4's ancient Jaguar CPU), or the sharp mechanical leap and living world design of IO Interactive's 007 First Light.

At least I had fun quoting Cioran and Feynman while messing around in the sandbox, with a copy of Six Easy Pieces sitting on the desk next to me. Mammalian biology can't rewrite dopamine, and Cioran would probably laugh at the hype machine—but at full price, this one is a pass for me.

author: AqueleCritico
quote:
Considering how far I've progressed in the story — and I'm already quite far along — I'd give the game a 7/10. It's a competent experience, but one that offers nothing particularly innovative. Its graphics are undoubtedly one of its biggest strengths, but it makes me wonder: nowadays, is a beautiful visual presentation really enough to sustain a game's overall quality?

When I first started playing, I have to admit I was quite impressed, but also somewhat taken aback by the similarities to Red Dead Redemption 2. It's practically impossible not to draw comparisons between the two. Perhaps I was exaggerating when I called them IDENTICAL, but the inspiration is so evident that ignoring it would be naive.

What disappoints me the most, however, is the narrative. At least up to the point I've reached, the story comes nowhere near matching the depth, character development, and ability to immerse the player that we find in Red Dead Redemption 2. This strikes me as particularly strange when I consider the historical significance of this franchise to Rockstar. After all, we're talking about a series that played a fundamental role in shaping the company's identity and contributing to its rise. Anyone familiar with Rockstar's history and the early days of GTA understands exactly what I'm getting at.

Simply recycling successful formulas, presenting visually stunning environments, and delivering a technically competent experience isn't enough. A game needs its own identity, personality, and, above all, something meaningful to say. Red Dead Redemption 2 didn't become a benchmark solely because of its graphics or the sheer scale of its world, but because of how it developed its characters, crafted its narrative, and made players genuinely care about the experience.

And that's precisely what's missing here. There's potential, there's technical quality, but it lacks that certain essence that turns a game into something truly memorable. Perhaps my opinion will change by the end of the campaign, but so far, the experience falls short of justifying all the expectations surrounding it. A 7/10 isn't an attempt to undermine the game; it's simply an acknowledgment that, despite its qualities, it could have delivered much more.

A NOTE ON FAKE CRITICISM!!

It's disappointing to see people trying to discredit a game they haven't even played, simply to favor another title they happen to prefer. That's not critical thinking; it's nothing more than fanboyism. A proper review requires knowledge, experience, and solid arguments, not childish rivalry. If you have to tear one game down to praise another, your opinion has already lost its credibility.

author: CodeMon33
quote:
Not really sure where to start with this review... but as you can read from many others, this game is a bit of a let down in some really important areas. 

Graphics wise, holy unbelievable! Max star rating. It's RDR2 but somehow 2 times more detailed and beautiful! 30 fps is a lil rough at first, but not unplayable at all. I have been blown away by some of the smallest little details in certain parts of gameplay and just putz'n around. Insane... but unfortunately, I feel like thats the only "good" part of the game, for me anyways. I didn't pay $100 bucks so I could say "Wow! Look how detailed that palm tree is!"...

We got GTA but without the ability to actually commit GTA... lol. Ok, sure you "can" steal a car you like but 80% of time its with consequences. Half the time I've just been beat up and fail getting it (yes I know, skill issues). And you can't keep it anyways until pretty far into the quite boring and dragged on story. Took me about 20 hours (a bit of that time was trying to explore) to get to the point where I can now register certain cars that DO NOT have trackers... which is pretty much only old, crappy cars. And its quite expensive if you want more then one car at a time. This whole feature, to me, is by far the biggest let down. It's a game! Let me do what I want lol.

Speaking of let downs... next biggest one, to me, is the fact you don't have a full weapon wheel. One thing I absolutely despised in rdr2 was the lack of a full weapon wheel. Again... a single player GAME shouldn't be limited like this. Let me do what I want! I want to relax and have fun. Not be stressed and die 2-3 time every mission that has a shoot out because my lack in brain cells forgot to grab my extra guns from my trunk! Matter of fact, I'm feeling stressed just writing about this and now think its worse to me then not being able to take whatever car I want.

Ugh... and I seem to have issues aiming even with full assist on. Not sure if thats litterally just my horrendous skills or something is just off. I loved gta v's and rdr2's shooting mechanics. But I have a heck of a time with this ones, so far. It's just not enjoyable for me. (Queue tiny violin).

Story wise, has been quite tedious and not engaging at all for me, thus far. Just going through it cause I have to. I would probably play through 1 more time after I finish my first, just because there are some things you realize later on that you wish you knew earlier...

And well, yeah. Those are my 2 cents worth of thoughts on the game so far... if you haven't bought it yet and are on the fence... I'd personally wait for a sale. I don't 100% regret my purchase but I am certainly not 100% satisfied. Which really stinks cause my hopes were about 1000%. Game is definitely a solid 6/10 for me and certainly not near a "99%".
