author: Messral
quote:
I registered just to give this a bad rating, because I'm mad as hell at both Rockstar and myself for wasting 80 dollars on it.

Gameplay: It's nonexistent. You drive from cutscene to cutscene, shoot once in a while, and the rest is QTE chores. It's too realistic to be fun, and the funny part is that it's not even realistic, it's just extra steps. You mash two buttons instead of pressing one. Character movement is extremely chunky, like in RDR, except this is not RDR.

I also want to talk about the "chores". You need to work out so you don't get fat and get beaten every time you steal a car. You need to track your protein or you're literally debuffed. You need to do cardio for stamina. Then there are missions that are literally chores: fix your house, wash dishes, do groceries, flip burgers, wash ships, etc. I literally cleaned my house, did my dishes and went out to buy food in real life, then logged into the game and it made me do the same things again. Why? They tell you all of this is "optional", yet if you don't maintain your relationships, the game soft-locks you out of HALF of the missions. The workouts, cardio and other stuff you need to do regularly hinder your character further if you skip them. It feels like maintaining a second life instead of playing a game. They literally ignored why people play games.

Story: Bland, cliché and extremely predictable. 80% of the dialogue is small talk with no direction or purpose. After my first 10-hour session, the story had progressed only THREE times. Two of those made me predict exactly what would happen, and I was, unsurprisingly, right!

Missions: Like I said, mostly chores. You go from cutscene to cutscene and it's always some kind of partying. It gets kind of exciting after a point with the bigger missions, but it's the exact same thing with a bigger production. Nothing that makes you go "wow".

Visuals: The graphics are good, and it's nice to just find a good spot and watch. Yet again, it's realism. I can do the same thing with a 15-minute drive, so it's not impressive. It also feels gray and bland, because, again, it's realism.

Sound/music: These are pretty good, ngl. You can hear exactly where a sound comes from. But again, realism, and nothing special about the music. It's the same singers you see in real life doing the same type of music.

Open world: This is probably the only thing that makes it "kinda" worth playing, yet it only justifies around twenty dollars, not all eighty. A bunch of random events happen in the world, and it feels good to drive around and explore even though there's no point. Also, those "random" events aren't even random. They're planned events placed at certain points on the map, and once you trigger them by getting close, the game just plays them for you. The same events happen to everyone who passes that trigger zone.

Technical stuff: It's full of bugs, visual glitches, broken physics and things despawning, and omg, it doesn't even hit 30 fps.

I mean, Rockstar is probably the most money-hungry game studio out there. I don't even wanna call them a studio anymore, its just an another company, nothing artistic about it. A trailer on Netflix, purchased critics, a console release first so thousands buy consoles, and then some people will want to play it at higher fps, so they'll buy it twice, for PC too, at the same price :). And microtransactions from day one. It was a FOFO case to buy this game. Money wasted, but lesson learned. I don't think I'll buy any Rockstar game after this flop.

author: JohnRater
quote:
Let’s be honest for a second here. This game is not BAD it’s just not 100 dollars good. 

GTA 6 is a really strange take on the formula. It feels almost like they built the game on top of RDR2 with things like the food system and the alignment stuff (which makes no sense to me for a GTA game but ig). It makes a bunch of weird concessions in the fun department for the sake of realism which then get unjustified by concessions on realism for the sake of fun. Why must the cops be the most unbearable thing to ever disgrace my PS5? I hate the new cops system. Part of GTA 6 is being able to commit crimes, I am fearful of committing crimes because the cops are so annoying (notice they’re not difficult to deal with, just annoying). Like, if I wanted to deal with cops after committing crimes in Florida, I’d go outside, not spend 100 **** dollars on a video game. I think that this design philosophy just soaks into a lot of the gameplay, making it a less fun experience than 5.

On the other hand, the game is gorgeous. I don’t think I’ve seen a game look this great in a while. People talk about how 30 fps is horrible, and although it’s definitely visible when frames drop even slightly, it’s permissible 90% of the time.

Glitches are definitely present as well. I’ve had a plethora of weird visual glitches (my favorite being a guy T-posing while rotating on his motorcycle) and a bunch of vehicle glitches that have made it annoying to drive. I don’t think it’s Cyber Punk levels of unplayable, but there have been moments I put down the controller.

The story is the story. Idk I’ve never really though GTA has had super compelling stories, this one is certainly less interesting then other installments, but it’s not the main reason I dislike the game writ large.

TLDR: GTA 6 is the best looking GTA game ever, but it falls short in literally every other department. It’s an ok game that obviously doesn’t live up to the ungodly amount of hype.

author: lilguy
quote:
GTA VI delivers an impressive visual experience, featuring highly realistic graphics, satisfying hand-to-hand combat, engaging random events, and entertaining side missions. It also offers an interesting cinematic narrative and makes a commendable effort to balance realism with fun, avoiding the extremes of becoming either too simulation-heavy or too arcade-like. These strengths initially create the impression of a rich, immersive, and carefully crafted open world.

However, despite its ambitious presentation, the game struggles to deliver on several fundamental aspects of its design. Unnatural animations, noticeable bugs, frame drops, and poor optimization undermine the technical experience. More importantly, while the world feels alive and dynamic, it rarely feels truly reactive to the player's actions. The player's decisions and behavior have little noticeable impact on the world, making it difficult to feel like an active force within it. In other words, GTA VI presents a dynamic world, but not necessarily a systemic one. Limited player freedom further weakens this experience. The main missions often feel boring and repetitive, while mechanics such as social media add quantity rather than meaningful gameplay depth. The characters also lack sufficient depth and development, making it difficult to form a strong emotional connection with them. 
This is my honest review after playing the game for five hours and i found it a downgrade in the serie and one of the most disappointing flops of video game industry .

author: MattEagleson
quote: I enjoy Grand Theft Auto, and this could have been fun, but we have some issues. Too many rules and restrictions for a supposed open-world “crime” based game. A lot of bugs for a game that had 13 years to develop. The story was kinda bland, even though the characters were great. I can tell millennials and Gen Z developed the game because it has zero personality and authenticity compared to GTA V. These 4 endings as a whole were a bit lacking to me. 1) The "No Surrender" Ending (Bonnie & Clyde): When cornered at the bridge roadblock, choosing the No Surrender prompt causes Jason to floor the gas. After sharing a final kiss, Lucia stands up in the car firing at the deputies as they smash through the barrier. The car crashes, and both Jason and Lucia are shot dead in their seats. The credits roll over an aerial shot of the scene, followed by a post-credits scene showing Cal opening the stolen files on his laptop. 2) The "Swim For It" / Escape Ending ("Happily Ever After"): Selecting Swim for It at the roadblock allows you to attempt an escape. If you meet specific late-game requirements—specifically having a high romantic bond between Jason and Lucia and hitting the $2 million cap in their shared Family Savings account—both survive the fallout and leave Leonida together with their baby son, Tomás, to start a fresh life. 3) The Betrayal / Sacrifice Variations: If your relationship bond is low, your Criminal Profile leans too chaotic, or you lack sufficient savings, the escape plays out differently. One partner takes the immunity deal or gets left behind—resulting in either Jason or Lucia going to prison (or dying) while the other walks free to raise Tomás alone. I can excuse these endings if it did not take 50 hours to get to one of these endings, you can't replay any missions except the last 3 missions, and it takes 200 hours to get all 4 endings. So, I unfortunately have to give this game a 7/10. This game is fun, but not as groundbreaking as its predecessor was 13 years prior on older hardware during the Xbox 360/PS3 era. Wait for a price drop if you want to experience GTA VI for yourself; otherwise, stick to GTA V on any platform you have.

author: tomariscool
quote:
Most of the criticism you see here is valid. The game is improperly paced -- the first act is slow, and the follow two acts are better, but many missions still feel slow, tedious, or downright stupid. Story aside, the game just isn't that fun to play. Aiming is incredibly clunky, hand to hand combat feels overly scripted, and walking around doesn't feel as responsive as previous entries. There were multiple instances in the beginning of my playthrough that I thought my controller was suffering from ~1/2 second of input lag. Nope, you character just responds like they're getting instructions from an earpiece. Luckily, the "relationship" mechanic people were complaining about before release isn't that intense, and you can skip most of the relationship-building side-quests if you so choose. 

The game is pretty, but the frame rate leaves much to be desired. Yes, I'd like 60 FPS, but even a consistent 30 would have been acceptable. Playing on a launch PS5, I get constant dips down to less than 25 during mild action, and there have been a handful of occasions where the game stutters down to around 20. It feels only marginally better than Zelda BOTW on the original Switch. 

Unfortunately, I think a lot of these issues are more than skin deep; most of my complaints can't be fixed with patches or even a PC release.

author: PumpkinPlatter
quote:
It’s pretty good as a regular game,  but couldn’t conquer its incomprehensible anticipation.

GTA 6 was frankly overhyped by both the community and by Rockstar. There was no way it was going to be able to satisfy the vast and ravenous desires of the hundreds of millions of people that are interested in it. It’s the biggest piece of media to date, and there was frankly no way it was going to accomplish that. The storyline is ok, the gameplay is great in my opinion, the graphics are amazing, and the sideline content is vast and satisfying. But, the storyline is a little boring/shallow, and I think that it really should’ve delved more into the sandbox elements and have let you do really whatever you desired. I can understand how people are saying that the game has gone “soft”, in the sense that it’s taking a backing off of any hardcore political stances in certain areas, but that’s expected for this game; it’s supposed to be the biggest game of all time, they didn’t want to take any unnecessary risks is what I’d say. Also, the game being buggy, while expected to occur for large scale games like GTA, is a little unacceptable, especially considering they had years to polish and smooth out the edges. The 30 FPS is also, while slightly understandable due to the size of the game, also completely able to be labeled as ridiculous, especially considering it’s 2026. Overall, yes, it’s a good game, and for people who like these kinds of open world games, it is worth the 80$ for some people. But, the game, as predicted by many, was extremely overhyped, and not everyone will enjoy it. Many  
old school GTA fans feel like the story is very different from classic GTA’s and that the story doesn’t fit at all, and that’s a totally justified feeling. The characters of Jason and Lucia do feel pretty stale as personalities, at least compared to IV’s, V, and San Andreas’s, which does take the charm out a bit. Overall, I’d give it around a 6 out of 10, which means that yes, it is obviously a good game just due to the quality of the side missions, graphics, and side content, but a lot of the game is pretty mundane, at least compared to the impossible hype of its release. Again, if you think that this game is a 10/10 industry revolutionizing and unbeatable digital masterpiece that’s the magnum opus of the gaming world, that’s totally justified, for there are many things about it that absolutely can make this you a diehard fan of it. But, if you think that this game is 1/10, and that it’s an overhyped, buggy, safe-edgy disaster that was overhyped by the media, fanboys, and Rockstar, and that GTA just killed its franchise with this waste of 80$ digital pile of steaming ****, then that’s honestly valid too. This game was too big to fail profits wise, but the next couple of years will see if this game is golden or garbage for most people.

It's 2026, and I still have to deal with 30 FPS after waiting this long? The performance, frame drops, stuttering and technical issues make it even more frustrating.

There are also so many little things that get on my nerves. Bugs, glitches, weird physics, clipping issues, missing textures and problems that can interrupt the experience. I also expected better combat, smoother controls, smarter AI and more freedom during missions. Some parts just feel repetitive, and not everything is as fun as I hoped it would be.

I won't deny that the world looks beautiful, but honestly, I don't play games just to look at pretty graphics. I want good gameplay, smooth performance and an experience that actually keeps me entertained. A huge map means nothing if I'm constantly annoyed by other problems.

What bothers me most is how long Rockstar had to make this game. More than a decade of waiting, endless hype and expectations, and I still feel like so much could have been done better. I expected to be blown away, but instead I'm left wondering why this took so long. I wanted to love this game, but I can't ignore the things that disappoint me. Maybe others enjoy it more, and that's fine, but personally, I expected much more from GTA VI. 5/10.

author: bhollows
quote: Where do I even start with this review?Do I even have the right to review GTA 6 after a little over six hours of gameplay? Maybe not, but those six hours started at midnight on release night, and for an old, sick 46-year-old man, midnight is already way past my bedtime. For a little perspective, I was 17 when I first played GTA on my PC, and I’ve been a Rockstar fan ever since. I’ve played and bought every GTA game, along with both Red Dead Redemption games. Between all the GTA titles, and especially GTA Online, I’ve probably sacrificed an embarrassing amount of my actual life to ****, I’ve even bought more Shark Cards than I care to admit. I work full-time, have a family, and gaming became a hobby I squeeze in whenever life allows. At some point, I had more money than free time, so Shark Cards it was. That’s why GTA 6 meant so much to me.I’ve been very ill for the past four years and came frighteningly close to dying. As crazy as it may sound, lying in a hospital bed makes you think about some strange things, and one of mine was, “Damn, I might actually miss GTA 6.”So yes, I was excited. Really excited.I preordered it and had it downloaded days before release. Then, in a cruel bit of timing, I was visiting family in Florida and ended up back in the ER and hospital for several days. Thankfully, I recovered enough to drive home on release day and made it back around 8 p.m.Naturally, the first thing I did was jump on YouTube to see what everyone was **** my excitement crashed.I saw the flood of negative reactions and immediately tried to refund my preorder, only to be denied because the game had already been downloaded. That surprised and frustrated me, considering I hadn't even played it **** I decided to give the game a chance **** after six-plus hours, I’m struggling. For me, this simply does not feel like the GTA I grew up with GTA, which was never supposed to be safe. That was practically its identity. These were the games parents hated in the late '90s and early 2000s because they were violent, offensive, inappropriate, politically incorrect, and completely unapologetic about it.Being bad was part of the **** made fun of everyone. Left, right, rich, poor, politicians, corporations, celebrities, rednecks, criminals, cops, influencers, America itself. Nobody was supposed to be safe from Rockstar's satire.Maybe that style doesn't work for today's audience. Maybe Rockstar simply wants GTA to become something different for a new generation. That's their **** I'm allowed to say that I don't particularly like the direction.What shocks me most is that I keep stopping GTA 6 and thinking about going back to older games. I'm sitting here looking at the 200+ GB taking up my drive and wondering whether I'd rather have the space back.I never imagined I would say that about GTA 6.I'm going to keep playing because six hours isn't enough for me to judge the entire game fairly. Maybe something will eventually click. Maybe I'll come back here after 30 or 40 hours and completely change my review. Honestly, I hope I do. But right now, after waiting 13 years for this game, I'm not angry as much as I'm disappointed. Maybe GTA isn't made for guys like me anymore. Maybe it's time for some smaller, hungrier developer somewhere to pick up the torch and create the next great open-world crime game that isn't afraid to be offensive, ridiculous, violent, politically incorrect, and completely unapologetic. If that happens, I'll be there. Six hours into GTA 6, I can't believe I'm saying this, but for the first time in my life, I'm playing a new GTA game... and wishing I were playing something else.

author: Linkobloke
quote:
Spoiler Free Review 

GTA 6 is a huge world. It is fun to explore as always, some fun glitches that keep the charm. Graphics are amazing, performance is lackluster as expected but I grew up a Nintendo fan, so it didn't bother me much.
It is fun how they tried to build character dynamics, but a lot of it is just an interactive movie. That's what I hate about modern non-Nintendo games. I press a button during a cutscene, and it feels like a slog. Character work is decent, but there's much better out there, like other rockstar game Red Dead Redemption 2 for the amount of time the game tries to get you in a relationship. GTA was always crime, and it's like a movie, it takes too long to kick in. I have patience yes, but how much more normal life simulator do I need until I can do some crimes. Obviously, there's freedom to it, but the game is too realistic. Gaming is going in the wrong direction of making everybody lose their imagination. Me personally, I don't want to play real life far-fetched version in a video game. It is like a slog at the beginning of the game and too much of it is an interactive movie. Like Minecraft story mode. When I try to mess around the performance starts tanking and because it's so realistic it is noticeable rather than like Mario where it's a cartoon, so it doesn't stand out much. A lot of this game is targeted towards the relationship between Jason and Lucia and I get that, but games like Majoras Mask have the best character work out of any video game ever while you still have freedom to play the game. The world is endlessly big, but the story locks you in it. 
BUT hence the 6 positive points the world is so fleshed out, and I don't think I'll ever run out of stuff to do. Doing what I want is the best part, but the story part of it disappointed me a lot. This game will definitely be better in the long run, but I can't help but feel disappointed with the story, gameplay, etc. However, this is my opinion, and I was disappointed, but I will definitely come back a few months from now and hopefully have better feelings.

The GTA franchise, which is the very definition of physical and moral freedom; Rockstar, the undisputed master of creating unforgettable characters with tremendous charisma, alongside memorable and masterfully crafted stories; and a $2B budget on the most hyped title in history, after a 13-year wait...

I expected something more than a recycling of RDR2's mechanics with a few improvements, paired with a completely forgettable story and protagonists—and pulling off the feat of limiting and punishing the very essence of the term "GTA," both physically and morally

author: PikeRoyal
quote:
It’s not about the FPS, and it’s not about the missions. It’s about standards. You buy a GTA game because you want to do one thing: commit grand theft auto. If the game gets in the way of that; and by “gets in the way,” I mean forcing you to sit through more than ten minutes of exposition before letting you loose; then it has already failed. At that point, it’s a GTA game in name only, bloated with unnecessary mechanics and tedious, pointless busywork that gets in the way of the actual fun.

Just look at the difference: in GTA III, you're behind the wheel of your first car in under five minutes. In GTA V, it takes less than four. In GTA VI, it takes twelve. Twelve minutes! Why?

And don't give me the argument that romance missions are optional. The average player isn't going to know that. They'll naturally assume they're part of the main progression and end up doing them anyway. You're being forced to go grocery shopping. Let me repeat that: grocery shopping in a GTA game! That's like walking into a Hannibal Lecter movie and finding him behind the deli counter.

And then there's the ridiculous car ownership mechanic. In GTA VI, you actually have to own the cars you steal. Let that sink in: you have to own the stolen cars in a Grand Theft Auto game! At that point, the entire premise feels like it's been turned on its head.

The characters aren't any better. GTA has always been known for its larger-than-life personalities, outrageous personalities, and unforgettable characters. Here, however, everyone feels painfully dull. Even characters from the earliest GTA games manage to be more interesting and memorable.

Ultimately, GTA VI feels like a GTA game in name only. Everything that made the series what it was; the comedy, the gameplay, the characters, and above all, the freedom to cause absolute chaos; feels fundamentally different. It's as if the developers forgot what people actually play GTA for.

author: Kovanend
quote:
Gorgeous world, shameless business model. 6/10.
Visually, Leonida is a triumph of modern computer graphics—an $80–$100 interactive postcard with breathtaking dynamic lighting and world density. Unfortunately, once you stop admiring the sunsets and try to play it as a video game, the "100/10" hype shield evaporates fast:
1. Rent-Seeking in Offline Single-Player
Nothing screams "generational masterpiece" quite like opening the pause menu of an offline, full-priced single-player game and getting pitched a $7.99/month GTA+ subscription. Paying monthly rent for 10% shop discounts, free bus fare, a car model, and an early-game Crosstown garage—in a neighborhood the story actually moves you out of right after the first heist—is peak Take-Two "innovation." Back in 2004, San Andreas gave us cheat codes for free; in 2026, Rockstar sells them back as a recurring utility bill.
2. High-Definition Set Dressing Over Actual Gameplay
In a game set in South Florida, Rockstar built gorgeous, detailed tennis courts across the map solely as non-interactive background props—apparently full matches were too ambitious compared to 2013's GTA V. Instead, players are treated to tourist-trap mini-golf, shooting hoops alone, watching nonsensical TV cartoons, playing completely made-up fake games, and literally doomscrolling a fake social media feed on an in-game phone. Truly next-gen immersion.
3. 2013 Mission Rails at a Cinematic 30fps
That's 30fps on a good day—from time to time, even on PS5 Pro, you get scenes turning into a 20fps slideshow. And don't even get me started on the bugs and glitches I personally ran into throughout the campaign (no story spoilers here). Either way, a 30fps cap with noticeable stutters in 2026 already feels dated, especially paired with a 25-hour slow-burn intro and rigid mission scripts that fail you the second you step three feet off the developer's invisible railroad tracks.
4. Predatory One-Way Account Lock-In
No physical disc in the retail box, no cross-save progression, and zero cross-platform ownership—even though you are forced to link a Rockstar account. That account exists purely to serve you subscription ads, ensuring you get the privilege of buying the exact same game a second and third time when PC and next-gen ports will finally arrive.
Strip away the access-media paid applause, and you are left with a stunning diorama wrapped in cynical corporate extraction. Calling this a 6/10 is actually being very generous, I think—and I really mean it.

author: UnpaidNPC
quote:
When realism becomes a chore, where exactly is the fun?
Let's get one thing straight. GTA VI is an incredibly ambitious game. The animations are fantastic, the world is ridiculously detailed, and there are moments when you genuinely stop playing just to take screenshots.
Imagine The Last of Us, but in a fully explorable open world, with an absurd number of activities, minigames and missions.
Sounds incredible, right?
Well, it is. Until you start playing it.
The Good Stuff:-
There is plenty to appreciate here. 
Animations: The sheer number of animations is impressive. Almost everything looks carefully crafted, and the gameplay is genuinely screenshot-worthy.
Living world: The world feels alive. Random events, NPC interactions and little environmental details make exploration worthwhile. 
Activities: Plenty of side activities, minigames and missions to keep you occupied. 
Soundtrack: Absolutely fantastic. Rockstar knows how to put together a soundtrack. Open world: A massive, fully explorable world with an incredible amount of detail.
Customization: A decent variety of weapons, vehicles and customization options.
Character development: Characters physically bulk up depending on their activities. Something we had already seen in GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2.
There is clearly an enormous amount of work here. Nobody can deny that. 
The Not-So-Good Stuff:
This is where expectations meet reality.
1. Performance in 2026: A game releasing in 2026, running at 22 FPS on PS5. On Xbox X it was even worse.
Seriously? Even GTA games on the PSP managed to target 30 FPS. I understand that the game is ambitious, but ambition shouldn't automatically excuse performance optimization.
2. Movement feels choppy: Walking, running and driving don't always feel as smooth as they should. The experience can feel unnecessarily sluggish, especially when you're expecting a modern AAA game.
3. Why do I need a day-one patch? If I'm paying premium money and pre-ordering a game, I shouldn't have to depend on a day-one patch to get the experience I was promised.
4. Where did the GTA freedom go? Remember when GTA was about doing absolutely ridiculous things in an open world? Well, some of that freedom feels strangely restricted now.
Can't steal cars in my own neighborhood.
Can't ram planes into buildings.
Can't drive a car over protestors.
Can't make out with a hooker even after 10 hrs gameplay.
Can't shoot the gay people
Can't drive car over protestors. 
Instead, I get plenty of realistic everyday activities.
5. Realistic chores nobody asked for: Fixing apartments. Painting walls. Performing mundane household activities.
Seriously, Rockstar?
I bought GTA, not an apartment maintenance simulator.
6. Weapon variety: For a game of this scale, I expected a more impressive variety of weapons. The arsenal I get is average. 

My Biggest Problem: The Price Let's put things into perspective.
I live in India, where the Ultimate Edition cost is ₹7,499 where Minimum wage is 7410 INR/ month.
That's essentially an entire month's income. Think about that for a moment.
I'm spending an entire month's salary on a video game. And what am I getting in return? 
A game where I can spend hours painting walls, fixing apartments and performing everyday chores.
If I wanted to experience the excitement of household maintenance, I could simply stay home. I didn't pay ₹7,499 to become a virtual apartment caretaker. 

My Final Take: My biggest disappointment isn't the graphics, animations or even the performance. It's the direction Rockstar seems to be taking. 
GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 gave us memorable worlds, freedom and experiences that made you want to keep playing. 
GTA VI feels like a game made by devs of GTA Online. (completely different team)
The game has an incredible world, fantastic animations, a brilliant soundtrack and an astonishing amount of detail. But technical achievement and entertainment value aren't necessarily the same thing.
And those journalists handing out 10/10 scores? I hope they got paid.
A beautiful, ambitious game. But at ₹7,499, I expected a lot more fun and a lot less virtual housekeeping.

author: zeldaracer1
quote:
GTA 6 unfortunately represents everything wrong with modern gaming: ridiculous budget, an obsession over graphical fidelity, digital-only release and high price tag (even higher if you want the full experience). 
If you're committing all these sins, the game better deliver on all these **** yet, what are you doing for the first few missions? Installing stairs. Painting walls. Working out. Perhaps grabbing some fast food in between missions? Doesn't sound 10/10 to me. Add in the fact the game doesn't even hold a steady 30fps in the big 2026 (unless you spend 900 dollars on the PS5 Pro - if you can find one). Don't forget the classic wonky GTA physics, including climbing out of an airplane at the last second, hitting a tree at hundreds of mph going to a dead stop!.. only to be perfectly fine.
Of course there's the lauded story too, with it's fascinating characters, so fascinating that you constantly have to convince yourself that they're better than previous protagonists and side characters. The oft praised relationship is lopsided btw, with Jason doing a significant amount of the heavy lifting until (spoilers) he gets hurt and Lucia finally has to pretend like she's putting in the effort.
There are, of course, more subjective aspects of the game, like the questionable commitment to realism in things like increasing stats, waiting to be able to own more guns, as well as the driving physics which yet again may not be everyone's cup of tea.
The open world does feature emergent gameplay, with lots of scripted but seemingly unique interactions with NPCs. Is the extreme size of the map really necessary though? Is it actually fun to spend minutes and minutes driving, biking, etc across the map?
And finally, the big elephants in the room: if this is 10/10, what about the PC release that will double the framerate? Or GTA6 online, likely sold separately to squeeze every last cent from the mainstream consumer. How can you add to a maximum score? There isn't an 11/10 just like this isn't a 10/10.

author: danny-r
quote:
A very polished entry in the GTA series as expected. However I have two major gripes with the game. 

1. GTAVI is by far the least "arcade" feeling entry in the series. Unlike the PS2 era GTAs and even IV & V, this entry is slooowww with some mechanics (ie: you can't simply steal cars, you have to either lockpick or smash windows instead of simply stealing any car off the bat) and mechanics that are limited for "realism" (you can only carry two longarm weapons on hand instead of having a weapon wheel carrying a variety of weapons) plus driving feels EVEN WORSE than V. 

2. Lack of blips of hostiles on the mini map. How the Hell am I supposed to fight off hicks in a camp without knowing there are alligators approaching me from behind that can kill me if I don't fight them off quickly in a QTE while in a damn shootout! 

3. The "criminal profile" system or whatever (From Professional to Irredeemable) punishes players who would expectedly commit crimes in a game about crimes. And not just that, you get penalized for anything the game deems "immoral" even if its accidental (like running over an animal by accident). Other actions that the game penalizes you for is punching NPCs, even in self-defense amd also shooting/killing enemies that again are trying to kill you. What is even worse is if you reach Irredeemable, it is locked in which from what I understand heavily affects gameplay. It makes playing the game anxiety inducing if you want to create chaos (in a series that used to be indifferent about outside of wanted levels)

I think patching in an "Arcade Mode" that eliminates some of the "life sim" elements and the "morality" system will get rid of these complaints and actually make the game more enjoyable cause there is a lot of side content

author: SparrowDev
quote:
Don't get me wrong, there are plenty of very impressive things this game has managed to pull off in ways the gaming industry has never seen before. From the downright astonishing graphics and animations to making the world feel more alive than ever by filling it with multiple random encounters. After launching the game, you can immediately see the budget that went into it.

I rarely leave reviews for games. However, as a consumer, I feel obligated to push back against these paid-off game journalists. It is not a 99-rated game. It does NOT deserve to win GOTY in ANY of the categories it was nominated for.

First of all, a 30 FPS cap is straight-up unacceptable in the big 26. This is supposed to be an action/crime game, yet you're essentially watching a slideshow presentation any time you get into a fight. I advise anyone to forget about playing it on the PS5 and wait for the PC release or another console (although RAM prices aren't going down, so it might take a while lol).

I think its main mistake is that the game is trying to appeal to literally everybody, therefore satisfying nobody except for Rockstar bootlickers. The story and characters are quite bland and clearly toned down compared to previous GTA games (so as not to offend anyone). This makes it significantly less funny and entertaining than previous installments, although it still has its moments, not gonna lie.

Not to mention the fact that the player's actions are much more restricted in the name of preserving the story, which, to me, is just a ******** excuse. What is the point of having a dynamic, beautifully simulated world with a huge map if you're going to restrict the player from fully interacting with it?

Another issue is its obsession with realism and poor pacing. There is plenty of content that feels out of place in a GTA game, to the point where it doesn't really feel like a GTA game anymore. That explains why it took 13 years to make, though. I get that it's meant to enhance immersion, but I think cutting a lot of the unnecessary content (and expanding on the action cuz ngl it's mid at best) in favor of releasing it earlier (and avoiding the impossible standards set by 13 years of waiting) would go a long way.

It is not a bad game in itself. Loved the new police system and driving in general. Definitely a product worth admiring on many levels, but the way it's being overhyped by critics is insane. I feel like gamers shouldn't settle for this lowkey corporate slop, otherwise things will only go downhill from here.

author: SlothofAcedia
quote:
GTA 6 is a deeply underwhelming game despite the absurd production value. 

The first issue is the game takes itself far too seriously. There are small hints of the previous humor the series used to have, but it's been stretched too thin and overly sanitized. GTA used to have some really funny parody and satire but the game feels too scared to actually riff on anything and spends way too much time trying to be a serious story to have any fun. But the game is so overstuffed with boring filler and minigames that it can't even tell a well paced dramatic story anyway, so it fails on both fronts.

Jason and Lucia aren't as interesting as previous GTA MCs that felt like larger than life characters. Jason feels like he is on sedatives with how little he emotes and how much he mumbles and grunts. Lucia is at best mildly irritating when she does something dumb and otherwise is just too plain. It felt like in their attempts to make the characters more realistic they pulled out too much personality. But at the same time they lack the nuance and complexity of a well written character like Arthur Morgan who could be interesting without being zany.

The game experience is also bogged down by far too much realism/lifesim content. Stealing a car went from quick and fun in GTA 5 to frustrating in 6. Often it's not even worth the effort because a car could have a tracker, or require you to make keys, or be unable to start, etc. And you'll end up driving overly safe anyways because early game funds are too tight that you don't want to pay for tune ups. And you can only carry a few guns at a time. And you need to drive to gas stations and pay to refuel. And the game penalizes you with negative karma points leading to bad endings if you kill too many cops or civilians. Yes, the classic GTA staple of random wanton violence is now something the game punishes you for. The game even makes the music all scary and amplifies the sounds of screams to guilt you about shooting weapons in public places. Rockstar has completely lost track of what a lot of people loved GTA games for: driving like a maniac around a cool open world causing mayhem and shooting stuff.

The game itself seems too afraid to let you make your own fun as well. "No, you can't shoot this person" , "No you can't hit these people with your car", "No you can't leave this person on the traintracks to get squished like you could in RDR2". Obviously this was just an attempt to avoid controversy, but that's a canary in the coal mine in and of itself: GTA used to BE the controversy. It was about violence and sexual content and it was the game parents didn't let their kids play. My question is: why include characters that you can neither steal from, hit or shoot in a game about shooting, hitting and stealing?

So in the end GTA 6 feels disappointing because it doesn't understand what made previous GTA games fun. Yes it's very detailed. Yes it's very pretty. Yes there's a ton of content. (Hence why I'm not putting its rating in the red) But it's a sandbox game that has far too many walls and elements of realism to be a fun sandbox and the overly serious narrative and weaker characters mean the story cannot carry the experience either.

author: Gabriel_gamer97
quote:
O game, como um todo, é extremamente satisfatório! É nítido o milagre técnico operado pela Rockstar, assim como o capricho nos detalhes, nos gráficos e na riqueza de seu mundo. Este jogo está claramente anos-luz à frente de quase todo o mercado de games.

Entretanto, minha avaliação é pautada pela relação entre expectativa e realidade. Considerando tudo o que foi prometido, o jogo fica aquém em algumas questões técnicas, apresentando diversos bugs que eu mesmo encontrei durante a experiência. Além disso, há momentos em que o ritmo se torna excessivamente arrastado — e nem me refiro ao capítulo 1.

Pessoalmente, amo Red Dead Redemption 2 e, por isso, um ritmo mais lento não costuma me incomodar tanto. Porém, em GTA 6, há momentos em que a experiência oscila demais. Sinto que faltou alguma coisa na direção do jogo, embora não consiga explicar exatamente o quê.

É um jogo massivo demais e, na minha opinião, também peca pelo excesso de colecionáveis necessários para alcançar os 100%. Chega a um ponto em que me senti como se estivesse trabalhando, tornando a experiência bastante massante.

Os personagens principais também foram uma grande decepção. Jason não tem absolutamente nada de interessante, enquanto Lucia é extremamente irritante. Os personagens secundários, por outro lado, roubam a cena — inclusive um em particular que, quando apareceu, me fez surtar!

Dito tudo isso, GTA 6 é, sim, um jogo incrível! Fui bastante criterioso em minha avaliação, principalmente pelo valor cobrado pelo jogo. E, mais uma vez, tudo se resume a uma única questão: Expectativa x Realidade.

author: LoadBR
quote:
I've played about 20 hours of the game, 33% of the story so far, and I'll tell you what this game is missing.
It's missing a Prologue, and options like in Cyberpunk.
For a game everyone has been waiting for, its way too linear.
Jason is a bore, Lucia gets too much spotlight especially with the emotional contrast between them, and there is a lot of small, but noticeable traits that make the game feel like you're a dog on a leesh.
"You can't do this, you can't do that..." Why can't a raise a gun here? Why can't I just do something else?
Why is there such emphasis on their relationship?... Like, in the middle of a damn job you have a prompt to hold Lucia's hand? Come on...
Also, people praise the graphics and all... guys, I can play modded Skyrim with the same looks, its not that deep. Looks don't make the game.
A hooker can go from a 3 to a 6 with lots of makeup, but what turns a 7 into an 8.5, or a 9.5 into 9.9 might just be some nice lipstick.
You know exactly what these developers wanted, and honestly, I don't think its a bad premise, its just missing context that could be solved with a prologue.
So how do you solve this?
Start GTA6 with some sort of failed Heist where Jason and some other bum are trying to raid some cartel and things go down the drain as halfway through it Jason has a PTSD attack from his time in the military, causing his friend to die and him to lock in or just run away like a bum and be thrown in the mud.
Add a timeskip, a flashback, showing what he did in the war, where he was deployed, what he did to fall out with the army... give him emotion as he cries over the body of a child in vietanam or some ****.
Then the prologue becomes his redemption where he slowly builds himself up, make amends to the family of his friend, connects with new people, new guys, and slowly recovers from his PTSD, becoming the calm Jason he is now.
He should blow out, explode with anger, cry, and then be embraced by the friends he made until then.Finally, perhaps as he realizes that living a life of a low tier thug isn't for him, Lucia appears and changes his life as he finally starts to get things together, culminating with him realizing he has a son and that perhaps he can indeed have a better life.
Lucia being in jail breaks him, and he spends many months thinking of what to do, and as he tries to distract himself by building things, such as repairing a house to give himself the illusion of a stable life, he learns Lucia is returning, and that perhaps the vision of the family he could have is just around the corner.
That is when he locks in a second time and becomes the real GTA protagonist he is supposed to be!
That is an easy fix, but to correct this story completely, the only way would be to add more options for every Quest like Cyberpunk.

author: Jaylolarper
quote: Yeah, GTA VI’s been a mess to talk about. Thirteen years of waiting, a 99 Metascore that feels completely disconnected from the actual game, and the usual review-bombing chaos on day one. Strip all that noise away and what you’ve got is an incredible open world stuck inside a pretty clunky, frustrating game.Leonida looks insane. The lighting, the crowds, the sheer density of the map… nothing else comes close. Rockstar’s detail work is still on another level. Problem is, that same obsession with “realism” makes the game feel heavy and slow as hell. If you liked how Red Dead 2 controlled, you might be fine. If you wanted something snappy, it feels like you’re wading through mud half the time. Characters still have to finish whole animations just to turn around or loot something, and free-aim gunplay is floaty garbage so you’re stuck relying on lock-on. The missions are where it really starts to drag. So much of the story is just point A to point B driving. Get in the car, listen to Lucia and Jason argue or monologue for five minutes while you follow the GPS, arrive, do a short set piece, then get back in the car and drive somewhere else. It’s the same structure Rockstar’s been running since GTA IV, and it feels even more noticeable here because the world is so dense and alive that you constantly want to stop and mess around… but the game won’t let you. Step off the pink line to flank someone or try a different approach and it’s instant mission failed. The story is basically a series of cutscenes connected by mandatory drives, and the driving itself is just filler while the characters talk at you. That doesn’t help the already shaky duo either. Lucia keeps making selfish, reckless calls and Jason just eats the consequences over and over. Watching that dynamic get framed as some deep tragic romance gets old fast, especially when so much of it is delivered during these long, forced car rides in the early hours that already feel like a stretched-out **** playing a big action game locked at 30 FPS (sub 30 fps in some cases) in 2026 just feels rough. Camera pans smear, gunfights feel sluggish, and the launch bugs and texture pop-in don’t help. Holding the PC version back only makes those compromises harder to swallow. The world itself is the best Rockstar’s ever made. As an actual video game though? It’s held back by outdated A-to-B mission design, sluggish controls, a frustrating lead duo, and that 30 FPS cap. author: Nuelo_
quote:
GTA6 es un juego que podría ser querido por varios y ser considerado un buen juego, pero son muchos los factores las cuales hacen que este titulo decaiga.
-La limitación de 30 FPS con decaídas hacen que varias partes de acción no se puedan a llegar a disfrutar como se deberían, carros volando, explosiones, múltiples disparos y hasta persecuciones son arruinados por los bajos frames.
-La historia no es realmente interesante y esto es gracias a sus protagonistas que no te dan ese interés de querer saber mas de ellos, como si lo hacen Arthur en DRD2 y hasta CJ en San Andres, además que los finales llegan a contradecir el inicio de la historia (y no olvidar que arruinaron por completo el mensaje final de la historia de Niko Bellic mostrándolo como un jefe criminal que trabajo toda su vida en esto).
-La jugabilidad no a cambiado en nada desde GTA 5 cosa que no es malo, pero si es triste que después de 13 años desde el antes mencionado GTA 5 no se haya agregado algo que lo haga único como en Borderlands o ya mas fantasioso, en Pragmata. 
-Las mecánicas "Realistas" son muy interesantes pero que terminan siendo molestas después de cierto punto. Presionar un botón o mover los joysticks para robar un auto son novedosos (Para la saga, porque en otros títulos si tienen esas mecánicas antes de la salida de GTA 6) pero terminan siendo enfadosas cuando se quiere robar un vehículo. 
-La economía no es un obstáculo al ser fácil el conseguir dinero, ya sea matando a NPCs, cometiendo asaltos y hasta completando las misiones.
-La moralidad no llega a ser tan importante, uno piensa: "Genial, será como en RDR2" pero no, es diferente y para mal, ya que no llegan a cambiar la historia o eventos que te encuentras por el mapa. Solo es una estadística mas que no influye en el gameplay.
-El mapa tiene el mismo problema que en GTA 5, la mayoría de zonas son aburridas y no tiene algo atrayente que te incite a explorar como si lo logran hacer en ToTK, Borderlands 2 o en Marvel's Spiderman para dar algunos ejemplos.
-Y finalmente lo peor de GTA 6 es la inclusión de bugs desde su salida aun sabiendo que tuvo un desarrollo de 13 años, es verdad que no tiene la misma cantidad de bugs como en Cyberpunk pero se espera mejor calidad en un titulo con un largo tiempo de desarrollo.

Esta critica solo se fija en los aspectos malos del juego pero también hay que resaltar las malas practicas anti consumidor que a hecho Rockstar junto a Sony, las criticas pagadas que dan un 100 aun sabiendo que describen cosas malas del titulo, la comunidad tan toxica que lastimosamente tiene esta saga y el obvio regalo que le dará Geoff Keighley en los Game Awards.

Chapter One in GTA VI focuses on character interaction with Lucia and Jason through cutscenes and non-action/low action missions. My personal issue is that we are not engaged in the relationship being built - rather it feels like we are being told to like the relationship. This picks up more at the end of chapter 1 (think the hospital mission), but even to get there takes around 10 hours.
-Removal of the weapon wheel really disincentivizes variety in gun play you’ll usually only use 2 weapons at a time, and this I think removes variety in missions. For instance, in GTA IV or V you might use a sniper at the start and as you get closer use an assault rifle, maybe use a shotgun in a building and an SMG while you drive off. In gta VI you’ll only be able to carry 4 weapons ahead of time, making spur of the moment gameplay limited.
In conclusion:
-You can tell this game is an evolution of the GTA franchise and that it takes massive inspiration from RDR2. I do not think it’s outrageous to say this is the best map Rockstar’s ever made. The foundations this game lies on is amazing and I cannot imagine how fun the online mode will be with others.However, I do not believe this game is perfect, its story so far does not have super fun missions in the first 2 chapters (16 hours in).I will edit this review of gta upon completion, however I believe my criticisms are fair and stop the game from being perfect. Upon replaying the game you it will be incredibly slow and the weapon system stifles creativity.

author: Gamingog
quote: GTA 6 – First Impressions at 30% Completion: Amazing World, Completely Missed the Target AudienceAfter reaching about 30 percent completion, my current verdict on Grand Theft Auto VI is pretty sobering. The open world itself is impressive, but when it comes to the core of the game—the story, tone, and mission design—Rockstar seems to have completely forgotten who made this franchise big over the last few decades.Story & Target Audience: Doesn't Feel Like GTA AnymoreInstead ****, bitingly satirical crime epic aimed at adult players who grew up with the series, the first third feels like a teen drama. Way too many missions revolve around mundane everyday tasks, parties, and the romance between Lucia and Jason, backed by generic "white girl party music." While older titles used over-the-top satire to expose drug abuse and excess, this game uncritically celebrates a shallow party-and-substance lifestyle. You can tell at every turn that the original lead writers are gone—the new writing feels like it was tailored for teenagers rather than GTA's actual core audience.Open World, Mission Design & Easter Eggs: Great Sandbox, "Ubisoft Loop" & Saints Row VibesThe open world itself is easily the game's biggest strength: the random encounters, reactive NPCs, and side missions are far more entertaining than the main story. That makes the repetitive design of the main missions—and especially the camp/hideout raids—even more disappointing. Find a hole in the wall, take out the enemies, loot the safes, wait 48 in-game hours, and repeat—that feels like a textbook Ubisoft formula (Far Cry or Watch Dogs), not Rockstar.Then there's how Easter eggs are handled: Rockstar used to hide mysteries like Bigfoot deep in the map so dedicated players could uncover them after finishing the story. In GTA 6, you practically run into Bigfoot within the first thirty minutes—as if the devs were terrified players might miss out on the joke. And when over-the-top "Hulk monsters" start getting into open shootouts with the police, the game crosses dangerously close into pure absurdity. Rockstar needs to be very careful not to go down the Saints Row route and ruin the credibility of its world.Police AI: Great Concept, Unfair ExecutionHaving a police force that actually feels threatening again and forces you to respect them is definitely a plus. Right now, though, the system constantly tips into unfair territory: even when you find a solid hiding spot, the cops seem to know your exact location straight through walls, surround you deliberately, and leave you zero chance. The balance between challenging AI and "wallhack cheats" is completely off.Tech & Graphics: Still Feels UnfinishedTechnically, the game runs far from smoothly on console:• Bugs & Streaming: You run into glitches almost every hour—from pop-in textures and muddy ground surfaces to tires sinking into the asphalt and wonky collision physics.• Image Quality & Reflections: Heavy ghosting, noticeable screen tearing, and terrible low-res reflections in rearview mirrors and on certain colored walls that look like shimmering aluminum foil.• Brightness/HDR: Dark areas get completely crushed; as soon as you turn up the brightness, a milky gray haze washes over the entire screen.Verdict After One-Third of the Game:A fantastic, living open world held back by an out-of-touch teen drama story, repetitive open-world mechanics, in-your-face gags, omniscient police AI, and glaring technical flaws.

author: Fiister
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI – A Beautiful World, But Is That Enough?

Rating: 5/10

GTA VI is an impressive game, and there's no denying the sheer amount of work Rockstar has put into it. The world is phenomenal, the environments are incredibly detailed, the characters have personality, and the soundtrack is excellent.

However, I think there's a difference between creating an impressive world and creating an exceptional game.

The Good

The world-building is arguably the game's greatest achievement. The level of detail, scale and immersion is genuinely remarkable. It feels like a world with its own identity, and there's clearly an incredible amount of effort behind it.

The characters are interesting, the presentation is excellent, and the soundtrack deserves particular recognition.

Visually and technically, there's a lot to appreciate.

The Bad

Unfortunately, I think the actual gameplay and storytelling let the experience down.

The core gameplay can feel clunky and repetitive, and the story missions are excessively restrictive. There are moments where the game feels more interested in controlling how you experience its world than allowing you to play freely.

The story itself was a major disappointment for me. I struggled to remain invested, and the pacing frequently made the experience feel unnecessarily drawn out.

There are also numerous bugs and technical issues that detract from the overall experience.

Another concern is the game's identity. At times, GTA VI feels much closer to Red Dead Redemption 2 than a traditional Grand Theft Auto experience. I appreciate Rockstar experimenting with its formula, but I don't think reinvention should come at the expense of the identity that made the franchise so popular.

I also question whether Rockstar has placed too much emphasis on its online ecosystem, potentially leaving the single-player experience feeling less developed than it should.

A Note on the Writing

Honestly, at certain points I started questioning who was responsible for the screenplay.

I'm beginning to suspect my childhood Teddy was involved.

For context, Teddy has absolutely no professional writing. Yet somehow, I'm convinced he'd produce a more engaging narrative.

His proposed storyline:

1. Get hungry.
2. Rob a convenience store.
3. Go home and clean the bedroom.
4. Take a nap.
5. Go on a date.
6. Forget about the date.
7. Rob a bank.

Somehow, I still think that has more narrative progression.

All jokes aside, the storytelling genuinely disappointed me.

Final Thoughts

I don't think GTA VI is a bad game. Far from it. It's an impressive technical achievement with an extraordinary world, but I don't believe that alone makes it a masterpiece.

There's a lot to enjoy, but there's also a lot to criticise.

I can appreciate the graphics, world-building, characters and soundtrack while still acknowledging that the storytelling, pacing, gameplay and technical performance have shortcomings.

I would rather see Rockstar deliver a more focused, engaging single-player experience than rely on the sheer scale of its world and the strength of its franchise name.

Final verdict: 5/10.

A very impressive world, but an underwhelming overall experience. I enjoyed parts of it, but I don't think it deserves the near-perfect scores it's receiving.

author: Tubey
quote:
At first, I could fully see why the critic reviews are what they are - this is an unbelievable achievement on a technical level and is often jaw-dropping in how it simply simulates a world. In that regard, GTA6 is a masterpiece.

But...

Well... the more I played it, the less I liked it. It has painfully bad pacing in the opening hours, with the 'dating simulator' criticism being very valid. It takes too long to open up to the open world it has, and when it does it is bogged down by busy work and chores which shows the influence Red Dead Redemption 2 had on the development of this game in a negative way - sometimes things need to be fun, not realistic, and GTA6 often misses the mark in that regard.

The story is outright bad. At first I thought 'well, it's different', and was willing to give it a pass - but no, the longer it went, the more I realised that there was literally no likeable or particularly memorable characters or story beats whatsoever. It's the worst writing the series has had in decades and doesn't hold a candle to GTA 4 or 5. Without spoilers, the Feng Shui mission will have you shaking your head in disbelief at just how outright bad it is, and it's indicative of the whole.

It also has far too many limitations for a GTA game. Areas you can't shoot, certain people you can't shoot, all sacrificed at the altar of ideological restraint. GTA was at its best as a sandbox that thumbed its' nose at sensibilities, and it's unfortunate that Rockstar has bent the knee to criticism to appease instead of sticking to their guns.

It is absolutely not a 10/10 game. Yes, the current user score (sitting at 5.4 as of review) is a result of brainless review bombing to counteract the 10s, but honestly I'd understand anything between a 6 and an 8, but would struggle to countenance anything higher or lower. 

It's going to go down as one of the most overrated and overhated games ever made, and make a boatload of money, whilst being nowhere near the best the series has offered.

author: JoshTar2005
quote: GTA 6 is genuinely one of the most impressive technical achievements I’ve ever seen in gaming. The sheer scale, attention to detail and number of things you can do are phenomenal. Rockstar has created an enormous, incredibly convincing world, and that deserves recognition. But I keep coming back to one question: just because you can do something in a video game, does that mean you should? For context, I'm approximately 7 to 8 hours into GTA 6, so these are very much my initial impressions rather than a definitive judgement of the entire game. My opinion on the story could certainly change as I progress, but I think I've played enough to form some thoughts on the game's overall design philosophy. There’s an almost obsessive pursuit of realism here that I don’t necessarily think makes the game better. Whether it’s maintaining your house, getting groceries or completing countless other mundane activities, I often find myself wondering what these things actually contribute to the experience. Yes, they’re optional, and yes, the attention to detail is extraordinary. But realism and entertainment aren’t inherently the same thing. It reminds me of Gabe Newell’s perspective on realism in games. Video games are, at least in part, an escape from reality. If I wanted to run errands, do chores and maintain a house, I could just do that in real life. And that’s perhaps my biggest criticism: GTA 6 sometimes feels massive for the sake of being massive. From a presentation standpoint, it’s phenomenal. The world is beautiful, the animations are extraordinary and the production quality is almost unmatched. However, the 30 FPS cap is particularly jarring, especially for a game that otherwise pushes technical boundaries so aggressively. Narratively, I’m considerably less impressed. The story hasn’t really grabbed me, despite some genuinely interesting characters. I really like Jason’s characterisation. He’s this relatively quiet, physically imposing bloke who seems to have a genuinely good heart, which is a refreshing direction for a Rockstar protagonist. Lucia is also exceptionally well written, although I’m not particularly fond of Jason’s vocal performance. What frustrates me most is the feeling that I’m once again becoming everyone’s errand boy, something that occasionally plagued the original Red Dead Redemption. Rather than feeling like I’m driving the narrative forward, I often feel like I’m simply completing tasks for other people. None of this makes GTA VI a bad game. Far from it. It’s an extraordinary accomplishment, and I can absolutely understand why people are blown away by it. But when I see people defending the game by listing the hundreds of things you can do, I can’t help thinking that they’re missing the point. A game shouldn’t be judged solely by how much it allows you to do, but by how much of that is actually worth **** VI might be one of the biggest games ever made.  I’m just not convinced that makes it one of the best.

author: 143Games
quote:
GTA6 hasn't hooked me the way I wish it did. And I want to start with my biggest issue, and it's the save system, because it's done in a way that I feel doesn't respect the players time. First, there isn't really an autosave system in place. I think I understand why, but even the manual save has it's issues. There were a handful of times I wanted to save, only to have it grayed out. At that point, I had to choose between losing my progress, or keep playing until the option becomes available again. For people that have a busy lifestyle, such as being a parent, some people may not have more than an hour or 2 a day to play. The perfect example for me was at launch. I played at midnight, it was past 2 am, and I wanted to get some sleep, but I couldn't save. I either had to lose progress or keep playing. I know the PS5 has a "Rest Mode", but I've been burned by that a few times. I've had issues where the PS5 would not wake up forcing me to force shutdown/unplug the console. For those that don't get much playtime, it's something they have to be mindful of. If you only have 1 hour to play, you could easily lose 30 mins of progress because of the save system. For a game of this magnitude, I find this disappointing, especially when other games take care of this without issue. Reviewers sometimes complain about save slots and such, so I'm really surprised no one talked about it. I'm guessing it's because they get to play the game for long hours for the review. 

There's no denying that the world is phenomenal. The visuals, the interactions, it's really impressive. It's what made me want to explore it's world. However, the pacing of the game eventually made me forget about the immersive world, and often times, the stuff I did in the game started to feel like a chore instead. I did get invested in Jason and Lucia's relationship, but often times, the game feels like it drags to the point that I kinda wished the game played like Heavy Rain or Life is Strange, simply because I wanted to get the story moving. And this is where I also have some issues with certain reviews. The game starts off very very slow, even some critics mention this, but for some reason, that's perfectly fine for GTA6.

I have other issues, such as performance, bugs, and the gameplay, especially gunplay, but I think this should be enough to share my opinion on GTA6. I can see why many praises this game, and it deserves it, but it definitely has its fare share of issues.

Ampliando en gran manera la posiblidad de ir y buscar nuevas aventuras por doquier. Tampoco hay que ignorar su apartado artístico y gráfico, que tal vez puede llegar a ser el mejor de la saga, constando con diferentes temáticas dependiendo de la zona en la que estés, y resaltando entre todas, la temática que representa a Vice City, siendo de la misma paleta de colores de la que se baña el título de juego (siendo esta una combinación de rosas, morados y amarillos, dando una estética entre retro y playera).

author: movompomoh
quote: Its like two different games stitched together. The foundation is a solid, beautiful and interactive Florida. The story is an absurd collection of equitable lessons baked into a poor imitation of past GTAs. I last felt this with Spider-Man 2, where you are confused about why you are being forced through contemporary morality simulations when you just want to play the franchise you've purchased. The strange part is that through this lens the characters become repulsive, not because of the mass violence and crime they commit, but because the writers' idea of morality is very skewed. Lucia is ultimately a selfish, ugly human and Jason is open to abuse an manipulation from everyone around him. Where GTA used to be a wide open world, there are now moral limits on the depravity, according to an unspoken list of who is considered too "down" to be punched. The result is an experience more like Clockwork Orange than a heist film, where you are without agency, making everything feel sort of pointless.

author: HammerDrill99
quote: What It Could Have Been vs. What We Got13 years of waiting, only to receive another unremarkable experience from Rockstar Games. In the end, we’ve lost almost everything that once separated GTA from other franchises: creative freedom, unforgettable storytelling, fun gameplay, edginess, and, most importantly, the freedom to do things we simply cannot experience in other entertainment products.Instead, we got performance issues, political correctness, unnecessary restrictions, and a disappointing lack of the rebellious spirit that once defined the franchise.Despite its absolutely amazing open-world design, incredible atmosphere, and enormous potential for player freedom, the game repeatedly restricts you. Throughout my playthrough, every time I started to forget about its problems and genuinely enjoy myself, something immediately pulled me out of the experience—whether it was a gameplay mechanic, a questionable storytelling decision, another restriction on player freedom, or a performance issue. It constantly ruins the immersion that should allow us to escape the real world for a while.Long story short, what bothers me the most is that this could have been the greatest game ever made if certain political and narrative decisions hadn’t been forced into the experience, and if Rockstar had stayed true to the spirit of GTA.I still have hope for the PC version, where the performance issues could potentially be fixed. Unfortunately, the damage done to the gameplay and storytelling cannot be repaired so easily without the efforts of modders. And that is something we should never have to rely on to get the GTA experience we expected from the franchise in the first **** it still better than most games out there? Absolutely. But is it the masterpiece we expected from Rockstar Games after 13 years? Not even close. It doesn’t feel like something truly special that will be remembered for generations.Sadly, I’ve lost hope that we will ever see another extraordinary Rockstar experience like Red Dead Redemption 2, GTA IV, San Andreas, or Vice City.With this release, I think it’s finally time to accept that the legendary GTA we once knew has come to an end.

author: kogi411
quote: Doesn’t feel like a true sequel to GTA 5—broken narrative dynamics and rough PS5 launch issuesAfter waiting 13 years and playing this on my PlayStation 5, I honestly have to say: GTA 6 doesn't feel like a true successor to GTA 5 at all.First off, the technical state on PS5 at launch is really disappointing. Being locked at 30 FPS in 2026 already feels sluggish, especially during heavy shootouts and high-speed chases where the framerate noticeably dips into the 20s—and even below 20 FPS at times. Combine that with clunky, stiff aiming mechanics, input lag, and random crashes (like the CE-108255-1 error that wipes out progress if you aren't constantly manual saving), and it feels way less polished than a 13-year development cycle should be. There are also plenty of immersion-breaking launch bugs—clipping through floors, weird NPC glitches, and mission softlocks.More importantly, the core identity of GTA—and its character writing—is completely broken here. GTA 5 was all about over-the-top freedom, chaotic sandbox fun, and charismatic leads you actually wanted to root for. GTA 6 feels like a slow, restrictive drama bogged down by tedious errands and a deeply flawed dynamic between Jason and Lucia. Instead of a mutual, two-way partnership where the player actually has agency, Jason is written like a spineless doormat who constantly bends over backwards for her. He is literally dragged around on a leash while Lucia does whatever reckless thing she wants with zero consequences or respect for him. It creates this bizarre, frustrating dissonance: in a GTA game where the player is supposed to feel the most free, it feels like Lucia is the only one with actual freedom, while you’re just stuck cleaning up her **** seriously, claiming that launching exclusively on consoles first is "for the players"? Give me a break. Everyone knows they're going to release it on PC later anyway just to double-dip and make us buy the exact same game twice—except the PC version will actually run properly above 30 FPS. What a joke.Look, I’ll give credit where it's due: visually, Vice City looks incredible, and sure, it has plenty of new features and details. But we are living in 2026—an era where AI is replacing human jobs and technology is advancing beyond imagination. How are you going to call a game "next-gen" or "cutting-edge" when it's locked at 30 FPS and dropping below 20 FPS? If console hardware clearly can't handle this game properly, you should have launched it on PC from day one instead of feeding us a choppy tech demo.Honestly, even if they had released it on PC from the start and let it be judged strictly on its story and gameplay without technical excuses, I’m convinced it still would have only landed around an 8.7 to 9.3. Because as I said, instead of a true GTA 5 sequel, it ended up becoming some bizarre hybrid of RDR2 and GTA that loses what made the series legendary. And after this mess, every single critic who handed out a 10/10 score is going to be completely ignored by gamers. Why would anyone waste their time reading paid advertisements?

author: HarunAS__
quote:
Honestly, the game is terrifyingly outdated, as if Rockstar jumps across the years without following them to see how much other games have evolved. The level and mission design are very old, don't live up to a game of this scale, and are completely unacceptable in this day and age.

The gameplay is below average, has no wow factor, and doesn't even match average games today. The story is weak, riddled with terrifying gaps. The characters and dialogue are as basic as it gets, and if we compare them to their previous game from eight years ago, they'd be wiped out without a doubt!

The game's pacing is lethal in this era, since it's unbearably slow. As for the music, its presence is very weak, and the memorable melodies barely count on one hand. Technical performance is catastrophic by every standard for a game that took so much time and got massive funding.

The restrictions that kept the player from getting the full experience are completely unforgivable; freedom in games from the same series can't be much greater than in a modern game!

Its biggest strengths will definitely lie in the visual and audio sides. The world design is exquisite in every detail, from the cities and their stunning lighting distribution to the environment design with its seas, forests, jungles, etc., accompanied by truly great sound design that had massive focus poured into it. Beyond that, though, everything is super simple and mid.

The game can never live up to players' expectations even if it delivered the greatest things the industry can offer, because their expectations are truly terrifying and impossible to reach. Yet from my perspective - someone who never exaggerated their expectations at all - the game didn't even try to reach those expectations - it didn't even attempt to!

author: Anford
quote:
13 Years of development. More than $1 Billion Dollars.
Other than Sony trying to normalize a digital future using the worlds most anticipated launch as a trojan Horse, GTA VI fails to live up to the hype for people other than casual gamers in its current state.

How can the game release in such a buggy state and still get praise from "game critics" and be forgiven by the average Rockstar Stan, while games like Cyberpunk release in a similar state and literally get pulled from the store and offered refunds? Is this not double standards at its core?

As for the game itself, it lost the arcade plot of previous GTA games as is now a RDR2+GTA Hybrid.

The realism mechanics behind RDR2 were heavily involved in GTA VI, from the relationship systems, limited loadout for weapons while storing everything else in vehicles (horses), animal and fauna study, eating for health and stamina buffs, manual looting, and Focus (Deadeye).
It is essentially a RDR2 simulator using a GTA disguise.

I would have no problem with this in any other game or title, but it is indeed a GTA title.

Regarding the "woke" allegations from many grifters, I do not believe the game itself is actually "woke" because the word has essentially lost its meaning.
It is not "woke" to gift your partner flowers, or do activities surrounding your partner.

Even so; a romantic relationship being a main part of the games identity does not work for a GTA game when you have to play as both characters.

As sexist as it may sound, 99% of the audience for GTA games have always been men that want to live a power fantasy, and these men do not want to play relationship simulator.

As for the graphics: this is probably one of the most beautiful and visually realistic games ever made.

The downside for consoles is the 30FPS cap, which many fans will say it is a cinematic experience.
Regardless, we should expect more from the most expensive entertainment product in history.

In conclusion: GTA VI betrays the GTA Formula and does not live up to its hype.
