author: Vilaaaas
quote:
# **GTA VI — A Good Game, But Far From a Masterpiece**

### **1. Graphics and Visual Presentation**

GTA VI's graphics and level of detail are undoubtedly its biggest strengths. However, I also consider this one of its main weaknesses: much of the experience seems to revolve around visual presentation. In my opinion, without such impressive graphics, the game's overall reception would be considerably lower.

### **2. Story and Narrative**

The story is interesting and does its job, but it is far from extraordinary. It isn't particularly complex, surprising, or profound. It's an enjoyable narrative, but not something that makes the game stand out on its own.

### **3. Gameplay and Innovation**

Perhaps the most disappointing aspect is the lack of genuinely new or surprising elements. Based on my own experience, both playing the game and watching others play, GTA VI offers very little that feels truly innovative.

At times, it feels like playing Red Dead Redemption 2 in a modern setting, with many of the same ideas and mechanics. Despite the visual improvements, attention to detail, and additional features, I haven't found anything particularly revolutionary. This takes away from the experience, especially considering how many people are calling it an absolute masterpiece.

### **4. Performance, Optimization, and Bugs**

One of my biggest disappointments is the game's performance. Considering its release year, lengthy development period, and enormous budget, I expected significantly better optimization, accessibility, and stability.

Rockstar seems to have prioritized graphics, minor details, and realistic mechanics at the expense of equally important aspects, particularly performance and optimization.

Another questionable decision is the excessive number of commands, interactions, and minor details that add very little to the actual gameplay. Many features seem to exist primarily to create an illusion of realism and complexity rather than meaningfully improve the experience. They make the game more complicated while potentially increasing its hardware requirements. It's fair to question whether all these additions are really necessary.

The game also has a considerable number of bugs, both visual and gameplay-related. Some are minor graphical issues, while others directly interfere with the player's experience. At times, it genuinely feels as though the game was rushed and didn't receive enough polishing and bug fixing before release.

It wouldn't be unreasonable to question whether there was pressure to release the game before The Game Awards, potentially increasing its chances of competing for Game of the Year (GOTY). Of course, there's no evidence to confirm this, but the number of problems certainly raises questions.

Furthermore, the game struggles to maintain a stable 30 FPS in certain situations, with noticeable performance drops. This negatively affects the experience and is difficult to justify for a production of this scale.

### **5. Accessibility and Localization**

Another drawback is the lack of dubbing in other languages. While this may not bother everyone, it negatively affects players who struggle to follow dialogue while simultaneously reading subtitles.

During action sequences and moments involving movement, it can be difficult to focus on what's happening on screen while keeping up with the dialogue. This can ultimately compromise the player's understanding of the story.

### **6. Final Thoughts and Value for Money**

Unlike many reviews that seem heavily influenced by hype, expectations, or simply the fact that this is a new GTA, I don't intend to give the game a high score for those reasons alone.

Overall, GTA VI is a good, enjoyable game that offers plenty of interesting moments. However, I don't consider it a milestone in gaming history or a masterpiece, as many people seem to claim.

When looking at the overall experience, its performance issues, poor optimization, bugs, accessibility limitations, and lack of innovation significantly affect my evaluation, especially considering today's industry standards.

Ultimately, I get the impression that Rockstar failed to deliver everything it had been promising over the years. It's a good and entertaining game, but nowhere near the extraordinary experience that Rockstar itself spent years building expectations for.

Finally, there's the price. In Brazil, the game costs approximately **R$400**, which is an extremely high price considering the purchasing power of Brazilian consumers. Personally, I wouldn't recommend buying it to someone who is still undecided, as I don't believe the price fully reflects the experience being offered.

I would be willing to pay **no more than half its current price (approximately R$200)**.

author: xevman
quote:
This game is an outstanding technical achievement. I am genuinely in awe of the world Rockstar has built within the confines of a video game. The environment is convincing, obsessively detailed, and visually stunning, setting a new benchmark for immersion and realism.

My biggest issues lie elsewhere. The game introduces a significant amount of life-simulation mechanics that, in my view, add very little to the overall experience and could have been omitted without any real loss. Rather than enhancing the core gameplay, they often feel like distractions from what makes GTA enjoyable. 

I am also not a fan of the writing. Lucia is difficult to connect with from the outset, and as the story progresses and more of her character is revealed, I found myself liking her even less. 

Jason, meanwhile, feels like a soulless supporting figure whose purpose is largely to facilitate Lucia's story. 

As a result, he experiences little to no meaningful character development of his own. That's particularly disappointing because I believe the concept of a female protagonist in a GTA game could have worked exceptionally well. However, the execution here is undermined by questionable writing, weak characterisation, and a narrative that feels overly one-sided. In the end, it's a real shame. I wanted this game to be exceptional, but despite its remarkable technical accomplishments, I was ultimately left disappointed, so far.

author: SpookySem
quote:
First time reviewing, so bare with me. 
I am currently nearing the end of chapter 2 in the game and I’ve played for around 20 hours now (I’m taking it slow)

I played and loved every GTA game since San Andreas. And this game is very very different. Played GTA5 for the most time. And personally I am the most excited about GTA6 Online

The game is in many ways incredible. Graphics, the map creation with all the interiors and every detail just being right. all the different mechanics. The NPC interactions and the entire feel of the game are amazing. I believe that online especially will be generational and fun for many years to come. 

The story is fun so far, there are 3 quests that have sticked with me so far. (SPOILER ALERT) The quest where Donnie gets eaten by pigs, the jetski ride with Matteo and the end of chapter 1 from the house explosion to the hospital scenes. These quests are amazing!

Now on the downside of the game.. 
The first 5-6 hours were extremely boring storywise. I really missed an action filled start like the bank heist in GTA5. A lot of these quests should have been side quests. Felt like a reallife simulator, I play these games to escape reallife. Getting groceries, fixing the house, going fishing, doing some diving, going to a bar with friends and playing VIDEOGAMES inside a VIDEOGAME really pissed me off (especially because I was tired after the midnight release)
Jason and Lucia also feel a bit bland sometimes, looking back at GTA-V, the protagonists had so much more character and energy. It felt like they went too safe for a GTA game.

Furthermore, the wanted system is something to get used to. On one side I think it is amazing, because the police is really a challange. On the otherside, I’m playing a game where I can be a criminal. And just protecting myself or stealing a simple car really gives me a hard time and it takes a while to get away from the cops. I’m starting to get better at it, and I’m happy that I can open doors without breaking the windows. But I’m not sure about this decision yet. The hotewiring and all the short ‘minigames’ are really fun and amazing tho! Really like this.

I’m still amazed at how big this map is. I do find it annoying that some cars are just locked behind features that I can’t use yet (like removing the tracker from cars and the key jammer) but I’m excited to unlock it.

So overall, I think the game did pretty well to live up to the hype. It has it’s amazing highs, but it really takes up to 10 hours to get into the flow and get started, which is my biggest complaint.

I am very excited to see what the rest if the story has in store for my. And especially GTA6 Online is something I’m hoping to see announced soon.

author: skepticals
quote:
***PROS***
Missions with action and actual grand theft and/or auto, are great.
Graphics are great
Great Map
Car play seems good

***CONS***
Performance hovering at or below 30 fps.
As a result, the difficulty seems to be orientated around the frame rate, as gun play would lag behind on more intense scenes. 
A large portion of the game are boring chores and watching events happen rather than being apart of them/causing them.
A large number of bugs on release
Pacing issues (More boring missions than fun ones)
No H00k3rs
$100 for the full game.
They try to force you to be more empathetic and it feels like you can't just screw around like you could as early as in the other games, so it feels like it's restricting in a way.

***OPINIONS*** I largely do not take this into account of my score given
I don't consider myself left or right, but there is a clear hatred toward men in the messaging. I don't recall running into one Lucia quest where she goes out of her way to make Jason happy. It's a one sided relationship of servitude towards her and only her. 
I also think it's pretty dumb they try to implement morality in a game franchise that's mean to escape from it.
***CONCLUSION***
Does it live up to the hype? At times, but in large part, no.
When its good, its great... but the cons are too much to overlook.
I think in time, the release hype window will fade and more honest and objective reviews will come more into light. 
That being said... Do I recommend? Not at it's current state.
I would say it's pretty mid, my opinions aside. If they fixed pacing, made the relationship optional, added the street women back, improved performance, and removed the morality aspects of the game, I would say it would be perfect and lived up to the hype and then could recommend. If/until then... I'd sit this one out boys.

author: mk0fficial
quote: I won't give GTA 6 a bad review like many people to fight against the corpo machine because Grand Theft Auto 6 isn't a bad game, it's just stale and monotonous 9 hours in. Much of the backlash against GTA 6's gameplay boils down to how clearly it's designed around the foundation they want for GTA 6 Online. Not being able to steal cars like traditional gta off the street like before is a massive slap in the face to the name and legacy of the franchise, yet it’s obvious they did it to push premium car sales in Online later. Story-wise, the dynamic between the two new protagonists, Jason and Lucia, wasn't particularly fun or interesting, it leaned way too far into melodrama than the nitty gritty gang violence and exageration GTA V exelled on that 4 felt lacking. I also thought the chore missions were stupid and dragged out, forcing you to repeat tedious tasks over and over instead of letting you get through them quickly, most of them could be just 1 cutscene, which reminds me alot of quantic dream, click for an action. A lot of these design choices feel like Rockstar trying to rival Naughty Dog's level of hyper-detailed interactions within the game, but in practice, they just feel distracting—unnecessary fluff meant purely to flex the new tech. Overall, the game feels weighed down by pointless micro-details that sound impressive on paper, bloat the hardware requirements, and are going to be a total b!t to patch down the line. It reminds me of The Sims, where the systems are so tightly interconnected that tweaking one small thing can trigger disastrous glitches. At launch, it’s a soft 7/10 for me since it has room to improve later on, but right now, the experience is just underwhelming. Large, long, huge! yet underwhelming. I had high hopes for this game and I still have because I'm someone who sees No Man's Sky as well as improvements that several companies can do to make their games better post launch. I hope they bring back prostitution, plane crashes on buildings and the core GTA DNA on the online.

author: takiseharata
quote:
One thing I can say for sure: none of the people responsible for the story and main characters in this game have ever watched "True Romance"...because they prefer to read Harlequin romances.

If, like me, you dgaf about the story and just want to drive cars and race through the streets at night—spoiler alert...
In a game whose  core essence is driving, there’s no car interior camera view...
...but this of course can be explained by insufficient time, limited resources, and a delay that was too short.

The difficulty level is so pathetic that a drunk child with one arm could beat the game in a single run.

The character of Jason is completely devoid of depth and personality. Yet, instead of easily shining against the backdrop **** stripped of all emotion and charisma, Lucia is simply insufferably annoying.

Aside from its visuals, this game lacks everything.

You can’t build an "empire of evil" here, even though there’s plenty of space to do so. 
I want the chance to do all the things I’d never actually do in real life.
I want to plant fields of weed, cook meth in an RV, or distill moonshine in a barn by the light of the moon.
I want to invest in real estate, play the stock market, and mine Bitcoin.
I want to gamble in casinos, bet on UFC fights, and even sponsor my own fighters.
I could go on forever—the game world is vast and stunning, with more than enough room for all of this.
It’s shocking that a project like this lacks the passion and brilliant talent needed to transform this sandbox into a work of art—a symphony of chaos and destruction, and simply endless fun.

I’m furious with them; I get the impression that the people who used to make good games are no longer in the industry.
And the people currently designing them have likely never even played a good game.

author: lowkey10
quote:
I genuinely wanted to like this game. I paid €80 for it. I have nothing to gain from hating it. If it was great, I'd be **** loving it.

But man, it's GTA. I want to have fun committing crimes, not simulate every little inconvenience of being a criminal.

The shooting feels worse than GTA V to me, the driving is just okay, and there's no first-person mode. Then you have weapon storage, having to rely on your car for your arsenal, fuel, repairs, calling the mechanic, waiting for **** to happen, forced animations, unskippable dialogue and all the other little things constantly getting in the way.

The performance is also a big problem for me. On PS5, the game doesn't even feel like a consistent 30 FPS. You constantly notice frame drops, especially when there's a lot happening on screen, and it makes an already heavy-feeling game feel even worse to play. Being forced to play at 30 FPS would already be a compromise for me, but when it can't even consistently hold that, it becomes really distracting.

Individually, these things aren't huge. Together, they make the game feel like administrative work.

I also really don't like Jason and Lucia. Jason feels bland and weirdly disconnected from the criminal world, while Lucia often feels more like a baby than a grown criminal. The tone is all over the place too. The game can't seem to decide if it wants to be a serious crime story or just a joke. Characters can be involved in shootings and genuinely dangerous situations, then immediately act like nothing happened and start joking around.

Despite all of that, it's still a big-budget game with a lot of stuff to do, and I wouldn't say it's completely unenjoyable. There are good moments and less good ones. I just found myself frustrated far more often than I expected from a game I've been waiting this long to play.

author: Lord_Ka1n
quote:
It's fine, but they've removed or restricted so much of what makes GTA GTA. I don't care about the relationship thing. That makes sense. They're going for Bonny and Clyde and there's nothing wrong with caring about your partner, and a lot of the hyper realistic tasks from RDR2 were cool and really helped immersion.

Problem is, on top of how horrible the game runs and how buggy it is, is all the restrictions. It doesn't seem to want me to play it as a GTA game. Can't steal cars, can't fly into buildings, can't shoot up a bar, etc. The morality system has no place in a game about being a criminal.

author: Raadob
quote: Playing GTA 6 always meant causing chaos, having a fun time and getting a adrenaline rush from each mission. It was never meant to be a slow burn or a sophisticated game. The story felt too slow and too underwhelming. The adrenaline rush you had from previous GTA games was gone. It was replaced by grinding for stuff you didn't even care about. And I understand realism is what we've asked for but the way rockstar have done it isn't the way we wanted. Instead of it feeling immersive it felt slow and boring. I also feel the characters in the game especially the protagonists are nothing special. Lucia isn't that interesting and honestly she's annoying at times, and Jason feels dull. Way too dull. The jokes we had in previous titles are now gone, replaced by cheesy lines that are hard to sit through. I haven't had a laugh like I did with other rockstar made games in GTA 6. Not only is there no humor but the characters lack depth. I do not like accusing games of being woke as I don't believe in such a thing. But GTA 6 is woke. I can say that with absolute certainty and I hate that rockstar fell astray from their right path. While the story and characters are disappointing I was amazed and shocked about the graphics and amount of detail. It's the best we have in any game in history and it set a very high standard for other games to complete. It's a shame the writers had ruined such an anticipated game. I wish it was done in a different way. GTA 6 is a major disappointment and that pains me to say it.

author: benditjuno
quote:
There is a ton of bias reviews from critics and people bombing the reviews. Many points are true on both sides but it's like they choose to ignore the other. I am giving what I see after 30+ hours of gameplay. 

Overall, Grand Theft Auto VI is a technical marvel. The amount of detail combined with the sheer amount of content is at a level never seen before (even playing at 30 fps). Everything from the hair physics, car crash physics, mini games within the game itself, amount of music/voice lines, the upgraded NPCs and amount of interactions there. It is all amazing and makes the world feel full with endless opportunities for content. 

Then comes the story, some characters are interesting but as many have stated, there is a ton left to desire with Jason and I don't find Lucia much better from a fun/interesting character perspective. They both have their moments but overall I could be playing as a side character and be just as happy. Which means I am sort of indifferent of the 2 main characters and for a GTA game that is just... not enough. I don't want to feel like more could have been done with the characters but that is what I feel as I play them. 

I believe once on PC with more frames and even better graphics this will be a 8/9 just due to the world itself but some of the characters and story sections leave a ton to be desired. I have no clue how this is a 99/100 from the critics.

author: Asthman7
quote:
Starting with the cons.
Incredible slow start, Im usually fine with slow starting games like RDR2, movies/series but I was getting annoyed running errands, going to a bar to touch a pregnant woman belly(?!?!?). In the first 5 hours I maybe shot my gun twice in a mission. Game name is Grand Theft Auto and I cant even steal a s**tbox to drive couple blocks to my house without police chasing me like I just killed president, and then I need to change my outfit and police still remembers my face. After 15 hours I maybe laughed once during some random side mission, the humour known from GTA series is gone in my opinion. I need to exercise to boost my character, eat protein, sleep well, like I dont want to do this in video game, this game was overdone with the realism. I will continue playing, I hope the game picks up because it starts getting boring like cmon I can understand 2-3 hours of slow prologue but 15 hours of basically nothing, zero progression is very bad. The game performance on base PS5 that I barely used and is in pristine condition is atrocious, switching from playing on beefy PC with 240hz oled monitor to console 30hz on that same monitor was shocking to me, when the framerate is stable its playable but when I was exploring swamps I swear it was like 15 fps, its killing a lot of fun, also aiming on controller with that kind of fps is really hard for me, and im average skilled controller COD player so I cant imagine what its like for people that playing shooting game for the first time with a controller. Graphics are incredible but I will happily exchange some fidelity, npc/cars density for at least stable framerate or 40fps mode. Also I dont like this criminal profile system especially if its affecting ending of the game, like what do you mean Im getting punished for killing criminals and not sparing them In an M rated game. Jason doesnt have a personality and Lucia is little annoying for me, the relation between these two characters is not that bad like everyone is saying on X (cuck simulator) but I would prefer having an option to be just partners in crime and not lovers. Playing the game as intended and maintaining relationship so I don't have to hear any annoying comments directed at me is little bit exhausting.
There are couple of pros too, driving is very fun for me even in 30 fps, graphics like I said before are incredible, sometimes I feel like Im playing a movie, exploring is very fun, especially the swamps, fishing, and diving for treasures are also good. Encounters with random NPCs and getting missions from them is better than the main story for now.
I get why people are really annoyed with this game because expectations were through the roof and this game really underdelivered, it doesnt deserve 0/10 but also doesnt deserve 99/100 on metacritic from journalists, idk if Rockstar paid them or they fear losing early access to Rockstar games but this is showing that you cant trust them. 
For now its 5/10 for me, maybe I will change my rating to 6-7 if the story picks up but I heard it stays the same even at the 50-hour mark. Its an average game with amazing graphics, and its sadly lost the spirit of the GTA series.

author: Plgtv
quote:
Franchement, plus j'en vois sur GTA 6, moins je comprends l'engouement démesuré autour de ce jeu.

Alors oui, c'est beau. Oui, Rockstar sait créer des mondes ouverts impressionnants. Mais à quel moment est-ce devenu suffisant pour annoncer le chef-d'œuvre du siècle ?

J'ai surtout l'impression qu'on nous vend une prouesse technique plutôt qu'une véritable révolution vidéoludique. Des graphismes photoréalistes, des PNJ qui vivent leur petite vie et une ville gigantesque, c'est bien joli, mais derrière tout ça, quelles sont les véritables nouveautés en matière de gameplay ?

Le plus inquiétant, c'est cette impression que Rockstar pourrait sortir absolument n'importe quoi avec le logo GTA dessus et que certains crieraient quand même au génie.

Et puis, après autant d'années d'attente, je trouve assez triste que l'argument principal reste essentiellement la claque graphique.

Je ne dis pas que GTA 6 sera mauvais, mais pour l'instant, je vois surtout une machine marketing monumentale portée par une communauté qui semble avoir décidé de lui attribuer un 10/10 avant même d'y avoir joué.

J'espère sincèrement me tromper, mais à ce stade, mon enthousiasme est proche du néant.

Un jeu qui semble vouloir impressionner tout le monde, mais qui, personnellement, ne me fait absolument pas rêver.

author: CliffX17
quote: GTA 6 is finally here after 13 years. Overall, I feel like the game is good, but it is certainly no masterpiece or perfect game. I’ve been playing it on a PS5 Pro, and it feels clunky. The game is capped at 30fps but struggles to maintain it and takes dives every now and then. I’ve also encountered a multitude of bugs, however, none of them have been game breaking. Another issue I have is that there are some npcs that have invincibility for some reason. GTA has always been a game that promotes crime, so I’m not entirely sure why there are protected npcs. The first few hours of the game definitely wasn’t my favorite, it’s a slow burn that eventually picks up. Last thing I wasn’t too fond of was the limitations on carrying weapons, I understand Rockstar was going for “realism” but it’s a video game and I believe gameplay mechanics tied to realism can negatively impact the experience. Yes, I have some issues with the game and I have also had fun with the game too. For me personally, the framerate, bugs, and the deviation towards a more “social friendly” GTA is what ultimately drove me to the score I’m giving it.

author: ExQueueSee
quote:
8-12 years of dev time, 1 billion dollars spent. and regardless, the result is clear:
> 10/10 graphics design (it is gorgeous ngl)
> 2/10 optimization and performance (should have waited for a next gen console or just released the pc version instead)
> 3/10 story (incredibly boring until the end of chapter 1, doesn't hook the player up)
> 3/10 gameplay (again, chores are really boring till the game really begins, can't even do basic stuff that you should be able to in a classic GTA game, ex: stealing a car)
> 4/10 character design and development (jason starts and stays behind in character development, lucia gets the real attention but even her story doesn't really build up, the dynamics of the duo is also quite weak throughout the game)
> 6/10 world design and exploration (the design is definitely great, but exploring it comes with barricades, as if it is an open world with invisible walls)
> 7/10 audio and sound design (very cool overall)
> 5/10 music & soundtrack (incredible track choices, but at least 90% of them are licensed and not really written for the game itself, hence lacking originality)
> 6/10 immersion and atmosphere (almost really good but not. the main issue is that you are almost always guided for stuff you can do, immersion means forgetting you are playing a video game while playing a video game. guidances have no place in a game for immersion)
> 8/10 difficulty and balancing (there are difficulty adjustment settings, which is cool. but getting used to especially the possession of vehicles has a steep learning curve if you are not familiar with gta 4 and 5. this one is a mix of both)
> 9/10 content & variety (speaks for itself)
> 1/10 technical stability and polish (should have been delayed more or needed a pc launch)
> 5/10 UI/UX & accessibility (cluttered menus and vibe coded looking UI here and there)
> 7/10 AI/NPC behavior (overall good, but still can be improved.)
> 0/10 Value for Money (an at least $80 dollar for a sloppy launch, 100 for more "in game, offline" content. sets a bad example for future games in the industry)

Overall: 5.07/10

author: Dyguren07
quote:
About 37-ish hours in, GTA 6 still doesn’t get better or fun. Yes, visually it is amazing, the map is huge. But that’s where all praise ends.

The story is the weakest in GTA series. Jason is unrelatable and boring, and Lucia just makes this whole experience into a humilliation simulator.

Most missions are just chores. Every aspect of this game, aside from the visuals, is simply inferior to GTA 5, to me personally. They just removed so much of what made GTA fun... just why?

The amount of bugs and nonsense you encounter are just unforgivable for a game that took this long, that we waitwd for THIS LONG. I have lost count on the amount of times I have glitched to underneath the map by just WALKING.

To top it all, the fact this is "targeting" 30 FPS is just unacceptable in this time of gaming. Even Cyberpunk, despite its horrendous launch, had more promise than THIS if it ever got fixed, and after it finally got fixed, it became an AMAZING game.

In GTA VI's case sadly, even if performance gets eventuallt fixed, the rest of aspects of the game such as characters, story, and the few things I touched on in my review, will still remain a disappointment compared to previous titles, because you know well the current devs of the game won't change any of the writting or weird decisions, despite any feedback we give them. If they took a lot of fun out of GTA, it is because us fans don't truly matter.

My personal score that I can give is, at best, a 5/10, and that's being generous.

This game is simply unacceptable overall at launch, ans I simply don't see myself replaying this, in fact, I genuinely recommend to just go back to play GTA V instead. This was genuinely a waste of money for me, and too much stress with not enough amount of fun as pay off, which is heart breaking as a fan of the series... the wait was NOT worth it man.

author: AzaarThaL
quote:
Unstable 25 – 30 fps coupled with very noticeable input delay in 2026 is inadmissible. 

The gameplay is just the same boring, outdated "banter" slop, same as the previous rockstar titles - literally dozens of hours of playtime are dedicated to using a vehicle (holding the right trigger) to go from point A to point B or chase a target while the characters are having some banter.
And then you have some shooting set pieces with, once again, the same outdated, boring shooting mechanics, as well as being pretty much invincible as long as you have heals (so much for "rEaLiSm"). 
You also have the slow and tedious sim-like "rEaLiStIc" mechanics from RDR2, which have nothing to do in a GTA title - *press ∆ to loot* *press ∆ to interact* *press ∆ to grab* *press □ to drop* press this, press that...

You also have invincible NPCs; the game doesn't give you the freedom of being able to fail missions by killing those "important" NPCs - no fun allowed in big 2026 boys... 

Worst protagonists and side characters in a Rockstar title for as far as I can remember, there is genuinely not a single memorable character, and those few cameo characters don't count.
Jason "yeah..." "sure..." "Ok..." Duval is a cheap autistic copy of Ryan Gosling's characters from Drive and Blade Runner 2049, and it doesn't work at all, while Lucia is genuinely unbearable...

The game is unusually glitchy and janky by Rockstar standards.

Alright this review is getting pretty long and I'm getting tired of typing so... for the positives - The game looks good, not as good as heavily modded Skyrim though, but there's a caveat, the game is kinda blurry and the anti aliasing is horrendous. also, the map is big and there's a lot of side activities, that's it...
It's pretty obvious that most of the development budget went to create a big sandbox in order to extract as much money as possible from the l0b0t0mites that are going to spend money on the upcoming online mode, while the story got the short end of the stick.

author: AgentApoc
quote:
I’ve always appreciated what makes the Grand Theft Auto franchise special. The freedom to explore an open world, interact with the environment, discover things organically and create your own experiences is a huge part of its **** original GTA games, particularly San Andreas, demonstrated how enjoyable that freedom could be. Being able to explore, open doors, steal vehicles, interact with the world and simply decide what you wanted to do made the experience **** me, that sense of freedom and player agency is an important part of what defines Grand Theft Auto. 

I picked a 5/10 because whilst there’s strengths aka the open world and interactions there’s also game breaking bugs

It’s not just about following missions; it’s about feeling that you’re part of a living, interactive world.I also believe reviews should be written for genuine and legitimate reasons. People should feel free to express their honest opinions, whether positive or negative, without feeling pressured to change their scores because of what other people are saying.Equally, I don’t believe anyone should feel compelled to leave a positive review simply because they think a game is being unfairly review-bombed. Your rating should reflect your actual experience, not a reaction to somebody else’s opinion or an attempt to influence an overall **** you genuinely love the game, say so. If you have criticisms, explain them. Reviews should be about honesty, personal experience and constructive feedback, not competing campaigns to push a score in either direction.Ultimately, players deserve to have their voices heard, and genuine criticism and genuine praise deserve equal respect.

author: m0ku
quote:
Visually impresive and it's what Rockstar managed to achieve in terms of scope is a technological marvel that is going to set the standard in the future. 

However, it's a fact that greed pushed them to release this game one generation too early for current generation consoles don't have enough hardware power to run this almost fantastical piece of software. No one can seriously claim that in terms of performance is being held back. Some bugs here and there are to be expected on a game of this scale and scope, and while personally I haven't experienced anything game breaking, I have seen videos of vehicles clipping through other assets and being launched to the stratosphere and characters falling to the shadow realm. More "funny" than "this **** is unplayable" to be honest.

As for gameplay, it's GTA but with a more grounded and "realistic" flair too it. It's less "arcadey". and some people are going to like it, some are going to hate it, both veteran GTA fans and new ones. Gun fights don't feel smooth but it's mostly because of noticeably frame drops when they take place, cars and most flying vehicles feel clunky to control, but motorcycles and aquatic vehicles feel smoother. It may be due to size of the map, but missions feel a bit long winded or "longer".than they are supposed to.

Nothing much to say in terms of audio design. Can't never go wrong with almost all of the most popular songs in America and LATAM. The tasteful parody to certain political figures was a nice touch and actually funny.

Now, for the story, in my opinion it's the weakest point and it's mostly because of the protagonists. Neither Lucia nor Jason are compelling characters (so far): Lucia feels like a caricature of an empowered Latina woman with delusions of grandeur while Jason feels like he was intended to be portrayed as this calm, cool and collected ex-military man but he feels like dullard pushover who's only redeeming quality is his physicality.

Long story short, GTA6 is a technological marvel with a massive scope that is being held back by the current hardware and questionable creative decisions. There's fun to be had, for sure, but it's nowhere near the nearly perfect game the critics reviews will lead you to believe.

author: IVorza
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI is the newest entry of one of the most influencial franchises in the world. The game's rendition of Florida is nothing short of impressive and the narrative seems to fall into what made Rockstar Games the juggernaut that they are.

However all the good things get a bit overshadowed by how terrible this game looks and runs on a standard Playstation 5 system:

- The framerate is terrible. It does run at 30fps if nothing's happening on screen, but as soon as you get into a shootout or in the middle of a lot of traffic and trees, the framerate gets a toll.
- The input lag is a bit too high - this can be sorta worked around by reducing the controller's deadzone and increasing aim acceleration a bit, but it's still bad regardless.
- The game looks extremely blurry and fuzzy overall. And I'm not talking about a reported glitch that has been floating around, regarding the image getting stuck in an "all blurry" state and you having to restart both your game and system for it to return to normal. I mean the actual AA implementation - it's goddamn awful and makes me feel like I have cataracts.

All these things combined make up for a mediocre experience and I just can't seem to enjoy the game as much as I'd hoped, which makes it come as a bit of a disappointment for me. 
I don't mind 30fps, but at least make the experience somewhat enjoyable. There's no point having fancy raytraced effects everywhere if the game lacks image clarity and feels choppy to play.

I hope rockstar throws a patch to fix these issues, or at least some of them. When they do, I'll change my rating to what this game truly deserves. 
Until then, this is where I stand.

Do better Rockstar Games!

author: Sam_Day
quote:
My experience so far...

It's not bad. But in no way is this game a 10/10, as some established critics have claimed.

For the most part, the gameplay follows the tried and tested GTA formula carried over from previous entries. The main differences are higher resolution visuals, denser foliage, accessible building interiors, NPCs with more reactive dialogue, and driving controls that feel slightly delayed and awkward.

Ultimately, it's more of the same.

For me, GTA VI doesn't feel like a particularly significant evolution of Rockstar's previous titles. In fact, it feels as though the franchise has barely evolved mechanically.

I'll give credit where it's due. The game is absolutely beautiful. Its varied terrain, sprawling cityscapes, volumetric clouds, environmental depth, and exceptional sound design are all incredibly impressive. Few, if any, AAA studios could replicate the environmental detail and atmospheric presentation that Rockstar consistently delivers.

During my playthrough of the prologue, I was genuinely awestruck by the graphical fidelity and visual presentation. The high resolution textures, incredible attention to detail, and environmental realism made for an astonishing introduction. It was an impressive demonstration of how Rockstar had managed to go beyond simply improving graphical quality, creating a level of visual immersion and environmental realism that few other studios have managed to achieve.

However, as impressive as that initial presentation is, its novelty gradually wears off the further you progress through the game.

What initially feels revolutionary eventually becomes the baseline, making the underlying gameplay and its shortcomings much more noticeable.

Impressive presentation, however, doesn't make a perfect game.

GTA VI has plenty of flaws, and it's certainly not the flawless masterpiece that some reviewers are making it out to be.

---

After spending considerably more time with the game, my impression has shifted somewhat. GTA VI feels more like Red Dead Redemption with elements of Grand Theft Auto sprinkled throughout.

The story missions often feel static and uninspired. While the way they're presented and filmed is generally impressive, the missions themselves aren't particularly enjoyable to play. Engaging with the core gameplay has increasingly started to feel like a chore rather than an engaging experience.

The majority of characters encountered throughout the campaign also lack the personality, memorable interactions, and genuine chemistry that made the supporting casts of previous entries so enjoyable.

While the NPCs inhabiting the overworld initially impress with their seemingly reactive dialogue and conversational abilities, the novelty gradually begins to wear off.

Despite the impressive premise of having seemingly every NPC capable of holding a conversation with the player, most of these interactions eventually boil down to repetitive, predetermined dialogue responses.

Over time, the illusion of meaningful interaction begins to fall apart. What initially feels like an impressive technological achievement eventually becomes an annoying and increasingly tedious gameplay mechanic.

I also find that many of GTA VI's characters and story beats feel considerably safer and more subdued than those of previous entries.

There's a noticeable lack of the irreverence, unpredictability, and willingness to push boundaries that once defined the franchise. It almost feels as though Rockstar, in attempting to appeal to a broader audience, has sanded down some of the more distinctive qualities that made its previous games so memorable.

As a result, much of the experience feels surprisingly restrained and, at times, downright bland.

---

## Characters and Gameplay

It feels as though Rockstar took what worked in GTA V and added more layers of realism without putting the same effort into making its supporting characters genuinely interesting.

On a more personal note, I cannot stand Bobby Moynihan's character. I found him particularly grating during Chapter 1, largely because his interactions with Jason and Lucia lack any natural chemistry.

The dialogue often feels incredibly mismatched, almost as though he's a character transported directly from GTA V. At times, his presence feels more like a satirical SNL sketch character interacting with two protagonists from an action film.

One aspect I find particularly frustrating, however, is how frequently the game asks you to engage with its realism mechanics.

Don't get me wrong. I think these systems have their place, and there are moments when they genuinely enhance the experience.

However, their implementation throughout much of the game often feels excessive. What initially adds to the immersion eventually becomes tedious, with certain mechanics feeling more like unnecessary chores than meaningful gameplay features.

author: achillejackson
quote: I waited all these years, through all the hype, anticipation and endless delays, just to end up playing a GTA that seems to have completely lost its identity.First of all, what happened to the prostitutes? One of the most iconic, provocative and unapologetically over-the-top elements of the GTA franchise is practically gone. GTA was always about excess, vulgarity, satire, absurd situations and that raw, chaotic freedom that made it different from every other game. Now it feels like Rockstar is afraid of making an actual **** then there's the pacing. It's painfully slow. At times, it feels more like playing Red Dead Redemption than Grand Theft Auto. Everything is dragged out, the rhythm is incredibly sluggish, and it feels like the game wants you to watch an interactive TV series rather than actually play a GTA game. I understand the desire for realism and deeper storytelling, but you can't sacrifice fun and pacing just to make everything feel more realistic.That's the real problem: GTA seems to have forgotten what made GTA special in the first place. I don't necessarily want the same old game recycled, but I do want the madness, the irreverence, the chaos, the dark humour and the unapologetic freedom that defined this **** far as I'm concerned, GTA died with Trevor, Michael and Franklin. GTA V had the perfect balance between crime, comedy, insanity and pure entertainment. Now it feels like Rockstar is trying so hard to make something more mature, cinematic and realistic that they've forgotten to make it fun.After all these years of waiting, I expected a GTA that would blow my mind, not one that would make me check my watch.

author: olli2209
quote:
Ein fantastisches Spiel, aber ist es noch GTA?

Ich habe mich jahrelang auf GTA 6 gefreut, und grundsätzlich kann ich sagen: Rockstar hat hier ein beeindruckendes Spiel geschaffen. Die Grafik ist unfassbar gut, die Spielwelt steckt voller Details und die Atmosphäre ist großartig.

Auch musikalisch liefert Rockstar ordentlich ab. Besonders der Radiosender Chamber hat es mir angetan. Metallica, Megadeth, Sepultura und weitere Bands dieser Richtung? Für mich ein absolutes Highlight!

Trotzdem habe ich nach meinen bisherigen Spielstunden ein Problem mit GTA 6:

Es fühlt sich für mich nicht mehr wirklich wie GTA an.

Ich habe zunehmend das Gefühl, dass Rockstar sich mit Red Dead Redemption 2 eine Designphilosophie angeeignet hat, die nun viel zu stark auf GTA übertragen wird.

GTA war für mich immer ein Spiel über Freiheit, Chaos, schwarzen Humor und grenzenlose Möglichkeiten. Man konnte sich danebenbenehmen, Autos klauen, völlig eskalieren und einfach machen, worauf man Lust hatte.

GTA 6 scheint dagegen immer mehr Wert auf Realismus und Simulation zu legen.

Training, begrenzte Waffen, Tanken, Peilsender in modernen Fahrzeugen und zahlreiche alltägliche Mechaniken. Das mag immersiv sein, aber muss das wirklich alles sein? Ich möchte in GTA nicht mein virtuelles Leben verwalten.

Besonders absurd finde ich das Karma-System. Warum bewertet ein Spiel wie GTA meine Handlungen moralisch? Warum werde ich bestraft, wenn ich mich gegen bewaffnete Gegner verteidige? Und warum werden mir bestimmte Freiheiten bei Interaktionen mit anderen Charakteren genommen?

Ich möchte selbst entscheiden, wie ich mich in dieser Welt verhalte. Genau das war für mich immer ein wesentlicher Bestandteil von GTA. Innerhalb bestimmter Grenzen natürlich.

Auch das Gameplay empfinde ich teilweise als etwas träge. Daran kann man sich gewöhnen, aber zusammen mit den langen Missionen entsteht ein Spielgefühl, das mir nicht immer gefällt. Manche Missionen ziehen sich gefühlt endlos. Die Party-Mission, die auf der Yacht beginnt, ist dafür ein gutes Beispiel. Ich hatte irgendwann das Gefühl, dass sie einfach nicht enden möchte.

Ich möchte nicht jede Mission wie einen interaktiven Spielfilm erleben.

Natürlich gibt es auch Dinge, die mich weniger stören. 30 FPS sind nicht ideal, aber für mich kein Weltuntergang. Eine fehlende Disc-Version interessiert mich persönlich ebenfalls nicht.

Unterm Strich ist GTA 6 für mich ein sehr gutes Spiel. Ich habe Spaß damit und werde sicherlich noch viele Stunden darin verbringen.

Aber ich bin auch enttäuscht.

Vielleicht ist das sogar das größte Problem: Ich habe nicht 13 Jahre auf eine Lebenssimulation mit kriminellem Hintergrund gewartet. Ich habe auf ein neues GTA gewartet.

Ich wünsche mir wieder mehr Arcade, mehr Freiheit, mehr Wahnsinn und weniger Einschränkungen.

GTA muss nicht realistischer werden, um besser zu werden.

Für mich ist GTA 6 bislang ein hervorragendes Spiel, aber kein besonders gutes GTA.

author: TwoCent
quote:
I've never felt the need to vent like this, so here I go. Let me prefix this by saying I'm 15 hours into the game.

​This is a real departure from the style GTA is known and loved for. It plays more like Red Dead Redemption than GTA—from the criminal profile pushing you to shoot hands or feet, to feeling like you have to save first just to wild out for a few minutes. Even the way certain NPCs are protected because it's "wrong" feels off. I always felt like GTA was a bastion of making fun of everyone and pointing out the stupidity on all sides.

​The characters aren't doing it for me either. The "simping" for Lucia is just meh to me—I don't care, I've seen men do worse. Lucia is really bringing down the mood, she reminds me of Micah: selfish, immature, and ignorant to the real consequences of the life she's pushing for. I really hope she changes because as of right now, I don't wan to play as her. Meanwhile, Jason sounds dead inside most of the time, giving you nothing until he finally shows a little emotion talking about Big Man.

​The graphics look good, though they kind of have a Red Dead look with a blurry filter—though I'm on a base PS5, so that might be part of it.

​I've never done a review here, so I don't know if I can update this when I'm done, but right now I'm very disappointed. I'll bump the score up if the story takes a hard turn and really picks up for the better.

quote:
GTA6 is without a doubt the largest, most graphically impressive and technically detailed game out there now, the world is massive and has things to do nearly everywhere. however all of that is largely brought down by a poorly done and overly long story opening, an underwhelming performance from Jason, an unbelievably ugly HUD/UI, high action moments that drop below 30fps, restrictions on the way you can play the game unless you want to brick your ending, many mechanics like the new criminal profile system and restrictions on stealing certain cars become tedious or out right annoying after the first few times you interact with them. - More criminal enterprises for you to own or be heavily involved in
- Deeper heists that aren't just 70% setup
- Gang affiliations and rival cartels
- Businesses that are actually used to expand your criminal empire
- More in depth player and weapon customization

author: Guymeleef
quote:
GTA VI Review
42 Hours Played | Overall Score: 79/100

After 13 years, I expected more from Rockstar. GTA VI is ambitious, but technically insufficiently polished. In my opinion, another six to twelve months of development would have made a significant difference.

**MAJOR SPOILERS**## 

##Gameplay: 
GTA has always been about freedom and chaos. GTA VI sacrifices much of that identity for excessive realism. You can't attack protesters or cause chaos in certain buildings like GTA IV allowed. Instead, we're forced into RPG mechanics involving training, eating, showering, renovating and registering stolen vehicles. Even customizing stolen cars now involves restrictions and additional expenses. Rockstar replaces traditional sandbox freedom with unnecessary grinding. The irony is that a franchise once celebrated for letting players do almost anything now constantly reminds you what you're not allowed to do. Realism doesn't automatically make a game better.

## Story: 
The narrative is bloated, poorly paced and filled with unnecessary content. It reminds me of Fallout 4, where your child gets kidnapped, yet the game encourages you to build settlements instead of searching for him. GTA VI has the same problem. Lucia's child should be emotionally significant, yet the story frequently ignores this responsibility. Too many distractions undermine the central narrative, leaving its emotional stakes surprisingly weak. The story repeatedly introduces serious personal conflicts without giving them the attention or consequences they deserve.

## Characters
Niko **** Bellic steals the entire show. His return exposes how underdeveloped Jason and Lucia are. Niko possesses the personality and depth that both protagonists lack. Jason feels like a disposable NPC, constantly following orders. Lucia dominates their relationship, but neither character managed to make me care about their fate. Previous GTA protagonists had flaws, motivations and personalities that made them memorable. Here, even after 42 hours, that connection simply never developed.

## Character Development
Jason is essentially a glorified yes man without meaningful development. Lucia handles most dangerous missions while Jason increasingly becomes a supporting character. Rockstar desperately wants Lucia to appear powerful, but neglects her emotional complexity, particularly her responsibilities as a mother. Neither protagonist develops convincingly enough to establish a genuine emotional connection.

## OST
For Vice City, the soundtrack is remarkably disappointing. Not a single song stayed with me after 42 hours. GTA V offered memorable rock, pop and hip hop that perfectly complemented Los Santos. GTA VI's stations feel generic and interchangeable. Kaleidoscope FM especially feels like promotional filler rather than a station with a distinctive identity.

## GraphicsVisually 
IMPRESSIVE!!! Just for the looks a 10/10. Vice City never looked more beautiful!
But, technically disappointing.Rockstar's artistic ambition is undeniable, but the technical execution lacks the polish expected after 13 years. Another six to twelve months of development could have significantly improved the experience.

## Map Design
Bigger doesn't mean better. We spent roughly 10 to 15 hours around Hamlet and the southern map regions. Much of the enormous world consists of swamps and underutilized terrain. Cyberpunk 2077 demonstrates how density creates memorable environments. Even GTA V offered more recognizable locations.I'd rather explore a smaller, carefully designed world than a massive but largely empty one.Exploration should reward curiosity, not simply demonstrate how many square kilometers a developer can create.

## Mission Design
Mission quality is wildly inconsistent.**40%** feel forgettable and narratively irrelevant.**35%** are genuinely enjoyable.**25%** roughly reach GTA V's **** many missions resemble Naruto filler episodes. Rockstar occasionally delivers brilliant moments, but they're buried beneath repetitive activities and unnecessary padding.

## Driving
One of the game's stronger elements.Vehicles finally have weight again, similar to GTA IV, instead of feeling like remote controlled cars in GTA **** heavier physics might complicate popular Asian stunt maps, but personally, I welcome this change.

## Final Verdict: 79/100
GTA VI offers impressive visuals, enjoyable driving and occasional brilliant missions. Unfortunately, its bloated narrative, forgettable protagonists, weak soundtrack and unnecessarily massive map prevent it from becoming a masterpiece or near a very good game. Its a IRL Simulator and not a game. Rockstar prioritizes realism over freedom and quantity over meaningful content.**GTA VI isn't a bad game, but it's nowhere near the masterpiece some reviews claim.**With better technical polish, stronger missions and more freedom, this could become a 90/100 experience.**For now, 79/100.**

author: Kaetoo
quote:
First, it loses one point for not having Brazilian Portuguese (PT-BR) voice acting. We can't pretend we haven't spent years fighting for dubbed versions and then let it slide just because it's GTA.

It loses another point for being 30 FPS. Previous games have been heavily criticized for running at 30 FPS, so we have to be consistent about this.

Now, let's talk about the game itself.

It's a fantastic game, but some of the mechanics introduced don't really fit. The honor system, brought over from Red Dead, doesn't make sense in this game. GTA has always been a game where we enjoy killing random people just to blow off some steam. Now, one random kill is already enough to make you look like a psychopath. The missions clearly favor a less violent approach.

Take the mission where we have to enter the yard and steal a car, for example. The mission makes it pretty clear that the intended approach is to steal the car without killing any police officers. In a game like GTA, our goal is to kill as many people as possible.

Some elements, such as the training system, home renovations, and the police recognizing you, were implemented really well. Others, like not being allowed to rob your neighbors or beat them up, are not welcome. We've all robbed Big Smoke's house. Taking Franklin and breaking into Michael's house to steal his car...

The dynamic between Jason and Lucia is really good. Making her story carry more weight was definitely the right call.

author: MeuCu
quote:
GTA VI é, sem dúvida, um jogo muito bonito. Seus gráficos são impressionantes, e existe um cuidado visual evidente em praticamente todos os aspectos da experiência. Mais interessante, porém, é a maneira como o jogo combina mecânicas de Red Dead Redemption 2 e GTA V, incorporando elementos como o sistema de honra e misturando suas respectivas abordagens para construir uma experiência própria. A quantidade de eventos aleatórios também merece destaque: há sempre alguma coisa acontecendo pelo mundo, o que ajuda a manter a gameplay interessante e viva. Além disso, os diversos minigames funcionam praticamente como jogos completos dentro do próprio jogo, e a dublagem americana é bastante competente.

Infelizmente, nem tudo funciona tão bem. A quantidade de glitches e bugs é simplesmente absurda. Não se trata de pequenos problemas ocasionais que exigem circunstâncias específicas para acontecer: são situações que praticamente qualquer jogador pode testemunhar durante uma partida normal. No meu caso, um bug me deixou preso dentro de uma caixa, o que me obrigou a reiniciar o jogo e, consequentemente, perder parte do meu progresso. Isso sem mencionar personagens atravessando o chão, objetos e NPCs indo parar fora dos limites do mapa, veículos simplesmente desaparecendo e diversos outros problemas semelhantes. É difícil ignorar esse tipo de coisa quando acontece com tanta frequência, não só comigo, mas com diversas outras pessoas online.

Para piorar, aparentemente o jogo não possui um sistema de salvamento automático confiável, ou sequer um sistema de auto-save propriamente dito. Isso torna a perda de progresso especialmente frustrante e, embora não tenha presenciado isso pessoalmente, vi relatos e vídeos de outras pessoas passando por essa situação. É uma falha bastante básica para um jogo dessa dimensão.

No que diz respeito aos protagonistas, Lucia é particularmente difícil de gostar. Ela é irritante, mesquinha e, de longe, uma das personagens menos interessantes do jogo. Estamos falando de uma mulher que abandonou o próprio filho enquanto continuava levando uma vida criminosa. Durante boa parte da campanha, sua personalidade também se resume a dar ordens e praticamente arrastar Jason de uma situação para outra. O que a torna um pouco mais suportável é sua personalidade jovial e descontraída, embora isso também acabe recorrendo a certos estereótipos associados à sua identidade latina.

Jason, por outro lado, sofre de um problema completamente diferente. Ele é, essencialmente, um personagem inexistente. Sua função parece ser servir como uma espécie de self-insert para o jogador, alguém que está ali para participar dos acontecimentos sem necessariamente possuir uma personalidade muito definida. Existe algum mérito nessa abordagem, especialmente considerando a dinâmica entre os protagonistas, mas o resultado é um personagem que se parece muito mais com um boneco controlável do que com uma pessoa de verdade.

A inclusão do Niko Bellic também é bastante questionável. Independentemente de qual final de GTA IV seja considerado, sua presença aqui não parece fazer muito sentido. Sua aparição em GTA VI acaba contradizendo boa parte do desenvolvimento que recebeu em seu próprio jogo. Ou houve um retcon, ou os dois jogos estão deliberadamente se contradizendo. Em qualquer um dos casos, fica a impressão de que os desenvolvedores simplesmente não se importaram muito com a continuidade narrativa do personagem.

Outro problema é a quantidade exagerada de easter eggs e referências espalhadas pelo jogo. Em determinados momentos, parece que alguém está sacudindo um molho de chaves na frente de um cachorro a cada dez segundos, desesperado para chamar sua atenção.

Existe uma missão envolvendo um personagem paródia do Hulk Vermelho, caranguejos gigantes, Pé-Grande, extraterrestres, etc. Individualmente, nenhuma dessas ideias é necessariamente ruim. Pelo contrário, um dos aspectos mais interessantes da franquia sempre foi a possibilidade de teorizar sobre criaturas diversas e os misterios por trás delas e do mundo. A maneira como esses elementos eram apresentados, tanto dentro dos jogos quanto na cultura popular, fazia com que parecessem verdadeiras lendas urbanas.

O problema é que GTA VI parece não ter muita paciência para esse tipo de mistério. Em vez de permitir que essas criaturas e acontecimentos permaneçam elusivos, o jogo faz questão de apresentá-los de maneira escrachada, repetidamente, como se precisasse lembrar o jogador de que eles existem. Isso diminui bastante o valor dessas aparições na minha opinião. 

No mais, GTA VI é uma experiência bastante competente em vários aspectos. Seu mundo é visualmente impressionante, a quantidade de atividades é enorme, a gameplay consegue combinar elementos de seus antecessores de maneira interessante e há momentos genuinamente divertidos. Entretanto, os problemas técnicos são difíceis de ignorar, e espero que os bugs em especial sejam consertados tão cedo quanto possível. 

Bom jogo. 7/10.

author: Lr1998uy
quote:
Es un juego decente. 
Hay mucha hipocresía en la prensa que juzga con una vara algunos títulos, y con otros omite esas mismas críticas.

El juego se podría decir que es un avance en cuanto a cantidad de contenido, y a la exigencia técnica que representa para las consolas de nueva generación.

Los puntos a favor son varios, entre ellos como ya se mencionó el contenido variado. Es un sandbox que se siente vivo por la gran cantidad de cosas que se pueden hacer, así como también los detalles en varios aspectos en las mecánicas del juego.

Todo esto lamentablemente se ve opacado por las siguientes cuestiones:

- 30 fps. En pleno 2026 el estándar debería ser otro, sobretodo por el tiempo en el que se sabe estuvo en desarrollo. Se siente como si faltara un trabajo de optimización importante. Y el precedente que dejan a la industria es que esto se debe aceptar. Me parece un punto gravemente negativo ya que no estamos hablando de consolas de generaciones pasadas o portátiles, estamos hablando de sobremesa. 

- Precio demasiado elevado para el contenido. Es un sandbox al puro estilo GTA SAN ANDREAS. Pero moderno, con físicas y gráficos actualizados. Sin embargo, hay otros juegos en la industria con mucho más contenido y horas de gameplay que no valen ni la mitad de lo que es esta entrega.

- La prensa lamentablemente le juega en contra a este juego. Desgraciadamente un juego cuando le hacen mucho hype ya está crucificado a cumplir. Y este juego deja mucho que desear respecto de su rendimiento, y el precio final. Considerando que ya existen otros juegos que tienen más contenido, mejor optimización y que no tienen un precio de este estilo.

Tocará esperar a que con actualizaciones, tal vez un Port a Switch 2, y con la salida de versión de PC se arreglen los fallos en rendimiento. Y que con rebaja de precio en ofertas tal vez se justifique su compra.

No entraré en detalles de la historia ya que eso es algo muy personal, de cada uno como la interpreta y si es o no de agrado. Pero convengamos que es un GTA y ya se sabe que es una historia que gira en torno al crimen. 

Una lástima limitaron al personaje a solamente estar atado a un guión, y no poder como ya en otras entregas se podía, tener la libertad de optar por "vivir" de forma alocada o de una forma conservadora en cuanto a relaciones entre los personajes. Aunque esto es una apreciación personal.

author: alessar
quote:
An Impressive World, but a Disappointing Experience

I played GTA VI for only about two hours, and I want to be transparent about that. I simply couldn't bring myself to continue and eventually requested a refund.

I genuinely wanted to enjoy this game and would have been happy to admit that my initial skepticism was misplaced.

The world is undeniably impressive, with remarkable attention to detail and technical ambition. Unfortunately, actually playing the game was a different story.

The 30 FPS limitation, noticeably blurry image, sluggish controls, and unresponsive camera made the experience uncomfortable. I tried different displays and settings, including disabling motion blur, but the fundamental issues remained.

I'm not claiming to have evaluated the story or the full open-world experience. Two hours would obviously be insufficient for that.

However, gameplay responsiveness is fundamental to an interactive experience. No amount of world-building can fully compensate for a game that feels unpleasant to control.

GTA VI may be an extraordinary technical achievement, but for me, its current console version falls far short of a 10/10 experience. I would rather wait for a proper PC release than force myself through a compromised first playthrough.

Anyone giving this a 0 is trying to make a point out of spite, obviously it’s an impressive game in many ways, great graphics, highly detailed, lots of things going on.

However, equally, this game should not have a 99, it’s clearly got a lot of flaws and plenty of room for improvement. 

Frame-rate isn’t an issue for me. All the crybabies blaming “woke” or potential female writers that they’ve invented in their heads, probably could do with some instructions on how to get laid. But this game has plenty of examples or poor game design, tapping a RT to lift weights or nail timbers isn’t fun, challenging or rewarding. The controls are often janky, particularly when shooting. The map is big, but often uninteresting. The missions don’t seem to expand on an already tired formula.

If you want to kill some pedestrians and get chased by the cops in a graphically rich and dense environment you can do that and it’s still fun.

If you want to pretend you’re a cool hot guy, with a hot girlfriend and lift weights in your house you’ve done up, you can live that fantasy.

Clearly a lot of work has gone into designing a groundbreaking sandbox to play in. But when it comes to things to do in that environment Rockstar seems to have focused on quantity over quantity.

author: iPznda
quote:
Before I get hate for not giving it a perfect review hear me out.

The Game is great and I've had a lot of fun so far. But its not a good GTA. The story is a slow burn (as of the end of chapter 3 which is where I'm at right now it's still very boring). The characters are boring and bland, Jason is a potato of a personality, there's never any emotion from him (yes I know he's ex army but look at Trevor, he was also ex army) and Lucia is an annoying girl boss who always acts like she's in the right.

The realism is great but it gets to a point where its overdone. Lets talk about stealing cars. In old GTAs u simply get in and drive off. Sure it was boring but simple. I get trying to change that, I don't hate the new system but key cloning is implemented horribly. Why does every 2nd car need a clone instead of keeping it simple with the exotic and really super end ones. 

A lot of freedom is also gone, you cannot kill every npc anymore because now theres protected classes (the gay bar or parades). You cannot cheat on Lucia with Mandy or a prostitute, why even introduce Mandy then? You introduced a character that you knew would have people drooling and then you can't start a relationship with her? You can't touch strippers in the strip club anymore but guess what, during the story mission you could touch a male stripper but you can't touch any female strippers. 

That being said the robberies you can do are great, but they're too simple sometimes. You don't have a big heist just a bunch of small time robberies. It's fun here and there but it gets boring doing it over and over and over.

As people have said its a Sims game but its really not a GTA. If this wasn't GTA6 but let's say a random new game from Rockstar it'd be a lot better received, but as a GTA title and with the story the past 2 GTA titles have given us it's not a good look.

I'll update this again later on but as of right now it's a 
2/10 story
8/10 gameplay 
11/10 graphics 
4/10 gameplay loop
10/10 realism (even if a bit annoying sometimes)

author: yalr
quote:
Graphically, the game is spectacular; the density of both traffic and pedestrians is impressive, and the reactions of the NPCs are truly admirable. However (and here is the major "but") the game lacks many fundamental elements, making the experience feel slow and, at times, tedious. First, the introduction is extremely sluggish. Typically, in this series, once a brief introductory sequence is complete, the player is set free to explore at their own pace; in this title, however, the beginning feels endless. You have to complete two missions and three memories just to be allowed to explore your own home, and the game is so packed with cutscenes that it often feels more like watching a movie than playing a GTA game.

Second, there is an extreme resemblance to Red Dead, from the interactive menus and weapon wheel to various gameplay mechanics. While this in itself wouldn't necessarily be a negative, there are many features that Red Dead implemented well, whereas GTA’s execution falls short. For instance, objects seem to teleport into your character's hand when picked up; eating animations often glitch, frequently resulting in your character biting into thin air; and your protagonist’s hair doesn't grow, requiring a trip to a shop whenever you want a change. Related to this is the system for sleep, hunger, and thirst; in my experience, it doesn't enhance the gameplay but instead feels like a tedious, poorly implemented mechanic that is simply unpleasant to engage with.

Third, the relationship mechanic with Lucia, while there are many activities you can share with her, feels more like a chore than an enjoyable experience when following the main story arc. Ultimately, it comes across as little more than a way to artificially pad out the length of the story. 
Fourth, the game was riddled with rendering errors, physics bugs, and instability that breaks immersion. To give an example, right when I started, the character models failed to load during the introductory cinematic, they appeared as low-polygon figures. This wasn't limited to the intro; throughout my playthrough, textures frequently failed to load properly during cutscenes, and the game would stutter whenever there was a lot of action on screen. Worst of all, the game’s graphical quality is highly inconsistent, for instance, the explosions look like generic, off-the-shelf Unreal Engine assets.

Fifth, and for me, the worst part is that GTA failed, first, to grasp what made the karma system in Red Dead so special, and second, it completely lost touch with what defines a GTA game. In Red Dead, you stepped into the shoes of cowboys fighting to ensure the world wouldn't forget them We embody a man who is caught in a constant internal conflict: trying to be decent toward the world and their own gang, while simultaneously doing whatever was necessary to survive. That is why the karma system fit the narrative so well. In GTA, that internal conflict is stripped away, replaced by a system that fundamentally clashes with the very core of the series. In GTA, we play as unscrupulous criminals, the game tells you this right from the start so such a mechanic has no place here. This ties into a broader disconnect from the franchise’s core message. Ever since the transition to 3D, the GTA series has been defined by its satire and critique of the real world, from San Andreas, with its commentary on gang culture, violence, and police abuse, to GTA IV, which followed a man fleeing his past to Liberty City in pursuit of the American Dream, only to encounter a city... Consumed by excess and a paranoid citizenry, GTA 6 remains stuck in a superficial satire of the modern era; it makes no attempt to delve deeper into a critique of our current world, nor does it explore its critique of discrimination in any meaningful way, ultimately coming across as little more than a never-ending, persistent joke.

In summary, the game is spectacular in its graphics and technical aspects regarding the NPCs, It lacks many things, from its execution in the pacing of the story to key mechanics and technical errors that are unforgivable for a production of this caliber.

author: V1Stretch
quote:
First off, the hate for GTA6 is incredibly overblown. The bigger the game, the more hate there will inevitably be. This happens to every single new game release, it is just amplified by tenfold here because this is arguably the most hyped release of all time. 

I will also say I am not a big GTA fan, so I don't feel as attached to these games as some people may be. I was simply curious because the hype for this game is just too big for me to ignore.

In terms of realism and fidelity, the game is very impressive; but in terms of performance, it doesn't feel great. It's common for the game to drop into the low 20 frames, especially during driving or venturing through dense environments. Maybe some people don't mind the fps cap, but it makes the game feel and look choppy at many moments. 

Overall the game is pretty good. I do think calling it 99/100 is way overcompensating and a few years from now once the hype settles down, more people will start to feel the same as me. 

Overall, GTA6 is far from a 10/10 game, but it is by no means bad. With future improvements and updates, this game has tons of potential. 

In it's current state, I am giving it a 7/10 due to the underwhelming performance, significant presence of bugs, and a story that hasn't really interested me. Despite this, the game is still pretty fun.

author: GameTruther
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI is Overhyped. By Removing Classic features from older games. No hookers, Rockstar claims that that hiring sex workers was cut after 25 years to preserve the romantic dynamic between Jason and Lucia. ****.
Submarines, pet companions, and Rampages (from GTA III / GTA V.) bowling and darts were cut to maintain quality standards, alongside tennis, triathlons, movie theaters, and inviting friends out (though pool, golf, and basketball remain).
bowling and darts were cut to maintain quality standards, alongside tennis, triathlons, movie theaters, and inviting friends out (though pool, golf, and basketball remain).
Buying houses, businesses, and online vehicles (from Vice City / GTA V). You can only own garages and one safehouse, with no passive business income or online boat/plane shopping because the duo is on the run. 
you cannot replay finished story missions or earn bronze/silver/gold medals because player choices ripple permanently into the open world. But previous games let you do those things. Unlimited "pocket arsenal" weapon wheel (from GTA III–V). Instead of carrying dozens of guns at once, you are limited to a realistic loadout on your body and must store extra long guns in your car trunk. Removed & Restricted Adult Content and Toned-Down Sandbox Mechanics are to appease a certain crowd of people. The story is very bland and flat. The Duo aren't really compelling and all 4 endings of the game Really are the worst in the series compared to GTA IV and GTA V. While critic scores are sky-high, Which i believe they are paid off or to be in high placements in the industry, the game leans heavily on spectacle and star power rather than the raw writing and freedom that made San Andreas, GTA IV, and GTA V timeless. Speaking Of GTA IV.  Bringing Niko Bellic Back is a disgrace to real fans of the franchise. Niko's return in GTA VI is textbook cheap nostalgia. Instead of letting Jason and Lucia earn their place among GTA legends through sharp writing and memorable missions, Rockstar took the easiest shortcut possible by pulling a beloved 2008 protagonist out of retirement for a few minutes of launch week shock value, but Without Dan Houser's sharp satire, Rockstar leaned on familiar real-world faces and legacy callbacks ( Niko Bellic) to generate hype instead of letting original characters carry the weight. Instead of honoring one of gaming's heaviest, most grounded character arcs, Rockstar treated him like a nostalgia prop. Pulling Niko Bellic back into a flashy Vice City drug plot feels completely tone-deaf to everything his original story stood for. Rockstar used wall-to-wall celebrity cameos as viral TikTok bait to mask a weaker story and thinner sandbox. 
Vice City looks breathtaking, but once the graphics novelty wears off, cut features (like buying properties, mission replays, and classic side jobs) and restrictive "good behavior" endings leave the open world feeling surprisingly hollow. To unlock the "Happily Ever After" ending where Jason and Lucia both survive and escape with their son Tomás, you have to keep a "Restrained" criminal profile—meaning no free-roam rampages, sparing targets, and avoiding random police shootouts. Basically the point of GTA. Every questionable design choice in the story points straight toward keeping players engaged for years of live-service updates rather than delivering a complete, satisfying single-player experience. GTA VI had to be sanitized to fulfill its role as Wall Street's savior which is why it feels so much more like a safe corporate product than the rebellious games that built Rockstar's name. The Rockstar You and i loved is Gone and this game proves it.
