author: ravielsG2
quote:
GTA VI: cuando la ambición no necesariamente significa perfección.
GTA VI es una producción técnicamente impresionante, pero eso no significa que esté libre de problemas. Uno de sus mayores inconvenientes es que parece confundir complejidad con profundidad. Rockstar ha construido un mundo extraordinariamente detallado, pero no todas esas posibilidades se traducen en mecánicas realmente **** historia de Jason y Lucia tiene una premisa atractiva, especialmente por el vínculo sentimental entre ambos. Sin embargo, el desarrollo narrativo pierde fuerza cuando dedica demasiado tiempo a personajes secundarios y encargos que terminan sintiéndose repetitivos. Hay momentos en los que los protagonistas parecen instrumentos para desarrollar las historias de otros, en lugar de ser el verdadero centro de su propia aventura.También resulta cuestionable el ritmo de algunas misiones. Tener que conducir, recoger objetos, realizar encargos y participar en situaciones que aportan poco al desarrollo principal puede convertir una experiencia que debería ser emocionante en algo innecesariamente prolongado. No todo necesita convertirse en una actividad interactiva para justificar su **** combate tampoco está exento de problemas. Aunque presenta mejoras, sigue dependiendo bastante de los enfrentamientos tradicionales con coberturas y oleadas de enemigos. La inteligencia artificial y ciertas situaciones de combate no siempre están a la altura de la ambición técnica del **** otra parte, el humor de GTA sigue apostando por provocaciones y situaciones sexuales que, en ocasiones, parecen buscar la reacción fácil antes que una sátira verdaderamente inteligente. La franquicia siempre se ha caracterizado por cuestionar la sociedad, pero provocar no es necesariamente lo mismo que hacer una buena crítica social.Incluso su apuesta por el realismo puede jugar en su contra. Los controles complejos, ciertas interacciones poco intuitivas y situaciones impredecibles pueden generar frustración en lugar de inmersión. A esto se suma la limitación de 30 FPS, que resulta discutible en una producción de esta **** principal crítica es que GTA VI parece haber invertido muchísimo en construir un mundo donde todo parece posible, pero no siempre consigue que jugar dentro de él sea igual de **** considero que sea un mal videojuego ni que carezca de méritos. Sin embargo, sus virtudes técnicas no deberían convertirlo automáticamente en una obra **** videojuego se mide por mucho más que sus gráficos, su presupuesto o la cantidad de contenido que ofrece. Se mide por cómo consigue entretener, sorprender y mantener el interés del jugador.Y GTA VI, pese a sus enormes virtudes, también merece ser cuestionado en esos aspectos.

author: r314
quote:
It's the first time i take time to rate a game, but really the disappointment for GTA 6 is huge.
I didn't like Red Dead Redemption 2 and couldn't finish it (even though i loved the first one, i even done the platinum) because it felt too slow, lacked action, and got way too boring and i was worried GTA 6 would go the same way.
So unfortunately i'm getting the same feeling here, heavy character movements, tons of pointless actions, and slow QTEs for every little things, and all of this is made even worse by the 30fps.
GTA 4 (my favourite GTA of all time with tied with San Andreas) also leaned more toward realism, yet it nailed the sweet spot between realism and fun.

I'm not saying GTA 6 is garbage, the attention to detail and NPC animations are so impressive, and there are many amazing things in the game, but the GTA feeling is not here, and as big fan of the series (bought them all since GTA 3 and most of them twice (console and pc)), it's the first time i've put the controller down this fast and i'm not rushing back.
I'm willing to forgive plenty of things including the lack of a physical release, but Rockstar is pushing it too far, it really feels like they put all their budget into marketing and squeezing out as much money as possible instead of actually focusing on making a fun game.
Special mention to the first-person view already being in the game (players found a glitch to activate it and everything is already coded and working so they deliberately cut it to keep it to sell us the game a second time).

I really hope GTA 6 Onlive will save this game, making it much faster and fun, as long as it's free and not built purely as a cash grab, but honestly now i have serious doubts.

author: Dronin
quote:
This game was bound to be Contraversial, clearly a review bomb 1-2 is unfair but also the glaze that the critics gave it is also rediculous. 

Visuals: 9/10
Based on consoles with 6 year old tech the game looks excellent with beautiful lighting. The shadows and night scenes are fantastic and on an OLED monitor it pops. The art style is also great, its not quite hyper realistic but its good. 

Performance: 3/10
The fact that this is a 30 FPS target and not even fully locked even on the PS5 Pro is unacceptable in 2026. The standard Xbox series X and PS5 are running down to low 20s in tests and the series S drops into the teens. There have also been numerous game breaking bugs demonstrated with falling through the world. physics and visual glitches. Usually glitches for an open world game of this scope would be fine but as its had 13 years of development and 2 billion dollars it should be in a better place. 

Sound: 7.5/10
The sound is great, a lot variety in tracks, you don't tend to hit the same tracks over and over again. The bespoke combat music is also really good. Gunshots sound slightly better than 5 and the driving is also quite atmospheric but engine noises are still poor. Some of the stations are better than others but overall its good. Some of the voice acting, particularly of the main characters let this category down. 

Story: 5/10 
The story is predictable and slow. There are a few minor twists but there is nothing that's particularly shocking or unexpected. It is certainly weaker than previous installations, particularly Vice city and San Andreas with few memorable characters. The pacing feels off particularly for the first 8-10 hours, it takes a good while to get going and even then its hardly exhilarating. There are a lot of boring tasks that you are assigned, even as the game progresses, the missions are certainly not an evolution from GTA5. The game takes itself way too seriously, its like GTA4 prior to the expansion.

Gameplay: 6/10
Movement feels heavy like RDR2, driving feels a little better than GTA5. Shooting is not amazing but its not bad either, PC's manual aiming may be quite a bit more interesting in future. The mundane quests, extended chit chats, romance and life situation don't do much for enjoyment. It just doesn't feel very GTA in many aspects. When you cant steal things in certain places, cant shoot in certain buildings, cannot punch certain annoying characters its somewhat frustrating. Further, if you hit 6 stars wanted it seems you cannot ever lose the cops no matter what you do. There is also the morality system which can have an impact on the finale which seems odd for GTA, the game kind of encourages you to be a kind of "moral, loyal criminal"

Characters: 2/10
Neither Jason or Lucia are particularly interesting. Many have said before that Jason mumbles and feels bland while Lucia is somewhat annoying. A lot of the side characters are annoying rather than funny. 

Customisation: 3/10
There is a lack of customization which i feel is unnecessary in 2026. We cant change the characters Body type, height, face, features or skin blemishes. This seems like an oversight and there should be more freedom here, particularly for those that don't resonate with Jasons "buff" alpha male shape or Lucias pear shape. You can of course go to the gym and eat which makes some changes but the overall frame is set as well as some ugly blemishes. There is a good variety of hairstyles though some of them are paywalled 

Value: 5/10 
Having some of the base game content paywalled behind the ultimate edition is a joke, that is massively scummy from R* and should never have happened. It was ultimate greed. There is however 50-120 hours of playtime to get through the story and side missions so you're talking about a dollar per hour for the average gamer, prior to multiplayer that is. It is clear R* forced this out on current gen so they can soft launch it again on PC then next gen. 

Worldbuilding: 9/10
Leonida is varied and beautiful. Some of it is a little repetitive and overwhelming but overall its a fantastic setting for a game. Multiplayer, mods and any DLC expansions (that hopefully don't feature Jason and Lucia) have a real chance of telling great stories here. There are a lot of call ambient events and secrets to find that one player isn't going to experience them all for months or perhaps years. 

Conclusions: The critics glazed this game way too hard giving it 99/100, 10/10 etc. It is clear that this game isn't perfect and people are finding that as they play. It is almost certainly going to win GOTY which is going to strip out further credibility from the Game Awards. When the game comes to PC and Next gen the performance will be likely be sorted. If they allow modding then some of the annoying issues may be ironed out. The writers dropped the ball on this one and trying to restrict GTA from chaos hasn't gone down well with the players. It just doesn't feel like a GTA game much of the time

author: MiloDuScorpion
quote:
GTA 6 est un bon jeu. GTA 6 est un très beau jeu. .
Mais après quelques heures passées sur le jeu, il y a des choses qui m’obligent à lui en enlever…
 Lorsqu’on passe 13 ans à attendre un jeu, avec un budget pareil, et pour un jeu d’action comme GTA, il est tout simplement inadmissible d’avoir privilégié les graphismes uniquement au détriment des FPS. 
Il était tout à fait possible d’éviter ces chutes de FPS en dessous de 30, car oui, régulièrement, j’ai observé des baisses, jusqu’à 24 très ponctuellement.
D’autre part, il y a des bugs d’affichage et des comportements étranges chez Jason, un personnage que je trouve d’ailleurs très raté et pour lequel je n’éprouve aucune affinité. D’ailleurs, comment se fait-il qu’en 2026 on ne puisse pas tout paramétrer dès le début du jeu ? 
Je ne parle pas des tenues, mais de toute la physique du personnage. 
C’est inadmissible pour un jeu censé être aussi immersif.
Bref, quand on constate des chutes sous la barre des 30 FPS , qui constituent pourtant un plancher minimal absolu sur ce genre de jeu (et je ne suis pas un puriste intransigeant sur ce point, mais j’estime que 30 FPS sur un titre comme GTA 6 est déjà le strict minimum vital), descendre en dessous, ce qui arrive régulièrement, est tout simplement intolérable.
D’autre part, certaines missions, même si elles ne représentent pas une grande partie du jeu, ne sont pas amusantes du tout. 
On retombe dans des simulations de vie ennuyeuses : je ne joue pas à GTA pour faire les corvées du quotidien.
À côté de cela, il y a quand même énormément de choses impressionnantes et, franchement, les courses-poursuites et certaines missions sont assez incroyables, c’est sûr. 
Mais le jeu ne mérite pas plus de 7 à mes yeux,

author: LetsReviewGames
quote:
First, I do believe that visually, GTA VI is a beautiful, staggeringly detailed open world game with the impact Skyrim and the BOTW had with their releases. The lighting, the water and the packed streets are stunning, and some of the cutscenes are excellent. 

But the game and critic reviews hide a real problem. It isn't as good or offer the escape as GTA5. The story is a real problem. Chapter 1 isn’t bad until a stupid ending, Chapter 2 is pure filler where nothing happens, and Chapter 3 finally gets you to Vice City but sticks to the same loop of driving somewhere, talking and driving back. Jason has no personality and I'm not going to comment on Lucia as she is god-damn awful and takes you from one bad decision to the next. The game also offers no real challenge either. The missions aren’t hard, just long, and the only real enemy is the clunky free-aim. There are hardly any gunfights, and the few robberies are short. Not one mission comes close to even the weakest heist in GTA V. Most of your time goes on chores: grilling burgers, walking the dog and looking after hunger and fatigue meters. Is this a SIM? 

Rockstar has also taken a lot away. There are no safehouses, no pets, no stock market and no mission replays. With only 15 save slots, one wrong choice can follow you for hours. Fast travel costs $100 every time. 

Okay, what are my biggest gripes. After CyberPunk I thought the industry had learnt it's lesson. Nope! How no critic has commented on the bugs is just plain unbelievable. The bugs never stop. 

Characters talk through closed windows, Jason walks straight through objects, cars flip if you clip a kerb, and I’ve had a mission cut to a black screen. It runs at 30fps even on the PS5 Pro and drops into the twenties during action, which is a joke on this generation of consoles.With a budget this big and 13 years of development, none of this is easy to forgive. 

Anyone calling this a 10/10 is deluded, and no person with integrity would rate it a 9 or 10.

author: chrystyna84
quote: Mucho espectáculo, pero más de lo mismo.Después de tanta expectación, tantos años de espera y tantas promesas, esperaba que GTA VI fuera una auténtica revolución. Sin embargo, mi sensación después de jugarlo es que estamos ante más de lo mismo, pero con mejores gráficos y una presentación **** voy a negar que tiene momentos impresionantes. Hay escenas que te dejan con la boca abierta y detalles que demuestran el enorme trabajo que hay detrás. Pero esos momentos no consiguen compensar las partes aburridas, las misiones que se hacen pesadas y esa sensación de estar jugando a algo que ya conocemos demasiado bien.Otro punto negativo, y para mí especialmente importante, es la ausencia de doblaje al español. Parece que algunos consideran que la solución es aprender inglés o leer los subtítulos. Pero ¿qué ocurre con quienes tenemos problemas de visión? Aunque los textos sean enormes, seguirlos mientras conduces, disparas o prestas atención a lo que sucede en pantalla no siempre resulta sencillo. La accesibilidad debería ser una prioridad en un videojuego de semejante presupuesto. Y no, no considero que tenga que aprender inglés para disfrutar plenamente de un juego por el que he pagado.También están los bugs. No es que el juego sea injugable, pero tiene errores que en otros títulos han provocado auténticas avalanchas de críticas y bajadas importantes de puntuación. Aquí, sin embargo, parece que algunos defectos se vuelven invisibles simplemente porque el juego lleva el nombre de GTA. ¿Por qué somos tan exigentes con unos videojuegos y tan permisivos con otros?Y lo más curioso de todo es que uno de los momentos más divertidos que he vivido no ha sido una gran misión, un tiroteo espectacular ni una persecución cinematográfica. Ha sido algo tan absurdo como ahogarme y que un perro viniera a rescatarme. Ese momento espontáneo me hizo disfrutar más que muchas de las situaciones que el propio juego intenta presentar como **** VI es un buen videojuego, tiene un mundo impresionante y momentos que merecen ser reconocidos. Pero eso no significa que sea perfecto ni que automáticamente merezca un sobresaliente por llevar detrás el nombre de **** nota: 6/10.Porque tener un presupuesto millonario, gráficos espectaculares y una campaña publicitaria gigantesca no convierte automáticamente un videojuego en una obra maestra.Y porque, al final, prefiero un juego que me divierta durante horas a uno que me impresione durante cinco minutos y me aburra durante los siguientes treinta.

author: MrMezz
quote:
Hi, 

I am Abdallah Mezzouri, lets talk about GTA 6...

GTA 6 started strong with the opening scene showing how Jason and Lucia met. Their story was a little hard to follow at first, but I liked seeing how much they relied on each other when things got rough. I didn’t find many of the other story characters interesting though, so it was mostly Jason and Lucia’s relationship that kept me invested.

I liked GTA 6’s attention to detail, but helping Jason’s friend move furniture felt like a chore. Having to play a story minigame and then a top-down shooter made the whole section drag. I wish both had been optional. I’m happy to spend time on a tough puzzle because solving it feels rewarding. Here, I was just pushing through to get back to the story.

Exploring Vice City was easily my favorite part. Everyone seemed to have their own personality. I found an influencer balancing on the side of a bridge yelling, “This is for you, chat!” He fell, grabbed the ledge, and I could decide whether to help him. Moments like that made me want to wander around just to see what would happen. It felt like Rockstar brought what I loved about Red Dead Redemption 2 into GTA. I’m also looking forward to exploring Vice City with friends when GTA Online comes out.

I’d give GTA 6 a 7/10. I loved exploring Vice City, but the very tedious stretches, glitches, and noticeable frame drops kept pulling me out of it. As beautiful as the game looks, I could’ve enjoyed it a lot more.

author: hamid155
quote:
myGTA 6 Review: a massive disappointment behind pretty ggraphics
I just finished the game, and honestly, it is disappointing to the extreme. I’m still in shock trying to process what I just played—this doesn't feel like a GTA title at all; it feels like a game from a completely different studio.
The writing and characters are the biggest letdowns. Jason is terribly written; he barely speaks, has zero agency, and never once questions or pushes back against Lucia’s catastrophic decisions, even though he’s the one paying the price and dealing with the fallout ruining their lives. As for Lucia, her character just doesn't work. The dialogue is weak, the story is below average, and the gameplay suffers from heavy repetition and boredom.
The only redeeming quality is the visuals—the graphics, attention to detail, and animations are great. However, that’s nothing miraculous; plenty of other games have achieved this level of visual polish while actually delivering where it counts.
It’s truly a shame, because the core pillars that make a game great—story, characters, and engaging missions—are completely missing here. Any review giving this game more than a 6/10 simply shouldn't be taken seriously.

author: Red_Apple_64
quote:
Positive: 
- The world is beautiful, and it is by far the prettiest game Rockstar have ever made.
- The game is packed with content that will make you stuck in the game for 300+ hours, and with 80 of them being the main story.
- I think it was an interesting bold move, to try to mix the gameplay elements from RDR2 and your typical GTA.

Bad: 
- Game not having a physical disk.
- The performance is one of the first thing that popped up, and most people will notice, normally i don't mind a game only being able to run at 30FPS, but when a game tries to get the player immersed in the world and the realism of the graphics, those 30FPS starts to hurt, and it not uncommon for the game to dip and hit 20 - 25 FPS in some sections.
- The story have a hard time following the red thread, and throws the players for a weird loop often, which can work as a shake up for some, but for me it feels very distracting, and the game suffers from pretty bad pacing.
- the characters feels rather weak, especially compared to the characters from the previous titles.
- The relationship part of the game feels very forced, and can come off as very cringe, and the pair just aren't very likeable, at least to me.
- Multiple game breaking bugs.

I don't think GTA6 is a bad game, but in its current state there is a lot that needs to be ironed out.
- 60FPS
- Game breaking bugs needs to be fixed
- Physical Disks

if those things could be ironed out it would be an easy 8/10 for me.
while the story isn't really my cup of tea, and the characters can be quite unlikeable, the gameplay elements are strong.

author: jetsetradio78
quote:
If you’re thinking about buying it, here’s what nobody wants to admit.
First, it’s locked at 30 fps on every console—even PS5 Pro—and still drops frames during heavy chaos. Add launch bugs like crashes that wipe half an hour of progress, pop-in, falling under the map, and an ugly UI.
The gameplay feels clunky, too. Shooting is awkward, the inventory and weapon wheel are a headache because buttons overlap, motorcycles feel stiff, melee is weak, and armored enemies are total bullet sponges.
Pacing is another issue: it takes about 15 hours just to reach Vice City. Missions are overly linear with no replay option from the menu, grinding for money slows things down, and Jason feels much weaker as a character than Lucia.
Worst of all, the extreme realism kills the classic chaotic fun. Crashing wrecks your car, and the police remember your clothes and vehicle, turning minor mistakes into a chore. If you want pure immersion, you might forgive it—but if you miss 60 fps and carefree chaos, you’ll hit a wall.

author: diamante55
quote: GTA VI definitely features top-notch graphics, with an incredible level of detail, especially when the camera focuses on the central character and car. The map is massive, so much so that you probably won't even have time to explore it all in a single day. I also really appreciate the driving physics, braking is a bit more challenging compared to the previous game, and you can genuinely "feel" the different horsepower of each vehicle. Personally my issues begin with how the game brings real-life mechanics, rules, and pointless bureaucracy into the gameplay. To me, this severely hurts the experience and makes it impossible for me to give it a top score. I believe GTA was fundamentally born as a parody and satire of real life, not as a full-blown life simulator. Having to wait around and struggle just to steal a car, or not being able to freely cause over-the-top, anarchic chaos like in GTA V, is a major drawback for me. Similarly, I wasn't a big fan of the story since it feels much less "GTA-like," even featuring moments that I personally find annoying or cringeworthy, making it feel more like playing The Sims or a real-life RP server, complete with all its flaws, rather than a Grand Theft Auto game. That said, you can still have fun moments which, combined with the upgrades in driving and graphics, brings me to a final score of 7.

author: ashlis
quote:
Sinceramente, esperaba muchísimo más de este juego. No digo que todo sea exactamente igual a los anteriores, pero sí siento que muchas de sus mecánicas, actividades y funciones siguen siendo prácticamente las mismas. Es como si hubieran tomado la fórmula de los GTA anteriores, le hubieran puesto gráficos mucho más realistas y listo.

Para mí, lo único que realmente destaca como algo original es la historia principal, además del apartado gráfico, que obviamente tiene una calidad impresionante, nuevas misiones algunas entretenidas otras aburridas algunas que son muy cortas y siento que no tienen sentido. Pero fuera de eso, no encontré esa evolución que tanto esperaba.

Estamos hablando de un juego que ha generado expectativas enormes y que ha tenido años de desarrollo detrás. Esperaba encontrarme con algo que realmente se sintiera diferente, que me sorprendiera y que me hiciera sentir que estaba jugando algo completamente nuevo. Sin embargo, mi experiencia fue todo lo contrario.

Y hay algo que me molesta muchísimo: que ni siquiera tenga traducción al español. Me parece una falta de consideración con una comunidad tan grande que lleva años apoyando esta saga. YO CREÍ QUE LA INDUSTRIA YA HABÍA AVANZADO LO SUFICIENTE COMO PARA ENTENDER QUE EL ESPAÑOL TAMBIÉN MERECE ESTAR PRESENTE EN LOS LANZAMIENTOS, PERO ME QUEDA CLARO QUE ESO NUNCA VA A CAMBIAR MIENTRAS SIGAN EXISTIENDO PERSONAS QUE SE CONFORMAN CON UNOS SIMPLES SUBTÍTULOS Y ENCIMA APLAUDEN COMO SI NOS ESTUVIERAN HACIENDO UN FAVOR.

También tuve bastantes problemas técnicos. Experimenté bajones de rendimiento y varios bugs que terminaron afectando mi experiencia. Incluso la introducción empezó con problemas de movimiento que ya hicieron que mi primera impresión fuera bastante mala. Y ni hablar de la cantidad de animaciones que tiene el juego. Entiendo que quieran darle realismo, pero llega un punto en el que simplemente te aburres, especialmente cuando son animaciones que ni siquiera puedes saltarte.

Pero creo que mi mayor decepción no tiene que ver únicamente con los gráficos, los bugs o las mecánicas. Tiene que ver con lo que me hizo sentir.

Yo jugué GTA V y lo amé muchísimo. Todavía le tengo un cariño enorme. Recuerdo esa emoción de descubrir el juego, conocer a sus personajes y disfrutar de cada momento. Fue una experiencia que hasta el día de hoy guardo con muchísimo cariño.

Con GTA 6 no sentí absolutamente lo mismo. No experimenté esa emoción, no conseguí encariñarme con ninguno de los personajes principales y tampoco encontré ese sentimiento tan bonito que esperaba volver a experimentar.

Quizás tenía las expectativas demasiado altas, pero tampoco considero que sea justo tener que conformarme con una experiencia que no consiguió transmitirme prácticamente nada de lo que esperaba.

Y ahora viene una de las cosas que más me han decepcionado de todo esto: la cantidad de críticas que parecen hechas por compromiso. He encontrado periodistas y reseñistas que reconocen que el juego tiene bugs, problemas y bastantes cosas que mejorar, incluso se toman el tiempo de hacer una lista de todo lo que está mal, pero después tienen el descaro de ponerle un 100 como si nada. Personalmente, me parece absurdo y hasta contradictorio. Lo que hasta cierto punto de entender de que quizás están comprados, pero sinceramente, este tipo de reseñas hacen que uno se cuestione qué está pasando detrás de tantas puntuaciones perfectas.

Y me parece todavía más triste porque estamos hablando de una saga que ya tiene millones de seguidores, que es profundamente querida y que no necesita que nadie le regale buenas críticas para demostrar lo importante que es. GTA es GTA, se ha ganado su lugar durante años. Por eso mismo me cuesta entender que exista tanta necesidad de defenderlo incluso cuando hay cosas que claramente están mal.

Yo amo profundamente esta saga, y precisamente por eso me duele ver todo lo que están haciendo con ella. Entre las decisiones que están tomando, las cosas de pago que han ido incorporando y todos los errores que siguen cometiendo, siento que están destruyendo poco a poco algo que durante años significó muchísimo para sus jugadores.

author: Lasto
quote: Critics handing GTA VI perfect 10/10 scores is a huge lie. The game is a massive, richly detailed production with an unmatched sense of place, but Rockstar’s design choices undercut the freewheeling chaos the series is known for. The locked 30fps target on every console (including the PS5 Pro) is the most obvious problem. Driving and gunfights feel choppy, camera movement smears under heavy motion blur, and the occasional dips into the low 20s make the game feel a generation behind. Rockstar’s technical justifications don’t change the fact that this frame rate is a serious limitation in **** relationship systems turn large stretches of the game into a couple simulator. Jason and Lucia’s bond is central: a heart meter responds to texting, holding hands, kayaking, mini-golf, and other domestic activities. Even if you can technically ignore the romance, the story and activities constantly pull you back into managing their relationship instead of letting you cause trouble on your own terms.Gameplay is also more restrictive than previous entries. Car theft requires tools for some vehicles, a criminal profile tracks your behavior, and the pacing favors story beats and systems that push back against pure sandbox freedom. The world is impressive when it gets out of its own way, but the 30fps lock, relationship focus, and tighter design keep GTA VI from delivering the unrestricted experience we’ve come to expect.

The plot is bland, Jason lacks personality, and Lucia comes across as a Mary Sue. While the NPC detail and modeling are top-notch, it’s obvious that GTA has been toned down. Because the hype was huge, expectations were sky-high, and Rockstar fell short—a warning sign already visible in the lackluster trailers. On top of that, the cheesy marketing—charging $1 for a map, cutting PlayStation deals, blocking Xbox ads, and running Netflix trailers—is pure nerve given the price, especially since a PC release and ports to future consoles are practically inevitable.

author: NamelessHero252
quote:
GTA VI - $13 Billion Errand Simulator: Lucia's Cuck Simulator Edition 

13 years. Over a decade of waiting. And what did Rockstar deliver? Grand Theft Errands VI. 

Welcome to Vice City, where your criminal empire consists of fixing sinks, moving furniture, shopping for neighbours and assembling coffee tables. Apparently, the biggest crime in Vice City is wasting the player's **** time. The gameplay loop: Wake up. Go shopping for someone. Fix something. Move furniture. Drive across the entire map. Listen to boring dialogue. Repeat until retirement. Imagine waiting 13 years for GTA just to get an IKEA internship. Lucia is supposedly one half of a criminal power couple, but sometimes Jason feels more like her unpaid assistant, personal driver and emotional support NPC. I expected a criminal Bonnie and Clyde experience, not an interactive relationship management simulator. Jason isn't a criminal partner. He's an unpaid Uber driver with an ankle-deep commitment to this relationship. And Jason himself? His entire personality seems to consist of saying "sure", "cool" and "that's fine". Rockstar gave us two protagonists and somehow forgot to give one of them a personality. Jason: The Human Loading Screen Remember Michael? Trevor? Franklin? Now meet Jason: the human equivalent of Windows Notepad. Barely any personality, monotone dialogue and the emotional range of a microwave. Even his dialogue sounds like he's replying to an email from HR. When Does the Actual GTA Begin? Go shopping. Fix a sink. Collect rent. Move a table. Play pool. Go fishing. Drive a boat. Meet somebody. Drive somewhere else. Listen to another conversation. Apparently, the criminal experience is mostly waiting for somebody to finish talking. GTA VI: The world's most expensive driving-to-an-appointment simulator. Viceless City The world looks incredible, but the writing and characters often lack the personality and absurdity that made previous GTA games memorable. People wanted Vice City. They got Viceless City. A beautiful tourist destination where the most dangerous activity is assembling furniture incorrectly. The Wanted System: Wanted for Having Fun... The wanted system sometimes feels unnecessarily restrictive and overcomplicated. Apparently, escaping the police now requires a degree in criminal investigation. Imagine successfully escaping the cops, only to be punished by the game's administrative department. Physics: powered by imagination, Vehicles glitching around, planes behaving like cardboard, boats having an existential crisis and water physics that sometimes look borrowed from a mobile game. Some planes have no meaningful damage progression. Forget watching wings or tail getting progressively damaged. Sometimes the plane simply decides its shift is over and explodes. Very immersive. And the water? Jesus Christ. No people casually swimming in pools or enjoying the ocean? Did Rockstar develop Vice City during a drought? 

The Great Disappearance of GTA IV's Euphoria
GTA VI has ragdoll physics, and jumping out of a speeding car can still be entertaining, but it doesn't feel as impressive as GTA IV. The visual damage feedback is also surprisingly underwhelming. And jumping out of helicopters or planes? Where's that satisfying free-fall experience from GTA IV? A game released years later shouldn't make me nostalgic for a physics system from 2008. 

The Story: A Beautifully Rendered Snoozefest? 
The storyline feels slow, some characters aren't particularly interesting and missions can lack the excitement of previous Rockstar games. The graphics are incredible. The map is enormous. Unfortunately, apparently nobody remembered to make the actual gameplay equally entertaining. I didn't wait 13 years to become Vice City's most reliable handyman. 

Final Verdict GTA VI: 
9/10 graphics.
8/10 environmental detail
11/10 coffee table assembly
11/10 neighbourhood handyman simulator
12/10 driving to appointments
3/10 mission excitement
4/10 Jason's personality.
0/10 swimming pool population
-10/10 reasons to remember GTA IV's physics
Final rating: 5/10.

A technical masterpiece that occasionally forgets it's supposed to be a video game. 

13 years of waiting just to become Jason's Uber driver, Lucia's personal assistant and Vice City's unpaid IKEA employee. Grand Theft Errands VI.

author: Dantemax29
quote:
GTA 6 is, without exaggeration, a technical and design breakthrough for open-world games. The game looks stunning: the level of detail on the streets, the weather effects, and the meticulously crafted interiors of hotels, shopping malls, and airports all combine to create an incredibly vivid sense of place. The world of Leonida is vast and diverse, making it sincerely engaging to traverse. With over 600 shops, trains and buses that run on real-world schedules, and a huge number of accessible buildings, the opportunities for exploration and immersion are immense.

On the PS5 Pro, the game feels particularly impressive; this version boasts noticeable improvements over the base console. The visuals are sharper and more detailed, lighting and effects are superior, performance is more stable and fluid, and fast loading times make the overall experience much smoother. It is on the PS5 Pro that this massive world truly shines to its full potential.

However, when it comes to the main character, I—like many other players—have some serious reservations. Jason comes across as a total "pushover." He appears passive and unmotivated, constantly playing second fiddle to Lucia. It feels as though the developers intentionally cast him in a submissive role—a "gofer" who exists solely to carry out tasks for his far more vibrant and proactive partner. Many players have labeled him a "simp" or a "henpecked boyfriend," and I largely agree: Jason doesn't feel like a full-fledged protagonist, but rather like an appendage to Lucia.

In this regard, I believe Rockstar made a mistake by forcing this specific pairing.  Instead of giving us a single strong, charismatic male protagonist—like Niko, Michael, or Franklin—we’ve been handed this “female fantasy” complete with a mandatory romantic narrative. Sure, you can choose whether or not to develop the relationship between Jason and Lucia; technically, it's "completely optional." But the plot is built around it regardless, and if you don’t engage with this “romance,” it feels like you’re intentionally shortchanging yourself. They should have just stuck to a single male protagonist with a proper criminal backstory, rather than all this.

Another point of frustration is the new set of restrictions. In GTA 6, you can no longer pick up a sex worker, shoot at protesters, or kiss anyone other than "your strong Latina partner." You can claim all you want that “it’s not about morality,” but the reality is that a series once famous for its unhinged freedom and lack of restraint has suddenly started acting like a “morality police.” It really hurts the atmosphere. Instead of being a wild, unrestrained crime simulator, the game occasionally feels like an "HR simulator," filled with mundane tasks like buying flowers, cooking, or cleaning.

Another major drawback is that the developers have limited the player to just one female lead. It would have been better to offer a choice of different female characters, rather than forcing Lucia on everyone. That would have allowed players to pick someone who actually resonates with them, rather than having one chosen for them by the developers. It would have provided more freedom, variety, and a stronger personal connection to the character—instead of the feeling that you’ve simply been “assigned” one specific, mandatory partner.

And then there’s the issue of GTA+.  People have already paid for the game, and now there’s a subscription on top of that—it’s absurd. Not only does the game cost a significant amount of money, but you’re also expected to pay extra for a subscription to get additional bonuses and features. It feels like paying twice for the same product, and personally, that just really irritates me.

Sure, it’s a bold experiment, and maybe it worked for some people. But for me, GTA has always been about freedom, masculine charisma, and the thrill of a life of crime. In this case, that freedom and intensity have been heavily diluted by forced romance and mundane domesticity; the protagonist comes across as a henpecked pushover, and there’s only one female lead—with no choice in the matter. On top of that, you have the “GTA+” subscription layered over a game you’ve already purchased. I really hope that in the next installation, Rockstar returns to its roots and stops experimenting with forced pairings and "feminist" agendas at the heart of the story.

author: Tomeshec
quote: My thoughts on GTA VI could be summarized as "GTA VI fails to be a GTA game". This game has many of the same issues that have always plagued "GTA-likes" for me. Where in prior GTA games the world was your playground and there was seemingly no limit to how much chaos you could bring to it, GTA VI for the sake of some sort of illusion of realism takes much of this freedom away from you. What really did it for me was the decision to make what you do in your freeplay chaos sessions have an impact on the game's **** and the story? Worst in series history, or at least on par with GTA III. Jason could have been a silent protagonist and not only would you not lose anything, it may have even made the game better. His voice work is horrid and his personality is almost non-existent. Lucia on the other hand has plenty of personality. She is reckless, impulsive and selfish and pretty much the reason why the plot of the game happens in the first place. She is highly unlikable and I would gladly just get rid of her early on if I was given the option. The worst part is the game is structured in such a way where focusing your efforts on Lucia is not only encouraged but straight up required to progress the **** even if the story and characters are what brings you to GTA and you don´t care about harassing the world in freeplay, GTA VI still manages to disappoint. While in GTA V the controller gunplay was tuned to be almost too easy, in GTA VI the guns are a lot harder to control and for me as a primarily mouse and keyboard gamer I think I will love this system once it's on PC but on controller I just found myself feeling frustrated. The driving in GTA VI definitely doesn´t feel as arcadey as the driving in GTA V but it also certainly isn't the exaggerated driving of GTA IV, instead it manages to be in this awkward middle ground where the acceleration of just about any car is still cartoonishly high but now the weight of the vehicles feel a lot more realistic which results in much more understeer. For me as someone that follows computer graphics closely the raw visuals of GTA VI don´t feel as impressive as they might for the casual person but even I have to admit that the amount of detail Rockstar was able to cram into this game is breathtaking, the problem is that to be able to keep even the rather awful mostly 30 FPS target sacrifices had to be made somewhere and that somewhere is the stability of these graphics. By stability I am not talking about the consistency of the graphical fidelity throughout the game, that´s precisely where the game excels, but rather the boiling, shimmer and grain of the game's raytraced effects. This has always been an issue with raytracing and Rockstar's approach is not horrible but when compared to the likes of Cyberpunk 2077 on PC and its DLSS Ray Reconstruction I can't help but feel like GTA VI already looks at least **** behind. The wanted system is a real mixed bag, while it's super nice the cops no longer feel like they know precisely where you are even if they have no reason to, them having an actual memory after you finally get away feels more and more annoying the further you get into the game. Another big positive of GTA VI has for me been the side activities the game features, without spoiling a single one I can say that many of them are more interesting than the game´s actual storyline and they completely explain to me how this game was possibly able to have such a gigantic budget. The soundtrack and general audio of the game absolutely live up to the series standards and are up there as some of the best I´ve heard. The UI is bad, like BAD bad. Rockstar frequently chooses form over function in its UI and it's no different this time, what is different this time is that the UI manages to be incredibly ugly anyways. Well, I've saved the worst for last, the missions. GTA VI continues Rockstar´s unwillingness to innovate on the general structure and design of missions and it's really starting to drive me mad. When I saw RDR2, a game with almost universal praise, was finally getting some deserved criticism for how flat and on rails its missions felt, I was really hoping GTA VI would finally change for the better. Instead we got the same thing again and this time it's packaged in a much more linear path than GTA V was. Worse, the game abandons the addictive criminal-empire progression that defined classic GTA. The game instead chooses to focus very heavily on Jason´s and Lucia´s relationship, and even if this premise was executed perfectly, which it is far from, it would still be nowhere near as compelling. GTA VI is undeniably a technical marvel even just for its stunning living world alone, but trading the snappy freedom of prior installments for sluggish realism while forgetting what GTA is all about makes it a world not fun spending time in.

author: ShreddermanVT
quote:
The most anticipated game is here and it has an identity crisis. 
After 15 hours and in the middle of Chapter 2, you can tell they spent a lot of time designing for Online first and tried to cram a GTA story into the engine without smoothing out the friction points. You want to play a life sim? This is actually pretty good at it. Convincing NPCs that are very impressive, realistic lighting shines through the 1440p 30fps, and driving is the best in the series, but then you get interrupted with the reality of the game still having to create an illusion instead of being a simulation. Want to play a GTA game? This is where it falls apart, and why it deserves a low rating. Cars are better, taking after the original Vice City and GTA IV, shooting is less precise unless special attachments, and a lot of mechanics are taken over from Red Dead Redemption 2 in a good and bad way, but then the life sim aspects come into play and create needless friction. I don't care to have to pump gas holding the right trigger button, or hot wire a car by pushing the thumb sticks together. Jimmying a car is actually an example of where it works, but those moments are few and far between. Cops are more aggressive but they forget you just as easy as past entries. But the worst part is the distance rendering and 30fps engine cap. The entire resource allotment is to NPCs, environments, and ray tracing, rendered at 1440p and upscaled. However the Xbox series S has/had a VRR glitch that unlocked the frame rate cap and revealed that the physics are tied to the frame rate. If the Xbox series S of all consoles can run the game at a higher fps, even physics tied, it proves that they artificially limited the game's performance to sell a future "next gen" version. If the CPU is bound but the game is rendering at 1440p, even with ray tracing they could have rendered in 4k and eased the CPU load. Even if still capped at 30fps and dynamic resolution, it would give the overall render a much better resolution that could excuse the low distance rendering. There's no excuse for this game to have bad frame rates, bad resolution, and bad distance rendering. Instead of pushing the limits in a playable manner and pushing the fidelity upgrade next gen, they pushed the limits in fidelity to sell you a playable upgrade next gen.

author: Spiderspider123
quote:
It’s hard not to feel saddened by how this turned out. I’ve been playing Rockstar games since the original Grand Theft Auto and have played every single release since, including both Red Dead titles. For years the build-up and hype were immense, fueled by the legendary track record of the GTA series and Rockstar’s other iconic games. When a studio carries that kind of legacy and after this much time you expect a generational leap. 
Visually it actually delivers, graphically the game is on another level. The few glitches and bugs I've had don't bother me much, since every massive open-world game has them for the first few weeks. However that visual achievement is still dragged down by an exceptionally poor framerate that holds the experience back. 
Beyond the performance issues, the game gets bogged down right out of the gate by roughly seven hours of boring, mundane tasks before things even start to pick up. On top of the slow pacing, it strips away a core part of the GTA fantasy by restricting your ability to steal good cars early on, to make matters even worse the dynamic between Jason and Lucia feels completely off, the writing makes it painfully obvious who wears the trousers in the relationship, leaving the partnership feeling lopsided rather than compelling and balanced. 
Ultimately had the game let me steal better cars right away and let me lean into the consequence free chaos the series is famous for where in everyone is fair game I would have given it a higher score. 
The simplest thing to do would be to allow us to get better cars earlier, this would at least bring back some of the fun in the early portion of the game.
I know little can be done about the FPS due to console restrictions and the story is set in stone but it would at the very least make it feel more like a GTA game again.
After such a massive wait, the whole thing just feels like a bittersweet letdown.

author: Thanioti
quote:
As a sandbox simulator, it is highly detailed and immersive. The engine produces amazing graphical detail, even though at times its physics are completely busted, which in itself is amusing and fun. FPS hovers at or below tolerable.

Is this GTA? Nope. The story is clearly forcing a cultural perspective, most noticeable through its sanitized objectives, quest outcomes, or removed mechanics. Really its weakest point, but great slop for the masses. 

Is it worth the money? The barrier to entry is high for a simulator, or more accurately, a simpulator. As a raw thrill, exciting single player story, with character connection, emotional highs and lows, and risk pushing elements, nope. 

If your life is mundane and have 50+ hours to distract you from reality, or, you need to be part of the moment with the heard, buy the goyslop and feed at the trough, dont do it expecting a GTA title. 

Ultimately, you are buying a unrestrained title, with immense development hours and years to produce a detailed playground built upon the bones of GTA open world mechanics, with elements of a life simulator, and a virtual signalling undertone of leftist fembot snowflake ideologues. If that is you, feed piggy and fatten yourself up for the feast.

author: LockedInFr
quote:
Wanted to wait until it came to PC in the rumoured 2027 first quarter, but FOMO and the 99 Metacritic got me, making me buy a PS5 Slim and GTA 6. I was expecting something that would change the game industry like Mario, Doom, TLoZ OoT, OG FF7 or OG RE2 and although it's great, it ain't what critics say it is. The first chapter is slow and doesn't let you do whatever you want + all the money u grinded during chapter 1 in Jason's house is lost if u saved it in the stash, so I would recommend you not to do it. There's no autosave or it's a bug, idk, Rockstar won't fix their game until November 26 so I had to redo the prologue. Although planes do crash when you have the damage reduction off, it isn't realistic, the explosion is bad and the planes don't get destroyed how you would see in accidents irl. After finishing chapter 1 and some of chapter 2 you can do whatever you want (took me 17h to reach here); at this point the game starts being fun and you can find random Easter eggs and secondary missions. I found 4 big bugs in my playthrough and probably didn't see small visual bugs in the background. The FPS dips are real; I have no problem playing at 30 FPS, but that's the bare minimum and should stay locked to 30 FPS, not aiming at 30 FPS. You can be driving or in a mission and notice dips to 18-26 FPS and PS5 has no VRR unlike Xbox, and I ain't paying 900€ or more for a PS5 Pro when I already paid 600€ for a PS5 out of FOMO for ONE game. Jason has no personality, maybe they did this on purpose so you could self-insert? So Lucia hard carries and it makes sense why they chose her actor instead of Jason at the Game Awards. This game doesn't shine for its story unlike GTA 4 or 5 and by the way, GTA 6's story is linear and rigid. Although all these flaws and some release bugs (not defending these bugs, an 8yo developed game with a 1.5B budget shouldn't have any major bugs and we got some releases this year without bugs), GTA is decent, not at a 9.9 rating, more like an 8.9-9.2, and this game should have come with online because it only shines for its open world, graphics and freedom in killing and doing any random action, so you should milk it with the online. I'm currently at 44h with 72% of the story done and I doubt finishing it will make my opinion change.

So the things I didn't like are:
-No autosave
-The pacing of this game isn't like other GTAs, it's worse than RDR2; you could compare it to being tortured by watching 2 arcs of One Piece
- The first hours of the game after prologue feels like go to place A kill some dudes come to place B + It feels like a sim.
-**** plane physics even with the damage reduction off
-Jason is a hollow character
-"30" FPS when it dips to 20 a lot of times and it's noticeable since there's no VRR on PS5 + I play FPS games on my PC.
-Although GTA shines in freedom of doing random actions, there are too many of these random actions and each button is linked to 4 or more, so it feels saturated; you literally have to press 2 buttons to swap characters
-The game physics are linked to your FPS and when u hit 18 it's more noticeable
-The weapon wheel/dial is trash, I didn't like it; compared to GTA 5 or RDR2 it's a downgrade whatsoever
-Some weapon designs like the P90 aren't accurate and look weird
-Some animations are a downgrade from RDR2, like when you put your gun strap to have your weapon hanging on your back; here it puts the weapon in your ass and then it appears on your back with the gun strap

What I did like:
-The Easter eggs and random events
-The freedom of letting you do whatever action you want
-The graphics
-I got spoiled on Twitter that Niko Bellic appears in GTA 6 as a mafia leader in chapter 5, which probably means that the ending where you accept the deal with Dimitri and Roman dies + Kate leaves you for betraying your own values is canon, due to the fact that being devastated would lead his character development back to criminal activities + GTA 5 C ending being canon.
-The NPCs' designs and them feeling alive
-Harder police

At the moment I'm giving this a 7.4; if this game CAME with autosave and better plane physics (ye I wanna crash into a building that bad and want to see a building fall) or online I would rate this higher, and I also gotta see the endings to see if the story is still mid or if it makes a comeback (if it does I will give it an 8.0), but for a 7.4 I wouldn't recommend anyone to fall for the FOMO and buy a console (if you don't have one yet) + the game, and the reviewers' Metacritic score cuz it's ****; this game won't have an impact on the gaming industry besides graphics + NPC comparisons for the next years like RDR2 did. I regret buying a PS5 Slim since I won't use it cause it has no good exclusive games (already played GoW, Spider-Man and TLoU on PC) and I regret buying GTA 6 for console instead of waiting for an official PC port with better frame time and graphics. (I would write more but theres a characters cap)

author: ATMOSESP
quote:
13 years of development, and GTA VI still doesn't feel finished...

I wanted to love this game, but the technical state at launch is hard to accept. The frame rate is inconsistent, with noticeable drops and stutter in busy parts of Vice City, during big firefights, or just driving fast through the city at night. For a game built around speed and chaos, that constantly breaks immersion.

The bugs are just as bad: NPCs clipping through objects, physics glitches, missions that don't trigger properly, late-loading textures and occasional crashes. A few issues at launch would be understandable. This many, after more than a decade of development and one of the biggest budgets in gaming history, is not.

Beyond the technical side, it isn't the generational leap we were promised. It plays like Red Dead Redemption 2 moved to a modern city: same heavy movement, same slow pacing, same systems with a neon coat of paint. RDR2 was a masterpiece in 2018, but repeating that formula in 2026 isn't enough.

The world looks great in screenshots, and the PC version may eventually run better, but that doesn't save what's available today: an unfinished product sold at a premium price. Rockstar had all the time and money they needed. Fans deserved far better than this.

author: SADCAT_11111
quote:
If video games were rated purely on graphics, Google Maps would be Game of the Year every single year. 

It genuinely pains me to say this, but GTA 6 is just incredibly mediocre.

For me, GTA has always been about being thrown into a massive 3D open world where you can do pretty much whatever you want. That's what made these games so special and what separated them from the competition. The freedom, the action, the chaos, and just being able to mess around for hours doing whatever you felt like. But GTA 6 feels more like an open-world life simulator than the action game I've always loved. It's almost like Rockstar became so obsessed with making everything realistic that they forgot what made GTA fun in the first placee.

The story didn't do much for me either. I honestly felt nothing for any of the characters, and I can't imagine I'll remember much about them a few months from now. Compared to previous games, the whole thing just feels bland, with nothing particularly new or interesting to offer.

One of my biggest disappointments was the writing. I genuinely can't think of a single cutscene or piece of dialogue that made me laugh or even found particularly entertaining. Go back and watch almost any scene from GTA 5 involving Trevor, or Franklin and Lamar arguing with each other, and the difference is night and day. Those characters were genuinely entertaining to watch, even when they were doing absolutely nothing. And that's the thing, it isn't just about being funny. It's about having interesting characters and dialogue that actually make you want to keep watching. I just didn't get any of that here.

And then there's the gameplay, which feels incredibly tired at this point. After all these years, I expected Rockstar to do something genuinely new with the formula, but so much of it feels like the same old gameplay design we've already experienced countless times before, only now with better graphics and more realistic details.

Don't get me wrong, the game looks incredible, and I can appreciate the amount of work that went into creating its world. But graphics and realism can only carry a game so far. If the story, characters, and gameplay aren't interesting, then what's the point?

I really wanted to love GTA 6, especially after waiting so long for another entry in the series. But for me, it's easily one of the most disappointing Rockstar games I've played. Not because it's terrible, but because I know how much better these games can be.

author: Gonzav
quote:
Introducción 

Después de jugarlo, debo decir que es una obra de arte, entre comillas. Sin embargo, no puedo ignorar sus limitaciones y los pasos hacia atrás en términos de libertad y censura, algo que siempre ha caracterizado a GTA. 

Lo malo

Para empezar, ¿por qué quitaron a las chicas de compañía? ¿Para mejorar la relación entre Jason y Lucia? ¿Nos damos cuenta de que hablamos de píxeles y personajes ficticios? ¿Por qué los aviones atraviesan edificios o no se puede atropellar a una multitud de manifestantes? Entiendo que estas críticas puedan sonar mal, pero la libertad siempre ha sido uno de los mayores atractivos de GTA. Considero que restringir estas posibilidades es un paso atrás respecto a entregas anteriores, especialmente cuando hablamos de decisiones editoriales y no de limitaciones tecnológicas. ¿Será que Rockstar está adoptando ciertas ideologías que censuran todo lo que no encaja con su pensamiento?Por otro lado, he encontrado una cantidad considerable de bugs y caídas de FPS en PlayStation 5 Slim. Son errores bastante evidentes y, curiosamente, también los he observado en las partidas de otras tres personas. ¿Cómo es posible que la nota media sea de 99 si estos problemas están presentes? Además, Rockstar debería ofrecer un modo de rendimiento que priorice los 30 FPS estables, aunque sea reduciendo la resolución a 1080p o 720p.También me llama la atención que no se pueda atacar a personas pertenecientes a determinados grupos. ¿Acaso el valor de una persona cambia según su pensamiento político, sexualidad o gustos? En el juego podemos matar a muchísimos personajes sin restricciones, por lo que estas limitaciones resultan contradictorias. 

Otro punto negativo es el formato físico. Distribuyeron cajas con el espacio destinado al disco, pero sin incluirlo. No le encuentro ningún sentido y considero que es una burla hacia quienes seguimos prefiriendo comprar nuestros videojuegos en formato físico. 

Ojalá Rockstar corrija estos aspectos y recuperemos parte de la libertad que siempre ha caracterizado a la saga. Insisto en que estas acciones serían terribles fuera de un videojuego, pero GTA se ha distinguido precisamente por permitir experimentar con su mundo sin restricciones.

Lo bueno

Una auténtica obra de arte visual, sonora y física. Los gráficos son extraordinarios, las físicas resultan asombrosamente realistas y el sonido ambiental es un trabajo de primer nivel.

Me atrevería a decir que tiene la historia más madura y el mejor desarrollo de personajes de toda la saga. Consigue atraparte y mantenerte interesado en descubrir qué sucederá a continuación. El mundo también destaca por lo vivo que se siente, incluyendo detalles relacionados con la fauna. Encontrarte con un ciervo cruzando la carretera o ver cómo los cocodrilos huyen ante tu presencia son pequeños ejemplos del enorme trabajo realizado. Recomiendo jugarlo, pero esperaría unos meses para que Rockstar corrija los bugs y pula el rendimiento. Es un juego que merece disfrutarse en todo su esplendor. 

Nota: 6,0.
Pido disculpas por la nota, pero para mí lo más importante en un GTA siempre ha sido la libertad y considero que esta entrega está incluso por detrás de las anteriores. No hablo de limitaciones tecnológicas, sino de restricciones deliberadas por prejuicios o decisiones editoriales.

Actualización de reseña

Tras varias horas más, he notado que los NPC y la inteligencia artificial están demasiado centrados en el jugador. Conseguir que se peleen entre ellos es muy difícil y lo mismo ocurre con los accidentes de tráfico, muchas veces terminan golpeándote a ti, incluso cuando eres una víctima ajena a la situación. También sucede con la policía, lo que resta naturalidad al mundo. 

Por último, estamos en 2026 y posiblemente ante el videojuego más caro de la historia. ¿Por qué no contamos con doblaje a distintos idiomas, como ocurre en juegos con presupuestos muchísimo menores? Lo siento, pero actualizo mi nota a 5,0. Saludos y suerte.

author: rananda
quote:
For a game that took ~13 years to developer, it is somewhat disappointing.

For starters, no physical disc option. They couldn't find the time to make a decent build ready for market release, and that is sad.

As for the game: The fps is 30 (or lower at times). The story is decent. But what gets me the most is that the realistic graphics doesn't suit GTA imo.

They went a very different route with the story this time, and you know what, it is fine. They can try something different.

I do like the added safety measures they added (which a lot of people seem to call "woke"), I appreciate they went into it caring about this, this shows they understand and acknowledge what the current world needs. So good job on that part Rockstar!

author: ackeeza
quote: After waiting this long for a new GTA, I really wanted to be blown away, but my experience so far on PS5 has been a mixed bag. I have not touched the main story yet and spent all my time in freeroam exploring Leonida, messing with random events, and testing the sandbox. On the surface, the game looks incredible. The character models and facial animations are top tier, and the audio design holds up really well. The problem is that you can barely appreciate the visuals because the frame rate on PS5 struggles way too much. On top of that, the explosion effects look surprisingly bad and completely out of place next to how detailed everything else is.Driving feels great, and the physics are mostly solid, even if they occasionally get a little overexaggerated like GTA 4. What really disappointed me is the car customization. You would think a direct successor to GTA 5 would expand on it, yet somehow we ended up with **** for the open world itself, it feels like it plays things too safe. Leonida is lively, sure, but not nearly as alive as you would expect from the most anticipated game ever made. There are way fewer enterable buildings than I was hoping for, and exploring starts to feel repetitive pretty quickly. The random events are fine, but they do not come close to what Rockstar pulled off in Red Dead Redemption 2. Robberies are fun at first before getting stale, and the police AI that was hyped up to be revolutionary is just okay at best. On top of the gameplay issues, the game leans way too hard into woke messaging, which feels forced and drags down the classic GTA **** biggest issue right now is the technical state. I have not had any crashes, which is nice, but the open world is packed with bugs. I am constantly running into teleporting NPCs, weird physics glitches, and straight up falling through the map. It honestly feels like Rockstar put all their polish into the main story missions and assumed nobody would spend hours just messing around in freeroam.There is a great foundation here, and hopefully patches will fix the performance and bugs, but right now the sandbox experience feels unfinished, crappy, and underwhelming.

author: Xenomorphdragon
quote:
Overall, Grand Theft Auto VI is a good game with impressive graphics, and I did enjoy playing it—however, it doesn't quite feel like a great *GTA* game. While there are some launch flaws and glitches, those are minor issues that will likely be ironed out in future updates. 

My biggest frustrations come down to missing quality-of-life features and replayability: 

* **No Mission Replay:** Not being able to replay individual missions is a major drawback, especially if you miss something and have to restart the entire game just to experience it.
* **No New Game Plus:** The lack of a New Game Plus mode hurts its long-term replay value.
* **Deluxe Edition Progression:** Having to wait until the end of the game to unlock Deluxe Edition content takes away from the excitement of buying it upfront.

It’s a visually stunning, solid experience on its own, but missing staples like mission replay hold it back from feeling like a true GTA classic.

author: Colltrain
quote:
Firstly, this is not a bad game at all. What it is not, is the 'greatest game of all time'. GTA 6 feels like the begging of the decline of the franchise, whilst it currently has huge sales numbers and interesting critical review scores. The fact of the matter is this. 
Game has released buggy with frame rate issues and that is fine, it's 2026 and people are willing to accept this a lot more than in previous years. A middling story that is in opposition to previous GTA games. Removal of key features and replaced by boring 'real world' items such as buying groceries, feeding pets, showering and working out daily. Sure, you don't have to do all these things but you will receive a bad ending if you do not follow along with the key concepts this game tries to force you to comply with. Also, having vehicles have 'engine damage', needing to pay for fuel and not being able to steal whatever you want, are in direct opposition to the freedom you were given in previous games.

The main protagonist is painfully boring and the other one is painfully annoying. Sure, you can ignore the relationship mechanic and not comply with the game intended direction but enjoy the bad ending if you do. 

My biggest complaint is the removal of choice and fun. Sure, the world is big and there is plenty to do BUT that is an illusion as the game systems are locking you into an ending based on your relationship and actions. 

Additional breakdown 
Graphics 10/10 (the best graphics of any game period and a serious technical achievement) 

Scope 10/10 (amazing scope and delivered, the world is huge, impressive, densely packed and plenty of side activities to keep you busy.) 

Technical boring stuff 7/10 (frame drops and visual bugs are to be expected in 2026 but to be fair, switch games get crucified for this and games in the past have been docked points for this same thing)

Gameplay 5/10 (where the game falters tremendously, the gameplay is boring, it's curated whereas other GTA game offer you unlimited freedom to do what you want. This game removes that or ties it to an unsatisfactory ending. That, a long with further removals of freedom make this too much of a realistic experience.) 

Story 5/10 (one of the most boring GTA stories I can remember, gone are memorable missions found in the likes of GTA San Andreas, vice city and 4. You almost feel like a passenger in the story, as the message it tries to tell is conveyed through other people? Your co main protagonist and attempting to keep them happy and blah, it's just not great and I can't articulate well enough why) 

Fun 6/10 (I've included fun, because games should, at their core, be **** a way to escape the mundane aspects of our life, you turn on a game and escape reality for just a moment. To be hit with real world concepts in a medium meant to escape the real world, is not acceptable in 2026, a time when humanity is not doing so well and seeing that bleed into my safe space of the last 39 years is depressing. Instead of giving you the scope to do whatever you want and have fun. Rockstar decided to remove that in place with adult related themes of saving for a new life, decorating homes, not being able to steal from your neighbours (at least initially), keeping your partner happy? And not being able to indulge in a little bit of adultery . Whilst not deal breakers, it's another way of jamming in ideas that aren't really suited to the medium of escapism.) 

Music 7/10 (music is fine but we've lost the magic of a non-stop pop, V rock (vice city), chatterbox. It is a clear clear downgrade from previous games and let me lament the omission of lazlow, missing from this game. This could be an age thing but I miss the classics and the music they provided, for me, there are no memorable radio stations.) 

Overall 6/10 (went to realistic, forget the core of what made these games fun and decided to ground I'm reality. Removal of freedom to just do what you want, whenever you want it. Clearly missing the input of previous staff members who moved on.
Visual bugs, frame inconsistencies and a boring boring story with middling protagonists and no memorable extra cast like in previous games. Graphics are amazing and the game is not anywhere near bad. It's just not a game for me and for the people who enjoyed the excesses of the previous games.) 

One final complaint. 
The professional review scores for this game are so ridiculous. This is a good game, it is not near the GOAT debate. To see this placed along side snes classics like Chrono trigger, terranigma, ff6. N64 classics like mario 64, Zelda etc. PS/2 games like metal gear, ff7, GTA vice city, San Andreas, resident evil 2, silent hill 2&3. Modern gaming titans like it's predecessors GTA 4&5, dark souls, elden ring etc, those upper echelon ****, i put my foot down on that. You have failed at your jobs and colluded amongst yourselves. There is no way that 160 reviewers a unanimously agreed this is the greatest ever. Shame you!

author: MGLthrBoy
quote:
An ambitious game 13 years in the making, though its rough edges keep it from living up to the wait. The story is compelling once it gets its feet underneath it, though it is somewhat of a slog in the first act. 

Lucia and Jason are amazing main characters with a funny, witty, and relatable relationship. The newly introduced "Heat" mechanic makes getting away from police more engaging, forcing you to be more thoughtful with how you make your escape. 

With several new ways to incapacitate enemies rather than outright killing them, the game gives new options for handling missions, turning how you navigate your criminal career into a more open-ended endeavor. 

The game is beautiful, with incredible detail to environments, characters, vehicles, and beyond. Characters and NPCs now show bruises and "battle damage" after getting into fights, and even entire limbs (and heads) can now not only be dismembered, but obliterated. Vehicles now show realistic body damage proportional to the location and severity of accidents, even going as far as being able to disable specific elements of vehicles such as lights, tires, and engines. 

For all of its ambition, though, performance issues tend to hold it back. The game is *capped* at 30fps, not *locked*, meaning it more often than not dips below that threshold, sometimes severely so. It could be the most gorgeous game in the world, but that doesn't mean much when the game is sometimes almost unplayable. 

Characters can often get catastrophically and unnaturally stuck in small-to-medium spaces, halting progress and once even requiring a save reload. Sometimes the physics can bug out, causing vehicles, characters, and other assets to fling haphazardly across the map or into the sky.

I would recommend this game, despite its flaws, but I personally wouldn't recommend the $100 "Ultimate" Edition, as most of the things you are paying extra for are locked behind story progression.

**After 30 hours**
The open world is one of the best of all time, the voice acting, shooting (when adjusted), driving, and chaos are all good, but the story, characters, and explosions are TERRIBLE. The story caps its own potential by forcing Jason and Lucia into a relationship that cannot be tested at ALL. I would have loved to form different relationships with different NPCs with the respective protagonists, while they worked together to make it out of the struggle together. Every side character pretty much comes and goes. In other GTAs, Characters you met at the start stayed with you mostly the entire way and helped build up the story but that is nonexistent so far. I have seen the trains stop instead of run people over, certain clubs that cannot be shot up, and planes/ cars dont fully blow up and give that "wow" factor. author: ibu_playz
quote:
GTA VI — 6/10: A Visual Masterpiece, but a Disappointing Gaming Experience

Grand Theft Auto VI is an impressive technological achievement, but graphical fidelity alone does not make a great game. After years of extraordinary hype, I expected Rockstar to redefine open-world gaming. Unfortunately, my experience so far has been underwhelming.

I'm playing on a PS5 Pro connected to a 120Hz LG CX OLED television. The lighting, ray tracing, environmental detail and world design are remarkable. However, beautiful graphics cannot compensate for compromises in performance, responsiveness and gameplay.

Performance Over Photorealism

My biggest criticism is Rockstar's decision to prioritise photorealism over frame rate.

GTA VI's 30fps target is disappointing, particularly on PS5 Pro. Coming from games running at 60fps, 120fps and higher, the difference in motion clarity and responsiveness is immediately noticeable. Camera movements feel sluggish, and the experience lacks the fluidity I expect from modern hardware.

Even a premium OLED with VRR and ALLM cannot transform native 30fps into 60fps. Display technology cannot replace genuinely higher frame rates.

I believe Rockstar should have approached development differently. Rather than pushing graphical fidelity so aggressively, the studio should have prioritised optimisation and explored multiple graphics modes.

Ideally, players would have been offered a 40fps fidelity mode with enhanced visuals and a 60fps performance mode with reduced graphical settings. A stable 40fps mode would work well on 120Hz displays, while 60fps would offer greater responsiveness.

GTA V's enhanced console versions demonstrated the value of multiple graphics modes, although its technology was considerably less demanding.

Reducing graphical settings doesn't guarantee 60fps. CPU limitations, traffic, physics and world simulation could prevent that. Nevertheless, Rockstar should have considered performance and player choice more carefully.

Future consoles such as the PS6 would have provided an opportunity to push graphical fidelity further without imposing the same compromises on today's players.

Optimisation and Console Limitations

GTA VI's technical demands raise questions about how effectively such an ambitious experience can run across different consoles.

Reported performance fluctuations on standard consoles are concerning, especially when the more powerful PS5 Pro targets just 30fps.

Players shouldn't need premium hardware simply to achieve relatively consistent performance. Optimisation should be judged by stability and responsiveness, not just impressive screenshots.

Storytelling and Gameplay

Beyond performance, the story has yet to capture my interest.

Jason and Lucia's relationship hasn't delivered the compelling narrative I expected. Their dynamic and the pacing haven't given me the same investment I experienced in earlier GTA titles.

GTA III, IV and V established memorable identities through their characters, atmosphere and storytelling. So far, GTA VI hasn't delivered that same impact.

The open world is visually spectacular, but impressive environments aren't enough. Engaging missions, meaningful gameplay and memorable characters are what make games worth returning to.

My assessment is based on the portion I've played, and my opinion may change as I progress.

The Hype and Critical Reception

The near-perfect critical reception is difficult to reconcile with my experience.

A reported 99 Metascore suggests something approaching perfection, yet I believe the limitations in frame rate, responsiveness and player choice deserve greater scrutiny.

Critics may prioritise artistic achievement and technical ambition, but graphical excellence shouldn't overshadow gameplay.

An enormous budget, prestigious developer and record-breaking anticipation shouldn't place any game beyond criticism.

Commercial success and critical acclaim don't automatically validate every design decision.

Final Verdict — 6/10

GTA VI is visually extraordinary, but Rockstar's pursuit of photorealism has, in my opinion, come at the expense of performance and player choice.

I would genuinely prefer a less graphically demanding GTA VI running at a stable 60fps over a photorealistic experience restricted to 30fps.

The world design and technical ambition deserve recognition, but my experience with the frame rate, storytelling and gameplay hasn't justified the hype.

Perhaps completing more of the game will change my perspective. For now, I cannot rate it higher based solely on its visual achievements.

6/10 — A remarkable technical showcase, but a disappointing gaming experience so far. Graphics should enhance gameplay, not come at its expense.

author: hdmonteiro
quote:
I have a love-hate relationship with the GTA franchise. My inner child loves the arcade-style approach the games offer; *GTA: San Andreas* played a much bigger role in my childhood than *GTA V*—a game I still can’t bring myself to play for more than three hours at a stretch.I’ll admit the issue isn’t the game itself; it’s me and my personal playstyle. However, I have a different concern regarding *GTA VI*. 
It is undeniably a technological milestone for the current generation of consoles—the technical excellence is truly remarkable. As of now, no other game matches this level of detail, with the sole exception of *Red Dead Redemption 2*. In a way, *GTA VI* is essentially *RDR2* set in modern times; it takes all the details found in *RDR2* and refines them even further. I don’t say this to be dismissive, but rather to get to my main point of criticism: beyond replicating the technical brilliance of *RDR2*, it also adopts its pacing. That is where my critique lies. Those who truly enjoyed *GTA VI* did so precisely because they appreciated the pacing of *RDR2*. In my view, however, the game has lost its "arcade" quality, which is a significant drawback for me. Perhaps once it arrives on PC—along with online play, roleplay (RP) servers, and mods—it might regain the arcade-style elements that fans love. But as it stands, I find it difficult to call the game "perfect" or give it a 10/10.
