author: Odytzi
quote:
I am writing to you as a dedicated fan who has followed and supported Rockstar Games since the days of Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas, GTA IV, and GTA V.
First, congratulations on the technical achievement of Leonida and the quality of the writing and core gameplay in Grand Theft Auto VI. However, after playing the game, I feel compelled to share a deep sense of disappointment shared by many longtime fans of the series.
For decades, what set Grand Theft Auto apart from every other open-world title was true player freedom—starting from nothing, building a criminal empire, buying properties and businesses, and living freely inside the world outside of the main storyline. In GTA VI, while the world looks incredible, it feels like a "look, don't touch" experience once the missions are set aside.
What makes this especially frustrating is how the early game specifically sets up the exact opposite expectation. You start out broke trying to make money, Lucia's friend brags about living the high life with big money, the Italian guy at the bar explicitly points out all the girls around and how wild Vice City is, and women actively hit on Jason right from the start—like the woman whose plumbing you fix, or the neighbor coming on to him. The game rolls out the red carpet both financially and romantically, only to pull the rug out from under the player by locking down every single romantic or social interaction outside of the main couple.
Similarly, in a modern crime game set in 2026, players expected to build real wealth through real estate, businesses, money laundering, or modern criminal ventures like crypto mining. Instead, we are left buying phone cases and only 8 garages, with zero ability to purchase actual homes or income-generating properties—making it painfully obvious that all true open-world freedom was held back exclusively for GTA Online.
Cataloging 500 animals and vehicles cannot replace the thrill of building an empire from the ground up. You created the most detailed city in gaming history, yet players are not given the freedom to truly own a piece of it.

author: Boosie
quote:
Rockstar clearly poured its effort into how this game looks and feels, but the story doesn’t live up to it.

Pros: The visuals are stunning. The graphics, lighting, and overall presentation are some of the best I’ve seen, and the world feels alive thanks to the incredible attention to detail. The map design and NPC dialogue add to the immersion, and I haven’t had any major issues with performance.

Cons: The story is the weak link. The plot is flat, the pacing drags, and the characters never gave me a reason to care what happened to them. It fails to pull you in the way past entries in the series did. I also felt more restricted in what I could do than in earlier games, which clashes with the freedom the series is known for.

Verdict: It’s worth playing for the world and presentation alone, but I wouldn’t pay full price. Wait for a sale.

I've put about 15 hours in to the game and want to love it - but it just falls short in so many ways.

The heaviness to the driving, shooting and other realism is more like RDR than previous GTA games, and that would be a fair direction, however this is then flipped with crazy over the top scenes where you get shot 5 times and carry on like nothing happened. You have to refuel your car and collect groceries, yet when you park outside a shop and come back outside it's facing the other way.

The frame rate on base PS5 is a poor experience on an OLED TV - it feels juddery and anything further than 10m away is just blurry and off. I'm not a graphics snob, but even my girlfriend commented on how it looks weird.

Some of the scenery and the level of detail is another level above any other game I've seen, but sadly it's just not that fun. I'm not eager to go back to it, and it just feels really overhyped and under delivered in the core GTA do crime and blow stuff up kind of sandbox way. It clearly had love from the develops for the little things you come across, but somehow that same soul feels like it's missing from the actual play.

author: Alwerino
quote:
GTA 6 looks great and has amazing world-building, but it's not the 100/100 game critics claim it is.
There are many changes I don't like compared to GTA 5. First of all, I don't like the characters nearly as much as those in GTA 5. I don't like the gym system, where you have to work out. I don't like most of the changes to the police system, and I don't like changes to mechanics such as stealing cars, especially your neighbors' cars.
The story feels more like a dating sim, and there's significantly less action. When the first side quests you encounter are things like "Buy this for your girlfriend," "Buy that for your girlfriend," or "Go grocery shopping," it's hard to get excited about them. After seeing what these side missions were like, I lost interest in doing more of them, which is honestly sad.
Realism doesn't automatically make a game good, in my opinion.
I also had my problems with GTA 5, but it feels like none of them have been fixed. For example, I still don't like the controls. You press one wrong button, and your character automatically walks five steps toward the nearest NPC just to punch them. If I'm that far away, why is the game controlling my character for me? I just don't like when the game takes control away from me (probably a me problem).
There are bugs, but that's somewhat understandable. They definitely need to be patched, though. The game is capped at 30 FPS, and the frame rate can even drop below that. There's also no PC release and no multiplayer at launch. We already knew that, but I still don't like it.
Yes, the random events on the streets can be cool, but the "smart NPCs" we were promised just aren't there. NPCs feel pretty much the same as in GTA 5, apart from the events. They're still dumb, crash into everything, and you still get the police called on you for seemingly no reason.
I like activities such as billiards, but I'll be very disappointed if we can't play them in multiplayer once it comes out.
Also, €100!!! for the standard edition is just diabolical. The €80 version feels more like a lite version.
Is this game a 100/100 like critics say? NO!
Is this game a 1/10 like some players say? NO!
In my opinion, critics seem almost paid to praise the game, while players are taking the hate way too far. The truth is somewhere in between.

author: LevysJKings
quote: There was great anticipation surrounding this title, a 13-year wait, to the point of being hailed as "The Most Anticipated Game of the Decade." Did it truly live up to the enormous expectations everyone had? It's a visually stunning game. Its graphics, lighting, and open world are extraordinary. You could say it's truly revolutionary. But beyond that, the story starts slowly and is weak, even bad in places. The game's performance isn't the best; it's a shame that a title of this caliber, with its budget and development time, barely manages to reach 30 FPS, with significant frame rate drops. And the bugs are numerous, occurring with the simplest actions or even while following the story. You don't even need to force it. The soundtrack isn't original at all, so it doesn't stand out in this aspect either. Streamers have to mute the music to broadcast their gameplay freely because it's copyrighted. I have no doubt that many of the problems will be patched over time with updates, but right now, it has many negative points. And the physical nightclub? It's not there, it doesn't exist. A real shame. Otherwise, the game is wonderful and fun, although it certainly deviates significantly from the essence and mechanics of previous GTA games, to the point of not feeling like one at all. The controls are clunky and heavy. There are many incredibly boring mechanics just to keep Lucia happy. Mechanics from previous installments have been cut. Hopefully, they'll fix its performance and stability issues soon.

author: BoxItNow
quote:
I want to state my thoughts about the problem with this and many other games. I would implore that the games industry not utilise this game as an excuse to use excessive budgets and high development times as while the game is good in many fields, it also brands a problem for how far we should really push the idea behind realism in video games. The graphics I have to state are immaculate but at what cost, performance, truly i say that 30 fps is not the end of the world in many cases (comp games are usually the ones that should be 60), however the game is not 30 fps, its 30 with many such dips and i think were just not at the point technologically AND economically to think we should sell things like this, this type of thing should be for experimental purposes or until it becomes less expensive to push for it. On a gameplay standpoint i see it confusing to push "realism" in some places but not in others like if you feel like doing so many quality life features, either just go all the way or dont push it like you have already. Most of the time its fine but i dont think this approach is all that great for what the GTA franchise of games used to represent. It is more fit for RDR since that one is more focused on being a serious game while GTA was pretty much always a sandbox experience with a high on life story approach, which in areas i see it but in others i see something lacking.

Overall, performance aint it chief, add options to remove some elements of reflections and such to improve the experience, gameplay is alright but very unsure of itself, the experience the devs go through allegedly was not good at all and i truly dont like the path of the industry to beat down workers to make "art". Dont sell me a product with this many flaws at this price and expect me to not be disappointed about aspects. I wont review bomb the game like others because i want to be fair to the games merits but will knock points from the overall experience and the behind the scenes of the games production.

author: alexHK33
quote:
A 13-year wait for this?
I genuinely cannot believe this is what Rockstar spent over a decade making. GTA 6 is probably one of the biggest disappointments I've experienced in gaming.
Let's start with the story. The writing feels incredibly underwhelming, the pacing is all over the place, and the characters never managed to make me care as much as Rockstar clearly wanted me to. The dialogue is unnecessarily long, several missions feel repetitive, and the narrative takes forever to get interesting. After RDR2, I expected something extraordinary. Instead, I got a story that feels like it desperately wants to be cinematic without having the writing to justify it.
The gameplay isn't much better. Rockstar is still obsessed with restrictive missions where doing anything slightly differently results in a mission failure. Apparently, having an enormous open world doesn't mean you get to actually play freely in it.
And then there's the technical side. Frame drops, crashes, clipping, characters falling through the map, broken animations and ridiculous glitches. How does a game with this budget and development time launch with these problems? Even worse, we're stuck with 30 FPS. In 2026. Seriously?
The graphics are impressive, but let's not pretend visuals alone make a great game. Sometimes I feel like I'm playing a beautiful tech demo with an underwhelming story attached to it.
The worst part is watching people defend practically every flaw because it's GTA. If another studio released a game with these technical problems, repetitive missions and questionable writing, the internet would tear it apart.
GTA 6 isn't a terrible game, but it is nowhere near the masterpiece people convinced themselves it would be.
13 years of waiting, billions of dollars, and this is what we get.
Final score: 50/100.

author: hazrinamri
quote:
I really want to love this game. I’m fairly confident that the story will eventually pick up once I reach the 8–10 hour mark, but unfortunately, the current state of the game is making it difficult for me to get there.

One of my biggest frustrations is the lack of an option to switch between Performance Mode (60 FPS with lower graphical fidelity) and Fidelity Mode (30 FPS with higher graphical fidelity). For a game of this scale, having that flexibility should be a basic expectation.

On top of that, the bugs I’ve encountered have significantly affected my overall experience. The controls feel sluggish and unresponsive at times, while certain animations can look awkward and unnatural. These issues might seem minor individually, but together, they make the game considerably less enjoyable than it should be.

I genuinely believe Rockstar should have delayed the game by at least another year to properly polish and optimise it. A game carrying the expectations of GTA VI should be more than just ambitious; it should be a complete and polished experience.

I want to love this game, but ambition alone isn’t enough. It needs to deliver on its execution, especially if it’s going to live up to a 99 Metacritic score.

author: glorybower
quote:
The game is not a 10/10 incredible masterpiece, but it isn't a bad game either. 

Pros: 
- Beautiful world with entertaining NPC interactions
- Driving is a blast. 

Cons:
- The game incentivizes you to not needlessly shoot/k*ll NPCs and perceivably even gives you long-term penalties for doing so. The entire foundation of GTA is to provide an escape from reality where you can do these things without any long-term repercussion. 
- Nothing groundbreaking was actually done with this game. The controls and combat are still clunky. New features such as furnishing your home with your gf or running chores for her are BORING and DEMORALIZING rather than being exciting or even entertaining
- Why would they make what is essentially a mass-sh**ting simulator while at the same time preventing you from harming certain "protected classes" of NPCs? Where is this arbitrary moral boundary that is drawn? This feature makes the game OVERTLY political
- The game focus way too much on "realism" to the point where it becomes irritating to play. For example, literally nobody asked for Rockstar to implement a required joystick/button sequence to jumpstart cars. Its just a completely unnecessary feature they added for the sake of making things more realistic. The irony of this approach is that there are countless other features in the game that are blatantly unrealistic. For example, slowing down time during gun fights and magically having yellow/red lights appear on appendages of your targeted enemies. I can understand why Rockstar would think it would be "ground-breaking" to make the game more realistic, but it just completely ruins the magic by giving you these unnecessary and irritating roadblocks to doing things that you could just instantaneously do in the previous GTA games. These aren't even hard things to perform, which makes it blatantly unnecessary and nothing more than just annoying.

author: Fernandotorres
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI – My Rating: 5/10

An enormous ambition that seems to have exceeded its own limits.

Grand Theft Auto VI represents one of the most ambitious projects in gaming history. However, bigger does not necessarily mean better. Rockstar Games has created a world of extraordinary scale, but such ambition raises serious concerns about whether technical quality, optimization, and the overall player experience have received the same attention as visual spectacle.

One of my biggest criticisms concerns the bugs and glitches that can emerge unexpectedly in such a complex open world. Unpredictable physics, unusual character behavior, and technical inconsistencies can seriously damage immersion. These problems should never be dismissed as amusing features or inevitable consequences of an enormous game. Rockstar has the experience, resources, and financial backing to deliver exceptional quality control.

Performance is another major concern. A production of this magnitude should prioritize a stable 60 FPS experience. Modern players deserve smooth, responsive gameplay without sacrificing technical stability. An impressive world filled with extraordinary details loses part of its appeal when performance limitations prevent players from enjoying it properly. Technical ambition should not become an excuse for inadequate optimization.

Another controversial aspect is the extreme violence associated with GTA VI. Although the franchise targets mature audiences, Rockstar should implement stronger parental controls, prominent adult supervision notices, and explicit warnings reminding players never to reproduce violent, criminal, or dangerous activities in real life. These measures would not represent censorship. Instead, they would demonstrate responsibility toward an enormous global audience, particularly considering that younger players may still gain access despite age restrictions.

Latin American Spanish dubbing should also be a priority. Latin America is a massive gaming market, and a production with GTA VI's international reach should provide complete professional localization. Subtitles alone cannot deliver the same immersion as high-quality voice acting in a player's native language. Rockstar should recognize Spanish-speaking audiences with the same commitment to excellence demonstrated in its visual and technical presentation.

Music is another area where I expect considerably more innovation. GTA's traditional radio stations have cultural value, but relying heavily on older songs and nostalgia does not necessarily create an exciting soundtrack. A modern experience should include more compelling contemporary music, international artists, and greater musical diversity.

Spotify integration would be a fantastic addition. Imagine connecting your personal Spotify account and listening to your favorite playlists directly through your vehicle's radio while exploring Vice City and Leonida. This would provide an entirely new level of personalization without eliminating the franchise's traditional radio stations. For a game aspiring to redefine open-world entertainment, such integration would be a meaningful innovation.

Ultimately, GTA VI should not receive automatic praise simply because it is enormous, expensive, or developed by Rockstar Games. The larger the investment and expectations, the greater the responsibility to deliver an exceptional experience.

Visual realism cannot compensate for technical instability. A massive map cannot excuse disappointing performance. Mature content should encourage responsible parental guidance. Global popularity demands better language accessibility, while musical innovation should go beyond nostalgia.

My rating is 5/10. This score reflects the high standards I believe GTA VI should meet, rather than denying its extraordinary ambition. A game of this magnitude must be evaluated by the quality of its execution, not merely the size of its world or the reputation of its creators.

Grand Theft Auto VI may aim to redefine gaming, but ambition alone does not guarantee excellence. Bigger is not always better, and even Rockstar Games should never be above criticism.

author: Oloncaster
quote:
GTA 6 é um jogo que impressiona visualmente, mas decepciona em vários aspectos que sempre fizeram a franquia ser tão especial. 

Graficamente, é um espetáculo. A Rockstar entregou um mundo extremamente detalhado, com cenários impressionantes e um nível de qualidade visual absurdo. Nesse quesito, não tenho absolutamente nada a reclamar. É nota 10.

O problema começa quando entramos no gameplay. A jogabilidade parece um pouco travada e encontrei diversos bugs que prejudicam a experiência. Outro ponto que incomoda bastante é a limitação aos 30 FPS, que acaba deixando a jogabilidade ainda menos fluida, principalmente em um jogo desse porte. Em diversos momentos, essa limitação compromete a sensação de responsividade e torna a experiência mais arrastada do que deveria. Acredito que boa parte dos bugs será corrigida com os próximos patches, mas, no estado atual, ainda falta polimento. E, sinceramente, jogar um lançamento dessa magnitude a apenas 30 FPS é bastante decepcionante.

Os personagens são, de longe, uma das minhas maiores decepções. Achei o elenco extremamente sem sal, sem aquele carisma que sempre marcou os protagonistas da franquia. Lucia, principalmente, conseguiu ser uma das personagens mais insuportáveis que já vi em um jogo.

A história tem seus altos e baixos, mas sofre justamente por dar tanto destaque aos relacionamentos entre personagens que, para mim, são completamente desinteressantes. Em vários momentos, parece que o jogo está mais preocupado em desenvolver um drama de relacionamento do que em entregar aquela experiência caótica, irreverente e imprevisível que espero de GTA.

E talvez essa seja minha maior crítica: a falta de liberdade. Senti que o jogo tenta me prender constantemente às suas próprias ideias, limitando a liberdade de experimentar, improvisar e simplesmente causar o caos. É estranho jogar um GTA e sentir que o jogo não quer que eu faça aquilo que sempre tornou a franquia divertida.

No fim, GTA 6 é tecnicamente impressionante, mas parece ter perdido parte da identidade da série. É um jogo que quer tanto contar sua própria história, do seu próprio jeito, que acaba esquecendo de deixar o jogador criar a dele.É um GTA que, ironicamente, parece não querer ser GTA.

Nota:
Gráficos:10/10
Gameplay: 6/10
Personagens: 3/10
História: 6/10
Liberdade: 5/10
Nota final: 6,0/10

I’m frankly sad, this game isn’t even a fraction of what people have been waiting for YEARS, and I’m pretty sure a vast majority of the players would have preferred a less detailed and graphically weaker game if that would have given more time to take care of what makes a good game, story, characters, and fun gameplay.

As the game is right now, a 5 is all I would give it….. and that’s only because I know the bugs will be patched, because it deserves even 1 or 2 points less for that…. The online will obviously make this game better, but not even that can fix the bland characters, the boring missions, and the feeling that this game is inferior to a 13 years old ps3 game

author: Andrudis
quote:
Too much went wrong with this game. It is not a bad game, just mediocre at best.

Good:
- detailed open world with multiple different side activities
- photorealistic graphics

Bad:
- Max 30 FPS on PS5 Pro and even those 30 FPS are not consistent
- lot and lots of bugs, sometimes game-breaking
- very limited and curated sandbox environment: some random open world NPCs are simply immune to any forms of damage, limited or absent interactions with vehicles that were present in previous GTA games.
- many missions feels like a stupid chore: ok to have one from time to time to get a relax between firefights, not not dozen in a row wasting hours of gameplay time.
- story is a meh.... best way to describe it: desperate simp's simulator
- content locked behind monthly subscription in a single-player game

Some people may like it, but I cannot recommend it to anyone I know.
Huge disappointment, better replay GTA5 main story one more time...

author: Fufirka335
quote:
Блестящий мир, который забыл, что он — ГТА
Я ждал эту игру 13 лет. И вот, проведя в ней достаточно времени, я понимаю, почему одни называют её шедевром, а другие — разочарованием. Это не плохая игра. 
Это, пожалуй, самая технически сложная и визуально ошеломляющая игра, которую я видел. Но в погоне за реализмом Рокстар, кажется, потеряла ту самую искру безбашенного веселья, за которую мы любим серию. Что здесь действительно гениально:· Мир Леониды: Это не просто карта, это живой, дышащий организм. 
Детализация НПС, их реакции, погода, отражения — всё это создаёт невероятное погружение. Мир настолько правдоподобен, что иногда просто ездить по улицам и наблюдать за жизнью — уже удовольствие. 
История Джейсона и Люсии: Вопреки моим опасениям, их отношения стали эмоциональным ядром игры. Это не просто «Бонни и Клайд», это два сломанных человека, пытающихся выжить вместе. Это, пожалуй, самая зрелая и взрослая история, которую Рокстар когда-либо рассказывала. Что вызывает раздражение:· «Симулятор быта» вместо криминала: Первые несколько часов игры — это не ограбления и погони, а ремонт раковины, походы за продуктами и прослушивание диалогов. 
Я понимаю, что это сделано для «погружения», но я не для этого ждал 13 лет.· Производительность и баги: 30 фпс на консолях в 2026 году — это больно. Управление машиной в городе ощущается вязким, а в напряжённых сценах частота кадров проседает ещё сильнее. Плюс ко всему, на старте полно технических ошибок: персонажи проваливаются сквозь текстуры, а физика иногда ведёт себя непредсказуемо. 
Спорные геймплейные решения: Механика угона автомобилей стала чрезмерно сложной и бюрократической. Чтобы угнать современную машину, нужны инструменты, которые открываются только по сюжету. А некоторые машины и вовсе нельзя трогать. Это убивает спонтанность, которая была в ГТА 5. 
Повествование и миссии: Сюжет местами провисает, а структура миссий часто сводится к повторяющейся формуле «приедь — поговори — постреляй». Некоторые игроки также критикуют игру за то, что она стала слишком «правильной» и осторожной, потеряв свою сатирическую остроту.
Вердикт: ГТА6 — это не «дно» и не «шедевр на все времена». Это невероятно амбициозный проект, который местами задыхается под собственным весом. Это игра, в которой хочется жить, но не всегда — играть. 7 баллов — это оценка огромного потенциала, который, хочется верить, раскроется в будущих патчах и, возможно, на ПК. А пока что это очень красивая, но местами утомительная и технически «сырая» история о двух преступниках, которая так и не решила, хочет ли она быть весёлой песочницей или серьёзной драмой.

author: MSO11
quote:
GTA 6 has most of the core things that made GTA 5 fun, but it feels like Rockstar is sacrificing too much of the gameplay experience in the name of "realism."

Realism isn't necessarily a bad thing, but there's a point where it stops enhancing the experience and starts limiting it. Not every mechanic needs to be realistic, especially when it comes at the expense of player freedom and convenience.

My biggest problem, however, is the story. It doesn't feel particularly good or entertaining. Instead, it feels like having a second life, but not in a good way.
One of the reasons I play video games is to escape from real life responsibilities, situations, and problems. I don't want a game that makes me deal with the same things all over again, just through fictional characters.

Another problem is that the game seems more interested in making you experience its world exactly as Rockstar intended rather than giving you
the freedom to enjoy it your own way.
I think people are confusing technical achievements
and realism with good game design. GTA 6 can have an incredibly detailed world and impressive presentation while still having fundamental problems with its gameplay and story.

It's nowhere near the perfect game some journalists make it out to be.

author: Jhoge04
quote:
I'm generally a Rockstar hater. I find their games slow, boring, and rife with outdated design elements and bad controls. I do not like the never-ending push towards hyper-realism and simulation elements, especially where the feel of gameplay and controlling your character is concerned.

With that said, I'll try to be as objective as I can here.

There's plenty to be impressed by in GTA 6. Clearly an ungodly amount of labor went into the making of this game, and it shows. They really nailed Florida. Having lived there for eight years, I feel like I'm right back at my old Bradenton apartment when I'm in Leonida. The vibe = perfect.

However, the controls are sluggish, unresponsive, and clunky. Again, the focus on everything being as realistic as possible is a detriment here, and would be a detriment to gaming in general were this to become even more standard practice from other devs in the wake of this game's success. 

The 30 fps, for me, is really hard to get past. I'm also playing on an OLED display, which exacerbates the choppiness. This is not a game that looks or feels good to play, especially as a brand new release in the year of our lord 2026. I absolutely do not feel that sacrificing a 60 fps experience for the sake of deep simulation elements and crowd density is a worthwhile tradeoff.

7/10 is pretty fair in my opinion.

author: ViejoRabiosote
quote:
GTA VI es un juego visualmente impresionante, que está repleto de detalles que hacen que la experiencia de jugarlo se vuelva algo innovador. Su mundo lleno de vida te invita a continuar explorando cada rincón del mapa sin necesidad de que se vuelva algo repetitivo o aburrido.

Pero, GTA VI no es un juego perfecto. Si bien la historia principal no llega a ser mala, sí es una historia que se siente diferente a lo que nos tiene acostumbrados la saga de Grand Theft Auto, con muchas misiones centradas en la relación de Jason y Lucía, que llegan a ser un tanto excesivas y que carecen de acción.

El rendimiento del juego también deja mucho qué desear. En ciertos momentos, los FPS llegan a caer por debajo de los 30 y es algo que llega a ser muy notorio. Además es posible encontrarse con algunos pequeños errores visuales durante la partida. 

La falta de un modo en primera persona también es un punto que es necesario mencionar. Al parecer, Rockstar no ha descartado totalmente la posibilidad de que este añadido llegue durante alguna actualización futura, pero de momento, quienes disfrutamos de jugar GTA V en primera persona, estamos forzados a acostumbrarnos a permanecer el 100% del tiempo con la cámara en tercera persona. 

En conclusión, Grand Theft Auto VI cumplió con las expectativas en el apartado gráfico y en el nivel de detalle que siempre entrega Rockstar Games, mas la historia principal no está a la misma altura que las de sus predecesores y el rendimiento del juego aún podría haber sido mucho mejor.

author: AdrielMizu
quote:
Para um jogo da franquia Grand Theft Auto, ele até cumpre razoavelmente bem aquilo a que se propõe. Entretanto, isso está longe de justificar a avaliação extraordinariamente elevada que recebeu. O desempenho inconsistente, a qualidade gráfica aquém do que foi apresentado nos trailers e a quantidade expressiva de bugs relatados pelos jogadores comprometem consideravelmente a experiência. Diante de tantas deficiências, sinceramente, não consigo atribuir-lhe uma nota superior a cinco.

O que mais me causa indignação, contudo, é a discrepância entre a recepção crítica e aquilo que o jogo efetivamente entrega. Ele foi tratado como uma obra-prima, praticamente um marco incontestável da indústria, e, confesso, também alimentava expectativas consideráveis da minha parte. Entretanto, ao me deparar com avaliações tão infladas e análises cujas próprias críticas parecem contradizer as notas atribuídas, torna-se difícil não questionar a credibilidade desses julgamentos. Há uma evidente incongruência em apontar tantos problemas e, ainda assim, conceder uma nota 99, como se suas falhas fossem irrelevantes ou incapazes de comprometer a experiência.

É difícil, para mim, compreender como esse jogo pode ser colocado em pé de igualdade com The Legend of Zelda, especialmente considerando o que essa franquia representa em termos de inovação, evolução, identidade e contribuição para a indústria. Zelda não apenas entrega uma experiência de qualidade, mas também demonstra uma capacidade extraordinária de reinventar suas próprias estruturas, expandir seus horizontes e introduzir mudanças substanciais sem perder sua essência. Atribuir tamanha excelência a um jogo que, em minha percepção, sequer apresenta o mesmo nível de refinamento e consistência é, no mínimo, questionável.

A narrativa é entediante, os personagens principais carecem de carisma e personalidade, e o protagonista masculino, em particular, é extremamente desinteressante. Não há envolvimento suficiente, profundidade ou construção que me faça sentir genuinamente interessado em acompanhar sua trajetória. São aspectos fundamentais que, somados aos problemas técnicos, tornam a experiência muito aquém do que se esperaria de um título supostamente tão aclamado.

No fim, tenho a impressão de que a reputação desse jogo foi construída de maneira desproporcional aos seus próprios méritos. Uma nota 99 deveria representar excelência praticamente incontestável, um nível de qualidade em que os aspectos positivos se sobrepõem de maneira extraordinária às falhas. Entretanto, quando os problemas são tão evidentes e as próprias críticas apontam tantas inconsistências, essa avaliação deixa de parecer um reflexo genuíno da qualidade do jogo e passa a soar como uma supervalorização injustificável. Para mim, cinco é uma nota muito mais condizente com aquilo que ele realmente entrega.

author: rwh100475
quote: I bumped the score up one cuz Van Halen’s in the game. This game is beautiful, no doubt about it, it is borderline photorealistic. That is probably the biggest compliment I can give this game. The game runs at 30 fps max, which wouldn’t be difficult to swallow, if it weren’t for that it can’t even stay at 30, it very often dips under 30, especially when fighting or driving, the two key parts of grand theft auto. The ui feels overlooked, with a rectangular map chucked into the bottom right corner of the screen being the most egregious example, the gameplay feels the exact same as in GTA V, or even GTA IV, the story is lacklustre at best, and coupled with your own player experience being hindered by said story, it makes for a Grand Theft Auto deprived of a lot of what made GTA V in particular so massive. Now, this wouldn’t be a problem if GTA online released alongside the story mode, but it didn’t, even with an 8 year development time. Not being able to replay story missions is another point away from this game, especially when you could do so in previous games. All of these problems are even more egregious when even just estimating the millions upon millions of dollars poured into this game, only for it to come out in the state that it is in, where it cannot run on base ps5 without crashing the system. Overall this is not the definitive gta, it does not improve upon previous games enough for me to recommend this game to anyone, especially when you need to buy the ultimate edition for basic content, content that you would have got for free with any other gta game. I know this review is all over the place, but it is because this game means so much to me, and seeing it be less than adequate, it hurts. Rockstar did have impossible expectations to rise to, however it seems they have fallen well short of them. If this was any other game, things would be different, of course things like frame rate and glitches are at the end of the day minor, but this is Grand Theft Auto VI, rockstar knew the standards and expectations they had to meet, and they fell short, even after 8 whole years of development time. They need to do better.

author: Doggie218

Not only does it not run well, but for the consoles that have prided themselves as "the world's most powerful consoles" and have ran many other impressive titles in the past to not be able to run this game at a stable framerate, that is a failure on Rockstar's part, not the console. author: Kurtabomba
quote:
GTA VI: Impressive Graphics, but It Has Lost Its Soul

GTA VI isn't a bad game, but it has some serious problems that are hard to ignore, especially considering the expectations surrounding it.

Visually, the game is stunning. The world is incredibly detailed, and you can clearly see how much effort went into creating it. However, performance is a major issue, especially during intense action sequences. Great graphics mean very little when the gameplay struggles to stay smooth.

One of my biggest disappointments is the NPCs. With all the technological advancements we've seen, I expected a real revolution in how NPCs behave and interact with the world. Instead, they sometimes feel even worse than in previous GTA games.

Sure, they have more animations and scripted interactions, but that doesn't make them intelligent. For example, you can drive an SUV through a crowded beach, running people over, and some NPCs will continue their activities as if nothing is happening. For a game that focuses so heavily on realism, this completely breaks immersion.

Another major issue is that GTA VI feels too realistic for its own good.

Realism can be impressive, but it shouldn't come at the expense of fun. Sometimes it feels more like a real-life simulator than a GTA game.

What made GTA special was the freedom to do whatever you wanted. You didn't have to follow the main story. You could steal cars, cause chaos, create ridiculous situations, and spend hours just having fun in the open world.

That freedom was the soul of GTA.

In GTA VI, I often feel more restricted. The game seems so focused on creating a realistic experience that it forgets what made the series enjoyable in the first place.

A bigger map, better graphics, and more realistic details don't automatically make a better game. What matters is how much freedom the player actually has and how the world reacts to their actions.

The story also didn't impress me. I found it rather generic, with some questionable narrative choices that didn't really engage me.

I appreciate the ambition and the incredible attention to detail, but I expected more from Rockstar after all these years.

GTA was never just about realism. It was about freedom, chaos, unpredictability, and having fun without being told how to play.

GTA VI is an impressive technical achievement, but somewhere along the way, it feels like Rockstar forgot what made GTA special.

Sometimes, more realism doesn't mean more fun.

author: goshdang
quote:
GTA VI features an absolutely massive open world, both in terms of geographical scale and immersion. Its level of interactivity is so ambitious that it could genuinely be considered a revolution in open-world design. The amount of things players can interact with, discover and experience throughout the world sets a new standard for the genre. Weapons, vehicle destruction, NPC behavior and countless other gameplay elements are exceptionally well designed, making the world feel remarkably alive.

The story is genuinely great at certain points, and Jason and Lucia have excellent chemistry together, making their relationship one of the strongest aspects of the narrative. However, the writing is inconsistent. Some sections become unnecessarily boring, and despite the protagonists' strong dynamic, the story occasionally struggles to maintain the player's interest.

Unfortunately, the technical performance is extremely disappointing. Framerate drops can reach as low as 15–20 FPS in certain situations, accompanied by various bugs. While these bugs are not widespread, they are still unacceptable for a production of this scale. Even more frustrating is the fact that, in 2026, Rockstar is still relying on physics systems tied to framerate. These are fundamental technical issues that should have been addressed back in 2004. It is genuinely baffling that Rockstar still hasn't properly moved past these limitations.

The excessive price is another major drawback. Regardless of how revolutionary its open world might be, that does not justify overlooking technical shortcomings or charging such an exorbitant amount for the experience.

Finally, there is something particularly questionable about the way some reviews approach this game. It is strange to see critics explicitly point out that certain sections of the story are poorly written, some characters are underwhelming, gameplay mechanics have significant flaws, or even describe entire aspects of the experience as disappointing, only to ultimately award the game a perfect 10/10. A perfect score should represent an experience with virtually no meaningful shortcomings, not one where major criticisms are acknowledged and then seemingly ignored when assigning the final rating.

GTA VI is an incredibly ambitious and, in many ways, revolutionary open-world game, but ambition alone does not make a masterpiece. Its technical problems, inconsistent storytelling and excessive price prevent it from reaching its full potential.

author: YoshimitsuWins
quote:
TLDR: GTA 6 looks great and runs okay for the hardware, but the story, characters, humour and player freedom are a big step down from older GTA and RDR games. The random developer controlled limits on what you can and can't do break the sandbox, and it is nowhere near the 99 it has. 5 out of 10.

I really wanted to like this one. The first few hours are genuinely impressive visually. The graphics, the scale, the detail, all of that got me at first. But after the wow factor wore off I was left with a game that felt dull and weirdly soulless. 

The story just did not grab me. It has none of the highs and lows of the older GTA games. The characters did not give me a reason to care, and the missions started to feel like I was going through the motions. I finished it without any real urge to jump back in. For this game to deserve the 99 it is getting, it would have to be more fun than Vice City, San Andreas, IV or V in characters, moments, story, gameplay and technically. Technically it beats those games, but it is nowhere close in the other areas. Out of all areas, it wins in 1.

The humour is another big miss. GTA used to have that trademark comedy running through everything. Nobody here comes even close to someone like Lamar from V or Brucie from IV. The jokes feel safe and forgettable, and I did not laugh once the way those characters used to make me laugh.

My biggest issue is player freedom. I could still shoot cops and random people on the street and cause the usual chaos. So the problem is not that the game is scared of violence. The problem is that the limits feel random. Certain scripted crowds or areas just ignore you, or you cannot interact with them the way you expect. That inconsistency breaks the sandbox for me. GTA used to feel like a world that reacted to whatever you did. This one feels like it picks and chooses when freedom applies. Red Dead Redemption and older GTA games trusted the player more than this.

Technically it is strong in some places but rough in others. For a game with 13 years of development and a years delay for polishing, the explosions look and sound bad, just downright lazy, among many other issues and bugs encountered. Some animations feel unfinished. For a game this big and this polished in some areas, those gaps stand out.

If you want a pretty world to look at, maybe give it a shot. If you want the story, depth, humour, freedom and fun of past GTA games, this one is not it. 5 out of 10 for me.

author: 3lgringo
quote:
Let’s address the elephant in the room. The wall-to-wall 10/10 reviews feel completely disconnected from the actual game. 

Whether critics are paid off or just terrified of going against the hype, calling this flawless is a joke, especially when they are giving Rockstar a free pass on monetization that would get any other publisher crucified. 
In a vacuum, I would give this a 7.5/10. 

It’s a good game with a massive world. But when every outlet is blindly handing out 10s, somebody has to balance out the average, so it’s getting a 6/10 from **** pricing and paywalls alone should have docked points. 

Rockstar bumped the base game up to $80, yet you don't even get the full experience for that money. 

If you want all the single-player content unlocked, you have to pay $100 for the Ultimate Edition. 

On top of that, they carved out actual story-mode perks, vehicles, and garages and locked them behind a $7.99 monthly GTA+ subscription. 

Charging more for the base game while locking single-player content behind a $100 edition and a monthly fee is pure greed. 

Are we really going to let this slip just because it’s Rockstar?

Then there is the performance. 
Playing at 30 FPS on a PS5 Pro in 2026 is ridiculous. For a flagship release on the strongest console out there, the frame rate feels sluggish and immediately ages the game.
Rockstar also quietly gutted staple mechanics that gave the series its grit and immersion. 

Removing first-person driving takes away one of the best ways to actually take in the city, and cutting prostitution feels like a sanitized, corporate move for a franchise built on unapologetic satire and street-level **** the story side, the game asks you to spend hours cultivating a relationship with a protagonist I just cannot relate to. When a narrative forces that kind of emotional investment without giving you any common ground, it drags instead of hooks **** be fair, the scale and density of Leonida are wild. 

I am willing to give the bugs I ran into during my first 40 hours a pass simply because a map of this size is bound to have rough edges at launch.

There is an impressive sandbox here with plenty to do, which is why it would normally sit at a 7.5 for me. 
Between the $80 price tag, greedy paywalls, locked 30 FPS, missing franchise staples, and a lead dynamic that falls flat, this is nowhere near a 10/10. 

Score: 6/10

author: Seawarrior
quote:
6/10 – Severely Disappointing
Honestly, GTA 6 was a massive disappointment for me. After waiting this long, I expected a lot more from Rockstar. The biggest issue is that it just doesn’t feel like GTA anymore. The characters are boring, the dialogue is forgettable, and the story really struggles to keep me interested.Lucia is probably one of my biggest complaints. She’s just a genuinely **** person, and not in the entertaining way that previous GTA protagonists have been. GTA has always been full of terrible people, but characters like Trevor, Michael, and Tommy Vercetti were at least interesting, funny, or memorable. Lucia doesn’t have that same appeal. I don’t find her likable, her personality does nothing for me, and the writing never gives me a reason to care about her. There’s a difference between writing a morally questionable character who’s entertaining to play and one who’s simply unpleasant to spend time with. For me, Lucia falls into the second category. The supporting characters aren’t much better **** humor also feels like it’s missing. GTA has always had ridiculous characters, memorable moments, and a certain attitude that made the games entertaining. GTA 6 feels like it takes itself way too seriously while somehow having a less interesting story. Even the missions feel repetitive at times. I also think the game relies too heavily on its impressive presentation rather than giving players genuinely memorable experiences. There’s plenty to look at, but surprisingly little that has really stuck with me.I’ll give Rockstar credit for a couple of things. The graphics are incredible, and the amount of detail they put into the world is genuinely impressive. The soundtrack is also fantastic and easily one of the best parts of the game. The music fits the setting perfectly, and the radio stations are one of the few things that still capture that classic GTA feeling. There’s clearly an incredible amount of work behind the game, and I don’t want to take that away from the developers.What I genuinely don’t understand is how this game received so many 10/10 reviews. I’m completely lost on that one. I understand that people have different opinions, and I can absolutely see why someone would enjoy the world, graphics, and overall presentation. But a perfect score suggests a level of quality that I just don’t see here. After roughly 25 hours of playing, I’ve spent enough time with the game to form a pretty solid opinion, and I still find myself wondering what everyone else is seeing that I’m missing. I respect that other people love it, but I strongly disagree with the idea that this is some kind of masterpiece.I think that’s what makes the disappointment worse. Rockstar has already shown that it can create incredible worlds while also delivering memorable characters and excellent storytelling. GTA 6 gets the world right, but for me, it falls short in the areas that actually make a game worth remembering.Unfortunately, great graphics and an excellent soundtrack don’t make up for boring characters, repetitive missions, and disappointing writing. I wanted to love this game, but I found myself playing it more because it was GTA 6 than because I was actually enjoying ****’s not a terrible game, but it’s nowhere near what I expected after all these years. If this had been released by a different studio without the GTA name attached, I genuinely wonder whether it would be receiving the same level of **** me, it’s a 6/10, and even that feels generous.

author: Toraya
quote:
Also spoiler warning on TLoU2

The situation with GTA 6 reminds me a lot of The Last of Us Part 2. Both studios seem to misunderstand what players actually enjoy about games.. They offer freedom, but then punish you for using that freedom in ways the developers didn't intend. And somehow, both receive 10/10 reviews from critics.

If we're going for realism by making me buy groceries for my partner, then why can't I choose not to be in a relationship with her?
If we're telling a serious story about forgiveness, then why can't I choose to kill Abby at the end? I didn't forgive her.

"But that's not the story we made for you!"
Then why give me the freedom to roleplay a character in the first place?

I can play Ellie as complete psycho, but the game barely acknowledges those choices. Instead, it creates the illusion of freedom while quietly imposing restrictions based on what the developers want me to do, rather than what makes sense within the game's world.

Take GTA, for example. You can't steal cars in the neighborhoods. Why? Just because the game says so? Let me steal the car. Let me deal with the consequences. Then I'll feel like: “I can, but it'll cost me something” and the game will steer me in the right direction.
Dishonored did this f****ng years ago.

It's a shame, because clearly an enormous amount of effort went into both games, but the basics are all f****d up.
Guiding players instead of putting up walls takes genuine talent. And unfortunately, that talent seems to be dying out.

Now let's get into the proper review

Gameplay: 6/10
The fundamentals are fine. Guns have weight. Movement is responsive enough. Switching between protagonists is cleaner than GTA 5. The new wanted system is kinda cool.. but that's pretty much it.. Nothing feels meaningfully evolved. The systems look complex on paper, but collapses into the same loop Rockstar has been selling since GTA 4 the moment your honeymoon period with the game falls off.

Story: 3/10
This is the part that should have justified the wait. It doesn’t. The Bonnie-and-Clyde setup promised in every trailer arrives thin, directionless, and strangely lifeless. The central conspiracy never generates real tension. Dialogue is functional at best and outright flat at worst. There is no emotional through-line worth following. GTA 4 had bite. GTA 5 had chaotic energy. Here the plot exists mainly to justify expensive set pieces. Been playing for days and the story has not once made me lean forward.

Characters: 2/10
Jason and Lucia are well-rendered. Their voice acting is.. fine. But neither of them has a personality strong enough to carry such a long game. Supporting characters feel like filler to increase size. The "optional" romance system is a neat checkbox, but they should have given the players the freedom to choose who they use that system for.

Character Development: 2/10
There is almost none. The game gestures at growth and then ignores it. Choices are mostly cosmetic. Neither protagonist meaningfully changes based on anything you do. This is very disappointing when looking at the development time of a decade and only a single romance option.

OST: 5/10
The radio is pretty great.. and there is a healthy amount of options when it comes to genre of music, but the original score never elevates a single important moment the way older Rockstar soundtracks did.

Graphics: 10/10
This is the one category where the budget is obvious. Lighting is excellent. Facial animation is strong. Vehicle detail is high. Crowds are dense. Night driving looks the way the trailers promised. It is the best-looking open-world game on current hardware. That is also the problem. The visual quality is so far ahead of everything else that it highlights how little else was finished to the same standard.

Map Design: 7/10
The map is big and usually dense.. but.. the roads are sometimes too narrow for the speeds and traffic density the game encourages. You constantly clip, ****, or get stuck in awkward geometry.

Mission Design: 4/10
Most missions are the same that have been in GTA games for over a decade, just with better production values. Linear corridors, scripted shootouts and the familiar follow the marker. The big heists look expensive and play like upgraded GTA 5 content. Side activities exist, but they rarely feel surprising. It doesn't really feel like the extra years were spent inventing new ways to structure play. There is only the sense that more money was spent making the old ways look nicer.

Driving: 7/10
Cars look and sound good. Handling is pretty much the familiar mix of arcade-realistic. Sadly the high-speed chases quickly turn into bumper-car nonsense. The physics are solid, but road design tends to fight against it.

Overall score: 5.1 (It's pretty much a 7 if we remove all the story aspects out of it, so I have high hopes for GTA 6 online and modding)

Taking into account the increased price, unsteady 30 FPS and all the bugs.. I should lower the score, but meh.

author: 13years4this
quote: GTA VI is a beautiful, technically impressive game, but it's also one of the most disappointing experiences I've had as a lifelong GTA fan. Rockstar seems to have forgotten what made GTA fun in the first place. Instead of an entertaining crime sandbox filled with memorable characters, hilarious dialogue, and chaotic freedom, we got an overly realistic life simulator. I didn't buy GTA to hang drywall, repair staircases, buy groceries, fix cars, or manage my relationship. The obsession with realism actively hurts the gameplay. Even committing crimes feels like a chore now, with an overly complicated wanted system that practically requires you to change your entire identity after losing the police. The characters are another major disappointment. Jason feels like an invisible sidekick to Lucia, and neither comes close to the memorable personalities of past GTA. The writing lacks the humor, charm, and personality that defined previous games. And what's the point of making money? Where are the meaningful purchases, progression, and rewards? The world is enormous and gorgeous, but there's surprisingly little incentive to actually engage with it beyond repetitive activities and cosmetic customization. Rockstar confused having more things to do with having more things worth doing. GTA VI might be the most realistic GTA ever made, but somewhere along the way, Rockstar forgot to make it fun.

author: Syrostas
quote:
7/10 – An Incredible World That Too Often Feels Like a Beautiful Facade

GTA VI is an extraordinary game. Its world is breathtaking, the atmosphere is captivating, and even after many hours of playing, I constantly find myself wanting to explore more and discover new things.

And yet, I'm disappointed. Not because GTA VI is a bad game, but because I believe Rockstar has missed an enormous opportunity.

My biggest criticism is the lack of genuine player freedom.

The game presents an incredibly detailed, seemingly living and breathing world. But whenever I try to interact with it beyond what the developers have specifically anticipated, I run into limitations far too often.

A dog plays with a tennis ball but doesn't react when I pick it up and throw it. An alligator threatens my character from a distance while completely ignoring another person walking right past it. I can operate an excavator, including its arm and bucket, yet I can't even scoop up a pile of sand. Countless buildings remain inaccessible.

What frustrates me even more is the mission design. Time and again, I come up with logical alternative solutions, only to discover that the game refuses to acknowledge them. Instead of reacting to my decisions, the story simply waits for me to follow the exact steps the developers intended.

This is especially disappointing because Rockstar already demonstrated with Red Dead Redemption 2 how believable a virtual world can feel. Meanwhile, games like Baldur's Gate 3 have shown just how rewarding creative problem-solving and genuine player agency can be.

So why do I still enjoy GTA VI so much?

Because when the game gets something right, it does so brilliantly. The world is fascinating to explore, the atmosphere is exceptional, and countless small encounters make the experience genuinely entertaining. Occasionally, the game even surprises me by allowing creative solutions I never expected it to support.

And that is precisely why my score isn't lower.

For me, GTA VI is a fantastic entertainment experience that falls significantly short of its potential when it comes to meaningful interaction and player freedom.

I would gladly have sacrificed some graphical perfection for a world that responds more consistently and logically to my actions.

I don't expect every building to be accessible or every imaginable action to be possible. But when a game gives me interactive tools, realistic-looking environments, and seemingly intelligent characters, I expect those elements to behave in ways that make sense.

GTA VI succeeds at making its world look alive. Too often, however, it fails to make that world behave as convincingly as it looks.

7/10 – A game I genuinely love playing, despite being repeatedly disappointed by how little freedom it actually gives me.

author: Dolgy

author: Zoldyck
quote:
La industria quiere que GTA 6 sea un éxito para poder imponer un futuro totalmente digital, juegos a 100 dólares, microtransacciones, códigos en lugar de discos físicos, ausencia de reembolsos, bloqueos regionales, códigos con fecha de caducidad, hardware costoso y otras prácticas contrarias a los intereses del consumidor. Todos están compinchados entre sí, por lo que no sorprende que los periodistas especializados le otorguen al juego una puntuación perfecta de 10. Sin embargo, no mencionan que quienes trabajaron en el título ya han perdido sus empleos. Si te preocupa que Rockstar y Take-Two hayan despedido a personal antes del lanzamiento de GTA 6, no te dejes llevar por su bombo publicitario ni por su propaganda. Exige que asuman las consecuencias y hagan lo correcto. Lamentablemente, la gente no hará caso, y las grandes corporaciones seguirán saliéndose con la suya gracias a su codicia, mientras continúan perjudicando a los jugadores.

A nivel gráfico es sin duda una locura. El movimiento del cabello, las expresiones faciales, el hecho de que cuando eres golpeado se te deforme la cara y se llene de moretones. A su vez, siempre están sucediendo cosas en el mapa, desde una avión que cae, una detención policial, NPCs realizando sus actividades diarias. Aunque estas son cosas ya vistas en videojuegos como The Witcher o Cyberpunk, incluso la rutina es un elemento que está presente desde Majora´s Mask. Sin duda el juego propone una cantidad gigante de sistemas a medida que avanza, pero ninguno es lo suficientemente profundo. 

Las interfaces y menús son paupérrimas, no evolucionaron nada desde GTA V. Hoy en día con franquicias como Persona, The Witcher, Resident Evil que ponen tanto enfásis en la estética, resulta mediocre observar como GTA no ha evolucionado nada en este aspecto. La interfaz de San Andras - Vice City sigue superponiéndose al minimalismo actual de Rockstar.

GTA VI sigue manteniendo una jugabilidad arcaica que no evoluciona, si bien es interesante el uso del sistema de moral/honor que preponderó en Red Dead Redemption 2, es un sistema que no tiene sentido que la identidad libre que posee GTA, de hecho, empobrece la experiencia. Por otra parte, el sistema de manejo no está a la altura de una saga que se caracteriza por la conducción, es como si se hubiese estancado. Hasta día de hoy, la conducción de GTA IV sigue siendo el mejor intento de Rockstar en lo que se refiera a innovar y buscar una jugabilidad única que no tenga ningún otro juego.

Y finalmente, GTA VI tiene una historia que no entiende la esencia de GTA. El humor es corny, la historia de Lucía y Jason tiene una identidad marvelizada, lo mismo sucede con los secundarios: todos son irrelevantemente nimios. Es un alivio que Niko Bellic solo haya aparecido unos minutos, porque el tono y la falta de comprensión sobre lo que significa ser un GTA pude destruir absolutamente su personaje.

GTA VI es un juego mediocre que tiene miedo a evolucionar, pero se sostiene en quizás, el mejor trabajo gráfico y técnico de la historia. Lo que le permite obtener 70 puntos a pesar de ser un juego soso que nuevamente no se atrevió a cambiar nada, ni revolucionar la industria de los videojuegos. 70/100

author: vgchess
quote: Is GTA 6 really perfect? Not even close. To be clear, it is a fun and polished modern triple A videogame. But that’s about as close as it comes to perfect. My biggest complaint as a fan of the series is that the game does not respect the brand of grand theft auto. You can’t even steal a car at the start of the game. When playing, it feels more like the developers lazily built a life simulation vaguely surrounding whatever IP they were given. Once Lucia enters the game, it also feels like Jason just stands around and waits for her to do things, like he wasn’t even meant to be in the game. I have never felt so invisible as a playable game character in my life. The realism also takes a lot away from the gameplay. I went to fill up my car with gas, and the pump was literally broken and I had to come back later. Thank god I still had half a tank. Some of these realism elements really drop the quality of gameplay down hard. Another thing I noticed is that there are toll booths in this game. If you drive through one it will deduct five dollars from your wallet. Well what if I don’t have 5 dollars? Am I gonna get a wanted level for driving through it? The very first thing I did in this game, the moment it gave me a free choice to make, was I started hanging drywall. Then I painted the room after hanging it. Then I went outside and replaced a staircase. Then I replaced the balcony. Then I fixed the leak in the roof. And just when I thought I was done playing home improvement auto, then it was time to go do chores for Lucia. Buy her flowers, get the groceries, get clothing from her friend, fix the car. And when there’s nothing else to do, **** I hit that home gym and do some squats, bench press, and deadlifts. And then, right after making gains you know you gotta drink a protein shake and then press R2 to throw that **** in the garbage. Oh and if you care about your physical fitness, you better do that every 20 minutes. No matter what you do, you are going to lose relationship points with Lucia over something stupid. I did everything for her. Danced with her. Drove her home from jail. And then the game asks me to get her a drink and bring it to her. I go to the bar and order a drink for 18 dollars, because she is my lady and she deserves something special. I carry the drink all the way to Lucia. Then she says “well where is my drink” and Jason walks back into the bar, and comes out holding the expensive drink I bought and a 5 dollar beer in the other hand. Then he hands her the beer, apologizes, and a little broken heart animation appears. So I broke her heart because I walked out with only one drink instead of two for us both. Nothing is ever enough for your loved ones. Another complaint I have about this game is one of its major selling points: the wanted system. Many changes from the fifth game make being wanted by the police **** more than ever. There’s now 6 stars, in case 5 wasn’t hot enough water for you. And once you lose the cops, you have to take extra measures or else they will recognize you and arrest you later. Not only do you have to respray your car, a previously optional speed up to lose the cops, but now it is mandatory to do that and also change your hair, glasses, hat, and clothing. Only after re-customizing your entire life do you lose the cops. These design changes, along with increased security levels in major theft locations, create an environment where committing crimes is scary and not fun. In a game called grand theft auto, you wouldn’t expect such severe consequences for stealing a car. They should have called the game approved by moms, a crime simulator for teaching young men not to steal or else they have to change their whole identity. As an aside, the realism element really changes the way you perceive the in game characters. I’m out here trying to collect rent like it’s job simulator, but then this **** needs me to fix her sink. And then while I’m under the sink fixing it, she has the audacity to walk out half naked and basically shove her **** right in my face. In GTA 5, even the hookers were pixelated enough for you to just go, oh okay, that’s supposed to be a hot girl. But now I’m out here trying not to cum in real life while plumbing in the game. In conclusion, is this the best ever video-game since 1998? No, it’s not even as good as GTA 5 was in 2013. That game had inspired, funny, memorable, and relatable characters. GTA 6 will go down in history as a game that got its 99/100 rating through corporate censorship. Is there any reason Ocarina of Time deserves a 95/100 but GTA doesn’t? No. This game is an 8/10 at best, once the novelty of playing dress up with Lucia wears off. But GTA 6 deserves a mixed review, especially after the record corporate bootlicking from the so-called professionals. Game critics may never recover, and their profession may never be respected again, without serious changes in accountability and journalistic integrity.

And I’m not blaming the developers, who have clearly poured an incredible amount of talent, effort, and passion into this game. I’m talking about the corporate decisions behind **** yes, the 30 FPS limitation is another disappointment. But at this point, the frame rate almost feels like the least of my **** saddest part is that underneath all these questionable decisions lies a game I genuinely want to **** world, the atmosphere, the characters, and the technical achievements are incredible. And that makes it even more frustrating when business decisions overshadow the actual gaming **** me, GTA 6 represents so much of what is wrong with the modern gaming industry: higher prices, more paid extras, less permanent ownership, and the growing expectation that players should continue spending money long after purchasing a full-priced game.I’m not a GTA hater. Quite the opposite.I’ve been a loyal fan since the very beginning, and that’s exactly why this direction disappoints me so much.I WANT to love GTA 6. But I don’t want to feel like I’m constantly being asked to open my wallet after already paying full price.Rockstar has created something that is technically and artistically extraordinary. But impressive graphics, a massive world, and incredible attention to detail don’t automatically make a game perfect.Respecting your players matters just as **** unfortunately, some of these decisions make me feel like that respect is slowly **** 6 doesn’t just show how far video games have come. Sadly, it also shows how far the gaming industry has drifted in the wrong direction.Final Score: 5/10An incredible technical achievement with a fascinating world and promising characters, held back by restrictive mission design, disappointing performance limitations, and monetization decisions that leave a bitter **** perhaps that’s the biggest disappointment of all: I never expected to feel this conflicted about a GTA game.

author: RiaCritic
quote:
After years of hype and anticipation, GTA VI is finally here !

I can confidently say it's a very good game, but nowhere near the masterpiece some people are claiming it to be. 
First, the positives. The graphics are absolutely stunning, Vice City looks incredible, and the soundtrack is fantastic, as expected from Rockstar. The introduction is excellent and immediately pulls you into the world. The story is genuinely interesting, and the relationship between Jason and Lucia is one of the game's strongest aspects. Their chemistry feels natural and makes you care about what happens next.
However, my biggest problem is the excessive realism. Rockstar has clearly pushed realism further than ever, but at what cost? GTA V had a perfect balance between realism and arcade-style fun. GTA VI sometimes feels so obsessed with being realistic that it forgets what made GTA enjoyable in the first place. 
More realism isn't always better.Then there's the technical side, which is honestly unacceptable. 

The FPS drops and bugs are embarrassing for a game of this scale, especially after such a long development cycle. The lack of convincing physics in certain situations is also extremely disappointing. For a game that puts so much emphasis on realism, that's quite ****'s also unfortunate that GTA Online and a PC version aren't available at launch. 
However, these are separate issues and don't affect my rating of the game itself.

Ultimately, GTA VI is a very good game with an engaging story, fantastic music, impressive visuals, and two compelling protagonists. But it also suffers from questionable design choices and technical problems that shouldn't be overlooked simply because it's GTA.

After 25 hours, I genuinely enjoy the game, but calling it the highest-rated game of all time is ridiculous. A 6/10 feels fair for now.

author: CatKalamazoo
quote:
I’ve persevered with this game for over 20 hours in total and it’s not gotten any better for me. The storyline and characters don’t feel like they belong in a GTA game. 

I think this storyline and these characters may have been better received in their own game, but not in this franchise.

I think the map and scenery are really stunning, but the playability of this game in single player mode is an incredible chore.

As someone who has played GTA since the first incarnation, I’m quite disappointed with how this has turned out. I’m never going to finish it, nor do I want to. After 20 hours I’m not in any way invested in any of the characters or their story.

One other criticism I have is regarding the 30 FPS issue. I’m not the sort of person who is obsessed with frame rates and would be willing to accept 30 FPS if the game at least ran consistently and smoothly at that rate. Having played the game for 20 hours, even I’m noticing some issues during certain sequences where the frame rate is quite noticeably dropping to very low levels. I feel this is unacceptable for a game that has taken this long to develop coupled with the price it’s currently being sold at.

I definitely think there is a fantastic sandbox to explore at the foundation of the very mediocre storyline structure that has been constructed on top of it. So, providing GTA 6 Online is free on the PC when it is released, then I think I may enjoy the game more when that arrives.

I would rate the storyline and much of the associated gameplay 6/10 if this were a standalone game, as it’s not great, but it’s not dreadful. It definitely wouldn’t be the sort of game I would ever choose to play if it hadn’t been shoehorned into the GTA universe. Within the GTA context though, I can only rate this facet of the game 3/10, as it badly misses the mark and just doesn’t fit the long established theme at all in my honest opinion.

The actual open world environment is well made and a sound achievement in itself which can’t be ignored, so I rate that aspect of the game 8/10 as it stands. If the associated bugs and frame rate issues were resolved, I would rate it higher.

author: killa187
quote: Incredible World, Completely Wasted on a Weak Story and Sandbox GuardrailsRockstar definitely nailed the technical side of things here. The open world is massive, detailed, and feels genuinely alive. The NPCs are easily the best the studio has ever made—just roaming around and seeing how the city reacts to everything is where the game actually shines.Unfortunately, the game constantly gets in its own way, both in the sandbox and in the campaign, dragging the whole experience right down to a 5. For a franchise literally built on equal-opportunity chaos and freedom, the new restrictions are ridiculous. The game actively blocks you from messing with certain protected classes, makes specific groups and areas completely untouchable, and even stops you from stealing certain cars—like your neighbors' vehicles—just slapping you with a blunt refusal. Being told you can't steal a car in Grand Theft Auto pretty much sums up how sanitized this **** main core of the game—the story and the characters—is even worse. The sharp, classic GTA humor is completely missing. None of the characters are funny, the dialogue falls flat, and the writing feels way too safe and lifeless for a series that used to be known for its edge.Lucia is honestly trash as a protagonist—annoying, poorly written, and impossible to actually root for. On top of that, the central plot is just lame and plays out like a cuck simulator, turning what should have been a gritty crime story into a frustrating, watered-down dynamic that completely kills the ****’s a massive shame to see such a great world and top-tier NPCs bogged down by an unfunny cast, a weak campaign, and artificial guardrails that ruin the core GTA sandbox. Great tech, terrible story, and way too restricted.

author: SpencerWilliams
quote: Grand Theft Auto VI is a marvel in graphical fidelity. It's easily the most gorgeous and detailed game I've seen, but where the game excels in side activities, world design, intricacies and life simulation, it fails in being a fun video game. Monotonous mission structure, severe restrictions compared to past games, a sub-30fps framerate-even on PS5 Pro, severe glitches that can disrupt normal gameplay, no physical edition, a bloated file size and a steep $80 asking price, makes this game more of a chore than a triumph. After the absolute masterclass that was Red Dead Redemption II and the chaotic slapstick hilarity of GTA V, it makes this game's shortcoming all the more noticeable. Rockstar still has a solid foundation on open world games design and structure, present since GTA III, so the core game is still there, but for a thirteen-year wait as well as being the most anticipated video game/media in human history, GTA VI had to walk on water in order to deliver. Instead, it's drowning.

author: Meliodaa
quote: Something I've increasingly noticed in modern games is this obsession with realism and everyday activities. And honestly, I'm getting tired of it. I want to drive around, explore, cause chaos and forget about everyday responsibilities.Instead, apparently, I get another list of chores. Fix this, take care of that, run another errand. At this point, I might as well turn off the console and start doing actual housework. The worst part? These activities aren't even fun. Most of the time, you're just pressing button prompts. It's not even an engaging minigame. It's literally virtual **** yes, the game looks absolutely incredible. Vice City is beautiful, but once you get past the graphics, things start getting frustrating. The controls and movement feel surprisingly clunky compared to GTA V. Driving, moving around and performing simple interactions often feel less smooth and responsive than they should. How does a game released 13 years later sometimes feel worse to actually play?The story is another disappointment. It feels like a step backwards in some ways, with too many mundane activities and filler moments taking away from the excitement. GTA V knew how to get you into the action while keeping things entertaining. And speaking of GTA V, remember Michael, Franklin and Trevor? Three completely different personalities, each with their own motivations, problems and memorable moments. Trevor alone had more personality and unpredictability than Lucia brings to the table for me. I understand that Rockstar wanted to make everything more realistic and immersive, but somewhere along the way, I feel they forgot something important: games are supposed to be fun. And yes it is incredible technical achievement, but a disappointing gaming experience.
