author: Ichiban-san
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI Review: The Façade of the ‘Perfect Game’

Let’s.start with the positive aspect of GTA VI namely the graphical quality (technical fidelity) and the graphical style (art direction).Both are a 10/10 to the extent that you will crash your car into things because you are too focused on the skyline, water, and many other amazing things. GTA VI will for this reason alone be remembered as the next level in the GTA series. However, we should not forget that Red Dead Redemption 2 (2018) was not far off. This brings me to the question if this is really a major graphical improvement from 2018. But maybe we will only see the real difference once it will come out on PC so let’s wait for that. However IF GTA VI  will still not look much better on a high end PC when compared to Red Dead Redemption 2 then it will be difficult to justify a 13 year wait from the last GTA game. 

You might be thinking: “What about the capped FPS (30)?”. Well, to be honest I don’t think this game was made for this generation of consoles, especially not the Xbox series S. Maybe it would have been better to wait for the Playstation 6 (2028-2030 ???) and to release the game with improved hardware of the PS6. This way you could exclude the extra development time (optimization) for the Xbox series S by simply excluding it. However, the counter argument would be that you can't keep the fanbase waiting and waiting for approximately 15-17 years. But to be honest during a longer waiting period they could have continued with GTA V Online and improved the storylines. In my opinion it’s all about communication and providing a good alternative (GTA V Online).Anyway, let’s now focus on the bad. 

Firstly, the storyline is so boring that I can’t justify spending time on the main campaign/storyline. When I play a game I want to be pulled into that world. If that world makes me do errands then I seriously start to question what ‘gaming’ even means at this point. On top of that it is un-Rockstar Games like, but we have to keep in mind that most of us are still thinking about the old Rockstar Games culture which changed between 2018 and 2022. This game feels like a life simulator whose foundations are built on the old GTA games. Who wants to think about fuel usage when you just stole a car? Who cares about the engine status? I want to see proper AND consistent damage mechanics that might sling me out of the vehicle when I crash. Why is there even an option to lower vehicle damage?

Secondly, Jason’s voice is so annoying that I barely can stand scenes where he is involved.  On top of that his entire character looks boring and depressed to the point that I would favor Lucia as the only protagonist. But this would be a problem as the vast majority of players are straight men that want to play as a charismatic male character. It should have been understood by the writers that you need a likeable and interesting protagonist otherwise people are not invested. A brain dead protagonist will not create an emotional attachment to that character.

Thirdly, the limitations put on the gameplay like who you can shoot or hurt,  and what limitations there are regarding flying an airplane into a building (with realistic physics and graphics) is absurd. This is not what GTA stood for, but again this is part of the internal change of the company. I really hope that they won’t restrict GTA VI Online even more but probably they will push certain story lines and narratives.

Fourthly, I have an issue with the fighting mechanics and visual representation. GTA V was really nice given the year (2013). But for some reason GTA VI  fighting looks  more like mortal kombat (1992). Don’t get me wrong, it says a lot about the quality of mortal kombat (1992) but I would rather see  mechanics something closer to GTA V.  

Overall, there are some very nice and interesting scenes/moments in the game but not enough to create an interesting storyline. The fact that the entire gaming industry rated this game as 100/100 is worthy of a serious discussion. We all need a platform that is truly independent and that represents gamers and voices their opinions. 

Realistically it looks like Rockstar Games will not go back to the old days which creates more opportunities for other game studios. I would give this game a 5/10 and for me it feels like a huge disappointment. Additionally, I think that there should be serious questions about the 13 years of development and the people that were working on it claim of; individually created NPC’s seem to be false or at least extremely misleading. The only hope that in theory could redeem this release is an optimized PC version with great Online stories and characters. And maybe that is what they want because there is a lot of money to be made with the Online version. Maybe, just maybe the main single player campaign is just a filler until we get GTA VI Online. 5/10

author: svabomat
quote:
The only reason I’m giving this game a 4 is that Rockstar did a genuinely great job with the map and the city itself. Vice City looks good. After 13 years, though, I expected it to take my breath away. I can live with the limits of the PlayStation hardware when it comes to frame rate. What surprised me was getting out into the countryside and thinking Red Dead Redemption 2 actually looked better out there.

I have no issue with a female protagonist in GTA. Lucia could have had her own corner of Vice City, her own contacts and her own reasons for getting into trouble. That’s what I liked about switching characters in GTA V. When I switched from Michael to Trevor, I felt like I was dropping in on somebody else’s life. I wanted that for Lucia and Jason. Hell, make them both a little older. Give them a 15-year-old son called Thomas and let us piece together what happened between them while we play two separate criminal careers. Have their paths cross again near the end. By then, I might actually give a damn whether they get back together.

Instead, I’m watching them cuddle and keeping an eye on my relationship status. Apparently, I can handle the police, but a lap dance in a Vice City strip club is where I need to think about my future. Thirteen years I waited for Grand Theft Auto, and somehow I’m playing Girlfriend Simulator. A love story this central to GTA feels about as natural as a zombie outbreak in Farming Simulator.

What bothers me even more is the freedom I’ve lost. There’s a world of difference between “you can’t steal that car” and “you really shouldn’t have stolen that car.” The second one is how half my best GTA stories started. Maybe the owner dragged me back out. Maybe a cop saw me, I panicked, clipped a taxi and turned a five-second decision into a ten-minute chase. Now I’m standing in my own neighborhood wondering why the game won’t let me take the damn car. Needing a key for a high-end sports car could make for a great theft mission. Putting hurdles in front of an ordinary car and then charging me a fortune to keep it? At those prices, the guy who got robbed was me.

The same inconsistency shows up with pedestrians. I can drive straight through a packed beach and the game lets the chaos play out, yet certain NPCs seem to be off-limits. Why should the rules change depending on whether someone is gay, straight, at a protest or sunbathing? Give me one set of rules across the city. If I do something reckless, send the cops. I always liked finding out how much trouble one bad decision could get me into.

And then there’s Jason. 
Tommy Vercetti had that Tony Montana ambition. CJ had Grove Street, his brother and a whole neighborhood pulling him back in. Niko balkan mentality got tangled up with the mob. Michael had a bit of Tony Soprano in him, Franklin saw crime as his way up, and Trevor was the guy who made an already terrible plan considerably worse. I can tell you who each of them was and what made him dangerous. Ask me about Jason and the first thing that comes to mind is that he’s Lucia’s boyfriend/lapdog. 

That’s a pretty thin legacy for the lead in a GTA **** Rockstar changes one thing in an update, let these two lead separate lives in free roam. Give them their own jobs, let me switch between them, and leave the relationship meter out of my night in Vice City. I want to start as a small-time crook, work my way up to heists and gang wars,build drug businesses ,buy property and muscle and occasionally lose an entire evening because I stole the wrong car on the way home. 

Rockstar gave me a beautiful city.
 What I miss is the freedom to make a complete mess of it.

author: norcalrowland
quote:
There seems to be a lot of cope and crying going on in the user reviews of this game in an attempt to justify the 13 year wait, and $70-$100 spent. More if you spent money on the garbage PS5 just for this game.

There's even weirdos review bombing other games (Like Zelda, Oot, which for weeks had a much higher user review score, and still is yet to drop below a 9 despite thousands of zero ratings being dropped in a day or two (not a coincidence) after this games user reviews utterly tanked (GTA 6 is 5.4 and dropping ).

*Spoiler free review of GTA 6*

Played it, seen it, enjoyed it a little even.

It's a improvement in a lot of ways to GTA V, but it's not a complete improvement. That being said after 13 years, hundreds of millions of dollars spent, the only people who are giving it perfect scores are the money gobbling reviewers gargling the coins they get for shilling out.

 Beyond that it's brain dead fans giving it a 10 with hardly any reasoning "best game I ever played!!" Or the other side of the fan coin being "worst game ever, you're a cuck and have to do chores and be nice to a girl".

There's infighting in its own community, it's not just random people review bombing this game exclusively, there are thousands that just find this game bad. That's okay, but I would say it's far from bad. The game isn't perfect. There are flat story beats, a mid story lul, lack of branching paths to handle certain missions, lots of actually on rail missions where nothing matters other than the interactive cutscenes playing out. If you don't press some on screen button prompts in a QTE, it'll do it for it, wolverine the game style. Truly a game of all time.

The gameplay is tighter, the driving is better, the gunplay has more impact and weight, and the details and realism are better than ever. However this game fails to deliver the full package. Forever locked at 30 fps, (something the world hung, waterboarded, flogged, burned and killed Cyberpunk for btw) is pathetic. It regularly chugs around 18-24 fps, that alone stops this game from being anywhere near a 10. No online after nearly 15 years , which will 100% cost money to activate, and potentially may even have a monthly fee as a part of the plan to profitmaxx this game. Maybe even some live service coming your way.

The weakest part of GTA 6 has to be Jason for me. Arthur Morgan lite really irked me throughout the game. It's his inability to become a fleshed out, memorable, charming, or even funny character that stand out the most. He gets completely outshined as a character by Lucia, who is written and voice acted way better than Jason. Side characters often completely outshine Jason as well. He looks and sounds too much like Arthur, as if it was by intention. But it comes across strange and like he's a simple and stiff dude just phoning it in.

No one can ever convince me that Franklin, Trevor, and Micheal aren't infinitely more entertaining and better characters than Jason and even Lucia. It's a step backwards in that respect, big time. Niko of GTA 4 makes these two characters look like goofy saints row avatars by comparison. Arthur Morgan himself? This game has been toated as a spiritual sequel to RDR2 Because of how it's made, but sadly it really can never compare. Arthur, his story, his portrayal, makes the best character moments in GTA 6 seem average to poor at best. 

This game isn't a 10/10.

I wouldn't call myself a huge GTA fan, but I've been playing every entry in the series since I was a kid. GTA has always been a solid AAA title worth checking out. But what the developers have come up with this time...

I don't even want to get into the fact that the game has once again launched on consoles first. That means we're stuck with downgraded graphics, 30 FPS, shooting with a gamepad, and all the other horrors of gaming on PS and Xbox. I'm so tired of this that I don't even have the energy to complain about it anymore.

I don't want to dwell on the story either. GTA has always had an awful, tedious, and boring story. It was basically just background noise while you explored the world, along with an excuse to make money, get weapons, and unlock everything the game had to offer. These have always been flaws in the series, and nothing has changed. Do I even need to mention that Rockstar is absolutely terrible at designing side quests?

BUT WHAT HAVE YOU DONE TO THE GAMEPLAY AND THE CHARACTERS? GTA has now turned into a relationship and everyday life simulator starring an annoying, pretentious, unattractive chick with a ladyboy face and a pathetic musclehead with absolutely zero charisma.There's barely any fun to be had in this game anymore: no prostitutes, and you can't just kill whoever you want (yes, I'm talking about woke ideology and protecting all kinds of activists).

The game has kept all the flaws of its predecessors while destroying everything people loved about the series. This is the biggest failure of the decade, no matter how many paid-off critics hand out 99/100 reviews. An absolute disgrace for this company.

The only people who deserve any credit are the game designers. The world is genuinely huge and well-crafted. That's the only reason I managed to give this game a 3.

I found the dialogue boring, Jason's voice and character unappealing, and the writing often feels more targeted towards a female audience than traditional GTA fans. The 30 FPS experience was frustrating, the glitches were far too frequent, and the game felt unnecessarily explicit, making it difficult to enjoy with my family. author: BierbaronMW
quote:
GTA VI – A Sims Game Disguised as Grand Theft Auto

What a massive disappointment. GTA VI is technically stunning. The graphics, the world and the attention to detail are incredible. But gameplay-wise, this is nowhere near what I expect from a Grand Theft Auto game.

I bought GTA because I want crime, chaos, robberies, shootouts, explosions, car chases, dark humour and Rockstar's usual outrageous satire. Instead, I get fishing, jet skis, furniture assembly, painting walls and endless domestic drama. Seriously? I don't want to renovate a house or build furniture just to keep Lucia happy.

And Lucia is probably my biggest problem. I find her incredibly annoying. She constantly nags Jason, talks down to him and makes their relationship feel like an obligation. Why can't I decide how my character lives his life? Maybe I don't want a relationship at all.

The whole game feels more like The Sims in an open-world setting than a proper GTA. It also seems to be aimed at a very different audience than the one that made this franchise so popular. The dark, cynical humour and outrageous satire of GTA V and the older games are largely missing. GTA VI feels surprisingly tame and lacks the rebellious spirit of its predecessors.

Yes, there are more action-packed missions later on, but they don't make up for all the tedious everyday activities and relationship drama.

My verdict: A technical masterpiece, but an enormous disappointment as a GTA game. Beautiful graphics cannot compensate for boring gameplay, unlikeable characters and a forced relationship storyline.

I wanted to play Grand Theft Auto, not The Sims with a gangster skin. I absolutely hate this game.

30 fps sluggishness and a one-sided dynamic kill the momentum> 
Behind the hype and massive map, actually playing GTA 6 feels heavy and underwhelming. Locking a flagship release at 30 fps—with drops during busy action—makes moment-to-moment movement and combat feel sluggish, while the core gunplay, controls, and scripted mission structure still feel stiff and dated after the slow opening stretches wear off. On top of that, Jason’s dynamic with Lucia is a major letdown: instead of two equal partners pushing each other, Jason spends way too much of the story just obeying Lucia’s lead like he was written by a woman to defer to her at every turn. Between the frame rate, dated feel, and one-sided dynamic, it never clicks.>

author: charankowlas
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI is a breathtaking technical showcase trapped inside a sanitized, heavily scripted playable movie that forgets what made Grand Theft Auto fun in the first place.

THE GOOD:
Leonida and Vice City look extraordinary, backed by a complex, hyper-reactive NPC network and dense environmental detail that set a new visual bar for open-world games. Voice acting, motion capture, and cinematic presentation are top-tier if you treat the game purely as something to watch.

THE BAD:
1. Unlikable, Flat Protagonists: Lucia comes across as self-destructive and frustrating, constantly creating her own problems while expecting sympathy. Meanwhile, Jason has virtually no backstory or backbone, functioning more like a passive sidekick tagging along for her mess than an equal co-lead.
2. Tonal Whiplash in the Writing: Serious crime stakes repeatedly collapse into goofy sitcom logic where hardened street gangs turn into cartoonish punchlines, completely undercutting the street-level tension.
3. On-Rails, Low-Stakes Missions: Creative problem-solving is dead. Stepping slightly off the developer's intended path triggers an instant fail, while checkpoints every couple of minutes, auto-aim, and slow-motion abilities strip away any real danger or tension.
4. Selective Censorship and Guardrails: Instead of equal-opportunity sandbox chaos, the game disables weapons and forces vehicles to brake around specific protected NPC groups and areas, undercutting the core freedom the franchise was built on.

VERDICT:If you want a gorgeous virtual Florida to drive around in, GTA VI delivers. As an actual Grand Theft Auto game with sharp underworld storytelling, protagonists worth rooting for, and true sandbox freedom, it is a massive step backward.

author: thibault123

Grand Theft Auto VI, is not a Grand Theft Auto game. It was marketed as one, promoted as one, sold as one, and it isn't. The story is not a GTA storyline, the gameplay is heavily restricted unlike prior GTA games, it's just not a GTA game.

So why was it sold under the guise of being one?

Very disappointing and duplicitous from Rockstar.

If this was marketed as a new game, new franchise, and they were open about what the story entailed, I wouldn't have bought it, but I would have been fine with the storyline existing. it's not the story per se I disagree with as people have the freedom to make whatever games they want. But this isn't a GTA game and they weren't open about that. It leaves you wondering why.

If they were so proud of this modern take, why not promote it as that? They wanted the sales from the fans who they knew would dislike this new twist, and they weren't honest with them about it.

The game itself (besides the story), is also stale, buggy, bland open world. It's like driving through a sandbox without things to do. Side characters having dialogue does not replace emptiness, it merely exists within it as vital signs in-between the long stretches of silence in the medical bay. It's essentially a AAA on sale for 20 dollars steam simulator game that a twitch streamer would play for 4 hours of clipped up YouTube content.

It's not GTA. They knew it and were dishonest with the fans about it. It's a shame. More honesty about what the game was going to be would have combatted a lot of the negativity towards the game. But they lied, and we know why, and that's why we're angry. You can't complain about backlash when you are responsible for the reason it exists.

The crowning achievement of the game is that it isn't in fact, a GTA game. Some achievement that is. Congratulations.

Where is the dopamine hot of completing a cool mission and seeing the cool ‘mission complete’ screens with added music etc…It was clear in previous GTA games that the team understood that they’re ripping into outrageous parts of society in a satirical way to please a vast majority of people, and ironically it was this humour that in fact highlighted the things they were ripping into even more, the releases would be really controversial and result in silly IRL news stories about GTA being responsible for psychopaths and serial killers, which was blatantly false and a political agenda against the contents of the game; people understood this and loved them for it. With GTA 6, instead of using humour reflective of the current state of the world, this game feels like it was made to please 35-40 year old women. To my mind this group are likely not making up a majority of the target audience for a grand theft auto game. Therefore, I don’t understand why they ever thought this story was a good idea?Jason feels dry, like an empty shell of a man, happy to exist as his girlfriend’s slave. Clearly this is the intention as the first several hours are spent doing boring tasks to please Lucia. The voice acting is horrific as well. I want a refund and will never buy a rockstar game without a disc again. The above makes me think that they knew about the poor story, performance issues a long time ago, and decided they’re going to cash in their chips with this release by removing the option to resell. I think they knew that people wouldn’t have wanted to keep hold of that disc for more than a couple of weeks.

GTA 6 is a complete pile of ****.

GTA used to be about freedom, crime, dark humor, unforgettable characters, and fearless satire. It was rebellious, politically incorrect, and unapologetically offensive. That was exactly what made it special.

This is not the Grand Theft Auto I grew up loving. Rockstar has lost its edge, and GTA 6 has lost the soul of the franchise.

author: JayJay2182
quote: I feel bamboozled slightly.  The presales, financial numbers, and critics ratings will reflect a resounding success. However, for me, the game is a tiger that has lost its teeth as well as identity. The visuals, water, lighting, traffic, and overall aesthetics are beautiful but the core and soul of what made GTA what it is, is missing if not heavily muted. What truly made GTA what it is, was the ability to to do whatever you wanted. I don't care specifically that they removed prostitutes, but more so that removing that fundamentally changes the DNA of what this game is. Further, not being able to steal cars or pull my weapons out in my neighborhood makes no real sense to me. Why?  What is even worse is this underlying empathy or morality system which forcefully reminds me every time I do some type crime, shooting, murder that I could get a psycho rating and to refrain or do some good things to offset. This is not a therapy session. I don't want that. Further, if I am alone in a swamp area and some hillbilly fights me and I  take him out, why am I getting a devil emoji to indicate my descent toward psycho level? There are no witnesses and he attacked me. What is this??? The voice actor for Jason is so monotoned and low emotion. I don't want to use the term "woke" just to use it and I know that will irritate some people. However, there is something to be said when you can clearly see the influences and undertones of story and narratives. The fact that you cant cheat or make ADULT decisions like all people do in relationships again is ridiculous. I can kill people, rob, kill police, but I can't flirt or do what I want. Its disingenuous. Can I find enjoyment in the game? Yes. Are there some really cool moments and visuals? Of course. But overall, this almost feels like a game cosplaying as GTA and while it comes very close, something just feels off. If I was offered to refund right now I most likely would. Sad to say that.

author: GuruGamer46
quote:
The game has the foundations for greatness. The map is surreal and utterly beautiful. The level of detail is genuinely unparalleled and I've never seen another game even come close.

However, the physics of the game are truly horrifying. The driving is nothing at all like what rockstar have been marketing, a mix in-between gran theft auto 4 and 5.  There are elements of 5, such as the faster cars handling like they are glued to the road, and elements of 4, such as needing to press that other pedal, I think it's called 'the brake' or something along those lines. However neither of those things actually give any feeling that the driving is between 4 and 5. 

The physics are (honestly) terrible, in the way that you have no initiative connection to the cars in any sense. They handle inconsistently, one second an input barely registered, a second later that same input sends the car veering across 3 lanes of traffic. One second you hit the gas and your wheels are spinning (even this is just executed horribly), the next, same speed, same scenario, same input, no spin. 

You want to just cruise around slowly? This is where the driving is in its element, proving that you only drive in a straight line, because the second you try to take a slow corner, smoothly, the game registers that you would like to turn the steering wheel 450° and do a full U-turn.


I have seen many people being criticised as having no skill, but in my defence I have a lot of top 50 times world wide in racing Sims, and even in Forza Motorsport. I have a genuinely decent understanding of car handling and physics, and can truly say, GTA 6 is possibly the worst I've ever experienced bar the NFS games, which it is not far from.

Overall this completely ruins a game that is primarily focused on stealing cars and driving them.


It is a genuine shame, because the car models, world, roads and map are just begging to be enjoyed, however implementing such an awful driving experience is almost just cruel.

Rockstar, please fire whoever is incharge of the vehicle handling and whoever approved this god awful driving model.

I’ve had trucks fall into the ground, Jason fall through the map, heavy frame rate drops, npcs phasing through each other, for $80 minimum it’s inexcusable. If you HAVE to dry wall the house or HAVE to get cookies - it's not an act of love or respect. It's subservience. It's a chore, it has no emotional meaning.
The freedom to act has been reduced a little from GTA 5 and A LOT from RDR2. SO much of the game is scripted. It might just hold on to the idea of "open world" - but that's debatable. 
I'm not sure how this is going to transition to online in a few months. I suspect they will either totally ignore the cuck stuff / misandry for online - or go at it REAL hard. If that happens (and I wouldn't give it more than 25% chance it will - but it might) won't be heists, there will be "man chores".
Then the bugs. Dear lord the bugs. After 90 minute you do your first real shoot out and I got trapped crouching behind a car. Could not stand - just shuffled around. Then 30 minutes later the guy I was talking to just vanished and the game wouldn't let me continue with the story. I had to restart the game and luckily he was back. Basic vehicle physics is pretty good, but as soon as you try anything crazy there is a high chance of buggy nonsense. Clipping through buildings, suddenly being upside down. 
I've lost count of the number of bugs. 2 or 3 game breaking - but lots of immersion breaking nonsense. This game needed another year in the cooker. I'll finish it because it cost so much, but I'll be MUCH more wary of GTA 7 if they ever make that in my lifetime. Clearly the story is written by people who just do not like men. author: Lesterthemol
quote:
After more than a decade of waiting, I expected GTA 6 to take everything that made previous games brilliant and deliver something even bigger, bolder and better. Unfortunately, from what has been revealed so far, I have some serious concerns about the direction Rockstar appears to be **** biggest concerns are:- Too much relationship focus: The emphasis on Jason and Lucia's relationship, domestic activities and everyday errands risks making GTA feel more like a relationship simulator than the criminal sandbox game we've come to expect.- Jason's character: Compared with Trevor, Michael, Franklin and Niko, Jason doesn't immediately appear to have the same distinctive personality or charisma. I want memorable, unpredictable characters, not protagonists who feel like they're simply there to support a relationship storyline.- The portrayal of white men: I get the impression that traditional white male characters and masculine stereotypes are increasingly being used as punchlines. I have absolutely no problem with female protagonists or greater diversity, but I don't want to see one particular demographic repeatedly portrayed negatively while others are treated more sympathetically.

Everyone should be fair game in GTA.- Political correctness and woke culture: GTA built its reputation on mocking absolutely everyone. Politicians, celebrities, corporations, the rich, the poor, conservatives, liberals and every aspect of society were fair targets. My concern is that Rockstar's satire could become more selective, with certain political and cultural viewpoints receiving considerably more criticism than others.

Corporate influence: I also question the growing influence of major institutional investors in the entertainment industry. Companies such as BlackRock have significant investment interests across major businesses. While that doesn't mean they control Rockstar's creative decisions, I believe developers should retain complete creative independence rather than feel pressured by corporate or political expectations.

Too many restrictions: One of the biggest attractions of GTA has always been freedom. The ability to explore, experiment, cause chaos and create ridiculous situations is what separates the franchise from ordinary open-world games. I don't want unnecessary restrictions taking away that experience.What I want Rockstar to rememberI don't want GTA to become sanitised, overly cautious or obsessed with delivering a particular social or political message. I'm not asking for the series to remain stuck in 2013, and I fully expect it to evolve. But evolution shouldn't mean losing its identity.I want the dark humour, outrageous missions, memorable characters, controversial satire and complete freedom that made GTA V, GTA IV and the earlier games so entertaining.
Most importantly, I want Rockstar to update and loosen the restrictions that risk making GTA 6 feel less like a true Grand Theft Auto experience. Give players more freedom to interact with the world, more opportunities to create their own chaos, fewer unnecessary limitations and the ability to play without constantly feeling that the experience is being controlled or restricted.

My final verdict: GTA 6 has enormous potential, but impressive graphics and a massive map aren't enough. It needs great characters, genuinely entertaining gameplay, balanced satire and, above all, freedom.

Rockstar built its reputation by breaking rules, challenging conventions and making fun of everybody. I want that Rockstar **** should be about freedom, chaos and entertainment, not restrictions, political point-scoring or playing it safe. 

Make it feel like GTA again remove restrictions make everyone fair game. The sooner the pc release comes the better as I feel mods will fix this game before Rockstar does.

author: thechecker111
quote:
GTA VI is feminist woke slop disguised as a crime simulator.

GTA used to be funny, outrageous, and unapologetically criminal. Now it's a tedious 9-to-5 chore simulator with a mandatory simping dating sim attached.

Jason is a soulless golem whose entire existence revolves around pleasing Lucia, one of the most unlikeable characters Rockstar has ever written. She's stupid, manipulative, irresponsible, and constantly flirts with other men.

She ghosted Jason, secretly gave birth to his child, then left the baby unattended in a café while robbing a store, which landed her in prison. And now Jason is expected to do absolutely everything for her.

Fix her roof, repair her stairs, paint her bedroom, buy her clothes and jewelry, get groceries, fix her car, pick her up from community service, defend her to her probation officer, meditate and do yoga with her, shop for a baby crib, assemble IKEA furniture, watch TV together, and massage her feet. And what exactly does Jason get in return? Practically nothing.

The most absurd moment was when I had to meet Lucia's pregnant friend outside prison and PRESS R2 TO FEEL HER BABY BUMP. IN A GTA GAME!

Meanwhile, the series' traditional male fantasies have been stripped away. Having multiple girlfriends or visiting prostitutes, features that existed in previous GTA games, are gone. Jason is forced into a monogamous relationship with Lucia, although apparently that expectation only applies to him. Lucia constantly flirts with other men, and the game even hints at infidelity.

And the endless chores! You have to refuel your car, drink protein shakes, work out regularly or lose muscle mass, feed your pet snake, maintain your house and vehicle, pick Lucia up from work, and keep contributing to your child's savings account.

I think the only thing Rockstar forgot was making us file our tax returns.

Countless new mechanics are being praised by professional critics as "immersive," when most of them simply make the game more tedious.

Rockstar also copied heavily from Red Dead Redemption 2. You can greet or antagonize NPCs, inspect animals and collect records of inspected species, and perform endless mundane chores. These mechanics made sense in a cowboy game set in the 19th century. In a game set in 2026, they're just digital repetitions of the boring responsibilities I already have in real life.

Even the morality system feels imported from RDR2. Kill too many NPCs and you get bad karma. Spare them and receive good-boy points. What a bizarre design decision for a franchise that's fundamentally supposed to be a crime simulator.

I remember GTA: San Andreas, where causing destruction and behaving like a dangerous gangster could increase your status and respect. Now the opposite is true.

The police are another problem. Practically every illegal action immediately attracts law enforcement. Getting arrested can cost you your mission progress and rewards, so you think twice before running over an NPC on your way home. Instead, you obediently drive back, follow the rules, and avoid causing trouble.

It's like buying a racing game that tells you racing is illegal and makes you wash cars instead.

And almost nobody among the professional critics seems interested in discussing what the game has taken away from the series.

GTA VI has turned a crime sandbox into a tedious 9-to-5 chore simulator with mandatory simping.

author: John7572
quote:
I want to be clear: if this were a debut installment in an entirely new franchise, I'd give it a 10/10. Well, maybe an 8 or 9; I genuinely don't like some of the writing and some of the voice acting. 

This isn't a debut game, however. It's an established franchise. 

The biggest departure, in my estimation, is the transition from wholesale caricature to grounded character drama. That's what I miss. The parody of it all. And don't get me wrong, there's some of that, but crucially, it has been completely turned away from the protagonists and aimed outward. 

Why does that matter?

People forget, but that was actually the narrative formula of the franchise running up until GTA V: a cold killer reacting to a ludicrous world and even wackier NPCs. 
But those games always had a problem. 
There was a constant friction between a serious protagonist and a sandbox that was so utterly cartoonish and unhinged that the lead felt out of place. 

GTA V came in with the antidote. 
Make the playable characters just as ridiculous as the world they live in. And it was a masterpiece. I mean, true spectacle. 
Finally, your indiscriminate murder sprees and carte blanche criminal enterprise made sense, because the characters you played as were literal nut jobs, each in their own way, not anti-heroes with tangible stakes. 

Where Rockstar went wrong was assuming that because their fans enjoyed the earnest melodrama from RDR2, the audience had somehow "matured" and moved past what made GTA V a generational piece of entertainment. 

One little problem. This is GTA, not Red Dead. 

I loved Red Dead Redemption when it came out. Had Undead Nightmare and everything. And RDR2, don't get me started. Masterpiece. The thing is, those games were built first and foremost as revisionist Westerns with tragic comedy. True dramas. 

That's not the DNA of GTA, which, from the very beginning, was about excess. GTA V was the ultimate realisation of that original architecture. 

As a technical achievement and a standalone crime game, it’s an 8 or 9 out of 10. As a Grand Theft Auto game, measured against the DNA it abandoned, it’s a 0/10.

author: Lima0007
quote:
**Uma experiência decepcionante que não justifica o preço cobrado.**

Minha avaliação de GTA VI é bastante negativa. O jogo apresenta problemas que comprometem significativamente a experiência e tornam difícil justificar seu custo.

- **Romance forçado:** situações românticas que parecem artificiais e desnecessárias, prejudicando a naturalidade da narrativa.
- **Bugs e problemas técnicos:** falhas que atrapalham a experiência e demonstram falta de polimento.
- **Jogabilidade horrível:** mecânicas pouco satisfatórias, controles frustrantes e uma experiência que deixa muito a desejar.
- **Preço injustificável:** pelo valor cobrado, o jogo deveria entregar uma experiência muito mais refinada, estável e divertida.

GTA VI decepciona em aspectos fundamentais. Um jogo não pode depender apenas do peso de sua franquia e de seu nome para justificar um preço elevado. O consumidor paga por qualidade, diversão e uma experiência bem executada, não apenas pela expectativa criada em torno de um lançamento.

**Não recomendo a compra pelo preço atual. Melhor esperar uma grande promoção ou até que os problemas sejam corrigidos.**

author: Unlock2020
quote: ¿En serio? ¿Trece años después de uno de los mejores videojuegos de la historia, esto es lo que nos ofrece Rockstar?Y no solo eso: después de anunciar una fecha de lanzamiento inicial y retrasarla, ¿este es el resultado final? Sinceramente, me parece una vergüenza y una de las mayores cagadas que ha cometido **** millones que ha generado GTA VI incluso antes de su lanzamiento no demuestran necesariamente la calidad del juego. El 95 % de los compradores conocíamos GTA V, sabíamos lo que había significado y esperábamos una evolución de aquello: lo mismo, pero mejor. No se han vendido millones de copias porque la gente supiera cómo era GTA VI, porque nadie lo había probado. Se han vendido porque detrás había una franquicia con un prestigio enorme y millones de jugadores que confiábamos en Rockstar.Pero muchos de los que hemos comprado el juego queríamos jugar a GTA, no a una mezcla de película interactiva, Los Sims y Red Dead Redemption. Cada videojuego tiene su propia identidad y no tiene por qué incorporar elementos de otros títulos simplemente porque hayan tenido éxito durante los últimos años. Queríamos GTA, no un experimento de Rockstar intentando convertirlo en algo que no **** más preocupante es el desarrollo de la historia. Llevar un 30-40 % del juego y haber realizado apenas dos misiones que valgan la pena me parece penoso. Han rellenado el juego de actividades, situaciones y mecánicas que, en lugar de enriquecer la experiencia, terminan haciéndola pesada y artificial.¿Dónde está la esencia de GTA? No matas, no disparas, no ejecutas acciones que antes formaban parte de la experiencia. En muchísimas situaciones, los propios personajes hacen prácticamente todo por ti. Parece que estás viendo cómo juegan otros en lugar de estar jugando tú. A eso se suman fallos, bugs, personajes que levitan y situaciones que rompen completamente la inmersión.Y, sinceramente, no quiero ni imaginar cómo será cuando llegue al final del juego si esta es la dinámica que mantiene hasta ahora.Rockstar parece haber confundido innovación con cambiar la identidad de una franquicia. Innovar no significa añadir mecánicas por añadirlas, ni convertir un videojuego en una película interminable. Significa mejorar aquello que ya funcionaba sin perder su esencia.Y una última cosa: el éxito comercial de GTA VI no debe confundirse con el éxito del videojuego. Que venda millones de copias no significa que esté a la altura de las expectativas ni que haya cumplido con lo que esperaban sus jugadores.Analicemos el juego por lo que ofrece, por su jugabilidad, sus misiones, su libertad y la experiencia que proporciona, no por el nombre que lleva en la portada ni por los millones que genera.Después de trece años esperando, lo mínimo que esperábamos era un GTA a la altura de GTA. Y esa es precisamente la decepción.

author: karenpagac334
quote: After 18 hours of GTA 6, I’ve decided to write this here **** technical performance on the standard PS5 is very poor. The game runs at a maximum of 30 FPS, suffers from frequent frame-rate drops, and has noticeably input delay. As a result, the controls feel imprecise and unreliable.There are also numerous bugs and glitches: vehicles suddenly disappear, textures load slowly, and objects visibly pop into view. NPCs, vehicles and animals occasionally get stuck in strange places or appear to float through the air. The AI can also seem rather unintelligent and behave strange.Overall, the game feels unfinished. In my opinion, it should not have been released in this state and just on **** current generations of consoles don't have enough processing power to play this game at 60 FPS minimum.  As a paying customer, I shouldn’t have to put up with such serious problems—it’s **** gameplay feels repetitive and is rarely much fun. Many tasks are unnecessarily drawn out, with lengthy cutscenes slowing things down even further. Exciting moments, such as shootouts or car chases, are unfortunately few and far between. Instead, you spend a lot of time on boring side activities, such as painting a wall or unclogging a **** missions are often predictable, too. It’s frequently obvious that something is about to go wrong because the NPC does something reckless or stupid. The wanted system and the game’s excessive focus on realism in certain areas also do little to improve the experience and often feel more irritating than engaging.Interactions with NPCs are often unpleasant as well: even when you greet someone politely, they frequently respond with hostility or tell you to leave them alone what is the point of interacting with the NPCs when they don't have any interest in you. Many NPCs also repeat the same animations and reactions. The world often seems empty and more like a set piece than a believable world—especially when you look beyond the **** game also gives you very little freedom in how you approach missions, as their progression is largely predetermined. There are three different currency systems, and vehicles come with frustrating restrictions: you can’t simply steal a car; some have to be unlocked first, while others can’t be stolen at all.Overall, I find the direction the gameplay has taken disappointing, especially compared with earlier entries such as GTA IV and GTA: San **** characters also feel bland and uninteresting. They lack distinctive personalities and charisma. Some character types—in particular, the redneck characters—feel like recycled ideas that were already extensively featured through Trevor’s missions in GTA V. The protagonists’ behavior also doesn’t always feel believable. They commit serious crimes but often seem to take the risks involved surprisingly lightly. Lucia, in particular, can come across as unrealistic in some situations. I’m also not convinced by how often she takes the lead in heists: Jason is a former mercenary with relevant experience, while Lucia sometimes seems more like a hindrance than a help. This makes her feel out of place in the criminal world. Overall, the game is a major disappointment for me—technically, in its gameplay, and in its story. There’s very little fun to be had; boredom, frustration, and tedious missions are what remain. The open world is available to explore after the first mission wich is good , but much of it consists of large, repetitive areas—natural landscapes, industrial zones, construction sites, etc— a lot of space with little to see or do. Many buildings can’t be entered, either. The game’s size is another drawback. At around 210 GB, it takes up a huge amount of storage. Since there’s no physical disc and the game has to be downloaded, it could take a very long time to download if you have a slow internet **** impressive graphics and physics are the only aspects that really stand out to me. Beyond that, I find it difficult to say much positive. In my opinion, anyone who waited 13 years for a game in the style of GTA IV or GTA: San Andreas is likely to be disappointed. I can only recommend it for around 20 hours if you want to explore the open world, maybe GTA 6 Online is where the fun begins but the Singleplayer-Story-Mode is just boring. Another issue for me is the game’s very over the top explicit sexual content. The frequent male and female nudity and revealing clothing, specially at the beach is offensive and just not necessary. The game may appeal more to fans of Red Dead Redemption 2's  slow,story driven cinematic gameplay than to players who primarily enjoy fast paced action and satire of former GTA Games or other Rockstar Action Game titles such as Bully and Max Payne. It's a 3/10 just for the Open World to explore and to mess around with the physics engine.

author: zanor
quote:
Waiting over a decade only to get a choppy 30 FPS life sim on the PS5 is a massive letdown.
Instead of the fast paced, chaotic crime sandbox that made the series legendary, Rockstar delivered a slow relationship simulator weighed down by tedious realism. Between babysitting character meters, rigid mission design, and endless mundane chores, the game feels like it actively gets in the way of having actual fun. You spend far more time managing life sim mechanics and sitting through sluggish animations than causing mayhem.
The technical state on PS5 is just as disappointing. Fast driving and shootouts feel unresponsive with constant frame rate drops, and the launch is packed with serious bugs. Players are falling straight through the map in the opening minutes, hitting mission softlocks where cutscenes fail to trigger, and dealing with broken physics where cars launch into the air and NPCs clip through objects. On top of that, frequent CE-108255-1 crash errors, lost save progress, and overheating issues that force the PS5 to shut down make it tough to even play.
Great visuals and a massive map mean nothing when the core gameplay feels like a glitchy chore list running in slow motion. Rockstar lost sight of what made Grand Theft Auto fun in the first place, and it simply does not live up to the hype or the price tag.

author: ZILIAN
quote: I went into GTA6 with pretty high expectations, and honestly, by the end most of that enthusiasm was gone.What bothered me most was how much the freedom shrinks. Take Jason's early-game section: step outside his house and there are cars you can't steal, pedestrians you can't touch. That's a far cry from the GTA I know — an open world where you can do whatever you want. For me, that constant feeling of being hemmed in stings more than any **** mission design didn't win me over either. In the footage, characters clip through each other and hit detection goes haywire, and a lot of scenes lean on QTEs and scripted sequences that leave almost no room to improvise. Melee combat boils down to "mash a few buttons and it's over," and some of the enemies in gunfights are so inaccurate they're not a threat at all. I even saw flying a plane into a building and getting no reaction whatsoever — the physics feel unfinished.What confused me even more was where all the attention went. Jason and Lucia's romance, plus decorating the house, cooking, dates, gift-giving — it takes up way too much space, and the protagonist ends up feeling passive. I don't play GTA to manage a relationship and do chores; it feels like the game is being pushed into being a dating sim / household **** save system didn't do me any favors either. Apparently you can't make multiple manual saves, which means every choice I make is locked in for the ending, with no way to jump back to an earlier point and try something else the way you can in GTA V or Red Dead Redemption 2. If you like experimenting with different choices, that's a real **** seeing the media mostly shower it with praise only made me more skeptical. Given everything I saw, I just can't get behind those scores.

author: sadadaa11231
quote: The characters lack soul, and the story lacks depth. It’s hard to see GTA 6 reaching the heights of GTA **** me, the biggest problems with GTA 6 are its characterization and storytelling. Those matter far more to me than the graphics, the size of the map, or the technical performance.Think back to Michael and Trevor in GTA 5.Michael is an exceptionally complex character. He has money and a family, yet he still can’t leave his old life of crime behind. He’s selfish, vain, and anxious. He wants stability, yet he can’t let go of his desires. He occupies the moral gray area between a clear-cut good guy and a straightforward villain. Those contradictions make him feel real and multidimensional.Trevor is a different kind of character altogether. He’s unhinged, volatile, and cruel, and he often acts in ways most people struggle to understand. At the same time, he has his own loyalties, feelings, and values. His extreme personality goes beyond shock value and is a big part of what makes him **** best part is how sharply Michael and Trevor clash. Their values, their ways of doing things, and their choices in life are worlds apart, yet their shared past keeps them tangled up in each other’s lives. Their scenes together are full of dramatic tension and unforgettable dark humor. That’s what makes great character writing so compelling.What I want from GTA 6 is a real step forward in character writing, with a more complex portrayal of human nature, deeper relationships, and conflicts between characters that genuinely drive the plot. A story that revolves solely around relationships and emotional entanglements can only go so far.There’s room for both affection and conflict between characters. For those relationships to work, they need to be grounded in distinct personalities, believable motivations, and meaningful character growth. Without that foundation, no amount of emotional drama can truly move players.Rockstar has already shown it can create unforgettable characters like Michael and Trevor. Along with more polished visuals and a bigger map, players should expect a major leap forward in GTA 6’s characters and story.Better storytelling takes more than better technology, and a deeper story takes more than a bigger open **** GTA 6 can’t surpass its predecessor in character writing and emotional impact, it’ll be hard to see it as a genuine step forward for the series’ storytelling.After more than a decade of waiting, players want more than a technical showcase. They want a more compelling story.

author: parislover
quote:
To be very honest, it's not a very bad game per se, but it's not a good game. The gameplay is a little bit slow, similar to Red Dead Redemption 2, so I'm not necessarily mad over that, but there's a lack of depth, and everything feels very frivolous, from the dialogues to the scenes that are lasting for way too long. It feels that we are again pushed to certain ideologies, and this is a bit **** because a video game should just be a video game.

Both characters have no depth. Lucia is a manipulating psycho but boring, so it's not even like she's a good joker or something like that; she's just plain boring who lacks accountability, who puts everything on the back of Jason, who seems to be just a good boy who obeys and follows orders. He barely has some dialogues, and whenever he has some dialogue, it's uninteresting. At least Arthur Morgan, though he was the kind of strong silent type, had some depth to it. There was a backstory that made sense or that we could hear about and get interested into.

After almost 20 hours into the game, I don't give a **** about both characters, and I want Lucia gone or Jason to be on his own. The characters are not good for each other. They go from "we cannot commit crimes because we will lose our son" to "let's rob every single place that we know of" in like 10 minutes. There's no transition; it's lazy. The writing is poor. . And overall, what really upsets me with this game is not the fact that they overpromised, but that they don't really respect people who want to play a video game that gives them a lot of freedom and do what they want.

There are many aspects to this game that are completely **** in my opinion.

author: Nahual_Eriol
quote:
Rockstar finally delivered the game progressive activists always wanted: a meticulously crafted simulator of the modern compliant male. GTA 6 isn’t an open-world crime sandbox anymore. It’s an elaborate digital etiquette course where the highest form of gameplay is nodding along, absorbing lectures, and carefully avoiding any action that might upset the correct people.

The most striking design choice is the selective invulnerability. Certain characters and groups are effectively sacred. You can run over civilians, rob stores, and cause chaos in the usual GTA fashion — until the script decides someone is protected. Attempting to treat activists, community organizers, or representatives of approved identity categories the same way you treat everyone else simply doesn’t work the way the series used to allow. The game gently (and not so gently) steers you away. Freedom is conditional. Some lives are more equal than others in Los Santos 2.0.

What remains is a long, expensive exercise in managed rebellion. You get the cars, the guns, the heists, and the satirical veneer, but the satire now mostly points at the player who still expects the old rules. The tone constantly reminds you which opinions are acceptable and which targets are off-limits. It’s less "crime does pay" and more "crime is fine as long as you don’t punch sideways."

The result feels less like Grand Theft Auto and more like a very expensive, very polished compliance simulator with occasional shooting galleries. If you wanted the classic Rockstar sandbox where almost nothing was sacred and the player’s agency was the point, this is not that game. This is the version that politely asks you to internalize the hierarchy before it lets you play. Zero stars.

Rockstar has kept millions of fans waiting, and the excitement is slowly turning into **** Overwhelming HypeAnother major problem is the enormous hype surrounding the game. Gameplay, storytelling, performance, and overall enjoyment matter just as **** It Really Worth the Wait?I also believe Rockstar needs to understand that expectations are extremely high. A successful game should speak for itself rather than depend entirely on marketing and anticipation.Final VerdictOverall, GTA 6 has already managed to frustrate me before its full release. author: danial-_-khan
quote:
I genuinely cannot believe Rockstar spent over a decade making this game just to deliver something so unnecessarily complicated, ridiculously overhyped and, quite frankly, disappointing.

After waiting 13 years, I expected a revolutionary gaming experience. Instead, I got a glorified relationship simulator with occasional gunfights and a map so unnecessarily detailed that you'd think Rockstar was trying to distract us from the actual gameplay.

Jason and Lucia are supposedly the heart of the story, but their entire relationship feels like watching two financially irresponsible criminals repeatedly make the worst possible decisions and somehow expect different results. The Bonnie and Clyde concept sounded fantastic on paper, but apparently the writers decided that emotional dependency and criminal incompetence were sufficient substitutes for an interesting storyline.

And don't even get me started on the pacing. The game somehow manages to make a criminal conspiracy spanning an entire state feel like an unnecessarily long administrative procedure.

The biggest plot twist is that Jason and Lucia actually have a baby named Tomás. Yes, that's right. Two people whose primary professional skill is committing increasingly stupid crimes are somehow responsible for an infant. Lucia literally leaves her baby at a diner during a robbery, gets arrested, and then spends the opening of the game begging police to let her go back. Absolutely phenomenal parenting. Truly the Bonnie and Clyde of questionable childcare decisions. Kotaku

The gameplay isn't much better. Apparently, Rockstar decided that robbing a convenience store should require the strategic planning of a military operation. You've got CCTV, safes, disguises, security systems, getaway planning and an entire financial management application called BuckMe. I'm playing Grand Theft Auto, not applying for a business loan.

The wanted system has six levels, which sounds impressive until you realise that escaping the police now requires more preparation than actually committing the crime. God forbid you forget to change your outfit after robbing someone.

And somehow, despite having an enormous map, the story manages to lose momentum in its later chapters. The game is so committed to making everything cinematic that sometimes I feel like I'm watching an expensive television series with occasional interactive advertisements.

Even the endings are apparently multiple-choice exercises in emotional disappointment. Instead of giving players one satisfying conclusion, Rockstar decided to make the outcome dependent on choices, because apparently 13 years wasn't enough time to write one definitive ending. Some endings are happier than others, but even that sounds like a low bar for a game about two criminals trying to build a future together. Kotaku

Final verdict:

GTA 6 is what happens when a company spends billions of dollars perfecting the water reflections, NPC schedules, gym animations and the way sweat appears on someone's back, only to forget that some people actually want to play a video game.

The graphics are fantastic. The world is detailed. The sound design is excellent.

Unfortunately, I bought Grand Theft Auto, not Grand Theft Relationship Counselling.

I'd give it a 0/10, but the loading screens deserve at least a 1.

Would I recommend it? Absolutely not. Wait another 13 years for GTA 7. Maybe by then Lucia will have learned not to leave her baby unattended during a robbery.

author: Drakkari
quote:
My honest review, because it seems that people are being paid to hype up this game. It is not a game worthy of the name GTA. Yes, it looks beautiful but they hired the wrong people to write/develop it.

Over a decade of hype and billions of dollars in development, yet Rockstar somehow managed to CASTRATE one of the most legendary and unapologetic franchises in gaming history. Instead of delivering an anarchic, boundary-pushing satire of modern America, Grand Theft Auto VI feels like a sanitized, corporate-approved lecture disguised as a crime game. The graphics are among the best in the industry, yet the game is completely gutless where it actually matters.

The Death of Satire and the "Woke" Hand-Holding: Grand Theft Auto built its empire on mercilessly mocking everyone: politicians, celebrities, corporations, subcultures, and society as a whole. Now, the writing feels terrified of offending anyone on social media. The sharp, cynical edge that defined Vice City, San Andreas, and GTA V has been replaced by safe, toothless humor that seems to punch in only one predictable direction while treating modern progressive talking points with kid gloves. 

Invisible Guardrails and Protected NPCs: The worst thing you can do in an open-world sandbox is introduce arbitrary restrictions. In a game built around criminal mayhem, invisible barriers suddenly lock your weapons or prevent vehicle collisions around certain locations, events, and groups of NPCs to avoid controversy. When a sandbox starts deciding who is off-limits just to avoid offending people, the illusion of freedom falls apart.

You Can't Even Steal Cars in Your Own Neighborhood: Calling this game "Grand Theft Auto" feels like false advertising. Between the tedious Red Dead Redemption 2 style horse-and-trunk system, which forces you to babysit your personal El Camino just to carry your own gear, and arbitrary neighborhood restrictions that prevent you from stealing cars right outside your own turf, the entire premise starts falling apart. Stealing cars and causing chaos should be the bare minimum in a game called "Grand Theft Auto".

Jason Is a Spineless Pushover: Rockstar took a male protagonist with a military background and turned him into an errand boy who puts up with constant verbal abuse without ever standing his ground. Watching Jason get bossed around, belittled, and manipulated while meekly going along with everything makes him one of the weakest and least compelling protagonists in the franchise. There's no outlaw swagger here. Just a guy constantly apologizing and running errands.

Lucia Is an Insufferable, Toxic "Girlboss": Instead of creating a charismatic and complex criminal mastermind, the writers seem to have fallen back on every exhausting modern character trope. Lucia treats Jason like a doormat, belittles him at every opportunity, drags him into one reckless situation after another, and expects him to clean up the mess while she gets away with everything. Rather than feeling like a genuine Bonnie and Clyde partnership, their relationship comes across as a miserable, toxic dynamic that you're forced to put up with for dozens of hours.

Endless Chores and Tedious Realism: Nobody waited over a decade to patch leaky roofs, open bank accounts, assemble furniture, do groceries, and manage relationship meters. Every time the game starts building momentum, it brings everything to a halt so you can deal with another mundane life-sim chore. There's a difference between immersion and wasting the player's time.

Terrible Driving and Unacceptable Technical Issues: Some cars handle as if they're driving on greased ice, spinning out at the slightest turn unless you spend money on upgrades. Worse still, locking a flagship 2026 release to 30 FPS, with noticeable frame drops during intense shootouts and launch bugs capable of wiping out hours of save data, is simply inexcusable for a studio with Rockstar's resources.

Rockstar traded the fearless, rebellious spirit that made Grand Theft Auto a cultural phenomenon for corporate sanitization, tedious chores, and frustrating character dynamics. The game looks like a next-generation masterpiece, plays like a heavily policed theme park, and reads like it was written by a focus group terrified of getting canceled and eager to send the message.

author: Crabtaculous
quote: A stuttering mess of an already handicapped framerate of 30 FPS. It feels like you're moving through molasses as the frames dip from 24 to 17. That said the graphics are appealing and the world is well designed but over purposed. The game runs best when you're doing mundane boring life simulator missions. Looks great, but we didn't pay $80 to $100 dollars to do boring chores and shopping. Everything has been given a process, pointless quick times to create a pseudo immersion.  No longer do you press Y to perform the games namesake, and your player character figures it out being a criminal and all. No, no you have to perform arbitrary button presses and joystick motions to choose the handle, smash the window, slim Jim, then another arbitrary double stick work to hot wire the car. Even after all this trash mechanics, you have to go through hoops to keep the vehicle. Shopping is tedious, eating is tedious, too much put into pointless activities.  On to the story, so far the story mediocre, the first time in GTA's history you play a character with no agency. An enormous beautiful open world playing a character with no freedom.  I see the big picture in the games design is you're pigeonholed into playing missions and sticking to the story. Causing havoc and having fun like the GTA of old is too much work, in the name of "realism'.  Losing wanted level now takes multiple finite steps that end up discouraging exploration and doing the things that put this franchise on the map.  Final verdict, a boring overhyped stuttering festival of glitches. That is absolutely unacceptable for a company that has been making GTA sandbox games since 2001, and invested two billion in creating this slop.

author: v4r0
quote:
The game is nothing special. Just your typical GTA game but larger and more boring than ever. 
The characters are a mistake – Jason sounds artificially tough and emotionless, Lucia is just annoying and is very unfitting to a GTA game. Putting romance in a so-called game about crime and gangsters is definitely a choice.
The plot and missions are on GTA online level, meaning really bad. There isn't anything revolutionary there.
The dialogue is mostly absolutely cringe, my god. Don't they have any good writers in Rockstar anymore?
The core gameplay like shooting and driving is decent but not 13 years of waiting worthy.
The soundtrack is good but it's certainly not as good as original Vice City.
The graphics are great but they are also blurry and inconsistent (e.g. the clouds look absolutely terrible, a 15 years old game has better).
Let's give them credit where it's due – the game is extremely detailed, just like RDR2. But it's a double-edged sword since the game reminds me more of RDR than GTA because of it's pace at this point. Are we supposed to look at all the details or actually have fun doing whatever just like in older GTA titles?
And lastly, Rockstar practices are extremely anti-consumer. No CD in the box. Paid reviewers. Being nominated for the Game Awards before the game launch. The lack of PC launch (they are scared that half of the people would just refund their game on Steam after seeing what it has to offer). They will now milk this game to oblivion for the next 10 years but fanboys will still buy it several times anyway. After all, it's a fast food amongst the video games.
13 years in the making, Ladies and Gentleman.

author: Kantoftes
quote:
This doesn't feel like a true GTA game anymore. It feels as though the series has gradually abandoned the very identity that made it one of the most iconic and influential franchises in gaming history. It has lost the rebellious spirit, unapologetic satire, dark humor, and raw personality that once defined Grand Theft Auto. Instead, it comes across as overly woke, sanitized, and afraid to push boundaries or offend anyone. The unfiltered humor and controversial social commentary that made the older titles so memorable seem to have been replaced by a much safer and more restrained approach.

While the open world is still enjoyable to explore on a surface level, it lacks the genuine freedom, unpredictability, and sense of absolute chaos that made previous entries so special. Older GTA games made you feel like you could do practically anything, stumble upon ridiculous situations, and create unforgettable moments without constantly feeling guided or restricted by the experience. Here, much of that spontaneity seems to be missing. The world may look impressive, but graphical fidelity and map size mean very little if the actual experience doesn't capture the spirit of the franchise.

What disappoints me most is the complete lack of memorable moments. I am already twelve hours into the game, and it still hasn't delivered a single sequence that made me feel the raw emotion, adrenaline, excitement, or sheer unpredictability I experienced countless times in previous installments. There is no moment that has genuinely shocked me, no mission that has left me wanting to immediately jump back in, and no memorable action sequence that makes me think, "This is what GTA is all about."

A GTA game should make you feel like you're part of a living, breathing criminal underworld, where absurdity, violence, satire, freedom, and chaos coexist naturally. It should be outrageous, unpredictable, occasionally offensive, and, above all, entertaining. It shouldn't feel like it's constantly trying to play things safe or appeal to absolutely everyone at the expense of its original identity.

I don't expect every new GTA to be a carbon copy of its predecessors, nor am I against innovation or change. But there is a difference between evolving a franchise and stripping away the characteristics that made it special in the first place. At this point, it genuinely feels like the developers have prioritized presentation and accessibility over substance and personality. And that's what makes it so disappointing. I didn't want another generic, polished open-world experience with a GTA logo attached to it. I wanted GTA. And fifteen hours in, I'm still waiting to find it, I really hope they start caring about the community more than the money!

author: yanix
quote:
0/10 – Une déception technique à la hauteur des attentes démesurées.

Après des années d'attente et un budget colossal, on pouvait légitimement espérer un jeu techniquement irréprochable. Pourtant, GTA VI fait des compromis difficiles à accepter en 2026.

Le choix de limiter le jeu à 30 FPS sur toutes les consoles, y compris la PS5 Pro, sans proposer de véritable mode Performance à 60 FPS, est particulièrement décevant. Les chutes de framerate sur PS5 classique viennent encore aggraver le problème.

Rockstar a visiblement préféré pousser les graphismes et la densité de son monde au maximum plutôt que de garantir une expérience parfaitement fluide. Or, un jeu vidéo ne se résume pas à sa qualité visuelle : la fluidité, la stabilité et le confort de jeu sont tout aussi importants.

Les problèmes techniques signalés au lancement, notamment les soucis de synchronisation audio et les problèmes de sauvegarde rapportés par certains joueurs, renforcent cette impression.

On nous a vendu une révolution vidéoludique, mais l'ambition technique ne devrait jamais servir d'excuse à des compromis aussi importants.

Un 0/10 volontairement sévère pour sanctionner ces choix techniques et rappeler qu'une attente de plusieurs années doit s'accompagner d'une véritable exigence de qualité.

author: Pljeskavac
quote:
Played for about 10 hours thus far, and the only time I genuinely had fun was when I played a 10min 2D zombie mini game.

Game looks gorgeous, and the level of attention of detail is insane, which makes the extremely big world feel alive, but that's where the positives stop.

Storytelling & the main characters are abysmal in every aspect, and the more I play the less I care about them. Jason is a soulless plank of wood while Lucia is obnoxious. The story itself is illogical, poorly written, and not engaging at all, at least thus far. For example, two leads in a "complicated but loving" relationship reunite for the first time in ages. On the drive from point A to point B, they exchange two sentences, and then there's dead silence.

The push for realism and consequences has gutted what made GTA fun. This plays more like a life sim than a GTA game. The crime-themed side activities you'd expect have been swapped for chores: instead of stealing cars, you go grocery shopping, and instead of robbing people, you go scuba diving for treasure. 
It's just boring.

The realism is also very restrictive and greatly modifies your experience playing the game. Dying or getting arrested wipes your inventory and cash. The "create your own chaos whenever you want" feeling the franchise was built on is gone. You either go with the flow or grind through prep work for some "planned chaos." If you just want to cause mayhem in the open world, you first have to run errands: go home, grab your money, buy what you need, go back home to deposit the rest, and only then are you free to have fun.

You now need to take care of your car, instead of just plucking the one you like right of the streets. The fun reckless GTA driving is replaced with pedestrian driving or auto-driving, because again realism, actions have consequences. And driving feels bad, while driving & shooting just feels extremely frustrating.

I hope it picks up and gets better as you progress but so far, disappointing at best. Definitely not worth the current price tag, and definitely not a unanimous 10/10 GOTY, as stated by the "critics".

author: NorthAF
quote: 0/10 for narrative design, character development, writing, and overall plot. After more than a decade of waiting, this is what Rockstar delivers? An incredibly disappointing game from a studio that used to define the standard for open-world gaming.I genuinely don't know who thought Lucia and Jason were compelling protagonists. Jason might as well be a cardboard cutout standing in the background of every cutscene. He has almost no personality, no backbone, and barely any agency. His entire contribution to the relationship seems to boil down to "yes, dear" whenever Lucia proposes something. Meanwhile, Lucia comes across as an insufferable, toxic girlboss character who constantly dominates the narrative. Their relationship feels forced, the dynamic is painfully one-sided, and neither character comes close to the memorable protagonists Rockstar used to **** this goes much deeper than two badly written characters.Rockstar has been on a downward trajectory since the later GTA 5 Online updates, and GTA 6 feels like the culmination of everything that has gone wrong with the **** creative direction has fundamentally changed. Instead of focusing on the core audience that made this franchise successful, Rockstar seems increasingly obsessed with appealing to everyone except its longtime fans. The shift toward a different, more female-centered creative direction isn't inherently the problem; the problem is sacrificing compelling characters, good writing, and the franchise's identity in the **** used to be unapologetic. It was offensive, outrageous, violent, politically incorrect, and, most importantly, it made fun of EVERYONE. Nobody was safe from its satire. That was the entire **** it feels like Rockstar is carefully deciding which groups can be mocked and which must be protected. Violence feels increasingly sanitized and selectively restricted, while the writing seems more interested in pushing a particular worldview than delivering entertaining, intelligent satire. Instead of trusting players to think for themselves, the game often feels like it's trying to lecture them, particularly younger audiences, while ridiculing people who **** was supposed to challenge social norms, not enforce a new set of **** then there's the technical side. A game this expensive, developed for this long, launching with noticeable bugs and a 30 FPS cap on modern consoles is simply unacceptable to me. We've waited over a decade, and apparently smooth performance is still too much to ask from one of the wealthiest and most successful developers in **** make matters worse, Rockstar continues its frustrating approach to PC players. No PC release alongside consoles, leaving millions of players waiting yet again. After what happened with GTA 5, it's difficult not to see this as another deliberate double-dipping strategy. Release on consoles first, sell the PC version later, and potentially sell another enhanced edition after that. Selling essentially the same game to loyal customers two or even three times has become an incredibly cynical business model.

author: BaDmineZ
quote:
GTA VI was supposed to be the next revolution in open-world gaming. After years of anticipation, enormous marketing campaigns and promises of an incredibly immersive experience, expectations were understandably high.

But sometimes, the hype becomes bigger than the actual product.

A massive map doesn't automatically make a great open-world game. Beautiful scenery, realistic NPCs and impressive graphics mean very little if exploration becomes repetitive or lacks meaningful rewards. 

After years of technological progress, players naturally expect smoother gameplay from a major AAA release. While impressive graphics and visual fidelity are important, sacrificing smoothness to achieve them is not necessarily the right decision.30 FPS can make camera movement, driving and combat feel less responsive, particularly for players accustomed to 60 FPS. 

Rockstar should not expect players to accept lower performance simply because the game looks beautiful.A visually stunning game is not automatically a technically excellent game. 

Perhaps the biggest disappointment isn't GTA VI itself, but what Rockstar sacrificed to make it.Where are the new Bully, L.A. Noire and Max Payne experiences? What happened to the creativity and diversity that once made Rockstar one of the most respected studios in the gaming industry?
For more than a decade, players have waited for something genuinely new from Rockstar. Instead, the company has continued to prioritize Grand Theft **** after all those years, players deserve more than recycled mission structures, familiar gameplay mechanics and an excessive focus on sexual **** problem isn't that GTA is a bad franchise. 

The problem is that Rockstar has so many incredible worlds and stories it could explore, yet continues to concentrate so heavily on one series.

Rockstar used to give us different worlds, different experiences and unforgettable stories. Now, it feels like everything revolves around Grand Theft Auto.
