author: Guilbem
quote:
I get the impression that Rockstar saw how successful RDR2 was and decided to bring some of its mechanics into GTA VI, without considering whether they actually belonged in a completely different type of game. There's a reason why certain activities are enjoyable in one game but tedious in another. Hunting for food in the middle of nowhere as a cowboy is an interesting activity, but driving to a grocery store just to buy supplies isn't exactly thrilling. The honor system is another example: it makes sense in a Wild West setting, but feels out of place when applied to a modern urban crime game.

There are also some questionable technical aspects. Basic animations, such as cars exploding, look unimpressive, and players have reportedly experienced game-breaking bugs from simply opening their phones. But if there's one thing that bothers me more than anything else, it's how aggressively the game seems to fight against player freedom. Certain NPCs cannot be shot, some groups of characters are untouchable (like protesters), all it takes to stop a train is having someone stand on the tracks, which is not as fun as seeing it ramming multiple cars like in GTA5. 

Then there's the humor, which feels outdated thanks to references to pop culture that aren't particularly relevant anymore. Given the fact this game has been in development for 13 years, this isn't entirely surprising. The story itself could also have been handled better, especially if players were given more freedom instead of being dragged through a lengthy introduction where the protagonist spends hours doing chores for his girlfriend.

At least the visuals are impressive. The amount of detail and graphical improvements is genuinely commendable, even if it comes at the expense of a 30 FPS cap on consoles. We'll have to wait and see whether other platforms manage to deliver a better experience.

All things considered, GTA VI could have been an absolute masterpiece, but its constant restrictions on player freedom drag it down considerably. It's especially ironic that a protagonist who received so much attention and marketing ends up spending practically the entire prologue being an errand boy instead of actually getting to be the character players were excited to play.

author: Ash_7127
quote:
Ce GTA est une déception globale. Cela fait depuis red dead redemption 2 que Rockstar semblait vouloir s'orienter vers un réalisme plus important, GTA 6 franchi la ligne et le résultat est discutable. Le mode histoire peut davantage être décrit comme un film interactif, alors certes il en reprend certains codes mais il les reprend mal. Le gameplay garde les mêmes problèmes que GTA 5 et RDR 2 ; des missions couloirs qui n'évoluent pas d'un jeu à un autre. Faire un open world ne suffit pas à faire un bon jeu, il faut aussi savoir user des outils scénaristiques pour le rentabiliser, et ce n'est clairement pas ce que Rockstar a fait. 
En ce qui concerne le scénario ; l'écriture de personnages et d'histoire n'a jamais été le point fort de Rockstar, les protagonistes de GTA 5 sont des archétypes peu originaux que l'on a déjà vu un peu partout. GTA 6, quant à lui, bat des records de médiocrité scénaristique, l'histoire est trop simple, peu divertissante et est clairement anesthésiée par le réalisme lourd et mal dosé. 
De par ce jeu Rockstar souhaite réinventer la licence GTA, sauf qu'ils oublient ce qui a fait son succès. En empêchant les joueurs de s'amuser à foutre le bordel dans la ville, en bloquant les codes de triches derrière des défis et en désactivant les sauvegardes et la progression, ça donne une sensation de **** qui nous laisse dans l'idée que Rockstar n'a pas cherché à faire un jeu pour s'amuser tant que pour montrer le peu de talent qu'il leur reste. 

En ce qui concerne mes attentes du online ; 
Je vois deux issues possibles. Soit le mode Online est un échec cuisant à la manière de Red Dead Redemption 2. Soit, c'est un nouveau Candy Crush sauce Open World dans lequel on reproduit maladivement les mêmes actions en boucle pour gagner de l'argent, une sorte d'usine virtuelle à la manière de GTA 5. 
En conclusion ; ce GTA est une déception pure et dure, rockstar n'est plus le studio qu'il était jadis et ça se sent. Une histoire à la qualité discutable, un gunplay toujours aussi mou qui vient mettre le dernier dans la tombe du Gameplay qui lui aussi est ruiné par le réalisme absurde du jeu. Rockstar voulait faire une expérience mais ce faisant, ils ont oublié de placer l'expérience utilisateur.

author: NikoBellic61
quote: This is the first GTA game where I find the story genuinely uninteresting. The writing feels extremely disappointing and, in my opinion, lacks the quality and creativity we came to expect from Dan Houser. The characters don't feel right either. Where are the memorable, funny and unpredictable personalities we had in previous games, such as Trevor, Roman, Lamar, Yusuf Amir or Big Smoke? That unique GTA personality seems to be missing.Instead, the first seven hours feel more like a boyfriend simulator than an actual Grand Theft Auto game. Don't get me wrong: the graphics and gameplay are not bad. The game clearly builds on the gameplay style established by Red Dead Redemption 2, which is what I expected from a project with a reported budget of around $2 billion. At the very least, the graphics should be impressive. However, being limited to 30 FPS in 2026, even on a PS5 Pro, is disappointing.Another major issue is the lack of freedom compared to previous GTA titles. For example, you cannot shoot inside certain clubs or other locations. This is the first GTA that feels like it is actively restricting the player's freedom in ways that previous games did not. I remember GTA as a series where you were the protagonist and had an enormous amount of freedom to play the way you wanted.That is one of the main reasons people buy video games: to escape reality and enjoy a world where they can make their own decisions without constantly feeling restricted by the game.After 13 years of waiting and paying around €100, this is what we get? I expected much more from Rockstar Games. And let's not forget the physical edition containing nothing but a download code. Honestly, that's another disappointment and a slap in the face to loyal customers.I also find it difficult to take all the perfect 10/10 reviews seriously. When so many major gaming outlets give a game a perfect score, it raises questions about how objective those reviews really are.Rockstar Games, your fans waited 13 years for this. We expected something revolutionary, something that would define the next generation of gaming. Instead, at least from my perspective, GTA 6 feels like a massive missed opportunity.

author: JacKK06
quote:
Years of hype, trailers that looked incredible, and nonstop “best game ever” talk, and what did we actually get? A game that can’t even hold a stable 30 FPS on the most powerful consoles on the market. Locked 30 with constant drops into the teens during combat, driving, or any time the city gets busy. Cars clipping through bridges like the collision detection was an afterthought. Planes flying straight through towers and buildings without a care in the world. Launch bugs everywhere. Mission design that feels restrictive and railroaded. This is not a finished $80 game. It’s a buggy tech demo with a map attached.

Then there’s the actual gameplay and tone. You can’t shoot the protesters. You can’t pick up hookers. The open world chaos that defined GTA has been sanded down and sanitized so it doesn’t offend anyone. Everything feels neutered. Lucia is a terrible protagonist unlikable, poorly written, and clearly designed more around modern talking points than around being a fun character to play as. Jason gets treated like the perfect boyfriend while Lucia gets the “difficult, low effort partner” treatment for a huge chunk of the early game. It doesn’t feel like Rockstar writing. It feels like a committee that was more worried about backlash than about making the game fun.

The ownership side is just insulting. It’s all digital. No disc. You buy a physical copy and get a code in a box so you don’t actually own anything. No resale, no real ownership, just another download that can be taken away or broken by an update. After years of GTA Online being turned into a microtransaction machine, this is more of the same anti consumer garbage dressed up as a “next gen experience.”

author: poopandcumeater
quote: Honestly I just think Rockstar completely missed the point of what made GTA so good in the first place. GTA 4 wasn’t some groundbreaking graphical achievement even for its time, but the story, atmosphere and characters were incredible. Niko was someone who wanted to escape his past and live a better life but constantly found himself dragged back into the exact life he hated, which made you genuinely care about him and made even the mundane missions feel meaningful because they actually developed the characters or progressed the story. GTA 5 was a bit of a mix, arguably the story suffered from having three protagonists and constantly switching between them, but it still managed to balance technical innovation with an entertaining story. GTA 6 feels like Rockstar took the realism and slower pacing of GTA 4 but completely forgot why those things worked. Jason and Lucia don’t have anywhere near the same convincing motivations, a lot of their problems seem completely avoidable, and there’s so much mundane **** that feels like filler just for the sake of making the game realistic. There’s a difference between making a world feel alive and making the player spend their time doing pointless errands. Even the physics feel like a downgrade in terms of actual game feel, GTA 4 had incredibly satisfying vehicle physics, weight and ragdoll interactions, whereas GTA 6 seems more concerned with technical complexity than making things enjoyable to play. My biggest issue is that Rockstar has spent over a decade and an absurd amount of money making the most detailed open world imaginable, seemingly while neglecting the actual writing and gameplay. I’d genuinely rather have a smaller GTA with a brilliant 25-30 hour story than a massive game full of filler. GTA 4 proved that you don’t need groundbreaking graphics, thousands of activities or an entire simulated world to make an incredible game, you just need compelling characters, good writing, atmosphere and gameplay that feels good. I don’t understand how Rockstar managed to make something this technically impressive while seemingly forgetting what made people fall in love with GTA in the first place.

author: KevinRevenger
quote:
GTA 6 may be one of the most expensive and ambitious games ever made, but I honestly don't understand why it deserves this almost untouchable level of hype.
For a game reportedly built with such an enormous investment, I expected much more than another return to the same formula: crime, violence, robberies, and the familiar GTA structure we've seen for decades. Of course, the level of detail and technical ambition are impressive, but impressive production values alone don't automatically make a game revolutionary.
What disappoints me even more is that, despite all the money and development behind it, the game doesn't even deliver the 60 FPS performance I would expect from a major current-generation release.
GTA 6 will undoubtedly be a massive commercial success, and I can respect the scale of what Rockstar has created. But personally, I don't think bigger budgets, bigger worlds, and bigger hype necessarily mean a better or more innovative game.

DO NOT BELIEVE THE HYPE.

GTA VI is an impressive feat of immersion and map-making, but unfortunately suffers from shortcomings in all other aspects.

Capped at 30fps, well below the standard that's to be expected for modern games, GTA VI often fails to meet even that, with performance issues often tanking the framerate to 20fps and below. The story of VI drags at many points, and lacks much of the charm in both its plot and core characters that has come to be associated with the series. Furthermore, despite a 13-year gap between the release of GTA V and VI, the game fails to innovate and improve on the gameplay, sharing many of the same flaws that have been present in several of the series's past games. 

In truth, GTA VI is, at its core, a 6-7/10 game whose score is further bogged down by low performance standards, a failure to meet even those standards, and bugs that lower the quality of the game to below what's acceptable for a AAA developer that has had over a decade to produce the game. What may be worst of all however, is that GTA VI fundamentally lacks the elements and charm that have made the GTA series so beloved to so many people.

quote:
Karantika (also spelled garantita or calentica) is a savory Algerian chickpea-flour flan baked until golden on top and soft inside. Here is a classic recipe using 250 g of chickpea flour.Ingredients
• 250 g (about 2 cups) chickpea flour
• 1 L (4 cups) water• 3 tbsp olive oil (or neutral vegetable oil)
• 2 tsp ground cumin (plus extra for serving)
• 1 tsp salt• 1 tsp black pepper (optional)
• 1–2 eggs, beaten (optional, for a firmer, custard-like texture)

Instructions
1. Make a smooth paste: Put the chickpea flour in a bowl. Whisk in about a third of the water until smooth and lump-free.
2. Finish the batter: Stir in the oil, salt, black pepper, and cumin. Gradually whisk in the rest of the water (and beaten egg, if using) until the batter is thin and runny.
3. Rest the batter: Let it sit for at least 30–60 minutes (or several hours) so the flour hydrates.
4. Prep and bake: Preheat the oven to 220°C (430°F) and lightly oil a baking dish. Stir the batter, pour it in, and bake for 25–30 minutes (or longer for deeper baking dishes) until the top is browned and the center is set yet slightly jiggly.
5. Serve hot: Slice and eat warm. Sprinkle with extra cumin and serve on its own or tucked into a baguette with harissa.

author: BotheJackHorse
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI: Too Much Tedium for Too Little Payoff

Coming from a longtime Rockstar fan who considers Grand Theft Auto IV and Red Dead Redemption 2 among the greatest games ever made, Grand Theft Auto VI is a frustratingly mixed experience. While the technical craft is undeniable, boasting strong visuals and the sharpest driving in the series, the pacing and mission design constantly get in the way of actual fun. Rather than balancing cinematic realism with engaging gameplay, the game bogs itself down in three major issues:

Excessive QTEs and mundane pacing: Main story missions lean far too heavily on quick-time events, forcing you to repeatedly tap buttons or hold triggers while watching characters slowly move objects. Paired with sluggish "slice-of-life" chores, it often feels less like an escapist crime thriller and more like a mundane real-life simulator.

Overly scripted "on-rails" set pieces: High-stakes moments repeatedly strip away player agency. Instead of letting you freely handle tense situations, the game funnels you down rigid, pre-scripted tracks. Frequent slow-walking segments through crowded areas only make things worse, lacking the sharp, memorable dialogue that made Red Dead Redemption 2’s slower moments worth sitting through.

Safe, repetitive writing: The script tries to sound edgy and crude like a classic GTA game, yet ends up feeling oddly sanitized and formulaic. Too many side characters fall into a repetitive loop of swearing, drug references, and sex jokes right before handing off an objective, missing the wild personality of past standouts like GTA IV’s Mikhail Faustin or Dimitri Rascalov. Among the leads, Lucia is compelling enough to carry the story, even if she is a walking red flag as a person, while Jason comes across as a flat, unengaging protagonist.

Word is that the game finally hits its stride around the 30-hour mark, but asking players to push through that much slog before it gets good is a tough sell. Ten hours in, staying awake is already a struggle at times, and enduring another twenty hours just to reach the payoff simply isn't worth it.
Writing: 1/10
Gameplay 6/10
Graphics: 9/10
Story: 2/10 (so far)
Overall Score: 4.5 / 10

author: Farodin11
quote:
The graphics and physics are genuinely impressive, and interacting with the world feels surprisingly natural. Whether you are experimenting with the environment, causing chaos, or simply messing around, the sandbox systems are the game’s biggest strength and make it easy to lose hours without a specific objective.
Unfortunately, that is where most of my enthusiasm ends. The game suffers from noticeable technical issues, including bugs and glitches that can undermine otherwise enjoyable moments. The 30 FPS cap is particularly hard to accept in 2026, especially for a game that puts so much emphasis on physics, visual detail, and dynamic interactions. It makes the experience feel less smooth and less polished than it should be.
The characters are also fairly bland, and the story never gave me much reason to care. It feels generic rather than memorable, and the game does not live up to its hype. More importantly, the older games in the series were much funnier because they did not care about political correctness and were willing to mock, offend, and mess with absolutely everyone and everything. This entry feels noticeably safer and more restrained by comparison, which drains much of the irreverent personality that made the earlier games stand out.
Verdict: This is a fun sandbox game, but that is about all it is. If you mainly want a physics playground and impressive world interaction, it can be enjoyable. If you were expecting the sharp, unapologetic humour, memorable characters, and stronger story of the older games, you will be disappointed.

author: SnowstormDevSwe
quote: GTA 6 is undoubtedly a technical achievement, featuring exceptional visual fidelity, advanced lighting systems, dense environmental simulation, and highly detailed character animations. However, graphical complexity should never come at the expense of fundamental gameplay responsiveness and player **** of my primary concerns is the increasing reliance on friction-driven gameplay systems within modern AAA development. When engagement is sustained through restrictive mission structures, delayed gratification, and excessive interaction overhead, developers risk undermining the intrinsic motivation that makes gameplay genuinely rewarding.From a game design perspective, effective player retention should emerge naturally from a compelling core gameplay loop, meaningful player decisions, mechanical mastery, and immediate feedback. A game should establish this foundation during its opening sequence rather than relying primarily on narrative investment, franchise recognition, or progression incentives to maintain engagement.Another concern with GTA 6 is its emphasis on interaction complexity and animation-driven realism. While these systems can strengthen immersion, additional inputs and contextual interactions must provide meaningful gameplay value. Otherwise, they increase the input cost per action without proportionally improving player agency or decision-making depth. Interaction density should not be mistaken for mechanical **** decision to target 30 FPS across console platforms, including PlayStation 5 Pro, also raises questions about Rockstar's technical priorities. Although a complex open-world simulation requires significant CPU and GPU resources, the absence of a higher-frame-rate option limits player choice and temporal responsiveness.Ultimately, my criticism is not that GTA 6 lacks technical ambition, but that technical sophistication, cinematic realism, and gameplay quality are not interchangeable. The most successful game systems are those that maximize meaningful player interaction rather than simply increasing mechanical complexity or extending engagement.

After 13 years of waiting, I expected at least the same pace and freedom that GTA 5 gave us. What I got was something else entirely – a game where you spend most of your time watching dialogue, listening to Jason and Lucia talk about their feelings, and only occasionally blowing something up.

What Disappointed Me Most

1. Too many relationships, too little action. This is the core problem. Rockstar clearly wanted a "mature" narrative, but the result is a game where relationship scenes and dialogue take up more time than the missions. GTA 5 had Michael, Franklin, and Trevor – their friction was funny and dynamic, but it never got in the way of the action. Here, the couple's drama just drags the pacing down.

2. Action missions are rare and bland. When you finally get a shooting or heist mission, it feels inserted between long narrative sections rather than being the core of the game. GTA 5's heists were memorable, with planning and choices. GTA 6's missions often feel like "go from point A to point B and watch a cutscene."

3. Slow pacing. The opening hours barely move. The first few hours are almost entirely walking, talking, and everyday routine. I understand it's a deliberate choice, but I wanted to play GTA, not watch a season of a TV series.

4. 30 fps and technical issues. This makes it even worse – the game isn't just slow in pacing, it's also locked at 30 frames per second on consoles, with noticeable drops in dense areas

author: Slxght3r
quote:
GTA 6 – 13 Years, Billions of Dollars, and Somehow This Is the Result?

I honestly expected far more from Grand Theft Auto VI. After roughly 13 years of waiting, an enormous development budget, and one of the biggest marketing campaigns in gaming history, this release feels incredibly disappointing. At this point, I have to question what all those years and resources were actually spent on.

One of my biggest issues is the game's seemingly insensitive treatment of Islam. Describing a strip club as the “Mekka of rich people” is an incredibly questionable choice of wording. Mecca (Makkah) is the holiest city in Islam, and comparing it to a strip club associated with wealth, sexual entertainment, and hedonism is disrespectful to a religion followed by billions of people. Satire is one thing, but there should still be a level of awareness and consideration when referencing religious symbols and sacred places. This just comes across as unnecessary and offensive.

The excessive nudity and sexual content are another major problem. GTA has always been provocative, but there is a difference between mature content that serves a purpose and content that feels excessive simply for the sake of shock value. At times, it feels as though the game relies too heavily on sexualization rather than delivering meaningful substance.

And then we get to the bugs and glitches. After 13 flipping years of development, how is a release with this many technical problems acceptable? This isn't some small indie project developed by a handful of people on a shoestring budget. This is Rockstar Games, backed by an enormous budget and years upon years of development time. Players have every right to expect a polished, stable experience. Spending over a decade developing a game and still having it launch with frustrating bugs, glitches, and technical inconsistencies is genuinely embarrassing.

The budget makes all of this even harder to justify. With hundreds of millions—potentially approaching or exceeding a billion dollars in total development and marketing costs depending on what figures are included—this should have been an exceptionally polished product. Instead, it feels like certain aspects were prioritized over quality control, common sense, and creative restraint.

After 13 years of anticipation, I expected something that would redefine gaming, not something that leaves me disappointed by its writing, excessive sexual content, and technical shortcomings. The amount of hype surrounding this game makes its flaws even more noticeable.

13 years. An absurd budget. Endless hype. And yet, somehow, this is what we got. The name GTA and Rockstar shouldn't be a free pass for criticism. **** takes this long and costs this much to make, it should deliver excellence—not excuses.

Freedom feels heavily restricted compared to older entries—too many scripted missions, rigid boundaries, and endless hand-holding instead of pure sandbox chaos. The map looks shiny, yet the world feels strangely lifeless and over-policed. It doesn't feel like a true GTA game anymore; it feels like a corporate checklist wearing a familiar name. author: Greenjungle
quote:
All Graphics, Zero Soul
You can buy out the gaming media and flood user scores with brand-new bot accounts dropping 10/10s, but you can’t fool longtime players. Aside from the graphics, this game is a massive disappointment that strips away everything that ever gave GTA its soul.
​Going from iconic leads like Michael, Trevor, and Franklin—or the energy of San Andreas—to Jason and Lucia is a brutal downgrade. Both leads are painfully unlikable, and Lucia in particular is grating; half the time it doesn't feel like a crime epic, it feels like a chore simulator where you're just running errands to keep her happy. The writing fell off a cliff. Instead of sharp satire, it’s sterile, safe, and full of cringe dialogue that makes you want to skip cutscenes on your very first playthrough.
​Worse, the gameplay itself feels neutered. For an open-world criminal sandbox, there are somehow more things you can’t do than can. You can’t even hijack any car you want anymore, and any actual shady activity feels heavily sanitized and committee-approved. The missions are dull, heavily railroaded with zero meaningful plot choices, and buried under unskippable filler that wastes your time between the rare fun moments.
​Even the basics took a step backward. Driving feels noticeably worse than it did in GTA 5, and watching the framerate dip under 30 FPS on PS5 during big action set-pieces in 2026—right when performance matters most—is completely unacceptable.
​Whatever regime changes happened behind the scenes at Rockstar and Take-Two clearly gutted the studio. They took the edge, freedom, and bite out of Grand Theft Auto and left behind a pretty, hollow shell. Save your money.

author: Warrior_Within
quote:
I feel scammed by GTA VI

I wasn't sure whether to buy GTA VI. I loved GTA V, it's one of my favorite games ever, and after so many years and so much money spent on development, I expected Rockstar to deliver something great. When I saw the ridiculously high review scores, I decided to give it a chance.

What an absolute disappointment.

At first, I thought this wasn't GTA, but Red Dead Redemption 3 in a modern setting. At least it seemed like a good game. 

The more I played, the more it felt like a bad Red Dead Redemption 2.

The story is terrible. The missions are incredibly boring, many feel like generic side quests, and the characters' motivations are forced and make no sense. Jason and Lucia feel like empty vessels who just do whatever other characters tell them. They have no voice, no real personality, and no meaningful choices.

Jason in particular feels like a terrible representation ****. Some scenes, especially the one where he hangs out and plays video games with his friend, are genuinely cringe. I could understand it if Rockstar were making fun of him, but it feels like they're actually trying to write a realistic male character. It's absurdly bad. If this is how women have felt regarding males writing female characters in films books and videogames I am so sorry for you 

And the relationship isn't optional. You have no say in it, no meaningful decisions, and you're forced to accept whatever happens between them.

But the worst part is the sandbox. GTA has always been about freedom, doing crazy **** and having fun. Now you can't even steal every car until Chapter 3, the police are more annoying and restrictive, and everything feels unnecessarily realistic. 

And why does a game about being a criminal have a morality system that rewards you for not killing people?

The graphics are absolutely insane. The engine, the optimization, the fact that this runs on a PS5 — technically, it's incredible. I'll give Rockstar that.

But graphics are secondary. Games are supposed to be fun.

And this game is just **** boring.

I didn't need a masterpiece. I just wanted a fun GTA game. Instead, I spent €80 on something that feels like a worse Red Dead Redemption 2 set in the 21st century.

I would put a higher score like a 7, 7.5 maybe maybe an 8 but I feel so  scammed by the paid reviewers that I put this score so other in my situation do not get scammed. There is no way someone who is critic or honest would put this game a 10/10. 

If I could get a refund on PlayStation, I absolutely would.

author: OElNino
quote:
GTA VI - Overhyped Masterpiece or Disappointing Reality ?

It was expected to redefine gaming and set a new standard for open-world experiences. While Rockstar has delivered an impressive world with incredible visual detail, several decisions and problems deserve serious criticism.

1. The 30 FPS limitation
One of the biggest disappointments is the 30 FPS cap, even on PS5 Pro. In 2026, a game of this scale and budget should offer a 60 FPS performance mode. Visual quality is important, but smooth gameplay and responsiveness should not be sacrificed entirely for graphics.

2. Physical editions without discs
Selling physical editions containing only digital download codes defeats the purpose of buying a physical copy. Reports of missing or already-redeemed codes have also raised concerns. Even more controversial are reports that codes could potentially be visible through certain packaging using a flashlight, creating a possible security issue.

3. Excessively positive reviews
The overwhelmingly positive professional reviews raise questions about critical standards. When critics award almost perfect scores while user ratings are dramatically lower, it creates a significant credibility gap. User reviews can be unfair, but professional reviewers should not treat a technically impressive game as automatically flawless.

4. Technical problems and bugs
Reports of crashes, disappearing weapons, lost character statistics, clipping, visual glitches, strange physics and other gameplay issues are disappointing for a production of this scale. A massive budget and years of development should translate into a more polished experience.

5. Restrictive mission design
Despite its enormous open world, GTA VI reportedly continues Rockstar's traditional problem of restricting player freedom during missions. Scripted sequences, limited approaches and excessive mission constraints can make an otherwise open experience feel surprisingly linear.

6. Pacing and excessive realism
The focus on everyday activities, lengthy conversations and relationship development between Jason and Lucia may improve immersion, but can also make the experience unnecessarily slow. Realism should enhance entertainment, not replace it.

7. No PC version at launch
Excluding PC players at launch is another questionable decision. A significant part of the gaming community has to wait, while console players are limited to 30 FPS. For a release of this magnitude, a simultaneous PC launch would have been preferable.

8. Price and consumer expectations
After years of hype, enormous marketing campaigns and premium pricing, expectations are understandably high. Consumers should not have to accept technical compromises, questionable distribution methods or unfinished features simply because the game carries the Rockstar name.

Final Verdict
GTA VI is undoubtedly an impressive technical and artistic achievement (so are others), but that does not make it immune to criticism. The 30 FPS limitation, performance issues, questionable physical editions, digital licence concerns, reported bugs and restrictive gameplay decisions deserve proper scrutiny.

The biggest problem may be the culture surrounding the game itself. Some players defend every Rockstar decision, while others criticise everything without giving the game a fair chance. A game should be judged by its actual quality, not by its reputation, marketing budget or hype.

GTA VI should be held to a higher standard precisely because it is one of the most anticipated and expensive games ever made. 

Being a Rockstar production should not grant it immunity from criticism!

Happy plays everyone! For GTA VI or any other game :)

author: NintendoFan77

GTA6 is a Soulless, Overhyped Disaster

What an absolute disappointment. Years of waiting, an insane budget, and THIS is what we get? A soulless, sanitized, politically correct mess that feels more like AI-generated corporate slop than an actual Rockstar game.

GTA used to be fearless, offensive, chaotic, and unapologetically entertaining. Now it feels like everything has been filtered through a committee of corporate executives terrified of offending anyone. The edgy humor, the rebellious spirit, the personality that made this franchise legendary – all gone.

And those endless 100/100 reviews? Give me a break. I wouldn't be surprised if half of them were bought. The disconnect between the ridiculous critical praise and what I'm actually experiencing is laughable.

This isn't the GTA I grew up loving. It's a billion-dollar monument to everything wrong with modern AAA gaming: woke pandering, corporate greed, artificial hype, and zero soul.

0/10. All that money, all that hype, and absolutely none of the magic.

author: Faeron1984
quote:
Fundamentally, this is not a Grand Theft Auto game - this is a poorly written Couple On The Run story, with minor improvements to graphics and car modifications over previous editions, and a cheap cameo thrown in to try and nostalgia bait. The HUD is uninspiring and dull to look at, with simple white text such as "+Ammo" appearing when looting corpses, and zero effort put into the weapon wheel compared to Red Dead's stylistic version. The vehicles handle too realistically yet too arcade-y to be enjoyed by either fanbase. There are too many things to complain about, and not enough positives to bother trying to justify this waste of $2bn and 13 years.

The biggest issue is the main story itself. If one were to play this game in a classic GTA fashion, you will inevitably achieve the "bad" endings. This is due to the awful karma system. The game attempts to punish players for their choices, and wants you to simply play-out the developer's ideal choices, rather than allow you to make your own versions of events. In a real GTA game, we would have the option to abandon Lucia entirely, if not outright kill her, as well as commit crime without moral judgement from the developers. I could go on, but this game has already wasted enough of my time.

Do not even get me started about the dodgy user agreement and the data it collects on your behaviour in-game.

author: Semo_abdu
quote: 0/10 – Grand Theft Auto has lost its identity.I waited 13 years for this game. Thirteen **** years. And what did I get? A game that feels more like Red Dead Redemption 2 than Grand Theft Auto.Rockstar seems to have forgotten what made GTA special in the first place: freedom, chaos, outrageous satire, unrestricted criminal fun and the ability to play however you **** does stealing a car have to be complicated? Why should I worry about whether a vehicle belongs to someone in my neighbourhood? Why am I being punished for killing enemies through a criminal profile system? Why should I have to incapacitate enemies instead of simply shooting them? Why does the game judge my playstyle by labelling me a professional criminal or a psychopath?And why did Rockstar take away the freedom of carrying a full arsenal? The old GTA games let you carry different types of weapons. GTA V expanded that freedom even further. Now we’re back to carrying a limited selection and having to rely on our vehicle for the rest. Why? Who asked for this downgrade?Rockstar keeps talking about realism, but apparently realism means restricting the player. The game can have aliens, Bigfoot, and red hulk and aliens? ridiculous characters and absurd situations, but when it comes to the actual gameplay, suddenly everything has to be realistic and carefully controlled. That’s not consistency. That’s selective realism.I don’t want GTA to become Red Dead Redemption. I love Rockstar’s games, but GTA and RDR are different franchises with different identities. The slower, more restrictive mechanics that worked for Arthur Morgan don’t automatically belong in a Grand Theft Auto game.I also miss the fearless satire, outrageous humour and unapologetic personality of the older GTA games. Grand Theft Auto used to feel like a franchise where nothing was off-limits. Now I worry that Rockstar has lost some of that **** Houser’s departure makes that concern even greater. He was one of the defining creative voices behind Rockstar’s storytelling and the identity of GTA. His absence is noticeable to me, and I question whether the new creative direction understands what made this franchise special.I know the game has positive aspects, and I still have things I’m looking forward to. I waited 13 years, so of course I’m going to play it. But that doesn’t mean I have to pretend I’m happy with these decisions.I wanted the next Grand Theft Auto. I wanted more freedom, more chaos, more satire and an evolution of GTA V.Instead, what I’m seeing feels like Red Dead Redemption 2 wearing a Grand Theft Auto costume.This isn’t the GTA sequel I waited 13 years for.

author: Ecckos
quote:
Worst GTA Ever! A Life Simulator, Dating Simulator, and Male Humiliation Simulator.

Zero fun, zero freedom, almost zero gangster action.

Half the game is spent dealing with Jason’s house, which belongs to Brian and which Lucia moves into, buying flowers and doing household shopping. Hell, there’s even a cutscene where you put groceries away in kitchen cabinets. WTF happened? Where’s the gangster attitude?

Jason is one of the most shallow protagonists in gaming. A former soldier who dreams of a quiet, easy life instead of having any real criminal ambitions. Seriously? This is a GTA protagonist?

Lucia and Jason come from completely different worlds. She wants money, criminal success, and to climb higher. He offers her a quiet life, dinners, and shopping, while she wants to take part in heists. When Jason refuses to take her along, she says she’ll handle things herself. Their ambitions couldn’t be more different.

Lucia’s goals and the future she wants for herself seem to come before the relationship. Jason, meanwhile, looks like a guy who has no idea what he wants and increasingly lets the relationship dictate his life.

You get the impression that Jason wouldn’t even mind if Lucia slept with another guy while he sat in the corner watching. Total cuckold!

Lucia fits perfectly into a certain model of modern Western relationships that is increasingly criticized today. Personal ambitions and convenience come first. The partner is expected to adapt, support, and follow along, even if it means abandoning his own plans. That’s exactly the kind of arrangement I find repulsive. A relationship should be based on mutual effort, not one person pursuing their ambitions while the other simply follows. Jason increasingly looks like a man who has lost his identity by subordinating himself to Lucia.

This isn’t a partnership. It’s yet another story about a man who has to subordinate himself to a woman.

Rockstar became so obsessed with their relationship that it created a separate system for developing their bond. Dates, holding hands, spending time together, maintaining the relationship. WTF?! How much more is missing before this becomes a full-blown dating simulator? Am I buying GTA or some teenage romance game?

And the criminal underworld? Influencers, female rappers, viral videos, social media, fame, clubs, and businesses. Even the criminal world feels like show business and reality TV. Instead of the streets and the gangster atmosphere, we get celebrities and internet personalities. WTF happened to GTA? Is this supposed to be **** GTA?! 

How is this a rom-com instead **** game? How low can you sink?

The game has been feminized, and aside from its beautiful graphics and a few interesting mechanics, it’s simply terrible.

The game is liberal, so forget about freedom. NPCs are protected, too. You can’t kill protesters. Try running them over and your car automatically brakes. Shoot them? They’re invincible. Clubs also restrict weapon use, so forget about starting a proper shootout.

A gangster game with a morality system, where certain choices can lead to a bad ending. Seriously? All that’s missing is a good-behavior meter and a reward for being a model citizen.

The storyline revolves mostly around the relationship between these two “protagonists.” Instead of gangster chemistry and uncompromising characters, we get romance, everyday chores, and emotional drama. 
The gangster elements are pushed into the background. 

This is a feminist fantasy. The story feels like a romance novel written for women. The relationship between Lucia and Jason takes center stage while the actual gangster story takes a back seat.

You could honestly get the impression that the game was paid off by liberal feminists.

A horrible, humiliating experience that forces you to perform everyday chores, when people play games precisely to escape that kind of crap.

Gaming is going downhill. A gangster game has turned into a dating simulator with a forced feminist agenda, a life simulator with a few heists thrown in. Rockstar has abandoned its identity. This is closer to The Sims than to previous GTA games.

It feels like Rockstar forgot what made GTA special in the first place.

This isn’t GTA VI. It’s GTA SIMP Cuckold Feminist Rom-Com Simulator.

My proposed new name: SCFRS.

My rating: 0/10. Why so low? Because this was supposed to be GTA, and it simply isn’t.

It’s like MasterChef: if the challenge requires a dish made with mussels but you serve chicken, you get zero points. That’s exactly how I’m judging this game. It failed to deliver what it was supposed to be. 

If this were a separate game, my rating would be much higher. But it isn’t what we were promised.

If it weren’t called GTA, it would never have achieved anything close to this level of success.

It failed to live up to the identity and expectations associated with the GTA name. 

That’s why I simply cannot give it a higher score.

Cuck simulator . Cuck is a disparaging slang noun and verb derived from cuckold. It refers to a man with an unfaithful partner, or—more broadly in modern slang and online politics—a weak, submissive, or contemptible man.

Definitions and Meanings• Noun (literal / romantic): A man whose wife or partner is sexually unfaithful (cuckold). It is also used in adult entertainment and consensual non-monogamy contexts.• Noun (insult): A derogatory label for a man viewed as weak, spineless, or submissive. On the internet and in political discourse, it is frequently used as an insult against men with liberal, progressive, or moderate views.• Verb: To be sexually unfaithful to a partner, or to have sexual relations with someone else's spouse or partner.Origin and Evolution• Etymology: Shortened from cuckold, which dates back to Middle English and connects to the cuckoo bird—known for laying its eggs in other birds' nests. Early uses of cuck appear in the 17th century.• Modern shift: While historically tied to marital infidelity, the term expanded in online forums and political slang to attack perceived weakness or political opponents. Opinions on Reddit differ on how the word is applied, with some viewing it primarily as a broad online insult implying weakness, while others stick closer to its literal meaning involving infidelity.

author: popkultklub
quote: Après environ 4 heures de jeu, voici mes premières impressions sur GTA 6. Et si le jeu impressionne indéniablement sur certains aspects, tout n'est pas aussi convaincant que je l'espérais.Visuellement, c'est absolument magnifique. Les graphismes sont impressionnants, les effets de lumière sont sublimes et le travail réalisé sur l'ambiance visuelle force le respect. En revanche, les 30 FPS deviennent assez gênants au fil des heures. C'est d'autant plus dommage que la fluidité aurait vraiment contribué à rendre l'expérience plus **** jeu multiplie également les scripts et les séquences mises en scène, parfois intéressantes et surprenantes au premier abord. Mais je me demande dans quelle mesure ces effets continueront à impressionner après plusieurs dizaines d'heures de jeu.Côté gameplay, GTA 6 ne révolutionne pas vraiment la formule. Mais après tout, on sait pourquoi on lance un GTA et ce n'est pas nécessairement ce qu'on lui demande. En revanche, je trouve les sensations assez étranges : toutes les actions semblent lourdes, les personnages sont parfois difficiles à contrôler et les déplacements manquent de naturel. La conduite, elle, paraît plus technique que dans les précédents opus, mais on finit par s'y habituer et je trouve même cette évolution plutôt bienvenue.Mention spéciale à la bande-son de Justice, qui est excellente, ainsi qu'à la sélection des radios, particulièrement réussie.J'ai cependant quelques réserves sur la direction prise par Rockstar concernant le ton du jeu. Le code moral qui semble se dessiner est assez discutable. À l'image de Red Dead Redemption 2, on a parfois l'impression que le jeu cherche à nous faire regretter nos propres actes. On ne s'amuse plus vraiment à être une ordure, on devrait presque culpabiliser de l'être. Si j'ai envie d'incarner un psychopathe dans GTA, laissez-moi le faire sans me donner mauvaise conscience !Plus généralement, j'ai parfois l'impression que Rockstar cherche davantage à nous faire vivre le quotidien de ses personnages qu'à nous laisser profiter de la liberté et de la folie qui ont fait le succès de GTA. D'ailleurs, je dirais presque que si vous aimez Les Sims, ce GTA 6 risque de beaucoup vous plaire. Si vous aimez GTA, c'est peut-être une autre **** trouve également que le jeu a perdu une partie de son ADN satirique, pourtant si caractéristique de la licence. À voir comment cela évoluera par la suite.Autre déception : les personnages. Pour le moment, je leur trouve assez peu de charisme. Ils sont beaux, très bien modélisés, mais cela ne suffit pas à les rendre attachants ou mémorables.Enfin, je m'attendais à une carte plus grande et surtout plus vivante. Pour le moment, elle me paraît finalement assez limitée et je ne retrouve pas encore cette impression de monde foisonnant que **** dernier point, et pas des moindres : les pratiques commerciales.Difficile de ne pas mentionner un studio qui, à mes yeux, adopte certaines des pires pratiques commerciales de l'industrie. Imposer un tel prix pour une version exclusivement numérique est tout simplement scandaleux. Ce genre de stratégie crée un précédent dangereux et risque d'avoir des conséquences directes sur le marché du jeu vidéo à moyen et long terme.J'ai eu l'occasion de jouer gratuitement et, en l'état, je refuse de dépenser une telle somme pour acquérir le **** avis reste évidemment provisoire après seulement 4 heures. GTA 6 a encore largement le temps de me surprendre, en bien comme en mal. Mais pour le moment, malgré ses qualités techniques indéniables, je suis loin d'être aussi emballé que je l'aurais imaginé.

author: Hynry
quote:
I dont know where to start this. 

Maybe with the positives. Game looks really good, it's a fact. One of the best looking games i've seen. Also in many cases the environment feels really immersive, and interesting. Makes you want to just roam and discover certain places. 

Unfortunately thats about it with the positives, and overall i'm very disappointed in this game. 

If this game was titled something else, i wouldnt be this harsh, but this is not the case. This is the new Grand Theft Auto, that i have been waiting for 13 years. I have played every single GTA, so i pretty much know what to expect, and what to love. 

GTA's have always been a crime chaos sandbox, and this is far from it. This game feels boring right from the start; it feels like sims. Doing chores, fixing pipes, painting the house and other boring stuff from the start, i really dont know what they were thinking. Compare to previous GTA starts (like GTA V bank heist), this was very lame. 

When thinking about chaos sandbox, it gets worse. The game imposes restrictions on actions that previous GTA titles allowed, which makes the sandbox feel less open than before. You cant kill certain nps, you cant run over certain groups (protesters for example). I mean, how is this GTA? GTA was always about freedom to do chaos, if that is what you want. Previously you could even shoot story characters. Of course the mission would fail, but still. Now you cant even kill certain people, that are not related to story. You cant steal a car in your neighborhood. What if i wanted to? If my version of the character is a psycho and he wants to steal a car in a game called Grand Theft Auto?

GTA's have also always focused on social satire, dark humour and overkilling things and phenomenons. This is totally gone. I have not laughed once in this entire playthrough. Radiostations are not fun, dialogue is not fun, none of the characters in unhinged or funny. This feels very sanitized or cencored. Previous GTA's have always been a blast, and i have laughed so much playing them.

Story and character are also very weird. Lucia is very unlikable, and Jason is just the blandest character, with a weird voice acting. And for some reason, we must like Lucia, even after what she did. The writers could use a tip; make characters sympathetic or likeable, so players would actually care. Now i do not care at all.

From a technical side; 30fps is already very low on modern standards, and you can really see it now, since most games are 60fps. It really stands out, and not in a good way. But the worst part is that the 30 fps is target fps, not locked. On many many occasions the fps drops heavily, to like 15-20fps. It is very bad.

Overall; i think this GTA is a letdown, sadly. I feel like the essence, the soul of GTA phenomenon is gone. I do not know the reasons for that; but i can feel it. 

I wouldnt care, if the graphics were worse, if the story and gameplay felt as good as it did with previous GTA's. Now its the other way around, looks good on the outside but is very bad on the inside.

author: Rezu
quote:
Grand Theft Auto 6 — 0/10: This Is NOT Grand Theft Auto

I genuinely don't know what happened to Grand Theft Auto, but this is not the GTA I grew up playing.

First off, why am I spending the beginning **** Theft Auto game repairing somebody's house? I barely even know who these characters are, and I'm already being forced to do tedious chores. It took me longer than most people to get through that section, and it was incredibly annoying. Then the game has me going grocery shopping. Seriously? I'm playing GTA to experience crime, chaos, freedom, and an entertaining story, not to play some everyday-life simulator.

And then there's the ridiculous number of restrictions. You can't even pick up prostitutes anymore. You can't run over protesters. But here's the most ridiculous part: you can't even steal the cars in your own neighborhood!

Let that sink in. The game is literally called GRAND THEFT AUTO, and apparently, committing grand theft auto is off-limits in certain areas. How does that make any sense? Stealing cars is one of the most fundamental mechanics of this entire franchise. If I see a car parked in my neighborhood, why can't I steal it? Why are there suddenly all these arbitrary restrictions in a game that's supposed to be about freedom and criminal chaos?

There are so many roadblocks that it feels like the game is constantly telling you what you're allowed and not allowed to do. GTA used to be about giving players the freedom to do outrageous things in a fictional world. That's literally part of what made the franchise famous.

What really bothered me was the inconsistency. Apparently, you can shoot inside a regular nightclub, but not inside a gay nightclub. Why? I'm not asking for special treatment either way. I'm asking why a game that built its reputation on unrestricted, controversial gameplay suddenly has different rules depending on the location. It makes the world feel artificially restricted.

Then came the mission that finally made me quit. The game forces you into a gay strip club, where you have to sit through a lengthy sequence watching nearly naked men dance. At one point, there's a dude wearing a tiny pink G-string with his massive bulge practically shoved right in your face. Seriously, why am I being forced to sit through this? The worst part is that I couldn't skip it. Whether I tried first-person or third-person, I still had to play through it.

I don't care what kind of club it is. I don't want to be forced to sit through an uncomfortable strip club sequence that has nothing to do with why I bought the game, especially when there's no option to skip it.

What frustrates me most is that GTA used to be about player choice. You could explore, cause chaos, do ridiculous things, and enjoy a world that didn't constantly hold your hand or restrict your actions. Now it feels like I'm being forced through boring chores, selective restrictions, and uncomfortable missions instead of actually having fun.

I didn't buy Grand Theft Auto to repair houses, shop for groceries, or sit through unskippable strip club sequences. And I certainly didn't buy a game called Grand Theft Auto just to be told which cars I'm allowed to steal.

I bought it to play Grand Theft Auto.

Final score: 0/10.

I gave it a chance, but that strip club mission was the final straw. I stopped playing, and I have absolutely no desire to continue. For me, this game completely misses what made GTA special in the first place.

author: DDSDD83
quote:
GTA VI: The Taylor Swift of Gaming - Popularity Over Substance?

After years of hype, delays, and promises of an open world that would supposedly revolutionize gaming, GTA VI has arrived. The graphics are undeniably impressive, at least considering what current consoles can accomplish. But beautiful graphics don't automatically make a great game.

For a franchise built around freedom, Rockstar seems increasingly interested in restricting it. Certain locations and interactions limit what players can do in a supposedly unrestricted sandbox. Even the controversy surrounding planes crashing into buildings, although partly explained by vehicle damage settings, raises questions about how much environmental interactivity has actually advanced. Wasn't this supposed to redefine open-world gaming?

The story is arguably my biggest disappointment. It's the same tired Rockstar formula: predictable, heavily scripted storytelling that practically spoon-feeds players everything. Much like RDR2, there's little of the psychological complexity, layered mysteries, conflicting motivations, subtle foreshadowing, or revelations that fundamentally change how you understand earlier events.

I want stories that challenge me intellectually, that require me to connect the dots rather than simply watch everything unfold. Emotional storytelling and complex storytelling are two entirely different things. Rockstar seems exceptionally good at the former but rarely interested in the latter. It's another cinematic experience masquerading as narrative brilliance.

And the supposedly revolutionary open world? Games like Crimson Desert demonstrate that Rockstar isn't alone in creating enormous, ambitious environments. Map size doesn't automatically equal quality, but neither does filling a beautiful world with familiar mechanics and scripted activities. Where are the groundbreaking innovations we were promised?

There are some genuinely cool details, including Dexter Morgan's apartment. I appreciate those touches. But Easter eggs, impressive lighting, and environmental detail aren't substitutes for meaningful gameplay innovation.

Then there are the bugs. Seriously? After all those delays and an astronomical budget, GTA VI still suffers from ridiculous technical issues. GTA IV, V, and RDR2 were notorious for bizarre physics glitches, including characters, horses, and vehicles launching into the sky. Apparently, some traditions never die. Imagine what condition this game would've launched in without those delays.

And that 99 Metacritic score? Give me a break. Are we seriously supposed to believe this game is practically flawless? Look at the criticism coming from actual players. How much of the overwhelming praise reflects the game itself, and how much reflects Rockstar's reputation, marketing machine, and the industry's obsession with its biggest franchises?

Would this exact same game receive comparable praise if it came from an unknown developer? I seriously doubt it.

This isn't the Rockstar I remember from 1997. The original GTA was rebellious, unconventional, and genuinely different. GTA III fundamentally transformed the industry. Those games weren't simply popular; they helped redefine what gaming could be.

Today's Rockstar seems more interested in refining an established formula than taking comparable creative risks.

And we're still waiting for the PC version. Given Rockstar's history, I suspect the modding community will eventually accomplish more with GTA VI's potential than Rockstar itself. Look at what modders have done with GTA V over the years. Countless features, customization options, graphical improvements, and gameplay systems have originated from or been expanded by the community. Many innovations now commonplace in gaming were pioneered by modders long before major studios embraced them.

GTA VI has potential, absolutely. But that potential shouldn't depend on the community fixing its shortcomings and expanding its possibilities.

Ultimately, GTA VI feels like the Taylor Swift of gaming: massive commercial appeal, extraordinary production values, overwhelming critical praise, and a devoted audience that frequently mistakes popularity for artistic superiority.

Beautiful graphics aren't revolutionary gameplay. Cinematic storytelling isn't automatically sophisticated storytelling. An enormous budget doesn't guarantee creativity. And a 99 Metacritic score doesn't make a game immune to criticism.

Rockstar once revolutionized gaming. Now it seems content to dominate it.

GTA VI may become one of the biggest commercial successes in gaming history, but that doesn't automatically make it one of the greatest games ever created. And somehow, Rockstar may have managed to produce a campaign even less intellectually engaging than RDR2.

author: ssden
quote:
追記：残念なことにこのゲームのユーザーの一部は無関係なゼルダへ爆撃している。
一部と書いたがどうやらかなりの数のようだ。
そのため不本意だが私はこのゲームの評価を0にする。
この評価諸共ゼルダへの攻撃が消えることを願うよ。

自分が求めていたGTAではなかった。

長年待ち続けたシリーズ最新作だっただけに、非常に残念な作品だった。

まず、本作はグラフィックや演出、街並みの作り込み、NPCの描写など、技術的な完成度に力を入れていることは分かる。しかし、自分がGTAに求めていたのは、単にリアルで美しい世界を眺めたり、そこで生活したりすることではない。

GTAの魅力は、広大な世界で自分の意思で自由に行動し、犯罪を起こし、騒動を巻き起こし、強盗を計画し、警察との壮絶な追跡劇を繰り広げるなど、プレイヤー自身が遊び方を生み出せることにあったはずだ。

ところが、本作はリアリティや生活感を重視するあまり、肝心の自由なゲーム体験が後回しになっているように感じる。

特に気になるのが、生活シミュレーション的な要素の多さ。家の修繕、買い物、日常的な作業など、犯罪アクションを楽しみたいプレイヤーにとって必ずしも魅力的ではない要素が盛り込まれている。没入感を高めるためなのだろうが、こうした作業が増えれば増えるほど、ゲームを遊んでいるというより、ゲーム内の日常生活をこなしているような感覚になってしまう。

さらに、ストーリー進行による行動の制約や、解放されるまで自由に利用できない要素なども気になるところ。せっかくのオープンワールドなのに、プレイヤーが自分の意思で遊び始めるまでに、ストーリーや決められた手順に付き合わされる。自由を売りにしているシリーズとして、これは大きな疑問が残る。

主人公2人の関係性や日常を描くこと自体が悪いわけではない。しかし、恋愛や生活面の描写が前面に出過ぎて、犯罪者としての生き方や、自由に暴れ回るGTAらしい楽しさが薄れてしまっているように感じる。プレイヤーが物語の登場人物たちの行動を追うことと、プレイヤー自身が自由に犯罪者として遊ぶことは別物だ。

犯罪アクションについても、もっと大規模で自由度の高い強盗や、そのための準備、計画、実行、逃走といった一連の体験を期待していた。単に犯罪をこなすだけではなく、プレイヤーの判断や行動によって展開が変わるような面白さが欲しかった。

警察との追跡劇も同様で、ただ逃げ切るだけではなく、予測できない追跡や包囲網をどう突破するかという緊張感が重要だった。新しいシステムが導入されても、それによって従来作以上に面白い駆け引きが生まれているのかは疑問が残る。

そのほか、銃撃戦の操作感や序盤の進行テンポ、繰り返し感のある作業など、基本的なゲームプレイに対する不満もある。さらに、コンソール版の30fps上限や場面による処理落ちも、アクションゲームとして見過ごせない問題だと思う。

もちろん、リアリティを追求した作風を好む人もいるだろうし、本作の方向性そのものを評価する人がいることも理解できる。しかし、リアルな世界を作り込むことと、自由に遊べる面白いゲームを作ることは同じではない。

自分にとってGTAは、現実の生活を再現するためのゲームではなく、現実ではできないようなことを自由に楽しめる犯罪オープンワールドだった。

本作は、世界の表現や技術的な進化に注力する一方で、自分がシリーズに求めていた自由度、犯罪の爽快感、予測不能な混沌、そしてプレイヤー自身が遊びを作り出す楽しさとは、違う方向へ進んでしまったように思う。

どれだけ世界が精巧でも、そこで自分がやりたいことを自由に楽しめなければ意味がない。

これは単に期待外れだったというだけではない。自分が遊びたかったGTAとは根本的に違っていた。

残念ながら、今作をGTAとしては評価出来ない。

author: discordfa8
quote: I really wanted to love GTA 6, especially if you consider waiting so many years, but so far I'm completely disappointed. The graphics are crazy, the world looks very good and the technical work Rockstar has done deserves a lot of respect. But this alone doesn't make a great GTA game. The story and the overall direction of the game feel weird and don't fit into the series and this is a big Problem. It just doesn't feel like the GTA I grew up loving. GTA IV had Niko Bellic, a character with an actual past, personal struggles and a story that made you think. It was a unforgettable Story and full of immersion. GTA V had three completely different protagonists with their own personalities, problems and motivations. Both games had memorable characters, dark humor and that typical Rockstar atmosphere. With GTA 6 I don't get that same feeling, not even nearly. The whole Jason and Lucia relationship doesn't really interest me that much it feels completly wrong in the GTA series. It feels like Jason is a completly simp an you can feel that again and again moving on in the Story.  I understand what Rockstar is trying to do with the Bonnie and Clyde concept, but I personally expected something darker, more unpredictable and more focused on crime, betrayal and memorable characters. Instead, the direction feels way too focused on the relationship itself, and I don't get why they would do that. For me its fully predictable and boring. There are so many possible stories which are far more interesting. And also the restrictions in the Game are just ridiculous. My biggest problem is that Rockstar seems to be moving away from the offensive and politically incorrect humor that made GTA special. GTA used to make fun of absolutely everyone. Nobody was safe from its jokes, and that's exactly what I loved about it. I don't want GTA to feel like it has to be careful about offending people. I want morally questionable characters like Trevor, uncomfortable situations like with Niko, dark humor and a story that isn't afraid to go too far. That's what made the older games stand out. Honestly, one of the few things that genuinely got me excited again was seeing Niko Bellic return. To this day, he's one of the best characters Rockstar has ever written. His Story was one of the most outstanding and memorable in the whole GTA series. Maybe I'm just expecting too much because of how much the older Games meant to me. But after such a long wait, I wanted more than an incredibly realistic open world. I wanted a story and characters that could stand alongside GTA IV, GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2. The technical Achievement alone is without question outstanding, and probably no other game could reach this level. But as someone who cares more about storytelling, atmosphere and memorable characters than graphics, I think the direction Rockstar is going in is very bad and could destroy the series. For me, GTA 6 is the best GTA ever made if you just look at graphics and technical achievements, but it doesn't really feel like the GTA I know. And that's the most disappointing part.

author: Honorius96
quote:
60 hours in, since the very first minute of launch, I finally finished GTA 6. And the ending made it even worse. I’ll be fair: the graphics are amazing and Vice City is the most detailed city ever built. But that’s where it ends.
The gangster vibe is gone. This feels more like a feminist relationship story than a GTA game: 
Rockstar turned Jason into a simp. You buy Lucia flowers, fix Mandy’s sink, run her errands and keep her happy, or your relationship meter drops. Mandy flirts with Jason, the game gives you dialogue choices, and then nothing happens, because Rockstar says cheating isn’t “complementary to the feeling and motivations” of the story. Hookers are gone for the first time since GTA 3, and you can’t steal the best cars until Chapter 3.
5 chapters, 91 missions, and most of them are chores. Chapter 2 is pure filler. 
The final act is about a hard drive with dirt on a senator. Then the cops trap Jason and Lucia on a bridge, and you get one choice: don’t surrender and they die in the car holding hands, or surrender and Jason goes to prison while Lucia walks free with her son. The best ending is locked behind a full relationship meter and $2 million in savings. After the credits, the game just rewinds and asks if you’re “ready” again. Cheat codes only unlock after the last mission, when there’s nothing left to do. No mission replay, only 15 save slots, $100 fast travel, and it’s locked at 30 FPS, even on PS5 Pro.
Rockstar calls it a love story. I call it a babysitting job with a wanted level. 13 years and 100€, and the payoff is a choice between dying and prison.

author: tenokami
quote: If you've been waiting 13 years for the next Rockstar game, this is not it. What you get instead of the razor-sharp satire, chaotic freedom, and unforgettable characters you expect from Rockstar is a sanitized, chore-heavy experience that feels like a different franchise wearing a GTA logo. The biggest problem is Jason — a cardboard cutout with short, generic lines, no edge, no humor, no personality, who exists entirely to support Lucia's bratty attitude, doing her groceries, buying her flowers, and managing her emotions like a total cu*k. Rockstar frontloads the entire opening with this relationship simulator; before the actual crime stuff kicks in, you're stuck in an on-the-rails "good boyfriend" routine that's a huge turn-off for anyone who wanted the classic GTA chaos. What is genuinely great: The visual detail and gameplay variety — the world is jaw-droppingly detailed and the most realistic Rockstar has ever built.

author: followedforgo
quote: I waited 13 **** years for this ****. Thirteen years of rumours, leaks, trailers and hype. I preordered it, paid $125 AUD for the standard edition on PS5, and counted down the days like everyone else. Now I'm about halfway through, and this is the most disappointed I've ever been in a game. I wanted a crime fantasy and got a life simulator. I play games to get away from reality, not to go back into the same **** with better **** don't really play this game, you obey it. Everything revolves around Lucia. Her needs come first, her storyline comes first, and Jason follows along like he's lucky to be there. Sure, you can technically ignore her, but the game punishes you for it, so it's not really a choice. You're constantly unloading her groceries, buying her flowers and keeping her happy. After a few hours it feels like I'm being trained to say "yes dear." It should be called Simp Sim **** worst of all are the scenes where nothing happens. Sometimes you literally just watch Jason and Lucia watch TV and watch Jason rub Lucia's feet like a good little slave. This is the series where you used to rob banks, blow things up and cause chaos across an entire city. Now I'm sitting through foot rubs that go on forever. I spent more time watching long, boring scenes than playing the game I paid for. Then there's the "realism." Somebody at Rockstar decided GTA fans really wanted to shop for groceries. You come home from work in real life, turn on the game, and start working all over again: errands, chores, upkeep, relationship stuff. I already have a real life with real chores, and it doesn't cost $125. When I do try to have fun the old-fashioned way, the game stops me. I tried to steal a car, the woman inside had a panic attack, and the game wouldn't let me take it. Let that sink in. In a game literally called Grand Theft Auto, I couldn't steal a car because a woman had a tantrum. That sums up everything wrong here. The core of the series has been sanded down so nobody gets upset. That's why there's barely any real action. Chores, cutscenes and relationship maintenance keep slowing you down, and when action does come, it feels like a break from the real game, which is apparently being a good boyfriend. And it isn't funny. GTA used to be crude, vulgar and hilarious, offensive in a way that made you laugh out loud. The radio, the side characters, the satire. GTA 6 took the safe route. There's no vulgar humour and nothing that made me laugh, like it was written by people terrified of offending anyone.This is where it lost me completely. The whole game feels like it was made by women who hate men. Jason works, takes orders and puts up with everything, and the game wants you to see that as the ideal. It feels like the people who made it want men to be slaves: do the chores, keep her happy, never get angry. GTA used to be a power fantasy. This one feels like a **** characters don't help. Michael, Franklin and Trevor from GTA 5 were chaotic, funny and unpredictable. Trevor alone had more personality than this entire cast. GTA 6's characters just ****, and halfway through I still don't care about any of them.I'll give it one thing: the graphics are quite beautiful. But that doesn't make up for all the bad. It's locked at 30 FPS on console, not even the PS5 Pro gets more, and paying $125 for 30 frames per second in 2026 is absolutely horrible. The driving is horrible too, which is unforgivable in a series where you spend so much time behind the wheel.There's also no online and no co-op. Nothing. GTA Online kept GTA 5 alive for over a decade and came out two weeks after launch. GTA 6 is single-player only, and Rockstar hasn't even given a date for online. You can't even escape the boyfriend simulator by jumping into a lobby with your friends.People will point to the nearly $4 billion it made on launch day. But that's mostly preorders from people like me who bought into 13 years of hype before knowing what we'd get. Sales show how good the marketing was, not the game. And for a game that reportedly cost well over a billion dollars to make, with estimates running into the billions, this is what we got.Then there's the media. Rolling Stone ran a piece tagged "Chudpocalypse" about gamers who don't like being forced to be nice to their girlfriend. Newsweek wrote that in GTA 6, "the ultimate male fantasy is being a good boyfriend." Not liking a game's design doesn't make you a chud or mean you want to disrespect women in real life. It's a video game called Grand Theft Auto. I didn't wait 13 years for a relationship lesson. I wanted Grand Theft Auto. It's beautiful, expensive and hollow. Rockstar made a game that seems to look down on the people who've bought GTA for almost 30 years, a life simulator when people wanted a crime sandbox. If you want to do chores, follow orders and rub someone's feet, real life does that for free. Do yourself a favour and play GTA 5 again.

author: Smoochoo
quote:
I have been playing this franchise since GTA 1 on Game Boy came out. I always loved and genuinely looked forward to it.
Now, I expected so much more after 13 years.
The game is full of bugs and glitches, which I have gotten used to in recent years, but I expected more from Rockstar and GTA 6.
There is nothing worth being called funny in this game. Been playing for 40 hours and have yet to laugh once. In comparison to GTA 5, that's a real downgrade. GTA 6 is just full of Gen Z content, that most people don't even think falls into the category of funny.
You can't even steal cars in your area, which...I mean, it's called Grand Theft Auto for a reason!?
The controls are horribly sluggish, as was expected from 30 fps but they couldn't even hold that promise, since in some situations I had low 20 fps.
You are stuck doing tedious relationship stuff for hours to keep your relationship going. I have a wife, I'd rather do that for her than for a poroly animated, ugly, male-looking character, with an insufferable personality. It seems Rockstar wanted to make a girl boss game. Mission accomplished. Pair that with the submissive beta male they call Jason and you get...I don't know what. All I can say is this is not GTA. GTA doesn't make you drywall in a way no one ever drywalled in real life, buy groceries, paint, massage feet and build IKEA furniture just to progress the game.
Enough said about the story, which in my view is a complete failure. Onto the graphics; I don't know about others, but I expected a way bigger graphical leap than what they delivered. I also don't see that improving more when it comes to PC. It just looks like GTA 5 but sligthly better.
I guess my question is what has Rockstar been doing for 13 years? Was the goal to piggyback entirely on the goodwill GTA 5 and GTA online established over the years?
And all that screeching about realism. Gamers never wanted realism in games. We play games to have an escape from reality. But when you actually wanna deliver something realistic, then atleast see it through, i.e. disappering airplanes, one handed shotgun, drywalling, furniture assembly and so on. 
What I really woulda loved was a return to player agency, i.e. if you find Lucia utterly insufferable, ignore her, kill her, get antoher girlfriend, and so on.
So, if you want a dating simulator, go for it. If you want a GTA game, I don't know what to tell you...hope they don't take another decade or abandon the story experience of GTA and do a better job next time around? As for me, this has soured me on Rockstar. 
I wish I could get my money back but since it's Playstation I guess I have to be happy with posting my honest thoughts about the game and take the loss.

author: Enzoka
quote:
GTA 6 é uma piada que demorou quase uma década para ser contada. Um jogo que virou símbolo da decadência da paciência humana, sustentado por trailers cinematográficos, promessas e uma comunidade completamente incapaz de distinguir expectativa de qualidade. A Rockstar parece ter descoberto a fórmula perfeita: não lançar absolutamente nada durante anos e ainda ser tratada como a maior desenvolvedora da história.

E o mais engraçado é assistir aos fãs defendendo o jogo como se tivessem recebido uma cópia antecipada diretamente de Deus. Os caras analisam três segundos de uma poça d'água e chamam isso de revolução tecnológica. Meu irmão, é um videogame, não um estudo da NASA sobre o comportamento dos fluidos.

GTA 6 carrega tanto hype nas costas que, se não reinventar a existência humana, vai ser considerado decepcionante por metade da comunidade. São anos de espera para, no fim, provavelmente dirigir, atirar, fugir da polícia e cometer crimes virtuais, exatamente como nos jogos anteriores. Mas agora com reflexos melhores na lataria do carro, aparentemente o ápice da evolução humana.

A Rockstar transformou o lançamento de um jogo em um evento geológico. Daqui a pouco será necessário consultar um calendário arqueológico para descobrir quando GTA 6 finalmente saiu. E os fãs? Continuam ajoelhados diante de uma empresa que descobriu que pode fazer qualquer coisa, demorar o tempo que quiser e ainda receber aplausos.

GTA 6 não é um jogo, é um experimento social sobre até onde uma comunidade consegue levar a própria ilusão. E o pior é que, quando lançar, vai vender milhões mesmo que venha com uma bicicleta e dois postes.

author: manrigoggs
quote:
30 hours in and the technical side is genuinely impressive. The graphics, animations, sound design, and the living, detailed world are spectacular — Rockstar still knows how to build a city that feels alive.

Everything else is a letdown.

The story is the weakest the series has ever had. The first couple of chapters are just endless drug trafficking runs back and forth with almost no momentum. Half the missions feel like busywork. The only consistently fun activities are the store robberies; everything else is a slog. Compared to the characters we actually remember — Niko, Trevor, Michael, CJ — Jason comes off as a flat, personality-deficient cuck. There’s no edge, no memorable presence, just a bland lead in a game that keeps trying to feel progressive and “modern.”

The selective morality is especially pathetic. You can mow down unlimited cops with zero consequence, but anything involving certain protected groups or protesters is apparently off-limits. It reeks **** made to tick boxes rather than deliver the chaotic, equal-opportunity mayhem GTA used to be known for. At times it feels closer to a dating sim with open-world window dressing than a proper Grand Theft Auto.

Boring main story, watered-down tone, and a protagonist who makes you miss the old psychopaths. Not worth the price if you’re coming for the classic GTA experience.
