author: Moiwen
quote:
After playing GTA VI, I honestly can't understand how so many critics are giving this game a perfect 99/100. I went into it with high expectations, especially considering Rockstar's reputation, the enormous development budget, and all the years we've waited for this game. Unfortunately, what I got was a huge disappointment.

I'll give credit where it's due. The graphics are impressive, the world looks beautiful, and the level of visual detail is incredible. But graphics alone don't make a great game, and they certainly shouldn't be enough to justify a perfect score.

My biggest problem is the lack of freedom.

GTA has always been about exploring a massive open world, experimenting, causing chaos, and doing things your own way. Yet in GTA VI, I constantly feel like the game is telling me what I can and cannot do.

For example, there are certain NPCs, including activist characters, that I can't attack or shoot. I'm not saying attacking those characters should be the purpose of the game. My point is that when a sandbox game starts placing arbitrary restrictions on which fictional characters you can interact with, it breaks the illusion of freedom.

The relationship system is another major disappointment.

From what I've experienced, the only intimate relationship option outside of Lucia involves a male ex-partner. Why are the choices so limited? Why can't I pursue other relationships, be unfaithful, or interact with adult characters in different ways?

I'm not against the existence of same-sex relationships in video games. What bothers me is feeling that certain creative or ideological decisions are being prioritized over player freedom. I don't want Rockstar deciding which relationships I should explore. I want meaningful choices and the freedom to make them myself.

For a game that constantly emphasizes realism and freedom, the actual possibilities feel surprisingly restricted.

Then there are the physics.

The game looks realistic in screenshots and trailers, but the illusion often falls apart when you actually interact with the world. Some physical interactions simply don't feel convincing. It's frustrating to see so much attention given to visual details while other fundamental aspects of gameplay feel underdeveloped.

I've also encountered plenty of bugs, which makes those perfect review scores even harder to understand. How can a game with noticeable technical problems receive a flawless rating?

Performance is another issue. We're in 2026, and GTA VI is still limited to 30 FPS on PS5 Pro. I understand that a massive open world requires considerable processing power, but that doesn't mean performance should suddenly stop being part of the evaluation.

Other games have been criticized for failing to reach 60 FPS, suffering frame drops, or having optimization problems. Why should GTA VI be treated differently?

And then there's the story.

Despite the enormous budget and technological advances, we're still dealing with a largely linear narrative. I expected more meaningful decisions, different outcomes, and greater control over how the story develops.

A beautiful open world doesn't automatically mean a game offers genuine freedom. You can explore an enormous map and still feel restricted by its systems.

What disappoints me most is that Rockstar had the resources, time, and experience to push the genre much further. Instead, I feel like too much attention went into presentation while some of the things that actually matter to me as a player were neglected.

And this brings me to professional reviews.

I'm tired of seeing inconsistent standards in gaming journalism. Some games lose points for technical limitations, bugs, restrictive mechanics, or a lack of innovation, while others seem almost immune to criticism because of their name and reputation.

If a reviewer gives GTA VI a perfect 100/100 while acknowledging significant shortcomings, I think they owe readers a convincing explanation of why those shortcomings don't affect the final score.

I'm not claiming every positive review is dishonest, and I'm not saying people shouldn't enjoy this game. But I do believe that professional critics should be consistent, transparent, and willing to judge every game by comparable standards.

A massive budget doesn't guarantee quality. A famous developer doesn't guarantee innovation. And impressive graphics don't automatically make a game a masterpiece.I wanted GTA VI to be extraordinary. 

I wanted a world that felt genuinely alive, with believable physics, meaningful interactions, freedom to experiment, and a level of technical polish worthy of its reputation.

Instead, I got a visually stunning game that feels far more limited than I expected.

For me, GTA VI is a massive disappointment. Not because it has nothing good to offer, but because it had the potential to be so much more.

And that's exactly why I can't agree with those perfect scores.

4/10 – Starke Grafik, aber überteuert und spielerisch enttäuschend.
Die 4 Punkte gibt es fast nur für die Grafik, denn optisch ist GTA 6 wirklich beeindruckend. Das nützt aber wenig, wenn das Spiel auf Konsole bei 30 FPS festsitzt und auf der normalen PS5 in actionreichen Szenen sogar darunter fällt. Einen Performance-Modus gibt es nicht. Auch nach fünf Stunden fühlt sich das zäh an.Dazu kommt der Preis: 80 € für die Standard-Edition, 100 € für die Ultimate Edition. Beim Kauf wird außerdem gleich das GTA+-Abo beworben, das sich nach dem Gratismonat automatisch um 7,99 € pro Monat verlängert.

Der 99er-Wertung der Kritiker traue ich absolut nicht. Rockstar ist seit Jahren dafür bekannt, sehr genau zu steuern, wer Testmuster bekommt. Ein ehemaliger Rockstar-PR-Mitarbeiter hat öffentlich erzählt, dass bei der Vergabe der Testmuster auch zählt, wer vorher negativ berichtet hatte. Ob das bei GTA 6 eine Rolle gespielt hat, kann ich nicht beweisen, die Vermutung steht aber wie ein Elefant im Raum. Wirklich unabhängig ist dieses System definitiv nicht. 
Mein Rat: Verlasst euch nicht auf die Zahl, schaut euch vor dem Kauf selbst Gameplay an.

Inhaltlich hat sich GTA viel zu weit von seinen Wurzeln entfernt. Statt Chaos und Freiheit verbringe ich viel Zeit mit Alltagskram wie Wohnung renovieren und Einkaufen für die Beziehung. Prostituierte hat Rockstar komplett gestrichen, und alles dreht sich um die glückliche Beziehung zwischen Jason und Lucia. Das kann man gut finden, mit dem anarchischen GTA von früher hat es aber nichts zu tun.

author: Gpro784
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI — A Beautiful World With a Bland Soul

My Rating: 5/10

GTA VI is one of the most visually impressive and detailed open-world games I have ever played, but unfortunately, that alone isn’t enough to make it a great Grand Theft Auto game for **** graphics are absolutely incredible. The world feels alive, the NPCs are packed with detail, the environmental interactions are amazing, and simply driving around Vice City and exploring Leonida is a genuinely impressive experience. Rockstar has created a world that feels like it could exist beyond the player’s screen. The amount of detail in the streets, vehicles, crowds and surroundings is insane.Free roaming is easily the best part of this game. I can spend hours just driving around, watching NPCs, exploring random locations and enjoying the world without even touching a mission. The driving feels great, the shooting is enjoyable, and the overall gameplay has plenty of **** here’s the problem: the world is incredible, while the story and characters feel disappointingly **** story so far feels more like a relationship drama than the outrageous criminal adventure I expected from GTA. Jason and Lucia are not particularly memorable to me, and the supporting cast feels forgettable. The dialogue lacks the sharpness, personality and absurdity that made previous GTA characters so entertaining.Trevor, Michael and Franklin had distinct personalities. Trevor was completely unhinged, Michael was sarcastic and miserable in an entertaining way, and Franklin had his own ambition and attitude. Even when those characters were doing ordinary things, their conversations and personalities made the experience **** VI’s characters haven’t given me that same feeling. I don’t need every character to be a psychopath like Trevor, but I want characters who are genuinely memorable, entertaining and unpredictable. So far, the cast feels too bland for a game of this **** mission design is another major disappointment. Too many missions feel like errands, with mundane activities and unnecessary tasks taking up time before anything exciting happens. Instead of immediately feeling like a criminal living in a chaotic GTA world, I often feel like I’m doing chores for people I barely care about.I don’t mind slower moments when they build characters or lead to something meaningful. But when the characters themselves aren’t interesting enough, those slower moments become boring rather than immersive.I also miss the classic GTA atmosphere. The older games had a certain irreverent, outrageous and unapologetically chaotic personality. The humour was sharper, the characters were crazier, and the criminal fantasy felt much more entertaining. GTA VI feels more grounded and relationship-focused, but for me, that direction has taken away some of the series’ old soul.I wanted memorable criminals, hilarious side characters, outrageous situations, big heists and that classic Rockstar madness. Instead, I find myself enjoying the world far more than the actual **** be clear, I don’t think GTA VI is a bad game because it has a realistic world or a relationship between its protagonists. My problem is that the writing, characters and mission structure haven’t made that direction interesting enough for **** game has a fantastic foundation. The graphics are 10/10, the open world is 10/10, the NPCs and environmental interactions are 10/10, and free-roam gameplay is incredibly enjoyable. But the story and mission design are nowhere near that level for me.A game can be technically brilliant and still fail to connect with the player emotionally or **** VI is a breathtaking sandbox that I love exploring, but a disappointing Grand Theft Auto story that I struggle to care about.Final Verdict: 5/10An incredible open world trapped behind a bland story, forgettable characters and too many boring missions. I enjoy living in this world far more than I enjoy following its story.

author: Vuvy
quote:
Grand Theft Auto 2077? 
A game anticipated for an entire decade, with an estimated development period of 7–13 years and a budget of approximately $2 billion, only to end up being released exclusively on two console platforms, particularly favoring PlayStation due to its licensing agreements.

Rockstar has invested heavily in advertising and promotion, while reviews appear to be disproportionately favorable. There are concerns about potential conflicts of interest and criticism being influenced by companies seeking to favor GTA VI's Metacritic score.

The story is rather mediocre compared to GTA V, or even San Andreas, and if we go further back, Chinatown Wars.

After years of anticipation and promises, the game risks becoming another Cyberpunk-like situation, plagued by bugs such as falling through the map, getting stuck in the environment, or being launched into the air while driving a vehicle.

The game has its ups and downs, and its only major strengths are its random events and impressive graphics. Its physics are inferior to those of GTA IV, and numerous technical issues significantly affect the experience.

Immersion is also reduced by the removal of the first-person mode, a feature that should have remained from GTA V. Ironically, there are even glitches that allow players to access first-person mode, effectively providing a workaround for something that should never have been removed in the first place.

Furthermore, Rockstar has invested heavily in promotional campaigns involving content creators, websites, and major companies, including Google, Discord, YouTube, and many others.

In my opinion, GTA VI does not deserve a score higher than 97. Considering all these criticisms, my personal rating is 4/10.

quote: It is truly inspiring to see Rockstar Games take such a bold, brave stance against entertainment. The storyline is a masterclass in narrative confusion, bravely abandoning logic and coherence in favour of absolute nonsense. Of course, the real stars are the characters, who have been meticulously engineered to be as unlikable as humanly possible. The male protagonist is a triumph of minimalist acting, offering the emotional range of a damp sponge as he mumbles his way through the plot and obediently follows every instruction without a single original thought. As for the female lead, words simply fail to capture her brilliance—mostly because the less said about her, the better for everyone’s sanity. Ultimately, this masterpiece is the inevitable result of handing over character development and storytelling to progressive woke women who clearly know far better than actual gamers what constitutes fun. It is a truly awful triumph that will be studied for generations as the ultimate cure for insomnia.

author: Alicsen34
quote:
A Beautiful World With Very Little to Say

GTA VI has an impressive world, but sometimes I feel like the developers spent more time creating things to look at than things to actually experience.


The city is full of details, but what is the point of all these details when the actual gameplay feels so outdated?

There is a strange contrast between the living world and the very basic game mechanics.

The combat is probably the biggest disappointment. Everything feels too easy and unrealistic. You can almost destroy an entire military base on your own. You are basically a one-man army. It doesn’t make any sense and completely destroys the immersion. Even the enemies feel more like targets than actual people.

The missions are another problem. There is very little creativity. Most of the time you just follow instructions, shoot some people and move on. After a while it becomes boring.

The story also feels surprisingly empty. There is a huge world outside, full of different people and social realities, but the game doesn’t seem to have much to say about any of it. Everything is there to make the world look alive, not necessarily to tell something meaningful.

And maybe this is my biggest problem with GTA VI. It has all the money, technology and resources to create something really special, but it feels like the ambition ends with making everything bigger and more detailed.

Final Verdict: GTA VI is a technically impressive game, but technical ambition and good game design are not the same thing. A living world means very little when the actual experience inside it feels so lifeless.Open world design will not save the game.

author: Junkgodx
quote:
Después de más de una década de espera, retrasos múltiples y un desarrollo que se alargó hasta volverse casi inmanejable, GTA 6 llega a PS5 y Xbox Series X|S como un producto inflado, técnicamente comprometido y artísticamente desorientado. Lo que se presenta como el pináculo de la ambición de Rockstar es, en la práctica, un monstruo de producción que se comió a sí mismo.

Un desarrollo sin dirección clara 
No hay una visión artística nítida que unifique todo. Hay detalle técnico descomunal y una ciudad densamente poblada, pero también una sensación de que se fueron añadiendo capas porque “podían”, no porque hicieran falta. El ritmo narrativo se alarga innecesariamente, las misiones principales a menudo se sienten como seguir órdenes en lugar de tener agencia real, y el tono oscila entre el realismo pesado al estilo Red Dead Redemption 2 y el caos sandbox clásico sin decidirse del todo. El resultado es un juego que parece diseñado por comité de sistemas más que por una dirección creativa con criterio.

Problemas técnicos de lanzamiento que no se pueden ignorar
Bloqueo a 30 fps en todas las consolas (incluida PS5 Pro). En 2026 esto es una decisión de diseño cuestionable que se nota especialmente al conducir y en persecuciones densas. Hay caídas por debajo de 15 en zonas cargadas. Bugs de lanzamiento clásicos pero molestos: personajes que caen a través del mapa, clipping a través de paredes y objetos, físicas rotas (coches que salen volando, aviones que atraviesan edificios), crashes en el prólogo y softlocks que obligan a reiniciar misiones.Tamaño de instalación brutal (alrededor de 210 GB) y copias físicas que son solo códigos de descarga.Criticos le dieron 99. Los jugadores están mucho más divididos (user scores en torno a 5-5.5 en los primeros días). La discrepancia no es casual: los builds de prensa y la experiencia real de millones de usuarios en el día uno no son lo mismo.

Las políticas internas de Rockstar (las que importan)
Aquí está el problema de fondo. Rockstar ha mantenido durante años una cultura de producción que prioriza la entrega de “el juego que queremos hacer” por encima de casi todo. Eso incluye:Contratos con opt-out de las regulaciones de tiempo de trabajo, facilitando horas extras **** sistema de bonuses opaco y variable que puede representar una parte importante del salario anual y que se gestiona de forma inconsistente entre departamentos.Acusaciones de brechas salariales y de usar los bonuses como herramienta de control.Despidos masivos (34 trabajadores en 2025) por compartir información confidencial en un Discord, en medio de un proceso de sindicalización. El tribunal laboral sigue abierto y las versiones de las partes chocan (la empresa habla de infracción grave de confidencialidad; los trabajadores de represalia).Estas políticas no son anecdóticas. Cuando un estudio de este tamaño y presupuesto tiene problemas crónicos de definición de alcance, de cierre de producción y de gestión del talento, el producto final termina pagando el precio: bloat, sistemas que no terminan de pulirse del todo, y una sensación de que el juego se lanzó porque había que lanzarlo, no porque estuviera realmente terminado según los propios estándares históricos de la casa.

Mi conclusion respecto al juego es

GTA 6 es técnicamente ambicioso, pero carece de dirección artística clara. El desarrollo se descontroló, los sistemas se hincharon hasta volverse difíciles de cerrar y el resultado se siente más como un monstruo de producción que como un juego con visión. A esto se suma el bloqueo a 30 fps, los bugs de lanzamiento y, especialmente, la polémica del formato físico: la caja solo contiene un código de descarga para un juego de más de 200 GB. El “físico” se ha convertido en un engaño.Estas decisiones no son anecdóticas. Reflejan políticas internas de Rockstar (alcance desmedido, presión laboral prolongada y priorización del control digital) que terminan trasladándose al consumidor en forma de precios altos, instalaciones enormes, limitaciones técnicas y la imposibilidad real de poseer el producto.Para la industria, el mensaje es peligroso: se puede inflar el alcance, retrasar, vaciar el formato físico y mantener estructuras conflictivas sin un castigo de mercado significativo. Mientras el público mayoritario siga priorizando el hype y la escala por encima de la coherencia, el pulido y el respeto al comprador, estas prácticas se consolidarán como el nuevo estándar.2/10.

author: Tohoder
quote: I waited 13 years for this game. 13 years of pure anticipation, all while being sold on a rumored $2 billion budget. And now I’m sitting here, genuinely struggling to comprehend what Rockstar has done to Grand Theft Auto. It honestly feels like they completely sold the soul of this franchise.What we ended up getting has nothing to do with the GTA we grew up loving. It feels like a watered down version of The Sims in a 3D look. The violence has been noticeably toned down, the sharp, dark humor is gone, and at every corner you can tell how desperately they tried not to offend anyone. It has become so overly "woke" and overly cautious that all its edge is gone. You get punished in a gangster game for actually acting like a criminal, you aren't even allowed to pull a weapon inside clubs anymore, and instead you’re pushed into playing out mundane relationship chores. Everything GTA used to stand for that uncompromising freedom and biting social satire—is just **** top of that, there is the technical state of the game, which strangely nobody seems to be talking about openly. The game is riddled with bugs, glitches, and crashes. When I think back to how games like Cyberpunk 2077, The Witcher 3, or MindsEye were torn apart at launch for their technical issues, I simply don't understand the double standard here. With any other developer, there would be massive outrage but because it has the Rockstar logo on it, the gaming press is suddenly silent and handing out 10/10s, while we are stuck dealing with sluggish controls and 30 FPS even on the PS5 Pro. What hurts the most, though, is the wasted potential. 13 years of development and a $2 billion budget with those resources, they could have changed gaming forever and given us a truly limitless world straight out of Ready Player One. Instead, we got a buggy, censored game that, underneath it all, just feels like a slightly better-looking GTA V. I am genuinely disappointed, and I will be requesting a refund.

author: SaarMichi
quote:
I’ve finished the story now, and one question comes to mind: how much did Rockstar pay for these positive reviews? The controls are absolute garbage; the vehicles feel incredibly floaty. The bugs in the game are reminiscent of the *Cyberpunk* launch—I fell through the floor three times in just 30 minutes! I’d be driving along normally, and suddenly the tires would just vanish. Planes fly right through buildings, and a dumpster next to me spontaneously exploded. As for the story, it’s told in a very boring way; the beginning, in particular, is so slow-paced that you have to fight to stay awake. The plot is also highly predictable—it’s okay, I suppose, but it’s nothing you haven’t seen a hundred times before in movies. Then there’s the mission design: the missions just repeat themselves over and over, and in between, you’re expected to perform mundane, everyday chores? I play games to escape daily life—I don’t need to be renovating apartments in a video game. And let’s address what is perhaps the biggest point of criticism for many: the 30 fps cap. I’ve accepted that the game is locked to 30 fps—even though that’s completely outdated for 2026—but when the frame rate drops well below 15 fps, even on a PS5 Pro, it’s an absolute joke. To be fair, I should mention the positives: the graphics look very good, though they don’t quite live up to what Rockstar promised in their trailers. The thing is, though, graphics are the least important aspect of any video game.
The map is massive, yet most of the action takes place in only a small portion of it; they would have been better off including a smaller map in exchange for a higher frame rate.
Verdict: the worst *GTA* of all time.

author: Lupin_3
quote:
I've rarely been this disappointed in my entire life. I was eagerly looking forward to this game, and it falls far short of my expectations.

The game crashed four times in 20 hours, on top of being incredibly buggy (not quite as bad as CP2077, but still the buggiest PS5 game I've played this year, if not since I got the console). GTA V's launch was pretty rough too, but what about Red Dead Redemption 1 and 2, or GTA IV? I don't remember them having these kinds of issues.

The gameplay is sometimes painfully slow, if not downright tedious. Controls have been changed after 25 years for seemingly no reason. NPCs overreact to absolutely everything and are generally less intelligent than those in RDR2 (stealth is an absolute joke: NPCs are just as incompetent as those in Marvel's Spider-Man. You can practically stand right next to them and they still won't notice you).

The physics are rather inconsistent. They're supposed to feel "realistic" and weighty, yet you somehow remain glued to your seat when driving a scooter down a mountain or practically going vertical on a bridge.

When it comes to certain vehicles, particularly planes and helicopters, there's no denying the regression in handling, controls and physics compared to previous games. It's as if Rockstar tried to imitate GTA IV without actually having the engine or technical expertise they had back then.

And of course, 30 FPS in freaking 2026 is simply unforgivable, Rockstar or not. It's embarrassing! To make matters worse, I've just learned that the PC version might also be capped at 30 FPS because the game's spawning system is supposedly tied to the frame rate. Absolutely unbelievable!

So, where are those 80 hours journalists wouldn't stop talking about? I finished the campaign in 48 hours, taking my time to explore and completing a few side missions along the way.

The story and characters are, by far, the worst in the entire franchise so far. I was promised an emotional experience, but all I got was boredom and complete indifference towards practically everything. Not a single genuinely funny or outrageous moment like in previous entries. Every single dialogue was either painfully awkward or terribly written and forced (Jason's voice certainly doesn't help).

The good ending is, in a way, even worse than GTA V's Option C. Jason and Lucia are the blandest, least interesting characters in the entire franchise, with absolutely no chemistry whatsoever (even Trevor and Michael looked like soulmates in comparison). Being forced to put them together, with no alternative path to explore, certainly doesn't help either.

Honestly, the graphics are this game's biggest saving grace, and even then, pretending to be completely blown away by them as if they were something groundbreaking or, to quote the most "OBJECTIVE" video game journalists in the universe, "REVOLUTIONARY, 100/10", after the release of Death Stranding 2, The Last of Us Part II and plenty of other titles over the past few years, would simply be hypocritical of me.

I'm not some hater or whatever people will probably call me just because I didn't give the most hyped game of the moment a 100/10.

Is my rating harsher than what I would give an indie game made on a shoestring budget? Yes, probably. But treating a Rockstar Games title, with a budget of over a billion dollars, thousands of developers working across the globe, more than eight years of development and an aggressive marketing campaign selling us the greatest gaming experience of all time, as some kind of masterpiece simply because it's good — or even technically excellent — despite being nowhere near as fun as its more arcade-oriented predecessors, is absolute nonsense.

You don't get a dopamine rush from repainting the walls of your virtual house or screwing wooden planks onto your virtual home.

P.S.: I would've given it a 8 or an 9 if we could've replaced Lucia with Mandy. 

Funny how little it takes to make some people happy...

A great open world cannot save everything else.

Extremely disappointing.
It lost its identity, no GTA style humor, very tame, mostly mundane characters and “small talk” type interactions. No pushing and pulling like with Lamar and Franklin, Trevor and Micheal or a lack of funny side characters like Simeon, the Yogi, Tracy, Jimmy, Franklins aunt etc. The main characters have nothing going for them expect being unreasonably hot for criminals, the look like they’re main casts for love island fss.

I don’t understand how nobody thought to hire someone to improve on this. GTA isn’t just a crime simulator, it has its own identity and the new team didn’t understand it in 13 years of development.
Honestly wished I was there to help them not **** this up.

Gameplan mechanics are to much RDR2, the slo-mo headshots are really horrible, the new camera angle isn’t good, cars are a pain to drive and it’s stressful, they don’t break and are extreme slippery (should add customizable driving physics like how much grip, braking power you want, GTA V was extremely fun because it was really arcade-like.), no first person mode is a shame. Like a big one this game looks really **** beautiful and not having an in car/boat pov is just lazy.

Mission design is the second biggest problem, it’s too repetitive, the pacing is really slow and you have to do 5-6 chores like missions the get one interesting cutscene/mission. It’s just not enough, you can’t play a mostly humorless, really taxing game for hours just to have a few minutes where you go “**** yeah this is gta”.

Should’ve crapped a third of the first chapter and added more fun missions.

The Bonny and Clyde thing is alright but it’s way to much 2k26 relationship sim and not enough crazy in love, ride or die. I mean one of them being silent and mild is okay but both of the characters are just painfully normal. Franklin was fun and had something to him, Micheal was an **** but a fun one and Trevor just was one of the most fun pop culture characters ever.

What I would wish for:

GTAV camera settings, GTAV driving physics in the options or at least an option to decide between “classic” gta driving or modern.
Turning headshot slo-mo’s off.
A option for a little less aggressive cop system at least when you just steal a car.
First person mode in vehicles, no “you need the money on your card to buy this upgrade” situations, it’s just pointless to have to abort tuning just to put cash into the atm, there is a point where realism just **** I mean at this point you could set a limit of 5k a month before the IRS comes questioning and blocks your account. 
Jason’s eye color looks like he got on neon anime contacts from temu, tame them down ffs.

Hot wiring cars seemed fun and clever at first but it’s just boring and tedious, I do appreciate the slim jim and cloning way of stealing cars.

Just give us the options to make it feel more like GTA and less like RDR2, it’s not hard for you, the developers to add these things.

Most importantly the radio is **** ass.

No good pop channel, no good hip hop channel, no good classic hits channel, no good rock or metal channel, no funky edm channel like come on!
Where are your roots rockstar, You could’ve at least taken over 5-6 radio los santos stations and switched their names and a few of their songs around. Maybe an east coast classics would’ve been great, some Nas, Jay Z etc.
And a pop channel, mannnn I just want to Britney, JT, and em. The rock playlist ass as well.

It’s a beautiful game, has some fun missions and is definitely playable but honestly speaking less fun than GTA V or cyberpunk, those are examples of games with great pacing that just pull you into them, I get that we are **** when it comes to attention spans but when we are labored from work we want to have fun, not grind pointless missions and then do chores for a girlfriend that isn’t even fun, she should’ve been a bit more like CJs gf from San Andreas.

And the Mandy thing should’ve been explorable, would’ve loved to see her try to do something to Lucia or the other way around if we tried to mess with her, as we know that Mandy has a very violent secret.

Tldr:

Not enough drama, not enough action, not memorable.

Not fun, funny or iconic.

It’s not a Grand Theft Auto, it’s a politically correct Crime Simulator/RDR3.

PS: given modern political context with Epstein Island, gay Technocrat overlords, the Groypers etc. I expected a lot more smart and funny jabs at all of them.

The best part of this game is the TV Stations, they are great and authentic.

You broke my heart rockstar, you had it all there but were too tame, and took out many things that were good and replaced them with boring stuff.

author: Leofiso10
quote: I would like to address several points to explain why I gave this game its rating.First: The woke agenda and LGBTQ+ elements have been forced into a game where they have absolutely no place.Second: After 13 years of waiting, the game failed to introduce any new mechanics or offer a genuinely fresh experience. Does the graphics alone justify a 99 rating? I honestly don’t know.Third: Based on my experience, the 30 FPS, stuttering, and various open-world performance issues had a significant impact on my experience. This is a major problem, and I genuinely couldn’t enjoy the game.Fourth: The excessive time spent on missions, where developers deliberately slow things down so you can admire their work, eventually makes the gameplay lose its enjoyment. Does fast travel hurt the game? Absolutely not. Whether someone wants to explore or travel quickly, both options support player freedom.Excessive realism isn’t necessarily a good thing. It restricts you to actions that would make sense in real life, when what you want from a video game is the freedom to do what you want without unnecessary **** many things have become tedious for the player because of these realism-driven restrictions. Why do I have to refuel my car? Why do I have to pay to repair it? Why am I given the option to break the window just to steal a car when pressing the enter-vehicle button already means I want to steal it? Why do I have to deal with electrical wiring puzzles?These mechanics had a significant negative impact on my experience and made the game unnecessarily complicated.There are many more points I could discuss, but I’ll leave it at that.

author: Aax
quote:
TL;DR: This is a visually stunning game on a massively unoptimized flawed engine, which shouldn't be acceptable. The story pushes you in one direction and that direction is not good in my opinion. The entire spirit of the GTA series is gone and replaced by a moralising dating simulator with an occasional firefight. 

Now let me break it down. 

30 FPS is the lowest acceptable bar that you can possibly imagine. If you target a platform (PS5), there is no excuse for a game to dip below 30 FPS. It doesn't matter how visually stunning your world is because if it dips below 30 then you must reduce visual fidelity. You are not making a product to look pretty on screenshots. You are making a product to be played so a stable 30 FPS is literally the lowest bar that is acceptable at all. And it is not acceptable on PS5 Pro, the most high-performance console in the world. Again at this point, you don't have a choice. Reduce the fidelity. Make sure that 30 FPS is achieved. Nobody cares about how good your water looks if the game runs like ****. 

Now the story. To achieve the only good ending you are forced to make choices that are completely contrary to the GTA experience. You're forced to speak "non-lethal good boy approaches" on missions and you're forced to date Lucia whether you like her or not. There is no player agency. 

The characters are awful. Jason has a personality of an old wooden board. Lucy is an extremely annoying, lying, exploitative, entitled **** that he is forced to please and massage her feet. If you want to survive the ending, that is. It is clearly a self-insert from the writing team. And they punish you for not accepting that self-insert by killing your character in the end. This is a horrible direction in a game that was always about getting away with crime. 
Why isn't there an ending where Lucia dies and Jason gets to live free? Why isn't there an ending where they break up? Why isn't there an opportunity to send Lucy off and not deal with her? Lucy is the one who is getting Jason into all the bad situations and yet she is the one who gets to enjoy the best endings in every option. At the very worst they get an equal ending and at every other time she gets off better than him. Why?

Further on the storytelling is just boring. There are no funny jokes. There are no interesting moments. Everything is polished down to be sanitised and dull. This is not a GTA story. This is an HR-approved Bonnie and Clyde rendition. 

"Why are you upset about a normal relationship between a man and a woman?" 
Because it's not normal. Lucia lies to Jason repeatedly, lies about having a husband and a kid, then comes to live in his apartment after prison but yanks the proverbial blanket onto herself and makes him constantly do things for her. She doesn't understand the dynamics of that relationship where she brings nothing to the table. She is constantly lying, acting entitled, and annoying. She is constantly emasculating him. This is not a good relationship. In fact it is very toxic. And the problem is that you can't choose not to engage with it. The game literally forces you to. And if you choose to engage at a bare minimum that you are forced to do, the game then punishes you by giving you a bad ending. 
If Lucia was a conventionally attractive (she's not), kind, nice, loyal, caring, humble, and feminine woman, then players would have zero complaints about building that relationship. Or even if there was a choice **** or even a boyfriend for people who like that sort of thing, players would have zero complaints. The reason players are complaining is that Lucy is objectively an annoying and bad girlfriend but you are forced to basically kiss the ground she walks on at every opportunity in the game. 

Now the question is: is it woke? It is less work than I thought it would be. In fact most of the game makes fun of both right-wing and left-wing ideologies, which is great. As long as things are kept in balance it's not woke. However there are certain elements of the game that are not in balance and those elements are always pointing in the same direction. Like inability to cheat on Lucia, inability to shoot at protesters and clubs, little things like touching a pregnant woman's belly (disgusting femslop) etc. The relationship with Lucy is a prime example. It paints a picture of a completely subservient man that has no agency and tolerates anything that she says or does. Because that's the fantasy that an all-female writing team has. 

In conclusion this game is not worth the money. Especially on PlayStation 5.  On PlayStation 5 it is an objectively bad product. When it comes on PC my score goes to about 6. It is mediocre. It has nothing special, no soul, and is just open-world slop. The only thing that it has going for it is that it's visually stunning, and the design of the city is amazing, and the attention to detail is exceptional. But those are all things that don't really matter for a game.

author: Magpxe
quote:
The graphics are very good. The overall design, buildings, water, etc., are impressive. But a “game” isn’t just the field it’s played on.

The gun mechanics are stiff and, frankly, not fun to use. It feels as though you’re constantly fighting just to get on target. The driving mechanics are equally unpleasant, seemingly in the interest of what I can only assume is “realism”. The cars are generally so fragile that even the slightest bump leaves you paying for repairs. Then there’s the traffic, which is absolutely terrible. It’s almost as if the cars are deliberately made so fragile, and the traffic so obstructive, that you’re being incentivised to drive safely in a GTA game.

That brings us rather neatly to where the game’s incentive structure lies, and what appears like what rapacious feminism, wokery and unsupervised women with green hair have done to what was otherwise a gloriously boisterous, offensive and liberating franchise. Namely, they’ve completely neutered it.

Of course, it isn’t just the feminists. What’s perhaps more disappointing is that the men involved in developing this game seemingly lacked the testicular fortitude to recognise that they were creating something fundamentally at odds with what a GTA game could and should be. And rather than pushing any cultural boundaries they’ve either stood by idly or, I suspect, actively participated in the development of these frankly ridiculous, tedious humiliation rituals they insist on calling missions.

And then there’s the lead character: one of the dullest protagonists to exist across any medium. So much so that they’ve seemingly had to give all the personality to Lucia, leaving Jason as little more than a handsome dog on a leash for her to walk through the chaos.

The Bonnie and Clyde angle is, frankly, such low-hanging literary fruit.

Separating the “game” from the “pitch”, the game itself is awful: neutered, boring, unrewarding, uninteresting, unsatisfying and politically self-conscious dog muck. The pitch, on the other hand, is well-groomed and expansive.Ultimately, you can play rugby or football on any acre of grass. But it’s the incentive structure, the rules and the freedoms that make those games special.

Do not buy.

author: seaemkay
quote: After more than a decade of waiting, Grand Theft Auto VI drops, and its world-building, visuals, and atmosphere feel genuinely unmatched. Leonida is alive—packed with tiny details, strong characters like Jason and Lucia, and a blockbuster-level presentation that raises the bar. Still, beyond the critics’ stadium-sized hype, there are real flaws that keep it from hitting perfection. Locking the game to 30 FPS on current-gen hardware in 2026 is a letdown, especially during high-octane action and fast driving, where frame drops and stuttering still show up on the base PS5. The open world may invite total freedom, but the main missions stay pretty scripted and restrictive—step two feet off the path and you’ll hit a “Mission Failed” screen in a snap. Compared to other open-world RPGs, like Skyrim, the core gameplay loop and the controls feel stuck in the past, hardly evolving much since GTA V. The heavy emphasis on slow, everyday drama slows the pacing in the early hours, making it easy to lose momentum. GTA 6 is a milestone for immersion and storytelling, absolutely worth diving into. Yet the 30 FPS cap and the rigid, decade-old mission design tug the score down. A fair rating lands around 0 out of 10, not some flawless 99. It’s bold, immersive, and memorable, but not quite the perfect storm.

author: cm64
quote:
Absolutely Disappointing – Grand Theft Auto VI

Honestly, what an absolute letdown. After years of waiting, endless hype and ridiculous expectations, this is what we're left with? GTA 6 feels less like a Grand Theft Auto game and more like a heavily restricted life simulator with a ridiculous number of bugs.

Let's start with the freedom, or rather, the complete lack of it. You can't even walk into buildings and cause the kind of chaos you'd expect from a GTA game. Want to go on a rampage? Forget it. Want to interact with the world freely? Apparently, that's asking too much. You can pick up women on the streets, but somehow the game still manages to make basic freedom feel restricted.

And then there's the chores. Seriously? Why am I doing everyday real-life activities in a game that's supposed to be about escaping reality? I didn't buy Grand Theft Auto to simulate having another mundane day at work. I want criminal chaos, ridiculous missions, freedom and entertainment, not a second job.

The restrictions are everywhere. It feels like Rockstar has gone out of its way to limit what players can actually do. The whole point of GTA has always been freedom, experimentation and doing things you simply couldn't get away with in real life. Where has that gone?

Then we have the technical issues. Falling through floors, clipping through stairs and countless other bugs that completely ruin immersion. After all these years of development and all that hype, you'd expect a polished experience, not something that feels like it still needs months of fixing.

Even the wider gaming community seems divided, with streamers openly criticising the experience and players reportedly seeking refunds. That's not exactly the reception you'd expect from one of the most anticipated games ever made.

The biggest disappointment is that GTA 6 seems to have forgotten what made GTA special in the first place. Freedom, chaos, unpredictability and the ability to play your own way. Instead, we're getting restrictions, tedious activities, technical problems and a game that constantly seems to tell you what you can and cannot do.

Years of waiting for something revolutionary, only to end up feeling like we're playing a glorified, restricted life simulator.

Massive disappointment. Overhyped, underwhelming and nowhere near what I expected from Grand Theft Auto.

author: nokipoki
quote:
Honestly, GTA VI is the worst GTA game in the series so far, at least in my opinion.

One of the biggest problems is how much freedom seems to have been removed. GTA has always been about doing whatever you want, stealing cars, causing chaos, exploring the world and creating your own fun. Even something as simple as stealing cars feels unnecessarily restricted and inefficient here.

Compare the opening of GTA V to GTA VI. GTA V immediately throws you into action with Michael, Trevor and Brad participating in a bank heist. The second protagonist introduction has Franklin and Lamar repossessing cars. You're immediately introduced to the criminal lifestyle that GTA is known for.

Meanwhile, some of the first activities in GTA VI involve getting Lucia flowers, fixing your house and buying groceries. Seriously? It feels incredibly slow, almost like playing a life simulator rather than Grand Theft Auto.

The driving is another major disappointment. It feels clunky, and I constantly find myself drifting even when I'm not trying to. Driving should feel natural and responsive, not like I'm fighting the controls every time I take a corner. It's worse than GTA IV's driving

My biggest issue is that GTA seems to have lost some of its identity. I don't want every little activity to feel scripted or restricted. I want the freedom to jump into a random car, drive wherever I want, cause chaos and create my own experiences.

GTA has always been about freedom, action and unpredictability. So far, GTA VI feels like it's moving in the opposite direction.

author: slumberzzz
quote:
Thirteen years after the release of GTA V, and you remember why this game's community wanted to cancel a journalist back then for giving it a 9/10. Not hard to think why this game only got "10's" this time around. As for GTA VI, I remember that Netflix trailer a few months back(that's right, you had to have a Netflix account to get 6 hour early access to the most anticipated game trailer in over a decade). In it, the beaches and streets were packed as were the sidewalks and businesses, the framerate and gameplay looked great, and overall, a lot of "GTA-like" things were happening and it seemed like a lock for most of us. Never mind the $80 and $100 price tags, am I right? Did you see that trailer?! Fast-forward 15–20 hours into the game, and assuming you do any exploring outside of the main missions, I’m still not seeing the classic Rockstar I love and this city doesn't feel lived in.

It's boring and it performs poorly. I don't say that lightly. Sure, it looks great, but given the tools available to developers nowadays, nice visuals should be expected if it's the intent. I’m not going to act like Rockstar spent all 13 years making this game. They gave us RDR2 during that time, and anyone with realistic expectations probably expected a similar experience. RDR2 was fantastic. My point is that Rockstar had a strong reference point for making another instant classic--one that didn't require overhyping every outlet GTA had available to it. That approach is exactly why real players feel so deflated.

There’s zero energy in GTA VI. The main characters have no presence; you could swap in almost any two NPCs, and it wouldn’t make a difference. The recreation of Vice City and the map as a whole is the best part, but overall, it feels thin and nothing like what we were shown. Mini-games are not systems, and you can’t tell me the game is a mile wide if it’s only an inch deep. There’s nothing here that hasn’t been done before, especially nothing that wasn’t already done better just eight months ago. It's definitely not worth the price tag on this generation of consoles, especially considering the next generation of hardware comes out in roughly a year. I learned a long time ago, that if something looks like a duck, and then it acts like a ****'s a duck. I don't need anyone else to come along and tell me what I'm looking at.

author: AnInstantNoodle
quote: GTA VI – A Step Backwards for the Franchise?It genuinely feels like GTA VI has had its roots neutered. Compared to previous entries in the franchise, the game feels noticeably dulled down, restricted and overly **** of the biggest things that made Grand Theft Auto what it was has always been the freedom to do whatever you wanted. That sense of unpredictability, unrestricted gameplay and being able to approach situations however you pleased. That freedom feels like it's slowly **** opening is an absolute slog. Instead of being thrown into the world and given the freedom to explore and play at your own pace, you're stuck doing what feels like an endless list of chores for Lucia. Fixing things around the house, running errands and carrying out mundane domestic tasks. It's an insufferable introduction that does very little to make you feel like you're actually playing a Grand Theft Auto **** this seems to be a wider issue throughout the game. There's an increasingly noticeable emphasis on domestic activities, relationship management and everyday responsibilities. At times, it feels less like GTA and more like a relationship simulator with a crime game bolted onto it.Rockstar seems to have confused realism with enjoyable gameplay. Having to manage increasingly mundane aspects of everyday life might make the world feel more realistic, but does it actually make the experience more entertaining? There's a point where immersion becomes busywork, and I feel GTA VI crosses that line far too often.What's more concerning is the apparent removal or restriction of mechanics that helped define previous titles. The freedom to interact with the world, engage in criminal activities and make your own decisions seems to have taken a back seat to Rockstar's increasingly controlled vision of how the game should be played. Even basic gameplay freedom feels compromised when so much seems dictated by story progression and predetermined activities.There's also a noticeable concern surrounding the game's identity. Where's the outrageous satire, the unapologetic dark humour and the ridiculous social commentary that made previous GTA games so entertaining? GTA was never supposed to be particularly tasteful or politically correct. Its willingness to push boundaries was part of its **** increasingly feels as though Rockstar is playing it safe, sanitising elements of the experience and restricting player interactions to avoid certain scenarios or controversies. An open-world crime game shouldn't feel like it's constantly putting boundaries around what you're allowed to do.There's a growing sense that the franchise is losing its rebellious edge. GTA used to thrive on letting players create absolute chaos, experiment with the world and do things simply because they could. Now, it feels as though Rockstar is more interested in controlling the experience than allowing players to enjoy it on their own terms.I appreciate the technical achievement, the attention to detail and the incredible world Rockstar has created. But impressive graphics, realistic animations and an incredibly detailed environment don't automatically translate into an enjoyable Grand Theft Auto experience. A beautiful open world means very little if the freedom to actually enjoy it has been stripped **** me, the biggest disappointment is that GTA VI seems to have lost sight of what made the franchise special in the first **** was about freedom, chaos, rebellion and doing things your own way. Not being micromanaged through a relationship, sent on domestic errands or restricted by an increasingly sanitised set of gameplay rules.Rockstar has created an impressive world, but I'm not convinced they've created a better Grand Theft Auto game.

author: moilmo
quote: This game is a complete scam. This isn't Grand Theft Auto—it’s Girlfriend-Tamed Amateur. It’s a woke Dating Sim and Construction Simulator disguised as a GTA game. If I wanted to play a domestic life and house-building sim, I wouldn’t have dropped $100 on it—let alone get forced to switch from my PC to a PS5 just to play this garbage at launch, which wasn't worth it at all. Gabe Newell once said in an interview that people play games to have fun and feel good, not to be handed a boring grocery list of chores—and Rockstar completely forgot that. I’m focusing mostly on Chapter 1 here to avoid major spoilers, and it is an absolute snoozefest that drags on forever, forcing you into tedious relationship micromanagement instead of actual crime and freedom.They completely killed the core spirit of the franchise since the very first game. The classic GTA spirit was running around shirtless in your boxers and pulling a whole RPG straight out of your underwear—now they ditched that fun arcade soul just to lazily copy Red Dead’s realism. Don't get me wrong, I loved Red Dead; its atmosphere and tone were great, and it was a phenomenal game. But Grand Theft Auto should never turn into Red Dead—they are two completely different franchises. If CD Projekt Red managed to keep The Witcher and Cyberpunk completely distinct from one another, it's pathetic that a giant like Rockstar, with all their massive budget, couldn't separate the identities of their own two flagship **** title is literally Grand Theft Auto, yet when you steal a car and try to store it in your garage, the game blocks you because "it's a stolen vehicle." Even the main storyline completely abandons the classic GTA themes and satirical edge we loved in previous entries. On top of that, woke identity politics ruined the sandbox freedom by making certain ideologically "protected" NPCs completely immune to damage. And the character writing is an absolute joke: your protagonist is built like an absolute tank who looks intimidating as hell, yet he’s calling his girlfriend crying for help because a random woman is chasing him. Even worse, when his partner leaves their kid unattended and you confront it, instead of getting rightfully angry, he completely brushes it off and says, "I'm **** happy." What kind of pathetic writing is that?Technically, it’s a broken mess—riddled with constant bugs, frequent crashes, and severe FPS dips into the low 20s during gameplay. This is completely unacceptable for a supposed "5-A" game in 2026 with a $2 billion budget and 13 years of development time. And don't fall for the bought-and-paid-for Metacritic reviews—critics literally admit in their own text that the game is incomplete and flawed, yet still hand it a 100/100 score. Top it all off with a rushed, unsatisfying finale where the decent outcomes are locked behind tedious money grinding. Total letdown.

author: Gaming_Jacker
quote:
Who could have predicted this? Well, if you've been paying attention to the landscape of the gaming industry for the past 10 years, it was obvious this was going to happen. And the 10/10 critic reviews (with multiple flaws pointed out) only validated our suspicions. Im going to keep this short:

 First of all less than 30 fps in 2026 is unnacceptable. GTA6 looks barely any better than RDR2, but somehow runs 4 times worse? Also there are a lot of ray tracing artifacts (boiling, shadow flickering, screen space artifacts) which ruin the immersion, so it doesnt even have that going for it.

 Secondly, the gameplay is an absolute chore to get through (literally). Somehow GTA6 has less gameplay in the first ~10 hours than Life is Strange, which is an interactive movie. The game doesnt even let you commit crimes whenever or wherever you want. A game literally called *GRAND THEFT AUTO* doesnt let you steal a car near your neighborhood because it would be mean to your neighbor. It is very clear that the GTA6 devs tried to copy RDR2 because it was successful, but they failed miserably because GTA is a sandbox, not an RPG. I want to be able to do whatever I want after the intro. Also the gunplay and the driving is painfully sluggish thanks to the 25 average fps this game runs at.

 Last, and probably most importantly, the story is boring and the characters are insufferable. There are no interesting or likeable characters, everyone is either boring or annoying. The two main MCs included. Lucia constantly acts entitled and ungrateful, and she mocks and demeans Jason who does everything to help her. He could literally fix all the problems in her life, and she's just gonna say "I could have done it better than you lol". And the worst part of it all is that Jason never stands up for himself. These two should have been the antagonists in the first chapter that the protagonist kills, and we never have to hear from them again, not the protagonists.

 So yeah all in all this is probably the worst entry in the series and one of the worst games I've ever played in general. It genuinely feels like it was made by people who either hate or don't understand why people play videogames.

author: Edu0347
quote:
A Graphical Masterpiece Ruined by Woke Storytelling

GTA VI is a breathtaking technical achievement, with stunning graphics, incredible attention to detail, and an impressive open world. Unfortunately, that's where my praise ends.

Rockstar has completely lost the narrative magic that made GTA V a masterpiece. GTA V was hilarious, outrageous, politically incorrect, and brilliantly written. Its characters were unforgettable, its humor was fearless, and its storytelling perfectly captured the rebellious spirit of the franchise.

GTA VI, on the other hand, feels trapped in a rigid woke culture, with forced political correctness replacing the sharp satire, provocative humor, and creative freedom that once defined Grand Theft Auto.Instead of pushing boundaries, Rockstar seems more concerned with avoiding controversy. 

The result is a narrative that feels sanitized, uninspired, and painfully disconnected from the franchise's identity.They had a graphical masterpiece in their hands, but gave it a story that falls far below the standards established by GTA. 

The graphics deserve praise. The storytelling deserves serious criticism.

author: GdHq1995
quote:
As a fan who has been with this franchise since GTA Vice City, I have to say: GTA 6 is a massive disappointment.

Performance: 30 fps at a constant 33.3 ms would be acceptable. That's not what you get. On the base PS5, the game dips to 23–27 fps in heavy scenes, and the frametime graph is full of spikes up to 40–50 ms, even in calm moments like walking out of your house in the morning. That isn't a locked 30, it's constant stutter. 

Independent tests confirm sustained drops below 30 fps on the base PS5, and even the PS5 Pro briefly drops to 24 fps in demanding scenes. 

It's unacceptable that the standard PS5, the console most players actually own, can't hold its own 30 fps target. No developer should get away with this unless they simply don't care about their fans.

Bigger isn't better: A bigger, more realistic world doesn't automatically make a better game. What good is all that detail when the stutter constantly pulls you out of it? Every hitch during a chase or a shootout completely breaks the immersion that this game is supposedly all about.

The community: Almost as disappointing as the game is how people react to any criticism. Critics are told they "just want attention." By that logic, you could just as easily say the people praising it are living out the fantasy of finally having a girlfriend. Neither statement is a real argument, and that's the point. Long-time fans are allowed to be disappointed. Right now, defending this game feels almost like a cult.

It's hardly a surprise. Dan Houser and many of the people who made GTA what it was are no longer at Rockstar. You can feel it. Sadly but may our beloved GTA️ Rest in Peace.

author: Metanart
quote:
Well, I’m kinda disappointed.

For a "game of the millennium" that everyone kept hyping up, this new GTA feels rather bland and toothless compared to its predecessors. The dialogue is tedious and dull, the characters are uninteresting, and there’s an overall sense of restriction regarding what you can and cannot do in an *open-world* game.

I have some issues with the new limitations - like the fact that you can’t steal every vehicle or kill every NPC - not to mention the idiotic karma system. It’s bizarre to see this in a GTA game; it makes you wonder- why are you even allowed to kill cops? Isn't that "bad" too? Why does the game decide for me what’s right or wrong, effectively dictating how I’m "supposed" to play? Sure, there are plenty of new mechanics, but they don’t actually make the gameplay any more engaging. 
As a game, it’s... fine, I guess- I’d rate it higher if it hadn’t been hailed as the greatest game in history. But as it stands? It’s just ok-ish game with some pros and cons. Definitely not worth the full price, and it’s certainly not the Game of the Millennium, lol.

And as for the main characters - they evoke nothing but antipathy, both of them equally. "Dumb and Dumber" - that’s the perfect description for them.

And once again, 30 FPS on the latest, supposedly powerful consoles? I have an Xbox Series X, and this isn’t even funny anymore - it’s just really bad. On my PC, almost all games have been running at 100+ FPS for a long time now. After playing on PC, trying to play new games on a console at 30 FPS just feels absurd.

author: PhatBoB
quote:
No one is questioning Rockstar’s technical work. Managing to get such a detailed world running on a PS5 is impressive—hats off to them. But are we judging a video game, or a tech demo?

I keep seeing videos celebrating the graphics, lighting, details, and realism, while gameplay, mission design, narrative pacing, and control responsiveness seem to take a back ****’re talking about a game with an astronomical budget, yet we still see objects magically spawning in characters' hands (have you tried buying a burger? Go ahead and try, then let me know), weapons sticking to backs like magnets, highly scripted missions, mundane interactions, and long sequences where the player does next to nothing. Not to mention the 30 FPS cap and technical issues—which don’t even seem to be factored in, even though for any other title, these would easily cost it a point or two in its final score.

Years ago, *Red Dead Redemption 2* already demonstrated an impressive level of care for certain animations and interactions. And *The Witcher 3* taught us that a game doesn’t need the best technical specs or the best combat system to be memorable; what it needs is strong writing, engaging missions, and gameplay that truly draws the player in.

I don’t mean to dismiss the merits of *GTA VI*, but everywhere I look, I see a great deal of confusion between technological excellence and excellence in game design. Everyone talks about "incredible depth," but I’d like to see concrete examples of this depth within the gameplay—not yet another video showing how realistic the puddles look.A video game must, first and foremost, be a *good* game. And that, in my view, is the question too many people are forgetting to ask.

author: AN0RAK_
quote:
GTA 6: 13 YEARS OF WAITING FOR THIS? IS THE FRANCHISE LOSING ITS IDENTITY?
GTA 6 had one mission: surpass GTA V and deliver an evolution worthy of more than a decade of waiting. After all, we're talking about approximately 13 years between the franchise's two main installments. But did Rockstar really make the most of all that time to deliver what players were expecting?
1. 13 YEARS OF DEVELOPMENT AND STILL 30 FPS? This is undoubtedly one of the most frustrating aspects. After 13 years, an entire generation of technological advancements, and one of the biggest investments in video game history, GTA 6 is targeting 30 FPS on ****'s hard not to question this decision. We're talking about a franchise that generates billions, a company that had more than a decade to develop its next major release, and a game that promises to revolutionize open-world gaming.Beautiful graphics aren't everything. Smooth performance matters too. In a game involving car chases, shootouts, driving, and constant movement, 60 FPS would make a huge difference. The bare minimum expectation should have been a 60 FPS performance mode, even if it meant sacrificing some graphical quality.After waiting this long, it's frustrating to see that the priority seems to have been visual spectacle rather than delivering the best possible experience in every aspect.
2. IS GTA LOSING ITS IDENTITY? GTA has always been known for its freedom, dark humor, exaggerated violence, and ability to satirize absolutely everything. Politicians, celebrities, corporations, religions, social movements, and American society itself have never been off-limits to Rockstar's jokes.That irreverence was precisely one of the things that made GTA different from every other game.However, there's a growing feeling that Rockstar is adopting a more cautious approach, seemingly concerned with not offending certain **** problem isn't modernizing the franchise. It's changing the very things that made it so popular. GTA was never supposed to be politically correct. Its appeal came from being exaggerated, provocative, and sometimes downright **** Rockstar starts limiting its own creativity to avoid controversy, we're looking at a significant shift in the franchise's identity.
3. LESS FREEDOM FOR THE PLAYER? Perhaps this is the most contradictory aspect of GTA **** decades, GTA built its identity around giving players freedom. You could cause chaos, commit crimes, engage in police chases, and experience absurd situations in an open world.That's why reports of restrictions on certain interactions involving protest characters and specific establishments have sparked so much **** GTA is a franchise about crime, violence, and freedom in an open world, why should certain situations have different limitations? This doesn't mean everything must be allowed in a video game, but it's perfectly reasonable to question the consistency of these decisions. Players shouldn't feel like they're being guided by a list of moral restrictions while exploring a game whose entire premise has always been freedom.Rockstar needs to provide a clearer explanation of this creative direction. After all, selective freedom is still a contradiction for a franchise that has always sold freedom as one of its biggest selling points.
4. THE EXPECTATIONS AFTER 13 YEARS Thirteen years have created enormous expectations. GTA V spanned multiple console generations, while GTA Online continued to be commercially exploited throughout that entire period.That's why GTA 6 needed to deliver much more than impressive graphics. It needed to bring significant improvements to physics, artificial intelligence, missions, player freedom, and the overall **** longer the wait, the greater Rockstar's responsibility to deliver something truly special.
FINAL VERDICT GTA 6 may be visually impressive, technically ambitious, and feature an incredibly detailed world. But that doesn't mean every decision Rockstar has made is the right one.After 13 years, targeting 30 FPS on consoles is disappointing. The potential shift in the franchise's identity and the questions surrounding restrictions on player freedom are also **** biggest fear isn't that GTA 6 will be different. It's that it might abandon the very characteristics that made GTA what it is.Rockstar built one of the greatest franchises in gaming history by being irreverent, provocative, and unafraid to satirize absolutely anything. It shouldn't have to abandon that personality just to follow cultural ****, did we really wait 13 years for a true evolution of GTA, or are we getting a prettier, more restricted, and less irreverent version of what we already knew?

author: m1nce
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI: A Bloated and Overrated Disappointment
​After over a decade of hype, Grand Theft Auto VI arrives not as a revolution, but as a massive disappointment. Beneath its stunning visuals lies a sluggish, creatively bankrupt experience that squanders its colossal budget.
​1. Outdated, Rigid Mission Design
​While Vice City and Leonida are technical marvels, Rockstar’s mission design is stuck in the past. Despite promising open-world freedom, the campaign rigidly holds your hand. Step slightly off the designated path, and you are instantly greeted with a "Mission Failed" screen.
​2. Clunky Mechanics and Tedious Realism
​Trying to inject Red Dead Redemption 2's heavy realism into GTA has completely ruined the flow. Character movement is sluggish, hiding behind cover feels broken, and micro-management mechanics turn basic tasks into chores. The chaotic, arcade-like fun that defined the series has been sacrificed for frustrating realism.
​3. Toothless Satire
​The sharp, fearless parody of American culture that made GTA iconic is entirely missing. Attempting to mock modern social media and influencer culture, the game relies on safe, predictable, and superficial jokes. Rockstar played it too safe, stripping the franchise of its edge.
​4. Built for Monetization
​The single-player campaign constantly feels like an extended promotional vehicle and tutorial for online microtransactions. The economy is artificially bloated, and progression is deliberately dragged out to push players toward spending real money.
​Verdict: GTA VI proves that gorgeous graphics cannot save archaic design, boring mechanics, and lazy writing. It’s a massive step backward for the franchise.

quote: This is my general opinion, with absolutely no bias toward the game or the company. I’ve played a lot of games, a whole lot, but this isn’t just a case of a few mistakes. The entire game, its concept, and its direction are ****’s start with GTA IV. I originally played The Lost and Damned because Luis was cool and wealthy, and he was on the cover. That was 12 years ago. Four months ago, I went back and replayed the game, this time playing through Niko Bellic, Johnny, and Luis. That’s when I realized the writer behind this game was practically writing with a golden pen. Sure, the writing has some flaws, but it’s still incredible.I’m disappointed because this isn’t the level everyone was waiting **** my opinion, take the last two GTA games and the Red Dead games, throw them all into a blender, and the result would be GTA **** V is good when it comes to Trevor and Michael’s stories, but Franklin feels incomplete. He doesn’t feel like Lamar’s close friend the way he should. I’m talking about character writing across the entire franchise, from the first game to the sixth. There should be at least one character out of every hundred who stands out as truly great, and at least one genuinely good storyline. I don’t see that here.What I see is a conflicting, inconsistent story. I have three reasons that make me question whether the writing team is even the same. There’s an aspect of storytelling they used to excel at, and we’re simply not seeing it **** studio seems to have changed its identity, and bringing back Niko Bellic, a character who’s on the run, is another questionable decision. You might say this isn’t the first time they’ve brought back an old character, but Niko is a character almost everyone loves. Putting him in a game that goes against the kind of person he is doesn’t make sense to me. I don’t think they even realized what went wrong. It feels like they just kept going because it was too late to turn back after the 2022 **** graphics look amazing, absolutely. The animations? Not so much. But the performance? That’s killing the game. Humanity has reached 1,000 frames per second, yet our beloved company can’t even maintain 30, or at least 24. At the very least, there should be a solution to this **** last two generations of gaming have brought some massive leaps forward in the industry. And in my opinion, Rockstar’s biggest mistake was Red Dead Redemption 2.Same quality, just improved, of course. Same characters, just wearing modern clothes. The same thing, over and over **** Red Dead Redemption 2 had never come out, we might have looked at this game as the game of the century. But no, I just don’t see that happening.I feel like the company stopped putting in real effort after 2021, when they discontinued updates for Red Dead **** just to be clear, I actually hate Red Dead. My favorite game of all time is GTA IV. There’s no bias here, just criticism based on an uncomfortable **** in the older games, everyone was treated equally. author: Tabbo2
quote:
The game has too much nudity and adding a female main character ruins the aurafarming that Jason does to make up for these graphics honestly very disappointing and underwhelming for 13 years of work you'd think they would put effort into this game, and speaking of the graphics, they are straight-up ass. Seriously, for a next-gen title with a massive budget, everything looks muddy, washed out, and outdated, like an early PS4 game upscaled with a blurry filter. The lighting is flat, reflections look pixelated and broken, character faces look like plastic mannequins with dead eyes, and the shadows flicker constantly whenever you move the camera. 

​The physics feel completely phoned in too. The driving mechanics lost all the weight and realism they used to have, making every car feel like a weightless arcade toy instead of an actual vehicle. You can slam into a concrete barrier at top speed and bounce off with barely a scratch, which completely ruins any sense of immersion. On top of that, the open world feels weirdly empty and lifeless compared to all the hype and trailers. Half the buildings you think you can enter are just painted-on textures and locked doors, and the NPC AI is somehow worse than games from over a decade ago. Pedestrians either stare blankly at walls or despawn the second you turn the camera around, making the city feel like a cheap movie set rather than a living, breathing environment.

​The mission design is painfully repetitive as well—just endless fetch quests, tedious driving segments, and slow tailing missions with zero creativity or freedom in how you complete them. If you step two feet outside the exact path the developers want you to take, you get an instant mission failed screen. For a modern open-world title, that kind of rigid hand-holding is embarrassing. Even the gunplay feels clunky and outdated, with awkward cover mechanics, terrible hit registration, and bullet-sponge enemies that take way too many hits to go down.

​Technical performance and glitches are by far the worst part of the entire experience. The game is practically held together with duct tape, with constant bugs completely breaking immersion every ten minutes. Cars randomly spawn inside each other and launch into the stratosphere, NPCs T-pose in the middle of serious cutscenes, and character models regularly clip straight through walls and floors. Mission triggers fail to activate constantly, forcing you to restart entire checkpoints from scratch because an AI partner got stuck on a curb or walked endlessly into a closed door. Falling through the map while driving is a regular occurrence, and saves can randomly corrupt or fail to load properly after a crash. On top of the glitches, the framerate tanks whenever you drive fast through the city or get into a big shootout, accompanied by jarring texture pop-in where roads and buildings turn into low-poly blobs right in front of your eyes, plus audio cutting out mid-dialogue. Waiting over thirteen years only to get a broken, choppy, unpolished mess is completely unacceptable. 

​Even the story pacing falls completely flat. The plot drags on for hours without anything meaningful happening, filled with forgettable side characters and forced dialogue that tries way too hard to be funny. The side activities feel like mindless filler copy-pasted across the map just to artificially pad out the runtime, offering zero worthwhile rewards for your time. Meanwhile, the in-game economy and progression system are clearly balanced to frustrate players rather than reward them, making basic upgrades, properties, and vehicles feel like an exhausting, tedious chore—obviously designed to push people toward spending extra money later on.

​Even the user interface and menus feel clunky, unresponsive, and poorly organized, making simple tasks like swapping gear, setting waypoints, or checking the map way more annoying than they should be. Sound design is underwhelming too, with weak weapon audio that sounds like airsoft guns and a radio soundtrack that lacks any real variety or memorable tracks. It honestly feels like the studio spent way more time and money on flashy marketing campaigns and CGI trailers than on actual gameplay depth, quality assurance, graphics, or innovation. Truly a massive letdown for the franchise and easily the most overrated, broken release of the year.
