author: jachu1899
quote:
Seriously, can the entire gaming industry really be bought off this shamelessly? 
10/10 scores? 
Are you kidding me?
How is it possible that Rockstar, a studio that once managed to release one hit after another, often just a year or two apart, now takes supposedly 13 years to develop its next instalment, with a budget that probably exceeds the combined production costs of all its previous games several times over, only to serve us something like this?
We were promised a juicy, perfectly cooked steak, but what we got was avocado toast. And a cold one at that.
Here's my list of disappointments:
-1 – Ultimate Edition.
 Instead of welcoming us with another iconic musical theme that stays in our heads for years, we're greeted by a store and an invitation to purchase a GTA+ subscription. Is this really what we expect from Rockstar?
-1 – Performance and optimisation. 
During the most action-packed moments, the game can't even maintain 30 FPS. 
After so many years of development and with such an enormous budget, that's simply unacceptable.
-1 – Bugs and glitches. 
Their number and severity are simply not what you'd expect from a production that took this long to develop and cost this much money.
-1 – Gameplay pacing. 
Just because certain mechanics worked well in a Western-themed game like Red Dead Redemption 2 doesn't mean they'll automatically work in GTA. Different world, different atmosphere, different expectations.
-1 – A life simulator instead of GTA.
 I don't buy Grand Theft Auto to spend my limited leisure time pretending to live an ordinary everyday life. That's what The Sims is for. I want fast-paced gameplay, chaos, freedom and the unmistakable GTA atmosphere, not another everyday life simulator.
-1 – Protagonists. 
I'm finding it difficult to like the main characters. One comes across as a submissive pushover, while the other's personality, at least in my opinion, seems to revolve mainly around money and personal interests. I'm missing charismatic characters that you remember for years.
-1 – Character design. 
Who came up with this combination of protagonists? A stereotypically fit, athletic blond guy paired with a woman with a completely different body type. Is this a game that's supposed to appeal to everyone, or yet another production where character design has been shaped by modern trends and the expectations of a particular audience? Can't developers simply create characters according to their own artistic vision anymore?
-1 – Storyline.
 What we got feels like a mediocre soap opera. I genuinely feel there's been a massive decline in storytelling quality compared to previous instalments. I'm missing the depth, personality and storytelling that used to be Rockstar's trademark.
-1 – Political correctness.
 Even in GTA, a franchise that built its reputation on fearlessly mocking society and reality, I can increasingly feel the presence of modern ideological restrictions. Where is the Rockstar that wasn't afraid to offend anyone or make fun of absolutely anything?
-1 – No physical copy of the game. 
At first, I thought it was about limiting the second-hand market. The reality turns out to be even more disappointing. It feels as though one of the reasons behind this decision was to make it harder for players to return the game after launch.
 In other words, to make it less convenient for us to get rid of a purchase we end up regretting.
And that's what I regret most.
Where has the real Rockstar gone?
The studio that once set industry standards, created games that lasted for years and didn't need to prove its greatness through 10/10 review scores.
After all these years of waiting, with this kind of money and such enormous resources at their disposal,
 I expected something that would redefine the genre once again.Instead,
 I feel like I've been given a product that's more interested in following modern trends than in resembling the very thing that made me fall in love with this franchise in the first place.

author: quintonC
quote: There's no greater disparity in audience than between action and story-driven games. As such, there's no greater potential profit than successfully appealing to both camps. Some recent titles such as Resident Evil 9 and Pragmata took the risk and succeeded, presenting emotional, relationship-based narratives without compromising gameplay. GTA6 fails miserably. It is a hollowed-out corpse of gameplay, and the story that inhabits it falls flat. We've gone from the endearingly flawed, profoundly human characters of GTA5 to utterly irredeemable homunculi without a single likeable or even tolerable quality. While the visuals can be stunning, they come at the cost of unacceptable framerates, which is emblematic of everything else wrong in the game; play bad in order to present well. This is an unacceptable compromise, antithetical to what games should be, and the ramifications this critical and commercial success stands to have on the industry are deeply concerning.

author: MrGenji
quote:
Aside from great visuals and lightning from a great variety of activities, this just doesn't give off the vibes of GTA a lot of times during the playthrough.
The MCs are both lacking depth and development throughout the whole story and the main gripe about both of their stories' barely ever comes into play or is relevant at all. Jason most of the times drops one liners like he doesn't care at all and this is not excusable with saying 'he was in the army, of course he is that way'. NO. He has no real values, opinions or motivations. Lucia instead is constantly an annoying and ungrateful counter part that takes away the fun and interest into these two. Checks out that she left their baby, whose existence she hid from Jason, at a coffee shop to rob a store across the street. It's nothing but a one-sided and toxic relationship put on display.
Combined with the 'missions' and 'activites' that come along with their relationship it's not really striking, but rather dampening, boring and annoying. These activities continue in different dimensions and ways throughout the whole game.
To a degree you have to take care of the relationship to unlock all possible missions and features, which is again a dampening and limiting factor. Especially due to abhorrent character that Lucia is and Jason's inability to call out on anything or ever have a different opinion.

The map is indeed vast and has variety of places to offer, which indeed feel worthwhile to visit! The city is also looking lovely, but the traffic could have been handled a bit better. The traffic AI seems at times too aggressive, noticeable at best in races. The streets are a tad bit too cramped and narrow. Given it's a city, it indeed makes sense, but for the fun factor this could be reviewed, so driving doesn't feel as stressful and straining at times.

There have been quite a few bugs, but I didn't encounter a gamebreaking like others seems to have.
My worst bug was me clipping once through a wall and flying around half the city with my car after a weird collision catapulted me. After that no issues aside from FPS drops at times and some animation bugs.

The story didn't catch me at all even though the setup about a Bonnie and Clyde kind of story is one I like.
Basically, Jason and Lucia got a child together, which Jason didn't know about, bc they split up. Leaving her child alone at a coffee shop to rob a store gets Lucia into prison.
She gets released early, bc the prison needs to make space. She tells Jason about this and their baby. Guy did not knew about baby, asks no questions about it, isn't mad or anything at all. Just shallow...
They get back together, continue with their criminal lives with the pursuit to make enough money and establish a frame work that could be a proper life they could live with their son Tomas without any sort of crime or financial problems. There is more than one ending, so I'm leaving it a that.
I've got to an ending, that felt okay. Wasn't too happy or sad about it.
Again this story is weirdly fleshed out and could have been more GTA-like over the top statements, actions and personalities, running over hookers, hitting the strip club etc. while also in a later stage of the game focussing on becoming proper parents either as a couple or simply as the child's parents. This would have opened up the possibilities that gamers could enforce based on their own desire. Romance is not everyonce liking in such an action loaded game, but could have very well been an option to pursue for those that wanted it. And of course this would encourage more people to explore different outcomes.
To sum up I just didn't vibe with the story at all. Peak moment was for me to meet the living Serbian legend again. He doesn't lack anything from the aura he used to have. Thank God!

Gameplay wise it felt completely fine. Nothing groundbreaking, but rather polished up from GTA 5 to a degree. The cars and their handling are quite something to digest, but tuning helps really well. Aiming and movement needs a review, but worked out fine if you also consider adjusting the controls.
NPCs need a review about getting aggroed too fast, but the interactions, that you can purse with them are great!

Unfortunately though this was to me not worth 13 years of waiting. It is not worth the price of the ultimate edition. The technical achievement is indeed a real thing and the graphics will impress people who mainly watch trailers.
Everything else is/feels undercooked. Critics are calling it a masterpiece because the lighting is expensive and the marketing was perfect. After finishing an actual playthrough with over 50h, it feels more like a beautiful Mona Lisa that wants to be a GTA game. A great one.

author: ruisantos
quote:
An absolute disappointment and a betrayal of what made GTA such an iconic franchise. For a game that supposedly revolves around freedom, the experience feels incredibly restrictive, with heavily scripted missions and very little room for genuine player creativity.

The technical performance is unacceptable, with numerous bugs, noticeable FPS drops and a serious lack of polish.

The writing is arguably even worse. The ideological messaging feels forced rather than naturally integrated into the narrative. Many missions are written from an overwhelmingly gender-focused perspective, sacrificing entertainment, authenticity and the irreverent humor that previously defined GTA. The female protagonist is particularly insufferable, with irritating dialogue, an unlikeable personality and painfully forced characterization.

Instead of delivering an entertaining sandbox experience, Rockstar seems more concerned with pushing a particular worldview and dictating how players should experience the game.

A complete disappointment that fails to live up to the franchise's legacy.

0/10.

author: BenChmark
quote:
After putting more than 40 hours into the game and having experienced most of the story, I can’t say it isn’t fun. But it isn’t a good GTA.

While it tries to modernize the franchise and become something of a spiritual successor to Red Dead Redemption 2 (if you haven’t played that one yet, I’d recommend playing RDR2 instead of GTA 6), it fails in many ways to live up to its own standards.

Although it looks absolutely stunning most of the time, it really struggles with low frame rates. Bugs are still very common. And to be fair, it’s a new release. But every other game gets criticized for being buggy at launch, so why should GTA 6 be treated differently?

I’ve had the sea disappear during diving missions, cars falling from the sky, NPCs standing halfway through doors, and save game issues that cost me hours of progress. All things considered, these issues are bearable for a new release, but they’re still annoying.

The level of detail is stunning. You can see how much love and effort went into creating this world and making it feel immersive. But the story is being celebrated as if it were the holy grail of innovative storytelling. There are so many games with far better stories. GTA 6 delivers hardcore clichés in just about every imaginable way.

It also constantly prevents you from acting freely in the way you’d expect from a GTA game. It cages you in, forces you to maintain a slow pace, and makes you follow instructions. That simply isn’t the GTA spirit.

A lot of people insult players who actually wanted GTA 6 to feel like GTA, calling them brain-rotted or simple-minded. But it’s just a matter of taste. If people wanted a new Sims game, they’d buy one, not GTA.

The game has lost its spirit, its identity, and its flavor.

The characters feel flat compared to the brilliant character writing in games like The Witcher 3, Baldur’s Gate 3, Disco Elysium, and many others.

Generally unfavorable if you’re looking for a Grand Theft Auto game that actually feels like **** you’re fine with a slow-paced crime simulator offering a rags-to-riches experience, some mildly criminal behavior, and a forced sense of romance, go ahead and buy **** probably won’t find a better life simulator right now.

author: matsminex
quote:
An impressive world without the soul of GTA...

At first I kept wondering: is this Grand Theft Auto or Grand Domestic Simulator?

Rockstar has once again built a world that is technically impressive, no doubt about that. But along the way they seem to have forgotten what actually makes GTA feel like GTA.

GTA V stood out with bold characters, charisma, crazy dialogue and sharp satire. GTA VI, on the other hand, sometimes feels more like interactive couples therapy than the sequel to one of the most iconic games ever made. Jason comes across as an emotionless rock with no presence or personality. The characters lack the spontaneity and charisma of Michael, Franklin and Trevor, and previous iconic GTA characters (I played many games myself). The story also often gets lost in long, slow dialogue and everyday tasks that do little for the pacing. And all the while, you have to kiss Lucia's feet and keep her happy. 

At times Rockstar seems so afraid of being politically incorrect that the spontaneity, satire and unfiltered personality that made GTA so recognizable fade into the background. Earlier GTA games had character, humor and a strong identity you could recognize right away .

This is the most expensive game ever made, but money can't buy passion. It's the exact same pattern we saw with Rings of Power.

Rockstar may have built a bigger world, but that doesn't make it a better GTA.

author: amiihan
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI – User Review

Rating: 4/10

Honestly, GTA 6 is disappointing. After all these years of waiting, I expected something much better. The storyline feels painfully slow, and the focus on Jason and Lucia's relationship doesn't make things any more interesting. Jason, in particular, feels like a pretty boring character. Compared to GTA V, where switching between Michael, Franklin, and Trevor kept things unpredictable, GTA 6 just doesn't have that same excitement.

The gameplay also has its problems. For a game that took this long to develop, it's disappointing that it doesn't even maintain a consistent 30 FPS. Frame drops are noticeable, and there are some  glitches throughout the experience. 

Another thing that bothers me is the overwhelming praise from streamers and critics giving this game perfect 10/10 scores. It feels like people are afraid to criticize it because of the hype surrounding Rockstar. Just because it's GTA doesn't automatically make it a masterpiece.

After years of waiting and all the hype, I expected something that would completely blow me away. Instead, it feels like a game that gets carried by its name and reputation rather than delivering the experience people were expecting.

GTA 6 isn't a terrible game, but it's nowhere near the masterpiece everyone makes it out to be.

author: Coldsmith
quote:
Let’s summarize:
- The game costs €100 and is currently available exclusively on consoles that cost €600 or more, just so they can double-dip on the game in two years when the PC version comes out.
- You pay €100 (€80 for a watered-down version of the game) for a plastic case with a code inside. The license for the game can theoretically be taken away from you at any time. If your PS or Xbox account gets banned, you’ll lose this and every other game without a disc forever. 
- It has an “optional” €13 monthly subscription that offers content in the game that normally should have been in the game from the start.
- The game removed everything that made GTA great in the past: You can’t bang prostitutes anymore, you can’t buy expensive properties like a successful gangster should and like you could in previous entries. You can’t steal cars in your own neighborhood even though the game is literally named that. You can’t shoot gays, lesbians, trans people, etc., and in gay bars you can’t even draw your weapon. Aside from your abusive Latina girlfriend who hides your baby from you, you can’t have any other romances in the game, and the only other sexual interaction in the game is with another dude. 
- It runs worse technically than Red Dead 2, which came out 10 years ago. In many cases it doesn’t even hit 30 FPS and causes headaches. - - It has more bugs than it should considering it was in development for 13 years and delayed multiple times. 
- All the old devs are gone and were replaced by woke left-wing activists projecting themselves into the game. 
- The male main character is a spineless cuck with no opinion of his own who is pretty boring and monotonous and agrees with his girlfriend on everything. 
- The female main character is an annoying “boss girl” self-insert character written by a woke activist, and it’s obvious she’s the real main character of the game. The guy is only there so the game doesn’t sell worse. 
- The story and dialogues were clearly written by women.
- The game is ultra boring for the first 10 to 20 hours and consists of chores, putting together IKEA tables, going grocery shopping for your girlfriend, and other “cuck simulator” activities. Meanwhile, other games start with bank heists and other sick action. 
- The game lost its soul because it wasn’t developed anymore by passionate gamer men who wanted to make a sick game (like the previous entries), but born out of corporate greed. The main purpose of the game is to make as much money as possible.
- The game isn’t unhinged like it used to be. The groups of people who would’ve been clowned on in earlier entries are protected this time. The humor isn’t the same as before either. Generic Marvel “comedy.” 
- Despite bugs, 30 FPS, missing content from earlier games, and obvious story and gameplay flaws, the game got a 99 critic score. Not even RDR2, which is way closer to a perfect game than GTA 6, would get a 99 score from me. No game in the world is that perfect.
People, wake up! Stop defending the megacorps that manipulate you and want your money and attention. The world is going down the drain right now, and all we care about is a stupid video game. Psyop well executed, I’d say. Video games aren’t passionate projects by hobbyist devs and people who like video games anymore. They only exist to milk your wallet, steal your attention and put a very specific worldview into your head. GTA 6 is no exception. The game is not good!

author: Rizzinomics
quote:
After 13 years of waiting, apparently Rockstar decided what the world really needed wasn't another Grand Theft Auto game, but a masterclass in being the perfect boyfriend. 

Welcome to Grand Theft Auto VI, where apparently being a criminal mastermind takes a backseat to buying your girlfriend flowers, picking up groceries, fixing the house, buying her clothes and making sure she's happy. Jason Duval isn't a criminal protagonist. He's a glorified personal assistant with a criminal record. The problem isn't that GTA has romance or relationships. 

Previous games had relationships, family drama and domestic storylines. The problem is the apparent emphasis on making Jason's relationship with Lucia such a central part of the experience, with an increasingly one-sided dynamic that makes him feel more like her errand boy than an independent character. Remember when GTA was about freedom? Robbing banks, causing absolute mayhem, making questionable decisions and being a complete menace to society? Now we're apparently being taught how to maintain a healthy household. 

And the irony is that Rockstar has spent years building a reputation around giving players freedom, only to introduce a protagonist whose personality seems to revolve around keeping his girlfriend satisfied. There's nothing wrong with having a relationship in a video game. There's something wrong with making relationship maintenance feel like a substitute for the criminal escapism people came to GTA for. 

13 years of anticipation for Grand Theft Auto, only to get Grand Theft Boyfriend. What a disappointment in terms of creative direction.

author: Iwott
quote:
After spending quite some time playing GTA 6, I have to admit that I'm genuinely disappointed. And surprisingly, my biggest issue isn't even the technical side of the game, but its very core: the story.

I find the narrative surprisingly uninteresting. I struggled to get invested in the events, to connect with the characters, or even to feel anything during certain moments. Everything feels emotionally flat. Missions, cutscenes and dialogue follow one another, but there's very little emotional weight or genuine motivation to make me want to see what happens next.

The Jason and Lucia duo didn't really convince me either. Their relationship failed to create the emotional connection I was hoping for, and I never truly felt attached to their journey.

What's even more frustrating is that Rockstar knows how to tell compelling stories. From a studio of this calibre, I expected so much more.

Visually, the game is impressive, no doubt about that. But beautiful graphics don't make a compelling story, and a massive open world doesn't automatically make an adventure memorable.

In the end, I feel like I've played a game that's absolutely stunning on the surface, but surprisingly empty when it comes to emotional depth.

GTA 6 might be a technical masterpiece, but a great game should be about more than what you see on screen. It should make you feel something. And unfortunately, this one left me completely cold.

author: usergamer727
quote:
I hate this game. Rockstar what have u done…

Franchement, je vais être totalement honnête : GTA 6 mérite un zéro sur vingt. Et je ne dis pas ça simplement pour provoquer ou faire le contraire de tout le monde. Je trouve qu’il y a un décalage absolument gigantesque entre l’engouement autour de ce jeu et ce qu’il semble réellement proposer. Depuis des années, on nous présente GTA 6 comme le jeu du siècle, comme une révolution vidéoludique, comme si Rockstar allait littéralement réinventer le jeu vidéo. À force de repousser les attentes toujours plus haut, on finit par créer une hype tellement démesurée qu’aucun jeu ne pourrait raisonnablement la satisfaire. Et c’est précisément ce qui me dérange. J’ai l’impression que les gens sont tellement occupés à glorifier Rockstar qu’ils en oublient de prendre du recul et de se demander si le jeu est réellement aussi exceptionnel qu’on le prétend. Les graphismes ? Très bien, mais des beaux graphismes ne font pas un bon jeu. Une ville immense ? D’accord, mais encore faut-il qu’elle soit intéressante, vivante et qu’on ait réellement envie de l’explorer. Des personnages ? Encore faut-il qu’ils soient attachants et que leur histoire soit captivante. On nous vend une expérience révolutionnaire alors que, pour l’instant, une bonne partie de l’argumentaire repose sur des bandes-annonces, des images soigneusement sélectionnées et des promesses. Je trouve également assez ridicule cette tendance à défendre absolument tout ce que fait Rockstar, comme si la moindre critique constituait un sacrilège. On peut apprécier une licence et reconnaître ses défauts. On peut même attendre un jeu pendant dix ans et finalement être déçu. Ce qui me dérange surtout, c’est cette impression que GTA 6 est devenu davantage un phénomène marketing qu’un simple jeu vidéo. Tout le monde semble déjà avoir décidé qu’il s’agissait d’un chef-d’œuvre avant même d’avoir pu réellement y jouer. Personnellement, je refuse de distribuer des notes sur la base d’une réputation, d’un logo ou d’une communauté de fans. Un jeu doit me convaincre par son contenu, son gameplay, son histoire et le plaisir qu’il procure, pas par le nombre d’années que j’ai attendu sa sortie. Et puisque je dois donner une note, je mets 0/20. Oui, zéro. Pas parce que je prétends que le jeu est techniquement mauvais sans l’avoir évalué, mais parce que je refuse de lui accorder le moindre point simplement parce que tout le monde semble considérer qu’il est intouchable. GTA 6 est probablement le jeu qui bénéficie du plus grand crédit d’avance de l’histoire du jeu vidéo. Et à mes yeux, ce crédit d’avance est précisément le problème. Et le pire c’est que le jeu a été repoussé deux fois, bah ptn j’imagine pas la gueule qu’il devait sortir lors de la première sortie prévue

Rockstar **** años en entregarnos una nueva generación de Grand Theft Auto, pero parece haber olvidado qué convirtió a esta franquicia en un fenómeno mundial.

GTA siempre destacó por su libertad, su humor negro, su sátira despiadada y su capacidad de burlarse absolutamente de todo. Nunca necesitó personajes moralmente ejemplares ni discursos para conectar con millones de jugadores.

No quería un GTA políticamente correcto. Quería un GTA que se atreviera a burlarse de todos, como siempre lo hizo.

author: SamTracey
quote: Rockstar’s long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI arrives as a perfect illustration of George Romero’s Dawn of the Dead. The record-breaking sales, the people calling in sick, the breathless coverage of every loading-screen detail is the living dead shuffling back into the mall, chasing the same empty consumption that the game itself once satirised. Worse, the game actively engineers the player. By locking Jason into a monogamous relationship with Lucia, removing prostitutes and side romances, and turning affection into a series of chores and gifts with little reciprocal agency, Rockstar has built a soft version of Huxley’s Brave New World. The player is not free to misbehave; he is gently conditioned into the approved couple dynamic, rewarded for compliance and denied the older sandbox vices. Yet the most humorous irony is watching large parts of the cultural “left” rush to defend this multi-billion-dollar product because it aligns with their preferred relationship aesthetics. The same voices that denounce corporate power suddenly discover that some corporations are more equal than others. What was once a vicious satire of American excess has become both the product and the propaganda. I wanted the old chaos. Instead I got a beautifully rendered cage.

author: NamelessAstral
quote: This may well be a polished commercial product, but the thing I feared most has happened anyway: Dan Houser’s departure really did strip GTA 6 of its soul. I cannot accept that this industrial junk—narrative and character writing flattened into hollow emptiness and papered over with graphics and sheer content volume—is the GTA we waited thirteen years for.Photorealistic game graphics are the least valuable thing a game can have. Over time, the visuals that once stunned you fade into nothing. Look back over the last ten or even twenty years: of the games that first hit you with their graphics, how many still hold up today? Only the ones that got by on a distinctive art style have a chance, and the GTA series is clearly not among them.Pouring resources into a game to pile on content is a way to show industrial muscle. It does not set the game’s tone, and it does not give the game a soul.What actually decides whether a game hits me, stays with me, and makes me think “this is a great game” every time I look back, even wanting to recommend it to friends and family, can only be the story, the direction, and the characters.Unfortunately, the opening of this game decides in advance that you must have a lover, not to mention that she's a stupid good-for-nothing.I can accept that I cannot freely shape the character I play the way I can in Cyberpunk 2077, Fallout, or The Elder Scrolls. That has always been GTA’s tradition. What I refuse is being handed such a central intimate relationship as a given—and you even have a child. I have to say this is nothing like Fallout 4. There, the player’s spouse is background, and the child is just a reason and a motive. In GTA 6, the entire main story revolves around that relationship, and it brings a pile of restrictions I cannot accept: you can’t do this, you can’t do that. So constrained. Is this still GTA? Even the ending is affected by the Criminal Profile. That is the system I hate most. I already loathed the similar chaos system in the Dishonored series for locking down how I **** I’m playing GTA, why can’t I run wild alone until I drop dead, like a dog chasing cars?

author: Ciccino11
quote:
After thirteen years of relentless hype, astronomical budgets, and industry-halting delays, Rockstar Games finally unleashed Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19, 2026. While mainstream critics fell over themselves to hand out automatic tens, playing this bloated, self-indulgent slog reveals a shocking truth: GTA 6 is not just a disappointment; it is the worst video game ever made. Every dollar of its rumored billion-dollar budget was spent actively sabotaging the concept of fun, burying the franchise’s iconic arcade chaos beneath a suffocating mountain of tedium, broken mechanics, and pretentious design.
The root of this disaster is Rockstar’s pathological obsession with hyper-realism at the expense of playability. Instead of an escapist crime sandbox, the developers built a miserable real-life chore simulator. Your first few hours aren't spent pulling off thrilling capers, but fixing leaky roofs, scrubbing grime, and enduring glacial, unskippable animations for every mundane action. The pacing is so sluggish it makes Red Dead Redemption 2 look like a twitch shooter. When a game forces you to carefully manage your outfit, vehicle appearance, and regional heat levels just because a neighbor saw you jaywalk, it ceases to be entertainment and becomes a second unpaid job.
Driving, the literal namesake of the franchise, has been utterly ruined. Rockstar replaced responsive, exhilarating vehicle controls with a punishing, brittle physics model where supercars handle like greased shopping carts and crumple like wet cardboard at the slightest tap. Clip a curb at forty miles per hour and your axle snaps, your engine sputters, and you are forced into an infuriating game of musical cars while hemorrhaging hard-earned cash at Pay-n-Sprays. Worse still, the game constantly traps you in artificially generated gridlock and roadworks, transforming high-speed getaways into bumper-to-bumper commutes.
The law enforcement system is an unforgivable exercise in player hostility. Gone is the thrilling, intuitive wanted-star chase of yesteryear. Now, escaping the initial pursuit only triggers a tedious "red star" surveillance phase where cops magically track your license plate and clothing across Leonida. You cannot simply lose the heat and move on; you must constantly duck into alleys to change shirts, swap vehicles, and hide from omni-present police scanners. It turns spontaneous mayhem—the very lifeblood of Grand Theft Auto—into a bureaucratic nightmare that punishes you for pulling the trigger.
Combat and movement fare no better. Controls feel unresponsive, heavy, and stubbornly stuck in 2013, making basic gunfights feel clunky and imprecise. The gunplay lacks punch, the cover system still glues you to the wrong walls at fatal moments, and the mission design remains rigidly linear. Step ten feet off the developer-mandated path during a heist, and you are greeted with an instant, **** mission failure screen. For a studio bragging about unprecedented freedom, Rockstar still treats players like toddlers on a leash.
Narratively, the game is a hollow, tonally confused mess. Jason and Lucia lack the magnetic charisma of past protagonists; Jason comes across as a cardboard cutout with zero emotional range, while their central Bonnie-and-Clyde romance feels forced and melodramatic. The biting, fearless satire that once defined the series has been neutered into safe, toothless commentary that pulls every punch. Even Vice City and the surrounding Leonida wetlands feel less like a vibrant playground and more like an empty museum of pretty reflections—a hollow tech demo obsessed with puddle physics while running at a sluggish, eye-straining thirty frames per second on modern hardware.
Grand Theft Auto VI is the ultimate monument to corporate hubris. It is a game that hates being a video game, mistaking friction for depth, misery for maturity, and graphical fidelity for soul. After more than a decade of waiting, Rockstar delivered an over-engineered, soul-crushing slog that fails at the single most basic requirement of the medium: being fun to play.

author: link2309
quote:
After 17 years of being a gamer and having the experience of this industry from knowing how they treat consumers, it’s clear GTA 6 completely forgot what made the franchise great. Gameplay is like salt—without it, the whole dish is ruined. Rockstar traded pure arcade fun for tedious hyper-realism: limiting weapon carrying to a car trunk, forcing gun-free "safe zones" inside clubs, and punishing classic open-world chaos with a hidden morality meter. Anyone who knew how they treated GTA online and have experience from the other GTA games, have experience to know what was coming, and people like me called it before it's release

Instead of innovating, it feels like a recycled mashup—mixing RDR2's slow restrictions, a cheap knockoff of San Andreas’s Officer Tenpenny (Mendez), and a bleak Bonnie-and-Clyde story with unrewarding endings and a time-loop post-game. People only defend this because of FOMO and Rockstar's past reputation. It is nowhere near worth $80+—wait until the next console generation and grab it in the $20–$30 bargain bin where it belongs. I'm glad i save up on this. Atrocious game, anyone rating this highly is purely coping lol

Moral: Never buy a game based the company's past reputation, graphics over gameplay or the hype folks create around it. If you want it always wait for the price to go down, coz it's all about quality per value at the end of the day to avoid losses. FOMO is a gimmick

author: Ramses9669
quote:
Disappointing after all the hype. Graphics alone don't make a great game.

Yeah, honestly, I'm just disappointed. I waited years for GTA 6, and while I expected a lot, I never thought I'd end up feeling this underwhelmed.

The launch was already rough with bugs, crashes, and technical issues, but that's not even my biggest problem. Even if I completely ignore those issues, what's left? A game with impressive graphics, but a mediocre story, underwhelming gameplay, and NPCs that are nowhere near as intelligent or realistic as Rockstar made us believe they'd be.

I've played around 13 hours, and sure, there were some good moments. But most of the time, I was genuinely bored. It often felt more like a glorified Sims simulator than the groundbreaking open-world experience we were promised. Everything looks incredible, but once you get past the visuals, there just isn't enough substance to keep me interested.
At some point, I genuinely thought I could've just gone outside and lived my actual life instead of spending hours pretending to live one in a video game.

And that's what frustrates me the most. I was genuinely excited at first. I wanted to love this game. But the more I played, the more I realized that all the hype, the massive budget, and the years of development don't automatically translate into a great gaming experience. 

For a game this expensive, with this much anticipation behind it, I expected something truly revolutionary. Instead, I got a beautiful-looking world that often feels surprisingly shallow.

Graphics: Incredible. Everything else: Nowhere near what I expected.

GTA 6 isn't necessarily the worst game I've played, but considering the expectations, the price, and the promises, it's easily one of my biggest gaming disappointments.

author: JoLan_07
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI – 1/10
This game has so many things worth criticizing that giving it a 10/10 feels just as ridiculous as giving it a 1/10. So, my initial review score will be exactly that: 1/10. That doesn’t mean my review is invalid, but I need to make several things absolutely clear.
1. No First-Person Mode. There is no first-person mode, and somehow none of the major critics seem to mention this. I guess that’s still a 10/10, right? They removed a feature that was already available in GTA V, a game originally released on PS3, and Red Dead Redemption 2, which came out on PS4. Yet somehow, GTA VI can’t have it? Seriously?
2. An Extremely Boring Protagonist
The protagonist is incredibly boring and has absolutely zero charisma. And apparently, I CAN’T CHEAT! This is the most anticipated game in 13 years, a game where you can supposedly build a relationship, yet I’m not even allowed to cheat on a woman who clearly isn’t mentally stable? That’s ridiculous. The lack of such a basic choice in a game that supposedly offers so much freedom is just stupid.
3. Jason’s Voice Acting
Jason’s voice acting is terrible. His delivery is so dull and lifeless that his dialogue genuinely makes me sleepy. Listening to him is a chore rather than an enjoyable part of the experience.
4. The Downgrade, Bugs, and the Media’s Double Standards (Cyberpunk) 
For what is supposed to be the most ambitious video game ever made, GTA VI is honestly a massive disappointment so far. The downgrade is noticeable, and don’t even get me started on all the glitches and bugs. But apparently, it’s still a 10/10 for the gaming press, right? What a **** we actually want games to improve, we can’t just stay silent and hand out perfect scores. Sometimes you have to be the black sheep and give an honest review, even if everyone disagrees with you. I’d rather be the black sheep than another mindless sheep blindly following the herd.
5. Ridiculous and Inconsistent Endings
Some of the endings are just ridiculous and completely inconsistent with the expectations many players have for the story. Sure, certain endings might work for a small minority of players, but that doesn’t mean the majority will find them satisfying. A game’s ending should feel earned, coherent, and consistent with the characters and the story. Not every ending deserves praise just because it’s different or unexpected.
Final thoughts: 1/10. A game doesn’t deserve a perfect score simply because it took years to make, has an enormous budget, or carries the weight of an iconic franchise. Judge the game for what it actually delivers, not for the expectations surrounding it.

author: Ambulanza
quote:
GTA VI: A boyfriend simulator that punishes chaos and kills sandbox fun.

I've played GTA VI for about six hours, and I'm already fed up with it.
After thirteen years of waiting, I expected the ultimate evolution of Grand Theft Auto: a massive, living, technologically impressive world, and above all, a giant sandbox where players could have fun on their own terms.
Instead, I got what feels like a Boyfriend Simulator disguised as Grand Theft Auto.
Endless dialogue, relationship drama I couldn't care less about, painfully scripted sequences, and missions that are simply boring. 
The bar fight after the prison release is a perfect example of this design philosophy: instead of letting me play, Rockstar seems determined to force me through its screenplay.
But the biggest problem is much worse.
GTA VI seems to have forgotten what made Grand Theft Auto special in the first place.
GTA has always been about freedom, chaos, experimentation, and having fun. Stealing cars, causing mayhem, getting into ridiculous police chases, and turning the entire city into your personal playground.
Now, apparently, I have to deal with negative karma, increasingly hostile police, and random pedestrians attacking me for seemingly no **** feels like the game is actively punishing me for doing exactly what GTA games have always encouraged me to enjoy.
I don't want to role-play as a responsible citizen. I don't want to manage a romantic relationship. I don't want to constantly worry about my character's reputation.
I bought Grand Theft Auto, not The Sims: Vice City Edition.

author: Forocochero
quote:
Look at the credits and you will immediately understand what happened to this franchise:

>GTA V main writers: Dan Houser, Rupert Humphries, and Michael Unsworth.
>GTA VI main writers: James Horton, Alexa D'Agostino, and Elizabeth Gauvey-Kern.

With this release, an era officially comes to an end. Apparently, from today onward, a new set of double standards rules the industry:

>Gaming journalists are suddenly never wrong.
>30 FPS with drops into the 20s is no longer a technical issue.
>Anti-consumer corporate practices no longer affect review scores.
>File size optimization is completely irrelevant.
>Not actually owning the game you paid for is "peak gaming."
>Buying an empty physical box with a garage-style poster inside is now considered a "lifehack."

Visually, I’ll give credit where it’s due: the game looks spectacular, the graphics are top-tier, and there is plenty of side content to pad out the runtime. 

Yet, despite all the technical sheen, I couldn’t shake one overwhelming feeling while playing: I was bored.

How is it possible that in a game literally titled Grand Theft Auto, stealing cars is more restricted and gated than in any previous entry in the franchise? Instead of immediate sandbox freedom, you’re bogged down by tedious, slow-paced everyday chores. 

That deliberate realism worked brilliantly in Red Dead Redemption 2 because immersing yourself in the daily grind of a 19th-century outlaw was novel and atmospheric. Doing mundane, modern-day errands in a world we already live in isn't immersive, it’s just boring.


Then there’s the story and cast, which completely lack the charisma that used to define Rockstar. The game forces you into a one-sided romance with a thoroughly toxic character (someone who mistreats her own kid, expects you to run constant errands for her with zero reciprocity), and is ready to go behind your back the second she feels neglected , all while forcing a guy who clearly has way better options to play the devoted errand boy for a mid latina coasting on physical appeal.

To top it all off, the entire game is soaked in that sterile, "safe-edgy" corporate tone. It only punches in directions that are politically safe and approved to criticize. The sharp, fearless satire is gone, you won’t find a character like Trevor anywhere near this script.Rockstar traded its rebellious identity, freedom, and bite for pretty graphics and a sanitized, tedious **** you want me to adjust the length (for instance, if you need to fit a strict character limit on Metacritic or YouTube comments) or tweak any specific phrase, just let me know!

And right on cue, this is the part where the gaming press goes into full retaliatory mode against the very players who built this franchise, insulting us, labeling us "toxic," and legitimizing personal attacks against real people simply for criticizing a video game. 

It’s the exact same smear campaign used against Tolkien fans during The Rings of Power Season 1, now recycled and aimed straight at us. Brace yourselves.

Anything goes for these people, desperate for quick cash and eager to use their shoehorned ideologies as a weapon against the fans rather than ever owning up to their own mediocrity.

author: E0syy
quote:
Rockstar delivered a stunningly photorealistic, grounded game, but at the cost of losing the whole Grand Theft Auto vibe. Compared to all the hype from the media and the players (myself included), it's a huge disappointment. As I said before, the only two good things about this game are:	
- the graphics and world design,	
- the random world events you can discover throughout the game.
My problems with the game:	
- Jason has no personality. He's just empty, probably the most boring protagonist in any Rockstar game.
- The plot is really weak. Missions like buying flowers or groceries for Lucia just don't fit the GTA vibe, where you play extremely dangerous characters capable of atrocities.	
- Shooting is the best mechanic in the game, but you get punished for using it. In the first 7 hours of the main story there's maybe 20–30 minutes of actual combat. A great mechanic, terribly underused.	
- “Grand Theft Auto" without stealing supercars at the start. Don't get me wrong: I understand why they locked supercars early on and that they wanted the game to feel realistic. I just don't think that's the direction they should have taken.	
- The prologue is a separate mission, but the whole of Chapter 1 feels like a prologue. This is subjective, but 20 missions that take 8–9 hours to get through remind me of the start of Red Dead Redemption 2. The difference is that RDR2 had a lot more going on than GTA VI does.	
- 30 fps with drops to 26 on a base PS5 makes the game feel clunky.
My subjective verdict: If I had known that this game would punish me for everything I used to do in previous GTA games just for fun, I would never have bought it. GTA VI stands far apart from what the series used to be. If you're thinking about buying it, first ask yourself what you actually want from it, because this is a completely different production from the GTA titles of the past.

author: ramelow
quote:
The biggest issue for me is the pacing and overall feel of the game. It doesn’t feel like a classic Grand Theft Auto. It feels much closer to an improved Red Dead Redemption 2 — slow, immersion-heavy, full of everyday activities and “chores.” There’s a strong life-sim vibe running through it, almost like The Sims mixed with Rockstar’s usual open world. After waiting this long, I expected more chaos and freedom, not something that feels this controlled and deliberate.
The dual-protagonist system with Jason and Lucia is another major problem for me. The game puts a lot of focus on Lucia, and the relationship system feels very one-sided. Jason is heavily restricted — he has to stay loyal, buy her gifts, and basically play the supportive boyfriend role, while Lucia seems to have more freedom in how she acts. A lot of people online are already calling it a “cuck simulator,” and I can see why that reaction exists. It doesn’t feel like the classic GTA freedom where you could do whatever you wanted.

author: Rotinpeaches
quote:
First of all, as a game, GTA has done an incredible job to the details, technical and graphical finesse, as well as the gigantic size of the map. If it was released under a different name, by a different publisher, without all the hype, marketing and delays, my score would be different. Hypocritical? Not really, and here is why. 

From as early as the top down GTA 1, GTA 2, GTA London series, the series has always considered a certain theme, a woven thread that would expand and come back with every new generation. A theme that you would instantly recognize the moment you started playing. A theme not influenced by politics or world events. 

And that's where GTA 6 has lost its plot majorly. Games are supposed to be places to escape reality, to be immersed in a fantasy world where creative expression is not limited in any way. And that, unfortunately, has been lost. 

The artistic language is clearly influenced by contemporary, societal and political factors. One could argue about the multitude of reasons why, but in the end, that won't change the game and it doesn't really matter. 

The facts are as they are, GTA has lots its soul and has gone astray from the legendary behemoth it once was.

author: JasonWinston
quote:
After a 13-year wait, Rockstar has delivered an unoptimized, sluggish life-sim that completely forgets what makes Grand Theft Auto fun. The visual scale of the map cannot hide the massive cracks in this broken, unplaytested product.
Terrible Optimization: In 2026, a premium title should easily maintain 30fps. Instead, this game constantly chugs and aggressively dips into the low 20s during dense open-world segments or basic driving.
Sidelined Characters: The narrative balance is entirely broken. Even before major plot points hit, Jason is immediately sidelined into a bland, one-note accomplice with zero meaningful character development across 15+ hours.
Boring, Lifeless Pacing: The lively, satirical chaos of past games has been replaced by a tedious, slow-burn "immersive life-sim." The missions are uninspired chores that drain every ounce of fun from the sandbox.
Unforgiving Save System: The auto-save strictly binds itself to main story milestones. If you drop the story to explore side missions and the game inevitably crashes, the system completely ignores your hours of open-world progression, wiping out massive chunks of playtime instantly.Everything that made GTA great is missing from this soulless game. Rockstar has managed to completely ruin a decade of anticipation. Save your money—this is a total failure on every technical and mechanical level.

author: Sunluss
quote: Jason Might Be the Worst Protagonist Rockstar Has Ever Written. While I appreciate the pacing of GTA 6, I find its story increasingly frustrating, largely because of how poorly Jason is characterised. He comes across as painfully bland, spineless and lacking any real personality or conviction. My biggest issue is the disconnect between Jason’s decisions and the choices I would personally make. I understand that this is a narrative-driven game and that I’m playing an established character rather than creating my own. I don’t expect complete freedom over every decision, but I do expect a protagonist whose actions I can at least understand, respect or find compelling. There’s something uniquely frustrating about having to actively participate in choices you find humiliating. It’s one thing to watch a fictional character behave in a way you disagree with; it’s another to spend hours personally carrying out those actions. Rather than feeling like a capable, independent protagonist, I feel like some spineless chore boy, constantly doing other people’s bidding without meaningful resistance. Jason doesn’t make me feel powerful, respected or invested in his circumstances. He makes me feel like a glorified errand boy with absolutely no backbone. This is particularly disappointing coming from Rockstar, a studio responsible for characters like Arthur Morgan, John Marston and Niko Bellic. These characters made plenty of questionable decisions, but they possessed distinct personalities, principles and motivations. Even when I disagreed with their actions, I could understand why they made those choices. With Jason, I struggle to find that same justification. His decisions feel less like those of an independently minded individual and more like the behaviour of someone who simply allows himself to be pushed around. I don’t need Jason to reflect my personality or morality. I simply need him to be someone whose decisions feel justified by compelling motivations. A protagonist can be weak, submissive or easily manipulated and still be brilliantly written. But Jason’s apparent passivity doesn’t make him interesting; it makes him insufferable. Ultimately, I enjoy the pacing and graphics, but the more the story progresses, the more I resent being forced to play as a character whose choices I find fundamentally objectionable. For a studio responsible for some of gaming’s greatest protagonists, Jason feels like an extraordinary step backwards.

Gameplay is just GTA V with a few extras, anything new or innovative, just the same formula as GTA IV that followed with GTA V. The physical combat is straight up ripped off from rdr2, nothing else.
The story is one of the worst stories that Rockstar has offered through the years. No character development, and no real personality between the protagonists. Jason and Lucía relationship is just... A pretty cliché relationship outside of the crime scene.

The release has been horrible, full of bugs, comparable to Cyberpunk 2077 release. This is unacceptable in a 13 year wait videogame with a 2 Billion budget. It is not unplayable, but bugs and glitches are recurrent and they lower the quality of the game a lot.

Lastly, the FPS rate. I am not really complaining about 30 fps, I think that if managed correctly they look fine, for example, the Switch 1 version of BOTW. But here, frame drops are constant on a PS5 and even thought it is true that in PS5 Pro they are more stable, it still drops a lot in gunfights or crowd areas.

This is not the game we expected and deserved for almost 100€, we are dissappointed.

author: Apherna
quote:
I wanted Grand Theft Auto, not Red Dead Redemption.
Gabe Newell once said, realism isn't fun. I play video games to have fun, not to simulate every little inconvenience of real life.

And don't get me wrong, I'm not against realism in video games. Quite the opposite, actually. I love realistic mechanics when they're well implemented and genuinely improve the gameplay. Take Helldivers 2, for example. Its reloading system adds an extra layer of difficulty and makes you think about how you manage your ammunition, but it never stops being fun. It makes the game more challenging without taking away from the experience.

That's what good realism should be: something that adds to the gameplay, not something that gets in the way of **** seriously, not being able to steal my damn neighbour's car because he'll recognize me? In a GTA game? Who the **** cares?The fact that you can't carry as many weapons as you want. 

A morality system??? In GTA???
I can understand these mechanics in RDR2, but we're talking about GTA here. The whole point is to mess around with everything and everyone.
Having to put gas in your car? This isn't Mafia, it's GTA, goddammit.
You can't even steal certain cars because the game artificially locks them behind endgame progression. In GTA IV and V, you could steal an Infernus or an Adder during the early game without any problem. 
Why take away that freedom?

And let's not even talk about Jason, who feels like an empty shell. Even if we put aside all the random chores you're forced to do at the beginning of the game, the missions themselves are boring as hell. 
Driving from point A to point B while listening to conversations isn't exactly exciting gameplay. 
And it's especially great when you have to keep your eyes glued to the subtitles instead of the road.

I have time for games like this, but holy ****, I genuinely feel sorry for people who come home after a long day at work, boot up the so-called "game of the decade", and end up playing this.

Overall, it feels like Red Dead Redemption with a GTA skin, except Rockstar somehow left out some of the best things about Red Dead. Namely, the story.

I've also heard people saying that anyone who dislikes GTA 6 must have a short attention span, be stupid, be too young, or whatever other excuse they can come up with.
People keep trying to find excuses to defend this game, as if every criticism needs to be dismissed somehow. You can enjoy a game while acknowledging its flaws. And you can dislike a game without being an idiot who doesn't understand its design.
I paid for GTA, not Red Dead Redemption 3.

We could also talk about performance issues and pricing, but I'll spare myself the time. Plenty of other reviews have already covered those topics.

All I wanted was to mess around in a fictional world, man.Some players will say, "But you can still do that!"
No, not really. Not when the consequences of doing so become so restrictive that they actively discourage you from having fun.

And that's the irony: I play GTA to escape real life, not to deal with another set of real-life inconveniences

author: taktlos
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI is a massive disappointment that completely loses what made the franchise iconic, and the manufactured hype around it only makes it worse. Instead of the raw, unfiltered sandbox freedom and over-the-top power fantasy of classic Vice City, Rockstar delivered a sanitized, overly restrictive experience.

You can’t even build a real criminal empire or freely buy luxury properties with your own money. Everything is locked behind scripted story progression and basic garages. On top of that, the game constantly slows you down with rigid, linear mission design, a tiny weapon wheel that forces you to run back to your car trunk for guns, punishing wanted levels, and constant relationship maintenance instead of letting you cause unrestricted chaos. Add in unstable 30 FPS performance on consoles, launch bugs, and GTA+ monetization pushed into a full-priced single-player game, and it’s clear this is a massive step backward.

The writing also feels completely watered down by modern toxic-feminist messaging. Instead of the edgy, anything-goes satire GTA used to be famous for, you are stuck babysitting a relationship meter the entire game, answering goodnight texts, holding hands, and staying strictly loyal to a flawless "girlboss" lead while classic sandbox freedom gets stripped out. Worst of all, anytime longtime fans point out how sanitized and restrictive this game actually is, defenders immediately throw around lazy buzzwords like "incel" to shut down valid criticism, even when it’s obvious the classic GTA soul is missing.

Verdict: All hype, pretty graphics, and zero GTA soul. A sluggish, preachy mess that forgets why people loved Grand Theft Auto in the first place.

author: worthitnow
quote:
I don't know what this nonsense is but it's not GTA, the main characters of Lucia and Jason are particularly unlikable, Lucia is a petulant self centered spoiled brat, and Jason is just a lifeless husk. The larger than life characterisation of past games is nowhere to be seen. I simply did not care what happened to either of them, pretty much from the outset.

The first half of the game is just boring, performing chores is not gaming, I perform chores in real life, who on earth thought this was a good idea, it feels like padding, and on a game that took, 13 years to make and $1b, thats unforgivable.

The game fails to fix some of GTA's biggest flaws, mission structure is the same old story, speak to an NPC drive a bit, it all goes wrong shoot your way out. they had the time and budget to break the mould but didn't.

The satire of all sides of the political spectrum is also gone, the game takes a decidedly sympathetic view of the left, which should be no surprise to anyone, given the woke DEI driven culture of western game studios. The biting commentary is just MIA the game failed to make me laugh the way previous games have, it's just very sanitised and millennial coded.

Performance is abysmal, I mean utterly ridiculous in 2026. the game stutters along at 20-30 fps, and when in combat it can get to slideshow type frame rates, I had to turn off due to nausea on multiple occasions. It's also buggy as hell, and some of these bugs are in the first few hours, after 13 years of development, it's odd to say the least that bugs in the first half of the game are so prevalent, what were the play testers doing for 13 years.

Overall, it's not GTA, but some kind of weird life sim, the main characters are utterly forgettable, and although the world is full it feels strangely lifeless, there is no real character to the world, its just there. Missions are same old same old. the story is often nonsensical, and the quality of writing is a definite downgrade from GTA V, the world is sanitised within an inch of it's life, the game takes no risks whatsoever. Performance is just ridiculous, often unplayable, what a waste of £80, I will never trust Rockstar again after this mess.

author: asura97

I’ve only been playing for 15 hours, so my rating might still go up or down as the time goes on. As it stands, I’m really disappointed with the game. I think this game is much worse than GTA: San Andreas, GTA 4 and GTA 5. I feel extremely restricted in this game, and everything is annoyingly regimented. There is much less freedom and fun than in previous GTA games. I have to eat, drink, work out, my car keeps breaking down, and I have to fill up the gas all the time. I can’t visit prostitutes, certain NPCs and locations can’t be attacked, you can’t carry an unlimited number of weapons, you can’t buy real estate, you can’t purchase shares and there are no boats or airplanes which you can buy. I also cant produce drugs or open a gang. Car tuning is, unfortunately, very very basic, and the morale system is absolute GARBAGE. The game now actively punishes you with permanent debuffs if you act recklessly or overly violently. Now you’re even being conditioned regarding your behavior in GTA (pathetic and embarrassing). There are no more fun side jobs. Also, the whole game is just about pleasing Lucia. The game doesn’t feel like a real GTA anymore. Nothing about the game is 100% fun, over-the-top, or controversial anymore. It’s hard to believe this came from Rockstar. On top of that, there’s the 30 fps and the clunky controls/aiming/driving. The game is really mediocre. I’d rather play GTA: San Andreas, GTA 4, GTA 5, or Sleeping Dogs than this. Unfortunately, this game is yet another reason why you can no longer trust gaming journalists. Objectively speaking, this game is not a 99 and its really not innovative at all. author: Nick2310
quote:
The only thing that lives up to the hype about this game is the graphics; they are as good as, no better than, what the reviews suggest. Incredible engineering by the GTA team. However, there are a few things that hold it back for me.

1. The life sim aspects: I get it, some people love the idea of total immersion in a world where you shower, work out, eat, sleep, etc. I do not. It’s boring, tedious, and something I should be allowed to turn off. The life sim aspects directly affect gameplay, so I am essentially forced to pull both triggers while mashing X for the 753rd time in order to bust out some bench presses. How Rockstar thought this was fun is beyond me.

2. Jason’s voice: I find he mumbles a lot of his lines, and I find him hard to understand a lot of the time. I like his personality. I like the fact that he is almost like a blank slate for the player to impose themselves on. But yeah, the voice often just seems unclear.

3. The driving: Rockstar just can’t get this right, can they? It’s such an unfun driving model. Yeah, they are going for hyper-realism. It’s their choice. And they have delivered an exceptional physics engine. But the driving is just boring.

4. Their relationship: I find Jason and Lucia’s relationship to feel a little empty and forced, even though I did all the extra relationship activities. It never felt like they had a real connection. I don’t think it was handled well in the game. Jason never seems that interested in her. I know that’s part of his personality, but it never once came across to me like these people loved each other. They came across like a couple who were together because they had a child together and just so happened to find each other attractive. I think other RPG games like Mass Effect and Baldur’s Gate handled romances vastly better.

5. Lack of creativity: The biggest failure of the game, though, by far, is the fact that this GTA does nothing new. Nothing. It has actually shocked me so far how stagnant and derivative the gameplay has felt. It feels like a game that was designed 15 years ago, with RDR2 life sim aspects bolted on. They are doing nothing new.

6. The new cop system: Much has been said about the new cop system, how it’s far more realistic, etc. I think it’s a vast downgrade from the simple system that worked before. Now the cops are aware of different aspects of you, like your car, car colour, clothes, etc. The problem is that every cop chase then descends into the same old boring routine: get ahead, drive away, change clothes, put on a hat, put on sunglasses, spray-paint the car. Rinse and repeat. Heat lost. It’s just another tedious, menu-hopping, over-engineered system that replaces a system that worked perfectly well. The old system created bedlam and incredible car chases with the police as you tried to evade them. This just has you driving around the corner and swapping things out in a radial menu! I mean, who—who thought this would be more fun? 

Anyway, my final word on this is: if you haven’t bought the game yet, please hold off. Wait a year. Get it at a discount. 

I played Saints Row 3 for the first time ever earlier this year, and from a gameplay point of view, that game is vastly more fun than GTA 6. 

If I could, I’d ask Sony for my money back. If I could trade the game in as a physical release, I would. 

It feels like to me that the gaming press has done every gamer a disservice by not calling out these glaring issues. As if they were all desperate for GTA to be a success, so fearful that if it wasn’t the game industry would collapse, gaming all these review sites with it. The problem is though, all it has done is made me distrust game journalism. By awarding this game the perfect score, which in no way it deserves, they have collectively acted as cowards, unwilling to call the game out for what it is: an incredible looking game with out dated game mechanics, boring life sim aspects, and poor gameplay choices.

author: Al12dean
quote:
Verdict: not worth it right now. I played the whole thing and requested a refund.
Performance and polish
Console is locked at 30fps with no 60fps mode, and driving feels rough. I've seen map falls and glitches. As a developer, the icons and UI look unfinished to me. It feels rushed, and I believe it was released in this state because delaying again would have hurt with investors.
Development
I don't believe real production started right after Red Dead 2. My read is that Rockstar spent years milking GTA Online and only got serious after the 2022 leak, then got pushed even harder by the Cyberleek leaks. The 2022 leak looked like a framework, not a game.
Systems that fight the sandbox
Hunger is not optional. and overeating is penalized too. You can't steal cars in your own neighborhood or equip weapons at home. For a game called Grand Theft Auto, that's a big limit. Autosave wasn't active right away, which is the bare minimum.
Monetization and release
Some in-world shops and salons are locked behind the Ultimate Edition. At launch, GTA+ was reportedly sold with a promise that it wouldn't lock gameplay behind a paywall. It's digital-only, and boxed copies ship with download codes, with reports of missing or already-used ones.
Content and tone
The sex-for-hire mechanic is gone for the first time since 2001. Strip clubs remain, but without that edge and with NSFW limits, I think the game lost what made GTA fun. I can't even cheat, yet the relationship system makes it feel like a dating sim. I support women's rights and normal feminism, but I don't like having it forced on me, and I feel the tone has been shifted toward a left-leaning audience compared with older games. I think it's designed for roleplayers, not people who want chaos, and that crowd will be the one that sticks around once online servers launch. The ending disappointed me.
Critics vs. players
Critics gave it a 99, but the Metacritic user score is around 5. I scrolled through comment sections on the biggest streams and saw almost nothing positive, and the few positive comments I saw got buried. I don't trust early-access coverage. I suspect gifts, access, and fear of losing publisher relationships shaped how many creators and outlets covered it, and I suspect Rockstar pressures people who get early access.
Refunds
I've seen claims it's the most refunded game ever. I can't point to public data, but I refunded mine, and I'm seeing others do the same.
Prediction
Once the hype fades, I expect the player base to drop sharply within one to three months. GTA V stays the better sandbox, and GTA 6 becomes a niche roleplay game.
Score: _/10

author: DepictDev
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI is a perfect game. A perfect game for people who don't actually play games. For those whose entire gaming experience consists of FIFA and Call of Duty. For people who apparently have no life of their own and need a virtual one to compensate.

The game is bloated with pointless activities, tedious animations, and unnecessary realism that adds absolutely nothing to the gameplay. Everything takes forever, as if wasting the player's time were some revolutionary design philosophy. Rockstar seems to have forgotten that video games are supposed to be fun, not a second job.

The characters are painfully uninteresting, the story fails to give you anyone worth caring about, and the female protagonist is especially off-putting. Instead of making me want to spend more time in this world, the game constantly gives me reasons to leave it.

And somehow, this glorified life simulator was nominated for Best Art Direction at The Game Awards. Seriously? Since when does copying reality count as outstanding artistic direction? Photorealism is not an art style, and technical fidelity is not the same thing as artistic vision.

The most ridiculous part is seeing professional critics hand out perfect 100/100 scores while openly admitting the game has flaws. Apparently, the hype surrounding GTA is more important than actually evaluating the game. At this point, I have to wonder whether these reviewers have ever experienced anything outside Rockstar's carefully manufactured virtual world.

Final verdict: 2/10. One of the most boring life simulators ever disguised as a video game. Basically The Sims 6, except with guns, cars, and an astronomical marketing budget.

author: Kamdislegacy
quote: GTA VI died the moment Dan Houser left Rockstar.What remains is a glorified Sims-style drama: Obsessed with identity politics, Forced strong-female-character clichés, and Spineless male protagonists. This isn't the Grand Theft Auto we knew. It's a hollow imitation of what GTA once stood **** people giving GTA VI high scores aren't GTA V fans; they're Sims 5 fans. I refuse to believe that someone who genuinely enjoyed playing as Trevor Philips in GTA V could possibly celebrate this miserable excuse for a story or a character like Lucia. We've gone from Trevor's insanity to a watered-down soap opera pretending to be Grand Theft Auto.Michael fought for himself and his family in a brutal criminal world. Even his chilling threats toward Amanda showed how ruthless he could be. Trevor was a monster, yet he visited the friend he'd believed dead, asked about Jimmy, and protected Tracey by humiliating a sleazy TV host. Beneath the violence, these men had loyalty, contradictions, and a fierce sense of family. That's what made them unforgettable: not flawless heroes, but characters with conviction.Here's the worst part of the narrative.There is a reason you don't see children walking around in GTA's criminal sandbox. It's a brutal world of robbery, murder, corruption, and organized crime. Rockstar understood why children should be kept out of that **** they apparently introduce a child into this miserable **** are presented with a mother unprepared to raise her child, with the father absent or unknown, who chooses crime over seeking **** gets arrested. The child is placed under state protection, presumably to provide a safer and more stable life. And instead of recognizing the consequences of her decisions, she resents the situation, becomes involved in even more criminal activity, drags her ex-boyfriend into more trouble, and ruins their lives **** we're supposed to admire this character? We're supposed to sympathize with this absolute train wreck of irresponsible decisions?They use a child as an emotional plot device to justify an increasingly unbearable protagonist's reckless **** what? Cheap drama? Forced emotional manipulation? Another desperate attempt to make a deeply irresponsible character seem sympathetic?Rockstar appears willing to abandon its own long-standing creative boundaries just to deliver this miserable story.Somehow, after all of that, we're expected to celebrate these two protagonists as the future of Grand Theft Auto.From characters like Trevor Philips to this? What an embarrassing direction for a once-fearless franchise.From what I've seen, female characters can humiliate, provoke, and physically attack male characters, yet the consequences seem completely inconsistent when the situation is reversed. If a female NPC attacks the player, the world apparently treats it as perfectly acceptable. But retaliate, and suddenly everyone is ready to punish you.What kind of ridiculous double standard is that?!Instead of believable characters and consistent mechanics, it feels like we're being handed a world where exaggerated, supposedly empowered female characters dominate deliberately weakened and submissive male ****'re supposedly playing a game where players can commit armed robberies, engage in massive shootouts, and attack heavily defended police or military facilities. Yet the so-called "gta6 people" and environmental activists reportedly receive special protection from player **** can a game celebrate unrestricted criminal chaos while selectively protecting certain NPCs from the very mechanics that define its universe?This isn't about whether those characters should exist in the game. It's about consistency. If Rockstar wants to build a believable sandbox, gameplay mechanics should not arbitrarily change according to the social or political message attached to an NPC.Stop pretending that forcing ideological messaging into a criminal sandbox automatically makes the writing mature or **** one thing GTA VI genuinely deserves praise for is its technical **** graphics, detail, and engineering are **** extraordinary technology cannot rescue what I consider a fundamentally disappointing creative direction.With an entirely different story, compelling protagonists, and without what feels like intrusive ideological messaging, this could have been something extraordinary.Instead, Rockstar appears to have built an incredible technological achievement around a narrative I find almost impossible to **** to those handing out perfect scores while dismissing every criticism of the writing, characters, and restrictive gameplay decisions: I seriously question how honestly you're evaluating the experience.A technological masterpiece is not automatically a masterpiece of game design or **** deserved better. And after all these years, so did its players.

author: DeLaMonkey
quote: I really wanted to like this game, but it's one of the biggest letdowns I've ever played. The story is awful. Jason and Lucia are boring and have no chemistry at all. Everyone keeps calling it a mature love story, but it's just two people having the same mopey conversation over and over for 40 hours. Neither of them has any real personality. Jason is completely flat and Lucia gets one trait that the game keeps hammering on start to finish. The dialogue tries way too hard to sound deep. Nothing interesting happens for huge stretches, there are no real stakes, and by the end I didn't care what happened to either of them. You're just relieved it's over. The satire that made GTA what it is is basically gone too. The older games were funny and actually had something to say. This one takes itself way too seriously and has nothing to say at all. There's also barely any action. Most of your time goes on driving somewhere, talking to someone, then driving somewhere else, over and over. It's a chore simulator. I kept waiting for it to pick up and it never did. The map is detailed and looks great, but that doesn't matter when there's nothing fun to do in it. Honestly it plays like a Ubisoft game. Strip the Rockstar name off and you've got a Far Cry game, a big pretty open world, a story that thinks it's deeper than it is, and a pile of filler to pad out the runtime. Far Cry is trash, and Rockstar spent 13 years and who knows how much money making their own version of it. The graphics are the only thing it really has going for it. Everything else is boring and slow, and the story is a massive letdown. I don't get the perfect scores at all, and I think a lot of people are just hyping it up because they waited so long. Do not let a single person in that building touch the development of Online, that's the only way this dumpster fire will end. And the coping will end they're just in denial for now.
