author: WaveWaveYT_
quote:
I’m writing this review because I love the entire series, and I don’t want to see the game die due to decisions that are being presented as "good." 
First of all, the story is boring; the most important elements, the characters, lack any life. Take the main characters: Lucia completely dominates Jason, and it shows, Jason barely opens his mouth to speak, and he has absolutely no vitality or emotion. It’s incredibly difficult to build any rapport or narrative between just these two characters. Rockstar tried, but it’s clear they didn’t succeed. The supporting characters lack any distinct personality; sure, they exist and go about their business, but that’s about it. The mechanics are interesting, but we expected more, for instance, that infamous bit where a bottle just suddenly appears in a character's hand. We didn’t ask for an "honor" system, and there’s no logical reason for it to be included; it feels forced and restrictive, it’s not as if I’m just going around hitting people over the head. From what I understand, the game supports the LGBT community, a deplorable move for Rockstar. Don’t get me wrong, I have nothing against the people themselves, but Rockstar, with their history of edgy, often over-the-top humor, just isn't the type of company for this. Also, I don’t get why there’s hate directed toward the "furry" community when it’s essentially the same thing as the LGBT community, it makes no sense to me. You can’t have any romantic interest other than Lucia; it feels forced and illogical. There are countless other reasons, but I can’t cover them all here.  To explain my perspective, here is a comparison between GTA 6 and other Rockstar games.
 In GTA 4, the protagonist is from Yugoslavia, and it really shows; he has the temperament of an avenger, quick to start a fight and the type of person who doesn't get along with his cousin. In RDR 2, we have Arthur Morgan, a remarkably well-crafted and cohesive character with a compelling backstory; he starts off as an immovable force, only to eventually crumble under the pressure of his circumstances. It’s a deeply moving experience, you aren't forced into a single path, and the "honor" system is central to the game; it matters immensely, which is why "redemption" is in the title. 
GTA 5 features three characters, offering a wider range of possibilities. Franklin comes from the streets, he’s right at the heart of the criminal world, a reality you can truly see and feel. 
Michael is a man who has stepped back from that life; he’s a family man struggling with personal issues and communication, a fallen figure who, at times, just completely gives up on life. 
Then there’s Trevor, who makes the story truly entertaining, he’s a man who fights everyone and embodies the very definition of "GTA-style" insanity.
 In GTA: San Andreas, we have CJ, a Black protagonist living amidst gang life; it’s fascinating to get a glimpse into that world and all its associated chaos. A common thread across these games is that the first mission usually involves stealing something, a car or some other vehicle. In GTA 6, by contrast, the opening missions involve... cleaning up a house. The "honor" system feels completely out of place here.
 In GTA 5, the characters were forced to steal just to survive, and from there, everything spiraled out of control.  Lucia wants to steal just for the sake of having things, a pathetic story.
 If I’m to be silenced for my own opinions, and if I’ve offended anyone with my previous remarks, I apologie, well, I’ve loved this series since I was 8 years old, back when I didn’t even know what I was doing on that computer, all the way back to GTA III. 
You can find more information online about how the trailer doesn’t align with the actual game, why the game is capped at 30 fps, and so on; I know all of it, but I’m not going to cover every single point. It’s just sad... I hate that I have to witness this.

author: TPrutsch
quote:
After a 13-year wait, two delays, and an estimated billion-dollar development budget, Rockstar delivered a game that looks like a technical showcase in trailers but plays like an unfinished product on launch day. Critics somehow handed it near-perfect scores; the actual experience for many players is a mess of crashes, softlocks, broken physics, and a stubborn 30 fps cap that makes the open world feel sluggish.
The most common problems hit early and hard. Characters regularly fall through the map (Lucia in the prologue is a frequent victim—sometimes she respawns, sometimes you have to restart the whole section). Clipping is rampant: people walk through walls, sink into couches, and pass through vehicles and objects with no collision. Physics regularly break—cars launch into the sky after minor collisions, aircraft fly clean through buildings, and NPCs swim sideways through the water. Mission-breaking softlocks exist (one early Lucia mission becomes unfinishable after leaving a bank), and crashes or freezes during the prologue have already wiped progress for some players. Missing textures, floating objects, audio glitches, and lost autosaves round out the technical problems reported across both PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.Performance is a major letdown for a game this hyped. Rockstar locked the title at 30 fps across the board—including on PS5 Pro—with no performance mode. Driving and dense scenes feel choppy, and base PS5 players have reported drops into the 15–20 fps range during shootouts and busy areas. Combined with a ~210–212 GB install (physical copies are code-in-box, not discs) and PlayStation Network sign-in issues during the launch rush, getting into and staying in the game is more frustrating than it should be.
Beyond the bugs, the launch itself feels incomplete. There’s no PC version and no online mode at release—just the single-player story of Jason and Lucia in Leonida/Vice City. The world can look impressive when it works, and the dual-protagonist setup has potential, but constant interruptions from glitches, softlocks, and performance problems undercut any sense of immersion or polish. After more than a decade and multiple delays specifically to “finish the game to the level of polish players expect,” this is the opposite of what Rockstar’s track record suggested.
A 3/10 reflects a title that is frequently broken, artificially frame-rate limited, and missing key platforms and modes at launch. The bones **** GTA game are somewhere under the glitches, but right now too many people are falling through the map, restarting missions, or fighting 30 fps stutter instead of actually playing. Wait for patches (or a PC release) unless you enjoy debugging a billion-dollar open world.

author: SaikZero
quote:
Mucho espectáculo sin excelencia.

GTA VI es un despliegue de producción, pero como videojuego me parece una obra profundamente sobrevalorada. Su mayor virtud es también su principal recurso para impresionar: un mundo gigantesco, visualmente espectacular y saturado de detalles. Sin embargo, jugarno no es verdaderamente extraordinario.

Apartado técnico: El nivel de detalle visual, las animaciones, la iluminación y la ambientación son sobresalientes, pero resulta difícil hablar de excelencia técnica sin cuestionar un rendimiento limitado a 30 FPS en consolas, con caídas adicionales en situaciones exigentes. Hay una contradicción entre la ambición tecnológica que presume el juego y las limitaciones de su ejecución. Los problemas de rendimiento no son una cuestión que afectan directamente la fluidez y la respuesta de la experiencia.

Jugabilidad y controles: La complejidad de sus sistemas no significan mejores mecánicas. Los controles contextuales pueden resultar torpes, algunas acciones se confunden entre sí y ejecutar una interacción sencilla puede convertirse en un dolor de cabeza. El combate tambien tiene problemas: la selección de armas y ciertas acciones durante los enfrentamientos entorpecen el ritmo.

Diseño de misiones: Su mundo presume libertad, pero no siempre se traslada a las misiones. Existen situaciones en las que el jugador tiene que ajustarse a procedimientos demasiado específicos, con poca tolerancia para resolver los objetivos de una manera diferente. Es contradictorio ofrecer un mundo tan elaborado y después restringir la creatividad del jugador. 

Narrativa y ritmo: La historia tiene personajes interesantes y momentos bien construidos, pero no mantiene la misma fuerza durante todo su desarrollo. El ritmo pierde intensidad en su segunda mitad y algunas situaciones no alcanzan el impacto que prometía su planteamiento. Una producción cinematográfica no necesariamente es una gran narrativa, y una buena interpretación de personajes tampoco garantiza una historia memorable.

Contenido y profundidad: Hay una cantidad impresionante de actividades, interacciones y elementos secundarios, pero poca profundidad. El detalle ambiental puede entretener, sorprender y generar momentos memorables, pero no sustituye la evolución de las mecánicas ni garantiza que las actividades mantengan su interés a largo plazo.

Veredicto:

No es necesario que un videojuego sea revolucionario para considerarlo excelente, pero sí necesito que sus virtudes estén equilibradas y que sus decisiones de diseño justifiquen las expectativas que genera.

GTA VI es un espectáculo tecnológico impresionante, pero no considero que eso sea suficiente para convertirlo en una obra maestra. Un presupuesto descomunal no compra excelencia, una cantidad desmedida de detalles no garantiza profundidad y un mundo extraordinario no convierte automáticamente en extraordinario todo lo que hacemos dentro de él.

author: idk32
quote: The core problem is tonal whiplash. For two decades, Grand Theft Auto sold you a distorted, loving, hateful mirror of America — the kind of place where you could rob a bank, marry a stripper, and still get a wink from the camera. GTA 6 scrubs most of that mirror away and replaces it with a quiet, earnest, almost **** romance between Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos. The Guardian’s review nails it: this is "the first GTA that wants to encourage some measure of empathy alongside its trademark violent chaos." Empathy is not what I paid $70 for. I paid for a caricature. I got a couples' counseling session set in a very expensive **** story is the weakest link in a series that used to be its strongest. Where GTA V gave you three wildly different egos colliding in a farcical plot about money and betrayal, and GTA IV gave you Niko Bellic’s grinding, nihilistic immigrant tragedy, GTA 6 gives you two small-time criminals who mostly just want to make it. Kotaku calls them "Rockstar’s most fully fleshed-out, believable, and relatable characters" — and that is precisely the insult. Relatable is the enemy of memorable. Niko Bellic was unforgettable. Michael De Santa was a mess you couldn’t look away from. Jason is "steady and unflappable, sincere but spare with words." That’s a LinkedIn bio, not a protagonist. The five-chapter structure is, by multiple reviews, "the best mission design in the series" — which is a sad award when the bar is a heist game that used to let you drive a **** "woke" criticism is real, and it’s also the least interesting part. The Verge notes the humor "doesn’t punch down like in past GTAs" and instead targets "men’s rights activists, NFT bros, conspiracy theorists, Bryan Johnson." That’s fair satire, and it’s the same satire GTA V did to its 2013 targets. What actually alienates longtime fans isn’t the satire’s target; it’s the absence of the old, cruel, "punch-down-at-everyone" tone that made the series feel like a Rorschach test for your own ugliness. GTA V let you be a monster and winked. GTA 6 lets you be a monster and then has Lucia quietly disapprove. The "woke" backlash on Reddit and X is less about the satire and more about the fact that the game won’t let you be the bad guy without consequence — no more shooting up a nightclub, no more attacking protesters without the game essentially sighing at you. That’s a design choice, and it’s a defensible one, but it is not the GTA I grew up **** world is the best open world ever made, and that’s the tragedy. Leonida is, by every review, the most alive, most detailed, most reactive sandbox Rockstar has ever built — PushSquare calls it "the deepest, densest, most accomplished open world since Red Dead Redemption 2," and the 30fps cap is the only real technical complaint.  You can spend 100 hours and still find new NPC conversations, new side gags, new ways the city reacts to you. The problem is that the world is so good that the story feels like a thin thread strung through it. You are not the main character. The city is the main character. Jason and Lucia are tourists in their own **** bottom line: GTA 6 is a 9.5/10 open-world game that forgot it was a Grand Theft Auto. It’s a masterpiece of world-building, mission design, and technical ambition that is also, for the first time in the series’ history, not fun in the way GTA has always been fun. It’s mature, it’s empathetic, it’s "relatable," and it is, for that reason, the first GTA I can’t stop thinking about critically rather than viscerally. I don’t want to defend it. I want to defend GTA IV. One out of ten, not because it’s bad, but because it’s not this.

author: KChito_Review
quote:
Plenty of graphical muscle, but little of the GTA soul

After more than a decade of waiting and an astronomical budget, we are left with an experience that beneath its spectacular visual polish is weighed down by baffling design choices and a sleep-inducing pace. Rockstar seems to have forgotten what made its games fun, opting instead for a heavy-handed realism that slows down every action.

The biggest drawbacks lie in the gameplay and the pacing. The opening in Leonida Keys feels endless, and the story takes far too long to truly get going once you finally reach Vice City. Midway through the campaign, the narrative stalls, bogged down by repetitive tasks aimed at accumulating money and reputation, while the conclusion feels rushed. Furthermore, the simulation-heavy approach inherited from *Red Dead Redemption 2* is a poor fit for this formula: the controls are clunky, melee combat remains awkward, and managing minor interactions such as opening a car trunk or picking up items is unnecessarily slow.

Compounding this are several cutbacks that are hard to justify after so many years of development. The inability to freely purchase businesses, the absence of classic activities, and most notably the inability to replay missions directly from the pause menu are clear steps backward compared to previous entries.

Technically, the visual leap is undeniable, but the price is high: being locked to 30 FPS with noticeable drops during intense action sequences completely **** the fluidity, which is unacceptable in 2026. When you add in questionable business practices such as selling a "physical edition" that contains only a download code, or locking side activities behind special editions the final impression is bittersweet. A technical marvel, certainly, but a step backward as a video game.

author: kaminter
quote: GTA VI – A Disappointment on the Scale of Its Hype?Despite the massive hype surrounding GTA VI, the game is far from the masterpiece everyone expected. Rockstar seems to have focused so much on impressive graphics, realistic details, and visual presentation that it has neglected some of the most important aspects of a video game: fun and **** world is huge and filled with details, but that doesn’t necessarily make it a truly interactive open world. What’s the point of having an enormous map if your interactions with it are limited? And what is the value of excessive realism if it makes certain activities feel boring and repetitive?One of my biggest frustrations is how restricted the experience can feel. Scripted missions, predetermined events, and an excessive reliance on cinematic sequences sometimes make the game feel more like watching a long movie than actually experiencing a living, breathing sandbox.Another problem is that an abundance of detail doesn’t compensate for a lack of meaningful interaction. I don’t just want a world that looks alive; I want a world I can genuinely influence, explore, interact with, and experience without unnecessary **** VI sometimes feels more interested in simulating real life than delivering an entertaining video game. Realism isn’t always an improvement, details aren’t necessarily meaningful content, and a massive map doesn’t automatically make a rich open-world experience.Ultimately, GTA VI might be one of the most visually impressive games ever made, but to me, it represents how excessive technical ambition can come at the expense of what truly makes an open-world game great: freedom, exploration, and above all, fun.

author: mithocht
quote:
I honestly don't even know where to start. How the hell do you manage to take one of the biggest and most successful gaming franchises of all time and screw it up this badly?

The story is absolutely terrible. Whoever came up with this garbage has either never played a proper GTA game before or simply has no understanding of what made this franchise so legendary in the first place. We're talking about GRAND THEFT AUTO! A series that made gaming history with Vice City, San Andreas, GTA IV and GTA V. Games that weren't just amazing because of their open worlds, but because of their characters, their humor, their completely insane stories and, most importantly, because they actually had a soul.

And then we get GTA 6...
yaers of development, an astronomical budget, unbelievable expectations, and somehow we end up with a story that genuinely makes me wonder who at Rockstar read this script and thought: Yeah, that's exactly what we should go with! Where are the brilliant characters? Where is that dark, twisted humor GTA used to be famous for? Where is the completely over the top social satire that made fun of absolutely everyone?

GTA used to be offensive, disrespectful, politically incorrect and completely unapologetic about it. Nobody was safe from being mocked, and that was exactly what made it so brilliant. now everything feels forced, artificial and painfully calculated. Instead **** story, we get something that, in my opinion, doesn't even come close to the charm or quality of its predecessors.

And that's what genuinely pisses me off. Not because I want GTA to be bad, but because I've loved this franchise for decades. Because I know what Rockstar used to be capable of. And that's exactly why it's so frustrating to watch them completely butcher something that could have been another masterpiece.

Yes, the graphics are fantastic. I'll give them that. The world looks incredible, and some of the technical details are genuinely impressive. For that alone, I'd almost give it three stars.
But since when did beautiful graphics become enough to make a great game? A Ferrari without an engine still looks amazing. Doesn't do me much good if I can't actually drive the damn thing.

And then I look at Metacritic and see all these perfect 100/100 reviews... 100 POINTS! Seriously?! At this point, I'm genuinely wondering whether we even played the same game. Some of these reviews are so ridiculously positive that you'd almost think the critics were paid for them. Obviously, I have no proof of that, but I honestly can't wrap my head around the ridiculous amount of praise this game is getting. Apparently, these days it's more important for a game to look impressive and generate massive hype than to actually tell a good story. Rockstar had the opportunity to create another milestone in gaming history with GTA 6. Instead, they've managed to prove that even the biggest budget in the world can't replace talented writers, creativity or a genuinely good story.

And the saddest part? This isn't just some random disappointing game. This is GRAND THEFT AUTO. A franchise that once set the standards everyone else tried to reach.

I never thought I'd see the day when I'd write something like this about a GTA game, but here we are. 2 out of 10. And those two points are basically just for the graphics.

What an absolutely monumental waste of potential.

author: BB5
quote:
Does not live up to the legacy of GTA V at all. At all. And this was always going to be compared to GTA V as the baseline we grew up playing and what built the franchise's brand reputation.

Compared to the amount of heists / actual "grand theft auto" missions throughout GTA V which kept the stakes high and tension throughout from the get go (literally from the first mission "Prologue"), I found the missions in GTA VI to be incredibly boring and slow. Honestly they are full of silly household tasks / other meaningless side quests and overall felt more like "The Sims" or a quasi relationship simulator than than a GTA title... Seriously all this relationship stuff like WTF is this? Like sometimes I am sat there, stop playing for a moment and just thinking is this actually a GTA entry??

Probably my biggest issue is that I found the characters to be incredibly lacking in personality and hard to relate to - they just don't have anywhere near the chemistry of Franklin / Michael / Trevor etc. that made GTA V so enjoyable for me. This applies to secondary characters too, probably even more so than the main leads Jason / Lucia. This just makes it so hard to feel immersed in the game and drawn back to play again and again.

30 FPS is another problem. I'm not super bothered about these things normally. But several instances particularly in shootouts were even I could notice problems on my screen. 13 years and this is the best they can do? Honestly disappointing.

There are some positives sure, I'm not unbiased and can accept that several things in the actual game design are better / an improvement vs. the previous GTA entry. But honestly, given the 13 year wait (they have had sooo long to work on this and technology naturally is expected to advance over time), plus the magnitude of the above which are all critical points to me, this still gets a 0. Not even mad, just disappointed and upset that something so many people were waiting so long for does not live up to expectations.

author: SerenaMacy
quote: I was truly hoping that GTA 6 would be an amazing game, but it’s ended up being one of the worst video games I’ve ever had the displeasure of playing. GTA 6 is riddled with bugs (many of which required full re-launches of the game, and some of which outright crashed the game), the gunplay is clunky and stiff, the melee combat leaves much to be desired (feeling more like a series of quick-time events rather than actual combat), and it lacks a large amount of detail that the previous GTA games were known for (planes just bounce off of buildings when colliding, NPCs constantly overreact, nothing happens when you collide your boat with an NPC boat, and planes just phase through buildings when you exit them). But even under all of the bugs, the game underneath isn’t that fun to begin with. Outside of the bugs and general lack of polish, the story and characters are bland and uninteresting. They just kept introducing character after character without fleshing out any of them past the most basic surface-level details, leading to the endings feeling extremely unsatisfying and rushed. Much of the early game was also quite unpleasant due to the amount of chores I had to do, which just felt like the game was padding out its runtime. Eventually I just stopped doing anything that wasn’t directly for the main story, as all of the side content felt like it was there for the sake of having extra content. Overall GTA 6 is a terrible game in its current state, and would only be slightly better with the bugs fixed. I’d recommend you spend your money elsewhere, as GTA 6 is nowhere near worth the high price tag.

author: Vanucci33
quote: Grand Theft Auto has spent decades turning crime into spectacle: steal the car, make the money, buy the upgrade, escape the cops. Its satire can be sharp, but it often gets tangled up in the same things it claims to mock. Drugs become edgy set pieces, violence becomes routine, and materialism becomes the reward loop. After so many games, the provocation feels less like a critique and more like a familiar sales pitch.That history makes GTA 6’s return to the same world hard to celebrate. author: damienstieg
quote: GTA VI has some of the most unlikeable protagonists in gaming. There are no characters, only stereotypes and caricatures, and the writing looks and reads like Ubisoft's: Far Cry 5 and Watch Dogs 2, asinine characters and their lingo. Lucia acts as irrational as the most stupid among us, incompetent to the point of hurting herself. The opening robbery goes wrong because she circles back to the scene and gets dazed by a dye pack going off in the car. In GTA V, the opening heist failed because of a setup from inside the team – an actually interesting premise with widespread story implications. At her parole hearing she says she's stupid and probably won't get released. Jason is stiff as a wooden board, answers everything with 'huh, okay' and 'yeah, I know,' and has friends he wouldn't put up with in real life, due to their sheer belligerence, incompetence and clumsiness (he is ex-military and merc himself). The cast puts on crazy voices to sound like cartoons. The game plays like a home renovation simulator and a deadbeat motherhood simulator, which is what happens when there's no real direction and the work is done by whoever. Technically it has Oblivion-level NPC barks, hands clipping through geometry, hair clipping into bodies, muffled dialogue and floaty driving. Florida is graded mud brown. The starter sound keeps playing after the car is already moving. Cutscene cameras cut to empty frames and wait for the characters to catch up, several times in a row. Gunshots and engines sound bad, and they should have been simulated instead of recorded. The UI is legacy, basic and mostly flat colors. Credit where it's due: I like the realism and the systems. Guns get holstered, slung, held or tossed, so there are no more miniguns in your pocket. You can't run over motorcyclists anymore, and the game tracks whether you play unhinged, which pulls me into the role. Too bad the characters are what they are. The worst thing is that there is a game in there somewhere. Anyone who reviewed it and found no bugs is blind.

author: Val91_
quote:
Nadie niega la ambición de su mundo abierto, gráficos y modelados pero hay una enorme doble vara de medir con esta compañía frente a otras. Rockstar ha tomado decisiones comerciales y técnicas muy cuestionables que, en otra compañía, habrían generado un rechazo masivo:

1. Políticas anticonsumidor y precios abusivos (80 € - 400 €):
• Muerte del formato físico: Sale solo en digital (las cajas de tienda solo traen un papel con un código, tan mal protegido que ya los están robando en tiendas alumbrando las cajas con linternas), sentando un precedente terrible. Ni Sony ni Rockstar se están haciendo responsables.

• Recortes y sobreprecios: Cuesta 79,99 € sin doblaje a ningún idioma (leer subtítulos en mitad de un tiroteo o persecución es incómodo y rompe la inmersión). Además, la edición Ultimate de 99,99 € bloquea tiendas, armas y vehículos que antes venían de serie, y la Edición Coleccionista de 400 € ni siquiera incluye el juego. Dicha edición ofrece merchandising algo básico y nada memorable a mi parecer y ni siquiera incluye el juego (obligándote a gastar casi 500 € en total para tenerlo todo).

2. Un lanzamiento incompleto:
• Llega a precio completo sin modo Online, sin posibilidad de repetir misiones, sin compra de negocios ni minijuegos clásicos de la saga, y bloqueando hasta los trucos de toda la vida hasta terminar la historia principal.

3. Rendimiento deficiente y bugs graves:
• Está capado a 30 FPS en todas las consolas —algo por lo que a cualquier otro estudio se le tacharía de incompetente—, con caídas a 20 FPS durante tiroteos y secciones o zonas densas. 

• Más allá de caídas al vacío bajo el mapa, problemas de colisión, cinemáticas en negro, pérdida de animaciones en algunas acciones, fallos de carga de textura y audio, el juego sufre cierres inesperados (crashes) que causan que el sistema de guardado falle, provocando la pérdida de varias horas de partida.

4. La hipocresía del discurso "woke" y la pérdida de libertad sandbox:
• En esta industria se ha popularizado el lema "Go Woke, Go Broke" y se ha crucificado a estudios enteros simplemente por incluir una protagonista femenina, por el diseño estético de sus personajes o por utilizar lenguaje inclusivo en un doblaje. Sin embargo, nadie señala que Rockstar ha impuesto restricciones ideológicas reales dentro de la jugabilidad.

• Colectivos intocables y moralina: Si intentas atropellar una manifestación o disparar en determinados locales como discotecas LGBT, el coche se frena automáticamente y las armas se bloquean, rompiendo las reglas básicas de un sandbox y estableciendo ciudadanos de primera y de segunda. A esto se suma la eliminación de mecánicas presentes desde GTA III (como contratar prostitutas) bajo la excusa de respetar la relación de los protagonistas —pese a haber afirmado que el vínculo era moldeable— y una sátira claramente suavizada por temor a la polémica.

5. La desconexión de la prensa especializada:
• Como ya han demostrado análisis comparativos de las propias reseñas profesionales, decenas de medios mencionan en sus textos caídas de rendimiento, controles torpes y problemas de ritmo narrativo, pero aun así le otorgan el 100/100 por pura inercia mediática.

author: Theikosh
quote: 13 years of waiting for a glorified chore **** a game that took over a decade to arrive, GTA 6 is one of the most disappointing gaming experiences I’ve had in years. The graphics are incredible, the world is massive, and the attention to detail is impressive. But once you look past the visuals, you start realizing how little Rockstar has actually improved where it **** protagonists are a massive downgrade.Jason has absolutely zero personality. He’s boring, forgettable, and feels more like Lucia’s personal assistant than an actual GTA protagonist. Compare him to Niko Bellic, Trevor, Michael, or Arthur Morgan. Those characters had depth, memorable dialogue, and personalities that made you want to keep playing. Jason is just there.Lucia is somehow even worse. She’s annoying as ****, her voice gets on my nerves, and I genuinely struggle to understand why I’m supposed to care about her. Her questionable decisions as a mother are brushed aside far too easily by Jason, making their entire relationship feel poorly **** speaking of their relationship, why the **** am I being forced to maintain it?Rockstar made it sound like the relationship mechanics would be optional, yet the story keeps pushing me into domestic activities and running errands for Lucia. I’m playing Grand Theft Auto, not Boyfriend Simulator 2026. I didn’t wait over a decade to play as some beta cuck doing chores and buying **** story is mediocre at **** pacing is painfully slow, the dialogue is forgettable, and the supporting characters barely leave an impression. Previous Rockstar games had side characters who were sometimes more entertaining than the protagonists themselves. Here, most of them feel like **** missions aren’t much better. Rockstar is still obsessed with overly scripted sequences where you follow someone, listen to endless dialogue, drive somewhere, watch a cutscene, and repeat. There’s barely any room for **** game constantly tells you exactly what to do and punishes you for deviating from its intended path. For a franchise supposedly built around freedom, that’s **** open world looks next-gen, but the freedom doesn’t feel **** interactions don’t feel like the revolutionary leap I expected after Red Dead Redemption 2. Sure, people react to things, the streets feel alive, and the animations look incredible. But where’s the meaningful interaction?Why can’t I befriend random NPCs? Why can’t I build relationships with people I meet around the city? Why can’t I flirt with or seduce random characters, have casual hookups, or develop my own social experiences?I’m not expecting every NPC to have an entire storyline, but after all these years, I expected Rockstar to push the boundaries of what an open world actually allows you to do.Instead, we get a beautiful world with surprisingly limited player **** when did GTA become so obsessed with realism that it forgot to be fun?Weapon restrictions, tedious management mechanics, errands, slow progression, and unnecessarily complicated systems don’t automatically make a game immersive. Sometimes they just make it **** Dead Redemption 2 could get away with its slower, more deliberate gameplay because it had an incredible story and characters worth investing in. GTA 6 borrows that philosophy without delivering the same emotional payoff.Even the shooting feels unnecessarily clunky at times. The controls can feel awkward, and the gameplay still carries some of Rockstar’s outdated design **** where’s the classic GTA personality?The absurd humor, the memorable psychos, the ridiculous situations, the ruthless satire of American culture, all the things that made GTA feel different from every other open-world game seem toned down. The game takes itself far too seriously while failing to deliver a story compelling enough to justify that **** biggest issue is that GTA 6 seems more interested in simulating everyday life than letting me escape it.I don’t play GTA to do household chores, maintain a forced relationship, or sit through endless conversations with characters I don’t care about.I play GTA for freedom, memorable characters, crime, chaos, and the ability to do things I can’t do in real **** somehow, despite having one of the most detailed open worlds ever created, GTA 6 still feels unnecessarily restrictive. Final verdict: 0.5/10. Rockstar has created a technological masterpiece wrapped around a mediocre story, unlikable protagonists, outdated mission design, and gameplay that frequently mistakes inconvenience for **** world is impressive. The graphics are phenomenal. But a beautiful map isn’t enough to make a great game.13 years of waiting, and somehow the most revolutionary thing about GTA 6 is how realistic doing chores has become.

author: Escanor89
quote:
The Good Guy Simp Simulator, A $2 Billion Social Experiment

A 5.5 user score? Honestly, I'm not surprised. This whole project feels less like a video game and more like a social experiment in modern entertainment, corporate messaging and manufactured controversy. 13 years in development, a reported budget of up to $2 billion, endless marketing hype and awards-season attention before players even had the chance to properly experience the finished product. 

And somehow we're supposed to believe this represents the pinnacle of gaming?To me, the writing and character portrayal feel increasingly artificial. Male characters come across as deliberately weakened caricatures, while supposedly progressive messaging often feels forced rather than organically integrated into the story. It's almost like the Good Guy Simp Simulator: an endless parade of manufactured outrage, predictable character dynamics and ideological signalling instead of genuinely compelling storytelling.

And here's the bigger question: Why are developers so increasingly disconnected from what a substantial part of their audience actually wants? Why does so much modern entertainment seem more interested in provoking, dividing and lecturing its audience than simply telling a great story?I'm not interested in turning this into a political debate about men versus women, left versus right, or any particular culture. I just want good writing, interesting characters, creative freedom and games that respect their audience. The gaming industry increasingly feels like a corporate circus built around hype, brand management and consumer manipulation. 

The physical media situation at Sony was another wake-up call for me.I eventually sold my PS5, and honestly, I don't miss it.I'm discovering new hobbies, spending more time outdoors, enjoying family life and investing my money in experiences that actually add something meaningful to my life. Gaming used to be about escapism, creativity and genuine fun. Maybe it's time we stopped treating billion-dollar corporations like they're doing us a favour.

My money, my time, my choice. And Boys who learned It the hard way: I hope you all get your refunds <3

author: 0syris
quote: I have played Grand Theft Auto VI for 21 hours on a base PS5. I have reached chapter 3 and decided to go back to chapter 2 to finish up some things that I had missed and because I thought I missed something in the last mission of chapter 2. Let's start with graphics and performance. Grand Theft Auto VI is FREAKING BEAUTIFUL!!!!! However, the games' beauty comes at great cost to performance. At various times whenever there's a lot of foliage, every major action sequence so far, and during the rush hour traffic in game, the game can't maintain a stable 30 frames per second. Do I wish this game had a performance mode with 60 frames per second? Of course I do, but I'd be willing to look past that, if this game could keep a consistent 30 frames per second. "Plays best on PS5" feels like false advertising. What it should've said is "Plays best on PS5 Pro." Now to the story and gameplay. I find it absurd that this game strongly discourages you from committing its name sake "Grand Theft Auto." They shove this morality system in a GRAND THEFT AUTO GAME!!!!!! A morality system made sense for Red Dead Redemption II since Redemption is literally in the name, but this is Grand Theft Auto. I want to go steal the nicest supercar I can find and start running over every pedestrian I can find. Not be told I can't steal the car without a clone of the owners car key. The new wanted system may just be the worst new addition to this game. It's cool that the cops will have a lot of details about the crime, but when I have to make sure my car is loaded up with outfits and I have to keep using the same method to avoid detection, it gets repetitive. The first chapter of the game is basically a chore simulator for the first half, and a dating sim in the last half. The game also strongly discourages you from killing people in missions, and the idea seems to be that the player should be aiming for the arms or legs in order to incapacitate people instead of killing them. That's great... if I hated having fun. It's a nice idea but as someone who wants to get the best ending I can with a good morality rating, it makes it really annoying when I maybe accidentally kill 2 or 3 enemies and at the end of the mission, it warns me that my morality went down because there were too many casualties (it's not clear how many casualties is too many). Most of the time I end up having to resort to grabbing a shotgun and just shooting the enemies legs out and then running over to knock them unconscious. Do I have to play the game this way? No I don't, but like I said, I want to end the game with a high morality and get the best ending I can get without looking up anything. By the end of chapter 2, I felt like I was stuck in a loop. Anytime I go to rob a place, whether it's a store or a gang ridden drug den, the second I hear that police scanner, I have to run back to my car, take off my mask, put my guns away in the trunk, change my outfit, and drive out of the big blue radius on my mini map before a cop arrives. Every. Single. Time. I realize this is all kind of self inflicted since this is the way that I've chosen to play the game, but god forbid we kill the NPCs that are shooting at us and trying to kill us. Jason and Lucia's story is all about them trying to get themselves in a physical and financial place where they would be able to get custody of their son and give him a good life. With this thought in mind, I am trying to play the game in the way I think will get them too their goal. To quote the great Gabe Newell "I've never thought to myself that realism is fun. I go play games to have fun." and my friend reading this, this game is so realistic, they forgot the fun. Cars are a chore too because they feel too floaty, brittle, and having to actually stop for gas is a minor inconvenience that irks me every time I have to do it. Threading the needle in the cars is fun, until you get trapped between an 18 wheeler and an offramp barrier because your car wasn't fast enough to get the timing right, and now you need to find somewhere to repair the car. I've kind of rambled here a bit and I do plan to continue playing the game, but to be honest with you all, finishing this game will be a chore. This is surely not the greatest game of all time. A 4/10 might seem unfair, and it might seem like I am trying to review bomb it, but I'm not. These are a handful of the  thoughts I've had as I've been playing the game. I haven't experienced some of the more major bugs and glitches that I've seen online, but, the performance is a big problem when you have a game like this with a big focus on big action sequences and should be at the top of the priorities list for the next patch. I eagerly await the PC version so that I can play this at 60 frames per second or better. I hope for the next Rockstar game, that they remember some of their other franchises, but more importantly, remember to focus on fun, and not on realism. 4/10 (subject to change as I continue to play).

author: Alexiusimfight
quote:
I waited over a decade for this and got a lecture with a map attached. GTA was never supposed to be a morality play. You play a criminal, so let me be one.
If I want to put a bullet in someone, I want the freedom to go all the way. Instead the game keeps pulling its punches, as if it's embarrassed by its own premise. When I commit a crime, I want to actually pull it off properly, with real planning, real consequences and real payoff. What I got is scripted hand-holding with a cinematic bow on top.
The writing is the worst offender. The game constantly nudges me to feel sorry for people I'm meant to be robbing and shooting. I don't want empathy. I'm the bad guy and the game should let me enjoy it. The old games understood that and mocked everyone equally. This one picks a side and preaches from it, and the sermon is dull. The satire has no teeth left, just smug, progressive box-ticking that reads like it came out of a corporate workshop.
The pacing is padded to hell, too. Endless drives, pointless cutscenes and filler missions only exist to inflate the playtime. The plot starts big, loses track of itself and wraps up in a mess. Underneath the polish, the gameplay is a decade out of date.

author: oldskoolgmr
quote:
Thirteen Years for This? GTA 6 Killed What Made the Franchise Great

After a 13-year wait and wall-to-wall glowing pre-release reviews that feel completely out of touch with the actual game, GTA 6 is a massive letdown for longtime fans. Every Grand Theft Auto before this was edgy, hilarious, chaotic, and packed with non-stop action. Players come to GTA to escape real life, do things they would never do in the real world, make their own unpredictable stories, and get hooked on characters with huge, unforgettable personalities. Instead **** you cannot put the controller down to play, GTA 6 feels like a boring job, a chore, or a cheesy relationship simulator—and I already have a real life, relationships, errands, and responsibilities to handle.

1. Sandbox Freedom Replaced by Restrictions and Chores: 
Grand Theft Auto has always lived or died by the freedom to do whatever you want, whenever you want. Here, the game polices you at every turn: restricting who you can kill, blocking carjackings from women, limiting interactions with other women, penalizing crime, and forcing you to buy a stolen car just to keep it—in a game literally named "Grand Theft Auto" and making you drive in traffic for fear of damaging your car because they break so easily and you have to pay for repairs. Worse still, fun and chaos are locked behind slow story progression and mundane tasks instead of letting you cut loose on your own terms.

2. No Instant Chaos or Cheat-Code Fun 
Growing up with GTA, the best memories came from spawning in, punching in cheat codes right away, spawning planes and cars, grabbing weapons and armor, fortifying a spot with stolen or spawned vehicles for a police standoff, or competing with friends to see who could survive the highest wanted level the longest. You could go on a rampage, explore the map, and treat the story as a secondary part of the experience. Locking cheats until after you beat the storyline kills that immediate, wild, freedom sandbox energy from minute one.

3. Spineless Lead, Rash Dynamic, and Zero Hook 
Past GTA titles had wild, funny, larger-than-life characters with real edge—people who made you laugh, get angry, cheer, or hate them while keeping you on the edge of your seat through plot twists and high-stakes action. GTA 6 throws that away for cheesy romantic nonsense and dull domestic filler. Jason is supposed to be an ex-military badass, yet he comes across soft-spoken, dull, and spineless—spending the campaign under Lucia’s thumb as a compliant errand boy with no real spine to push back or operate independently. Meanwhile, Lucia is rash and reckless, constantly creating so many problems that any player would happily ditch her over if the game ever gave you the opportunity. When there is not a single character worth liking or laughing with, it is easy to stop caring about the game altogether.

4. Rough Performance and Graphics That Don't Beat GTA 5 
When GTA 5 launched, We set up of our consoles and TVs all in one lounge room with friends and jumping in felt immediate, seamless, and thrilling within the first 30 minutes. GTA 6, by contrast, drags through six hours of slow, unexciting relationship drama, frame drops during action that get you killed, glitches where taking cover drops you through the map, and visuals that still feel like no clear step up over GTA 5. Between the sluggish pacing, restrictive rules, and technical rough edges, the 10/10 pre-release scores look less like honest verdicts and more like bought-and-paid hype.

Bottom Line: Thirteen years of hype cannot rescue a game that trades away GTA’s edge, comedy, adrenaline, and wide-open freedom for chores, restrictions, cheesy romance, and a spineless lead. When a sequel makes you feel like you are clocking into a shift instead of escaping reality, it is no wonder longtime fans walk away frustrated.

author: Zadyr
quote:
GTA 6 is the perfect example of how a studio can spend a fortune and thirteen years to deliver something technically impressive… and at the same time deeply boring, restrictive, and disconnected from what made the series great.

The four points that actually work (and the only reason it gets a 4):

1. The world is ridiculously detailed and feels alive. I really respect that part as an open worlds full explorer.
2. The map is enormous and dense.
3. The police system and criminal profile are better thought-out than in GTA V.
4. The atmosphere, radio, and overall vibe of Leonida are very well done.

That’s it. The rest of the game can go and f itself.

Now the important part: why it’s such a massive disappointment:

Rockstar decided that this time GTA was going to be “serious” and “realistic.” The result is a toxic relationship life-simulator dressed up as a crime game. Jason is the spineless boyfriend, absent father, who does everything Lucia tells him to. The relationship dynamic is the center of the game and feels forced, heavy, and one-sided most of the time. You have to do domestic chores, fix the house, go shopping, keep her happy… all so the relationship meter doesn’t tank. It’s exactly the kind of mechanics that kill the spirit of GTA.

PERSONAL TAKE (you can skip this part if you don’t like “pro-w0kE” tantrums): They talked about “loyalty to the relationship” to justify removing prostitutes and any sex or romance options outside the couple. Fine. So why can Jason still go to strip clubs, pay for private dances with girls, and get **** shoved in his face without it affecting anything? Where’s the equivalent for men? Where are the gay clubs with the same sexualized freedom? They basically don’t exist in any meaningful way. Gay clubs and male sexual interactions are practically non-existent. It’s the most blatant double standard: they protect the heterosexual “fidelity” of the main story while keeping the traditional straight sexual content. For a gay player it’s especially insulting.Honestly, I’m just tired and fed up with censorship, restrictions, and cut content when it comes to inclusion and equality, especially when we’re all paying the same $100 USD as everyone else. **** is willing to settle for scraps, good for them, I guess. Good luck with that. As for me, it’s an automatic PASS. If the situation were reversed and the game catered exclusively to gay people, there would be an uproar and people would be going on strike. But I’m just supposed to **** it up and accept it? Nope. And by the way, as strange as it may sound, in this particular case, the anti-woke crowd and I actually agree on something: putting my personal opinion aside, this just doesn’t feel like GTA. Period. I don’t need capitalism lessons or lessons on how to treat a woman. That knowledge already comes factory-installed. I want to play a GTA that expands in every aspect including freedom and diversity, not one that does the opposite. What a waste.

The pacing of the early hours (and a good chunk of the game) is slow to the point of absurdity. It feels like an endless domestic crime tutorial. The chaos, the pure freedom, and the “do whatever the hell you want with no real consequences” of previous GTAs has been diluted. Stealing a car is more complicated, cars break easily, you have to fill up gas, go to the bank to store money, eat, sleep… All that RDR2-style realism forced into a GTA. Some call it immersion. I call it expensive boredom.

30 fps locked even on PS5 Pro. After thirteen years and the budget this thing had, that’s unacceptable. In combat or dense areas it drops lower. Driving feels heavy, combat is clunky compared to what was promised, and there are bugs and pop-in that shouldn’t exist in a release of this scale.

The main characters have nowhere near the charisma of GTA V’s cast. Jason is flat. Lucia is hard to like for a lot of people. The story takes itself way too seriously and loses that savage, ruthless satire that defined the series.

In short: they spent a decade and a fortune to make a game that prioritizes a heterosexual couple’s relationship, cuts classic freedom, keeps selective straight sexual content, forces chores on you, and locks you at 30 fps. All for $80–100.

If what you want is a pretty, detailed world to walk around in, fine. If you want the GTA of always  chaotic, free, absurd, and without all the couple drama, this isn’t it. It’s a generous 4/10: one point for each of the four things that actually work. The rest is an expensive, pretentious disappointment.

author: reyesrca
quote: The excessive reliance on FMV sequences and the repetitive nature of several activities make the experience feel more tedious than entertaining. Too many missions seem to prioritize spectacle and presentation over genuinely engaging gameplay. Taking 13 years to deliver what feels, in many ways, like an upgraded version of GTA V, with improved graphics and presentation, is disappointing. After such a long development cycle, expectations naturally go beyond visual improvements. Players should be getting a meaningful evolution in mission design, gameplay mechanics, storytelling, and world interaction. Of course, there will always be players who appreciate the experience largely because of nostalgia, much like those who enjoy Nintendo's remakes of classics such as Ocarina of Time. However, I think there is a fundamental difference between revisiting a beloved classic and spending over a decade developing the next major installment of one of gaming's biggest franchises. Nintendo understands that nostalgia is part of the appeal, but Rockstar had an opportunity to redefine what an open-world game could be. Instead, if the experience relies too heavily on familiar formulas, repetitive activities, and cinematic sequences, it risks feeling like a graphical upgrade rather than a genuine generational leap. After 13 years, better graphics should be the bare minimum, not the main selling point. A massive open world means very little if exploring it and completing its missions aren't consistently engaging. Rockstar should be pushing the boundaries of gameplay, not simply polishing a formula that was already successful more than a decade ago.

GTA 6 is massively overrated. People seem to confuse graphical quality and attention to detail with an actually great game. Yes, the world looks impressive, but where is the chaos, the fun, and the freedom that made GTA so entertaining in the first place? The game doesn't provide enough genuinely entertaining and chaotic moments, and too much of the experience feels underwhelming despite all the hype.

The soundtrack is nowhere near what I expected either. The music lacks the memorable impact and atmosphere I was hoping for. Even the story and certain sections fail to leave the impression I expected from Rockstar. RDR2 had moments like Guarma that were genuinely memorable because of their atmosphere, but GTA 6 hasn't managed to create that same feeling for me.

A game isn't automatically a masterpiece because it has incredible graphics, realistic animations, or thousands of details. Those things are impressive, but they don't replace fun. GTA 6 feels like a game that prioritizes presentation over entertainment in some aspects. I expected a revolutionary experience, something that would completely blow me away, but instead I got a game that feels overhyped and underwhelming. It absolutely does not deserve a 9.9 in my opinion.

Some people are going to dismiss this as chud/incel whining, and that's okay. They are too far gone to be reasoned with. However, not everything needs to be a vehicle for virtue signaling. We don't need to tone GTA down and use it to spread a message. These games are supposed to be a break from reality where we can use our imaginations to do ridiculous and funny things. If the entire game's purpose is to be violent and engage in crime, then political guardrails shouldn't be put into the game. Just let people be unhinged and do as they please. 

I wish I had the foresight to see this coming and avoid wasting my money. I guess now I know for the future. 

RIP Rockstar. Hire some people that aren't brainwashed zombies. Or watch as another company rises to take your place.

author: AlaskaYeen
quote:
My Personal Review: GTA 6 – The Biggest Letdown of 2026?
I actually took leave from work for this game. I made plans, rearranged my schedule, and organised everything so I could have an entire week off to enjoy GTA 6.
After years of waiting and all the hype surrounding this supposedly groundbreaking AAA title, I was ready for the experience of a **** after just 7–8 hours of gameplay, I found myself asking: WHAT THE ACTUAL **** IS THIS **** SIMULATOR 2026?!
My Ratings
Storyline: 2/10 – Boring, disappointing, and nowhere near what I expected from Rockstar.Graphics: 8/10 – Visually impressive, but graphics alone don't make a great game.Missions: 3/10 – Repetitive, underwhelming, and lacking the excitement GTA is known for.
What Happened to the GTA We Loved?Seriously, Rockstar, how do you take one of the biggest gaming franchises in history and turn it into something that feels more like a daily-life simulator?
I genuinely don't understand where these critics are getting their 90+/100 ratings from. From the community reactions I've seen, I'm clearly not the only one ****'s talk about some of the ridiculous gameplay decisions.
WHY DO I HAVE TO TAKE A SHOWER EVERY TIME I WAKE UP?!
What if I WANT to run around dirty? 
What if I don't feel like showering? Since when did GTA become a personal hygiene simulator?
And then there are the restrictions.Apparently, you can't shoot certain protesters or groups of NPCs. You can't shoot inside certain clubs. But somehow, shooting a furry is perfectly acceptable?
WHERE IS THE CONSISTENCY?!
GTA has always been about freedom, chaos, outrageous situations, and doing things in a fictional world that you would NEVER do in real life.That was the beauty of Grand Theft **** was an escape from ****, instead of escaping reality, I'm apparently expected to LIVE IT.Buying groceries? Fixing the house? Showering? Running errands?
ROCKSTAR, I ALREADY HAVE A REAL LIFE!I didn't spend money on a AAA game to come home from work and do MORE HOUSEWORK!
I understand that developers want to create a realistic, immersive world. But there is a massive difference between realism that enhances gameplay and realism that makes a game feel like a **** honestly feels like the developers have prioritised their own vision of everyday life over the chaotic freedom that made GTA **** 5 Understood Its Characters. What Happened Here?Let's compare this to GTA 5.
Michael, Franklin, and Trevor each had their own personalities, motivations, problems, and storylines.
Michael had his family drama and criminal past.
Franklin wanted to escape his circumstances and build something bigger.
Trevor was absolute chaos, unpredictable and completely unhinged. Every character brought something different to the **** that was BRILLIANT.
Now, in GTA 6, I feel like I'm spending half my time babysitting Lucia, taking care of her, and running ****. NO. AND ABSOLUTELY NO!
I wanted an exciting criminal storyline, unforgettable missions, unpredictable characters, and the freedom to create absolute mayhem.I did NOT sign up to become someone's personal assistant.
My Biggest Problem With GTA 6
It's not the graphics. Those are genuinely ****'s not even the ambition to make the world feel ****'s the fact that GTA seems to have forgotten what made GTA FUN in the first **** franchise was built on freedom, satire, controversy, ridiculous situations, memorable characters, and complete **** endless chores, unnecessary restrictions, and gameplay mechanics that feel like responsibilities rather than entertainment. If I wanted to shower, buy groceries, maintain a house, and run errands, I WOULD JUST GET UP AND GO TO WORK!
Final Verdict: 3/10GTA 6 might be a technical achievement, but for me, it's a massive disappointment in terms of entertainment.Beautiful graphics cannot compensate for boring missions, frustrating mechanics, and a storyline that fails to keep me interested.I waited years for this game.I took leave from work for this game.I rearranged my life to enjoy this **** after only a few hours, I was already questioning whether it was worth the wait.
ROCKSTAR, PLEASE REMEMBER WHO MADE THIS FRANCHISE SUCCESSFUL IN THE FIRST PLACE.
Listen to your community. Bring back the freedom, the chaos, the humour, and the unforgettable storytelling.
WE WANTED GRAND THEFT AUTO 6, NOT THE SIMS: CRIMINAL EDITION.
I'm not impressed. I'm not entertained. And I'm DEFINITELY NOT HAPPY.This is my personal opinion based on my first 7–8 hours of gameplay. Everyone is entitled to their own experience, but this is mine.

I typed everything out in a Word document and pasted it here, so I apologise if some of the sentences are a bit disorganised.

author: chxr1s
quote:
GTA 6 is a Massive Disappointment - Honestly, GTA 6 is one of the biggest disappointments I've experienced in gaming. First of all, the bugs are absolutely terrible. For a game of this scale, the technical issues are unacceptable. Beyond that, the story is incredibly boring. The pacing is dull, the writing is uninspired, and neither of the two main characters manages to leave any meaningful impression. Both protagonists feel completely soulless, lacking personality, depth, and genuine character development. What's even more disappointing is the complete lack of humour. GTA has always been known for its satire, dark comedy, outrageous characters, and willingness to make fun of absolutely everything. Here, there's barely any of that. The game feels overly sanitised, excessively politically correct, and afraid to take risks or offend anyone. It honestly feels like the soul of GTA has been stripped away. A franchise that was once bold, hilarious, controversial, and full of personality now feels bland, predictable, and painfully safe. For all the hype, development time, and expectations surrounding this game, I expected something extraordinary. Instead, I got a boring story, forgettable characters, endless bugs, and a game that feels like it has completely forgotten what made GTA special in the first place. Massive disappointment.

We all know this happened due to Dan Houser's departure from Rockstar, he created all the previous iconic characters, you can't expect anything good with a completely new team that don't know what it's core users want.

author: jakeconstantine
quote:
Thirteen years. Billions of dollars. Thousands of developers working crunch hours. And this is what we waited for? Grand Theft Auto VI isn’t a video game—it’s a painfully slow, hyper-realistic chore simulator wrapped around the exact same archaic, brain-dead mission design Rockstar has been recycling since the PlayStation 3 era.

If you have the attention span **** and get hypnotized by pretty puddle reflections and realistic sweat physics, you’ll love it. For anyone who actually cares about gameplay, it’s an insulting, bloated slog.

Rockstar’s Formula Has Officially Rotted
The disconnect between the open world and the actual missions is borderline satirical at this point. The game drops you into this massive, living state of Leonida, and then the second you start a mission, it puts a digital shock collar on your neck. Drive down this exact street. Park on this exact yellow dot. Shoot these guys from this exact chest-high wall. Breathe wrong or try to use an ounce of actual brainpower to flank an objective, and you get hit with a patronizing "MISSION FAILED" screen. It’s less like playing a sandbox game and more like being an unpaid extra on a movie set with a tyrannical director screaming at you every time you step off your mark.

Controls That Feel Like Wading Through Wet Cement
Whoever decided that "realism" means making your character handle like a drunk refrigerator needs to be fired. Turning around takes three business days. Picking up a single item requires watching a four-second animation of Lucia or Jason reaching out, grabbing it, examining it, and putting it in their pocket. Gunplay is still an absolute joke—without aggressive auto-aim snapping your reticle onto enemies' chests for you, the shooting feels like trying to aim a firehose in zero gravity. It isn't "immersive"; it's tedious, clunky, and actively hostile to the player's time.

Sanitized Satire Written by Corporate Cowards
Remember when GTA actually had teeth? GTA 6’s attempts at paroding modern social media and Florida culture feel like they were written by a 50-year-old marketing executive scrolling through TikTok trends from three years ago. Every joke is safe, toothless, and terrified of actually offending anyone. The story itself is a pacing nightmare—twenty hours of boring, repetitive "drive here, listen to exposition, shoot 40 brainless cops, drive back" filler sandwiched around a handful of decent cutscenes.

A Glorified Storefront Disguised as a Sequel
Worst of all, you can feel the greedy corporate fingerprints all over the single-player campaign. Whole storylines end abruptly with zero payoff because they were blatantly carved out to be recycled into GTA Online DLC. And speaking of Online—it’s a predatory, pay-to-win casino from day one. Want a basic sports car or a decent safehouse? Either treat this game like a full-time, unpaid second job, or pull out your credit card and buy Shark Cards on top of the absurd base price you already paid.

GTA 6 is the ultimate triumph of style over substance. It’s a gorgeous, lifeless tech demo that mistakes tedium for depth and graphics for innovation. Save your money, watch the cutscenes on YouTube, and let this dinosaur of a franchise finally go extinct.

author: hasnard
quote:
Technically, Grand Theft Auto VI is a masterpiece. Vice City feels astonishingly alive, offering the most detailed open-world sandbox ever built. However, beneath the dazzling graphics lies a painfully hollow narrative. After Red Dead Redemption 2 set the bar for mature, character-driven storytelling, GTA VI feels like a massive step backward. Instead **** crime drama or a believable romance, we get a chaotic parody filled with cheap fanservice, inconsistent character motivations, and frustratingly spineless relationship dynamics. It’s an incredible playground for mindless chaos, but if you came looking for a serious story with real weight, you’ll leave deeply disappointed.
Ultimately, when a game only stands out for its setting and graphics, it isn’t a masterpiece—it’s just a sandbox and a tech demo. A true masterpiece demands harmony between its story, gameplay, and every element that builds its world. When those pieces clash and feel disconnected, the imbalance **** immersion and drags the entire experience down. There is undeniably massive effort here, yet pouring it almost exclusively into visuals leaves the core incomplete. What made RDR2, GTA IV, GTA V, and even much smaller 2D games great was balance—every component pulled its own weight. Otherwise, why would anyone still play 2D games today? Building a massive world is hard, but channeling it through a compelling narrative to truly bring it to life is even harder. Unfortunately, it is painfully obvious that Rockstar rushed this project, leaving fans bitterly disappointed. At the end of the day, a great game is like a film—and to keep watching a film, you need a story.

author: Cydek
quote: ​Instead of pushing the medium forward, GTA 6 stands as a bloated monument to corporate greed and creative stagnation.​After more than a decade and a rumored billion-dollar budget, Rockstar threw everything at hyper-realistic lighting, skin pores, and street clutter, while doing very little to actually evolve the core gameplay. Nothing exposes the true priorities behind this 'immersive world' faster than carving out completed in-game storefronts and holding them hostage behind a $100 Ultimate Edition paywall, all on top of an already steep $80 entry fee.​Behind the scenes, the human cost is just as grim. Even as Take-Two Interactive reaps billions from the launch, the company has already gutted its workforce, from mass corporate layoffs and studio closures like Roll7 and Intercept Games, to laying off a third of the staff at sister studio Firaxis on the very eve of GTA 6's release, and firing over 30 union-organizing Rockstar staffers under the guise of "gross misconduct." Between grueling crunch hours and an employment tribunal over blatant union-busting, the remaining developers who built this record-breaking juggernaut are now left fighting for basic union recognition just to protect their jobs from post-launch cuts and heavy AI replacement.​Even locking a promotional trailer behind a paywall, if only for a short period of time, shows just how disgusting the industry has become and what publishers will normalize next. It is a game that will confirm for every game company CEO, who only sees dollar signs instead of fans and art, that you don't need physical media because GTA 6 didn't need a disc. This will be the catalyst for the end of physical media, stripping players of true ownership and turning a beloved medium into a disposable, digital-only storefront. All of this reflects an industry now completely dictated by casual gun-and-ball gamers who only play annual shooters, sports titles, and expensive AAA releases, sending the message that a massive budget is the only thing that matters in a game, a narrow mindset that inevitably trickles down and homogenizes everything else in the medium.​As for the 99 Metascore, seeing over a hundred critics ignore obvious technical compromises, game-breaking bugs at launch (since patched, to be fair), and largely unchanged gameplay to hand out perfect 10s just shows how broken mainstream games journalism has become. It only reinforces the rumors about the blacklisting of journalists who refuse to give perfect, not even near-perfect, scores. GTA 6 will break every sales record on earth, sure, but all it really proves is that the AAA industry now confuses the most expensive product ever made with the greatest art.

author: tabbycatt
quote:
Massive let down. Rockstar Games have lost the sauce. You don't pull your punches in a GTA game. They need to go back to their playbook and relearn what made their games unforgettable, culturally defining experiences. The memorable dialogue, unapologetic writing exploring morally complex human behaviour and pure unrestricted sandbox freedom are all missing from this entry.

The writing is shockingly mediocre. Strangely, the secondary characters feel like GTA characters and the writing improves when anyone is talking besides the protagonists. The humor didn't work at all and Lucia was annoying and insufferable without being compelling. That's the last thing you wanna do in a story driven videogame. What exactly is the takeaway from the story? Whoever was responsible for writing these characters had no idea what they were doing and for the most anticipated game ever, this is shockingly bad. 

Certain design choices unnecessarily limit player freedom, which is the antithesis of GTA. Unfortunately, these minor personal gripes only add to the frustration. For instance, restricting players from stealing vehicles in your neighbourhood because it supposedly doesn't make sense for the story. You'd imagine a Rockstar game would let the consequences play out rather than throwing a pop-up in your face telling you "no touchy!" There are several instances of this throughout the game, breaking immersion and replacing fun with frustration. A GTA game should let you **** around and find out. 

Another example: trains have always been one of my favourite parts of GTA and RDR. I spend hours messing around with them, but in this game, the train stops immediately when you throw an NPC onto the tracks. It's a bizarre design choice. There are also inexplicably invincible NPCs that you can't run over. Clothes magically pop onto your character out of nowhere when you leave your house in pajamas or night dress is something you'd expect from a game like Samson or Mindseye. Fire whoever thought that was a good mechanic to add to the game.


TL;DR:

My rating is based entirely on my experience. I was left thoroughly disappointed after finishing the game. It's a shame, really. It would be a 7.5/10 if it weren't being sold to me as a GTA title. There's a technically great game here, but not a GTA I waited years for. Technical ambition means very little when you lose the soul of the franchise. Perhaps I'm being harsher with the score than I otherwise would be because I can't shake the feeling that I've been robbed of my money.

The horrible TAA, coupled with the blurry visuals and low framerate, makes for an experience nowhere near as good as it should be for a $100 game. A lot of fun elements from previous games seem to have been removed, seemingly to avoid offending the developers themselves. If this is true, these people shouldn't have been in charge **** game in the first place. Rockstar Games is in desperate need of a course correction.

Can't say I'd recommend it, but if you intend to play it, get the standard edition or wait for a sale in the future. You're not missing out on anything, unlike RDR2, which remains Rockstar's magnum opus and one of the greatest pieces of media ever created.

author: userfounddelete
quote:
Here's a negative review for GTA 6, written in a critical review style:

---

Title: All Flash, No Substance — GTA 6 Is a Beautiful Disappointment

Rating: ★★☆☆☆ (2/5)

I wanted to love this game. I really did. After years of hype, GTA 6 finally arrives, and the result is a stunningly polished, wildly ambitious, and ultimately hollow experience that prioritizes spectacle over substance at every turn.

The Good (Yes, There Is Some)
Let's be fair: the visuals are genuinely breathtaking. Vice City at sunset is postcard-perfect, the character models are incredibly detailed, and the dynamic weather system is the best I've seen in an open-world game. The voice acting is top-notch, and the soundtrack is fantastic. On a technical level, Rockstar has outdone itself.

The Bad: A Story That Goes Nowhere
Here's the problem—the story is a mess. The dual-protagonist setup (Lucia and Jason) had so much potential, but the narrative constantly meanders. Just when a plot thread gets interesting, it's dropped. The pacing is all over the place, with long stretches of tedious setup followed by rushed, unsatisfying conclusions. By the third act, I stopped caring about either character. The emotional beats feel unearned, and the ending is abrupt and confusing. It's as if the writers had a dozen great ideas and couldn't commit to any of them.

Gameplay: More of the Same, But Worse
The core gameplay loop is virtually unchanged from GTA V—which would be fine if it weren't for the new "realism" mechanics that actively make the game less fun. Your character now needs to eat, sleep, and manage a stress meter. Sounds immersive, right? In practice, it's just annoying busywork. I spent more time microwaving virtual meals and finding a bed than I did causing chaos.

The driving physics feel floaty and imprecise, and the shooting mechanics are clunky compared to modern standards. The mission design is painfully linear—most missions boil down to "drive here, shoot these guys, drive back." The much-touted "freedom" is an illusion; deviate from the script and you fail instantly.

Technical Issues & Microtransactions
For a game this expensive, the technical state is unacceptable. I encountered framerate drops in crowded areas, texture pop-in during high-speed chases, and at least three hard crashes in my first ten hours. And don't get me started on the online component—GTA Online 2 is a shameless cash grab, with aggressive monetization and paywalls that make the single-player feel like an afterthought.

The Verdict
GTA 6 is a gorgeous, bloated, and ultimately frustrating experience. It's a game that wants to be everything—a crime epic, a life simulator, a technical showcase—and ends up being none of them particularly well. Rockstar has proven they can make beautiful worlds, but somewhere along the way, they forgot to make them fun.

Final Score: 4/10 – A Pretty Shell With Nothing Inside.
