author: Parkergames1655
quote:
My Honest Review
 From a Longtime GTA Fan
There are a few main issues with this game that I believe are felt throughout a large portion of the GTA community.First off, my biggest problem with the game is that it is completely focused around the relationship between Jason and Lucia. I have been playing GTA for many years, and never have I seen so many people upset about a game that they’ve waited so long to play.After a long day of work and living my normal life, following the rules, being a decent citizen, I expect GTA to allow me to commit CRIMES…Are you serious, Rockstar??Why am I not able to SLEEP WITH HOOKERS?? That has been in the series for multiple games, and y’all decided to remove it? Whoever decided to remove hookers from GTA should be fired immediately.Secondly, why do you introduce a beautiful, sexy, AWESOME, woman like Mandy and not allow Jason to cheat on her? What is that??! Like, you’re forced to be a good boyfriend in a game about killing people, robbing, and committing countless other crimes?How does that make any sense?Also, I know it’s optional, but why am I doing chores in a GTA GAME? For my fake girlfriend???Look, Rockstar, my issue isn’t that the game has a romantic storyline. My issue is that GTA has always been about FREEDOM. The freedom to do whatever you want, make terrible decisions, and experience things you would never do in real life. That’s literally what made this franchise so iconic in the first place.I’m not asking you to remove the relationship between Jason and Lucia. I’m asking you to stop making players feel like they have to be loyal, responsible boyfriends in a game where they can literally murder innocent people and rob banks.Rockstar, please put your political ideas aside and focus on what made GTA so successful in the first place. You have a massive fanbase, predominantly made up of men, who have supported this franchise for decades. Give those players the freedom and ridiculous, over-the-top experiences that made them fall in love with **** let’s not forget something VERY important.PEOPLE PAID $80–$100 FOR THIS GAME.That’s a lot of money, especially for fans who have been waiting years for this release. When people spend that much money on a GTA game, they expect the full GTA experience, not a watered-down version where certain activities and choices are suddenly **** Rockstar doesn’t want to see disappointed customers requesting refunds or eventually turning to mods just to experience the freedom they expected from the beginning, then these are things worth **** here’s what makes this even more frustrating: Rockstar has already made over $3 BILLION. You’re telling me that a company generating that kind of money can’t make a few relatively minor changes to satisfy a large portion of its fanbase?Come on, Rockstar. We KNOW you can do better because you’ve DONE IT BEFORE.There are also countless bugs and glitches that need fixing, not to mention certain gameplay mechanics that could use improvement. But those are separate issues. My biggest disappointment is that a franchise built around freedom seems to be unnecessarily restricting the player’s choices.I genuinely believe that addressing these concerns could make a massive difference in how longtime fans feel about the game. I wouldn’t be surprised if the rating on this website went from a 5.2 to something closer to a 9/10 if Rockstar listened to its community and brought back some of the features and freedom that made the older games so enjoyable.I’m not writing this because I hate GTA. Quite the opposite. I’m writing this because I’ve loved this franchise for years, I know what Rockstar is capable of, and I want this game to be as good as it possibly can be.Rockstar, let us play GTA the way we WANT to play GTA. That’s what made your games legendary.

From yours truly,
A longtime GTA fan.

author: French_Fried
quote:
[True review at the bottom]

A question as old as time:  "When does a game become so realistic it's no longer fun?"  Well, you found it.

This whole release rubs me the wrong way.  The digital only copies, PS5 only to secure that GotY nomination and prevent refunds, most of the devs being Jeets that are just vibe-coding most of the game with ****, simp simulator, the list goes on.

This is NOT a GTA game.  You can't even do the NAMESAKE OF THE GAME (grand theft auto) properly till later in the story.  Can't hire hookers cuz "muh toxic gf," and you can't run over and kill anyone and everyone cuz Wokestar loves the protesters.  This game has become a parody of itself and it's sad.

Gameplay - Slow and boring.  Most things just take some getting used to to control and stuff but I'm not kidding when I say it's ACTUALLY SLOW.  It takes 1/4 of the time extra to get somewhere on-foot than it would take in GTA 5.  As stated above, you can't steal any vehicle until way later in the game.  There's no FUN here to be had.  It's an awful dating/life sim that has none of  the original DNA **** game.

Graphics - They're good, but there are countless issues I have with it.  Namely, the framerate struggles to stay at 30 on a normal PS5 and I am not paying more money for a Pro just to be at ~30FPS in this economy.  The game is either too bright, too dark, or washed out.  At night time the game is DARK and you can't see a THING in some situations.  Lighting is the same issue.  It will blind you sometimes.

Presentation - I've pretty much said everything I wanted to about this in the beginning.  It was supposed to be a great hoorah and return to Vice City like 5 was for San Andreas.  This just isn't it man.  It's so disappointing.  Only 2 characters that are constantly together that you can coordinate robberies and stuff sounds great on it's own but, then you had to add all this other stuff that just downplays all the fun you SHOULD be having.  Gabe Newell said it best:  "You'd have these conversations where you'd be sitting in a design review and somebody [would] say, that's not realistic.  You're like, 'okay, what does that have?' like, 'explain to me why that's interesting.' Because in the real world, I have to write up lists of stuff I have to go to the grocery store to buy. And I have never thought to myself that realism is fun. I go play games to have fun."

PLEASE don't buy this game.  If you absolutely MUST get this game, just wait for the PC release so you can mod all the garbage out of it and make it more fun and enjoy more features and better framerates.

author: ruseldust
quote:
English/Español

Rockstar put a tremendous amount of effort into the graphics and creating a massive game world, but in doing so, it neglected things that many of us consider essential to a great game: the excitement, the emotional connection with the player, and the overall experience it delivers.

GTA 6 overlooks something as fundamental as evoking emotions and connecting with players on a deeper level. This is something that should never be neglected. In an industry increasingly focused on graphical power, the quality and depth of the gaming experience are being left behind, even though those are precisely the things that keep players immersed and invested in a game.

I admire the graphical work, but it didn't make me feel anything deeper. Previous entries in the series offered more in that regard. This isn't an achievement, it isn't progress, and it isn't even a revolution for the GTA franchise. That's disappointing.

This review and rating may seem harsh to some, but I believe it's important for us as gamers to let the industry know that maintaining a balance between technical achievements and the depth of the gaming experience matters to us.

GTA 6 is not a balanced game, and we cannot allow the industry to keep moving in this direction. We need genuine commitment to deeper storytelling, emotional impact, innovative gameplay mechanics, artistic direction, and the overall experience of the entire work—not just graphical eye candy and inflated expectations designed to drive sales.

--------------------------------

Rockstar dedicó un esfuerzo enorme a los gráficos y a la creación de un mundo de juego masivo, pero al hacerlo, descuidó aspectos que muchos consideramos esenciales para una gran obra: la emoción, la conexión emocional con el jugador y la experiencia general que ofrece.

GTA 6 pasa por alto algo tan fundamental como evocar emociones y conectar con los jugadores a un nivel más profundo. Esto es algo que nunca debería descuidarse. En una industria cada vez más centrada en la potencia gráfica, la calidad y la profundidad de la experiencia de juego están quedando relegadas, a pesar de que son precisamente los elementos que mantienen a los jugadores inmersos e involucrados en un título.

Admiro el trabajo gráfico, pero no me hizo sentir nada profundo. Entregas anteriores de la saga ofrecieron más en ese sentido. Esto no es un logro, no es progreso y ni siquiera supone una revolución para la franquicia GTA. Es decepcionante.

Esta reseña y calificación pueden parecer excesivamente duras para algunos, pero considero importante que, como jugadores, le hagamos saber a la industria que nos importa mantener un equilibrio entre los logros técnicos y la profundidad de la experiencia de juego.

GTA 6 no es un juego equilibrado y no podemos permitir que la industria siga avanzando en esta dirección. Necesitamos un compromiso genuino con una narrativa más profunda, impacto emocional, mecánicas de juego innovadoras, dirección artística y la experiencia integral de toda la obra; no solo atractivo visual y expectativas infladas diseñadas para impulsar las ventas.

author: ColonialKayak
quote:
Grand Theft Testosterone: VIrtual simpulator Review
(NON-SPOILERS)

After 20 hours game time and almost into chapter 3, I've given up.

It's a decent game in terms of scale, graphics and activities but lacks old Rockstar writing, criminal empire building and an actual soul for the sake of "immersion" and unsatisfying relationship drama making it feel like a chore. It has more in common with Watch Dogs 2 than its own franchise. It's only recieving the attention from its highly anticipated name and trend. 

GTA VI is a hoax and the critic reviews are undeniably sus because it became Game of the Year mere hours post-release yet it's a 50-65 hour game? Some even saying they'd happily play for the rest of their lives after only completing the epilogue?? ️

This is easily the worst game of the series. Replacing the founding formula of empire building with a heavily grounded netflix melodramatic love story that has sprinkles of GTA action powder only unlocked 30+ hours in.

As a long time GTA fan, that being IV, III & Vice City, this has nothing alike from the old Rockstar magic with the houser brothers & benzies. It's a pretty game visually with lots to do but that makes it okay at best.

The Rockstar writing has ironically killed it off. The characters are very 2D and unlikeable, aka the Plank (Jason, who does anything to make anyone happy) and the Torta (Lucia, the one who has no accountability for bad behaviour and gets away with anything). 
How can you root for these characters when the whole games reoccurring cycle is: 
- Petty relationship drama, 
- Rekindle with intimacy or affectionate gift runs, 
- Talking about building a safe environment for their child and financially supporting them, 
- Then back to crime and building 'enough' money, 
- Then back to getting screwed over by another employer they fell for because they're desperate and one of them was naive, 
- Then back to petty drama...

Then there's the controversial situation where your bullets do no damage to certain activists/ groups of people however harms others. Then there's the unbearable sluggish pace of daily chores... Yes, things ramp up eventually, but by then you've lost a good portion of your legacy players.

Even after the 13 year wait, I got to the point I was so uninvested I spoiled the different endings and I was still disappointed, I'm actually relieved I saved myself more hours playing this and following up by instantly uninstalling. 

This is not Grand Theft Auto. Slap the rockstar logo and call it what you wish, but it sure as hell isn't GTA whether you agree with that or not, we can all definitely agree that this game has divided the community, and that the constant 10/10 reviews are sus.

An online mode where we make our own characters is likely to be better off, but as it stands, this is an eyesore and a slog as a completionist.

4.9/10

author: EzzaNinja
quote:
The graphics are nice, I'll give it that. But honestly, the story is woke garbage. You can't shoot certain "protected groups" anymore, including gay characters, animal rights activists and people of certain skin colours under certain circumstances. Since when did GTA start putting restrictions on who you can shoot? The whole point of GTA was that you could do pretty much whatever you wanted. It's always been an over the top, chaotic sandbox where nobody was off limits. Now Rockstar seems more interested in worrying about offending people than actually delivering the experience GTA fans have come to expect.

And why does this game feel like The Sims 4 with a GTA skin? House renovations, fixing pipes, buying flowers for Lucia... seriously? If I wanted to spend my evenings doing boring everyday chores, I'd just go outside. I play games to escape modern day life, not to simulate it. I want crime, chaos, ridiculous missions and absolute mayhem, not a bloody home improvement simulator.

And what makes it even more ridiculous is that you can't even steal cars in certain neighbourhoods. Let that sink in for a second. Grand Theft Auto, a game literally named after stealing cars, now has restrictions on where you can steal them. What's next, not being allowed to commit crimes in certain areas because it might upset the locals? The whole identity of GTA has always been about freedom, stealing cars, causing chaos and doing whatever the hell you want. If Rockstar is going to start putting invisible boundaries around basic GTA mechanics, then what's the point? It's called Grand Theft Auto for crying out loud, not Grand Theft Auto (Terms and Conditions Apply).

And then there's Lucia as a character. Rockstar seems desperate to portray her as this morally grounded, sympathetic character that we're supposed to care about and root for. But how exactly am I supposed to buy into that when she's leaving her newborn child behind to go rob a bank and gets caught doing it in the very first mission? I understand this is GTA and the characters are criminals. That's literally the point. But you can't have it both ways. You can't write a character who makes completely reckless, selfish decisions and then expect the audience to constantly feel sympathy for her just because the story tells us she's supposed to be some strong, misunderstood woman. It feels like Rockstar is trying so hard to make a statement with Lucia rather than just writing a genuinely interesting, believable character. Honestly, the whole thing comes across as forced feminist messaging rather than natural character development.

The game is also a buggy mess. Sure, it's nowhere near as bad as Cyberpunk or Mindseye at launch, but it's still pretty embarrassing. In the FIRST mission, Lucia is already glitching through the ground and falling endlessly into the void. How does something like that make it into the final game? Did nobody bother testing this thing?

And then there's the 30 FPS cap on PS5. Seriously, 30 FPS in a game released in 2026? I understand the game is graphically demanding, but we're well into the current console generation. 60 FPS should be the bare minimum, or at least give us a performance mode. I don't care how pretty the game looks if it feels sluggish to play.

Overall, I'm extremely disappointed. GTA is supposed to be an escape from reality, a place where you can do ridiculous things and have fun without the restrictions of everyday life. Instead, this feels like Rockstar is trying to turn GTA into some politically correct life simulator. Nice graphics, but that alone doesn't make a good game.

Just play GTA V.

author: ammaaya
quote:
I only became excited for this game after the extended look on Netflix and the ensuing promotional interviews following it which gave the impression that that not only would this entry of the GTA franchise would be a big step up from its usually lackluster writing quality but also feature almost Bioware-esque RPG elements and player choice and agency.

Now that the game is actually here, after all the fan excitement and fan perception that was a result of that marketing, and been here long enough to experience the whole story... it's safe to say that the marketing of this game was downright deceptive. 

The saddest part is that much of this was an unforced error.

Rockstar knew that they could've marketed pretty much anything and still made record profits, they could have marketed yet another simple story-on-rails which writing that isn't trying to get an award anytime soon— something that is to be expected from all previous GTA entries —and yet, Rockstar insisted, almost duplicitously, that this entry was so so "different" and meant to be an almost wholly new experience.

Well, as someone who was originally unexcited for this game because I assumed it would be the same old same old generic story with the shallowest of RPG elements and a flimsy veneer of player choice and agency, I wish I had never changed my original assumption.

I shouldn't have gotten taken in by the marketing hype. I really thought this one was gonna be different. The only "difference" is the main characters are just as shallowly written as usual, but in a specific way that feels very dated to the era that this game was originally developed in, which is already a few years ago at this point, mind you!

We have what, 1 hour per evening MAX to hop on have some fun, do crazy criminal activities and release from the stresses of day to day life - we don't expect our free time to be painting walls, told not to pee standing up, grocery shopping, arguments over not texting back, having to refuel cars, the need to eat and train... The first few hours of gameplay here are genuinely so mundane its hard to call it a game at all.

Positives are the graphics are stunning and the vice city nostalgia are still very much there, 30FPS makes certain dialogues or movement look goofy however. I also imagine there will be updates to bring the game to a playable level but for them to not be delivered after 13 years of development is honestly shocking. I won't be playing any further until the game is fixed, no interest in the missions, no interest in the story line. Very sad to see the game delivered like this. 

Giving a 3, because the scope of the game is obviously huge, the graphics are nice and i'm praying big updates will come based on user feedback.

quote: In its current state, this game is trash. Running at 20 FPS makes it practically unplayable—driving feels unresponsive and awful when the game plays like a PowerPoint presentation. Jason is the most boring character imaginable with an unbearable voice, and Lucia kicks off the game with the dumbest decision I’ve ever seen. Right after getting out of jail, she immediately starts making reckless choices while acting like she knows what she’s doing, followed by 6 to 10 hours of tedious **** map is massive, yet completely boring—it honestly would have been much better if it were smaller. I'll preface this by saying I have around 17 hours in this game and I've gone from wanting to be hooked by this game to being completely dejected. Jason and Lucia themselves I have problems with, but at least they are memorable. The same cannot be said for the rest of the cast featured in this game. They tend to be bland and forgettable and I honestly can't think of one interaction I've come away from being entertained.

While Red Dead 2 saw success with the Honor system implemented into its story, it's not suitable for a title such as GTA VI. Grand Theft Auto has built it's reputation off of it's massive open world and the chaos and freedom given to you as the player. GTA VI takes that relaxing care free power trip and instead has you entering every firefight trying to aim for shoulder/arms/knees, and worrying about body count in the fear that it will negatively effect the outcome of Jason and Lucia's story. You would think that playing nice and keeping casualties to a minimum would net you some nice rewards, when in reality the only thing the game does in return is NOT penalize you with a drop in honor. It doesn't matter who it is you're killing either,  even if it was some scumbag gang like the Hells Angels, the game would still treat it the same as shooting a cop/civilian. There are also far fewer opportunities to fix your honor than there were in RDR2, which plays into a whole different issue of how grindy the game is, and how slow the pacing is.

In conclusion ☆☆☆☆☆☆ this game is so ahh ️

author: raah87
quote:
Trece años esperando un juego que, por momentos, parece más preocupado por demostrar cuánto dinero se ha gastado Rockstar que por revolucionar realmente la forma de **** 6 es un monstruo tecnológico, nadie lo discute. 

Tiene una ciudad impresionante, animaciones espectaculares y un nivel de detalle enfermizo. Pero conviene hacerse una pregunta incómoda: ¿de qué sirve construir el mundo abierto más realista jamás visto si seguimos arrastrando problemas de diseño que Rockstar lleva años sin solucionar? Las misiones continúan dependiendo demasiado de situaciones guionizadas, los controles siguen teniendo momentos torpes y buena parte de la acción acaba recurriendo a la misma fórmula de siempre: conducir, disparar, escapar y repetir. Se ha perfeccionado el envoltorio, pero no se ha reinventado el contenido. 

Y luego está el apartado técnico. Estamos en 2026, hablamos de uno de los videojuegos más ambiciosos de la historia y tenemos que conformarnos con 30 fotogramas por segundo en consola. Resulta bastante irónico que un juego que presume de llevar la tecnología al límite no pueda ofrecer una fluidez que muchos jugadores consideran básica en casi 2027. 

Pero el mayor problema de GTA 6 ni siquiera está dentro del juego. Está en lo que representa. Rockstar ha conseguido que una parte del público confunda presupuesto con calidad, realismo con diversión y popularidad con excelencia. Parece que cuestionar cualquier decisión del estudio es poco menos que una herejía.

También resulta difícil ignorar cómo GTA Online contribuyó a convertir una franquicia legendaria en una máquina de generar ingresos recurrentes. Y después de tantos años explotando ese modelo, es perfectamente razonable desconfiar de las prioridades comerciales que puedan marcar el futuro de esta entrega.

GTA 6 puede ser un videojuego extraordinario y, al mismo tiempo, estar tremendamente sobrevalorado. Ambas cosas son compatibles. Que tenga un mapa gigantesco, miles de detalles y una producción multimillonaria no significa automáticamente que cada una de sus mecánicas sea sobresaliente. Lo verdaderamente decepcionante es que a Rockstar ya no parece exigírsele que revolucione los videojuegos: basta con que publique otro GTA para que medio mundo lo proclame una obra maestra.

Después de trece años, lo mínimo exigible era una revolución en todos los aspectos, no simplemente una evolución espectacular de una fórmula conocida. GTA 6 demuestra que Rockstar sigue siendo una referencia construyendo mundos virtuales. Lo que no demuestra es que sea intocable, que todas sus decisiones sean acertadas o que su juego merezca ser considerado automáticamente el mejor de la historia.

Y quizá esa sea la crítica más dura que se le puede hacer: Rockstar ha construido un mundo que parece no tener límites, pero todavía no ha conseguido liberarse del todo de los límites de su propia fórmula.

Y tampoco podemos ignorar los problemas narrativos. Jason resulta un protagonista sorprendentemente plano, con una personalidad demasiado pasiva y unas reacciones que muchas veces lo convierten en un simple acompañante de Lucia. Ser reservado no equivale a tener profundidad. A esto se suman personajes secundarios caricaturescos, situaciones innecesariamente alargadas y un ritmo irregular. Mucho espectáculo, pero no siempre una escritura a la altura de Rockstar.

Y qué decir del fanatismo absolutamente ridículo que rodea al juego. Es vergonzoso ver a auténticos imbéciles atacando otros videojuegos simplemente por lanzarse el mismo mes que GTA 6, como si Rockstar fuera dueña del calendario. Más lamentable todavía es responder a cualquier crítica con el infantil "lo criticas porque no tienes dinero o no lo has jugado". Es un argumento estúpido y clasista. Tener dinero no obliga a admirar un producto. Defender ciegamente a una multinacional no demuestra pasión por los videojuegos, sino una preocupante ausencia de criterio propio.

Pero lo que más me duele es la muerte del verdadero formato físico. Que una compañía multimillonaria como Rockstar venda una caja con un código de descarga en lugar de un disco es una auténtica vergüenza (y encima defectuosas, con codigos visibles a transluz o directamente sin él). Eso no es formato físico: es una licencia digital disfrazada.

Estamos normalizando perder la posibilidad de conservar, prestar, intercambiar o revender nuestros juegos libremente. Nos hacen cada vez más dependientes de servidores, cuentas y decisiones empresariales, mientras algunos celebran esta pérdida de derechos como si fuera progreso.

Y ese es el verdadero problema: si GTA 6 puede hacerlo sin consecuencias comerciales, ¿qué impedirá que el resto de la industria siga el mismo camino?

GTA 6 podrá ser un prodigio tecnológico, pero también puede representar uno de los mayores retrocesos para el consumidor. Y lo verdaderamente triste es ver cómo parte de la comunidad aplaude mientras pierde aquello que durante décadas hizo especial coleccionar videojuegos.

author: gdgassafda
quote: The hour has come to speak of this latest creation of the American machine. Grand Theft Auto Six has been released. The masses cheer. The critics call it a masterpiece. I call it what it is. It is a perfect portrait of a race in collapse. Look at the world they have built. Vice City. Leonida. A sun-drenched swamp of palm trees and neon and endless concrete. Every street crawls with the same mixture. The Negro. The Latin. The Oriental. The rootless white who has forgotten his blood. They rob. They murder. They chase money that vanishes the moment it is touched. This is not fantasy. This is the daily reality of the American cities that have abandoned hierarchy and blood. The two leads are a man and a woman bound by crime. They are not heroes. They are the natural product of a system that has destroyed the family and the nation. He is a broken soldier cast aside by the very state that used him. She is a criminal marked by the ankle bracelet of a justice system that no longer believes in justice. Together they steal and kill because that is all that remains when the higher purpose of race and soil has been erased. Struggle remains. But it is the struggle of rats in a sewer. The technical achievement is real. The streets live. The light falls correctly. The crowds move with the restless energy of a people who have no direction. That is precisely the point. The machine can render every drop of sweat and every reflection on wet asphalt. It cannot render honour. It cannot render the will of a people that knows itself. It can only render the chaos that follows when the Jew has done his work. For years the same forces have sold this poison under the name of entertainment. They dissolve the sense of hierarchy. They make the criminal the only figure who still acts with force. They turn the white youth into a spectator of his own replacement. Then they collect the money and call it art. The eternal pattern never changes. Finance and empty spectacle. Blood and soil reduced to background noise while the cameras linger on the next explosion. Democracy produced this. Internationalism produced this. The cult of comfort and silence produced this. A people that no longer believes it has the right to rule its own streets will eventually play games about ruling the streets of others. That is the true content of Grand Theft Auto Six. It is not rebellion. It is confession. The struggle continues. The race that forgets this law will be swept away by those who still remember it. This game is only a symptom. The disease is older and deeper. Those who still possess the will to see must look past the glowing screens and recognize the hour.

author: AAAGamesEU
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI is a monumental open-world achievement that sets a new benchmark for environmental detail and grounded storytelling, even though its core shooting and driving mechanics still feel noticeably dated.

The Good• Unmatched World Design: The state of Leonida, centered around a vibrant Vice City, bursts with life, dynamic weather, and organic random events that make exploration endlessly rewarding.• Grounded Narrative: Rockstar trades its usual over-the-top satire for an intimate, surprisingly emotional crime drama following Lucia and Jason's struggle for a fresh start.• Smarter Law Enforcement: Police now remember your face, outfit, and vehicle, turning escapes into tense, tactical getaways where changing clothes or wearing a mask actually matters.• Tactical Realism: Borrowing from Red Dead Redemption 2, limiting your loadout to two main weapons and adding a focus-aim ability makes firefights feel much more deliberate.

The Bad• Slow Opening Hours: The campaign takes roughly six to eight hours to build up its characters before throwing you into your first major shootout.• Dated Controls and Gunplay: Despite cinematic set pieces, the cover system, shooting mechanics, and occasionally sluggish vehicle handling feel stuck in the past.• Missing Side Activities: Longtime fans will notice the absence of classic franchise staples like real estate purchases, the stock market, and taxi missions.• 30 FPS Cap: Even on mid-gen console hardware like the PS5 Pro, the frame rate is locked at 30 FPS, though rock-solid pacing keeps it visually smooth.

author: Darkkao
quote:
Grand Theft Auto VI – The Most Overhyped Disappointment of the Decade

Final Score: 4/10

Grand Theft Auto VI was supposed to be the biggest gaming event of the decade. After years of anticipation, endless trailers and an almost absurd level of hype, Rockstar has delivered an experience that falls far short of expectations. Despite its impressive presentation, the game has some serious problems that are difficult to ignore.
Let's start with the technical side. For a production of this scale, the number of bugs and technical issues is disappointing. Glitches, inconsistent animations and performance problems are not what you expect from one of the biggest studios in the industry. After so many years of development, a much more polished experience should have been the minimum requirement.
Then there is the elephant in the room: 30 FPS. In 2026, releasing such an ambitious blockbuster with a 30 FPS limitation is difficult to justify. Beautiful graphics are impressive, but they should never come at the expense of gameplay fluidity. Driving, shooting and exploring would benefit enormously from a stable 60 FPS experience. This alone makes waiting for the PC version a much more sensible decision.
The missions are another major disappointment. Despite the enormous open world, too many missions feel repetitive, predictable and unnecessarily prolonged. Driving from one location to another, listening to lengthy conversations and following restrictive objectives does not automatically make for engaging gameplay. A massive map means very little if the actual missions struggle to keep players entertained.
There is also the question of the game's writing and overall tone. GTA has traditionally been known for its irreverent humour, controversial satire and willingness to make fun of absolutely everyone. However, GTA VI sometimes gives the impression of adopting a more contemporary, politically conscious and arguably woke approach. Some players may feel that the franchise has lost part of its provocative identity. GTA should be fearless, unpredictable and willing to challenge everyone equally. It should not feel afraid of its own satire.
Perhaps the most frustrating aspect is the critical reception. Reading some professional reviews, you would think GTA VI has reinvented video games. Technical shortcomings are dismissed, repetitive missions are praised as deliberate pacing, and the 30 FPS limitation is treated as an acceptable compromise.
And then there are the fanboys. Some players seem completely incapable of acknowledging any flaws in a Rockstar game. Every bug is excused, every criticism is dismissed, and anyone who questions the game's quality is labelled a hater. At some point, blind loyalty becomes fanboyism. Being a Rockstar fan does not mean defending every decision the company makes. If you cannot recognise obvious problems simply because of the name on the box, you are not evaluating the game objectively. You are defending a brand.
GTA VI is not necessarily a terrible game, but it is nowhere near the untouchable masterpiece its reviews suggest. Its impressive world cannot compensate for its technical limitations, uninspiring missions and questionable creative decisions.
My recommendation? Wait for the PC version. Save your money and see whether Rockstar can deliver the experience players actually deserve.

Final verdict: 4/10. An enormous amount of hype, an enormous amount of excuses, and a disappointing result.

author: mzpkf9
quote:
GTA 6 feels less like the future of gaming and more like the dead end of the culture industry.
After more than a decade and a rumored billion-dollar budget, Rockstar threw everything at hyper-realistic lighting, skin pores, and street clutter. Underneath all that tech showcase, though, it is still the same rigid mission design from ten years ago, bogged down by sluggish pacing and a 30fps cap in 2026 even on high-end consoles. Spending a fortune to make a city look like a photograph does not hide the fact that the actual game design has barely moved forward.
What bothers me even more is how completely the series has been tamed. GTA used to have real bite and messy, irreverent satire. Now it plays like a safe, sanitized prestige TV drama built to offend nobody and maximize global sales. Locking finished shops behind an Ultimate Edition paywall on top of an $80 price tag says everything about what actually drives this "immersive world."
As for the 99 Metascore, seeing over a hundred critics ignore obvious technical compromises and stale gameplay to hand out perfect 10s just shows how broken mainstream games journalism has become. GTA 6 will break every sales record on earth, sure, but all it really proves is that the AAA industry now confuses the most expensive product ever made with the greatest art.

author: DGuerra_99
quote:
I’m genuinely disappointed with Grand Theft Auto VI.

The main story is the biggest letdown. You’re basically forced into a specific path of maintaining a romantic relationship with Lucia whether you want to or not. There’s no real freedom to reject or ignore that dynamic, the game constantly pushes you to keep the couple together, and it feels restrictive and unnatural. On top of that, the pacing is painfully slow, and many of the missions are absurd, repetitive, and just plain boring. They actively damage the legacy of a series that used to be known for chaotic freedom and memorable set pieces.
Jason is completely flat and uninteresting, while Lucia is just detestable. Neither of them carries the story in a way that makes you care.

There are also a lot of restrictions on actions that were perfectly possible in previous GTA games. The freedom the series was built on has been noticeably dialed back in several areas, which is frustrating.

Technically, the game is sold as a massive leap forward, yet it struggles to even hold 30 FPS in many situations. It’s almost funny how some critics will destroy other games for not consistently running above 30, but when GTA VI can’t even hit that mark, it’s suddenly a “masterpiece.” The amount of bugs at launch doesn’t help either.
The only things that are truly impressive are the visual quality, the level of detail in the world, and the NPC interactions. Those parts are genuinely excellent. Unfortunately, they’re not enough to carry the rest of the experience.

For a game that was supposed to redefine the series, this feels like a step sideways at best and a step backward in several important ways.

author: saeed_lm10
quote:
GTA VI – A Critical Look at Its Content and Design

GTA VI should not be praised simply for its graphics and visual realism. Realistic textures, impressive lighting, and detailed environments mean very little if the actual gameplay lacks depth, originality, and meaningful interaction.

The excessive focus on visual spectacle risks overshadowing more important elements, including mission design, gameplay mechanics, AI, storytelling, character development, and world interaction.

Another major concern is the excessive sexualization and explicit adult content. There is a clear difference between mature storytelling and relying on provocative imagery, sexual references, nudity, and vulgarity to attract attention. Such content can easily become unnecessary, distracting, and excessive rather than adding genuine artistic value.

The same applies to violence and crude humor. Mature content should serve the narrative, not become an excuse for shock value.

A great game should offer depth, creativity, meaningful gameplay, and artistic quality. Graphics alone cannot make up for weak design, and explicit content should never be confused with mature storytelling.

GTA VI needs substance, not just spectacle, excessive sexuality, and visual extravagance.

I am on a launch model PS5. I enjoy high framerates when I play games on my PC, but I am not a framerate snob. I have played many console games at 30 fps. Which happens to be half the "CiNeMaTiC" 24 fps it usually hovers around. 30 fps isn't consistently achievable for this game. Instead, it is a nice surprise that rarely drops by to visit, and never stays long. 

The good: Flat out, the shooting and visuals are a massive improvement over GTA V. 

The bad: everything else. 
They ripped out half of what made Grand Theft Auto GTA in the first place and what they replaced it with is boring and lame. Gone is the arcadey crime sandbox where nothing was off limits and everything was on the table. In its place a skin-walker wearing the flesh a GTA game and using the mechanics from RDR2 tries to gaslight you into thinking GTA was always a life sim dating game with crime on the side. You can not commit crime in your neighborhood. You can now only carry two hand guns and two long guns on your person cause "ReAliSm". You are not always able to carjack a car. The train stops for dead bodies now. You can no longer shoot up some clubs, it forces your gun down if you try to aim inside from outside. You can no longer run some NPCs over, they are either invincible or the game forces your car to brake. The NPC and vehicle reactions seem noticeable worse. They removed prostitutes from the game set in Florida because of the poorly executed "Bonnie and Clyde" storyline. The supporting cast of characters are unfunny and not very interesting. The male main character has the personality of a soggy piece of toast. "Yeah. Okay, sure." Is his entire range. The Female character is your classic toxica girlboss. Ultimately GTA VI is a vapid and soulless GTA game. Do not buy this game to play on the launch PS5, Xbox X or S. Do not by a PS5 pro for 1500 to play this game. Wait for this game to go on sale. author: shinobi_21
quote:
GTA VI: The Monument to Hype, Arrogance, and Unrealistic Expectations

At this point, GTA VI is no longer just a video game; it is a monument to corporate hype, excessive marketing, and an audience that has somehow convinced itself that Rockstar is incapable of making mistakes. The sheer amount of blind worship surrounding this game is almost more entertaining than anything the game itself could possibly offer.

Rockstar has spent years cultivating an aura of untouchable prestige, as though every delay, every vague announcement, and every cinematic trailer were part of some masterful artistic vision. Yet, the reality is that the gaming industry has become increasingly comfortable treating consumers like an endlessly patient audience whose standards can be postponed indefinitely, provided the company occasionally releases a few seconds of footage accompanied by dramatic music.

The expectations surrounding GTA VI have become so absurd that the game is practically expected to revolutionize every conceivable aspect of entertainment. It is expected to have flawless storytelling, unprecedented realism, groundbreaking AI, an immaculate open world, and enough content to justify years of anticipation. And if it fails to meet even a fraction of those expectations, people will inevitably find excuses. Because apparently, criticizing Rockstar has become an offense against gaming itself.

What makes this situation particularly ridiculous is that Rockstar's reputation is largely built upon its past achievements. GTA V and Red Dead Redemption 2 were remarkable games, certainly, but past excellence does not grant a company permanent immunity from criticism. Nostalgia is not a development tool, reputation is not a guarantee of quality, and a billion-dollar corporation should not be treated as though it were an independent studio surviving on passion and goodwill.

The gaming community has also played an embarrassing role in this spectacle. Every leaked image, every rumor, every alleged detail is dissected with the enthusiasm of someone examining sacred scripture. People have spent years speculating about mechanics that have not even been officially demonstrated, constructing imaginary versions of the game that no developer could realistically deliver. The problem is no longer simply Rockstar's marketing; it is the audience's willingness to surrender its judgment before the product even exists.

Ultimately, GTA VI might genuinely be an excellent game. It might even surpass its predecessors. But that is precisely the point: it should be judged as a game, not as a mythical masterpiece whose greatness has already been predetermined by marketing, nostalgia, and internet hysteria.

Until it actually delivers, GTA VI deserves neither unconditional praise nor the ridiculous pedestal on which it has been placed. It is a video game, not the second coming of the gaming industry. And perhaps the most embarrassing thing about this entire spectacle is that some people have already decided it is a masterpiece before they have even had the opportunity to play it.

Great graphics. Terrible story!  It plays like a soap-opera from 1990 with some added game-style gun-play. I think RockStar became confused and spent 13 years working on a photo-real version of "The Sims" or something.

62% finished and it's been like: 2 hours of "The Sims" followed by 30min. of psudo-GTA - repeated for the past umpteen hours. 

I use "The Sims" as a parallel because those such quests and activities are socialite, house-keeping, and very dull robotic meaningless dialogue sessions - quite a bit like one imagines while playing "The Sims". 

If you like TV Soap Operas with a little gun-play now and then this game is for you! Although I suspect not too many house wives or green-haired single mothers will be spending $80 or $100 on a game with GTA's past reputation.  I mean, I think the target audience for most of the past GTA games were mostly men and boys 13 to 35 with a few tom-boys sprinkled in - ALL of whom were entertained by over-the-top sx and violence mixed with wildly silly antics, no?  There's NONE of that in GTA VI.

Given the gameplay expectations one likely has from previous GTA versions this is a huge disappointment!  I have about 4,000 hours in GTA-V but not nearly that much in I, II, III, and IV just to qualify myself and my thoughts here.

Jason then had to accept her and her story about the child without any DNA tests. Jason then had to fight to raise 2M $ with her to regain custody of the child while being locked into a dynamic that is trying to strengthen their relationship through his efforts mostly, buying her flowers and doing other domestic tasks. “Freedom to avoid the relationship” was misleading in the sense that you’re locked into bad endings then. You don’t want to play into the Romance but want a good ending? You don’t want to get involved with Lucia in any shape or form but want a good ending? No chance. author: RyanJohnson1998
quote:
TL/DR: 
The Verdict: 1/10
Grand Theft Auto VI is a monument to modern AAA hubris. It asks you to wait thirteen years, pay top dollar for an empty box with no disc, suffer through 30fps performance and game breaking bugs, and grind through artificial wait timers in a watered-down story. Rockstar didn't deliver a revolution they delivered a gilded storefront disguised as a video game. 

The Review:
Thirteen years. 
Over a decade of trailers, delays, corporate excuses, and a reported two-billion-dollar budget: all culminating in what might be the most cynical, anti-consumer, and technically broken release in modern gaming history. 

If you were hoping Grand Theft Auto VI would be the triumphant return of the unapologetic, boundary-pushing Rockstar Games of old, prepare for a massive, overpriced reality check. 
Here is a breakdown of how Rockstar managed to fumble the most anticipated game on the planet. A thirteen-year wait for a Cyberpunk Style mess you would assume that taking more than a decade to develop a single video game. while milking GTA Online for billions in the meantime would guarantee a spotless, airtight launch.

Instead, players were greeted on day one by a buggy, unoptimized wreck that immediately drew comparisons to Cyberpunk 2077. Across both PS5 and Xbox Series X/S, the game is riddled with immersion **** glitches: Game-Breaking softlocks: Repeated crashes during the opening prologue, hard freezes, and an early Lucia mission softlock right outside a bank that completely halts story progression.

Broken Physics and Geometry: Launch-day footage is flooded with aircraft clipping straight through ****, characters falling endlessly beneath the map, NPCs swimming sideways through concrete, and vehicles spontaneously detonating or launching into the stratosphere from minor fender-benders.   Performance Compromises: Despite the endless wait, console players were slapped with a 30fps cap, accompanied by frame drops, missing textures, and cut-out audio. 
The Ultimate Anti-Consumer Cash Grab: No Disc, No Ownership Even worse than the technical state of the game is the sheer corporate greed surrounding how it is sold. For a franchise built on iconic physical releases complete with fold-out paper maps and thick manuals Rockstar and Take-Two decided to spit in the face of collectors and everyday consumers by shipping GTA VI without a physical disc.
If you walked into a retail store, you weren't buying a game; you were paying full AAA price for a hollow plastic case containing a glorified piece of paper with a download code and not even a physical map to soften the blow. 
By killing the physical disc, Rockstar effectively: Eliminated True Ownership: You don't own GTA VI; you are renting a revocable digital license. 
Destroyed Resale and Lending: You cannot lend the game to a friend, trade it in at a local shop, or buy a used copy. Every single person who wants to play is forced to pay full price directly into Take-Two’s digital storefront. 
Trapped Pre-Order Buyers: By locking down pre-loads early and stripping away standard retail alternatives, consumers were cornered into digital lock-in before the public ever saw the 30fps cap or the launch-day bugs.
Trading Classic GTA Chaos for Tedious "Realism" and Gated Grinds. Perhaps the most disappointing part of GTA VI is that it actively abandons the fast-paced, satirical DNA that made Vice City, San Andreas, and even GTA V fun to play. Instead of leaning into classic arcade chaos, Rockstar doubled down on the sluggish, hyper-realistic mechanics of Red Dead Redemption 2 and then padded the campaign with artificial roadblocks. 
Artificial Story Gating: Rather than letting you play through the narrative at your own pace, the campaign introduces mandatory wait timers and cash hurdles between story missions. Want to see what happens next? Go grind petty store robberies or fence cars until the game decides you're allowed to progress.   Nickel and Diming Basic Convenience: Even basic quality-of-life features from older titles have been turned into tedious money sinks- you can't even skip a cab ride without paying an extra $100 fee on top of the fare.
Safe, Toothless Writing: Gone is the sharp, irreverent bite that once defined the series. Critics and longtime fans (Myself included) alike have pointed out that the dialogue and narrative payoffs feel sanitized, flat, and noticeably weaker than past entries clearly designed to funnel players away from a forgettable single-player campaign and straight into the next decade of GTA Online microtransactions. 
The Verdict: 2/10
Grand Theft Auto VI is a monument to modern AAA hubris. It asks you to wait thirteen years, pay top dollar for an empty box with no disc, suffer through 30fps performance and game-breaking bugs, and grind through artificial wait timers in a watered-down story. Rockstar didn't deliver a revolution, they delivered a gilded storefront disguised as a video game. 

SHAME.

author: Worldmanone
quote: GTA VI: Is Rockstar Losing the Soul of GTA?GTA V made me eager to discover what its characters would do next. GTA VI seems more interested in showing me what I can do in its world.**That's my biggest disappointment with GTA VI.Having played the game, I appreciate its graphics and open world. Yet I felt disconnected from its **** characters haven't captured my attention, and the narrative hasn't given me a reason to care about what happens next.A story can be a slow burn, but it shouldn't leave players indifferent.* GTA V Was Driven by Its CharactersGTA V wasn't memorable because of its massive open world. It was memorable because of Michael, Franklin, and Trevor.Michael was a wealthy but unhappy criminal struggling with his past. Franklin was desperate to escape his circumstances. Trevor was violent, unpredictable, and obsessed with loyalty and betrayal.Their personalities constantly clashed.Michael wanted to escape his past. Trevor refused to let it go. Franklin wanted a better future but found himself caught between them.These conflicts made the story compelling even without constant **** North Yankton robbery established mysteries that unfolded as their relationships developed. Players weren't simply waiting for the next heist. They wanted to know what these men would do to one another.**GTA V succeeded because its characters drove the story, rather than existing merely to justify its missions.**# GTA VI: Where Is the Same Character Chemistry?GTA VI centres on Jason and Lucia, a criminal couple whose relationship involves love, trust, crime, and ****'s a promising concept, but the execution hasn't convinced me.Michael and Trevor could generate tension simply by being in the same room. Their personalities made every interaction unpredictable.Jason and Lucia haven't inspired the same curiosity or emotional investment.I understand their circumstances, but understanding characters isn't the same as caring about them.**If the protagonists aren't compelling, even elaborate missions and conspiracies may struggle to make the story memorable.**## When the World Becomes More Important Than the CharactersGTA V's environments reinforced its characters.Michael's mansion reflected his hollow success. Franklin's neighbourhood represented the life he wanted to escape. Trevor's desert home embodied his chaotic **** world strengthened the **** VI seems more focused on realistic NPC behaviour, environmental detail, and everyday activities.These achievements are impressive, but realism alone doesn't make a better GTA.I don't play GTA to simulate ordinary life. I play it for crime, dark humour, social satire, and unforgettable characters.**An open world should strengthen its characters' stories, not overshadow them.**## Why Do GTA V's Characters Still Interest Me More?I've wondered whether bringing Michael, Franklin, and Trevor into Vice City could have created a more compelling narrative.Imagine Franklin expanding his empire, Michael caught in another conspiracy, and Trevor disrupting everything.Jason and Lucia could find themselves caught between them, creating conflict between two generations.This isn't simply nostalgia. These characters already have strong personalities and conflicting **** VI deserves its own protagonists, but one question remains:**Why do three characters introduced over a decade ago still inspire more curiosity in me than Rockstar's new leads?**## Has Rockstar's Creative Direction Changed?With figures such as Dan Houser and Leslie Benzies having departed, Rockstar's leadership has changed significantly.That doesn't automatically mean its games have declined. But it raises questions about the studio's priorities.Does Rockstar still prioritise memorable characters, sharp satire, and complicated crime stories?Or has creating an enormous, realistic virtual world become its greater ambition?Both goals can coexist, but their balance matters.**Better graphics don't guarantee better storytelling. A bigger world doesn't guarantee better characters. Commercial success doesn't guarantee creative superiority.**#Conclusion: What Will Players Remember?Ten years from now, what will players remember about GTA VI?Its realistic NPCs, detailed buildings, and countless activities?Or the unforgettable things Jason and Lucia did?We still remember Trevor's madness, Michael's contradictions, and Franklin's **** because GTA V had the most realistic city, but because it created characters worth remembering.I hope GTA VI's story changes my opinion. But so far, it hasn't delivered the same excitement or anticipation that GTA V gave me.**GTA V introduced me to its world through its characters. GTA VI seems to be asking me to discover its characters through its world.**That's the fundamental difference.**Rockstar, GTA's soul has never been about how realistic its cities are. It's about the unforgettable, outrageous, deeply flawed characters who bring those cities to life.

author: A_Yuki
quote:
Rating: 4–6/10 I initially gave it a 6 and called it generous; I now feel even that is too high. I scored previous GTA titles 7-9/10 despite not being a hardcore fan.

Core reasons it is not a GTA game and scores low:

- It feels like a life/relationship simulator or “chores” game rather than a crime/sandbox fantasy. The opening and overall tone lack the punchy, iconic chaos of earlier entries (GTA V’s bank robbery with Franklin, Michael, and Trevor; GTA IV’s ensemble; GTA III, San Andreas, Vice City, etc).

- It was marketed with a Bonnie and Clyde-style couple-on-the-run premise, but I feel it fails to deliver that energy. GTA V felt more like a proper heist/crime game by comparison.

- Classic unrestricted freedoms are gone or heavily restricted: no hiring hookers, no free shooting in bars/clubs, limited ability to interact with certain NPCs (e.g., protesters), car theft via key cloning instead of hotwiring, and other sandbox limits.

- Tone and satire are sanitized. Strong language exists but is extremely dialed down and infrequent compared with GTA V, IV, San Andreas, Vice City, etc., where swearing was constant. This removes the unfiltered edge and immersion.

- The official justification (Jason and Lucia are a couple, so classic activities were removed) does not hold up. In GTA V, Michael was married with kids and still hired prostitutes, visited strip clubs, and the story showed his wife cheating with the yoga instructor, yet none of those features were cut.

- Photorealistic graphics break immersion for me. You prefer the stylized or less fully photorealistic approach of games like Ocarina of Time, FF7 Remake, FFXV, and even RDR2, which still feel immersive within their fantasy/world rules.

- Early GTAs were pure fantasy playgrounds with almost no restrictions. GTA VI deliberately moves away from that, and removing the defining unrestricted elements leaves it without the series’ “soul.”

In short, I see it as a high-production simulator that keeps the GTA name and setting but abandons the unrestricted, satirical, consequence-light crime fantasy that defined the series for me. That identity break is why the score drops to 4–6/10 and why I do not consider it a true GTA game.

author: Username15737
quote: Honestly, GTA 6 is one of the biggest disappointments I've ever experienced. Between the alleged review manipulation, endless delays, and the constant exploitation of hype just to capitalize on awards season and chase GOTY recognition, this game feels more like a marketing product than a genuinely great game. It shouldn't even have been considered for GOTY in its current state. And honestly, if this game had released at the beginning of the year, around the same time as Resident Evil Requiem, it probably wouldn't be nearly as relevant anymore. The amount of hype surrounding GTA 6 is artificially keeping it in the spotlight, and without that massive marketing machine constantly pushing it, people would have moved on already. It feels like the game is relying more on its name, its release timing, and the community's obsession than on its actual quality. The performance is pretty bad, reaching 20 FPS with constant drops, accompanied by horrendous bugs, terrible collision detection, and interactions that feel completely lifeless and unresponsive. For a game of this scale, these problems are simply embarrassing. And somehow, in 2026, after 13 years of development, millions in budget, and all the resources Rockstar has at its disposal, we still don't get proper voice dubbing? Instead, we're expected to pay €80 for an unfinished, poorly optimized, unpolished, and seemingly cut-down product that absolutely does not justify its price. The story isn't necessarily terrible, which makes the whole situation even more disappointing. There is potential here, but it's buried beneath technical issues, questionable decisions, and a ridiculous amount of hype that the game simply doesn't live up to. What bothers me the most is how GTA 6 exposes the ugly side of both corporations and gaming communities. If this game had been released under a different name, without the Rockstar logo or the GTA brand behind it, people would be tearing it apart for its bugs, performance, and lack of polish. We've seen games like Cyberpunk get heavily criticized for technical problems, and even Zelda: Breath of the Wild get complaints over its 30 FPS performance. Yet when it's GTA, suddenly everything is "normal," and people defend issues they would never tolerate from any other developer. That double standard is ridiculous. Rockstar shouldn't get a free pass just because of its name, and fans shouldn't blindly defend a product simply because they have been waiting years for it. After 13 years of waiting, a massive budget, and all that hype, getting something this poorly polished for €80 is honestly a disgrace. What a waste of potential. The GTA name shouldn't be an excuse for mediocrity, and hype shouldn't replace quality. What a shame..

author: VenTheGentleman
quote:
AMAZING CONCEPT.... Horrible execution!

GTA 5 came out and it was a huge deal. I remember picking up Sleeping Dogs at the same times. I played through both single player campaigns and I realized, whiie I enjoyed Sleeping Dog's story mode more... GTA surpassed it in terms of the world, graphics, humor and freedom. 

I have played every single GTA since the very 1st one. What made GTA important is that it became the benchmark for everything. Every game was an upgrade toward something special.

Unfortunately, I can't say the same for GTA... 

After GTA 5, one of the central questions was how we expand and evolve. One idea I thought would be genius is to continue the theme of GTA 5 but explore different character types in more meaningful ways. The idea of playing as a woman is actually genius. Imagine being a female character in the GTA world and some guys harass you, then you can do GTA stuff to them. 

The idea of a female protagonist is not a bad one. It's excellent. Just like GTA allowed us to step into the body of A. A wealthy ****, B. A psychopath, C. A Hood black character... it actually does something important. It brings us all together as people and allows us to see the world through different eyes. A female character was golden opportunity to do the same, especially if she was a rational and cool character.

The female protagonist of this game... isn't rational. The game isn't rational. YES, GTA is meant to be an insane game, but by the end we are cheering for the protagonists and watch there journey + gain meaningful lessons from them.

What did I learn from this game???? 1. Your baby momma can lie, manipulate, hurt, complain about, abuse, misuse and cheat on you... and you die trying to simp for her. 2. Rockstar views itself as so lucrative and excellent that it can do whatever it wants... and people will buy it.

Well, the developers made a gross miscalculation. On tops of terrible leads, the game is buggy, ridiculous, broken and at times frustrating to play. It's mind boggling and forces you to wonder if all that 2 billion development + marketing budget was actually used on the game or just enriched a lot of invisible people.

You almost have to wonder if the behind-the-scenes development of this game should be the real GTA 6, because someone went for a heist and fans got robbed. And THAT deserves a 5 star police rating.

author: JulianneSTR
quote:
- Extremely high price
- Scummy ultimate edition that cuts content from the game
- Promotes all digital future (ew).
- Runs like absolute crap.
- Pause menu is the worst in the series and it's made to sell you microtransactions.
- Music is heavily inferior to previous entries.
- MORALE SYSTEM IN A GAME ABOUT BEING A BAD PERSON. 
- Excessive realism mechanic wise like if anyone asked for Rockstar to not let us have the classic weapon wheel.

Gameplay wise, the devs clearly wanted to make a red dead auto. It doesn't work. It just does not feel like GTA. I don't want a random invisible meter to change the way the game develops, it has no place in this franchise. There has always been a tacit pact between player and game in GTA: The game allowed the player to be the most free individual ever in the sandbox, but said player accepted the story as it is, and understood the crazy things done in the sandbox might or might not have actual correlation with the story. This game, however, breaks that pact, since it wants you to live the sandbox the way they intended and not the way you want. Sure, you can just say "**** it" and play it like any GTA, but then the game will make sure you feel like **** for doing so. The gameplay also limits your immediate access to weapons heavily, like RDR2, and does not allow you full freedom to shoot in many places you'd want. To finish this off, it's clear that GTA VI is constantly fighting with it's own nature as a GTA, and you feel it while playing because the game does not respect that tacit pact I have described before. Instead, it tries to enforce it's view of Jason and Lucía in the way that you play with them in the sandbox, and if you don't follow that path, you'll get punished by the game system. GTA did not need more consequences for being an ****, as such consequences already existed and they go from one to six stars.
Music wise it's just inferior to all main entries since GTA III, it's not horrendous but it really can't compare to GTA V or IV.

The price is extremely high, with cut content from the base game being packed inside an "ultimate edition" yet they have the balls to put a **** STORE in the pause menu. Disgusting. All that WHILE selling you an empty physical box with NO DISC, so you can't refund, share the game with any friends, or own the product at all.
Moreover, after so many years in development, and behind such a high price, you'd expect the game to run accordingly. No, it doesn't. It not only doesn't run at 60 which is the standard, but it also doesn't run at stable 30 FPS. Rockstar tries to justify this by saying the PS5 is "too weak" instead of admitting their lazyness or doing their job. We can have debates about if the PS5 could or could not run it at 60 with a performance mode, but not being able to reach stable 30 is objectively pathetic and a scam.

It's a shame, because the game behind all this crap is good. If it wasn't because of it's fundamental contradictions with the nature of the franchise GTA (Which would be as simple as not to call it GTA VI), the horrendous anti-customer practices, and the atrocious performance, it'd probably deserve a high score. If you, dear reader, are curious on why I chose a 0 instead a 5-7 of a score (which would be more faithful to the game's content), it's mostly because of how this game tries to boycott the rights of it's customers and make them think it's okay.

My recommendation? Don't give Rockstar your money. The game is good but it's not worth it's price. It's basically a tech demo with bad writing and various simulations for you to go through. This product attempts against customers, their rights, and their intelligence.

author: Niko_Belic
quote:
Hello, my friends. Niko Bellic here.

I came for the American Dream. 
I found betrayal, dead friends, and vengeance.

Now GTA VI has incredible graphics, world, and technology.
And the story? Complete **** garbage. Worse than the smell of my balls!

I survived a war and killed half of Liberty City just to return as a drug kingpin and watch two idiots surrender to a politician.

What happened to Grand Theft Auto?
Tommy killed Sonny and ruled Vice City. CJ buried Big Smoke and Tenpenny. Franklin defeated his powerful manipulators. Even Claude, a **** mute, killed his betrayers.
And me? I lost people I loved. I was exploited by criminals and politicians. But when someone destroyed my world, I could still shoot them in the face.
GTA protagonists could lose everything except the balls to fight back.
Now in GTA VI, to survive, Jason and Lucia must cooperate with the corrupt state prosecutor responsible for so much of their misery. 
I expected them to put a bullet in her head. Instead, they beg for **** the middle ending, Lucia gets pardoned and Jason goes to prison. In the supposedly GOOD ending, Jason STILL goes to prison, unless you have over **TWO MILLION **** DOLLARS TO BRIBE A JUDGE** for early release.

Back in Liberty City, I killed people for $5,000. Now these two are paying millions to the people who ruined their lives? Its like going bowling with Dimitri Rascalov.
The old GTA let you overturn the table. GTA VI makes you work fifty hours to afford the privilege of bending over for politicians.

And do not call this a "mature, realistic tragedy." GTA IV was a tragedy. I know. I was there. Tragedy means losing something precious, not thanking the bastard who took it.
And the characters? **Why raise a child in Grand Theft Auto?**Tommy wanted an empire. CJ wanted his family and streets back. Franklin wanted out of the hood. I wanted the American Dream. 
Jason and Lucia apparently want affordable childcare and a nice school district. Roman was practically a child. I spent half my life to kept that idiot alive. But at least he actually called me! There was no interaction with the kid of Jason and Lucia throughout, not even a video call, when Lucia hold Jason in her dream, it felt like burden or than love. 
And what happened to freedom in relationships? CJ had SIX girlfriends. I had FOUR, or FIVE if you count that **** rat Michelle. Jason and Lucia cannot even choose to break up.I am not promoting cheating. I am promoting CHOICE. 
Chapter Five even locks you inside a house. Roman's taxi had more freedom than these two. 
Credit where due: the missions are entertaining, the world is extraordinary, and Rockstar's engineers deserve respect. But beautiful graphics cannot save a story that forgot what GTA is about.
And my favorite moment? **My own **** cameo.**There I was in Vice City. Once a poor immigrant running errands for the Russian Mafia; now apparently I AM the Mafia. It only took twenty years, several hundred murders, and a questionable business model.
Then I met Jason and Lucia. I looked at their guns. Their faces. Their problems. My disappointment is at Roman gambling level
"So this prosecutor ruined your lives?"
"Yes."
"And she is corrupt?"
"Yes."
"And you are going to kill her?"
"No, Niko. We are going to cooperate."
Apperently, two of them could not gather one pair of balls.
"Jason, my friend. When someone ruined my life, I did not give them two million dollars."
"What did you give them, Niko?"
"Usually, a funeral."
I crossed the Atlantic to escape people who treated me like a dog. These two crossed Vice City just to find a nicer leash.
I can teach someone to shoot, to survive, to escape a burning car. But I cannot teach a man to grow a pair of balls.
And that is the insult of my cameo: Rockstar brings back someone who fought against betrayal and exploitation, just to watch the new protagonists willingly accept the chains I tried to break.
Even my disappointed facial expression had more character development than Jason and Lucia combined.
I do not need every protagonist to become a kingpin. I do not need a happy ending. I certainly did not get one. But I need them to have some dignity.

The old GTA said: "The world is corrupt. Fight your way out."

GTA VI says: "The world is corrupt. Work hard, save money, follow the rules, and maybe the corrupt will let you go."

— **Niko Bellic, Liberty City**

*P.S. Jason, if you ever need help dealing with that prosecutor, give me a call. I know a very reliable gentleman named Little Jacob. He does not charge two million dollars.*

author: Neklat
quote: Grand Theft Auto, or Grand Relationship Simulator?Rating: 0/10I bought Grand Theft Auto VI expecting what made this franchise legendary: criminal freedom, chaos, dark humour, outrageous activities, unrestricted exploration and the ability to live out a criminal fantasy in an open world.Instead, I feel like I’m playing a heavily restricted relationship simulator disguised as Grand Theft **** biggest disappointment is the lack of player freedom. Jason is supposed to be a criminal, someone who steals cars, commits robberies and kills people, yet the game seems determined to restrict his personal choices and make him an accommodating partner to Lucia. The relationship mechanics are particularly frustrating. Ordinary domestic activities become mandatory, and refusing to comply can negatively affect the relationship. There are moments when you cannot even pursue another activity because Lucia demands your attention. Why give players an open world if their freedom is constantly subordinated to scripted relationship obligations?The double standards in the relationship are also disappointing. Jason feels increasingly like a supporting character in Lucia’s story rather than an independent protagonist with his own personality, boundaries and desires. A committed relationship is perfectly reasonable as a narrative choice, but forcing the player into a particular relationship dynamic is another matter **** adult content is another disappointment. Previous GTA games offered a degree of freedom in their adult interactions that helped define the franchise’s irreverent identity. Male performers appear in the game, yet I haven’t found a way to request a private dance from one while playing as Jason. The absence of meaningful choices in this area feels particularly inconsistent with the franchise’s traditional sandbox approach.Then there is the vehicle system. This is Grand Theft Auto, yet stealing a car and keeping it involves additional registration and ownership mechanics. I don’t want to pay for a car I’ve already stolen! Vehicle theft should be an organic part of the experience, not another administrative exercise.I am also concerned about the direction of Rockstar’s monetization strategy. I don’t want to see basic gameplay freedom, activities or meaningful advantages withheld from the full-price single-player experience to make a future subscription-based online mode more attractive. That would be an unacceptable approach to consumers, although I acknowledge that the future GTA Online model has not yet been established.I recognize the technical achievements, production values, graphics and attention to detail. However, technical excellence does not automatically translate into an enjoyable Grand Theft Auto experience.I didn’t buy this game to spend my time being Jason’s girlfriend’s ideal boyfriend, managing a relationship, asking permission to enjoy activities or paying to retain stolen property.I bought Grand Theft Auto because I wanted to be a criminal in an open-world **** far, that is precisely what I feel this game has forgotten.Rockstar, I wanted Grand Theft Auto. Not Grand Relationship Simulator.

author: Tamimikun
quote: When a game ships packed with bugs while simultaneously serving up effortless, overly casual gameplay, the result is a uniquely frustrating experience that fails on two fronts at once. On the technical side, broken physics, soft-locked quests, desynced hitboxes, unreliable AI, dropped inputs, and sudden crashes punish you for flaws completely outside your control. Instead of losing because you misread an enemy attack or mismanaged your resources, you lose because a script failed to trigger, a character clipped through geometry, or an autosave captured a corrupted state. On the design side, overly casual tuning removes every ounce of genuine tension, mastery, and earned satisfaction. When a title floods you with bottomless health pools, instant healing items, overly generous stun windows, magnetic aim assist, auto-block crutches, and forgiving checkpoints, combat and progression collapse into mindless button mashing. There is no real need to learn enemy telegraphs, spacing, timing, build synergy, or resource discipline when every encounter can be brute-forced with minimal attention. Worse still, many modern titles mask shallow mechanics behind bloated checklists, repetitive fetch quests, and constant waypoint hand-holding that keep players busy without ever demanding real skill.Dealing with a buggy, low-challenge game requires tightening both the difficulty curve and the technical stability of your setup so you are not stuck fighting broken code in a brain-dead loop. First, eliminate every artificial safety net built into the options menu and difficulty settings. Turn off auto-aim, aggressive lock-on assists, automated defensive prompts, and intrusive tutorial hand-holding so you actually have to read animations and react deliberately. Push the difficulty setting up immediately rather than settling for standard modes that function more like tourist tours than genuine tests of skill. Higher difficulty tiers force you to respect enemy patterns, manage stamina or cooldowns carefully, and capitalize on narrow punish windows instead of trading hits carelessly. When built-in difficulty options still leave the game far too forgiving, apply clean mechanical self-restrictions that restore real stakes without creating artificial tedium. Avoid hoarding or spamming healing items mid-encounter, skip overpowered early bonuses or broken meta exploits that trivialize core progression, and resist over-leveling past intended encounter thresholds. At the same time, cut out repetitive filler content and mindless map-clearing busywork, focusing instead on tough encounters, boss fights, and core systems where execution actually matters.Second, treat a buggy game like an unstable system that demands strict risk management. You cannot fix sloppy developer code through sheer willpower, and piling messy modifications or careless save habits onto a fragile engine only multiplies the headaches. If you use mods, script extenders, or custom launchers, keep your setup lean and organized. Add or update changes in small, testable batches rather than dumping dozens of files into your load order at once, and watch carefully for overlapping scripts, conflicting interface tweaks, or version mismatches that silently break quest flags and trigger crashes. Even in an unmodded game, never rely solely on autosaves or quick-saves, which frequently record a broken state moments before a crash or soft-lock occurs. Maintain clean, dedicated manual saves before major boss encounters, zone transitions, critical story triggers, or risky experiments so you can roll back cleanly without losing hours of progress. When strange behavior happens, isolate whether it stems from a genuine engine bug, a poorly explained mechanic, or an unintended exploit, verify your game files and patch status, and keep backups of important saves or configuration files before editing anything manually.Ultimately, a game that combines constant technical jank with zero mechanical challenge offers neither fair difficulty nor reliable polish. Tightening your settings, stripping out casual crutches, enforcing clean self-imposed rules, and keeping disciplined manual backups can salvage a rough title if there is a worthwhile core underneath. However, if the controls remain stiff, the scripts keep breaking, and the gameplay loop still feels shallow and effortless even after tuning, recognizing when to walk away saves time and frustration. Life is far too short to babysit broken software that refuses to challenge you, especially when sharper, tighter, and far more rewarding games are waiting to be played instead.
