author: InjuMarina
quote:
This is my first review here, but I had to make one for such a monumentally hyped up game like this.  I've played every GTA since the first on PC back in the nineties, and I've been a fan since. This game here is a bit of a mess. Performance issues, glitches, and the like. For how long they have worked on this game, these should have been ironed out, but they weren't. For such a big game like this, they should have combed through this game with a VERY fined toothed comb. Within the next few months or year, I'm sure they'll roll out fixes and patches and maybe the game will perform better.

As for the game itself, it's not much different than the previous games. There are some upgraded gameplay elements, but there are also less here than the previous games have had.  It's also a bit TOO realistic at points, like having to clone keys, and having to buy cars.  Sure it's more immersive but I find that it kinda takes me out of the game world and more into the real.

The characters for the most part aren't my cup of tea. Jason is pretty basic, not very offensive or inoffensive, and Lucia is annoying imo.  The relationship aspect of the gameplay just doesn't fit in a GTA game if I'm being honest. At least not in a major part of it. Maybe if it wasn't prominent I wouldn't mind it so much. The story is serviceable, but nothing too outstanding.

The environment if very nice looking and varied. It's also very large, almost too big, but not quite. The framerate dipping below 30 is jarring at times though. Sometimes it can give me a headache.

All in all, I see potential here. Just give out some fixes and patches for the performance, and maybe when the online comes out there'll be more for me to do.

After finishing the story, my verdict is that while the visuals are great, the gameplay is standard, but not bad. The characters are okay, and the story is fine.
The performance for me really hit this game hard for me though. If it wasn't for that I would rate the game a bit higher, but 4 is where it is now.  You all may have better luck than me there, and I hope you do, but it is what it is.

Maybe give it a few months and maybe I'll revisit my review. I really wanted to like this game, but the issues really took me out of it.  Come on Rockstar, fix your stuff, I want to like it like I do the older games.

author: El_Alligator
quote:
Massively overhyped and surprisingly boring.

After 13 years of waiting, I expected GTA 6 to be something special. Instead, it feels like a very pretty game that's nowhere near as fun as it should be. If good graphics at 30 FPS with vapid gameplay is your thing, you might like it.

I'll give Rockstar credit for the graphics and the amount of detail in the world, but that only goes so far. The actual gameplay gets boring surprisingly quickly. Too many missions feel like variations of the same drive somewhere, listen to dialogue, shoot some people, and drive somewhere else routine. There's a huge world to explore, but a lot of what you're doing in it just isn't that interesting.

The technical side is disappointing too. I've encountered bugs and noticeable frame dips on PS5, and being stuck at 30fps in a major 2026 release is ridiculous. The controls feel standard Rockstar game clunky, the pacing drags, and some of the realism mechanics feel more like chores than entertainment. 

Bigger and more detailed doesn't automatically mean better. It takes almost ten hours to get through the girlfriend life simulator chapter.

I'm also disappointed by the lack of a physical release at launch. After waiting this long, I should at least have the option to own a disc instead of being forced into a digital purchase.

I think a lot of people are overlooking the problems because it's GTA and because of how much hype has surrounded it. Strip away the impressive graphics and the Rockstar name, and I don't think the gameplay comes close to justifying the praise.

It's not a terrible game, but it's a pretty mediocre one underneath all that polish. Certainly not worth the wait, and nowhere near the masterpiece it's being made out to be. 4.5/10.

author: Atomsx
quote:
The open world is impressively alive, and the graphical fidelity is among the best the medium has seen. Beyond those technical achievements, the experience is significantly more limited.

Once Lucia is fully introduced, Jason’s presence and agency diminish sharply. The narrative and mission structure increasingly revolve around her, leaving him with little independent substance or compelling characterization. He comes across as passive and accommodating rather than a fully realized lead, ranking among the weakest protagonists in the series.

Despite thirteen years of development and a reported budget of two billion dollars, a substantial portion of the gameplay consists of domestic and relationship-oriented tasks home maintenance, errands, and interpersonal maintenance that feel closer to a life simulator than traditional Grand Theft Auto. Sequences spent watching television or managing everyday relationship dynamics undermine the sense of escapism the franchise has long provided.

The story itself is notably brief and underdeveloped. It offers limited escalation or meaningful character arcs and concludes after a relatively short playtime of roughly two days, with an ending that feels abrupt and unsatisfying. Players waiting for the series’ characteristic large-scale criminal set pieces and chaotic freedom will find them scarce.

Perhaps most striking is the near total absence of the sharp, irreverent satire and dark humor that defined earlier entries. The tone is restrained and polished to a degree that feels sanitized, stripping the experience of much of the edge that once distinguished the series. 

In the end, GTA 6 delivers a technically impressive but narratively thin and tonally cautious game. What remains is an open-world relationship drama with occasional criminal elements, rather than the bold, satirical crime epic many expected after such a long wait…

author: glads18
quote:
GTA VI. A Technical Masterpiece That Has Lost the Identity of Grand Theft Auto?
After all these years of waiting, this is what we’ve been anticipating?I’m genuinely disappointed with the direction of GTA VI. For a franchise that practically redefined open-world gaming, something about this instalment feels fundamentally different from its predecessors and not necessarily in a good way. My biggest criticism isn’t the graphics, the map or the technical achievements. Those are impressive. It’s the identity of the game **** III, Vice City, San Andreas, GTA IV and GTA V each had their own personality. They had memorable characters, distinctive storytelling, brilliant satire, dark humour and an atmosphere that made their worlds feel alive. They weren’t simply games with enormous maps; they were experiences with character and substance . GTA VI, however, leaves me questioning whether Rockstar still understands what made Grand Theft Auto so special in the first place. And I don’t think we can completely ignore the departure of some of Rockstar’s most influential creative minds. Dan Houser was one of the principal creative forces behind the franchise’s storytelling. Lazlow Jones helped establish its unmistakable satirical identity, particularly through its radio stations, dialogue and cultural commentary. These people understood the DNA of GTA. Their departure doesn’t automatically mean Rockstar has lost its ability to create great games, but it certainly raises questions about the creative direction of the studio. A bigger map doesn’t automatically mean a better game. More realistic animations don’t make better characters. More detailed environments don’t compensate for storytelling that fails to leave an impression.What happened to the unapologetic Rockstar humour? The outrageous social commentary? The brilliantly written characters? The unpredictable storytelling that made previous GTA titles so memorable?I don’t want GTA to become another generic cinematic open-world experience that happens to have the Grand Theft Auto name attached to it.I want its original attitude, its rebellious personality and its distinctive storytelling **** frustrating part is that Rockstar has already demonstrated what it is capable of. GTA IV delivered an incredibly memorable narrative. GTA V gave us three unforgettable protagonists. Red Dead Redemption 2 demonstrated that Rockstar could still produce exceptional storytelling. So why does this instalment leave me questioning the direction of the franchise?Rockstar spent over a decade building anticipation. The expectations were astronomical, and perhaps that is precisely the problem. The company has become so confident in its reputation that the GTA name itself seems to carry more weight than the experience being delivered. A technical achievement is not automatically a creative masterpiece. GTA VI might be an impressive game, but impressive and unforgettable are two very different things. And for a franchise that once set the standard for everyone else, simply being impressive should never have been enough. 
I didn’t wait 13 years just to see a prettier Vice City. I waited for another Grand Theft Auto.

author: Akgames

Thirteen years in development it’s more of the same old stuff we’ve seen throughout the GTA series. Sure, there are graphical improvements suited to the current era and some refined mechanics, but the core gameplay loop remains identical (weapons, corruption, drugs, robberies, scams, etc.). Now, you can also go shopping, cook, clean, paint, and so on extra content to keep you occupied, but nothing that adds any real substance. The physics feel familiar; it’s as if they threw *Red Dead Redemption 2* and *GTA V* into a blender, tossed in some graphical and mechanical mods, and called it a day. Despite all this and all the hype I’m deeply disappointed by the sheer number of bugs and issues present at launch. Was it rushed? I mean, thirteen years and a massive budget and they release a GTA game riddled with bugs? As I said, there’s nothing truly new here; it feels like little more than a graphical remake with a few minor additions. Honestly, I expected more from Rockstar Games.

I’ve played GTA V with texture mods and lighting enhancements, and it’s not that far off from GTA VI... so I have to ask: 13 years for what? Where did all that money go? And why are there so many bugs?

author: AmonStrix
quote: GTA VI: Beautiful Graphics, But Where Did the Freedom Go? Let’s be completely honest: GTA VI feels like the same old formula—another GTA with a different story, but nothing groundbreaking. After all the hype, several issues are hard to ignore. Missing classic features: No prostitutes? Something that has existed in GTA for decades is suddenly gone. Why remove features that were part of the franchise’s identity? Forced “woke” elements: The game feels increasingly focused on pushing certain messages instead of simply letting players enjoy themselves. It’s exhausting.Where did the freedom go? This is my biggest complaint. You can’t even attack or kill every NPC anymore. Some characters appear to be protected, including certain gay characters and women, while others aren’t. Why the double standards? I don’t care about an NPC’s gender or sexual orientation. The same gameplay rules should apply to **** was always about freedom, chaos, and doing whatever you wanted in a fictional world. That was the entire point! Now we’re getting restrictions on who we can attack and what we can do. What’s the point of a massive open world if the game constantly limits your choices? Apparently, we can smoke cigarettes, sit on benches, and enjoy countless realistic animations, but we can’t experience the unrestricted sandbox gameplay that made GTA **** I’m tired of being Lucia’s lapdog. Seriously, I’m sick of feeling like Jason is constantly playing the submissive boyfriend, following Lucia around and doing whatever she wants. If I wanted that kind of relationship dynamic, I could experience it in real life. I didn’t spend $90 on GTA to play a boyfriend simulator. I want crime, chaos, action, and freedom—not a relationship where I’m constantly taking orders.30 FPS in 2026 is unacceptable: I don’t care how gorgeous the graphics are. Being locked to 30 FPS on PS5 Pro is ridiculous. Not even a 60 FPS performance mode? Worse, I’ve experienced drops to 15–18 FPS in certain areas. How is that acceptable in a $90 AAA game?Clunky physics and missing details: Character movement and physics feel poorly tuned. Even basic immersion details, like animations for putting on or removing a helmet, are missing.Realism is hurting the experience: Visually, GTA VI is absolutely stunning. But Rockstar seems so obsessed with realism that it sometimes forgets what makes a game enjoyable. More animations, more environmental details, more activities—but less freedom where it actually matters.I played it on my PS5 Pro and eventually dropped it. Playing at 30 FPS on an 80-inch 240Hz TV looks terrible. Maybe it feels acceptable on older displays, but on modern high-end hardware, it’s disappointing.Hopefully, the eventual PC version will finally let us enjoy 60 FPS or even 150 FPS with an RTX 5090 and DLSS 5, assuming the technology and optimization allow it. And hopefully, the physics improve **** performance isn’t even my biggest disappointment. It’s the loss of GTA’s identity.I don’t need a beautiful open world where I can sit on a bench, smoke cigarettes, and admire realistic scenery while the game constantly tells me what I can and cannot do.I don’t want to be Lucia’s personal lapdog, either. I WANT GRAND THEFT AUTO. I WANT CHAOS. I WANT FUN. I WANT FREEDOM. It’s a video game, not real life. It’s supposed to let us escape real-world restrictions and enjoy a fictional sandbox without unnecessary limitations. Rockstar gave us a bigger, prettier world, but somehow made it feel smaller by taking away the freedom that made GTA legendary. And that’s the biggest disappointment of all.

author: thx2208
quote: 30 FPS dating simulator wrapped in a buggy launch.Despite the 99 critic score, actually playing GTA 6 on PS5 is a massive letdown. Locking a 2026 flagship game to 30 FPS—with zero 60 FPS performance mode even on the PS5 Pro—is bad enough, but on a base PS5, high-speed driving and big shootouts regularly tank the frame rate into the mid-20s. Add in launch-day physics glitches (cars flying into the sky, falling through the map) and constant CE-108255-1 crashes wiping unsaved progress, and the technical state is **** pacing is even worse. The opening hours are an agonizing, hand-holding crawl full of slow exposition and endless tutorials before the game finally lets you play freely.Most disappointing is how soft and sanitized the gameplay feels compared to past GTA games. Rockstar leaned so hard into hyper-realism and Jason and Lucia’s romance that it feels like a glorified dating and life simulator. Instead of chaotic mayhem, you’re building coffee tables, keeping your car clean and refueled for dates, showering, and eating.Everything else is bogged down by tedious friction: rigid on-rails missions that fail you for stepping off the scripted path, no mission replays or medals, sluggish controls with a clunky inventory replacing the weapon wheel, and $80+ gets you a 210 GB install missing GTA Online, buyable properties, and locked-off landmarks like the zoo and casinos. All style, no classic GTA soul.

author: twistingtornado
quote:
GTA VI tries to change the rules of GTA, and in the process, stops being GTA. The storyline is a hackneyed Bonnie and Clyde romance with forgettable characters. For this storyline, hookers were cut from the game. The first thing I ever heard about GTA when I was a kid was "you can run over hookers!" That's been replaced with "you can buy your girlfriend flowers!" Yeah, none of the kids are saying that.

But even worse, R* invented a social credit score to punish players for killing civilians and cops without abandon during the storyline. If either Lucia or Jason fall into the psycho categorization (or stay psycho too long and become irredeemable), cops will no longer try to arrest and always try to kill no matter the wanted rating. You also end up with the bad ending. The bad ending results in both MCs dying like Bonnie and Clyde. Real original. And the six star level rating is inescapable, further punishing players for being too violent. Cops also don't automatically forget you and still search for you after evading them.

While it was nice to see Niko again, seeing him was a reminder of the stark contrast between older GTA titles and GTA VI. GTA was a crime drama sandbox. GTA VI is a romance thriller whose storyline is more important than giving the player freedom in an open sandbox. It's a fundamental shift. Gone are the jokes of Niko shooting up a Cluckin' Bell and griping about being trapped in a cycle of crime and violence in story mode. Gone are the days of feeling invincible after escaping a maximum-star wanted rating.

No more ruthless Tommy, man of the people CJ, tragic Niko, or psycho Trevor. Welcome to reserved Jason and girlboss Lucia. Welcome to not being allowed to steal your neighbor's car. Welcome to not being to shoot up a club. Welcome to gameplay mechanics that convinces users that shooting limbs is not lethal. Welcome to a game where going psycho and massacring a town gets met with consequences. 

This game is an insult to players who played GTA when R* nearly went bankrupt due to the hot coffee mod. GTA VI made one unforgivable mistake to earn 0 points. You can pick the game. But you can't change the rules.

author: mumuyouming
quote:
Title: 99 on Metacritic? A Masterpiece of Technology, Not Game Design.
As only the second game in history to receive a 99 on Metacritic, GTA VI is supposed to represent the absolute pinnacle of gaming. Yet beyond its stunning visuals and industry-leading production values, I struggle to find a single groundbreaking design decision that actually justifies such an extraordinary score.What's even more disappointing is that, in some respects, the level of detail doesn't even match Red Dead Redemption 2, a game Rockstar released years ago. It genuinely makes me wonder what Rockstar has been doing all this time.Instead of delivering meaningful gameplay innovation, GTA VI often feels like an endless sequence of meticulously scripted events and predetermined cinematic moments. Everything looks spectacular, but how much of it actually translates into a better gaming experience?And don't even get me started on the new wanted ****'s genuinely infuriating. Committing a crime has become so tedious and time-consuming that simply obeying the law feels like the more rewarding option. Want to steal a car? Great. Now you have to change your clothes, swap your face covering, repaint your vehicle, and spend ages shaking off the **** that just to steal a damn car in a game called Grand Theft **** what point did Rockstar forget that this is supposed to be a video game?Realism should serve gameplay, not the other way around. When the pursuit of realism starts actively undermining player freedom, pacing, and enjoyment, you've completely missed the point.Games should be judged by how well they play, not by how convincingly they imitate **** breathtaking graphics and extreme realism are all it takes to earn a near-perfect score, then everyone's real life deserves a 100 on **** VI is undoubtedly a technical achievement. But technical excellence does not automatically equal great game design, and an astronomical budget does not make a game **** the end of the day, GTA VI is an overproduced, overhyped, and fundamentally disappointing game that has been praised into the stratosphere by a gaming media seemingly more impressed by technological spectacle than actual gameplay.99/100? What a joke.

author: zhuizi
quote: Over a decade of waiting, and somehow Rockstar still hasn't figured out how to make a character walk through a doorway without feeling like a drunk ****'t get me wrong—Leonida looks incredible. The lighting, the water physics, the sheer density of Vice City at night are genuinely impressive. For the first five hours, just driving around feels like a generational leap. Then you actually have to play the game, and the illusion falls apart **** mission design is stuck in 2013. You have this massive, reactive open world, yet the moment you start a story mission, the game puts you on invisible rails. Step ten feet outside the yellow zone or try to flank an enemy from a slightly different angle, and you get hit with an instant "Mission Failed" screen. There is zero room for **** gunplay is equally frustrating. Without heavy auto-aim, shooting feels stiff and unresponsive, and the cover system constantly snaps you to the wrong wall. Combine that with relentless frame drops in downtown areas—even on high-end hardware—and combat becomes a chore.Worst of all, you can feel the shadow of GTA Online hanging over the entire single-player experience. The in-game economy is artificially grindy, basic customization options are bizarrely limited, and it's obvious that the best content is being held back to sell Shark Cards ****'s a technical showcase wrapped around outdated, rigid gameplay. Wait for a steep sale and a year of patches.

author: Paco_el_Frutero
quote:
Este título es lo que obtendrías de despellejar GTA y usar las mecánicas de RED DEAD 2 para la historia.

En el caso de los protagonistas no se siente un equilibrio de relevancia al igual que no se ve un sentido a algunas de las acciones de los personajes. Jason es un personaje que cuando has jugado te da la idea de que la intención del estudio frente al personaje era más ejemplificar un estereotipo mediante un diálogo flojo y una tolerancia excesiva al igual que presenta un guión que lo hace parecer poco favorecido en el desarrollo cognitivo. Lucia es otro caso en el que se ha utilizado su procedencia para realizar lo que parece un personaje de padre de familia pero que Peter fuera mujer, presentará inteligencia promedio-baja en algunas situaciones y que fuera latina porque Lucia trata a Jason de una forma un poco denigrante en algunos casos y parece que el estudio ha usado un muy mal ejemplo como formato de pareja. Jason se comporta de forma muy sumisa y pasiva, mientras que Lucia es muy tóxica y se queja a cada cosa que Jason hace, mostrándose como una pareja muy molesta y nada saludable dado que Jason cede en todo. En el caso de la historia, es muy buena la idea del guión pero su ejecución y adaptación para unir los capítulos es desastrosa. La sensación que proporciona es de estancarse en una tediosa marcha o espera para realizar un avance en la misma y no es por dificultad dado a que es muy sencillo en general. Esta sensación se debe a la mala continuación de las misiones y la carencia de ese caos y seriedad al que nos habían acostumbrado todas las anteriores entregas.

En el apartado visual es increíble pero en general y para especificar, este título se nota que no se ha hecho en una colaboración correcta por parte de los que están en el equipo y una mala gestión general tanto en decisiones como en historia. A más añadir, la falta mayoritaria de un lenguaje peyorativo además de un control sobre las acciones del jugador, hace que el juego se sienta manchado por una agenda o ideal que no es lo que esta saga representa. Hay más cosas de las que me quejaría como la sensación de que el juego se siente como un tutorial para el online o que el juego te fuerce a cosas que no son necesarias en un título de este tipo como las tareas o la de repostar y en general para poder arreglar este juego tendrán que retirarlo del mercado y rehacerlo casi en su totalidad para que se pudiera llamar de verdad GTA. Sé que me faltan cosas pero si sigo escribiendo **** mucho.

Entiendo que el creador original no participe pero el relevo deja demasiado que desear y me hace recomendar que los jugadores gasten su dinero en otros títulos o cuando la oferta de este sea de 60% para arriba.

author: HeritageBA
quote:
Where do I start? It feels like we can't use media for escapism anymore, as developers seem more focused on pushing political agendas than just entertaining us. I'll break my review down by Story, Gameplay, and Graphics on a 1-5 scale.

STORY:
The game centers on the relationship between Jason and Lucia—think Bonnie and Clyde—with the story prioritizing their romance above all else.
3/5

GAMEPLAY:
It's pretty much copy-paste from previous GTA titles with minor tweaks. Because so much emphasis was placed on the characters' relationship, other areas suffered; there are no major improvements to the controls, and the shooting mechanics feel like a watered-down version of Red Dead Redemption 2. After a few hours, you realize it just isn't fun. The side content feels like a chore, and the supposedly dynamic NPCs are an overstatement—they mostly just overreact in unnatural ways. It's hard to believe this took 13 years to make.
2/5

GRAPHICS:
This is where the game shines, as expected from Rockstar. The world is massive and the detail is amazing, though there are still some glitches. The biggest issue is that they missed the chance to make something as fun to play as it is to look at. The "girl boss" narrative felt forced, and you can write strong female characters without putting down the male ones. The relationship arc also felt unnecessary; they should have given players more choice. It feels like Rockstar is banking on their reputation to push a feminist agenda. I won't be fooled again; your next game will have to really earn my money.

author: ritesh_gg
quote:
A Technical Masterpiece, but a Disappointing GTA Game.

I'm currently 26 hours into my playthrough, and I have very mixed feelings about this game.

From a technical standpoint, GTA 6 might genuinely be the most visually impressive, detailed, and ambitious open world game ever created. The world is breathtaking, and some of the missions and activities are incredibly fun.

But here's the problem... As impressive as it is technically, it's an incredibly disappointing GTA game. Perhaps even the worst in the franchise.

I've been playing GTA since GTA 2, and every subsequent installment has been a masterpiece in its own way. Rockstar consistently pushed boundaries, not just in graphics and storytelling, but in player freedom, creativity, and the sheer joy of exploring a sandbox world.

Unfortunately, GTA 6 feels like it has forgotten much of what made this franchise so special.

So many little freedoms and interactions that were possible in previous GTA games have either been removed or unnecessarily restricted. Instead, Rockstar has introduced an overwhelming number of tedious, time consuming mechanics that contribute very little to the actual gameplay experience. Rather than making the game more immersive or enjoyable, many of these systems feel like unnecessary obstacles that waste the player's time.

The characters are another disappointment. They lack the personality, charm, and memorability that made previous GTA protagonists so iconic. Lucia is genuinely interesting and shows some depth, but Jason might be the blandest and most forgettable protagonist Rockstar has ever written for a GTA game.

I could go on about the countless little details, activities, and freedoms that previous GTA games offered but are missing or restricted here. There are simply too many to list in a single review. And that's what makes this so frustrating. GTA has always been about freedom, experimentation, and having fun in an openworld sandbox. GTA6 may have created one of the most detailed worlds in gaming history, but somehow, it feels less liberating to actually play in.

A bigger, prettier, and more detailed world doesn't automatically make a better game.

What disappoints me the most is that Rockstar had an extraordinary track record. For decades, they consistently delivered unforgettable experiences and raised the bar for the entire gaming industry. I genuinely never imagined I'd see the day when I would consider a mainline GTA game disappointing.

It feels like even GTA has fallen victim to some of the worst trends in modern game design, prioritizing unnecessary complexity and restrictions over the simple freedom and fun that defined the franchise.

As someone who has loved this series for more than two decades, that genuinely breaks my heart.

GTA 6 is an extraordinary technical achievement, but to me, it has lost much of the soul that made Grand Theft Auto special.

author: pngkbo
quote: I was genuinely so excited for this game to release. And when I say excited, I mean I went out and bought a brand new gaming TV and a PS5, even after the price increases, just so I could experience this game the way I had imagined for years. I had my doubts about the direction Rockstar was taking with this game, but I pushed them aside because I wanted so badly to love it. I even found myself feeling reassured by articles, statements from Rockstar representatives, and comments from developers who made it seem like we were getting something incredible. But ultimately, that’s all it was. A dream that was sold to us. We were led to believe that the romance aspect of the game would be optional. It isn’t. Instead, the game does an almost impressive job of forcing a particular experience onto the player, regardless of how they actually want to play. I’ve never experienced this level of restriction in a GTA game before, and frankly, it’s frustrating. What’s even more irritating is how Rockstar seemed to tiptoe around these details leading up to release rather than being transparent about them. The removal of prostitutes is another example of something that should have been communicated before launch. As a woman, do I personally have some desperate need to interact with prostitutes in a video game? Absolutely not. But I would’ve appreciated having the option. And that’s really the point. My frustration isn’t necessarily about any one missing feature. It’s about the growing list of restrictions being placed on a franchise that was once defined by its freedom, unpredictability, and ability to let players create their own experiences. I wanted to love this game more than anything. I genuinely did. But instead, I found myself bored throughout much of the gameplay with both protagonists, something I’ve NEVER experienced with another GTA title. And that’s probably the most disappointing part of all. Visually, the game is gorgeous. I’ll give Rockstar every bit of credit for that. But beautiful graphics cannot compensate for lackluster writing, restrictive gameplay, and creative decisions that seem to prioritize a specific vision over the freedom that made this franchise so beloved in the first place. As someone who’s been playing GTA since I was eight years old, it genuinely hurts to write this. This franchise has been a part of my life for well over a decade, and I never imagined I’d feel this disconnected from a game I spent so many years anticipating. Rockstar, do better. Remember what made Grand Theft Auto Grand Theft Auto. Stop trying so hard to push agendas or appeal to everyone that you lose sight of the identity you’ve spent decades building. There’s nothing wrong with evolving as a franchise, but evolution shouldn’t come at the expense of the very things that made people fall in love with it. When you stay true to what makes your games special, the players will follow. And after waiting all these years, it’s incredibly disappointing that my biggest hope now is that Rockstar finds its way back to what made this franchise great, hopefully before another 13 years pass.

author: KaeporaGaebora
quote:
10 hours in.  Biggest problems.  Can't change primary car.  Majorly inconvenient to steal other cars in a game called grand theft auto.

The issue is that not much choice is given to the player.  The girlfriend, the car, the lack of capabilities and power the character has.  And the choices you do have, like stealing other cars; sometimes isn't worth the hassle.

Feels like you are controlling a character that is very limited and as such it's just not fun.

The character, car, etc is so unresponsive, weighty, and slow it feels like a chore to do almost anything in the game.

Some examples.  

I washed up on shore was thinking about stealing a car to drive half a mile to my destination, decided to just jog there knowing the inconvenience that stealing a random car would have.  Feels like the player is too kneecapped in the game.

Some gang members started shooting at me for no reason.  I had to defend myself.  The police came immediately to start kicking my ass, but every interaction in this game seems like the police and criminals are working together against me.  It's just not realistic for a game that's trying to be more realistic than before.  If someone else attacks me its all good, if i do anything police show up in 10 seconds to murk me.

Stole a woman's car at a grocery shop, within 10 seconds, she had called the police, the police responded, were in pursuit and tracking the car.  In 10 seconds, if it was realistic either the police wouldn't have showed up at all or would have responded in 20 to 30 minutes.  

What I'm getting at is, the game is trying to be more realistic than before but it's realistic in ways that hurt the players experience and unrealistic in ways that hurt the player experience even more.

As someone who played GTA 5 for half a thousand hours, this game is just slow, boring, devoid of GTA character, tedious, doesn't give the player agency, control, power, or choice.   I'm all for a game making things more challenging or difficult but in return it has to be fun.

The best part of the game for me so far was playing the game within the game, Street Trash III: Dezombifier.  That was actually fun, maybe they should have just made that game instead?

Update:
I logged back in.  I step a couple cm onto some NPCs property and there is a warning the cops might be called soon.  The NPC's call me all kinds of names, very profane.  And i do nothing because the risk of having the cops called is not challenging but annoying to deal with.  In an old GTA I would have run up and slapped the NPCs with a **** until they were unconscious. author: bwolf29834
quote:
The graphics are the only reason anyone is still defending this game. And sure, they're good. Vice City has never looked this alive, and the details are real: hair that actually moves, water, light on wet asphalt at night, a world dense enough to get lost in. Rockstar spent the entire budget on making it pretty, and you can tell. But all of that sits on top of a 30fps ceiling with frame pacing bad enough to stutter you right out of the scene. They spent everything on the paint and then shipped it with the engine in first gear. For a game being sold as the next generational leap, it keeps feeling like it's catching up to a 2020 release.

Strip the visuals away and there's not much story doing the work. The two leads read more like delivery systems for the game's agenda than like people, and the "twists" are telegraphed so far in advance they land as reminders, not surprises. It's a game that clearly has a point it wants to make, and it built the narrative around that point instead of the other way around. All the money went into making it beautiful, and almost none of it went into making it worth your time.

I own a PS5, so the console window isn't the problem, and I'm not pretending it is. The problem is I know this game will run better on my own PC, and I can't play it there, so I'm stuck at early 2000s frame rates on the one machine that actually can do the job. For those that don't already have a PS5, though? Memory scarcity means the PS5 Pro is now a nine hundred dollar console, so the price of adoption to play this game ahead of a PC release is nearly a grand. I'm half expecting that guy from Blizzard to pop out with a "You guys don't have PS5s?" quip. A launch window is normal. One built on the assumption that everyone's ready to drop nine hundred on hardware is a bet, and it's a bet Rockstar is making against the people who already bought into the hype. Hype that unfortunately amounts to little more than a pretty slideshow, and a story that left me wondering if we should have waited just a few more years for GTA 6 after all.

author: Refdangke
quote:
The Good: 

Ragdoll Physics: The physics are fantastic. The way NPCs react to being damaged in different body parts is incredible.

Driving Mechanics: Driving is a massive improvement, striking the right balance by avoiding both the overly arcade feel of GTA V and the exaggerated weight of GTA IV.

Graphics: Visually, the game is stunning. The skin, hair, and overall character models couldn't look better.

The Bad (Making this game mediocre at best...)

For a game so eagerly anticipated and in development for over eight years (as far as we know), it launched in a deplorable state. The game is plagued by bugs of all kinds, crashes that threaten your progress, aggressive frame rate drops plummeting to 10 FPS, and visual glitches, most notably on Sony's console, where everything looks blurrier than it should or displays a white outline when aiming at nearby objects.

The game's performance is abysmal. Frame rate drops during cutscenes, as well as aggressive stuttering while driving or during gunfights, are just the tip of the iceberg. Everything else might have been forgivable (setting aside the years of development and wasted budget), but the constant, unpredictable crashes are unacceptable, especially for a AAA title that doesn't even feature an auto-save option. The frame rate situation is particularly bizarre, as it feels like we've stepped back more than 10 years to an era where a game's physics engine was tied to the maximum FPS. Anyone who claims this game couldn't run at a fairly stable 60 FPS on a base PS5 with proper optimization either knows nothing about video games or is completely blinded by Rockstar fanboyism.

One of the most frustrating aspects, and arguably the most damaging to the core experience is the severe restriction placed on the freedom that defines this franchise. Adding a morality or karma system to a GTA game is simply incomprehensible. Stealing cars, running people over, shooting, and causing chaos is what makes these games fun. Instead, the game punishes you with a permanent, irrevocable system based on how many crimes you commit, which arbitrarily affects your ending. Which leaves me wondering:

Whose bright idea was it to limit and punish crime in a franchise literally built around it? 

GTA is not just a driving or narrative simulator; it is a crime sandbox where power fantasy matters. Yet, the game restricts you at every turn.

Want to steal a car? You can't, unless you unlock that mechanic later in the game.

Want to go on a rampage? The game tanks your morality meter and permanently alters your ending.

Want to customize a freshly stolen car? You have to grind for hours in the story before that's even an option.

But now, the narrative issues are quite straightforward.

Jason lacks personality, clear aspirations, or personal goals outside of his relationship with Lucia, making him feel like a last-minute addition to a game originally designed around a single female protagonist. He lives purely to please others while receiving little to no appreciation. This is evident in their dynamic, where the game constantly pushes you to support and adore Lucia, while she drags him into constant danger and never offers a single genuinely "supportive" gesture in return to the person she supposedly loves.

Lucia is an extremely impulsive character, and most of her actions feel driven as a proxy for the writers' female power fantasy. Throughout most of the story, Lucia lacks moments that make you empathize with her, especially since she never faces tangible, personal consequences resulting from her persistent recklessness and lack of awareness.

Furthermore, it's striking how the story fails to portray Jason and Lucia's relationship as reciprocal. In a game that mechanically removed features like prostitutes or optional partners from previous entries, their dynamic feels like a toxic, one-sided relationship where a criminal tries to redeem his past mistakes for the mother of his child, while she constantly puts both their lives at risk and shows zero initiative to return his affection. (This is especially glaring when the game never lets you, as Lucia, do optional missions solely for Jason's benefit).

In short, GTA 6 is an enjoyable game, provided your industry standards are set by Call of Duty and FIFA. But any fan of the franchise can easily see this wasn't made by the same people who crafted previous entries. The game is the digital equivalent of a Skinwalker wearing your pet's skin: it feels familiar at times, but jarring quirks constantly pull you out of the immersion, reminding you why so many veteran developers and key executives ultimately left the company.

author: kinruiz
quote: GTA VI is a technically impressive game, but it's also one of the most overrated releases in recent memory. Critics treat it as a revolutionary masterpiece, yet the core formula remains largely unchanged from what Rockstar has been doing for over two decades: drive here, shoot there, watch a cutscene, repeat. The map is bigger, the graphics are better, and the level of detail is absurdly high, but technical advancement should not be confused with innovation.Many of the features being praised as groundbreaking are simply refinements of systems that already existed in other games years ago. Better AI, more interactive environments, and deeper character relationships add immersion, but they do not redefine the medium.What's even harder to ignore is the double standard. Some franchises are criticized for not reinventing themselves with every entry, while GTA receives universal praise for polishing essentially the same design philosophy. Add the bugs, visual glitches, and technical issues that somehow get overlooked in reviews, and the near-perfect scores become even more **** VI is a good game. It is not a revolution. author: tinyviolin
quote:
$2 Billion Later, and This Is What We Get?

The game itself is OKAY. Not terrible, not amazing, just okay. And that's honestly the most disappointing part. After years of hype, an astronomical budget, and Rockstar marketing this as the next generation of open-world gaming, I expected something revolutionary. Instead, we got what feels like an unfinished, poorly optimized, politically driven work of art that needed another year or two in development.

Let's start with the biggest issue, which makes up about 60% of my frustration: **30 FPS. ARE YOU SERIOUS?** We're in 2026, and somehow one of the most expensive video games ever developed is still targeting 30 FPS on consoles? It's sickening. Smooth performance should be a priority, not something we have to sacrifice for graphical fidelity. I don't care how beautiful your world looks if the experience feels sluggish. We've spent years upgrading hardware, buying expensive consoles, and being promised next-generation experiences, only to end up right back at 30 FPS. Where is the optimization?

And then there's **NO PC RELEASE AT LAUNCH.** Absolutely ridiculous. Rockstar knows exactly what it's doing. Release the game on consoles, collect billions, then release an improved PC version later so people buy it all over again. It's a brilliant business strategy, but as a consumer, it feels like a massive marketing scheme and cash grab.

The gameplay itself is a mixed bag. The core foundation is genuinely good, and that's what makes this so frustrating. There's clearly an incredible game buried underneath everything. But some of the systems feel cheesy, unfinished, and surprisingly outdated. Certain interaction prompts and pop-up buttons look like something pulled straight out of an alpha build. They lack polish, immersion, and the level of detail I'd expect from Rockstar. These might sound like minor complaints, but when you're selling the most anticipated game of the decade, those details matter.

The writing and presentation also feel unnecessarily focused on social and political messaging at times. I don't mind commentary or satire. GTA has always been built around that. But there's a difference between clever satire that naturally fits the world and messaging that feels forced. I want Rockstar's signature storytelling, not something that feels like it's constantly trying to make a statement.

And that's what bothers me most. **The potential is absolutely there.** The world, the atmosphere, and the core gameplay show flashes of brilliance. But potential doesn't justify releasing a product that feels unfinished.

This reminds me way too much of Cyberpunk 2077. A massively hyped game with incredible ambition that needed years of updates before it fully delivered on its promises. I genuinely wouldn't be surprised if GTA 6 takes another two years of patches, optimization, and improvements before it becomes the experience we were originally sold.

**TWO BILLION DOLLARS.** Let that sink in. An alleged $2 billion budget, years of development, and an industry-leading studio with practically unlimited resources. And somehow we're still talking about 30 FPS, questionable optimization, unfinished-feeling systems, and missing PC support.

Rockstar didn't need to reinvent gaming to impress me. They needed to deliver a polished, complete experience worthy of the hype they created.

Instead, it feels like we paid full price for the privilege of waiting for the finished product.

**The foundation is great. The execution is disappointing. The marketing was phenomenal. And the consumers got played.**

**Final rating: 3/10.** There's a potentially incredible game here, but I'm reviewing what was delivered, not what it might become two years from now.

author: fairamano
quote:
I don't usually review games, but this game was bad enough to put in the effort to write one.

Yes, the game is incredible in terms of graphics. However, that's all it has going for it. I won't delve too much into the campaign for two reasons: first, it's a generic GTA campaign. You'll either love it or hate it, and I was in the camp that simply didn't care for it. Second, as many GTA players have said, they're more interested in the gameplay and multiplayer. Although the multiplayer hasn't come out yet, it's safe to assume it'll be terrible unless they give the game a massive overhaul.

**Gameplay Issues:**

1. **The controls** are as wonky as ever.
2. **Stealing cars** requires considerably more effort than it should (...in a GTA game, I know).
3. **Tedious weapon selection.** Carrying weapons is now penalized depending on their size and visibility. More often than not, you're better off leaving your weapons in your car's trunk.

**Miscellaneous Annoying Content:**

- **Relationship mechanic:** Lucia is a mandatory romance in the game. If you ignore her, you'll be soft-locked from progressing through the campaign until your relationship is healthy again.
- **Minigames:** Grocery shopping, woodworking, etc.
- **Crime limitations:** Crime can no longer be committed freely. Certain zones restrict criminal activities, including stealing cars.
- **Polish:** The game is incredibly buggy. It's hard to believe it was in development for 13 years. 

Maybe these criticisms would be void in a different context. Maybe if this game wasn't advertised as GTA, and instead as a dating sim, it would be a lot better, perhaps even immersive. But the game is supposed to be a sandbox that gives players the freedom to do wacky (often violent) things in its open world.

                                                 **This is not that.**

This is simply a high-budget Sims game. If you like that, you'll love this game. If not, spend your money somewhere else.

**Summary:** Rockstar was so preoccupied with whether they could do something that they never stopped to ask whether they should. Realism was prioritized at the expense of fun.

**P.S.** Don't support games that are anti-consumer. I heavily regret spending money on a company that sees us as nothing more than a quick buck.

author: skyzenn_00
quote: This is incredibly disappointing for a game that has been hyped for so many years.Rockstar seems to have forgotten what made GTA great in the first place. GTA is supposed to be a crime sandbox where players have freedom to experiment, cause chaos, break rules and have fun. Instead, so much of the experience feels restricted, scripted and unnecessarily controlled. What's the point of creating such a massive open world if the game constantly limits what you can actually do in it?The writing is another disappointment. The characters lack the depth, charisma and memorable personalities that made previous GTA protagonists so iconic. The dialogue and character interactions often feel forced, and the story seems more interested in pushing its preferred messaging than delivering genuinely compelling **** increasingly obvious DEI and woke-oriented approach also feels distracting when it comes at the expense of natural storytelling. Representation itself isn't the problem. Poorly written characters and forced messaging are. A character should be interesting because of their personality, motivations and development, not because of what demographic box they **** gunplay is another major letdown. Combat should feel satisfying and responsive, but the shooting mechanics feel unnecessarily clunky. For a game with this much emphasis on crime and action, that's a fundamental problem.Then there's the performance. The optimization is disappointing, the frame-rate limitations are frustrating, and the technical experience doesn't feel worthy of a release carrying this much anticipation.Ultimately, GTA 6 feels like a game that prioritized cinematic presentation, realism and social messaging over the things that actually make a sandbox enjoyable: freedom, gameplay, memorable characters and fun.Rockstar spent years building expectations, but beautiful graphics and an enormous map cannot compensate for weak gameplay decisions.A technical showcase is not the same thing as a great video game.

Grand Theft Auto VI - Disappointing After 13 Years

author: Patata0015
quote: Mi crítica negativa de GTA 6: decisiones que arruinaron parte de la experienciaAunque GTA 6 tiene muchas cosas que ofrecer, hay varias decisiones que, desde mi punto de vista, dejaron mucho que desear y terminaron afectando mi experiencia con el juego.1. La eliminación de las prostitutas de las callesUna de las cosas que no me gustó fue la eliminación de las prostitutas que tradicionalmente han formado parte del mundo de GTA. En mi opinión, debieron conservarlas e incluso ampliar las posibilidades de interacción con ellas. Por ejemplo, permitir contratarlas o incluso asaltarlas. También habría sido interesante que estas acciones tuvieran consecuencias dentro de la relación con Lucía, especialmente si descubriese que Jason le está siendo infiel. Eso habría añadido más profundidad, consecuencias y realismo a las decisiones del jugador.2. Perder los objetos de la edición UltimateOtro punto que considero inaceptable es comprar una edición Ultimate para disfrutar de determinados objetos y recompensas durante toda la historia, y que después te los quiten sin posibilidad de recuperarlos. Si estoy pagando más dinero por una edición especial, espero poder disfrutar de todo su contenido durante la experiencia completa. No tiene sentido pagar por objetos exclusivos para terminar perdiéndolos. Desde mi perspectiva, es una decisión que se siente como una estafa para quienes compraron esa edición.3. Los finales y el sistema de honorLos finales de la historia me dejaron un mal sabor de boca. Personalmente, creo que GTA 6 debería tener un único final bien construido, en lugar de permitir que el sistema de honor determine cómo termina la historia.Para mí, el sistema de honor debería influir principalmente en el comportamiento de los NPC, sus reacciones, sus relaciones con el protagonista y la manera en que el mundo responde a nuestras acciones, pero no modificar el desenlace principal de la historia. La narrativa debería tener una dirección definida y un final que realmente cierre la experiencia.4. Una historia que necesitaba una verdadera evolución criminalEn cuanto a la historia, esperaba algo mucho más parecido a la esencia clásica de GTA: comenzar desde abajo, sin dinero, sin poder y sin grandes contactos, e ir subiendo escalón por escalón hasta convertirse en alguien importante dentro del mundo **** habría gustado una historia con una evolución más marcada, llena de traiciones, ambición, alianzas, pérdidas y decisiones difíciles. Una trama donde los protagonistas fueran escalando posiciones hasta llegar a la cima, para finalmente enfrentarse a una gran traición o a un acontecimiento que pusiera todo en **** tipo de narrativa es lo que esperaba: empezar desde cero, construir un imperio criminal y terminar en lo más alto, después de todo lo que costó llegar allí.ConclusiónGTA 6 tenía la oportunidad de ofrecer una experiencia criminal mucho más profunda, con consecuencias reales, libertad para el jugador y una historia que transmitiera esa sensación de progreso. Sin embargo, estas decisiones me dejaron decepcionado. No se trata solamente de tener un mapa enorme o mejores gráficos; también importa la libertad, las consecuencias de nuestras acciones y, sobre todo, una historia que realmente valga la pena recordar.

author: FalseCape
quote:
If this were another game with a significantly smaller budget and development time, I might be able to give it some grace and give it a high 6 or low 7. If it was an indie dev's first game made on a fraction of the budget I might even be inclined to give it an 8. But this isn't another game. This is Grand Theft Auto 6 with a 13 year development time and nearly 2 billion dollar budget and it fails to even pass the bar set by it's previous entry. 

Who cares about physics when the game can't hold a stable 30fps in 2026? If the game can't even hold a stable 30fps, why would you EVER tie the physics engine to the frame rate leading to situations where you can clip out of bounds when the frame rate gets wonky? Who cares about fixing up a house before we've even had a chance to establish a deep connection with Lucia? Why do chase missions hold your hand and respawn you if you end up in the water instead of giving you the proper mission failed that GTA used to expect of you? Why is there only a single autosave slot that can be corrupted by power loss losing you hours of progress? Why does playing a GTA game like a GTA game or not doing enough housework lock you out of the "good" ending? These are things I would expect **** clone's first attempt at the genre, not from the creators of it and certainly not with the amount of time and money that was sunk into it. 

Maybe with time, patches, and some mods once this game eventually hits PC, this game will be brought up to the proper GTA standard and I'll give the PC version a more favorable score, but the game I played on release is not that game.

author: juudai
quote:
Looking at all the debates over the past couple of days, both the 10/10 praise and the player backlash make sense. However, when you objectively compare GTA 5 and GTA 6 side by side, the "laundry list of issues" players are complaining about is completely valid:
1. Shift in Design Philosophy (Action vs. Realism): GTA 5 was an explosive Hollywood blockbuster—three wild protagonists and an adrenaline-pumping bank heist right out of the gate. GTA 6 forces Red Dead Redemption 2’s slow, hyper-realistic pacing into a modern setting, bogging down the first few hours with tedious chores and errands at the expense of classic GTA arcade fun.
2. Technical Compromises (30 FPS & Launch Bugs): Pushing extreme visuals and NPC density came at the cost of locking consoles to 30 FPS (with noticeable dips during heavy gunfights), alongside uncharacteristic launch bugs like clipping, texture pop-in, and broken mission AI—a sharp contrast to GTA 5’s rock-solid polish.
3. A Safer, Less Punchy Story: To fit the serious tone of the dual-protagonist romance, Rockstar dialed back its signature biting satire. The main campaign drags in the middle and suffers from weak, forgettable antagonists.
Bottom Line: GTA 6 is easily the most detailed open-world sandbox ever built, and it’s fun if you want to cruise around and soak in the atmosphere. But if you were expecting the fast-paced, smooth, over-the-top thrill ride of GTA 5, the letdown is very real.

author: riskyvega
quote:
I waited 13 years for this, and somewhere along the way Rockstar forgot what GTA is supposed to be.

GTA is supposed to be a power fantasy. This is a chore simulator.

 I didn’t buy a Grand Theft Auto game to watch my fuel gauge, juggle a tiny weapon inventory, and sit through slow “everyday life” busywork between missions. Rockstar has dropped the “magic pockets” in favor of limited weapon slots, and the “realism” doesn’t stop there. Every system seems built to slow you down instead of letting you cause chaos. If I wanted to manage errands, I’d do my own. GTA used to be about freedom. Now it’s a to-do list with a Vice City skin.

The cut content is obvious. no first-person mode, no dual wielding, no prone stance, no infinite weapon wheel, no infinite fuel, and no easy way to recover a flipped vehicle, among others. Some of these things were in GTA 5 thirteen years ago. In before half of this is going to be locked behind DLC if ever released.

The main characters are exhausting. Jason and Lucia are supposed to be the heart of the story, but I couldn’t stand either of them. The dialogue tries way too hard to be edgy and emotional at once, and it lands on neither. GTA protagonists used to be fun to play as even when they were awful people. These two are just annoying, and you’re stuck with them for dozens of hours.

I don’t trust the 99. A score tied with Ocarina of Time for the highest Metascore ever recorded, and not a single mixed review? For a game that runs at 30fps on a PS5 Pro, cuts basic features, and costs more than ever? To me that doesn’t look like honest criticism. It looks like an industry too scared of losing access to the biggest publisher around to say anything bad. The critic score reads like marketing, not a review. Look at the user scores instead.

Overpriced, stripped down, and more interested in making you do chores than letting you have fun. 0/10.

author: EternalReditus
quote: GTA VI: Trece años de espera para confundir realismo con diversión Calificación: 0/10 Trece años después de GTA V, varios retrasos y expectativas gigantescas, esperaba que Rockstar revolucionara nuevamente los mundos abiertos. En cambio, nos encontramos con una producción visualmente impresionante que parece confundir el realismo con la diversión y la cantidad de detalles con la profundidad de sus mecánicas. 1. El realismo no significa buena jugabilidad. Gabe Newell explicó una idea fundamental del diseño de videojuegos: el realismo no es automáticamente divertido. Lo importante es que el mundo reconozca las acciones del jugador y responda a ellas.¿De qué sirve tener animaciones para limpiar la casa, pintar paredes o realizar tareas cotidianas si luego las misiones siguen imponiendo restricciones artificiales?No necesito que mi personaje haga todo lo que puedo hacer en la vida real. Necesito un mundo donde mis decisiones, los objetos y los NPC reaccionen de manera coherente. 2. Un mundo abierto que limita la libertad. GTA siempre ha destacado por permitir experimentar, provocar caos y descubrir posibilidades **** embargo, GTA VI conserva una de las mayores debilidades de Rockstar: misiones excesivamente dirigidas donde desviarse del camino previsto puede significar fracasar.Después de tantos años, esperaba más libertad para completar objetivos, improvisar estrategias y utilizar el entorno.¿De qué sirve una ciudad gigantesca si sus sistemas no evolucionan al mismo ritmo que sus gráficos? 3. Tecnología impresionante, ejecución cuestionable. Rockstar ofrece una presentación visual espectacular, pero eso no debería ocultar problemas como el límite de 30 FPS en consolas, críticas sobre controles poco refinados y fallos **** bugs son normales en videojuegos ambiciosos. Lo cuestionable es que, después de múltiples retrasos anunciados para alcanzar los estándares de calidad del estudio, todavía existan problemas que afecten la **** considero que un presupuesto gigantesco o unos gráficos extraordinarios justifiquen automáticamente una nota perfecta. 4. ¿Qué pasó con la esencia de GTA? No tengo ningún problema con que Jason y Lucia sean pareja o con que exista una historia **** problema es que el énfasis en actividades domésticas y convivencia no representa la evolución criminal que **** San Andreas ofrecía pandillas, territorios, personalización y una gran variedad de actividades. GTA IV exploraba el crimen y la desilusión del sueño americano. GTA V apostaba por golpes espectaculares, conflictos y protagonistas muy **** VI también contiene crimen, pero esperaba que ampliara las posibilidades de sus antecesores, no que dedicara tanto protagonismo a acciones cotidianas. 5. Red Dead Redemption 2 ya había demostrado lo que Rockstar podía hacer. En 2018, Rockstar estableció un estándar extraordinario de animaciones, físicas e interacción con el **** eso resulta decepcionante encontrar inconsistencias o limitaciones en una producción **** realismo no debería limitarse a cómo se ve un objeto, sino extenderse a cómo se comporta cuando interactuamos con él. 6. ¿Dónde está la innovación que justifica un 99/100? Ocarina of Time ayudó a transformar las aventuras tridimensionales. Half-Life, Portal y otros videojuegos introdujeron o popularizaron ideas que influyeron en generaciones **** VI puede tener una escala gigantesca, pero sigo preguntándome qué avances jugables justifican considerarlo prácticamente perfecto.Más edificios, mejores reflejos y animaciones detalladas no equivalen necesariamente a mejores **** todos los videojuegos necesitan revolucionar la industria, pero una puntuación de 99 exige, como mínimo, una ejecución excepcional.7. La diferencia entre críticos y **** GTA VI haya alcanzado un 99 entre críticos mientras su puntuación inicial de usuarios rondaba el 5.4 muestra una diferencia de opiniones **** no demuestra que los críticos estén comprados ni que todas las opiniones negativas sean legítimas. Pero tampoco deberían descartarse automáticamente como review bombing.Resulta razonable preguntar por qué tantos análisis reconocen defectos y aun así conceden puntuaciones perfectas. No esperaba simplemente un GTA V con mejores gráficos.Esperaba una evolución profunda de la libertad, las interacciones, el combate, las actividades criminales y el diseño de misiones.Rockstar ha construido un mundo técnicamente impresionante, pero un videojuego no debería medirse únicamente por lo bonito que resulta contemplarlo.Debe medirse también por lo que permite hacer y por cómo responde a nuestras decisiones.Trece años después, no necesitábamos únicamente una ciudad más realista. Necesitábamos un GTA más libre, más interactivo y verdaderamente innovador. Para mí, GTA VI no cumplió esas expectativas. Y un 99 en Metacritic no cambia eso.

author: IDarkSkywardI
quote:
I've now put 31 hours into the game, and honestly, it's just a massive disappointment. Does GTA 6 seriously deserve a 99 rating? Bought and paid for, that's all I can say. 
ᅠ
30 FPS in 2026, an extremely ridiculous amount of bugs on the same level as Cyberpunk 2077's release. Gameplay that feels like a step backwards in many areas, because the story is far too tame, overly serious, and at times a straight-up simp simulator. Most of the characters are boring, the humor is weak, and classic GTA moments are practically nowhere to be found.
ᅠ
On top of that, there are invincible NPCs such as Wokes and protesters, people in clubs and other protected NPCs, an extremely restricted and censored chaos system, and ridiculous restrictions such as not being allowed to use weapons inside clubs, etc.... The game keeps taking away more and more of the freedoms GTA is actually known for. Even stealing cars is unnecessarily complicated, the wanted system feels like a downgrade, and even the combat system is clunky, the controls are sluggish, the movement feels sluggish, and the input lag is quite noticeable at times.
ᅠ
The beginning feels like it goes on forever. The characters spend far too much time on pointless everyday activities, and you're constantly stuck in dialogue-heavy driving sequences that slow down the pacing. On top of that, missions hold your hand way too much, there are barely any proper heists, no mission replay feature, mission softlocks, vehicles that get destroyed way too quickly, and an overall downgraded UI.
And as if all that wasn't enough, crashes can even result in losing your entire game progress in the worst-case scenario..That's not just frustrating; it's simply unacceptable for an AAA game of this scale.
ᅠ
I could keep going with this list, but at some point you really have to wonder what exactly makes this game so ridiculously hyped. Apparently, just having GTA in the title makes everything untouchable. This is certainly not what innovation and progress look like to me. ‍♂️

author: Deterion95
quote: After a thirteen-year wait, eight years of development and a historic budget, Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived on the market crowned with perfect scores from much of the gaming press. However, judging the game by the exact same standard applied to any other studio—such as Ubisoft, Bethesda, Nintendo, or CD Projekt Red—reveals that Rockstar Games operates under a shield of absolute impunity. Had any other developer released a title in this state, we would be talking about a technical, commercial, and preservation scandal.Disregard for Physical Media and CollectingHaving the biggest video game launch in history arrive without a physical edition at launch—or delaying the disc to a much later date under the excuse of preventing leaks—is a slap in the face to consumers. If Microsoft or Ubisoft announced that their flagship title could only be bought digitally on day one, social media would erupt over monopolies, lack of true ownership, and the death of game collecting. With Rockstar, however, the decision is excused as "necessary," forcing millions of players into digital storefronts with no way to lend, resell, or keep a copy on their shelf.Indefensible Technical Performance in the Current GenerationIn late 2026, seeing a current-gen console-exclusive AAA release locked at 30 FPS with no 60 FPS performance mode—not even on PS5 Pro—is something that would have gotten any other studio crucified by the media. Worse still, it fails to even hold that framerate steady. On base consoles (PS5 and Xbox Series X), sharp drops during heavy shootouts or dense areas are frequent—dipping close to 15 FPS in extreme cases—while the Xbox Series S version suffers from a blurry resolution that compromises the visual experience.Excessive Realism at the Expense of Fun ("Everyday Life Simulator")Following the heavier approach of Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar has prioritized obsessive simulation over responsive gameplay. Having to manage weapon inventories in a car trunk, worry about hyper-vigilant law enforcement, redecorate a house, or perform slow mundane chores completely breaks the fast-paced arcade energy that once defined the franchise. Moving on foot indoors or in crowded spaces still drags along the clunky, heavy feel characteristic of the RAGE engine, where animation takes precedence over immediate controller responsiveness.A Slow, Interrupted Campaign with Less SparkThe narrative pacing takes far too long to get going, dedicating its opening hours to domestic life and the everyday struggles of Jason and Lucia before diving into major criminal heists. Additionally, the game overuses cutscenes that interrupt key action sequences and robberies that should clearly be playable. In terms of tone, the absence of key figures from Rockstar’s old guard is noticeable: the script opts for a much more grounded, restrained crime drama that loses some of the biting, irreverent satire that made the series unique.Predatory Business Practices from Day OneDespite being a full-priced game after more than a decade of development, Rockstar has not hesitated to lock in-game shops and cosmetic items behind the Ultimate Edition. On top of this comes the company’s usual fragmentation: PC players are once again left behind with no official release date, and the multiplayer mode is missing at launch—turning the release into an incomplete package designed to make players double-dip down the road.Grand Theft Auto VI is a technical marvel in scale, lighting, and open-world density, yet as a product it suffers from performance flaws, rigid gameplay, and anti-consumer decisions—starting with the snub to physical media—that on any other publisher’s cover would have meant an automatic failing grade.

You barely have time to think “**** finally” before the game grabs you by the scruff of the neck and drags you back into the story. Why the **** do I have to wait this long to play GTA in GTA?

And the whole **** time, somebody’s talking. They talk in the car, they talk while you’re trudging along behind them, they talk in cutscenes. When the whole mission is driving to a waypoint while they have yet another conversation, by the time we get there I’ve already forgotten where we’re going. I just want them both to shut the **** up.

Jason’s dumb as a stump. I haven’t played a game in a long time where I wanted so badly to be playing as literally anyone else. Lucia gets on my nerves too, and I still have no idea what either of them actually wants. They go out to rob a few shops and pick a **** waffle joint. **** the story for a minute. What is there to do in the open world? Play a console game inside the game I’m already playing on my console? Shoot some pool? The way people gush about these minigames, you’d think they’d never played a GTA before. But hey, now you can keep tabs on your car’s condition and get it delivered through Scooter Bros. A regular delivery costs in-game cash, and the in-game Premium upgrade gives you three free deliveries per in-game day. Why the **** am I working out car delivery rates in GTA? I just wanted to drive the damn thing.

And here’s Rockstar trying to show us the future of open-world games on a console generation that started in 2020. By the time GTA VI came out, the base PS5 was already six years old, and a high-end gaming PC could do more even back then. I fire it up on a PS5 Pro, and even on the Pro it looks like the same **** smeary mess. I turn the camera and it feels like someone’s rubbing sandpaper across my eyes. Jesus **** Christ, it looks so bad I physically want to look away.

Eleven **** years. That’s roughly how long it’s been since work on the game started. What the **** is in this game that took eleven years to make? Yeah, the world’s huge. Yeah, they put a lot of work into the little details. And somehow it still feels like I’m playing a **** mash-up of Red Dead Redemption, The Sims, and some random GTA clone. Which is pretty **** funny considering I booted up GTA itself.

Real life already has enough **** that makes me go “****, this again.” I boot up GTA to have fun. By the time this game finally let me cut loose for a bit, I was already wondering if I’d bother turning it on the next day. If I ever give a **** how it ends, I’ll watch the ending on YouTube. I’m sure as **** not playing this **** twice.

author: FoxEngine
quote:
GTA 6 is a bloated, overhyped, creatively bankrupt mess that proves Rockstar has completely lost the plot.
For over a decade, the gaming world was force-fed the idea that this game would be the second coming of interactive entertainment. Trailers were dissected frame by frame. People treated every rumor like gospel. And when it finally dropped, what did we get? A technically impressive but soul-crushing open-world checklist that prioritizes quantity over quality, spectacle over substance, and corporate metrics over actual fun.
Let’s start with the most obvious problem: the game is a technical disaster at launch. Rockstar has a long history of shipping unfinished products and then patching them into “masterpieces” months later while the community does free QA. GTA 6 continues that proud tradition. Frame rates dip hard in dense areas, pop-in is constant, physics glitches turn cars into ragdolls, and the AI still can’t handle basic traffic without looking like a drunk NPC convention. After thirteen years of development and one of the largest budgets in entertainment history, this is what they delivered? A game that needs a day-one patch the size of a small indie title just to stop breaking itself?
The world is massive, yes. But size is not depth. Vice City in 2026 feels like a theme park designed by marketing executives. Every street is packed with distractions, side activities, and collectibles that exist solely to inflate playtime metrics. The map is full of stuff to do, yet almost nothing feels worth doing. It’s the same open-world formula Rockstar has been recycling since GTA V, just with better lighting and more NPCs. The novelty of “look how many people are walking around” wore off after the first hour. What’s left is a checklist simulator dressed up as living world.
Then there’s the story. Rockstar used to write sharp, cynical, darkly funny narratives that actually had something to say. GTA 6’s campaign is a safe, focus-tested soap opera that tries to be edgy while carefully avoiding anything that might upset the algorithm. The protagonists are designed to be broadly appealing rather than interesting. The writing swings between try-hard cool and awkward attempts at social commentary that feel ten years late. The humor is blunt, the drama is predictable, and the whole thing feels like it was written by committee after three rounds of sensitivity notes. Compare this to the vicious satire of San Andreas or the bleak brilliance of Red Dead Redemption 2 and the decline is embarrassing.
And the fanbase’s reaction has been even more revealing. The same people who spent years defending every delayed patch and every microtransaction are now review-bombing other games because they’re terrified their precious GTA might not win every popularity contest. That level of insecurity says more about the game’s cultural position than any trailer ever could. When your community’s primary form of engagement is attacking other titles instead of celebrating your own, something has gone deeply wrong.
GTA 6 isn’t a failure because it’s broken (though it is). It’s a failure because it represents the complete victory of scale over soul. Rockstar used to make games that felt dangerous, funny, and alive. Now they make content platforms that feel expensive. The industry celebrated the trailers. The numbers will be enormous. The critical scores will be high because the bar for “impressive open world” has been lowered so far that technical ambition alone is enough.
But none of that changes the truth: under the marketing, under the hype, under the pure spectacle, GTA 6 is a hollow, overproduced, creatively exhausted product that mistakes size for greatness. It’s not the future of gaming. It’s the logical endpoint of a company that stopped taking risks a decade ago and started optimizing for engagement metrics instead.
And no amount of fanboy damage control will change that.

author: JayDL
quote:
Grand Theft Auto 6 felt surprisingly underwhelming. For a franchise known for sharp satire, there isn’t a single memorable or genuinely funny moment from the story or cutscenes that stuck with me. The pacing at the start is painfully slow, making the early hours feel like a chore rather than an adventure. Overall, the narrative falls flat and fails to live up to the hype or the high bar set by previous Rockstar titles.

Even the core gameplay feels conflicted; it’s a game about committing crimes that constantly feels like it doesn't actually want you to commit them. Worse, the ending transitions poorly into the post-game, abruptly dumping you right back into the pre-finale state. Compare that to Red Dead Redemption 2, where (SPOILER ALERT): 
Arthur Morgan’s death seamlessly transitions into an epilogue that lets you roam the open world as John Marston.

Ultimately, the only reason GTA 6 will be remembered for generations is its incredible graphics. Beyond the visuals, there isn't much substance. After all, what’s the point of a meal that looks like it was plated by a Michelin-star chef if it tastes like a frozen dinner from the grocery store?
