author: impixelated
quote: Sinceramente, é difícil entender todo esse hype em torno de GTA VI sem também questionar algumas coisas. Estamos falando de um jogo que levou mais de uma década para chegar até aqui, com um orçamento estimado em 1 bilhão de dólares, e que carrega a expectativa de ser um dos maiores lançamentos da história dos videogames. Mas, depois de tudo isso, algumas decisões simplesmente não fazem sentido. Começando pelos 30 FPS. Estamos em 2026. É realmente frustrante pensar que um jogo dessa magnitude possa ficar limitado a 30 quadros por segundo. E não, não estou dizendo que todo jogo precisa rodar a 60 FPS para ser bom. A questão é, depois de tantos anos de desenvolvimento, com tantos recursos disponíveis, realmente decepcionante. Não dá para usar gráficos bonitos como justificativa para qualquer limitação técnica. E isso sem falar nos bugs e nos problemas de otimização que podem acompanhar um lançamento desse tamanho. É claro que nenhum jogo é perfeito e que desenvolver um mundo aberto dessa complexidade não é uma tarefa simples. Mas também não podemos fingir que essas dificuldades justificam tudo. Quanto maior a produção, maior deveria ser a responsabilidade de entregar um produto bem acabado. Agora, vamos falar do preço. Quase 600 reais por um único jogo no Brasil é simplesmente absurdo. Não é uma compra pequena, não é um valor que qualquer pessoa pode gastar tranquilamente. É uma quantia considerável, principalmente quando levamos em conta a realidade econômica do brasileiro. E parece que, cada vez mais, as empresas estão confortáveis em cobrar valores exorbitantes simplesmente porque sabem que existe uma legião de pessoas dispostas a pagar. Outro ponto que me incomoda bastante é a ausência de dublagem em português brasileiro. Estamos falando de uma das maiores franquias do entretenimento mundial, com uma comunidade enorme no Brasil. Sinceramente, qual é a justificativa para não oferecer uma localização completa? Não estamos falando de uma desenvolvedora pequena, com recursos limitados. É a Rockstar. Uma empresa que tem condições de investir muito mais do que a maioria das desenvolvedoras do mercado. E o pior de tudo é que parece que não podemos criticar nada disso sem alguém aparecer para defender a empresa. Você questiona os 30 FPS e dizem que você não entende de tecnologia. Questiona o preço e dizem que é só não comprar. Questiona a falta de dublagem e dizem que legenda já é suficiente. Desde quando exigir um produto de qualidade, especialmente pagando tão caro por ele, se tornou exigir demais? Não estou dizendo que GTA VI será um jogo ruim. Muito pelo contrário, espero que seja uma experiência incrível. Mas isso não significa que precisamos aceitar qualquer decisão da Rockstar de olhos fechados. São mais de 13 anos de espera, um orçamento estimado em 1 bilhão de dólares e uma das empresas mais poderosas da indústria por trás do projeto. É justamente por isso que as expectativas deveriam ser tão altas. No fim das contas, parece que estamos tão ocupados esperando GTA VI ser o jogo da década que esquecemos de questionar se estamos realmente recebendo tudo aquilo pelo que estamos pagando. A Rockstar não está fazendo um favor ao consumidor. Ela está vendendo um produto. E, por mais incrível que esse produto possa ser, isso não a torna imune a críticas.

author: Police1987
quote:
I bought GTA 6 expecting GTA and instead got something that feels like it's missing polish, soul, and heart. The gameplay is slow, clunky, and often frustrating. Most things in this game from the radio stations to the gameplay and the design choices made here all feels very flat and lacking of that GTA spark.
For a sequel that took many years and reportedly cost billions to make, I expected far more refinement.

Framerate issues and glitches aren't even my main complaint. Those can potentially be patched out over time. 

The bigger problem is that, at its core, this doesn't feel like a GTA game. If Rockstar wanted to make a Bonnie and Clyde simulator, they should have made it a different franchise.

The combat is another major disappointment. It's in a strange place where both the player and enemies can feel like bullet sponges, yet the game still finds ways to kill you with cheap deaths. It's the worst of both worlds. Gunfights drag on longer than they should, but sometimes i didnt feel truly in control of the outcome.

Features that were talked about and shown off, such as more enterable buildings, open interiors, and beaches packed with NPCs, don't feel present in the way I expected as a player. 
The world is large, but much of it feels less interactive than I was hoping for.

What disappoints me most is that the GTA spark feels largely absent. 
The humour and satire that helped define the series are at their weakest here. The jokes rarely land, the social commentary lacks the edge that made previous entries so memorable, and much of the dialogue feels surprisingly safe and forgettable. 
Moments that should be funny often fall flat, making this feel like a huge step backwards for the series.

When I think back to Vice City, San Andreas, GTA IV, and GTA V, I can immediately remember characters, quotes, radio stations, and ridiculous situations years after playing them. I don't get that feeling with GTA 6.
To be fair, the game can look incredible at times. The graphics are often stunning, and there are moments where Rockstar's technical talent is impossible to ignore. Unfortunately, great visuals can't make up for gameplay that feels hollow or a world that lacks the personality and charm that made previous GTA games special.

Overall, GTA 6 looks fantastic, but beneath the graphics I found a shallow experience that lacks the freedom, personality, humour, and fun that made the series legendary.

author: CynthiaDevelle
quote:
One approaches Grand Theft Auto VI with the trembling anticipation of a soul awaiting the dawn, only to discover that the sun has risen upon precisely the same landscape, illuminating nothing new. Here lies a curious paradox: a game so immense in its proportions, so lavish in its technical splendour, and yet so desperately impoverished in its essence.

Where once there was audacity, there is now calculation. Where once there was a rebellious spirit, a peculiar madness, a world teeming with irreverence and unexpected life, there remains only the sterile machinery of a familiar formula, polished until every trace of its former soul has been rubbed away.

The earlier titles possessed something ineffable: an identity, a pulse, a certain beautiful vulgarity that made their worlds feel alive. They were imperfect, certainly, but their imperfections were human; their excesses were joyful; their absurdities were their poetry. This, by contrast, feels like the melancholy shadow of a departed greatness, wandering through the ruins of its own legacy.

And what, one must ask, is progress if not the discovery of something beyond oneself? What is innovation if the future merely rearranges the furniture of the past? We have travelled so far, technologically speaking, only to arrive at the same old destination, with a more expensive carriage and considerably less enthusiasm.

Perhaps this is the inevitable fate of all things that become too beloved: they cease to live and begin merely to reproduce themselves. The creators, fearing the loss of what once made them great, preserve its outward appearance with such devotion that they inadvertently destroy its spirit. - Thus GTA VI stands before us: not quite a failure, for failure would at least possess the dignity of having attempted something daring, but something far more depressing — mediocrity concealed beneath an extraordinary amount of polish.

author: skullmonkey9999
quote:
Far from perfect, this installment delivers what the franchise does best: criminal chaos, a huge map, and a world that reacts to what you do. But it falls short of that premise. On the story side, I’d say there are plenty of memorable missions and good character appearances, but there are others that lean toward being a kind of life simulator, which is tedious and boring. They fall into a cliché of interactions that force you to do activities far from what the series used to do, and this drags down the protagonists, who in my view have the least personality of the whole saga, without a doubt. I think Claude is more iconic, and he doesn’t say a single **** have to be objective when judging a game that has been in development for eight years, but many of us expected a lot and feel let down by the characters and the way the story unfolds when compared to earlier entries. It’s fair to say the gameplay is by far the best open-world game to date, but the story and its characters are the weakest in the series, and a letdown for many veteran players who were used to that epic, movie-style criminal saga.
 I believe this game realistically deserves a score between 86 and 92. The score I’ve left here is a deliberate protest, meant to push back against inflated ratings and remind people that this game is far from perfect.

author: nastrondVI
quote:
The GTA series were respected for providing players the power of choice: be as much of a scumbag criminal as you like, hire prostitutes, steal every single vehicle in sight, store the ones that matter the most, burn and blow up the others, murder every human you want. You could hijack from someone in the middle of the road, run them over with it, pick a prostitute and take them somewhere discreet for a health buff, kill them afterwards and repeat the process if you're so inclined. These are not good things at all, but you were given the valuable choices to make your character do said not-good things and more. To top it all off, if you did feel like actually playing it for the plot you were still treated with entertaining and unforgettable characters and storylines between missions.

Not this game though! Instead what you have here is the single most anticipated video game of all time, featuring a Netflix Original Series-esque plot where you are obligated to play the good loyal boyfriend who needs to keep his unpleasant girlfriend happy. In a game called Grand Theft Auto you are now given much less freedom in regards to stealing and keeping vehicles. 

And the signature choice in committing represensable acts on your own terms, something all fans have appreciated since GTA3 (if not the classic entries before) is neutered. You'll find that, for the sake of keeping with the times and making this game as realistic as possible, many people who may or may not exhibit divisive agendas you may or may not agree with, are actually completely exempt from violence and destruction, granting them total immunity. Just like real life.

It was better off released under a new IP. But Rockstar knew perfectly well this cow was worthless milking out for over a decade without the GTA brand tacked onto it.

1 undeserved point out of 10 for actually finishing and releasing the damn thing. Now let's hope the overblown hysteria completely dies sooner than later.

Hurry up with ES6, Bethesda. I'm not holding much hope there either, but surely you can't do any worse than this.

author: KiwiZ
quote: A game that released ONE DAY before the GOTY nominations were announced SHOULD NOT EVEN BE ELIGIBLE for consideration. The timing alone is ridiculous. It feels like a desperate last-minute attempt to sneak its way into the conversation before anyone has time to properly digest it. Critics got completely fooled, apparently. Locked at 30 FPS, somehow sitting at a 99 overall score, and treated like the second coming of gaming itself.Sure, they might have added a bunch of new features, improved certain mechanics, and thrown in enough content to make the marketing department cream its pants. But here's the thing: adding features doesn't automatically make a game revolutionary. A GOTY contender should be more than a glorified checklist of improvements. It should leave a mark, push the industry forward, inspire developers, and give future games something worth learning **** hey, 99/100, right? Who needs standards anymore?What's even funnier is watching people treat that Metacritic score like it's some divine revelation handed down from the heavens. Apparently, a number next to a game's name is now a substitute for critical thinking. Who cares about technical compromises, actual innovation, or long-term influence when you can just point at a 99 and declare everyone else objectively wrong? Truly, we've reached the peak of gaming criticism: spreadsheet worship disguised as **** sure, let's celebrate a 30 FPS experience like it's the technological achievement of the century. Let's pretend the score is untouchable, the timing is perfectly normal, and questioning its place among the nominees is somehow a personal attack against gaming **** this point, the GOTY conversation feels less like a celebration of the year's best games and more like a popularity contest where the loudest fanbase gets to hand out participation trophies.Congratulations, I guess. A 99 Metacritic score, a last-minute entrance, and the groundbreaking discovery that GTA VI apparently doesn't welcome furries. Gaming has officially peaked. Pack it up, developers. There's nothing left to invent.

author: jakeabambo916
quote:
I’ve played every GTA since GTA3, so it hurts to write this. GTA 6 is a gorgeous game, maybe the best looking thing I’ve ever played (if you can get over 30 FPS). But somewhere in the 13 years of polishing they sanded off everything that made GTA feel like GTA. The old games felt like they were daring you to do something stupid. You’d steal a tank, cause a five-star meltdown, laugh, reload. This one feels like it wants you to behave. Everything is slow and “realistic.” Half my first night was walking, talking, watching cutscenes, and doing errands that feel more like chores than missions. There’s fishing, mini golf, working out, canoeing. Cool, I guess, but I didn’t wait over a decade for a vacation simulator. The whole game is built around the main character's relationship, and it makes everything feel careful and soft. Tommy, CJ, Niko, Trevor: none of those guys needed a hug. They were unpredictable and a little dangerous, and that was the point. Here it feels like the edge got taken away, and honestly it left me feeling kind of emasculated playing it. I’m not the guy running the city anymore, I’m the guy getting managed. 

The satire is weaker too. Earlier games roasted America with no mercy. This one pokes at Florida Man memes and social media, but it feels like it’s nervous about offending anybody. 

I’m sure a lot of critics will love this game. But for me, fun used to be the whole point of GTA, and this one seems more interested in being impressive than being fun. I put the controller down feeling bored, which I never thought I’d say about a GTA game.

author: Wickedest
quote:
I’ve played 15 hours of the game and so far I can’t see how making this game cost Rockstar over $1bn. Rockstar claimed that they built this game from the ground up but the game seems to me like a “red dead redemption 2” re-skin. It feels like they have used the same engine a lot of the same game physics & game play loops and just changed the map, replaced horses with modern day vehicles, replaced the characters, added poorly written lack lustre story, added new NPC’s and upgraded all the in game assets to more modern day looking stuff. I wouldn’t be surprised if there are some re-used RDR2 assets in this game. Yes the graphical upgrades and extra detail work especially with the many impressive new encounters with random NPC’s and all new in game assets is not free but I don’t think $1bn was spent on just making the game I think a lot of that budget was spent elsewhere like on licensing for in game music, marketing and other things that have nothing to do with game design. Even Jason the main male protagonist looks a lot like Arthur Morgan the main protagonist from RDR2. There are a lot of similar animals that you can find in GTA6 which you can also study like in RDR2, there is dead eye in shoot outs like RDR2, there are some random burnt out buildings in the sticks that looks like something out of RDR2, there is a morality mechanic in the game like RDR2, The Gun and item storage mechanic is a lot like RDR2 but instead of using your horse to Stowe guns/items you use your car and the wanted system in this game feels a lot like RDR2 which breaks the mayhem because there is no real gradual progression through the wanted system which allows you to cause carnage. It feels like a more slow realistic RDR style game rather than the more fast paced arcadey style gameplay we have been used to on previous GTA entries. For me there is way to much tedious detailed gameplay to everything that slows the game down a lot and for me I enjoyed the fast paced action of previous GTA entries and I am disappointed that Rockstar has decided to move away from that. The story so far is definitely not my cup of tea there are a lot of in my opinion boring & patronising missions/tasks that I definitely wasn’t expecting to have in this game. There is no real edgy lead protagonist like we have been used to in previous entries in this game. Both protagonist’s in this game feel boring & dull. They seem like 2 models that are supposed to be on an episode of love island not on a crime spree in a GTA game. I’ve not really been that engaged with the story so I decided to look up the endings of this game and it seems to me like this game leans heavily on RDR2 styled morality mechanics to tell its story but for me this story that GTA tries to tell can’t light a candle to the RDR2 story. It’s a story that dictates to you how to play and doesn’t give you the feeling of a free roaming sandbox game that GTA is famous for. 

Deal breaker for me is that there is a lot of things missing from this GTA game that for me are non-negotiable like not being able to pick up prostitutes, not being able to customise stolen cars at the beginning of the game, not having any Rampage missions, not being able to buy property/businesses, no Taxi/vigilante/paramedic missions, no in game internet or stock market, the classic GTA bottomless weapon wheel has been replaced with a tedious RDR2 style weapon selection mechanic and most annoying of all there is no dedicated mission replay menu. So far not all my experience in this game has been bad there has been some good points. I’ve enjoyed some main story missions and had some satisfying shootouts. The random NPC encounters have been fun at times and this GTA probably has the best driving mechanic of all other previous GTA titles. However it’s not enough in my opinion to justify marking up my score for this tremendous anticlimactic blunder **** game. It tells a terrible story and is basically a RDR2 re-skin. It does look really great graphically and the amount of random NPC encounters are impressive but for me it falls short in so many other areas and it doesn’t scratch that 13 year GTA itch I’ve been having for so long. 3/10 so far.

author: Akakarant7
quote: Malgré un monde ouvert vivant et rempli de détails, je ressens un immense vide en jouant à GTA 6. Une sensation d’ennui qui finit par prendre le dessus. On est très loin de l’essence des anciens GTA : les crimes, la folie, la provocation et la liberté qui faisaient l’identité de la licence semblent avoir disparu au profit d’une histoire de couple que je trouve particulièrement **** problème, c’est surtout la place qu’occupe cette relation dans le jeu. On a parfois davantage l’impression de jouer le rôle d’un homme soumis aux caprices de sa compagne que celui d’un criminel dans GTA. Une grande partie des activités consiste à la satisfaire, à respecter ses exigences et à accomplir des tâches pour elle. On ne peut même pas envisager de la tromper ou de vivre réellement sa propre histoire : le jeu nous impose presque une relation amoureuse. À force, le mode histoire ressemble davantage à une succession de corvées conjugales qu’à une véritable aventure GTA.J’ai également le sentiment que le jeu cherche tellement à être politiquement correct qu’il en perd son identité et son côté provocateur. La liberté d’action semble elle aussi beaucoup plus limitée.Techniquement, je suis également déçu. Les 30 FPS rendent l’expérience particulièrement saccadée. Les graphismes sont détaillés, certes, mais le rendu général n’a rien d’extraordinaire. Certains visages et personnages sont même assez décevants. À titre de comparaison, je trouve Cyberpunk 2077 largement supérieur sur le plan **** final, GTA 6 possède un monde ouvert impressionnant, mais je le trouve étonnamment vide d’intérêt. Beaucoup de détails, mais peu de liberté, peu de folie et surtout, cette identité GTA que j’ai l’impression d’avoir perdue.

author: goodfellas69
quote: People are very dishonest with the actual scope of this game and how it is. For starters, the story and main protagonists are written horribly. You play as a guy (Jason) who tries to mend his relationship with his jailbird girlfriend Lucia, who goes to jail because she tried to rob a bank while abandoning their baby in a coffee shop. Why is this bad writing? Because she robbed the bank AFTER breaking up with Jason because he told her “no” that she can’t join him on an illegal job. She didn’t tell him she was pregnant after she realized as well, BUT it gets worse because he doesn’t call her out on her reckless behavior, which is something that is a trend throughout the story. With a story focused on getting their son back and falling in love, it’s no excuse for the lack of accountability written for their characters when child custody is a high stakes thing. The story takes a hit because they go around committing crimes to make money while also making more enemies with getting their kid back as motivation only to never stop and ask if they should even be on this criminal streak for the sake of their kid to begin with, they just double down more on crime. Second reason why the game is not good: the game can’t consistently run at 30 fps even when walking around and doing nothing, that is unacceptable when most players are gonna wanna blow up cars and kill npcs. Third reason; the game is a limited sandbox. You can’t hire hookers anymore, some npcs you can’t kill, some cars you need to progress through the game to be able to steal unlike previous GTA games, you can’t steal cars from neighbors which is ridiculous, you can’t romance any other characters except Lucia or Jason, and worst of all you are forced to romance Lucia to get the good ending of the game. The rockstar team says romance with her is optional but takes away player choice by not giving you other romance options, and having you stuck with her for the good ending. Fourth reason and last: the game is woke and chalked full of girlboss energy, putting Jason on the sidelines through the dialogue with others in the cast while propping up Lucia to be this great criminal, mother, and girlfriend meanwhile she has to learn the ropes and gets pep talks from other npcs on how she complains about the jobs they do. This stinks because Jason has military experience and more criminal experience than her but the story focuses on her more. Only real positive things about the game are the visuals, random encounters, and radio music. Gameplay is very similar to gta 5.

author: goytheftauto6
quote:
After 13 years of waiting, GTA 6 is easily the biggest disconnect between critic hype and reality in gaming history. On base PS5, it isn't even a stable 30 FPS—heavy driving and gunfights dip into the teens and low 20s, alongside constant launch bugs.
Worse, Rockstar stripped out the classic GTA sandbox DNA: no mission replay menu, restricted NPC interactions, locked cars, and cut features that made previous games fun. The story also feels heavily one-sided and overly focused on a forced relationship dynamic rather than classic GTA freedom. Lucia is written to dominate every scene while Jason feels reduced to a passive, weak sidekick with awkward, strained voice acting, and the forced Niko Bellic cameo feels completely out of character just for cheap nostalgia points.
Charging $80 for a single-player-only code-in-a-box with no physical disc, pushing GTA+ subscriptions on day one, and likely paywalling GTA 6 Online separately in 2027 is pure corporate greed. Pretty graphics and a big map don't excuse an unoptimized, restricted game that hides behind FOMO and blind hype while locking players out of refunds.

author: HimHidora
quote:
Hot take: From the gameplay I’ve played, GTA VI feels more like Red Dead Redemption in Vice City than the GTA I grew up playing. 
Part of what I loved about San Andreas, IV, and V was how fast a random drive could turn into absolute chaos. The four-gun limit changes that. Picking a loadout makes sense, but I liked opening the weapon wheel halfway through a chase and coming up with a completely different plan. I miss some of the old free-roam options too, even little things like being able to pick up a sex worker. Those choices gave the city some of its personality.Focus looks cool, but I’d rather have a choice. Let me give Jason Franklin’s slow-mo driving for a getaway or give Lucia Trevor’s rage for a shootout. I’d replay the same mission just to try **** yeah, I know VI has big heists. Lester’s planning board was half the fun in V. You picked an approach, decided whether the cheaper crew member was worth the risk, and got to see how your choices played out. Even IV’s Three Leaf Clover nailed that feeling of a bank job spiraling out of control. The heists I’ve seen in VI haven’t hit me the same way.Vice City looks incredible. I’d still rather boot up V and see how much trouble I can get into on the way to a mission I’ve already played five times.

author: kazz54
quote: After over a decade of delays, astronomical budgets, and industry-halting hype, Rockstar Games finally released Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19, 2026. Instead **** masterpiece, what we actually got is a structurally unstable launch plagued by console-crashing bugs and an aggressive monetization model that turns a premium-priced product into a glorified subscription storefront.   A Technical Trainwreck in Vice CityYou would think thirteen years of development time would buy basic stability, yet GTA 6 plays like an unoptimized early-access build. The technical failures are not just cosmetic—they actively prevent you from playing the game:Hard Console Crashes: On PlayStation 5, players are repeatedly hit with error code CE-108255-1 within minutes of booting up, forcing hard crashes back to the home screen and wiping unsaved progress. Even worse, the opening cutscene causes console fans to redline and trigger false overheating shutdowns. Xbox Series X fares no better, suffering hourly dashboard crashes and full system power-offs.Soft-Locked Progression: Mission scripting is brittle. Doing basic activities out of Rockstar’s rigid expected sequence—such as upgrading a vehicle at night before meeting Joey after the lab fees job—completely breaks mission triggers, leaving NPCs missing and forcing players to abandon hours of progress if they don't have a backup save.Broken Physics and Collision: When the game actually stays running, Vice City feels held together with duct tape. Characters regularly fall straight through solid geometry during missions and police encounters, cars launch inexplicably into the stratosphere upon minor fender-benders, and boats violently clip into bridges. Combined with floating world objects and frame-rate dips below its already sluggish 30fps target on console, the immersion **** **** $80 to $100 Entry Fee Is Just the BeginningEven if Rockstar patches the crashes, the underlying business model is predatory. GTA 6 pushed standard console pricing up to $80—with the Ultimate Edition demanding $100—only to treat paying customers like free-to-play users.   Despite pre-release claims that the single-player experience would remain free of microtransactions, Rockstar immediately locked in-game content behind GTA+, its recurring monthly subscription paywall. Buying the base game is no longer buying the full experience; it is merely purchasing an entry ticket into Take-Two's revenue-extraction ecosystem. Between Ultimate Edition car upgrades interfering with early mission progression and core content gated behind recurring fees, the message is clear: your initial $80 isn't enough.   VerdictGrand Theft Auto VI is a monument to corporate greed and rushed quality assurance. Between a $100 ceiling, subscription paywalls creeping into single-player, and crashes that literally shut down your console, Leonida isn't worth visiting until it's heavily discounted—and heavily patched.

I have to start it with saying I'll explain my score. This game, when started up, had an extremely slow start, a start which I thought, okay, this will rapidly increase in speed. However, after only playing for 4 hours, I already immediately realized the very big flaws that hindered the performance of this game. In my opinion, these flaws may include, but are not only limited by, the extremely tedious tasks, annoying quests, and for lack of a better term, spiceless things to do.

Not only did I start out with just the quests, I'll be talking about the characters now. The characters are dull, bland, not well-written, and are clearly not as thought out as they should be for a game that has been in development for over seven years.
With most of the characters feeling like they're extremely based, and extremely average character. Nothing remarkable, or something that reminds me of them, nor something that will stick with me after having experienced these characters.

As for the map, I think the layout in terms of streets and functioning property places, like stores, I think the layout is okay, even though it could have been better with a more organized layout, meaning a more efficient way to traverse, more efficient way to get from one place to the other because sometimes it feels tedious going from the barber, to the gym, etc. When talking about the graphics, I wouldn't call them revolutionary, but they're definitely a step in the right direction, although we have already seen these graphics with, for example, Black Myth: Wukong, The Last of Us, and Horizon Forbidden West. Those games are extremely well and good made.

In conclusion, this game just felt like it tried to be everything all at once, but just failed on most aspects with delivering a mediocre experience for anyone. This for me, the mediocrity of this game, plus the fact that how much money they have spent and the amount of developers and the amount of time they have got to release this, plus the delays, make it for me a zero out of ten game!

author: SheogorathYeet
quote:
Not an acceptable product for 13-years and 2 billion dollars. Better games more deserving of the title of “perfection” were made for less, in less time, and with much more functional launches. 

This title loses nearly all charm and allure seen in previous installments, and feels like a rapid departure from the series as a whole. This game is intended more for the person seeking a mix of Sims with some crime, as opposed to the person looking primarily for the latter, despite still bearing a name that would suggest otherwise.

Main story flaws aside, the game leans too heavily on the whacky elements that previous games employed as Easter eggs. From ‘bigfoot’ to aliens, there is no grace or elegance to the bizarre side of the GTA universe anymore, not when so much of it is unavoidably discovered within 24-hours of launch (even despite the several hours of constant chores and errands bloating the early game).

Functionally, the game is Red Dead Redemption 2 with a coat of paint. Seemingly the same engine, largely the same interaction system, the same dialogue system, even the same quirk of using your vehicle for storage, which does feel more plausible with a car than a horse. Even things like the karma system is carried over as your “criminal profile”, and arguably the camp donation box taking the form of a joint savings account with your partner. 

Gunplay feels fine in this game, far from the worst I’ve experienced. The driving is abysmal, and NPCs on the road haven’t lost their homicidal tendencies that were so well known in GTA 5, which is much more annoying now that vehicle damage matters. The player character essentially has Deadeye which isn’t terribly surprising given Michael and Franklin’s abilities in GTA 5, though it does add to the overwhelming feeling that the development of this game was a lot of foot-dragging up until Red Dead Redemption 2 and its success could serve as a framework.

If you enjoyed Red Dead Redemption 2, there is a good chance you’ll like GTA 6. If you found it to be a drag, and couldn’t bring yourself to finish the story, GTA 6 will not be much different for you.

TL;DR - 3/10, awful story with unenjoyable characters, beautiful graphics, mediocre gameplay— all effectively taped onto Red Dead Redemption 2. Deserves a $20 price tag.

author: lfc009
quote:
SSS-tier world, weak story, bad leads—agenda-driven characters, no freedom. 
My Full Review of GTA 6

1. The World — SSS Tier

The world is excellent. It may be the best world I’ve seen in a GTA game in terms of detail, map design, and how alive it feels. Even compared to GTA 4 and San Andreas, GTA 6’s world is far ahead. The streets, the atmosphere, the details — almost everything is at the highest level.

2. The Story — Weak

This is the big problem. The beginning is bad, and the game feels restrictive. You can’t steal your neighbor’s car, you can’t kill people freely, and you don’t have the freedom you were used to in the older GTA games. The story didn’t pull me in. Even if the world is amazing, the story is what keeps you playing — and here it failed.

3. Main Characters — 1/10

This is the worst part of the game for me.

· Jason: weak, shaky, his way of talking is annoying, and he feels like a follower, not a protagonist.
· Lucia: cold, emotionless. She feels like she was written as “the man” in the relationship.
· Their relationship: dead. At the end of Chapter One, Jason was about to die, and she acted like nothing happened. No emotion, no fear, nothing.
· The overall feeling is that the characters were written according to an agenda, not naturally. Not because a woman is the lead — but because the characters themselves are not convincing.

4. Animation

· Main characters: bad, especially Jason and Lucia. Their movement don’t feel like real people.
· The rest of the game: excellent. NPCs, cars, the environment — almost everything else is great.

5. Freedom

At the beginning, it’s very restricted. It’s not like San Andreas, where from the first hour you can do whatever you want. Here, the game traps you in a weak story and gives you limited freedom.

author: ARCAS0
quote:
It’s sad to see my favorite franchise like this.

They have the map and the physics, but the writing is terrible — the worst in the franchise. The story and dialogue are very annoying, to say the least. Very little in the game can be called a good script. They could have done something so extraordinary if they had left the same assets in the hands of a better writing team.

The sound of the guns is terrible. For an action shooter, that’s unforgivable. All the guns sound like potato guns or at best spring-powered gun. None of them have a real firearm kind of sound.

The level design is also very bad for a Rockstar game. Many missions are as simple as going somewhere and doing some simple stuff. Then the simple stuff doesn’t work and enemies start appearing from everywhere. It’s not even that they’re hard to kill, the number of enemies for the area and objective just doesn’t make sense. They did that to try to make the game harder, but it didn’t work. They should have just improved the enemies’ aim and used a realistic number of enemies.

“Stay put and just shoot” moments are back, and no one asked for this. Once, or maybe even three times, in the campaign is okay, but here it’s all the time. You will feel like you’re playing a rail shooter but with good graphics. Another questionable decision by Rockstar, everyone in the game industry has agreed that rail shooters are dead for good.

Quick time events are also back. No one asked for that. And even worse is the introduction of the new Slow Time Events. It’s very simple: the game stops the animation and waits for you to press a button to continue the animation. This is ridiculous. Is Rockstar doubting the players’ ability to press one button? Even in a scenario where all the other buttons do nothing and only one button will work? It should just play the animation already.

The user interface is very weak. Changing the radio, the inventory, the cellphone minimap/GPS, none of these look well-made or even pleasant to look at.

Most of the cutscenes are longer than necessary. It’s mostly just close-ups and over-the-shoulder camera shots for long and meaningless conversations, very forgettable. Also, a negative of having two protagonists that are so close is that the talk is excessively abundant about everything. All the time something will happen with one or the other. The player already has the information, but the player will have to hear the information again when one encounters the other and they talk about what happened. In the end this is a disaster: all the story is told to the player twice.

The driving is good, a little floaty, but it works well.

You still can have fun when you’re setting your own objectives and doing what your guts tells you to do. But every time you go to do a mission, you will be a little annoyed with something.

Rockstar still can fix the game, but I don’t think they will. A patch changing the firearm sounds to more realistic sounds would improve a lot in the game. Add that with an expansion/DLC with new protagonists and characters for better dialogues and everything, with +20h of story and extra content after completion. And most important: a better writing team. It would be terrific.

author: Vanmccheese
quote:
Disgusting MTX practices, including a monthly subscription that affects your single-player world. To make matters worse, the content you gain through that subscription is removed from your world after completing Chapter 1. 

Horrible frame rate and optimization. Consoles should've either received a scaled-down version of the game or not gotten the game at all until next-gen hardware was available. 

Then there are the weird mission choices, like picking up groceries, building a table, or buying flowers. These things don't need to be done by the player. They could easily be shown in a three-second cutscene of Jason maintaining his relationship. It's not meaningful gameplay; it's filler, and Rockstar is using it to create a false sense of scale. Either that, or they genuinely don't know how to make these moments engaging.

It's your typical slow-paced, cutscene-heavy movie slop that normies eat up these days. It's barely even a game, at least in terms of the campaign. If we're strictly talking about the open world, then it's comfortably mid, I suppose.

Ultimately, the characters, themes, and plot are all very forgettable. I can't imagine this story ever reaching the iconic status of its predecessors, nor do I see it having much of a lasting cultural impact.

The game's long-term value will more than likely come from single-player modding and roleplay (RP). Although even RP could end up being compromised, considering Rockstar's partnership with NoPixel.

author: TheDish16
quote:
Una entrega bastante decepcionante.
Ya tenía mis dudas y temores viendo que el juego no mostraba gameplay en ningún trailer, y lamentablemente, el juego salió con una experiencia peor a lo esperado.

Ya desde RDR2, había mecánicas y minijuegos que simplemente me parecían tareas y quehaceres en lugar de ser experiencias divertidas pero inmersivas.
Lamentablemente, esta entrega continúa con ese rumbo, dónde ya no se centra en elementos divertidos y fantasiosos, sino en una entrega confusa que no sabe si entregar la experiencia deseada de GTA, o un simulador de vida real con sus tareas molestas y poco entretenidas

Las misiones son repetitivas y es lo que ya hemos visto en los GTA previos, solo que ahora sin diálogos o situaciones divertidas.

La cantidad de bugs en su lanzamiento es algo simplemente inaceptable junto con su rendimiento en consolas.
30FPS es algo simplemente lamentable para las consolas de esta generación y saber que en ocasiones baja a 22fps, ya es de plano una burla para los jugadores que pagaron entre 80$ y 100$

La historia nunca ha sido el elemento más fuerte de GTA, pero aquí simplemente se vuelve algo extremadamente flojo y olvidable si lo comparamos con San Andreas o GTA IV
Los personajes son poco interesantes y no tienen carisma.
No se acercan en lo absoluto a Niko Belic, ni a CJ, ni a Franklin, Trevor o Michael
Son personajes mediocres, aburridos y poco importa el destino de estos, sin mencionar los distintos finales del juego.

Teniendo en cuenta el presupuesto, el marketing y el costo de la experiencia completa del juego ($100), sin contar las malas prácticas como la falta de un formato físico o la inclusión de suscripciones para el modo de 1 solo jugador; 

Esta entrega es la mayor decepción de todo 2026 y hasta se podría decir en la historia de los videojuegos.
Que el juego más esperado de la historia sea tan mediocre y poco pulido, simplemente denota una decadencia muy grande para la industria AAA y una falta de interés por entregar experiencias divertidas y memorables.

Incluso arreglando el rendimiento y los bugs, sigue siendo un videojuego que recomiendo saltarse para darle un mejor uso al dinero que tanto trabajo cuesta conseguir.

author: sethmako
quote:
I've been waiting 13 years for this game to come out, as many other have, and unfortunately, despite all the hype and anticipation, what we got ended up being a massive disappointment. Where do I even start...
1. The game is limited to consoles, and the optimization is so bad that it can't even hold a steady 30 fps, unless you drop 1000$ on the highest-tier console available. No framegen to help it, no lower resolution performance mode, nothing. For the "next generation" of the grand theft auto series, this is a massive letdown, and leads to our next point.
2. The physics are tied to framerate. The drops in framerate not only give me and others headaches, but they severely negatively impact gameplay as well. Tying physics to framerate has been a no-no in the industry for decades, and despite GTA V not having this issue, GTA VI, running on the same engine, does. It's completely baffling why they would do this, as it causes game-breaking glitches like falling through the map, vehicles flying through the air, objects not moving as expected, missed inputs, etc. For 13 years of development, releasing it in this state is unacceptable.
3. The main characters are awful, and the story sends a bad message. Lucia is a woman that abandons her child, robs a bank, and ends up in jail. She doesn't regret it, and calls it a "bad day" to try and push the viewer to feel sympathy. She's cheating on Jason, she uses him constantly, and berates him over and over. And Jason has almost no personality whatsoever. He's completely insufferable to listen to, and he has no will of his own, just doing everything his psychopathic girlfriend that you have no option but to be with tells him, which leads to another point.
4. Story progression. It would be acceptable to have the relationship stuff as an optional side mission to get weapons or cars or skins, but having the menial tasks, chores, and the requirement to please and make the awful female protagonist happy to progress the main storyline is insulting and a complete slap in the face to the target demographic. This is GTA, not The Sims. People want to steal cars and sleep with prostitutes, not paint the walls for you awful lady-friend. That bring up the next point.
5. Where's the GTA? It would be one thing to change the formula a bit and create different ways to steal cars instead of all prior games having the triangle button be the only thing required to take anyone's car, but this is on a whole 'mother level of insulting. You need to clone keys to get cars, and you need to unlock the ability to drive more premium cars. You can't just steal an expensive car right off the bat, even though the realism of that is completely detached from reality. And even after gaining that ability, you STILL don't get to keep the car, you have to PAY to get it registered. Pay. To get it registered. A stolen car. Registered. In the single player campaign. It's just a big F U to every fan of the series, and completely against everything the franchise stands for (you know, THE TITLE OF THE GAME)
Overall, I couldn't be more disappointed. This game has completely ruined Rockstar's reputation for me, and I won't be purchasing any further entries from them. If this is the best they can do with 13 years and 2,000,000,000$, then everything else from here on out is a pass for me. 2/10

author: matt-fighter
quote:
GTA 6 : une prouesse graphique, mais une énorme déception

Note : 3/10 

Après plusieurs heures de jeu, je suis franchement déçu de GTA 6.

Il faut reconnaître que les graphismes sont magnifiques, les effets visuels impressionnants, la carte immense et détaillée, et l'intelligence artificielle des PNJ et des policiers particulièrement réussie. Sur le plan technique, Rockstar a fait un travail remarquable.

Mais malheureusement, GTA 6 a perdu une grande partie de son identité.

On a davantage l'impression de jouer à un simulateur de vie réelle qu'à un véritable GTA. Le réalisme est poussé tellement loin qu'il devient contraignant. Entre les alarmes, le clonage des clés pour voler des voitures et les limitations sur le transport des armes, la liberté qui faisait le charme des anciens épisodes semble avoir disparu.

Le pire reste les cinématiques et les dialogues interminables. On a parfois l'impression de regarder une heure et demie de film pour seulement dix minutes de gameplay. Les personnages passent énormément de temps à discuter, ce qui casse complètement le rythme.

Dans GTA 5, on pouvait rapidement profiter du monde ouvert, voler des véhicules, provoquer des courses-poursuites et simplement s'amuser.

Je ne suis pas contre le réalisme, bien au contraire. Mais il devrait améliorer l'expérience de jeu, pas devenir une contrainte permanente.

J'aurais largement préféré un GTA 5 modernisé, avec les graphismes de GTA 6, une carte plus grande et une police plus intelligente, tout en conservant la liberté des anciens GTA.

Rockstar a réussi à créer un monde incroyablement réaliste, mais semble avoir oublié qu'avant tout, GTA est censé être un jeu vidéo où l'on s'amuse.

Après toutes ces années d'attente, c'est une véritable déception. Pour la première fois, je ne suis même pas certain de vouloir terminer l'histoire, encore moins de chercher à obtenir tous les trophées.

Ma note : 3/10.

GTA 6 est peut-être une révolution technique, mais pour moi, c'est une régression en matière de liberté et de plaisir de jouer.

Un jeu magnifique à regarder, mais beaucoup moins amusant à jouer.

author: jomariseca
quote:
As someone who has practically grown up playing every GTA game, I was genuinely excited to return to Vice City. Unfortunately, this experience turned out to be a major disappointment. There is no denying that the graphics and gameplay are excellent. Visually, the game is impressive, and the overall gameplay feels great. But that's pretty much where my praise ends. The story is simply terrible. Jason, as a character, feels incredibly bland and almost robotic, often seeming out of place. Lucia isn't much better either. Both characters feel empty, lacking distinct personalities or meaningful character development. Compared to the protagonists of previous GTA games, they just don't leave much of an impression. 

The same problem extends to the side characters. Unlike previous GTA games, where even minor characters had something memorable about them, most of the supporting cast here feels like they're simply there to fill space. There's very little that makes them interesting or memorable.

And then there's the radio. It's completely lifeless and misses the Miami vibe that Vice City should naturally deliver. One of the things that made previous GTA games so memorable was how much personality their radio stations brought to the world. The music, DJs, commercials, and overall atmosphere helped define each game's identity and made the cities feel alive. Unfortunately, this time around, the radio feels like a huge missed opportunity. It simply doesn't capture that iconic Vice City feeling. 

After growing up with this franchise and waiting so long to return to Vice City, I expected so much more. The technical side is impressive, but a GTA game needs more than good graphics and gameplay. It needs a compelling story, memorable characters, and an atmosphere that makes the world feel alive. Sadly, this one falls short of my expectations. Ultimately, I don't think the game is worth its price, and more importantly, it definitely wasn't worth the 13-year wait. If this were a GTA game released after just a few years, I could probably justify giving it a 5 or maybe even a 6 out of 10. But after 13 years of waiting and anticipation, I expected something far more ambitious and memorable.

The biggest issue is the story, particularly its main characters. The narrative feels boring, and the protagonists lack the charisma, depth, and eccentric personalities that made characters like Trevor, Michael, and CJ so memorable. Their relationship fails to remain engaging, and the overall story feels more like a conventional crime drama than an authentic Grand Theft Auto experience.

Another major disappointment is the lack of the dark, irreverent, and politically incorrect humor that has always been one of Rockstar's trademarks. Previous GTA games made fun of absolutely everything: society, politics, the media, consumerism, and American culture itself. They weren't afraid to be provocative, absurd, offensive, or downright outrageous. That satirical edge seems to have been toned down, taking away a fundamental part of what made the franchise unique.

On top of that, several gameplay decisions unnecessarily restrict the player's freedom. Invulnerable NPCs completely undermine the sense of freedom that has always defined GTA. The removal of mission replayability is another frustrating step backward, especially for players who enjoyed experimenting with different approaches or simply revisiting their favorite missions.

And then there are the household chores, cleaning, grocery shopping, and other mundane activities. There's a difference between adding optional activities that make an open world feel alive and turning everyday errands into actual gameplay content. Realism doesn't automatically make something fun, and doing virtual household chores is hardly what most people expect from a Grand Theft Auto game.

Ultimately, GTA VI might be a technical masterpiece, but technical achievements alone don't make a great GTA game. The franchise was built around freedom, chaos, satire, memorable characters, and the ability to do things that would be completely unacceptable in real life. When those elements are compromised in favor of realism and routine activities, it's fair to question whether Rockstar has lost sight of what made GTA special in the first place.

A bigger, prettier world doesn't necessarily make a better Grand Theft Auto

author: DoctorMK
quote:
GTA 6 is the biggest bait and switch in gaming history. The people making it clearly didn't want to make a GTA game, they wanted to make a RDR3 game, they wanted to make "Bonney and Clyde 2026" but this was supposed to be a GTA game, and it's a failure at that. 

GTA 6 is a game about committing crimes and mass murder that doesn't *want you* to commit crimes or murder people. Everything is on rails. The relationship is forced, poorly written, and a female power fantasy. Everything about the Lucia and Jason relationship is obviously from a female perspective. Jason is a soulless Gollum that exists only to serve Lucia. Lucia is a horrible person that no man would ever want to see again. She never has to face any accountability for anything. 

Grand Theft Auto is supposed to be Male Power Fantasy the Game. Period. Lets look at Vice City for example: its a clear Homage to Goodfellas and Scarface without any of the consequences. Your character escapes a jail transfer is working for the mob within a day. You're committing crimes, moving up the ladder and there are no consequences for killing anyone. The game doesn't try to force morality on you. There is no "bad ending" you win. Unlike Scarface or reality, we don't want a realistic ending, we want to become the big Kingpin and sit at the top of the tower as a Billionaire and Roll Credits. All our enemies are in the ground. The End. That was Vice City. 

GTA 6 is a Relationship Sim game, Female empowerment fantasy, and it doesn't want you to commit crimes or be awesome. It wants to tell you a story and you're supposed to sit down and listen. It wants you to make the soft choices and retire from a life of crime with your gf and baby and kill as few people along the way as possible. Again, that is not GTA at all. 


You can't steal whatever cars you want. You cannot kill whoever you want wherever you want. And not just for story reasons. For "Modern Audience" reasons. There are tons of gameplay flaws too. There are missions you either cannot fail or have large windows of "crash the plane while triggering the cut scene and you're fine" type stuff. There are car jumps on a highway section that you can't fail. This is all within the first 5 hours of the game too, so who knows how much Wolverine nonsense they put in there. 

GTA is dead. Modern Writers killed it
RIP GTA
1997-2026

author: shayman420
quote:
Probably the most mid GTA game so far. I'm 20+ hours in and honestly it's just mediocre. Not even because of nostalgia or GTA 5 being so good, it's just genuinely not that great ****.

Obviously the graphics are incredible and the world itself is really well done but great graphics don't automatically make a good game.

The missions are mostly just boring fetch quests, caretaking and relationship building tasks. There's almost none of the humor GTA was known for or the ridiculous outlandish missions that made the older games so much fun.

I played RDR2 to play RDR2. I didn't buy GTA 6 to play a modern version of Red Dead Redemption. GTA used to have its own identity and it feels like Rockstar has let way too much of Red Dead bleed into it. Cleaning guns, hunting and setting up camp makes sense in a Western. Fixing your house and doing chores for your girlfriend in GTA is just ridiculous.

And Jason is probably one of the most soulless protagonists they've ever made. He's basically a Ken doll version of what a woman would imagine a strong gritty man is supposed to be rather than what the older GTA characters represented. Those characters were basically a man's fantasy of all the things he'd love to say or do if there were absolutely no consequences. Jason just feels watered down and completely lacking in personality.

Honestly this game just sums up everything wrong with modern gaming. Amazing graphics and a beautiful world but mediocre writing, boring missions and none of the personality that made the franchise great.

GTA was supposed to be about crime, chaos and ridiculous humor, not playing house and maintaining a relationship.

3/10 so far. Rockstar made an incredible world and forgot to make it fun.

What really bothers me is that certain mechanics and design decisions give me the impression that the game was built with a future online mode in mind. Some things simply feel strange and out of place. It doesn't feel like GTA. As for the story... the brilliant Bonnie and Clyde concept feels like it has been completely thrown away. Lucia is **** annoying, while Jason is extremely passive. It's as if they took the most extreme aspects of each personality and exaggerated them to the point of absurdity. And even though they can sometimes work well together and actually make for an entertaining duo, individually, I'd say they're insufferable roughly 85% of the time. GTA has always had strong personalities, YES! But there's a difference between memorable characters and characters who are simply exhausting to deal with. In Vice City and GTA IV, we had protagonists with very distinct identities, deep stories and, at times, genuinely melancholic narratives. Meanwhile, GTA V and San Andreas leaned much more heavily into comedy, exaggeration and ridiculous humor, but still managed to make their characters work. GTA VI seems to be trying to combine these approaches, but at least during my first few hours, it fails at fundamental aspects that a franchise like GTA, especially under Rockstar's direction, simply should not get wrong. And to make matters worse, we also have the return of an extremely important character from a previous installment, in a decision that, in my opinion, completely undermines the narrative development of his past and the weight of his own story's conclusion. It's simply frustrating to see a franchise that has always placed so much importance on character development make decisions that seem to disregard precisely what made those stories so memorable. My score is much more a statement of disappointment over wasted potential than a straightforward technical assessment. The graphics, the details and the Easter eggs were already expected. And enough with the hypocrisy, because if companies like Activision, EA, Ubisoft or even Bethesda released games today, got the things they're traditionally good at right, but failed at the one thing that actually matters, fun and entertainment, you'd be dragging their scores down too. ENOUGH WITH THIS MEDIOCRE GENERATION OF GAMES! WE WANT INNOVATION, BETTER GAMEPLAY, NEW AND UNIQUE MECHANICS, FUN AND, ABOVE ALL, WE DON'T WANT PRODUCTS, WE WANT GAMES!

author: Kbuto06
quote: 4/10 or 5/10 Unfortunately, this game is a disappointment. Let's get into the actual reasons why.First, let's talk about Rockstar's blatant disrespect toward its audience. They released this game at a premium price, running at 30 FPS with frequent frame drops on the PS5 Slim, with no voice acting in Portuguese, no physical edition, and riddled with several stupid yet genuinely detrimental bugs that negatively affect the player's ****, let's talk about the story. As of the time I'm writing this, having played nonstop since the game's launch at midnight on November 19th, the story has been absolute garbage. It's practically nonexistent. The plot is generic, the characters are generic, and most of them lack any real charisma. Sure, there are a few likable characters, but the overwhelming majority feel personality-less and completely forgettable.Take Jason, for example. He's basically a walking rock. All he ever seems to say is "Okay," "Alright," "Let's go," "Sounds good," and variations of the same meaningless responses. He displays virtually no personality whatsoever. Rockstar should take a look at its own previous work and remember the characters it has created. Even some characters who barely had any dialogue managed to have twice as much personality as **** for Lucia, she's neither particularly good nor particularly bad. Sometimes she's annoying, other times she's likable, but she's never particularly ****, moving on to the gameplay. I have to admit, it's actually pretty good, but nothing particularly impressive. Rockstar essentially mixed GTA V with Red Dead Redemption 2, and somehow, that middle ground ended up feeling rather bland. You don't feel the same urge to cause absolute chaos that you do in GTA V, but you also don't feel compelled to play as carefully and honorably as you do in Red Dead Redemption 2. Ironically, some of the game's best mechanics are directly borrowed from **** since we're on that subject, it's worth pointing out that this game brings absolutely nothing new to the table. It reuses mechanics from previous titles and improves upon some of them, but there's nothing groundbreaking or extraordinary ****, let's talk about the graphics. Yes, the game looks beautiful, but that doesn't justify running at 30 FPS. Rockstar was simply lazy and couldn't be bothered to properly optimize its own game. The biggest proof of this is that the game runs at 2K resolution with ray tracing enabled, without even giving players the option to turn it off. Games developed by much smaller studios have managed to achieve far more while delivering comparable graphical fidelity and performance. That's downright embarrassing for a company of Rockstar's caliber, especially considering how much money went into making this game.Finally, this game suffers from a severe lack of identity. There's nothing truly memorable about it. There are no truly memorable songs, aside from licensed tracks by outside artists rather than music composed specifically for the game by Rockstar, no distinctive art style, no particularly interesting design choices. It's an entirely forgettable game, carried almost exclusively by the GTA name and the Rockstar brand.

author: DragoonMeta
quote: GTA 6: A Stunning World That Has Lost Some of Its IdentityAs a longstanding GTA fan, I find it disappointing to feel so underwhelmed by a Rockstar release. This isn’t review bombing or outrage for attention. It’s criticism from someone who loves the series and wants it to **** was never just about graphics or the size of its world. Its identity came from freedom, taboo subjects, biting satire, dark humour and the thrill of doing things other games wouldn’t allow. It invited us to create chaos, take risks and pursue criminal ambitions on our own **** much of GTA 6 has left me feeling less like a criminal with choices and more like someone trapped running errands. Where are the ambitious heists, high stakes chases, daring escapes and unpredictable missions? There are flashes of the old excitement, particularly when Mattia is involved, but they’re too rare. Slower missions can build character and tension. Here, too many simply feel like chores.Jason and Lucia also leave me conflicted. Jason often feels passive, lacking the conviction and personality of Tommy Vercetti, CJ or Niko Bellic. Lucia has more drive, but her pursuit of status and impulsive decisions repeatedly create problems for them both. That’s not an objection to flawed characters. GTA has always thrived on them. My issue is that Jason seldom pushes back, even when their shared interests are at stake.I welcomed the idea of a female protagonist. My concern isn’t Lucia’s presence but the balance in the writing. A compelling, ambitious Lucia shouldn’t require a diminished Jason. Both deserve agency, complexity and the ability to challenge each other.I also miss the confidence, bravado, rivalry and unapologetic masculinity that helped give earlier protagonists their edge. Those qualities needn’t exclude strong women or more nuanced storytelling. They can **** satire feels muted too. GTA once revelled in exposing society’s hypocrisy through outrageous characters and uncomfortable comedy. Much of this story feels restrained, closer to a conventional television crime drama than the irreverent series I **** Rockstar’s credit, the graphics, atmosphere and environmental detail are extraordinary. The world is a technical achievement. But a beautiful setting cannot compensate for missions that lack excitement or a story that struggles to hold my attention.I don’t expect GTA 6 to recreate Vice City, San Andreas, GTA IV or GTA V. Those games had flaws of their own. I want the series to evolve, but evolution should expand its possibilities, not narrow them.I miss the feeling that I could attempt almost anything, make reckless choices and find my own adventure. Instead, too often I’m following instructions in a world that looks limitless but feels restrictive.I remain open to changing my mind as I play more. For now, though, this feels like a remarkable technical accomplishment that hasn’t consistently captured the spirit of Grand Theft Auto.This isn’t review bombing. It’s a disappointed fan holding Rockstar to the standard it set itself. I wanted GTA 6 to push the boundaries of freedom, not make them feel smaller.

author: yanakaevt
quote:
GTA6 has it's perks and plenty of flaws. Beyond having to take care of your virtual tamagotchi known as your girlfriend, so that you can continue playing through the story, because if you're broken up you can't even play as her (or accept missions). This, along with a boring story, bland characters, and a forced dynamic; you have the makings of a bad game.

However, despite it's flaws. The game itself has many upsides. There are cool dynamic events, stories you run into, wacky and zany findings, some hilarious content, an amazing map, and beautiful graphics to go along with the map. The game is super fun to run around in, when you're not dealing with the tedious slop forced upon you.

Certain aspects of the game are locked throughout the game till you go further in the horrid story. Such as being able to steal certain cars or go into venues that normally are open in previous titles Day 1 in game. Which would be alright, if I didn't have to eat slop just to get to the good stuff.

On top of that, with a less than optimal system running this game, you can guarantee some parts of the game will not feel great to play through. Jumping down to 20fps or below, you will wish the PS6 came out with this game.

Overall, I have to give this game a bad review. But I believe a 4 is fine as there are redeeming qualities. As well, I believe this is simply the start for something greater. I'm sure once online comes out and roleplay servers get going, GTA6 will become a pillar in gaming. But as a single player game, GTA6 does little new and falls short.

author: Sensui87
quote:
After waiting over a decade for Grand Theft Auto VI, the technical state of the game is honestly a massive letdown. Being locked to a sluggish 30 FPS on console immediately makes it feel dated, especially when smooth 60 FPS gameplay is the bare minimum I expect from a modern release. Worse still, my system can't even hold that target. The second I hit high speeds in dense Vice City traffic or get caught in a chaotic shootout, the frame rate tanks into the mid-20s, turning what should be exhilarating action into a choppy, unresponsive slideshow.
​On top of the dismal performance, my playthrough has been relentlessly ruined by constant, immersion-breaking bugs. I’m constantly dealing with aggressive texture pop-in, flickering shadows, and heavy upscaling blur that smears distant details into a hazy mess. Sound effects randomly cut out mid-chase, and I've already had multiple hard crashes force me to reboot right in the middle of missions. Instead of setting a new benchmark for open-world games, GTA 6 feels severely undercooked, and I feel like I paid full price just to beta-test an unstable, poorly optimized mess.

author: BestInSlot
quote:
Just finished the ending (2 different selections).
Disclaimer: GTA5 was my favorite game of all time, I'm a PC gamer and I bought a PS5 pro just to play this game sooner, so I may not be competely unbiased.

1. Story is not GTA. It's just not. There is no over-the-top humor, no WTF extremes that GTA was famous for. It feels like a knock-off made by a separate studio that seen GTA5 success, but did not had the balls to make it as spicy as original.
Endings just amplify it, I got a selection of 2 choices without a real choice - both of them lead to death of them. Internet told me if I played like a good boy in completely non-GTA fashion I would get option for different ending, but this IS a GTA game. 
2. First hour of the game is a compete boring trash, not even an action game, let alone GTA. I was forcing myself to compete it.
3. Non-mainstory events and episodes are the only thing that kept me from stopping and trying to refund. Some of them are funny, provocative, and give of glimpse of what this game could actually be if main story was made on the same level.
4. Price - is unjustifiable. I cannot give a game that cost 100$(80$ for a gutted version) with this quality anything higher than 2. Request AAAA price - get ready to be evaluated accordingly. I would give it a 6 if it was a 60$ game.

tl;dr: 2/10 garbage for its full price, but 7/10 ok if you get on a heavy steam sale for non-main story elements.

quote: I have a couple issues with the game. the story is good which is the most important thing, but this game is a perfect example of two things. why bigger isn't always better and why doing too much realism is a problem. First of the bigger thing. The map is simply way too big when you need to get somewhere. like when Jason gets his first hunting mission it's so far away it takes forever to get there and somehow you lose signal on the way and can't see where to go anymore etc it was very problematic. then in vice city it took forever to reach the side of the city where I could grab my vintage car from the ultimate edition and get back to the main quest, they could benefit a lot with condensing the size a lot more. making it this much bigger makes it take longer to get places and makes it a bigger chance you crash into things on the way. on that note we get to the realism stuff. the way some cars are near impossible to drive. muscle cars feel like you're driving on ice, the moment you start pressing the drive button and need to turn your car begins to do donuts, and the first time you get one of these cars is in a mission you need to escape cops so cops will get free shots while you're trying to figure out how the hell this car even works. then there's gas... why the f did they add gas in the cars? there's literally no reason but annoy players to force you to refuel a car. It's GTA not real life. i should be able to take my car and run anytime, not have to worry about running out of gas for some reason. then we have the equipment... i'm fine with only able to have two long guns and two side arms. what is a problem is you need to stash the long guns in your car or people panic. it's extremely annoying because when you actually NEED the guns you're in a mission where your car isn't around and now you don't have the guns you desperately need. Cops impounding your cars when you die is also really annoying, especially because it's hard to get in and out without being noticed, and then you have to waste time trying to outrun them again. and then you get the whole thing abut a big ass search area, even worse if a main quest is in the middle of it. then comes mission lock bs... there's moments in the game where you're stuck with "explore" It's extremely annoying for someone who doesn't WANT to explore and do side content and just want to do main story content, because it wastes valuable time I could have used to enjoy story. So it has a lot of flaws, some can be manageable, but it would have been better to have less realism, smaller size and more robust game

author: mackb996
quote:
Rockstar managed to turn what should have been a compelling ride-or-die relationship into a poorly written, conditional romance. Instead of building genuine chemistry between Jason and Lucia, the relationship feels like a progression system where Jason constantly has to earn affection through errands, gifts, groceries, and chores. The story never really picks up, and the game keeps forcing players to maintain the relationship by switching between both protagonists. Unlike GTA IV, there is no organic system of calling your companion to hang out, despite having a texting system.

The open world suffers from restrictive mechanics that undermine the very sandbox freedom GTA is known for. Certain NPCs are inexplicably invulnerable, some NPCs and random events cannot be run over, and trains conveniently stop whenever NPCs or vehicles obstruct them. You cannot take weapons into nightclubs, and the absence of prostitutes removes another familiar aspect of GTA's world.

Vehicle mechanics introduce unnecessary friction, with driving feeling excessively floaty and drifty. Long, uneventful drives, a lack of action, restrictive mission design, fragile vehicles, and selective realism further drag down the experience. Rockstar seems to have confused immersion with friction. Making ordinary interactions unnecessarily restrictive doesn't make a world realistic; it makes it tedious. The result is a game that sacrifices player freedom, organic interactions, and compelling storytelling for mechanics that actively get in the way of having fun.

For me, this doesn't feel like a proper GTA game. It feels like Rockstar has lost sight of what made the franchise so special.

And a 99 on Metacritic? Absolutely not. That's nowhere near how I'd rate this experience.

Maybe others will love it, and that's fair enough, but I'm not going to pretend it's brilliant just because it's GTA 6.

This is Grand Theft Auto, not Real Life Simulator 2026.

author: mal_ware
quote:
I can't believe I am doing this, but this is the first time I have ever bought a game (that I've been dying to play since the trailer) made me want to make an account to display how disappointed I am. This game made me and a ton of fans around the world wait 13 years to experience a game that would make us laugh the same way that GTA V did, and it utterly failed. Not only that, but everything surrounding it's release was just horrible to go along with it. Anyone who dares to leave a review without even explaining why they gave that review should be ashamed of themselves, including the critics. How is it that a majority of 100 scores from critics say very little about the gameplay?

GTA VI is a good game, but it is FAR from perfect.

It has massive performance issues, trying to target 30 fps when it struggles to reach 25 at most times. The story is subpar from that of GTA V: the story is long and boring about 65% of the time, leaving a lot to be desired for. The story is predictable and not even original, following the premise of old-time classics. Comparing this story to RDR2 is a self-report given that they are two different types of games. RDR2 is meant to be a slow burn, not GTA.

The movement is clunky and weird, and the combat is as boring as the most recent LEGO Star Wars game in the sense that you have variety, but you only need to mash one to win. Not only that, but certain inputs just did completely different things at most times.

The game is just overall way too easy. It just lets you skip missions if you fail too much according to my friends, since I didn't find much challenge in the missions.

Some minor critiques I have is that content and places are locked behind an ultimate edition paywall. Not only that, but you aren't able to buy and own properties now?

As for bugs, this game has a LOT of them. Yes, most of them are cosmetic bugs. But that does not mean that it won't hurt player experience, as it did for me. I have been softlocked in missions 2 times, forcing me to load to a previous save point that was several hours ago.

The characters, Jason and Lucia, are both insufferable for two distinct reasons. Jason is bland as heck, having the most boring dialogue I have read in a GTA game to date. Lucia on the other hand has so much more personality, but her personality is just being annoying, impulsive, and quite frankly stupid. In most missions, it always happens because Lucia ended up escalating the situation far more than it needed to, forcing Jason along. Speaking of Jason, he does so, SO much for Lucia, and yet Lucia doesn't do ANYTHING for Jason for the sake of being a good girlfriend. She only does things for Jason when he is injured, which is almost always caused by something she started.

What about their motives? Compared to previous titles and protagonists, she is selfish. Trevor is a funny and crazy man who does crime for being turned away because of his craziness. Michael does crime to try to change his life, away from abuse. And Franklin does crime because he was kicked out of an education and turned to side hustles. They come together and get roped into government dealings, eventually managing to overcome those that wanted Michael and Trevor dead.

Lucia on the other hand? She becomes a criminal because she decides to have a child "with" Jason before ensuring that she is financially capable to raise it. Jason however wants to live an easy life after his military service was over, only doing smuggling crimes. Why does he do larger crimes? Because he is forced to tag along with Lucia.

So what are the positives then? The only positives I can really give is that the game looks stunning, bigger crimes can be organised outside of missions compared to GTA V, and you can kill furries. That's it. Graphics are phenomenal compared to the last game, but I wish that they put more of that budget into other places.

This game, for being in development for several years, is just a major letdown. I was an avid fan of R* and their games, but this just leaves a sour taste in my mouth. I just wish that it could stand side-to-side to GTA V, both in writing quality for story and characters. When I went back to GTA V today just to see how it held up, I got really depressed. Not because of nostalgia, but because I laughed. Not after 30 hours. Not after 10 hours. Not even after 1 hour. I laughed within 10 minutes of GTA V. Why couldn't the writing be as absurd as the last game?

My final thoughts are that this game does not deserve it's critic ratings. 95-100 ratings are games that are defining and innovative. All this game did was do realism again, which isn't original. 80+ ratings should be games that are worth playing. 50+ ratings should be reviewed to see if you might like it. I give this a 20/100 because I don't think that I could suggest anyone to play this, not until it gets a rewrite.

The first sign this wasn't going to be the same was when Dan Houser left R* in 2020, and it clearly shows.
