author: black_groyper
quote:
Great, immersive atmosphere (for the free roam part of the game) on a large map with stunning graphics.

However, nearly everything that you can traditionally find in a GTA game (good writing, iconic moments, missions that genuinely have something leading up to them, etc.) is missing.
For example, GTA V had multiple setup missions to heists that were in-depth and genuinely affected the outcomes. In VI, most of these are single-mission linear setups that barely feel immersive/fun at all. Just one and done.
Rockstar openly spoke about how you'd have many choices on how to do your missions, unlike their previous games, with tons of unique paths. However, if you choose to be free and don't follow the strict sequence of events Rockstar has hardcoded, you will STILL get an instant mission fail. No changes there.
The only time your choices make a genuine difference is the game's ending, which feels very underwhelming as all of the (very limited) outcomes are predetermined by previous actions, some of which are undoable. For example, going on rampages (Playing GTA like a GTA game), can lock you into the worst endings possible with no way back.
Jason feels like a horribly written character with no personality, following Lucia around like her lap dog. There is very little synergy between the two characters, and most of the time it's just "Jason, do this side mission for Lucia to gain affection points" and "Jason, follow Lucia".
Not only that, you can't attack all NPCs in the game. Street activists are entirely immune to damage, and you can't drive close to them either. All NPCs are equal, some are just more equal than others. Welcome to diversity inside GTA.

I'd like to also state that the game is a buggy mess. Simply standing on top of your car can get you launched 50 feet in the air, you can crash planes without taking ANY damage or said planes exploding, and if you hop out of a plane right before it's about to crash into something, it simply phases through. (many people claim these bugs are rare, but they are VERY easy to recreate on accident). I even encountered a ship glitching over/under a bridge TWICE in my own playthrough of the game, in addition to the bugs previously stated.
The realism in this game feels like it was targeted at specific things only for the purpose of flaunting how realistic the game is, while leaving everything else behind. For example, when moving a couch during a mission Jason can move a lamp out of its way to make room for him to walk (WOW!), and you can see calf muscles moving while your character is running. However, NPCs can walk past dead bodies and not notice a thing, and when grabbing most items, they just phase into your hands, without even a generic animation to show how they got there. Even when pulling someone off of a motorcycle, your character can mention a "car", making it obvious that Rockstar didn't even bother to record separate voicelines. In GTA V, there were extra voicelines for when the player was intoxicated. Hundreds of them. Barely anyone noticed, and yet the developers still cared back then.

GTA VI feels like a watered-down version of V with better graphics, and this launch may be worse than CP2077. It doesn't help that Rockstar is missing nearly everyone who made their older games, and is beginning to outsource most of its work. AAA games aren't what they used to be.

More than six hours of this nonsense before you're finally allowed to experience something resembling the freedom that made GTA famous. I bought Grand Theft Auto, not a home improvement simulator!And where the hell did Rockstar's sense of humour go? The franchise was famous for outrageous satire, controversial jokes and making fun of absolutely everyone. Now all the sharp edges have been removed, replaced by corporate sensitivity and politically correct writing. The satire is practically dead, and it's hardly surprising considering the feminist driven creative direction. Apparently, being funny and offensive is no longer part of the GTA formula.
Then there's Jason, one of the most disappointing protagonists in the franchise. The poor bastard spends most of his time trying to please Lucia, incapable of doing anything other than being her obedient boyfriend. He can't visit prostitutes, pursue other relationships (exuding getting it from behind by his friend...) or even make his own decisions without worrying about upsetting Lucia. Meanwhile she seems to enjoy considerably more freedom, including being unfaithful. What is this supposed to be, a crime simulator or a masterclass in being a doormat? You're also expected to be nice and accommodating towards practically everyone, including characters representing particular political causes. Your decisions are constantly tracked and supposedly influence the ending. Even reloading a previous save won't necessarily save you from the consequences. Instead of letting players experiment, Rockstar seems determined to judge their behavior. Since when did GTA become a morality examination?
The censorship is another disappointment. GTA has always been about freedom, chaos and pushing boundaries. You can commit violence and murder against plenty of NPCs, but certain politically protected characters and activists apparently enjoy a different set of rules. What happened to the franchise that didn't give a damn about offending people?And then there's the technical disaster. What an absolute clown fiesta! The amount of bugs is ridiculous, including issues serious enough to break gameplay. In my experience, it's worse than Cyberpunk 2077 infamous launch. Naturally, fanboys are already working overtime to justify everything. Apparently, no bug is too serious when it's happening in their beloved GTA.Performance isn't much better. 30 FPS in 2026 is already disappointing, but frequent drops towards 20 FPS are simply unacceptable. We're talking about Rockstar Games, not some tiny independent studio struggling with its first open-world let's talk about the reviews. An absurd number of 100/100 scores, even when the reviews themselves acknowledge significant problems with pacing, mechanics, combat and performance. Really? A perfect score despite all these shortcomings? Some of these reviews read more like marketing material than independent criticism.
Finally, the real Grand Theft Auto experience might actually be the price tag. Multiple editions, increasingly expensive packages and premium pricing for a product packed with questionable design decisions. Apparently, the biggest crime Rockstar wants to commit is against your open-world game should give players freedom, not constantly tell them how to behave. GTA should be outrageous, unpredictable, funny and offensive. That's what made the franchise special.

After 13 years of waiting, I got a glorified household simulator with a toxic relationship, questionable performance, endless bugs and a morality system nobody asked for.Congratulations, Rockstar. 
You managed to make a game about criminals feel like doing your taxes.

author: WMediaLiteracy
quote: This game is 100 dollars if you want the full content available for the game. For that price tag, you would expect the game to be the most polished and bug free game you can get. That would be a fair expectation considering this game has been in development for around 12 years and is more expensive than a large majority of other games on the market. GTA 6 proves this expectation wrong by being littered in bugs, having an uninteresting cast as well as not giving you freedoms past games have. One of the main protagonists, Jason has one of the most uninteresting personalities out of any game I’ve ever played and on top of that, his voice acting is incredibly lacking in emotion or personality and instead sounds like an e-boy in 2020 trying to force his voice which just ends up sounding like grunts and mumbles. The game also punishes you for behaving like a criminal, which has been since the very first title in the series, a large portion of the activity in the game. GTA 6 punishes you for behaving like a criminal or doing traditional activities that basically everyone who has played a GTA has done like getting max stars. They do this by locking you into a “bad” ending if you do too much crime. I will say that the only two endings that seemed interesting to me in any way were the worst ending, in which both Jason and Lucia are killed, and the good ending where they both make it out. This good ending is only available through not pursuing crime in a game where crime is literally in the name. The other two endings, where either Lucia or Jason get captured with the other going free is very unfulfilling and does not satisfy the incredible wait for this game. Another large issue with the game is the lack of freedom. One example of this is the inability to use weapons in clubs or one certain side mission characters. In a way this feels too hand holdy, stopping you from doing things that could lock you out of quests, while also feeling restrictive. Rockstar would honestly have no reason to stop you from consequences like this because they allow you to lose out on doing certain quests by behaving like a criminal already, so this feels very forced and out of place. One last complaint for the game is the 30 fps cap. In 2026 I never thought I would see a new AAA game release with a 30 fps cap, especially from a company as large as rockstar with a 2 billion dollar budget. This leads me to believe that the game has been poorly optimized because even the strongest consoles such as the ps5 pro are unable to go beyond this 30 fps threshold. In conclusion, GTA 6 is a very mediocre game which is overpriced, overhyped and lacking in personality which made past rockstar games such as the older GTA games as well as the RDR series so great.

author: shotbyrima
quote:
The story and the everyday chores are not the problem. I actually think they are necessary to establish Jason and Lucia’s relationship, their circumstances, and the world they live in.

My biggest issue with GTA VI is that Rockstar seems to have prioritized realism over player freedom and enjoyment.

I’ve played for around 10 hours, exploring the map, flying planes, driving around, completing missions and doing side activities. Despite being a huge GTA fan who has played every installment in the franchise, I genuinely don’t feel the urge to return to the game anytime soon. And that is something I never thought I would say after waiting so many years for GTA VI.

The world is absolutely breathtaking, but somehow the experience feels strangely restrictive and hollow. Instead of feeling encouraged to experiment, explore and create chaos, I constantly feel like I have to be careful not to make mistakes.

The police are more intelligent, NPCs behave more realistically, and almost every action feels like it carries more serious consequences. Technically, these are impressive achievements, but from a gameplay perspective, they don’t necessarily make the game more enjoyable.

Previous GTA games gave you a sense of freedom that few other games could match. You could spend hours doing absolutely nothing related to the story and still have an incredible amount of fun. The world was essentially your **** GTA VI, I feel more like a citizen living within the rules of a virtual society than a player enjoying a sandbox.

And that’s the paradox: Rockstar has created its most immersive and advanced world ever, yet I feel less free within it.

I don’t want Rockstar to remove the realism or simplify the entire game. I would love to see an optional gameplay realism setting:

Classic GTA Mode: A more accessible, arcade-style sandbox experience, similar to previous GTA games.

Balanced Mode: A balance between realism, consequences and traditional GTA freedom.

Simulation Mode: The full realistic and challenging experience for players who prefer maximum immersion.

This would allow everyone to enjoy the incredible world Rockstar has created without sacrificing their preferred style of gameplay.

author: Booggers
quote: I waited over a decade for this game and I never thought the biggest issue with a new GTA would be how painfully bad and sanitized the story is. Rockstar completely lost the edge that made this franchise legendary in the first place. Instead of sharp satire that used to make fun of everyone equally, we got a safe, preachy, overly woke script that feels like it was approved by a corporate HR department. The jokes fall completely flat, the writing is scared to actually offend anyone, and the plot drags on with zero real stakes. It honestly does not even feel like a real Grand Theft Auto game **** worst part by far is the main cast. The male lead is a complete joke, totally bland, passive, and treated like a doormat for basically the entire campaign. He feels like a nobody compared to the female protagonist, who is written like the most cliché modern girlboss imaginable. She is always right, always effortlessly tough, bosses everyone around without ever facing real pushback, while he just stands there taking orders and looking incompetent. There is zero real chemistry between them, and by the halfway point I could not care less what happened to either of **** does not get any better with the supporting cast either, because there is not a single memorable or genuinely interesting character in this entire game. Previous GTA titles gave us iconic characters and unforgettable dialogue, while everyone here feels flat, generic, and completely forgettable. Every cutscene feels like a chore to sit through. Combine that with rough performance on PS5 and the same outdated mission structure, and you get the biggest gaming letdown in years. author: markelzubi
quote:
Más de una década de desarrollo, unas expectativas prácticamente imposibles de satisfacer y el resultado, al menos en mi caso, es bastante decepcionante.

Empezando por lo técnico, el juego presenta bugs y un rendimiento que dista mucho de ser óptimo. En mi PS5, la tasa de imágenes sufre para mantener unos 30 FPS estables, algo difícil de justificar en un lanzamiento de estas dimensiones. Pero es que, más allá del rendimiento, tampoco tengo la sensación de estar ante un salto técnico tan revolucionario respecto a otros títulos de su generación. Precisamente uno de los mayores reclamos de GTA VI era llevar el apartado técnico y visual un paso más allá, y no creo que el resultado esté a la altura de semejante expectativa.

En lo jugable tampoco encuentro una evolución especialmente significativa. No termino de ver ese salto que justifique tantos años de espera. Las misiones se sienten, en demasiadas ocasiones, aburridas y algunas incluso repetitivas. Me cuesta encontrar esa frescura que cabría esperar de una entrega que tenía la responsabilidad de reinventar, o al menos hacer evolucionar, una fórmula que lleva tantos años funcionando.

Por último, creo que la cobertura de la prensa especializada tampoco ha ayudado. Se ha generado una especie de unanimidad artificial alrededor del juego, con puntuaciones perfectas que parecen responder más a la magnitud del acontecimiento que a una valoración verdaderamente crítica de sus virtudes y defectos. Paradójicamente, creo que esta insistencia en presentarlo como una obra prácticamente intocable está provocando el efecto contrario en parte del público: un rechazo cada vez mayor hacia el juego y hacia unas expectativas que se han alimentado hasta niveles absurdos.

author: jchucky81
quote:
I was so insanely excited to finally play GTA VI. I went in completely blind, fired up the game, and watched an awesome cutscene. Then the prologue started, and I immediately noticed the framerate was terrible, so i went into the menu to set it to Performance Mode. Only to receive a massive slap in the face and a gut punch while lying down. To find out the BIGGEST GAME OF THE YEAR BY FAAAR, in the year 2026 DOSENT SUPPORT performance mode!!! I am playing on a PS5 Pro, with one of the best TVs on the market, last year’s LG G5. Even on a base PS5, this would be unacceptable.  What the … is going on??? 
The game forces ray tracing, which locks it to 30fps, yet almost every other modern game includes a non ray-traced mode that runs at 60fps. WHAT WHERE THEY THINKING??? And people are blaming PlayStation and Xbox for outdated hardware and weak CPUs. Yes, the PS5 and Xbox Series X are aging, and even the PS5 Pro is held back by its CPU, but Rockstar chose to develop this game for current-gen consoles. They must have known the hardware limitations on this consoles. The PS6 hasn't even been announced yet. It's probably still 2 or 3 years away, and a PC release date still hasn't been confirmed. Where is the logic here?  who cares how good this game will run on playstation 8. Everybody knows this game is going to last for 15-20 years, but I didn't buy a version meant to be enjoyed five years down the line. 

When Gta v and Red dead redemption 2 came out 30 fps was the standard, games did not support 60 fps back then at least on consoles. These games was freaking awesome and a solid 10/10 masterpieces, but if they had released as brand new games now in 26 with only 30 fps i would have given it a 0 star. And that's because games capped that low, is simply unplayable for this type of game in 2026. Any modern 3D game locked at 30fps is a hard pass for me. When you are used to only play open world games at a minimum of 60fps. Since the PS4 Pro and Xbox One X introduced performance modes back in November 2017. Some of us have been gaming whit high frame rate for almost nine years, and the biggest game of all time is dragging us back to 2017, because they wanted ray tracing instead. 
Rockstar is one of the biggest, richest, and most talented developer in the world. They’ve never made a bad game, only masterpieces, and I have no doubt this game would be an absolute blast at 60fps. Why Rockstar games made this decision is completely mind baffling!

How critics and other players don't care about the framerate is beyond me. Yes it's an absolute stunningly beautiful game with amazing detail when standing still and admire the scenery. But that illusion shatter the second you start to move the camera. In a fast paced game, the stuttering, choppy screen every time you touch the analog stick ruins everything. What is the point of better graphics in a game where constant movement is the whole point? Walking slowly or driving in a straight line makes up maybe 0.07% of gameplay, and standing still in menus or admiring the view is maybe 0.8%. Why sacrifice performance and smoothness, which affects 99% of the experience, just to make the game look prettier for 1% of the time. Imagine how "razor sharp" the image would be at 15 fps. Would people had accepted that too. Are my eyes that different from most people's? like the soap opera effect which most people don’t notice, but is the first thing I turn off on a new TV. I wear glasses, but my vision is only slightly impaired with a tiny bit of astigmatism. Is it just a few off us that even notice how bad 30fps looks?
Do most people play all games in fidelity mode? and rarely use performance mode? I'm sure they'll love this game. And if i was back in 2017 i would have loved it too. But coming from 60 makes 30fps unplayable for me. 60fps should be the bare minimum for any AAA game. 

Rockstar confirmed the game will not receive a performance mode on modern consoles, even on the beefier PlayStation 5 Pro. It's possible they technically could ​​​​​​release a performance mode on console. BUT THEY SIMPLY DON'T THINK THE VISUAL TRADE OFF IS WORTH IT!!! And that they won't budge, is what they have stated. All because of ray-tracing, which is actually possible to fix. But sound like something Rockstar is hesitant to allow.   WHAT???  Even my 66 year old father took one look at the screen and said it looked choppy. I would even sacrifice graphics dropping down to PS3 visuals just to avoid 30 fps. That is how much i despise low frame rates! I can count on one hand, maybe two hands, games which did not support performance mode, and i have played hundreds of games, but they all has received a patch that supports Performance Mode, with the exception of maybe a couple from 4 years back. My whole day has been spent writing this review, time that should have been spent playing GTA 6. this is 2026! I feel betrayed! Until the developers add a Performance Mode, my score stays at a 0. An absolute disaster.

author: Fuzzypet
quote:
Thirteen years. That's how long we waited for another mainline Grand Theft Auto, and the result is deeply disappointing. GTA VI looks spectacular, but its enormous map and staggering budget cannot disguise its shortcomings. I expected Rockstar to advance the franchise, not prove that technological ambition and great game design are two different things.

Start with performance. Every launch console, including PS5 Pro, is capped at 30 FPS without a 60 FPS option. In 2026, that's a major compromise for a flagship action game. Worse, even 30 FPS isn't guaranteed. Digital Foundry found drops during ordinary driving on base PS5 and sustained slowdowns in demanding combat. Xbox Series S fares worse, frequently falling into the mid-20s during driving and firefights, occasionally approaching 20 FPS under heavy stress. PS5 Pro is far more stable, but holding a 30 FPS ceiling does not make that ceiling impressive. Why must responsive gameplay be sacrificed for visual spectacle?

Then there are the bugs. Launch reports document characters falling through the map, clipping through scenery, erratic vehicle behavior, missing textures and progress-blocking glitches. Some PS5 owners have encountered repeated crashes, including during the opening. These problems aren't necessarily universal, but they are real reports. A release this anticipated should be far more reliable.

Even favorable reviews mention awkward context-sensitive controls that trigger unintended actions or make ordinary interactions frustrating. Looting, reloading and manipulating objects should not require fighting the interface. Rockstar's animations may be beautiful, but a realistic-looking character doing the wrong thing is not good design.

Combat doesn't feel like the revolution I expected, either. Beneath the visual effects, the familiar cover-and-shoot formula remains, and reviewers have criticized enemies that are too easily picked off or rarely flank intelligently. Bigger explosions are no substitute for more engaging firefights. That is a modest return after thirteen years.

The campaign is inconsistent. Reviewers describe slow stretches, storylines that outstay their welcome and some missions that feel like glorified driving assignments or rigid cinematic sequences. Yes, other missions offer more freedom than earlier GTA games, which makes the restrictions even more irritating. Why construct an elaborate sandbox if portions of the main story still insist on tightly directing the experience? I want to play Grand Theft Auto, not just watch an expensive movie.

The obsession with realism creates additional friction. Weapon carrying is restricted, with extra firearms kept in vehicles or lockers. That might increase immersion, but it can also get in the way of the chaotic experimentation GTA is known for. There is no complete first-person mode at launch, either, despite later editions of GTA V having one. Not every realistic mechanic makes a game more enjoyable, and losing a familiar option certainly isn't progress.

The map is extraordinary, but size isn't substance. More streets, interiors and crowds cannot compensate for frustrating controls or uneven missions. GTA became legendary because its worlds were entertaining playgrounds, not because their surfaces were photorealistic. I want memorable gameplay and freedom, not endless opportunities to admire reflections.

The writing isn't beyond criticism. Reviews note uneven pacing, overlong plot threads and satire that can feel stale. GTA's rebellious humor and distinct personality were central to its identity. Making everything more cinematic doesn't automatically make it more entertaining.

PC players were also excluded from the November 19 launch, with no confirmed PC release date. After thirteen years, a huge part of the fanbase is still being asked to wait.

Most baffling is the wall of 10/10 reviews. A game can be visually groundbreaking and still deserve serious criticism for its 30 FPS cap, verified performance dips, reported crashes, awkward controls and uneven pacing. Would a smaller studio receive the same forgiveness? A perfect score should demand more.

I'm not saying nobody can enjoy GTA VI. But longtime fans have every right to question its priorities. GTA IV and GTA V had flaws, yet they had distinctive personalities built around freedom and memorable chaos. After this wait, I wanted Rockstar to refine those strengths rather than become consumed by scale, realism and cinematic spectacle.

Bugs may be fixed and performance may improve. But putting presentation ahead of enjoyable play is a deeper problem. GTA VI is an astonishing visual achievement, yet for me a deeply frustrating sequel. After thirteen years, graphics and map size simply aren't enough. It feels like Rockstar remembered how to build a world but forgot what made that world fun to play in. A famous logo should never make a game immune to criticism.

author: Mmnin
quote:
It's an above average life/crime sim, nothing more. Perhaps revolutionary for interactive story production values, but this was marketed as the next great GTA mainline game and presents very little of the GTA formula everyone has expected and found so entertaining in the franchise. With tons of unnecessary restrictions, added surprise content that often is tedious or doesnt make sense, and extremely tame story, main characters and dialogue, this game is excessively mundane compared to its predecessors. 

The graphics, animations, and physics are all very lifelike and beautiful for what is there, however noticeable corners were cut for the sake of "ethics." Many of the things you think you should be able to do, you won't be able to. For every unneeded addition is one equally nonsensical omission, and even with all the ideas, attention to detail, and tech that went into its creation, it still often feels like just old game design with a pretty coat of paint, not something you would expect from a game 13 years in the making touted as the best game of all time. 

Performance issues. While I have only experienced a handful of mostly non intrusive glitches, the internet is currently overrun with examples of in-game performance issues affecting gameplay, again, not something you would expect from the budget and time spent on this development, not when other companies are putting out near flawless complete content at launch with a small fraction of the budget. Scope of game should not be an excuse to release unfinished or low quality content and it shouldnt excuse those issues from affecting the scores which indicate the overall game experience.

Now probably the biggest issue with GTA VI. 
With everything considered, this game has been overhyped industrywide for some reason unknown to consumers in its final form. The reviews that have given the game a perfect score while admitting the game has its flaws were not genuine in their scoring and I now question the legitimacy of all outlets. If this wasn't a GTA game, but labeled as a GTA spinoff or some other new property, marketed simpy as a life/crime interactive story experience from the makers of the Red Dead Redemption and GTA series, then I would say this game is deserving of 96/100, but with the marketing push, forcing a position as the coveted "greatest game of all time" and the premature GoTY push, and the fact that this simply is not the game fans had obviously expected, being a new flagship GTA, I have to use this review and platform to help counter the industry corruption in GTA VI's favor.

No this is not the greatest game of all time. It is an industry wide push to ensure that a particular type of game by a particular company is labeled such so that more people will be socially coerced into purchasing. GTA VI does nothing that other games in the life/crime sime genre haven't done before and in some cases even does it worse. It simply does a lot of it with a bit more polish and a higher budget. It is not a revolutionary title as claimed, no moreso than Read Dead Redemption 2 was. 

What pours more salt on this infected wound is that this game is digital only to minimize returns and prevent resells. They knew many players would not be happy with the gameplay changes, so they timed the launch to steal the "Greatest game of all time" label using arguably false review scores to propel and secure word-of-mouth/hype sales. This was the overall and defining "gimic" of this release, to pull the wool over the eyes of the consumer and heist as much money as possible at launch.

The saddest thing is, is that GTA VI does show a lot of developer love and labor. It does open the door to more "movie-esque" interactive high production experiences, albeit more interactive novel than game, and on its own it doesnt deserve the amount of controversy it is having, but we'll never know honestly how well this game could have performed on its own merits thanks to the commercial manipulation that has taken place.

author: eyeskiller
quote: A Technical Masterpiece, but a Massive Narrative DisappointmentI'm over 80% through GTA VI, and I honestly think Jason might be the weakest protagonist in the series.First, credit where it's due: Rockstar has achieved something extraordinary on a technical level. The graphics, lighting, animations, physics and environmental interactions are incredible. Vice City and Leonida feel alive, and the sheer number of tiny details is almost absurd. Exploring this world is an experience in itself. The developers responsible for it deserve enormous **** an incredible open world doesn't automatically mean an incredible story.Chapters 1 and 2 were fantastic. Jason and Lucia had chemistry, their relationship was interesting, and I genuinely wanted to see where things would go. Then Chapters 3 and 4 arrived and, for me, almost everything that made the opening compelling fell apart.What exactly is Jason's character arc? What does he want? What drives him? What changes about him? He mostly follows orders and reacts to whatever the next mission throws at him. Claude from GTA III never said a word, yet somehow had a more recognizable personality. CJ had his family, Niko had his past, Michael had his midlife crisis, Trevor was Trevor, and even Franklin had clear ambitions.Jason's defining trait seems to be that he's Lucia's **** to be absolutely clear: I like Lucia. I'm happy she's a protagonist, and my criticism has nothing to do with her being a woman. My problem is the writing.Rockstar spends two chapters making us care about their relationship, then separates them for what feels like 13 hours of gameplay. During that time, there's barely any opportunity to develop the very relationship the story is supposedly built around. Instead, we get endless detours with side characters I struggled to care about. The gym storyline in particular felt ridiculous and completely out of place.Then there's Yago. We meet him through street races, do a handful of missions, and suddenly the game expects an emotional response to the reveal that he's an undercover cop with feelings for Jason. Where's the buildup? Where's the actual bond between these characters? His scripted death happens regardless of our choice, making the whole arc feel like a cheap twist instead of an earned **** problem isn't the premise of any of these storylines. It's the execution. Characters are introduced to deliver plot points, not developed into people who matter.Separating Jason and Lucia could have been a great decision if the game used that time to give them meaningful individual growth. But Jason barely develops, Lucia gets some questionable detours, and the central relationship loses momentum. Yes, there are robberies and tons of optional activities, but I shouldn't need another hundred hours of side content for the main narrative to feel satisfying.That's why I can't understand reviews calling this Rockstar's best story. GTA IV gave us Niko Bellic. RDR2 gave us Arthur Morgan. Here, despite the enormous production value, I struggle to care about the person I'm **** verdict after more than 80% completion: GTA VI is a technological masterpiece with a deeply disappointing narrative. The world design, graphics, physics and attention to detail are outstanding. But Chapters 3 and 4 killed much of my investment in the characters and story. Maybe the ending changes my opinion, but if the protagonist needs the final 20% of the game to develop a personality, that's already a serious writing problem.Rockstar built an astonishing world. I just wish they'd filled it with a story worthy of it.

There were some genuinely funny moments, which got a laugh out of me but they seemed so few & far between. 

I think once it releases on PC, RP and private servers will be what really bring this game to life. But for a release title, 30 FPS is insane.

The TV and radio features are cool like always, but beyond that, I'm struggling to see what feels genuinely groundbreaking. 

This is far from a perfect game, and I actually think it might follow a similar trajectory to Cyberpunk. A rocky launch, plenty of criticism, and potentially a much better experience six months down the road.

I'm not writing it off, but I'm certainly not blown away either.

I’ve been waiting since 2013, and my patience has aged worse than the original Vice City soundtrack. For that kind of wait, I expected to be personally tucked in by Rockstar staff.

Fourth, the map is too big. I got lost, I got hungry, and I realised I’d been in the same state for six hours doing nothing. That’s just my life.

Would not recommend to anyone who isn’t already planning to buy it anyway.

Verdict: 1/5. Still playing it right now.

author: JeffGold
quote: Rockstar said the romance story was optional and then tied the entire story to the romance and locked core basic features behind mandatory story progression. You cannot even save a custom car until you complete TWENTY-SEVEN missions. If you save money and weapons before a certain story point, all your progress will be wiped and reset when you reach that point. Are we really doing the "take the player's guns and gear" BS in 2026, Rockstar? Not being able to commit violence in your neighborhood makes no sense and is immersion-breaking, as are so many other issues in this game. Rockstar promised the most immersive and realistic game of all time, and yeah, it looks pretty, but it's missing so many basic features that have been in previous GTA sandboxes—it's hard to comprehend. For example, you can only take 32 pictures with the in-game camera, and the powerful in-game photo editor isn't viewable inside the game. Rockstar decided to turn the open world into a Bethesda-style loot operation, with houses and businesses serving as "dungeons," and the entire world doesn't even feel like GTA; it feels like something from the millennial quirky Marvel Cinematic Universe mixed with Gearbox-style humor. Why is there supernatural and sci-fi stuff in this game that is played deadly seriously? In every other GTA game, none of that was treated as real; it was a device used to mock conspiracy theorists and UFOlogists. Now, apparently, Rockstar has decided that GTA lore officially includes giant hulks, Bigfoots, and driving dogs. So much for realism, right, Rockstar? Totally immersion-breaking and ridiculous. The game constantly punishes you for playing how you want to play and restricts what you can and cannot do. It isn't an actual sandbox game; it's an artificial world with scripted events like a Ubisoft or Bethesda game. This is not a "next-gen" game. It's just more of the same we've already seen in a hundred other open-world games from this console generation. I have encountered numerous game-breaking bugs where objects randomly start pulling me into them, clipping through the cells and then randomly launching me across the map. At times, the game dropped to a legitimate 10–15 FPS on PS5 Pro when I had a five-star wanted level and a lot of action on screen. A totally unoptimized mess. The driving is terrible; it's way too easy; no vehicles have unique physics; everything is floaty and feels like driving on ice, and you can make sharp turns easily. The crashes are highly inconsistent and the damage to health makes no sense; you can be driving 150 mph on a bike and get launched 100 feet into a tree and barely take any damage. Realism, Rockstar? Immersion? The gunplay and combat improvements are completely undermined by the game being so easy that a baby could play it. You and all the enemies are bullet sponges; you can run around like a combination of John Wick and John Rambo and have no fear whatsoever of dying. You have to be a complete idiot to die and be doing so intentionally. The game has unfailable QTEs; literally all that happens is a slightly different cutscene with a few words of dialogue changed to no effect. The game has no ending; you literally just get thrown back to before the last mission, so none of your choices matter at all. You pretty much can't even beat the game. Rockstar just acts like you never did, no matter what you choose. That's the worst condemnation I can make of Rockstar. Even they couldn't commit to forcing the player to accept the consequences they spent so much time trying to build the illusion of. Completely unacceptable. There is so much wrong with this game; it's hard to even list it all. Is it all bad and a 0/10? No. But it's closer to that than a 10/10, that's for sure. Jason and Lucia are utterly annoying. Jason is a mumbling, marble-mouthed Wonderbread cornball doofus; Lucia is annoying, unlikeable ghetto trash with no positive characteristics, just a completely unsympathetic character you're supposed to like for some reason. This entire game is played deadly seriously, and it is one of the strangest tone clashes and decisions for a GTA game. But this is barely even a GTA game; it's a game wearing the skinsuit **** game. Simply put, this is not for Rockstar or GTA fans. It's for the modern gamer. Triple-AAA gaming is utterly obsessed with making "cinematic" and "emotional" stories and pretending they are Hollywood. Just stop; it is bad, and you are cringe and talentless. You aren't David Lynch, you aren't David Cronenberg, and you are not Terrence Malick. And you aren't Errol Morris. Stop trying to write these terrible stories and force players to sit through hours of cutscenes to do simple bits of gameplay. The writing here is so far removed from GTA. GTA was meant to be a satire of American life, not a deadly serious romance story. Yes, it still retains some of the GTA charm and humor, but it's vastly reduced compared to previous games and constantly superseded.

author: NikoBellicIV
quote:
This game was clearly not made for Grand Theft Auto fans. We waited 13 years for this game, and what we got was a (at best) 30FPS mess **** that tries extremely hard not to be a GTA game at every step of the way. 

The story is mind numbingly boring, there has not been a single iconic scene that I've seen yet! The romance between Jason and Lucia feels extremely childish and shallow. The humor and satire from all the previous GTA games is non existent. The characters are forgettable with zero impact. When you play GTA, you want to rob banks and do cool ****, not buy groceries for your virtual baby mama and paint walls. Games are about escaping reality and having fun, this game forces you to waste hours of your life doing the most mundane activities. Also, the game does not allow you to make your own choices. You cannot shoot up nightclubs, you cannot harm protesters, you cannot steal cars in your neighborhood, etc... Did the people that made this game even play a single older GTA? This game feels like RDR3.

Moving on to the gameplay, the shooting mechanics feel extremely stale. They are directly imported from RDR2, which seems fine on paper, except when you realize GTA is not about a slow paced story in the Wild West, but a cartoony game about organized crime, police chases, shoot outs, bank robberies, etc... Several new mechanics have been added that complicate things that would be one button away in previous GTA titles. Why do I need to complete some half baked boring minigame to steal a car? Who asked for this? Even if it doesn't seem like a big deal at first glance, when you play a game for thousands of hours, this adds up. Small things like this make the game too tedious and **** all the fun out of it. Again, this is a GAME, not a real life simulator. The driving feels like a mix between GTA IV and V, which would be fine if it wasn't for the FPS drops if you go fast. 30 FPS in November 2026 is unacceptable, you cannot play this game without experience nausea. There are a bunch of tedious mechanics in the gameplay, like buying groceries/food, which would take too long to list. The overall point is that the gameplay is too slow, tedious, boring and has moved away from what GTA is, in a bad way.

The user interface is atrocious. This is something most people will completely overlook, but the UI of a video game is its heart and soul. You can tell how much love went into the game by looking at its UI. The UI in this game is extremely minimalistic, corporate and ugly. You could make a better UI using Claude ffs! 13 years and 2 billion dollars for this sorry excuse of a UI? This is undefendable even by the biggest Rockstar fanboys. The UI is the final nail in the coffin that makes this game feel more like a cheap GTA clone built on RDR2's engine than the next entry in the most successful video game title of all time.

To sum up, GTA VI is a corporate, safe game made for everyone but the fans of this franchise. The game feels like a cash grab made to maximize sales numbers, while reducing the chance of controversy to the minimum. This is the first GTA that has not received extreme public scrutiny from the media, and for obvious reasons. It is an absolute sell out, that will trick a lot of people that don't know any better with its beautiful graphics and immersive world. The world looks incredible, the random events are great, the graphics look immaculate, but this game will leave you unfulfilled and empty. That's because the soul of this franchise is long gone, leaving only an empty shell that is going to look more shiny and more polished with each new GTA, yet the players are going to wonder why the games feel worse and worse. Extremely disappointing from Rockstar games, but it's what was to be expected looking at signs from the company this last decade. The people know what Rockstar games has become, and we will no longer hold them on a pedestal. I hope this game crashes and burns to show the Gaming Industry what happens when you delay the most highly anticipated video game for years and years, you do a "physical release" of the game with NO DISC, you lock playable content of the base game behind a $20 paywall to market the game for $80 dollars, you hire 1600 Indians to cut costs, illegally pay every game journalist for 100/100 ratings, write a terrible story that is antithetical to the themes of the game and delay the PC release to shamelessly double dip on your customers and expect us to buy both the console and PC editions. Screw Rockstar and the glazers of this game.

There are a LOT of other issues with this game that I'm not getting into but other reviewers mention. A 0/10 Rating is too generous.

author: kurokku
quote:
I waited 13 years for this, paid full price, and honestly? I feel straight-up scammed. Don't get me wrong, Vice City looks insane, and all those fake 10/10 review scores from big outlets made me think we were getting the game of the century. But once you actually boot it up, it’s not Grand Theft Auto .it’s a laggy, overpriced 9-to-5 dating and chore simulator.
First off, playing a massive AAA game in late 2026 locked at 30 FPS with zero performance mode is a complete joke. On my OLED TV, fast driving and camera pans turn into a blurry, juddery mess. Even worse, my base PS5 can't even hold 30 FPS—blow up a few cars or start a big police chase and the frame rate tanks to 25 FPS and stutters like crazy. On top of that, the driving feels weirdly clunky and unnecessarily frustrating.
The story and characters are the biggest letdown, though. You can immediately tell the original writers behind GTA 5 and Red Dead left Rockstar years ago. The plot has terrible pacing and completely falls apart by the end. Jason has zero soul—he’s literally like Jon Snow in the final season of Game of Thrones, just nodding along saying "yeah" and "yes, my queen" while Lucia constantly nags him. None of the side characters are memorable either.
Worst of all, the first 10 to 20 hours are pure misery. GTA 5 started with an epic bank heist; GTA 6 forces you to spend three or four evenings picking up Lucia's laundry, buying groceries (with an unskippable cutscene just to carry bags inside), buying her flowers, flipping burgers, getting a gym membership to work out, and fixing a house with quick-time events. I didn't wait 13 years to play The Sims—I can do chores in real life for free. Throw in running back to your car trunk for heavy weapons, an overly punishing police heat system, no online mode at launch, and a "physical" box with just a download code inside, and it's an absolute disaster.
Pretty graphics can't save a broken, soulless chore simulator. 2/10

author: JTVJuice
quote: GTA 6 – A Game That Seems to Have Forgotten What Made GTA FunHonestly, I’m finding it hard to understand who this game is actually being made for. At some point, Rockstar seems to have confused realism with entertainment. I don’t need a second job when I turn on my Xbox, and I certainly don’t need to simulate the inconveniences of everyday life in a game that’s supposed to be an escape from it. Between the meaningless chores, unnecessary errands, excessive animations, and hyper-realistic mechanics that seem to exist solely to make simple tasks take longer, the experience feels more like a commitment than entertainment. I understand wanting an immersive world, but immersion doesn’t mean making every little thing a chore. There’s a difference between creating a living, breathing world and wasting the player’s time.What bothers me even more is how restricted the experience feels compared to what traditional GTA games offered. GTA was always about freedom. The freedom to cause absolute chaos, explore, experiment, get into ridiculous situations, and play the game however you wanted. That’s what made the franchise special. Now it feels like you’re constantly being funneled into mundane activities and scripted interactions instead of being given the freedom to create your own fun. And don’t even get me started on the two protagonists. The dynamic between them is exhausting, and the female character in particular comes across as incredibly irritating. Instead of feeling like two compelling characters navigating an interesting criminal world, their relationship and constant interpersonal drama make the whole experience feel like a modern dating simulator with a criminal backdrop.I get on GTA to escape real life, not recreate it. I already have responsibilities, errands, relationship complications, and enough pointless inconveniences waiting for me when I turn off the console. I don’t need to spend my free time doing digital versions of the same things. Give me the freedom, absurdity, unpredictability, and unapologetic fun that made GTA what it is. I don’t need a second life simulator disguised as a Grand Theft Auto game. Realism is great when it enhances gameplay, but when it starts getting in the way of actually having fun, something has gone seriously wrong. I wanted Grand Theft Auto, not Grand Theft Adulthood.

author: NavyandGuts
quote:
GTA 6 represents everything I fear modern Rockstar has become, and a complete abandonment of the values that made this franchise legendary in the first place.

The original Grand Theft Auto games were built on irreverence, controversy, unapologetic satire, dark humour, and an absolute refusal to bow to social expectations. Rockstar wasn’t afraid to offend, provoke, mock institutions, expose hypocrisy, or push boundaries. That rebellious spirit was the very identity of GTA.

What made GTA special wasn’t simply its open world, graphics, or gameplay. It was its attitude. Its willingness to be politically incorrect, morally ambiguous, provocative, and downright outrageous. It was a satirical reflection of society that spared absolutely nobody.

Somewhere along the way, it feels like Rockstar has forgotten what made its own creation special. Instead of embracing the fearless creative identity that defined the franchise, modern GTA increasingly feels like a product designed to satisfy corporate expectations and avoid controversy.

I don’t want a sanitized version of Grand Theft Auto. I don’t want a game afraid of its own identity. I don’t want Rockstar trying to convince me how progressive, acceptable, or culturally relevant it can be.

I want the Rockstar that had the courage to make fun of everyone and everything, without discrimination or apologies.

GTA was never supposed to be comfortable. It was supposed to be outrageous.

And if Rockstar has abandoned that philosophy, then it hasn’t just changed the franchise. It has abandoned the very spirit that made it great.

I don’t miss the old graphics, mechanics, or technology. I miss the old Rockstar.

author: Elnaito
quote:
GTA VI: 13 Years, $100, and a Bug Compilation Rockstar Calls a Masterpiece.

We crucified Cyberpunk 2077 for way less than what this thing shipped with. $100 for an incomplete, boring, bugged game. Just a scam, textbook example. 

Start with launch day. Thirteen years of development, and within hours people were falling through the map, clipping through walls, watching planes phase through buildings and NPCs swim sideways like broken animatronics. Crashes in the prologue. The PROLOGUE. On base PS5 and Series X. Softlocks in early Lucia missions. Lost saves. Missing textures. Audio dropping out. PSN buckling under the launch. There's an entire Reddit megathread just to catalogue the damage. "Not even 15 minutes in and a game-breaking bug" isn't a meme, it's a user review.

And it all runs at 30fps. In 2026. On a console exclusive that skipped PC at launch. Driving, the thing you do most in a game literally called Grand Theft AUTO, feels like wading through syrup.

Speaking of the title: Grand Theft Auto, where you can't just grand-theft an auto anymore. Old beaters, sure. Anything modern? Scan it with a phone app, grind a hacking skill, wait for the story to hand you a Key Cloner. Luxury cars come with GPS trackers that ping the cops. Realistic? Congrats. Fun? The one fantasy this franchise is named after is now locked behind a progression system. Hop in, hit the gas, nothing happens. Peak 2026.

That's the real disease: Rockstar confused realism with quality. People watching others play are comparing it to The Sims, not GTA. "You can't just wreak havoc like in GTA 5" is the most damning sentence anyone has said about this game. The world is gorgeous, but every system is built to make chaos cost more and feel worse. Rockstar even admitted they prototyped full grocery runs and fridge restocking. That's where the design head was at. They cut that one feature, but the mindset survived everywhere else: errands, chores, friction, "immersion." Nobody buys a GTA to roleplay a supermarket receipt.

Then the missions. The same railroaded, hand-holding Rockstar formula people have been complaining about since RDR2: follow the marker, stay on the path, take a different route and get "Mission Failed." Thirteen years and the design philosophy is still "watch the cutscene, then do exactly what we tell you."

Now the money. $80 for Standard, $100 for Ultimate. It's the first $80 PS5 game, and it just set the price floor for the whole industry. For that you get single-player only, no online mode, reports of content gated behind the $100 tier, and a "physical edition" that's literally a download code in a box. You pay premium-plus and you don't even get a disc.

And yet: Metacritic 99. Tied with Ocarina of Time. 150+ reviews, almost all perfect, many quietly admitting problems with combat, mission design, performance and bugs, then giving it a 10 anyway. Critics played pre-release builds and barely mentioned what players hit on day one. When a 10/10 sits right next to a bug megathread, the score stops measuring the game and starts measuring access.

Remember Cyberpunk? Pulled from the PlayStation Store, mass refunds, years of apology patches. CD Projekt got dragged through the mud, and rightfully so. GTA VI ships glitchy, at 30fps, gated, overpriced, and it gets a parade. Same crime, different defendant, and this jury showed up with VIP passes.

Will Rockstar patch it? Probably. They have the money and the track record. But "they'll fix it later" was never an excuse for CDPR, and it shouldn't be one for the richest studio in gaming. Thirteen years. $100. This is what they shipped.

author: MinoriaPrime1
quote:
*long review incoming* 
Alright so, this is a long review ahead boyos, get your popcorn and drinks ready for this one. 
I made an account just to say just how much I hate this worthless excuse and what these troglodytes have managed to do to this beloved franchise with just a single game. As a long time Rockstar and GTA fan, this game seriously pissed me off.

(You can skip this bit to read just the review of the game if you wish)

VVVVVVVVVV
Before we even get to the game itself, let's cover on what happened before the game even dropped:
Right from the get-go we're already starting off bad with the announcement that there will NO disk for the game, and me, being a lover of disk games, already left a bad taste in my mouth. THEN when you finally start shipping the games out with the codes in the boxes, you **** couldn't have bothered to actually put the damn things in a spot where people couldn't just outright steal them, not to mention the fact that some boxes shipped WITHOUT a code, and when people were flooding your customer support, of which I know a few of my friends that got screwed over, you either outright ignored refunds or just ignored everyone with radio silence.
VVVVVVVVV

Now, onto *THE GAME ITSELF* 

This... thing spits in the name of Grand Theft Auto. 
it has basically none of the DNA of what made the previous iterations of GTA so awesome, which is seriously impressive how they even managed to pull that off. It is GTA only in name. 
I have played every installment since GTA III, and I loved them all, loved the characters, the satire, the comedy, the freedom to do whatever you want, the list goes on. GTA VI, on the other hand, has basically none of what made the previous games amazing. The *only* thing I can genuinely say Is improved is the graphics and the car physics, but that's about where it ends, and it's not enough to counter everything else that is wrong with this dumpster fire ****.

*THE PROTAGONISTS*

Jason and Lucia are both terrible, bland characters, with personalities not too dissimilar to that of a wet paper towel. They are a microscopic fragment of what previous protagonists were in the GTA franchise. Oh but you may be asking "What about GTA 5? The protagonists are all also terrible people!", and you would be right. They ARE terrible people. However, I never felt like the game forced me to actually like them as people, and they actually had the chemistry, charisma and actual development to carry them, while this game does the opposite. 
Like seriously... did no one even clock that Lucia left her goddamn baby to commit a crime at the start of the game?? and then throughout the story it constantly felt like the game was yelling at me "LOVE HER GODDAMNIT"

*THE STORY*

The start was slow, but I didn't mind, I say to myself, since I've sunk ~600 hours in RDR2, I think it'll really pick up after chapter 1, but It never feels like it does, the whole time I'm thinking "Maybe it'll get better, might just need more time" and the chapters go on by and... I realize I've reached the end of the damn game... What??? How does end like that??? The whole story was just a romance nothing-burger with stupid quests all around. Who looked at the storyboard and went "Yup, that's the one". How and why anyone with a singular neuron firing off in their brain would say this is the best GTA, I have no idea. Rockstar have genuinely lost the plot. 
Anyone who praises this game deserves to be publicly shamed and have rancid sewer water dripped down their nose while they're tied to a chair upside down.
 
Every GTA game made me love the characters, and just get lost in the world, Red Dead Redemption 2 made me bawl my eyes out like a child. But this game made me feel absolutely nothing but boredom, disappointment and anger at how far they've fallen as a developer and took a big ole' steaming, fat, oily dump all over their fanbase, and people are celebrating it. 

Spend your 100$ elsewhere and don't make the same mistake I did.

Sincerely, **** you Rockstar. 
Never make another video game again, go **** on ogre toes.

author: mamadulce69
quote:
This is not a GTA game. This is a $80 monument to corporate cowardice and creative bankruptcy, and the people calling it a masterpiece are either paid, delusional, or so desperate for a new GTA that they’ll orgasm over anything Rockstar dumps on them.**

Thirteen years. A reported billion-dollar budget. The most hyped piece of entertainment in modern history. And what did we get? A glossy, overlong Florida tourist brochure with guns, where the biggest innovation is that the female lead can also commit crimes while the game pretends this is somehow revolutionary feminism instead of the same old blood-soaked sandbox with a new coat of pastel paint.

Lucia and Jason are the most aggressively marketed “complex couple” in gaming history, and their chemistry has all the heat of two wet paper bags dry-humping in a humid alley. The writing keeps insisting their relationship is profound and tragic while every other mission reduces them to interchangeable shooting galleries. Rockstar used to have teeth. Now they have focus-group-approved “representation” and the same tired satire of influencers, cops, and Southern trash that felt edgy in 2013 and just feels exhausted in 2026.

The world is massive, yes. It’s also the most expensive empty shell ever built. NPCs still move like they’re on rails, the AI still has the decision-making capacity ****, and the “living city” mostly consists of background chatter designed to make streamers say “wow the detail” while the actual gameplay loops remain identical to GTA V. Drive. Shoot. Escape. Repeat. The physics still break in embarrassing ways. The frame rate still chokes when too many people are on screen. After more than a decade of development, current-gen hardware still can’t run this thing without compromises. That’s not ambitious. That’s incompetent.

And then there’s the Ultimate Edition scam. You paid the extra money for the “Ultimate” package, right? The one they waved in your face during pre-orders like it was some exclusive paradise of content? Congrats, you’re locked out of half of it until you grind through specific story beats and progress gates. Want that special vehicle, that exclusive outfit pack, those early access bonuses they sold you? Too bad. The game literally holds your paid content hostage until you’ve jumped through the exact narrative hoops Rockstar decided you needed to complete first. It’s not a reward. It’s a leash. They charged you more money and then put a progress wall in front of the very things you already bought. That is pure, unfiltered contempt for the player.

The online is already positioning the single-player as the appetizer so they can milk microtransactions and FOMO events for the next ten years. The same exact playbook that turned GTA Online into a predatory casino with cars. Anyone surprised by this has been living under a rock made of Rockstar’s own marketing.

The people giving this a 10/10 are not reviewing a game. They’re reviewing their own sunk-cost emotional investment. They’re reviewing the trailer they watched fifty times. They’re reviewing the idea of GTA 6, not the thing that actually shipped. The rest of us are stuck with a bloated, safe, self-congratulatory open-world that mistakes scale for substance, nostalgia for progress, and paid content locks for “player engagement.”

author: slavanofficial
quote: After the departure of Dan Houser, who was responsible for deep storytelling and dramaturgy, his brother Sam Houser chose a strategy of visual spectacle and smoke and mirrors instead of thoroughly developed main characters.Jason and Lucia act like two fifteen-year-old immature teenagers whose sole motivation is making money, while the child serves merely as a formal plot anchor. Lucia goads Jason into getting rich by using her cellmate’s boyfriend’s yacht as an example. Instead of considering realistic, legal ways out for the sake of their child and family, the protagonists immediately decide to rob and kill. Prison leaves a mark on anyone, and upon release, a woman who ended up there out of desperation and a willingness to take a risk for her son would hardly jump straight back into crime. After getting parole, she would have gone to Liberty City to be with her child, far away from the criminal underworld, to start a quiet life.Donnie and Cal are two completely unserious characters with the psychological profile of teenagers. The entire premise hinges on Donnie overdosing in his cabin, getting captured by the "Kingfishers," who then kidnap Lori and feed Donnie himself to the pigs. Meanwhile, Cal, who was mourning Donnie so deeply, snaps right back to his usual mood just two minutes later after a single fishing trip, and the script doesn't even explain why he was grieving and drinking beer to sad music in a lawn chair **** first, Brian comes across as a serious man with experience and life principles, but once it becomes clear what a pushover he is—how easily he yields to the younger crowd and decides to quit after rescuing Lori—all interest in him as a character vanishes instantly.Jason is the most foolish, underdeveloped, flat, and emotionless protagonist, which is the exact definition of broken dramaturgy. After surviving a gunshot wound and spending a week in a motel on the brink of death and pumped full of pills, he immediately suggests going back to robbing and killing, and Lucia agrees without a second's hesitation. He is a disaster of a character—it takes real effort to write this level of **** a mother and as a woman, Lucia is no different: she behaves like a fifteen-year-old with zero psychological brakes and no real pressure anchoring her decisions. If the two of them had crushing debts and extreme circumstances forcing their hand, one could at least understand their willingness to survive at any cost. Instead, all they have is a bag with a statuette and a hard drive from some rich spoiled kid—who makes zero sense as a trusted associate to older, heavyweight criminals, because reckless risks have no place in serious business.Raul is just as incompetent. He seems to have a crew and some strategic sense when he uses the duo as bait during their first meeting, yet later at the hideout, he announces they need to hit three banks in downtown Miami within half an hour. This is utter absurdity—and it’s not even just about the sheer unrealism of the other two Fleeca branches not being immediately locked down by police and security after the first hit, but about Jason and Lucia’s reaction. No planning, no tactics, no preparation—Jason simply tells Raul, "Yeah, we're ready, let's do it," and that's it. Because of this, the final Bonnie-and-Clyde-style shootout evokes zero emotion: they are just childish background caricatures who, in reality, would have been eliminated before they even got into the **** other episodes stand out for their complete lack of logic: the hospital scene and Booby’s first mission in the ghetto. Lucia walks into the hospital to bust Jason out because there’s supposedly a hit out on her and their house was burned down. She unplugs him from the machines, wheels him out in a wheelchair while he shoots at mercenaries on the move, hijacks an ambulance, drags him backward down a pier into a boat, and they escape the police out in the ocean. Writing this with a straight face is a total catastrophe—in reality, she wouldn't have made it past the hospital reception **** for Booby’s first mission: he tasks Jason with moving product and claims that cut product is more profitable than pure. Someone who knows nothing about this business walks into a deal in the ghetto and offers stepped-on product to local guys. The game literally tells players that selling cut product is totally fine and profitable, whereas in reality, he would have been shot on the spot for pulling a stunt like that, and no Dre'Quan could have saved him, even with the warning that a lone outsider gets killed in Crosstown. Worse still, Jason goes along with it: even though you're given a choice between pure or cut product, the supplier says pure runs at a loss, and the developers put the higher-profit icon directly on the cut option.

author: amase
quote:
It should've been called "Jason & Lucia"  NOT GTA 6
Where did things go wrong? Waiting 13 years for this, only to watch the core identity of the franchise get tossed out the window, is completely insane. Did the developers even ask longtime fans what they actually wanted? The only two things worth praising are the graphics and the size of the map, everything else is horrendous. I genuinely don’t understand how people are giving this a 10 out of 10. We have seen this exact pattern with multiple games in the past, and it’s time to stop pretending it’s acceptable.Look at Monster Hunter. Monster Hunter: Wilds had a rough launch with performance issues and got hit with negative reviews early on, but a couple of months later they patched it and the positive reviews rolled in. The reason I’m using Monster Hunter as an example is because they have stuck to the same core formula for 22 years, and they still make great games. Straying away from the original formula that made your franchise legendary makes zero **** story here is rough and falls completely flat, they honestly should have just stuck with one protagonist. Even worse, why are developers removing features that worked in past games instead of building on them? Stop stripping things out and start adding more content that expands on those features. On top of that, the controls feel clunky, there are noticeable glitches, there’s no autosave, and it runs at 30 FPS. Fix those issues and maybe I’ll bump my score up to a 1 out of 10.Whatever happened to the classic GTA mindset of not caring about rules and doing whatever you want? Sure, you can technically ignore the main missions and mess around in free roam, but if you actually want to unlock features and trigger more world events, you are forced to play through the story. With 13 years of development, the studio could have easily given us way more freedom and player choice. I do not care about the forced couple dynamic at all. Keep Jason and Lucia in the game if you want, but at least give players the option to opt out of the relationship storyline, or include another protagonist we can switch to. After 13 years, they could have given us multiple distinct protagonists and let us shape their personalities, lifestyles, and romantic choices however we wanted. Look at Baldur's Gate 3, those developers managed to build vibrant, engaging characters where you have complete freedom over who they are and who they date, whether straight, gay, or anything else. Here, you have zero say. Honestly, as a straight guy, I would rather have the freedom to make Jason gay than be forced into a scripted romance with Lucia. On top of that, restricting basic sandbox chaos, like locking down weapons inside clubs or heavily policing where you can cause mayhem, completely defeats the point of an open world crime game. Stop forcing players down a narrow path with this controlling mindset.What really killed the soul of this game is the writing and the characters. They aren't just unrealistic, they’re boring and cringe at points. What happened to the raw, unfiltered comedy that made classics like San Andreas and GTA V iconic? Look back at characters like CJ, Franklin, and Trevor, and moments like "Ah ****, here we go again" or Lamar roasting Franklin. That kind of sharp, unhinged dialogue is completely gone. It’s a video game, a fantasy sandbox, not a corporate seminar. Bringing real-world sensitivity rules into a series built on over-the-top satire strips away everything that made it fun in the first place.When the old creative leadership walked out and the writing room shifted to a massive corporate committee heavily dominated by women and modern studio politics, the entire tone changed. Social pressure inside a room like that inevitably sands down every rough edge before it ever makes it into the script. Nobody is pushing boundaries anymore because everyone is terrified of crossing a line. Meanwhile, other games out there let you play through straight-up World War II Axis campaigns or extreme scenarios without blinking, yet GTA, a franchise literally named after a felony, suddenly has to walk on eggshells. It makes no sense. This doesn't feel like the gritty, unapologetic game built for its core male audience anymore, it feels completely sanitized.I could list flaws for the next two hours, but there’s no point putting it all here. Honestly, this feels like it was planned from the day it was announced. The studio knew longtime fans would hate these changes, and they pushed it through anyway. Get over yourselves, bro. We are not here to learn morals and love lessons in a video game, especially in GTA 6. Take that preachy nonsense to another franchise. What have you done to this series? Just remake the past five games at this point. This is the last straw for me. From now on, I am never buying a game without knowing exactly what I’m getting into first, even if it means spoiling the entire story beforehand. I am genuinely appalled.

author: SilkyMonstar
quote:
I was so excited. GTA 5 came out when I was in highschool and I played with friends for years. I ignored all the hype and negativity around the game before release and approached it objectively.

My HONEST opinion is this is not a GTA game at its core.
Rankings: 
Gameplay: 5/10; feels like watchdogs with more RP but the wanted system is a nice change.
Story: 3/10. Unlikable protagonists; roughly 50% of the story felt like watching a movie instead of playing a game - and not a good movie either. Contrary to past Rockstar games, most of the characters felt like caricatures of my elementary school teacher's idea of a "good person" and "bad person". What does that mean? "Do unto others what you want them to do to you" and the game's reputation system thoroughly punishes you for being an actual criminal. Yes - you commit crimes - we rob banks, steal cars, raid drug stashes etc. But if you shoot one of the lying drug dealers in the skull while you steal his blood money, you get dinged for "bad behavior". Should've kneecapped him instead, or maybe given him a big old kiss and asked nicely?
Graphics: Good, slightly slow -- re: what my earlier remark about Watchdogs 2.

This feels like it stripped down the GTA franchise for parts. The writing didn't really feel authentically "crime-centric"; it instead felt like a survival game with optional crime mechanics that you can be punished for enjoying. 
In free roam, I didn't feel encouraged to steal cars or rob people: the reward wasn't there and the little demon emoji (telling me I misbehaved) was in its place.

It is certainly a massive departure from the franchise's roots: become a criminal kingpin, get out all the fantasy criminal energy that everyone has. I would return the game if I could.

I wanted to love it, but found myself trudging through. The absolute highest hopes have been crushed along with a piece of my childhood. Certainly cannot recommend a buy.

author: crizoliveira_
quote: GTA VI é um exemplo de como expectativas gigantescas podem acabar mascarando problemas que deveriam ser inadmissíveis em uma produção desse porte.Depois de mais de uma década de espera, bilhões investidos e uma campanha de marketing praticamente sem precedentes, o que deveria representar uma evolução significativa da franquia acaba tropeçando em decisões de design bastante questionáveis.O jogo parece excessivamente preocupado em alcançar o realismo cinematográfico, mas nem sempre consegue transformar esse realismo em uma experiência divertida. As missões continuam excessivamente roteirizadas, limitando a liberdade do jogador justamente em um título que deveria ter como principal virtude a autonomia. Em diversos momentos, parece que estamos apenas seguindo instruções dentro de uma sequência de acontecimentos previamente coreografados.A jogabilidade também não escapa das críticas: combate pouco refinado, mira pouco responsiva, movimentação por vezes desajeitada e uma progressão que parece artificialmente prolongada. Some-se a isso uma narrativa cujo ritmo pode ser arrastado, personagens que não agradam a todos e um humor que, para alguns jogadores, perdeu parte da irreverência que ajudou a construir a identidade da franquia.Tecnicamente, a situação também merece questionamentos. É difícil justificar um lançamento dessa magnitude limitado a 30 FPS nos consoles, especialmente quando existem relatos de quedas de desempenho, travamentos, bugs de colisão e problemas que chegam a comprometer o progresso em determinadas missões.O mais preocupante é perceber que a Rockstar parece ter investido uma quantidade extraordinária de recursos na construção de um mundo visualmente impressionante, mas isso não significa necessariamente que tenha conseguido aperfeiçoar todos os aspectos responsáveis por torná-lo **** fim, GTA VI pode até ser uma demonstração impressionante de engenharia e produção audiovisual, mas isso não o torna imune a críticas. Um mundo aberto não deveria ser avaliado exclusivamente pela quantidade de detalhes que consegue reproduzir, mas também pela qualidade das experiências que proporciona.A Rockstar não deveria receber um cheque em branco simplesmente por ser a Rockstar. Depois de treze anos de espera, o mínimo que se poderia esperar era um jogo que não precisasse depender de sua reputação, de seu orçamento ou da nostalgia dos jogadores para justificar suas escolhas.

author: IiiNasser_7
quote: After years of waiting, countless promises, and an enormous amount of anticipation, Grand Theft Auto VI finally arrived with expectations higher than almost any other game in history. Rockstar Games has always been known for pushing the boundaries of open-world gaming, but that reputation also comes with a responsibility to deliver an experience that lives up to the standards they have set for themselves.Unfortunately, the current situation raises several concerns that should not be **** of the biggest issues is the technical performance. Players have reported crashes, characters falling through the map, clipping issues, missing textures, strange vehicle physics, and several bugs that can interrupt the gameplay experience. These are not the kinds of problems players expect to encounter in a release of this scale, especially after such a long development cycle.Another major concern is the performance experience on consoles. Frame rate stability is extremely important in a massive open-world game, particularly during intense driving sequences, combat, and crowded city environments. A visually impressive game should not have to sacrifice a consistently smooth experience.What makes these issues even more disappointing is the amount of time players have spent waiting for this release. Expectations were naturally enormous, and nobody should pretend that a few technical problems are irrelevant simply because the game carries the Grand Theft Auto name.
