quote: Thirteen years. Thirteen damn years since GTA V. And after all that time, I'm supposed to fall to my knees because Rockstar made a beautiful city? NOT A CHANCE. I'm playing GTA VI. This is my money, my time, and my judgment. I don't owe Rockstar applause for its budget, its reputation, or its marketing. A famous logo earns no immunity. WHAT HAPPENED TO GRAND THEFT AUTO? I remember the chaos. The dark humor. The criminal adventures. The unpredictable characters. The freedom to explore, experiment, and make my own trouble. That was the heart of GTA. Now I'm spending too much time with errands, domestic responsibilities, and Jason and Lucia's relationship. Flowers. Chores. Everyday problems. I waited thirteen years for Grand Theft Auto, not Grand Theft Couples Therapy. And spare me the excuses: "It's realistic." "It's immersive." "It's a slow burn."Realism doesn't automatically mean fun. A beautifully animated chore is still a chore. A slow story can be brilliant, but it needs characters and tension that earn my patience. Telling me to wait another ten hours isn't a defense of pacing I find dull.JASON? GIVE ME A REASON TO CARE. He doesn't need to be Trevor. He needs to be interesting. His dialogue and personality haven't grabbed me, and the relationship-heavy storytelling makes the pace feel even slower. Romance isn't the problem. It's how much of the experience revolves around a dynamic I don't find compelling. NOW LET'S TALK ABOUT FREEDOM . Rockstar removed the ability to hire prostitutes, an optional interaction available in earlier GTA games. And the story-focused explanation for that decision doesn't satisfy me. This is a franchise about criminals making terrible choices. GTA V even let Michael cheat while married. Why should Jason and Lucia's relationship determine which optional choices exist in the sandbox? Nobody was forced to use that feature. That's the point. Players could choose. Removing an interaction doesn't automatically make a story better; it makes one choice unavailable. I'm not asking Rockstar to endorse cheating. I'm asking why a fictional crime game needs to narrow its possibilities to protect a romance. A bigger map doesn't mean more freedom. A prettier world doesn't mean a more interactive one. If I have fewer meaningful options, I'm going to call that a step backward. And the reported 30 FPS limit on PS5 Pro? Compromises happen. We don't have to celebrate them. After thirteen years, expectations should go up, not down. NOW FOR THE CORPORATE MACHINE . Here's the ugly irony: GTA made its name partly by mocking greed, power, and corporate absurdity. Now this installment feels to me like a product polished for shareholders, headlines, and brand protection. I can't prove what was said in a boardroom. I can question what the finished game seems to prioritize. Who helped build this empire? THE PLAYERS. People who bought the games and built its legacy. We weren't just numbers on an earnings slide. If the audience that built the franchise feels forgotten, Rockstar shouldn't be surprised when it hears about it. LOYALTY IS NOT A BLANK ****, THE CRITICS.Perfect scores. Glowing headlines. And anyone who disagrees is apparently a hater. DID YOU REVIEW THE GAME OR THE ROCKSTAR LOGO? A 10/10 doesn't mean literal perfection. But it demands a convincing explanation. If you acknowledge weak pacing, performance compromises, or restrictive design, tell readers why those flaws don't change your verdict. Don't hide behind "ambitious" and "cinematic" like those words settle everything. Would a smaller studio get the same forgiveness? Would the same issues be excused without Rockstar's reputation attached? Those are fair questions. I'm not claiming bribery, blacklisting, or rigged scores without evidence. I'm demanding consistency. A critic's job is to evaluate a game, not act like a publisher's public relations department. AND NOW GAME OF THE YEAR?Fine. Nominate it. Then judge EVERYTHING: gameplay, mission design, pacing, characters, freedom, performance, and actual enjoyment. Not just the graphics. Not the budget. Not the name on the box . GAME OF THE YEAR ISN'T A LIFETIME ACHIEVEMENT AWARD. And to the people defending every Rockstar decision: have some damn standards. You can love GTA and still criticize GTA. You can disagree with my score without pretending my experience doesn't count. Brand loyalty isn't critical thinking . HERE'S THE VERDICT. A gorgeous city can still feel restrictive. A cinematic story can still bore me. A massive budget can still produce choices I dislike. And a wall of perfect reviews cannot change what I'm experiencing with the controller in my hands. ROCKSTAR DOESN'T GET A FREE PASS. NEITHER DO THE CRITICS. NEITHER DO THE AWARDS. Thirteen years to raise the bar.r DON'T EXPECT ME TO LOWER MINE.0/10. RESPECT IS EARNED. NOT GIVEN.

GTA 5 is disappointing. Not sure where to even start, I have many bad things to say about it and a few good things too. First of all it's a console exclusive (no disc), so I had to play it on my friend's PS5 locked at 30fps while my RTX 4080 PC was sitting unused. The graphics were nice sometimes, but it kept alternating between good and bad, and definitely wasn't all like in the trailers. The game feels unfinished, explosions are underwhelming, shooting fuel tanks or crashing a plane feels lame... 

Story is horrible, Lucia is annoying and toxic to Jason, I would not wish such a relationship upon any friend. You also don't have the choice to ditch her and experience the story by yourself, you are forced to deal with her and avoid anyone else. Besides Lucia, the writing is bad in general, the characters feel stupid and unfunny, it does not have the GTA 5 spark. You cannot commit car theft in many situations, you cannot go to the strip club because it would impact your relationship with Lucia, you cannot do a bunch of things that we once saw normal. It feels as if the narrative of the developers and journalists try to set a really bad relationship standard and example to the average man, ridiculing, shaming and dehumanizing him at every possible point. Never thought GTA can be a moralist.

Besides the 30 fps the game is buggy and sometimes laggy. Aiming with a controller was bad enough from the start, it being even worse with bad performance. People crucified Cyberpunk 2077 over this, but somehow it's fine when GTA does it.
The game tries to push bad industry practices such as a new price standard with a subscription for in-(singleplayer)game advantages, the taketwo CEO has been talking about how hyped he is about pushing cloud gaming, which is currently the only way to play the game on PC, and you bet that GTA 6 multiplayer will be very grindy again and full of microtransactions as well. They are an union busting company that allegedly, under rumors, blackmailed reviewers to give a perfect score or not give them games for review again in the future. Now this game is the best rated game on metacritic with a user score of only 4/10. 

It rigged its way into the game awards, people were able to vote for it a day and a half before even being able to play it, that is criminal, you bet they got a ton of votes from people that were simply excited about it.



And yet the people with the worst possible taste in games will talk about it like it's the second coming of Jesus Christ. 

The positives: art is great, the artists made a very good looking world. Driving is also nice, the music is great, including tracks that were made specifically for the game. I am very happy they picked Justice for the original track, and Slayyyter also made a song for it, however I am very disappointed in this game.

author: cbaelectronicos
quote: I'm not going to say the game is completely broken, but it's close. I encountered several problems in the first 18 hours of gameplay. While not completely broken, it's definitely broken. There are already videos online showing bugs and glitches everywhere, but perhaps that's not the worst part. There are also things that aren't broken but are poorly thought out, designed, and executed. The physics of characters, NPCs, and vehicles are poor and basic. Sometimes people look like crash test dummies; their movements don't seem realistic and they feel heavier than they should be. The gameplay is very clunky, heavy, and lacks fluidity and agility. The sound effects are average, nothing impressive. The music? It doesn't have any original music. There aren't any memorable original tracks that you'll find yourself humming in 10 or 20 years. Everything is licensed from other artists. This aspect is very weak; not creating original music and relying on the budget to pay for licenses is a very, very bad point. And the performance? You can't be so hypocritical. Either performance deducts points from all games, or it doesn't deduct points from any. Games like Starfield were killed for their performance at launch. There's no dubbing. It's one thing for games in the '80s or '90s not to have dubbing, but in 2026, most games have dubbing in multiple languages: Spanish (ES, LA), Portuguese (PT, BR). The AI ​​isn't well-balanced. I found several situations where the NPCs' behavior in relation to Jason didn't make sense. As for fun, the story mode, if you only follow the story mode, is more than boring, it's incredibly boring. Innovation? There's no innovation in anything, folks, nothing. Not in gameplay, physics, music, or sound effects. Graphically, they're not innovations, just improvements on GTA V and RDR2. But come on, how can a game that doesn't innovate in any aspect have a 99? Even the menu isn't innovative, and on top of that, it's quite shoddy, basic, and ugly, in short. The Woke story of me teaming up with Jason to do everything Lucia wants could be the best game of 2026, but far from being the best in history, it will possibly remain the most overrated game of all time.

author: moinmeister
quote:
GTA 6 bietet eine unglaubliche Grafik, die im Jahr 2026 aber bei einem Preis von 80 bis 100 Euro kein alleiniges Kaufargument mehr ist. Die Interaktionen mit den NPCs, kleine Weltevents und deren Reaktionen auf Raubüberfälle sind dafür außergewöhnlich gut und überhaupt nicht zu kritisieren. Der Story-Einstieg zieht sich über mehrere Stunden und ist stark verurteilenswürdig. Nach etwa 20 Stunden Spielzeit wirkt keiner der Charaktere wirklich interessant, da die Hauptcharakterin unsympathisch und der männliche Hauptcharakter einfach langweilig ist. Die Handlung selbst ist weder besonders gut noch besonders schlecht, was nach 13 Jahren Entwicklungszeit enttäuschend wirkt und durch die lange Wartezeit sogar noch schlechter erscheint.
Ein Hauptproblem ist, dass die Spielmechaniken nicht mehr wie echtes GTA wirken, weil das Ausleben von freiem Willen und Kriminalität eingeschränkt ist. Sogar moralisch fragwürdige Handlungen wie das Betrügen der Freundin sind nicht oder nur indirekt möglich. Das Spiel hätte unter einem anderen Namen erscheinen sollen, weil der Titel GTA 6 eine echte Fortsetzung der bisherigen Teile verspricht. Stattdessen rückt das Spiel eine Beziehung in den Vordergrund und wirkt wie ein eigenständiges Werk.
Auch die riesige Open World passt nicht zum typischen GTA-Gefühl, weil sie stark auf Essen, Training und Beziehungsarbeit setzt. Bei GTA erwartet man stattdessen mehr begehbare und ausraubbare Gebäude statt Nägel machen zu lassen. Die 30 FPS stören zwar etwas, sind aber kein Gamebreaker, weil sie den Preis für die starke Grafik darstellen und höhere Bildraten diesen GTA-typischen Eindruck geschmälert hätten. Trotz des hohen Budgets, der langen Entwicklungszeit und zweier Verschiebungen sind offensichtliche Glitches und Bugs in einem längeren Durchlauf fast inakzeptabel.

author: bigdog3700
quote: I have finished the game and plenty of side activities and I came away from GTA 6 pretty disappointed. I absolutely loved the graphics, the level of detail in the world, and the gameplay itself. The combat, shooting, and overall mechanics were enjoyable, the game is just visually impressive. However, I was really disappointed by the 30 FPS cap on the PS5 Pro, which made the experience feel less smooth than I would have liked. My bigger issues were with the writing, voice acting, and overall characterization. A lot of the dialogue felt awkward, unnatural, or strangely delivered, and many conversations lacked genuine emotion or personality. Some characters felt flat, dull, or difficult to connect with, and certain scenes that should have carried some emotional weight (as much as GTA game possibly can) just didn't land for me. Jason felt unusually lifeless, with a monotone delivery that made it difficult to get invested in his character. The writing also felt inconsistent, sometimes trying to be serious or emotional but failing to make those moments feel believable or impactful. I was also disappointed with how restricted the overall freedom of choice felt. For a game of this scale, I expected more player agency, more ways to approach situations, and more freedom to make decisions that genuinely affect how things play out. At times, it felt like I was being pushed through a predetermined experience rather than given the freedom that I associate with GTA. On top of that, I felt like the game was missing a lot of the humor and entertaining, memorable moments that make GTA so enjoyable in the first place. There weren't nearly as many genuinely funny cutscenes, ridiculous situations, memorable interactions, or moments of pure chaos as I expected. A lot of the game felt oddly serious, subdued, or just lacking personality, and I rarely found myself laughing or experiencing those unexpected moments that make GTA memorable.

author: zachknows
quote:
GTA VI: A Beautiful World That Forgot What Makes GTA Fun

GTA VI has been a massive disappointment. Rockstar seems more interested in cinematic sequences, superficial features, and forcing players through its story than in delivering the freedom that made Grand Theft Auto great.

Even simple additions feel half-finished. Early on, you can repair part of a house's railing, but not the rest. You can't fix the stairs, and you repair only part of the roof before a cutscene finishes the job. I don't mind home maintenance, but if you're going to introduce it, make it a real mechanic instead of a scripted chore to impress Lucia, someone we barely know.

The story is worse. Lucia pressures Jason into a reckless opportunity involving people neither of them really knows. When he reasonably says no, she walks out and apparently considers that a breakup. Only a later flashback explains she ghosted him. Her childish explanation is simply accepted.

Then she reveals she had his child without telling him. Jason has never met his kid, doesn't know the child's name or face, while Lucia is in prison. Rather than feeling betrayed, furious, or even conflicted, he reacts like it's the happiest moment of his life. It's emotionally absurd.

Lucia's own arrest resulted from another impulsive armed robbery, committed after leaving her child in a nearby store. Yet the story continually expects us to sympathize with her, even as her reckless decisions endanger Jason, get him shot, and send them both on the run. Flawed protagonists can be compelling; protagonists whose choices never receive believable scrutiny are not.

The gameplay repeatedly makes the same mistake: showing us what should have been playable. During a breakfast outing, Lucia spontaneously suggests robbing people at gunpoint. Great! That's exactly the chaotic freedom I want from GTA. Except most of the ensuing string of robberies happens in a cutscene. We barely participate, and after roughly five locations and a police chase, we walk away with about $2,000.

Meanwhile, Moses lets you earn roughly $4,000 in a day from eligible vehicle deliveries alone, before additional missions. Why would a much riskier robbery spree pay so poorly? Even the weapon-shop interface makes it unnecessarily hard to tell which guns you already own, something GTA V communicated better.

When I tried robbing stores freely afterward, Lucia's AI was embarrassing. She stayed outside while I did everything myself. She apparently got into a random shootout, the supposedly alerted police never arrived, and she was just as useless at the next store. For a game centered on criminal partners, you'd expect your partner to actually help commit crimes.

The supposed need to "keep a low profile" is another convenient excuse for restrictions, not a consistent story principle. We're collecting airborne drug drops by boat almost immediately. Another improvised robbery somehow ends with Jason performing a striptease onstage. The script permits absurd risks while restricting the player.

Worst of all, basic sandbox freedom has regressed. Some vehicles cannot even be stolen until you've progressed far enough through the story. In a game called GRAND THEFT AUTO, you must unlock the ability to steal certain automobiles. You can't freely draw your gun in some neighborhoods either. Why is a franchise built around freedom imposing arbitrary limits on its most fundamental activities?

The upgraded police and vehicle systems often compound the frustration. My car gets impounded constantly; reclaiming it can trigger another chase; escaping frequently means tearing through woods and damaging it all over again. Realism should deepen gameplay, not trap players in an exhausting loop of penalties for trying to have fun.

I love realism. The physical weapons, immersive detail, and grounded mechanics are among the few things I appreciate here. But those are largely the strengths Rockstar already demonstrated in Red Dead Redemption 2. All they needed to do was bring that level of immersion into a modern GTA while preserving the crime, nightlife, spontaneous chaos, and freedom of choice that define the series.

Instead, GTA VI offers a gorgeous world full of systems that feel unfinished or unnecessarily restrictive, alongside a story that mistakes forced emotional beats for believable writing. Too often I watch characters commit crimes I should be allowed to commit myself.

I'm sure the game will sell spectacularly after so much hype, but sales aren't proof of quality. If Rockstar interprets that success as approval of this direction, I worry GTA VII won't enjoy the same goodwill.

I didn't wait all these years for an interactive movie that occasionally lets me play. I wanted Grand Theft Auto. For me, GTA VI is a huge step backward. (Had to rate 0 to offset the fake 10/10 reviews.)

author: Jaepetto
quote:
Visually, GTA VI undeniably delivers: the graphics are impressive, richly detailed, and technically top-tier. Yet beyond this polished exterior, nothing remains that deserves to carry the name of this legendary franchise. Anyone who grew up with GTA 1 through 5 and all their story DLCs will not connect with this game—quite the opposite. Calling this sixth installment GTA instead of launching it as a completely separate franchise was a massive mistake. 

x A "Pseudo-GTA" Stripped of Revolution and Resistance 

For over twenty years, Grand Theft Auto stood for uncompromising revolution and relentless resistance against the status quo. The classic entries were loud, anarchic, and driven by a ruthless anti-establishment and anti-mainstream-sheep mentality. They thrived on biting satire, wildly exaggerated characters, punch-down humor, and radical freedom of speech—firing shots at politicians, corporations, societal hypocrisy, and even the gamers themselves.
In GTA VI, that entire rebellious DNA has been erased. There is no trace left of anarchic chaos, punk attitude, or genuine resistance against mainstream conformity. Instead, players are handed a sanitized, safe product designed not to offend anyone. While the core gameplay mechanics vaguely resemble its predecessors, its soul and tone make it a hollow "pseudo-GTA"—a game that never wanted to be a true GTA in the first place and was developed completely past its actual fanbase.

x The Departure of the Original Creative Minds

This creative sellout comes as no surprise when looking behind the scenes. The original writers, programmers, and the infamous "frat-bro" guard who gave the previous games their sharp, unbridled edge have largely left Rockstar and had nothing to do with this installment. Without its original creators, the game simply lacks the rebellious spirit that once defined the series.

x A Calculated Distribution Strategy at the Fans' Expense

Even the release strategy feels like a deliberate slap in the face to longtime supporters. Ditching traditional physical disc hardcopies in favor of digital-only download links speaks volumes: the publisher knew exactly what kind of product they were putting on the market. Enforcing a digital-only model was clearly aimed at curbing a massive wave of refunds while cutting out the retail market to maximize corporate profits. Millions of gamers who pre-ordered based on the legacy of GTA V feel outright deceived. By trading the spirit of revolution and resistance for a pretty graphical shell, Rockstar may have inflicted lasting damage on its own brand.

x Technical Regressions and Restricted Sandbox Freedom

The issues don't stop with the writing—GTA VI also takes massive steps backward technically and mechanically. Being limited to just 15 manual save slots and having no direct mission-restart option is unacceptable for a modern open-world title. If you make a mistake or hit a bug during a mission, you are forced into tedious manual **** top of that, the once-boundless sandbox freedom has been noticeably neutered. Certain NPC groups are suddenly under artificial protection, making them impossible or needlessly difficult to harm, while classic series staples have been stripped away out of misplaced sensitivity. Where unbridled chaos used to reign, invisible moral guardrails now dictate what you are allowed to do.

x Relationship Simulator, Sims Mechanics, Voice Acting, and "The Message"

Instead of a fast-paced crime epic, players are subjected to a sluggish, heavy-handed storyline that struggles to gain momentum. For long stretches, GTA VI degenerates into a glorified relationship simulator complete with Sims-style chores—running errands, managing interiors, and babysitting relationship meters take priority over actual high-stakes **** voice acting and character dynamics only make this worse. Jason sounds like a dim-witted Patrick Star, while Lucia quickly becomes outright irritating to listen to. Worse still is the heavy-handed ideological slant: the game relentlessly shoves modern clichés and "The Message" down the player's throat. While Lucia is propped up as an untouchable "girlboss" archetype, Jason is reduced to a spineless cuck and glorified errand boy whose primary purpose is to keep her happy. None of this has anything to do with the uncompromising anti-hero spirit that once made Grand Theft Auto iconic.

author: Gibbyreviews
quote: For a game that took over a decade to make, it's surprisingly clunky, unfunny, and obsessed with realism at the expense of good gameplay. Worse, it feels like the game actively discourages you from doing the very things the franchise was built around: breaking the law and causing chaos. And that's before getting into the bugs, like clipping through the floor or getting stuck on random objects. Don't get me wrong, the game is fun, but not as nearly as fun as 4&5. The map is beautiful, the world feels alive, and some of the mechanics are genuinely impressive. But you're telling me that in the past 13 years, not a single person sat in a meeting and thought, "Hey, maybe making the game fun should take priority over making it realistic"?This is Grand Theft Auto. A franchise built around stealing cars, driving like a maniac, and doing whatever the hell you want. Yet somehow, the game makes doing those things feel like a financial burden. There are so many cars on the road in the name of realism that driving at high speeds becomes more frustrating than enjoyable. You either drive like a responsible adult or have fun and blow your entire budget repairing your car every five **** then there's PAYING FOR GAS. Seriously, who on earth decided that what GTA was missing was the experience of worrying about fuel expenses? I already pay for gas in real life. I don't need to come home from work, boot up GTA, and start budgeting for my fictional commute. What's next? Oil changes? Car insurance? Then there's the morality system. For a game that's supposed to be about breaking the rules, it sure loves punishing you for doing exactly that. I paid for the full game, and naturally, I want to experience the good ending. But that means constantly worrying about my morality score in a game that regularly forces me into situations where violence is unavoidable. I bought the game, I’m going to play all the missions, and If a mission sends 100 bikers after me, what exactly am I supposed to do? Fistfight every single one of them and knock them unconscious? The game practically forces you to shoot your way out, and with auto-aim constantly snapping toward enemies' heads, you're going to end up killing people whether you're trying to or not. Why am I being punished for playing the missions the way the game designed them?That's ultimately my biggest frustration. The developers seem so focused on making the world realistic and giving every action consequences that they've forgotten what made GTA fun in the first place. Realism doesn't automatically equal good gameplay, and consequences aren't inherently fun. I'll have fun, and I'll keep playing. There's plenty here to enjoy, but God, I hope they had a different team working on GTA Online. Give me ridiculous cars, chaotic driving, absurd missions, and the freedom to do whatever I want without worrying about my bank account or whether the game thinks I'm a good person. Make it an arcade game, not real life.

author: Boombumi
quote:
A massive disappointment disguised as a video game.

After years of waiting, hype and marketing, GTA VI looks like a perfect example of how a franchise can lose its identity. From a world of freedom to a world of wokedom. We were sold the game of the century. The mere fact that opinions are so divided already tells us that it is nowhere near deserving that title.

The two protagonists are painfully uninteresting, with little personality or charisma. The dialogues feel uninspired, the writing lacks depth, and the story doesn't seem to offer anything particularly compelling. Having two playable characters means absolutely nothing when neither of them is worth caring about.

What bothers me most is the direction Rockstar has taken. GTA used to be a satirical, provocative and genuinely entertaining franchise. Now it feels increasingly focused on looking impressive rather than delivering an engaging experience. Better graphics and a bigger map don't automatically make a better game. There is no freedom, missions are still linear, and it's still FedEx gameplay...
Without repeating every other comment about how it's not a romance between the two characters, but rather a boss lady and her slave.

At this point, it feels less like playing Grand Theft Auto and more like being sold an expensive interactive simulator with a forgettable story attached to it, and a slave boyfriend simulator that does everything the boss lady wants him to.

I play a game for fun, not to do chores that I already do in real life.

Final verdict: 1/10.

A disappointing direction for one of gaming's most iconic franchises. All that waiting for something that, at least from what it offers, doesn't deserve the name GTA.

author: MacBinary
quote:
The graphics are great, the city is huge, but this isn't a GTA game in the sense of being a "GTA" game. Painting walls, picking flowers, plunging sinks, fixing roofs, doing the shopping... plus you can't steal cars in your own neighbourhood in a game literally called Grand Theft Auto.

When you make a game for "everyone" you end up making a game for no one. Perhaps Rockstar should have made this version as a DLC for females to play, or even as a different game, but this isn't the gritty, raw, unapologetic GTA many of us grew up with. Having played since the first GTA in 1997 as a teenager it's been a favourite of mine for decades but this just doesn't seem to work. This is more like playing The Sims than it is a game about crime, drugs and violence.

And it has an empathy metric... empathy... And none of this touches on the problem of this 2026 game being capped at 30FPS, which it often falls well below. At times I thought I was playing Stunt Car Racer on an old Amiga 500!

Come on Rockstar, know your audience, and stop trying to repackage already successful franchises as something else to appeal to the "modern" audience. You used to be cool, now you're more akin to the Steve Buscemi "Fellow Kids" meme!

author: Betrueermicha
quote:
GTA 6 – 2/10 

Ein Milliardenbudget und jahrelanger Hype machen noch lange kein Meisterwerk.

Nach dieser endlosen Wartezeit hätte ich deutlich mehr erwartet. Die Grafik ist beeindruckend, aber hinter der hübschen Fassade steckt erschreckend wenig Innovation.

Die Story ist vorhersehbar, die Charaktere enttäuschen und das Missionsdesign ist teilweise lächerlich linear. Rockstar verkauft uns eine riesige offene Spielwelt, in der man angeblich alles machen kann – außer in Missionen vom exakt vorgeschriebenen Weg abzuweichen.

Das Gameplay wirkt stellenweise veraltet, viele Aktivitäten wiederholen sich und wirkliche Innovationen sucht man vergeblich. Im Grunde bekommt man bekannte Rockstar-Mechaniken mit einem extrem teuren Grafikupdate.

Noch absurder sind allerdings die professionellen Reviews.

Da werden lineare Missionen, spielerische Schwächen und fehlende Innovationen kritisiert, nur um anschließend völlig selbstverständlich 100/100 Punkten zu vergeben. Bewertungen, die derart offensichtlich nach gekaufter Werbung aussehen, kann ich schlicht nicht mehr ernst nehmen.

Man könnte fast meinen, manche Magazine hätten die perfekte Punktzahl bereits vor dem eigentlichen Test festgelegt. Hauptsache, man schwimmt auf der Hype-Welle mit.

Natürlich beweist das keine gekauften Bewertungen. Aber wenn selbst gravierende Kritikpunkte offenbar keinerlei Einfluss auf die Endwertung haben, stellt sich schon die Frage, welchen Wert solche Reviews überhaupt besitzen.

Fazit: Technisch beeindruckend, spielerisch enttäuschend und von einer Kritikerkultur begleitet, die scheinbar Angst davor hat, einem Rockstar-Spiel weniger als 90 Punkte zu geben.

2/10 – Für die Grafik gibt es zwei Punkte. Den Rest hat offenbar das Marketing übernommen.

author: d25bev
quote:
I'd almost say it's a technical marvel but i've run into a number of annoying glitches & have seen others suffering even worse. As expected, the open world is great. Detailed & graphically beautiful. The interactions, the driving & the 'living world' are top notch.

What i didn't expect was for the rest of the game to be such a huge disappointment & completely waste that open world. The writing is poor, the story & mission design is dull, the gameplay is overly restrictive in favour of realism, the classic 'GTA' humour is virtually non-existent & the characters are so annoying & so hard to like.

It's sanitised. It's restrictive. It's flat. It's overly progressive. You can argue it being a good game. You can't argue it being a good 'GTA' or a good Rockstar game. 

The core issues with the game are unfixable but if Rockstar were smart, they'd fire the current writers, beg Dan Houser & the others to come back & let them adapt Houser's better VI story/characters that were rejected into some story DLC.

author: arceuskyske
quote:
The game is undoubtedly a graphical milestone in the video game industry. Wherever you look on the map, you can see where the investment went.

That being said, the game brings absolutely nothing new to the table, with extremely simplistic gameplay mechanics.

I would even consider the gunplay a downgrade compared to Red Dead Redemption 2. Any weapon larger than a pistol is something I simply pick up off the ground during missions.

The life simulation mechanics are cool at first, but they're shallow and repetitive. At some point, I simply got tired of doing them. They're impressive initially, but after dozens of hours, they become tedious and add absolutely nothing meaningful to the experience.

Committing crimes, even something as simple as stealing a car, is incredibly frustrating because the police remember your physical appearance. There were several occasions when I couldn't go somewhere because I was wanted, but I also couldn't buy new clothes because there were no stores available. The game doesn't have instant fast travel (you can call a taxi, though), so whenever I want to escape the police or get back home quickly, I simply quit and reload the game 

The game runs at 30 FPS, and yes, it does suffer from frame drops, especially in heavily forested areas when driving through them.

Another thing that bothers me about the game is the gradual darkening at the edges of the screen. There is no option to disable it.

Finally, what breaks my immersion the most in a game that presents itself as cinematic and somewhat realistic is having obnoxious characters and a story that feels like something straight out of a cheesy American teen movie. First of all, GTA IV isn't nearly this silly (maybe that's why it wasn't as successful?). This makes it incredibly difficult for me to connect with the missions, especially when both protagonists are complete idiots who are responsible for the situations I'm referring to. Those who have played the game know exactly what I mean.

It's perfectly legitimate for people not to enjoy a game like GTA (I personally enjoy Red Dead much more). The magic and impact of a massive game like GTA might last for the first 10 hours or so. After that, if you actually care about how the narrative unfolds, you start noticing how simplistic and shallow its world, story, narrative, characters, and motivations really are.

Some franchises don't necessarily need to be groundbreaking, but for a game of this scale, with this level of investment, these aspects could have been explored with much greater depth.

author: Luxox412
quote: While GTA VI undeniably feels like a Rockstar game in many respects, I can't help but feel disappointed by the overall experience. After 13 years of waiting, I honestly expected a much more polished and ambitious product. The amount of bugs, performance issues, occasional frame drops, and the fact that the game runs at 30 FPS make the experience feel bittersweet. It simply doesn't feel like the kind of leap forward we were promised after such an incredibly long development cycle.What makes things even worse is seeing players and modders manage to improve certain aspects of the game with relatively minor adjustments. When individuals can make noticeable improvements to a game that was developed by one of the largest studios in the industry, with an enormous budget, hundreds of talented employees, and millions of dollars generated through digital pre-orders, it raises serious questions about Rockstar's priorities and quality **** situation is even more frustrating when you consider the game's pricing and marketing practices. Releasing an extremely expensive collector's edition without including the actual game, and selling physical editions that contain nothing more than a download code instead of a disc, feels like a slap in the face to consumers. These decisions only add to the growing list of reasons why players have every right to be **** let's not forget the so-called "professional critics" who awarded the game perfect scores while simultaneously pointing out flaws that clearly prevent it from being perfect. What exactly does a 10/10 mean anymore if the game still has significant technical, gameplay, and design issues? It feels like these scores are increasingly disconnected from honest **** a game costing around $100, locking content behind additional purchases that should arguably have been included in the base game is an undeniably anti-consumer practice. Rockstar knows exactly how passionate its fanbase is and how many people have been waiting for this game for over a decade. Taking advantage of that anticipation while releasing a product with noticeable graphical and gameplay shortcomings, repetitive missions and storytelling elements, and the removal of several iconic features from previous entries is extremely **** VI deserved more care, more polish, and a greater commitment to delivering the experience players expected. Rockstar has the resources, the talent, the reputation, and the budget to set a new standard for the industry. Instead, it feels like the company relied too heavily on its name and the enormous hype surrounding the game.I genuinely hope Rockstar continues working on the game and fixes its technical issues, improves performance, and addresses the shortcomings that currently prevent it from being the experience it should have been. At the very least, players deserve a polished, properly functioning game worthy of the Rockstar **** honestly, the fact that the game received near-perfect scores on Metacritic and was nominated for The Game Awards before even being released to the public makes the whole situation even more absurd. How can a game be universally praised, awarded perfect scores, and nominated for major awards before players have even had the opportunity to experience the finished product for themselves? To me, that's a perfect example of how hype and reputation can overshadow genuine criticism.

author: Seven95
quote: Grand Theft Auto VI: A Jaw-Dropping Digital Playground Held Back by Chugging Performance and an Unforgivable NarrativeAfter thirteen years of breathless anticipation and massive budgets, Grand Theft Auto VI has finally arrived. Stepping into its neon-drenched streets and expansive coastal setting feels like a generational leap in virtual world-building. Yet, once the initial awe wears off, a frustrating reality sets in. Behind the photorealistic sunsets and unmatched scale lies a deeply flawed experience crippled by a sluggish frame rate and a story mode so painfully dull that it undermines the brilliance of its own setting.A Masterclass in Map Design and ScaleThere is no denying that this is the greatest open-world map ever constructed. From bustling, palm-lined boulevards to murky, alligator-infested wetlands and sprawling island chains, every square inch feels deliberately crafted. What sets it apart is its verticality, density, and seamlessness. You can stand on a downtown rooftop watching ocean waves crash miles away while traffic hums below without a hint of pop-in. Neighborhoods transition naturally from wealthy beachfront enclaves into gritty industrial districts, while dynamic crowds and roaming wildlife make the world feel genuinely lived-in.Photorealistic VisualsVisually, the game is breathtaking. Ray-traced global illumination transforms every puddle and glass **** into a mirror reflecting the pastel skyline. Tropical rainstorms roll in with gusting winds and slick asphalt that glimmers realistically under neon signage. Character models, fabric physics, and interior spaces packed with bespoke clutter reach a standard few games can **** Painful Reality of a Low Frame RateUnfortunately, this graphical nirvana comes at an unacceptable cost. In an era where 60 FPS is the standard, being forced into a locked 30 FPS experience feels antiquated—and the hardware frequently buckles even at that target. Weaving through dense downtown traffic or triggering chaotic shootouts causes the frame rate to tank into the mid-twenties. Input latency spikes, camera panning turns into a smeary slideshow, and high-stakes races become exercises in **** Abysmal Story ModeEven more damaging is the single-player campaign, which fails in pacing, tone, and mission design. The narrative following the central criminal duo is shockingly flat and devoid of momentum, dragging endlessly through tedious errands and repetitive busywork. Far too many hours are wasted driving slowly across the map listening to uninspired dialogue that mistakes endless swearing for wit, all while a rigid mission structure punishes any creative problem-solving with an instant "Mission Failed" screen.VerdictGrand Theft Auto VI is a triumph of technical artistry trapped inside a sluggish, poorly written game. Exploring the gorgeous map is an unmatched thrill for aimless sightseeing, but the choppy frame rate and abysmal campaign make it a frustrating chore to actually play.

author: Henepp
quote:
When this game is running well and looking how rockstar intended, it is genuinely really impressive to see, the fact games can look like this now is absolutely incredible But, beauty is pain as they say. There are so many issues I have that critics just simply left out of their review that honestly add up quite a bit. There are CONSTANT frame dips on the base PS5, and pretty major bugs and glitches. Normally I don’t care about these things too much, especially on day 1, but this is an $80-100 game from one of the biggest studios in the world. This is genuinely inexcusable, especially when the main selling point of this game is just how realistic and immersive it is, it constantly is ripping me out of the experience.Also, this game just isn’t very fun honestly. Don’t get me wrong, a lot of the life sim elements are genuinely impressive but they don’t add anything to the GTA experience, and if anything they detract. Not being able to flip cars and keep causing havoc, not being able to have a full weapon wheel, having to spend the first chunk of the game on fixing a house, not being able to just steal any car you want from the get-go, and especially the new karma system…Yes all these things are more realistic, but they ultimately make the game just less fun, and that’s really a shame. GTA is fun havoc, not a life sim. Ultimately, the game itself is impressive, but flawed in some pretty serious and important ways. Regularly, I’d say that makes it a 7? Maybe 7.5?
But it is genuinely impossible to ignore the industry and how rockstar is changing it for the worse. Overworked devs, insane union busting, and all this isn’t to mention no physical. My dislike of this game isn’t directed to just the game itself, but also to rockstar and how they’ve treated this release. It has genuinely been a Trojan horse for the worst business practices that I really hope don’t become the standard. I love GTA 5, it’s one of the most fun games I’ve ever played
But I can’t love this game for what it spells for the industry. This game needs to be criticized for what it’s trying to do, and I think it’s a damn shame the critics were really paid off for this one. An all digital future is NOT the future you want, even if you think it is, I promise having the choice to go physical will always ALWAYS be better. Do better rockstar

author: Xovizo
quote:
Where to begin...

I cannot commit automobile theft in a game called Grand Theft Auto. This sentence essentially says it all. Rockstar Games, in the attempt to make hyper-realistic game, they ended up making it unbearable. We play games to dive into a virtual world and live a life that is completely fictional. In that life, anything is possible. When it comes to GTA 6, all of those couldn't be further away from being the case. In the pursuit of seriousness and realism, The studio has completely forgotten what constituted a great game. A great game is something you would like to come back to, to have fun. It's something that you turn your console ON for if you have a spare hour or two and it's something that if you have company, you could all have fun. GTA 6 is neither of those. In order to steal cars, you need to spend hours upon hours building mechanics to do so. In order to get the good ending you have to play a particular way that the developers have envisioned... It's not a game. It's a virtual life simulator. 

GTA has always been known for being the game where you can do it all. Being the game that does not judge you and allows you to be the craziest the most reckless player that you know would never exist in the real world. This is exactly the reason why we played those games. It's to do stuff that we cannot do in the real life. Some because they are illegal, others because they are unethical. But what does it matter? It's a darn video game about criminals as main characters. 

I don't want to start a game where I know that I have to plan my getaway. I do not want to start a game, where I have to change clothing, change vehicle or any other little aspect of the character in order for me to get away from being chased. I do not want to start a game where i have to do groceries, repair cars and houses in order to use them. I want to start a game where I am free to do anything. Whether it's to carry 60 weapons or break into a hypercar parked on the street. 
By trying to make this game overly realistic, Rockstar Games effectively brought the most boring aspects of real life into a con-led story game.

Additionally, following the online posts about the game displaying invincibility on particular NPCs, the developers are effectively telling us that we have to live by their morals. The removal of S*x workers, the inability to draw guns in particular areas or to drive through specific groups of people is a choice that should be left to the player. If the developers are very strict and sensitive about those aspects, don't bring them into the game. Morals should always be left to the player to decide. 

Lastly, I would like to cover the technical aspect of the game. 30 frames a second is not a problem at all as many people criticize... Your eyes get used to it within the first 15 minutes, and the game is gigantic and beautiful, which is why we are unable to run it on better specs. This part is totally understandable and completely fine and acceptable. What is unacceptable is to take away features that were available in previous games, and make them unavailable or un-functional in the current game. In particular I'm talking about air and sea travel having completely zero physics. Boats sailing at full speed have absolutely no impact onto objects they hit. Plane physics break entirely if you hit something from a front or if you leave the vehicle behind. But the saddest part is that the explosions and effects of destruction makes the game look like Fortnite instead of Grand Theft Auto. Their goal was to make the most realistic GTA up to this point but they decided to remove the far more realistic effects from the previous game for a spark explosion effect in this one? How is this possible? How come the wings on planes do not break when you hit a physical object? That's a feature that was present in a game that came out in 2013. 
Speaking of games that came out 13 years ago, what is going on with the plot? People responsible for script writing were trying to replicate a movie instead of creating a Satire video game. The characters are boring, the plot is uninteresting, and overall, this feels like one of the binge Netflix series instead of being a standalone story.

Oh and let's bring up the question of realism in which we have superhuman Hulk-esque characters, giant crabs, and "non-failable" mission sequences. It does not matter how bad you are, dying from the likes of an enemy is a crime. 

To conclude, this game broke the lineage of traditional Rockstar Grand Theft Auto games. Instead of making the games more fun with more options as well as more things that you can do, with an interesting story and unforgettable views (only present thing), we got ourselves a low-budget Netflix studio Drama movie. 

The expectations were high, but they were not unachievable for a company that had the budget to build a second Burj Khalifa. 

Hopefully this game serves Rockstar as a lesson for what NOT to do next.

Para un proyecto de esta magnitud y con tanto tiempo de producción, esperaba una experiencia mucho más **** otro lado, la dirección creativa del juego se siente limitada. Hay decisiones de diseño y contenido que, más que ampliar la experiencia, la constriñen. Después de unas ocho horas, la sensación de que el juego te va poniendo trabas —y no precisamente por desafío jugable— termina por desgastar el interés. Es decepcionante notar que, en lugar de sentirte libre en un mundo abierto, sientes que te prohíben más de lo que te permiten.Y luego está la polémica de las valoraciones. Ver que algunos críticos le otorgan un 99 a un juego que, como mínimo, tiene carencias evidentes, deja una mala impresión. No se trata de exigir una nota baja por deporte, sino de coherencia: una puntuación tan alta para un producto con estos problemas hace que uno se pregunte qué criterios se están aplicando. Al final, esas notas tan exageradas terminan por restar credibilidad a quienes las **** resumen: GTA VI es un escaparate técnico impresionante, pero como experiencia completa se queda corto. El tiempo de desarrollo, los fallos y una dirección que limita más de lo que ofrece hacen que el juego no esté a la altura de lo que se esperaba. Una pena

author: P00000L5
quote:
When reading this review and any others with a low score, ask yourself: am I going to dismiss this review with a score of 1 from a random user but believe the many perfect scores of 100, something just unprecedented and seemingly impossible.

 This game is not perfect, and I’ve rated it as such (maybe a little more graciously).  Many have been disappointed, me included, in how it decided to drive forward the GTA franchise. But the critic review has disappointed us the most. Universally, we can all agree this is not an 100 greatest game of all time. 

The performance is not the best, often with many bugs and glitches, just search online for compilations of this. FPS falls to low 20s and even below. Now this would normally bring down a reviewers score on any other game, this time 160 critics seemingly decided to look past that and still give this a glowing 100 perfect score. 

The story has been described as many as boring, which I can completely agree with for the first 20 hours or so. Instead of the normal GTA heist and action packed gameplay we are all used to, we get to instead do chores, play life, and take care of a woman who seemingly cannot think her decisions through. Lucia constantly makes bad decisions and for some reason seemingly forgets she has a child after being released from jail. The story just seems to drag on and splits off into many confusing directions and leaves me wondering, what happened to GTA. Certain characters are barred off from being attacked or certain locations are off limits. Classic GTA gameplay has been swapped out, for what can only be described as a sanitization of the freedom we all loved.  

The one thing that can be unanimously agreed upon is the graphics. It is a very gorgeous at times breathtaking games but at what cost? A game that cannot break 30 FPS in 2026, that has many bugs and glitches, that lacks a story that draws us in. At what point do we stop caring about graphics and start caring about what matters: FUN. All of these problems can be seen as a direct result of all the money and effort being poured into graphics that nobody asked for. Now this is not the first time this has happened though. Most modern triple a games have been following this trend and it’s disappointing. Are we as players going to collectively continue to support this and watch as our favorite franchises are torn apart and our favorite developers are fired? How is it that games with a quarter of the budget and capture all of us but the games with the big corporation backing cannot?

We play games to have fun. We don’t play games to play life.

author: winterMAM
quote:
Spoilers Free

TL;DR: the good doesn't outweigh the bad.

The Good
-Visuals. Easily one of the better looking games that came out in recent years.
-World. The map is big and full of mostly interesting spots.
-Gunplay. Mostly good and it stayed really consistent.
-Sound design. The foley sounds are great. Car sounds great, explosions, gunfire, etc.

The Average
-Driving. It has the GTA feel but nothing that really felt outstanding. There are a lot of cars that has the same feel which can be bad because the distinction of good cars from bad cars vanishes, so a good car will sometimes control just a bad car.
-Gameplay. The way you interact and move in the game is overall good and satisfying. It has mostly the RDR2 feel which is good which I think can lead to satisfying loop.

The Bad (that don't matter)
-UI. It has no effect on gameplay and I got used to it but it's still very ugly. It has no personality. The minimap and the weapon wheel looks bad.
-Music.

The Bad (that matters)
-Main Story. I can appreciate telling a different story for a GTA game. It's slow (my type of game) and more grounded. But the story being told is very uninspired and how it's written is very bad.
--Dialogue. The dialogue is one of the culprits. Most of the conversations are just bland that just leads to average payoffs. Jason has a lot of bland generic conversation and I can understand most of it is in the early game but it didn't get any better. Lucia has a much entertaining interactions to say the least but again nothing too compelling that really made me engage with the story. I feel like this a result of the game being more grounded and that naturally leads to very bland dialogue. Dialogue during side missions are not that great either.
--Missions. Very generic. This is a main selling point of GTA story mode for me because this bridges the story when the dialogue fails and they're just not good.

-Characters.
--Jason and Lucia. They are nuanced characters as they should and that's the only good thing I can say about them. Their characters as a pair has very little focus and their dynamic when they're together is not really engaging. I'm catching myself wanting more from them more than cheering for them. Obviously they have issues as a couple in general but throughout the whole game until the ending that I got, I can feel a massive disconnect in their characters. And I'm disappointed because the main story can be very average but as long as both of them are fun and engaging, they can make the game for me. They just didn't benefit from the story they're in.
---Jason. I feel sorry for how boring his character is. Bland and dull and it shows in most of his interactions. There's nothing that he did that really stood out to me as interesting or memorable. He'll have his "awesome" scripted scenes during missions here and there but those are still very generic. He did have some character development but his character arc is so off and not satisfying. He's the personification of the word "meh". He's a very safe character though he is in a grounded story, I just want him to react more, to do more.
---Lucia. Her character is just bad to say the least. I couldn't care less about whatever agenda is behind her character or any other characters for that matter, I just feel very disappointed with her character the most and at first I'm very excited to the play her because she's the first major fleshed out female lead with a voice in a GTA game. I do not agree with how she interacts with Jason and I find it hard to cheer for her or to progress her story. The story isn't just fun when she's involve. heck, even when she's just sharing the spotlight she's equally being very hard to stomach. It has nothing to do with her gender. If the genders are reversed and Jason is a straight up ****, I'd be annoyed and frustrated with him too. And, yes GTA protagonists are written flawed but this is not a normal GTA game. A character like Lucia in a very grounded GTA game is huge disconnect. A grounded story needs grounded flaws and grounded resolutions, that doesn't happened to her. The game doesn't give a realistic outcome for her character and her actions and that's really frustrating. And I do like her interactions better than Jason's but her character is just very frustrating.
--Side Characters. Again mostly forgettable characters. They're in very mundane missions that don't really do anything for me. And that's really disappointing because the world they're in is great but I feel like the protags interactions with them are sometimes limited which is to be expected but again even there very noteworthy side characters in past GTA games and RDR2. Given that I haven't interacted with all of them and there are plenty of different interactions to have but still, so far after finishing the game, they were mostly disappoint. I put this in the bad and not the average because side characters are important, they fill the gaps of the game.

author: westco
quote: For all its technical brilliance, Grand Theft Auto VI feels less like a video game and more like an interactive movie that hates letting you have fun. After waiting over a decade, Rockstar delivered a gorgeous world held back by outdated design and restrictive mechanics.Outdated Mission Design: Despite the modern coat of paint, missions are still painfully linear. Stepping slightly off the designated path or trying a creative approach often triggers an instant "Mission Failed" screen.Style Over Substance: The obsession with realistic physics—like limited weapon carrying and sluggish movement—actively punishes players for trying to cause the classic, over-the-top GTA mayhem.Empty Scale: While Vice City and Leonida look breathtaking, much of the massive map feels like set dressing, lacking meaningful, repeatable activities once the main story wraps up.Anti-Consumer Tactics: Between the 30 FPS console cap, missing PC version, and content locked behind expensive editions, the launch feels engineered to maximize profit rather than player **** short, Rockstar focused so much on making GTA VI look like real life that they forgot to make it play like a great game.

quote: Despite its impressive visuals, Grand Theft Auto VI has disappointed many fans who feel it prioritizes hyper-realism over the classic, fast-paced fun the series is known **** main criticisms boil down to four issues:Slow, Tedious Gameplay: Like Red Dead Redemption 2, the game bogs down simple actions with lengthy animations and heavy, sluggish controls, making it feel more like a chore simulator than an arcade sandbox.30 FPS Limit: Locking current-gen consoles to 30 frames per second—with noticeable frame drops during intense action—feels outdated for a flagship release.Loss of Classic Satire: Without longtime writer Dan Houser, the sharp, cynical humor has been replaced by a grounded, overly serious romantic drama that restricts the chaotic freedom players expect.Greedy Monetization: Locking single-player content behind expensive special editions and delaying the PC release has frustrated the fanbase.Ultimately, in trying to build the most realistic crime drama possible, Rockstar lost the irreverent, chaotic soul that made GTA fun in the first place.

author: Mycatdied
quote:
Grand Theft was, in fact, committed. Unfortunately, the victim was the franchise itself.

Everything that made GTA the legendary series it once was seems to have been thrown out the window in favor of an experience that feels less like an open-world crime sandbox and more like an aggressively supervised episode of The Real Housewives of Vice City.

GTA used to be about freedom. Glorious, ridiculous, unapologetic freedom. Steal cars, cause mayhem, ignore the rules, and do whatever the hell you wanted. It was an escape from reality, where the only limits were your imagination and how quickly the police could develop a personal vendetta against you.

Now? Apparently, it's about being put on rails, following someone else's schedule, doing chores, managing relationships, and getting lectured for failing to participate in your virtual domestic responsibilities.

If I wanted to be forced to do things with my significant other, run errands, complete household chores, and get griped at by my significant other, I'd simply turn off the game and return to my actual life. At least there, I might get some credit for taking out the trash.

I don't boot up GTA to experience a second job with better graphics. I don't need a virtual relationship counselor, a digital chore chart, or another reminder that I'm disappointing someone in yet another universe. Video games are supposed to be an escape from reality, not a second subscription to it. 

The whole appeal of GTA was that it let you live a ridiculous virtual life on your own terms. It was a sandbox, not a guided tour through somebody else's idea of how you should behave and spend your fictional free time.

Rockstar seems to have confused making a world feel alive with making the player feel obligated to participate in every mundane aspect of it.

Congratulations. You've taken a franchise built around freedom and turned it into a simulator where the biggest crime is apparently failing to do your damn chores.

Grand Theft Auto? More like Grand Theft Autonomy. And they stole every last bit of it.

author: RIEZE
quote:
PROS
Graphics: Great overall. Not flawless, but a lot of areas look really impressive.
Scale and map: Easily GTA 6's biggest achievement. The world is massive.
Interactivity: There's a ton to interact with and you can do almost whatever you want, though it comes with a major catch.

CONS
Weak characters: Zero charisma. Honestly the worst cast in GTA history (not counting GTA 1 &2).
Core GTA freedom got nerfed: Even with so much to do, the staples that actually make a game feel like GTA were watered down. You can't just steal any car anymore, certain NPCs can't be killed, and you get penalized too heavily for going on a rampage. This is GTA, I don't want it to feel like real life. 
Feels like a bad Sims game: Fixing up and managing your house has its charm in other games, not in GTA.
Boring story: Flat and forgettable. You can tell the focus was on everything else except just writing a great story.
Technical issues and FPS drops: Obvious launch bugs, glitches, and noticeable frame-rate drops when the action picks up.

To put it simply, GTA 6 lost its soul and doesn't feel like a real GTA game anymore. It's just a shell of the franchise, carried by overhype and FOMO. Don't get me wrong, there's still some charm here, it's just not the GTA that I, or a lot of us, actually wanted.

On top of the game itself, one of the biggest issues for me is the media reviews. It's obvious there are bugs, technical problems, and FPS drops, yet outlets still handed out 10/10s anyway, while denying those same high scores to games that actually deserve them.

Obviously, user scores deal with review bombing, while critic scores get skewed by publisher perks, hype, and fear of losing early access. Even so, when a game is truly great, the noise eventually balances out and the critic and player scores end up pretty close. That's not what's happening here!

GTA 6 looks incredible. There. I said the nice thing. 

The writing feels like somebody pitched a Bonnie-and-Clyde story and then forgot to give Clyde a spine. There’s plenty of room in GTA for a woman who runs the show. It’d just be more fun if her partner had a personality beyond “whatever you say, babe.”

GTA used to let you do something awful to ANYONE and send the cops after you. That was the appeal of GTA. It was lawless and no one was safe. Half the fun of GTA was finding out what happened when you did something stupid. 

Even the dialogue sounds like it’s trying to get invited back to dinner. GTA used to be vulgar, petty, and happy to make everybody look ridiculous. That was half its personality. Now the city looks more alive than ever, and the people talking in it sound like they’re on their best behavior. 

The dialogue’s been scrubbed, the satire’s lost its bite, and the puddles look incredible. Great. I can see the reflection of the game I used to like.

Look at who’s writing today’s biggest games and you’ll start to see why so many of them sound the same. As long as studios keep hiring with the same worldview, we’re going to keep getting the same crap with better graphics.

author: Ozvalace
quote:
Genuinely abhorrent industry practices from Rockstar, just a straight up blunt hatred of their consumers, seeing them as normal but blind cattle who will worship them in spite of it all. 
- Pushing a stripped down version of the game for an insane $80
- Releasing the standard version with all the content you would expect at an even worse price of $100
- Pushing us further towards a digital only future with no disc release as well as cheap and lazy code system that allowed thousands to illegally steal others copies
- Deceptive pay-to-see marketing that showed the game as being capable of far more than it is, with no true gameplay being shown
- Clearly buying their way into the nominations of an awards show they do not qualify for 
- Buying off and blackmailing journalists for perfect review scores with the looming threat of a blacklist

And all that just to spend 13 years making a game that is a glorified boring chore simulator with a stripped down GTA game strapped on to the side of it. The large open world has almost nothing worth actually doing making it a shallow life sim instead of enjoyable GTA game, they went way to wide for the sake of having a massive map because it sounds more impressive and that's all that apparently matters. Graphic fidelity and 'ground breaking' realism for the sake of itself, with no thought given as to how any of it improves the gameplay experience, just throw pretty colors at the consumer and they'll be too dazzled to care. Not to mention that it's riddled with so many unacceptable bugs, a terrible performance on release despite a delay to address this exact issue. The game advertises 30fps which in 2026 is abhorrent alone, except for the fact that it rarely ever hits 30fps, you'll be constantly middling around the mid 20s range feeling like a slug trailing yourself over a hill of salt. And the characters are all so bad,  Jason is a bland nothing burger yes man, Lucia is just plain annoying and verges on being blatant stereotype at times. It's a bad game but none of that matters because when you're too big to fail you can just bully and buy your way to success and the hoards of cattle will believe it anyways. The industry is relying on this game to keep it supported in dire times to show that the western games industry can still produce critical successes capable of generating billions because investors and profit are the only things that matter anymore to these people. But GTA is the exception, the normalization of this anti consumer sentiment will backfire in the face of any other series and only accelerate us further to an inevitable industry crash where hopefully everybody will lose their jobs.

author: notmycupoftea
quote:
I was really looking forward to this game, like so many others. Rockstar hyped the you know what out of it and we fell for it, or least many of us did. Should have known better after the last decade of crappy releases.This game is not the GTA of old, nor is it RDR2. It's woke slop, bad writing, a less than mediocre story, and an extremely annoying sidekick you can't get rid of.
Pros
- Visuals/Frame Rate - On a PS5 Pro the visuals are excellent. The lighting is stunning, the ocean waves, the city skyline, the attention to detail. The occasional visual glitch, but nothing out of the ordinary. Frame rate on Pro doesn't drop as it appears to do on other consoles, but considering they are pushing the limits of tech, no complaints here.  9/10
- Audio - The audio engineering is probably the best I've ever heard in a game for realism. Every single detail related to audio is present and recorded/presented in a manner that doesn't pierce your eardrums. 10/10.
- Controls - Nothing out of the ordinary, exactly what you would expect. 9/10
- Driving Mechanics - Much better than GTA V. Cars feel heavy, corner properly and it avoids that arcadey feel that makes driving a pain. Collisions are very entertaining. Vehicles now behave as you would expect them to. 10/10
- Combat - Fun and fairly realistic. Targeting of different areas on enemies is very well thought out and well done. Overall, no complaints about combat, except button mashing for fighting, which is lazy. 8/10

Cons - now for the bad...
- Story/Writing - I don't know who this was written for, but this game really feels like a relationship simulator for simps. It should be called GTA 6: The Sims/Simps. You can sense it was written by women, for women, to train or crap on men and not for the GTA audience. Michael, Trevor and Franklin were wildly entertaining - no one in this game is. They are dull, boring, and forgettable. There is the occasional funny one liner, but even those are few and far between. It's the opposite of GTA V. 2/10
- Relationship - This is where it gets annoying. At first, I gave a chance to Lucia, getting the groceries, buying her flowers, etc. But that didn't last long. It was a only a matter of time before I just wanted to kick her and her annoying voice out of the house, never to be seen again. What in the heck were they actually thinking??? This game desperately needs a ghost the annoying girlfriend toggle. 1/10
- Engagement - At first, you'll be wildly entertained by the gunplay and chase sequences, but it wears off fairly quickly. Before you know it, you'll just be doing missions for the fun of it and to collect bank, just so you can avoid going home to Lucia and her snarky attitude. So yeah, it gets old and it gets old fast. 2/10
- Criminal Profile Nanny - The annoying criminal profile warnings can be turned off. Or at least I though they could. I disabled the feature. The messages appear to go way. And several hours later, I started getting warnings about how harming innocent civilians will negatively impact my criminal profile. I was literally shooting some rednecks out on some island in the middle of nowhere. This is a GTA game. It's about crime, violence, auto theft, and over the top, non real world experiences. Who on earth that in an Mature 17+  rated game that you need to 'lecture' players about their behaviour? C'mon Rockstar - what were you thinking. Get rid of that nanny nonsense. If you're so concerned about it, stop making crime games. 0/10

In Summary, the game is boring and the woke slop is real. GTA has always targeted everyone. Fair play, open season, no holds barred. In the first 15 hours of gameplay I left with the following impression; men bad/predators, women good, don't be violent. And in a GTA game, that is not the impression you want to leave with. I found myself actually thinking of picking up groceries in real life because the engagement factor drops fast. And when you star going down that road, it's all downhill from there as we all know. This game is simply not engaging. Lucia is beyond annoying. And it resembles very little of what we have come to expect in the GTA series. Rockstar is going to learn a hard lesson because people like me, who bought 3 copies last time round, are done at one and avoiding the next product. You made your bed Rockstar - now you get to sleep in it, just like Ubisoft.

author: Worthyreview
quote:
Worse than you could possibly imagine.
Games like GTA are of course held to a significantly higher standard than others and have their shortcomings amplified. 

Like many recent releases, to the misfortune legions of adoring fans, GTA is another franchise to have been neutered of the soul and fun that originally propelled it into ****.

Players can expect an almost familiar sandbox world that is extraordinarily beautiful but still somehow tragically dull and unexciting. 

The lack of excitement is noticeable quickly; mechanics of former entries in the franchise that once enhanced player experience are gone, simple activities such as stealing vehicles and driving around, are depreciated in favour of disappointing realism; immobilised cars and running out of fuel. Side quests which may have lured players into an crime laden adventure in past titles are replaced with DIY and running errands for an ungrateful girlfriend.

Performance is inexcusable. Attempting to use heavy explosive weapons, the use of which now must be carefully planned due to an inexplicably reduced weapon inventory, will grind your frame rate to sub-20. If you do managed to create some explosions , whether it is with a weapon, or a vehicle or plane? Prepare for the most deflating, cartoonish excuse for an explosion you can imagine. All that attention to detail in the scenery but you reused the explosion animation from GTA3? 

And perhaps most frustrating of all, invincible NPCs. Nothing saps the fun out of crime based sandbox quite like preventing the player from committing crimes they want to.

The direction Rockstar have taken with GTA 6 is depressing. Genuinely sad. It is not worth buying, not just because it is no fun, but because it will make you angry.

author: Sailingfan
quote: When I heard that GTA VI was going to actually release on November 19th 2026, I never thought the day would come. I was so hyped like many, many other people in the gaming community. I was not turned away by the limitations the game had (console limited and big download). When the day finally arrived, I couldn't sleep. I was so hyped and I had taken the day off to play the game. After I had played the game for the day, I started to see the cracks pop through GTA VI's shiny legacy. The game felt unpolished to me. I started to question if GTA VI really deserved the hype and praise from critics. There was more glitches than Pokemon Scarlet and Violet, the pacing of the beginning was one of the worst ever. Don't get me wrong, GTA VI is a gaming icon but we need to question if this game that took over a decade to develop and 2 billion dollars is actually a good game. I think we are just living on legacy of this game and some of us are blind to the many flaws that this game has. It baffles me that this game gets a 99. There are so many other games out there that I believe should score a 99 instead of this game (Elden Ring, Final Fantasy VII, etc.). At the end of the day, when we pull back GTA VI's shiny cover, we see a unpolished, glitch, and horribly paced story that I guarantee would not rank this high if this was any other game. But no this is GTA VI, so some of us are blind to what this video game actually is. We are giving this game more praise than it deserves. This game hardly revolutionised anything like I and many others thought. A lot of highly rated games and highly praised games have revolutionised how gaming works. We have games like The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. This game gave video games a step into 3D and its "z" targeting. The only other 99 has had a massive revolution, into 3D. GTA VI's mechanics come no where close to this. I am very disappointed in this game. I wish I could enjoy it more, I wish I could, but for the love of me, I just can't. This game is a icon but we still must question ourselves, Does GTA IV deserve the praise it gets or are we all just blinded by legacy?

author: kevandrades
quote:
The game seems to have lost the essence of what GTA is, which has always been a sandbox where you can do anything in the craziest way possible. It's still possible to do that, but it feels like the game penalizes you when you do; it seems like they tried to steer the experience so that you DON'T do it, so that you don't play GTA as if it were GTA. They tried to make you play a Red Dead Redemption 2 under the GTA name, which would be good IF this game had a story as good as RDR2 (it doesn't, and it doesn't even come remotely close). I was also very bothered by the fact that, having had 13 years of development and a budget of over 2 billion, this game arrived with so many bugs, as there were several times when I simply sank into the scenery from absolute nowhere, and it seems that the characters' hitboxes don't match their visuals. Furthermore, it's absurd that, being so expensive, this game doesn't come with voice acting in multiple languages, and this greatly hinders the experience for those who are not native English speakers. This game disappointed me, and I eagerly awaited it. 

There are several options and content enough to have play for several months, lots of references and lots of easter eggs (as GTA usually do). I prefer GTA V, though, because it was still a GTA game. And one of the most beaufitul games I've saw too.

author: Janitschar
quote: For the most anticipated game of all time, 13 years in development and reportedly costing nearly $2 billion, I expected something far more impressive than this buggy, painfully boring mess.I genuinely cannot remember the last time I felt this bored playing a game. The whole experience feels more like a boyfriend simulator than a Grand Theft Auto game. The ending was incredibly anticlimactic and downright disappointing. It only reinforced my impression that the story was driven more by an underlying agenda than by genuinely compelling storytelling.Then there are the technical issues. Being locked to 30 FPS, with the frame rate seemingly tied to the game’s physics, is unacceptable. Performance issues and stuttering were already being reported within hours of launch. The game takes up around 200 GB, yet optimization is still underwhelming. I experienced a crash myself and encountered several bugs throughout my **** for the gameplay, the missions and activities were incredibly repetitive and uninteresting. The game calls itself Grand Theft Auto, yet there’s barely any actual grand theft auto happening. Where is the chaos, the freedom, the excitement and the unpredictability that made this franchise so iconic?The only genuinely impressive aspect is the graphical fidelity. However, even there, I feel something is missing. It’s hyperrealism for the sake of hyperrealism, with very little artistic identity or visual creativity behind it. Realistic graphics alone do not make a game visually exceptional.After 13 years of development and a budget reportedly approaching $2 billion, this is an unbelievably disappointing result. I expected a generational masterpiece. Instead, I got an experience that looks incredible but feels remarkably hollow. Sadly this game is used to approach a digital future for gaming…

author: DjBiz2003
quote:
Like Star Wars: The Phantom Menace, Grand Theft Auto VI arrives under the weight of massive anticipation. Years of buildup set expectations sky-high, making even minor compromises feel glaring. A shiny new coat of paint and familiar franchise DNA cannot erase the sense that the headline event fell short of the myth surrounding it.

Forced Relationship Dynamics: Centering the experience on a fixed relationship dynamic feels restrictive rather than liberating, pushing players along a narrower emotional track than open-ended sandbox freedom allows.​

Lack of Romantic & Nightlife Freedom: Locking out other romantic pursuits and omitting sex work/prostitutes—staples that longtime players expected in a gritty, boundary-pushing GTA sandbox—feels like a major step back in player agency and series identity.

​Missed Opportunities: Across gameplay freedom, sandbox unpredictability, and player choice, too many corners feel played safe rather than pushed forward.
