If you order a burger and someone brings you chocolate instead, you wouldn't award the restaurant with top marks even if the chocolate is actually nice, would you? After all, it's not what you wanted - and GTA 6 is the same. It's not made for any existing fans - if you like it, then great -enjoy it, the steep price was worth it for you, but nobody can honestly say that this is a step up from GTA5 with any metric other than graphics.

author: Sushiguyy
quote:
What has happened to Rockstar? 

First off there’s no disc so you can’t return the game or resell it if you don’t like it. The game is also locked in at 30 FPS and it frequently drops lower than that during intense moments. How is that acceptable for a game with this much money behind it?

The characters are super annoying and bland, Jason has the personality of a plank of wood, and the story is so bad and poorly written. The physics feel off compared to the older GTAs, and the movement is way too heavy and sluggish. It feels more like Red Dead Redemption II than GTA, and not in a good way.

And why is so much of the gameplay so boring? For example at the start of the game it makes you do household chores and run errands. I bought GTA, not The Sims. The relationship between Lucia and Jason is also painfully cringe.

The humour is another massive letdown. GTA used to parody and make fun of absolutely everything, and that’s what made it so good. Now the jokes barely land or are just not funny, the satire is heavily watered down, and the game takes itself far too seriously. Prostitutes have been removed from the game, you can’t attack certain groups of people such as protesters, and you can’t even steal the cars around your neighbourhood. I thought this was supposed to be Grand Theft Auto! 

With so many of the old writers gone, it really shows. The older games had memorable characters, brilliant humour, and their own personality. Rockstar has completely lost sight of what GTA is supposed to be.

I’ll give it credit for the graphics and some of the open-world gameplay, but that’s about it. GTA 6 is an absolute disgrace to the franchise, and this is coming from someone who loves all the previous GTAs.

author: Zksy01
quote:
GTA 6 delivers impressive graphics, but fails at the very core of what defines the franchise. The game isn't an unplayable disaster, it's just mediocre, and given the massive hype, that's deeply disappointing. 

Bugs and unfinished physics: The game launched full of technical glitches and broken collisions. A clear example is crashing a boat at full speed into another one at sea: there is zero real impact, the boats feel like cardboard, and the NPCs just sit there acting like nothing happened. 

A lack of freedom and artificial restrictions: the classic chaos of GTA has been replaced by a rigid simulator. There are immortal NPCs and missions that remain locked into a linear structure, leaving the player with no real choice whatsoever. 

Bland story and characters: The dialogue feels artificial, the humor lost the sharp satire of GTA 5, and the narrative lacks the emotional weight of Red Dead Redemption 2 leaving it stuck in a bland middle ground. 

Locked performance: Capped at 30 FPS with noticeable drops during gunfights, alongside pedestrians getting stuck in the environment and animation glitches. It's pretty on the outside, yet stiff, buggy, and average on the inside. 

After more than a decade in development, we expected a revolution, not a restricted simulator.

author: LayZKing
quote:
My disappointment with GTA 6 so far is enormous. I wish I could say the 30 FPS lock was the only issue or even the biggest one, but it’s actually my smallest complaint (though it is still completely unacceptable and should never happen again). 

The story pacing is way too slow; after multiple hours, I feel like I’ve achieved nothing. I’ve met plenty of characters, yet none of them are memorable or likable. 

Most of the activities I’ve done are mundane simulation chores like fixing a sink, patching a roof, and painting a wall, After being asked to run errands for my in-game girlfriend, who, as far as I’ve noticed, does nothing in return for Jason. It already sets up a one-sided dynamic that feels degrading both for Jason and for me as the player. 

When I’m not doing chores, I’m stuck watching endless cutscenes or listening to characters talk for ages about things that don't matter and don't move the story forward. 

You might think, "Well, GTA is all about driving," except the driving **** too. The cars handle way too realistically, making it feel like you're playing Forza, except in Forza, you don't have to shoot while driving or weave through massive amounts of traffic. 

Then there’s gunplay, another core pillar of GTA. Aside from getting heavily punished just for killing a single person, the aiming feels terrible, and the aim assist barely helps. In GTA 5, you aimed, it snapped onto the target, and you fired. Here, even with aim assist turned on, you still have to manually fight the reticle. 

Finally, one of the most unbelievable parts is the audio. For a company like Rockstar, which knows how massive the streaming and content creation scene is, they clearly didn't care at all. They included a "streamer mode," except all it does is mute every track in the game, with no replacement soundtrack or original score whatsoever, leaving you in dead silence. It’s lazy and honestly disrespectful.

And last but not least, the game is straight up boring it doesn't do anything other games haven't all ready done better. True definition **** turd is still a turd

1/10. It's not a 0/10 because of Dolores, the house snake.

author: ivXn200416
quote:
GTA VI impresiona técnicamente, pero pierde la esencia irreverente de la saga.

Sinceramente me parece un juego bastante extraño. No puedo negar el enorme trabajo que hay detrás de GTA VI ni la calidad gráfica y la cantidad de experiencias que ofrece. Sin embargo siento que Rockstar está poniendo demasiado empeño en cosas secundarias como los NPCs y sus comportamientos mientras que la historia principal y lo que realmente caracteriza a GTA parecen quedar en segundo plano.
Entiendo que quieran actualizar la fórmula e incorporar elementos de la cultura actual. Pero cosas como la música, los furros y otros elementos que buscan representar estas nuevas tendencias hacen que el juego se sienta bastante alejado de lo que uno espera de un GTA. Incluso la ausencia de elementos que durante años formaron parte de la identidad de la saga como las prostitutas hace que se sienta cierto vacío.
Lo que veo es un Rockstar que parece tener miedo de apostar por aquello que hizo grandes a sus anteriores entregas. Un Rockstar demasiado preocupado por adaptarse a las nuevas sensibilidades culturales y que en el proceso parece estar perdiendo parte de su propia identidad. Por momentos da la impresión de que estamos ante una especie de guía sobre cómo mantener una relación sentimental en lugar de un GTA. Yo quiero acción. Quiero persecuciones policiales. Quiero ese caos y esa libertad que siempre han sido parte de la experiencia.
También me cuesta entender el entusiasmo desmedido que está generando. Siento que gran parte del apoyo viene de la enorme expectativa que ha provocado su larga espera y de todo el fenómeno mediático que representa más que de lo que realmente está ofreciendo.
No deja de ser un juego impresionante en términos técnicos y seguramente tendrá muchísimo que ofrecer como experiencia. Pero hay algo que simplemente no termina de convencerme. Se siente diferente y no necesariamente para bien. Esperaba un GTA que llevara la esencia de la saga a otro nivel y lo que encuentro es una propuesta que parece estar intentando convertirse en algo distinto. Y la verdad es que eso me resulta bastante decepcionante.

author: sydney88
quote:
The start of the game is very strong (and really fun!), but immediately after that it gets really bad (and very boring!). You're forced to do a lot of stuff for someone who treats you poorly. Some of these tasks could be interesting, maybe two or three times strategically spread throughout the game (just to be clear that's not exactly how they handle it). Some of the mechanics that you know are back, and just maybe one or two of them may feel a bit improved. The graphics look pretty, but the game runs poorly. You may think that when producing any big-budget interactive media; the resources would flow into optimizing frame-rate above trying to make it look like a movie. But you would be wrong. I want to judge it as a modern video game released in this current year, but it feels really hard to do at thirty frames per second (when it is locked).

I don't quite understand how this game managed to fail on the hardest-to-fail expectations, especially for a studio of this prestige, size, and past successes. The story is likely the greatest departure from the series, as my experiences with the earlier games were really good in terms of the story. This one, nothing makes sense. The characters, their decisions, it's not very relatable to most people. We've had crazy characters before, but you learn why they act the way they do and when it blends with their individual personality; the story elements all sync up and fit into place. The two main characters here are not just lazily written, but poorly written. Almost like someone tried, but they were just very bad at it.

I had a great time for a very short mission near the start of the game, and there were a few select times here and there that were close to that. But overall, this is objectively a bad game. Not even just for today's standards. It's not just the frame-rate, but its the busy-work tasks that you only have to do because of bad writing. It's the censoring (or total removal) of things that were okay, and addition of things like normalizing abusive relationships. It's the people in charge who were making the big decisions that produced such a terrible product, it's a whole lot of different stuff that happened with the game.

I would not recommend this game to anyone.

quote: Played this for several hours, and I'm sad I can't get those back. Is the game visually beautiful? Absolutely. And that's why it gets any score at all. author: Themanfrom1982
quote: I need to be extra clear on this scoring. If you have never played GTA, this game might be okay for you. If you instead spent 80 to 100 dollars in anticipation of the next GTA due to how much you love the gameplay and chaos of the game, you’ll score this game lower than I have. The only way to enjoy this game is to ignore the side missions and main missions after you’ve made enough progress to actually have fun with doing things like finally being allowed to steal an automobile. This is “Grand Theft Auto” after all, it’s no great sin to expect then that one would be able to steal an automobile- as it is intrinsic to the gameplay. Rather it should be. This game has been stuffed with the weirdest side missions ever seen in GTA, and no, it isn’t fluff to talk about this, because you skip relationship missions at the cost of your endgame cutscene. You may choose not to toil over the roof, the burgers, and the flowers at your own peril. You may also choose not to play this game. What you may not choose is to open fire on special protected NPCs, or drive through a group of protestors (though plowing through a beach is fair play) you may not choose to fire a weapon inside of certain locations. You may not choose to induce the chaos for which the games have become renowned for, but the game itself may in fact choose to throw you straight through the earth’s surface, ending with a chaotic respawn and instant wasted landing. If I hadn’t spent 80 dollars on it, if the weapon wheel worked as it was supposed to, if I hadn’t faced three no clipping events in my play through after vehemently going online to defend against the “misinformation” of the haters, I would definitely have given this a five. This game has taken my time reserved for enjoyment and replaced it with full on regret. I have no interest in a second play through nor do I see myself coming back after any patches and updates. I wanted GTA, so it seems I have to return to decade old game. Stay away from this and wait for the next GTA online, the story and missions are a grind to get through, and even when Online drops, I shudder to think of what that online experience will entail for the early players.

author: sorax86
quote: 3 years of waiting for this. Rockstar promised a revolution, but delivered a desperately hollow marketing product, devoid of soul and utterly lacking in innovation.Sure, Vice City is impressive for the first couple of hours, but once the novelty wears off, you realize what it really is: a rigid movie set where you spend more time watching than actually playing. The missions recycle a formula that's twenty years old, the writing mistakes vulgarity for satire, and the gunplay feels straight out of 2013.Everything feels like GTA V: the motion capture, the voice acting, the cinematography, everything. Or does it? Not quite, actually. What's missing is the talent, the writing, the irreverence, and above all, the **** worst part? This pathological obsession with realism that turns every single action into a chore. Everything feels clunky, slow, and tedious. Rockstar became so obsessed with simulating real life that it forgot to make an entertaining game.Behind its undeniable technological showcase (albeit a buggy one running at 25 FPS), GTA VI embodies everything that's rotten about modern AAA gaming: self-congratulation and a complete unwillingness to take any risks when it comes to gameplay.A masterpiece of marketing. Utterly forgettable.

author: bennoreviews
quote:
Let me start this by saying, the only reason this review is rated 3/10 is for the graphics, some innovative mechanics and attention to detail with the little things i.e. when you take a photo of an NPC it will react. They are genuinely cool and make the game feel immersive.

Now lets get into why I gave this review such a low score:

The writing. For about 1/4 of the game you play as Lucias skivvy, you do chores for here, decorate her house, repair her house, go grocery shopping, tend her while she has her period. Seriously Rockstar? I don't enjoy doing most of this stuff IRL, what possibly made you think I would enjoy doing it in one of the most anticipated, violent gamging titles ever created? And this idea of "empathy" in a game about stealing & m*rdering indiscriminently is just so dumb, if I wanted to play a woke boyfriend simulator I wouldn't be playing GTA now would I? 

The writing is so damn tame, safe and boring. It's just safe, millenial approved humour. There's no edge, no "punching down" (heaven forbid we're a bit meany weany in a 18+ previously edgy video game series). But you only have to look at the staff and "new company culture" at Rockstar to figure out why that is.

Also, giving godmode to certain NPCs i.e. protestors so you can't do what you've been able to do in GTA games forever? How about not being able to use guns in, indoor spaces i.e. nightclubs? Really? It's all safe, safe, safe, thou shalt not offend! It's just not the GTA I remember. 

Maybe I'm no longer the target audience of the franchise, after all I grew up on San Andreas, GTA III and later GTA V. Absolute masterpieces in my humble opinion and it's really quite sad that gaming companies are now catering for the "wrapped up in cotton-wool" generation.

author: dwtj
quote: Grand Theft Auto 6 is a perfect game. The story experiences nothing but exhilarating highs, every mission showcases Rockstar's timeless design philosophy that has only grown more sophisticated with age, every section delivers precisely the right amount of gunplay, the geography of Leonidas boasts impeccable consistency and unparalleled biome variety, the ownership system is everything we could have dreamed of, and the PS5 Pro's cinematic frame rate is exactly what we wanted. Yet even these countless triumphs pale in comparison to what GTA 6 achieves at its core. Rockstar hasn't simply built the biggest, most beautiful open world with the greatest variety of activities ever conceived: it's built a world where every system, character, environment, and player interaction exists in perfect harmony. A heist isn't just a mission, a car isn't just a vehicle, the sea isn't just a border, money isn't just a number, and Jason and Lucia aren't just two characters to switch between. Everything becomes part of something greater: GTA 6 is an open world so flawlessly realized that it generates stories through its systems even more masterfully than through its already impeccable script. Some will probably find themselves overwhelmed by the sheer perfection of an experience that leaves absolutely nothing to be desired. We, however, believe this is not merely the evolution the series needed, but the absolute pinnacle of interactive entertainment. There is nothing to improve, nothing to criticize, and nothing left for the medium to achieve. Grand Theft Auto 6 is perfection itself.

author: Giogex
quote:
There are a lot of issues. We waited 11 long years for this game, followed by another 2 years of delays because Rockstar Games promised to optimize it to avoid glitches and bugs. Launching with glitchy physics, random crashes after just a few hours of gameplay, and significant FPS drops, sometimes even after explosion scenes, is simply unacceptable. Rockstar Games has failed to deliver on its promises this time. It's not fair to treat the hundreds of thousands of players who have been waiting for this moment for over a decade this way. From a technical standpoint, the game is nowhere near where it should be. Without a doubt, it will set new standards for the future, but first, they absolutely need to fix all of these issues.
In my personal opinion, in 2026, having fewer than 60 FPS is absolutely unacceptable. For this reason alone, it doesn't deserve a 99/100. Other games have been heavily criticized for these exact same issues, while in this case, this aspect has been completely overlooked. It's a double standard that seems to favor Rockstar Games. Games like Cyberpunk 2077, Mass Effect Andromeda, Pokémon Scarlet and Violet, No Man's Sky, and Forspoken immediately come to mind, just to name a few. These games were heavily criticized for glitches, severe FPS drops, poorly expressive facial animations, lack of multiplayer, and shallow dialogue. author: Jean4521

GTA 6 sacrifices enjoyment for realism, and that’s its biggest problem. None of the characters, including the protagonists, have any real personality, making it difficult to care about the story. 

The missions are repetitive and uninspired, mostly revolving around stealing cocaine, killing a bunch of people, and leaving, with little buildup or memorable **** game also forces you into a relationship-driven storyline that feels restrictive rather than engaging. 

There’s a fine line between realism and enjoyment, and GTA 6 crosses it, whether through its driving mechanics, or unnecessary everyday tasks.

GTA 5 understood what made the franchise fun: absurdity, freedom, edgy missions, memorable characters, and the ability to pull a machine gun out of nowhere. GTA was never meant to be a simulation of everyday life. 

Better graphics and more realism don’t necessarily make a better game, especially when they come at the expense of fun

author: nameisnight
quote:
Visuals are amazing and the base world is great, what ruins the game is the Storyline and the forced limitations that remove core GTA game mechanics that have been around for years.

Spoiler: You spend actual hours doing chores to get your girlfriend to be happy while the whole game she is emotionally abusive to you and you have no real choice but to take it and keep going or the game gives you a fail state. Vary little actual crime gameplay. The entire game you are given little to no choice but to follow the writers story how THEY want it. Past GTAs you had options, now you don't.

Special groups of NPCs in the game have a protected status meaning you cannot do anything to them, GTA has always been about being able to be free in a world of crime, to be able to do what you want and have fun, Now they introduced rules that break the core GTA experience. The game is called Grand Theft Auto, it implies crime is the whole game, but what they did was add systems and fail states that make you follow the rules. 

This is NOT GTA, what they made here is a Crime/Romcom Dating simulator and stole the GTA name. 

Dont get me started on the paywall, if you buy the lower priced version of the game you get gatekeeped from locations, features, items and more. A large part of the game is kept away from you that was part of the base game in past GTA titles. Even if you pay the extra fee to get the premium version of the game they give you items like special skins, weapons and vehicles... Just to remove them after a in game event or quest. THEY REMOVE THE ITEMS FROM THE GAME AFTER A QUEST THAT YOU PAID EXTRA TO GET.

I have played every GTA since GTA 3, this game is not GTA. Its like they started world building but when they got to the story planning they just transplanted someone's poor excuse for a fantasy into a game style that does not work with it. 

The only way to redeem this mess is to rewrite the entire storyline, remove the anti-fun and gatekeeping mechanics and apologies to the what used to be fans who Rockstar burned and Disappointed. But they wont, I bet they will double down. GTA and Rockstar North will probably end up getting shut down like all the other studios who thought ruining their franchises and losing their fanbase just to appease others would be a good idea. 

I filed a refund for this travesty of a excuse ****, This is no GTA. Years of hype wasted. I hope a smart studio or indie studio takes this chance to make something that GTA fans actually wanted.

author: Universe123
quote: Después de 13 años esperando GTA VI y de escuchar cifras de presupuesto cercanas a los 2.000 millones de dólares, aunque no estén confirmadas, me encuentro con una de las mayores decepciones que he sufrido como jugador. He experimentado cierres inesperados, misiones bloqueadas, personajes atravesando paredes y suelos, vehículos que salen disparados sin sentido, animaciones rotas, texturas que no cargan, errores de sonido, controles que dejan de responder y problemas con el progreso de mis partidas. El rendimiento es lamentable: esperaba una experiencia fluida a 60 FPS y me encuentro con un objetivo de 30 que, en mi caso, ni siquiera se mantiene durante buena parte del tiempo. Tirones constantes, caídas de fotogramas y una optimización indigna de semejante superproducción. ¿De qué sirven unos gráficos espectaculares si el juego funciona a trompicones? ¿De qué sirve un mundo gigantesco si sus físicas parecen una broma? No he pagado para trabajar gratis como probador de errores de Rockstar. También me indigna el modelo de licencias digitales, que limita el control real sobre lo que compramos y nos hace depender de plataformas, cuentas y condiciones ajenas. Estoy harto de que la industria normalice vender juegos que necesitan parches para funcionar correctamente. No me valen las excusas de que todos los juegos tienen bugs ni que algún día lo arreglarán. Rockstar dispone de experiencia y recursos para ofrecer muchísimo más. Después de tanta publicidad, tanta espera y tantas expectativas, lo mínimo era un producto estable. En mi experiencia, GTA VI es un desastre técnico disfrazado de revolución gráfica. Mucho espectáculo visual, pero demasiados errores fundamentales. Mi tiempo y mi dinero merecen más respeto. No compro promesas ni pago para hacer de beta tester. Una decepción monumental. 0/10.

author: nomaddc
quote:
A game that not only doesn't work as one would expect a game in 2026 to work, but also under delivers and in many ways betrays the fans.
Atrocious performance, we are still being told that 30fps "target" is an acceptable video game performance in 2026, but it doesn't stop there - there are of course bugs, lots. Cyberpunk 2077 got a lot more flak for a messy launch, and while it's comparable here we see a lot of people coming out to let us know that we should not trust our lying eyes and ears.
Narrative is... bad, even for a GTA game. Gone is the fire it had for merciless satire of modernity, now it's safer, more equitable, with soft and rounded corners. Instead of a compelling but ultimately tragic criminal story we get a girlfriend simulator disguised as a boyfriend simulator, where Jason is just the right kind of imaginary bf for all the players (do they exist?) who can see themselves in a feisty latina. Good on you, at least someone is getting what they have wanted.

It's a step down even from GTA V - bouncy airplanes, unstealable cars, restrictions on who you can fire an imaginary gun at. But hey, you can work out now and paint walls!

The monetization is there to stay - GTA plus has wormed its way even into single player, so you can be sure there are plans for when the Online part of the game comes (if it will at this point).

Overall, if you enjoy the current thing, but want to still maintain a sort of image of a free thinker and a rebel, and be edgy because the news lady is freaking out yet again about your favorite game (are we sure it's not a weird paid marketing campaign? Every damn time a GTA comes out they roll them put) then this is for you. A nice change of pace from Madden/CoD and your other favorite gacha/gamba/annual slop that you can consume and wear proudly as your gamer badge.

Lucia hides Jason's kid and gives him away, and Jason just acts like it's the happiest day of his life. You hold a door open and get "as you should" thrown back at you, or you walk up to a half naked male stripper grinding on your girl and just get brushed off and sent away like a punk. Even GTA 5 had Michael in a miserable marriage getting cheated on, but the entire point of his arc was snapping, tearing down the tennis coach's house, and breaking free from that humiliation. Here, you are just stuck taking it with spineless writing that makes zero **** has always been about escaping real life for a bit and living out those crazy, messed up impulses we all have sometimes. In real life, you obviously don't act on that trash because life is complicated, actions have real consequences, and you share the world with actual human beings. In GTA, you're supposed to let loose, take **** from nobody, and go full maniac. quote: The characters are boring and unlikeable, especially Lucia. She's a terrible person who abandons her child to commit a robbery, doesn't tell the father about it and allows her son to get taken into state custody. Speaking of that, the game seriously has you spend considerable time doing domestic menial tasks like painting and roofing, working out, paying bills, getting groceries. Jason is also incredibly dull, he's a cardboard cutout, he has no opinions and does everything Lucia asks. The game is incredibly slow, boring and unfun. Genuinely who at Rockstar thought a 10 hour prologue taking up almost ⅕ of the game was a good idea? The story is also boring. There's no good missions or fun to be had, compare that to the multiple heists in GTA 5 and RDR 2. There's no interesting NPCs or villains, and no conflict. The writing and dialogue are terrible, and are not well acted. All things considered, 13 years and a billion dollars, with a $100 price the and no disc, this game is a MASSIVE let down. It's not GTA. author: wamozartk466
quote:
I wanted to love it so badly as huge fan of this franchise.  But I have to be honest.  This is a travesty to the GTA franchise.  A complete departure from the tone and feel we've come to know and love from Rockstar Games.  

The pacing is god awful.  The voice acting is cheesy and poorly executed.  Especially Jason.  He just flat out ****.  Lucia is not much better.  The dialogue is hackneyed and eye-rolling.  It takes hours to even get to the point that you can commit the crime the game is NAMED AFTER.  You spend more time doing chores and taking care of your virtual girlfriend than doing any Grand Theft Autoing.  And you still can't steal nicer cars until you get a clone key much later in the playthrough.  This completely ruins the game for me off rip but this doesn't even begin to scratch the surface of the flaws this game is filled with.  I don't want to drone on too long so I will give a list of the reasons I would not recommend this game if you are a longtime fan of the franchise:

1. The game is 30 FPS sometimes.  Its not even locked. It's "targeting".  That's a joke in 2026.  Poor optimization is the only explanation.  If it's pushing the limits of the console, it's because it's a mess. Not because it's a marvel of software development.
2. Bugs.  This ties in with Point 1.  If this was optimized, there wouldn't be bugs. Unbelievable that they launched the game in this state.
3. Story ****. Straight up.  I hate it. It's so jarring going from any game in the series to this.
4. Characters **** and have very little personality or what personality they do have I can't stand (looking at you, Lucia). The voice acting is so bad.
5. Far too much focus on romance and mundane tasks and the missions are not that fun.  If I wanted to do romance and life sim, I'd play the Sims 4.
6. Loss of agency and the empathy/morality system.  Don't tell me how to play your game.  GTA was renowned for player agency.  Any design idea that reduces agency should've been mocked and scrapped.  I guess that's what happens when you put a bunch of soft leftists in the development team that can't handle their ideas being challenged and told no.
7. There are obvious Feminist undertones in this game throughout and Lucia **** and is representative of everything that I hate about modern feminist politics. Cry all you want, I don't want that crap in my game. Period.  I play games to get away from that nonsense.  I don't want any politics in my game, actually.  Not even politics I agree with.  This game is woke and that automatically makes me not like it.  Delete my review and avoid reality all you want. I don't care.  It's not going to make me agree with your opinion.
8. Protected NPCs that can't be killed.  Seriously.  I can't believe they thought this was okay at all.
9. Not one cutscene made me laugh.  Not one of these characters is funny or charming in anyway.  This is unprecedented for a Rockstar release.  Especially GTA.

In conclusion, this game is a joke and a slap in the face of the franchise. 

Shame on you Rockstar.  I will never buy another game of yours again!  I hope your studio goes out of business.

author: Falsiq
quote: I've played around 29 hours of GTA VI so far, and I genuinely don't understand how people are calling this a masterpiece. My biggest problem is that it barely feels like GTA anymore. It feels like Rockstar took Red Dead Redemption 2, threw some cars and modern buildings into it, and called it GTA VI. Everything is slower, more restrictive, and way more focused on realism than actually being fun. The first 10 hours are **** exhausting. The pacing is terrible, the missions are repetitive, and the game constantly forces you to do boring **** before letting you experience anything interesting. It honestly feels like a life simulator at times, and no, making everything realistic doesn't automatically make it good gameplay. Then there's the freedom, or the lack of it. What happened to just jumping into GTA and doing whatever the hell you wanted? Now you've got a karma system, activities and interactions locked behind progression, NPCs reacting to your behavior, and ridiculously overpowered cops that make causing chaos more frustrating than entertaining. I understand what Rockstar was trying to achieve, but I don't understand why anyone would pretend this offers the same experience as previous GTA games. It doesn't. The whole game feels like it's constantly telling you how to play. The missions aren't much better either. Sure, there are some genuinely great moments, and a few missions are absolutely fantastic. But those are exceptions. Most of the time, you're following instructions, watching conversations, driving somewhere, and repeating the same boring routine. Having a massive open world means very little when the actual gameplay feels so restrictive. And the worst part? The game is technically incredible. The graphics, animations, NPC behavior, world details, all of that is impressive. I won't deny it. But I really couldn't care less about how realistic an NPC's daily routine is when I'm bored out of my mind playing the game. I'm also tired of this idea that criticizing GTA VI means you don't appreciate good games. I can appreciate the insane amount of work that went into it while still thinking the actual experience is disappointing. Maybe people who love Red Dead Redemption 2 and slow, heavily scripted experiences will absolutely love this game. That's fine. But I wanted GTA, not a crime-themed life simulator where I have to worry about consequences every time I want to have some fun. After 29 hours, I can say it's not a terrible game. It's just a massive disappointment compared to what I expected from GTA. Rockstar created one of the most detailed open worlds I've ever seen, but somehow made me feel less free than I did playing GTA San Andreas over 20 years ago. And for a GTA game, that's a pretty **** big problem.

author: AstroBot149
quote: Grand Theft Auto VI is the most expensive argument for game preservation I have ever played: thirteen years, two billion dollars, and a world so detailed you can almost forget there is nothing to do in it. Rockstar has confused technical ambition with design, realism with entertainment, and a character with a personality disorder. A beautiful world is worthless if inhabiting it feels like a shift at work. Here is the question nobody at Rockstar seems to have asked: do you actually want to spend sixty hours with these two? Lucia is not a strong female protagonist. She is a customer complaint with a criminal record. Impulsive, rude, and convinced her bad decisions are everyone else's fault, she’s exhausting that the writing mistakes for complexity. There is a difference between rebellious and irresponsible, between independent and treating your partner like an inconvenience and having an attitude problem. The relationship is a one-way street: Jason accommodates, she decides, she creates the mess, he cleans it up. A couple is not compelling because the writers announce they are in love. Show us why. The motherhood angle is worse. Having a child is not character development. It is a promise the game makes about responsibility and then breaks every time she does something reckless. If you want sympathy, earn it. I do not need her to be good. I need her to be well written, and those are not the same thing. Jason is the opposite failure: a man with the personality of a plank. Quiet? fine. Empty is not. Where are his convictions, his ambitions, his conflicts? He is furniture with a gun. And no, flawed does not mean good. Impulsive, rude and irresponsible are ingredients, not a character. Real complexity is contradictions that hold together, decisions that reveal something, mistakes that cost something. If the writing wants me to read selfishness as strength, that is not my failure as an audience. That is the writing. Realism is not an excuse for tedium. GTA used to be an adult playground stealing a car in V was a crime. Here you need a permission slip. It is a video game, not a simulator, and Rockstar seems to have forgotten the difference. Missions are worse. Cinematic is fine, but restrictive scripting and drawn-out busywork have sanded off the freedom that made this series matter. The technical achievement is real, and it excuses nothing. They do not excuse the bugs, the broken mission sequences, the inconsistent performance or the controls. Graphics are not gameplay. Animation is not mission design. Detail is not writing. A two billion dollar screensaver is not a game. Thirteen years, and the result is GTA V with a better skin and a worse attitude. Where is the evolution in mission design, the freedom of a playground, the humour that used to have teeth? The RDR2 comparison is where this falls apart. Red Dead earned its quiet moments. You knew the gang, you understood Arthur, you had spent dozens of hours with those people, so fishing and camp upkeep meant something. VI demands the same patience before earning a second of it. Why should I care about maintaining a household or buying flowers for a woman I do not like yet? Six hours of groceries, haircuts and painting walls is not immersion It is a second job, and it does not even pay. Same with freedom. Red Dead's slow content was optional. VI makes domestic life mandatory, importing the FiveM role-play crowd's idea of fun into a campaign the rest of us bought for crime and chaos. Offer immersion. Do not enforce it. The best immersion is the one the player chooses, and the best open world is one you are allowed to ignore. You already have groceries, errands and obligations. You play GTA to escape ordinary life, not to clock into a second one. I wanted this to be exceptional. Buy it at 80% off in two years, or watch someone else play it for free.

author: jetsplat
quote: Considering the game's budget and development time, it falls far short of expectations. A "perfect" game was promised, which is why it was delayed multiple times yet it is nowhere near perfect; it is riddled with bugs, some of which appear right from the start. The story mode is merely average, failing to meet the standards one would expect from the series. There are noticeable frame-rate drops, it doesn't even hit 60fps on the PS5 Pro, and the standard PS5 struggles to maintain 30fps. The gameplay mechanics are hardly revolutionary, offering only minor improvements over GTA V, and while the map is large, there is very little environmental variety. I am deeply disappointed with Rockstar’s work, especially given the budget spent; the only decent aspect of the game is its graphics. As mentioned, the missions are lackluster compared to the rest of the series. The narrative focuses a bit too heavily on the relationship between the two protagonists, which would be fine, if this weren't a game about heists, as the title implies. The car physics are reasonably decent in terms of acceleration, but the flight mechanics for aircraft are in desperate need of an overhaul. Now, we just have to wait and see how the online mode is handled and how the game performs at full capacity on PC, though right now it doesn't even come close to the hype.

author: ZUH2614
quote:
El lanzamiento de Grand Theft Auto VI deja en evidencia una grave desconexión entre la ambición técnica prometida durante trece años de desarrollo y la realidad de su ejecución en consolas. En una PlayStation 5 estándar, la experiencia se ve seriamente comprometida por una tasa de fotogramas inestable que desciende hasta los 15 o 20 FPS, acompañada de constante stuttering durante la conducción a alta velocidad y los enfrentamientos armados, lo que degrada la respuesta de los controles y la fluidez jugable. A esta deficiencia de rendimiento se suman problemas evidentes de pop-in en elementos del entorno, múltiples errores visuales y fallos en el motor de físicas —como colisiones defectuosas en aeronaves y comportamientos erráticos en los personajes— que rompen la inmersión y recuerdan al problemático estreno de Cyberpunk 2077. Asimismo, el producto final presenta un recorte notable frente a la calidad exhibida en sus tráilers iniciales, resultando en un mundo abierto que se percibe vacío, con animaciones y expresiones faciales menos realistas que las vistas en entregas previas del estudio como Red Dead Redemption 2, y sostenido por mecánicas tan anticuadas que hacen sentir el título más como una expansión de GTA V que como una evolución generacional. Resulta difícil justificar que un juego de alto costo y con un ciclo de producción tan extenso dependa de la potencia adicional de PlayStation 5 Pro apenas para alcanzar una estabilidad aceptable, demostrando una optimización insuficiente que penaliza directamente al jugador en el hardware base.
Más allá de su apartado técnico, el título evidencia un claro estancamiento creativo que se oculta detrás de un lavado de cara visual con gráficos semirrealistas. A pesar del fenómeno mediático y el FOMO generado por ser el estreno más esperado de la década, la obra no aporta una verdadera innovación a la industria del videojuego ni reinventa su propia fórmula; en esencia, sigue siendo un GTA convencional que recicla las mismas estructuras jugables y recurre nuevamente a los clichés habituales de la franquicia centrados en el exceso de sexo, drogas, alcohol y lenguaje altisonante. En lugar de arriesgarse a transformar el género o evolucionar narrativamente, el estudio optó por ofrecer una entrega continuista que prioriza la zona de confort comercial por encima de una genuina revolución en el diseño de videojuegos.
Por todo lo anterior, en una escala de 0 a 100, la calificación final para este lanzamiento es un 20. Resulta indefendible que una producción con una inversión estimada de entre 1,000 y 2,000 millones de dólares, que además exige al consumidor un desembolso de 80 USD (y hasta 110 USD en sus ediciones especiales) bajo la promesa del mayor acontecimiento en la historia del entretenimiento, entregue un resultado tan mediocre frente al hype generado. Esta puntuación refleja el incumplimiento de los estándares mínimos de calidad: un título con serios problemas de jugabilidad en su plataforma base por su pésima optimización, plagado de fallos técnicos, carente de innovación frente a sus predecesores y sustentado únicamente en el peso de su marca para cobrar precios abusivos por un trabajo inacabado.

EDIT: Le bajo a 1 porque me acorde que no hay idioma a español y leer puro subtitulo arruina mas la experiencia. Y todo por no querer arrumar "la visión del artista" en esta novela que parece pelijuego haciéndole de mandadero de Lucía y un simp sin identidad.

author: Apocali
quote:
This game should not be called GTA.

GTA is more than just a title. It's a promise of a certain experience: a satirical criminal underworld filled with dark humor, morally dysfunctional antiheroes, and the freedom for players to explore the sandbox on their own terms. This identity was established and refined over decades, largely thanks to the legendary Dan Houser.

GTA VI, however, was written under different creative leadership.

What I find particularly disturbing is Rob Nelson's interview with The Guardian (November 15, 2026), where he discusses deliberately encouraging different player behavior through gameplay mechanics. From a player's perspective, this can easily feel like an attempt to impose the developers' own values rather than preserve the freedom that has always defined GTA.

Technically and graphically, GTA VI is an absolute marvel. But when the creative leadership prioritizes pushing a particular message over respecting the established identity of the franchise..

After 13 years of waiting, I feel robbed.

author: manuelhfx
quote: I grew up with Grand Theft Auto. From the early top-down games onward, the appeal was never just the missions. It was the feeling that the city belonged to you: take a car, make a mess, get chased, find a way out, and create your own story between the objectives. GTA VI is an extraordinary technical achievement, but after playing it on Xbox Series X, I’m left wondering whether Rockstar still understands that particular kind of fun.Leonida is stunning. The streets, people, interiors and background activity create a world with an absurd level of detail. But a world can feel alive and still feel restrictive. Too often, I’m moving through a carefully staged sequence of errands, tutorials and relationship beats instead of being let loose in a crime sandbox. The game is full of things to do, but many of them feel like chores dressed up as immersion.Stealing a car is a good example. It has always been one of GTA’s most basic pleasures: spot a vehicle, take it, improvise. Here, getting the car you want can involve breaking in, hot-wiring it and dealing with alarms or other extra systems. I understand the idea: make theft feel more believable and give different cars different risks. In practice, it adds friction to an action that used to feel immediate and mischievous. Realism is only an improvement when it makes the play more fun. Here, it often makes the fun **** same issue appears in the small rules of daily life. You can leave the house in swimwear, but apparently not in underwear or nightwear. At first, I thought it was a glitch. Then I found out it was intentional. That’s the sort of detail that makes me question what this game means by realism. The world can simulate an astonishing amount, yet it draws a firm line at walking outside in pajamas. Why? It doesn’t make the game more believable to me; it makes it feel like I’m being managed by a set of arbitrary **** relationship between Jason and Lucia is central, and the game asks me to invest in it through shared activities and domestic details. That may work for players who want a crime story built around a couple. I don’t. I felt tethered to their relationship when I wanted the freedom to define my own experience in the city. Instead of feeling like a criminal making choices, I often felt like an audience member being guided through a story about two characters whose priorities I didn’t share.Then there’s the strange question of what the game considers acceptable chaos. You can kill people in places like a parade or a gay bar, yet other parts of the criminal fantasy feel increasingly managed and procedural. That doesn’t come across as bold or transgressive to me. It feels arbitrary: the game will let you do something shocking, but it doesn’t consistently give you the playful, unpredictable freedom that made those acts part of a wider sandbox. Shock value isn’t the same as agency.Even the spectacle can feel oddly restrained. I expect planes to be part of the same unpredictable physics toybox as cars and helicopters, where a bad decision can turn into a spectacular disaster. Instead, the experience can feel protected from the kind of absurd collision and escalation that older GTA players learned to create for themselves. The series used to thrive on the gap between what the game expected and what the player decided to do. GTA VI often feels like it has already decided how the moment should go.I can see the craft everywhere. The city is gorgeous, the performances are strong, and the systems are ambitious. I can also see why people will love the density, the realism and the focus on Jason and Lucia. But those strengths don’t fix the central problem for me: the game seems more interested in simulating a believable life than giving me the liberating, ridiculous crime fantasy I came here for.I don’t need every GTA to be a copy of the first games. I do need it to remember why those games were exciting. A huge map, thousands of details and elaborate systems don’t add up to freedom if the moment-to-moment play feels like a set of chores with occasional permission to cause mayhem.I grew up with GTA because it made me feel like anything could happen. In GTA VI, I keep feeling like the game has a preferred way for everything to **** this a GTA? It looks like one. It has the name, the city and the crime. But for me, the freedom that made GTA feel like GTA is buried under all the things it wants me to do.

author: tyresia2
quote:
Extremely boring game, filled with not-so-veiled feminist propaganda. Just as everyone expected, all women are strong, wise, powerful, resilient and even physically superior to men in most instances. 

Lucia is bossy and obnoxious, constantly starved for attention and borderline psychotic, but the game somehow forces you to like her. Can you complete the game without romancing her? Sure you can, but you'll be soft-locked out of most of the narrative if you do. So you're stuck with an extremely unbalanced girlfriend simulator where a spoiled, unsufferable woman constantly takes the scene, leaving the bumbling protagonist to lie in shadows. I mean, for a game called "Grand Theft Auto", it's quite symbolic how most of the time she's the one behind the wheel during chases and action sequences. 

I spent the entire game praying Lucia would be incarcerated again, this time for good. And we're supposed to bond with her.

Besides that, the gameplay is tear-inducingly boring. We waited 13 years for a modern reskin of Red Dead Redemption 2, minus the charming characters, the charismatic main charachter, the breath-taking setting, the compelling story, and the powerful script. All we've got is an "open world" that leaves you with very little to do, lots and lots of invisible walls and limited content, and endless indoctrination hidden nearly everywhere. We were expecting action, destruction, freedom, silly comedy, social criticism, and explosions. What we've got is a wannabe The Sims with some foid-written misandrist romance.

My best advice is to avoid paying $100 for an HR struggling session padded with fake gameplay and a daily chores simulator. Unless you really like the idea of experiencing the pain of dealing with a toxic woman. Like the ones who wrote the script of this overpriced dumpster fire.

author: Thalazon
quote:
I see more people reverse review bombing than actually review bombing. What concerns me are the amount of people leaving it 9/10 and 10/10 when they openly admit egregious negatives and that they haven't even gotten out of chapter 1.

The game is not anywhere close to a 10/10 for me. Feels too much like RDR2. The lead characters are weaker than GTAV, the story is weaker, the plot is weaker, the graphics are improved but 30fps dropping down below 20 at times is terrible. Lucia is an absolutely terrible character and not likeable in the slightest. 

That being said the 4 points I did give it are for several positive directions. NPCs and their random interactions are absolutely hilarious and a clear improvement over GTAV. The map itself is wonderful and has a TON to offer along with the NPCs. I didn't enjoy the vehicle controls and gunplay but I can see how some people enjoy it, for a game that seems to ripoff RDR2 (especially with several story points) the gunplay is not as fun as RDR2 but again that's just my preference. 

I can see how new players to the franchise would like the game since they don't have the expectations set from previous rockstar titles. But this game just feels like a step in the wrong direction in so many ways. 

If people think the relationship between the lead characters is amazing then I shudder to think their real life relationships are like. Sure they have some good chemistry and there are some genuinely good moments between the two over the course of the game, the relationship as a whole is far from healthy and shouldn't be championed (a critique of the journos here). 

The relationship emphasis was a deliberate game design choice and genuinely detracts from the freedom previous titles game, looking at GTAV here. It is a serious step backward that hurts the experience. I'm sure this won't be a problem once they release the multiplayer but this version being weighed for GOTY doesn't have that.

I could go on more but y'all get the gist. Is it a bad game? No. Is it worth playing? Yeah I can see it appealing to a lot of people. My review is "generally unfavorable" because it's impossible not to compare it to GTAV and see it as disappointing to say the least. Nothing they did here is innovating or groundbreaking except the AI... BUT the AI is the reason for the terrible 30fps cap since the CPU on consoles are the issue. I can't help feeling that a PC release with smoother technicals and less bugs would make it far more enjoyable. Don't get me started on the bugs either.

4/10 a good game that was over hyped by the journos, released locked at 30fps, multiple day one bugs that break the game, a mediocre story, with a lot of steps backwards for the franchise, but it's a GTA game so there's still enjoyment to be had.

author: dh2ix78
quote:
Beautiful Game, but the Story Isn't for Me 

I've been watching YouTube videos of my favorite streamers playing this game. I wanted to see how they played it and what they thought of the story. I was even looking forward to the PC version, supposedly coming in March. But after seeing more of the story, I've decided to skip it. And I want to explain why. First, I'm not saying this is a bad game. It genuinely looks beautiful, with really cool designs. The environments and characters clearly took a lot of effort. I can appreciate that, even if I don't enjoy the direction of the story. Good visuals just aren't enough for me. What really puts me off is the relationship drama. You have a character basically deciding, "You know what? I'm going to cheat on my boyfriend." And I'm sitting here thinking: seriously? I already deal with this kind of **** in real life. Why the **** would I want more of it in a game? I grew up with games that were simply fun. They offered fantasy, adventure, excitement, and escape. Now, some games feel like they're pushing propaganda or constantly reminding me of the worst parts of everyday life. Sometimes I want a fantasy, not another depiction of reality. People turn to games to escape that ****. Why bring so much of it into the worlds we're trying to enjoy? That doesn't mean every game needs to be cheerful. It just means this kind of story isn't what I'm looking for. And if this is your cup of tea, go ahead and enjoy it! I'm not telling anyone to stop playing or having fun. People are allowed to like things I don't. But if a story makes me uncomfortable before I even play, what's the point of spending money on it? Another disappointment is the lack of relationship choices. The first trailer showed several interesting female characters. A **** ton of people were excited about those designs. There was even that mosh-pit girl with the rocker, festival-girl aesthetic, who immediately caught my attention. She looked like someone with a fun personality to explore. It made me think we might get different relationship options, with different women and different personalities. Instead, it seems we're stuck with one main female character. And, frankly, not everyone likes her. I've seen people criticizing her, and I can understand why. Not everyone has the same taste in women. Some prefer a rocker girl; others want someone completely different. So why show all these interesting characters if the game gives us so little choice about romance? That feels like a massive missed opportunity. And the male protagonist isn't helping matters either. From what I've seen, he feels really two-dimensional. He's just doing basic chores and fixing up the house. At times, it looks like he renovates an entire home in one afternoon. How the hell is that realistic? Yes, she's in prison. Okay, cool, that's part of the story. But meanwhile, this guy is just fixing a house. It all looks strangely empty to me. Where's the personality or anything that makes him interesting? I don't mind slower games or everyday activities. Those things can be enjoyable if they're written well. But the way they're presented here doesn't grab me. I'm watching and wondering why I should care. That's not the feeling I want from a game. When the PC version arrives, I expect modders may step in. I wouldn't be surprised to see mods that supposedly "fix" the story problems that some players complain about. Maybe people will even try creating completely new storylines, or letting players romance characters they actually prefer. Whether huge story mods will be possible is another question. But I can see why people would want to try. For me, the final decision is pretty simple. It's a beautiful game, and I respect anyone who enjoys it. But its story, characters, and limited choices aren't for me. I want games that let me escape, have fun, and choose my path. I don't need another dose of real-life cheating and drama. If you love it, great! Enjoy yourself. I'm not calling it a bad game or telling you to stop. Personally, though, I'm skipping this one.

author: TheOnlyXeridian
quote:
X-Reviews:This game gets a 1 strictly for its amazing graphics, and that is the only praise it deserves. From start to finish, the experience feels like a bait-and-switch that strips away the core identity of the Grand Theft Auto franchise. It takes six hours just to reach any real gameplay, and even then, the pacing never picks up. Instead of classic series staples, players are locked into mandatory relationship missions and unwelcome story beats that do a disservice to male protagonists, women, and military veterans alike. On a technical level, the game is a broken mess—ridden with severe bugs, broken AI, unresponsive NPCs, and abysmal frame rates that struggle to maintain 30 FPS on console. Worse yet, these major gameplay and performance issues were hidden until after launch, leaving players trapped past refund windows while outlets handed out glowing pre-release scores and early award nominations without real player input.

Positives:   
 • Graphics: They did a great job on the Fidelity of the game, though this is what mainly hinders the frame rate until a PC version is released.    
• Sound & Music: This isn’t hard to get right these days and the music has some great selections from licensed offerings while the Composed music is serviceable.

 Negatives:
    • Bugs and glitches: Ridden with bugs throughout, including falling through the map, texture pop-ins, and flying through buildings without explosions or consequences.    
• Poor console performance: Struggles to hold a steady 30 FPS on any console, with lower-end consoles dropping to 10–15 FPS.    
• Slow pacing: Takes six hours to reach real gameplay and never picks up momentum.    
• Weak AI and NPCs: Features scripted, unconvincing AI and poorly coded NPCs, including unresponsive characters standing overnight inside closed stores.    
• Shifted core mechanics: Reduces car theft and removes staple series elements such as sex workers and harming protesters.    
• Forced story and character direction: Locks players into mandatory relationship missions and unwelcome story beats, while main characters' faces closely resemble those from Red Dead Redemption 2.    
• Writing and representation: Criticized for its writing direction and for how it portrays women, military veterans, and male protagonists.    
• Refund and business practices: Accused of hiding rough gameplay until past refund windows, denying most refunds after launch, and facing fallout from firing 34 unionized employees in October 2025.    
• Critic scores and awards: Faulted for receiving perfect critic scores despite noted bugs, as well as eight pre-release award nominations before any player sentiment existed.   
• Price and MTX: Pushes the trend of raising base game prices to $79.99 while locking major pre-existing content behind a $20 Day 1 paywall, and even interrupts gameplay with an in-game pop-up pushing a GTA+ subscription for additional Day 1 exclusives.

Conclusion:
Ultimately, after 12 to 13 years of development and an estimated budget of $1 to $2 billion—making it the most expensive game ever produced—delivering an unpolished, bug-ridden product is inexcusable. Expecting players to simply accept a deeply flawed launch explains why so little real gameplay was shown prior to release and why refunds are being aggressively denied. When you spend over a decade and billions of dollars as a flagship AAA studio, players deserve a complete, functional, and faithful experience—not a broken game loaded with Day 1 paywalls.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND GTA VI, SAVE YOUR MONEY AND PLAY SOMETHING ELSE INSTEAD THAT DOESNT HOLD YOUR HAND , WASTE YOUR TIME, BELITTLE YOU AS A CHARACTER OR BAIT AND SWITCH YOU WITH SUBPAR GAMEPLAY.

author: NukemNintendo
quote:
Never mind all of the bugs and really bad drops and frame rate this game has. Even without those things, it is still a very boring and uninspiring game that spends a great deal of time forcing me to watch it play itself. 

I understand most games might start off slow and build up to the action but this game just never gets going. 

If you are expecting to have a great time playing a crime simulation game like previous GTA games, I hope you are ready for a very boring life Sim instead. 

While life simulators can be fun, this game doesn't actually reward you for doing the boring chores and couch conversations you spend most of your time doing. 

I was also very disappointed to see how empty the beaches were despite singing hundreds of people walking around the beach in the trailers for this game. 

Instead it is just a very empty and soulless Beach. 

The very last thing that was disappointing was the very bland relationship between Jason and Lucia. The chemistry between them just seems very shoehorned and lacks any bit of passion and authenticity to it. There just isn't any real rawness to their relationship. 

I was at the very least hoping this would be a really intriguing Bonnie and Clyde story but it's just one boring life Sim.

author: TheloVely
quote:
13 years in the making and 80 bucks later, I must say, this game is exactly what's wrong with modern gaming. A game that punishes you for having fun, stops you from killing NPCs the same way you could in any other GTA title, and down right stripped the game of things that were in every other one before it. Rockstar is showing such disrespected to the players that have played their games since GTA 3. Let's break it down. 
1 - 30 FPS: The idea that this game is locked in 30 FPS in consoles, for the sake of realistic graphics, shows that Take Two and Rockstar are leaning heavily on the Movie Game style of design that has been plagging the market ever since TLOU was a huge success.
2- The Added Mechanics: A karma level was added, just like in Red Dead Redemption 1 and 2. The problem is that in those games, it made sense for the karma to exist, because the whole point of the games is to go on a REDEMPTION journey. GTA isn't that. It has never been that. GTA 6 is the only game I've ever seen that punishes a player for landing headshots, because killing people in this game is bad, and you're supposed to simply maim them. How noble. They made stealing vehicles a pain, in a GRAND THEFT AUTO game. The new wanted system is not needed, period. And to top it all off, no spoilers, but just like in RDR2, your actions lead to different consequences, which in a GTA game, a game about being a cold blooded bastard, doesn't work well.
3- The Writing: It's not as good as GTA 5, 4 or San Andreas. It's not as good as Red Dead Redemption 1 or 2. It's the exact type of writing that has you slugging through it, because you paid 80 bucks for this game, and Rockstar refuses to refund, so might as well force your way to the end. 
4- Attempting to Erase GTA's Legacy: The game stops you from killing NPCs around town, in bars and in random events, because i guess it would be fun, and we can't have that. No more prostitutes. They dumbed down the strip teasing to simply watching, when in GTA 5 you could do much more, if you know you know. The franchise that is known as THE gangster simulator, is suddenly trying to shove the moral weight of committing crimes and doing wrong things down players throats.
5- Fitness: They brought working out back. I will say, i really liked working out on GTA San Andreas. The difference is, in San Andreas, you got lean to get laid, you got fat to get laid, and you gained muscle to get laid. But in GTA 6, you're stuck with Lucia, who is a pain in the ass, and even if you let the relationship die, the game doesn't let you get anyone else.
6- The Protagonists: This is another case **** that was clearly made with a female protagonist in mind. But anyone with a brain cell knows that wouldn't sell, so they added Jason as a playable character as well. The same thing happened in AC Syndicate, and It's what's happening to the new Fable game. As GTA protagonists, Jason and Lucia are NOT it. Not even close. Jason is a good guy. A GOOD GUY. That's not GTA. Lucia is a woman, written by women. The type that Trevor Phillips would tell to shut the F up. That's not GTA.
7- Chores in a GTA: Why are you making me do stuff that I already do in real life in GTA? Groceries, maintenance, painting? IT'S GTA, Motherf*c***rs! A game where you build your base is one thing, but making a player do it just to make Lucia happy? Hard pass.
8- Game Feel: Games like this have a solid base when it comes to gameplay. But it does not feel any different from GTA 5. You got indie games making such amazing animations for every little different thing, but GTA 6 just feels like GTA 5, but new, if that makes any sense. Landing headshots still feels good, but like I said, the game punishes you for it. Driving is solid, but it's supposed to, because god forbid they manage to mess that up as well.

Another disgraceful sequel to a beloved IP. The amount of games like this keeps pilling on. I had hope that the same guys that made Bully would still be there, working at that studio, but I guess not. No point in coping. Use your 80 bucks for something else.

author: Brutalxfish
quote:
Es increíble que un juego que **** 13 años en desarrollarse termine ofreciendo un resultado tan decepcionante. Y no me refiero a los bugs, sino al apartado gráfico y a todo lo que nos prometieron durante años. Basta con comparar los primeros tráileres con el producto final para darse cuenta de la enorme diferencia entre lo que nos mostraron y lo que realmente recibimos.
Las misiones son aburridas, sosas y carecen de originalidad. El mundo abierto, aunque visualmente atractivo en ciertos aspectos, se siente vacío y carente de vida. ¿Dónde quedó aquella playa repleta de NPC, actividad y detalles que vimos en los primeros avances? Es evidente que el juego da la impresión de estar incompleto, como si muchas de las ideas originales hubieran sido recortadas o simplemente abandonadas durante su desarrollo.
Por otro lado, la historia de Jason y Lucía resulta decepcionante. Su relación parece más una representación de una pareja tóxica que una historia verdaderamente interesante. En general, siento que castraron por completo el potencial del juego, eliminando gran parte de aquello que podía convertirlo en una experiencia extraordinaria.
Lo más preocupante es que, incluso después de tantos años, GTA V sigue demostrando su superioridad en numerosos aspectos. Este nuevo título parece estar dirigido a un público con poca experiencia en videojuegos, apostando por una propuesta más simplificada y superficial.Y es aquí donde las comparaciones resultan inevitables. Mientras The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake es una auténtica oda a su obra original, donde se perciben el cariño, el respeto y la dedicación en cada detalle, este GTA parece haber perdido parte de la identidad que hizo grande a la franquicia
.Después de 13 años de espera, lo mínimo que esperaba era una obra que superara a su predecesor, no un juego que me hiciera valorar todavía más lo extraordinario que fue GTA V.
Una decepción monumental para una franquicia de la que esperaba muchísimo más.

author: Sfulzele
quote:
Waited over a decade for this and got the most restrictive GTA ever made. This series was built on chaos, and Rockstar sanded every edge off. You can't run over or shoot protesters. Trains slam on the brakes the second anything touches the track. Whole areas feel like the game is babysitting you. It's Grand Theft Auto with the theft and the auto taken out. 

Jason has zero spine. He follows Lucia around like a lapdog and never makes a decision of his own. Then the game keeps hinting that he's gay, and it feels less like character writing and more like Rockstar ticking a diversity box. Lucia is one of the most unlikable protagonists Rockstar has ever written: selfish, reckless, a terrible mother, and sleeping around behind everyone's back until she ends up with herpes. That subplot is cheap shock value, and the game still expects you to root for her.

You can feel daddy corporate's hands all over this. Somewhere a boardroom decided the biggest game of the decade needed to be a vehicle for their messaging, and the result is a GTA scared of offending anyone. The rebellious, anything-goes spirit that made this series legendary has been replaced by a corporate checklist. Every design choice feels like it went through a PR department first.

Gorgeous world, nothing to do in it. Hard pass. Biggest letdown in gaming history.

author: davidfelipe96
quote:
13 Years of Waiting for This? Rockstar Has Lost Its Identity.

Score: 0/10

After 13 years of waiting, GTA VI is one of the biggest disappointments I've ever experienced in gaming.

GTA used to stand for freedom, controversy, dark humor, and the ability to do almost anything in an open world. Unfortunately, GTA VI feels like a watered-down, politically correct version of what this franchise once represented.

- Removed adult content: Prostitutes and spontaneous sexual encounters were part of GTA's controversial identity. Their removal makes the game feel unnecessarily sanitized. Even intimate interactions between Jason and Lucia are extremely limited. GTA is an adult-rated game, so why does Rockstar suddenly seem afraid of adult themes?

- Limited player freedom: Too many aspects of the game feel restricted. From relationships to personal choices and activities, Rockstar seems more interested in controlling the player's experience than offering a truly open world.

- Frustrating progression mechanics: Losing money stored in your house and dealing with restrictions on personal belongings makes the experience unnecessarily frustrating.

- A disappointing direction for the franchise: Instead of pushing boundaries like previous GTA titles, GTA VI feels overly cautious and politically correct. The rebellious, provocative spirit that made GTA legendary seems to be disappearing.

Rockstar had 13 years, enormous resources, and an opportunity to create the ultimate open-world experience. Instead, we received a game that feels more restrictive in several important areas than its predecessors.

I wanted a GTA that expanded player freedom, relationships, adult activities, property ownership, and immersion. Not a game that takes away features and limits personal choices.

13 years for this woke garbage? Are you serious, Rockstar?

Bring back the freedom, the controversy, and the real GTA identity.

author: LegenDrx
quote:
Un juego que ha creado una expectación tan elevada en estos 13 años que le ha pasado factura y resulta decepcionante. Analizo punto por punto:
-Gráficos: Las imágenes son increíbles pero tampoco es único, ya existen títulos con ese nivel gráfico. Le resta, además, que corra a 30 fps y presente tantos bugs con la cantidad de dinero y tiempo invertido en él.
-Jugabilidad: EL cambio en los controles es fresco y mejora la jugabilidad, pero hay cosas tan detallistas que rozan la absurdez para un juego como es GTA, que se asemeja más a "The Sims" que un juego de esta categoría. La linealidad también deja que desear... no es un mundo libre, el juego te dice exactamente dónde hay que ir en cada momento y a veces te hace esperar hasta que te llaman por teléfono.
-Historia: Lo más aburrido y sin sentido para este título. Desde el minuto uno se siente más una telenovela que un GTA. Demasiada historia, demasiados diálogos. Horas y horas de solamente estar leyendo subtítulos. Se da mucha importancia a la cinemática y muy poca a la jugabilidad. Por no decir que no se sabe qué es lo que hay que hacer en el juego...¿ligar con Lucía y Jason dependiendo de a quién manejas? ¿Recuperar al hijo? No queda claro.
-Idioma: Relacionado con los diálogos, es increíble que con el presupuesto que se maneja no se traduzcan las voces. No me vengan con la película de que es una sátira de EEUU y que tal y cual. Es de vergüenza que te hagan estar leyendo todo el tiempo, ¿de que sirve tanto paisaje y detalle artístico si no se puede disfrutar y ver tranquilamente? Hay que estar el 95% del tiempo leyendo subtítulos.
Espero que se espabilen y saquen el modo online rápidamente, pues es lo único que puede salvar el juego y donde realmente la gente va a disfrutar. Y prefiero ni mencionar la polémica por las ediciones comercializadas, que eso ya es otro tema...

author: Vishal-k
quote:
Rating: 1/10

Honestly, one of the biggest disappointments in the entire GTA franchise.

The world-building and NPCs are genuinely impressive. The map is beautiful, the environment feels alive, and Rockstar has clearly put a lot of effort into creating an immersive world. Unfortunately, that's where the appreciation ends.

Lucia and Jason are, in my opinion, two of the weakest protagonists the GTA franchise has ever had. Their characters, personalities, and overall dynamic are incredibly frustrating. The story is painfully disappointing, filled with stupid character decisions and an uninteresting relationship dynamic. I genuinely question why this story was even made part of the GTA franchise.

The gameplay doesn't help either. Instead of feeling like an exciting GTA experience, it often feels like a collection of mundane everyday chores. Buying flowers, grocery shopping, washing cars, going on dates and doing other pointless activities don't automatically make a game immersive or entertaining. At times, the gameplay feels awkward, tedious and downright stupid.

The only real saving grace is the beautifully designed world and its atmosphere. But even that comes with a frustrating number of bugs.

A beautiful world cannot compensate for a terrible story, unlikeable protagonists and disappointing gameplay.

For me, this is nowhere near what a GTA game should be. The franchise deserved much better.

author: SHINNI9AMI
quote:
30fps in 2026 is indefensible. Every console version is locked to it, with no performance mode, so a flagship that looks gorgeous in screenshots feels dated the moment you move the camera. After a 13-year wait, smoothness shouldn’t be a premium feature.
The story is the other letdown. Jason and Lucia’s relationship plays like a simp simulator. For me it felt like a romance first and a crime game second, and the chaos and heists that made GTA what it is took a back seat to long drives and chores. 

GTA built its name on freedom, and GTA 6 trades a lot of it for realism. Street prostitution, in every 3D GTA since 2001, is gone, and Rockstar says it only kept features that suit Jason and Lucia’s story. Rampages and carrying unlimited weapons are gone too, and pedestrians now react the moment you pull out a gun, so the old do-whatever-you-want chaos feels policed rather than playful. Killing anyone is still possible, but your actions are tracked and carry lasting consequences, which feels like the opposite of the sandbox that made this series. The strip clubs survive; the mischief doesn’t.

Beautiful graphics, but hollow where it counts. Not worth full price.
