author: otavioshow87
quote: O jogo é uma verdadeira obra de arte no quesito ser uma porcaria. Eu não sei exatamente qual público a Rockstar queria atingir, mas provavelmente foram esses idiotas do TikTok, uma galera que nunca jogou GTA na vida e que só está jogando agora por causa do hype.Então, vamos lá. Muitas pessoas criticam o primeiro capítulo por ser extremamente lento, ter pouca ação e focar demais no relacionamento entre Jason e Lucia. Sinceramente, isso não me incomodou tanto. Como eu vim de Red Dead Redemption, achei aceitável que o primeiro capítulo fosse mais demorado e focado no desenvolvimento dos personagens, apesar de algumas situações terem parecido forçadas pra caralho.Não sou o tipo de cara que faz questão de ir a lojas de sapatos, trair a Lucia ou ficar explorando essas possibilidades de relacionamento, mas entendo perfeitamente quem gostaria de ter essa liberdade. Na minha gameplay, particularmente, não me importei com isso. Porém, não deixa de ser ridículo o Jason não poder fazer determinadas coisas com a Lucia, enquanto ela pode agir como uma vagabunda em várias partes do jogo. Até agora, não vi nenhum relato concreto de traição por parte de nenhum dos dois personagens. Talvez isso nem seja possível, mas, enfim, não deixa de ser uma escolha questionável.Agora, a decisão mais idiota dessa equipe que fez GTA 6 foi justamente acabar com a porra daquilo que sempre tornou GTA divertido, a liberdade de fazer praticamente qualquer merda que você quiser. Roubar carros, fugir da polícia até ela esquecer de você, sair matando quem quiser, causar o caos pela cidade e simplesmente fazer o que der na telha. Tudo isso sempre fez parte da identidade da franquia, mas agora parece que tudo é limitado, controlado ou bloqueado. O jogo simplesmente não deixa você fazer porra nenhuma! É uma experiência extremamente restritiva, que vai completamente contra aquilo que tornou GTA tão popular. Simplesmente uma porcaria!A equipe também parece ter tentado apelar excessivamente para a luxúria, criando personagens extremamente sexualizados e uma história progressista pra caralho. E antes que algum idiota venha falar sobre moralidade, quero deixar uma coisa bem clara. Ninguém joga GTA esperando encontrar um exemplo de bons costumes, porra! A imoralidade sempre fez parte da identidade da franquia, mas não desse jeito. A imoralidade presente em GTA 6 parece artificial, exagerada e completamente forçada. Sinceramente, parece que a Rockstar tentou enfiar uma pegada feminista na narrativa de qualquer jeito, mas acabou entregando uma merda contraditória e superficial.E o sexo explícito? PUTA QUE PARIU! Eu sei perfeitamente que sexo, prostituição e temas adultos sempre estiveram presentes nos jogos da franquia, MAS, CARALHO, TUDO TEM LIMITE! Parece que a porra da equipe feminista da Rockstar era formada por um bando de viciadas em pornografia, porque não é possível que tenham achado uma boa ideia levar a sexualização a esse nível! Se eu tivesse que resumir essa merda em uma única palavra, seria RIDÍCULO! PORRA, EU ESTOU JOGANDO GTA, NÃO NAVEGANDO EM UM SITE PORNÔ!O que eu quero de um GTA é um jogo em que a imoralidade esteja ligada principalmente ao mundo do crime. Quero uma história envolvendo máfia, organizações criminosas, corrupção, violência, traições e personagens completamente insanos, que vivem à margem da sociedade e não estão nem aí para regras, moralidade ou até mesmo laços familiares. Quero sentir que estou controlando um criminoso de verdade, um filho da puta perigoso que faz parte daquele universo caótico que sempre caracterizou a **** não! Em vez disso, vem essa porrinha de mulheres com corpos perfeitos, praticamente seminuas, situações sexualizadas a cada momento e um monte de merda que não acrescenta absolutamente nada à experiência. Parece que a Rockstar tentou forçar esse tipo de conteúdo para atrair um bando de punheteiros que nunca se interessaram de verdade pela franquia, apostando em uma sexualização exagerada e em um progressismo feminista barato.E o mais ridículo é justamente a contradição dessa porra toda. O jogo parece querer transmitir uma mensagem feminista enquanto utiliza constantemente a sexualização feminina para chamar a atenção. Que caralho de lógica é essa? Querem pagar de progressistas enquanto transformam as personagens em uma forma barata de atrair público?No fim das contas, o que poderia ser uma história marcante sobre o submundo do crime acaba perdendo espaço para um monte de elementos forçados, desnecessários e completamente **** sempre foi sobre liberdade, criminalidade, caos e sátira social. Não precisava transformar essa porra em um espetáculo de apelação sexual para continuar sendo relevante. Eu queria jogar GTA, caralho, não uma mistura de pornografia com progressismo barato!

author: Rgclay
quote: Story: 1/10This is the part that should have justified the wait. It doesn’t. The Bonnie-and-Clyde setup promised in every trailer arrives thin, directionless, and strangely lifeless. The central conspiracy never generates real tension. Dialogue is functional at best and outright flat at worst. There is no emotional through-line worth following. GTA IV had bite. GTA V had chaotic energy. Even Red Dead made you care. Here the plot exists mainly to justify expensive set pieces. After two days the story has not once made me lean forward. It has mostly made me check the time.Characters: 2/10Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos are well-rendered. Their voice acting is competent. They are also empty. Neither has a distinct personality strong enough to carry a game this long. Supporting characters feel like stock types dropped in to fill space. The optional romance system is a neat checkbox that goes nowhere because the writing never gives the relationship any actual weight. You are not inhabiting people. You are moving two expensive digital mannequins through a very expensive map.Character Development: 2/10There is almost none. The game gestures at growth and then ignores it. Choices stay cosmetic. Neither protagonist meaningfully changes based on anything you do. Compare this to Arthur Morgan’s gradual decline or even Michael and Franklin’s smaller arcs. Here the characters start and end in essentially the same place. The decade of writing time produced very little that ****: 1/10The radio is dead. Licensed tracks feel like safe playlist filler. The original score never elevates a single important moment the way older Rockstar soundtracks did. Justice’s work exists but never feels integrated into the world. You mute it. For a neon Miami-inspired setting this is a baffling miss. The music should have been one of the things that makes the city feel alive. Instead it makes the silence after you turn it off feel better.Graphics: 8.5/10This is the one category where the budget is obvious. Lighting is excellent. Facial animation is strong. Vehicle detail is high. Crowds are dense. Night driving looks the way the trailers promised. It is the best-looking open-world game on current hardware. That is also the problem. The visual quality is so far ahead of everything else that it highlights how little else was finished to the same standard. Pretty is not the same as **** Design: 5/10Leonida is big. Vice City is dense. The Keys and swamps exist. Size is not the same as good design. Roads are frequently too narrow for the speeds and traffic density the game encourages. You constantly clip, ****, or get stuck in awkward geometry that should have been solved years ago. The map often feels like a collection of impressive set pieces rather than a place that was built to be driven and lived in. The scale is there. The thoughtful layout is not.Mission Design: 2/10Most missions are the same rigid structure Rockstar has used for over a decade, just with better production values. Linear corridors. Scripted shootouts. Follow the marker. The big heists look expensive and play like upgraded 2013 content. Side activities exist but rarely feel emergent or surprising. After two days the mission fatigue is already real. There is no sense that the extra years were spent inventing new ways to structure play. There is only the sense that more money was spent making the old ways look nicer.Driving: 5/10Cars look and sound good. Handling sits in the familiar arcade-realistic range. Then you hit the roads. Narrow lanes, aggressive traffic, and constant environmental obstacles turn what should be the series’ signature joy into regular frustration. High-speed chases collapse into bumper-car nonsense. The physics are solid. The road design actively fights them. The follow-up complaint about unrealistic narrow roads is accurate and constant.Addiction: 0/10This is the category that ends the argument. I keep putting the controller down. There is no “one more mission” pull. There is no desire to keep exploring after the first few hours of visual spectacle. The game impresses in short clips and screenshots. It does not grip as a sustained experience. For a title that took 13 years and carried this much expectation, that is the most damning result of all.Overall: 2.5/10

author: LegitCritic87
quote:
WTF is this? I didn't buy GTA to do what I already do IRL with my wife. I wanted to get the greatest game of all time, (or so I thought) to wreak havoc from the jump. The game prevents you from doing so. How do you call this grand theft auto if you can't commit grand theft? Where are the hookers? I give it a 0 for story, graphics are phenomenal and outside world stuff is fun (some areas limited) but over-all a straight 1. This was a cash grab, bait n' switch. Rockstar hasn't been the same since Dan Houser left. What an embarrassment. Here is a list of what I've experienced: 

Why does everything feel like a damn chore? I wanted to play GTA, not do a second job.
You can't just cruise through a neighborhood and steal whatever car you want.
Where the hell are the hookers? They don't even exist.
Everything feels overly restricted compared to previous GTA games.
I don't want to spend half my time doing everyday activities.
Why does everything have to be so realistic? It's a video game.
I miss being able to cause absolute chaos without the game making everything complicated.
The police seem like they take forever to lose.
Why does it feel like I'm constantly being told what I can and can't do?Too many activities feel like pointless busywork.
I want to steal cars, rob people and cause trouble without jumping through hoops.
The game sometimes feels more like a life simulator than GTA.
Why are basic things so unnecessarily complicated?
I don't want to spend my gaming session running errands.
The game takes away some of the freedom that made GTA fun.
I want more random encounters instead of everything feeling scripted.
Why does everything have to be an entire mission?
I miss the ridiculous freedom of GTA San Andreas and GTA 5.
There's too much emphasis on realism and not enough on having fun.
After waiting this long, I expected to feel like a criminal in a sandbox, not somebody completing a daily chore list.
 
I'm done with Rockslop. I'll never buy a GTA game again, let alone... I highly doubt another one would be made. Dan Houser was the heart of rockstar and when you don't have him you have Relationship Simpulator Girl Boss 6. No thanks, I expect everyone to request a refund as I did. Rockstar is done for.

author: MattSaiyan
quote:
Una enorme decepción: perdió la esencia de la saga
Después de más de una década de espera, retrasos.. Este juego es una de las mayores decepciones. Esto no se siente como un GTA. Se siente como un "simulador de la vida real" lento, pesado y que se olvida de lo más importante en un videojuego: divertir.
En lo técnico: Es inaceptable. La optimización es pésima, está limitado a 30 fps incluso en PS5 Pro, y se encuentra plagado de bugs que arruinan la experiencia a un nivel que rivaliza con el desastre inicial de Cyberpunk 2077. Sin embargo, el problema más grave no son los fallos técnicos, sino el diseño mismo del juego. El exceso de realismo arruinó la jugabilidad: controles pesados, animaciones eternas para cualquier acción cotidiana y sistemas que cortan el ritmo constantemente. Se perdió por completo esa libertad caótica, la sátira ácida y el humor negro que siempre definieron a la franquicia; ahora todo se toma demasiado en serio y resulta tedioso.
A nivel narrativo tampoco levanta. La historia es aburrida y nunca termina de arrancar, los personajes no tienen el carisma suficiente para atraparte, y el diseño de las misiones llenas de caminatas lentas, Diálogos eternos y traslados interminables sin acción literalmente da sueño y te quita las ganas de seguir jugando.
Nadie niega que el apartado gráfico y el nivel de detalle del mapa sean impresionantes, pero de nada sirve un mundo hermoso si jugar en él es un somnífero. 
Incluso GTA V, que ni siquiera es mi entrega favorita de la saga, resulta muchísimo más ágil, entretenido y fiel al espíritu de la franquicia que este supuesto nuevo "GTA".

author: dnettoRaw
quote:
Um mapa incrível num GTA que perdeu a graça

O mapa e a ambientação são as únicas coisas que eu realmente gostei em GTA 6. A cidade tem personalidade e dá vontade de explorar. 
Aí você entra num carro e parece que tá empurrando um carrinho de supermercado atolado na lama. A direção é uma porcaria. Num GTA, onde você passa metade do tempo atrás do volante, isso estraga até a vontade de conhecer o mapa.

O modo história, pra mim, é uma merda. A série passou anos construindo uma identidade em cima de crime, humor ácido e personagens que faziam todo tipo de merda. Aqui, parece que tiveram tanto medo de ofender alguém que tiraram o veneno da sátira.
 A história perdeu justamente a irreverência que fazia GTA ter personalidade.
O sistema de honra também é completamente torto. Eu reajo a um assalto e saio com a honra negativa. Que lógica é essa num jogo sobre gângsteres? Pra mim, quanto mais golpes eu dou e mais carros eu roubo, mais meu nome deveria crescer no submundo. A polícia pode vir atrás de mim e os rivais podem querer me pegar. Ao mesmo tempo, a minha gangue pode passar a me respeitar mais pelo mesmo golpe. Isso faria sentido dentro do jogo.
Também senti falta da liberdade de roubar um carro qualquer, das interações adultas e da bagunça fora das missões. 
O melhor dos GTAs antigos era sair pra fazer uma coisa e, cinco minutos depois, estar no meio de uma confusão que você mesmo inventou. Em GTA 6, eu olho pra cidade e penso em tudo que eu queria poder fazer ali. Aí lembro de como é dirigir até a próxima esquina.

author: metacritic0auhc
quote:
After a thirteen-year wait, the world's most famous crime game opens with a . . .  to-do list?

Expecting a bank job, I found myself flipping burgers, playing mini-golf, fetching a dog, grocery shopping, assembling furniture, and painting walls. HOURS of errands, which was roughly the length of a heist in any previous GTA.

Then there is the morality system. Imagine buying a game whose title is a felony and getting graded on conduct. For thirty years GTA sold consequence-free chaos, whereas GTA 6 force-feeds us a conduct record, cars that stay broken, and a solipsistic partner with insane opinions that you have to treat with kid gloves lest the game punish you like an errant child.

After awhile, the 30 frames per second, with no 60fps mode, is terrible on the eyes. It dips even below that low bar in crowded streets. The whole time playing, I experienced constant crashes, and several times I lost progress despite autosave. Lucia fell through the ground during the prologue. In one mission, Jason walked straight through the side of a plane. At other points NPCs swam sideways, planes flew through buildings, and cars launched into orbit. 

I have to wonder: what alternate game are the 10/10 reviewers playing?

O jogo tem bons pontos positivos: a história é muito boa, os personagens são excelentes, os gráficos são impecáveis e os protagonistas são extremamente bons e marcantes. Porém, todos esses bugs, erros e a ausência de detalhes básicos no primeiro dia de lançamento do jogo mais aguardado da década são simplesmente inaceitáveis.

É um ótimo jogo, e quem gosta da franquia provavelmente adorou, mas, sem dúvidas, não merece nenhum GOTY, muito menos uma nota tão alta no Metacritic, levando em consideração que é apenas mais um GTA como os anteriores, com poucas inovações e que acaba se tornando entediante depois de poucas horas de jogo.

Não há todo o livre-arbítrio que deveria existir, há diversos bugs e erros nas missões, animações mal feitas e, sem contar, o fato de que o jogo foi lançado com inúmeros problemas, sem dublagem, com um preço elevado, limitado a 30 FPS e com vários outros erros.

Ainda é um bom jogo, porém deixou muito a desejar para os jogadores, que esperavam algo verdadeiramente revolucionário depois de 13 anos de espera. Se os problemas que muitos usuários estão relatando forem corrigidos, o jogo certamente melhorará bastante, mas ainda deixa muito a desejar, principalmente considerando que se trata do jogo mais esperado da década.

Em resumo, é um bom jogo, porém está longe de corresponder às expectativas que foram criadas ao longo de tantos anos. Definitivamente, não merece uma nota 99.

author: Tieleneez
quote:
Grand Theft Auto was historically built around an exaggerated but recognizable portrayal of American society. Its criminal underworld, gang hierarchies, institutional corruption and social dysfunction drew inspiration from actual human behaviour and social structures. GTA was vulgar, cynical and irreverent, but its satire had a foundation in recognizable reality.

GTA VI seems to represent a departure from that philosophy.

My criticism of Lucia as a central criminal protagonist isn't simply that she's a woman. It's that the criminal world GTA draws inspiration from is overwhelmingly male-dominated, particularly at the highest levels of organized crime. This isn't merely a cultural stereotype; criminological research documents substantial gender disparities in criminal networks, authority and access to leadership positions.

Women certainly participate in organized crime, and some become influential leaders. But exceptions shouldn't be confused with the general structure of a social phenomenon. Fictional representation should account for these realities rather than treat demographic representation as an independent creative objective.

The same concern extends to Rockstar's approach to satire. A franchise once characterized by indiscriminate irreverence now appears increasingly conscious of contemporary cultural sensitivities. It still has violence, profanity, nudity and vulgarity, but being explicit isn't the same as being genuinely transgressive. Its jokes about contemporary culture can feel recycled, while its willingness to challenge prevailing sensibilities appears more selective.

This is the contradiction: Rockstar seems interested in preserving the aesthetics of rebellion without necessarily preserving the creative philosophy that made the franchise rebellious.

The issue isn't diversity, female characters or emotional storytelling in themselves. It's the possibility that ideological considerations are increasingly taking precedence over anthropological realism, sociological correspondence and artistic consistency.

GTA VI might still look dangerous, sound vulgar and behave like Grand Theft Auto. But if its creative priorities have shifted from interpreting reality to accommodating contemporary ideological expectations, then what remains is increasingly the aesthetic of transgression rather than transgression itself.

author: tcost
quote:
A loss of Rockstar's identity.
My score comes from comparing what Rockstar used to do exceptionally well with what GTA VI appears to represent so far. And I think something fundamental is being lost.
One of the most important things about GTA V is that you start with three genuinely terrible people. They're selfish, dysfunctional, violent, deeply flawed ****. That's the starting point, and it's precisely what makes the world, the humour, the missions and the narrative work. You aren't playing some generic character who happens to get involved in crime. You're inhabiting people whose entire personalities are shaped by it.Compare that with Red Dead Redemption. John Marston is an ex-outlaw, a cold-blooded killer trying to escape a past he knows he can never truly outrun. Arthur Morgan is an outlaw, too. Max Payne is a self-destructive detective going through drugs, violence and the darkest corners of society. These characters have an identity before the game even begins. Their psychology, appearance, history and circumstances naturally inform the missions and the entire experience.
With GTA VI, however, the initial impression is quite different. We seem to have a modern man and woman with fantasies of crime, presented almost like two conventional, attractive player avatars. I miss the distinct criminal physiognomy and darker spirit that defined Rockstar's characters. It's not about making characters ugly for the sake of it. It's about giving them a visual and psychological identity that communicates something about who they are.
And this matters more than people might think. Rockstar's gameplay loop has always been relatively familiar: drive, shoot, explore, complete missions, repeat. What made that loop exceptional was the staging, the characters, the writing, the absurdity and the sheer **** nature of the situations you found yourself in. The missions worked because of the people involved and the circumstances surrounding them.
This is also where I think games like Cyberpunk 2077 have demonstrated how much more can be done with mission design, narrative setup and player involvement. It has some genuinely excellent missions and storytelling sequences. Rockstar shouldn't be the studio that starts falling behind in these areas.
Character groundedness. Compare that with John Marston in the original Red Dead Redemption. His story is about a man who understands exactly what he has done, knows there is no real redemption waiting for him, and ultimately dies trying to secure a future for his family. There is something brutally honest about that. Redemption isn't a sudden realisation that you're a good person. Sometimes it comes at the cost of your own **** that's what made those stories so memorable. They were dark, uncomfortable, absurd, tragic and occasionally completely deranged. They had a particular creative identity.I can't help wondering whether Dan Houser's departure, alongside Rockstar's enormous growth, has contributed to this shift. I don't think a studio should have to repeat itself forever, but there's a difference between evolving your identity and gradually abandoning the very things that made you distinctive in the first place.There is also an increasing sense of standardisation in modern AAA character design: attractive, polished, conventionally relatable protagonists who feel designed to appeal to everyone. Rockstar's older protagonists had uncomfortable personalities and a certain darkness. Their appearance and character belonged to the same world. They weren't simply interchangeable male and female avatars.
To be clear, I'm not claiming GTA VI cannot surprise me. I'm noting the creative direction and the impressions established so far against the standard Rockstar itself created. But based on what I've seen, I feel that Rockstar is losing some of its edge, its identity and, most importantly, its soul. 
And for a studio that once consistently delivered some of the most distinctive characters and stories in gaming, that's significant. Loved the graphics, the world, but I'm missing on gameplay expansion, cohesion, and staging.

author: xdestron
quote: Despite thirteen years of hype and undeniably impressive graphics, Grand Theft Auto VI ultimately buckles under the weight of its own obsession with hyper-realism. In trying to replicate the grounded, slow-burn simulation of Red Dead Redemption 2, Rockstar stripped away the immediate, anarchic sandbox fun that defined the franchise, replacing it with tedious chores, sluggish pacing, and restrictive inventory mechanics that make simply causing chaos feel like a hassle. The narrative struggles to justify the glacial opening hours, leaving Jason and Lucia's Bonnie-and-Clyde dynamic feeling surprisingly flat alongside dated, rigid mission design that punishes creativity. Paired with a jarring 30fps cap on consoles and no PC release in sight, Vice City ends up feeling less like a thrilling criminal playground and more like a gorgeous, overly serious tech demo that forgot how to be fun

author: notafan23
quote: I have never been more disappointed in a game. For those of you calling this a "masterpiece" and "game of the year," you are clearly not looking beyond the graphics and realism, which I can say for certain are the only enjoyable aspects of the game. In reality, the story line is not interesting or engaging, Jason is an incredibly boring, mumbling idiot, and Lucia is an annoying, pushy girlfriend who expects you to do everything for her. The game is mostly centered on maintaining a relationship between the two, and in order to do so Jason must perform chores, tasks, and missions for Lucia to keep her happy, leading to everyone criticizing it for being a "dating simulator." Due to the game also being overly realistic, the wanted system and the inability to steal certain cars is incredibly frustrating. The free-aim is clunky, the driving physics are stiff and difficult, the dialogue between the characters is boring, and the humor is bland, just like majority of the missions. This game had so much potential, and it is upsetting that Rockstar prioritized flashy, modern graphics, while ignoring the importance **** storyline, in-depth characters, and exhilarating missions, which is why we all play the game. Overall, the most accurate word I can use to describe GTA 6 is Boring, which is exactly what a GTA game should NOT be. This is a MASSIVE fail for Rockstar, and I know myself and other fans of the franchise are extremely devastated after waiting years for what was to be a groundbreaking game. Do better.

author: erilink
quote:
Lo único que he disfrutado de este juego es la experiencia de conducir. El sistema de vialidad es increíble y el paisaje luce fenomenal cuando estás conduciendo. Es una lástima que sea totalmente eclipsado por una historia predecible de Hollywood al estilo fast and furious, un gameplay sencillo, y que no está pulido como lo es el combate y manejo de armas similar a last of us, pero muy por debajo. No hay absolutamente nada de dificultad en el juego, solo he fallado 2 veces y una fue por 1 bug.

Esto es de mi propia percepción pero ninguno de los personajes tiene el carisma necesario como para ser entrañables. Si tuviera que rescatar a uno sería a Jason ya que es con quien pasas la mayor parte del tiempo y es agradable el ver cómo protege a los suyos y a su familia. Pero los demás son horribles estéticamente y con personalidades desagradables. Quiero pensar que este no es el estilo real de vida de los Americanos, por que de ser así sería muy triste.

Muchas misiones son simplemente tediosas que solo están ahí con la finalidad de aportar más a la experiencia de sentirte que estás viviendo sus vidas pero… no es posible empatizar para muchos que no tenemos ese tipo de caracter social o forma de pensar, por ende se vuelven aburridas.

Lo malo de no tener doblaje más allá de darle el gusto a uno de escuchar su propio idioma, es que estos juegos tiene diálogos durante el gameplay, y pierdes mucho contenido curioso de la historia. Preferiría que mejor hablasen cuando fuese una cinemática o momento de calma.

No voy a criticar los fps porque en mi opinión eso no influye en si un juego es bueno o no. Tampoco de los bugs porque alguien con un poco de conocimiento sobre programación de videojuegos sabría que es prácticamente imposible no ternerlos. Sobre todo con un juego de esta magnitud.

Hay escenarios muy emocionantes como las persecuciones policiacas o de bandos enemigos,  pero son muy pocas en comparación a las misiones de historia que solo se enfocan en ir de punto A a punto B solo para ir desbloqueando las importantes.

Gráficamente es increíble pero eso no basta para dar esa calificación de 99.

author: Vetsrx
quote:
GTA 6: Beautiful Graphics, but where did the fun go?
After waiting 13 years for GTA 6, I genuinely wish I could say it was worth it. Unfortunately, if I could go back and make the decision again, I probably wouldn't buy it. I'm considering requesting a refund.

I'll start with the positives. The graphics are phenomenal. Rockstar clearly put an incredible amount of effort into making the world look realistic. But there's a massive problem: 30 FPS. Coming from games that run at 60 FPS or higher, the difference is immediately noticeable. Beautiful graphics don't make up for gameplay that feels sluggish.

But my biggest disappointment isn't the frame rate. It's the lack of freedom.

Grand Theft Auto has always been about player choice. GTA 5 gave us Michael, Franklin, and Trevor, three very different characters with different personalities and motivations. Even the ending allowed us to make a significant decision about their futures.

GTA 6 felt like the opposite. Instead of having the freedom to make meaningful decisions, I felt like I was following an arrow down a predetermined path. The storyline felt predictable, the endings were cliché, and I struggled to connect with the characters.

And don't even get me started on the relationship management.

I didn't wait 13 years to play a simulator where I'm fixing a roof, painting walls, repairing stairs, and trying to keep my girlfriend happy so she doesn't leave me. I already have responsibilities in real life. I play video games to escape them.

It genuinely felt like I was playing a relationship simulator with occasional criminal activities thrown in.

The combat and driving didn't help either.

I'm not a fan of the free-aim gunplay. Vehicles felt clunky, aircraft felt clunky, and the overall gameplay never gave me that satisfying feeling I expected from a new GTA.

Then there's the professionalism system. Why am I being punished for defending myself against people actively trying to kill me?

Someone pulls a gun, starts shooting at me, and I'm supposed to worry about how professionally I handle the situation?

What am I supposed to do? Shoot the gun out of his hand, tip my cowboy hat, and say, "Not today, partner," before walking into the sunset?

This isn't a Clint Eastwood movie.

The restrictions on interacting with certain NPCs, including protesters, made the world feel even less free. I'm not saying everyone needs to play like a complete psychopath. I'm saying the player should have the choice, and the game world should respond accordingly.

That's what made GTA entertaining. You could be good, bad, reckless, responsible, or somewhere in between.

Instead, GTA 6 felt determined to tell me how I was supposed to play.

And where is the criminal empire fantasy?

You're pulling off heists, taking over criminal operations, and supposedly building something bigger. Yet somehow, you're still struggling financially.

What's the point of taking over an empire if you can't enjoy the rewards?

In GTA 5, making money meant buying cars, properties, upgrades, and enjoying the ridiculous lifestyle that came with being a successful criminal.

Here, it felt like I was working just to survive.

I'm already doing that in real life. Why would I want to spend my free time doing it again?

The lack of an autosave system in my experience was another frustrating issue. Having to constantly remember to save manually, with the possibility of losing progress, felt unnecessarily outdated.

Ultimately, GTA 6 looks incredible but feels incredibly disappointing.

The humor, the freedom, the memorable characters, the excitement of building wealth, and the ability to play the way you wanted were what made this franchise special to me.

I didn't feel that magic here.

When the credits rolled, I wasn't excited to jump back in. I wasn't thinking about replaying the story or exploring different outcomes.

I was thinking, "That's it?"

If GTA 6 Online follows the same direction, count me out. I'd rather return to GTA 5 and GTA Online, where I can actually enjoy the freedom that made me fall in love with this franchise.

Thirteen years of waiting for better graphics and less freedom isn't the evolution I wanted.

Rockstar made a beautiful world. I just wish they'd remembered to make it fun.

author: crazydaydreamer
quote:
GTA 6 feels like a franchise hijacked by a new creative team more interested in pushing its own social agenda than delivering the experience that made Grand Theft Auto legendary.

The game constantly moralizes your actions, using its morality system to steer you toward the writers' worldview. Instead of giving players the freedom to be criminals in an outrageous sandbox, it lectures and judges you for playing the game the way GTA was meant to be played.

The humor is just as disappointing. It's flat, predictable, sanitized, and painfully safe. Gone is the fearless satire that mocked everyone and everything without apology. The writing feels like it was reviewed and approved by an HR department terrified of offending anyone.

GTA used to be rebellious, offensive, absurd, and unapologetically entertaining. Now it feels like the developers are more concerned with teaching players how to think than letting them have fun.

The world is bigger and prettier than ever, this the 1 not a 0, but the personality that made GTA special is gone. Rockstar traded its edge for ideological conformity, and the result is a corporate-approved imitation of its former self.

author: Porrabdalf
quote:
An incredible technical achievement, but a step backward in what made GTA special.

GTA VI is visually impressive, with remarkable animations, environmental detail and production values. Unfortunately, technological sophistication doesn't automatically translate into better gameplay or storytelling.

Previous GTA games offered freedom, experimentation and sharp social satire. GTA VI increasingly replaces that freedom with restrictive progression, tedious routines and excessive simulation. There may be more things to do, but that doesn't necessarily mean more meaningful choices.

Building furniture, watching TV, buying flowers and performing repetitive everyday activities may create familiarity with the characters, but familiarity isn't the same as character development. Stronger writing and meaningful decisions could achieve more in far less time. Calling these activities optional also ignores how relationship progression can influence the endings players want.

The morality system raises similar questions. When scripted criminal behavior and player-initiated violence are treated differently, it becomes difficult to see the system as a coherent exploration of morality rather than another restriction on player freedom.

The monetization makes these design choices even harder to defend. The Ultimate Edition provides functional conveniences, while GTA+ offers economic and transportation advantages. These benefits reduce costs and inconveniences created by the game's own systems. Restricting cheats and access to resources further undermines the freedom traditionally associated with GTA.

We cannot prove these mechanics were originally designed to sell convenience, but their relationship with paid benefits deserves serious scrutiny, especially in an $80 game.

Rockstar once satirized corporations that monetized every aspect of people's lives. The irony of its current business model is difficult to ignore.

GTA VI is an extraordinary technological showcase, but technology eventually becomes outdated. What lasts is artistic identity, meaningful interactivity and good game design.

More realism doesn't necessarily mean more freedom, more depth, or a better GTA.

The upgrades are cool, don’t get me wrong—the police are better, the NPCs are better, and the random world interactions are good. I wish they had focused on a few key things. GTA 4 and 5 were only 5 years apart and both are arguably better story-wise. GTA 4 even has some realistic aspects that 5 and 6 don’t. After 13 years, they might as well have run polls on every major decision and let players help shape the game.

author: JeffmiTheX
quote:
If I could write more than 5000 characters on this website, I would be happy to do so. This game is the symbol of the ending of physical media, and this is the best that Sony and Rockstar can do to justify the option of physical media being taken away,

First of all, this is proof that game journalists are completely censored for being vocal about games that all the multibillion-dollar companies release. They will give the most positive review of all time in order not to be blacklisted, then wait for everyone to give what they genuinely thought about this game, and then let the "fanboys" give the game a good review, despite the consensus being that GTA VI didn't reach our expectations and that it totally destroyed what made GTA... "GTA".

It is an insult to even call this game "The game of the Year", or even the most anticipated game of all time, when what the bare minimum that Rockstar can do for their ultimate editions is asking the gamers to pay 100$ for barely anything behind this version, when not delivering anything, to this game to justify the insane price that cost all the groceries of the week.

It should be a shame to call this game a sequel to GTA V, when all this game does is deliver a simulator game where you can't even commit crimes anymore (not to many) in order to not shift the story, when this wasn't a thing in previous GTA games, and having the ability to steal high-end cars locked behind the progression of the story. You can only steal low-end cars, when once again, stealing every car was the main premise of previous GTA games, and also the fact that your car will come to a stop when running out of gas, and have to pay with your own money to keep it running again, and the repair as well, I guess cars can't restore themselves anymore, some people will say, I bet.

Let's not forget that all of the "arcady" mechanics of this that made GTA games iconic have been completely stripped away from this game in favor of realism, when most of the people on this platform just wanna lose themselves and have fun playing video games. This is what makes video games a hobby for everyone to enjoy, but the concept of realism is the main objective for Rockstar to achieve in order to satisfy their shareholders, which wasn't well received.

The 30 fps debate should not be an excuse to look at your customers and say "yeah, let's add more people to the beach and make anything choppy in order to put the PS5/Xbox to its limits" when the games are struggling to even hit 30 fps because it was targeted to be this way, by Rockstar. The game struggles to hit that number and sometimes, in the worst-case scenario, would drop to 25 to 15 fps. I could only imagine how much the framerate will be online in this game when GTA Online will be released to the public.

This game is filled with bugs, like Cyberpunk 2077. While this might be a terrible comparison to some people, they both have things in common: They were overhyped and praised by the public before the game was released. The only difference was that Playstation took Cyberpunk off the store and refunded their customers. With GTA VI on the market, I wonder why they won't give any refunds anymore, aside from being "digital only" and just "codes in the box". It's a bit strange that Sony would go down this path just for this game, in order to keep the customers money that they work so hard to get, just to be taken away by all the multibillion-dollar corporations, just for them to keep doing their bad business practices

With my thoughts left out of my chest, I want you, the reader, to remind you that no matter what game you love, the "fanboys" and journalists will always add some false reviews just to increase its score. It's up to you to play the game, or at the very best, watch some gameplay around any games, and give your thoughts in order to spread your words to other people.

My score number I gave on GTA VI might not represent the actual game, but just know that I didn't play this game. My sources to inform myself about any video games are to watch gameplays of other people on social media and make my own thoughts and get them out of my chest for you to read and review. I might make some spelling mistakes here and there, but what is more important is leaving a message, so people can understand you.

With not many characters left. I would like to say that this game isn't worth being "Game of the Year" or being "the greatest game of all time". For me, a great game isn't about taking away the features it had back in the days; otherwise, this would be a game that no one or the fans who love this game series would enjoy playing, or getting new people to enjoy the game and make them learn more about previous games.

If you made it all the way to the end, you are a good reader, who takes his time to read anyone's points and gather them one by one and make his own thoughts about them, to help everyone be informed about many topics around the world while having skepticism.

author: NightCrusader
quote: The attention to detail is extraordinary. The graphics, environments, and immersion are genuinely impressive. Unfortunately, that’s where much of the praise ends.Rockstar seems to have forgotten what made GTA iconic: freedom, chaos, dark humour, outrageous characters, criminal ambition, and unapologetic satire.Instead, we get what increasingly feels like a boyfriend simulator disguised as a crime game. Relationship meters, domestic chores, moral consequences, and unnecessary restrictions have taken priority over the criminal freedom that defines this franchise. Since when did GTA become a game about worrying about your relationship instead of causing absolute chaos?The gameplay is unnecessarily overcomplicated, the story feels weak, and the edgy, provocative identity that once made GTA special seems to have been sacrificed for a safer, more restrained experience.A breathtaking world cannot compensate for a disappointing game. Rockstar has delivered incredible technical detail while losing sight of the very things that made Grand Theft Auto legendary.

author: ArminDRK
quote:
As an avid GTA fan who's loved the series for years, I'm genuinely disappointed with GTA 6. It simply doesn't feel like GTA anymore. The freedom, chaos and ridiculous fun that made this franchise iconic have been replaced by excessive realism and boring life simulation.There's way too much focus on mundane real-life activities, errands, maintaining relationships and everyday chores. 

I play GTA to escape real life, not to experience its most boring aspects.What's even more frustrating is how selective this realism is. Rockstar wants everything to feel realistic until it comes to actual player freedom. 

You can't even cheat on Lucia with another character, pursue other romantic interests or hire prostitutes like in previous games. Apparently, you can commit serious crimes, but being unfaithful is where Rockstar draws the line? 

The irony is **** increasingly restrictive gameplay, punishing police mechanics, slow missions, clunky controls and a disappointing 30fps cap, and it feels like Rockstar has forgotten what made GTA special.

Realism should enhance freedom, not replace it. GTA was always about having the freedom to do things you wouldn't do in real life, not being forced to live a second, more tedious version of it.Beautiful graphics, but a massive step backwards in what actually matters: fun and player choice.

author: playedit3467
quote:
A masterpiece, and the people crying about it are telling on themselves. Let's get the real criticism out of the way first, because unlike half the reviews on this page, I actually played the game: the 30fps cap is frustrating. On a game this gorgeous, it stings. That's a legitimate gripe. Almost nothing else in this pile of zero star tantrums is.
Scroll through the negative reviews and count how many say "got a refund" or "watched my friend play it." Are you **** kidding me? You didn't play the game. You played twenty minutes, got upset that Jason bought his girlfriend flowers, and ran to Metacritic to cry about it. Thirteen years of development, judged in the time it takes to microwave a burrito.
"It's gone woke." Really? You can snort coke, rob, carjack and gun down half of Vice City, but because you can't hire a prostitute anymore, it's feminist propaganda. Mmm. Super woke. Truly the most progressive game ever made, right up until your fortieth homicide of the afternoon.
And the big scandal: there's a woman in it. For some of you, probably the first woman you've spent this much time with. Oh, and she's Latina. In Florida. They're really forcing that **** down our throats, aren't they? A Latina in Miami. What's next, humidity?Think the satire is dead? Turn on the radio. Listen to the talk stations and the podcasts. Rockstar is still roasting everyone, left and right. If the humor feels gone, maybe it's because you finally noticed some of the jokes are about **** it perfect? No. Is it an evolution of the formula that made GTA what it is? Absolutely.
The review bombing says nothing about the game and everything about the times. It's anonymity behind a keyboard, basement-dwelling incels being toxic for sport, a fake culture war, misogyny and plain stupidity. GTA has spent 25 years satirizing America. Turns out the Metacritic user reviews do it better than Rockstar ever could.

author: wacaat
quote: I was born in 2003, and the first game I ever played was GTA: San Andreas. For as long as I can remember, GTA has been part of my life. I grew up with these games, and I waited years for GTA 6 with real excitement. That's why it hurts to say this: GTA 6 has no Turkish subtitles. Turkey has one of the biggest and most loyal GTA communities in the world. We've supported this series for over two decades, bought every release, and kept GTA Online alive. Yet in 2026, in one of the most expensive and story-driven games ever made, Rockstar still couldn't add Turkish subtitles. Many smaller studios with far smaller budgets manage to do it. A story this big deserves to be understood fully by everyone who plays it. Without subtitles in their own language, a lot of players will miss the dialogue, the humor and the details that make GTA special. Rockstar, please listen to your Turkish fans and add Turkish subtitles in an update. Until then, I can't recommend this game, even though it breaks my heart to say it.

author: Caiogamerado
quote: Para começar minha avaliação negativa, deixo claro que sou um superfã de GTA pela liberdade que a franquia dá, junto com a imoralidade, a ação e o humor ácido e negro com todos os grupos detalhe: sou autista e não consegui jogar o jogo porque a mercenária e corporativista Rockstar não quis lançá-lo para PC, querendo lucrar duas vezes em cima dos jogadores e deixando claro que não somos prioridade para eles — além de terem acabado com a mídia física. O que vou avaliar aqui é a minha percepção geral acompanhando o jogo pela internet, em uma nota de protesto e revolta pelo estado atual do título.Para começar, o jogo tem pontos positivos, como os gráficos e a jogabilidade, mas nada disso adianta se você joga a 30 FPS. Vamos ser sinceros: eles tiveram 12 anos para otimizar o jogo e um orçamento de 2 bilhões de dólares para, simplesmente, lançar um título mal otimizado, que não mantém nem os 30 FPS em vários momentos. Além disso, o jogo também tem uma quantidade considerável de bugs — não chega a ser no nível de Cyberpunk, mas ainda assim incomoda. Detalhe: os gráficos usam upscaling até o limite, mostrando que eles se esforçaram de forma preguiçosa para manter o jogo no máximo a 30 FPS da maneira mais porca possível. Esse tipo de técnica de resolução não é muito boa quando usada de forma exagerada. De coisa boa, temos apenas os gráficos e a jogabilidade, que ainda assim acabam prejudicados pela má otimização, embora sejam melhores que outros requisitos técnicos do próprio jogo.Continuando: o jogo literalmente te coloca em um simulador de namoro, com mecânicas de simulador de vida nas missões, deixando a ação e um roteiro complexo de lado para você virar um "namoradinho beta" da Lucia. O Jason não tem quase nenhum momento de destaque; o desenvolvimento de roteiro e de personagem vai todo para ela.Você não tem liberdade nenhuma. Por exemplo:• Não pode roubar o carro do vizinho;• Não pode atirar em todos os NPCs;• Não pode contratar prostitutas;• Não pode rejogar missões;• Não pode trair a Lucia;• Pode matar brancos, negros e animais, mas não pode matar pessoas LGBTQ+ em boates nem alguns NPCs militantes específicos.E isso porque ainda há muita coisa que o jogo não permite fazer. Eles literalmente sacrificaram toda a liberdade, a imoralidade, o humor ácido e a ação narrativa que o título poderia ter para entregar um jogo politicamente correto, com roteiro de namoro e simulador de vida por enquanto, minha avaliação termina aqui. Vou esperar o jogo sair pirata para PC para ter minha opinião final e completa.

author: Luhm0nk
quote: GTA 6 is genuinely one of the most ambitious games Rockstar has ever attempted, and I feel like a lot of people aren't fully appreciating just how much has changed from previous entries. We're talking about a game that's trying to push open world gaming beyond simply having a massive map with missions scattered around it. The level of detail, environmental interactions, NPC behaviour and everyday activities makes the world feel like something that actually exists outside of the player. That's something I've always wanted from an open world game. A world where you aren't constantly the centre of everything happening around **** of the biggest things I appreciate is the direction Rockstar took with realism and life simulation. Being able to experience ordinary activities alongside the criminal side of GTA adds another layer to the experience. Not everything needs to involve shooting someone, stealing a car or blowing something up to be entertaining. Sometimes the enjoyment comes from exploring, interacting with people and seeing how the world responds to your actions. The relationship between Jason and Lucia also introduces a different kind of storytelling that we haven't really experienced in previous GTA games. Instead of constantly relying on the same chaotic personalities and nonstop action, Rockstar is attempting something more grounded and **** obviously the game isn't without criticism. Performance issues, frame drops, bugs and restrictions on player freedom are completely reasonable things to bring up. Especially considering how long people have waited and how much the game costs. A technically impressive world doesn't automatically excuse poor optimization, and realism shouldn't come at the expense of making the gameplay unnecessarily restrictive. Those are actual criticisms worth discussing, and Rockstar should be held accountable for **** what genuinely confuses me is some of the reasoning behind these negative reviews. I've seen people give the game terrible ratings simply because the story focuses on a relationship, because certain missions involve everyday activities or because the pacing isn't identical to GTA 5. Some people are acting like GTA has always followed one specific formula when that couldn't be further from the truth. GTA 4 took a more serious direction compared to San Andreas, and GTA 5 introduced an entirely different approach with three protagonists. Every major installment has experimented with its own identity.A new game in a franchise isn't supposed to be a carbon copy of the previous one. If Rockstar released GTA 5 again with a bigger map and improved graphics, people would be complaining about the lack of innovation. Yet when Rockstar actually expands the formula and introduces new experiences, suddenly people are saying it isn't GTA anymore. Just because a game doesn't match the exact experience you personally wanted doesn't automatically make it a bad **** the whole argument that GTA shouldn't have life simulation elements because people play video games to escape reality makes even less sense to me. Escaping reality doesn't necessarily mean escaping everything realistic. For some people, immersion is the entire reason they play games. Being able to experience a believable world where you have opportunities, responsibilities and consequences that you might never experience in real life is literally part of that **** the end of the day, I think GTA 6 deserves to be judged on what it actually accomplishes rather than how closely it recreates GTA 5. You can dislike the direction Rockstar took, and that's completely fair. But personal disappointment and genuine flaws aren't always the same thing. For me, the ambition behind creating a world that feels more alive, interactive and unpredictable is exactly the kind of evolution I want to see from this franchise. GTA doesn't need to abandon its identity to evolve and evolving doesn't mean abandoning everything that made the series special.

author: Everest117
quote:
From the moment you jump into GTA VI, it’s hard not to be impressed. The visuals, the atmosphere, and the sheer amount of detail Rockstar has put into this world are incredible. Even with the game running at 30 FPS, the experience feels smooth and consistent. I haven’t encountered any noticeable performance issues so far.  

The story, in my opinion, is one of the strongest in the entire franchise. Unlike previous GTA titles, where chaos and mayhem often take center stage, GTA VI takes a more grounded and cinematic approach. The story feels like you’re playing through a well-written crime drama. I haven’t even finished the game yet, but every time I complete a mission, I immediately want to jump into the next one. That’s how invested I’ve become in the characters and their story. 

One thing I particularly appreciate is the pacing. The game starts relatively slowly, giving you time to understand the characters and get comfortable with the world. Then, little by little, things begin escalating into the kind of chaos you’d expect from Grand Theft Auto. It feels natural rather than overwhelming. 

And the open world? Easily one of the most impressive I’ve experienced in gaming. The attention to detail is remarkable. Whether you’re flying a plane, driving a boat, exploring underwater, or getting into a shootout, there’s always something that makes you appreciate the amount of work that went into creating this game. The shooting mechanics, exploration, and overall gameplay have been a blast.

Is it perfect? Not entirely. There are definitely a few features I wish had returned, including some of the more controversial interactions from previous GTA games and the ability to purchase your own properties, something GTA Online eventually expanded upon. Hopefully, we’ll see some of these features introduced or expanded when GTA VI Online arrives. I’m especially curious to see how Rockstar builds upon this already impressive world with multiplayer.

Despite those missing features, I genuinely believe GTA VI deserves a 10/10 based on my experience so far. It’s not because the game is flawless, but because everything it does well far outweighs the few things I wish were included.

Rockstar has created a world that’s incredibly easy to get lost in, and even after spending hours playing, I still find myself wanting more.

I haven’t been able to stick with a game for more than an hour at a time in ages, but I just spent 10 hours on this in a single day. It’s incredible.

quote: First 15 hours of the game you do chores. Everything is restricted and locked, and despite being a GTA game, it punishes you for wanting to do crimes. Jason has terrible writing and voice acting, the most boring character in any video game ever. Every line he says is just like "Yep", "Yeah", "Lucia Caminos" and not a single note worthy thing. He buys Lucia clothes, jewelry, fixes the house for her, and a bunch of other stuff, just for her to talk to other men whilst he's doing so, literally making him a genuine c*ck and making you play as one. You can't even try to rob certain cars, shoot a lot of certain NPCs because they didn't want to offend people (even though the whole reason why the first GTAs were popular was because it offended people). Despite being a game about committing crimes, it has an honor-like system that punishes you permanantly for committing said crimes, which would fit in other games where you redeem yourself (rdr2), but in a game about Grand THEFT Auto, you get punished permanently for doing said grand theft auto. There's barely any progression and you make like $0. Not to mention the 30 fps. Anybody who says this is a good game are only looking at the graphics and completely disregarding everything else. This game is not worth $100, just go buy the other older Rockstar games instead.
